findings.name: Free Trial: one-time $5 credit for new accounts
findings.detail: New accounts receive a one-time $5 promotional credit, usable across all public models (currently gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b). Free Trial rate limits per model: 5 RPM, 30K uncached TPM, 90K total TPM, 1M tokens/hour, 1M tokens/day; qwen-3.8-27b vision capped at 2 images per request / 10 MiB payload. Free context is truncated vs paid: gpt-oss-120b 65k vs 131k, qwen-3.8-27b 64k vs 128k. Official changelog entry 2026-07-16 ('Free Trial credits for new accounts') introduced it; it replaces the prior always-free tier.
findings.eligibility: Any new account — no .edu email, no startup status, no funding cap. A verified payment method (credit/debit card) IS required before Playground/API activate; you are not charged unless you buy PayGo credits. No region limits stated on official pages (one third-party tracker notes access is intended outside mainland China, unverified).
findings.claim: Sign up for Cerebras Inference → add a valid payment method (activates Playground + API and grants the $5 credit) → build within Free Trial limits; a first PayGo credit purchase upgrades the account to Developer tier (much higher limits, e.g. gpt-oss-120b 1K RPM / 1M uncached TPM; no hourly/daily caps).
findings.expiry: Credit expires 30 days after it is granted; no renewal. When the credit is exhausted or expires, API and Playground access pause (keys/projects/settings stay intact); you must purchase PayGo credits to resume.
findings.gotchas: Card required despite being a 'free' trial (unlike most free tiers); credits are non-transferable, no cash value, and may be withheld/revoked for fraud, abuse, or duplicate accounts; 5 RPM breaks any agent that fires parallel tool calls (instant 429s); limits are per organization and per model; 'free' context windows are shorter than paid; model menu keeps shrinking (GLM-4.7 and Gemma 4 31B no longer on public endpoints as of Aug/Sep 2026); many guides still quote the old '1M free tokens/day' tier which no longer exists.

findings.name: YC Startup Deal: up to $22,500 in Cerebras Cloud inference credits
findings.detail: YC startups from any batch receive up to $22.5K worth of inference on Cerebras Cloud, plus priority support and co-marketing opportunities. Official page states 'No setup fees, no strings.' No published credit expiration, deadline, or per-startup amount caps.
findings.eligibility: YC (Y Combinator) startups from any batch — the current offer is YC-only on the official page. No funding/age caps stated. Non-YC startups are instead routed through Cerebras channel partners.
findings.claim: Apply via the 'Apply Now' button on https://www.cerebras.ai/yc-startup-deal (links to a HubSpot application form); an RSVP button on the same page points to the same form.
findings.expiry: No end date or credit-expiry stated on the official page; 'up to $22.5K' is discretionary and no separate terms page is on record.
findings.gotchas: Eligibility is YC-batch-only (the earlier open 'Cerebras for Startups' program is marked no longer available on third-party trackers); the exact credit amount you receive is not published — 'up to $22,500'; co-marketing commitment is mentioned but undefined.

findings.name: No student/education program exists (negative finding)
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 there is no .edu/student or academic licensing offer from Cerebras. Neither the pricing page, the inference docs, nor searches of 2025-2026 coverage surface a student discount, education license, or academic credit program. The only education-adjacent item is a free DeepLearning.AI short course 'Fast LLM Inference with Cerebras' (built with Cerebras, launched ~July 2026) — instructional content, no API credits.
findings.eligibility: N/A — nothing to claim for students specifically; students use the standard $5 trial (card required) or Cerebras models hosted on partner platforms (OpenRouter, HuggingFace, AWS Marketplace), where the partner's own free allowances may apply.
findings.claim: None on Cerebras itself; students may take the free DeepLearning.AI course (enroll at deeplearning.ai, free) for hands-on Cerebras inference learning.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: No .edu verification anywhere in Cerebras's onboarding; if a tool offers 'Cerebras student credits', it is not an official Cerebras program. Partner front-ends (OpenRouter free models, HuggingFace free tier) are how cardless users actually reach Cerebras-hosted models for free.

findings.name: Referral token-bonus program (third-party reported, unverified)
findings.detail: A third-party tracker (Model Speed Arena) describes a Cerebras referral program: +200K Qwen3-Coder tokens/day for both referrer and referee, capped at +1M extra tokens/day, with personal referral links generated from an in-product signup flow. This does not appear on any Cerebras official page I could find.
findings.eligibility: Unknown — described as an in-product signup/referral flow; likely open to existing users.
findings.claim: Per the third-party description: generate a personal referral link from the Cerebras console's signup flow and share it; both parties gain daily token bonuses.
findings.expiry: Unknown; no stated deadline in the third-party source.
findings.gotchas: Treat as unverified/stale: the model it references (Qwen3-Coder) is not in the current public model catalog (only gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b as of Oct 2026), and Cerebras official pages make no mention of a referral program. Confirm in-console before relying on it.

sunset_notes: 1) The old always-free tier ("1M free tokens/day", no card required — announced June 2025 when Cerebras opened the API without a waitlist) ended in July 2026: the official changelog shows the $5 Free Trial credit launching 2026-07-16 and a third-party tracker (pricepertoken.com) dates the old free tier's end to 2026-07-21. Cerebras now states plainly there is no permanently free or auto-renewing tier; a verified payment method is required for any access. 2) The earlier general "Cerebras for Startups" program (up to $22,500 GPU/inference credits, direct application, no partner required) is marked "No Longer Available" on third-party trackers; the surviving startup offer is the YC Startup Deal (YC startups any batch, up to $22.5K), recorded on the official site as of early Aug 2026. 3) Public shared-inference model menu shrunk through 2025-2026: Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen 3 32B deprecated (Feb 2026), zai-glm-4.7 deprecated 2026-08-17, gemma-4-31b removed from public endpoints 2026-09-03 (dedicated only), qwen-3.8-27b added 2026-09-03; as of Oct 2026 the public catalog is just gpt-oss-120b and qwen-3.8-27b. 4) Cerebras Code Pro ($50/mo, ~24M tokens/day) and Code Max ($200/mo, ~120M tokens/day) flat-rate coding plans were sold out / on waitlist at time of reporting — neither is free. 5) No region restrictions are stated on official pages; third-party trackers suggest access outside mainland China.

provider: Cloudflare Workers AI (inference platform free tier) — LLM & AI APIs

findings.name: Workers AI free tier: 10,000 free Neurons/day (no signup offer needed)
findings.detail: Cloudflare's Workers Free AND Workers Paid plans each include 10,000 Neurons per day at no charge; the cap resets daily at 00:00 UTC; exceeding it makes further Workers AI requests fail. 72 models currently listed (39 LLM, 6 embeddings, 6 image, 10 audio, 11 other). Pricing page was restructured: "updated to be more granular, with per-model unit-based pricing presented" (per-model $/token, $/tile, $/minute alongside Neuron equivalents); backend billing still uses Neurons. On Workers Paid, usage above the daily allowance costs $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons; prepaid AI Gateway credits can also cover frontier-model usage and raise rate limits for those models.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Cloudflare account on the Workers Free plan (no credit card, no application, no .edu/funding requirements); the same allowance also ships with Workers Paid. US region: no student-only or startup-only gate.
findings.claim: Create a free Cloudflare account (no payment method required for the Free plan) and call Workers AI (HTTP API or Worker binding). 10,000 Neurons/day auto-applies; nothing to redeem.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; daily 10k-Neuron window resets at 00:00 UTC. No fixed end date.
findings.gotchas: 8 frontier models (kimi-k2.6, kimi-k2.7-code, glm-5.2, glm-5.3, glm-5.3-flash, deepseek-v4-flash-0731, deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, deepseek-v4-pro-0813) require a paid billing method — unavailable on Free plan alone, even within the free Neuron allowance. Neurons-per-request varies by model and input/output direction, so the effective free daily quota in tokens differs widely per model; per-model caps also exist. On Paid, overage is $0.011/1k Neurons. Egress/data costs: Workers AI calls from a Worker are same-edge, but if your app is outside Workers, standard API call costs apply.

findings.name: Cloudflare for Startups: up to $350,000 in credits (3 tiers: $10k / $100k / $350k)
findings.detail: Current structure (read on cloudflare.com/startups today): Tier 3 = $10k credits (bootstrapped/self-funded or under $1M raised, no partner needed); Tier 2 = $100k (under $5M raised, funded by an affiliated partner, account manager + expert sessions); Tier 1 = $350k ($5M+ raised, funded by affiliated partner, account manager, priority support, bi-weekly Solutions Architect office hours). Credits are valid 1 year or until fully consumed, whichever comes first; no extensions. Credits cover usage-based services; Workers AI is subject to per-tier caps: $2,500 (Tier 3), $10,000 (Tier 2), $50,000 (Tier 1), at standard partner-model pricing; R2 capped at $10,000; AI Gateway temporarily NOT covered by credits. Free at every tier: 3 enterprise domains, unlimited Pro/Business plans, DDoS/bot protection, WAF with 1,000 custom rules, CDN/DNS, LB (2 origins), 100% SLA. Business email matching company domain required; a valid payment method on file is required.
findings.eligibility: For-profit tech company incorporated within the last 10 years; funding up to Series B, funded within the last 12 months; live public website; active LinkedIn/X/GitHub; first-time program applicants only; business email matching your company domain (no personal email). Tier 2/1 require funding by an affiliated (approved VC/accelerator) partner.
findings.claim: 1) Create a standard Cloudflare account and add a billing/payment method. 2) Fill the application at /lp/startups (company domain email, website, social link, Cloudflare account ID). 3) Manual review ~48 hours; on approval credits and plan upgrades are applied to the account. Rejections include a reason and you may request re-evaluation.
findings.expiry: Credits: 12 months from approval or until consumed; no renewal/extension offered (upgrading tier does not reset the 12-month window). Program expansion (Sept 2025) also covers non-profits/civil-society orgs (up to $250k, per Birthday Week 2025 announcement).
findings.gotchas: Credit card/payment method IS required despite being a 'free credits' program. Overage beyond the credit balance is billed automatically. The old 4-tier structure ($5k/$25k/$100k/$250k, announced April 2025) was replaced — Tier 3 raised $5k→$10k, top tier $250k→$350k. Workers AI sub-cap ($2.5k–$50k depending on tier) means most of the $350k is NOT spendable on Workers AI. AI Gateway excluded for now. Non-US regional pages (e.g. en-in) still show the outdated $250k/4-tier structure — the US .com page is authoritative.

findings.name: Cloudflare for Students: 12 months of Workers Paid at no cost (US .edu students)
findings.detail: US students 18+ with a verified .edu billing email get the Workers Paid plan's $5/month base fee waived for 12 months, with increased usage allotments vs. the free plan: up to 500 Worker scripts, 10M requests/month (+$0.30/M after), 20M included logs/month (+$0.60/M after), up to 30s CPU per request, 6,000 build minutes/month, 6 concurrent build slots, extra Workers KV edge storage. The announcement post (Sept 22, 2025) additionally listed Hyperdrive unlimited DB queries/day, Durable Objects 1M req/day (+$0.15/M after), Logpush 10M events/month, and Queues 1M ops/month — usage beyond the paid-tier allotments still incurs standard rates, and Workers AI remains metered at $0.011/1k Neurons (10k Neurons/day included on any plan). Includes a dedicated student Discord. Announced at Birthday Week, Sept 22, 2025.
findings.eligibility: United States only; 18+; currently enrolled in an eligible educational program; verified .edu email address that must be the BILLING email (not just signup email). Expansion to other countries is requested via the program's school-domain registration form.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up (or log in) with your verified .edu email. 2) On the Billing page, add a valid credit card and confirm your billing email is the .edu address. 3) Add the Workers Paid plan at the Workers plans page — the $5/mo fee auto-waives for 12 months. 4) Confirmation email arrives in your inbox.
findings.expiry: 12 months; if you don't renew to standard Workers Paid, the account auto-reverts to Workers Free with no charge. No automatic renewal of the waiver.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (verification + overage billing) even though the fee is waived; overage usage above student allotments is charged to that card. Not stackable with the Startup Program's business email requirement (personal .edu vs company domain). Workers AI 'free' access here is just the plan's standard 10k Neurons/day — the student offer does NOT add extra AI neurons; heavy LLM use costs money on the student account.

findings.name: Workers Launchpad: cohort accelerator — Startup Enterprise Plan ($250k in credits) + VC access
findings.detail: Cohort-based funding program for startups building on the Cloudflare Developer Platform. Benefits per the program page: Startup Enterprise Plan worth $250,000 in credits plus enterprise features (Workers, Workers AI, KV, Durable Objects, R2, Images, Stream, D1, etc.), VC introductions from Cloudflare's partner network (program claims >$2B committed to Workers startups), Workers Founders Bootcamp, weekly office hours, virtual Demo Day with blog feature. Cohort #6 was announced Sept 2025. Note: the live page is heavily JS-rendered; my direct fetch of the page today returned only the high-level landing copy — the $250k benefit text comes from the cached/extracted page content in search results, not a full live re-read.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups building on Workers/Cloudflare platform; application via cohort-based process (no public age/funding caps published on the page I could fully read; cohort selection at Cloudflare's discretion). Launchpad alumni/participants are also eligible for Cloudflare's 2026 office 'hubs' in SF, Austin, London, Lisbon.
findings.claim: Apply to the next cohort via the Launchpad page/application form; participate in the program; receive credits via the Startup Enterprise Plan, VC intro, bootcamp, and demo day.
findings.expiry: Cohort-bound; the underlying $250k credit follows the Startup Program's 1-year validity. New cohorts announced roughly annually.
findings.gotchas: Details on credit amounts/caps couldn't be confirmed from a clean live page read today (JS-rendered page returned only landing copy) — treat the $250k figure as medium confidence. Overlaps/stacking rules with the standard Startup Program tiers are not spelled out on the page.
findings.source_url: https://www.cloudflare.com/startups/workers-launchpad/ (direct fetch today returned partial content; benefit details from the page's cached extraction)

findings.name: No standalone 'trial credits' or education license for Workers AI inference itself
findings.detail: Cloudflare does not publish a separate AI trial-credit pool, per-model free-token grant, or academic/education license for Workers AI inference as of 2026-10-22. The only AI-related free offers are (a) the plan-embedded 10k Neurons/day free tier (finding 1) and (b) Workers AI caps inside the Startup Program ($2.5k–$50k by tier). The only 'credit-adjacent' paid option is prepaid AI Gateway credits, which can route frontier-model Workers AI usage and grant higher rate limits — but prepaid, not free. Offer trackers (e.g. perq.sh) list exactly two tracked Cloudflare offers: the startup credit tiers and the 10k Neurons/day free tier — no trial-credit offer exists. Non-profit/civil-society orgs can receive up to $250k credits via the Sept 2025 Startup Program expansion (announced at Birthday Week 2025; dedicated program page could not be located — likely under the startups portal).
findings.eligibility: n/a — absence finding. Non-profit orgs: civil society/public interest orgs (up to $250k credits, incl. AI, databases, security products).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim for trial credits/education license; use the free tier + Startup Program + Student program above. Non-profits apply through the Cloudflare for Startups application portal with org details.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse 'trial' with the free tier: free tier is permanent but hard-capped (requests fail beyond 10k Neurons/day, not throttled). Prepaid AI Gateway credits are a paid product, not a free grant. The old 'up to $250k, 4 tiers' startup structure (April 2025) is superseded by the $350k 3-tier structure — third-party trackers may still show stale $250k/4-tier data.
findings.source_url: https://perq.sh/vendors/cloudflare (offer tracker, checked 2026-10-22) + https://blog.cloudflare.com/ (Birthday Week 2025 non-profit announcement, Sept 22, 2025)

sunset_notes: Changes in 2025–2026: (1) The Cloudflare for Startups program was restructured from the April 2025 four-tier layout ($5k/$25k/$100k/$250k, per blog post 'Startup Program update') to the current three-tier layout ($10k/$100k/$350k) — Tier 3 raised $5k→$10k and top tier $250k→$350k; regional pages (e.g. cloudflare.com/en-in/forstartups) still display the outdated $250k/4-tier structure, so use the US .com page as authoritative. (2) Sept 22, 2025 (Birthday Week 2025): Students program launched (12 months free Workers Paid for US .edu 18+) and the program was extended to non-profits/civil-society orgs (up to $250k credits). (3) Sept 2025: 'Come build with us' hubs — program participants get office access in SF/Austin/London/Lisbon from Jan 2026. (4) Sept 28, 2026: 'The Cold Start' competition announced — 5 early-stage companies pitch at Cloudflare Connect; grand prize $500,000 in credits (competition, not a standing program). (5) Workers AI pricing page (last updated Oct 20, 2026) moved to per-model granular unit-based pricing display while backend billing remains Neuron-based; 8 frontier models are now gated behind a paid billing method. Sunset of 2022–2024 programs: the original $1.25B/$2B-pledge Workers Launchpad funding program (2022) evolved into the current cohort Launchpad; no free-offer sunsets this cycle — all five offers above remain active as of 2026-10-22. Note: one follow-up web search (non-profit program page URL) could not be executed because the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted; non-profit and Launchpad findings lean on blog/press summaries and cached page content, hence medium confidence.

findings.name: Replicate 'Try for Free' free runs (no-credit-card free tier)
findings.detail: New accounts can run a rotating set of select models a limited number of times without purchasing credit and without a credit card. Current 'Try for Free' collection: google/imagen-4, black-forest-labs/flux-1.1-pro, black-forest-labs/flux-dev, black-forest-labs/flux-kontext-pro, ideogram-ai/ideogram-v3-turbo, topazlabs/image-upscale, topazlabs/video-upscale, tencentarc/gfpgan, szcho/codeformer, minimax/video-01, luma/reframe-video. Replicate does NOT publish a dollar amount or exact run count; third-party trackers estimate ~50 free predictions total. It is a one-time allowance with no monthly reset.
findings.eligibility: Any new user who creates a Replicate account (GitHub, Google, or email sign-in). No .edu, no startup, and no credit card required to start. One account per person (farming multiple accounts to re-collect free runs is against the one-account rule). Global. Verified today on the official collection page + FAQ.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at replicate.com (GitHub/Google/email — no card). 2) Go to replicate.com/collections/try-for-free. 3) Pick a model, upload/provide input, run it in the web playground or via API token (r8_...). 4) When the free cap is hit, Replicate asks you to add a credit card and purchase credit to continue. Claim is automatic on signup; no application.
findings.expiry: One-time allowance, no renewal/monthly reset. Models in the collection rotate over time. After the cap you move to pay-per-second or per-output billing (e.g., FLUX 1.1 Pro $0.04/image, FLUX dev $0.025/image, deepseek-r1 $0.01/1k output tokens).
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: these are free RUNS, not a free subscription — once used you must add a card and buy credit. No published $ or exact run count. Each model keeps its own license that can restrict commercial use even when the run is free. Cardless accounts with granted credit are rate-limited to ~1 req/sec / ~6 req/min (no load testing); 600 predictions/min only once you have a paid account. Free set rotates, so a model you want may not currently be in it. A banner ('Wan 3.0 is 30% off this week') is a temporary discount, not a free offer.

findings.name: YC Summer Fellows (2025): Replicate $10,000 credits for students
findings.detail: In YC's 2025 Summer Fellows Grants, Replicate was one of the YC companies contributing $10,000 in compute credits to selected fellows (alongside Fly.io $50k, Supabase $10k, Resend $3k, plus YC's own $20k cash + $90k AWS/Azure/GCP credits). This is a real student-facing benefit tied to Replicate, but it is delivered through YC's grant, not a standalone Replicate program.
findings.eligibility: Undergraduate CS/engineering students, including freshmen, and students outside the US (global). Must be SELECTED for YC's Summer Fellows grant (apply; 15-min interview; YC estimated ~20-50 grants). It is merit/selection-based, not a .edu-email self-serve discount. This is a 2025 cohort (events Jun-Aug 2025).
findings.claim: Apply to YC Summer Fellows Grants (ycombinator.com/blog/summer-fellows; the 2025 application deadline was end of March 2025). If selected, Replicate credits are part of the grant package — there is no self-serve claim on replicate.com. No company/business required; grant is to the individual student.
findings.expiry: 2025 cohort only (now closed for that cycle). YC may run a new Summer Fellows round in a later year, possibly with different partner credits — the $10k Replicate figure is not guaranteed to recur.
findings.gotchas: It is YC's grant, not Replicate's education program; you cannot claim it by yourself on Replicate. Credits land via YC selection, not a .edu program. Do not confuse with Replit/Google education programs that DO offer .edu discounts.

findings.name: Replicate Startup Program (claimed up to $10,000 credits) — UNVERIFIED / DISPUTED
findings.detail: Third-party aggregators list a 'Replicate Startup Program' of up to $10,000 in inference credits (~$1,000-$10,000), ~6-month validity, pre-seed to Series A/B, no VC referral, global, company-domain email, no equity. HOWEVER: replicate.com/startups returns HTTP 404 (verified today), and at least one tracker states Replicate has no startup program. No official Replicate page confirms the program today, so this cannot be verified or claimed through an official channel.
findings.eligibility: As claimed by third parties only: AI/ML startup, pre-Series B / Series A, building a production product (not pure research), company-domain email; not Series C+; not research-only/academic.
findings.claim: Per third parties: (1) create a Replicate account with a company-domain email + API token, (2) submit the startup application (form was said to be at replicate.com/startups), (3) receive credits on approval. Because replicate.com/startups 404s, this path is currently dead and the offer is not confirmable. Do not rely on it; contact Replicate sales if a startup is seeking volume terms.
findings.expiry: Unknown — no official terms or live application page. Treat as possibly sunset or never-officially-live.
findings.gotchas: CONFLICTING sources: the official URL is gone (404) while aggregators still advertise $10k. Low confidence it is a live, claimable program as of 2026-10-22. If it does exist it likely requires a company email + production use case. The startup-pricing alternative listed by trackers is to use Modal/Together AI/Fireworks programs instead, or ask Replicate for volume discounts.

findings.name: Partner-granted micro-credits (e.g., IBM Granite invite = $0.50)
findings.detail: Replicate invite links can be pre-loaded with a small amount of credit granted by a partner/distributor (e.g., an IBM Granite invite that reads 'you've got $0.50 of credit to run and fine-tune models'). These are partner-specific and modest, not a general student or startup program.
findings.eligibility: The holder of the specific invite/partner link; sign-in (often GitHub) required to accept. Not gated on .edu or startup status.
findings.claim: Open the specific partner invite URL and sign in as instructed (e.g., GitHub) to accept the credit.
findings.expiry: Per-invite; varies and not a recurring program.
findings.gotchas: Tiny amounts (fractions of a dollar); only applies for the specific partner invite; not a free tier you can self-serve. Illustrative only.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22: (1) Replicate's official free offer is the 'Try for Free' collection — a limited number of free runs on select models with no credit card and no published dollar amount or exact run count; it is a one-time allowance, not a recurring free tier. (2) replicate.com/startups returns 404 — so a live, self-serve Replicate Startup Program is NOT verifiable today, even though aggregators advertise up to $10k; treat that offer as disputed/possibly-sunset and prefer contacting Replicate sales or using Modal/Together AI/Fireworks startup programs. (3) No dedicated Replicate education/.edu program was found (unlike Replit or Google, which do run .edu programs). (4) The YC Summer Fellows 2025 program (Replicate $10k student credits) was a 2025 cohort and is closed for that cycle; it may recur in a later year with different partners/amounts. (5) Recurring 'Wan 3.0 30% off this week' banners on Replicate pages are temporary discounts, not free offers. Net: the only clearly-live, self-serve, card-free offer is the 'Try for Free' free-runs collection; all student/startup credit offers are either YC-cohort-gated (students) or unverifiable (startups).

provider: Mistral AI (La Plateforme / Mistral Studio — API & Vibe)

findings.name: Free mode API (default, no card required)
findings.detail: Every new Mistral account starts in Free mode by default; API access is enabled with no credit card required. Included monthly usage is shared across Studio, the API, and Vibe Code, and is drawn first; when exhausted and pay-as-you-go is off, usage stops until the next billing period. Rate caps (requests/second, tokens/minute, tokens/month, per model) are set per organization and shown ONLY on the Admin Panel Limits page — Mistral publishes no public numeric quota. Described officially as the lowest limits, 'intended for evaluation and prototyping'. Since 2026-10-07 the pricing page no longer states a dollar figure on the Free card (the '$10/mo in API credits' line was removed without announcement); the 'pre' number was archived Sep 1–Oct 7, 2026. Pay-as-you-go is a switch, not a plan: prepaid credits must exist before enabling it, and adding credits does NOT raise rate-limit tiers (tiers move on cumulative billed usage: Tier 2 >€20, Tier 3 >€100, Tier 4 >€500 billed).
findings.eligibility: Anyone who creates a account (docs: 'Free mode is the default state for new accounts'). No credit card required (stated in the Studio quickstart: 'no credit card required'). Restricted regions per Mistral terms (as read 2026-09-26, medium confidence): Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk regions. NOTE: since 2026-08-05 (US) / 2026-08-07 (EU) the consumer terms exclude Mistral Studio/API from individual use — API is limited to business customers under the Commercial ToS, so personal-project use is technically out of scope.
findings.claim: Create an account at console.mistral.ai (Free mode is default, no card) → Studio → API Keys → 'Create new key' → call api.mistral.ai/v1 within your included monthly usage; inspect your own numeric caps on Admin Panel → API → Limits.
findings.expiry: Included monthly usage resets each month; Free mode itself has no stated expiration or renewal terms. Rate caps are persistent per org.
findings.gotchas: Shared pool: heavy Vibe Code/Vibe app usage eats the same monthly allowance as API calls, so a free account's API budget can vanish. Training/privacy: API calls may be used to improve Mistral models unless the 'Anonymous improvement data' toggle is switched off (default opt-out). Third-party report (Oct 2026): mistral-large-4 on a free key answered 'This model is not available in your subscription tier' even after $10 credit — flagship/labs models may be unavailable on Free. Free-model lineup shifted over 2026 (e.g., mistral-medium dropped 2026-08-14).

findings.name: Free plan for Vibe (formerly Le Chat) consumer app
findings.detail: Separate from the API tier: the consumer 'Free' plan is 'Your personal AI agent for everyday tasks' — web + mobile access with limited messages, web searches and coding sessions; limited image generation/editing; 100+ connectors. Published multipliers in the pricing table: messages & voice 'Up to 6x free', web searches 'Up to 5x free', image generation 'Up to 40x free', task scheduling 'Up to 5', project folders 'Up to 1,000', model-training data use 'Opt-out', support = help center only. No API credits included (Pro starts at $15/mo in API credits). All subject to fair-usage limits and the ToS; absolute counts are not published.
findings.eligibility: Public; no credit-card requirement stated on the page. Subject to Mistral's regional restrictions (embargoed regions excluded).
findings.claim: Sign in to the Vibe console/app — Free plan is the default consumer tier; no application needed.
findings.expiry: No expiration; monthly fair-usage caps reset with the billing period; 'Subject to fair usage limits and Mistral's Terms of Service.'
findings.gotchas: The 6x/5x/40x multipliers are relative to a baseline, not absolute counts. Free-tier inputs/outputs may train models unless you opt out. This is app-only: it grants no API access — API calls still come from your Free-mode API keys and the shared monthly pool.

findings.name: Education plan (student/teacher discount — paid, not free)
findings.detail: Not a free offer: verified students at accredited higher-education institutions get Mistral Pro at $5.99/month instead of the standard $14.99/month, capped at 12 months of eligibility. Eligibility is limited to students who have NOT previously used Vibe or Le Chat. Per a third-party pricing read (2026-10-11, medium confidence) the Education plan bundles $15/mo in API credits shared across the API, Studio and Vibe Code. There is no fully free education license from Mistral.
findings.eligibility: Student verification at an accredited higher institution (the page says 'verified students'; the mechanism is the console's student-verification flow, typically institutional email — the page does not explicitly say '.edu email required'). 12-month cap; new-to-Vibe/Le-Chat users only. No card-free access: it is a paid subscription, though students can pay at the discount price.
findings.claim: Purchase the Education plan from the Mistral console using student verification; help-center article 'Students and teachers can check whether they are eligible for a discount' (referenced from docs.mistral.ai/admin/billing-usage/subscriptions).
findings.expiry: Eligibility limited to 12 months; the subscription itself renews monthly at $5.99 while eligible.
findings.gotchas: Do not count this as a free tier — $5.99/mo is real money. The 12-month window means the discount does not renew beyond that. Includes limited API credits ($15/mo reported third-party), not the Pro $25.50/mo figure.

findings.name: Mistralship startup program (€30K credits) — currently unavailable
findings.detail: Launched late 2024: 6-month cohorts of 10 startups; each winner received up to €30,000 in La Plateforme credits, dedicated 1:1 support from Mistral's Solutions & Science team, and early access to new models/products. Original eligibility (per the Dec 2024 announcement press): registered startup with a company website and a business email, founded less than 7 years ago, and no Series B or later round raised (Series B+ companies could apply for a separate offering). First cohort applications closed 2025-01-05. As of today (2026-10-22) both https://mistral.ai/startups and https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-ship return HTTP 404 (verified directly); no replacement public offer or closure notice exists. Third-party trackers (May 2026 and Oct 2026) classify the program as discontinued and route would-be applicants to Mistral sales/partners.
findings.eligibility: Historically: early-stage startups (pre-Series B), founded <7 years, registered company with public web presence; competitive selection (10 per cohort). No longer applicable — no live application path as of 2026-10-22.
findings.claim: Cannot be claimed right now: no public landing page or form (both /startups and /news/mistral-ship are 404). The only remaining route is contacting Mistral sales / startup team directly.
findings.expiry: Cohort 1 closed 2025-01-05; the program page disappeared by mid-2026 (confirmed 404 today); no stated new cohort or deadlines.
findings.gotchas: Credits were La Plateforme platform credits (not cash, not transferable). Absence of a public page does not guarantee the program is dead — but with no closure notice and 404s on all paths, treat it as sunset/unavailable; do not plan around it.

findings.name: Trial credits — none exist; free 'labs-' models and free Moderation 2 instead
findings.detail: Mistral has no published trial-credit program (no dollar grant to new API customers) as of 2026-10-22. Two small free items exist on the API: model IDs prefixed 'labs-' are free but experimental and not for production (third-party pricing read, 2026-10-11), and Mistral Moderation 2 is priced at $0. The legacy free 'Experiment' plan (2024–2026, with published caps around ~1 req/s, 500K tokens/min, ~1B tokens/month) has been replaced by Free mode with unpublished limits; its old help/docs pages now return 404. Open-weight Mistral models (Ministral 3 8B/14B, open-mistral-nemo; Mistral 7B Apache-2.0) can be self-hosted for free, which is the real 'free' route beyond the shared pool.
findings.eligibility: labs- models: any account key (free-mode included) — experimental, not production-safe. Open-weight self-hosting: no account needed; Mistral-licensed weights, research/individual use covered, commercial deployment requires a Mistral license.
findings.claim: Call 'labs-*' model IDs with a free-mode key at no token cost, or download open weights and self-host; there is no trial-credit claim flow to follow.
findings.expiry: labs- models may change or retire without notice; Moderation 2's free pricing is a list-price item, subject to change.
findings.gotchas: Free 'labs-' inference is explicitly for testing; don't build on it. Self-hosting has no egress cost but you own compute. Beware aggregator sites (e.g., 'AI Credits') selling 'Mistral credits' — that is a paid resale, not an official free offer.

sunset_notes: 1) Mistralship startup program (up to €30K La Plateforme credits, 10 startups/6-month cohort): cohort-1 applications closed 2025-01-05; the program's public paths are dead — https://mistral.ai/startups and https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-ship both return 404 as of 2026-10-22 (verified directly today); Mistral published no closure notice and no replacement offer; third-party trackers mark it discontinued. 2) On 2026-10-07 (no announcement), the pricing page dropped the '$10 /mo in API credits' line from the Free plan and reduced Pro's included API credits from $30 to $25.50/mo — the Free card now states no dollar figure; included monthly usage remains, visible only on the account's Limits page. 3) The legacy 'Experiment' free tier (published caps ~1 rps / 500K tokens/min / ~1B tokens/month) was retired and its pages now 404, replaced by Free mode with per-org unpublished limits. 4) Free-tier model lineup shifted during 2026 — e.g., mistral-medium was dropped from the free tier on 2026-08-14; mistral-large-4 (public preview 2026-10-06) reportedly rejects free-tier keys with 'not available in your subscription tier'. 5) Since 2026-08-05 (US) / 2026-08-07 (EU), consumer terms exclude Studio/API from individual use — API access is for business customers under the Commercial ToS, which quietly constrains who 'free mode' actually serves. 6) No free education license exists: the education offer is a paid $5.99/mo student discount (12-month cap), not a grant.

findings.name: Cohere Trial API key (free tier, self-serve)
findings.detail: Auto-issued Trial API key on account creation: all API calls free, 1,000 API calls/month across all endpoints combined (per official docs.cohere.com rate-limits page; not stated on the pricing FAQ itself), with per-endpoint rate limits: Chat 20 req/min per model (Command A+, A Reasoning, A Translate, A Vision, Command A, R+, R, R7B, North Mini Code), Embed 2,000 inputs/min (same as production), Embed (Images) 5 inputs/min, Rerank 10 req/min, Tokenize 100 req/min, Parse 500 req/min, Audio Transcriptions 5 req/min. No credit card required; non-commercial use only — trial keys are explicitly 'not permitted to be used for production or commercial purposes'. No expiry date published; monthly quota resets on calendar month.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — any email, sign up at dashboard.cohere.com (email, Google, or GitHub). No .edu requirement, no student status, no region limit stated. No credit card or payment required.
findings.claim: Sign up at dashboard.cohere.com; the Trial key is generated automatically and is copyable from the dashboard / 'API Keys' section. No application step. Usage caps: 1,000 calls/month total; 429s when rate limits or monthly cap hit; 402 when account billing limit reached.
findings.source_url: https://cohere.com/pricing (FAQ: 'How do I get a Trial API key?', 'What's the difference between a Trial API key and Production API key?') + https://docs.cohere.com/docs/rate-limits (official limits tables, read today)
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: this is a permanent free tier, not a time-boxed trial, but strictly non-commercial — commercial production use requires a paid Production key (Owner completes 'Go to Production' workflow; pay-as-you-go, invoiced monthly or at $250 outstanding balance). 2026 change: for newer Chat model variants (Command A+, Command A Reasoning/Translate/Vision) production keys are capped like trial keys (1,000 calls/month, 20 req/min) and commercial use of those models requires contacting sales@cohere.com — so the free tier is the only self-serve access for the newest models. Data: Cohere logs prompts/generations, deleted after 30 days; opt out via Settings -> Data Controls. Third-party 'student deal' listings (e.g. The Modelverse) that tout '.edu verified, 365-day grant' are just rebrands of this same universal trial key — no .edu verification or separate grant exists.
findings.expiry: No published end date; 1,000-call monthly quota resets each calendar month. Key remains available for the life of the account.

findings.name: Cohere Labs Catalyst Grants (research / education / public-benefit API credits)
findings.detail: Free Cohere API access (credits + compute) for academic partners, civic and public-impact organizations. Amounts per grant are not fixed or published; program page shows running totals (counters for grants awarded, $k in API credits, countries, university affiliations; third-party mid-2025 figure: 250+ grants, ~$350K API credits, 35+ countries). Credits tracked in the dashboard Billing tab; a Production API key is required to use them; if credits run out, contact brittawnya@cohere.com for more. AI-safety research has disclosure obligations: vulnerabilities must be disclosed unconditionally to labs@cohere.com at least 4 weeks before publication; no other pre-publication approval required.
findings.eligibility: Academic partners, civic and public-impact organizations (not strictly .edu-only — no formal .edu rule, but projects must be public-benefit or open-science research; non-commercial). Focus areas: education, healthcare, climate, sustainability, multilingual work, model safety, prosocial applications, values alignment. Credit card not required.
findings.claim: Apply via the form at cohere.com/research/grants/application (official page cohere.com/research/grants). Rolling consideration, no fixed deadline. Colleagues outside your institution can be invited to use the credits via the dashboard Team tab. Optional acknowledgment line: 'This work was supported by compute credits from a Cohere Labs Research Grant.'
findings.source_url: https://cohere.com/research/grants (read today) + cohort/education framing: https://cohere.com/blog/exploring-ai-in-education (Sep 23, 2025, 'Using Cohere Grants to transform students into AI builders')
findings.gotchas: Credits are project/eligibility-scoped, not a universal student tier — individual students only get access via a faculty/institutional grant (or they apply as part of a qualifying organization). Grants are competitive and rolling, so timing is unpredictable. Grant access uses a Production key, meaning the non-commercial restriction of trial keys is replaced by the public-benefit/open-science restriction instead. The Sep 2025 education post is marketing for this same program, not a separate education license.
findings.expiry: No sunset published; application status shown as 'Open / rolling basis' as of today.

findings.name: Cohere Startup Program (2024 cohort) — 25% off for 12 months + partner-VC credits — CLOSED
findings.detail: Launched June 6, 2024: 25% discount on Cohere's proprietary models for one year, plus engineering support, logo/use-case showcase on cohere.com, joint webinars and co-marketing; zero equity; historically up to $100,000 API credits available to startups affiliated with partner VCs/accelerators. It was a discount program, not upfront free credits. Cohere's own post carried the note 'Applications are now closed for 2024' and no 2025/2026 cohort was announced.
findings.eligibility: At closure: early-stage AI startups from bootstrapped through Series B, building on Cohere tech, global (no published country restriction). The 25%-off benefit ran for 12 months from acceptance.
findings.claim: No live claim path: cohere.com/startup-program and /startup-program-application now redirect to the cohere.com homepage (verified today, 2026-10-22, and re-verified by independent trackers on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10); cohere.com/startups returns 404. While it was open: submit the application, Cohere's team reviewed fit, then 25% discount applied at the billing layer for a year. Current substitute for prototyping: the free Trial key; for paid use: production keys or AWS Activate credits on Cohere models in Amazon Bedrock.
findings.source_url: https://cohere.com/blog/cohere-launches-startup-program (June 6, 2024 launch post) + closure verification of https://cohere.com/startup-program (redirects to homepage) and https://www.cloudroutehq.com/startup-credits/cohere (2026-10-09)
findings.gotchas: Do not plan around this program: no closure notice was published, it simply lapsed — the launch post body is thin and the numbers above come from the post plus trackers. It is distinct from the Catalyst Grants (which cover research/public-benefit, not commercial startups). Third-party directories still list it as 'active' (e.g. SaaSTweaks, Startup Intros 'Cohere for Good') — ignore those; the official URLs are dead as of October 2026.
findings.expiry: Closed: 'Applications are now closed for 2024' per Cohere's post; program URLs dead as of 2026-10-09/10-22. No renewal announced.

findings.name: No dedicated student .edu license — education access rides on the universal trial key + Catalyst Grants
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 there is no Cohere student/education license, no .edu-verified free tier, and no student credit card offer. Students get the same 1,000-calls/month trial key as everyone else (non-commercial, which covers coursework/personal projects but not a commercial product), plus eligibility for free API credits through a faculty/academic Catalyst Grant.
findings.eligibility: N/A — this is the absence of an offer. Verified across cohere.com (pricing, startup, research pages) and the Sep 2025 education blog post, which is Catalyst-Grants content only.
findings.claim: Students: self-serve trial key for non-commercial use; apply (with a university/institution) to cohere.com/research/grants/application for public-benefit/open-science API credits.
findings.gotchas: Third-party perk aggregators (The Modelverse 'Cohere Free Trial API Key Free Student Deal', resets.pro, freellmapihub) list Cohere under student/research programs, but the 'student deal' entries are the generic trial key with fabricated framing (e.g. '365-day grant', '.edu verification') — Cohere requires no student verification. The only genuinely student-relevant first-party offer is the researcher-facing Catalyst Grant.

sunset_notes: 1) Cohere Startup Program (2024: 25% off models for 12 months, no equity, up to ~$100K partner-VC API credits): CLOSED — Cohere's launch post (June 2024) notes 'Applications are now closed for 2024'; cohere.com/startup-program, /startup-program-application and /startups now redirect to the homepage or 404 (verified 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-22). No successor program announced; ignore third-party directories still listing it as active. 2) 2026 material change to the free tier itself: production keys now behave like trial keys for the newest Chat model variants (Command A+, Command A Reasoning/Translate/Vision) — 1,000 calls/month and 20 req/min — and commercial use of those models requires contacting sales@cohere.com, so free trial-key access is the only self-serve route to the newest models (per docs.cohere.com rate-limits page, read today). 3) Fine-tuning for legacy text models (command, command-light, command-r, classify, rerank) was retired 2025-09-15 (third-party reference; not a free offer per se). 4) No student/education license has ever existed at Cohere — the Sep 2025 'AI in Education' blog is Catalyst Grants content, and student-perk listings on aggregators are rebranded trial keys. 5) Trial-key Embed limit: current official docs say 2,000 inputs/min; an older third-party summary (Sep 2025) claimed 100/min — the official docs figure stands.

findings.name: Free tier: ':free' model variants and openrouter/free Free Models Router
findings.detail: Any signed-in OpenRouter account gets rate-limited (not credit-limited) access to the catalog of $0/token free models. Limits today: 20 requests/minute in both tiers; 50 requests/day if lifetime purchased credits < $10; 1,000 requests/day once at least $10 of credits has been purchased all-time (the threshold in the docs table is 'at least 10 credits' and the higher tier is granted starting one credit below the threshold, i.e. effectively $10 lifetime spend). The daily counter/ceiling is exposed in `free_model_daily_requests` on GET /api/v1/key. The pricing page (Oct 2026) advertises the Free plan as '25+ free models, 4 free providers, 5 workspaces, 50 requests/day'; the openrouter/free router page lists 29 free-variant models in the router (the catalog rotates). `openrouter/free` is an auto-router that picks a random free model matching your request's capabilities; a :free model's `models` fallback array bills fallbacks at their own price, so keep requests free by listing only :free / openrouter/free entries.
findings.eligibility: Any OpenRouter account (email, GitHub, or crypto wallet signup). No credit card required (Free plan lists 'Payment options: No'). No .edu or region requirement. is_free_tier = 'user has never paid for credits'; BYOK requests and exempt accounts/arenas are not gated by the daily counter.
findings.claim: Sign up at openrouter.ai (no card needed) and call the API with a model ID ending in ':free' or with model 'openrouter/free' (OpenAI-compatible REST or SDK; Chat Playground at openrouter.ai/chat lists 'Free Models Router'). To raise the daily cap: buy >= $10 of credits once (credits purchased are lifetime-counted; the tier is permanent even if balance later drops below $10). Check remaining free quota via GET /api/v1/key.
findings.gotchas: 20 RPM cap is fixed even at the 1,000/day tier. OpenRouter charges a 5.5% ($0.80 minimum) card fee or 5% crypto fee on credit purchases, so the effective cost to unlock 1,000/day is $10.80 via card (16% overhead at a $5 top-up; $10 costs $10.80 = 8%). Free-model availability rotates ('which models are free changes frequently'); free models may have reduced context/quality. Free-model providers may log prompts/completions and use data for training unless your account's privacy routing settings exclude such providers; there is also an opt-in logging setting that trades a 1% usage discount for logging. OpenRouter reserves the right to expire unused credits one year after purchase (FAQ), which partially conflicts with third-party claims that 'credits never expire'. Fallbacks to paid models are billed even if the primary model is :free. Mid-stream rate limits arrive as an SSE finish_reason 'error', not a separate HTTP code.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; no expiry or renewal. Daily counter resets each UTC day. The $10 threshold is lifetime (all-time credits purchased), not a subscription.

findings.name: OpenRouter for Startups: up to $5,000 universal inference credits + 12 months of 0% platform/BYOK fees
findings.detail: Official startup program (openrouter.ai/startup-program, terms last updated Aug 22, 2026). Benefit: up to $5,000 USD of universal inference credits usable across 500+ models, plus 0% processing fees for 12 months (covering both platform fees and BYOK fees); pay only token list price. Credits are promotional: no cash value, non-refundable, non-transferable, not stackable with other promotions; amounts are at OpenRouter's discretion ('up to'). Terms also allow benefits to vary by referral source and available program capacity. Rolling applications; decisions typically within a few days; if approved, credits/fee waivers are auto-applied to the OpenRouter account tied to the applicant's email.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Series B stage (or equivalent as determined by OpenRouter); building an AI-native product full-time; referred by an approved OpenRouter partner; public company website; professional email on the company domain (generic aliases like admin@/support@/ops@ rejected); valid OpenRouter account with less than $500 lifetime OpenRouter spend; applicant has not previously received startup-program credits (once per applicant, even across multiple partner affiliations). No .edu requirement, no card requirement, no region cap stated.
findings.claim: Fill out the application form at openrouter.ai/startup-program (or via your partner's perks page, e.g. Mercury/Stripe Atlas); questions to startups@openrouter.ai. Review is rolling; on approval the credits and fee waivers are automatically applied to your account. Ask for the specific credit amount in writing (benefits are 'up to' amounts).
findings.gotchas: Amounts are discretionary and vary by referral source: the public page says 'up to $5K' while the program has also been advertised at $3,000 (third-party trackers noted the page previously showed up to $3,000; terms allow up to $5,000). The <$500 lifetime spend cap and partner-referral requirement exclude users who already spend on OpenRouter or lack a partner referral. 'Program availability may change over time'. Unused purchased credits may expire after one year per FAQ policy, so plan credit burn. 0% fee waiver is time-boxed to 12 months; standard 5.5% (Standard) / 8% (Business) platform fees resume after.
findings.expiry: No published deadline; rolling while the program is operational. Fee waiver: 12 months. Credits: promotional, no stated fixed expiry on the program credits themselves, but subject to OpenRouter's general right to expire unused credits one year after purchase.

findings.name: Mercury Perks partner tier: $1,000 in OpenRouter credits (6 months) + 12 months of 0% fees, for Mercury customers
findings.detail: A partner-referred variant of OpenRouter for Startups offered through Mercury's perks portal. Benefit: $1K of universal inference credits, valid for 6 months, usable across OpenRouter's full model catalog, plus $0 processing fees for 12 months (platform and BYOK fees). Same rolling application and auto-apply mechanism as the main program. Each applicant may receive startup credits once even if affiliated with multiple partners.
findings.eligibility: Mercury customers (online business banking for startups) who are also Pre-Series B, building AI-native products, with a public company website, professional company-domain email, and an OpenRouter account with < $500 lifetime spend. No .edu, no card requirement.
findings.claim: Redeem/apply from Mercury's perks page (mercury.com/perks/openrouter) — OpenRouter reviews the application on a rolling basis and applies credits + fee waiver to the applicant's OpenRouter org account.
findings.gotchas: Credit validity is shorter (6 months) than the direct program's open-ended promotional credits; the '300+ models' wording on the Mercury page predates OpenRouter's '500+ models' catalog copy — catalog size has grown. Once-per-applicant rule applies across partners; you cannot stack Mercury, Stripe Atlas, and the direct program credits.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 6 months; fee waiver 12 months; rolling application, program can change or close.

findings.name: Stripe Atlas partner tier: $500 inference credits with 0% fees for approved Stripe Atlas founders
findings.detail: A smaller partner tier of the same OpenRouter for Startups program, delivered through Stripe Atlas's perks catalog: $500 in inference credits plus 0% fees, redeemed after company formation approval via Atlas. Vendor eligibility and compliance requirements may apply.
findings.eligibility: Approved Stripe Atlas founders (company incorporated via Stripe Atlas) meeting OpenRouter's startup eligibility (Pre-Series B, AI-native product, company website, professional email, < $500 lifetime OpenRouter spend).
findings.claim: Redeem from the Stripe Atlas Perks tab after Atlas approval; OpenRouter applies the credits to your account.
findings.gotchas: Smallest of the three official partner tiers; once-per-applicant rule applies. Sourced from a third-party aggregator (heap.page) that also tracks OpenRouter's recorded offers; confirm the current amount on Stripe Atlas's own perks page before relying on it — partner benefit amounts vary and can change.
findings.expiry: Partner perk; no published credit-expiry beyond the program's promotional-credit rules and OpenRouter's right to expire unused credits after a year.

findings.name: Student/education license: no dedicated program — free tier is the student path; trial credits: none published
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 OpenRouter runs no student/education license, no .edu-verified grant, and no public trial-credit or welcome-credit offer. The free tier (above) is open to any account including students. Third-party FAQ tracking (Oct 2026) explicitly states OpenRouter 'doesn't offer a dedicated student or education discount' and 'doesn't issue public promo codes, coupon codes, or discount codes' (claims of '$5 welcome credits' are false). An SEO aggregator page (themodelverse.in) markets an 'OpenRouter Free Models Router Free Student Deal / 365-day grant' with .edu verification — this is not an official OpenRouter program; no OpenRouter page describes any student grant, and the claimed 'auto-renew tripwire' contradicts the no-payment Free plan. OpenRouter's FAQ does contain the line 'All new users receive a small free allowance to test out OpenRouter', but no amount, duration or claim process is published anywhere official; treat trial credits as unverified.
findings.eligibility: N/A (no student-specific or trial-credit offer exists to claim). The standard free tier requires only an OpenRouter account.
findings.claim: Students should simply create a normal OpenRouter account and use :free / openrouter/free models; startups should use the OpenRouter for Startups program. There is no form, code, or .edu verification to submit for a student benefit.
findings.gotchas: Ignore third-party 'student deal' aggregator pages claiming 365-day grants, auto-renewals, or .edu-gated perks for OpenRouter — they are not backed by any OpenRouter page and mix in invented renewal mechanics. Verify anything against openrouter.ai only.
findings.expiry: N/A.

sunset_notes: Major 2025-2026 changes: (1) April 9, 2025 policy shift (announced; widely reported): the daily free-model cap was cut from 200 to 50 requests/day and the '>= $10 lifetime credits -> 1,000 requests/day' incentive was introduced at that time — the 50/day figure has held through 2026. (2) Startup program terms were last updated August 22, 2026, and the public page now advertises 'up to $5,000' — third-party trackers (programscape.com) recorded the startups page at 'up to $3,000' earlier in 2026, indicating the credit ceiling was raised during 2026; the program's partner tiers (Mercury $1K/6mo, Stripe Atlas $500) are the older/lower amounts. (3) June 9, 2025: credit-purchase fee was simplified to a flat 5.5% ($0.80 min) on card / 5% on crypto (removed the old fixed $0.35 Stripe charge) — this affects the effective cost of the $10 unlock. (4) OpenRouter's FAQ reserves the right to expire unused credits after one year of purchase, contradicting common 'credits never expire' lore; confirm current treatment before banking on long-lived startup credits. No student/education license ever existed to sunset; no trial-credit program was found (the FAQ's 'small free allowance' line is unpublished/unverifiable). Free-model catalog size has grown to 25-29 rotating models under 4 free providers as of Oct 2026.

provider: Google Cloud (Alphabet) — LLM & AI APIs: free tiers, trial credits, startup and student/education offers

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial — $300 welcome credit (90 days)
findings.detail: New customers get $300 free credit, valid 90 days from Free Trial billing account creation. Credit covers any product including overages beyond Free Tier limits; it does not roll over (expires 90 days from signup even if you upgrade to paid). Free Trial billing account auto-closes when the $300 is spent or 90 days pass unless you manually upgrade to a Paid billing account (then you keep remaining credit until the 90-day mark and keep Free Tier access). Eligibility: you must have NEVER been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase, and never signed up for the Free Trial before (one per person/billing profile). GPUs, Windows servers and some features are not covered. During trial you are not billed — only if you manually upgrade to paid do charges begin. 30-day data-export window after the trial ends. Compute Engine trial restricted to 8 concurrent cores.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, any country with GCP access (no .edu or startup status needed). Credit card/other payment method REQUIRED at signup for identity verification (Google may run a pending authorization, not a charge). US/Mexico government entities excluded.
findings.claim: Sign up at cloud.google.com (Get started for free) -> add card -> $300 credit is preloaded into the Free Trial billing account automatically; spend over 90 days on any product incl. Vertex AI/Gemini API; optionally click Upgrade in console to keep credit alive beyond trial features. Do NOT click 'Activate a paid account' unless you want charges.
findings.expiry: 90 days from signup or until $300 is exhausted, whichever first; unused credit does not survive account closure. Free Tier usage continues if you convert to a paid account.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs Free Tier: the $300 is for trial billing only; Free Tier allowances are separate, not charged against it. CC required but you are only charged if you manually upgrade to paid. Egress, third-party models (e.g. non-Google LLMs on Vertex) cost above free allowances. 30-day migration window after end; GCE resources may be deleted and are not recoverable.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Tier — 20+ always-free products (no expiry)
findings.detail: Per-product monthly free allowances, reset each month, do NOT expire but limits are 'subject to change'. Verified examples from cloud.google.com/free: Compute Engine 1 e2-micro/month; Cloud Storage 5 GB Standard; BigQuery 1 TB scanned/month; Cloud Run 2M requests + Cloud Run Functions 2M invocations/month; GKE 1 Autopilot/zonal cluster; Pub/Sub 10 GB messages; Vision AI 1,000 units; Speech-to-Text 60 min; Natural Language 5,000 units; Cloud Build 120 build-minutes/day; KMS Autokey 100 active key versions + 10k ops; Artifact Registry, Firestore 1 GB, Secret Manager 6 versions, Cloud Shell 5 GB. Includes 'AI APIs' free usage — the GCP-hosted AI endpoints (Vertex AI GenAI preview limits apply separately).
findings.eligibility: All new GCP users (not student-only). A Google Cloud billing account with a registered payment method is required even to use the Free Tier ('eligible customers' in a paid or trial billing account).
findings.claim: Any GCP account (trial or paid) automatically gets the free monthly allowances; no separate claim. Sign up at cloud.google.com with a card.
findings.expiry: No expiry (renews monthly), but usage resets on the 1st; unused allowance does not roll over.
findings.gotchas: Overspending beyond free limits is billed pay-as-you-go to your card. Free Tier products are region/feature-specific (e.g., e2-micro, us-central1 historically); GPU workloads are not in the free tier. Third-party LLMs on Vertex AI are billed. 'Not charged against $300 credit' means free-tier usage is on top of trial credit.

findings.name: Gemini API / AI Studio Free tier — free LLM access, no credit card
findings.detail: The Gemini Developer API has a Free tier: free input/output tokens with limited access to certain models, plus free Google AI Studio usage; no billing account or card required (Free tier qualification = 'Active project or free trial'). Per the current official docs, exact RPM/TPM/RPD are now model-specific and only viewable in aistudio.google.com/rate-limit (docs stopped publishing the static table). As of mid-2025 community-referenced Free-tier limits were ~Gemini 2.5 Pro 5 RPM / 250K TPM / 100 RPD, 2.5 Flash 10/250K/250, 2.5 Flash-Lite 15/250K/1,000. Pay tiers: Tier 1 needs a linked billing account (cap $250/min-rolling), Tier 2 after $100 spent + 3 days ($2,000 cap), Tier 3 after $1,000 + 30 days ($20k-100k cap). Upgrading to paid now requires prepaying min $5. Flagship 'Gemini 4 Argon' is NOT available on the Free tier.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Google account; no card, no .edu. Region: available in most countries; Google AI Studio usage is free in all available countries.
findings.claim: Go to aistudio.google.com -> create project -> generate an API key -> call Gemini models within Free-tier limits. For deploying up to 2 full-stack apps without GCP billing, use the Google Cloud 'Starter Tier' (AI Studio -> Deploy, eligible accounts only).
findings.expiry: Indefinite while the Free tier exists (no renewal); limits subject to change; RPD resets midnight Pacific.
findings.gotchas: Free-tier content/prompts may be used by Google to improve its products (Paid tier does not); newest flagship models excluded from Free tier; limits are per-project not per-key; from June 19, 2026 the Gemini API stops accepting requests from unrestricted API keys (must restrict keys to the Gemini API endpoint); '429' when hitting limits; AI Studio playground daily caps have been tightened in 2026 (community reports ~10-30 req/day for top models under capacity pressure).

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program — Start tier: up to $2,000 credits / 1 year (self-serve)
findings.detail: For digital-native tech startups with a working MVP planning to seek venture funding. Benefits verified from the official benefits page: up to $2,000 USD GCP credits valid for 1 year; $200 Google Skills training credits; Google Workspace Business Plus free 12 months (new signups); access to partner Startup Perks (e.g. Datadog, ElevenLabs 33M credits, Render $500, GitLab Ultimate 20 licenses) — the ones starred are Scale-only.
findings.eligibility: Founded within the last 24 months; not yet received Google Cloud credits (beyond the free trial); tech startup that plans to raise VC funding; clear product roadmap. No funding cap (pre-funding/bootstrapped is fine). Decision at Google's discretion. Company email matching public domain expected; GCP account + billing ID needed.
findings.claim: Apply via the Google for Startups Cloud Program application form at cloud.google.com/startup (self-serve 'Apply now') — or via the Startups Perks/partner pages. Complete the onboarding checklist at cloud.google.com/startup/onboarding (billing account setup) so credits attach to the correct billing account.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 1 year from issuance. Program itself is ongoing (self-serve available).
findings.gotchas: Requires a GCP billing account (payment method on file; credits offset charges, card isn't used if spend <= credit). Third-party (non-Google) models on Vertex are billed directly, not covered. 'Beyond the free trial' means the $300 trial doesn't disqualify you.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program — Scale tier: up to $200,000 credits over 2 years ($350,000 for AI-first startups)
findings.detail: Year 1: 100% of GCP spend up to $100,000 in credits (AI-first startups: up to $250,000). Year 2: 20% of GCP spend up to an additional $100,000 (both tracks). Total: up to $200,000, or up to $350,000 for AI-first startups using/planning to use Gemini as a foundation of their product. Credits cover Google models (Gemini, Gemma); third-party models billed separately. Also: up to $12,000 Enhanced Support credits (1 year, 1-hr critical response), $500 Google Skills credits, $600/month Google Maps Platform usage credits (separate application), Workspace Business Plus free 12 months, dedicated Startup Success Manager + Customer Engineers, and starred Scale-only partner perks (ElevenLabs 33M, Datadog up to $100k, OpenSearch $100k+30k, Render up to $100k, etc.).
findings.eligibility: VC-funded (equity funding Pre-Seed/Seed within last 5 years; Series A within last 12 months); founded within the last 5 years; not yet received more than $5,000 in GCP credits; stealth mode OK with funding verification. AI track additionally requires Gemini (or planned Gemini use) as foundation of primary product. No explicit revenue cap; decision at Google's discretion.
findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup ('Apply now') or apply through a Google Cloud partner (VCs/accelerators: Y Combinator — dedicated GPU/TPU access + Scale-tier benefits for AI cohorts; 500 Startups, AI2, ERA, StartX, Berkeley Skydeck). Approval is reviewed; YC and similar partners get high acceptance rates.
findings.expiry: Credits structured as Year-1 match + Year-2 20% top-up, 2-year program window; no renewal beyond that (case-by-case requests exist via partners).
findings.gotchas: To hit the $100k Year-2 top-up you must actually spend $500k in GCP in Year 2 — it's a match, not a grant. Year-1 '100%' also means real spend must occur. Third-party LLMs excluded from credit coverage. GPU/TPU access in partner cohorts may be ad-hoc scheduling, not reserved capacity. Maps and some perks need separate applications.

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education — student & faculty course credits (no credit card)
findings.detail: Faculty at regionally-accredited US institutions (or degree-awarding universities in eligible countries; for-profit institutions excluded) apply via a form and receive GCP credit coupons: faculty get their own, and a URL is emailed that students open to verify student status (school/college email confirmation) and receive coupon codes. Credits land in per-course Cloud Billing accounts. Official help docs state the program 'does not require a credit card to sign up'. Credits valid for 12 months after the course start date / 12 months after redemption; Free Tier usage does not count against them; GCP credits may not be used for crypto mining; GPU access must be requested. Separate 'training credits': current students can request 200 free Google Skills credits (online labs, courses, badges; credits expire 1 year after issue; request processing up to 2 weeks).
findings.eligibility: .edu / school email of an eligible institution (regionally accredited in US; degree-granting in eligible countries abroad). Students get credits only through a course whose faculty applied. No funding or startup criteria. Amount per course varies (historically ~$50+ per course; Google awards at its discretion).
findings.claim: Faculty: apply via the Google Cloud for Education form (cloud.google.com/edu). Students: use the invitation URL your faculty sends -> confirm school email -> redeem coupon code in the Google Cloud console (Billing -> Coupons). For Google Skills: request the 200 training credits via the training-credits form linked from cloud.google.com/edu/students.
findings.expiry: GCP course credits: valid 12 months from course start/redemption; per-course billing accounts. Google Skills credits: expire 1 year after issued.
findings.gotchas: Student credits are tied to faculty applications — there is no longer a self-serve $300/12-month 'student credit' grant on the official pages (the older student program appears sunset; see sunset notes). Credits are non-commercial, for learning. GPU/CPU/project quotas capped; requests may be denied. School email must be verifiable; .edu generators violate ToS.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial / program status as of 2026-10-22
findings.detail: No sunset: the $300/90-day Free Trial and the Free Tier remain current as of this date (pages updated 2025-2026, terms archived 2025-01-30). No new standalone free LLM 'trial credit' has been announced in 2025-2026; the AI offer is the Gemini API Free tier (no card) plus free-tier products. Startup program remains two tiers (Start/Scale) with the 2024 restructured amounts. Gemini API added spend-based tier caps and (in 2026) mandatory API-key restriction and Prepay min $5 for paid tiers.
findings.eligibility: n/a (status note)
findings.claim: n/a
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Treat static free-tier RPM/RPD numbers as volatile — Google moved them to a per-account dashboard in 2026.

sunset_notes: 2024-11-08 (AI Startups Summit, Bengaluru): Scale tier was restructured/raised — the prior program's 'up to $150,000 over 2 years' became $200,000 (or $350,000 for AI-first) with the Year-1 100% match / Year-2 20% structure; the pre-2024 tiered Grow/Scale legacy offers (which varied ~$5k-$150k by funding stage) were folded into the current Start ($2,000) / Scale ($200k/$350k) two-tier model — the earlier larger multi-stage tiers are gone. The standalone self-serve 'Google Cloud for Students' $300/12-month credit program is no longer advertised on current official pages (cloud.google.com/edu/students now lists faculty-applied course credits + free Google Skills access, 200 credits); it appears sunseted in favor of the faculty/course-based Education credits program (medium confidence — university IT pages still cite the old $300 offer). Historical note: GCP Free Trial was extended from 30 to 90 days back in Aug 2020 (unchanged since). Vertex AI's older '1M free GenAI units' promotional offer has not been re-announced in 2025-2026; AI free access now flows through the Gemini API Free tier and GCP Free Tier instead. 2026 changes worth flagging: Gemini API Free-tier rate limits moved to per-account dashboard (static per-model table removed from docs), unrestricted API keys blocked from June 19 2026, and paid tier now requires min $5 prepay.
