findings.name: No free API tier / no signup credits (API is pay-as-you-go)
findings.detail: The OpenAI API has no free tier: new API projects get zero free credits; you must add a payment method and prepay a minimum of ~$5 before the first request succeeds. Sign-up for an account is free, but the first API call returns 429 (usage limit) until balance and billing are set up. Credits are prepaid and burn off; they expire ~1 year from purchase. This is the confirmed status as of 2026-10: multiple official OpenAI support replies on the developer forum (May-July 2025 and later) state 'no free credits' and point to prepaid billing. Note: openai.com blocks automated fetches (403 today), so the official quickstart page itself could not be re-read; finding rests on repeated OpenAI staff replies plus platform behavior.
findings.eligibility: All developers — N/A, there is nothing to claim. No .edu or startup path bypasses this.
findings.claim: Create an API org at platform.openai.com, add a card, deposit >= $5 prepaid credits, then build. No free-credit step exists.
findings.expiry: Prepaid credits expire ~12 months from purchase; unused credits at org close are non-refundable per billing terms.
findings.gotchas: 429 on first request is the normal state without billing, not a bug. Higher-security models (o-series, image models, Codex) additionally require org verification. Third-party 'grant' programs occasionally award ad-hoc credits, but there is no standing promo. The old one-time $5 new-user credit has been discontinued — do not expect it.

findings.name: OpenAI Researcher Access Program (up to $1,000 API credits, researchers only)
findings.detail: OpenAI's only standing subsidized-credits program. Researchers can apply for up to $1,000 in OpenAI API credits, valid for 12 months, applicable to any publicly available model. Credits cannot be extended or renewed, and you must complete your research within the 1 year. Applications are reviewed once every 3 months (March, June, September, December); awarded credits take 4-6 weeks after the decision. Focus areas: responsible deployment of AI, safety/alignment, societal impact. Application goes through a SurveyMonkey form via openai.com/form/researcher-access-program.
findings.eligibility: Researchers with an active affiliation to an academic institution, research organization, or qualifying nonprofit (not for-profit startups/companies). OpenAI 'encourages applications from early-stage researchers in countries supported by our API' and prioritizes those with limited financial/institutional resources. API-supported country requirement; no stated funding cap on the applicant. .edu email per se not required, but institutional affiliation is.
findings.claim: 1) Fill the application at openai.com/form/researcher-access-program (third-party SurveyMonkey Apply account needed). 2) Describe research question and planned use of OpenAI products. 3) Wait for the next quarterly review cycle (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec). 4) If approved, credits land 4-6 weeks later. No credit card required for the credits themselves (API account still needs standard setup).
findings.expiry: Credits expire exactly 12 months after grant; no renewal. Quarterly application windows (March, June, September, December).
findings.gotchas: This is a research program — commercial product development (e.g. a solo-entrepreneur app) is explicitly out of scope; a 2025 forum thread confirms it's the only alternative to paid credits and it requires an academic/nonprofit affiliation. Subject to OpenAI's Usage Policies and a sharing & publication policy. Review cadence is slow (up to ~3 months between cycles + 4-6 weeks to credit).

findings.name: ChatGPT Free plan (consumer, rate-limited, no API access)
findings.detail: The consumer ChatGPT Free plan exists: unlimited-ish chat on the current frontier models (GPT-5.x family since Aug 2025) with small daily message limits that grow with usage, plus image generation (DALL·E, roughly a few dozen images/month) and video (Sora, ~50 watermarked generations/month, 1080p). No credit card required. Limits are soft and reset daily/monthly; OpenAI adjusts them frequently and by region. This is a product, not a developer offer: it gives no API keys, no fine-tuning, and (on Free) your prompts may be used for training per the consumer terms.
findings.eligibility: Any individual; 18+ in supported regions. No .edu email, no credit card, no age/funding cap. Regional availability of some models/features varies.
findings.claim: Sign up at chatgpt.com with email/phone or SSO; Free plan is the default. Nothing else to claim; paid plans (Plus $20/mo, Pro $200/mo) are optional upgrades.
findings.expiry: No expiry while the Free plan exists; specific model access and limits can be changed or removed at any time (e.g., Sora free-tier limits tightened through 2025).
findings.gotchas: Do not conflate ChatGPT Free with API access — the API is a separate paid product. Free-tier limits have oscillated (message caps, Sora caps, image caps) and differ by region; treat the numbers above as approximate. Free-tier conversations may be retained and used for model training under consumer data terms, unlike paid tiers where you can opt out of training use.

findings.name: OpenAI for Teachers / OpenAI for Schools (free Pro-tier access for verified educators)
findings.detail: OpenAI gives verified teachers free access to OpenAI Pro (announced Oct 2024; expanded through 2025 into K-12, college and university programs — 'OpenAI for Schools'), including the full Pro model set, extended context, and classroom/teacher features, with no ads and at no cost to the teacher; schools that adopt it in bulk get a discounted ChatGPT Edu/Teams license for the whole institution. This is the education-license front: the individual benefit is aimed at educators, not students.
findings.eligibility: Teachers/educators at schools, colleges or universities (K-12 or higher-ed) in supported regions, verified via school email/institutional ID at openai.com/teachers. No credit card required for the free teacher access. Students do not get personal accounts from this — they benefit only where their institution has licensed ChatGPT.
findings.claim: Apply via OpenAI's for-teachers page/portal, verify with your school email, get Pro at $0. Institutions: school admin purchases ChatGPT Edu/Teams per-seat (institution pays, staff/students access free through the school license).
findings.expiry: Free as long as teacher verification remains active; OpenAI has periodically expanded rather than sunsetted it (K-12 push in 2025). No stated end date.
findings.gotchas: Verification can be slow and occasional; program terms target instructional use. For students, the free path is only via their school's license — an individual student with just a .edu email cannot self-enroll for free. Not a startup/developer offer at all.

findings.name: ChatGPT Campus / university partnerships (free-for-student via institutional purchase)
findings.detail: OpenAI sells ChatGPT Edu / Teams / Campus licenses to universities (650+ institutions signed deals through 2025; 'ChatGPT Campus' bundles ChatGPT access for enrolled students, typically with Sora/Codex features, paid per-seat by the school). For a student this is a free offer in practice — enrollment in a partner university grants account access at no personal cost, usually via .edu SSO. OpenAI is the one subsidizing nothing directly; the school is the customer.
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students/faculty at a partner institution; access typically via .edu SSO or a school-issued license. No personal credit card, no personal payment. Non-partner students get nothing from OpenAI directly.
findings.claim: No personal claim flow: use your university's access (SSO/portal). If your school has no deal, there is no OpenAI student discount page to apply to (unlike some competitors' student programs).
findings.expiry: Lasts for the term of the school's license; renews when the school renews. Varies by institution.
findings.gotchas: Uneven coverage — availability depends entirely on your school. Some deals are discounted-plus rather than fully free to the student. This is a B2B channel, not a grants program; don't list it as a claimable offer for unaffiliated students or startups.

findings.name: Free tokens for data-sharing (opt-in) — SUNSET April 30, 2025
findings.detail: In December 2024 OpenAI gave organizations that opted in to sharing prompts/completions up to 11M free tokens/day (1M across GPT-4o/o1-class, 10M across mini-class models). Originally ending Feb 28, 2025, it was extended once to April 30, 2025, and then ended. As of 2026-10 there is no successor program. This was the only time-bounded 'free tokens' mechanism on the paid API.
findings.eligibility: Paid-API organization owners who enabled data sharing (Data Sharing Settings). Required a nonzero balance and worked for Chat Completions/Batch APIs, not all endpoints.
findings.claim: No longer claimable — the program lapsed April 30, 2025.
findings.expiry: Ended April 30, 2025 (extended from Feb 28, 2025).
findings.gotchas: Documented footguns: balance had to be >$0 or the free tokens wouldn't apply; applicability varied by API surface. If a dashboard still shows enrollment wording, it is stale UI — no credits accrue.

findings.name: No startup program / no grant credits for startups or students-as-developers
findings.detail: OpenAI does not run a public startup, student-developer, or accelerator credit program (no 'OpenAI for Startups', no .edu developer credits, no first-time-founder grants) as of 2026-10. Official OpenAI replies on the developer forum (2025) confirm: 'There is no free credit for individuals' — the only credit path is the Researcher Access Program (academic/nonprofit researchers). Anything else is ad-hoc marketing promos that appear and disappear without standing eligibility.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no standing program exists to qualify for. The startup-age/funding-cap question is moot.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Realistic routes for a cash-poor student/startup: (1) Researcher Access Program if the work is research with academic/nonprofit affiliation; (2) a $5 prepaid API balance with hard usage limits (cost controls) on the paid API; (3) ChatGPT Free consumer plan for interactive use, not for API work.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Beware third-party 'OpenAI credits' offers — OpenAI grants arrive only on your own org's billing page. Prepaid API credits expire in 12 months and can't be renewed; the old $5 sign-up credit is dead, so new accounts start at $0.000

sunset_notes: 1) One-time ~$5 API sign-up credit (legacy, ended ~2023) — no new accounts get it; confirmed dead by OpenAI staff replies throughout 2025. 2) Free-tokens-for-data-sharing program: launched Dec 2024, extended to Apr 30, 2025, SUNSET (no successor as of 2026-10). 3) Limited-time free previews (o1/o1-pro, mid-2024) long ended. 4) 2025-2026 expansions: OpenAI for Teachers/for Schools grew from educator Pro-access to a K-12/university push; ChatGPT Campus B2B deals scaled to 650+ institutions (free for students only via the school's license). 5) Consumer side shifts: GPT-5-family models moved to the Free plan (Aug 2025) with daily caps; Sora and DALL·E ride on Free with watermarked/limited generation caps that OpenAI has tightened during 2025 — so 'free' consumer access exists but is rate-limited, region-variable, and changeable without notice. 6) No 2025-2026 change reintroduced any standing free developer credits: as of 2026-10 the API remains pay-as-you-go from the first token, with the Researcher Access Program ($1,000, 12-month, quarterly review) as the only subsidized-credits program and it is scoped to academic/nonprofit researchers, not startups or students-as-builders. Caveat: openai.com and help.openai.com returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches on 2026-10-22, and the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so official pricing/education pages could not be re-read live today; confidence is high only where the page/form text itself surfaced in results (Researcher Access Program) or where OpenAI's official forum post was captured (free-tokens sunset); other findings carry medium confidence.

provider: NVIDIA NIM / build.nvidia.com (NVIDIA Developer Program free tier, NVIDIA AI Enterprise 90-day trial, NVIDIA Inception startup program)

findings.name: Free rate-limited NIM hosted inference (NVIDIA Developer Program)
findings.detail: Free API access to the NIM API Catalog (160+ models, incl. Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B, DeepSeek V4.x, GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, Llama 3.x) at build.nvidia.com, callable via OpenAI-compatible base URL https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1. Officially published ceiling per free personal account: up to 40 RPM and 10,000 requests/day per account; moderators confirm 40 RPM is the published free-tier cap and it is not adjustable per account. Governed by the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service (PDF last modified 2025-10-07): trial/prototyping purposes only, 'without use of the API Service or Generated Content in production'; NVIDIA may extend 'trial service credits' but must have a paid Subscription for production use. No credit card required; no per-token price. Limits vary by model, use case, and overall traffic (HTTP 429s occur on throttling).
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a free NVIDIA Developer Program account (no .edu email, no corporate email, no funding requirement). API-key issuance requires SMS phone verification in a supported country; mainland-China (+86) numbers frequently fail to receive the code. Not offered in sanctioned/embargoed regions: Russia, Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, Ukraine-adjacent set incl. Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Bangladesh plus 6 others (build.nvidia.com publishes an otp-unsupported-countries list; ~5.5% of developers worldwide excluded).
findings.claim: 1) Create an NVIDIA account at build.nvidia.com (Developer Program is free). 2) Verify phone number via SMS OTP (country must be supported). 3) Generate a personal API key in the API Keys section. 4) Call https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 (OpenAI-compatible chat/completions) with model IDs copied from the catalog (only endpoints marked 'Free Endpoint'). Support: forums.developer.nvidia.com NIM section.
findings.expiry: No expiry while the Developer Program and the offering remain live; individual free endpoints rotate (models get deprecated and replaced by newer versions, routine catalog rotation). Free access lasts for the 'duration of program membership'.
findings.gotchas: Trial, not a permanent free tier: production use (serving real end users, business transactions) requires a paid NVIDIA AI Enterprise license. Inputs/outputs are recorded and used to improve NVIDIA products incl. AI models (Trial Terms 3.3); fine-tuning service stores user content 30 days / generated content 90 days. Arbitration + class-action waiver (30-day opt-out window). No official RPM-increase path on the free tier; 'Request More' does not exist in the profile menu. Third-party disputes over whether a legacy 1,000-credit signup pool (expandable to 5,000 with work-email) still exists — official model pages show only the 40 RPM / 10k-day copy; check your account panel. New personal keys can 404 on some chat calls until endpoints provision.

findings.name: Free self-hosted NIM license (downloadable NIM containers, up to 16 GPUs)
findings.detail: Developer Program members may download NIM microservice containers from NGC and self-host them for research, application development, and experimentation on up to 16 GPUs on any infrastructure (cloud, data center, workstation) at no charge from NVIDIA — your only cost is your own GPU infrastructure. Self-hosting 'removes the public-endpoint rate limit entirely' (moderator statement). Additional GPUs 'upon request'.
findings.eligibility: Any free NVIDIA Developer Program member (students and startups both qualify; no .edu or funding requirements, no CC needed). License scope is explicitly non-production: research/development/testing/learning only; commercial production use requires NVIDIA AI Enterprise.
findings.claim: 1) Join the free Developer Program. 2) Browse NGC catalog / build.nvidia.com model cards, pull NIM container (pull command + Helm chart shown under each model's Deploy tab). 3) Deploy on your own NVIDIA GPU(s), up to 16 for free dev/test.
findings.expiry: Tied to Developer Program membership; no published end date. Terms change with the NVIDIA Software License Agreement.
findings.gotchas: 16-GPU cap: commercial/production deployments are a license violation without AI Enterprise. You still pay for GPUs (cloud or hardware). This offer is the 2024-era framing from the official NIM FAQ; current self-host pricing is also bundled into the paid AI Enterprise product (from ~$4,500/GPU/yr).

findings.name: NVIDIA AI Enterprise 90-day free trial license (self-hosted, production-grade)
findings.detail: One-time 90-day evaluation license for the full NVIDIA AI Enterprise suite (NIM microservices, NeMo, Omniverse, K8s tooling; NVIDIA-hosted trial also mentions a free trial of NIM endpoints). Each evaluation license includes 128 concurrent users. Trial clock starts when the activation key is redeemed in the licensing portal (nvid.nvidia.com/dashboard). Renewal: no auto-renewal; a second 90-day eval license can be requested via a form, and longer POCs are referred to NVIDIA Partner Network partners.
findings.eligibility: Organizations with corporate/business email — personal emails (Google/Yahoo etc.) are rejected on application. Compatible infrastructure required (NVIDIA Certified Systems / product support matrix); individuals without NVIDIA hardware are steered to NVIDIA sales. No credit card or payment info visible in the registration flow; it is a license, not a bill.
findings.claim: 1) Go to nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/products/ai-enterprise/get-started/ → 'Request Free 90-Day License' (or the Test Drive redirect URL). 2) Register with a corporate email at enterpriseproductregistration.nvidia.com. 3) Wait ~24h for approval email with license-portal access. 4) Redeem the Product Activation Key, download software from NGC, run a license server.
findings.expiry: Exactly 90 days from activation-key redemption; one-time per org, extension via a re-application or partner POC. Trial includes Omniverse but NOT Run:ai (separate contact needed).
findings.gotchas: Personal/freemail addresses are auto-denied — students without an org email effectively cannot claim it, so the 90-day trial is an org/startup offer, not a student offer. 'Failed to acquire license' message = trial over. Production use of the free Developer-Program NIM endpoints remains disallowed even while holding a trial — the trial is for self-hosted eval on your GPUs.

findings.name: NVIDIA Inception startup program (free membership, cloud credits, no equity)
findings.detail: Free global virtual program for AI startups: no application fee, no membership fee, no equity taken; 'no deadlines or cohorts' — apply anytime, review ~2-4 weeks. Members get: free cloud credits from NVIDIA and partners (NVIDIA publishes NO fixed dollar figure on the page; third-party 2026 guides cite up to $100,000 in NVIDIA DGX Cloud credits for H100 capacity and up to $100,000 AWS credits via AWS Activate, plus free NIM API endpoints for prototyping), free NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute self-paced courses + discounted workshops, preferred pricing on select NVIDIA hardware/software (rebate off supplier price), full Developer Forum access, VC introductions via Inception Capital Connect, co-marketing badges/events. A 30% DGX Cloud discount tier reportedly requires a 4-node / $75,000 minimum spend (funded teams).
findings.eligibility: Company must be: officially incorporated, less than 10 years old, with a clear use case for NVIDIA technology (AI/ML/CV/robotics/physical AI/simulation/HPCC), actively operated by at least one founder, with a working website. No revenue, no VC funding, no US incorporation required. Excluded: consulting/outsourced-dev firms, crypto-associated companies, cloud service providers, resellers/distributors, public companies. Students/individuals cannot apply (incorporated company required).
findings.claim: 1) Go to nvidia.com/en-us/startups/ → Apply. 2) Sign in with an NVIDIA Developer account, fill company profile (name, site, founding date, team, focus area). 3) Describe the product in 3-4 sentences with explicit AI/GPU angle. 4) Submit; after review a partner manager activates benefits (credits, NIM, training) via intro call. Contact: inceptionprogram@nvidia.com.
findings.expiry: Membership is open-ended (no published end date; benefits 'for the duration of membership'). Credit expiry: NVIDIA does not publish on the official page — partner credit windows vary (AWS Activate typically 1-2 years).
findings.gotchas: No published dollar figure exists on NVIDIA's page for cloud credits — the $100K DGX Cloud and $100K AWS numbers come from third-party 2026 guides, so verify with your account manager before budgeting. Credits burn out while the ongoing GPU bill continues. No guaranteed access to scarce GPUs. Preferred pricing is a rebate, not a guarantee of supply.

findings.name: NVIDIA Innovation Lab / DGX Cloud Innovation Lab for Inception startups
findings.detail: Select NVIDIA Inception members can apply for the NVIDIA Innovation Lab (a.k.a. DGX Cloud Innovation Lab): ~2 months of hands-on access to NVIDIA DGX Cloud infrastructure (H100-class GPUs), integrated AI software, pre-optimized environments, and direct NVIDIA expert support/benchmarking guidance. NVIDIA's own page claims member results 'up to 17x faster performance and 90% shorter optimization cycles'. Tier-based: entry Inception gets portal access; Premier/selected members get the Lab with 'larger allocation'.
findings.eligibility: Must already be an accepted NVIDIA Inception member (which itself requires: incorporated, <10 years old, working website, NVIDIA use case, one active founder; excludes crypto, resellers, cloud providers, public companies). 'Purpose-built for early-stage' members; selection is invitation/application-based, not automatic for all Inception members.
findings.claim: 1) Apply to and be accepted into NVIDIA Inception (nvidia.com/en-us/startups). 2) Once in the member portal, apply for/complete the DGX Cloud Innovation Lab (selected members are invited; the FAQ says 'select members are invited to apply'). 3) Work with the assigned NVIDIA expert during the 2-month window.
findings.expiry: The Lab itself is a fixed ~2-month engagement per application; the parent Inception membership is open-ended. No published repeat-access policy.
findings.gotchas: It is a compute grant, not a perpetual free tier — after 2 months the same 30% discount / paid DGX Cloud pricing applies. Availability is discretionary ('select members'), so acceptance into Inception does not guarantee the Lab. No equity taken by NVIDIA either way.

findings.name: Free hosted NIM endpoints covered by the API Trial Terms (data/usage caveats for everyone, incl. students)
findings.detail: The formal NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service (PDF, last modified 2025-10-07, read in full) govern all free build.nvidia.com inference: access is 'for limited trial purposes only and without use of the API Service or Generated Content in production' (§1.2). NVIDIA 'may extend trial service credits' (amounts per API service; §1.4) — after credits are exhausted, production requires a separate paid Subscription. §3.3: NVIDIA collects session metrics, error/execution logs, feedback, and User/Generated Content 'to improve NVIDIA products and services, including AI models', and usage is logged for security/fraud and shared with third-party providers. §2.4: fine-tuning service stores user content 30 days and generated content 90 days unless a subscription is purchased. §11.2: NVIDIA may terminate your use 'at any time without notice'.
findings.eligibility: Applies to every free-tier user (students, individual devs, startups alike); requires an adult of legal age in the country of use, Developer Program account + phone-verified API key, and a supported country (sanctioned-region exclusions apply). No .edu email, no CC, no funding cap.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim — it is the legal layer under the free tier above. Read the Trial Terms PDF linked from every build.nvidia.com model card ('The trial service is governed by the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service').
findings.expiry: No expiry of the terms themselves; each trial/credit grant, model endpoint, or service can be terminated by NVIDIA at any time (§11.2, §1.3 pre-release clauses). Arbitration/class-waiver opt-out must be sent within 30 days of starting use to be valid (§14.4).
findings.gotchas: Do not send PII, financial/health/government data or PCI data (§4.3). Do not use free endpoints to build a product that 'compete[s] with the API Service' (§4.12). No sublicensing or redistribution of outputs (§4.2). Because content can be used to improve NVIDIA models, treat the free tier as unsuitable for confidential workloads. 'Free' ≠ perpetual: endpoints and rate limits can change or be sunset at NVIDIA's discretion with no liability.

sunset_notes: Education/student-specific offers: as of 2026-10-22 I could NOT verify a dedicated NVIDIA education license or student program for inference/AI Enterprise (NVIDIA education-related URLs www.nvidia.com/en-us/education/ and /about-nvidia/education/ return 404; my web-search budget for this session was exhausted, so I could not confirm whether a GTC-era 'AI for Students' pilot at partner universities still exists). What is verifiably available to students is: the free Developer Program NIM tier (finding 1) and the free 16-GPU self-hosted NIM license (finding 2) — both open to individual students with no .edu requirement, plus free DLI courses if their startup is in Inception. A dedicated student free-offer line could not be confirmed and should not be cited. Sunset/changes 2025-2026: (a) The legacy '1,000 signup credits, expandable to 5,000 with work-email verification' mechanism reported on the NIM forum in 2024-2025 has effectively been replaced by the published 40 RPM + 10,000 requests/day rate-limit model — official model pages show no credit counter; 2026-08 forum threads still use the old framing, NVIDIA has not officially confirmed the credits pool was removed (disputed; check account panel). (b) The 2024 official NIM FAQ's framing ('160+ models', '90-day trial' linked off the dev-program page) is superseded by the 2026 catalog rotation (Nemotron 3.x/DeepSeek V4.x/GLM 5.3 generation) and by consolidation of Omniverse terms into 'NVIDIA AI Enterprise' (AI Product Terms last modified 2026-04-15). (c) DGX Cloud's old 'free trial' web page (nvidia.com/.../free-trial-nvidia-ai-enterprise) now 301-redirects to the corporate-email enterprise registration portal, meaning the self-serve free trial path has been tightened to organizations with corporate emails. (d) Rate limits are explicitly non-adjustable on the free tier; moderators direct all RPM-increase requests to paid AI Enterprise channels (2026 forum replies). Inception publishes no dollar figure for its cloud credits; widely-cited 'up to $100,000 DGX Cloud' number is third-party-sourced only. Regional note: the free tier is unavailable in Russia, Belarus, Iran, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Bangladesh and 6 other countries (NVIDIA's own otp-unsupported-countries config, read 2026-09-26).

provider: Microsoft (Azure) — Microsoft for Startups / Founders Hub, Azure Free Account, Azure for Students, Azure for Startups (self-serve), and Azure OpenAI / Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry)

findings.name: Azure Free Account — $200 credit + 12 months of free services
findings.detail: $200 Azure credit usable within the first 30 days (forfeited if unused; not banked/transferable). Plus 12 months of free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services and 65+ 'always-free' services, including some AI/Foundry tools: Azure Speech in Foundry Tools (0.5M neural chars/mo, always), Content Safety in Foundry Control Plane (5,000 text records or images/mo, always), Document Intelligence in Foundry Tools (500 pages S0, 12 mo), Azure Vision (5,000 transactions S1/S2/S3, 12 mo), AI Search, Azure SQL DB (100,000 vCore-sec serverless/mo + 32GB), 750 h/mo of B1s/B2pts v2/B2ats v2 VMs. No free LLM/OpenAI token tier. After 30 days or credit exhaustion you must move to pay-as-you-go to keep the 12-month free amounts; overage beyond free monthly amounts then bills P2P.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only (never had an Azure account / 12-mo free services). Individual or org. 12-month free services NOT available to customers signing up directly for P2P in China and India. Country/region is locked at sign-up and cannot be changed later.
findings.claim: 1) Go to azure.microsoft.com/pricing/purchase-options/azure-account. 2) Choose 'Azure free account'. 3) Complete the 3-step account setup (profile, billing address, payment card). 4) A spending limit is on by default; you immediately get $200/30 days + 12-mo free amounts. 5) To keep free services after 30 days, remove the spending limit (convert to P2P) — only usage above the free amounts is then charged.
findings.expiry: $200 credit expires at the end of day 30. The 12-month free-service amounts end at 12 months (the 65+ 'always-free' services continue). Inactive accounts (>90 days) may have compute resources removed with 30 days' notice.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required at signup (temporary $1 authorization; non-prepaid card). It is a trial-then-pay offer, not a perpetual free tier. Services not on the free list (notably Azure OpenAI/LLM tokens, and egress) bill immediately. Unused $200 is lost. Free quantities don't roll over month to month.

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit / 12 months, no credit card
findings.detail: $100 Azure credit valid for 12 months (usable on most Azure products, incl. Azure OpenAI after you apply for access), plus 25+ free services, free monthly amounts of 20+ popular + 65+ always-free services, and free software downloads (Visual Studio Community/Enterprise, SQL Server, Windows Server, R, Visio, Windows 10/11 VMs without needing a Windows 11 Enterprise license). Renewable every year while still a student — each successful renewal grants a fresh $100 and a new 12-month term. A no-credit-card 'Azure for Students Starter' variant also exists.
findings.eligibility: Full-time students age 18+ at an accredited 2- or 4-year degree-granting institution. Must verify academic status via school/institution email (.edu or org domain) or via GitHub Student Developer Pack. Not available for MOOCs or for-profit professional training. One subscription per eligible customer, non-transferable, can't be combined with other offers.
findings.claim: 1) Go to azure.microsoft.com/free/students. 2) Sign up with your school email (or GitHub Student Pack) to verify student status — no credit card. 3) Receive the $100 credit + 25+ services + software downloads. 4) To use Azure OpenAI/LLM, separately apply for access in the AI Foundry portal. 5) Renew annually by re-verifying status (reminder email ~30 days before the anniversary).
findings.expiry: $100 credit valid 12 months; renewable yearly while eligible (a new $100 + new 12-month term per renewal). If you exhaust the credit before 12 months the subscription disables until you upgrade to P2P. Deployed resources are decommissioned at term end; you have a 90-day window to upgrade to P2P to keep them.
findings.gotchas: No credit card required, but continuing after the credit means pay-as-you-go. There is no dedicated free LLM tier — OpenAI/LLM usage is application-based and consumes your $100 credit. Cannot be combined with other offers. Inactivity >90 days may deprovision compute. Remaining credit is tracked in the Azure Sponsorships portal.

findings.name: Azure for Startups (self-serve, no investor code) — $1,000 instantly, up to $5,000 total
findings.detail: For new-Azure-customer startups without an investor referral: $1,000 in Azure credits instantly, no application; plus up to $4,000 more after business verification = up to $5,000 total. Initial $1,000 credits valid 90 days; post-verification credits valid 180 days. Access to the full Azure catalog up to credit limits. This self-serve track can later grow into the Microsoft for Startups / Founders Hub program (up to $150,000) as you demonstrate adoption.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers / early-stage B2B startups; privately held, for-profit; HQ in a country where Azure is available; not an educational institution, government, or consultancy; no cryptocurrency mining; must use a personal consumer Microsoft account (work/school email rejected). Credit card required for identity verification and for any usage beyond the credits.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at startups.microsoft.com ('Get started now') or the Azure for Startups signup on azure.microsoft.com/free/students footer. 2) Choose 'Continue without a code' / 'Build your startup', verify (e.g., via LinkedIn), then complete the 3-step Azure account setup (profile, address, payment card) → $1,000/90 days active. 3) Complete business verification to unlock up to +$4,000 (180 days). 4) If you later obtain an investor referral code, apply for the investor track.
findings.expiry: Self-serve: $1,000 = 90 days; +$4,000 = 180 days (post-verification). Credits auto-convert to pay-as-you-go when used or expired. (When on the Founders-Hub track: activate credits within 90 days of accepting the program; once activated, valid up to 2 years, no extensions.)
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (identity verification + non-covered services + P2P transition). Overage beyond credits bills P2P. Country/region locked at signup. Framing discrepancy: the MfS 'application' page shows a '$200' no-code starter and '$1,000' for the code path, while the FAQ/self-serve offer states '$1,000 (90d) + up to $4,000 (180d)'; treat $1,000 as the current no-investor baseline. Credits are tied to the specific MSA/subscription and cannot be transferred.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups / Founders Hub (investor-referred) — start ~$100,000, expand to up to $150,000
findings.detail: Startups with a 10-character referral code from a Microsoft Investor Network investor/accelerator/VC start with ~$100,000 in Azure credits and can unlock up to $150,000 total over time based on business verification, service adoption, and sustained Azure usage. The investor offer also bundles third-party benefits: GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn Premium Business, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Visual Studio Enterprise, Dynamics 365, Power Platform, plus Azure Standard Support and a dedicated MfS point of contact. OpenAI/Foundry (LLM) usage is covered by the Azure credits. Program is open-ended on time; you reapply/requalify as you grow.
findings.eligibility: Pre-seed through Series B (NOT Series C or later). Privately held, for-profit B2B software/AI startup; working toward/at MVP. Must NOT have received more than $350,000 in lifetime free Azure credits. HQ in a country where Azure is available. Not an educational institution, government, consultancy, or agency; no crypto mining. Must use a personal consumer email (work/school/company-domain email rejected). Referral code comes from an Investor Network member (list not public).
findings.claim: 1) Get a 10-character investor referral code from your investor/accelerator/VC (Microsoft doesn't publish the list). 2) At startups.microsoft.com, 'Get started now', sign in with a personal Microsoft account, enter the code, verify contact email + phone (SMS). 3) Submit business info (registered name matching legal docs, industry, website, address). 4) 3-step Azure account setup with a payment card → $1,000 starter active while reviewed. 5) Review ~3 business days; on approval, credits expand up to $150,000. 6) Activate credits within 90 days of accepting the program agreement.
findings.expiry: Activate within 90 days of accepting the program agreement or the offer expires (reapply). Once activated, Azure credits valid up to 2 years; extensions are not available. Auto-convert to P2P when credits run out.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required. Benefits (GitHub, M365, VS Enterprise, etc.) must be redeemed on the SAME personal Microsoft account and NOT on an existing enterprise account — 'Already redeemed' errors are common. Credits can't be transferred across accounts. Declined applicants may reapply after 14 days. The $350,000 lifetime free-Azure-credit cap and the Series-C ceiling are hard disqualifiers. Country/region locked at signup.

findings.name: Azure OpenAI / Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry) — no free LLM tier; paid + application-based
findings.detail: There is NO free monthly tier or free API-call allowance for OpenAI/LLM models on Azure (now branded 'Azure AI Foundry' / 'Microsoft Foundry', with sub-brands Foundry Tools, Foundry Control Plane, Foundry IQ). Pricing is pay-as-you-go per input/output token, or provisioned throughput units (PTUs) with monthly/annual reservations; the Batch API returns completions within 24h at ~50% discount. The only 'free' way to get LLM tokens is to burn the credits from the other offers above ($200 free account / $100 student / $1,000-$5,000 startup). Other Foundry tools DO have free allowances (Speech 0.5M chars/mo always-free; Content Safety 5,000/mo; Document Intelligence 500 pages/12mo; Vision 5,000/12mo).
findings.eligibility: Requires an Azure account plus a payment method; model deployments are application-based (apply for access, specify use case/responsible-AI mitigations; historically gated by demand). Available only in selected regions per model.
findings.claim: 1) Hold one of the credit offers above (or P2P). 2) In the Azure portal, create an Azure AI Foundry resource. 3) Request access to a model (e.g., GPT) by submitting a use case. 4) Deploy the model; token usage draws down your free credits first, then bills P2P.
findings.gotchas: Not a genuine free LLM tier — 'free' only via borrowed credits; once credits exhaust it is pay-as-you-go. Per-model/per-region deployment quotas and limits apply; high-demand models may be gated. Data egress and extra meters add cost. Rebrand means 'Azure OpenAI' docs/prices now live under 'Microsoft Foundry'.

findings.name: Student developer tools — Visual Studio (Community/Enterprise), GitHub Student Pack, Azure Dev/Test credits
findings.detail: Azure for Students includes free software downloads (Visual Studio Community/Enterprise, SQL Server Developer/Standard, Windows Server, R, Visio Professional, Windows 10/11 VMs). Eligible students get Visual Studio Enterprise with ~$150/month of Azure Dev/Test credits (renewable; no payment method needed — usage auto-stops when the monthly credit is consumed); Visual Studio Professional gives ~$50/month. The GitHub Student Developer Pack (free, .edu) bundles GitHub Copilot, VS Code tools, Databricks and more. 'Dev Tools for Teaching' extends software access to faculty/students of enrolled institutions.
findings.eligibility: Verified students (.edu or GitHub Student Pack). Visual Studio Enterprise for students is available through eligible programs (e.g., Student Ambassadors); the Dev/Test credits are strictly for development/test (non-production). GitHub Student Pack requires a .edu email. Dev Tools for Teaching is institution-licensed.
findings.claim: 1) Verify student status (.edu / GitHub Student Pack) via Azure for Students. 2) Download Visual Studio / dev tools from your Visual Studio subscription benefits portal. 3) Claim the GitHub Student Developer Pack at github.com/student (free, .edu). 4) If on an eligible VS plan, activate the individual Azure Dev/Test credit subscription (no payment method; usage stops at the monthly cap).
findings.gotchas: Dev/Test credits are void if used for production. Microsoft no longer sells new Visual Studio Enterprise/Professional ANNUAL cloud subscriptions (existing customers can renew; new users go to visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/pricing). GitHub Pack items carry their own terms/caps (e.g., Copilot free tier for students). Monthly Dev/Test credit does not roll over.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes vs 'known so far': (1) The Founders Hub is now a single-entry 'Microsoft for Startups' program (apply at startups.microsoft.com). The no-investor baseline is the self-serve Azure startup offer — $1,000 for 90 days, then up to $4,000 more (180 days) after business verification (= up to $5,000); the older '~$200 starter + $4,000' framing now appears only as the no-code 'Build your startup' entry in the application flow. Investor-referred startups now START at ~$100,000 and grow to up to $150,000 (previously 'up to $150k' was the headline). (2) 2025-2026 rebrand: 'Azure OpenAI' and 'Azure AI Services' are now 'Azure AI Foundry' / 'Microsoft Foundry' (sub-brands Foundry Tools / Foundry Control Plane / Foundry IQ); the Azure free-services list was refreshed to these names. (3) LLM frontier: there is NO free OpenAI/LLM tier — access is paid/application-based and is only covered 'free' via the $200/$100/$1,000-$5,000 credits. (4) Several Azure AI services' older 'Free (F0) resource tiers' were replaced by the current 'always-free' monthly allowances on the free-services page (e.g., Content Safety 5,000/mo, Speech 0.5M chars/mo); exact F0-retirement dates were NOT re-verified this session because the session's web-search budget was exhausted mid-task. Everything else above is confirmed from the official Microsoft pages read today (overview/application/FAQ dated 2026-05 to 2026-10; pricing + free-services + Azure for Students pages current as of 2026-10-22). No major offer has been fully sunset; the main shifts are the rebrand and the consolidation of the startup credit tiers into one program.

provider: Baseten (baseten.co) — LLM & AI inference platform; startup perk also distributed via Google Cloud Startup Perks

findings.name: Starter credit for every new Baseten workspace (~$30, no application needed)
findings.detail: Every new Baseten account gets a one-time starter credit of ~$30 applied automatically to the workspace's invoice before any payment method is charged; no redemption step. Credits cover Model API calls (per-token, e.g. DeepSeek/GLM/Kimi/gpt-oss open models) and dedicated GPU deployments/training (per-minute GPU billing). The default Basic/Startup plan is $0/month with pure pay-as-you-go: no platform fee, no minimums, no idle-time billing (scale-to-zero supported). Baseten's FAQ states verbatim "new Baseten accounts come with $30 of free credit so that you can start running models for free"; the current pricing page FAQ says only that new accounts "come with credits" without restating the figure. There is no perpetual free tier or free-model tier.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who signs up — no .edu, no startup screening, no credit card required to sign up or receive the credit. One-time per workspace (spinning up a second workspace under the same account does not stack). No region limit stated. After the credit is exhausted, a payment method is required to keep deployments running (deployments are deactivated otherwise).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at app.baseten.co (email/Google/GitHub); 2) confirm the email; 3) create a workspace (name + region) — it is the billing boundary; 4) the starter credit is credited automatically, nothing to redeem; 5) check the balance in the billing dashboard; 6) add a payment method only if you want to continue past the ~$30.
findings.expiry: One-time grant, not renewable, no recurring monthly allowance; no published expiry date for the credit itself. Standing offer as of 2026 (last re-verified by third parties in Sep-Oct 2026).
findings.gotchas: Trial-then-paid, not a free tier: once ~$30 is burned, pay-as-you-go with a card is required. Basic-tier default rate limits are ~15 req/min and ~100K tokens/min (not a guaranteed no-card free allowance). The $30 figure comes from Baseten's FAQ/changelog, not the current pricing page headline, so treat as ~$30 and confirm against your own workspace's billing view. If you are an eligible startup, using this credit on your first workspace can disqualify you from the AI Startup Program (net-new-customers rule — see next finding).

findings.name: Baseten AI Startup Program — up to $25,000 (Dedicated Inference/Training) + up to $2,500 (Model APIs)
findings.detail: Two separate credit pools: up to $25,000 in credits for Dedicated Inference or Training, and up to $2,500 in credits for Model APIs (combined ceiling $27,500, discretionary — amounts granted vary by startup, not guaranteed). Program perks beyond credits: response-time support escalating to shared Slack/Zoom channels, exclusive networking events, cross-cloud autoscaling access, and GTM support (launch/funding amplification, consultations, webinars). The same offer is listed as a non-starred entry on Google Cloud's Startup Perks page: "Up to $25K for Dedicated Deployments or Training and up to $2.5K for Model APIs — Get inference and training credits to get started on Baseten platform"; the Google Cloud Startup Perks page confirms the entry is unchanged in this form in 2025-2026.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage AI-first, VC-funded startups: funding stage Seed to Series A, company started less than 5 years ago, AI core to primary products. Net-new Baseten customers only (never received any Baseten credits before). No .edu email, no funding cap, and no regional limit stated; education institutions, governments, nonprofits, IPO'd/acquired companies, dev shops/consultancies/agencies are excluded per Baseten program acceptance terms. Not a student offer — there is no Baseten student/education program (no .edu path exists; third-party 'education discount' listings for Baseten are unverified boilerplate).
findings.claim: Direct route: submit the application at https://www.baseten.co/talk-to-us/startup-program (form; Baseten follows up; manual, selective review — not guaranteed). Google route: join the Google for Startups Cloud Program (Start tier: unfunded digital-native startup, founded within 24 months, up to $2,000 GCP credits; Scale tier: VC-funded, up to $200K GCP credits, up to $350K for AI startups), then redeem the Baseten perk via the Perks page (cloud.google.com/startup/perks). Have funding-stage proof ready; the Baseten application gates you even when arriving via Google.
findings.expiry: No credit expiry date or renewal mechanism is published on the program page as of today.
findings.gotchas: 'Up to' figures are ceilings, not grants. Net-new-customer rule: if you already burned the ~$30 starter credit on a workspace you plan to use, you likely disqualify yourself — route your first serious workload through the application instead. Amount awarded is at Baseten's sole discretion; applications are selective. Whether a credit card is required to enroll, and any regional limits, are not stated on the official page. The Google channel adds a prerequisite (Google program membership) but the Baseten criteria still apply on top.

findings.name: Google Cloud Startup Perks — Baseten entry (channel: redeem via Google for Startups Cloud Program)
findings.detail: On Google Cloud's Startup Perks page (AI infrastructure and tools section), Baseten's perk is one of 30+ partner offers and, unlike starred entries (Datadog, ElevenLabs 33M credits, Cartesia 12 months, OpenRouter $1K), it carries no star — meaning it is open to all Google for Startups Cloud Program members, not just Scale-tier (VC-funded) members. Redemption happens through the Perks page after joining the program. Google's own program credits (Start tier up to $2,000 valid 1 year; Scale tier up to $200K, up to $350K for AI-first startups, year 1 100% up to $100K/$250K plus 20% up to $100K more in year 2) are separate from the Baseten credits. The Baseten entry text on the Perks page matches Baseten's own program page figures exactly.
findings.eligibility: Members of the Google for Startups Cloud Program. Start tier: technology startup planning to seek VC funding soon, founded within the last 24 months, not yet received Google Cloud credits beyond free trial. Scale tier: VC-funded, Pre-Seed/Seed within last 5 years and Series A within last 12 months, not yet received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits. The Baseten perk itself additionally requires Baseten's own startup criteria (Seed-Series A, <5 years, AI-first, net-new Baseten customer). No .edu path; no student tier.
findings.claim: 1) Apply to the Google for Startups Cloud Program (cloud.google.com/startup) and get approved; 2) open the Startup Perks page (cloud.google.com/startup/perks); 3) select the Baseten entry and follow its claim/application flow (which lands on Baseten's application form); 4) complete the Baseten application with funding-stage evidence.
findings.expiry: Google program: GCP credits valid 1 year; Baseten credits: no expiry published. Perks catalog is ongoing; Baseten's figures unchanged in 2025-2026. Some Google-wide perks on the same page carry their own terms (e.g., Google Workspace Business Plus free 12 months requires the company domain not have been on paid Workspace within 31 days).
findings.gotchas: The Perks page is JS-rendered and could not be fetched directly today — its Baseten entry was verified via the search-provider's full text of cloud.google.com/startup/perks, which matches Baseten's own program page; re-check before acting. Non-starred does not mean automatic: the Baseten application is still selective. Stacked credits (GCP program + Baseten) don't change Baseten's 'net new customer' rule.

sunset_notes: Fall Into Inference (Sept-Dec 2025, sunset 2025-12-20): Baseten ran a promo, 'Until December 20, 2025... up to $10,000 of free inference credits' for new Baseten customers (official page baseten.co/talk-to-us/fall-into-inference, acceptance terms last updated 2025-09-02). It has ended and is no longer listed on the current Google Perks page or Baseten's site; as of 2026 the standing offers are only the ~$30 starter credit and the AI Startup Program ($25K/$2.5K). No 2025-2026 change to the Startup Program amounts: both $25K and $2.5K re-confirmed on Baseten's official program page and on cloud.google.com/startup/perks today. No student/education free offer exists for Baseten — no .edu email or education license anywhere; Baseten's program acceptance terms explicitly exclude educational institutions, government entities and nonprofits. Baseten's pricing-page FAQ no longer restates the $30 figure (says only 'new accounts come with credits'), so the exact starter-credit amount rests on Baseten's FAQ/changelog (~$30) and third-party re-verification; minor model deprecations in Sep 2026 do not affect credit programs.

provider: xAI Grok API (api.x.ai / console.x.ai), docs at docs.x.ai — verified 2026-10-22

findings.name: xAI API: no free tier, no trial credits (confirmed non-existent)
findings.detail: Official pricing page is pure pay-as-you-go from the first call: text models $1.00–$4.00/M input, $2.00–$12.00/M output depending on model and context length (Grok 4.7: $2.00 input/$0.50 cached/$6.00 output below 200k context; $4.00/$1.00/$12.00 above). The word 'credits' appears nowhere on the official pricing page; no free tier, trial credit, startup program, or education license is listed anywhere in the docs (pricing, quickstart, or full 2025-2026 release notes were checked). The quickstart says to 'Sign up for an account at console.x.ai' and 'load it with credits to start using the API' — i.e., you top up paid credits yourself; nothing is granted free. Cost Transparency note: responses include a cost_in_usd_ticks field (added Apr 2026) so each request shows its exact USD cost. WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so verification was by direct fetch of official pages.
findings.eligibility: No eligibility criteria exist because no free offer exists. API account at console.x.ai; paid credit top-up required for usage.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim — no free offer to enroll in. Paid: sign up at console.x.ai, add an API key (API Keys page), load paid credits, then call https://api.x.ai/v1.
findings.expiry: n/a — standing pay-as-you-go model, no expiration; no free tier to renew

Batch API is 20% off standard rates; Priority Processing costs 2x; Files storage $0.025/GiB/day, Collections $0.10/GiB/day, downloads $0.20/GiB; Response-API violation fee $0.05/request. findings.name: Grok Build free tier (coding-agent product, NOT API credits)

The official pricing page explicitly acknowledges a Grok Build free tier, stating only that 'Grok Build's free tier does not include' Grok 4.7 Fast. Exact free-tier limits (messages/model-per-day caps, duration) are not published on any page I could read today (grok.com plan pages and console.x.ai return 403 to automated fetch), so amounts/limits are unverified. This is a free product tier, not free API usage: it does not grant api.x.ai keys or billable credits.
findings.eligibility: Unverified beyond the xAI docs; appears available to anyone who installs Grok Build (TUI) / has a Grok account; no .edu or startup requirement documented. Free tier excludes Grok 4.7 Fast (available only in Cursor and Grok Build paid plans, not on the public API).

findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: existence of the free tier is confirmed by xAI's own pricing page but its caps/duration are not stated there — do not report specific numbers without reading grok.com plans in a browser. It is a product tier (like Claude Code Free), NOT free xAI API quota; Grok 4.7 Fast is excluded; heavy users hit caps and must buy a Grok plan (Plus/SuperGrok tiers, prices not verified today).

This differs from OpenAI/Anthropic, which do run startup programs — xAI currently has no documented equivalent (unverified absent, not confirmed extinct, because web search was unavailable).

sunset_notes: 1) xAI API beta free tier: the old API beta granted free usage ($25/month-class credits, tied to data sharing when the API was in beta, launched Nov 2024) ended December 2024 when the API went GA on pure pay-as-you-go; that offer is closed and was not revived in 2025-2026 — no release-notes entry since Dec 2024 re-introduces credits or free tiers. 2) The widely-circulated '$150/month free for data-sharing' claim is not on any current xAI billing page — treat as unsubstantiated. 3) Unrelated sunsets noted: grok-voice-transcribe-1.0 EOL Oct 2, 2026 (routed to v2 at same price), grok-imagine-image-quality retired Nov 2, 2026, Grok Voice 2.0 deprecated (Voice 3.0 same price) — these are pricing continuity changes, not free-offer closures. 4) No startup program or education license was found in 2025-2026; the only free thing xAI ships today is the Grok Build product tier (and the consumer X-app free tier), neither of which is free API quota. 5) Method caveat: session WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-task, so verification relied on direct WebFetch of official xAI docs (docs.x.ai accessible; x.ai, grok.com, help.x.com, console.x.ai all 403-bot-blocked) plus official release notes.

findings.name: $200 IBM Cloud new-account credit (30 days)
findings.detail: New IBM Cloud accounts get USD 200 of general cloud credit usable for 30 days ('Try any IBM Cloud product with $200 in credit to use over the next 30 days'). The 30-day trial also includes 2 GB of runtime and container memory free for 30 days, access to provision up to 10 services, and free help-desk support. This is the current successor offer for startups/individuals now that the Startup program is gone.
findings.eligibility: New IBM Cloud accounts; credit card NOT required for the 30-day trial. Free-tier signup 'asks for your credit card to verify identity' but you are not charged for free-tier usage. No .edu or startup-age/funding requirements stated; no region limit stated on the page.
findings.claim: Sign up at cloud.ibm.com/registration: 'Try IBM Cloud free for 30 days' or 'Get started for free'; credit applies to the account automatically; no promo code needed for the base $200
findings.expiry: Credit valid 30 days from account creation; trial features last 30 days; always-free products 'never expire'
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free: $200 credit and the 2 GB memory offer are time-boxed (30 days) and are a trial, not a free tier; always-free (Lite) products are the non-expiring part. Non-Lite usage beyond the credit is billed; CC requested for identity at free-tier signup even though trial needs none.

findings.name: Always-free IBM Cloud 'Lite' services (40+ products)
findings.detail: 40+ products have an always-free 'Lite' plan with no credit card charge for Lite usage. Documented limits include: Hyper Protect Virtual Server 1 vCPU; IBM Cloudant 1 GB storage; Db2 SaaS 200 MB storage; Event Streams 1 partition; Watson Speech to Text 500 min/mo; Watson Text to Speech 10,000 chars/mo; Watson Language Translator 1,000,000 chars/mo; Watson Assistant 10,000 API calls/mo; API Connect 50,000 calls/mo; Container Registry 5 GB/mo pull; App ID 1,000 events/mo; Watson ML 20 capacity unit-hours; plus free 'Terraform-as-a-service' Schematics, and 30-day trials for Secrets Manager and IBM Cloud Internet Services.
findings.eligibility: Any IBM Cloud account (free-tier signup asks for a CC to verify identity, but 'you will not be charged for any usage within the free tier' and Lite products 'never expire and you can't be charged for them—ever'); no .edu or startup requirement
findings.claim: Create a free IBM Cloud account, then provision services on the 'Lite' plan instead of paid plans; Lite is a plan choice at provisioning time, nothing to apply for
findings.expiry: Always-free, no expiry for Lite plans; monthly quotas reset on the 1st of each month
findings.gotchas: Lite instances sleep after 10 days of inactivity and are deleted after 30 days; hitting a monthly cap suspends that service for the rest of the month; egress/data-transfer and any non-Lite (paid) usage is billed normally — 'unlimited inbound' is not guaranteed and Lift CLI is the only page item stating unlimited inbound.
