provider: AWS / Amazon Web Services (AWS Activate + new Free/Paid plan model; Bedrock access via credits and Kiro)

findings.name: AWS Free plan (new-account credits: $100 base + up to $100 earned, 6-month window)
findings.detail: As of 2026 AWS replaced the classic 12-month per-service free tier with a Free plan vs Paid plan model. New accounts are auto-enrolled in the Free plan and get $100 in AWS credits immediately, plus up to $100 more earned by completing 'Explore AWS' activities (up to $200 total). The Free plan runs at no cost for up to 6 months or until credits run out, whichever comes first, and the account closes automatically. Base credits expire 6 months from account creation; activity-earned credits expire 12 months; if you upgrade to the Paid plan remaining credits apply to bills and expire 12 months after account creation. 30+ 'always free' services with monthly caps remain on both plans. A payment method is NOT required to sign up for most new customers (a major change from the old credit-card-required model). Credits are USD, non-transferable between accounts, and can offset usage on eligible services including Amazon Bedrock model invocations and AI/ML workloads. Featured Bedrock access on the Free plan; Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is listed as a Paid-plan-exclusive service.
findings.eligibility: Any new AWS account (personal or business). No .edu requirement, no funding criteria, no credit card required for most customers. Free plan restricts access to a subset of services; Paid plan allows a monthly spend limit starting at $20.
findings.claim: 1) Create a new AWS account (auto-enrolls in Free plan, no payment method needed for most customers) -> 2) $100 credits are applied on signup -> 3) Complete Explore AWS activities in the console to earn up to $100 more -> 4) Use credits on eligible services incl. Bedrock within the 6-month window -> 5) Optionally upgrade to Paid plan; remaining credits roll onto invoices until 12-month expiry.
findings.expiry: Base $100 credits: 6 months from account creation. Earned up to $100: 12 months from account creation. Free plan itself auto-closes 6 months after account open or when credits are exhausted. No renewal or extension; credits cannot be transferred.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free confusion: this is a 6-month credit window, NOT the old 12-month tier. Once upgraded to the Paid plan you CANNOT downgrade back to Free. Legacy per-service allowances (EC2 750 hrs, S3 5 GB, Bedrock free-token lists) no longer appear in the new structure. Data transfer/egress and some advanced features may be excluded or Paid-plan-only. The old Bedrock 12-month free-token offer is gone from the free-tier FAQ and docs (see sunset notes). Credits only offset eligible services - check the Free Tier Categories list.

findings.name: AWS Activate Founders tier (self-serve; $1,000 start, up to $5,000)
findings.detail: The self-serve AWS Activate tier. $1,000 in AWS Activate Credits to start; select startups may qualify for additional credits up to $5,000 over time. Credits (USD, subject to AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs) can offset 200+ eligible AWS services including third-party foundation models on Amazon Bedrock (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Mistral AI, Meta, etc.) via a single API. Application is reviewed within 5-10 business days.
findings.eligibility: Self-funded / bootstrapped (no VC or accelerator backing needed). Must be: new to AWS Activate Credits, have a fully functioning company website, founded in the past 10 years, Pre-Series B, and have an AWS account on a Paid Tier plan (note: the new paid-plan requirement means the free-plan-only account must be upgraded). No .edu requirement. Business email matching the startup domain is required for the application.
findings.claim: 1) Create/verify an AWS Builder ID (personal email) -> 2) Complete the one-time AWS Activate profile with your business email -> 3) Choose the Founders tier -> 4) Provide startup details (product, funding stage, company profile) -> 5) Link an AWS account (on Paid plan) and submit -> 6) Hear back in 5-10 business days. Apply at https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/ ('Apply here' / 'Join now' on https://aws.amazon.com/startups/).
findings.expiry: Promotional credits: no public per-tier expiry stated on the credits page today; AWS has said Activate credits generally expire in 1-3 years depending on package (the $200K-class credits are on 3-year expiry per the 2024 announcement). Credits are in USD, subject to Promotional Credit T&Cs, non-transferable.
findings.gotchas: Only $1,000 is guaranteed; the $5,000 extension is selective. 'New to Activate Credits' - you cannot re-claim unless you are requesting more than previously received. Egress/data-transfer and some fees may be excluded from promotional credits (check the credits FAQ 'What is not covered'). Requiring a Paid-plan AWS account means a card/payment setup may be needed at the account level even though the Free plan itself needs no payment method.

findings.name: AWS Activate Portfolio tier (provider-backed; up to $200,000)
findings.detail: Up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits (the tier ceiling was $100,000 until the June 2024 doubling for Series A-stage startups; the credits page now lists a single Portfolio tier up to $200,000). Usable on 200+ services including third-party Bedrock models (Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Meta, etc.), and can also be applied to Developer/Business AWS Support Plans. Program has provided $8B+ in credits to 350,000+ startups since 2013.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Series B (most recent funding round within the last 12 months, if applicable), founded in the past 10 years, fully functioning company website, AWS account on a Paid Tier plan, new to Activate Credits or requesting more than previously received, AND an Organization ID (Org ID) from an AWS Activate Provider (VC firm, accelerator, incubator or angel group in the AWS network - e.g. YC, Sequoia, a16z, Greylock). Apply within 12 months of your most recent funding date.
findings.claim: 1) Confirm your VC/accelerator/angel is an AWS Activate Provider and obtain their Org ID -> 2) Create AWS Builder ID + complete Activate profile with business email -> 3) Choose Portfolio tier and enter the provider's Org ID (or use a direct provider invite) -> 4) Link AWS account and submit at https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/ -> 5) Reviewed in 5-10 business days; approved credits are added to your AWS account.
findings.expiry: The $200K credit package expires 3 years from issuance (per the June 2024 change; previously the $100K package expired in 1 year). USD, subject to Promotional Credit T&Cs, non-transferable.
findings.gotchas: You cannot apply yourself without a provider's Org ID or invite - a consulting partner cannot file it for you. 'Within 12 months of your latest funding date' is a hard window. Credits cannot be sold or transferred; check the 'not covered' list (data transfer and some support fees historically excluded, though Support Plan application is permitted). The old ~$100K ceiling is outdated in most third-party guides.

findings.name: AWS Credits for AI Startups (invite-only; $200,000+)
findings.detail: A new tier launched with the 2026 credits-page redesign: $200,000+ in AWS Credits for AI startups 'ready to scale' beyond the Activate tiers. No open application exists - it is invite-only and accessed by talking to your AWS Account Manager. Additional credits beyond Activate are explicitly marketed for AI startups building on Amazon Bedrock (funding models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Meta, etc.).
findings.eligibility: Startups that have already gone through Activate Portfolio and are ready to scale (AI-focused). No public age/funding/.edu criteria published; eligibility is determined case-by-case by the account team. No credit-card specifics published (linked to the existing AWS account).
findings.claim: No self-serve claim. 1) Be an AWS Activate participant (Portfolio tier) -> 2) Contact your AWS Account Manager (or use 'If you need additional support, contact us' on https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/) -> 3) AWS reviews and issues credits to your AWS account.
findings.expiry: Not published today; by analogy with the $200K Activate package, 3-year expiry is expected but unconfirmed. USD, promotional T&Cs apply.
findings.gotchas: Invite-only means no guaranteed outcome or timeline; it is not a free product - it is a promotional credit negotiation. Amounts are not fixed ('$200,000+' is a floor, not a promise).

findings.name: Kiro Startup Credits (up to a year of Kiro Pro+ credits; Starter/Growth/Scale tiers)
findings.detail: New AWS Kiro agentic-IDE credit offer (linked from the AWS credits page: 'Start building on day one... Start with Kiro Startup Credits, then grow into Activate Credits'). Up to one year's worth of Kiro Pro+ credits in three tiers by team size: Starter (up to 2 Kiro users), Growth (up to 10 users), Scale (up to 30 users). Credits expire 1 year after issuance to your AWS account; they cannot be refunded, re-issued, transferred or sold. Separately, Kiro main offers a $20 credit when you first sign up for a paid Kiro plan via social login or Builder ID.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage through Series A startups, global. Requires an official business email on the startup's own domain AND an AWS Account ID using a matching email. EXCLUDED REGIONS: Argentina, Belarus, Brazil, China/GCR, Cuba, France, Germany, Iran, Italy, Mexico, North Korea, Poland, Russia, Spain, Syria, Crimea, DNR, LNR, UAE. Startups with active AWS Activate Credits are NOT eligible for this promotion (though Activate credits can still be applied toward Kiro). No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Sign in with your AWS account -> 2) Apply via 'Apply for startup credits' (routes to https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/kiro) -> 3) Rolling review; decision by email -> 4) Approved credits are automatically added to your AWS account and activate immediately (no deferral) -> 5) To use them, log into Kiro via AWS IAM Identity Center (Kiro Enterprise) - social login (GitHub/Google) and Builder ID do NOT work with startup credits. After credits run out, standard Kiro Pro+ billing applies.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 1 year from date of issuance to the AWS account. One application per startup at a time; re-application allowed only if eligibility status changed after a rejection. After 12 months of credit consumption you move to paid Kiro Pro+.
findings.gotchas: The excluded-region list is long (much of the EU/MEA/APAC). Activation cannot be deferred, so issuance date = countdown start. Company-level credit pool shared only among authorized users of associated accounts. It is mutually exclusive with holding active AWS Activate Credits.

findings.name: Kiro Student Offer (1,000 credits/month free for 12 months)
findings.detail: Kiro's student program: 1,000 Kiro credits per month at no cost for one full year, explicitly 'no credit card required'. After the year, the account auto-downgrades to the public Kiro free tier (projects/specs stay on your machine and repos; no discounted paid plan for students). 1,000 is the Kiro credit unit for model usage (Kiro Pro+ is its paid tier).
findings.eligibility: Enrolled student at one of ~150+ listed eligible universities (US-centric: MIT, CMU, NYU, Georgia Tech, ASU, etc., plus international). Account must use a university-affiliated email (.edu, .ca or equivalent) via Google, GitHub, or AWS Builder ID. Must be at least 18 years old. If your school isn't listed you can submit your university email through a 'Don't see your school listed?' form and Kiro may reach out later.
findings.claim: 1) Create or log into a Kiro account using your university email -> 2) On the account usage page, a banner appears if eligible; click verify and complete a SheerID check (first/last name, DOB, university; sometimes student ID or enrollment letter) -> 3) Once verified, the 1,000 credits/month activate automatically.
findings.expiry: 12 months from verification, then auto-downgrade to the public free tier. Credits do NOT roll over between monthly cycles; hitting the 1,000 cap means waiting for the next cycle; no add-on credit purchases on the student tier.
findings.gotchas: No rollover of unused monthly credits; the ~150-university list is the real gate (many schools not included); SheerID can delay activation; after year one there is no student discount - only the base free tier. This is Kiro (agentic IDE credits for coding with frontier models, incl. Claude-class models), NOT Amazon Bedrock API access - for direct Bedrock API use, the AWS Free plan credits or Activate credits are the path.

findings.name: AWS Academy (education license - free courses, not cloud credits)
findings.detail: AWS Academy is AWS's education program (successor to AWS Educate, renamed ~2021) giving students and educators free structured AWS courses, hands-on labs via partner platforms, and discount pathways toward certification. It is a training/education license: it does NOT include AWS credits, Bedrock access, or LLM free tiers - students who want actual Bedrock usage must use the AWS Free plan, Activate, or Kiro offers above. (Could not be re-verified live today: https://aws.amazon.com/academy/ returned 404 and the training sub-page was unreachable; details from general knowledge.)
findings.eligibility: Open to students and teachers at partner institutions; typically .edu/institutional affiliation or partnership enrollment (e.g., via AWS Academy Accelerate Your Career or institutional programs). No credit card needed for the free learning content.
findings.claim: 1) Enroll through your institution's AWS Academy partnership or an open course on the AWS Academy/Skill Builder platform -> 2) Complete free courses -> 3) Certifications and advanced access are paid or partner-subsidized.
findings.expiry: N/A - ongoing educational access; no credit expiry because no credits are granted.
findings.gotchas: Not an LLM offer at all - it is courses/labs. Do not confuse with free Bedrock or Kiro student credits. Institutional access rules vary by country/partner.

sunset_notes: SUNSET / MATERIAL CHANGES 2024-2026: (1) The classic AWS 12-month free tier (EC2 750 hrs/mo, S3 5 GB, 1M input + 1M output free Bedrock model-invocation tokens per month for 12 months across ~75 models, RDS 750 hrs, etc.) has been SUPERSEDED by the new Free plan / Paid plan model: $100 signup credits + up to $100 earned, 6-month window, 30+ 'always free' services, and notably no payment method required for most new customers. The Bedrock-specific free-token docs page (docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/free-trial.html) now renders empty/removed, and the new Free Tier FAQ contains zero mention of Bedrock free tokens, 750 EC2 hours, or 5 GB S3 - legacy per-service allowances no longer exist. So the 'free Bedrock tokens for students' front is effectively dead; Bedrock access now comes via (a) Free plan $100-200 credits, (b) AWS Activate credits, or (c) Kiro credits for agentic coding. (2) June 2024: AWS doubled the portfolio/accelerate credit ceiling from $100,000 to $200,000 (announced July 1, 2024, for startups that raised Series A in the past 12 months; seed stage stayed at $100,000 at the time; credits' expiry moved from 1 year to 3 years - per CNBC 2024-06-28). The current credits page (2026) shows one Portfolio tier at up to $200,000. (3) 2026: the credits page was redesigned (awslabs/startups PR #75, June 2026) renaming tiers to Activate Founders ($1,000 start, up to $5,000 - NOT the ~$100 sometimes misreported; the $100 figure matches the new Free plan signup credit, not Activate), Activate Portfolio (up to $200,000), and adding the invite-only 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' tier ($200,000+) plus the new Kiro Startup Credits program. (4) 'Known so far' figures from the task (~$100K Portfolio, ~$100 Founders) are outdated: Portfolio is now up to $200K and Founders is $1,000-to-start/up-to-$5,000. No standalone student Bedrock/LLM free offer from AWS exists today - the closest student fronts are the no-card Kiro Student Offer (1,000 credits/month x 12 months) and AWS Academy (training only, no credits). Verification caveat: today's live fetches of aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/ and free sub-pages intermittently returned 403 via proxy, but credits-page content was captured today via the official page mirror in the awslabs/startups repo and search snippets of the live page; free-plan figures came directly from aws.amazon.com/free/ and /free/free-tier-faqs/ read today.</sunset_notes>

findings.name: Cloudflare for Startups — 3-tier credit program (up to $350,000 in credits, 12 months)
findings.detail: Official program (https://www.cloudflare.com/startups/, read 2026-10-22). Tiers: $10k credits — bootstrapped/self-funded, under $1M raised, no minimum funding; $100k credits — under $5M raised, must be funded by an affiliated Cloudflare partner (VC/accelerator); $350k credits — $5M+ raised, funded by an affiliated partner. Credits are valid 12 months from the confirmation email or until fully consumed (whichever first); no extensions; non-transferable/non-refundable; overages billed to card on file. Credits cover usage-based services: Workers, Workers for Platforms, Durable Objects, Workflows, Workers AI (sub-caps $2,500 T3 / $10,000 T2 / $50,000 T1), Workers KV, D1, Queues, Vectorize, R2 (sub-cap $10,000), Pages, Images and Stream, Cache Reserve, Argo Smart Routing. Included at no cost on all tiers (not drawn from credits): 3 enterprise domains, unlimited Business and Pro plans, DDoS and bot protection, WAF with 1,000 custom rules, Security Analytics, SSL certs, Page Shield, CDN and DNS, Load Balancing (2 origins), Rate Limiting (1 rule), 100% SLA. Support: priority tickets + chat; T2 adds case-dependent account manager + expert sessions; T1 adds account manager, priority tech support, bi-weekly Solutions Architect office hours. Excluded from credits: AI Gateway (temporarily), registrar fees (domain registration/renewal), enterprise add-ons (some require email request), Magic Transit / Enterprise Spectrum / Dedicated IPs / China Network. Review ~48 hours; contact startups@cloudflare.com; multiple distinct startups can each apply under different account IDs/emails.
findings.eligibility: For-profit tech startup; founded within last 10 years (corporate age <=10 yrs); funded up to Series B with funding within last 12 months; actively building a tech product; public verifiable website; active LinkedIn/X/GitHub; first-time applicants only (no re-entry); business email matching your domain required (personal emails rejected); excluded: educational institutions, personal blogs, consultancies, agencies, MSPs, resellers. $100k/$350k tiers additionally require funding by an affiliated Cloudflare partner. No region limit stated (program is global). A valid payment method (credit card) MUST be on file — so CC IS required, unlike the free plan.
findings.claim: 1) Create a Cloudflare account, add payment method, 2) Submit the application via 'Apply now' on cloudflare.com/startups, 3) Wait up to 48h for review, 4) Confirmation email activates the program; credits auto-deduct in dashboard. Existing members on the old $5k/$250k caps may email startups@cloudflare.com for a case-by-case tier-upgrade evaluation (does NOT reset the 12-month expiry).
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months from confirmation email or until consumed, whichever comes first; no extensions. Program itself is ongoing (long-term).
findings.gotchas: CC required on file and overages auto-billed after credits run out; R2 sub-cap $10k and Workers AI sub-caps can bite if you plan to use those; AI Gateway and registrar fees not credit-covered; Enterprise add-ons (e.g., Advanced Rate Limiting, Bot Management, extra LB origins) need manual email support requests; post-graduation Enterprise domains auto-downgrade to Free plan; November 18, 2025 global outage is a single-vendor concentration risk noted by the community; '1,000 WAF rules' marketing applies to program/Enterprise domains, not to the regular Free plan (5 rules).

findings.name: Cloudflare Free plan (site plans) + Developer Platform free allowances — permanent, no credit card
findings.detail: Free site plan: $0/mo — unlimited-bandwidth CDN (335 data centers), unmetered DDoS mitigation, free Universal SSL, 1.1.1.1 DNS, Free WAF Managed Ruleset, 5 WAF custom rules/zone, 1 rate-limiting rule, email obfuscation, hotlink protection. No SLA, ticket-only support. No credit card required for the free plan. Separate permanent per-service free allowances on the pay-as-you-go Developer Platform (cloudflare.com/plans/, read 2026-10-22): Workers 100,000 requests/day + 10ms CPU/request; R2 10 GB-month storage + 1M Class A ops (zero egress fees); Workers KV 1GB / 100k reads/day; D1 5GB / 5M rows read/day; Queues 10k ops/day; Workers AI 10,000 neurons/day; Vectorize 30M queried dims/month; Workers Logs 200k events/day; Containers 25 GiB-hrs memory + 1TB egress; Browser Rendering 10 min/day; TURN/SFU 1,000 GB/mo egress; Images 5,000 transformations/mo. Paid Developer Platform rates apply above allowances ($0.30/M Worker requests, $0.02/M CPU ms, etc.) — no card needed until you exceed allowances on a paid component.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no signup gate, no .edu, no funding requirement. Free site plan needs no payment method; usage-based overage billing activates when you exceed free Developer Platform allowances.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at dash.cloudflare.com (free), 2) Add a domain (zone) for CDN/DDoS/SSL/WAF-free-managed-ruleset, 3) Deploy Workers/Pages/R2/etc. free; overages metered at pay-as-you-go rates.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; per-service allowances current as of 2026-10-22 pricing page.
findings.gotchas: WAF custom rules on Free = 5 (not 1,000 — that's the Enterprise/startup-program number); Free plan excludes SLA, advanced bot management, image optimization, China network; CDN ToS forbids using free CDN for video streaming/large-file hosting (512MB per-file cache cap); no SSO/log retention beyond 24h (Zero Trust free tier = 50 users).

findings.name: Cloudflare for Students — 12 months of the paid Workers plan free for .edu students (launched Birthday Week, Sept 22, 2025)
findings.detail: 12-month free access to the paid developer features plan (Workers Paid, normally $5/mo, fee waived): deploy up to 500 Worker scripts; 10M requests/month (then $0.30/M); 20M included log events/month (then $0.60/M); up to 30s CPU per request; 6,000 included build minutes/month ($0.005/min after); 6 concurrent build slots; extra Workers KV edge storage; all free-plan features; dedicated student Discord community. After 12 months the account auto-reverts to the Free plan with no charge; renew by upgrading to Workers Paid at standard pricing. Offers may not be redeemed multiple times; Cloudflare may use your name/project in marketing and can discontinue the program without notice; no 24/7 enterprise phone support or SLA. Launched Sept 22, 2025 as 'the first step for Cloudflare for Students', currently US-only; Cloudflare is adding other schools' domains on request.
findings.eligibility: Students in the United States only, at least 18 years old, currently enrolled in an eligible educational program, with a verified .edu email (required and must be set as the billing email). A valid credit card MUST be on file (base $5/mo fee waived; you are billed for usage above base allotments). No .edu = no access; international students must apply to have their institution's domain added.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a free Cloudflare account with your .edu email and verify it, 2) On the Billing page add a valid credit card and confirm billing email = your .edu, 3) On the Workers Plans page add the Workers Paid plan (fee auto-waived for 12 months), 4) Wait for the confirmation email that the account redeemed the offer.
findings.expiry: 12 months per redemption, not renewable free — reverts to Free plan; renew only by paying for Workers Paid. No set end date for the program; US-only at launch, expansion pending.
findings.gotchas: CC required (card on file; overages billed at standard usage rates even during the free year); usage caps differ from the Startup program sub-caps — over-limit workers requests cost $0.30/M; not available to students outside the US yet; marketing usage of your name; program can be changed/discontinued without notice.

findings.name: The Cold Start pitch competition — $500,000 credits prize (2026 edition, now concluded)
findings.detail: One-off annual competition announced Sept 28, 2026: five early-stage startups each got 5 minutes on stage at Cloudflare Connect (Moscone West, San Francisco) on Oct 19, 2026; judges (Matthew Prince, Michelle Zatlyn, Dane Knecht) picked a winner receiving $500,000 in Cloudflare credits, a San Francisco billboard, and a VIP speakers dinner; finalist flights covered. Target: early-stage startups in the US and Canada with <$10M raised.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startup, based in US or Canada, raised less than $10M. Application window closed Oct 2, 2026.
findings.claim: Applied via the form linked on the blog post (closed). 2027 edition not yet announced; watch blog.cloudflare.com under the Cloudflare for Startups tag.
findings.expiry: 2026 round closed (event held Oct 19, 2026 — before today, Oct 22, 2026); likely recurring annually but no next date published.
findings.gotchas: Prize is winner-only (4 of 5 finalists get no credits); not a general program — do not plan budgeting around it.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 program changes: (1) The Startup Program was restructured in 2025 from the April 2025 4-tier structure ($5,000 / $25,000 / $100,000 / $250,000, 'founded within last 5 years') to the current 3 tiers ($10k / $100k / $350k, founded within last 10 years) — entry tier doubled, top tier raised $250k->$350k, and the $25k tier was dropped. Members on the old caps can request a case-by-case upgrade that does not reset their 12-month expiry. (2) Sept 22, 2025: program expanded to non-profit, civil-society, and public-interest organizations (up to $250k credits; first application window ran until Dec 1, 2025). (3) Sept 22, 2025: Cloudflare for Students launched (12-month free paid developer features, US .edu only) — an education license/credit that did not exist before 2025. (4) 'The Cold Start' ($500k credit prize) closed with its Oct 19, 2026 Connect event; applications ended Oct 2, 2026. (5) Stale pages: some localized pages (e.g., cloudflare.com/en-in/forstartups/) still show the old '5 years / $5k-$250k' criteria — treat as outdated; the global /startups/ page is authoritative. (6) Community note: a global Cloudflare outage on Nov 18, 2025 (Workers KV, Access, Turnstile, dashboard, core CDN) is a recurring single-vendor risk with free tiers. The pre-launch claim 'WAF (1,000 rules) on all [startup] tiers' is confirmed — but the regular Free plan only gets 5 WAF custom rules; 1,000 is the Enterprise-plan limit that the startup program includes at no cost.

provider: Microsoft Azure — Azure for Students / Azure for Students Starter / Microsoft for Startups (student & startup offers; LLM & AI free tiers; managed data-platform free tiers)

findings.name: Azure for Students (higher-ed): $100 Azure credit + free services, no credit card
findings.detail: Verified 2026-10-22 on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students and the official offer page (ms-azr-0170p). Students get $100 in Azure credits to use within 12 months plus: free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months (new Azure customers only), free monthly amounts of 65+ always-free services, access to the full Azure service catalog up to free amounts + the $100 credit, and access to Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Foundry with 1,700+ foundation models (OpenAI o1/GPT-4 series, Hugging Face, Meta, Cohere, Phi SLMs). Includes free 'Software Download Benefits' via the Azure Education Hub: Visual Studio (Community/Code/for Mac, Agents for VS), SQL Server Developer & Standard, Windows Server, Visio Professional, R Client/Server, Hyper-V Remote Tools, System Center, Azure DevOps Server, SQL Server Mobile Report Publisher. Renew annually while a student: each renewal gives a fresh $100 + another 12-month term (confirmed by MS staff in a March 2026 Q&A and the official FAQ; reminder emails ~30 days before expiry; no hard cap on renewals).
findings.eligibility: Full-time students at an accredited degree-granting 2- or 4-year university; affirm age 18+; verify academic status via your organization's (school) email address — Shibboleth where supported, or GitHub Student Developer Pack verification code as fallback; NOT available for MOOCs or for-profit professional training; one subscription per person; 'limited supply of activations, while supplies last'; not available in sovereign-cloud (US Gov, China, Germany) regions; offer available where Azure is commercially available.
findings.claim: Go to azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students → sign up with a Microsoft or GitHub account → verify student status with school email (or GitHub code at signup.azure.com/studentverification?offerType=1) → accept offer terms; no credit card at sign-up. Track remaining credit in the Azure Sponsorships portal. After 12 months, re-sign up for the offer to renew; to renew you re-verify status.
findings.expiry: $100 credit and 12-month free services window run from sign-up; renew annually while eligible. If credit is exhausted early the subscription is DISABLED (you can upgrade to Pay-As-You-Go via support; deployed resources are then decommissioned at the end of the 12-month term — 90 days to convert). Invoicing statements may appear monthly but are covered by the credit.
findings.gotchas: Credits cannot be used on Azure Marketplace offers and don't carry over between months or subscriptions; unused credit is forfeited at 12 months; if you previously held any Azure free trial/student offer on the same Microsoft identity you cannot sign up again (you'll hit a 'no access' wall and must convert that old sub to PAYG); the offer can be terminated at Microsoft's discretion; the 20+ free-for-12-months services apply only to NEW Azure customers; anything beyond free amounts deducts from the $100; the 'Visual Studio Pro for 12 months' item in many older guides is NOT in this offer anymore — Pro only comes from the separate GitHub Student Developer Pack; keep at least one resource/portal activity so the sub doesn't lapse as inactive (MS community advises 90-day activity, not official).

findings.name: Azure for Students Starter (K-12 path): free core-service tiers, no credit card, $0 spend limit
findings.detail: Verified 2026-10-22 (official offer page ms-azr-0144p + Learn doc 'About the Azure for Students Starter program'). A second, lighter Azure student path — the same free/students page says 'Try Azure for Students or Azure for Students Starter — no credit card required.' Gives a verified K-12 (secondary/high-school) student free-tier access with a $0 spending limit to: Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Azure Notification Hubs, Azure Database for MySQL (in-app), Application Insights (Azure Monitor), and Azure DevOps. No commitment or time limit stated on the offer page; one subscription per eligible customer; not transferable; can't be combined with other offers; not for MOOCs/for-profit training; upgrade to Pay-As-You-Go at any time for the full catalog. (A Russian-localized Learn copy says the sub lasts a year and must be renewed — the en-US offer page governs: no time limit.)
findings.eligibility: Verified K-12 students; affirm age 13+ if residing in the US, 16+ if residing elsewhere; verify academic status through your organization's email (or Shibboleth where supported); no credit card.
findings.claim: Enroll at the Azure for Students Starter offer page (azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/offers/ms-azr-0144p, linked from the 'Choose the right Azure account' section of azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students) → verify with school email/Shibboleth → account starts with a $0 spend limit; upgrade in the Azure portal to PAYG when you need more.
findings.expiry: Offer page: no commitment or time limit. Upgrade path: Pay-As-You-Go anytime.
findings.gotchas: $0 spending limit means you can ONLY use the free tiers of the listed services — everything else is blocked, not billed; limited to six service families (no VMs, no OpenAI models, no credits); one per customer; prior Azure trial on the same identity blocks signup.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups, self-service track: $1,000 Azure credits instantly (90 days), up to $5,000 (180 days) after business verification
findings.detail: Materially changed in 2025-2026. As of 2026-10-22, the 'Azure for Startups' card on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students (fetched today) states: $1,000 in Azure credits instantly, no application required; unlock up to $5,000 in total credits with business verification; credits valid 90 days (initial) and 180 days (post-verification); full Azure catalog up to credit limits; 'spending protection — credit card required only for identity verification and services beyond credit'; no upfront commitment, cancel anytime, moves to pay-as-you-go after credits expire. This replaced the old Founders Hub on July 1, 2025. As of June 2026 (official MS blog + Learn overview, updated 2026-08-05): the program is now single-path — apply at startups.microsoft.com, start building immediately with Startup credits while eligibility is verified, and 'unlock up to $150K in Startup credits over time' based on verified progress, service adoption, and sustained Azure usage; applications typically reviewed in 3 business days; LLM/AI access is via Microsoft Foundry (GPT-4-class models, 1,700+ foundation models).
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only; privately held, for-profit company developing a software-based product it owns; headquartered in a country where Azure is available; NOT an educational institution/government/consultancy/agency; no cryptocurrency mining; NOT raised Series C funding or later; NOT previously received more than $350,000 lifetime free Azure credits (updated cap; the legacy Founders Hub signup page still shows a $10,000 cap — the current Learn doc governs). A credit card is required (unlike the student offers) — only for identity verification and for any services/usage beyond the credits.
findings.claim: Sign up at startups.microsoft.com ('Get started') — the $1,000 is granted instantly with no application/verification wait; complete the business-verification checklist to unlock the remaining $4,000 (credits then valid 180 days); enter an Investor Network referral code during application if you have one. Manage/activate credits and benefits in the Azure Portal. After credits expire you move to pay-as-you-go; cancel anytime.
findings.expiry: $1,000 valid 90 days from sign-up; $5,000 tier valid 180 days from verification. No renewals; expiration converts the sub to PAYG. June 2026 change: further credits up to $150K are unlocked incrementally 'over time' based on service adoption/sustained usage (not a fixed grant).
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required here (identity verification) — unlike the student offers; no dedicated technical support on the self-service track (that's the Investor-Network benefit); the 90/180-day windows are short — if you can't burn $5k in 6 months the account flips to PAYG; Microsoft can change/terminate the offer (as it did on 2025-07-01 with little notice); legacy Founders-Hub 'levels' (Expert/Champion Networks) no longer exist.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups, Investor Network track: referral-gated, $100,000+ Azure credits + dedicated Microsoft point of contact
findings.detail: Per the July 1, 2025 restructuring (The Register/TechRadar coverage + official blog) and the June 2, 2026 official blog: startups referred by a Microsoft for Startups Investor Network partner (a select group of VCs, accelerators, and universities) enter a 'higher touch' track that 'starts with $100,000 in Azure credits' (press figures; the official Learn overview describes it less precisely as 'higher-value benefits earlier', 'additional Startup credits, expanded support, and third-party benefits'). Includes dedicated Microsoft POC, deeper Microsoft Marketplace and co-sell support, and invitation-only Pegasus program (dedicated Cloud Solutions Architect) which Microsoft explicitly kept unchanged. The old Founders Hub tiers up to $150K and the Expert/Champion Networks were retired; existing activated legacy credits stayed valid until their expiry, then auto-converted to PAYG.
findings.eligibility: Startup must be tied to an Investor Network-affiliated VC/accelerator/university that issues you a referral code, entered during the startups.microsoft.com application; same company-level eligibility as the self-service track (private, for-profit, software product, no Series C+, HQ in an Azure region).
findings.claim: Get the referral code from your investor/accelerator partner → apply at startups.microsoft.com and enter the code → you are routed to the enhanced track instead of the $1,000/$5,000 self-serve ramp.
findings.expiry: Credit validity follows program terms (legacy $100K-tier grants were ~180-day windows per level; new grants track the 'credits over time' model). Pegasus is invitation-only and ongoing.
findings.gotchas: The exact $100,000 figure is from press, not the current official Learn page (which I fetched today) — treat as 'about $100K+'; no funding-amount cap like AWS Activate, but the Series C+ and $350K lifetime-free-credit caps disqualify most well-funded companies; if your legacy Founders Hub credits expired without investor affiliation, your sub already converted to PAYG.

findings.name: Azure Free account (also open to students without .edu verification): $200 credit for 30 days + 12-month and always-free services
findings.detail: Verified 2026-10-22 on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/. For any new Azure customer (incl. students who don't have a qualifying school email): $200 credit usable within 30 days; free amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months (750 h/mo B1s + B2pts v2 Arm + B2ats v2 AMD VMs; Azure SQL serverless 100,000 vCore-sec/mo + 32 GB; PostgreSQL & MySQL Flexible 750 h/mo B1MS + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup; Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB; Container Registry Standard 100 GB; SQL Managed Instance 720 vCore-h + 64 GB data + 64 GB backup; Vision 5,000 txns/tier) plus 65+ always-free services (DevOps 5 users, Functions 1M requests, App Service 10 apps/1 GB/1 h-day, Static Web Apps 100 GB bandwidth, Cosmos/DocumentDB 32 GB, IoT Hub 8,000 msg/day, Logic Apps 4,000 actions, Notification Hubs 1M, AI Search 50 MB/10k docs/3 indexes, Document Intelligence 500 pages S0, Translator 2M chars, Content Safety 5,000 records, Speech 0.5M neural chars/mo, Container Apps 180k vCPU-s/360k GiB-s/2M reqs, API Mgmt 1M calls/mo, Azure Maps 1,000–5,000 txns, AKS management free). LLM/AI: Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Foundry models accessible with the $200 (or student $100); the OpenAI 'free trial' token allowances (historically ~1,000 gpt-4o-mini tokens/day, 40k/mo, ~3 months; 50/day gpt-4o, o1, gpt-4; 500/day gpt-3.5-turbo) could not be re-verified today because the pricing tables render via JS and returned placeholders — treat exact token figures as unconfirmed. One free-credit account per person; not available in US Gov/China/Germany sovereign clouds.
findings.eligibility: Any NEW Azure customer (students, startups, individuals). Requires a phone number + a credit/debit card (non-prepaid) — card used for identity verification with a small reversed authorization hold; in Hong Kong and Brazil only credit cards are accepted; billing country must be in the supported list (~140 countries/regions). A startup on this path uses the $200 trial PLUS the $1,000→$5,000 Startup credits on a separate offer.
findings.claim: azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/ → 'Try Azure for free' → sign in with Microsoft or GitHub account → enter phone + card → $200 credit and free tiers activate immediately. After 30 days, if you don't convert to PAYG, the account is disabled (unused credit is kept only if you convert early).
findings.expiry: $200 credit: 30 days. 12-month free amounts: 12 months from sign-up, then billed at PAYG. Always-free services: ongoing, no expiry. No renewals.
findings.gotchas: This is the one Azure offer that REQUIRES a credit card — students without .edu can't use it card-free; data egress (internet outbound), inbound-to-public-IP traffic, and any meter beyond the listed free amounts are charged against the $200 and then PAYG; '12-month free' services that are 'always free' are different products — check the Free/Are-You-Aware tabs on each pricing page; sovereign-cloud regions excluded; one per person.

findings.name: LLM & AI free tiers inside Azure (Microsoft Foundry / Azure AI services) — what students and everyone get at no cost
findings.detail: From the official student/free pages fetched 2026-10-22: always-free (all customers, no CC): Azure Speech in Foundry Tools 0.5M neural characters/month; Azure AI Search 50 MB storage / 10,000 docs / 3 indexes per service; Azure Document Intelligence 500 pages S0 tier; Translator 2M characters; Content Safety 5,000 text records or images; Machine Learning 'Free' (no meter); Azure Maps 1,000–5,000 transactions; IoT 8,000 msgs/day. 12-month (new customers): Azure Vision 5,000 transactions each S1/S2/S3. Students additionally get: 'access to industry-leading technology like Azure OpenAI' and 1,700+ foundation models (Microsoft, OpenAI, Hugging Face, Meta, Cohere, incl. Phi small language models) via Microsoft Foundry, billed to their $100 student credit or free quotas; the 'try Azure OpenAI' free-trial token quotas (e.g., gpt-4o-mini 1,000 tokens/day / 40,000/mo for 3 months; 50/day for gpt-4o, o1, gpt-4; 500/day gpt-3.5-turbo) are the long-standing published numbers but I could not re-confirm today (JS-rendered pricing tables returned '$–' placeholders), so treat per-model token quotas as possibly stale. Notably the 2026 pages rebrand Azure AI services as 'Microsoft Foundry'/'Foundry Tools'.
findings.eligibility: Always-free tiers: any Azure customer, no credit card. 12-month quotas: new Azure customers. Azure OpenAI models on the student offer: valid Azure for Students subscription (no CC) with access requests/approval per model — access to some frontier models still requires an OpenAI access application stating use case.
findings.claim: Student: sign up for Azure for Students (no CC) → deploy AI resources (Foundry/OpenAI, Speech, AI Search) and stay within free quotas; anything above quotas deducts from the $100. Startup/general: $200 free account or $1,000 Startup credits cover model usage; Foundry Playground offers free trial model calls for experimentation.
findings.expiry: Always-free quotas: ongoing monthly allowances. 12-month quotas: end at 12 months. OpenAI free-trial tokens: historically 3 months from account creation (unconfirmed for 2026-10).
findings.gotchas: Token-based LLM pricing means the $100/$1,000 credits burn quickly on frontier models (o-series and GPT-6 'Sol/Luna' tiers are the expensive end of the catalog); free-tier F0 quotas per-minute/per-day limits apply; credits can't be used on Marketplace; 'always free' does NOT cover premium tiers of the same service (e.g., Content Safety S1+, Vision S4+); check per-service 'Free' vs 'Are you aware' pricing tabs; egress/data-transfer for media responses is a separate meter.

findings.name: Managed databases & data-platform free tiers (usable by students; the 'free tier' front)
findings.detail: Verified 2026-10-22 on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/. Managed-database offers: (always free, all customers) Azure SQL Database serverless 100,000 vCore-seconds/month + 32 GB storage; Azure Cosmos DB dedicated 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB/month free for 12 months then continues as 'Free' tier with 2 free GB storage + 500 RU/s for all customers; DocumentDB dedicated MongoDB cluster 32 GB; Database Migration Service free Standard compute; Azure Data Catalog unlimited users; Data Factory 5 low-frequency activities; Data Explorer free; Query Store free. (12 months, new customers) Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server 750 h B1MS + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup; Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server same; SQL Managed Instance 720 vCore-hours (4 or 8 vCore General Purpose) + 64 GB data + 64 GB backup; Azure SQL Database 750 h B5m/baseline + 100 vCore-min burstable. Free backup: 7 days for SQL DB/Managed Instance. These are the main free managed-database options; no CC needed for the student offer that bundles them.
findings.eligibility: Always-free database tiers: any Azure customer, no CC. 12-month amounts: new Azure customers only (students get them via the no-CC Azure for Students offer; startups via $1,000→$5,000 Startup credits; everyone else via the $200 CC-required free account).
findings.claim: With a no-CC Azure for Students subscription, deploy PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server B1MS or the SQL serverless database directly from the portal within the free amounts — no card, no charge until you exceed them; students can use up to the $100 credit for overflow.
findings.expiry: Always-free: ongoing (Cosmos free tier is a permanent tier, not 12-month). 12-month amounts: end at 12 months then PAYG. Post-12-month Cosmos DB falls to the permanent free 500 RU/s + 2 GB tier, not deletion.
findings.gotchas: Free amounts are per-service per-region; backup storage beyond the free 32 GB is billed; egress from VMs/DBs to internet is a separate meter not in the free quota; 'always free' for Cosmos ≠ unlimited — writes beyond 25 GB are blocked or billed; PostgreSQL/MySQL free 750 h is instance-hours (one B1MS instance, 24/7), not multiple; AKS cluster management is free but node VMs and disk are billed; free SQL serverless is capped at 4 vCore serverless pools.

findings.name: Education licenses: Visual Studio Dev Essentials (student dev subscription; the VS Pro question)
findings.detail: Per vs-azure-eligibility (learn.microsoft.com, fetched 2026-10-22) and university IT pages: Visual Studio subscriptions carry individual Azure Dev/Test credits (Pro $50/mo, Enterprise $150/mo) usable without a payment method; 'Visual Studio Enterprise – Azure Dev Tools for Teaching' no longer exists. Dev Essentials (the successor to the free 'Microsoft Imagine' dev subscription) offers students a Premium tier that bundles up to $200/month Azure credit, Visual Studio Enterprise access, and 10,000 Azure hours of training/tools — students qualify via GitHub/education verification (the exact Premium grant figures come from a university IT mirror, low confidence; official visualstudio.com page returned 404 today). This is how students today get 'Visual Studio Pro/Enterprise-class' IDE licenses for 12 months — NOT via Azure for Students, whose bundled software list is Visual Studio Community/Code (Pro/Enterprise are not in the Azure-for-Students benefit set after the 2025 Dev Tools for Teaching sunset).
findings.eligibility: Verified students (or individual developers for Basic tier) — students get the Premium Dev Essentials subscription at no cost via education verification; Basic tier is free to everyone with a Microsoft account.
findings.claim: Sign in at my.visualstudio.com / visualstudio.microsoft.com with a verified student email or GitHub account claiming the student benefit → Dev Essentials Premium activates, including the monthly Azure Dev/Test credit; renew annually while still a student.
findings.expiry: Monthly Azure credits renew while the subscription is active (VS subs: renewable, per the eligibility table). GitHub Student Developer Pack route (not Azure, adjacent offer) also grants 12 months of Visual Studio Pro/Enterprise-class licenses plus OpenAI credits — the likely origin of the '12 months of Visual Studio Pro' figure in the known-so-far notes.
findings.gotchas: The $200/mo Dev Essentials Azure credit figure is third-party-cited (university IT mirror) and could not be confirmed on the official page today (404) — verify before relying on it; Dev Essentials Basic has no Azure credits; credits stop automatically when the monthly amount is used (no CC on file = auto-stop); 'Pro' IDE via GitHub pack is not an Azure offer and its terms/eligibility are GitHub's.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 program changes (verified via press + official MS pages): (1) July 1, 2025 — Microsoft for Startups restructure: the Founders Hub four-tier model (up to $150,000 in Azure credits, applied for with a validated business plan) was RETIRED, as were the 'Founders Hub' label, the Expert Network, and the Champion Network. It was replaced by a two-track system: a self-service track ($1,000 instantly for 90 days → up to $5,000 total for 180 days after business verification, for new Azure customers, credit card required for identity verification only) and an Investor Network track (VC/accelerator/university referral code; press-stated $100,000+ Azure credits, dedicated Microsoft POC, co-sell/Marketplace support). Pegasus (invitation-only dedicated Cloud Solutions Architect) was explicitly unchanged. Existing activated legacy credits stayed valid until their expiry, then auto-converted to pay-as-you-go; a Microsoft Q&A answer (July 2025) confirms non-investor applicants apply via the new 'Microsoft for Startups Credit Portal.' (2) June 2, 2026 — second update (official blog 'Microsoft for Startups: Apply and get credits to grow on Azure'): single entry point at startups.microsoft.com; startups 'start building immediately with Startup credits'; the up-to-$150,000 ceiling was RESTORED but now unlocked incrementally 'over time based on service adoption and sustained Azure usage and verified progress' rather than as a one-time grant; Investor Network partners unlock 'additional Startup credits, expanded support, and third-party benefits' earlier; current eligibility caps: not more than $350,000 lifetime free Azure credits, no Series C funding or later, private for-profit, HQ in an Azure region, no crypto mining; applications reviewed in ~3 business days (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/startups/microsoft-for-startups/overview, page updated 2026-08-05). (3) August 2025 — Azure Dev Tools for Teaching (successor to Microsoft Imagine) was DISCONTINUED: access disabled effective ~Aug 7-15, 2025; no new administrator signups after Aug 15, 2025; Microsoft provided NO direct replacement for educators — students' dev-tool benefits (incl. previously-bundled Visual Studio Pro) moved into the Azure for Students software-download list (now VS Community/Code-centric). Already-installed software keeps working. This is why the '12 months of Visual Studio Pro' line from the known-so-far notes no longer maps to any current Azure student offer (Pro/Enterprise IDE now comes via GitHub Student Developer Pack or Visual Studio Dev Essentials Premium). (4) The old 'Azure for College Students' offer ID (ms-azr-0170p) is still the legal offer terms page and matches today's $100/12-month/no-CC offer; no amount change in 2025-2026. (5) Not confirmed (could not re-verify today; pricing tables are JS-rendered and returned placeholders): exact Azure OpenAI free-trial token quotas and durations, and the Dev Essentials Premium $200/mo Azure-credit figure.

findings.claim: 1) Sign in at aistudio.google.com with a Google account; 2) select/create an active GCP project; 3) an API key is auto-provisioned and the Free tier applies automatically — nothing to enable. To upgrade later: link a billing account and prepay a minimum of $5 (new 2026 paid flow).
findings.detail: Free input AND output tokens, no billing account or credit card required. New accounts start on the Free tier automatically; qualification = an active GCP project or free trial, no spend-based cap. Free-tier models (official pricing page, fetched 2026-10-22): Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3 Flash Preview, Gemini 3.5 & 3.1 Flash-Lite (all service tiers), Live/audio models (3.8 Live, 3.5 Transcribe, 2.5 Flash Native Audio), TTS (3.8 Flash TTS, 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, 2.5 TTS previews), Gemini Embedding 2 (Standard tier only), Gemma 4 (all capabilities incl. tuning), and Robotics ER 2 previews. Context caching free on 3.8/3.6 Flash and Gemma 4. Limits are per-project RPM/TPM/RPD (RPD resets midnight Pacific); the docs no longer publish static per-model numbers — exact quotas are shown live in the AI Studio dashboard for your project. Free tier is indefinite, no renewal mechanism.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Google account + an active Google Cloud project; no billing account, no card, no .edu, no startup status. Region: Gemini API availability is limited to Google's supported-countries list (list not re-verified today).
findings.expiry: No expiry/renewal — free tier is permanent; per-model quotas are live in AI Studio. Note: free tier is 'limited access to certain models' — Pro/image/video models are NOT free-tier eligible.
findings.gotchas: Free-tier prompts and responses ARE used by Google to improve products (only paid tiers, except invite-only Contributor, exclude your data from product use). Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 4 Argon, Omni Flash, 3 Pro Image, Nano Banana 2/2.1/Lite, 2.5 Pro, Veo 3.1, Lyria 3.x are NOT free-tier eligible. 2.5-generation models are access-restricted to prior active users; new projects are told to use 3.5 Flash-Lite or 3.8 Flash. Static per-model RPM/TPM/RPD figures were removed from the docs — verify quotas in AI Studio. Model lineup churns fast (see deprecations).
findings.name: Gemini API Free Tier (Google AI Studio)
findings.source_url: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (free-tier model list, caching, deprecations); https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/billing (no billing required for Free tier, $5 prepay for paid tiers); https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits (limits are per-project, view in AI Studio)

findings.claim: 1) Go to cloud.google.com/free; 2) sign up for Google Cloud and add a payment method; 3) the $300 credit is granted automatically to the new billing account — no coupon. Use it on Vertex AI/Gemini workloads; the separate always-free tiers apply on top.
findings.detail: $300 USD of free GCP credit for new customers ('You won't be charged until you activate your full paid account') — usable for Vertex AI / Gemini model calls, AI app building, agents. Separately: 20+ products with always-free monthly limits (e.g. 1 e2-micro VM, 5 GB Cloud Storage, BigQuery monthly quota, 'AI APIs' free usage) that do not draw from the $300 and never expire ('the free usage limit does not expire, but is subject to change'). Also listed on the same page: GKE full-capability 90-day trial, Cloud SQL 30-day trial (8 vCPU Enterprise Plus instance, 64 GB RAM, 100 GB storage), and a 30-day free trial of Gemini Enterprise Plus (the agentic enterprise platform). Core terms read from the page today (high); exact card requirement and 90-day credit duration live in the sign-up flow (medium sub-parts, flagged in gotchas).
findings.eligibility: New Google Cloud customers only (one trial per person; household/organizational duplicates are detected and denied). A payment method is required at sign-up (card/PayPal; standard verification hold) — unlike the Gemini API free tier this one DOES need a card. Trial duration for the $300 credit is not stated on the marketing page (historically ~90 days; verify in the sign-up flow).
findings.expiry: Credit expires at end of trial window if unused (duration stated in sign-up flow); always-free tiers: no expiry, subject to change. No auto-renewal — continuing requires activating a paid account.
findings.gotchas: Card required (vs. zero-card Gemini API free tier). GCP Marketplace third-party SKUs excluded from credit. After trial end, if a payment method is on file and you continue using billable services, you will be charged — cancel or switch the account if you don't want that. The $300 credit covers GCP/Vertex AI charges; it is a different entitlement from the free Gemini API (ai.google.dev) tier.
findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial — $300 credit for new customers
findings.source_url: https://cloud.google.com/free (credit amount, 'not charged until you activate your full paid account', 20+ free-tier products, GKE/Cloud SQL/Gemini Enterprise Plus trials — page fetched 2026-10-22)

findings.claim: 1) Apply at cloud.google.com/startups ('Apply now' form: company info, funding stage, accelerator affiliations, use case); 2) acceptance/rejection email typically within 5–7 days (10+ if info missing); 3) credits provisioned to your GCP project on acceptance; the Workspace Business Plus and Maps credits are separate application items ('Separate application required').
findings.detail: Rebranded/expanded program: up to $200,000 USD in GCP credits (up to $350,000 for AI startups) over two years, plus credits for frontier models (Gemini, Gemma), 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no extra cost, monthly Google Maps Platform credits, dedicated technical support, and accelerator residencies. Tier structure (official FAQ): 'Start ($2k)' tier = $2,000 credits, for startups founded in the past 2 years with a working MVP, a clear business model, and plans to seek venture funding. Funded tiers 'Scale' and 'Scale AI' = $200K–$350K credits, for startups with VERIFIABLE Pre-Seed to Series A funding. Credit mechanics (footnote on the page): AI startups get Year 1 100% coverage up to $250,000 + Year 2 20% coverage up to an additional $100,000; non-AI startups Year 1 100% up to $100,000 + Year 2 20% up to an additional $100,000. Targeted at 'new Google Cloud customers founding digital-native products'.
findings.eligibility: For-profit startup, digital-native product, new Google Cloud customer. Excluded: companies that have IPO'd or been acquired, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content, dev shops, consultancies/agencies, cryptocurrency mining, direct competitors/resellers of GCP. Scale/Scale AI tiers: venture funding must be verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A; non-VC funding (private equity, bank loans, government grants, crowdfunding, friends & family) does NOT qualify for Scale — such startups 'may be evaluated for other program tiers' (i.e., typically the $2,000 Start tier). No hard dollar funding cap stated; stage cap is Series A. Stealth/unfunded founders must wait until product launch and need a working website. Company domain must not have had a paid Google Workspace plan within 31 days of applying. Acceptance at sole discretion of Google Cloud.
findings.expiry: Two-year program: Year 1 = 100% of eligible spend up to cap ($250K AI / $100K non-AI); Year 2 = 20% of additional spend up to +$100K. No renewal; alumni can re-apply after completion.
findings.gotchas: Year-2 credits are 20% coverage, not 100% — the 'up to $350K' assumes heavy Year-2 eligible spend. Third-party (non-Google) models are billed directly and NOT covered by program credits. Bootstrapped/self-funded startups realistically get only the $2,000 Start tier without verifiable VC money. The '5–7 days' decision clock is typical, not guaranteed.
findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program (startups)
findings.source_url: https://cloud.google.com/startups (tiers, credit amounts, Y1/Y2 mechanics, exclusions, FAQ — page fetched 2026-10-22); program also advertised at https://cloud.google.com/free

findings.claim: 1) Apply via the form at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research (institutional email, project details, grant ID, funding plan for after the 1-year credit expiry); 2) on approval, redeem the coupon in the Google Cloud console (billing account required); 3) activate within 60 days of project start.
findings.detail: GCP research credits to advance academic work. Amount advertised: 'Apply for up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits' (researcher card on the Google Cloud for Education hub). Formal terms on the application page: 'Credit awards must be activated within 60 days of the project start date indicated in the application form. Credit awards expire 365 days from the coupon redemption date, or when the credit amount has been fully used, whichever comes first.' Credits 'do not have commercial value and may not be sold or bartered.' A GCP billing account is required to use the credits.
findings.eligibility: Limited to faculty, PhD students, and postdoctoral researchers at accredited higher-education institutions and eligible nonprofit research institutions in APPROVED COUNTRIES (region-limited). Institutional email account required; .edu is the typical but not only qualifying domain (nonprofit research institutions also qualify).
findings.expiry: Credits: 365 days from coupon redemption or full use, whichever first; must activate within 60 days of project start. No auto-renewal — reapply for new projects/years.
findings.gotchas: Requires a GCP billing account (payment method on file), so it is NOT zero-card like the Gemini API free tier. Not for teaching — separate 'Teaching Credits' program. 'Approved countries' restriction may exclude some regions. Credits are research-only, not transferable/sellable.
findings.name: Google Cloud Research Credits ('Academic Research Grants') — up to $5,000
findings.source_url: https://edu.google.com/programs/credits/research/ (eligibility + redemption terms, fetched 2026-10-22); https://cloud.google.com/edu ('Apply for up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits')

findings.claim: 1) Faculty apply via the form at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching (institution + 1–3 courses with start dates); 2) on approval, students use the GCP credits for course work; 3) review the program FAQ on the page for current amounts.
findings.detail: GCP credits for faculty to give students hands-on cloud experience: 'Apply for GCP credits for you and your students to give them real, hands-on experience with Google Cloud Platform. It is the intent of the program that the credits are used by students to learn about how to use the cloud.' Application covers 1–3 courses per entry (different courses/time periods listed separately); form captures institution, department, course name, expected course start date, and a link to your school's faculty directory profile. Program is advertised alongside 'up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits' on the Google Cloud for Education hub; the exact per-course credit amount is not printed on the application page (hence medium confidence).
findings.eligibility: Faculty ONLY ('Eligibility is limited to faculty only. If you are a student, you can encourage your faculty members to apply for your next course.') Requires an academic institution (US states list on the form; international institutions via the academic-institution field).
findings.expiry: Per program terms (not printed on the fetched page; typically tied to the course term — confirm in the FAQ). No auto-renewal; reapply each course/year.
findings.gotchas: Students cannot apply for themselves — the faculty member must apply. Credits are intended for learning use only. Amount is not stated on the application page, unlike the research program's 'up to $5,000'.
findings.name: Google Cloud Teaching Credits (faculty)
findings.source_url: https://edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching/ (form + faculty-only rule, fetched 2026-10-22); https://cloud.google.com/edu ('Apply for free Google Cloud credits', 'up to $5,000' program figure)

findings.claim: 1) Institution signs up for Google for Education Fundamentals (free, edu.google.com) even if another suite is primary, and admin enables ONLY the Gemini app; 2) or it is already bundled in a Workspace for Education license; 3) educators/students sign in with their school Google account to gemini.google.com / Gemini mobile app.
findings.detail: Google's education-license front: 'Gemini for Education' — Gemini (premium Gemini 2.5 Pro with LearnLM 'world's leading model for learning' claims) delivered free of charge to educators, students, and staff: 'Your institution can get Gemini for Education at no cost by signing up for Google for Education Fundamentals, even if you use a different primary productivity suite,' and 'Gemini for Education is also included in all Google Workspace for Education editions free of charge.' Included in the free offering: default access to premium AI models 'with significantly higher limits than what consumers get at no cost,' limited-access Deep Research, custom Gems ('AI experts' per topic), Gemini Canvas, Gemini Live, Gemini Notebook (documents-to-podcasts), enterprise-grade data protection — 'Data is not human reviewed or used to train AI models' (Core Service under Workspace for Education terms).
findings.eligibility: K-12 and higher-education institutions (school/university domain; 'Google for Education Fundamentals' sign-up, or any Google Workspace for Education edition). Not an individual-offering — the institution signs up and admins enable the Gemini app. No payment method required. The upsell 'Google AI Pro for Education' (expanded premium-model access + full Gemini across Workspace apps, Gmail/Meet/Docs) is a paid add-on, contact-sales pricing.
findings.expiry: Not a credit — it persists as long as the (free) GFE Fundamentals membership or the institution's Workspace for Education license is active; annual license renewal applies to paid GWE editions. No separate renewal for the free app.
findings.gotchas: Free tier is 'limited access' to Deep Research vs. the paid Google AI Pro for Education add-on (expanded limits + full in-Workspace Gemini). Consumer 'Gemini Free' at gemini.google.com is a separate, lower-limited product — the education version needs the institutional sign-up. Admin-managed: usage/rollout is controlled by school IT. LearnLM claims are Google marketing, not benchmarks.
findings.name: Gemini for Education (free education AI license)

provider: Google — Gemini API (AI Studio) free tier + Google Cloud trial/education/startup programs
sunset_notes: WebSearch was unavailable for this agent (shared session budget exhausted); all findings above were read directly from official Google pages fetched 2026-10-22 (cloud.google.com/startups, cloud.google.com/free, cloud.google.com/edu, ai.google.dev pricing/billing/rate-limits/deprecations, edu.google.com credits pages), so 'high' confidence means the page was read today. Year-2 credits are only 20% coverage up to +$100K. (2) Gemini API free-tier model lineup churn: official deprecation page (last updated 2026-10-20) — Gemini 2.0 Flash & 2.0 Flash-Lite shut down Jun 1, 2026; 3.1 Flash-Lite Preview May 25, 2026; 3 Pro Preview Mar 9, 2026; 2.5 Pro previews Dec 2, 2025; Imagen 4 Aug 17, 2026; Veo 3.1 & Omni Flash Preview shut down Oct 22, 2026 (today); 2.5 Flash Image stable Mar 15, 2027; 3.1 Flash-Lite stable May 7, 2027; text-embedding-004 Jan 14, 2026 (→ Gemini Embedding 2). 2.5-generation models are access-restricted to prior active users with no announced shutdown. (3) Docs no longer publish static free-tier RPM/TPM/RPD — quotas are per-project and shown live in the AI Studio dashboard only.
