provider: Oracle — Startup Cloud-Credit Programs (VC / Accelerator Funded)

findings.name: Oracle Startup Growth Engine — OCI credits (LatAm startup program)
findings.detail: Up to US$60,000 in Oracle Cloud Infrastructure credits; program rules allow US$5,000–US$100,000 at Oracle's discretion, for VC/accelerator-backed, high-growth startups with a validated product. Launched June 2026 for Brazil, Argentina, Colombia with LatAm expansion planned. NOT verifiable today on public oracle.com pages: the global (oracle.com/cloud/oracle-for-startups/), LatAm, and Brazil startup pages read on 2026-10-22 contain no Growth Engine, credit-amount, VC/accelerator, or application content — they are generic 'cloud for startups' landing pages. The program front is likely a gated/partner portal.
findings.eligibility: VC- or accelerator-funded high-growth startup with a validated product; LatAm at launch (Brazil/Argentina/Colombia); no .edu requirement; no published startup-age or funding-cap figure on any public page read today.
findings.claim: VC/accelerator partner nominates portfolio startup → startup applies through the program front (Startup Cloud-Credit Programs, VC/Accelerator Funded) → Oracle reviews product validation → credits awarded at Oracle's discretion (US$5k–US$100k band, up to US$60k) and applied to an OCI tenancy; spend on eligible OCI services.
findings.expiry: Not published on any public page read today; credit-consumption window unverified.
findings.gotchas: As of 2026-10-22 the program has zero public footprint on oracle.com global/LatAm/BR startup pages (all checked today) — expect partner/VC-gated application, not self-serve signup; award size is discretionary; these credits are separate from and in addition to the US$300 free-tier trial; WebSearch was unavailable this session, so no independent announcement could be located.

findings.name: OCI Free Trial — US$300 credits / 30 days
findings.detail: US$300 of free credit usable on all eligible OCI services for up to 30 days; consumption at discounted IaaS-equivalent rates during the 30-day promo; ends when credits are exhausted or 30 days elapse, whichever comes first; unused credits automatically expire. One trial per person. 'Oracle Cloud Promotion' is Oracle's alias for this same Free Trial.
findings.eligibility: Anyone signing up for an OCI account (FAQ explicitly names students, academics, developers, startup founders); no .edu requirement; available in all regions where commercial OCI is offered, but the US$300 credit is 'available in select countries' per the official footnote; credit or debit card (credit-like) IS required at signup.
findings.claim: Sign up via signup.cloud.oracle.com (linked as 'Sign Up for Free Cloud Tier' from oracle.com/cloud/free/) → provide contact + card info for identity verification → tenancy created with US$300/30-day credit → optionally upgrade to Pay As You Go at any time via Console Account Management.
findings.expiry: 30 days or credit exhaustion; then a 30-day grace period to upgrade, after which trial (paid) resources and data are permanently reclaimed/deleted; Oracle sales reps can extend trials or add credits on request; upgrade during trial defers billing until credits/30 days run out; no downgrade after upgrading.
findings.gotchas: CC required — 'credit card NOT required' is false for this offer; virtual/single-use/prepaid and PIN debit cards are rejected; Oracle may place temporary authorization holds (3–5 days, no charge); no SLAs; only 'limited support' during trial — full support requires paid upgrade; paid instances created during trial are reclaimed when trial ends; some special trial offers suspend the account immediately after expiry (30-day suspension, then account deletion); multiple free accounts prohibited; idle 30+ days risks suspension.

findings.name: OCI Always Free services — unlimited duration (incl. for students)
findings.detail: Unlimited-time Always Free services (per official FAQ read today): HeatWave, AMD-based Compute, Ampere A1 Arm-based Compute, Block Volume, Object Storage, Archive Storage, Flexible + Flexible Network Load Balancer, Site-to-Site VPN/VPN Connect, Autonomous Data Warehouse/Transaction Processing/JSON Database, NoSQL Database (Phoenix region only), APEX, Resource Manager (Terraform), Monitoring, Notifications, Logging, APM, Service Connector Hub, Vault, Bastions, Security Advisor, VCNs, Content Management Starter Edition, Email Delivery. Numeric limits published on Oracle's LatAm OCI landing page (read today): 2 Autonomous AI Database instances of 20GB each; AMD and Arm compute VMs; 200GB total block storage; 10GB object storage; 10TB/month egress. Global free/FAQ page does not print per-service OCPU/RAM caps today ('Some limitations apply').
findings.eligibility: Anyone, explicitly including students and academics (one account per person); no .edu required; card required at signup (identity verification); NoSQL free only in Phoenix region.
findings.claim: Sign up for the same Free Tier (signup.cloud.oracle.com) → Always Free resources usable immediately and independently of trial credits → keep them after trial ends by staying within tenancy limits.
findings.expiry: No expiry for in-limit Always Free resources ('unlimited time'); tenancy subject to abandoned-account rules (idle 30+ days may be suspended); new Always Free services are added automatically.
findings.gotchas: The 10GB object-storage / 10TB egress / 200GB block figures come from the LatAm landing page while the global free page omits numbers — verify per region before relying on them; if you provision more Ampere A1 instances than the Always Free tenancy allows, ALL existing Ampere instances are disabled and then deleted 30 days post-trial unless you upgrade; data egress beyond the free monthly amount and anything outside Always Free limits is billable; no SLA/support on Always Free (community forums only); capacity estimates can sell out ('out of host capacity' errors); Always Free status is not transferable between resources.

findings.name: Oracle University free training & accreditation (education offer)
findings.detail: Oracle University (oracle.com/education, read today): 'Start learning for free' — free entry-level 'Foundations' training and certifications across Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications, and AI; free Oracle University Learning Community (3.5M+ learners); free hands-on labs that run in free lab environments or in Oracle Cloud free mode; Oracle MyLearn AI-personalized learning. This is a training/accreditation offer, not cloud credits or a software license.
findings.eligibility: Open to individuals and organizations; no .edu requirement stated on the page; no fee for the free Foundations tracks.
findings.claim: Go to oracle.com/education → 'Start learning for free' / 'Explore free training and certifications' → join the Learning Community → complete free Foundations courses/accreditations; run free labs in Oracle-provided free lab environments or your free-tier tenancy.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated; free training catalog appears ongoing.
findings.gotchas: Advanced role-based tracks and the Oracle Unlimited Learning Subscription are paid; free training does not include free cloud capacity (resources still count against Free Tier/trial limits).

sunset_notes: (1) Oracle Academy (oracle.com/academy) returns a 403 'Technical Issue | Oracle Academy' error page as of 2026-10-22 — the Academy program appears sunset or relocated; no education-license offer could be verified there. (2) oracle.com/cloud/free-trial/ now 404 — the trial lives under oracle.com/cloud/free/ (US$300/30-day confirmed on the free page and FAQ today; no amount/duration change observed vs. historical US$300/30-day terms). (3) No public mention of the 'Oracle Startup Growth Engine' (June 2026 LatAm launch) on the global, LatAm, or Brazil startup pages as of 2026-10-22 — no sunset observed, but the front is partner/VC-gated and unlocatable without web search. (4) Verification method: oracle.com blocks datacenter fetchers (HTTP 403 via WebFetch) and this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so all official pages were curl-fetched directly from this machine on 2026-10-22; 'high' confidence = official page read today. 2025–2026 change history beyond these pages could not be independently searched.

findings.name: Techstars accelerator investment: $220K day-one (APAC: $120K)
findings.detail: $220,000 invested at acceptance in most programs worldwide: $200,000 via uncapped MFN SAFE (no valuation cap, no discount; auto-adopts the lowest-cap or most-favorable terms of any SAFE issued between MFN start and the priced round) + $20,000 via post-money Convertible Equity Agreement (CEA) for 5% common stock (post-money, incl. existing option pool). Wired within 3 weeks of acceptance; offer issued 1-2 weeks after acceptance with standardized docs. Both instruments convert when the company closes a priced round of at least $1M. Asia-Pacific programs: $100K MFN SAFE + $20K CEA = $120K total. 'No fee (i.e., monetary cost) to join a Techstars accelerator program' — official. Total package advertised as $1.5M+ including credits. 3-month mentorship program; network access 'for the life of the company'.
findings.eligibility: Startups only (no .edu email or student requirement); idea-stage OK ('we've accepted companies with no more than an idea, and a dream') up to companies already holding $1M+ funding. Founded anywhere; must be legally present in program country during the 3-month program. Must be a US C-corp or foreign equivalent; companies incorporated in non-approved jurisdictions (e.g., India) need a 'flip' reorg first. Pre-Series A seed stage in practice. Applications via apply.techstars.com for a specific program; acceptance is competitive.
findings.claim: 1) Apply to a specific Techstars program at apply.techstars.com (application takes ~30 min). 2) On acceptance: upload pitch deck, answer questions; accelerator offer + MFN SAFE term sheet issued within 1-2 weeks. 3) Complete Techstars' checks (background, incorporation, ownership, IP, company bank account) — $20K wired as soon as checks pass; legal close of standardized MFN SAFE docs in <=3 weeks. 4) $220K wired to company account; partner cloud credits activated across AWS/DigitalOcean/Google platforms at the same step.
findings.expiry: SAFE + CEA have no expiry; they convert on the first priced round of $1M+. Ongoing side-letter shareholder relationship (pro-rata, digital-assets, drag-along rights; company must report key operating metrics and burn). Cloud/AI credits: 24 months per Techstars' capital page (see separate findings).
findings.gotchas: Not a grant: $20K is equity, $200K is a convertible instrument — Techstars' future ownership = 5% + SAFE conversion value (e.g., $200K converts to 1% extra on a $20M pre-money round per official example). Uncapped MFN means if you later issue a better-term SAFE (lower cap or 20% discount), Techstars automatically inherits it. Side letter imposes reporting and exit obligations. APAC deals are only $120K. $20K/5% is structured as a CEA (converts at the priced round), though the marketing /capital page describes it as '5% common stock for $20,000'.

findings.name: AWS Activate — Techstars portfolio tier: $100,000 AWS credits
findings.detail: $100,000 in AWS promotional credits over 24 months, 'PORTFOLIO' tier, per Techstars' official capital page (lists H100, SageMaker, EC2; infrastructure access). Zero equity taken by AWS. Techstars has been a long-standing AWS Activate Provider (a ~10-year partnership per Amazon). 2026 notes from AWS: Founders tier starts at $1,000; Portfolio tier can be up to $200,000 depending on provider; credits now redeemable on third-party models in Amazon Bedrock; new AWS accounts start on a Free plan that is NOT eligible for Activate credits (must be on Paid plan); eligibility = pre-Series B, founded within last 10 years, functioning website, business email on company domain, most recent funding round within 12 months.
findings.eligibility: Requires Techstars acceptance (or an AWS Activate Provider Org ID — each Org ID usable once, and AWS does the final approval above the $5K tier). No .edu email requirement. Global. Startup-stage constraint: pre-Series B per AWS rules.
findings.claim: For Techstars companies: nothing to do separately — credits are 'activated across all partner platforms' at the capital-wire step after acceptance (Step 3 of Techstars' capital deployment). Standalone: apply at the AWS Activate portal (aws.amazon.com/activate) with your provider's Organization ID; decision in 5-10 business days.
findings.expiry: 24 months from activation per Techstars' capital page (AWS generally states 1-2 year validity and now enforces expiry strictly with no extensions).
findings.gotchas: Credits are promotional dollars on a paid-plan AWS account — overage beyond the credits is billed; AWS Marketplace third-party software, Route 53 domain registrations, and some support tiers are excluded. Free-plan AWS accounts cannot receive Activate credits. The AWS Techstars partnership page (aws.amazon.com/startups/partnerships/techstars → startups.aws.com) returned 404 today, so the $100K/24-month figure rests on Techstars' own official page; AWS may grant less than $100K at its discretion (the partner 'recommends' a tier, AWS approves).

findings.name: DigitalOcean Startups — HATCH tier: $100,000 credits (2026 premier partner)
findings.detail: $100,000 in DigitalOcean infrastructure credits over 24 months, 'HATCH' tier, per Techstars' official capital page (lists H100 GPU access). DigitalOcean is a former Techstars portfolio company and was welcomed in March 2026 as a 2026 'Premier Partner': Techstars founders gain access to DO's Gradient AI Platform and the DO startup community. DO's own program is tiered (historically HATCH ~$100K / SPARK ~$25K, ~12 months, 1-2% equity on HATCH, 0% on SPARK); the Techstars deal line states 24 months.
findings.eligibility: Requires Techstars acceptance (or a qualifying accelerator/VC partner path). No .edu email requirement. Global. Early-stage startup.
findings.claim: For Techstars companies: no separate application — HATCH credits are activated at the same capital-deployment step as the AWS/Google credits after acceptance. Standalone: apply through the DigitalOcean Startups program with a partner reference.
findings.expiry: 24 months per Techstars' capital page (DO's standard tiers historically ~12 months — confirm current tier at claim time).
findings.gotchas: Credit-card-free access to DO itself: DO Startups tiers do not take meaningful equity on HATCH beyond a small % and SPARK is equity-free; DO pages are currently unreachable via the standard partner URLs (digitalocean.com/partners/startups 404 today), so the 24-month/HATCH details rest on Techstars' official page plus the March 2026 premier-partner announcement. Unused credit expires; overage beyond credits is billed on the DO account.

findings.name: Google Cloud for Startups — via Techstars: $100,000 GCP credits
findings.detail: $100,000 in Google Cloud credits over 24 months, 'FOUNDERS_PROGRAM' tier, per Techstars' official capital page (lists A100, GKE, Vertex AI, Cloud GPUs). Google co-hosts Techstars investor events (e.g., Fall 2025 NYC Investor Day hosted by Google for Startups). Google's own startup portal has been reorganized (cloud.google.com/launch now 404s; program now under the 'Google Cloud for Startups' umbrella) — Google's publicly cited figures are up to $200K credits generally, with partner-accelerator cohorts getting the top package; Techstars' deal line is $100K/24 months.
findings.eligibility: Requires Techstars acceptance (or Google's accelerator-partner path). No .edu email requirement. Typical GCP startup program rules: early-stage (<5 years, funding/revenue caps per Google's current terms — not re-verifiable today as the program pages 404).
findings.claim: For Techstars companies: no separate application — GCP credits activated at the capital-wire step after acceptance, alongside AWS/DigitalOcean. Standalone: apply via the Google Cloud for Startups portal or through a partner (Techstars, YC, 500 Global, Antler).
findings.expiry: 24 months per Techstars' capital page (GCP credits historically 12 months at claim; confirm at activation).
findings.gotchas: Google's own program pages currently 404/moved, so the $100K/24mo details rest on Techstars' official page (high) rather than Google's current terms (could not be read today). Marketplace/SaaS add-ons and support fees are typically excluded from GCP startup credits; overage beyond credits is billed.

findings.name: AWS + Techstars Impact Bootcamps (free for underrepresented founders, incl. students/early founders)
findings.detail: Free 2-day bootcamps (launched 2025, 6 cities: Atlanta, New York, Mexico City, London in 2025; Tokyo, Berlin in early 2026) managed locally by Techstars: hands-on AWS technical training, business coaching, mentors/investors. Each participating founder gets $5,000 in AWS promotional credits. Best-in-class startups are invited to the AWS Founder Retreat — a weekend with in-person investor meetings and the chance to win up to $50,000 in unrestricted grant funding plus an additional $15,000 in AWS promotional credits. Top participants considered for Techstars accelerator or Founder Catalyst programs. Part of AWS's $30M commitment (announced 2022) to Black, Women, Latino and LGBTQIA+ founders.
findings.eligibility: Founding teams must identify as a member of an underrepresented community (Black, Women, Latino, Indigenous, LGBTQIA+, founders with disabilities) or demonstrate work/engagement supporting such communities; self-funded, angel-backed, or raised up to Series A; clear need for cloud technology; interest in scaling/fundraising. No .edu email requirement; free to attend (event slots filled by application).
findings.claim: Apply via the AWS Impact Bootcamps page (https://aws.amazon.com/startups/lp/aws-impact-bootcamps) for one of the six city cohorts; attend the 2-day workshop; receive $5,000 AWS credits as a participant; winners advance to the AWS Founder Retreat for the up-to-$50K grant + $15K credits and Techstars pipeline.
findings.expiry: Event-driven (2025-2026 city calendar); the $5,000 promotional credits follow AWS promotional-credit terms (short validity, no extensions). No standing free tier — only while a cohort is running.
findings.gotchas: The $50K + $15K prizes go only to 'best-in-class' retreat participants, not all attendees. Bootcamp pages may be city-specific and time-boxed. 'Free' = free workshop + credits, but the AWS credits require a paid-plan AWS account to activate (Free-plan accounts are ineligible).

findings.name: Techstars Founder Catalyst (free pre-accelerator, no equity)
findings.detail: 10-week part-time, primarily virtual pre-accelerator for early-stage/idea-stage founders: training, tools, mentorship, cohort community, and network access. 'There is no equity exchange in Founder Catalyst programs.' No tuition listed. Current/planned editions include Techstars x EIT Urban Mobility Founder Catalyst, Alabama, and Global Fall 2026. Complements Techstars' 'Startup Weekend' community events (paid event series) and the University Catalyst pipeline.
findings.eligibility: Pre-funding or idea-stage founders who have raised less than $400K, possess domain expertise in the problem space, have a defined customer need with a lead on a solution, and collaborative spirit. No student/.edu requirement — open to any early founder. Free to join; no equity.
findings.claim: Sign up via the Airtable 'Hear About Future Programs' form on the Techstars Founder Catalyst page or through apply.techstars.com; selected cohorts run 10 weeks; strong participants can feed into Techstars accelerators.
findings.expiry: Cohort-based, rolling; specific editions (EIT/Alabama/Global Fall 2026) have their own application windows; benefit access is not perpetual like accelerator network access.
findings.gotchas: Not a funding program — no capital invested (the $220K deal requires actual accelerator acceptance). Some editions are co-branded (EIT, University of Alabama) and may carry local eligibility emphasis.

findings.name: Techstars University Catalyst / university-partnered accelerators (student & alumni pipeline)
findings.detail: Techstars University Catalyst (with USC) targets the student/alumni pipeline, referenced on Techstars' own pages with a 2026 class in progress; 'USC and Techstars Accelerator' is an official accelerator in the Spring 2026 cycle (alongside Johns Hopkins/CareFirst AI Health Baltimore, Northwestern Medicine, Columbus/Ohio State, etc.). Accepted university-partnered programs receive the same $220K structure (or APAC $120K where applicable) plus the $1M+ credit package. No separate student-only free tier or education license exists at Techstars itself.
findings.eligibility: Students/alumni via University Catalyst (pipeline, free-to-attend format); accelerator acceptance through the same application as other programs. No .edu email requirement for the investment itself.
findings.claim: Attend the University Catalyst cohort offered at your university (USC partnership), or apply to a university-branded accelerator (e.g., USC and Techstars Accelerator, application window closed Nov 19, 2025 for Spring 2026 per Techstars' blog) via apply.techstars.com.
findings.expiry: Cohort-based; new university partnerships announced per year (March 2026 update lists active editions).
findings.gotchas: University-branded cohorts are still funded on the standard accelerator terms — the university is a partner, not the investor; expect the same side-letter obligations. Student-facing 'free' elements are the pipeline events, not the $220K deal.

sunset_notes: Changes/sunsets in 2025-2026: (1) April 17, 2025 — Techstars replaced its $120K deal ($100K MFN SAFE + $20K/5%) with the $220K deal ($200K uncapped MFN SAFE + $20K post-money CEA/5%) for Fall 2025 cohorts onward, explicitly mirroring YC; the $120K structure now applies only to Asia-Pacific programs. (2) The ARM Labs Lagos Techstars accelerator (Techstars' Africa-specific program, launched Dec 2022, 2 cohorts) closed in late 2024 as part of a global restructuring; African founders can still apply to global programs. (3) No Techstars program was sunset in 2025-2026 that would reduce the credit stack — DigitalOcean Startups was upgraded to 2026 'Premier Partner' (announced March 2026), expanding rather than reducing access. (4) Verification gaps today (2026-10-22): the AWS Techstars partnership page (aws.amazon.com/startups/partnerships/techstars → startups.aws.com/...), DigitalOcean's partner/startup pages (digitalocean.com/partners/startups, /startup-cloud), and Google's startup program pages (cloud.google.com/launch, /application/startup-faqs) all return 404, so AWS/DO/GCP per-credit-line details above rely on Techstars' official /capital page (read today) plus partner-program public docs; treat exact $100K/24-month figures as Techstars-stated until re-confirmed against the partners' current portals. (5) There is no Techstars student free tier, trial-credit self-serve offer, or education license (no .edu requirement anywhere in the funnel); student access is via University Catalyst and the free AWS Impact Bootcamps.

provider: a16z / Andreessen Horowitz (VC) — startup cloud-credit programs

findings.name: AWS Activate Portfolio Credits via a16z Org ID (up to $200K)
findings.detail: a16z is a confirmed AWS Activate Provider (listed as 'Andreesen Horowitz' in the Featured Activate Providers, alongside nvidia, carta, Y Combinator). a16z-backed startups use a16z's secure Organization ID to claim AWS Activate Portfolio credits: up to $200,000 USD in AWS Activate Credits at the Activate Portfolio (Pre-Series B) tier. Self-funded startups (no provider) are limited to the Activate Founders tier at up to $5,000. Invite-only AWS Credits for AI Startups ($200K+) are available post-Portfolio. All credits in USD under AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs.
findings.eligibility: Must be backed/referred by an AWS Activate Provider (here a16z = a16z portfolio company or a16z referral). Pre-Series B, founded within the last 10 years, AWS account on the Paid Tier plan, and either new to Activate Credits or requesting more than previously received. No .edu email; global program (US-centric). Self-funded founders are NOT eligible for the Portfolio tier.
findings.claim: 1) Create an AWS Builder ID with a professional email and complete your profile; 2) choose the Activate Portfolio tier; 3) enter a16z's Org ID (request it from a16z); 4) provide startup product/funding/profile details; 5) link an AWS account and submit. Response in 5-10 business days.
findings.expiry: Credits governed by AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions; portfolio credits are usable within a defined window from issuance (exact window not stated on the public page).
findings.gotchas: Requires a live provider relationship (a16z investment/referral) and an Org ID; Paid Tier plan required; pre-Series B cap; self-funded startups are capped at $5K via the separate Founders tier; additional AI-startup credits are invite-only via an account manager.

findings.name: a16z Speedrun Marketplace credits ($10M+ pool across AWS/GCP/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft/NVIDIA/Stripe/Deel)
findings.detail: a16z's Speedrun residency (an a16z operating/accelerator program for early-stage startups) advertises a '$10M+ in free credits' speedrun Marketplace spanning AWS, GCP, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Stripe, Deel and others. Other perks: dedicated advisors/experts, Launch Lab, Brand Lab, Creator Connect, Press Club, talent matchmaking, immigration support (Global Founders Program), in-person Demo Day and access to a network reaching 1,000+ investors. No per-founder dollar cap is disclosed — '$10M+' is the aggregate program pool.
findings.eligibility: Must be accepted into an a16z Speedrun residency; open to founders/companies worldwide, but the program takes place in the US (in-person Demo Day + residency component). No revenue/stage/headcount thresholds are published.
findings.claim: Apply to Speedrun (a16z.com/speedrun); specific credit allotments and claim steps are shared post-acceptance. Next cohort SR008: Feb 1 - Apr 16/18, 2027 in San Francisco; applications close Nov 1, 2026.
findings.expiry: No credit or perk expiry dates disclosed on the public page.
findings.gotchas: Entirely gated behind residency acceptance (not open/self-serve); in-person/US component (international founders use the Global Founders Program); per-founder credit amounts, claim mechanics, and post-program access windows are withheld until after acceptance.

findings.name: a16z x Alchemy onchain Startup Program ($5,000 AWS credits + Alchemy credits + 24/7 engineering support)
findings.detail: An Alchemy co-branded program for a16z portfolio companies building onchain: qualified companies receive Alchemy credits applied directly to their account (offsetting pay-as-you-go or enterprise invoices) plus $5,000 in AWS credits and 24/7 dedicated engineering support on the infrastructure used by Visa/Stripe/Robinhood.
findings.eligibility: a16z portfolio company building onchain (eligibility subject to team qualification). To receive the AWS credits specifically: pre-Series B, a company website/profile, founded in the last 10 years, an AWS account on the Paid Tier plan, NOT previously having received $5,000+ in AWS credits, and an active Alchemy Enterprise account.
findings.claim: Fill out the form at alchemy.com/startup-program/a16z (mention a16z portfolio status to fast-track review); no pitch deck or lengthy application; team qualifies and credits can hit the account within days. Non-a16z teams are directed to the general Alchemy Startup Program.
findings.expiry: No expiry date stated on the page.
findings.gotchas: Onchain/blockchain-building only; requires an active Alchemy Enterprise account; the AWS-credit leg is blocked for teams that already received $5K+ in AWS credits (explicit anti-double-dip), so it complements rather than stacks with the main AWS Activate award.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups / Azure credits via a16z (Investor Network referral, up to ~$150K) — UNVERIFIED
findings.detail: Per prior context, a16z is a Microsoft for Startups Investor Network member, so a16z-backed startups apply for Microsoft/Azure credits (commonly up to ~$150K in Azure credits) using a16z's referral/Org ID. This was NOT independently verified this session: the Microsoft for Startups page returned 404 and the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so the exact current dollar figure and a16z's membership are unconfirmed.
findings.eligibility: a16z-backed startup referred through Microsoft for Startups program terms (standard: early-stage, not already a large Microsoft enterprise account). Specific caps/duration not confirmed this session.
findings.claim: a16z refers/submits the startup into the Microsoft for Startups program; the startup then completes onboarding and receives Azure credits.
findings.expiry: Azure credit windows are typically ~12 months (not confirmed this session).
findings.gotchas: Low confidence — not verified; a16z's current Microsoft Investor Network membership and the current Azure credit amount should be re-confirmed against microsoft.com/startups before relying on this figure.

sunset_notes: a16z is a VC, not a SaaS provider: it has NO standalone free tier, trial, or education (.edu) license of its own. Every "free offer" routes through third-party provider programs where a16z acts as an investor/provider/referrer (AWS Activate, Microsoft for Startups, Alchemy) or through its own Speedrun residency. Active as of 2026-10-22: (1) a16z is a confirmed AWS Activate Provider — Portfolio tier is currently capped at up to $200K; self-funded (Founders) tier only up to $5K; AI-startup credits are invite-only. (2) a16z Speedrun is not sunset — SR008 is scheduled Feb 1 - Apr 16/18, 2027 in San Francisco, applications closing Nov 1, 2026. (3) The a16z x Alchemy onchain program is active but explicitly excludes teams that already received $5K+ in AWS credits (no double-dipping). NOT completed this session: verification of a16z's Microsoft for Startups / Azure (~$150K) referral leg — the Microsoft page 404'd and the shared web-search budget was exhausted, so that finding is low-confidence and should be re-verified. No student-specific free offer from a16z was found.

findings.claim: 1) Attend a YC university event and RSVP via Hacker News account; 2) receive the confirmation email after the event; 3) sign in at https://deals.ycombinator.com/students with the same Hacker News account; 4) browse and redeem each partner deal individually (each runs its own redemption flow).
findings.detail: Bundle of free credits from ~20 partners for students who attend a YC university event (in person, starting Fall 2025). YC's official blog (Jan 16, 2026) headlines it as 'over $20,000 in cloud credits on Azure and AWS, over $5,000 in credits for GPT/Claude/Grok, plus generous credits for AI devtools' (14 YC companies), marketed as 'over $25,000' total. The live deals page deals.ycombinator.com/students (read 2026-10-22) currently names only AWS $10,000, OpenAI $1,000, Anthropic $500 plus 17 devtool logos; earlier 2026 snapshots of the same page also listed Azure $10,000, Grok (xAI) $2,500 and Cursor $720. Per-provider amounts are still fluctuating as YC 'rolls this out.'
findings.eligibility: Students who attend a YC university event starting Fall 2025 (in person). No startup, company or funding requirement. No .edu-domain check and no credit card required per the page. Access auto-detected via the Hacker News account the student used to RSVP.
findings.expiry: Access lasts one year from the date of the qualifying event. Each partner's credits carry their own expiry. One third-party guide (blurredai, Feb 2026) says the email must be re-verified every 30 days to keep access.
findings.gotchas: Live-page named amounts are LOWER than the Jan 2026 blog headline ('$20K+ cloud / $5K+ GPT-Claude-Grok') and the page is explicitly still expanding, so exact credit values vary by event/cohort. Devtool per-tool dollar caps are not published. Only available where YC actually hosts university events (regional/US-centric). No .edu gate is stated, so it is event-attendance-gated rather than verified-student-gated. Secondary claim URL: https://deals.ycombinator.com/students
findings.name: YC AI Stack (a.k.a. YC AI Student Starter Pack) — student program

findings.claim: Be a YC batch company -> receive partner Org IDs / promo codes during YC onboarding -> apply through each partner's portal -> redeem the YC-partnered deals through the sign-in-gated deals portal (account.ycombinator.com / YC company account at deals.ycombinator.com).
findings.detail: YC's official apply page states 'Each YC company gets access to $12M+ in free credits and deals from top partners, including OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Stripe, and a long list of others.' This is the accelerator-funded stack delivered to accepted YC companies during/after the batch; a single company's realizable value is far below the $12M marketing total (roughly the ~$350K+ multi-partner stack in the task's 'known so far').
findings.eligibility: Must be accepted into a YC batch (YC invests when a company is accepted, not when the batch starts). No public funding-age cap on the umbrella itself, but each partner program below imposes its own caps (e.g. AWS pre-Series B, <10 yrs old).
findings.expiry: Varies per partner program (see individual partner findings below).
findings.gotchas: '$12M+' is YC's aggregate marketing figure across all partners, not what one company gets. The full deals catalog is sign-in-gated, so individual YC-partner amounts are not publicly itemized on YC's own site; per-company value depends on which partner tiers you qualify for.
findings.name: YC Startup Credits Program (VC-funded umbrella for YC batch companies)

findings.claim: Receive the YC Org ID from YC onboarding (Y Combinator is a designated AWS Activate Provider) -> create/sign in an AWS Builder ID -> apply for Activate Portfolio with the YC Org ID -> link your AWS account; expect a ~5-10 business day review.
findings.detail: Up to ~$500,000 in AWS Activate credits for eligible YC batch companies (the $500K level was confirmed for the W24 cohort), typically split ~$200K general cloud + ~$300K AI silicon (Trainium/Inferentia, Amazon Bedrock incl. third-party FMs, reserved H100). The public AWS Activate Portfolio tier caps at $200K; the $500K is the YC-negotiated tier. As of 11 May 2026 AWS Activate credits became redeemable for third-party models on Amazon Bedrock.
findings.eligibility: Active or very recent YC batch company (W24 onward at the $500K tier); company <10 years old; pre-Series B or self-funded; valid company website plus matching business-email domain; cannot have already received AWS Activate Portfolio credits of equal or greater value.
findings.expiry: 2 years from the moment AWS activates the credits on the account; no extensions permitted.
findings.gotchas: Credit card MUST be on file (no charge while within credits, but overages bill with no hard stop). Credits are non-transferable and locked to one AWS billing org; AWS auto-applies them; excluded spend includes AWS Professional/Managed Services, Mechanical Turk, crypto-mining, Route 53 domain fees and upfront RI/Savings Plan fees. The 2-year clock starts at activation, not Demo Day, so applying early in the batch preserves more usable time. YC Startup School / older alumni / rejected applicants get only the standard Portfolio tier (up to $200K), not the $500K.
findings.name: AWS Activate credits for YC startups

findings.claim: Arranged through YC's partnership with OpenAI and distributed via YC onboarding / the YC deals portal, not a self-serve public application.
findings.detail: OpenAI overhauled its YC startup program in 2026: up to $500,000 in API credits with NO equity requirement, plus an optional ~$1.5M additional tranche in exchange for equity stakes. In May 2026 (Spring 2026 batch, ~169 companies) Sam Altman announced $2M in OpenAI API credits per startup via uncapped SAFE agreements (~$338M total for that batch). Per WSJ-quoted reporting, the two firms could together hand out up to $800M/yr to YC startups.
findings.eligibility: YC-backed / YC batch startups. The $500K tier has no equity requirement; the $1.5M and $2M amounts require signing equity (SAFE) agreements.
findings.expiry: Not publicly stated; credits are redeemable exclusively with OpenAI (intentional vendor lock-in).
findings.gotchas: A large share of the headline value is equity-funded (SAFE/equity), so it is not 'free' — it is equity-for-credits. Credits usable only on OpenAI models. The structure changed materially in 2026 (baseline offers were far smaller, ~$30K, in earlier years).
findings.name: OpenAI API credits for YC startups

findings.claim: Arranged through YC's partnership with Anthropic and distributed via YC onboarding / the YC deals portal.
findings.detail: Anthropic raised its standard YC credit offer in 2026 from $30,000 to $500,000 per YC startup, with NO equity requirement — explicitly pitched as the founder-friendly counter to OpenAI's equity-based offer (a ~16x increase).
findings.eligibility: YC-backed / YC batch startups. No equity requirement for the $500K tier.
findings.expiry: Not publicly stated; usable on the Anthropic API (and, for some stacks, via AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex AI where Anthropic models are hosted).
findings.gotchas: The jump from $30K to $500K happened in 2026. Figure is from WSJ-quoted press coverage, not read on Anthropic's public page today; actual per-startup allocation may vary by negotiation.
findings.name: Anthropic (Claude) credits for YC startups

findings.claim: Applied via YC's Google Cloud partnership; GCP for Startups application with YC as the referring provider.
findings.detail: Google Cloud is now handing out up to $500,000 in GCP credits to YC startups, plus early access to new Gemini models and occasional access to DeepMind engineers. The public 'Google Cloud for Startups' program generally caps around $200K; the $500K is the YC-negotiated level.
findings.eligibility: YC-backed / YC batch startups; standard GCP-for-Startups eligibility otherwise (early-stage, technology-based).
findings.expiry: GCP startup credits are typically good for ~12 months.
findings.gotchas: The $500K YC figure is from a Google spokesperson quoted in WSJ-press, not from YC or Google's public page today; early Gemini access / DeepMind engineer time are not guaranteed entitlements.
findings.name: Google Cloud / Gemini credits for YC startups

findings.claim: Apply through Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub, or receive Azure credits via YC partner onboarding.
findings.detail: Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) offers up to ~$150,000 in Azure credits unlocked across milestone tiers, plus free GitHub Enterprise, Visual Studio and Microsoft 365, with Azure OpenAI model access included. YC founders commonly reach it through YC's partnership or via the public Founders Hub.
findings.eligibility: Startups (self-funded or VC-backed; no equity required); YC batch companies can access Azure credits through the YC partnership or apply directly to Founders Hub.
findings.expiry: Azure credits are generally valid ~12 months; further tiers unlock by meeting product/milestones rather than auto-renewing.
findings.gotchas: Credits are 'up to $150K' and gated behind milestone achievements, so most startups land well below the cap. Sourced from a third-party 2025 comparison guide, not read on Azure/Founders Hub today — lowest confidence of the partner programs.
findings.name: Microsoft Azure credits for YC startups

findings.claim: Sign in to https://deals.ycombinator.com/students (students) or the YC deals portal (startups), then redeem each devtool deal individually through that company's own signup flow.
findings.detail: 14-17 YC devtool companies provide free AI devtool credits bundled into both the YC AI Stack (students) and the YC startup deals portal: Firecrawl, Exa, Vapi, Browser Use, Reducto, Gumloop, Deepgram, Greptile, Supabase, AgentMail, Langfuse, sync., Coinbase, Roboflow, Tavus, Blaxel, Bolna AI, Respan and Cursor ($720 in one student snapshot). These cover voice AI, browser automation, web search, video generation, document parsing and databases. Per-tool dollar caps are not published on the YC page.
findings.eligibility: Students via the YC AI Stack (attending a YC university event); startups via being a YC batch company / deals portal.
findings.expiry: Varies per tool; YC does not publish per-tool expiry dates.
findings.gotchas: Per-tool limits are hidden and the partner roster/changelogs shift as YC expands the stack; some entries are trials rather than perpetual free tiers, and each carries its own terms and expiry.
findings.name: YC AI devtools bundle (voice / browser / search / video / DB)

provider: Y Combinator (Accelerator / VC) — Startup Cloud-Credit Programs (VC / Accelerator-Funded)
sunset_notes: 2025: YC reportedly REMOVED the public "YC Startup School Deals & Offers" page (per startcamp.com, Feb 2025). Startup deals moved behind sign-in at deals.ycombinator.com, so YC Startup School members no longer automatically get the old public AWS $5K (non-China) / $1,500+3K rebate (China) tier; that older startup-school AWS deal is effectively retired. 2025-2026 partner CREDITS CHANGES (all EXPANSIONS, no partner program was sunset): (a) Anthropic raised its YC offer from $30K to $500K, no equity; (b) OpenAI overhauled to $500K no-equity + optional $1.5M equity tranche, and offered $2M via uncapped SAFE to the entire Spring 2026 batch (May 2026); (c) Google Cloud up to $500K + early Gemini access; (d) YC's apply-page headline raised to "$12M+ in free credits"; (e) as of 11 May 2026 AWS extended Activate credits to be redeemable for third-party models on Amazon Bedrock (previously credits could not cover third-party AI model usage). Student PROGRAM CHANGES: the YC AI Student Starter Pack was rebranded the "YC AI Stack" and is being 'rolled out' to more students in 2026; the live deals page's named credit amounts have rotated down from the Jan 2026 blog headline ($20K+ cloud / $5K+ GPT-Claude-Grok to currently ~$10K AWS + $1K OpenAI + $500 Anthropic + devtools), so the per-provider figures are moving. No genuine YC-branded free-tier or education-LICENSE program (in the software sense) exists — YC is a VC/accelerator, so all 'offers' are partner credit bundles delivered through YC.

findings.claim: 1) Create a NEW DigitalOcean team account with a company-domain email (free-mail not accepted) and a valid credit card; 2) Apply via digitalocean.com/startups / do.co/AIStartups — through an approved partner (accelerator/VC such as Techstars) or directly by selecting 'Other'; 3) On acceptance the credit amount is set per partner and stated in the onboarding email; 4) Spend within the 12-month window, max $10,000 usable per month. 15 months of Standard-tier support and the Welcome Kit partner perks (Stripe Atlas 20% off, QuickNode up to $5k, Airtable $2,000, 100ms $2,500, Miro $1,000, Notion $1,000, Cloud66 $500, Bolster $1,000, Mercury $500 cash on $50k deposit, HubSpot up to 90% off year one, ChargeBee free until $1M revenue, Shortcut 2 months free, Ovvy 90 days free) are included on acceptance.
findings.detail: DigitalOcean Startups (rebranded from 'Hatch', program running since 2016). Official program page (read 2026-10-22): '12 months to scale' — credits for 12 months, amount varies by partner and is stated in the onboarding email, with a $10,000 monthly limit and charges for any monthly use above it. January 22, 2025 press release (investors.digitalocean.com, official) states 'up to $100,000 in Compute Credits' plus 'Complimentary Premium Support' and marketplace access to 600,000+ customers; BusinessWire's release also stated 'up to 3 Months of Free GPU Usage' for qualified startups. Current page lists 'Free access to Standard-tier paid support for 15 months.' Official ToS (last updated May 11, 2026) confirms a 12-month program term and 1-year credit window. Enrollment itself is free ('no fee to participate'); non-transferable credits.
findings.eligibility: Must have raised $10M or less total funding. Requires a company website with a matching company-domain email (no Gmail etc.) and a new DigitalOcean team account on that email. A valid credit card IS required on the account (for billing/overages). Startups that have previously used DigitalOcean credits are excluded. Service-based businesses (consulting, web/app dev shops, marketing agencies) are ineligible. AI-native startups are prioritized but not required. No .edu requirement. No published country restriction; apply through a partner (VC/accelerator/incubator, e.g. Techstars) or directly via the application form ('Other').
findings.expiry: Credits expire 12 months after DigitalOcean accepts you into the program (one year from acceptance per ToS, §1.2); unused credits are forfeited with no extension or rollover. Free Standard-tier support lasts 15 months. ToS auto-terminates the arrangement on acquisition, IPO, insolvency, or ceasing normal operations; liability capped at $100; no resell/sublicense; crypto mining prohibited.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required at signup — not 'free' in the no-CC sense. Core credits as of May 13, 2026 explicitly EXCLUDE: GPU Droplets, NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, Dedicated Inference, Serverless Inference/third-party AI models, Paperspace Machines, Cloudways, and third-party pass-through charges — GPU access is a separate invite-only benefit, and the January 2025 'up to 3 months free GPU' is no longer published. Amount is unpublished and partner-set; the $100,000 ceiling comes only from the Jan 2025 press release. Usage above $10,000 in a month is billed to your card. Powered-off Droplets still bill. Egress beyond bundled allowances is charged separately.
findings.name: DigitalOcean Startups program (formerly Hatch) — up to $100,000 in compute credits over 12 months + 15 months free Standard-tier support

findings.claim: Invitation-only: acceptance into the program does not guarantee GPU credits. The DO team reviews application and infrastructure needs, invites selected startups to submit a separate GPU credit application. In 2025, per the press-release package, qualified startups got 'up to 3 Months of Free GPU Usage' (terms apply), with H100 GPUs available for AI/ML workloads; no amount/duration is currently published on the official page. To run H100s without GPU credits you pay list price (~$1.90/GPU-hour, third-party figure — unverified on official pages today).
findings.detail: Official page states 'Selected startups will be invited to apply for GPU credit packages.' under 'Early-Stage Boost'; GPU credits are 'a separate benefit' from the core credits, and core credits do not cover GPU Droplet usage — your payment method is charged for it. The H100 pool / GPU benefits were a headline of the Jan 22, 2025 announcement ('generous credits for our GPU-powered Droplets and other AI/ML resources', 'priority access to GPU power').
findings.eligibility: Accepted DigitalOcean Startups participants (i.e., same eligibility as the core program: <= $10M raised, new DO customer, company-domain email, credit card on account, product not service business), then invitation from the DigitalOcean team. No .edu requirement.
findings.expiry: GPU credit package terms (amount/duration) not published; determined per invitation. Core program credit window is 12 months from acceptance.
findings.gotchas: Since the May 13, 2026 exclusion update, GPU Droplets, H100 GPU Kubernetes and Bare Metal GPUs are off the core credit table — teams relying on GPUs must get the separate GPU package or pay list. Acceptance into the main program does NOT guarantee the GPU package. Exclusions also cover third-party model hosting on inference products.
findings.name: GPU credit packages ('Early-Stage Boost') — separate, invite-only GPU credits for accepted startups

findings.claim: None — the credit is applied automatically to the first team on a new account; just sign up at digitalocean.com with a payment method. The current offer is $5/90 days; the previously advertised $200/60-day trial no longer appears anywhere on the official pricing page or in docs.
findings.detail: Official pricing page FAQ (read 2026-10-22): 'if you received a $5 credit for 90 days, then that $5 credit is automatically applied to your account.' Credit card required at signup (a ~$1 temporary pre-authorization is taken and reversed). No perpetual free compute tier exists: Droplets start at $4/month, managed databases from $15/month, Spaces from $5/month. Billing is per-second with a 60-second/$0.01 minimum.
findings.eligibility: Any new DigitalOcean account (all regions where DigitalOcean is available). A payment method (credit card) IS required before creating resources — no CC-free path. No .edu, no age/funding limits. Applies once, to the first team.
findings.expiry: $5 credit expires 90 days after signup; then normal pay-as-you-go billing begins for anything provisioned.
findings.gotchas: Do not expect the old $200/60-day trial — the official pricing/docs pages list only the $5/90-day grant as of today. Payment method required up front, so 'free' is really a trial with a card on file; overage is billed at list price. Stopped Droplets still bill (resources stay reserved) — only destroying them stops charges.
findings.name: New-account trial credit: $5 for 90 days (current trial; replaced the older $200/60-day offer)

findings.claim: No claiming needed — all existing/new accounts get these inclusions automatically; provision the resources. The 'starting at $0/month' products (App Platform, Functions, Container Registry, VPC) have a free base allowance but paid tiers for usage beyond it.
findings.detail: Official pricing page 'Platform benefits' (read 2026-10-22): free to build/deploy 3 static sites on App Platform; 90,000 GiB-seconds/month of Functions compute free; free Container Registry with 1 repository and 500 MiB storage; free DNS management; free cloud firewalls; VPC free (ingress free; inter-datacenter VPC peering $0.01/GiB); Droplets include free outbound transfer starting at 500 GiB/month per Droplet; DOKS starts at $12/month with a free control plane. Spaces object storage is NOT free (from $5/month).
findings.eligibility: All DigitalOcean accounts; no eligibility filters, no .edu, no card-for-free (a card is required for the account, but the listed free inclusions do not require spending). No published regional restriction.
findings.expiry: No expiry — ongoing inclusions as long as the account is active. There is no sunset date published for these allowances; treat them as permanent but subject to change without notice.
findings.gotchas: This is not a free-tier substitute for compute: there is no perpetual free Droplet. Free allowances are per-resource (e.g., 500 GiB outbound is per Droplet plan; extra egress beyond bundled allowances is billed — list rate is ~$0.01/GiB per third-party pricing trackers, unverified on the official page today). App Platform's free static sites cap at 3 sites with 1 GiB outbound each.
findings.name: Always-free platform inclusions (de-facto free tier: static sites, Functions, registry, DNS, firewall, VPC, DOKS control plane)

findings.claim: AI startups apply through the Typeform application linked from the AI Startup Ecosystem announcement (same do.co/AIStartups pipeline as the Startups program). Techstars founders go through Techstars' cohort/support track; partners (VCs, accelerators, university entrepreneurship programs, AI developer platforms) apply separately to join the ecosystem and then route startups to DigitalOcean.
findings.detail: DigitalOcean announced its 'AI Startup Ecosystem' on October 29, 2025 (official blog): it brings together 'established technology partners, vibrant community organizations, AI developer platforms, and university entrepreneurship programs' with Techstars as the named founding partner. Members get 'discounted infrastructure and tooling', technical support and go-to-market resources; the Techstars deal includes 'GPU discounts, infrastructure credits and hands-on technical support', plus hackathon support for early-stage ideas. No dollar amounts are disclosed in the official post — benefits funnel into the Startups program benefits above.
findings.eligibility: AI startups (founder-led; early-stage ideas through growth). No .edu requirement; university entrepreneurship programs are partners, not applicant types. No funding cap published for the ecosystem itself (the $10M cap belongs to the core Startups program). No regional limits published.
findings.expiry: No published end date; amounts/durations are partner-set and evolve. Underlying Startups program credits, if awarded, expire 12 months from acceptance.
findings.gotchas: Amounts are not published anywhere official (unlike the $100k press-release figure for Hatch compute credits), so treat any third-party numbers as unverified. 'Discounted infrastructure' is not necessarily free. Application links point to Typeforms that change; verify the current link from the official blog post.
findings.name: AI Startup Ecosystem (Techstars founding partner track) — discounted infrastructure + GPU discounts + infra credits

sunset_notes: 1) No student/education offer found: as of 2026-10-22 DigitalOcean has no public student, .edu, or education-license program. The URL requested in the task (digitalocean.com/community/solutions/digitalocean-for-startups) and a guessed .../digitalocean-for-students both return HTTP 404; the startup program now lives at digitalocean.com/startups. No .edu email requirement appears anywhere in official pages. 2) Program rebrand + duration change: 'Hatch' was rebranded 'DigitalOcean Startups' with a new 2025 benefits package announced Jan 22, 2025 (investors.digitalocean.com press release + BusinessWire). The previously referenced 'up to $100,000 over 24 months' is superseded: the official ToS (last updated May 11, 2026) sets a 12-month program term and a 1-year credit window, and the current page states amounts 'vary' per partner with a $10,000 monthly limit. 3) May 13, 2026 restriction expansion: core startup credits now explicitly exclude GPU Droplets, NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, Dedicated Inference, Serverless Inference/third-party AI models, Paperspace Machines and Cloudways (previously only GPU Droplets and H100 products were excluded); GPU support moved fully to the invite-only 'Early-Stage Boost' packages, and the Jan 2025 'up to 3 months free GPU usage' language is no longer published. 4) Support wording changed: 'Complimentary Premium Support' (Jan 2025 release) is now '15 months of free Standard-tier support'. 5) The older $200/60-day new-account trial no longer appears on the official pricing page or docs (docs.digitalocean.com/resources/free-trial/ 404s); the current trial is a $5/90-day credit automatically applied to a new account. 6) Oct 29, 2025: AI Startup Ecosystem launched with Techstars as founding partner — no published amounts, funnels into the Startups program.

findings.name: 500 Global FounderHub — bundled partner cloud/tech credits (the actual 'Startup Cloud-Credit Program')
findings.detail: Free perks platform for 500-affiliated founders: 400+ partner perks/discounts covering AI tools, hosting, banking, cap-table management, expert network, investor directory. Official 500 Eurasia program page states participants get 'access to over $1M in credits in the 500 FounderHub'. No per-provider dollar amounts (AWS/GCP/OpenAI not itemized publicly); partners include Deepgram, Mercury and others via the perks catalog. Platform launched 2022. There is no public-facing free cloud-credit program — the $1M+ credit pool is only reachable by 500-affiliated founders.
findings.eligibility: 500 portfolio companies, accelerator alumni, and 500 education-network alumni (1,400+). Free account at 500founderhub.com; no .edu requirement; not open to the general public — gating is by 500 affiliation. No funding cap stated; region limits only apply to the accelerator that grants access.
findings.claim: 1) Join a 500 program or be a 500 portfolio company. 2) Create a free account at 500founderhub.com (sign-in/signup page is public). 3) Redeem partner perks from the 400+ Perks catalog; book expert office hours, request investor intros.
findings.source_url: https://500.co/founders/eurasia/accelerator (primary claim of $1M+ credits); https://www.500founderhub.com/ and https://www.500founderhub.com/auth/signup ; https://500.co/partnerships
findings.expiry: Per-partner terms; 500 publishes no global expiry/renewal date
findings.gotchas: 'Credits' are mostly partner-usage allowances and discounts, not cash; per-provider caps vary by partner and are not public; access is gated (trial-vs-free: it is free only to 500-affiliated founders); platform counts 400+ perks but the $1M figure is marketing language from the Eurasia page.

findings.name: 500 Fellowship (500 Global Flagship Accelerator, Palo Alto)
findings.detail: Up to $50K upfront with 'potential for up to $1M more as you progress' (official flagship page, read today). 4-month in-person San Francisco program; Batch 37 cohort Nov 30, 2026 – Apr 9, 2027. Program fee: $35,000 per startup for Phase 1, excluding travel (fee is typically deductible from the investment). Not a free offer — VC deal with equity dilution plus a $35K program fee; the free component is only the bundled FounderHub perks/network.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage tech startups; official page targets 'top 0.1% of founders' (just started, or first users/revenue/pilots all accepted); geographic requirement: founder in the U.S. or plans to be within six months. No .edu requirement; no funding cap published.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at flagship.aplica.500.co. 2) Five-stage process: Apply -> Talk to us (interviews) -> Kick off -> Build (weekly group days, 1:1s) -> Finish (demo to stakeholders). Batch 36 application close was Oct 11, 2026.
findings.expiry: Batch cycles: Batch 36 closed Oct 11, 2026; current cohort runs Nov 30, 2026 – Apr 9, 2027
findings.gotchas: $35K Phase 1 fee (excl. travel) — not free; old 'up to $150K for 6%' deal no longer published (deal restructured, see sunset_notes); US-presence requirement excludes most students/international founders; equity % not stated on the page.

findings.name: 500 Global in Eurasia Accelerator (Tbilisi)
findings.detail: $100,000 investment per accepted startup ('subject to final terms and diligence'), 12-week hybrid program: 2 weeks in-person Tbilisi (Sep 21–Oct 2, 2026) + 8 weeks remote (Oct 5–Nov 27, 2026) + Fundraising week in Tbilisi (Nov 30–Dec 11, 2026), Demo Day Dec 10, 2026. Includes 'over $1M in credits in the 500 FounderHub' (AI tools, hosting, banking, cap-table management). Third-party coverage (Eurasia Biz Monitor, May 2026) reports a $35,000 Phase 1 fee, but the official page does not state a fee.
findings.eligibility: Early-revenue-stage tech startups with a functional prototype, global-market potential, cross-functional team with market expertise, 'VC backing potential'; must have direct or indirect operations in one of 28 listed Eurasian countries (Balkans, Caucasus, Eastern Europe, Central Asia, Baltic states, etc.). No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Apply year-round at eurasia.aplica.500.co. 2) Priority deadline for Batch 12: Aug 2, 2026; final deadline Aug 9, 2026. 3) Three-phase program with in-person Tbilisi phases.
findings.expiry: Batch 12 application deadline Aug 9, 2026; Batch 11 demo day Dec 10, 2026
findings.gotchas: Fee not disclosed on the official page (third-party reports $35K Phase 1 fee); $1M+ credits claim is program marketing, provider breakdown not public; country-restricted (28 countries); equity % not stated on page.

findings.name: 500 LatAm Program (Silicon Valley immersion)
findings.detail: 500 Global commits $300,000 investment to the 5 most promising Latin American tech startups per cycle; package includes 3 weeks at 500 San Francisco HQ plus ongoing dedicated accompaniment from a 500 team member. No program fee or cloud/tech credits disclosed on the official page. A Nov 2025 press call (contxto, Nov 11, 2025) described the structure as $300K for 10% equity.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage Latin American tech startups with a global vision; Latin America founders only. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at latam.aplica.500.co ('APLICA AQUI'). 2) Official page: call open until July 31, 2026 (CONVOCATORIA ABIERTA HASTA EL 31 DE JULIO 2026).
findings.expiry: Application deadline July 31, 2026; 2025-cycle Silicon Valley immersion was scheduled for April 2026
findings.gotchas: Official disclaimer: participation does not include or guarantee an investment; only 5 startups selected per call; equity terms not published on the official page; page footer says 'updated as of Dec 2024' — verify current terms at application.

findings.name: Sanabil Accelerator by 500 Global (MENA, Riyadh)
findings.detail: Equity investment of 'US$100,000 and above' from 500 Global for selected startups; 12-week program in Riyadh (Batch 11: Apr 5 – Jul 1, 2026); Phase 1 program fee of $35,000 per startup excluding travel (stated on the official MENA page). Partnership between 500 Global and Sanabil Investments (Saudi PIF).
findings.eligibility: MENA tech startups with an MVP and early traction, ready to scale; focus on the Middle East/North Africa region. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Apply via the MENA portal (mena.500.co/founders/mena/seed-accelerator). 2) Batch 11 deadlines: priority Feb 15, 2026, application close Mar 5, 2026; next cycle final deadline Aug 9, 2026 (Sep 27 – Dec 9, 2026 run).
findings.expiry: Batch 11 closed Mar 5, 2026; next batch runs Sep 27 – Dec 9, 2026, final deadline Aug 9, 2026
findings.gotchas: $35K Phase 1 fee reduces net cash value; region-restricted; no cloud-credit amounts published on the page.

findings.name: 500 Education bootcamps / startup academies (Georgia Startup Academy, Egypt Seed Bootcamp, Sanabil Startup Unlocked)
findings.detail: Country-local, typically government-backed short bootcamps (5-day bootcamps; Egypt Scale Up is a 7-week program) aimed at students and early-stage founders in Georgia, Egypt, and MENA. They are training programs, not funding deals: no investment, and no cloud/tech partner credits are disclosed anywhere in the official listings.
findings.eligibility: Students and early-stage founders in the host country (Georgia, Egypt, MENA); application-based; no .edu email requirement stated. Free or low-cost in practice, but 500 does not publish cost or credit terms for these.
findings.claim: 1) Browse program pages from 500.co/accelerators (11 programs listed). 2) Use the quiz at 500.co/founders/quiz to identify the right program, then follow each program's application link.
findings.expiry: Per-country rolling cycles; not published centrally
findings.gotchas: No cloud credits, no funding — training only; cost/credit details not published, so do not assume 'free'; details page (500.co/founders/georgia) returned no content at fetch time, so treat Georgia Startup Academy specifics as unverified.

sunset_notes: 1) No standalone public free cloud-credit program, free tier, or education license exists at 500 Global — the "Startup Cloud-Credit Programs (VC/Accelerator Funded)" front is realized only as bundled partner perks (the 500 FounderHub platform, 400+ perks, "$1M+ in credits" claim on the official Eurasia page) that are reachable exclusively by 500-affiliated founders; nothing is open to students or the general public. 2) Flagship deal restructured: the historical ~$50K–$100K for 5–7% (and 2025 third-party listings citing "$150K for 6%, $37.5K fee") is no longer published; the current official flagship page (read today, 2026-10-22) states "up to $50K right away, up to $1M more as you progress" with a $35K Phase 1 program fee — so known-so-far numbers are stale. 3) LatAm: the Nov 2025 call was "$300K for 10% to 5 startups" (contxto, Nov 11, 2025); the official page now shows a $300K investment commitment with a July 31, 2026 deadline, equity undisclosed. 4) Domain note: www.500global.com refused connections (ECONNREFUSED on a DigitalOcean IP, Oct 22, 2026) — the official site of record is 500.co; treat 500global.com as parked/unreliable. 5) No 2025–2026 sunset of the FounderHub perks platform itself; credit amounts are partner-controlled and unpublished.

findings.name: Neon Free plan (permanent free tier)
findings.detail: Verified on neon.com/pricing + FAQ today. $0/month, permanent (explicitly 'not a trial'). 100 projects/org; 10 branches/project (extra branches not available on Free); 100 CU-hours compute per project/month; autoscaling capped at 2 CU (8 GB RAM); auto-pause/scale-to-zero after 5 min inactivity (cannot be disabled on Free; suspended compute = $0); 1 GB Postgres storage per project with a 20 GB account-wide cap; 5 GB public egress per project; 6-hour instant-restore history capped at 1 GB of changes; 1 manual snapshot/project; Managed Better Auth up to 60k MAU/project; Object Storage 5 GB/project (free in beta); Functions 10 active + 400 waiting capacity-hours and 1M invocations per project; monitoring retention 1 day; unlimited org members; community support only. CU-hours and egress reset monthly; storage/branch/project counts are continuous. Hitting limits suspends compute or blocks writes — data is never deleted and there is no overage billing on Free. Suspended computes still count against storage.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, no credit card required (official pricing docs: 'The Free plan is permanent (not a trial); no credit card required'), no .edu email or company status needed. No region limits stated on the page.
findings.claim: Sign up at console.neon.tech (neon.com signup); Free plan is default — no activation steps. Included backend primitives (auth, object storage, functions) also come automatically with each project.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal needed; it is a permanent free tier. Invoices under $0.50 are not collected (paid side).
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse with paid plans: Launch starts at $0.106/CU-hour, Scale at $0.222/CU-hour, storage $0.35/GB-month on paid. Hitting the 100 CU-hour or 5 GB egress cap suspends that project's compute for the month. The stale pricing.md mirror still says 0.5 GB/project — current limit is 1 GB/project since Oct 2, 2026. No instant-restore, no scheduled snapshots, no IP allow rules, no HIPAA/SOC2/SLA on Free.

findings.name: $20 trial credits (paid-features trial)
findings.detail: The official pricing page offers 'Claim $20 in free credits to try paid features' via a console promo link. $20 of prepaid value usable against paid-plan usage (Launch/Scale rates). Exact terms (credit-card requirement, credit expiry, one-time vs repeatable) are not documented on the pages fetched today.
findings.eligibility: Not stated on official pages; presented as a general trial-credits claim (console promo code 'beepboop'). No edu/startup requirement indicated.
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://console.neon.tech/app/?promo=beepboop (linked from neon.com/pricing). 2) Sign in / create account. 3) $20 credits applied to try paid features.
findings.expiry: Not stated on official pages today.
findings.gotchas: Trial credits are NOT the permanent free tier — once the $20 is exhausted, standard usage-based billing applies to whatever plan is selected. Confirm CC requirements and credit expiry before claiming; unverified as of today's fetch.

findings.name: Neon/Databricks Startup Program
findings.detail: Verified on neon.com/startups today. Two tracks: Self-funded — up to $1,000 in Neon credits; Venture-backed — up to $200K in combined Neon + Databricks credits (hero banner says 'up to $200K in credits'). Credits valid 12 months from date of acceptance. Note a marketing discrepancy: the pricing page's 'Special programs' section still says 'up to $100k in credits', while the dedicated startup page details $1K / $200K. Application is now routed through a Databricks form (Neon is 'part of the Databricks Platform').
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups. Self-funded track: less than $1M in funding, early-stage product/MVP, no investors required. Venture-backed track: VC-backed with at least $1M in funding, or participation in a recognized accelerator (Y Combinator cited). No stated caps on company age beyond 'early-stage', revenue, headcount, or geographic region.
findings.claim: 1) Submit the application at neon.com/startups (Databricks application form, 'Apply Now'). 2) Reviews take a few business days. 3) If qualified, credits are applied directly to your account. Alternative: 'apply or ask your investor' / name an accelerator (e.g. YC) in the investor field.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months from acceptance; no renewal mechanism described. After credits lapse or are exhausted, normal plan billing applies.
findings.gotchas: Not automatic — application-based with review. Billing is set up so usage beyond the credits is billed normally (a payment method will likely be needed once credits run out, though the page does not state a CC requirement up front). The '$100k' figure on the pricing page is stale marketing copy versus the page's own $1K/$200K structure. Databricks credits in the VC track may be constrained by Databricks' own program terms.

findings.name: Claimable Neon (agent-provisioned no-signup projects)
findings.detail: Verified on neon.com/claimable-neon today. A coding agent can spin up a real Neon project before a human signs up: 'No account or payment details required.' Includes a temporary Lakebase Postgres database; optional Data API and Managed Better Auth (both stay enabled after claim). Unclaimed projects are capped at 100 MB storage and 1 GB transfer and expire in 72 hours. Provision via scoped agent credentials (auth.md/WorkOS flow, CLI, neon.ts), then a short-lived claim link (claimable.neon.tech/claim?user_code=…) transfers the project into the human's Neon org, establishing ownership with team access.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — no account, no credit card, no sign-up required for the agent-provisioned phase; to claim into an account you need (or create) a Neon org, where the Free plan applies.
findings.claim: 1) Provision: agent creates project + scoped credentials via GET https://neon.com/auth.md then POST to claimable.neon.tech. 2) Build: agent works against the live DB. 3) Claim: use the claim link to transfer the project into your org.
findings.expiry: Unclaimed projects expire after 72 hours (100 MB/1 GB caps until claimed). After claiming, the project lives under your normal plan (Free tier limits if on Free) with no expiry.
findings.gotchas: The 72-hour 100 MB cap makes it unsuitable for any sustained workload — it is an on-ramp, not a free tier. After claiming, Free-plan quotas (1 GB storage/project, 100 CU-hrs, 5 GB egress) govern. Data built in the 72h window survives claim; an abandoned project is deleted at expiry.

findings.name: No student/education-specific program found
findings.detail: No Neon student or education license offer exists on the official site as of today: neon.com/education resolves to the generic product page (no program), the pricing page lists only Agent Plan, Startup Program and Open Source Program among special programs, and no .edu-email-verified offer or education pricing appears in the FAQ or 2025-2026 changelog entries. Students get the same permanent Free plan as anyone else (no CC, no limits on who signs up). (Out of scope but adjacent: an Open Source sponsorship program exists at neon.com/programs/open-source.md for maintainers, and an 'Agent Plan' for app-generation platforms.)
findings.eligibility: N/A — no distinct student offer; standard Free plan eligibility (anyone).
findings.claim: Students: sign up for the Free plan normally; no .edu email required or requested by Neon's published materials.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse with generic Databricks-for-education programs (e.g. Databricks education/community tiers), which are not surfaced on Neon's site. Search budget for further confirmation was exhausted this session; if an education program exists, it is not referenced from Neon's pricing/startup/claimable pages.

provider: Supabase (managed Postgres / data platform) — verified 2026-10-22 against supabase.com/pricing (fetched today), supabase.com billing docs, supabase.com/education (404), supabase.com/startups and /solutions/startups, and AWS/Mercury partner pages

findings.name: Supabase Free Plan (free tier) — the only direct, self-serve free offer
findings.detail: $0/month, verified on the official pricing page today: 500 MB Postgres per active project (Shared CPU, 500 MB RAM), 1 GB file storage (50 MB max upload), 5 GB egress + 5 GB cached egress, 50,000 MAU included (50K third-party-auth MAU too, raised from 50 in March 2025), 500,000 Edge Function invocations/month, 25 Edge Functions allowed, 2M realtime messages/month, 200 realtime peak connections, 1 GB log ingestion + 100 GB log query, unlimited API requests, 2 active projects per user (limit applies across ALL orgs where the user is Owner/Admin), community support only. Quotas are organization-level. 500 MB database limit is per ACTIVE project (paused/deleted projects don't count). No trial needed: this is the permanent free tier.
findings.eligibility: Everyone — no .edu email, no startup requirements, no funding cap, no region limit, credit card NOT required. 2 active projects cap per user, counted across every Free-plan org they own/admin.
findings.claim: Sign up at supabase.com/dashboard -> create an organization (plan: Free) -> create up to 2 projects. No application, no verification. 'Start for Free' on the pricing page.
findings.expiry: Indefinite / free forever. Projects auto-pause after 1 week of inactivity (data kept; paused projects don't count toward the 2-active-project limit and can be resumed). Paid-plan behavior (no pausing) is not available on Free.
findings.gotchas: Free projects sleep after 7 idle days — bites students between deadlines; data persists while paused but the DB is down until resumed. Hitting quota on a Free org doesn't auto-upgrade: overages simply aren't billed on Free; you must upgrade to Pro ($25/mo + $10/mo compute credits) to get more. SSO MAU and Storage Images Transformed are unavailable on Free. Only 1-day log retention. To mix plans you must create separate orgs. No backups on Free. Third-party sites' 'up to $10K' / '$2,500' / '6 months Team plan free' Supabase startup-credit claims are unverified against any Supabase page and contradict each other.

findings.name: Student/education offers: NONE (no education license, no .edu discount, not in GitHub Student Developer Pack)
findings.detail: Supabase has no student program, no education pricing, and no application path. supabase.com/education returns 404; the pricing page contains no student/academic wording; Supabase does not appear in the GitHub Student Developer Pack offer list (checked today); a 2024 Supabase-maintained GitHub discussion confirms the stance is 'use the free tier.' A co-founder once said YC Summer Fellows students (a YC run, not Supabase-run, grants program) received $10K in Supabase credits (2025 cohort only). Students effectively get exactly the general Free plan.
findings.eligibility: N/A — students get no special tier beyond the general Free plan (no .edu verification, no academic license).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; sign up for the Free plan like anyone else. If a class project needs more, email support@supabase.io (no program exists to apply to).
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Pricing-page footer copy 'free projects for students and hobbyists' (2020 founding post) is aspirational marketing, not a program. Do not rely on third-party 'Supabase for students' deal pages — they all just restate the free tier plus paid upsells.

findings.name: Startup credits via partner channels: $300 over 12 months (AWS Activate) and $300 over 1 year (Mercury Perks), plus unpublished YC/accelerator/investor partner tiers
findings.detail: No self-serve application on supabase.com. Credits are distributed through partner deal books: (1) AWS Startups/Activate marketplace offer: '$300 Supabase credits for free over 12 months' (AWS-official listing; page now sits behind login at startups.aws.com). (2) Mercury Perks (mercury.com/perks/supabase, live-verified by a third party 2026-10-20): $300 in Supabase credits over 1 year, new Supabase customers only, for Mercury business-account holders (Mercury requires US-formed company). (3) YC and 80+ accelerator/VC partner tier: amounts unpublished, delivered through the partner's own portal (Supabase blog, Oct 2025: 1,000+ YC companies on Supabase; 'Supabase YC Program' gives YC companies credits). Non-dilutive, no equity.
findings.eligibility: AWS route: AWS Activate membership (per third-party detail, institutional-VC-backed, pre-seed to Series A, < $5M raised — verify in the AWS portal since the offer page is login-gated). Mercury route: Mercury business customer + NEW Supabase customer. YC/accelerator route: being in that partner's portfolio. No funding cap/age cap published for the $300 tiers themselves.
findings.claim: AWS: redeem the Supabase offer inside the AWS Activate/Startups portal and attach to a Supabase org. Mercury: redeem from the Mercury Perks portal. YC/investor: claim through your accelerator or VC's startup-perks portal. Credits attach to one Supabase organization (moves only via support ticket).
findings.expiry: Credits delivered over 12 months and reduce only FUTURE invoices (not already-issued ones); no published review SLA; partner terms can change.
findings.gotchas: Page-gating: AWS offer page redirects to login, so current terms must be confirmed inside the AWS portal. The '$2,500', '$3,000 over 12 months', '6 months Team plan free' figures circulating on deal aggregators conflict and are NOT published on any Supabase page — treat as unverified. No public application means bootstrapped startups with no partner affiliation get only the Free plan.

findings.name: Trial credits: NONE — no free Pro/Team trial or new-signup credit
findings.detail: Supabase has no trial-credit program for Pro/Team. Paid plans are billed monthly up front (Pro $25/mo + $10/mo compute credits covering one Micro instance; Team from $599/mo). The only 'credits' a new user gets are partner-distributed (AWS/Mercury/YC, above). The 2026-09 OrioleDB public-beta and AI/model-gateway features carry standard Postgres pricing, no student/startup-specific credit.
findings.eligibility: N/A
findings.claim: Nothing to claim.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: 'Pro plan trial' language on third-party perk sites (e.g. 'Pro plan free 12 months, $300 value') describes partner credit redemptions, not a genuine self-serve trial; don't expect one on signup.
