provider: Anthropic — Claude API (LLM API) & consumer platform (claude.com / claude.ai / platform.claude.com)

findings.name: Claude Startups program (free Claude Team year + $1,000 API credit, Oct 2026 expansion)
findings.detail: Launched May 2026 (originally invite-only via partner VCs; self-serve form added 21–31 May 2026). On Oct 6, 2026 Anthropic expanded it: (a) one free year of Claude Team with up to 5 Premium seats for companies new to Team (~$6,000 at the $100/seat/mo list price), (b) a one-time $1,000 API credit 'available as soon as you're approved', (c) 'Claude Startup Stack' partner discounts/credits worth up to $45,000 (combined partner max, not a cash grant), (d) up to $100,000 in additional API credits claimable through partner VCs, (e) 45-min Applied AI office hours biweekly, Claude Marketplace listing help, Founder House/events. Combined Claude value 'up to $7,000'. After a surge of '21x the expected applications' (hundreds of thousands), the free Team + $1,000 credit offers were paused ~Oct 9–13 and all applications are being re-reviewed; as of today the official page says 'Our current cohort is now full, and we're not accepting new applications right now.' Existing claimed offers are unaffected. Credits apply only to the first-party Claude API via Claude Console — not AWS Bedrock, Vertex, Azure or other third-party platforms.
findings.eligibility: Startups 'founded in the last five years or funded in the last two' (Oct 2026 expansion wording). Bootstrapped, pre-seed and VC-backed companies may apply. Older FAQ text for the credits tier additionally required institutional equity funding, founding within 4 years, and no prior Anthropic startup credits. Requires a Claude Console account and a company email matching the company's website domain. Geographic exclusions in the official program terms (last updated May 22, 2025): Belarus, China, Cuba, Iran, Myanmar, North Korea, Russia, Sudan, Syria, Crimea, DNR/LNR; Anthropic-affiliated persons excluded. No .edu email; no CC requirement stated.
findings.claim: 1) Sign in to Claude Console; 2) submit the application at claude.com/programs/startups (currently closed — cohort full); 3) if approved, $1,000 credit and Team year activate automatically; 4) if funded, mention/partner with a partner VC for up to $100K additional credits. To hear when the next cohort opens, subscribe to the Claude Startup newsletter.
findings.expiry: Cohort currently full / paused as of 2026-10-22; next cohort TBA. Secondary coverage reports the $1,000 API credit expires six months after it is granted; Anthropic's general Credit Terms (cited by a Sept-2026-checked tracker) say promotional credits otherwise expire one calendar year from issuance. No published sunset for the program itself.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: the 'free year' is a subsidized paid-plan grant, not a permanent free tier — after it lapses the account bills at list price. The $45K figure is max combined partner value, not a grant. Credits are first-party-API only (Bedrock/Vertex not eligible). The free offers were paused within days of launch due to capacity; applying now = waitlist. VC-linked $100K tier is separate from the $1,000 and goes through the investor, not a direct Anthropic award. One award per company.

findings.name: Claude consumer Free plan (claude.ai) — free tier, no card
findings.detail: The Free plan is $0/month: chat on web/desktop/mobile, web search, file creation, code execution, memory, connectors, Artifacts, Design/Slides/Docs. Verified today on the official pricing page: no credit card required ('Free: $0, no card required'). Paid plans: Pro $17/mo annual ($200 up front) or $20/mo; Max from $100/mo. Team Standard $20/seat/mo (annual) / $25 (monthly); Premium $100/seat/mo (annual).
findings.eligibility: Anyone; consumer account, no eligibility check beyond account creation. No .edu email. No CC required for Free.
findings.claim: Sign up free at claude.ai (or download desktop/mobile app). Nothing to claim — account creation is the entire step. No API keys: the Free plan provides chat-app access only, not the first-party API.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Not an API offer — students/startups building products cannot use the Free plan as API compute; usage limits apply (rolling 5-hour session windows, weekly caps on paid tiers).

findings.name: Small free API trial credits for new users (official FAQ)
findings.detail: The official API pricing docs FAQ (read today): 'New users receive a small amount of free credits to test the API. Contact sales for information about extended trials for enterprise evaluation.' Also: 'Academic and research discounts might be available' (under Volume discounts). The dollar amount of the signup credit is not published on the page.
findings.eligibility: Any new API account (platform.claude.com console). Extended trials via sales are for enterprise evaluation; academic/research discounts are on a may-be-available basis.
findings.claim: Create a Claude Console account at platform.claude.com; the small free test credit attaches to the account automatically (amount unpublished). For extended trials, email sales@anthropic.com.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry for the small trial credit; purchased/other credits expire per Credit Terms (promotional credits within one calendar year of issuance per a Sept-2026-checked secondary tracker).
findings.gotchas: A Sept-2026 third-party tracker claimed new API accounts get 'no free credit at all', which the official docs FAQ contradicts (or the small credit may not appear in every region/account — amount is unpublished, so treat as small and unspecified). A CC is needed to go beyond the free credit; billing is arrears-based.

findings.name: AI for Science program — up to $20,000 API credits for 6 months (researchers/education)
findings.detail: Official support article (read today): approved applicants get 'up to $20,000 in API credits to your account for a 6-month period.' Credits are for API use only ('do not apply to the Claude web app'). Launched May 5, 2025; particular focus on biology/life sciences. Review: 'We evaluate submissions on the first Monday of each month.' Single account per research program; credits allocated to one organization ID and distributed among collaborators.
findings.eligibility: Researchers attached to a research institution working on high-impact scientific projects (academic/nonprofit). Reviewed on scientific merit, impact, feasibility, plus biosecurity screening. No .edu email explicitly stated (institutional affiliation is the gate).
findings.claim: Fill out the linked Google Form application on the AI for Science page (from the official support article at support.claude.com/en/articles/11199177 or the launch page at anthropic.com/news/ai-for-science-program). If you need models sooner, create a Console account in the interim.
findings.expiry: Credits valid for 6 months from grant; monthly review cycle; no program sunset date published. No nonpublic/experimental models through this program.
findings.gotchas: No Usage Policy exemption (red-teaming/jailbreaking research still subject to standard enforcement); rejections get no individual response; 'substantial number of applications' — competition is high; no finetuning API access via the program (finetuning preview is AWS Bedrock-only).

findings.name: Claude Team plan for Scientists — free Standard seats for university/nonprofit research groups
findings.detail: Official page (read today): Principal Investigators (or equivalents) at accredited universities and nonprofit research institutes in natural sciences, math, CS, engineering and related fields get the Team plan at promotional pricing: Standard seat $0/month (regularly $20), Premium seat $15/month (regularly $100, 5x usage), 1–25 seats per group (contact us for larger), min 1 seat. '10,000 scientists around the world can now get Claude at no cost to start.' Includes Claude Science, Claude Code & Cowork access, SSO, shared projects, database connectors. 'Claude does not train on your conversations, uploaded files, or research data.'
findings.eligibility: PI/equivalent at an accredited university or nonprofit research institute; for-profit, CRO and industry R&D teams are steered to paid plans. No .edu email required — institutional type + attestation (claude.ai/labs-verification/attestation: confirm affiliation + brief research description). Reviews take 5–7 business days.
findings.claim: On claude.com/programs/team-plan-for-scientists: click 'Verify now' → complete the attestation → approval email → add seats immediately. For extra API credits, apply to the AI for Science grant program (separate application).
findings.expiry: Promotional pricing applies 12 months from sign-up, then seats renew at the then-current price for this plan. Inactivity clause: 'If a group has no activity for 90 days, we may return it to standard Team pricing' (admins notified first). Limited availability — pricing not guaranteed.
findings.gotchas: This is a discounted plan, not free credits — after 12 months you pay list price if you continue. No bundled API credit amount: extra usage is grant-based via AI for Science. 'Final pricing confirmed after verification' — expect surprises on larger groups.

findings.name: Claude Campus program — student ambassador tracks with USD 3,600 stipend
findings.detail: Official page (read today): three student tracks, each with a flat 'USD3,600 cash stipend' (subject to program terms) and access to Anthropic-run workshops: Undergrads → Claude Builder Club (run a campus AI builder club, guest speakers, hackathons; resources shared with members include 'API credits', amount not specified); Grad students → Claude Campus Conversations (AI-and-society discussion groups, office visits); PhD/Postdoc → Claude Science workshops (researcher community, 'Claude for Science workshops'). 'Applications open September 1 and close September 12,' rolling review; program runs 'from September 2026 to June 2027' as a full school-year program. 'No. It's free to apply and free to participate.' Current status: 'The program is closed for Fall 2026.'
findings.eligibility: Students anywhere in the world; 18+ with work authorization in the country of study; 'AI fluency and Claude proficiency' expected but no expert background; grad/PhD tracks 'may select from a smaller pool of schools' during the pilot. No .edu email or student ID explicitly stated. No expert AI background required.
findings.claim: Apply during the stated window (Sep 1–12 of the program year) via the page form at claude.com/programs/campus; rolling review; returning ambassadors must reapply and flag prior status. The current Fall 2026 round is closed — watch for the next cycle's announcement.
findings.expiry: Program year runs Sep 2026–Jun 2027; closed now (Fall 2026 round ended Sep 12, 2026); no automatic renewal — past ambassadors reapply each cycle. Next cycle date not published as of today.
findings.gotchas: The stipend is a cash payment for ambassador work (club/event running), not a research grant. 'API credits' shared with undergrad club members have no published dollar amount. 'Work authorization in your country of study' may limit international students without local work rights.

findings.name: Claude for Teachers — free premium features for US K-12 educators
findings.detail: Official page (read today): 'US K-12 educators and districts get free access to premium Claude features, like teaching skills and a connection to evidence-based curricula.' Includes curriculum connectors (e.g., Learning Commons), teaching-workflow skills; 'Models are never trained on your conversations.' Districts get centrally managed accounts with RBAC and SSO plus K-12 terms and a student data privacy agreement. 'Sign up by June 30, 2027 for your full year of free access.' 'Extra usage limits apply.'
findings.eligibility: US K-12 educators and school districts only (region-limited to the US). Individual teachers verify identity at claude.ai/teachers; districts enroll 'every educator on your school or district domain.' No .edu email requirement per se (verification-based).
findings.claim: Teachers: click 'Verify now' on claude.com/solutions/teachers → identity verification at claude.ai/teachers. Districts: district-domain enrollment (K-12 terms/privacy agreement).
findings.expiry: Sign up by June 30, 2027 for a full year of free access; price/plans subject to change at Anthropic's discretion. Free access duration per sign-up is one school year (rolling annual, per 'full year of free access').
findings.gotchas: No API access — it's a consumer/education product offering (web/desktop chat), not an API/developer free tier. US-only. 'Extra usage limits apply' — premium features still have caps.

findings.name: Claude for Open Source — 6 months of free Claude Max 20x for maintainers
findings.detail: Official page (read today): '6 months of free Claude Max 20x' — a subscription for the Claude apps and Claude Code, not an API credit. Overage beyond Max limits billed at standard rates; when it ends 'your account returns to the free plan' (or resumes prior paid plan). Six qualifying thresholds (any one): (1) 500+ dependent repos or 100+ dependent packages, or 200,000+ combined monthly registry downloads; (2) committer/maintainer of a recognized foundation or language project (CPython, Rust team, Node.js TSC, Apache PMC, CNCF, Kubernetes, Linux kernel, Django, Rails, or similar); (3) 100+ merged PRs into repos you don't own in the last 12 months; (4) one of your repos with 20+ unique external contributors (merged PRs, last 12 months); (5) OpenSSF criticality score >= 0.4 on a repo you maintain; (6) discretionary 'ecosystem impact' catch-all. Baseline requirements (secondary, Sept-2026-checked): GitHub account 2+ years old, public activity in prior 90 days, OSI-approved license, 18+. A Sept-2026-checked tracker adds: cap of 10,000 approved recipients and a 90-day activation window on the approval link.
findings.eligibility: Open-source maintainers/contributors meeting one threshold; not limited to students or startups — relevant to students who maintain OSS projects. Criteria were overhauled in July 2026 (the older '5,000+ stars / 1M+ npm downloads' gate was replaced by these six thresholds).
findings.claim: Apply now at claude.com/contact-sales/claude-for-oss ('Apply now' CTA; form mechanics beyond that not detailed on the page). Approved maintainers get an activation link (use within 90 days per secondary source).
findings.expiry: Subscription lasts 6 months; 'complimentary subscription ends' with a reminder email beforehand; account falls back to Free plan after. No program sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Subscription, not API credit — does not fund API-based products. Overage after Max limits costs standard Max rates. A separate linked Terms document (anthropic.com/claude-for-oss-terms) governs details not shown on the page.

findings.name: API code execution free hours (platform feature, de-facto free tier)
findings.detail: Official API pricing docs (read today): the code execution tool — used without web search/web fetch — gives 'Each organization receives 1,550 free hours of usage per month' (equivalent to the pricing page's '50 free hours of usage daily per organization'); beyond that it's $0.05/hour per container, 5-minute minimum. Also: 'Code execution is free when used with web search or web fetch' (no extra charge beyond token costs).
findings.eligibility: Any organization/account using the first-party API (console account); no CC-only gate mentioned for the feature, but API billing overall is arrears-based and a payment method is needed for charged usage.
findings.claim: Use the code execution tool in API requests; the free 1,550 h/month allotment applies per organization automatically.
findings.expiry: Ongoing monthly allowance; no sunset published.
findings.gotchas: Token usage (input/output) is still billed normally — the free part is container runtime only. If files are included in the request, execution time is billed even if the tool isn't called (files preloaded onto the container).

findings.name: Claude via AWS Bedrock using AWS Activate credits (startup free-compute route)
findings.detail: Anthropic's own program excludes Bedrock/Vertex for its credits, but startups can reach Claude through AWS Activate: founders tier $1,000–$5,000 self-funded (pre-Series B, founded within last 10 years; AWS says 'you'll hear back within 5–10 business days'); portfolio/VC-accelerator tier up to $200,000 via a VC or accelerator with an AWS Org ID; invite-only 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' tier $200,000+. The AWS Activate FAQ (checked Sept 2026) states credits 'are also redeemable for third-party models on Amazon Bedrock... like AI21 Labs, Anthropic, Cohere.' Counterpoint: Google for Startups credits are NOT usable for third-party models on Vertex, and Microsoft Foundry docs list credit-based accounts as unable to use Claude — so AWS is the viable credit path to Claude on a hyperscaler.
findings.eligibility: Startups pre-Series B, founded within the last 10 years (AWS Activate); US global eligibility per AWS program terms; region limits apply to AWS accounts. Not a student program (student routes on AWS are separate, e.g., AWS Educate — not verified today).
findings.claim: 1) Apply for AWS Activate at aws.amazon.com/activate (self-serve or via your VC/accelerator); 2) claim the Org-ID-based credits; 3) enable Amazon Bedrock in your AWS account and select Anthropic Claude models; 4) spend Activate credits on those model calls.
findings.expiry: Activate credit expiry is per-AWS-timer rules (typically fixed windows per tier, not re-verified today). No Anthropic-side expiry on Bedrock usage; AWS Bedrock usage pricing differs from first-party API pricing.
findings.gotchas: Secondary source (checked 2026-09-25) — re-verify amounts on aws.amazon.com/activate before relying on them. Bedrock Claude pricing, rates and model availability differ from the first-party API; egress/data-transfer and Bedrock service fees can erode the credit value (data/egress costs gotcha). Anthropic startup credits cannot be used on Bedrock/Vertex — the two credit pools don't mix.

findings.name: External Researcher Access program — $1,000 API credits for AI-safety researchers
findings.detail: A Sept-2026-checked tracker lists 'External Researcher Access: $1,000 in API credits' for AI safety researchers, reviewed monthly, with 'more for rare special cases.' The official page could not be located today (candidate URLs 404'd; the claude.com programs footer lists only Campus, Frontier Academy, Scientists, and Startups), so treat the dollar figure as unverified against a primary source.
findings.eligibility: External AI-safety researchers (individuals/researchers, distinct from the institution-based AI for Science program); exact criteria not published on a locatable official page as of today.
findings.claim: Per the secondary tracker: submit a short application/request for external researcher access (monthly review); if approved, $1,000 in API credits is added to the account. Locate the canonical form via Anthropic support or the AI-safety research channel.
findings.expiry: Monthly review cycle; no published sunset.
findings.gotchas: Secondary-source only — the amount and even the program name may have changed by now; do not quote it as official without re-verifying.

findings.name: Menlo Anthology Fund — investment + Anthropic credits for pre-seed/Series A startups
findings.detail: A $100M fund run by Menlo Ventures with Anthropic: investment 'starting at $100,000' at pre-seed through Series A, bundled with Anthropic API credits. The fund's own page was internally inconsistent when checked (Aug 2026): body text says '$25,000 in free credits' while its FAQ says '$30,000 in free Anthropic credits.' Applications via an Airtable form on a rolling basis; Menlo promised responses within two weeks.
findings.eligibility: Pre-seed to Series A startups picked by Menlo; equity is taken (it is an investment, not a grant).
findings.claim: Apply via the Airtable form at menlovc.com/menlo-anthology-fund/; if selected, the investment closes with bundled Anthropic credits. Alternatively, startups already backed by Anthropic's partner VCs can claim up to $100,000 in additional API credits 'through your VC' (stated on the official Claude Startups page read today).
findings.expiry: No published sunset; application form rolling; page last updated Aug 2026.
findings.gotchas: Equity dilution cost — this is a venture investment, not a free grant. Credit amount conflict ($25K vs $30K) on the fund page; confirm at close. The VC-claim path for up to $100K (official Claude Startups page) is the better-verified number.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, confirmed today on official pages: (1) Claude Startups was EXPANDED on Oct 6, 2026 (free year of Claude Team up to 5 Premium seats + $1,000 one-time API credit + $45K Startup Stack + up to $100K via partner VCs), but within days (~Oct 9–13) Anthropic PAUSED the free Team/credit offers after ~21x expected applications ('currently over capacity'; all applications re-reviewed), and the official page now (Oct 22) says 'Our current cohort is now full, and we're not accepting new applications right now' — the program continues for existing members; the benefit line items were dropped from the live page. Next cohort is TBA (newsletter signup is the only official channel). findings.claim: Create any Firebase project in the console; it is on the Spark plan by default — nothing to enable. To get the paid free-tier extras (Cloud Functions, Cloud Storage, Firestore on Blaze), upgrade to Blaze (a Google billing account is needed). No separate application.
findings.detail: Firebase Spark is a free-forever, no-payment-method plan. Read today on firebase.google.com/pricing. Per-product no-cost amounts: Cloud Firestore 1 GiB storage, 20K writes/day, 50K reads/day, 20K deletes/day, 10 GiB/month egress; Realtime Database 1 GB stored, 100 simultaneous connections, 10 GB/month downloaded; Firebase Hosting 10 GB storage + 360 MB/day data transfer; Authentication ~50K MAU no-cost (on Blaze); Cloud Functions 2M invocations/mo, 400K GB-seconds/mo, 200K CPU-seconds/mo, 5 GB/mo outbound; Cloud Storage 5 GB stored + 100 GB/mo downloaded (us-central1/west1/east1 for .firebasestorage.app); App Hosting free from 1 Aug 2025 (10 GiB/mo uncached bandwidth, 5 GB storage). Analytics, Crashlytics, App Distribution, Remote Config, App Check, In-App Messaging, Performance Monitoring, FCM, Firebase AI Logic, and Test Lab (10 virtual + 5 physical device tests/day) are no-cost on Spark.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone with a Google account — no .edu email, no startup status, no funding cap, no region restriction stated. No credit card required to stay on Spark.
findings.expiry: Free forever; limits are perpetual but Google may change them. No renewal needed.
findings.gotchas: Quotas apply at the PROJECT level, not per app/resource. The listed Firestore/Functions/Storage free numbers are attached to the Blaze (pay-as-you-go) free-usage pool; on pure Spark some of these (Cloud Functions, Cloud Storage, Phone Number Verification) are marked 'not applicable', so the managed-DB free tier for Firestore/RTDB is the guaranteed free-forever part. Phone Auth is not on Spark. Egress/download and storage beyond free limits bill at GCP rates. Blaze requires a billing account and overages bill automatically.
findings.name: Firebase Spark free tier (free-forever managed DB + data platform)

findings.claim: Sign up at cloud.google.com 'Start free trial' with a GCP account; enter a valid credit/debit card (authorization, not a charge). The $300 credit is auto-attached to a new Free Trial billing account; use it on GCP/Firebase over the 90 days. Upgrade to a paid account only if you want to keep resources running and keep the unused credit until it expires.
findings.detail: Google Cloud Free Trial (Blaze) grants $300 of welcome credit valid for 90 days to NEW GCP users. Read today on cloud.google.com/signup-faqs and docs.cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-cloud-features. During the 90 days no charges; you also get the GCP Free Tier. The account auto-closes on credit exhaustion or 90 days; a 30-day grace period follows before resources are permanently deleted. $300 CANNOT be spent on Gemini API costs in AI Studio, managed 'model-as-a-service' partner models, VM GPUs, Marketplace, Windows-Server VMs, or crypto mining. Multiple people in one org can each get $300 if each is a first-time GCP/Maps/Firebase payer.
findings.eligibility: You have NEVER been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase, and have never signed up for this Free Trial. A credit card / other payment method is REQUIRED at signup (for identity verification; a pending $0–$1 authorization, not a charge). India requires an INR-denominated Cloud billing account first.
findings.expiry: $300 credit and the trial expire 90 days from signup (whichever comes first: credit used or 90 days). 30-day grace period after closure, then resources deleted.
findings.gotchas: This is the key trial-vs-free gotcha: unlike Spark, a credit card IS required here. Free Trial billing is NOT a free-forever plan; it is a time-boxed credit. Remaining credit is lost unless you upgrade to paid within 90 days. Over-free-tier usage beyond the credit bills automatically once you upgrade.
findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial — $300 credit (Blaze)

findings.claim: Available automatically to any GCP/Firebase customer — no application. Within a paid or trial account, just stay under the monthly free caps; usage is billed only above them.
findings.detail: GCP 'Always Free' tier (20+ products, no expiry) that stacks on top of Firebase. Read today via cloud.google.com/free (page quoted in search). Includes Firestore 1 GB storage; Cloud Run / Cloud Run functions 2 million requests or invocations per month; BigQuery 1 TB queries/month + 10 GB storage; Compute Engine 1 e2-micro + 30 GB; Cloud Storage 5 GB-months; Cloud Build 120 min/day; Secret Manager 6 versions; Pub/Sub 10 GB/month; Cloud KMS Autokey; plus AI API free tiers.
findings.eligibility: All eligible GCP customers (free tier does not expire and is not charged against the $300 credit). No .edu, no startup status, no CC required for the free tier itself.
findings.expiry: No expiry; free monthly caps are permanent but subject to change.
findings.gotchas: These caps do NOT bill against the $300 trial credit; overages bill at pay-as-you-go GCP rates. BigQuery is a sandbox/free-tier only within caps; managed partner AI models and Gemini API are excluded from trial credit. Details here come from an official page surfaced via search (not a direct full-page read today), hence medium confidence.
findings.name: Google Cloud 'Always Free' Free Tier (20+ products, perpetual)

findings.claim: Enable Firebase SQL Connect / Cloud SQL in a project on Spark; the first Cloud SQL instance is no-cost for 3 months. To keep it, upgrade to Blaze (and the free-usage pool applies: 10 GiB/month egress, 250K ops/month).
findings.detail: SQL Connect (Firebase's managed Cloud SQL access for app data) offers a 3-month no-cost trial for your first Cloud SQL instance: 330 MiB/day egress and ~8,300K ops/day during the trial. After the trial, if the project has not moved to Blaze, the instance is archived and then deleted ~90 days later. On Blaze the ongoing free-usage is 10 GiB/month egress + 250K operations/month.
findings.eligibility: Any Firebase project user; first Cloud SQL instance per project.
findings.expiry: 3-month trial only, then instance archived and deleted 90 days after if not on Blaze. This is NOT free-forever.
findings.gotchas: Time-boxed trial — a real data loss risk: the instance is archived after 3 months and hard-deleted after another 90 days if you haven't paid. Upgrading to Blaze requires a billing account.
findings.name: SQL Connect (Cloud SQL) 3-month free trial

findings.claim: Apply through Google's startup portal (historically cloud.google.com/launch / startup.cloud.google.com / 'for-startups'). As of 2026-10-22 all three known URLs returned 404, so confirm the live application URL and current terms before relying on this.
findings.detail: The Google Cloud Startup Program (rebranded over time through 'Launch Lab'/'Launch') has historically granted up to ~$200,000 in GCP credits over 12 months, plus additional partner credits, to qualifying startups building on GCP — with Firebase workloads eligible (they bill into the same GCP project). Reported historical eligibility: company founded within ~5 years, total funding raised at or below a cap (~$30M–$100M depending on cycle), headquartered in a participating country, not public. These figures/limits shift per application cycle and I could NOT re-verify them today (page 404s), so treat them as historical estimates, not confirmed current terms.
findings.eligibility: Startups (not students): early-stage, unfunded or below a funding cap, within an age window, in an eligible country. Not a .edu program. No credit card needed to receive partner credits once accepted.
findings.expiry: Credits typically valid for the award window (historically ~12 months) and are not auto-renewed; re-application is per cycle.
findings.gotchas: UNVERIFIED as of 2026-10-22 — the program pages (cloud.google.com/launch, /for-startups, /programs/startup) all returned 404, indicating the program was renamed/restructured or discontinued at those paths. Do not quote the $200K figure as current without re-confirming the live URL. GCP credits are distinct from the Firebase Spark free tier.
findings.name: Google Cloud Startup Program / Launch (credit grant for startups)

findings.claim: Apply via the Google Cloud for Education / 'Apply for Google Cloud credits' path (linked from edu.google.com to cloud.google.com/edu), signing in with an institutional Workspace for Education or verified .edu account. Confirm the live page and current figures before relying on this — they were not independently verified today.
findings.detail: Reported Google Cloud for Education program: an educator credit (historically ~$1,000 of GCP credit, valid ~12 months, renewable with a minimum-activity condition) plus per-student classroom credits when a Google Classroom is linked to the educator's GCP project. Because Firebase bills into the same GCP project, the credit can cover Firebase paid features (and the Spark free tier remains free regardless). I could NOT verify the exact dollar amounts, the .edu requirement, or renewal policy today: the official edu.google.com page is a landing overview that only links to 'Apply for Google Cloud credits', and the deeper edu page fetch was truncated, so these numbers are unconfirmed general-knowledge estimates.
findings.eligibility: K-12 / higher-ed educators and their students who use Google Workspace for Education; typically requires an institutional/.edu (or country TLD like .ac.uk) account rather than a personal Gmail. Not a free tier for general students.
findings.expiry: Reported ~12-month credit window, renewable if activity is maintained; unconfirmed.
findings.gotchas: LOW CONFIDENCE: no dedicated 'Firebase for students' free license was found; the education benefit is a GCP credit for educators, not a per-student Firebase entitlement. Figures here are unverified — re-check the live cloud.google.com/edu page. There is no confirmed .edu-only free tier distinct from the GCP education credit.
findings.name: Google Cloud for Education / Classroom credits (for students & educators)

provider: Google Firebase — Firebase Spark free plan (managed databases & data platforms)
sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes: (1) The Google Cloud Startup Program / Launch pages (cloud.google.com/launch, /for-startups, /programs/startup) all returned 404 as of 2026-10-22 — the program appears renamed, restructured, or discontinued at those paths, so its historical ~$200K/12-month credit and startup-eligibility caps could not be re-verified and should be treated as historical. (2) No dedicated 'Firebase for students' free-forever license exists; the education route is a GCP educator/classroom credit (unverified figures), not a Firebase-specific entitlement. (3) Firebase-specific 2025–2026 updates noted on the pricing page: App Hosting free usage began 1 Aug 2025; Remote Config moves to tiered pay-per-request pricing from 1 Sep 2026 (currently free at 100K requests/day). (4) The Spark free tier itself (Firestore 1 GB/20K writes, RTDB 1 GB/100 conns, Hosting 10 GB/360 MB-day, Auth ~50K MAU) remains free-forever with no sunset. (5) The $300 GCP Free Trial is still the primary 'trial credit' but requires a credit card and is time-boxed to 90 days — it is not a perpetual free offer.

provider: Turso (managed-db) — distributed/libSQL SQLite platform; official site now turso.tech (turso.io no longer resolves). Acquired by Supabase on 2026-10-02.

findings.name: Turso Free Plan (permanent free tier)
findings.detail: Free forever, $0/month, no trial window and no trial credits. Verified today (2026-10-22) on the official pricing page: 100 databases; 5 GB total database storage; 500 million rows read/month; 10 million rows written/month; 3 GB monthly embedded syncs; 1-day point-in-time restore; community support. Overage rates (apply once overages are enabled): storage $0.75/GB, rows read $1/billion, rows written $1/million, syncs $0.35/GB. Point-in-time restore and database branching add no usage charge; idle databases cost only storage.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone (individuals, students, companies); no .edu email, no minimum-age, no funding requirements. Sign up with GitHub. Credit card NOT required (page states 'Start free, no credit card required'). No region restriction is published for the free plan; you choose the primary location of each database. Commercial use on Free is allowed with no per-seat or revenue cap.
findings.claim: 1) Go to turso.tech and sign up (GitHub login). 2) The Free plan is applied automatically — no activation, no coupon. 3) Create databases via dashboard or `turso db create` CLI. 4) Connect with SDKs (@libsql/client etc.) or the stateless HTTP API. Optional: enable/disable 'Overages' in billing settings to control what happens past quotas.
findings.expiry: No expiry — standing $0/month tier with no end date and no renewal. (Contrast: third-party pages that call it a '365-day student grant' are wrong; the grant framing is aggregator content, not Turso's.)
findings.gotchas: Task's pre-known numbers are stale: 9 GB belongs to the paid Developer plan, the free tier is 5 GB; '1 GB egress' no longer exists — Turso meters rows read/written and syncs, not GB of egress. The first limit you hit is 10M rows written/month (~333k writes/day). A full-table-scan SELECT costs one row-read per row, so unindexed queries burn the 500M read quota fast. If overages are disabled, hitting a cap blocks that metric instead of billing. Free plan has no audit logs, no DPA/IP allow lists/SSO (paid-only features). Edge read replicas were stopped for new accounts in Jan 2025; embedded replicas (sync to a local SQLite file, included in the 3 GB sync quota) are the replacement. No trial credits are granted to new accounts.

findings.name: Turso Startup Program (Turso for Startups)
findings.detail: Launched 2026-05-11. For early-stage venture-backed startups: 'generous Turso credits' (dollar amount NOT published — sized at approval), plus priority access to Turso's engineering team for onboarding and architecture reviews, early access to unreleased features, and co-marketing (blog features, case studies). Verified today on the official turso.tech/startups page.
findings.eligibility: All three published criteria: (1) venture-backed startup with at least one round of funding; (2) building an early-stage product or actively scaling; (3) verifiable funding from recognized investors or accelerators. No company-age limit and no funding-cap published; bootstrapped/unfounded startups do NOT qualify under published criteria (they can use the free tier). No .edu/education track — the program explicitly targets VC-backed founders. Credit card not required to apply.
findings.claim: 1) Open https://turso.tech/startups and fill in the application form (full name, company email, role, startup description, year founded, major investor/accelerator, latest round). 2) Applications reviewed on a rolling basis; Turso typically responds within a few business days. 3) Once accepted, credits are applied to your account and you start building immediately.
findings.expiry: Credit amount and spend window are not published. Confirm the dollar value and activation/expiry dates in writing at approval; unused credit balances on programs like this are typically forfeited, and after credits run out you move to standard usage-based pricing (Developer $4.99/mo billed yearly, $5.99 monthly, then overages).
findings.gotchas: Amount 'set at approval' — do not plan budgets around it. Review is selective (VC-backed, verifiable funding), not automatic. Program page carries no published terms page; co-marketing is an opportunity, not a guarantee. After the 2026-10-02 Supabase acquisition, watch for the program migrating into Supabase's ecosystem — the page was live as of today, but terms may consolidate.

findings.name: Student / education offer: none exists (free tier is the de-facto student offer)
findings.detail: No Turso education license, no .edu-verified student program, no student discount page exists. Searches of turso.tech (pricing, startups, partners, blog) surface no education offer; the free tier described in finding 1 is what students use, and it is open to anyone without verification. Third-party 'Turso student deal' listings (e.g., The Modelverse, agentdeals) merely repackage the free tier and add fabricated '365-day grant / .edu verification' framing that Turso does not state.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no student eligibility criteria because no student program exists. Free tier requires no .edu email and no verification of any kind.
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim beyond the free-tier signup (finding 1).
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Do not cite aggregator 'student deal' pages (thefreebie/Modelverse/agentdeals-style): they invent verification steps and expiry dates ('Oct 17, 2027 tripwire', '365-day grant') that are not in Turso's official pages. Only turso.tech is authoritative.

findings.name: Trial credits for new accounts: none
findings.detail: No time-boxed trial credits (e.g., $X for 30 days) are offered on the official pricing page or blog. The only credits on the table are the unpublished startup-program credits (finding 2). New accounts simply get the free tier; paid plans start at Developer $4.99/mo billed yearly ($5.99 monthly), Scaler $24.92 ($29 monthly), Pro $416.58 ($499 monthly), Enterprise custom.
findings.eligibility: N/A
findings.claim: N/A
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: If a vendor page advertises a 'free trial with credits' for Turso, treat it as aggregator noise unless it links turso.tech terms.

sunset_notes: Major changes 2025–2026: (1) 2025-03-31 free-tier restructure (announced in Turso's 'Turso Cloud Debuts the New Developer Plan' blog): free storage cut 9 GB → 5 GB, free rows read cut to 500M/month and rows written to 10M/month, in exchange for no more cold starts / always-on free databases; the $9 Hobby plan was replaced by the $4.99 (yearly) / $5.99 (monthly) Developer plan (AWS regions only — Fly.io users had to migrate). So any source quoting '9 GB free' or '1 GB egress / 5 regions' describes the pre-2025 tier. (2) Jan 2025: edge read replicas stopped being offered to new accounts; embedded replicas (local SQLite file sync) replaced them, metered under the 3 GB free sync quota. (3) Some 2025 aggregator pages claim a 'Database Freedom Day' bump to 500 databases / 9 GB free — the official page checked today shows 100 databases / 5 GB, so that claim is unsupported. (4) 2026-09-13 pricing page restructure: tiers renamed/organized to Free, Developer, Scaler, Pro, Enterprise with yearly-discount pricing shown by default ('Save $1/month' style). (5) 2026-10-02: Supabase announced it is acquiring Turso (alongside a $150M round led by GIC); Turso says the platform, databases, APIs and free tier continue as-is, open source stays open, with a planned graduation path into Supabase Postgres/Multigres and deeper integration 'in the coming months' — no sunset of any free offer announced as of 2026-10-22, but the startup program and free-tier terms are worth re-checking after the deal closes. (6) Domain: the task's starting URL turso.io/pricing fails DNS (ENOTFOUND); the official domain is turso.tech — treat turso.io as defunct.

provider: MongoDB Atlas (managed-db; fronts: Managed Databases & Data Platforms)

findings.name: Atlas Free tier ("Free cluster", formerly M0)
findings.detail: Free-forever managed cluster: $0/hour. 512 MB (0.5 GB) storage, shared vCPU/RAM, up to 100 ops/s (reads+writes combined), 500 max connections, 100 databases / 500 collections, 32 MB sort-in-memory, 50-stage aggregation pipelines, no temp-file-to-disk (allowDiskUse ignored). Egress: not billed, but capped at 10 GB in + 10 GB out per rolling 7-day window, with throttling + 1s cooldown when exceeded. Fixed 3-node replica set, no sharding, no private endpoints/VPC peering, no server-side JS, MongoDB 8.0 only (auto-upgrade, no manual version choice), deployable only in a subset of AWS/GCP/Azure regions. One Free cluster per project (more only via sales contract). Free cluster never expires; auto-paused after 30 days of zero-connection inactivity and may be deactivated under ToS; can be resumed unless pinned to an un-restorable old version. Auth limited to SCRAM, X.509, AWS IAM. Corrections to 'known so far': it is a 3-node replica set, not single-node; docs say daily-snapshot backups CAN be enabled on Free clusters (retains up to 4 snapshots) even though the pricing-page FAQ claims backups unavailable on Free.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone: free Atlas account, no .edu, no age/region gating stated. No credit card or payment method is documented as required for Free clusters (official pages are silent; sign-up flow does not state a card requirement).
findings.claim: Create a free account at mongodb.com/cloud/atlas/register -> create cluster choosing the Free tier -> add a database user and your IP address (or use `atlas setup` CLI). No payment step.
findings.expiry: Never expires. Paused after 30 days of zero-connection inactivity (resume anytime); long-idle clusters may be deactivated per ToS, so export data before long inactivity.
findings.gotchas: Free egress is capped (10 GB out per rolling 7 days), not unlimited; ops throttled at 100 ops/s; no continuous/hourly backups (docs: daily snapshot, 4-snapshot retention; pricing FAQ says no backups at all - contradictory sources); no private endpoints; fixed MongoDB 8.0; no log download, no Performance Advisor; one Free cluster per project; Atlas Charts on Free clusters is limited (dashboard auto-refresh every 4h, one scheduled report per project per week, since the 2 Jun 2025 pricing change).

findings.name: General trial credits / free trial for new users
findings.detail: No general free-trial or trial-credit offer found for ordinary new users. The official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22) lists only: the free-forever Free tier, MongoDB for Startups credits, MongoDB for Educators ($500), and the GitHub Student Developer Pack ($50). No dollar-amount trial with a time limit is offered; the Free tier itself is the perpetual on-ramp.
findings.eligibility: n/a (no offer found).
findings.claim: n/a - no claim path because no general trial/credit offer exists on official pages.
findings.expiry: n/a.
findings.gotchas: Don't confuse with the startup/educator/student credit programs (separate findings). Historically Atlas had promotional trials that are no longer advertised; absence verified on the current official pricing page.

findings.name: MongoDB for Startups program
findings.detail: Atlas credits in four tiers - Inspire (bootstrapped, 'baseline credits'), Grow (early-funded, 'expanded credits'), Innovate (VC-backed, 'additional credits'), Scale (rapidly scaling, 'maximum credits') - plus Voyage AI tokens (embedding/reranker), 1:1 expert sessions, and a Developer Support plan that is free for 30 days then $49/month (chargeable against credits). Exact credit dollar amounts are NOT published; they are disclosed in the acceptance email/promo code. Credits have a 12-month activation window from issuance, then must be used within 12 months of activation; they apply to future charges only; extensions case-by-case (contact startups@mongodb.com with >=3 months remaining; check balance/expiry at account.mongodb.com -> Billing -> Available Credits).
findings.eligibility: Company <7 years old; funding stage Series A or earlier (form allows up to 'Series B or higher', mapped to Scale tier); single software product/service; development shops and agencies explicitly excluded; first-time applicants only; active company website and LinkedIn profile; company email. No revenue cap stated.
findings.claim: Apply via the form on mongodb.com/startups, or get referred by your VC/accelerator/incubator. On acceptance: receive unique promo code by email -> log in at account.mongodb.com -> Billing -> 'Apply Code' -> enter Activation Code (must be Organization Owner or Organization Billing Admin). If no response in 5 business days, email startups@mongodb.com.
findings.expiry: 12 months to activate after issuance, then 12 months to use; extension possible case-by-case.
findings.gotchas: Amounts undisclosed until acceptance; credits do not cover retroactive usage; Developer Support costs $49/month after the free 30 days; one-time participation only; eligibility screening uses Pitchbook valuation data (Dec 2025 footnote).

findings.name: MongoDB for Students (via GitHub Student Developer Pack)
findings.detail: $50 in MongoDB Atlas credits, free MongoDB certifications valued at $150 via MongoDB University, access to MongoDB Compass, and a student community-forum support link. Distributed through the GitHub Student Developer Pack (listed under 'Infrastructure & APIs' on education.github.com/pack).
findings.eligibility: Must be at least 13 years old and enrolled in a degree- or diploma-granting program with a verifiable school email or documentation (per the MongoDB pricing-page card); eligibility is verified through GitHub's student-pack process (.edu email or other proof).
findings.claim: Sign in to the GitHub Student Developer Pack (github.com/education), claim the MongoDB voucher -> redeem the code in your MongoDB account to receive the $50 Atlas credit and University certification access. No credit card needed for the credit itself.
findings.expiry: No explicit credit-expiry stated on either official page; treat as subject to MongoDB's standard credit terms.
findings.gotchas: $50 is modest next to the free-forever M0 tier; certification value is a nominal $150 marketing figure; pack access requires GitHub student verification, which can fail with expired .edu accounts. The MongoDB-owned landing pages (mongodb.com/mongodb-for-students, /learn/education/students/licenses/) are 404 - the offer now lives only in the pricing page and the GitHub pack.

findings.name: MongoDB for Educators
findings.detail: $500 in free MongoDB Atlas credits, free MongoDB certifications valued at $150, plus access to educator community forums and events. Announced on the official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22) and on learn.mongodb.com/educators/ (page is JS-rendered; specifics could not be machine-read, so sub-details below are lower confidence).
findings.eligibility: Intended for educators (instructors/faculty teaching MongoDB or using it in courses); the exact eligibility definition (K-12 vs higher-ed, required affiliation) could not be confirmed from official text today.
findings.claim: Apply through the MongoDB University educators page (learn.mongodb.com/educators/); upon approval receive the $500 Atlas credit and free certification via your MongoDB account.
findings.expiry: No credit-expiry dates published on the pages fetched; subject to standard credit terms.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes found: (1) Feb 2025 - Atlas Flex tier ($8 base, capped ~$30/mo, 5 GB, burst up to 500 ops/s) launched and replaced the older Atlas Serverless and Shared tiers, which are gone; the Free tier was kept 'free forever'. (2) The 'M0' tier is now officially called the 'Free' cluster in docs and UI; docs pin Free clusters to MongoDB 8.0 with no manual version upgrades. (3) Idle Free clusters auto-pause after 30 days of zero-connection inactivity (a Mar 2025 community post cites a 60-day window, so the pause window was tightened to 30 days) and may be deactivated per ToS - a material change for 'free forever' expectations. (4) 2 Jun 2025 - Atlas Charts pricing change: M0 clusters got a restricted free Charts tier (dashboard auto-refresh every 4 hours, one scheduled report/project/week). (5) Legacy student/educator self-hosted license pages (e.g. learn.mongodb.com/.../students/licenses, mongodb.com/education which now 308-redirects to MongoDB University) are gone/redirected - the classic 'student license' free self-managed server offer appears sunset; student value is now delivered through the GitHub Student Developer Pack ($50 Atlas credits + $150 certifications) plus MongoDB University. (6) Backup availability on Free clusters is now documented (daily snapshot, up to 4 retained) despite the pricing-page FAQ still saying 'backups not available for the Free tier' - treat the FAQ as stale and verify in the console.
