provider: Microsoft (with Y Combinator / VC Investor Network partner front)

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — self-serve offer (no investor code)
findings.detail: Milestone-based Azure Startup credits, current structure per official docs dated May–Oct 2026: $200 starter credit immediately (LinkedIn identity check); after approval (~3 business days) $1,000 in credits valid 90 days; +$4,000 valid 180 days after business verification = $5,000 total at Milestone 2. Unlocks without separate applications: $25,000 (use 5+ Azure workloads, ~60 days sustained), $50,000 (7+ workloads, ~60 days), $150,000 (10+ workloads AND ~$3,000/month usage over ~60 days; each workload must stay >$1 spend for the full 60-day window; non-sequential skips allowed). One-time 2-year extension to use credits at the $25K milestone. Credits apply to eligible Azure services including Azure AI / Microsoft Foundry models.
findings.eligibility: Startup (or founder 'with an idea'): privately held for-profit, software-based product/service owned by the company, pre-seed through Series B / not Series C-or-later funding, HQ in a country where Microsoft for Startups operates, lifetime free Azure credits received <$350,000, not an educational institution/government/consultancy/agency, no cryptocurrency mining. Sign-in must use a personal consumer Microsoft account (work/school/company-domain emails rejected); phone number required. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: startups.microsoft.com (or microsoft.com/en/startups 'Get started now') → sign in with personal MS account → 'Continue without a code' → Verify with LinkedIn (personal, not business) → create Azure account (profile, billing address, payment card) → $200 unlocked → decision email in ~3 business days → $1,000 → complete business verification → $5,000. Credits viewable in Azure Portal > Cost Management + Billing > Payment methods. If declined: reapply after 14 days.
findings.expiry: Credits valid up to 2 years once activated (extensions not available except the one-time 2-year extension at the $25K milestone). Credits must be activated within 90 days of accepting the program agreement or the offer lapses and you must reapply. Subscription auto-converts to pay-as-you-go when credits are exhausted or expired. Cannot transfer credits between Microsoft accounts/subscriptions.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (identity verification, uncovered services, PAYG transition). Services not covered by credits, egress, or usage on a different billing profile still bill while credits remain. 'Already redeemed' error if your MSA previously redeemed another Microsoft program's credits. Country/region chosen at account creation cannot be changed later. The headline 'up to $150,000' is end-state: an unfunded solo startup realistically lands at $5,000 after verification. Trial-vs-free: this is a program, not a trial, but the first $200/$1,000 are time-boxed trial-style credits.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — Investor Network offer (referral code; YC/VC/accelerator front)
findings.detail: With a 10-character referral code from a Microsoft for Startups Investor Network partner (VC, accelerator, incubator, angel network, university), most startups begin with $100,000 in Azure credits 'with the opportunity to earn more', up to $150,000. Includes Azure Standard Support, technical expert access, go-to-market support, and free/discounted tools: GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn Premium Business, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Visual Studio Enterprise, Dynamics 365, Power Platform; higher levels add unlimited Azure Pairing consultations and Expert Network access plus third-party benefits.
findings.eligibility: Same company criteria as self-serve (privately held, for-profit, software-based, not Series C or later, <$350K lifetime free Azure credits, HQ in an MfS-supported region) PLUS a valid referral code; YC is an explicit partner — YC and M12 were first to access Microsoft's free GPU cluster preview (Nov 2023), and YC is among organizations that can supply codes. Microsoft does not publish the list of participating investors.
findings.claim: Ask your VC/accelerator (e.g., YC) for the 10-character code → startups.microsoft.com → enter code → verify contact email + phone → business info must exactly match legal documents (mismatches fail verification) → application review ~3 business days → $1,000 starter credits immediately → approval unlocks expanded credits/benefits. Alternatively 'Sign up here' via the investor-referral link on microsoft.com/en/startups.
findings.expiry: Same mechanics as self-serve: credits valid up to 2 years once activated; activation due within 90 days of acceptance; PAYG after exhaustion.
findings.gotchas: Benefits often cannot be redeemed on an existing enterprise account or on an account that previously redeemed the same benefit. YC-affiliated founders without YC's code only get the self-serve track. Business verification failure stalls the high-value tier. Credits locked to one MSA.

findings.name: YC / M12 free Azure GPU clusters (Founders Hub GPU program)
findings.detail: Free Azure AI infrastructure: high-end GPU virtual machine clusters for training/running LLMs and deep learning, delivered as a private preview. Announced 8 Nov 2023 with Y Combinator's cohort first (M12 portfolio next); 11 Jan 2024 Microsoft extended it to AI Grant Fund, Alchemist Accelerator, Conviction, The House Fund, OpenAI Startup Fund, Neo, and Elad Gil. This is the 'GPUs' element of the 2025–2026 successor framing to Startup Grad.
findings.eligibility: YC/M12 startups: limited preview cohort via the accelerator relationship — not a general self-serve application. Extension partners: founders 'affiliated' with the listed organizations.
findings.claim: No public self-serve claim: access flows through the YC/investor relationship and Founders Hub application (referral-code path above).
findings.expiry: Described as private preview; no public sunset date published. Availability may have changed since the 2024 announcements (unverified in 2026).
findings.gotchas: Cohort-based and capacity-limited; GPU access is separate from Azure credit tiers; 'free' applies to the preview infrastructure, not necessarily to all surrounding egress/storage. Do not assume a YC alum can self-claim in 2026 — confirm with YC/Microsoft.

findings.name: Azure free account — $200 trial credit + 12-month free services
findings.detail: $200 credit usable on Azure services within 30 days; 12 months of free monthly amounts for 20+ popular services (750 hrs each of B1s/B2pts v2/B2ats v2 VMs; 750 hrs PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server B1MS with 32 GB storage+backup; 720 vCore-hrs SQL Managed Instance; 1 ACR Standard registry with 100 GB; 1M Function requests/mo; etc.); plus 65+ always-free services with free monthly amounts (Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB, App Service 10 web apps, Container Apps 180k vCPU-seconds, etc.), which continue after 12 months at their monthly limits.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers; one free-account offer per person; phone number and a credit card or non-prepaid debit card required (credit card only in HK/Brazil); Microsoft or GitHub account.
findings.claim: azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free → 'Try Azure for free' → 3-step account creation (profile/country, billing address, payment card) → $200 usable for 30 days.
findings.expiry: $200 credit expires at 30 days (unused credit persists only within the 30-day window); 12-month free service amounts end at 12 months → pay-as-you-go for overages; always-free service amounts continue indefinitely.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free: the 'free forever' services keep their monthly caps after the trial; 'spending protection' means the card is not charged while the offer is active (a temporary $1 authorization may post and reverse), not that no card is needed. After expiry the sponsorship subscription auto-converts to PAYG with no commitment. Egress/data beyond free amounts is billed. A .edu email does NOT upgrade this offer (student Azure access comes via the GitHub Pack instead).

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack (incl. Azure for students, no credit card)
findings.detail: Free GitHub Pro while a student; GitHub Copilot for verified students (unlimited completions + AI-credit allowance, limited chat/agent); free Pro-level GitHub Codespaces; GitHub Pages (one user site); free domain offers (Namecheap .me + SSL 1 yr, Name.com free domain, .TECH 1 yr). Microsoft Azure track for 18+: 25+ Azure services free plus $100 Azure credit, explicitly 'no credit card required'. Track for ages 13–17: limited services (App Services, Functions, Notification Hubs, MySQL, Application Insights, Azure DevOps). Other partner benefits: Heroku (24 months), Datadog Pro (2 years), JetBrains, DataCamp, Notion, MongoDB, 1Password, ~50 more.
findings.eligibility: Current enrolled students (verified via .edu/school email or manual GitHub enrollment verification); separate age bands 18+ vs 13–17 for the Azure offers; the Azure portion is 'no credit card required', unlike the general free account.
findings.claim: Sign up at education.github.com/pack on a GitHub account, verify student status, then redeem each partner offer (Azure credit via the Azure redemption inside the pack).
findings.expiry: Benefits last while student status is verified; individual partner offers carry their own time boxes (e.g., domains 1 yr, Heroku 24 mo, Datadog 2 yr).
findings.gotchas: Redeeming the pack's Azure offer can make an MSA 'already redeemed' for other Microsoft program credits (see MFS FAQ). $100 is small — pair with MFS self-serve for more. Free Pro/Copilot stop when you're no longer a student. No explicit 2-year duration stated for the core pack itself.

findings.name: Microsoft 365 A1 for Education + limited-time college Premium offer
findings.detail: Free 'A1' plan (donated by Microsoft): web Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote plus PC-only Publisher and Access for educators/students of qualified K-12 and higher-ed institutions; no OneDrive quota or desktop apps stated on the page. Limited-time college offer: 12 months of Microsoft 365 Premium free using a college email. Paid institutional tiers for contrast: A3 ($3.25 faculty/$2.50 student per user/mo), A5 ($8/$6).
findings.eligibility: .edu/institutional email required — 'working at, or enrolled in, a qualified educational organization' (K-12 and higher ed); college Premium offer requires a college email. No credit card.
findings.claim: microsoft.com/en-us/education/products/office → 'Get started for students' (or 'for institutions'); automated email verification is usually instant, manual institution checks can take up to a month. College Premium: sign up with college email.
findings.expiry: A1 lasts while enrolled/employed; Premium college offer lasts 12 months, after which apps drop to reduced-functionality (view-only) mode.
findings.gotchas: A1 is web-centric: no full desktop suite and no stated 1 TB OneDrive. If the institution's plan lapses, existing files become view-only. 'Premium on us' is limited-time and regional — confirm availability.

findings.name: Visual Studio free tiers (Community, VS Code, Dev Essentials)
findings.detail: Visual Studio Community edition (current VS18-generation IDE) free for individual developers on Windows; VS Code free on Windows/macOS/Linux; 'Visual Studio Dev Essentials' bundle offering free tools, Pluralsight training, and Azure credit for free. This is the surviving student IDE path: the dedicated 'Visual Studio for Students' download no longer exists (visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-studio-for-students/ now returns 404 and the free-developer-offers page lists no student-specific program), consistent with Microsoft's 2025 shift to free IDE licensing for individuals.
findings.eligibility: Any individual developer, students included; no credit card; Dev Essentials is free via devessentials.microsoft.com. Community edition may not be used as an enterprise tool in large organizations (standard MS license terms).
findings.claim: visualstudio.microsoft.com/free-developer-offers/ → download Community or VS Code; Dev Essentials registration for the bundle + Azure credit.
findings.expiry: Licensing is ongoing while free; no time-boxed expiry for Community/VS Code. Dev Essentials Azure credit has its own (small, unspecified) duration.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: 'Visual Studio 2022 for individual developers' is now a permanent free edition, not a trial; VS Enterprise/for Teams are paid. If you specifically need the 'Visual Studio for Students' SKU, it is gone — students should use Community or VS Code.

findings.name: Azure OpenAI / Microsoft Foundry models — free rate-limited quota tier
findings.detail: Microsoft Foundry (Azure OpenAI) model quotas now run on seven tiers: Free Tier plus Tiers 1–6 with automatic upgrades based on usage/payment history. Free quota tables published per model (e.g., current docs: gpt-5 GlobalStandard ~1,000 RPM / 250,000 TPM; gpt-4o-mini GlobalStandard ~20,000 RPM / 2,000,000 TPM in the lowest tier; several models show 'N/A' for the Azure-for-Students/free-trials column, meaning no special free quota). MFS participants get model access 'through Microsoft Foundry' inside their startup credits.
findings.eligibility: Any Azure subscription; free tier available to new/free-trial accounts; no .edu requirement and no credit-card requirement beyond the underlying Azure account (which does need a card for the standard free account — the card-free student path is the GitHub Pack offer).
findings.claim: Create an Azure resource for Foundry/OpenAI and select the free deployment tier; MFS startups simply use their startup credits on the same Foundry endpoints.
findings.expiry: Rate limits, not a dollar allowance; the page documents no hard monthly token cap or end date for the free tier today (older 90-day time limit unverified on the current page); auto tier-upgrades can be opted out of (NoAutoUpgrade flag).
findings.gotchas: Rate limits can throttle heavy dev use; model availability is region-dependent; free-tier endpoints may exclude data retention guarantees paid tiers get; 'free tier' ≠ the $200 trial credit — it coexists with pay-as-you-go billing once limits are hit.

sunset_notes: 1) Startup Grad (Microsoft x YC, historical ~$50,000 Azure credits per YC company) is no longer offered: superseded by Microsoft for Startups Founders Hub (up to $150K via milestones/Investor Network, verified on official docs dated May–Oct 2026) plus the 8 Nov 2023 YC/M12 free GPU-cluster preview (extended 11 Jan 2024 to other incubators). The ~$50K figure could not be re-verified on any official Microsoft page today (secondary sources only), so the historical detail is low-confidence. 2) Major 2025 change (reported 2 Feb 2026 by theainewsdigest; corroborated by the current official docs' milestone structure): on 2 Jul 2025 Microsoft restructured Microsoft for Startups — the old four-level grid ($1K/$5K/$25K/$100K-up-to-$150K, where Level 1 gave every approved startup $1,000) was replaced by the milestone ladder (self-serve $200 → $5K → $25K → $50K → $150K) plus an Investor Network referral-code track (most investor-backed startups start at $100K). Unfunded startups effectively dropped from up to $150K to $5K total. Eligibility also shifted: lifetime-free-credit cap raised from $10K to $350K, and the funding ceiling moved from pre-Series D to pre-Series C. 3) 'Visual Studio for Students' appears sunset: its URL now 404s and the free-developer-offers page (fetched 2026-10-22) lists no student program; VS Community/VS Code are the free path (consistent with MS's 2025 move to free individual IDE licensing). 4) YC's 'successor' claim in the brief — 'up to $150K + AI Foundry + GPUs' — verified: up to $150K milestones on MFS docs, Microsoft Foundry model access inside MFS benefits, and the YC-first GPU cluster program (status in 2026 unconfirmed). Web search budget was exhausted mid-task; all 2026 items above were read directly from official pages today, except the 2 Jul 2025 restructuring (secondary source, corroborated by current docs).

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — Azure Startup Credits (milestone program, up to $150K)
findings.detail: Tiered 'Startup credits' on a sponsored Azure subscription: M1 $200 (sign up + verify with a personal LinkedIn account), M2 $5,000 (business verification: registered legal entity), M3 $25,000 (5+ Azure workloads active ~60 days; also grants a one-time 2-year extension to use credits), M4 $50,000 (7+ workloads ~60 days), M5 $150,000 (10+ workloads AND ~$3,000/month Azure usage ~60 days). The 60-day clock starts once each workload has at least $1 of spend; all required workloads must stay above $1/day for the full 60 days. Tiers are NOT sequential — accounts are auto-evaluated and upgraded, so a scaling startup can jump tiers. Credits apply to eligible Azure consumption, select first-party Microsoft Foundry models, and GitHub Copilot/Codespaces/Actions (only if the Azure subscription is connected as the GitHub billing method). When credits are exhausted or expire, the subscription auto-converts to pay-as-you-go.
findings.eligibility: B2B software/AI/tech startups, pre-seed through Series B (must NOT have raised Series C or later); privately held, for-profit, not a subsidiary; owns its software product; HQ in a country/region where the program operates (country/region is locked at sign-up and cannot be changed; unsupported country = offer unavailable); not an educational institution, government, consultancy, or agency; not involved in crypto mining; company has NOT received more than $350,000 in lifetime free Azure credits. Sign-in must use a personal consumer Microsoft account — work/school/company-domain emails are rejected.
findings.claim: 1) microsoft.com/en-us/startups → 'Get started now'; 2) sign in with a personal Microsoft account; 3) 'Continue without a code' (or enter a 10-char investor code, see separate finding); 4) verify identity with a personal LinkedIn account; 5) complete 3-step Azure account creation (profile, billing address, payment card); 6) 'Build your startup' dashboard shows $200 unlocked immediately (balance can lag up to 24h); 7) application reviewed in ~3 business days, decision by email; manage credits/portal in Azure Portal and MfS portal.
findings.gotchas: CREDIT CARD IS REQUIRED (non-optional: card number/expiry/CVV at sign-up; auto-converts to pay-as-you-go when credits run out or expire — no upfront commitment, subscription cancellable). Personal consumer email only. Country/region cannot be changed later. GitHub usage is NOT credit-covered out of the box — you must connect the Azure subscription as a GitHub payment method, and then only metered/eligible GitHub services draw on credits. Third-party (partner/community) Foundry models are separately billed and not covered. Egress and other metered Azure items are still billed through the credits, not free forever.
findings.expiry: M3 ($25K) grants a one-time 2-year extension of credit validity; otherwise no fixed validity per tier is published on the pages fetched — when credits are fully used or expired the subscription automatically becomes pay-as-you-go. Set Azure budgets/alerts; 'credits eventually run out' is Microsoft's own framing.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups Investor Network referral code ($1,000 starter credits, up to $200K cap, earlier tier unlocks)
findings.detail: Startups with a referral from a Microsoft for Startups Investor Network partner (VC/accelerator) enter a 10-character code during application and immediately unlock $1,000 in starter Azure credits instead of $200 while their application is under review. Per the benefits page (updated 2026-06-15), eligible Investor Network-backed startups may unlock up to $200,000 in Startup credits (vs the $150K standard cap) plus expanded support and third-party benefits, and 'may unlock higher-value benefits earlier in their journey'. Microsoft does not publish the list of participating investors.
findings.eligibility: Same base program eligibility (pre-seed→Series B B2B software startup etc.), PLUS the referral code from your VC/accelerator. Code is obtained directly from your investor — not issued publicly. Business name/address must match legal documents or business verification fails and acceptance is delayed.
findings.claim: 1) Ask your investor/accelerator for the 10-character code; 2) at microsoft.com/en-us/startups select Get started and enter the code; 3) verify contact email (code expires in 10 min) and phone number; 4) submit business information (registered name, industry, website, legal address); 5) complete Azure account setup — dashboard shows 'We're reviewing your application' with $1,000 in starter credits immediately available; 6) approval (~3 business days) unlocks expanded credits (up to $200K cap) and the full benefits package.
findings.gotchas: Code is not public and investor lists are not shared — ask your accelerator/VC directly. Mismatched legal name/address = failed business verification. The $1,000 is while the application is under review; higher tiers follow the same workload/usage milestones (M3–M5) as the standard track.
findings.expiry: Email verification code expires in 10 minutes. Credit/term rules follow the standard milestone program (2-year extension at the $25K milestone; auto pay-as-you-go on exhaustion).

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — free software/tool benefits (M365, GitHub Enterprise, Power BI, Dynamics, LinkedIn, GPU, support)
findings.detail: Technical benefits table (learn.microsoft.com, updated 2026-08-12): Microsoft 365 Business Premium 50 seats/1 year; GitHub Enterprise 20 seats/1 year; Power BI Pro 10 seats/1 year; Visual Studio 5 seats (until time in the MfS portal ends); Power Apps & Power Automate 10 seats/1 year; Dynamics 365 Customer Service & Sales Enterprise 10 seats/1 year; Dynamics 365 Team Member 25 seats/1 year; LinkedIn Premium Business 1 seat at 75% off for 4 months; 'Startup Cluster' short-term GPU access (ND H100, NDm A100 VMs, subject to availability); higher Azure OpenAI quota limits; ACA serverless GPU quota (2–7 day approval); 24/7 Azure Standard Support (normally ~$1,200/year); dedicated MfS point of contact; go-to-market benefits (Microsoft Marketplace, co-sell).
findings.eligibility: Approved Microsoft for Startups members (apply per the program; investor-backed startups get the expanded set). GPU/AI-access items are explicitly 'subject to availability' and gated by support tickets.
findings.claim: Sign in to the MfS portal / Azure Portal after approval; 'find, activate, and manage benefits' per the program docs; GPU VMs: request per Azure quota guidance (or ticket via the MfS portal including the Azure request number, 2–7 days); serverless GPUs: Azure Container Apps → Support ticket; AI limited-access features: formal registration then MfS ticket if not auto-approved.
findings.gotchas: GPU and AI quota benefits are availability-based, not guaranteed. Benefits are 1-year seats and must be re-earned/refreshed with program membership. Credits do not cover non-Azure products, Microsoft Support Plans, or Azure Marketplace purchases.
findings.expiry: Software seats: 1 year (Visual Studio: until MfS membership ends). LinkedIn discount: 4 months. GPU access: short-term/availability-based.

findings.name: Azure free account — $200 trial credit + 12-month free services + 65+ always-free services
findings.detail: Any new customer: $200 credit usable for 30 days; 20+ popular services free for monthly amounts for 12 months (e.g., 750 hrs of B1s/B2s burstable VMs, 750 hrs PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server B1MS + 32GB storage, 720 vCore-hrs SQL Managed Instance, Container Registry 100GB/10 webhooks, plus Azure DevOps 5 users, Functions 1M requests, Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25GB, App Service up to 10 web/API apps, Static Web Apps 100GB bandwidth + .5GB storage, AKS management free, AI Search 50MB/10,000 docs, etc.); 65+ 'always-free' services (Speech 0.5M neural chars/mo, Bot Service 10K premium msgs, Notification Hubs 1M pushes, API Management 1M calls, etc.) have no time limit. One $200-credit free offer per new customer.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers in one of 140 commercially available countries/regions. Sign-up requires a phone number and a credit or non-prepaid debit card (a ~$1 verification hold may appear and is reversed; credit cards only in Hong Kong and Brazil). Excludes sovereign clouds: US Government, Azure China, Azure Germany. No .edu, no age cap, no startup restriction.
findings.claim: azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free → 'Try Azure for free'; sign up with a Microsoft account (or 'Sign in with GitHub'); if you switch to pay-as-you-go before day 30, remaining credit stays valid for the full 30-day window.
findings.gotchas: CREDIT CARD REQUIRED — the free account is NOT a no-CC offer. After 30 days or credit exhaustion the account is disabled unless converted to pay-as-you-go; the 12-month free service amounts lapse after 12 months (service then bills metered). Data egress and non-free meters are always billed. Trial is 30-day; only the 'always-free' tiers are indefinite.
findings.expiry: $200 credit: 30 days. Free monthly amounts: 12 months. Always-free tiers: indefinite. Auto-convert/disability to pay-as-you-go after credit expiry.

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit + free cloud services, no credit card
findings.detail: Students get $100 in Azure service credits plus free access to popular cloud services and developer tools (Visual Studio, VS Code, AI/ML/data learning resources), 12-month-style free service access; via the GitHub Student Developer Pack the Azure offer is '25+ cloud services and $100 in Azure credit' for students 18+ (a separate 13–17 track exists). No credit card required and 'no need to enter a credit card' — eligibility is proven with a school email.
findings.eligibility: Current, verified students — sign up with your school/academic email; no CC. The GitHub Pack routes 18+ students to the main Azure offer and 13–17 to a separate offer. Faculty offer ($200 in past pages) could not be verified today (education pricing page now 404).
findings.claim: azure.microsoft.com/en-us/education → 'Start free' → verify with school email → $100 credit and free services available; or claim the Azure offer inside the GitHub Student Pack (github.com/settings/education/benefits).
findings.gotchas: No CC required (contrast with the $200 free account). Credit is not a subscription; separate from any pay-as-you-go account. Regional availability follows Azure availability.
findings.expiry: $100 credit: single allotment; free services tied to active student status. No renewal cycle published on the page fetched.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack — free GitHub Pro, Copilot, Codespaces + 100+ partner benefits (incl. Microsoft 365/1TB, Azure $100)
findings.detail: For verified students: free GitHub Pro; unlimited GitHub Copilot completions plus an allowance of GitHub AI Credits with limited chat/agent usage; free Pro-level Codespaces; GitHub Pages (1 site + unlimited project sites); Microsoft Azure $100 credit + 25+ services; Microsoft 365 productivity apps with AI + 1TB OneDrive; JetBrains subscription (renewed annually); MongoDB $50 Atlas credits + free certification; Datadog Pro (10 servers, 2 years free); 1Password free 2 years incl. Developer Tools; Heroku $13/mo for 24 months; Notion Education plan; free domains/SSL from Namecheap/Name.com/.TECH; 6–12 month access to Educative, FrontendMasters, Scrimba, DataCamp, Appwrite; learning bundles organized into 'Experiences' tiers.
findings.eligibility: Verified students via the GitHub Education portal (school academic email or institutional proof; 18+ main track, 13–17 separate track). No credit card needed for the pack itself.
findings.claim: Sign in to GitHub → github.com/settings/education → verify student status → claim offers from the benefits page ('All offers' listing, filterable by category).
findings.gotchas: Most benefits end when student status ends ('while you are a student'); specific durations vary (1 month–24 months); JetBrains requires annual renewal; Copilot access is 'limited chat and agent usage' under the student allowance, not full Copilot plans.
findings.expiry: Per-benefit: 1–24 months (Heroku 24 mo, Datadog/1Password 2 yr, learning platforms 1–12 mo, JetBrains annual). Pack © 2026; 2025–26 changes: new AI-partner additions (Camber, Boot.dev, ToDiagram) and the 'Experiences' bundle layer; several older standalone offers no longer listed.

findings.name: Microsoft 365 Education — free Office (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/OneDrive) with a school email
findings.detail: Students and faculty can get free Microsoft 365 with a verified school email: Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, Teams and ~100GB OneDrive (desktop + online apps). The microsoft.com/en-us/education landing page (fetched today) confirms 'student offers for Microsoft 365, GitHub, and Azure' are live; the detailed office-online offer page timed out on repeated fetch attempts, so the app list and storage figure are based on the long-standing offer structure rather than a page read today.
findings.eligibility: Currently enrolled students or faculty with a valid academic/school email (typically K-12/higher-ed .edu or national equivalents); no credit card, no payment details.
findings.claim: 1) microsoft.com/microsoft-365/education (or /education/office-online) → 'Get Office online with your school email'; 2) enter the school email; 3) verify; 4) download/sign in to desktop apps — renew annually.
findings.gotchas: Free tier is for personal/educational use — not a license for companies; OneDrive storage is far below the 1TB in the GitHub Student Pack's M365 benefit; page could not be fetched today (timeouts), so treat exact app/storage list as medium-confidence.
findings.expiry: Renewable annually while a student/faculty; benefits end when school-email status lapses.

findings.name: Microsoft 365 / Office Developer Program (Individual) — free development licenses, no credit card
findings.detail: For individual developers (not companies) building add-ins/extensions for Microsoft 365: free enrollment in a developer tenant with M365 E5-based developer licenses carrying hard service limits (e.g., ~25GB OneDrive per user; tenant refreshes every 30 days), plus Visual Studio and dev tooling access; no credit card and no cost. Intended for students/bootstrapping founders prototyping on M365. NOTE: today, multiple candidate URLs on developer.microsoft.com for this program returned 404 — the page structure appears to have moved; program terms could not be re-verified on an official page this session.
findings.eligibility: Individual developers only — companies/organizations are excluded (they need the paid Partner Developer Program); free Microsoft account; no credit card.
findings.claim: Enroll from the M365/Developer hub on developer.microsoft.com (Individual Developer Program); after enrollment the dev tenant (with limited E5 licenses, 30-day refresh) is provisioned; claimable without payment details.
findings.gotchas: Service quotas/limits apply per license (not full E5); the 30-day refresh resets data/usage limits; dev licenses are for development only, not production use; today's 404s on the program's sub-pages mean the exact quotas may have changed — verify on the live page before relying on specifics.
findings.expiry: Tenant refreshes every 30 days; benefits continue while enrolled.

provider: Xata (xata.io) — branch-native Postgres, managed-db front: Managed Databases & Data Platforms

findings.name: Xata Open Source (self-hosted, free forever)
findings.detail: Xata's core Postgres branching platform is open source under Apache 2.0 (github.com/xataio). Self-hosting it on your own infrastructure is $0 platform fee and includes copy-on-write branching, scale-to-zero (wake-up ~10s), OpenEBS/Mayastor storage and community support. It does NOT include managed observability, SOC 2/GDPR compliance, multi-region, or dedicated support — you operate your own cluster. This is the only PERMANENT free path; there is no permanent free hosted/managed tier.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card, no region restriction. Requires you to provision and operate your own infrastructure (Kubernetes + CloudNativePG + OpenEBS). Self-managed.
findings.claim: Free forever, no trial clock, no CC required. Clone the xataio GitHub org and deploy on your own cluster to use the platform at $0.
findings.expiry: None (permanent, Apache 2.0 open source).
findings.gotchas: It is self-hosted, not a managed service: you carry all ops burden, no multi-region, no SOC 2/HIPAA compliance tooling, no 24/7 support, and wake-up is ~10s (vs ~1s on managed Xata Cloud). The managed convenience (SOC 2, multi-region, dedicated support) requires paid Xata Cloud or BYOC.

findings.name: Xata Cloud 14-day free trial (managed)
findings.detail: The fully managed Xata Cloud (SOC 2/GDPR, multi-region on AWS+GCP) is offered as a 14-day free trial with NO credit card required during the trial. After the trial you must add a credit card to continue. Post-trial billing is pure usage: from $0.012/hr for a micro instance (<=2 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, ~$9/mo) up to $1.536/hr (32 vCPU, 128 GB), plus $0.28/GB/month storage billed by the minute. No per-branch or per-user fees; scale-to-zero means idle branches cost no compute.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who signs up at console.xata.io; email required, no credit card during the 14-day trial, no .edu or startup proof. A credit card IS required to keep using it after the trial. Managed Xata Cloud currently runs on AWS us-east-1 and eu-central-1 (third-party-reported), so US/EU regions apply.
findings.claim: Start the 14-day managed trial at console.xata.io; no card needed to begin. Add a card afterward to convert to pay-as-you-go.
findings.expiry: 14 days, then pay-as-you-go.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a free tier: the clock runs and a card is mandatory after 14 days. After the trial you still pay for compute hours plus $0.28/GB/mo storage — a side-project database that wakes up frequently keeps accruing cost, and idle branches still incur the storage line. The 'no CC required' promise applies only to the trial window. The docs (n8n quickstart) confirm: 'To keep using Xata after the free trial, add a credit card in the billing system.'

findings.name: Xata Cloud $100 onboarding / signup credit (unconfirmed)
findings.detail: Several 2026 third-party pricing trackers and the open-source release coverage describe a $100 onboarding/signup credit applied during the first 14 days of Xata Cloud. This credit is NOT shown on the live xata.io/pricing page nor in the machine-readable pricing.md I read today (both only state a '14-day free trial', no dollar figure), so its current availability is unconfirmed.
findings.eligibility: Reported as tied to new Xata Cloud signups / the trial; no .edu or startup proof found (unverified); a credit card is required to continue past the trial.
findings.claim: Reported as a '$100 onboarding credit (first 14 days)' by third-party trackers; not confirmed on the live official pricing page today. Verify via the signup flow or sales contact before relying on it.
findings.expiry: Reported as tied to the first 14 days / signup; unconfirmed.
findings.gotchas: Could not verify the amount against the live official pricing page or pricing.md today; the figure and whether it is still offered may have changed. Treat as unconfirmed. Corroborating third-party sources: srvrlss.io and dev.to coverage of the Apache 2.0 release both cite a '$100 signup credit' alongside the 14-day trial.

findings.name: Startup program / startup credits — not found
findings.detail: No dedicated Xata startup program or startup-only credit exists on the official site, and Xata does not appear in 2026 free-startup-credits aggregators (e.g., StudentPerks startup-credits list). Xata's free-adjacent offers are generic to everyone (open-source self-host, 14-day trial, the reported $100 credit), not gated on startup age or a funding cap.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no official startup program found; therefore no startup age or funding cap, because the program does not exist. A sales contact (cal.com/team/xata/xata-sales) is the only bespoke path.
findings.claim: No official startup program found as of 2026-10-22. Any discount for a startup would be via the generic 14-day trial (and the reported $100 credit) or a direct sales conversation.
findings.expiry: N/A (absence-based finding).
findings.gotchas: This is an absence finding, not a confirmed program. A third-party SaaSOffers page lists a generic 'free plan' as a startup deal, but that is an aggregator description, not an official Xata startup program. Confirm with Xata sales before assuming a startup offer exists.

findings.name: Education license / student (.edu) offer — not found
findings.detail: No Xata education license, .edu program, or student-specific offer was found on the official site or in 2025–2026 sources, and Xata is not listed in GitHub-Student-Developer-Pack-style aggregators. The only free paths available to a student are the same generic ones: open-source self-hosting (free, no CC) and the 14-day Xata Cloud trial.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no .edu email requirement because no education program was found; students are not treated differently from any other signer for the trial or OSS.
findings.claim: No official education/student license found as of 2026-10-22. Students get the same generic 14-day trial and open-source self-host path as anyone; no .edu credential is required or requested.
findings.expiry: N/A (absence-based finding).
findings.gotchas: Absence finding, not a confirmed offer. Verify with xata.io or Xata sales before concluding that no education program exists.

sunset_notes: Major 2025–2026 sunset/change: the permanent free hosted tier that students/startups relied on is GONE. Xata's original product was a hosted 'serverless data platform' (spreadsheet-style UI, REST/TypeScript data API, full-text search, file attachments over Postgres) that shipped a permanent free tier with 15 GB of storage, no cold starts and no pausing. Sunset timeline: (1) On January 10, 2025 Xata pulled the search and files APIs out of the free plan; (2) in May 2025 Xata announced a rebuilt product centered on vanilla, unmodified Postgres with copy-on-write branching and data anonymization (pgstream) — the old platform was briefly renamed 'Xata Lite' and now returns HTTP 410 Gone at lite.xata.io; (3) in late 2025 Xata open-sourced its core under Apache 2.0, and the permanent free hosted tier was replaced by 'self-host the open-source version' plus a 14-day Xata Cloud trial (with a reported $100 signup credit) and no permanent free cloud plan. Consequence: if you used the old Xata free tier for a managed database, it no longer exists — the only permanent-free option is self-hosted open source; the managed path is the 14-day trial then pay-as-you-go ($0.012/hr + $0.28/GB/mo) or BYOC (quote-based). Note: WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-task, so verification relied on the official pricing page + pricing.md + n8n docs read today plus multiple corroborating 2026 third-party trackers; the $100 credit could not be confirmed on the live official page.

provider: Fauna Cloud (fauna.com, Fauna Inc. — managed document-relational DB "FaunaDB")
sunset_notes: No live free offers as of 2026-10-22: the entire Fauna service was sunset. Timeline: Fauna Inc. announced on 2025-03-19 that it would stop accepting new customers and wind down the service; the service ended Friday 2025-05-30 at 12:00pm PT, after which all Fauna accounts and their data were permanently deleted (official EOL FAQ, docs.fauna.com/fauna/current/eol-faq; announcement, fauna.com/blog/the-future-of-fauna). EVERY offer closed: (1) Free/Community plan ("Free Plan — For learning Fauna"): free shared managed DB, ~1 GB storage, ~1M requests/mo, no credit card required — ended with service; (2) Free trials on paid Startup (from $150/mo, US+EU region groups, 4k reads/s, 1k writes/s) and Pro (from $500/mo) tiers — new signups disallowed from 2025-03-19, and per the EOL FAQ existing trial customers could not upgrade to paid accounts; (3) No startup-credit program, trial-credit program, or .edu education license ever existed at Fauna. Continuity: Fauna committed in the same announcement to open-sourcing its core database engine (OSS Fauna + FQL + drivers + CLI), so self-hosted open-source Fauna is the only remaining free path. Live-site verification today: direct fetches of fauna.com fail at the edge (ECONNREFUSED, CloudFront 3.33.139.32) and docs.fauna.com no longer resolves (DNS ENOTFOUND), consistent with company dissolution; search-engine cached copies still show the banner "The Fauna service will be ending on May 30, 2025". The SaaSOffers "Fauna Free Tier" page is stale filler, not an active offer. Caveats: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before additional independent cross-checks; confidence is HIGH that the service closed on 2025-05-30 and that signups/trial upgrades were prohibited (official announcement + EOL FAQ text read today via search cache), and MEDIUM on the historical free-plan caps (~1 GB / ~1M requests/mo, carried from task context, not re-verified on a live page).

findings.name: AWS Free Account (new credit-based Free plan) — the restructured AWS Free Tier
findings.detail: New AWS accounts automatically enter a credit-based Free plan: $100 USD credits at sign-up + up to $100 more earned by activating foundational services = up to $200 total, spendable across 90+ services. Free plan runs up to 6 months (account auto-closes at 6 months or when credits run out, whichever is first). 30+ services also have recurring 'Always Free' monthly limits on both plans. On the Paid-plan path, the same credits are valid for up to 12 months from account creation. Free-plan accounts are migrated from the legacy usage-based 12-month Free Tier for accounts created on/after July 15, 2025; a new sign-up experience launched October 2026 (older accounts still use the legacy credits console view).
findings.eligibility: New AWS customers only (existing/previous account holders excluded). No .edu requirement; open to students and startups alike. Payment method NOT required to sign up for most new customers, but AWS may request a payment method or extra info to verify identity. Unavailable in China (Beijing and Ningxia) regions and AWS GovCloud (US) (with a note that some services such as Lambda are exceptions in GovCloud).
findings.claim: 1) Create a new AWS (Builder ID) account via the registration portal — Free plan is selected automatically; 2) use the $100 signup credit, then earn up to $100 more by activating foundational services (credits appear in billing console within ~30 min); 3) optionally upgrade to Paid (remaining credits become bill credits expiring 12 months post-creation).
findings.expiry: Free-plan credits: 6 months from account opening or exhaustion, whichever first; account then suspends, data retained 90 days, then account and data permanently erased if not upgraded. Paid-path credits: 12 months from account creation. No renewal; downgrading Paid back to Free is not allowed.
findings.gotchas: Legacy 12-month per-service Free Tier no longer exists for new accounts. Activating 'advanced features' is irreversible and voids remaining earnable credits; joining an AWS Organization or deploying a Control Tower landing zone immediately voids remaining earnable credits. Paid-only services are excluded from the Free plan. After 6 months the account closes itself — you lose access to resources/data unless you upgrade within the 90-day grace window. Egress/data transfer and overages beyond limits are paid.

findings.name: AWS Activate — Founders tier (self-funded/bootsrap startups)
findings.detail: $1,000 in AWS Activate credits guaranteed; select participants may qualify for up to $5,000 over time. Credits apply to 200+ AWS services (compute, RDS, DynamoDB, S3, CloudFront) and Amazon Bedrock, so founders can evaluate/customize/deploy third-party models from OpenAI, Mistral AI, Anthropic, and Meta. Excluded: Mechanical Turk, AWS Managed Services, AWS Professional Services, AWS Training & Certification. Credits apply monthly to new usage, never retroactively. Application processed within 5-10 business days.
findings.eligibility: Self-funded/bootsrap startup (no VC backing needed), founded within the last 10 years, pre-Series B, AWS account on the Paid plan, either new to Activate credits or requesting more than previously received. No .edu or institutional requirement; professional email required for the Builder ID.
findings.claim: 1) Create an AWS Builder ID with a professional email; 2) select the Founders tier at /startups/join?destination=/credits/apply; 3) provide product, funding-stage and company-profile details; 4) link your AWS account to the Builder ID and submit; decisions in 5-10 business days.
findings.expiry: Credits 'usually expire within 1-2 years depending on the package' (official FAQ wording). No renewal, but you may reapply if you request a higher amount than previously approved and haven't hit the lifetime credit cap.
findings.gotchas: The extra $4,000 (up to $5,000) is discretionary ('select participants'), not guaranteed. Requires a Paid-plan AWS account, so expect a billing relationship even if credits cover usage. Credits don't cover AWS Professional/Managed Services or certification fees. $1,000-5,000 amounts are small vs the Portfolio tier — check provider-backed tracks first if you have accelerator/VC contact.

findings.name: AWS Activate — Portfolio tier (VC/accelerator/angel-funded startups)
findings.detail: Up to $200,000 in AWS Activate credits for VC/accelerator/angel-backed startups, claimed with an Organization ID issued by the participating provider (network includes Andreessen Horowitz, Brex, Carta, Greylock, Sequoia, Y Combinator; 'thousands' of providers). Providers structure multi-step offers (FAQ example: $25K at pre-seed stepping up to $100K at seed; you receive the difference between tiers). Credits usable on 200+ services including Amazon Bedrock third-party models (OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Meta).
findings.eligibility: Backed by an Activate Provider (VC, accelerator, angel investor, or enabling organization); founded within the last 10 years; pre-Series B (the /free/offers/ hub phrases it as 'up to and including Pre-Seed, Angel, Seed, Debt Finance, and Series A'); must apply within 12 months of the most recent funding date; affiliation with the provider must still be active; AWS account on Paid plan; new to Activate or requesting more than previously received.
findings.claim: 1) Get the provider's Organization ID from your VC/accelerator; 2) apply at /startups/join?destination=/credits/apply selecting Portfolio tier and entering the Org ID; 3) submit company/funding details and link your AWS account; 4) response in 5-10 business days (offers hub says 7-10). Alternatively the provider portal can claim on your behalf.
findings.expiry: Per package, credits usually expire within 1-2 years (official FAQ). Reapply for a higher tier amount if you've raised further, as long as you're under the lifetime cap and still affiliated; you receive the difference between the old and new tier.
findings.gotchas: Without an active provider relationship you cannot access this tier (fall back to Founders). The /free/offers/ hub still shows the Activate range as '$1,000 to $100,000', contradicting the credits page/FAQ's $200,000 portfolio ceiling — the offers hub appears stale. Credits don't cover excluded services (Professional/Managed Services, Training & Certification) and never retroactively apply to past bills. Applying outside the 12-month post-funding window is not allowed.

findings.name: AWS Credits for AI Startups (invite-only, above the $200K Portfolio cap)
findings.detail: $200,000+ in additional AWS credits, positioned for 'startups ready to scale post Activate Portfolio' — i.e., AI startups that have exhausted the Portfolio ceiling. Official FAQ wording: 'Additional AWS Credits above $200,000 are available for AI startups ready to scale beyond Activate's tiers.' Invite only; no public dollar figure beyond '200,000+'.
findings.eligibility: Invite-only; AI-focused startups already at/above the $200,000 Activate Portfolio ceiling (or approaching it). AWS reaches out; existing customers work through their Account Manager. No public self-serve application.
findings.claim: No public claim path. Routes: (a) AWS outreach/invitation; (b) ask your AWS Account Manager or Activate provider about additional AI-startup credits; (c) the /startups/credits/ page routes AI-tier interest to the account-manager channel.
findings.expiry: Governed by the AWS Promotional Credit T&C; per the Activate FAQ, Activate credits generally burn down over 1-2 years depending on package. Exact expiry for the AI tier is not published.
findings.gotchas: Amount, eligibility thresholds and even the program's public name are not itemized on the credits page — treat specifics as account-manager-mediated. Do not confuse with Kiro credits or the Founders/Portfolio tiers. Credits still exclude AWS Professional/Managed Services.
findings.source_url: https://aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/ ('AWS Credits for AI Startups' card) and FAQ https://aws.amazon.com/aws-startups/learn/everything-you-need-to-know-about-aws-activate-credits/

findings.name: Kiro startup credits (1 year of Kiro Pro+ IDE access)
findings.detail: Up to 12 months of Kiro Pro+ credits (AWS's agentic AI IDE) in three team tiers: Starter (up to 2 Kiro users), Growth (up to 10 users), Scale (up to 30 users). No USD figure published. Issued at the company level, so authorized users on associated AWS accounts can share it. Once exhausted, the account automatically switches to standard Kiro Pro+ billing.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage to Series A startups; a business email matching your company domain AND a matching AWS account ID. Startups with ACTIVE AWS Activate credits are NOT eligible (though existing Activate credits can be spent on Kiro). Regionally limited: available in most countries where AWS billing works, excluding Argentina, Belarus, Brazil, China regions, Cuba, France, Germany, Iran, Italy, Mexico, North Korea, Poland, Russia, Spain, Syria, Crimea/DNR/LNR, and UAE.
findings.claim: Apply through the AWS Startups portal at kiro.dev/startups (rolling review, email notification). On approval credits are automatically added to your AWS account; to use them you must log into Kiro via AWS IAM Identity Center (Kiro Enterprise) — GitHub/Google social login and AWS Builder ID will not work.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 1 year after issuance. One application per company; a rejected applicant whose eligibility later changes may reapply. No refund, reissue, transfer, or sale.
findings.gotchas: Marked 'for a limited time only' with no published end date. Choosing a plan above Pro+ or exceeding your tier's user cap triggers charges. If you're mid-Activate-credits, this offer is off the table (but your Activate credits already cover Kiro, so no loss).

findings.name: Amazon RDS free database (legacy 12-month tier for accounts created before July 15, 2025)
findings.detail: For legacy accounts: up to 750 hours/month of a single-AZ instance on select database classes, across MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server (Express Edition only), plus 20 GB General Purpose SSD (gp2) storage and 20 GB automated backup storage per month, for up to 12 months. Usage aggregates across instance types. Accounts created on/after July 15, 2025 instead get the credit-based Free/Paid plans ($100 + up to $100) in place of this 12-month free database.
findings.eligibility: New AWS accounts created before July 15, 2025 (or existing legacy accounts still within their 12-month window). Not available in AWS GovCloud (US) or China (Beijing) regions. No extra eligibility gate beyond a new account.
findings.claim: 1) Create a new (pre-cutover) AWS account; 2) launch an eligible single-AZ RDS instance in an eligible engine; 3) stay within 750 instance-hours + 20 GB storage + 20 GB automated backup per month for 12 months. Nothing to activate — it applies automatically.
findings.expiry: 12 months from account creation. After that, standard on-demand pricing. For post-cutover accounts, the equivalent benefit is the $100-200 account credit instead.
findings.gotchas: Single-AZ only (Multi-AZ is paid); SQL Server Express only for that engine; cross-AZ VPC traffic (EC2 in a different AZ than RDS) costs $0.01/GB in/out; backup storage beyond 20 GB is paid. Manual snapshots beyond the automated-backup allowance are charged. Don't rely on it: new accounts after July 15, 2025 cannot get this tier.

findings.name: Amazon DynamoDB free tier (ongoing per-region allowances + account credits)
findings.detail: Current per-Region, per-payer-account monthly free allowances: 25 WCUs + 25 RCUs, 25 GB of data storage, 25 rWCUs for global tables deployed across two Regions, 2.5 million DynamoDB Streams read requests, and 1 GB data transfer out (15 GB during your first 12 months, aggregated across AWS services). The page notes it is 'enough for about 200M requests/month' at small item sizes. New accounts can also get up to $200 in AWS Free Tier credits to 'experience the full set of DynamoDB features for up to 6 months'.
findings.eligibility: Per-Region monthly allowances apply to all accounts (Standard table class, provisioned capacity model). The $200/6-month credits require a new AWS account (new-customer Free/Paid plan enrollment).
findings.claim: Allowances are automatic per Region — no activation. The $200 credits come automatically when creating a new AWS account on the Free plan; apply at signup.
findings.expiry: Allowance is recurring monthly (no published sunset; legacy 12-month wording no longer appears on the page — it now reads as ongoing per-Region benefits tied to the new free-tier structure). Credits: 6-month window on the Free plan.
findings.gotchas: Applies to provisioned capacity + Standard table class only; on-demand capacity workloads pay standard rates. Data transfer-out beyond 1 GB/month (15 GB in year one) is paid. Free allowances are per Region, so multi-Region deployments multiply costs.

findings.name: Amazon Redshift free trial (Serverless $300 credit / 90 days; provisioned 2-month trial)
findings.detail: Serverless: new users are eligible for a $300 credit with a 90-day expiration toward compute and storage use. In Regions where Serverless is not available, customers can start a free trial for provisioned clusters that expires after two months or when usage exceeds 750 hours per month, after which you must shut down or pay the standard on-demand rate.
findings.eligibility: New Redshift users/accounts. No funding or .edu requirements; the trial attaches to a new-customer account.
findings.claim: 1) Activate Redshift Serverless in the console — the $300 credit applies automatically; or in a non-Serverless region, launch a provisioned cluster free for the trial window. No separate application.
findings.expiry: Serverless credit: 90 days from issuance. Provisioned trial: 2 months or 750 cluster-hours/month, whichever comes first, then standard on-demand pricing.
findings.gotchas: The legacy RA3/RA2 developer free tier (1-node, 12 months) and 30-day standard tier are no longer shown on the current pricing page — the trial structure changed in the 2025-2026 credit-model restructure. The page does not publish node size/warehouse size for the provisioned trial; verify in console. After trial, standard on-demand rates apply immediately.

findings.name: AWS Glue Data Catalog free tier (recurring, data-platform front)
findings.detail: First million metadata objects stored are free and the first million catalog requests per month are free, every month (ongoing allowance, not a 12-month grant). Lake Formation permissions are also 'provided at no charge', and Lake Formation example billing shows $0 catalog/permissions usage inside the free tier. Pricing varies by Region per the regional product-services table.
findings.eligibility: All AWS accounts; per-Region recurring allowance; no funding or .edu requirements.
findings.claim: Automatic — no activation. Using the Glue Data Catalog / Lake Formation permissions under the allowances simply bills $0; the first million objects + first million requests per month are deducted first.
findings.expiry: No published sunset; allowance recurs monthly. (The legacy '1 million source records processed per month' Glue ETL free allowance no longer appears on the current Glue pricing page — ETL/crawler/development-endpoint work is billed per DPU-hour, so that recurring ETL freebie is effectively gone from the published pricing.)
findings.gotchas: Compute (ETL jobs, crawlers, DataBrew, development endpoints) is paid per DPU-hour — 'catalog free' does not make pipeline runs free. Data transfer and storage (S3) remain separate paid items. Verify Region-specific availability.

findings.name: AWS Educate (free education license/program for students, 13+)
findings.detail: Completely free self-paced cloud training and hands-on labs (S3, EC2, VPC, RDS, compute, storage, networking, databases, cloud operations), plus shareable digital badges, a job board (18+), and the AWS Emerging Talent community. Coverage: learners as young as 13; open to any individual regardless of education stage, technical experience, or career — not restricted to students/educators or accredited institutions.
findings.eligibility: Anyone 13+ can register with just an email address — no .edu email, no institutional enrollment required. Job board access requires 18+. No credit card needed to register (the 'no credit card' label refers to registration, not cloud credits — the program bundles no AWS usage credits).
findings.claim: Register at awseducate.com (learner registration link carries promo code 'EducateLP'), sign in, then take courses and complete labs at no cost.
findings.expiry: No expiry for the program; badges are permanent. Course catalogs evolve over time; labs run in AWS-provisioned lab environments, not your account.
findings.gotchas: No cloud usage credits, no exam vouchers, and no certification discounts are published on the page — do not expect a free Cloud Practitioner exam. Labs are scoped sandbox environments, not your own AWS account. Employer/recruiter features are a separate registration.

findings.name: AWS Skill Builder free digital courses
findings.detail: 600+ free digital courses (the startups AI hub cites 900+ free courses in 11 languages) curated by AWS, self-paced and at no cost; paid Skill Builder subscriptions unlock additional lab experiences on top of the free catalog. Free training events (Twitch/virtual) also advertised at no cost.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone with a free AWS Builder ID / Skill Builder account — students, educators, or self-learners; no .edu requirement, no funding requirement.
findings.claim: Create a free account at skillbuilder.aws (or via the Builder ID), browse the free digital catalog, take courses; events via /training/events/.
findings.expiry: Course access has no published expiry; free vs paid boundary changes with subscription offerings.
findings.gotchas: Certifications themselves are NOT free (exam fees still apply; the AI hub's 'Certified AI Business Strategist' cert is sold separately). Paid lab tiers cost extra. Free courses refresh/retire, so the exact count (600 vs 900) varies by page and date.

sunset_notes: Major 2025-2026 changes (all verified on official AWS pages fetched today, 2026-10-22; WebSearch budget was exhausted so only official-page fetches were used): (1) The legacy usage-based 12-month AWS Free Tier (750 RDS hours, 5 GB S3, etc.) was replaced by a credit-based model for accounts created on/after July 15, 2025 — $100 at sign-up + up to $100 earned, Free plan (6-month auto-closing account) vs Paid plan (12-month credit validity); a refreshed sign-up experience launched October 2026, and pre-October accounts still see the old credits console. The RDS pricing page still documents the legacy 750-hour/20 GB free database for pre-July-15-2025 accounts only. (2) Per-service 'Always Free' and legacy free-trial figures (e.g., Athena GB-per-month, Redshift RA3/RA2 1-node 12-month developer tier and 30-day standard tier, Glue 1M source-records ETL free allowance, Bedrock character-based free tiers) no longer appear on today's service pricing pages — the credit model absorbed them, so do not quote legacy numbers for new accounts. (3) Activate program structure is now three tiers: Founders ($1,000, up to $5,000), Portfolio (up to $200,000 via provider Org ID), and an invite-only 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' tier adding $200,000+ for AI startups scaling past the Portfolio ceiling. Credits now explicitly cover Amazon Bedrock third-party models (OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Meta). Note a discrepancy: /free/offers/ still lists Activate as '$1,000 to $100,000' — likely stale vs the $200,000 ceiling on the credits page/FAQ. (4) New Kiro startup credits program (up to a year of Kiro Pro+, 2/10/30-user tiers, 'limited time only', excludes France/Germany/Italy/Spain/Poland/UAE and ~13 other countries). (5) AWS Academy / Cloud Career Academies: no working page found on today's main AWS site (URLs 404; cloudcareeracademies.org DNS-failed) — status unconfirmed; AWS Educate (free, 13+, no credits/vouchers) is explicitly still active with a 2026 copyright. Also of note: AWS Educate bundles no cloud credits and no free exam vouchers on any page I could read today.

findings.name: Azure Free Account — $200 credit / 30-day trial
findings.detail: New Azure customers get $200 credit usable within 30 days across the full catalog (up to free amounts + credit), with spending protection so the card is not charged during the trial. After 30 days or credit exhaustion the account moves to pay-as-you-go (or is disabled). This trial is the only path that makes Azure's dedicated/bare-metal-adjacent SKUs (dedicated hosts, larger VM sizes) reachable at $0, since no dedicated-server free allotment exists.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only. Phone number + non-prepaid credit or debit card REQUIRED (a ~$1 temporary authorization may be placed); Microsoft or GitHub account. Commercially available in ~140 countries; explicitly excludes US Government cloud, Azure China, and Germany sovereign regions.
findings.claim: Sign up at https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/ → provide phone/card/account → $200 credit is live immediately; no application or approval.
findings.expiry: Credit valid for the full 30 days from account creation even if partially unused; then pay-as-you-go or disable.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (not card-free). Free 12-month and always-free services continue after the 30-day trial; unused 12-month services keep running at PAYG billing. Egress/data charges apply above free amounts. No free dedicated-host or bare-metal allotment — dedicated servers are only reachable via this credit or startup credits.

findings.name: Azure free services tier — 12-month + 65+ always-free services (VPS & managed-database fronts)
findings.detail: On the same free account: free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months, incl. VPS front: 750 hours each/month of B1s, B2pts v2 (ARM) and B2ats v2 (AMD) burstable VMs; managed-DB front: Azure Database for PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible 750 hours B1MS + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup; SQL Managed Instance 720 vCore-hours of a 4- or 8-vCore General Purpose instance + 64 GB data + 64 GB backup; Azure Container Registry 1 Standard registry/100 GB; Data Factory 5 low-frequency activities; Vision 5,000 transactions each of S1/S2/S3. Plus 65+ always-free services: Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB; SQL Database serverless 100,000 vCore-seconds/month + 32 GB; Functions 1M requests/month; Container Apps 180,000 vCPU-seconds + 360,000 GiB-seconds + 2M requests; App Service 10 F0 web/API apps (1 GB); Static Web Apps 100 GB bandwidth + 0.5 GB storage; Logic Apps 4,000 executions; AKS control plane; DevOps 5 users; AI Search 50 MB/10K docs/3 indexes; Speech 0.5M neural chars; Translator 2M chars.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers (12-month items); always-free items available to any Azure customer including students (no card needed under Azure for Students).
findings.claim: Automatic once the free account or student subscription is created; nothing to redeem separately.
findings.expiry: 12-month amounts stop at the 12-month anniversary (running services continue, now billed PAYG); always-free services have no expiry.
findings.gotchas: Only burstable b1ms-class VMs are free — no guaranteed-performance VMs; no free dedicated/bare-metal capacity; egress above free allowances and any service beyond free amounts bill to the card on file (trial account).

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit / 12 months, no credit card, renewable
findings.detail: Azure for Students: $100 credit usable within 12 months plus the same 20+ 12-month free services (incl. 750 h VMs, managed-DB free amounts) and 65+ always-free services; full catalog access up to free amounts + $100 credit; includes Azure OpenAI access and software download licenses (Visual Studio, SQL Server Developer/Standard, Windows Server, Hyper-V, R, etc.). Balance visible in the Azure Sponsorships portal. Official offer terms: age 18+, accredited degree-granting 2/4-year institution, full-time student, verified via the organization's email address; one subscription per person, nontransferable, not combinable, limited supply.
findings.eligibility: Full-time university/college students (2- or 4-year accredited, degree-granting; 18+). Verified with school/organization email — .edu not required, but MOOC/for-profit trainings excluded. No credit card required.
findings.claim: Sign up at https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/ with school email → no card → $100 credit available immediately. Also obtainable through the GitHub Student Developer Pack.
findings.expiry: 12 months; unused credit does not carry over month-to-month and lapses at 12 months. Renewable annually as long as you remain a full-time student (reminder emails before the anniversary). If you exhaust the credit or let the year end without upgrading, the subscription is canceled; you have 90 days to upgrade to pay-as-you-go.
findings.gotchas: $100 is small next to the $200 trial credit; after expiry your deployed resources are decommissioned; the offer is while-supplies-last and Microsoft can terminate it at discretion.

findings.name: Azure for Students Starter — card-free free-product tier
findings.detail: Card-free alternative to Azure for Students: select Azure products (e.g., App Service) free for students, without the $100 credit. Listed in Microsoft's official AcademicContent repo ('Azure for Students Starter | use select Azure products like App Services for free - no credit card required with academic verification'); the /free/students page offers it as 'Try Azure for Students or Azure for Students Starter — no credit card required'.
findings.eligibility: Students with academic verification (school email); no credit card.
findings.claim: Offered from https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/.
findings.expiry: Tied to student status; per-service limits are not itemized on the pages fetched today.
findings.gotchas: Exact service list/limits are not documented on the fetched page — verify in-portal before relying on it; WebSearch budget was exhausted before a dedicated offer-detail page could be pulled.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack — Microsoft Azure benefit
findings.detail: The GitHub Student Developer Pack (student-verified, via GitHub or school email) includes Microsoft Azure's student offer: $100 Azure credit plus 12-month free amounts of 25+/20+ services, under the Pack's 'Microsoft Azure' offer. It is the alternate redemption route when a school email isn't accepted by the Azure for Students flow.
findings.eligibility: Verified students through GitHub Education (school email or enrollment proof); not .edu-only.
findings.claim: Sign up at https://education.github.com/pack with student verification → open the Microsoft Azure offer to activate the Azure for Students subscription.
findings.expiry: 12 months, matching Azure for Students.
findings.gotchas: Same $100 credit as Azure for Students; Pack benefits are partner-offered and can change; one Azure student subscription per person.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — 2026 milestone program, up to $150,000 in Azure credits
findings.detail: Current model (docs ms.date 2026-05/2026-10, page updated 2026-08/10): every startup enters the same way. Apply without an investor code → $200 starter credits immediately, no application form (identity via personal LinkedIn). With a 10-character investor-network referral code → $1,000 starter credits immediately while the application is reviewed (~3 business days); approval unlocks expanded credits. Credits then auto-progress in tiers — no separate applications: $5,000 after business verification; $25,000 after 5+ distinct Azure workloads in active use for a sustained ~60 days (each workload must spend >$1/month for the whole 60 days; one-time two-year extension of credit validity at this tier); $50,000 at 7+ workloads; $150,000 at 10+ workloads plus ~$3,000/month Azure usage sustained ~60 days. Milestones can be skipped straight if requirements are met. Program support, AI capabilities (Microsoft Foundry models), and go-to-market resources are included.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage B2B software/AI/technology startups; funding stage pre-seed through Series B; at or working toward MVP; privately held independent companies (not subsidiaries); headquartered in a region where MfS operates (country choice at signup cannot be changed; if your country is absent, the offer is not available). Sign-in must use a personal consumer email (work/school/company domains rejected); phone number; registered business name matching legal documents; payment card is entered at Azure account creation (spend protection; converts to pay-as-you-go when credits are used up or expired).
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/startups → 'Get started now'. 2) Sign in with a personal Microsoft account. 3) No code: 'Continue without a code' → 'Verify with LinkedIn' → 3-step Azure account setup (profile, billing address, payment card) → '$200 in Azure credits' unlocked. With code: enter the 10-char investor code → verify email + phone → business info form → submit → $1,000 credits immediately, approval within ~3 business days. Credits are managed in the MfS portal (portal.startups.microsoft.com); usage is auto-evaluated monthly.
findings.expiry: Per program FAQ guidance: credits must be activated within 90 days of accepting the program agreement; once activated they are valid up to 2 years with no extensions — except the one-time two-year extension awarded at the $25K milestone (per official docs).
findings.gotchas: Contrary to 'no card' expectations, the application flow requires a card at account creation (identity verification + billing above credit). 'Up to $150,000' is a ceiling, not a day-one grant — day one is $200 (or $1,000 with an investor code). Marketing pages still show stale 2025-track copy: /free/students advertises 'Azure for Startups: $1,000 instantly, up to $5,000, 90/180-day validity', which is the retired self-service track. The $150K figure in the Azure portal is a generic ceiling indicator, not a grant; additional credits are applied automatically (no 'redeem more' button exists). All activation must use the same personal Microsoft account registered at signup.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — Investor Network (enhanced track)
findings.detail: Startups referred by Microsoft for Startups Investor Network partners (VCs, accelerators, incubators, universities; the partner list is not public) get the enhanced experience on top of the base program: dedicated Microsoft point of contact, deeper Microsoft Marketplace and co-sell support, and access to additional Startup credits beyond the standard program (up to the $150,000 ceiling). Under the current docs the investor path starts with $1,000 in credits immediately and unlocks up to $150,000 after application approval. (The interim 2025 track had started at $100,000 for investor-backed startups.)
findings.eligibility: Same base MfS eligibility (pre-seed–Series B, B2B, privately held, supported region) plus a 10-character referral code from a participating investor/accelerator/university.
findings.claim: Ask your investor/accelerator for the 10-character referral code → apply at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/startups with the code.
findings.expiry: Same activation/validity rules as base MfS (activate within 90 days; valid up to 2 years; 2-year extension at the $25K tier).
findings.gotchas: Extra credit amounts above the standard tiers are investor-dependent and not standardized publicly; the partner list is unpublished, so you must get the code from the investor directly.

findings.name: Azure for Education — faculty dev-tool licenses (no cloud credits)
findings.detail: Education-licensing front: Azure for Education gives teachers/educators free access to Microsoft and Azure development tools and software licenses for teaching (Visual Studio Community, SQL Server Developer/Standard editions, Windows Server, Hyper-V, R Client/Server, VS Code, etc.) — included even inside Azure for Students subscriptions. No cloud credits are part of the education program; faculty who want credits must take the standard $200 free account (card required) or request an academic grant/sponsorship (custom spending-limit Azure Sponsorship subscriptions, e.g. for competitions, via Azure for Education support).
findings.eligibility: Educators in K-12 and higher education; verification through school/organization. Not a credit offer.
findings.claim: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/for-education/ for the dev-tools program; sponsorship/academic grants via Azure for Education support (azureforeducation.microsoft.com contact).
findings.expiry: Licenses valid while the account is a qualifying educator/student.
findings.gotchas: No credits — if the research question is 'free compute for faculty', the answer is the standard $200 trial card or a bespoke sponsorship request, not an education program. This page was not directly re-fetched today, hence low confidence.

findings.name: Bare-metal & dedicated servers front — no dedicated free offer
findings.detail: Azure publishes no free tier, free trial allotment, or always-free amount for dedicated hosts or bare-metal VM SKUs. The VPS front is covered by the free 750 h/month burstable VMs + $200 trial credit; the managed-database front by the free Flexible Server/Managed Instance/always-free Cosmos and SQL serverless amounts. Dedicated/bare-metal capacity is reachable only by spending trial credits or Microsoft-for-Startups credits on eligible services — i.e., the 'free' path for a dedicated server is a credit, not a free allotment.
findings.eligibility: Via the $200 free-account trial (card required) or MfS startup credits (card at account creation).
findings.claim: No standalone claim; use a trial or MfS credit in a paid subscription.
findings.expiry: As the underlying credit (30-day trial credit; MfS activation + up to 2-year validity).
findings.gotchas: Do not plan runways around free dedicated capacity — it does not exist; credit ceilings are hard caps, and beyond them it is straight PAYG.

sunset_notes: TWO program sunsets in 2025-2026: (1) Effective ~June 27/July 1, 2025, the pre-2025 multi-tier Microsoft for Startups program — 'up to $150,000 in Azure credits' via L1 $1,000 / L2 $5,000 / L3 $25,000 / L4 $150,000 tiers, open to non-investor startups with a validated business plan — was retired and replaced by a two-track system: Investor Network track (~$100,000 start + additional awards, by investor referral) and a self-service track capped at $5,000 ($1,000 valid 90 days + $4,000 valid 180 days after business verification). Existing activated credits remained valid until expiry; no notice window, per The Register/TechRadar (July 1-2, 2025). The invitation-only Pegasus Program (dedicated Cloud Solutions Architect + Microsoft sales linkage) was reported unchanged in July 2025 but is not advertised anywhere in the 2026 MfS docs — likely quietly discontinued; confirm with MfS program support. (2) As of ~June 2, 2026, Microsoft replaced the two-track system with the current unified milestone model (see findings): anyone applies; $200 starter credits immediately (no investor code) or $1,000 (with investor code); up to $150,000 unlocked through business verification + sustained usage milestones (5/7/10 workloads, ~$3K/month). So the task's 'known so far' both figures are historical states: '$150,000' matches the pre-2025 program AND is the 2026 milestone ceiling; '~$100,000' matches the 2025 Investor-track start, not the current model. Marketing pages are lagging the docs: azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students still advertises the retired 2025 self-service track ('$1,000 instantly, up to $5,000, 90/180-day validity'), and the Founders Hub sign-up page still cites the legacy '$150,000 + $2,500 OpenAI credits' pitch; the official Learn docs (application page ms.date 2026-10-08) are the authoritative current state. Stale-URL note: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/for-startups/ 404s today; the program now lives at microsoft.com/startups with docs under learn.microsoft.com/en-us/startups/. Note: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-task, so a few secondary items (MfS FAQ's exact URL, Azure for Students Starter per-service limits, Azure for Education page) were verified only indirectly and are marked medium/low confidence accordingly. provider: AWS Impact Bootcamps (with Techstars) — Amazon Web Services / AWS Startups

findings.name: AWS Impact Bootcamps (with Techstars): up to $5,000 in AWS Activate credits
findings.detail: Two-day intensive bootcamp for underrepresented startup founders, run with Techstars in six cities: Atlanta (Sep 8-9, 2025), New York (Sep 15-16, 2025), Mexico City (Oct 1-2, 2025), London (Oct 16-17, 2025), Tokyo (Mar 26-27, 2026; apply by Feb 27, 2026) and Berlin (Apr 16-17, 2026; apply by Mar 13, 2026). Selected startups get access to up to $5,000 in AWS Activate credits to build, train, and launch products, plus consideration for Techstars Founder Catalyst / accelerator and AWS startup programs. Up to 50 founders per city, ~300 founders annually. Workshops: fundraising mindset, customer discovery, go-to-market, AI product optimization, SAFE/convertible notes, pitch practice. Launched Jul 30, 2025, building on AWS's 2022 $30M commitment to Black, Women, Latino, and LGBTQIA+ founders.
findings.eligibility: Self-funded, angel-funded, or early-stage startups (press release: raised up to Series A) with a goal to scale or prepare to raise funds; at least one founding/exec team member must identify with a historically underrepresented community (Black, women, Latino/Latinx, Indigenous, LGBTQIA+, people with disabilities) OR be engaged in work supporting such communities. In-person attendance at the two-day event. No .edu email required; no credit card required for participation; global (any region, in-person at the city stop).
