findings.claim: All 2025-2026 cohort application windows are closed (Tokyo closed Feb 27, 2026; Berlin closed Mar 13, 2026); as of 2026-10-22 no open application window is posted on the official page, so the $5,000 offer is not currently claimable - watch for new city cohorts. To claim the $5K: apply to a bootcamp before its deadline, attend, then apply for the AWS Activate credit through the AWS Startups portal (startups.aws.com); review takes ~5-10 business days and the credit is issued to a good-standing AWS account.
findings.source_url: https://startups.aws.com/lp/aws-impact-bootcamps (serving HTTP 500; full content recovered from its embedded Next.js payload; cross-checked with the Jul 30, 2025 press release https://press.aboutamazon.com/aws/2025/7/aws-and-techstars-launch-impact-bootcamps-to-support-underrepresented-founders-globally and https://aws.amazon.com/aws-startups/learn/what-to-expect-from-the-aws-impact-bootcamps/)
findings.gotchas: Press release states $5,000 is given; the landing page says 'up to $5K', so awards are at AWS discretion. The bootcamp page currently returns HTTP 500 at the server level even though its content payload is intact. 'AWS Activate Credits' are promotional credits subject to AWS's standard rules: startup <10 years old, funding stage <= Series A, most recent funding round within 12 months of application, application email domain must match the AWS account domain, free email providers rejected, website must be live, and AWS may decline applications in its sole discretion; availability can be limited by country/region.
findings.expiry: Not a rolling offer: cohort-based. 2025 (US/EU/LatAm) and 2026 (Tokyo, Berlin) cohorts have concluded; future cohorts to be announced (the learn page said more locations would be announced in 2026). Credits, once issued, follow AWS Activate terms (page did not state a burn period today).

findings.name: AWS Founder Retreat (bootcamp capstone): up to $50,000 unrestricted grant + up to $15,000 extra AWS credits
findings.detail: Invitation-only weekend capstone for 'best-in-class' bootcamp participants: in-person investor meetings and a chance to win up to $50,000 in unrestricted grant funding plus an extra $15,000 in AWS promotional credits, per cohort (up to 4 winners per press-release math; actual 2025 event: 12 finalists from the Atlanta, NYC, London and Mexico City bootcamps attended a retreat at Ritz-Carlton Half Moon Bay, culminating in a pitch competition for US$100,000 in grants with three recipients - Pilou, FoodStream Network, SyncPop). Includes one-to-one mentoring with AWS leaders and investors.
findings.eligibility: Invite-only; top-performing AWS Impact Bootcamp participants (hand-picked from hundreds of global participants). Underlying bootcamp eligibility applies (underrepresented early-stage founders, self-funded/angel/early-stage, goal to scale or raise).
findings.claim: Cannot apply directly. Path: apply to an AWS Impact Bootcamp -> be selected as a top participant -> receive the Founder Retreat invitation. Currently no open path (all bootcamp windows closed as of 2026-10-22).
findings.gotchas: The 'up to $50,000' grant is per capstone event, not per winner; the 2025 cohort split a US$100,000 pool among 3 winners (i.e., ~$33K each, not $50K). Winners are also 'considered' for Techstars programs, not guaranteed. In-person, US-based venue in 2025.
findings.expiry: Event-based; one per program cycle. The Tokyo/Berlin 2026 cohorts will presumably feed a 2026/2027 retreat.

findings.name: AWS Activate Program (flagship startup credit program; the VC/accelerator-funded front): up to $100,000 - $200,000 in AWS credits
findings.detail: AWS Startups portal (read live 2026-10-22): the join page advertises 'Apply for up to $200,000 in Activate Credits' and the credits widget says 'Eligible startups can receive up to $100,000 in AWS Activate Credits. These credits can be used for AWS services and support, including infrastructure and emerging technologies.' Credits are claimable in one step when affiliated with an AWS Activate Provider (VC, accelerator, angel group, or other partner); the portal notes 'Home to over 350,000 startups globally.' Legacy structure (2023-2025): standard AWS Activate up to $1,000 in credits; Accelerate (VC/accelerator-backed) up to $100,000 over 12+ months. The $200K figure on the live join page indicates a 2026 headline increase; the $1,000 standard-tier copy no longer appears on the pages read today. Benefits besides credits: partner offers/exclusive deals, global events, training, technical support.
findings.eligibility: Startup founded within the last 10 years; funding stage at or below Series A (Series B+ explicitly rejected); most recent funding round within 12 months of application; application email domain must match the AWS account email domain (free email providers rejected); company website must be live and functional (no under-construction/maintenance/404/redirect); account in good standing; reseller-affiliated accounts need reseller confirmation; not available in every country ('AWS Activate is not available in your country' rejection exists); if you already received equal-or-greater Activate credits, a new award is the current offer minus the previous amount. No .edu requirement; no credit card to receive the credit itself (a payment method is normal for the AWS account).
findings.claim: Apply at the AWS Startups portal (startups.aws.com) - if you have a VC/accelerator/angel partner, apply 'in one step' through provider affiliation (provider must confirm within 30 days or the application can stall). Processing ~5-10 business days. Alternatively, the $5,000 bootcamp credits are claimed through the same Activate application flow. As of 2026-10-22 the program is live and open to qualifying startups.
findings.source_url: https://startups.aws.com/aws-startup-credits-promotion and https://aws.amazon.com/startups/activate/ (portal app shell read live 2026-10-22)
findings.gotchas: 'Up to' is literal: actual awards are tiered and smaller than the headline (widget says $100K max while the join page says $200K - the $200K ceiling is not broken down on the pages read today). Promotional credits are not redeemable for data egress/inter-region transfer beyond free allowances and expire unused. Duplicate applications rejected; email-domain mismatch is the most common rejection reason; provider non-confirmation after 30 days stalls the application. Regional availability restrictions apply.

findings.name: AWS Free Tier (revamped): Free plan - up to $200 in credits, 90+ services for up to 6 months; Paid plan - pay-as-you-go plus up to $200 in credits
findings.detail: Current AWS Free Tier page (read live 2026-10-22) describes a restructured model: Free plan - 'Start building on AWS with up to $200 in credits. Get access to over 90 services for up to 6 months as you build and experiment with no charges and no surprise overages.' Paid plan - 'Access the full range of AWS services with pay-as-you-go pricing. New customers on the Paid plan are also eligible for up to $200 in credits.' Short-term trials - 'Try selected Paid plan services through limited free trials. Your trial begins when you activate the service, and any eligible credits automatically apply to usage beyond the trial limits.' Always Free - '30+ AWS services are always free within monthly usage limits on both the Free and Paid plans; if you go beyond these limits or access paid features, credits are automatically applied to cover the costs.'
findings.eligibility: All new AWS customers (including students; no .edu email or credit card documented on the page). Free plan requires simply opening a new account; a payment method is normally required for the account but the Free plan's usage up to limits is covered by the $200 credits with 'no surprise overages'.
findings.claim: No application: open a new AWS account at aws.amazon.com; Free plan benefits and trial offers are automatic, and the $200 credits apply to usage within the 6-month window / beyond trial limits.
findings.gotchas: This is NOT the old '12-month free tier' - see sunset_notes. The $200 is a usage-credit ceiling, not a cash grant; after 6 months or when credits run out, Paid-plan usage is billed. Data transfer, inter-region egress, and paid features beyond always-free monthly limits can incur charges ('credits are automatically applied to cover the costs' - credits, not a no-cost promise, cover overage). Trial periods are per-service and only start on activation.
findings.expiry: Free plan: up to 6 months of covered access; Always Free items: indefinite within monthly limits; $200 credits: burn off over the period, unused value does not roll over as cash.

findings.name: AWS Educate: free education license for students and educators (no credit card)
findings.detail: Official AWS Educate page (read live 2026-10-22): 'AWS Educate provides students and educators with no-cost access to cloud computing skills training developed by AWS experts, plus career pathways for students.' Includes self-paced free learning ('build your cloud skills... completely for free'), hands-on labs - e.g., build a static website on S3, EC2 instance, VPC networking, RDS database, Cloud operations course with a cost-estimation lab - and a job board / employer program ('AWS Educate for employers'). Page states explicitly: 'Sign in to AWS Educate: No credit card needed.' No dollar credit pool; the value is free training + sandboxed lab access rather than account credits.
findings.eligibility: Students, K-12 and higher-ed educators, and employers (recruiters). No .edu email is documented as required on the current page; no credit card needed. Institution-based accounts have historically been free 12-month licenses renewable annually - the current page does not state a duration, so treat renewal terms as unverified.
findings.claim: Register at https://aws.amazon.com/education/awseducate/ (Register for AWS Educate), sign in to the AWS Educate portal, then complete courses/labs for free. No payment or card at any step per the page's 'No credit card needed' statement.
findings.gotchas: Not a credits offer - no cloud spend allowance for personal AWS accounts beyond the generic Free Tier. Distinct from AWS Academy, which is an institutional/licensed program (usually paid by the institution) - AWS Academy's own site was unreachable during this research, so no claim is made about it. Labs are time-boxed sandbox environments.

findings.name: AWS Skill Builder: 600+ free courses and certification exam prep
findings.detail: AWS Skill Builder (skillbuilder.aws, read live 2026-10-22): 'an online learning center where you can learn from AWS experts... With access to 600+ free courses, certification exam prep, and training that allows you to build practical skills.' Free for self-directed learners, including students; no enrollment gate, no credit card. This is the successor to much of AWS's formerly free training content.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, for free; no .edu requirement, no card. Free content is the baseline; AWS has added paid professional subscription tiers in recent years (not verified in today's read - treat as a gotcha, not a fact).
findings.claim: Sign up at skillbuilder.aws and take courses/digital badges at no cost.
findings.gotchas: Do not assume everything is free if you later see 'Professional' tier marketing; today's read confirms the free 600+ course base only.

sunset_notes: (1) AWS Free Tier revamp: the classic structure - 12 months of Free Trial on ~75 services plus a separate 'Always Free' tier - is no longer on the official page; it has been replaced (2025-2026) by the Free plan / Paid plan model with up to $200 in credits, 90+ services for up to 6 months, and '30+ services always free within monthly usage limits'. The exact launch date of the revamp could not be confirmed (web-search budget exhausted mid-session); the page read today (2026-10-22) shows only the new structure. (2) AWS Activate: the legacy 'standard program up to $1,000 in credits' copy no longer appears on the live portal; the join page now says 'Apply for up to $200,000 in Activate Credits' while the application widget caps at 'up to $100,000' - consistent with a headline increase beyond the old $100K Accelerate ceiling, unconfirmed via a dated press release. (3) AWS Impact Accelerator, the US-only predecessor (part of AWS's 2022 $30M commitment to Black, Women, Latino and LGBTQIA+ founders), was superseded by the global AWS Impact Bootcamps announced Jul 30, 2025; the 2022-2023 US cohorts are closed. (4) All AWS Impact Bootcamps application windows through the 2026 Tokyo and Berlin cohorts are closed (deadlines Feb 27 and Mar 13, 2026), so as of 2026-10-22 the $5,000 credits, $50K grant and $15K credits are only obtainable in future, not-yet-announced cohorts. (5) Research caveat: https://startups.aws.com/lp/aws-impact-bootcamps currently returns HTTP 500 at the server level (its Next.js content payload is intact and was extracted from the raw HTML); the shared WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted, so 'was this changed in 2025-2026' checks rely on today's live pages rather than dated announcements.

provider: AWS (Amazon Web Services) — Free Tier Credits incl. RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB (hyperscaler-free-tier, Managed Databases & Data Platforms fronts)

findings.name: AWS Free Plan (new accounts, credit-based, in effect since 2025-07-15)
findings.detail: New accounts get $100 in credits immediately at sign-up, plus up to $100 more by completing 'Explore AWS' service-exploration activities in the Console Home widget (filtered to 'Earn AWS credits') = up to $200 total usable over 6 months. Covers 90+ services for up to 6 months, including Amazon RDS, Aurora Serverless, and DynamoDB. 'No charges and no surprise bills on the Free plan' unless you convert to a Paid plan or activate paid-only services. Account auto-closes at the earlier of 6 months after account opening or when credits run out; on expiration AWS suspends the account and retains your data 90 days (upgradable to Paid within that window), then account/content is permanently erased. Free plan is NOT eligible for promotional credits (e.g. AWS Activate).
findings.eligibility: One free grant per identity: 'ineligible for the Free plan or Free Tier credits if you have an existing AWS account or have previously had one'. Payment method NOT required for most new signups (AWS may still request one for identity verification). Credits are USD, apply across participating global regions; NOT available in China regions or AWS GovCloud (US). No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Sign up for a new AWS account choosing the Free plan at aws.amazon.com/free -> $100 credit applied automatically. Complete service-exploration activities in the 'Explore AWS' widget on Console Home (filter: 'Earn AWS credits') within 6 months of account creation to earn up to $100 more.
findings.expiry: Initial $100 credit expires when the 6-month Free plan window ends (credit validity stated as 'up to 12 months' on service pages; activity-earned credits expire 12 months after account creation per FAQ). Account auto-closes at 6 months or when credits are exhausted, whichever is first; 90-day data retention after closure; no renewal, no second grant on a new identity-linked account.
findings.gotchas: Auto-close at 6 months means long-lived free work must be migrated/billed; data permanently deleted 90 days after closure. Free plan excludes promotional credits (Activate) and some paid-only services; upgrading to Paid to unlock those is irreversible (cannot revert to Free plan). Credits apply across regions but China/GovCloud excluded. Upgrading converts to pay-as-you-go once credits burn.

findings.name: AWS Paid Plan new-customer credits
findings.detail: New customers choosing the Paid plan get 'up to $200 USD free credits' plus full access to all AWS services (including paid-only services like Bedrock AgentCore) and eligibility for promotional credits. Selected services can be trialed via 'limited free trials'; the trial clock starts at activation and remaining credits 'automatically apply to usage beyond the trial limits'. Pay-as-you-go billing applies beyond credit exhaustion.
findings.eligibility: Same one-free-grant-per-identity rule; a billing/payment method is in practice expected for a Paid plan (Free plan needed none). No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Sign up choosing the Paid plan, or convert an existing Free-plan account to Paid (irreversible).
findings.expiry: Credits usable 'for up to 12 months' on the Paid plan per service pages (e.g. Aurora pricing page), vs the 6-month Free-plan window; trial clocks start at service activation.
findings.gotchas: Pay-as-you-go charges begin the moment credits run out; Free-to-Paid conversion is one-way; trials are time-boxed per service.

findings.name: Legacy 12-month Free Tier for RDS (accounts created before 2025-07-15)
findings.detail: Grandfathered pre-2025-07-15 accounts keep the service-level 12-month free tier: up to 750 hours/month of single-AZ instance databases (aggregated across instance types), engines limited to MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQL Server (Express Edition only), 20 GB/month of gp2 general-purpose storage, and 20 GB/month of automated backup storage for 1 year.
findings.eligibility: AWS accounts created before July 15, 2025 only; not the credit-based model.
findings.claim: N/A - grandfathered automatically; nothing to claim.
findings.expiry: 12 months from account creation, then billed.
findings.gotchas: No free-tier credits available in AWS GovCloud (US) regions or the China (Beijing) region; SQL Server only in Express edition; 750 hours aggregate means running multiple RDS instances splits the hours.

findings.name: DynamoDB always-free allowances plus credit boost
findings.detail: Per the DynamoDB pricing page today: 25 WCUs and 25 RCUs of provisioned capacity (per Region, per payer account, monthly), 25 GB of data storage, 25 rWCUs for global tables deployed across two regions, 2.5 million stream read requests from DynamoDB Streams, 1 GB data transfer out per month (15 GB for the first 12 months, aggregated across AWS services); plus 'up to $200 USD in credits' to use the full DynamoDB feature set for up to 6 months on the Free plan.
findings.eligibility: Always-free allowances apply while you are an AWS customer (Free or Paid plan); the $200 credit boost is for new accounts under the credit-based model. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Always-free allowances apply automatically; the credit boost comes with a new Free/Paid plan account (see the main Free plan finding).
findings.expiry: Monthly allowances recur; the 12-month egress allowance lapses at month 12; the $200 credit is within the 6-month Free plan window (or 12-month credit validity on Paid plan).
findings.gotchas: The page presents allowances without an explicit legacy/new split - the '15 GB first 12 months' egress language is legacy-style; request-based allowances (25 WCUs/25 RCUs) are the current always-free shape. Old (pre-2025) free tier was expressed as 25 GB + 2.5M write/5M read requests, so verify the exact current RCU/WCU mix against AWS Billing if cost-critical.

findings.name: Aurora free availability (Free plan) + credit validity
findings.detail: The Free plan 'provides Aurora PostgreSQL serverless instances with up to 4 ACUs and 1 GiB of storage per cluster' (paid plans scale to 256 ACUs and 256 TiB). New customers receive '$100 in AWS credits at sign-up' usable 'for up to 12 months, in both Free and Paid plans' plus 'an additional $100 in credits, for a total of $200'.
findings.eligibility: New AWS accounts (Free or Paid plan); no .edu requirement; no payment method required for most Free-plan signups.
findings.claim: Automatic with new-account signup ($100); extra $100 via service-exploration activities.
findings.expiry: Credits usable up to 12 months per the Aurora page; the Free plan account itself auto-closes at 6 months - so the 12-month credit validity practically matters only if you convert to the Paid plan before closure.
findings.gotchas: Only Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless is named as a free-plan offering (not MySQL, not provisioned instances, no I/O/storage free GB figures on today's page - the legacy 120 hours db.t3.medium/10 GB storage/100 GB backup tier is not listed on the current Aurora page).

findings.name: AWS Activate Founders (self-funded / bootstrapped startups)
findings.detail: 'Up to $5,000 USD in Activate Credits', with 'Start with $1,000 USD in Activate Credits' - select participants may qualify for the full $5,000. Credits offset infrastructure, data services, and AI/ML models, and are redeemable on third-party models on Amazon Bedrock. Includes mentorship, AWS Startup Advisor, and partner-network co-build/co-market access.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Series B stage; founded in the last 10 years; must have an AWS account on a Paid-plan tier; must be 'new to Activate Credits or requesting more credits than previously received'; apply with an AWS Builder ID using a professional email - no .edu requirement and no country restrictions stated on the page. USD credits subject to AWS Promotional Credit T&C.
findings.claim: Create an AWS Builder ID -> choose self-funded (Founders) tier at aws.amazon.com/startups/join?destination=/credits/apply -> provide product, funding stage, and company details -> link/create a Paid-plan AWS account and submit; response in 5-10 business days.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page - governed by the AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions (typically ~12-month burn-down, unverified today).
findings.gotchas: Amount is 'up to' $5,000 - default grant is $1,000; must run a Paid plan (the Free plan excludes promotional credits entirely); no .edu, but a professional email is required.

findings.name: AWS Activate Portfolio (VC / accelerator / angel-backed startups)
findings.detail: 'Up to $200,000 USD in Activate Credits' for Pre-Series B startups, gated by an 'Organization ID (Org ID)' issued by an Activate Provider (accelerator, angel investor, or VC firm; named examples: Andreessen Horowitz, Brex, Carta, Greylock Partners, Sequoia, Y Combinator). The /startups/ page headlines 'Get up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits and expert support'.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Series B; founded in the last 10 years; AWS account on a Paid plan; must be new to Activate credits or requesting more than previously received; requires provider-issued Org ID (no .edu requirement; no country restrictions stated on the page).
findings.claim: Get an Org ID from your VC/accelerator/angel provider, then apply via the AWS Builder ID credits-application flow choosing the Portfolio tier; 5-10 business day review.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page - AWS Promotional Credit T&C apply.
findings.gotchas: The ceiling is 'up to' $200,000 (variable award); provider gating means bootstrapped founders cannot use this tier; credits are USD and promo-T&C bound.

findings.name: AWS Credits for AI Startups (invite-only add-on track)
findings.detail: '$200,000+ in AWS Credits' described as 'Invite only for startups ready to scale post Activate Portfolio', accessed through an Account Manager; separate 'AI startups ready to grow may be eligible for additional credits beyond Activate' noted on the main startups page.
findings.eligibility: Invitation-only; aimed at AI startups that have already gone through Activate Portfolio; via an AWS Account Manager.
findings.claim: No self-serve application - request via your AWS Account Manager after Activate Portfolio participation.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page - promo T&C apply.
findings.gotchas: Invite-only means no guaranteed path; the '+' after $200,000 is not quantified on the page.

findings.name: Kiro Startup Credits (separate, smaller credit track)
findings.detail: A separate, smaller AWS credit program 'available to eligible startups without current Activate Credits' from the Kiro agentic IDE program (launched 2025); also described as 'Kiro credits designed for startups'. Exact amounts, duration and eligibility criteria were not retrievable today (kiro.aws and /aws.amazon.com/kiro/ did not resolve from this environment).
findings.eligibility: Startups without current Activate credits, per the credits page; further criteria unknown.
findings.claim: Details not retrievable in this environment; check Kiro's official site/credits page directly.
findings.expiry: Unknown.
findings.gotchas: Unquantified in official AWS pages fetched today; treat any third-party numbers as unverified.

findings.name: AWS Educate (free student/individual training, not a credit program)
findings.detail: AWS Educate (successor of Cloud Academy) is active and 'completely for free': free self-paced online training and hands-on labs covering Storage (S3), Compute (EC2), Networking (VPC), Databases (RDS) and Cloud Operations, with shareable digital badges. Open to any individual, 'no credit card needed'; learners as young as 13 can register with just an email address; 18+ also get job-board access; 'AWS Educate for employers' gives recruiters access to the trained talent pool. The page (copyright 2026) contains no dollar-credit amounts and no mention of granting personal AWS Free Tier accounts.
findings.eligibility: Any individual with an email - no .edu requirement, no institutional enrollment required; age floor 13.
findings.claim: Register at aws.amazon.com/educate/ with any email address; complete self-paced courses and labs; earn badges.
findings.expiry: No expiry; free while the program is live.
findings.gotchas: Not a money-credit offer - value is training/badges, not AWS usage credits; if you need actual AWS usage (RDS/Aurora/DynamoDB) you still sign up for the regular AWS account (and, if brand-new, get the Free plan credits under the general program, which does not itself require .edu).

sunset_notes: Key 2025-2026 changes: (1) 2025-07-15 cutover - AWS replaced the legacy 12-month service-level Free Tier with a credit-based model: new accounts get a 6-month 'Free plan' ($100 signup credits + up to $100 service-exploration credits = up to $200) or a Paid plan; accounts created before 2025-07-15 are grandfathered on the old 12-month per-service free tier (e.g. RDS: 750 hours/month single-AZ, 20 GB gp2 storage, 20 GB backup). (2) Free-plan accounts auto-close at 6 months or when credits run out; data retained 90 days, then permanently erased. (3) Startup program restructuring: the /startups/credits/ page now lists 'Activate Founders' (up to $5,000; starts at $1,000) and 'Activate Portfolio' (up to $200,000, was the $150,000 Founders' Program era ceiling; the previous 'Accelerate' up to $100,000 tier name no longer appears) plus two newer tracks - 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' ($200,000+, invite-only post-Portfolio) and 'Kiro Startup Credits'. The exact 2025-2026 rename/retirement dates could not be confirmed: WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted, so only the current official pages could be verified. (4) No .edu-gated student dollar-credit license was found: the education front is AWS Educate (free training/badges, no credits) and institutional 'special pricing' programs; AWS Academy pages returned 404 on fetched sub-paths, so its current status/offerings are unverified rather than confirmed active or sunsetting. (5) Free-plan credits are unavailable in China regions or AWS GovCloud (US); the Free plan also excludes all promotional credits (Activate), so startup credits effectively require a Paid-plan account.
label_name: AWS Free Tier Credits (incl. RDS, Aurora

findings.name: AWS Free Plan (new-customer Free Tier): up to $200 credits over 6 months
findings.detail: New AWS customers get $100 in Free Tier credits immediately on account creation, plus up to $100 more earned by completing 5 console activities in the 'Explore AWS' widget ($20 each: launch & terminate an EC2 instance; configure an RDS database; build a Lambda function with a function URL; submit a prompt in the Bedrock text playground; create an AWS Budgets alert). The Free plan covers 90+ services for up to 6 months with 'no charges and no surprise bills'; 30+ services remain always-free within monthly limits on both plans. Credits are auto-applied to eligible usage, including always-free overages. Free-plan accounts cannot use 'certain AWS services that would rapidly consume the entire credit amount, or hardware purchases'; Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is paid-plan exclusive. Announcement: AWS 'what's new' July 16, 2025; AWS News Blog July 15, 2025. Eligible EC2 free-tier instance types for accounts on/after Jul 15, 2025: t3.micro, t3.small, t4g.micro, t4g.small, c7i-flex.large, m7i-flex.large (t2.micro no longer eligible). RDS free on db.t3.micro / db.t4g.micro (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, SQL Server Express); Aurora PostgreSQL serverless up to 4 ACU + 1 GiB storage; Aurora DSQL always free at 100k DPU + 1 GiB storage/month.
findings.eligibility: New AWS customers only (any existing or previously-held AWS account disqualifies you). All customers can sign up online; no .edu or startup requirement. Excluded regions: China (ZHY) and China (BJS) regions, and AWS GovCloud (US) regions (with a carve-out for certain services such as Lambda in GovCloud). Credit card NOT required to sign up for most new customers (AWS may request a payment method to verify identity in some cases).
findings.claim: Go to https://aws.amazon.com/free/ -> 'Create a free account' -> choose the Free account plan during signup. $100 credit posts automatically (may take up to ~10 min to appear on the Credits page). Complete the 5 Explore AWS activities inside 6 months to earn the remaining $100. Monitor balance via the Cost & Usage widget on console home.
findings.expiry: Free plan expires at the earlier of (a) 6 months from account creation or (b) credits exhausted. Unused credits stay usable up to 12 months from account creation if you upgrade to a Paid plan within the window. After the Free plan period, you have 90 days to upgrade; then AWS permanently closes the account and deletes content/resources. Earned-credit activities must be completed within 6 months of creation; eligibility to earn ends permanently if you join AWS Organizations or set up a Control Tower landing zone.
findings.gotchas: Free plan is NOT eligible for promotional/incentive credits (e.g., AWS Activate) - those require a Paid plan; enrolling a Free-plan account in AWS Organizations auto-upgrades it to Paid. Usage is aggregated across all regions; no monthly free-usage rollover. AWS may reclaim resources unused for 3 months after 30 days' notice. Free plan is for evaluation only - 'should not be used for processing sensitive data'. Data transfer/egress beyond always-free allowances draws on credits, then pay-as-you-go once credits run out. New sign-up experience launched October 2026 (credit expiry view moved to Settings Portal; older accounts use the Credits page in the Billing console).

findings.name: AWS Always Free offers: 30+ services with monthly free usage limits (all customers)
findings.detail: On both Free and Paid plans, '30+ AWS services are always free within monthly usage limits' (ongoing monthly allowances, e.g., Lambda free requests/month, Aurora DSQL 100k DPU + 1 GiB storage/month). If usage exceeds the monthly allowance, remaining Free Tier credits auto-apply to cover eligible costs (Free plan); on Paid plans you pay standard rates beyond the credit balance. Per-service numeric limits are listed on the Free Tier page filters ('Explore our offers' by offer type + product category) and on individual product pricing pages; the main page does not publish the full numeric list.
findings.eligibility: All AWS customers, new and existing, on either plan. No credit card needed to keep an account. No regional restrictions stated beyond the general Free Tier exclusions.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim - always-free allowances are automatically active on any AWS account. Find each service's allowance at https://aws.amazon.com/free/ via the offer-type/category filters, or on the product's pricing page.
findings.expiry: Ongoing for as long as you have an AWS account (no 12-month sunset). Unused monthly allowances do not roll over. AWS may terminate any offer at any time (Free Tier Terms, last updated Jul 9, 2025).
findings.gotchas: Overage handling differs by plan (credits vs pay-as-you-go). A few services/trials are paid-plan exclusive. AWS can reclaim resources idle for 3 months (30 days notice); usage is aggregated across regions.

findings.name: Legacy 12-month Free Tier (accounts created before July 15, 2025)
findings.detail: Accounts created before Jul 15, 2025 keep the classic per-service 12-month Free Tier instead of the credit model: e.g., EC2 750 hrs/month of t2.micro/t3.micro with free-tier-eligible EBS (standard, st1, sc1, gp2, gp3); legacy allowances like 30 GB EBS / 2M I/Os / 1 GB snapshot storage and 750 hrs/month ELB (Classic+ALB shared, 15 GB data processing, 15 LCUs). Exceeding limits bills pay-as-you-go. RDS legacy free usage (db.t3.micro/db.t4g.micro) runs up to 12 months from signup for such accounts. The legacy EC2 free-tier box in the console only appears for pre-Jul-15-2025 accounts.
findings.eligibility: Only AWS accounts created before July 15, 2025.
findings.claim: No claim - applied automatically at legacy signup; track via the EC2 'Free Tier usage' console box (end-of-month forecast / exceeds-free-tier warnings).
findings.expiry: 12 months from account creation; then standard pay-as-you-go rates with no credit-based protection.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse the two regimes: new accounts (on/after Jul 15, 2025) have NO per-service 12-month allowances - usage is instead covered by the $200 credit pool and always-free offers. t2.micro is not free-tier eligible for new accounts.

findings.name: AWS Activate Founders (self-funded startups): $1,000, up to $5,000 credits
findings.detail: Activate Founders tier: start with $1,000 USD in AWS Activate credits; 'select participants may qualify for additional credits up to $5,000' over time. Credits offset costs on 200+ AWS services incl. infrastructure, data services, and third-party models on Amazon Bedrock (OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Meta). Includes technical guidance, business mentorship, and go-to-market resources. AWS Activate has served 350k+ startups and granted $8B+ in credits since 2013.
findings.eligibility: Self-funded/bootstrapped startup; new to AWS Activate Credits; fully functioning company website; founded in the last 10 years; AWS account must be on a Paid plan (Free-plan accounts are ineligible).
findings.claim: https://aws.amazon.com/startups/ -> 'Apply now' (/startups/join?destination=/credits/apply) -> create/sign in with an AWS Builder ID using a professional (business-domain) email -> complete the one-time AWS Activate profile with your business email (matching startup domain) -> choose Founders tier -> provide product description, funding stage, company profile -> link your AWS account and submit. Response in 5-10 business days.
findings.expiry: Govered by AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions; check the specific award notice for the credit's expiry window (not stated on the program page).
findings.gotchas: Paid-plan account required - convert your Free plan account first; using an inconsistent email domain hampers validation; if you previously received equal-or-greater Activate credits you cannot re-claim. Kiro Startup Credits exist as an on-ramp for startups that do NOT yet hold Activate credits. Credits are USD and non-transferable between programs.

findings.name: AWS Activate Portfolio (VC / accelerator / angel-backed startups): up to $200,000 credits
findings.detail: Activate Portfolio tier: up to $200,000 USD in AWS Activate credits, applied through the backing provider's Organizational ID (Org ID). Named provider examples on the page: Andreessen Horowitz, Brex, Carta, Greylock Partners, Sequoia, Y Combinator, NVIDIA (among 'thousands' of VCs, accelerators, and startup-enabling organizations). Credits work across 200+ services and Bedrock third-party models. Program page headlines 'Get up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits' and notes AI startups 'may be eligible for additional credits beyond Activate'.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Series B stage (most recent funding round within the last 12 months, if applicable); affiliated with an Activate Provider who issues your Org ID; not previously received AWS Activate credits of equal or greater value; functioning company website; founded in the last 10 years; AWS account on a Paid plan.
findings.claim: Verify your investor/accelerator is a listed Activate Provider at https://aws.amazon.com/startups/ -> apply with the provider's Org ID (same Builder ID / Activate profile flow as Founders) -> submit startup details -> link AWS account. Rolling review, 5-10 business days.
findings.expiry: AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs apply; per-award expiry is in the award notice.
findings.gotchas: Without an Org ID from a participating provider you cannot access this tier - bootstrapped founders should use Founders instead. Pre-Series B requirement and 10-year founding-age cap apply. The Free plan does not qualify (Paid plan required), and Free-plan accounts became ineligible for promotional credits effective Feb 16, 2026.

findings.name: AWS Credits for AI Startups (invite-only): $200,000+ credits
findings.detail: Separate, invite-only track on the official credits page: '$200,000+ in AWS Credits' for 'startups ready to scale post Activate Portfolio', accessed by 'talk with your Account Manager'. The June 4, 2026 step-by-step guide confirms 'Additional AWS Credits above $200,000 are available for AI startups ready to scale beyond Activate's tiers.'
findings.eligibility: AI-focused startups that have already moved through Activate Portfolio and are scaling; not publicly self-service - routed via an AWS Account Manager. Pre-Series B context applies to the Activate program family; account on Paid plan.
findings.claim: Engage your AWS Account Manager; no public application form.
findings.expiry: AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs; per-award notice.
findings.gotchas: Not available to self-funded/bootstrapped founders; no public quota or deadline - purely relationship/invite-driven.

findings.name: Kiro Startup Credits: up to 1 year of Kiro Pro+ credits (3 user tiers)
findings.detail: Kiro (AWS's agentic AI IDE) offers startups 'up to 1-year's worth of Kiro Pro+ credits' in three tiers: Starter - up to 2 Kiro users; Growth - up to 10 users; Scale - up to 30 users. Credits are added to the startup's AWS account and used via AWS IAM Identity Center. Described as designed for startups and serving as an on-ramp for startups that do not yet hold Activate Credits.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage to Series A startups; official business email address matching the startup's domain; an AWS Account ID with a matching email required. Startups already holding active AWS Activate credits are NOT eligible for this promotion (their existing credits can still be used toward Kiro). Offer excludes residents of several listed countries/regions (listed on the page).
findings.claim: Submit the form on the linked AWS Startups page (kiro.dev/startups/) -> sign in with your AWS account -> applications reviewed on a rolling basis -> if approved, credits are automatically added to your AWS account.
findings.expiry: Credits expire one year after issuance to the AWS account; after depletion, billing automatically switches to standard Kiro Pro+ billing. No dollar amount is published (value = 1 year of Kiro Pro+ at the tier's user count).
findings.gotchas: No exact dollar figure on the official page; tier is by user count, not dollars; region exclusions apply; Kipro... (correct: Kiro) usage requires logging in through AWS IAM Identity Center - set that up before claiming.

findings.name: AWS Builder Center Student Rewards (launched Aug 20, 2026): up to $579 value for verified university students
findings.detail: New student program on AWS Builder Center, part of AWS's $500M+ commitment to student cloud/AI training: verified + profile complete = 12 months of Skill Builder Premium ($449 value; 900+ courses, hands-on labs, cert exam prep, game-based learning); 7 badges = $10 AWS credits; 14 badges = additional $20 AWS credits; 21 badges = AWS Foundational-level certification exam voucher (~$100, e.g., Cloud Practitioner). Total potential value $579/student. Free Builder Center workshops (no credit card) and Student Builder Groups in 60+ countries available to all.
findings.eligibility: Students 18+ enrolled at an accredited higher-education institution, worldwide; enrollment verified via SheerID (name, college name, school email; sometimes extra documentation, 24-48h). No .edu-only restriction beyond SheerID verification; no credit card.
findings.claim: https://builder.aws.com -> sign in with AWS Builder ID -> /student-rewards -> start SheerID student verification -> complete profile (photo + About section) to unlock the 12-month Skill Builder Premium -> earn community badges (publish articles, comment, maintain 7/30/90-day activity streaks, wishes) to unlock $10 / $20 credits and the exam voucher -> claim at builder.aws.com/profile/rewards.
findings.expiry: Skill Builder Premium lasts 12 months from claim. The 21 badges include time-gated ones (7-day, 30-day, 90-day streaks), so the program effectively requires sustained engagement over ~90 days to capture the full value; credits/voucher per promotional terms.
findings.gotchas: The credits/voucher are NOT handed at signup - they require earning 7/14/21 Builder Center activity badges (community badges, not course-completion badges). Start long-timer badges on day 1 or you can stall at 15-18. Verification is individual; your college does not need to be an AWS Academy member.

findings.name: AWS Educate ('Cloud Skills for Education'): free self-paced learning, hands-on labs, no credit card
findings.detail: AWS Educate is open to any individual regardless of education, experience, or career stage: free curated learning paths in cloud and AI with five hands-on 'Getting Started' lab tracks (Storage/S3 static website, Compute/EC2, Networking/VPC, Databases/RDS, Cloud Operations/cost estimation), shareable digital badges, and a Job Board (learners 18+; separate recruiter portal). Learners as young as 13 can register with just an email address - 'no credit card needed'. Complemented by free self-paced digital training on AWS Skill Builder (500+ on-demand courses, 17 languages) and free Builder Center workshops in real AWS environments.
findings.eligibility: No .edu email required - any valid email; age 13+ to register, 18+ for the Job Board. Global.
findings.claim: https://aws.amazon.com/education/awseducate/ -> sign in / register for AWS Educate; each hands-on lab links to a registration page (promo code 'EducateLP'); Skill Builder at https://skillbuilder.aws (free tier) or Builder Center workshops.
findings.expiry: Ongoing program - no expiry. (Legacy monetary grants no longer exist; see sunset notes.)
findings.gotchas: Since Feb 21, 2023 AWS Educate focuses on pre-professional learners and no longer offers grants to institutions or educators; classroom credit allotments now run through AWS Academy/instructor-managed labs. Educator tools were migrated to AWS Academy. Hands-on lab accounts are restricted/sandboxed (third-party docs describe ~3-hour activity logoff and feature limits).

findings.name: AWS Academy: free ready-to-teach curriculum + educator certification vouchers (instructor/education track)
findings.detail: AWS Academy provides higher-education institutions a free, ready-to-teach cloud/AI-ML curriculum (6 foundational courses incl. Generative AI Foundations and ML Foundations, 5 associate-level courses, 2 lab sets, plus an ad-hoc 'Learner Lab' sandbox). Educators: complimentary enablement sessions, 100% discount vouchers on AWS Certification exams, and complimentary 12-month AWS Skill Builder subscription. Students: complimentary 12-month Skill Builder subscription and, on course completion, access to the Emerging Talent Community (challenges redeemable for discounted certification exam vouchers). Institutions: 50% discount voucher on certification exams (redeems to students for 100% of value). No cost to join. Third-party university IT docs (Univ. of Iowa) describe 'Learning Labs' giving instructors $100 of AWS credit per student for the course duration, no credit card from students, instructor-funded.
findings.eligibility: Institution level: higher-ed institutions offering accredited degrees, diplomas, certificates, or continuing-education programs, with an authorized Program Administrator/CPOC who applies. Educators must be nominated by the member institution and complete the mandatory Educator Getting Started course (associate-level courses additionally require educator certification). Courses may only be delivered to students enrolled at the institution.
findings.claim: Institution applies via https://aws.amazon.com/training/awsacademy/ -> CPOC nominates educators -> educators set up portal access, acknowledge Program Guide, complete onboarding course -> deliver courses (synchronous/asynchronous, LMS integration allowed) -> students register an AWS Training & Certification account and get course links; classroom credits (where available) are provisioned by the institution's AWS team.
findings.expiry: 12-month Skill Builder subscriptions from award; certification vouchers per program terms ('all rewards subject to change'); Emerging Talent Community rewards vary.
findings.gotchas: This is an education-license/curriculum offer, not direct cash credits - the per-student classroom credits (~$100, per institution docs) are not published on AWS's national pages and depend on your institution's enrollment; confirm amounts with your AWS regional team. No cost to join, but delivery requirements (accredited educators, full curriculum) apply.

findings.name: AWS Cloud Credit for Research: up to $5,000 for students, uncapped for faculty/staff
findings.detail: AWS Public Sector Cloud Credit for Research Program grants AWS Promotional Credit to support finite research projects: building cloud-hosted science-as-a-service applications/tools, proof-of-concept or benchmark tests of moving research workloads/open data to the cloud, or training the community via workshops/tutorials. Student awards capped at $5,000; faculty and staff awards are not capped; recipients may receive less than requested. EC2 usage is on-demand and spot instances only. Awards are AWS Promotional Credit under the AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs, valid one year from application to the account or until fully utilized.
findings.eligibility: Full-time faculty, full-time research staff, or graduate/post-graduate/PhD students at an accredited research institution. An institution-issued email (.edu, .org, or equivalent) is REQUIRED - non-institution domains are not accepted. An existing AWS account is required. Program is global except the greater China region (India administered by AISPL). Effective Feb 16, 2026, Free Tier (Free plan) accounts are ineligible for promotional credits.
findings.claim: Submit a short single-page proposal (problem statement, project summary, specific AWS services, timeline/milestones, plan to share outcomes, future use, AWS contacts, any AWS Public Datasets used) via https://pages.awscloud.com/aws-cloud-credit-for-research.html; rolling review; decisions via aws-research-credit@amazon.com.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 1 year from application to the account or until fully used - plan the project timeline accordingly.
findings.gotchas: Does NOT fund administrative workloads, operations, ongoing/established research, or general lab funding. Review cycle is listed as 30-60 days on the apply page (the main page says 90-120 days) - plan ahead. Promotional credits cannot cover upfront fees of services. Free-plan accounts are excluded as of Feb 16, 2026 - you need a Paid-plan account to hold the award.

findings.name: Amazon SageMaker Studio Lab: free hosted Jupyter ML environment (CPU/GPU sessions, no AWS account)
findings.detail: SageMaker Studio Lab is a completely free notebook environment for learning/experimenting with ML code and models: Jupyter-based with terminal access and GitHub integration; per university ITS documentation, access to CPU (12 hours per user session) and GPU (4 hours per user session) plus 15 GB of persistent storage that survives between sessions. No credit card or even an AWS account needed - a valid email is enough. Instructors can obtain reference codes from their regional AWS team for classroom access.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a valid email address; no credit card, no AWS account, no .edu requirement. Class-wide access via instructor-issued reference codes.
findings.claim: Sign in at https://studiolab.sagemaker.aws/ (linked from https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/studio-lab/) with a valid email; instructors request reference codes from the AWS team supporting their institution.
findings.expiry: Session-based limits (CPU/GPU hours per user session); the 15 GB persistent storage persists between sessions.
findings.gotchas: For learning/experimentation only - not a production or long-term workload environment. Exact current session caps should be confirmed at sign-in (the site blocked automated fetching today, 403; figures above are from a 2024 university IT page).

sunset_notes: Major 2025-2026 changes: (1) July 15, 2025 - the classic 12-month per-service Free Tier was replaced for NEW accounts with a credit-based model: $100 sign-up credit + up to $100 earned via 5 console activities, a 6-month Free plan window (account closes at 6 months or when credits run out), 90+ services, and 30+ always-free services; accounts created before July 15, 2025 retain the legacy 12-month tier. Free-tier-eligible EC2 instances changed too (t2.micro dropped; t3.small, t4g.small, c7i-flex.large, m7i-flex.large added). (2) Short-term free trials are now paid-plan-only; the Free plan only gets 'Always Free' offers. (3) Feb 21, 2023 - AWS Educate stopped its old monetary grants ($35/$100 student grants, $75/$200 educator grants); educator tooling moved to AWS Academy. (4) Feb 16, 2026 - Free plan (Free Tier) accounts became ineligible for promotional credits, which affects AWS Cloud Credit for Research and similar programs (a Paid plan is required to hold awards). (5) Aug 20, 2026 - AWS launched Student Rewards on AWS Builder Center as part of a $500M+ student commitment; the old 'AWS Activate for Students' style offer no longer appears on aws.amazon.com - student benefits are now Builder Center Student Rewards + AWS Educate + AWS Academy. (6) October 2026 - new AWS sign-up experience launched; credit-expiry display moved to the Settings Portal (accounts that signed up before Oct 2026 still use the Credits page in the Billing console). No free offer listed above was fully sunset as of 2026-10-22.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial — $300 welcome credit (90 days)
findings.detail: Any new user gets $300 in free 'Welcome credit' valid for 90 days, plus access to the always-free GCP Free Tier and product-specific trials (e.g., Spanner 90-day instance with 10GB storage, 30-day AlloyDB basic cluster 8-vCPU/1TB, 30-day Cloud SQL trial, 30-day Looker trial). The $300 credit covers usage beyond free-tier limits on covered products. No billing during the trial. One trial per person (must never have been a paying GCP/Maps Platform/Firebase user and never have signed up before). Trial cannot be paused or extended. If you don't upgrade to a paid account within 90 days (or exhaust the $300), the account enters a 30-day grace period, then resources/data are permanently deleted.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide (no .edu, no age limit). Must not be an existing paying Google Cloud/Maps/Firebase customer, and must not have previously signed up for the Free Trial. A valid credit/debit card (or other accepted payment method) IS required at sign-up — Google places a temporary $0.00–$1.00 authorization hold for identity/fraud verification, not a charge. Depending on country, bank verification may also be needed.
findings.claim: Sign up at console.cloud.google.com/freetrial (or cloud.google.com/free → 'Get started for free'): provide card, verify identity; $300 credit + Free Tier + product trials activate. To keep resources: click 'Activate' on the console Welcome page to upgrade to a Paid billing account before day 90 (remaining credit stays usable until day 90 from signup).
findings.expiry: $300 credit expires 90 days from signup; free-tier quotas continue indefinitely with monthly resets (no rollover); Google can change/eliminate Free Tier limits with 30 days' notice.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free: during trial you can't add GPUs/TPUs, can't use Cloud Marketplace, can't request quota increases, can't use Windows Server VMs; the $300 credit cannot pay for Gemini API-in-AI-Studio costs (use the separate Gemini API free tier) or third-party managed AI models ('model as a service'); crypto mining prohibited. After trial end + 30-day grace, data on services like Compute Engine is deleted. Overage after trial charges the card on standard rates.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Tier (always-free monthly quotas, 20+ products)
findings.detail: Free-forever monthly usage on select GCP products, e.g.: Compute Engine 1 e2-micro VM/month (us-west1/us-central1/us-east1; time-based across those regions) + 30GB standard persistent disk + 1GB egress; Cloud Storage 5GB US regional storage, 5,000 Class A / 50,000 Class B ops, 100GB NA egress; Cloud Run 2M requests, 360,000 GB-s memory & 180,000 vCPU-s, 1GB NA egress; Cloud Run functions 2M invocations; BigQuery 1TiB queries + 10GiB storage/month; App Engine Standard 28 F1-h/day + 9 B1-h/day + 1GB egress/day; Firestore 1GiB, 50k reads/20k writes/20k deletes per day; GKE 1 cluster charge/month; GCS egress and other egress outside NA or beyond limits bill at standard rates. GPUs/TPUs never free.
findings.eligibility: Requires an active GCP billing account (Paid or Free Trial) in good standing; no negotiated pricing contract. No .edu or age requirement; effectively free tier is available to any GCP account holder. Free-tier benefits on Cloud Storage apply only to us-east1/us-west1/us-central1.
findings.claim: Create any GCP billing account (usually via the $300 Free Trial signup, which requires a card); stay within per-product monthly quotas and you are never billed. Do not create paid resources beyond quotas, or overage bills on your card.
findings.expiry: No end date, but Google reserves the right to change or eliminate limits with 30 days' advance notice; quotas do not roll over.
findings.gotchas: Common trap: creating a GCP account for 'free tier' still typically needs a card (Free Trial signup requires one); egress, cross-region traffic, GPU/TPU, and overage are billed; limits are per billing account.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program — Start tier ($2,000 GCP credits)
findings.detail: For 'digital-native' startups with a working MVP and plans to seek venture funding soon: $2,000 in GCP credits, valid 12 months (applies to GCP services and select GCP offerings; covers Google's proprietary models — program credits do NOT cover third-party models, which are billed directly). Also included: free-tier AI Studio (Generative AI Studio) access, 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus free (new signups), $200 Google Skills training credit, and 'Startup Perks' (partner discounts/offers).
findings.eligibility: Founded within the last 24 months; has NOT yet received Google Cloud credits beyond the free trial; digital-native tech startup with working MVP + clear business model + plans to seek VC funding soon. Excluded: service agencies, consultancies, traditional small businesses; companies that have IPO'd or been acquired; educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content companies, dev shops, crypto mining companies, token distributors contrary to regulatory guidance. Acceptance at Google Cloud's discretion. No VC funding required at this tier (it's the pre-funded stage).
findings.claim: Apply self-serve at cloud.google.com/startup/apply (per-tier page: cloud.google.com/startup/pre-seed). You must sign in with a Google account whose business email matches your public website domain, and provide your 18-character GCP billing account ID (create a GCP billing account if you don't have one); Google reviews (most decisions within a few business days); credits are deposited to your billing account.
findings.expiry: GCP credits: 12 months from issuance. Workspace Business Plus: 12 months. Google Skills $200 credit: training credits; expiration not stated on the Start page (student program credits expire 1 year after issuance — treat similarly). No renewal; re-applications case-by-case via cloudstartupsupport@google.com.
findings.gotchas: Start-tier page does not state a credit-card requirement, but you need an existing GCP billing account to receive credits, and creating a new GCP account/payment setup typically requires a payment method (Free Trial signup definitely does, per docs). Workspace benefit: your company domain must not have been on a paid Google Workspace plan within 31 days of applying, and the benefit cannot be applied to annual Workspace plans. Credits excluded from Marketplace/third-party products; egress/networking costs beyond free tiers still billable.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program — Scale tier (up to $200,000 GCP credits over 2 years; $350,000 for AI-first)
findings.detail: VC-funded early-stage startups get up to $200,000 in GCP credits over two years: Year 1 = 100% credit up to $100,000; Year 2 = 20% credit on year-2 spend, up to an additional $100,000. AI-first startups: Year 1 = 100% up to $250,000, Year 2 = 20% up to +$100,000 → up to $350,000 total (equivalently, 'qualifying venture-backed startups can tap an additional $150,000 with the AI startup program' on top of the $200K base). Program credits cover Google's models (Gemini, Gemma); third-party models billed directly and not covered. Also: up to $12,000 Enhanced Support credits for one year (1-hour critical response), 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus free, $600/month Google Maps Platform credits for one year (separate application), $500 Google Skills training credits, dedicated Startup Success Manager + Startup Customer Engineers, Web3 program access, and partner perks.
findings.eligibility: Must have received 'recent startup equity funding' (pre-seed to Series A by an institutional investor/VC, or common Web3 funding sources — SAFE agreements and verifiable token raises/blockchain foundation grants count; definition: Pre-Seed/Seed rounds within the last 5 years, Series A rounds within the last 12 months). Founded within the last 5 years (stealth mode OK with investor-verified funding). Must not have received more than $5,000 in GCP credits already. Not eligible: IPO'd/acquired companies, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content, dev shops, consultancies/agencies, crypto-mining companies, token distributors against regulatory guidance; private-equity, government-innovation-grant, crowdfunding, angel and friends-&-family funding do NOT qualify for Scale tier (may be evaluated for Start tier instead).
findings.claim: Apply self-serve at cloud.google.com/startup/apply (per-tier page: cloud.google.com/startup/seed-series-a). Sign in with the company business email matching your public website domain + provide the 18-character GCP billing account ID + verification of funding (public sources; stealth: work with your investor). Decision usually within a few business days (manual review may take longer); credits deposit to your billing account and you receive an in-console benefit tracker.
findings.expiry: Year-1 credits usable in year 1; year-2 credits (20% of spend, capped +$100K) accrue in year 2 → program spans 2 years. Workspace 12 months; Maps $600/month for 1 year (separate app); Enhanced Support credits valid 1 year.
findings.gotchas: Year-2 benefit is a 20% discount-style credit on actual year-2 spend (max $100K) — it is not a pre-funded $100K; you must keep spending. Credits exclude Marketplace third-party offerings, third-party AI models, and per footnote only 'GCP Services and Select GCP offerings'. Workspace 31-day paid-plan rule applies. Google 'unable to accept' a long exclusion list (see eligibility); acceptance at Google's discretion. AI tier requires being genuinely 'AI-first' (AI in foundational structure/strategy, not a bolt-on) — some applicants get rejected even if they say AI. Data/egress: credits offset compute/AI usage, but egress and overage still bill if credits exhaust.

findings.name: Startup program add-ons announced 2025–2026: 'New: AI benefits' ($350K ceiling), Web3 benefits, ISV Startup Springboard, Gemini Startup Forum
findings.detail: The benefits page now labels 'New: AI benefits' (AI webinars/content, dedicated AI training, resources, experts, access to up to $350,000 in credits) and 'New: Web3 benefits' (Web3 Perks: partner offers from Quicknode, TRM, Allium and more). FAQ: Web3 startups get 'up to $200,000 USD over two years for Google Cloud and Firebase usage' plus Discord channel, foundation grants, VIP event access. Scale-tier page adds ISV Startup Springboard (12-week program for emerging AI startups: bespoke technical guidance + GTM resources) and the Gemini Startup Forum (Google for Startups + DeepMind + Cloud; curated in-person gatherings for seed–Series A founders). Benefits page also lists a 'Future of AI: Perspectives on generative media for startups' report and Cloud Startup Customer Engineers with faster response times for critical issues.
findings.eligibility: AI tier: Scale-tier VC-backed startups that are AI-first (AI foundational to product/strategy). Web3: startups with verifiable token raises / blockchain foundation grants (SAFE also eligible). ISV Springboard: emerging AI startups in the program. Forum: seed-to-Series A founders (invitation/curated).
findings.claim: No separate application — benefits come with Scale-tier approval; Web3 program has its own qualification via the same application (flag yourself as Web3); Springboard/Forum through program onboarding. Re-applications or questions: cloudstartupsupport@google.com.
findings.expiry: AI-credits structure (Y1 $250K 100% + Y2 20% up to $100K) spans 2 years; Web3 $200K over 2 years; Springboard is a 12-week cohort.
findings.gotchas: Web3 'up to $200,000' covers Google Cloud AND Firebase (distinct from the $350K AI cloud-credits ceiling — these are different track framings). Third-party models still billed direct. AI-first qualification is subjective and at Google's discretion; being an 'AI company' in name isn't enough (FAQ example: another AI startup founder did not qualify).

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education — faculty teaching credits (up to $100 per teaching staff + up to $50 per student)
findings.detail: Eligible faculty can apply for GCP credits for classroom use: up to $100 in GCP credits per teaching staff and up to $50 in GCP credits per student, so students get hands-on cloud experience at no cost. Application is limited to faculty (students cannot apply for their own teaching credits; they can encourage faculty to apply for their next course). Course start date must be no more than 1 year out; approved credits are redeemable from approval until 16 weeks after the course start date, and are good for up to 1 year after course start. Credits attach to specified school-issued email domains and are non-transferable. Faculty Community access is restricted to verified/approved faculty. Also linked: Career Launchpad program (coach students through Google Cloud certificates/credentials) and Google DeepMind AI Research Foundations curriculum.
findings.eligibility: Faculty only, at an academic institution; requires official school email with a valid .edu (or equivalent institutional) domain ('Please use your official school email address with a valid edu domain'; if none, you may nominate another address, credits attach to it and are non-transferable); must provide faculty directory profile link. Country restriction: the teaching program is 'currently only available in' a listed set of ~60 countries (Argentina, Australia, Canada, Germany, India, Japan, Nigeria, UK, US, etc. — the country dropdown on the form; if your country is absent you can only 'express interest').
findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching/ (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/faculty → 'Apply for Cloud credits'). Fill personal info with school .edu email, country, institution, faculty directory link, course details (name, start date, abstract, course URL) and member info (all school-issued domains, expected students/TA-staff count). Check spam for CloudEduGrants@google.com confirmations; redeem credits via the education-credits redemption guide once approved.
findings.expiry: Credits good for up to 1 year after course start; redeemable window = approval through 16 weeks after course start; course start must be within 1 year of application.
findings.gotchas: Not open to students directly (students must go through faculty). .edu/institutional email effectively required (nomination of alternate email loses the .edu gate but credits stay non-transferable). Country list is restrictive — not all countries served. Small amounts ($100/$50) — intended for learning, not production. Students should avoid accidentally signing up for the GCP Free Trial with personal cards in classroom contexts (Google's own faculty guide warns of this).

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education — student training credits ($200 Google Skills credits) and free labs/badges
findings.detail: Students can request $200 in Google Skills (formerly Cloud Skills Boost) training credits, which expire one year after issuance, plus free access to online hands-on labs, skill badges, and courses; Google Skills Arcade (gamified challenges with badges) is free. The student page also points to DSC (Developer Student Clubs) and the Career Launchpad pathway. This is training credit, not GCP usage credit — students do not get a separate GCP-usage student credit program (the individual $300 Free Trial is the only personal usage credit, and it requires a card).
findings.eligibility: Students (individuals); request via the student training-credits form (services.google.com/fb/forms/googlecloudskillsbooststudenttrainingcreditsapplication/). No .edu gate stated on the page, but it's a student-facing learning program; free labs/courses also available without the credit.
findings.claim: On cloud.google.com/edu/students click 'Request credits' → complete the Google Skills Boost student training-credits application form; $200 credits are issued to your account and usable on Google Skills courses/badges within 1 year.
findings.expiry: $200 Google Skills credits expire one year after issuance; free labs/Arcade have no stated end.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse with GCP usage credits — this buys courses/badges, not compute. A separate 'apply for free Google Cloud credits' line on the /edu hub for students appears to funnel to the same faculty/teaching-credit program (per the hub, students get free credits via the higher-ed program, i.e., via faculty).

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education — research credits ('Academic Research Grants', up to $5,000)
findings.detail: Researchers can apply for up to $5,000 in GCP credits to advance research (computing power; GCP tools; proposal-based). Eligible roles: Faculty, Postdoctoral Researcher, PhD Student (and IT Admin option on the form), from accredited higher-education institutions or eligible nonprofit research institutions. Application requires: email (institution account preferred), country (restricted list of ~60 countries — program 'currently only available in' those countries), job title, organization (select from institution list), researcher/faculty directory link, project name, start date, a ≤250-word proposal (research problem, GCP tools, timeline, milestones, how GCP supports future work; Google Doc link allowed), field of research, intended use (proof of concept / evaluation-comparison / workshop-training / open-source development), optional Google Scholar link.
findings.eligibility: Faculty / PhD students / postdocs at accredited higher-ed or eligible nonprofit research institutions in the listed approved countries; institutional email preferred; faculty directory link required. Related institutional program: GPAR (Google Public Sector — Program for Accelerated Research) with co-investment, industry-leading pricing for AI accelerators (GPUs/TPUs), early access to TPUs/foundation models/datasets (AlphaFold, Earth AI), agentic AI (Co-scientist, AlphaEvolve), compliance (HIPAA, CMMC 2.0, FedRAMP), on-campus research days — GPAR is currently US-only.
findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research/ (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/researchers 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'). Submit the Academic Research Grant form with the fields above; credits are awarded to the institutional account and redeemable per the education-credits redemption guide.
findings.expiry: The public pages do not state a redemption window for research credits (teaching credits: 1 year post course-start; assume similar ~1-year usage window until confirmed in the FAQ); GPAR is a standing institutional program (US only).
findings.gotchas: Country-restricted list; institution must appear in the form's institution list ('begin typing and select'). Amount is 'up to $5,000' — awards may be less and are grant-reviewed. GPAR co-investment benefits are US-only. Institutional (not individual student) gate: undergraduates are not listed roles.

findings.name: Product-specific free trials for GCP databases/BI (no GCP-usage credit needed)
findings.detail: Separate short trials available on a GCP billing account: Spanner 90-day free trial instance (10 vCPUs? listed as '10 GB of storage' in docs: '10 vCPUs…' — docs say 90-day Spanner instance with 10GB storage at no cost); AlloyDB for PostgreSQL 30-day trial cluster (8 vCPU basic + 1TB storage capacity); Looker 30-day trial (all standard features); Cloud SQL 30-day trial. These require a billing account but cost nothing for the trial window.
findings.eligibility: Any GCP billing account (Free Trial or Paid); one instance per product per the trial terms.
findings.claim: In GCP console, provision the trial instance (Spanner/AlloyDB/Looker/Cloud SQL trial buttons in each product's UI) on a billing account; delete before trial end to avoid charges.
findings.expiry: 90 days (Spanner) / 30 days (AlloyDB, Looker, Cloud SQL); auto-conversion to billable instance afterward.
findings.gotchas: These are time-boxed, not free-forever; after trial end instances bill at standard rates unless deleted; GCP docs also point to Google Maps Platform free usage caps, Gemini AI Studio free tier, and Firebase no-cost plans as adjacent free offers.

sunset_notes: Verified as-of 2026-10-22 directly on the official pages (build stamps on the pages date 2026-10-21), so all core offers above are live. No sunsets found in 2025–2026; instead the startup program was expanded: (1) 'New: AI benefits' and 'New: Web3 benefits' labels appear on cloud.google.com/startup/benefits — the $350,000 AI-first ceiling (Year 1 100% up to $250K + Year 2 20% up to +$100K), ISV Startup Springboard (12-week AI program), and the Gemini Startup Forum are recent additions; Web3 track adds up to $200,000 over two years covering Google Cloud + Firebase plus Discord/foundation-grant access. (2) The program's public pages no longer present the older accelerator/VC partner-referral model — both tiers now have self-serve 'Apply now' portals (cloud.google.com/startup/pre-seed and /seed-series-a) with direct Google application, funding-verification (public sources; investor verification for stealth), and 18-character billing-account ID. I could not date the exact 2025 announcement of the AI-tier amounts because this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted; the current-state amounts/eligibility are high-confidence from the official pages, the historical-change framing is medium confidence. (3) Google Cloud Free Program: the $300/90-day trial and 20+ always-free products remain unchanged in today's docs, with the standing caveat that Google may change/eliminate Free Tier limits on 30 days' notice; trial resources are permanently deleted after the 30-day grace period. (4) Education: no sunset; GPAR research program is currently US-only (footnote on cloud.google.com/edu/researchers), and both the teaching and research credit forms carry country-restricted eligibility lists. Known-claims check: Start tier $2,000 pre-funded/MVP — confirmed; Scale up to $200,000 over 2 years, up to $350,000 AI-first — confirmed; 12-month free Workspace Business Plus — confirmed; accelerator/VC-funded framing — now replaced by self-serve application with VC-funding eligibility (VC/institutional equity from pre-seed to Series A still required for Scale tier). One caveat: the GCP startup pages never state a credit-card requirement; the FAQ says to have your 18-character billing account ID ready, and GCP account creation/payment setup generally requires a payment method (the Free Trial signup explicitly requires a card), so treat 'credit card NOT required' as unverified/likely false for account setup even though the program credits themselves cost nothing.

provider: Azure (Microsoft) — Managed Databases & Data Platforms (free tiers, trials, startup program, education offers)

findings.name: Azure SQL Database (serverless) — 'Free forever' tier
findings.detail: 100,000 vCore-seconds/month of Azure SQL Database serverless compute plus 32 GB storage, at $0 while within the free amounts, with no time limit (monthly recurring allowance). 100,000 vCore-sec ≈ 3.33 vCore-hours/day: a continuously running 1-vCore database ≈ 27.8 hrs/month; a 4-vCore database ≈ 6.9 hrs/month. Verified 2026-10-22 on the official /free/ page and the student-offer page; the dedicated SQL serverless pricing-details URL now 404s (Azure has reorganized pricing URLs).
findings.eligibility: All new and existing Azure customers (free account, student account, or pay-as-you-go); no credit card needed to stay inside the free amounts (signing up for an Azure account may still require a payment method unless using the no-CC student route). Not available in sovereign-cloud regions (US Government, Azure China, Azure Germany).
findings.claim: 1) Create an Azure account (free, student, or PAYG). 2) Deploy an Azure SQL database with serverless compute. 3) Stay within 100,000 vCore-seconds/month and 32 GB storage; compute auto-stops idle. No separate enrollment needed.
findings.expiry: No expiry — the free allowance recurs monthly for the life of the account (student accounts renew yearly while enrolled).
findings.gotchas: Compute beyond 100,000 vCore-sec/month and storage beyond 32 GB bill at PAYG rates; backups beyond included storage bill; data persists while compute auto-stops, but the DB is not 'free' if you exceed allowances. Not the old provisioned F0 'free' SKU — that SKU was retired in favor of this serverless allowance.

findings.name: Azure Cosmos DB — 'Free forever' tier
findings.detail: 1,000 RU/s provisioned throughput plus 25 GB storage per month at $0 while within free amounts, no time limit. Official pricing page (read 2026-10-22): 'New accounts are eligible to receive 1,000 request units per second (RU/s) throughput and 25 GBs storage per month with Azure Cosmos DB free tier.' Applies to the RU-based APIs: NoSQL, MongoDB (RU), Cassandra, Gremlin, and Table. Autoscale minimum is 1,000 RU/s (scales 100–1,000 hourly).
findings.eligibility: All Azure customers (listed on the official page as a free-forever service; pricing page phrases it as 'new accounts'); no credit card needed to stay inside the free amounts; sovereign-cloud regions excluded.
findings.claim: 1) Create an Azure account. 2) Create a Cosmos DB account on an RU-based API (NoSQL/MongoDB/Cassandra/Gremlin/Table). 3) Provision 1,000 RU/s and keep storage ≤ 25 GB.
findings.expiry: No expiry — recurring monthly allowance for the life of the account.
findings.gotchas: Throughput above 1,000 RU/s, storage above 25 GB, data egress, and overage requests bill at PAYG rates; no separate 12-month Cosmos serverless allowance (400,000 RU + 32 GB) appears on the current pricing page — the live free tier is the provisioned 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB one. Staying on standard provisioned 1,000 RU/s is the safest configuration to remain inside free amounts.

findings.name: Azure free account — $200 credit (30 days) + 12-month free services
findings.detail: $200 credit usable on Azure services within 30 days of account creation, plus 12 months of free allowances on 20+ services (first-usage amounts). 12-month database/data allowances include: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server 750 hrs B1MS + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup; MySQL Flexible Server 750 hrs B1MS + 32 GB + 32 GB backup; Azure SQL Managed Instance 720 vCore-hours of a 4- or 8-vCore General Purpose instance incl. 64 GB data + 64 GB backup; Azure Container Registry 1 Standard registry with 100 GB. If you convert to PAYG early, remaining credit stays available for the full 30 days from creation.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only (one free-account offer per new customer). Phone number plus a non-prepaid credit/debit card required at sign-up; only credit cards accepted in Hong Kong and Brazil. Sign-in with Microsoft or GitHub account. Sovereign-cloud products excluded (US Government, China, Germany).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at azure.com/free with a Microsoft or GitHub account. 2) Provide phone + non-prepaid card (a temporary ~$1 authorization may be placed and reversed). 3) Choose the 'free account' (not pay-as-you-go) option at sign-up so the $200 + 12-month allowances attach.
findings.expiry: Credit expires 30 days from account creation; 12-month allowances end 12 months from creation. Account then automatically converts to pay-as-you-go (card on file), or services are disabled if you don't add payment.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a free tier: after 30 days or when $200 is spent, all usage bills at PAYG. Credit cannot be applied to Azure Marketplace offers, Azure Spot VMs, or combined with Hybrid Benefit. Data/egress beyond free amounts bill even during the 12-month window. 12-month VM allowance: 750 hours each of B1s, B2pts v2 (ARM) and B2ats v2 (AMD) burstable VMs.

findings.name: Azure managed databases 12-month free quotas (PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server, SQL Managed Instance)
findings.detail: The 12-month free quotas, available on both the new-customer free account and the student offer: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server — 750 hours/month of Burstable B1MS instance + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup storage; Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server — identical (750 hrs B1MS + 32 GB + 32 GB backup); Azure SQL Managed Instance — 720 vCore-hours/month of a 4-vCore or 8-vCore General Purpose instance, incl. 64 GB data storage and 64 GB backup storage. 750 hours ≈ one continuously running small server. (Azure SQL serverless 'free forever' is a separate, perpetual allowance — see its own finding.)
