findings.eligibility: New-customer free accounts and Azure for Students accounts; one account per person for students; sovereign-cloud regions excluded; PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server B1MS is only offered in select regions (region availability varies).
findings.claim: 1) Create an eligible free or student account. 2) Deploy PostgreSQL or MySQL Flexible Server on B1MS (or SQL Managed Instance on 4/8-vCore General Purpose). 3) Monitor meters in the Azure portal so usage stays within 750 hrs / 720 vCore-hours and the included storage each month.
findings.expiry: 12 months from account creation; student accounts renew annually while still a full-time student; then PAYG pricing applies.
findings.gotchas: Monthly quotas do not roll over; any hour/vCore-hour or GB beyond the allowance bills at PAYG rates immediately; backups beyond included 32/64 GB bill; there is no 12-month free allowance for managed instances of MySQL/PostgreSQL (only Flexible Server / the listed SKUs).

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit + 12-month free services + always-free (no credit card)
findings.detail: Verified 2026-10-22 on the official student-offer page: $100 credit usable on most Azure products within 12 months (not $200 — the $200 figure is the general new-customer trial) + free monthly amounts on 20+ popular services for 12 months (including the PostgreSQL/MySQL B1MS and SQL Managed Instance quotas above) + always-free services (SQL serverless 100,000 vCore-sec/month + 32 GB; Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB; Azure DevOps 5 users; Functions 1M requests; App Service; AKS management; AI Search 50 MB; and more) + free developer tools via the Azure Education Hub (Visual Studio Community, SQL Server, Windows Server). No credit card required; one account per person.
findings.eligibility: Full-time university students only. A school email is the gate: 'Use your school email to sign up and renew yearly while you're a student.' The page documents no alternate Microsoft Learn enrollment route and no credit card required. New Azure customers; accounts are 'new Azure customers only' for the 12-month monthly amounts.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at azure.com/free/students using your school email (no payment method). 2) Receive the $100 credit (12-month validity) and the 12-month free monthly amounts. 3) Renew the subscription annually with your school email while enrolled; free-forever items continue without renewal.
findings.expiry: Credit: 12 months. 12-month service allowances: 12 months, then annual renewal required while a full-time student (renew by email prompt; otherwise subscription and products are disabled). Always-free services: no expiry. One account per person.
findings.gotchas: Credit cannot be applied to Azure Marketplace offers; after the 12-month window or on renewal lapse, moving to PAYG requires adding a payment method or the subscription is disabled; students who graduate or leave full-time status lose renewal eligibility. Note the $100 student credit is distinct from the $200 new-customer trial credit — an existing free-account holder is not a 'new' customer.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack — Azure benefits (secondary claim route)
findings.detail: Verified 2026-10-22 on the official GitHub Education page: for verified students 18+, the pack includes 'Free access to 25+ Microsoft Azure cloud services plus $100 in Azure credit' (no credit card). For students aged 13–17, a separate 'Microsoft Azure (for ages 13-17)' benefit gives named free services instead of a monetary credit: Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Notification Hubs, MySQL database (in-app), Application Insights, and Azure DevOps. Claiming the benefit provisions the equivalent of an Azure student account.
findings.eligibility: A free GitHub account plus GitHub student verification (18+ tier for the $100 credit; 13–17 tier gets restricted free services, no credit). No credit card required per the GitHub page. GitHub's verification can accept school-issued credentials, so it is a practical route for students whose school lacks a verifiable .edu address.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for the GitHub Student Developer Pack at education.github.com/pack. 2) Complete GitHub's student verification. 3) Redeem the Azure benefit, which creates the Azure student account with the $100 credit and 12-month free services.
findings.expiry: GitHub's page prints no expiry window; the $100 Azure credit mirrors the Azure for Students offer (usable within 12 months).
findings.gotchas: The 13–17 tier has no monetary credit; the $100/25+ services benefit is for 18+. Exact credit expiry and 12-month allowance terms live in the resulting Azure account, not on GitHub's page.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups (Founders Hub) — up to $150,000 Azure credits
findings.detail: The official Microsoft for Startups page (read 2026-10-22) states startups get 'up to $150,000 in credits' that 'can be applied across eligible Azure services to support your startup from early development through production workloads,' plus M365 licenses, GitHub Enterprise access, and co-sell support via the Microsoft network. The program now runs through the 'Founders Hub' portal with tiered Azure credits: an entry tier requiring no VC/accelerator referral (historically ~$1,500 Azure credits), intermediate tiers (community reports of ~$25,000), and a 'Scale' level unlocking $150,000, typically investor-referred (investor network: Y Combinator, Techstars, 500 Global, MassChallenge, Plug and Play, Seedcamp, Antler, Founder Institute, and others).
findings.eligibility: Private, software-based startups in program-available markets. Community/third-party reports (not republished on the pages fetched today) put the classic thresholds at less than 5 years since founding and less than ~$30M raised; entry tiers are open without a VC referral, higher tiers require referral from the investor network. Tiers advance via an automated 'engagement score' (e.g., consuming ~50% of the current tier's credits and using a mix of services).
findings.claim: 1) Apply at microsoft.com/en-us/startups via 'Get started now' into the Founders Hub portal (sign in with Microsoft account). 2) Complete the application: company name/website, industry, stage (pre-seed/seed/Series A+), product description. 3) Review takes days to weeks; grants appear in the Founders Hub portal, where 'Level Up' requests to the $150k tier are also submitted.
findings.expiry: Credits are granted per tier with tier-specific expiry windows (typically 6–12 months per tier; not stated on the official page fetched today). Extensions are generally not granted; the stated path is leveling up to the next tier.
findings.gotchas: Headline 'up to $150,000' is from the official page today; the specific tier dollar amounts ($1,500 entry, ~$25,000 mid, $150,000 scale) and the age/funding caps come from third-party/community sources, so treat them as medium/low confidence. Credits do not apply to Azure Marketplace offers; the program is a customer-acquisition channel, so post-credit consumption is what Microsoft monetizes; co-sell/transaction fees (3% new / 1.5% renewal) attach to the co-sell program, not to credits.

sunset_notes: No free offer for this front was sunset as of 2026-10-22, but several were materially changed in 2025-2026: (1) Microsoft for Startups was restructured into the tiered 'Founders Hub' model; the current headline is 'up to $150,000 in credits' (replacing the older 'up to $300,000 in total benefits' framing), with level-ups gated by an automated engagement score. (2) The live Cosmos DB 'free tier' is now the provisioned 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB allowance (confirmed on the current pricing page today); the previously documented separate 12-month serverless allowance (400,000 RU + 32 GB) does not appear on the current page, so plan against 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB. (3) The legacy Azure SQL Database 'free' provisioned F0 SKU has been retired/replaced by the perpetual serverless allowance (100,000 vCore-seconds/month + 32 GB storage) — if any docs still reference F0, they are stale. (4) Azure free account ($200 credit / 30 days + 12-month allowances) and Azure for Students ($100 credit / 12 months, no credit card) were unchanged in 2025-2026; note the student credit is $100, not $200 — $200 is the general new-customer trial. (5) Housekeeping: the dedicated SQL Database serverless pricing-details URL (azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/sql-database/serverless/) now returns 404 as of today; the free allowances are instead confirmed on the /free/ and /free/students pages, and Azure has rebranded much of its AI surface to 'Microsoft Foundry' (product-name changes only, no free-allowance changes observed).

provider: InfluxData InfluxDB Cloud (Serverless) free (time-series-db) — Managed Databases & Data Platforms

findings.name: InfluxDB Cloud Serverless Free Plan (permanent, quota-limited)
findings.detail: Free forever multi-tenant serverless plan. Limits (official docs): data-in writes 5 MB per 5 min (~17 kB/s avg), reads 300 MB per 5 min, cardinality 10k series, 2 buckets/databases, 5 dashboards, 5 tasks, 2 alert checks, 2 notification rules, 30-day data retention, 1 organization per account, no uptime SLA, community/Slack support only. No expiration; an idle account (zero writes and queries for 30+ days) is closed with email notice first. Multi-tenant regions: AWS US-West-2 (Oregon), AWS US-East (Virginia), AWS Frankfurt, Azure East US + West Europe, GCP US Central (Iowa).
findings.eligibility: Anyone with an email account; no .edu required, no credit card required, no startup or age criteria. Sign up at cloud2.influxdata.com/signup. Note the free plan runs the InfluxDB 2.x (TSM) engine; InfluxDB 3 workloads are the new serverless offering (see credit finding).
findings.claim: 1) Go to cloud2.influxdata.com/signup and create a free account (no credit card). 2) Choose a region (AWS Oregon/Virginia/Frankfurt, Azure East US/Amsterdam, GCP Iowa). 3) Pick Free Plan; create up to 2 buckets, 5 dashboards, 5 tasks. 4) Keep writing/reading at least once a month to avoid 30-day inactivity close. Upgrade to Usage-Based any time from the Billing page.
findings.expiry: No expiration. Account auto-closes only after 30+ consecutive days with zero writes/queries (email warning first). Free-plan quotas apply indefinitely.
findings.gotchas: Rate limits are very tight: 5 MB per 5 min (~14 MB/day max) and 30-day retention means only a few hundred MB of total data can be alive. Cardinality capped at 10k series (pricing page says 'contact sales' to scale, which implies not available on free). No HA, no uptime SLA, no dedicated support, no SAML/SSO. Free plan is InfluxDB 2.x TSM — the 2.x OSS line is in end-of-life/maintenance mode, and InfluxData is pushing InfluxDB 3, so feature investment has shifted. Pausing usage does not pause storage billing on paid plans; on the free plan storage is free only within the 30-day retention window.
findings.source_url: https://www.influxdata.com/influxdb-cloud-pricing/ and https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/cloud/account-management/limits/ (limits page: writes 5 MB/5 min, reads 300 MB/5 min, 10k series, 2 buckets, 5 dashboards, 5 tasks, 2 checks, 2 notification rules, 30-day retention)

findings.name: $250 free credit on new paid InfluxDB Cloud accounts (30 days)
findings.detail: New paid accounts (InfluxDB Cloud Serverless, usage-based plan) receive $250 in credit applied to the first 30 days. Usage rates the credit pays against: data in $0.0025/MB written; query count $0.012 per 100 query executions; storage $0.002/GB-hour; data out $0.09/GB. Marketing: '$250 free credit to start', 'no minimum commitment', 'no credit card required' to start serverless. Rates for queries are per month for tasks/alerts (an alert check every 5 min = 8,640 billable query executions/month). Billing cycles are calendar months; you are billed early the following month.
findings.eligibility: Any new paid account — no .edu, no startup certification, no funding cap; regional limits are the same 6 multi-tenant regions as the free plan. A payment method (credit card; ACH/invoice via support@influxdata.com) is required to stay on the Usage-Based plan — the 'no credit card required' applies only to the free/starting tier; the moment you're on usage-based billing, charges hit the card. No student/startup-only version of this credit exists on official pages.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at cloud2.influxdata.com/signup (no card needed for the free plan). 2) From the Billing page, upgrade to the Usage-Based plan. 3) The $250 credit applies to your first 30 days of usage-based billing. 4) Usage rates accrue across four vectors (data in, query count, storage, data out); the credit offsets those charges.
findings.expiry: Credit applies only to the first 30 days of the new paid account; after it is exhausted or the 30-day window ends, standard usage-based rates apply and your card is charged on the calendar-month cycle.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial credit, not a free tier — once $250 is spent or 30 days pass, all usage is billed; data out at $0.09/GB and storage $0.002/GB-hour add up fast (30 days of ~10 GB = ~432 GB-hours = ~$0.86/mo just for storage, plus queries). An alert check every 5 min alone is 8,640 billable executions/month. Late payments trigger a de-escalation ladder: 2 retries over 72h; at 7 days or 3 declines, all operations except writes are disabled; at 14 days the whole account is disabled; at 21 days suspension. Canceling charges the payment method immediately. Older marketing copy said the credit was given 'upon upgrade' from the free plan; current /pricing/ copy frames it as '$250 free credit to start' — in practice it is tied to the first 30 days of a new paid account. Web search was exhausted partway through this task, so I could not verify whether InfluxData added/removed credit wording in 2025-2026 news; rely on the live pricing/FAQ pages.
findings.source_url: https://www.influxdata.com/pricing/ ( '$250 free credit to start', 'no credit card required', usage rates $0.0025/MB in, $0.012/100 queries, $0.002/GB-hr storage, $0.09/GB out; FAQ: 'New paid accounts receive $250 in credits applied to the first 30 days') and https://www.influxdata.com/influxdb-cloud-pricing/ ('Upgrade anytime to get $250 in credit for your project')

findings.name: InfluxDB 3 Enterprise 30-day free trial (no credit card)
findings.detail: InfluxDB 3 Enterprise (self-managed, on-prem/private cloud/edge, or a Cloud PoC) has a 30-day free trial with 'no commitment' and explicitly 'no credit card needed'. During the trial you get: unlimited scale (no service quotas), HA + read replicas, SAML/SSO + OAuth, enterprise security/compliance, and a technical support SLA. After the trial, Enterprise is custom pricing based on CPU configuration (there is also a Cloud Dedicated offering and Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB billed to your AWS account where existing AWS credits/EDP discounts apply — no separate InfluxData free-credit program of its own).
findings.eligibility: Anyone (developer, student, or startup); no .edu required, no funding/age cap, no credit card required during the trial. Trial download or 'Talk to Sales' for a Cloud PoC. No region restriction on self-managed; Timestream requires AWS account (US regions where Timestream is available).
findings.claim: 1) For self-hosted trial: download InfluxDB 3 Enterprise from the InfluxData site / trial page and run it for up to 30 days. 2) For a managed PoC: click 'Run a PoC' / 'Request a proof of concept' on the pricing page; a sales rep contacts you. 3) No card required; decide on license or cloud contract afterwards.
findings.expiry: 30 days. No auto-conversion to a paid license — the trial simply lapses; contact sales to convert. The marketing page headline now says '30-day trial · Installs in under 5 minutes · Enterprise SLA available'.
findings.gotchas: Trial, not free: after 30 days you must license Enterprise (custom pricing, contact sales) or move to the free InfluxDB 3 Core OSS (self-hosted, community support) or the free Cloud plan. Trial has no SLA guarantee beyond 'available' language; dedicated cloud (Cloud Dedicated) has NO free trial at all — custom pricing only. Timestream pricing inherits whatever AWS free-tier/credits you have but InfluxData adds nothing.
findings.source_url: https://www.influxdata.com/pricing/ ('InfluxDB 3 Enterprise — 30-day free trial, no credit card needed, no commitment'; 'Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB — AWS consumption pricing, existing AWS credits & EDP discounts apply')

findings.name: InfluxDB 3 Enterprise free tier for at-home, non-commercial use (alpha)
findings.detail: Announced 2025-01-27 (blog post 'updated November 20, 2025' by Paul Dix): a free tier of InfluxDB 3 Enterprise for 'at-home, non-commercial use' — all Enterprise capabilities (unlimited-range querying, compaction, no 72-hour query-span cap) at zero cost, 'rate limited in some way' with the concrete limits still being defined with the community. Status at the time of the update: alpha. Access is via the InfluxData community Discord (tell them what rate limits work for your use case). Non-commercial: personal/home use only — student capstones are borderline, startup commercial use is explicitly NOT covered.
findings.eligibility: At-home, non-commercial users (personal sensors, home metrics, hobby projects). Commercial use excluded — so it is not a usable free tier for startups shipping a product. .edu not required; rate limits were still being shaped as of the Nov 20 2025 update. No formal sign-up form; engagement via community Discord.
findings.claim: 1) Join the InfluxData community Discord (link in the blog post). 2) State your at-home use case and the rate limits you'd want. 3) Get a free at-home InfluxDB 3 Enterprise build/license. 4) Verify the alpha status and any published rate caps before relying on it.
findings.expiry: Not formally defined — this is an alpha program; terms (rate limits) were still open as of the 2025-11-20 update. No renewal question, but expect terms to be finalized (or the program to ship as a proper free tier) later; re-check the blog/Discord before treating it as stable.
findings.gotchas: Alpha: features/limits can change or be withdrawn. 'Non-commercial' is the hard eligibility boundary — it does not satisfy a startup's production workload. No SLA or support commitment. Because I could not re-verify the current (Oct 2026) status (web search budget exhausted for this session), treat the exact rate limits as unconfirmed — the official pages I read today (pricing, cloud pricing, FAQ) do not list this at-home tier at all.
findings.source_url: https://www.influxdata.com/blog/influxdb3-open-source-public-alpha-jan-27/ (announced two weeks into InfluxDB 3 Core/Enterprise alpha; updated 2025-11-20)

findings.name: InfluxDB OSS (1.x / 2.x / 3 Core) — free forever, self-host
findings.detail: Self-hosted open-source builds are free forever: InfluxDB 1.x (Apache-2.0), InfluxDB 2.x OSS (MIT/Apache 2.x engine), and the new InfluxDB 3 Core (permissively licensed open source) — 'Full InfluxDB 3 engine · Linux, Mac, Docker', community support only, no HA, no enterprise security. Known trade-off: InfluxDB 3 Core's original hard 72-hour limit on writable/queryable timestamp ranges was lifted in late January 2025 (you can write any historical timestamp and query arbitrary start/end), but the maximum single-query range still defaults to 72 hours (432 ten-minute Parquet blocks), configurable at server start. InfluxData's own marketing labels 3 Core 'Free Forever · Self-managed · Community supported' for local dev, exploration, and prototyping.
findings.eligibility: Unlimited — anyone can download and self-host. No .edu, no startup cap, no credit card, no region limits (you run it wherever you have machines). Commercial use of the OSS builds is permitted (standard OSS licenses); the 'at-home' restriction only applies to the free Enterprise tier, not to OSS.
findings.claim: 1) Download InfluxDB 3 Core (or 1.x/2.x OSS) from influxdata.com/downloads or the relevant Docker Hub / package repos. 2) Install locally or on your own VM/container (Linux, Mac, Docker). 3) Use the influx CLI / HTTP API to write and query. No account, no billing.
findings.expiry: None — perpetual OSS builds (Apache/MIT lineage). 1.x is in maintenance/end-of-life mode (security fixes only); 2.x is frozen in favor of 3; 3 Core is the actively developed OSS line.
findings.gotchas: OSS has no support SLA, no HA, no enterprise security (SAML/SSO), and no service quotas but you carry all the ops. 3 Core is optimized for short query ranges (hours, not years) — for multi-year history you need Enterprise (paid or the alpha at-home tier). If you need a managed free database instead of self-hosting, use the Cloud Free Plan above.
findings.source_url: https://www.influxdata.com/pricing/ ('InfluxDB 3 Core — Open source. Local dev, exploration, and prototyping. Free Forever · Self-managed. Community supported. Full InfluxDB 3 engine · Linux, Mac, Docker. No HA, no enterprise security') and https://www.influxdata.com/blog/influxdb3-open-source-public-alpha-jan-27/ (72-hour limitation update)

findings.name: InfluxDB University — free self-paced courses (no license offer)
findings.detail: InfluxDB University (influxdata.com/learn / /university) offers free self-paced courses and instructor-led training ('free courses and instructor-led training, on your schedule') for learning InfluxDB. It is an education resource, not a free product license — it does not by itself grant InfluxDB Cloud free capacity, a reduced-rate subscription, or a credential (the landing page does not mention certifications). Listed here because it is the closest thing InfluxData has to a student/education offering, and it has no .edu requirement or cost.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, free, no .edu or startup requirement, self-paced. Instructor-led training is also free per the landing page ('free courses and instructor-led training').
findings.claim: 1) Go to influxdata.com/learn (or /university). 2) Pick a self-paced InfluxDB course. 3) Complete at your own pace. No sign-up gates are documented on the landing page.
findings.expiry: None documented; it's a standing free resource.
findings.gotchas: No product license, no credit, no certificate/credential language on the page. For actual free database capacity use the Cloud Free Plan / $250 credit instead. Confidence is medium because I read only the landing page (course catalog details, whether certificates exist deeper in the program) — I did not enumerate every course.

sunset_notes: No student-specific or startup-specific program exists as of 2026-10-22: /education/ and /startups/ on influxdata.com both return 404, and the pricing, cloud-pricing, FAQ, and marketing pages contain zero mention of .edu eligibility, startup age/funding caps, or startup grants. For students and startups the only free offers are the general ones above (Cloud Free Plan, $250 new-account credit, Enterprise 30-day trial, OSS). 2025-2026 changes worth flagging: (1) The Free Plan's documentation and limits still describe InfluxDB Cloud TSM (the 2.x engine) — InfluxData's current marketing (influxdata.com/pricing) has been rebuilt around InfluxDB 3 (3 Core OSS, 3 Enterprise trial, Timestream on AWS, Cloud Serverless with $250 credit), so the TSM-centric docs may be superseded as 3-serverless matures; (2) InfluxDB 3 Core's original 72-hour write/query-range limitation was lifted on 2025-01-27 except the single-query span default (432 blocks = 72 h, configurable); (3) the InfluxDB 3 Enterprise at-home free tier announced 2025-01-27 was still alpha with unconfirmed rate limits as of its 2025-11-20 blog update and is absent from all pricing pages today; (4) InfluxDB 1.x/2.x OSS lines are effectively end-of-life, with InfluxDB 3 as the active OSS line; (5) an old InfluxDB Cloud test pricing page (influxdb-pricing-test-old, marked 'PAGE NOT IN USE') described the credit as '$250 credit for 30 days upon upgrade' — current copy frames it as a new-paid-account credit applied to the first 30 days. Caveat: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted partway through, so program-level news (e.g., InfluxData joining Launchpad/CloudSparkle-style startup programs, or any 2026 credit changes) could not be independently re-verified; official pages fetched today are the basis for the high-confidence findings above.

findings.claim: Sign up free at aiven.io (no credit card, no trial form), open the Aiven Console, create a service (PostgreSQL/MySQL/Kafka/OpenSearch/Valkey) and select the free plan — service is live in minutes. Startup credits: apply via the form at aiven.io/startups (Typeform), acceptance ~2 business days, 15-min kickoff call, then apply the credit code to your Aiven account.
findings.detail: Aiven's always-free tier covers 5 services at $0/month: PostgreSQL (1GB storage, 1GB RAM, 1 CPU/VM, single node, network egress included), MySQL (1GB storage, 1GB RAM, network egress included), Apache Kafka (up to 250 KiB/s combined produce+consume, max 5 topics x 2 partitions, up to 3-day retention, free Karapace Schema Registry + REST proxy, only ONE free Kafka service per organization, no Kafka Connect/MirrorMaker 2/integrations/tiered storage), OpenSearch (4GB RAM, 20GB persistent storage, up to 20 shards, single node, k-NN/vector enabled by default), and Valkey (1GB RAM, network egress included). It is a permanent free tier, not a trial: no expiry, no time limit, no credit card required. Free services are automatically powered off during extended inactivity and can be reactivated anytime; Aiven reserves the right to shut down services that violate acceptable use or are unused for extended periods. No SLA; support is documentation-only. No specific cloud/region can be chosen (geographical area only, e.g. Europe/NA/APAC).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone — no .edu email, no age cap, no company verification, no region-of-residence restriction, and no credit card. Free of any trial or time limit. The only implicit caps: one free Kafka service per organization, and per-service resource caps listed above. ClickHouse has NO free plan.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal — the free tier persists indefinitely within limits; services power off on prolonged inactivity but can be reactivated at any time. Aiven can discontinue/reduce the program (they did reduce storage in 2025).
findings.gotchas: Not a trial, but: (1) idle services auto-power-off, so no uptime SLA and no production use; (2) since 15 May 2025, PostgreSQL/MySQL free storage is only 1GB (was 5GB) — a full 5GB-database won't fit; (3) network egress is included only up to the free tier's stated network allowance — the free-tier page labels PG/MySQL/Valkey as 'network costs' included, verify on the plan page if your traffic is heavy; (4) you cannot pick a specific cloud/region on free plans, so cross-cloud peering/VPC features are unavailable; (5) no connection pooling or service integrations on free PostgreSQL; (6) the paid upgrade path is the new $5/month Developer tier (launched Nov–Dec 2025) with 8GB storage and no auto power-off; (7) one-off prize competitions (Dec 2025 $5,000 free-Kafka competition closed 31 Jan 2026; $1,000 free-tier competition closed 17 Apr 2026) are marketing campaigns, not recurring credits.
findings.name: Aiven Free Tier (always-free managed PostgreSQL, MySQL, Kafka, OpenSearch, Valkey)

findings.claim: Apply through the Aiven for Startups form (aiven.io/startups, Typeform: aiven-startups.typeform.com/to/STphOA6R); select your VC/accelerator affiliation if you have one; on acceptance (~2 business days) you get a welcome email, book a 15-min kick-off call with the Startup Program Manager, and receive a credit code; sign up on Aiven, apply the code, and spend credits on any managed service for 12 months.
findings.detail: Aiven for Startups (the program formerly called 'Aiven Cluster', revamped Aug 2023) grants from $12,000 up to $100,000 in Aiven platform credits usable over 12 months across all managed services (Kafka, PostgreSQL, MySQL, OpenSearch, ClickHouse, Valkey, etc.), plus startup-Slack community, technical guidance/office hours from Aiven solution architects, promotion on Aiven channels, and virtual events. Partner-marketplace listings (e.g. Stand Together Ventures, Aug 2026) state explicit stage-based tiers: $12K pre-seed, $30K seed, $75K Series A, $100K Series B, with the option to upgrade tier as the company grows; the $12K tier also exists for startups with no partner affiliation. Credits are valid 12 months; no payment commitment after they expire.
findings.eligibility: Startup founded no more than 7 years ago; external funding raised from pre-seed up to and including Series B; application with company website + business email (personal emails rejected as verification); preferred affiliation with an Aiven ecosystem partner (VC, accelerator, incubator — e.g. Techstars, Digital Ocean Hatch which offers a $10K variant, Aalto Startup Center, SMU iie with $30K). Excluded: agencies, consulting firms, NGOs, and educational institutions; applicants must be a new Aiven customer or a paying customer with monthly invoice under $400, and must not have previously received startup credits. No .edu requirement (it is a company program, not a student one).
findings.expiry: Credits must be used within 12 months of receipt; no auto-renewal. Program has been running since Nov 2021 (launched as Cluster), revamped Aug 2023 (funding cap raised Series A→B, age cap 5→7 years, new $12K tier), and is branded 'Aiven for Startups' as of 2026.
findings.gotchas: The official page says amounts 'vary based on your startup's credit tier' without publishing the per-stage numbers — the $12K/$30K/$75K/$100K mapping comes from partner listings, not the main page. Credits are not cash: they offset Aiven service spend only, and unspent credits lapse after 12 months. Approval is discretionary ('apply anyway' is encouraged but not guaranteed). A partner (VC/accelerator/incubator) affiliation is effectively expected for the higher tiers. The Digital Ocean Hatch variant caps at $10,000 even though the headline is $100K. Verify current form/eligibility in the Typeform at application time.
findings.name: Aiven for Startups (formerly 'Cluster') — up to $100,000 platform credits over 12 months

findings.claim: No application or license step — students simply use the always-free tier (aiven.io/free-tier, no credit card). Free Aiven Developer Workshops (aiven.io/developer-workshops) are open, free training sessions on PostgreSQL/Kafka/OpenSearch.
findings.detail: No dedicated education program, .edu license, student discount, or student credits program was found in Aiven's official pages or press releases as of 2026-10-22. Aiven supports students indirectly: (1) the always-free tier is explicitly marketed for 'learning databases & streaming' and is open to any individual — a student with a personal email can get free managed PostgreSQL/MySQL/Kafka/OpenSearch/Valkey with no credit card; (2) free online 'Aiven Developer Workshops' (aiven.io/developer-workshops) are open education events; (3) universities (Aalto Startup Center, SMU iie) partner on the STARTUP program side, where their incubatee startups (companies, not students) get $30K–$100K credits. Notably, the startup program explicitly EXCLUDES educational institutions as applicants. Confidence is medium rather than high because the web-search budget for this session was exhausted before a final confirming sweep of aiven.io/education-style URLs could run.
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — no student/education offer exists to qualify for. (Students qualify for the general free tier by simply having an Aiven account; no .edu email required or beneficial.)
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse university partner listings (Aalto, SMU) — those are startup-company offers for incubatees, not student licenses; the startup program's terms bar educational institutions. If Aiven ever launches an education program it would likely surface at aiven.io/startups or the press room; check the free-tier page, not a nonexistent '/education' page.
findings.name: No dedicated student/education program (negative finding)

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes that materially altered the free landscape: (1) 15 May 2025 — free-plan storage for PostgreSQL and MySQL reduced from 5GB to 1GB for all new and existing free services (changelog aiven.io/changelog/6ad6c429-6c1c-4418-abfb-2ca82f927414); no data loss, connections unchanged, but hobbyists needing more must move to paid 'hobbyist/Developer' plans. (2) Nov 12 / Dec 10 2025 — a new $5/month Developer tier launched for PostgreSQL and MySQL (1 CPU, 1GB RAM, 8GB storage, Basic support, services never auto-power-off, region area but not cloud selection); one changelog dated Nov 12 2025 says the Postgres Developer plan starts 'at $8 USD' while the Aiven blog states $5 — treat $5/month as the advertised starting price and verify in-console. (3) Dec 10 2025 — the Kafka free tier itself is new (previously Kafka had no $0 plan); before that date the free tier was PostgreSQL/MySQL/OpenSearch/Valkey only. (4) The startup program rebranded from 'Aiven Cluster Startup Program' to 'Aiven for Startups' (revamp in Aug 2023: age cap 5→7 years, funding cap Series A→B, new $12K non-partner tier; current form is aiven.io/startups). (5) One-off prize competitions, not recurring offers: $5,000 Free Kafka competition (closed 31 Jan 2026) and $1,000 Free Tier competition (closed 17 Apr 2026, winner announced 27 Apr 2026). Nothing was shut down in this window; the only reductions were the 2025 free-tier storage cut and Kafka's free-service-per-org limit (1).

findings.claim: Sign up at cloud.google.com/free or console (billing free-trial flow), accept terms with a payment method; $300 credit attaches to the new billing account on signup. Product trials (Cloud SQL/Spanner/AlloyDB/Bigtable/Looker/GKE) are claimed from the 'Explore more offers' section of the same /free page.
findings.detail: New GCP customers get $300 in free credit to try products (incl. Cloud SQL, BigQuery, AlloyDB, Spanner) and build a proof of concept. Per the live /free page: 'You won't be charged until you activate your full paid account.' The $300 is not charged against the always-free allotments. No day limit is printed on the current page (historically a 60-day trial; verify in console at claim). Credits apply to PayG Google-owned 1P GCP services; excludes Marketplace/third-party products.
findings.eligibility: New Google Cloud customers (first-time). Credit card / payment method IS required to hold a billing account - the faculty education page explicitly warns students that the Free Trial 'requires them to use a credit card.' No .edu requirement.
findings.expiry: No duration published on today's page; historical term was 60 days. Unused credit lapses when the trial term ends; account converts to pay-as-you-go only on activation of the full paid account.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free-tier confusion: $300 trial credit is finite; the 'Always Free' caps persist after the trial. Credit card required - not a no-card offer. Internet egress and any usage beyond free caps/credit is billed. Trial is one per person; students should prefer education credits (no card) over the trial.
findings.name: Google Cloud free trial: $300 credit for new customers

findings.claim: Nothing to claim - free allotments are automatic for any new GCP billing account/project. Set budgets/alerts in Cloud Billing to cap overage.
findings.detail: Live /free page lists: BigQuery 1 TB queries/month; Cloud Storage 5 GB-months Standard; GKE 1 Autopilot or Zonal cluster/month; Cloud Run functions 2M invocations/month; Firestore 1 GB storage; Pub/Sub 10 GB messages/month; Compute Engine 1 e2-micro instance/month; Datastream up to 100 GiB CDC from eligible first-party sources/month; Agent Engine first 180,000 vCPU-seconds + 360,000 GiB-seconds/month; Application Integration up to 400 executions + 20 GiB data/month; Artifact Registry 0.5 GB/month; Cloud Shell 5 GB disk; Secret Manager 6 secret versions/month; KMS Autokey 100 key versions + 10,000 ops/month; plus Vision/NLP/STT/Video quotas and Workflows/Cloud Build allotments. Page: 'There is no charge to use these products up to their specified free usage limit. The free usage limit does not expire, but is subject to change.'
findings.eligibility: All GCP customers, including students and startups, every month. No .edu email, no funding cap. A billing account (with payment method) still required to open a GCP project; $0 billed while inside caps.
findings.expiry: Perpetual, resets monthly. No end date, but Google may change or remove allotments without notice ('subject to change').
findings.gotchas: SHRUNKEN free tier: legacy Cloud SQL micro-instance free hours, Memorystore free hours, Spanner free 20 vCPU-hr/32GB, and Dataflow 9,600 worker-hours are no longer listed - managed-DB/data-platform users should plan on the finite product trials + $300 instead. BigQuery's 10 GB free storage is no longer listed. Cloud Storage free space is 5 GB-months (vs the historical 50 GB). Overage beyond caps bills at standard rates. Egress to internet is not a free allotment.
findings.name: GCP Always Free tier (ongoing, ~24 products incl. BigQuery 1TB queries/month)

findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup/apply (Google sign-in). Prepare the 18-character GCP billing account ID (credits are deposited there) and a business email that owns/admins the GCP account. Stealth founders get in via investor/VC/accelerator referral. Automated responses: rejection in 5-7 days; 10+ days if information is missing.
findings.detail: First rung of the revamped program. FAQ on the live page: 'Start ($2k) tier is designed for startups founded in the past 2 years, with a working MVP, a clear business model, and plans to seek venture funding soon.' The prototyping stage also includes instant access to Google AI Studio for rapid MVP prototyping. Adjacent benefits on the page: Gemini Startup Forum membership and equity-free accelerator cohorts.
findings.eligibility: Unfunded/pre-VC: founded within past 2 years, working MVP, clear business model, plans to seek VC; new Google Cloud customers founding digital-native products. Must be in a region where GCP is GA with self-service purchasing. Excludes IPO'd/acquired companies, educational institutions, government, nonprofits, personal blogs, dev shops, consultancies/agencies, crypto mining, token distribution contrary to regulation.
findings.expiry: Credits usable for the program's first-year window (per footnotes, Year-1 coverage rules apply; funded tiers run two years). Re-application is allowed if prior credits were unused and in-year eligibility still met.
findings.gotchas: Credits are non-transferable, cannot be shared/split/resold (violation = termination); cover only first-party PayG GCP services - subscription/prepay/annual-license billing and all Marketplace/Model Garden third-party products excluded; third-party models billed directly; acceptance at Google's sole discretion based on company age, stage, prior GCP credit usage, and funding type.
findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program - 'Start' tier (up to $2,000 credits)

findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup/apply (Google sign-in) via the 'Grow and scale / Up to $350k in Cloud credits - Apply to the program' flow; submit billing account ID + business email; list VC/investor/accelerator affiliations to expedite. Credits are deposited to the selected billing account on approval.
findings.detail: Headline: up to $350,000 in GCP credits over two years (AI startups), up to $200,000 (other startups), i.e. the program's 'Funded tiers (Scale, and Scale AI) range from $200K-$350k in credits'. Footnote math: Scale AI - Year 1: 100% of eligible spend up to $250,000; Year 2: 20% up to an additional $100,000. Other startups - Year 1: up to $100,000; Year 2: 20% up to an additional $100,000. Stated benefits: credits for frontier models (Gemini/Gemma), Google Skills training, 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no cost, monthly Google Maps Platform credits (separate application), Startup Success Managers + Customer Engineering support, and Cloud Marketplace listings to sell alongside Google sales. Eligibility: verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding, founded within the last 3-5 years (tier-dependent).
findings.eligibility: Funded early-stage: verifiable Pre-Seed through Series A; company age 3-5 years depending on tier; company must be in a GCP GA region (self-service purchasing); exclusions same as Start tier (no IPO/acquired, no edu/gov/nonprofit/agency, no crypto mining, AUP-compliant). Funding is the gating factor - this is where the 'funding cap' lives: Pre-Seed to Series A, no Series B+ shown on the page.
findings.expiry: Two-year coverage structure: Year 1 full (100% up to cap), Year 2 at 20% up to an additional $100K; end-of-term lapses for unused credits. Prior participants who left credits unused may re-apply if still meeting in-year eligibility.
findings.gotchas: Only PayG first-party GCP products - subscription-billed items and Marketplace/Model Garden third-party products excluded; third-party models billed directly and not covered; credits can't be shared/resold; Workspace benefit requires the company domain to have had no paid Workspace subscription in the prior 31 days; Maps Platform is a separate application; 'up to' amounts are coverage rules, not guaranteed grants (Year 2 = 20% of spend, not a lump sum).
findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program - 'Scale'/'Scale AI' funded tiers (up to $200K-$350K over two years)

findings.claim: Claim from https://cloud.google.com/free ('OFFER' cards, 'Start a ... free trial' buttons) or the per-product docs 'free trial' links; create the trial instance in a GCP project under a billing account.
findings.detail: Finite, no-cost product trials listed under 'Explore more offers' on the live /free page: Cloud SQL - 30-day trial, 8 vCPU Enterprise Plus instance, 64 GB memory, 100 GB storage; Cloud Spanner - 90-day trial instance, 10 GB storage; AlloyDB for PostgreSQL - 30-day trial, 8 vCPU basic primary instance, up to 1 TB storage capacity; Bigtable - 10-day trial, 1-node SSD cluster, up to 500 GB storage; Looker - 30-day trial with all standard features; GKE - 90 days with full capabilities; Gemini Enterprise Plus edition - 30 days. Each page notes 'new Google Cloud customers get $300 in free credits on signup' alongside.
findings.eligibility: New GCP customers (trials are tied to new-account offer; existing customers may still trial but the '$300 on signup' line applies to new customers). No .edu requirement; payment method on the account per GCP billing policy.
findings.expiry: Fixed durations: 30 days (Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Looker, Gemini Enterprise Plus), 90 days (Spanner, GKE), 10 days (Bigtable). After expiry the instance converts to standard PayG pricing.
findings.gotchas: During the trial period usage beyond the trial spec (e.g., more storage, extra instances) bills; after expiry everything bills. GCP's managed-DB trial instances skew toward the premium/Enterprise Plus editions - budget accordingly. No free-tier replacement for Memorystore appears on the page. Egress/network costs are separate line items.
findings.name: Managed-database & data-platform free trials (Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, Bigtable, Looker, GKE, Gemini Enterprise Plus)

findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/faculty 'Apply for teaching credits'): enter course details (up to 3 courses), expected student count, school domains, and how credits will be used. Then redeem in GCP and manage billing per the 'Manage Google Cloud credits' guide.
findings.detail: Eligible faculty can apply for up to $100 in GCP credits per teaching staff member and up to $50 in GCP credits per student for hands-on classroom use. Credits attach to the applicant's email and are non-transferable; group projects may pool students' individual credits (documented in faculty resources). Country-restricted: the application shows a fixed country list (US, Australia, Brazil, Canada, ... not worldwide).
findings.eligibility: Faculty/teaching staff at accredited educational institutions; official school-issued email on a valid .edu (or equivalent national) domain required - if you lack one you can nominate another email, but credits attach to it permanently. Course start date must be within 1 year of application.
findings.expiry: Credits are redeemable from approval up until 16 weeks after the course start date, and are good for up to 1 year after the course start date.
findings.gotchas: Not available in every country. Credits are per-student capped ($50) - large cohorts need many enrollments or instructor credits only. Explicitly do not have students use the $300 Free Trial (credit-card required) instead of these credits. Credits are non-transferable and locked to the school domains listed.
findings.name: Google Cloud for faculty / classroom - teaching credits (up to $100 per faculty + up to $50 per student)

findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/researchers 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'): project abstract, start date, use of credits, post-credit funding plan; create a GCP billing account to hold the coupon. GPAR/campus research day via the express-interest form (edu.google.com/programs/express-interest).
findings.detail: Faculty/researchers (incl. PhD students) can apply for up to $5,000 in GCP research credits via the Academic Research Grants form ('Google Cloud for Researchers'). Applications specify intended use (proof of concept, evaluation/comparison, workshop/training, open-source development) and external funding status. The Google Public Sector 'Program for Accelerated Research' (GPAR) layers on top: co-investment pricing for GPUs/TPUs, early access to new accelerators, foundational models/datasets (e.g., AlphaFold, Earth AI), agentic AI (Co-scientist, AlphaEvolve), generative-AI grant tooling, and campus research days.
findings.eligibility: Researchers/faculty at accredited academic institutions, including PhD students acting on behalf of the institution; .edu/institutional email; some country restrictions on the credits form; credits may only be used on behalf of the educational entity for the described project, not personal use, and not for commercial purposes.
findings.expiry: Credit coupon is valid for 60 days from the stated project start date; the credit itself expires 365 days from the coupon redemption date or when the amount is fully used, whichever comes first. Credits can be issued in increments as you use them.
findings.gotchas: Academic, non-commercial use only - cannot be resold, bartered or transferred. If you miss the 60-day redemption window the coupon lapses. 'Up to $5,000' is a per-application maximum; approval amount is at Google's discretion. Students who are not at an institution do not qualify - use the student offer below.
findings.name: Google Cloud for researchers - research credits (up to $5,000) + GPAR program

findings.claim: Go to cloud.google.com/edu/students -> 'Get started' (Google Cloud for students) and 'Request credits' for the 200 Google Skills credits; join a Google Developer Student Club chapter via the same page.
findings.detail: 'Google Cloud for students': free self-paced learning, Google Cloud Certificates and skill badges, hands-on Google Skills labs (formerly Cloud Skills Boost/Qwiklabs) and the gamified Google Skills Arcade, plus Google Developer Student Club communities. Students can request 200 free Google Skills credits (redeemable toward lab/training use); exam previews are free on YouTube. No GCP dollar-credit pool and no managed-DB free tier is granted directly to students - their hands-on GCP usage comes via faculty teaching credits, the $300 trial (card required), or the always-free caps.
findings.eligibility: Students at participating/any accredited institution, verified via school email where the request flow asks for it; Google account required. No credit card needed for the learning program or Skills credits. No funding/stage criteria.
findings.expiry: Google Skills credits expire one year after they are issued. Learning/arcade access is tied to active student status.
findings.gotchas: These are training/lab credits, NOT $200 of GCP service credit - don't budget them for Cloud SQL/BigQuery instances. If students need GCP compute, route through faculty credits ($100/$50) or the card-required $300 trial.
findings.name: Google Cloud for students - free learning + 200 free Google Skills credits

provider: Google Cloud (GCP) - Managed Databases & Data Platforms front
sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes observed today (2026-10-22) on live pages: (1) The startup program is now branded "Google for Startups Cloud Program" at cloud.google.com/startups; the task's "known so far: up to $200,000" equals the current non-AI "Scale" funded-tier cap, but the headline cap is now up to $350,000 over two years ("Scale AI" tier: Year 1 100% coverage up to $250,000; Year 2 20% up to an additional $100,000; non-AI "Scale": Year 1 up to $100,000 + Year 2 up to $100,000). Legacy partner-accelerator network (Y Combinator/500/Techstars-era "Accelerate" listings) is replaced on the page by generic "equity-free accelerators" cohorts plus a "Gemini Startup Forum." Old URL cloud.google.com/programs/startups now 404s. (2) The Always-Free tier was restructured on cloud.google.com/free: the legacy free allotments for Cloud SQL (micro instance 750h/mo + 20GB SSD/375GB HDD), Memorystore, Spanner, and Dataflow (9,600h/mo) are no longer listed, and BigQuery no longer lists the 10GB storage free allotment (only 1TB/mo queries); Cloud Storage was cut to "5 GB-months Standard" and Cloud Functions was replaced by "Cloud Run functions." GCP now pairs this with finite product-specific free trials (30-90 days) for managed databases/data platforms. Confidence in this "changed" comparison is medium - I read today's page (high) but could not archive-compare (web search budget exhausted this session). (3) The $300 trial page no longer states a day limit or "60 days" wording; it says "You won't be charged until you activate your full paid account" (activation-based; historical 60-day term not visible today). (4) "Cloud Skills Boost" is rebranded as "Google Skills" (student offer is "200 free Google Skills credits"). (5) New 2025-2026 offers not previously on GCP: Gemini Enterprise Plus edition 30-day trial, Agent Engine free allotment (180,000 vCPU-s/360,000 GiB-s per month), Datastream free 100 GiB CDC/month, GKE 90-day trial. No GCP free offer appears to have been fully closed in this window - the major move is shrinkage of the always-free tier plus product trials and a bigger AI-leaning startup program. All findings above were verified by reading the cited official pages directly on 2026-10-22.

findings.name: 30-day Developer Free Trial (ScyllaDB Cloud)
findings.detail: A 30-day free trial on small instances — the official pricing FAQ says 'A 30-day trial running on smaller instances (e.g., AWS t3.micro)', 'perfect for exploring the CQL interface and building prototypes'. Docs add: trial includes drivers and monitoring; trial clusters support Vector and Text Search at no cost but are limited to the smallest index node sizes (AWS t4g.medium, GCP e2-medium, 2 vCPU/4 GiB). 'The free trial is limited to one cluster per account.'
findings.eligibility: Any user who registers a ScyllaDB Cloud account (no .edu email, no startup requirements). AWS and GCP; deployments supported in most AWS/GCP regions except restricted locations like China. No credit card is explicitly required for the trial itself — the docs quick-start says payment info is only prompted when creating a regular (paid) cluster ('If not already provided, the wizard will prompt you to provide the required payment information').
findings.claim: 1) Register an account at cloud.scylladb.com (auth.cloud.scylladb.com/oauth/account/login); 2) log in and click 'Free Trial'; 3) configure cluster (name, AWS or GCP, limited instance-type selection, optional Vector/Text Search); 4) launch and connect. One free trial per account.
findings.expiry: 30 days; not renewable — one trial per account, after which you must 'create a regular ScyllaDB Cloud cluster' on a paid plan (On-Demand, Flex Credit, or Contract).
findings.gotchas: No SLA and no usual support during the trial. Not for production workloads. After expiry, upgrading to paid triggers payment-info entry. Instance type on the current pricing page (t3.micro) differs from docs trial-cluster sizes (t4g.medium/e2-medium) — the docs figures refer to the smallest vector/text-search index nodes, so confirm the available storage-instance list in the UI when you claim. Web-search budget for this session was exhausted partway through, so a couple of side checks (exact trial-instance list, current 48-h evaluation instance) could not be re-verified today.

findings.name: 48-hour Production Evaluation (ScyllaDB Cloud)
findings.detail: 'Production Evaluation: A 48-hour free trial of production-grade instances', 'designed for performance benchmarking and testing ScyllaDB's single-digit millisecond latency under real-world workloads' (current pricing-page FAQ). Launched April 2022 on a high-performance AWS i3.2xlarge instance with known limitations: no backup or repair, no multiple data centers, no cluster resize. Enabled for every ScyllaDB Cloud user since June 2022.
findings.eligibility: Any registered ScyllaDB Cloud account; aimed at DevOps teams validating performance. Same AWS/GCP coverage as ScyllaDB Cloud (majority of commercially available regions except China and other restricted locations). No credit card explicitly required for the evaluation itself.
findings.claim: Register a ScyllaDB Cloud account, log in, and start the production evaluation (per the 2022 launch post: 'Create a New Cluster' and select the free trial option in instance types; solutions architects are available to help design the 48-hour scenario).
findings.expiry: 48 hours; no renewal. After it ends, continue on a paid plan. No backup/repair during the window, so capture data yourself before expiry.
findings.gotchas: Trial-grade: no SLA, no support commitment, no backup/repair, no multi-DC, no resize — data loss risk at expiry. The i3.2xlarge instance detail comes from the 2022 launch post; current docs only restate 'production-grade instances' without naming a type, so verify in the UI. Not available for actual production traffic.

findings.name: ScyllaDB Startup Program (12-month free Enterprise licensing)
findings.detail: Free ScyllaDB licensing 'in accordance with our Master Software License Agreement' for 12 months. Official page: 'Enterprise-grade, hardened, full-featured, no ceiling on the scale of deployment', plus partner opportunities at no additional cost (virtual events, co-marketing collateral; in-person events possible with travel costs that may apply). A 2025 LinkedIn post by a ScyllaDB sales rep frames it as 'beyond the 50 vCPU / 10 TB free-tier cap' — that cap figure is unverified on any official page and should not be relied on.
findings.eligibility: 'A startup with less than $20M USD in total funding'. No company-age limit and no region limit stated on the official page. It is a licensing program (self-hosted / Bring Your Own Account), not a free ScyllaDB Cloud trial — free managed hosting is not included. No credit card required to apply.
findings.claim: Go to https://lp.scylladb.com/startups and submit the application (page has an 'Apply here' link / #apply form).
findings.expiry: 12 months; renewal available 'if still within the funding threshold' (i.e., total funding still under $20M).
findings.gotchas: Free license only: if you run it on AWS/GCP you still pay your cloud bill (or use BYOA). No end-of-term data policy is stated. The 50 vCPU/10 TB 'free-tier cap' referenced in marketing is not on any official page I could fetch — treat as unverified (my web-search budget ran out, so a deep-dive confirmation wasn't possible).

findings.name: ScyllaDB University + free education resources (no .edu student license)
findings.detail: ScyllaDB University (university.scylladb.com) is a free, self-paced NoSQL training platform: courses, videos, hands-on labs, and free accounts; free live 'ScyllaDB University LIVE' virtual trainings (e.g., 2025 editions) that are interactive and not available on-demand afterwards. There is no student-specific software license, no .edu-verified discount, and no dedicated education program found — scylladb.com/education/ is a 404, and no startup/education page appears on the pricing page.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; a free University account is enough. No .edu email requirement. No credit card.
findings.claim: Register at university.scylladb.com (free account) and take courses or join the next LIVE event listed there.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no expiry on course content. Free access to labs may use a free trial cluster (one per account, 30 days).
findings.gotchas: This is learning content, not a free managed-database offer — the DB itself still comes from the 30-day trial or a paid license. Do not confuse with other vendors' student programs; ScyllaDB has no equivalent student-credit program found as of 2026-10-22.

sunset_notes: No permanent free tier: the only recurring free offers are the two one-time trials (30-day dev trial, 48-hour production evaluation) and the 12-month Startup Program (licensing, under-$20M funded startups). 2025-2026 changes: (1) X Cloud (elastic, tablets-based) launched June 2025 with Flex Credit annual commitments — pricing model changes, but no free tier added; (2) Vector and Text Search became usable on free-trial clusters at no cost, with trial clusters limited to the smallest index node sizes (AWS t4g.medium, GCP e2-medium) and the trial capped at one cluster per account; (3) the 2022 trial definitions (t3.micro dev instance, i3.2xlarge prod evaluation) still appear in the pricing FAQ, while current docs no longer name the dev-trial instance type — the offer survived but its smallest-instance list now differs; (4) no student/education license program exists or was sunset — education/education-licensing offers were not found and scylladb.com/education/ returns 404; free education is via ScyllaDB University only. Note: session web-search budget was exhausted during this research, so instance-level details (current dev-trial instance types, any '50 vCPU / 10 TB' free-tier cap mentioned in a 2025 sales rep's LinkedIn post) are marked medium/unverified.

findings.name: Aiven Free Tier ($0/month, perpetual)
findings.detail: Standing $0/month free plan, no time limit, no credit card or payment details required. One free single-node service per type per account. Caps (network/egress costs still apply): PostgreSQL 1GB storage / 1GB RAM; MySQL 1GB storage / 1GB RAM; Valkey 1GB RAM; Apache Kafka up to 250 kb/s IN and OUT with retention up to 3 days; OpenSearch 20GB storage / 4GB RAM / up to 20 shards. Free services are single-node (multi-node HA is paid-only), no integrations or connection pooling. Aiven may shut down services that violate acceptable-use or stay unused an extended period.
findings.eligibility: Any user — no .edu, no company email, no funding/age cap, no credit card. Open to students and individuals.
findings.claim: Create a free Aiven account at console.aiven.io/signup (no payment details required), then deploy the desired service (ready in minutes). Upgrade to paid is one-click with no data migration/downtime.
findings.expiry: No expiry / no trial clock. 'Always free.' Aiven reserves the right to shut down unused or policy-violating services.
findings.gotchas: Capped resources, not for production; network/egress costs are not included; one free instance per service type; deleting a service deletes its data; Kafka retention max 3 days on free tier.

findings.name: 30-day free trial / new-account credits
findings.detail: Pricing FAQ offers a 'free 30-day trial' when you need more memory or advanced features. The Developer-tier page states new accounts get '$300 in free credits' and 'no credit card required.' The two pages describe the offer differently (the $300 figure appears only on the Developer-tier page, not on pricing), so treat the exact credit amount as unconfirmed.
findings.eligibility: New Aiven accounts; no .edu requirement; no credit card required per the Developer-tier page.
findings.claim: Sign up at console.aiven.io/signup and start a trial / pick a plan beyond the free tier. No card needed to start.
findings.expiry: 30-day window for the trial; free credits are new-account promotional credits. End-of-trial outcome (downgrade vs auto-charge) not stated on the page — consult docs; auto-billing behavior not confirmed.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free-tier distinction: the 30-day trial is for higher-memory/advanced features, not the perpetual free plan. $300 figure not corroborated on the pricing page, so verify in-console before relying on it. Whether a card is required after trial to continue is not confirmed.

findings.name: Aiven Startup Program (startup-credits)
findings.detail: Up to $100,000 in Aiven credits over a 12-month period (tiers from $12,000 up to $100,000), tiered by the startup's stage of growth and funding. Credits expire if unused by the end of the 12-month program. Plus perks: 1:1 technical expert mentoring/office hours, Aiven startup Slack community, blog/social/event feature opportunities, exclusive early-stage virtual events; perks are unlocked in levels based on activity/usage. Aiven may extend credits (not guaranteed, needs strong growth reasoning) and reserves the right to cancel on T&C breach/misuse. No credit card or payment requirement is stated on the page.
findings.eligibility: Company founded no more than 7 years ago; external funding from pre-seed through Series B; must apply with a company/business email; proof of affiliation with a VC investor and/or an Aiven ecosystem partner (or an affiliated accelerator/incubator/co-working space) helps. Agencies, consulting firms, NGOs, and educational institutions are explicitly excluded. Existing Aiven customers with a monthly invoice under $400 may still qualify case-by-case. .edu email is NOT required.
findings.claim: Submit the application via the Typeform on the startups page (primary: aiven-startups.typeform.com/to/STphOA6R; secondary: form.typeform.com/to/BqNrcMLJ). Reviewed on a rolling monthly basis, ~14 days for review. Once accepted, reserve a required personal kickoff session.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months and expire unused; one-time only ('you can only receive Startup credits once'). No program-wide sunset date is published.
findings.gotchas: You can only receive the startup credits once. Perks/credits are level-gated on activity. One-time + 12-month expiry means no renewal. No sunset date stated, so confirm still-accepting status at the Typeform.

findings.name: Education license / .edu student program
findings.detail: No dedicated education or student program exists. aiven.io/education returns HTTP 404. The free tier and Developer-tier FAQ mention students/solo developers/side projects as an audience, but there is no separate .edu-verified education license, no academic discount, and no student-only offer.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no such offer found. Students are covered only via the general Free Tier (no .edu, no card).
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim; use the general Free Tier for student projects.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Do not assume an education license; verify only against aiven.io/free-tier and aiven.io/developer-tier.

sunset_notes: No free offer was sunset in 2025–2026. The aiven.io/education URL 404s (no dedicated education/.edu license has ever been offered; students use the general Free Tier). A dedicated /startup-program and /blog/aiven-startup-program URLs 404; the live startup program lives at aiven.io/startups and is currently active (Typeform applications open). WebSearch budget was exhausted this session, so 2025–2026 change claims could not be verified via search; findings above were read directly from the live official pages (aiven.io/free-tier, aiven.io/pricing, aiven.io/developer-tier, aiven.io/startups) today, so current-state detail is high-confidence. The $300 new-account credit figure and the 30-day trial end-of-trial behavior (auto-charge vs downgrade vs data deletion) are not fully corroborated on the official pages — verify in-console before relying on them.

findings.name: Starter free tier ($0/mo + metered usage)
findings.detail: Starter plan: $0/month base + usage; 10 databases and 10 team members included. Metered rates: writes $2.50/GiB (logical, uncompressed, billed once per write — no background-index charges), storage $0.33/GiB/month prorated hourly, queries $0.0075/TiB queried (each metadata/full-text predicate counts as extra queries), network $0.09/GiB returned, forking $0.03/fork, Sync $0.04/GiB processed + $0.01/page extracted/scraped. Self-hosted open-source ChromaDB (Apache 2.0) is also $0 with no limits.
findings.eligibility: Anyone creating a new Chroma Cloud account. No .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card required at sign-up (auth via Google, GitHub, SSO, or email). No regional restrictions published; service endpoints are aws-us-east-1 (US) and gcp-europe-west1 (EU); BYOC single-tenant only on Enterprise.
findings.claim: Sign up at trychroma.com/signup (Google/GitHub/SSO/email) and select the Starter plan at trychroma.com/pricing — $0 base, no application. Exceeding 10 databases or 10 team members requires the Team plan ($250/month + usage).
findings.expiry: No duration limit: it is a permanent $0 plan, not a trial; no commitment. Plan changes pro-rate to the calendar month. Unused usage credits 'do not expire' in most cases (per pricing FAQ).
findings.gotchas: Exceeding either customer-set or Chroma-set usage limits pauses the service until a limit is changed — set a billing limit after the $5 credits run out. After credits are used, a credit card must be added to keep using the service (per Chroma's Oct 2025 '5 Things to Know' video). Egress/network ($0.09/GiB returned) and hourly storage billing apply; filter-heavy queries cost more than query count suggests (each predicate adds query units). Team plan floor is $250/month; Enterprise adds single-tenant/BYOC/SLAs.

findings.name: $5 trial credits for new users
findings.detail: One-time $5 in usage credits granted to new Chroma Cloud accounts (docs FAQ: 'We offer $5 in credits to new users'). Chroma's own video estimates $5 covers ~100K document inserts and ~100K queries. Billing is account-level, aggregated across all collections/tenants in the account.
findings.eligibility: Any new Chroma Cloud account (new users only; not per team member). No verification, no .edu requirement, no credit card required to receive the credits.
findings.claim: Automatic at sign-up via trychroma.com/signup — no application, no code, no separate claim step.
findings.expiry: Credits do not expire in most cases (pricing FAQ: 'in most cases your credits do not expire'; the $100 Team-plan inclusion does not rollover — not relevant to Starter). No renewal cycle; new credits are not re-granted.
findings.gotchas: Small grant: $5 buys roughly 2 GiB of writes at $2.50/GiB. After the credits are exhausted, a credit card is required to continue (trial-vs-free: the $0 plan is permanent, but the trial credits are one-time — ongoing usage is metered). Hitting usage limits pauses the service until limits are adjusted.

findings.name: Partner startup perk: $5,000 Chroma credits via PostHog for Startups
findings.detail: Listed on third-party directory creditbase.in (database category): accepted PostHog for Startups participants can receive $5,000 in Chroma credits as a partner perk (Chroma-issued, global). No Chroma-owned startup program, age cap, or funding cap is documented on Chroma's own pricing or docs pages.
findings.eligibility: Startups accepted into PostHog for Startups (i.e., PostHog's program rules apply, typically early-stage companies); no .edu requirement from Chroma.
findings.claim: Via the PostHog for Startups partner perks, not through any Chroma page or form found as of 2026-10-22.
findings.expiry: Not stated in the listing; treat as current-until-confirmed (directory is a third-party aggregator).
findings.gotchas: Could not verify this offer on any official Chroma page today (not on pricing, docs, or changelog); amount, availability, and whether it still applies are unconfirmed — confirm with Chroma/PostHog before relying on it.

sunset_notes: No official Chroma education/student licensing or Chroma-owned startup program exists on trychroma.com or docs.trychroma.com as of 2026-10-22 — no education or startup pages, and no such offers are mentioned on the pricing page, docs, or changelog. The free offer set is: (1) the $0/mo Starter plan with 10 databases / 10 team members, (2) one-time $5 new-user credits, (3) self-hosted open-source ChromaDB (Apache 2.0, fully free, unlimited), plus one unverified third-party-listed startup perk ($5,000 credits via PostHog for Startups). History/sunset: Chroma Cloud launched 2025-08-18 (changelog 'Introducing Chroma Cloud'), superseding the earlier Chroma Cloud trial; third-party tracker AgentDeals records a pricing-model change (discovered 2026-09-07, effective date unknown) from a legacy free tier (reported ~1M embeddings, 1 collection, 10K queries/day — unverified) to the current $0 Starter + $5 credits + metered pricing; the current metered terms were confirmed on the official pricing page today, so no free offer was sunsetting recently. Beware name confusion: 'Chroma Awards' (chromaawards.com), a film/music/games competition that recruited universities and students in 2025 with 'starter packs', internships and a $3M+ credit pool, is a separate organization, not the ChromaDB vendor. Course-sponsored credits (e.g., $250 Chroma Cloud credits for students of Hugo Bowne-Anderson's 'Building AI Applications' masterclass, Nov 2025 and Mar 2026 cohorts) are time-limited, sponsor-funded, cohort-specific — not a Chroma program.

findings.name: ClickHouse Cloud free trial: $300 credits over 30 days (no credit card)
findings.detail: Official pricing page (verified 2026-10-22): "$300 in credits over 30 days", 1 ClickHouse Credit (CHC) = $1 USD of usage. FAQ: "Is there a free tier? ClickHouse Cloud starts with $300 in credits over 30 days, no credit card required." Trial ends after 30 days or once credits are consumed, whichever comes first; account then converts to pay-as-you-go with no monthly minimum (invoiced in $0.01 increments). No permanent free tier: entry paid tier is Basic (up to 1 TB storage, 8-12 GiB total memory, 24h backups retained 1 day, 1 availability zone). Compute scales to zero when idle ($0 for idle compute time; storage still bills continuously).
findings.eligibility: Anyone. Sign up at https://console.clickhouse.cloud/signUp via email, Google SSO, or Microsoft SSO. No .edu email, no startup status, no company size limits stated. Available on AWS, GCP, and Azure. Credit card explicitly NOT required.
findings.claim: Single step: sign up at console.clickhouse.cloud/signUp; the $300 trial credit is granted to new organizations automatically (campaign page: "Get started for free... Create a free account"). No application or form.
findings.expiry: 30 days or credit exhaustion, whichever comes first; no renewal or re-application. After the trial the account continues on pay-as-you-go usage-based billing.
findings.gotchas: Trial is not a free tier: once the 30 days/credits end, usage billing begins (no card on file doesn't mean no bill - you can accrue charges after trial, so monitor console). Egress/data transfer, backups, and ClickPipes ingestion are billed separately; public internet egress is from ~$0.1152/GB since the Jan 2025 price change (egress used to be free - now a migration 'divorce fee'). Storage bills even when compute is scaled to zero. Basic plan caps (1 TB, 8-12 GiB, single AZ) apply to the cheapest tier.

findings.name: Open-source ClickHouse - free forever (self-hosted)
findings.detail: "Open source (free forever)" per the official pricing page; Apache 2.0 core, no license cost, no per-unit billing, no duration limit. Official one-liner install: `curl https://clickhouse.com/ | sh`. This is the genuine free option for students on any budget: run it on a laptop, student cluster, or own cloud VM. Certain advanced/enterprise features are reserved for the proprietary/Enterprise edition or Cloud.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (students, academics, startups, enterprises); no .edu or application required.
findings.claim: Install locally or on self-managed infrastructure via the curl one-liner or package manager; no signup.
findings.expiry: No expiry; license is free indefinitely.
findings.gotchas: Self-hosted means you own ops (upgrades, replication, hardware, cloud instance costs). Open-core model: enterprise-locked features unavailable in the OSS build; OSS version lags behind Cloud features.

findings.name: ClickHouse Startup Program: $5,000 credits for 12 months (partner-gated)
findings.detail: Official startup-offer page (verified 2026-10-22): "Founders can apply for $5000 in ClickHouse Cloud credits, expert training, and promotion opportunities". Credits valid for 12 months. Package also includes ClickHouse Basic Support, expert training, a joint blog-post feature/promotion on ClickHouse channels, and speaking slots at ClickHouse community events.
findings.eligibility: All of: company less than 3 years old; pre-Series D ("haven't raised a Series D or later funding round"); has NEVER been a paid ClickHouse Cloud customer; belongs to a program run by one of the listed partners (Antler, Bessemer, Blackbird, Google For Startups, Lightspeed, Merantix, Station F, TechLeap, TechStars - selected via dropdown in the form); holds a valid verification code obtained from the accelerator/incubator/VC. No .edu/region limits stated on the page. Headcount limits not stated.
findings.claim: Three steps on the page: (1) sign up for a free ClickHouse Cloud trial (console signup); (2) complete the application form with your ClickHouse Organization ID, company details, and the partner-program dropdown; (3) wait for approval - the team reviews and confirms the credits.
findings.expiry: Credits valid for 12 months from approval; no renewal or re-application window described on the page. One-time, new-customer-only offer.
findings.gotchas: Partner-gated: you cannot apply directly - must be inside a listed partner's program and have its verification code, or the application can't be validated. New-to-ClickHouse requirement excludes any prior paid usage. Hitting Series D before applying disqualifies. Support included is 'Basic' tier only, not enterprise support. No stated extension of the 12-month window.

findings.name: ClickHouse x Y Combinator deal: $10,000 credits for 24 months
findings.detail: Official deals/ycombinator page (verified 2026-10-22): "$10,000 in ClickHouse Cloud credits, valid for 24 months" plus ClickHouse Basic Support, a one-hour expert training session, a joint blog-post feature/promotion, and speaking opportunities at ClickHouse community events. Audience labeled "Current & Alumni" of YC, pre-Series D, new to ClickHouse Cloud.
findings.eligibility: All of: "You're part of the current Y Combinator program"; pre-Series D ("You haven't raised a Series D or later round"); holds a valid YC secret code for verification; "You are not a current ClickHouse Cloud customer". No .edu email requirement (this is a startup program, not a student one). No region limits stated.
findings.claim: Three steps on the page: (1) sign up for a free ClickHouse Cloud trial; (2) complete the application form including your ClickHouse Organization ID and company details; (3) wait for approval - the team reviews and confirms the credits. The YC secret code is used for verification.
findings.expiry: Hard 24-month expiry on the credits; no renewal, extension, or stacking language on the page. One-time offer.
findings.gotchas: Existing ClickHouse Cloud customers are explicitly excluded. The YC secret code is mandatory - without it verification fails. Pre-Series D cap is a hard ceiling. No stated path to re-apply for a second tranche.

findings.name: Student/education license: none found (no dedicated program as of 2026-10-22)
findings.detail: No free education license, academic tier, .edu discount, or student-specific credit program was found. clickhouse.com/startups and /education return 404; the official llms.txt page index (90+ entries) lists no education/student program - only the trial ($300/30 days), the two startup programs above, a paid/optional certification track (learn/certification: "ClickHouse Certified Developer Exam"), and a government self-managed offering (FedRAMP). Students' free paths are: (a) the $300 trial for any individual, (b) open-source ClickHouse free forever. Verified via official page index and 404 checks on 2026-10-22, but the whole site was not crawled, so a low-visibility program cannot be fully ruled out.
findings.eligibility: N/A - no dedicated student eligibility (no .edu email gate found anywhere on official pages).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; students use the $300 trial (sign up at console.clickhouse.cloud/signUp, no credit card) or self-host open-source ClickHouse for free.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: The trial is not student-specific and converts to pay-as-you-go; if the program is ever launched, it would likely live at clickhouse.com/education or similar - none exists today.

sunset_notes: No ClickHouse free offer was sunset or materially reduced in 2025-2026. The $300/30-day trial has stayed unchanged on the official pricing page through 2026. Material related changes: (1) January 2025 pricing overhaul - a ~30% increase for typical production workloads plus the introduction of egress/data-transfer fees (egress was previously free; the change made migration off ClickHouse Cloud expensive, e.g. ~$115.20/TiB \"divorce fee\" estimate); old prices were grandfathered for six months until 2025-07-23. These post-trial fees affect trial users who stay on pay-as-you-go. (2) No permanent free tier ever existed (third-party 2026 reviews confirm \"free trial but no permanent free tier\"), and none was added or removed in the window. The two startup programs (YC $10k/24mo; partner-gated $5k/12mo) are current as of 2026-10-22; no sunset of any named program was found. Note: session web-search budget was exhausted mid-task, so verification relied on official pages (read directly today) plus one pre-budget-exhaustion search result set; no 2025-2026 changelog beyond the Jan 2025 price change was found.

provider: Qdrant (Qdrant Cloud) — free tier, startup program, education

findings.name: Qdrant Cloud Free Forever tier
findings.detail: Permanently free 1-node cluster: 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB RAM / 4 GB disk, 'around one million 768-dimension vectors'. Free cloud-inference works on it, but only with free and external models (free models: sentence-transformers/all-minilm-l6-v2, intfloat/multilingual-e5-small, qdrant/bm25, answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1).
