Tier is described as 'for testing, and prototypes' and 'without high availability'. Support: community, best-effort response, 99.5% uptime SLA. No HA, no VPC links, no enterprise SSO. Exceeding 1 GB RAM / 4 GB disk prompts upgrade to the Standard (paid) tier, where compute/memory/storage are billed hourly.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no .edu, no funding or age cap. Credit card NOT required ('No credit card, no minimum spend' per qdrant.tech/cloud). No region limit stated on the page; cloud availability depends on the chosen infrastructure/region at signup.
findings.claim: Sign up at cloud.qdrant.io/signup (the 'Start Free' button on qdrant.tech/pricing and qdrant.tech/cloud) -> choose Free plan and a region -> 'spin up a permanently free cluster in under 90 seconds'. No form review; instant activation.
findings.expiry: No expiry: explicitly 'free forever', not a trial. Free forever as long as the tier is not upgraded; on upgrade, hourly billing starts for compute, memory, storage, backups, and paid-model inference tokens. Data retention on free clusters is not documented.
findings.gotchas: Not high-availability; single node. Free inference is limited to free/external models - paid inference models are not free on the free tier (external models like OpenAI/Cohere/Jina are billed directly by the provider under your API key, no Qdrant markup, but not free). RAM/disk caps (1 GB / 4 GB) are the hard upgrade trigger. Community support only. The ~1M-vector figure is approximate ('around one million').

findings.name: Free inference tokens on paid clusters (5M tokens/model/month)
findings.detail: Paid Qdrant Cloud clusters receive up to 5 million free inference tokens per model per month on paid inference models; BM25 hybrid search has no token cap. This is a recurring monthly free allotment, not a one-time trial. Paid inference otherwise billed per 1,000,000 tokens, with per-model rates shown in the Inference tab of the Cloud console. Qdrant-hosted paid models include mixedbread-ai/mxbai-embed-large-v1, qdrant/clip-vit-b-32-text/vision, prithivida/splade_pp_en_v1.
findings.eligibility: Any paid Qdrant Cloud cluster (Standard tier or above). No startup/student requirement, no credit cap. Note: the cap is stated per model, so different paid models each get their own 5M/month allowance.
findings.claim: No separate claim step: create/upgrade a paid cluster, enable cloud inference in the console, and the free monthly tokens apply automatically. Prices per model are visible in the Inference tab of the Cluster Detail page.
findings.expiry: Recurring: 'per month' allowance, renews monthly with the subscription. BM25 is explicitly uncapped. No sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: The 5M figure comes from the FAQ on qdrant.tech/cloud (and is what 'free credits' known-so-far refers to) - it is not restated with the same number on qdrant.tech/pricing itself, so treat the exact cap as FAQ-stated. Free models (including qdrant/bm25) are free on all tiers including the free tier; the 5M free tokens specifically apply to PAID models on PAID clusters. No dollar-denominated trial credits for new customers were found on any page fetched.

findings.name: Qdrant for Startups program (20% off for 12 months)
findings.detail: 20% discount on Qdrant Cloud for 12 months from date of acceptance; no dollar cap on savings stated. Extras: partner perks from Hugging Face, LlamaIndex, and Airbyte, expert technical-advice sessions, and co-marketing (social media, Discord talks/webinars, case studies). Reviews in 7-10 business days; after a rejection you must wait 2 months to re-apply. Billing runs through Stripe (not a cloud marketplace), so discounted usage still requires a card.
findings.eligibility: Pre-seed, Seed, or Series A startups; under 5 years old; less than $5M in funding; must be a NEW user of Qdrant Cloud (existing customers qualify only if the cloud account was created within the last 30 days). Agencies and dev shops are explicitly NOT eligible. No employee/revenue cap and no region limit stated on the page. Credit card IS required to use the discount.
findings.claim: Apply through the online form on qdrant.tech/qdrant-for-startups/ (do not email submissions). Provide startup details and planned Qdrant usage. Wait 7-10 business days for review; on acceptance add a credit card to the Qdrant account to activate the discount.
findings.expiry: Discount lasts 12 months from acceptance, then standard pricing. Program page current as of fetch (site footer © 2026); no announced end date or 2025-2026 changes on the page.
findings.gotchas: This is a 20% discount, not free - ongoing spend still applies and a credit card is mandatory (unlike the free tier). 'New user' rule means most incumbent Qdrant users cannot stack it; the 30-day account window is the only exception. No stacking rules with other discounts are documented. No geographic restriction is stated, but Stripe billing applies.

findings.name: Education: free self-paced courses + free certification exam (no .edu program)
findings.detail: Qdrant's education offer is free, not an academic license: (1) 'structured, free, online courses' on qdrant.tech/course - Beginner Course (<5h, embeddings/vector search/hybrid search + multimodal capstone), Essentials Course (9-12h, indexing/optimization/API), Multi-Vector Search Course (4-6h, ColBERT/ColPali/late-interaction); upcoming Intermediate (Optimizing Performance, Scaling and DevOps) and Advanced (AI Engineer, Search Engineer) tracks. (2) Qdrant Developer Certification at train.qdrant.dev: multiple-choice quiz based on the official docs and courses, self-paced, earns a public badge; registration is email/Google/LinkedIn-only with a verification code - no price is displayed anywhere on the registration or course pages.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone - no .edu email, no student status, no enrollment or funding requirements. Not an education license or classroom license; no student-specific discount exists because the material is already free.
findings.claim: Courses: go to qdrant.tech/course and start a course directly ('See Courses'). Certification: train.qdrant.dev/register -> 'Continue with Google/LinkedIn/email' -> verify -> complete the quiz at your own pace -> earn the badge. For more topics, email devrel@qdrant.com.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal noted; courses and exam are self-paced with no stated sunset. Upcoming advanced courses currently only have 'Register Interest' Google Form links, not open seats.
findings.gotchas: The courses page explicitly says free, but the exam page never labels itself 'free' - absence of any price/payment is the evidence, hence medium confidence that the exam is truly free vs. gated later. Free cloud-inference on self-hosted/open-source Qdrant is NOT available (cloud-only feature; docs suggest FastEmbed as the OSS alternative). Web search was unavailable in this session (budget exhausted), so any 2025-2026 changes not visible on the pages fetched today could not be cross-checked against news/blog posts.

sunset_notes: No sunsets found as of 2026-10-22: the free tier is still 'free forever', the startup program is live (page footer © 2026) with the 20%/12-month terms unchanged on the page, and no dollar-denominated trial-credit program exists (the only 'free credits' are the recurring 5M free inference tokens/model/month on paid clusters). Two gaps, both from primary pages fetched today: (1) number of free clusters per account and free-tier data-retention policy are not documented on qdrant.tech/pricing; (2) a session web-search budget limit prevented checking third-party reports for 2025-2026 program changes, so 'no change' is a statement about the official pages only. Key distinction for classification: the free tier requires NO credit card; the startup program REQUIRES a credit card; the 5M-token allotment is a standing monthly benefit of paid plans, not a signup trial.

provider: Google Cloud (Google) — free trial + always-free tier, fronts: Managed Databases & Data Platforms (Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Cloud Spanner)

findings.claim: 1) cloud.google.com/free → 'Get started for free' / console signup; 2) create a Google account; 3) complete Free Trial signup: name, address, payment method; 4) Google verifies identity/payment, trial billing account 'My Billing Account' + 'My First Project' are created, $300 preloaded; 5) use products for 90 days; optionally click 'Activate' to upgrade to a paid account before the trial closes to keep resources.
findings.detail: New GCP customers get $300 in free 'Welcome credit' valid for 90 days from signup (NOT 60 days as previously believed; official docs and the Jan-30-2025 archived T&Cs both say 90 days/3 months). Credit covers 200+ products (incl. Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Spanner) including usage beyond free-tier limits; Free Tier usage does not draw down the $300. No billing unless you manually upgrade to a Paid account. On upgrade mid-trial, remaining credit still expires 90 days from signup. No SLA during trial; restrictions: no GPUs on VMs, no GCP Marketplace, no quota increases, no Windows Server VMs, no Cloud VMware Engine, no crypto mining; the $300 cannot pay Gemini API in AI Studio costs or managed partner models (MaaS). Trial account ends at $300 spent or 90 days, then a 30-day grace period — resources stop, then are permanently deleted if not upgraded.
findings.eligibility: Must have never been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase, and never signed up for the Free Trial (one per person/identity). A valid credit card or other payment method IS required at signup (identity verification; a $0.00–$1.00 authorization hold may appear, it is not a charge). Bank-account verification needed in some countries. US/Mexico government entities excluded. No .edu requirement; no startup-only gating.
findings.expiry: 90 days from signup or when $300 is exhausted (earlier); then 30-day grace period, after which trial resources are deleted. Free Tier (below) continues indefinitely after.
findings.gotchas: Credit card/payment method required even though you aren't billed; resources are permanently deleted after the 30-day post-trial grace period; GCE limited to 8 concurrent cores during trial; 'eligible customers' free-tier availability can vary by country (e.g., India trial needs an INR billing account; Maps Platform not available on INR accounts); free limits are 'subject to change'.
findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial: $300 credit, 90 days

findings.claim: 1) Console → Cloud SQL 'Get Started' page → 'Experience Cloud SQL at no cost for 30 days' section; 2) choose engine, instance ID, password, region; 3) 'Create free instance'; 4) monitor remaining days on the instance Overview page; 5) click 'Upgrade' before trial/grace ends to keep the instance (switches to normal pricing).
findings.detail: Official free Cloud SQL offer today: a 30-day free trial instance at no cost — Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus edition, N2 machine series, 8 vCPUs, 64 GB memory, 100 GB storage. Covers MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. In addition to the $300/90-day GCP free-trial credit (new customers). Upgrade to a paid instance anytime during the 30-day trial or the following 90-day grace period; if not upgraded the instance is stopped. Deleting the trial instance makes the trial non-restartable.
findings.eligibility: Both existing AND new GCP customers can use it, but the trial instance must be created in a NEW Google Cloud project, one trial instance per project. An enabled Cloud Billing account is required: existing users verify billing is enabled; new users must set up a billing account with a card/other payment method (which normally means going through the $300 trial signup). No .edu requirement, no startup requirement.
findings.expiry: 30-day trial period + 90-day grace period, then stops if not upgraded to paid.
findings.gotchas: Old 'Cloud SQL Always Free plan' (free shared-core instance in select regions, 750 h/month E2-micro/C2D + storage/backup/egress allowances) is NO LONGER listed on the Cloud SQL pricing page — the current official free offer is only this 30-day trial instance; egress and backups are charged once you upgrade; SQL Server trial carries 4-core license minimum rules; instance is 'evaluation' — production use not guaranteed.
findings.name: Cloud SQL Free Trial Instance (30 days, Enterprise Plus)

findings.claim: 1) Console → Cloud Spanner → create a 'free trial instance' (console or CLI, per 'Create a free trial instance' docs); 2) pick a regional configuration and region; 3) optionally use the preloaded sample ecommerce database; 4) upgrade to paid Enterprise before the 90-day trial / 30-day grace ends to retain data.
findings.detail: Official free Spanner offer today: a 90-day free trial instance, Standard edition features + Spanner Graph, up to 10 GB (GiB) of stored data. In addition to the $300 GCP free-trial credit (new customers) — the trial instance itself costs nothing and does not need the $300. Regional configurations only (any region; NOT dual-region/multi-region). Not meant for production; no backups/restore, no CMEK, no Data Boost; ~500 QPS reads / ~100 QPS writes achievable. After 90 days the instance stops serving and enters a 30-day grace period, then instance + data are permanently deleted unless upgraded to a paid Enterprise instance (upgrade is downtime-free and can be done anytime during trial or grace).
findings.eligibility: Both existing and new GCP customers: you need an ACTIVE Cloud Billing account with Cloud Billing enabled on the project (new customers can create one via the $300 trial, which requires a card/payment method). One free trial instance per project lifecycle; maximum five free trial instances per Cloud Billing account. No .edu or startup requirements.
findings.expiry: 90-day trial + 30-day grace period; data deleted after that unless upgraded. Re-eligibility: up to 5 trial instances per billing account, 1 per project lifecycle.
findings.gotchas: Data is deleted, not retained, after the grace period; read/write QPS caps make it unsuitable for real workloads; region choices are all regional (no multi-region DR); the previous '1 free 96 GB node (us-west1)' always-free allowance is not present on the current pricing page — the trial instance replaced it.
findings.name: Cloud Spanner Free Trial Instance (90 days, 10 GB)

findings.claim: Nothing to claim: free tier usage is automatic for any GCP account; use BigQuery normally. During a $300 free trial you also get the Free Tier at the same time. To keep using it after trial without paying: stay within 1 TiB queries + 10 GiB storage per month.
findings.detail: Current official BigQuery free tier (per billing account, no expiry): the first 1 TiB of query data processed per month is free (on-demand pay-per-query; beyond that $6.25/TiB in US); the first 10 GiB of storage free each month (active and long-term logical/physical). Also free: batch loading from Cloud Storage/local files (uses free shared slot pool 'default-pipeline'), table reads/copies/metadata ops, and the first 2 TiB per month of gRPC Storage Write API (REST streaming inserts cost $0.01/200 MiB beyond). The old '100,000 slot-hours/month free' allowance is not listed on the current BigQuery pricing page. BigQuery free tier is available to all GCP accounts (free-trial or paid) as long as usage stays under the caps.
findings.eligibility: Any GCP billing account (free trial or paid) staying under the monthly caps; no card needed beyond trial signup; no .edu/startup requirement; applies per billing account (free query bytes ~1 TiB/month/account).
findings.expiry: Indefinite monthly recurring allowance (no expiry; Google may change limits).
findings.gotchas: Free query allowance is per billing account and monthly; streaming inserts via REST are NOT free (only gRPC write API has the 2 TiB allowance); data egress/export to GCS is free but egress to other services/Internet costs; scheduled heavy queries can exceed 1 TiB in a month; the 100K free slot-hours claim found in older docs is no longer published — assume it no longer applies unless you buy editions/slots.
findings.name: BigQuery Free Tier (always-free): 1 TiB queries + 10 GiB storage per month, plus free operations
findings.source_url: https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/pricing (free tier limits also shown on https://cloud.google.com/free)

findings.claim: From cloud.google.com/free, click the relevant 'OFFER' card → product console trial creation flow; upgrade to paid before the trial window to keep resources.
findings.detail: cloud.google.com/free lists additional time-boxed trials that stack on top of the $300 credit: GKE free trial (full product capabilities, 90 days, no cost); AlloyDB for PostgreSQL free trial (30 days; 8 vCPU basic primary instance, up to 1 TB storage capacity); Bigtable free trial (10 days; 1-node SSD cluster, up to 500 GB storage); Looker free trial (30 days, all standard features). Each card notes 'Plus, new Google Cloud customers get $300 in free credits on signup'.
findings.eligibility: Trial-eligible per product docs (generally one trial per new project/billing account pattern; an enabled Cloud Billing account is required, which for new customers means the $300 trial signup with payment method). No .edu requirement.
findings.expiry: Fixed windows: GKE 90 days, AlloyDB 30 days, Bigtable 10 days, Looker 30 days.
findings.gotchas: These are evaluation windows (10–90 days), not free tiers; exceeding the stated size or outliving the window requires upgrading to paid; Bigtable 10 days is very short.
findings.name: Other product-specific free trials on the Google Cloud free program page (data platforms)

findings.claim: 1) cloud.google.com/startup → 'Apply to the program' (AI-focused: cloud.google.com/startup/ai); 2) apply with a company (non-personal) business email matching your website; 3) provide an active 18-character GCP billing account ID; 4) complete onboarding checklist at cloud.google.com/startup/onboarding; 5) on approval credits are deposited to that billing account.
findings.detail: Replaced the older 'Google Cloud Startups Accelerator' (old /startups now serves this program). Tiers as of today: Start ($2k) — $2,000 in credits, for startups founded in the past 2 years with a working MVP, clear business model, and plans to seek VC funding soon; Scale — Year 1: 100% of GCP spend up to $100,000; Year 2: 20% up to an additional $100,000 (up to $200,000 total), for Pre-Seed to Series A funded startups (founded within last 3–5 years, tier-dependent); Scale AI — same structure but Year 1 up to $250,000 (up to $350,000 total) for startups using Gemini as a foundation of their primary product (Pre-Seed/Seed within last 5 years, Series A within last 12 months, founded within last 5 years). Credits cover most GCP pay-as-you-go products incl. Gemini/Gemma model usage; third-party models (e.g., Anthropic) are billed directly and NOT covered. Additional benefits: 12 months Google Workspace Business Plus at no cost (separate application, requires not having paid Workspace within 31 days of applying), monthly Google Maps Platform credits (separate application), Google Skills training, dedicated Startup Success Managers as you grow.
findings.eligibility: VC-funded for Scale tiers: verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding from a known investor within last 3–5 years (tier-dependent); NOT yet received more than $5,000 in GCP credits (non-venture funding — PE, bank loans, grants, crowdfunding, friends-and-family — does NOT qualify for Scale). Exclusions: IPO'd/acquired companies, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, dev shops/consultancies/agencies, crypto mining, token distributors against local rules. Must be in a Google-Cloud-GA region with self-service purchasing; company email domain must match the public website domain; a valid 18-char Cloud Billing account ID is required. Acceptance at Google's sole discretion; not for regulated industries.
findings.expiry: Credits structured as Year-1 (100% up to cap) + Year-2 (20% up to cap) windows over two years; annual re-evaluation of eligibility — prior enrollment doesn't guarantee current-year eligibility; rejected applicants may re-apply later as they raise funding.
findings.gotchas: Credit cap 'up to' amounts assume sustained GCP spend; the $350k is AI-tiers only (other startups cap at $200k total); credits cannot be shared, split, or resold (violation terminates program); 're-apply if you got credits before but didn't use them' is allowed only if you still meet in-year requirements; the $5,000-prior-credits ceiling blocks heavy past GCP usage from Scale tiers (a $300 trial is fine). There is also a separate 'Ecosystem tier' (startups in select accelerators/incubators: $25k–$250k credits) per Google's two-pager.
findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program (credits: Start $2,000 / Scale up to $200,000 / Scale AI up to $350,000)

findings.claim: 1) startup.google.com/programs/accelerator → find your regional accelerator; 2) apply to the cohort (deadline-driven, limited seats); 3) participate in program sessions; 4) apply for Cloud credits during the accelerator; 5) TPU access via program.
findings.detail: Global series of regional accelerator programs (Americas, EMEA, APAC; e.g., AI-focused cohorts). Each cohort is 10–15 startups doing intensive mentorship/training from Google experts; benefits: equity-free support, dedicated mentoring, bootcamps, access to Google Cloud credits applied for during the accelerator (subject to eligibility review), free Cloud TPU access for open-source ML research, Early Access Program/Trusted Tester benefits for Google AI products. Regional variants run in partnership with governments/VCs (e.g., Komdigi Indonesia May 2025: up to $350k credits upon graduation; Singapore 'AI First').
findings.eligibility: Startups demonstrating traction, ideally Seed to Series A, deeply technical (AI/ML strongly preferred in current cohorts), scalable product, commitment from CTO/technical team to required sessions; selection at Google's discretion per regional program. No .edu requirement.
findings.expiry: Cohort-based (e.g., 10–15 weeks / 3 months); credits and TPU access tied to program participation and eligibility review; no standing monthly free tier.
findings.gotchas: Seats are competitive and now effectively AI-focused (2025 cohorts are ~100% AI-native/AI-enabled startups); availability varies by region and year; credits are not automatic — applied for and subject to approval.
findings.name: Google for Startups Accelerators (equity-free, region-specific)

findings.claim: 1) cloud.google.com/edu/faculty → 'Apply for teaching credits'; 2) verify faculty identity/school affiliation; 3) on approval, receive/manage credits in your Cloud Billing account; 4) allocate student credits for classroom use.
findings.detail: Verified faculty can apply for Google Cloud teaching credits: up to $100 in GCP credits per teaching staff member plus up to $50 in GCP credits per student, for hands-on classroom learning. Credits are redeemed and managed in a billing account; guides cover billing management, budgets, group projects pooling student credits. Faculty community (verified faculty) access via school-issued email.
findings.eligibility: Verified faculty/teaching staff at educational institutions; school-issued email address used; students then use their individually allocated credits instead of signing up for the credit-card Free Trial.
findings.expiry: Issued education credits have expiry/renewal governed by the education credits program (re-apply per program cycle); exact credit shelf-life is set in the application/FAQs.
findings.gotchas: Amounts are modest ($100 + $50/student) — designed for learning, not production; faculty must verify before students get credits; Google explicitly advises preventing students from signing up for the $300 Free Trial (which requires a credit card) when they have education credits.
findings.name: Google Cloud for Education — Faculty/teaching credits (up to $100 per teacher, $50 per student)

findings.claim: 1) cloud.google.com/edu/students → 'Request credits' for Google Skills; 2) complete labs/paths to earn badges; 3) optionally join a Developer Student Club or apply to start one; 4) earn Google Cloud Certificates for credentials.
findings.detail: Student offer today is learning-focused, not dollar credits: 200 free Google Skills credits (online labs, skill badges, courses, Google Cloud Certificates) that expire one year after issuance; Google Skills Arcade (gamified challenges, badges, swag); Google Cloud Certificates (shareable digital credentials, no prerequisites); Developer Student Clubs (DSGs) and Cloud OnAir events. There is no general GCP dollar-credit free license for students on these pages — students instead get faculty-allocated credits or the standard $300 trial (which needs a card).
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students/learners; request access to Google Skills; .edu or school affiliation typically used for DSG chapters; no credit card required for the learning credits.
findings.expiry: 200 Skills credits expire 1 year after issuance; program is renewable/re-requestable.
findings.gotchas: If the goal was free GCP dollar credits for students, they don't exist outside faculty-allocated teaching credits (up to $50/student) and the standard $300 Free Trial (credit card required); the student offer has shifted to 'Google Skills' (rebranded Cloud Skills Boost) credits.
findings.name: Google Cloud for Education — Students (200 Google Skills credits, no GCP dollar credits)

findings.claim: 1) cloud.google.com/edu/researchers → 'Apply for your credits'; 2) submit research-credit application (institutional context); 3) for US institutions, engage GPAR benefits (co-investment pricing, early TPU access, on-campus research days).
findings.detail: cloud.google.com/edu/researchers: researchers apply for $5,000 in Google Cloud research credits. GPAR (Google Program for Accelerated Research, via Google Public Sector) adds: co-investment opportunities with industry-leading pricing for AI accelerators (GPUs/TPUs), early access to new-gen TPUs, foundational models and datasets (AlphaFold, Earth AI, agentic AI like Co-scientist), grant-lifecycle AI tooling, compliance support (HIPAA, CMMC 2.0, FedRAMP), and Google/expert access. Noted on the page as currently only available in the United States.
findings.eligibility: Researchers at research institutions (US for GPAR); institutional/academic affiliation; application-based via cloud.google.com/edu/researchers; GPAR accelerator benefits noted as US-only.
findings.expiry: Applied per program cycle; $5,000 credit issuance and validity governed by the program; GPAR benefits note US-only availability as of today.
findings.gotchas: US-only for GPAR; $5,000 is per researcher application, not an org-wide license; heavy HPC/TPU workloads go far beyond $5,000 — co-investment/pricing options are where the real scale is.
findings.name: Google Cloud for Researchers — GPAR research credits ($5,000)

sunset_notes: Corrections/sunsets vs. the 'known so far' baseline, all checked against official Google pages on 2026-10-22: (1) FREE TRIAL DURATION: the $300 credit is valid for 90 days, not 60 — the current docs (docs.cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-cloud-features), signup FAQs, and the archived Jan-30-2025 Free Trial T&Cs all state 90 days/3 months; no 2025–2026 shortening found. (2) CLOUD SQL ALWAYS FREE: the old 'Cloud SQL Always Free plan' (free shared-core instance, 750 h/month, storage/backup/egress allowances in select regions) is NO LONGER on the Cloud SQL pricing page — the only official free Cloud SQL offer today is the 30-day free trial instance (Enterprise Plus, 8 vCPU/64 GB/100 GB) plus the $300 trial credit; treat the 750 h C2D claim as stale. (3) SPANNER FREE 96 GB NODE (us-west1): not present on the current Spanner pricing page; replaced by the 90-day free trial instance (10 GiB, Standard edition + Graph, regional-only) usable by both new and existing customers, with 30-day grace before data deletion. (4) BIGQUERY '100,000 slot-hours/month free': not published on the current BigQuery pricing page (which lists only 1 TiB free on-demand queries + 10 GiB free storage per month, plus free batch loads and first 2 TiB/mo of gRPC Storage Write API) — likely subsumed by the 2023–2024 move to Editions/slots pricing; treat the 100K slot-hour figure as superseded. (5) STARTUP PROGRAM REBRAND: 'Google Cloud Startups Accelerator' (cloud.google.com/startups, previously up to $150k single tier) is now 'Google for Startups Cloud Program' at cloud.google.com/startup — the old /startups URL serves the new program. Current structure: Start $2k tier (founded <2 years, MVP, pre-VC) + Scale (Y1 up to $100k + Y2 up to +$100k = $200k) + Scale AI (Y1 up to $250k + Y2 up to +$100k = $350k), with the $5,000-prior-credits gate and non-venture-funding exclusion for Scale tiers; marketing copy on cloud.google.com/free says 'up to $200,000 USD (up to $350,000 for AI startups)'. (6) EDUCATION: no general free GCP dollar credits for students; student offer is 200 Google Skills credits expiring after 1 year; the substantive education offers are faculty teaching credits ($100/faculty + $50/student) and GPAR research credits ($5,000, US-only). Note: no 2025–2026 sunset announcement changelogs were retrievable (web-search budget was exhausted mid-task), so items 2–4 'no longer listed' reflects absence from the live official pages today rather than a dated official announcement.
label_name: Google Cloud Free Trial + always-free ti

provider: Netlify (Free plan) — Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment

findings.name: Netlify Free plan (credit-based, current default)
findings.detail: $0/month with a hard 300-credit monthly limit. Confirmed on the official pricing page and docs today: 300 credits/mo, 'You'll never be charged for the Free plan', hard limit means no auto-recharge and no credit packs. At current credit rates (bandwidth 20 cr/GB, production deploys 15 cr each, compute 10 cr/GB-hr, web requests 2 cr/10k) this is ~15GB bandwidth OR ~20 production deploys per month. Includes: unlimited deploy previews, Functions + Edge Functions, AI models, Netlify Database, Blob storage, global CDN, custom domains with SSL, 1 concurrent build, 1-day observability/analytics retention. Sign up on the Free plan for a new account (all new accounts default to credit-based plans as of 9 Sep 2025).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (individual audience). No .edu email, no startup age/funding requirement, no referral. Global. No credit card required to sign up or use — the hard credit limit means there is no billing mechanism and no auto-recharge/add-on purchase path on this tier. New accounts can start on Free without payment details.
findings.claim: Sign up at app.netlify.com / netlify.com and select the Free plan, then deploy from Git, AI, or API. No card, no application. Just create an account and push a site.
findings.expiry: Credits reset monthly; the $0 tier is ongoing (no sunset). If a project exceeds 300 credits it pauses until the next billing cycle instead of charging.
findings.gotchas: Credit-based, NOT the legacy 100GB/300-build-minute metered plan — do not compare by bandwidth. Unused credits do not roll over. Only 1 concurrent build and 1-day observability retention. Credits-out = project paused (not billed). AI inference is metered separately ('varies by model') and can burn credits faster than static hosting.

findings.name: Netlify Open Source plan
findings.detail: Free plan for qualifying open-source projects: 10,000 credits/month, free production deploys, deploy previews on every PR, unlimited team members, and sites stay live even if credits run out (extra credits at Pro rates if needed). This is a genuinely free offer distinct from the 300-credit Free tier.
findings.eligibility: Project-based, not student/startup-specific. Requirements: OSI-approved (or Creative Commons with attribution/public-domain) license, a Code of Conduct in the repo, a visible 'This site is powered by Netlify' link/badge, and the project must be non-commercial. Commercial projects excluded. No .edu or funding requirement; open to any qualifying OSS project (docs sites, changelogs, issue trackers, team blogs).
findings.claim: Apply via the Open Source application form (opensource-form.netlify.com, linked from the open-source page/policy). Netlify reviews the repo (license, CoC, activity) and provisions the plan; approval can take days to a week.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; renews monthly. Netlify will downgrade (with notice) if the project no longer meets the criteria or the Netlify link is missing.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial only — even commercial support/hosting disqualifies. Requires the backlink. It applies to the project/repo, not to individual maintainers. (Secondary source corroborates 10,000 cr/mo confirmed against the policy page.)

findings.name: Netlify for Startups (VC-backed program)
findings.detail: Discounted pricing — NOT a free-credit or free-tier offer. Eligible startups receive a discount on Netlify (including AI Gateway and Agent Runners), shared only on approval. It is referral-only: you enter through an accelerator, investor, or partner that works with Netlify.
findings.eligibility: VC-backed portfolio companies of Netlify's approved venture partners. Referral only — apply through that partner (accelerator/investor), not a self-serve form. Not available to bootstrapped/non-VC startups, and not .edu-based.
findings.claim: Ask your VC/accelerator whether they are an approved Netlify partner, then apply through that partner. There is no public self-serve application (the official /startups/ URL currently 404s; details come from a third-party directory).
findings.gotchas: It is a discount, not free hosting/credits — do not list it alongside the free tier as a 'free' offer. Requires VC backing and a partner referral. Official page not retrievable today (404), so terms were read from a third-party directory (last checked 11 Oct 2026); verify directly with your investor before relying on specific numbers.
findings.expiry: Ongoing, shared on approval; no fixed stated expiry.

findings.name: Netlify Creator Program (earn free Pro)
findings.detail: Secondary reward program, not a student/startup free tier: publish educational blog post or video about Netlify (topics: shipping with AI, Netlify platform, everyone-is-a-developer). Reward per published piece: 3 months of Netlify Pro (at $20/mo value) plus Netlify credits/resources at onboarding and a swag pack.
findings.eligibility: Content creators who produce original, ready-to-publish, educational content on Netlify. Not gated on .edu or startup status; new and returning creators welcome. Content must be original and not fully AI-generated.
findings.claim: Fill in the application form on the Creator Program page (topic, format, audience, links to past work). Editorial team reviews; ~3 weeks pitch-to-publication; accept → onboard → create → publish → receive 3 months of Pro.
findings.gotchas: Rewards are per published piece, so recurring but requires new content each time. 3 months of Pro is a time-boxed grant, not a permanent free tier. This is a creator incentive, not a student or startup license.

findings.name: No dedicated student / education license (and no trial credits)
findings.detail: Netlify has no separate education plan, student discount, .edu-verified license, or one-time trial-credit offer. Netlify support staff have repeatedly stated there is no educational plan; students are directed to the self-serve Free plan or the Open Source plan (for open repos). No .edu requirement anywhere — access is via the universal Free plan.
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — no such offer exists.
findings.claim: No claim mechanism; there is nothing to apply for. Students simply use the $0 Free plan (300 cr/mo, no card) or, for open-source coursework repos, the Open Source plan.

sunset_notes: Big 2025-2026 change: the old usage-metered Free/Starter plan (100GB bandwidth, 300 build minutes, 125,000 function invocations, 1M edge invocations, 10GB storage, no card) is now a LEGACY plan. From 4 Sep 2025 all NEW accounts use credit-based plans (Free = 300 cr/mo). Existing legacy accounts keep their old plan but may switch to credit-based (irreversible). So the 'known' free tier was restructured from metered (100GB) to credit-based (300 credits ≈ ~15GB or ~20 deploys). Other timeline: 1 Oct 2025 credit-pack rebalance (Personal 500cr/$5, Pro 1500cr/$10; Pro monthly cut 5000→3000 credits); 17 Apr 2026 Pro = unlimited seats, form submissions made free on all credit plans, meter rates changed (bandwidth 10→20 cr/GB, compute 5→10 cr/GB-hr, web requests 3→2 cr/10k). No student/education program was launched or sunset; one never existed. Startup program is a VC-backed discount (referral-only) and is not a free-credit offer; its official /startups/ page returned 404 today, so specifics come from a third-party directory.

provider: Meilisearch Cloud (search engine; open-source engine is MIT self-hosted)

findings.name: Meilisearch Cloud 14-day free trial
findings.detail: Cloud plan (usage-based or resource-based billing) ships with a 14-day free trial, 'no credit card required' — stated verbatim on the pricing page and reconfirmed in its FAQ ('No credit card required to start'). Sign-up is self-serve at cloud.meilisearch.com/register. No trial-specific caps (docs/searches/instance size) are published; the page only states the trial is included with the Cloud plan. After 14 days a paid plan applies: from ~$20/mo (resource-based XS instance: $18 instance + ~$5 disk, 0.5 vCPU/1GB, 32 GiB) or ~$30/mo (usage-based, covering 100K docs + 50K searches).
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no .edu, no startup criteria, no region limit stated, no credit card at signup (card needed only to keep using it after the trial).
findings.claim: 1. Go to meilisearch.com/pricing (or /cloud). 2. Click 'Start free trial' → cloud.meilisearch.com/register. 3. Create account, provision an instance (usage- or resource-based), use it for up to 14 days. 4. Add a card before expiry to continue.
findings.expiry: Trial lasts 14 days per account; no published data-retention-after-trial-end policy found on the official pages.
findings.gotchas: Trial ≠ free tier: there is no permanent free plan — paid billing (from ~$20/mo) kicks in if you keep the instance. No published trial quotas; over the trial you enter paid usage-based billing for extra searches/docs. Eggress/data costs are folded into the per-plan resource/usage pricing, not separately itemized on the page.

findings.name: Open-source Meilisearch (MIT) self-hosted — free, no usage limits
findings.detail: The Meilisearch engine is open source under the MIT license and the pricing page states self-hosting has 'no usage limits' (no per-document or per-search charge). This is the genuine always-free option for students and startups: host it on any infrastructure (or a cheap VM/container) with no vendor license cost. A separate paid 'self-hosted support agreement' with SLA is available for compliance-driven customers.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (unlimited use); not gated by .edu, funding, age, or region. Only constraint is you run the infrastructure yourself.
findings.claim: 1. Pull the engine (Docker/npm/binary) from GitHub (github.com/meilisearch). 2. Self-host anywhere. No signup, license, or payment. 3. Optionally contact Meilisearch for a paid support agreement if an SLA is needed.
findings.gotchas: Free means you own ops, scaling, and hosting cost — your cloud/VM bill replaces Meilisearch's. No SLA or support by default. Not 'free cloud storage'; docs live wherever you host.

findings.name: No dedicated startup program or education license exists (the /solutions/startup page is marketing only)
findings.detail: The 'Startups' page (/solutions/startup) is a general early-stage-marketing page: no free credits, no fixed discount, no company-age or funding cap, no application/verification flow, no expiry. Its only 'free' hooks are (a) the MIT self-host engine and (b) the standard 14-day Cloud trial. Its FAQ says custom pricing and volume discounts are available 'regardless of company size or funding stage' — i.e., startup deals are via sales, not a public program. No education page exists: candidate URLs (meilisearch.com/solutions/education and /education) return 404; site navigation and the official llms.txt list no education/student page and no .edu-email offer.
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — nothing distinct to claim. Startup deals would be negotiated with sales ('Request a demo'), with no published eligibility (age/funding cap unknown).
findings.claim: Students: use the 14-day Cloud trial or self-host the MIT build (no .edu gate, no license fee). Startups: same as everyone else, or contact sales for custom/volume pricing.
findings.expiry: None published. Re-verify with sales for any negotiated startup discount — it is not a self-serve offer.
findings.gotchas: Do not assume a startup discount exists just because the page exists; there are no verifiable credit amounts or eligibility windows. Any deal comes through sales and may carry custom (not discounted) terms.

sunset_notes: No 2025-2026 sunsets or material changes identified from the official pages read today (2026-10-22): the 14-day, no-credit-card trial and the paid-from-$20/month structure are live and match known-so-far. Caveat: the WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted, so I could not run a 2025-2026 changelog search; I rely on the live official pages (pricing, startup, llms.txt, /cloud) instead. Meilisearch has no education/student license and no public startup credit program at present — if either was ever offered, it is not advertised anywhere on the current site; absence on site ≠ confirmed historical sunset. 'Fronts: Managed Databases & Data Platforms' is a category mismatch: Meilisearch is a search engine, not a managed database.

provider: Weaviate — Weaviate Cloud (managed vector DB + cloud-native AI services: Weaviate Embeddings, Query Agent, Engram)

findings.name: Free Plan ("Always free" managed Weaviate cluster)
findings.detail: Forever $0/mo. Limits verified on the live pricing page 2026-10-22: 1 cluster per user (shared cluster on AWS, 2 regions), 100,000 objects, 1 GB memory, 10 GB disk, 1 collection (up to 3 tenants). Includes hybrid search, vector compression, multi-tenancy, RBAC. Excludes HA/replication, flexible index types, SSO/SAML, backup retention, PrivateLink, encrypted volumes, metrics. Uptime SLA: best effort (no %). Support: basic/email only. Upgrade to paid anytime (Flex from $45/mo, Premium shared from ~$400/mo, dedicated contract) with no migration.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; NO credit card required (page states "No credit card required"); no .edu email or startup requirement; 1 cluster per user; deployment limited to 2 regions (shared AWS cluster)
findings.claim: Click "Start free" at weaviate.io/pricing -> sign up at console.weaviate.cloud (routed via /go/console); quickstart at docs.weaviate.io/cloud/quickstart; no card or approval needed
findings.expiry: None - "Forever $0/mo", "no credit card or time expiration" (per the 2026-06-17 launch post); persists indefinitely as long as the cluster is in use; can upgrade to paid at any time
findings.gotchas: Data transfer is free only for a "promotional period" - footnote says Weaviate may introduce egress charges in the future with advance notice; page defines no hard stop/overage mechanism for the Free plan (implicit path is upgrading to Flex/Premium); shared cluster means no uptime SLA; not suitable for production HA

findings.name: Free AI services on the Free plan: Weaviate Embeddings 2,000 req/day; Query Agent 1,000 req/mo; Engram "Always free"
findings.detail: Free plan AI-service allowances: Weaviate Embeddings 2,000 requests/day; Query Agent 1,000 requests/month (paid plans: "Free to try" 1,000 req/mo, then $30/organization per month with 4,000 req included, then usage-based); Engram (managed agent-memory layer) labeled "Always free" with no itemized quota on the pricing page. Part of the 2026-06-17 rollout making the entire suite free to start. Embedding models otherwise billed by usage at $0.025 / $0.040 / $0.065 per 1M tokens across three model tiers.
findings.eligibility: Same as Free plan: anyone, no credit card, 1 cluster per user; Query Agent/Engram are cloud-only services (not runnable via local Docker)
findings.claim: Same account as Free plan; enable services in the Weaviate Cloud console - no separate enrollment
findings.expiry: Indefinite while on the Free plan; overages on paid plans are usage-based
findings.gotchas: Engram free-tier quota is not specified anywhere on the page; exceeding embedding/Query Agent caps leads to usage-based billing or upgrade on paid plans; "Free to try" on Query Agent for paid tiers is a standing allowance, not a time-boxed trial

findings.name: No trial-credit program (time-limited sandbox sunset, replaced by permanent free tier)
findings.detail: No trial credits, 14/30-day trial, or credit packs exist on the official site as of 2026-10-22. The 2026-06-17 launch post states managed Weaviate Cloud previously offered only "a time-limited sandbox," which was replaced by the permanent free tier ("free as long as it's useful to you" vs "free until the clock runs out").
findings.eligibility: n/a - absence of offer
findings.claim: n/a
findings.expiry: Time-limited sandbox model retired effective 2026-06-17, replaced by the permanent Free plan
findings.gotchas: Absence verified by direct page inspection only (pricing, homepage, blog index pages 1-2, 404 on /startup-program); the shared session web-search budget was exhausted, so third-party/press confirmation of older trial programs was not possible

findings.name: No startup program and no education/student license found
findings.detail: weaviate.io/startup-program returns HTTP 404; homepage, pricing, and blog index (2025-2026 entries visible) contain no startup program, startup credits/grants, or education/academic pricing tier. Closest items: Weaviate Hero Program (weaviate.io/community) - community contribution program rewarding active community members with "Cool Merch, Books & Credits" plus workshops and event access; credits have no stated dollar value, cap, or deadline, and it is contribution-based, not status-based (not aimed at students or startups). Weaviate Academy (academy.weaviate.io) is free learning content (courses/resources), not a license. The Weaviate database is open source and free to self-host on your own infrastructure - the only genuinely unrestricted "education-grade" free path.
findings.eligibility: No .edu requirement or startup age/funding cap exists because no such program exists; Hero Program is open to any community contributor via a Google Form application
findings.claim: No claim path for startup/education offers; Hero Program: apply via "Become a Hero" form (forms.gle/FHwhfPYwCVKkzw5h6)
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Hero Program "credits" are unquantified - do not treat as a free-credit offer; absence findings are limited to the official site (search engine verification unavailable this session); check Weaviate's social channels/blog for any program launched after the visible blog index

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: (1) 2026-06-17: Weaviate sunsetted its time-limited sandbox model for managed Weaviate Cloud and launched the permanent free tier spanning the whole product suite (managed Database + Query Agent + Engram), free without credit card or time expiration (blog: "Weaviate Cloud is now free to start"). (2) Price-book revision effective 1 September 2026 (noted on the pricing page): RQ-4 compression added as its own rate tier between RQ-1 and RQ-8, and backup rates restructured to a common base with regional adjustments - affects paid Flex/Premium plans only, Free plan unchanged. (3) Data transfer is free on all plans only for a "promotional period"; Weaviate reserves the right to charge for egress in the future with advance notice. No evidence was found of any sunset of a startup program or education license (none appear to exist; /startup-program is a 404). Caveat: verification was done by fetching official pages directly on 2026-10-22 (weaviate.io/pricing, /blog, /blog/page/2, /blog/weaviate-free-tier, /community, homepage; docs subpages now 404 - docs moved to docs.weaviate.io/cloud/quickstart); the session's web-search budget was exhausted, so third-party/press corroboration and deeper blog archive pages were not checked.

findings.claim: Sign up at redis.io/cloud (Google/GitHub login or form + email activation), then in the Redis Cloud console: 'New database' -> select the 'Try 30 MB for free' subscription option -> pick database name/version, cloud vendor (AWS/GCP/Azure) and region -> 'Create database'. CTA on the pricing page: /try-free/?rcplan=0.
findings.detail: Permanently free managed Redis Cloud database: 1 database, 30 MB memory, shared cloud deployment, 30 concurrent connections, best-effort SLA, community support. No time limit, no credit card required. Free plan is a type of Essentials plan; no replication/auto-failover and no REST API on the free tier; upgrade to paid Essentials is seamless with no data loss. (Third-party trackers add ~100 ops/sec ceiling and ~5 GB monthly bandwidth allowance to the free plan - not stated on the official pages read today.)
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Redis Cloud account. No .edu requirement, no company, no credit card. Region limits: only in cloud regions Redis Cloud supports per vendor; region+cloud fixed at subscription creation. Only one free database per account - delete the old one or upgrade to paid before creating another.
findings.expiry: No expiry - always free while the plan exists; no renewal needed. Third-party (Layerbase, 2026-08) notes the agreement permits data deletion after ~14 days of inactivity. No SLA compensation on the shared deployment (best-effort).
findings.gotchas: 30 MB is rarely the binding constraint: 30 concurrent connections and ~100 ops/sec are hit first. No REST API, no high availability on the free tier. No card needed for the free tier, but upgrading to paid requires a payment method + business address. No replication/failover - treat data as disposable. Third-party trackers report the free plan allows only 100 ops/sec and ~5 GB monthly bandwidth.
findings.name: Free Redis Cloud Essentials (always-free 30 MB tier)

findings.claim: From redis.io/pricing select the Pro plan 'Try for free' CTA (/try-free/?rcplan=plan3), sign in, add a credit card, create a Pro subscription; the first $200 of usage is covered. No separate application or form.
findings.detail: On the official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22), the Pro plan (dedicated infrastructure, unlimited RAM, multi-DB, Active-Active multi-region, from $0.014/hr with a $200/month minimum) advertises 'First $200 free' - the first $200 of usage is complimentary before the hourly minimum kicks in. Effectively up to ~$200 of free Pro usage. This is a trial/credit on a paid plan, NOT a permanent free tier.
findings.eligibility: Any Redis Cloud account; no .edu/startup status stated on the pricing page. It is a paid plan with a usage credit, so a credit card/payment method and business address are required (card-backed billing account).
findings.expiry: The $200 credit is consumed as usage accrues; no credit expiry date is stated on the pricing page. Not renewable; billing resumes at the $200/month minimum (or hourly usage) afterwards unless the subscription is deleted. How long the 'free' window lasts depends on how fast $200 of usage is consumed.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: card required, charges begin after the $200 credit is exhausted - delete or manage the subscription promptly. Pro annual-plan variants differ (AWS/GCP only for annual). Throughput/egress limits still apply on the paid tier. 'First $200 free' is the only free-credit offer for general users found on official pages.
findings.name: Pro plan 'First $200 free' (free-usage credit on paid Pro plan)

findings.claim: When live: apply via the form on redis.io/startups/ ('Apply here'), sign in with a company email, fill company details/website/funding stage/Redis use case, await approval (typically days to ~2 weeks), then activate credits/promo code in the Redis Cloud console. NOTE: as of 2026-10-22 the English program page no longer serves the program (see sunset_notes) - this path is only valid if Redis re-enables the form.
findings.detail: Redis ran a startup program: 'Free Redis for 6 months - usage limits apply' plus early access to new features, dedicated support with monthly office hours, access to the applied-AI team, co-marketing opportunities, and VC/customer intros. Third-party trackers value it at up to $10,000 in Redis Cloud credits (some listings say up to $25K via Google for Startups perks) with 6-12 months free access and usage limits. Credits apply to Redis Cloud usage; monitor balance/expiration in the console.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups: pre-seed/seed/Series A, privately held, commonly cited funding cap ~$5M total raised, active company website, building real-time/AI workloads with Redis. No VC backing strictly required; approval at Redis's discretion; global. No .edu requirement; not an education offer.
findings.expiry: When live: free period advertised as 6 months (older localized pages said 12 months); credits valid ~12 months. Inactive companies risk removal. Program currently unreachable - see sunset_notes.
findings.gotchas: Credit amounts ($10K vs $25K) come from third-party trackers, not a page readable today. 'Usage limits apply' means even the free months are metered. Access was discretionary. Do not plan around this offer without Redis confirming current availability - the English page now redirects to the homepage.
findings.name: Redis for Startups program (free Redis Cloud for qualifying startups)

provider: Redis Inc. - Redis Cloud (managed-db), fronts: Managed Databases & Data Platforms
sunset_notes: 1) Redis for Startups (redis.io/startups/): as of 2026-10-22 the English page serves the Redis homepage instead of the program. Two independent trackers confirm the removal (CreditBase 2026-10-02: "redis.io/startups redirects to the Redis home page... needs a check"; StartupPerks 2026-10: "Redis removed the English page in 2026; program page live in German/Spanish/French/Italian/Korean" per its last check, with 'Redis kostenlos fur 6 Monate'). The program was live as of June 2025 ("Free Redis for 6 months"). Treat as sunset/uncertain on the English site; no application form reachable today. 2) Education: no official Redis education license or .edu student program exists - redis.io/education/ is a 404, and nothing on the pricing/docs pages references an education offer; students simply use the always-free 30 MB tier. 3) Essentials restructure December 2025 (per third-party Layerbase/Upstash, not on official pages read today): Essentials is now published as 250 MB-12 GB RAM-only tiers plus "Redis Flex" SSD+RAM tiers up to 100 GB; the free 30 MB tier's shape (30 MB / 30 connections / single shared DB) was unchanged. 4) Free-plan inactivity: the agreement permits deletion of inactive free databases (~14 days per third-party), so "forever free" does not mean "forever data retention". 5) No general free-trial-credit scheme beyond the "first $200 free" on Pro (credit-card required) was found on official pages. Caveat: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-task; redis.io facts above come from pages fetched today (pricing, docs) plus third-party trackers, cited per finding.

findings.name: Hobby plan (permanently free, no card)
findings.detail: $0/mo. Per official pricing page fetched 2026-10-22: 100 GB fast data transfer, 1M CDN requests, 1M function invocations, 4 hrs Fluid Active CPU, 360 GB-hrs Fluid Provisioned Memory, 1 GB blob storage, 5K image transformations/mo, unlimited deployments, 1 developer seat. Per /docs/limits (last updated 2026-09-16): 200 projects, 100 deployments/day, 25 projects per Git repo, 1 concurrent build, 45-min max build time, 32 GB disk, 120s proxied-request timeout. Fair-use doc adds Hobby includes first 10 GB fast origin transfer, image cache reads 300K/writes 100K per mo. Hobby is a hard cap: you cannot purchase extra usage; exceeding limits pauses/degrades the team. Hobby is restricted to non-commercial personal use only.
findings.eligibility: Any individual account; .edu not required; no credit card or payment method required to sign up or use Hobby; no region limits documented (ToS sanctions restrictions apply as usual). Limited to 1 developer seat; teams/commercial use require Pro.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up free at vercel.com (email/GitHub/Google) - no card. 2) Hobby plan is the default team plan. 3) Deploy via CLI or import a Git repo; usage accrues against monthly allotments.
findings.expiry: Never expires; allotments reset monthly. No renewal needed. Paused if caps hit; commercial use on Hobby is a ToS violation that can get the account actioned.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial only: any ad revenue, payments, ads, affiliate purpose = commercial and requires Pro. No overage billing on Hobby - you get paused, not billed. 200-project and 100-deploys/day caps. 'Unlimited deploys' on the pricing page coexists with the 100/day general limit. Free Vercel Remote Cache also applies.

findings.name: Pro trial: 14 days with $20 credit (one per user)
findings.detail: 14-day Pro trial including a $20 usage credit and trial limits: up to 10 team members, 200 projects, 16 CPU-hrs Active CPU, 1,440 GB-hrs Provisioned Memory, 1M function invocations/mo, 10K image transformations/mo, 50 domains per project. No payment method is required to run the trial; if you add one, billing starts immediately after the trial. Excluded from trial: Drains, account webhooks, free first-year domain, sandbox failover regions. Trial pauses when any of Active CPU / Provisioned Memory / invocations hits 100%; ends at 14 days or limit hit, whichever first, then reverts to Hobby.
findings.eligibility: Any user account; exactly one Pro trial per user account (cannot repeat or transfer). No card, no student or startup status required.
findings.claim: Dashboard -> team switcher -> Create Team -> name team -> select 'Pro Trial'. To continue on Pro, add a payment method at Settings > Billing before trial end; otherwise it auto-reverts to Hobby.
findings.expiry: 14 days from start, or earlier when trial usage limits are reached. Post-trial: upgrade to paid Pro ($20/mo base seat) or automatic revert to Hobby limits.
findings.gotchas: Owners cannot be changed during trial; charges apply only if a payment method exists; free first-year custom domain (a Pro benefit) is explicitly excluded from the trial; downgrading removes all team members.

findings.name: Vercel for Startups: up to $30,000 Flexible Commitment + Enterprise tier for a year
findings.detail: Enterprise-grade contract with a Flexible Commitment Amount up to $30,000 usable across seats, data transfer, compute, AI Gateway, v0, Eve, Workflows, Sandboxes and the rest of the platform; account runs on Enterprise T&C for 1 year or until the amount is consumed. Since Aug 6, 2026 acceptances the amount is partner-determined (varies between partners, max $30,000). Per-month sub-cap: max 50% of each month's credit may go to Vercel AI Gateway usage; excess is billed at list rates even with unused credit. Extras: Vercel Team Slack, demo days/hackathons, marketing features, swag.
findings.eligibility: Startup must be affiliated with an approved Vercel Startups Partner (VC/accelerator network) with proof (screenshot of partner dashboard/hub/wiki/console); Series A or less raised; must apply within 12 months of the most recent funding round; company website with matching email; must not have previously received Vercel startup credits. Bootstrapped startups without a partner affiliation do not qualify.
findings.claim: 1) vercel.com/startups/credits -> fill application (email, select/create team, choose partner, upload partner proof, country). 2) Accept Flexible Commitment terms. 3) Add a valid payment method (required for activation). 4) Credits and Enterprise access go live 5-7 business days after acceptance.
findings.expiry: 1 calendar year from when the Flexible Commitment is applied; unused amount does not roll over. If consumed early, account auto-moves to standard ToS at list rates; benefits cannot be postponed; one-time only.
findings.gotchas: Credit card/payment method IS required (unlike Hobby). Vercel can revoke credits for abuse. Partner-dependent amounts - often far less than $30K (some partner deals, e.g. Paralect Kickstart, provide ~$2,400). The AI Gateway 50% cap binds AI-heavy apps. Credits are the 'discount' mechanism - overage is billed at standard rates, so it is not free hosting, it is subsidized paid hosting.

findings.name: Vercel AI Accelerator: cohort credits (40 AI startups, $8M+ pools)
findings.detail: 6-week cohort of 40 early-stage AI teams; per current official page: 'Over $8M in credits' from Vercel, v0, AWS and partner AI platforms. Per-participant pools listed on the page include: Vercel $30k/participant ($12k winner), v0 $5.4k/participant ($1k winner), AWS $25k/participant, Anthropic $15k/participant, OpenAI $2.5k/participant ($10k winner), plus dozens of sponsor pools (Modal, ElevenLabs, Supabase, Neon, Auth0, etc.); finalists earn $100K+ in additional credit prizes per program blogs. Also weekly fireside chats/workshops, private AI-builder community, and SF demo day with investors.
findings.eligibility: Selection-based, early-stage AI startups; application via external Typeform; no eligibility criteria published on the page. Cohorts capped at 40 teams - not an open offer.
findings.claim: Apply at vercel.com/ai-accelerator ('Apply now' -> Typeform). Most recent cohort: applications closed Feb 16, 2026 for a 6-week program; new windows announced via blog.
findings.expiry: Credits are distributed within the cohort (6-week program); per-platform credit terms govern each pool; winner prizes at demo day.
findings.gotchas: Competitive and intermittent, not a standing program. Pool sizes vary by year: $4M+ (May 2025 cohort) -> $6M+ (Feb 2026 cohort) -> $8M+ on the current page. Payment-method requirement not stated on the page.

findings.name: v0 for Students: 1 year of free v0 access at 15 active schools
findings.detail: Program launched ~Oct 2025. Official page (fetched 2026-10-22) grants '1 year of complimentary v0 access' to enrolled students at the 15 active schools: Stanford, Harvard, Princeton, UC Berkeley, MIT, San Francisco State, Arizona State, Georgia Tech, University of Waterloo, NYU, Grand Canyon, Northwestern, University of Washington, Cornell, USC ('more coming soon'). The exact tier/credit is NOT published on the official page; the launch post advertised '1 year of free v0 premium' - note v0 no longer sells a 'Premium' tier, it now has Free / Plus ($30/user/mo, shown discounted from $90, incl. $30 monthly credits) / Business ($100/user/mo). For reference, v0's regular Free plan: $0, 7 messages/day, $5 one-time credit for new users.
findings.eligibility: Must be enrolled at one of the 15 active schools; sign-in is via school email and the verification form requires a .edu domain (reported verbatim: 'Email must be from a .edu domain'), which excludes non-US institutions on the list (e.g., University of Waterloo). No manual verification path; other schools join a waitlist.
findings.claim: 1) Go to v0.app/students. 2) 'Join with student email' with a school email. 3) Verify via confirmation link. 4) Free student access for 1 year. If school not listed, join the waitlist.
findings.expiry: 1 year from verification. Renewal/re-verification terms are not published.
findings.gotchas: What students actually get (tier/credit level) is unpublished - reports say some only get free-tier-equivalent credits. .edu-only means most international and even some non-US schools are excluded. The program covers v0 (Vercel's AI app builder), not Vercel hosting plans - it is not a discount on Vercel Pro/Hobby.

findings.name: No Vercel education license or student/nonprofit discount exists (for core Vercel hosting)
findings.detail: Vercel has no .edu discount, education license, or nonprofit discount for its core platform - Vercel support/community staff stated in Oct 2025 ('we don't have a discount specifically for students at the moment') and reiterated Jan 2026 ('Vercel doesn't offer student or non-profit discounts. All services must be paid at full price'). The only education-adjacent offers are: the v0 for Students program above, and Vercel Academy (vercel.com/academy) which is free self-paced courses/workshops only, with no hosting credits or plan discount.
findings.eligibility: n/a - absence of offer. Students get the same Hobby (free) plan as everyone else, subject to the non-commercial-use restriction.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; use Hobby free plan or v0 for Students (15 schools).
findings.expiry: n/a.
findings.gotchas: Assume there is no .edu path to free Pro; any non-.edu or non-listed-school request is told to join the waitlist. Commercial work (e.g., a client project) cannot run on Hobby even for students.

findings.name: Vercel Open Source Program (adjacent, not student/startup-specific)
findings.detail: Periodically reopens applications for maintainers of active open source projects, granting free Pro-level access/support for the project (a Vercel staffer said in Oct 2025 'applications for the Open Source Program will open again soon'; a third-party directory lists it as '$3,600 in credits over 12 months' - that dollar figure is not confirmed on any official page I could fetch and the program page sits behind a login wall). A startup that maintains an active OSS project can claim it even if it doesn't qualify for Vercel for Startups.
findings.eligibility: Active open source project; application-only (no open application window on the public page; per community/directory the next window was expected ~April 2026). Not tied to .edu or startup status.
findings.claim: Watch vercel.com/open-source (behind login) / Vercel community announcements for the application window, then apply per instructions.
findings.expiry: Granted for a 12-month period per the (unverified) third-party listing; program runs in recurring windows.
findings.gotchas: Amounts/tier officially unpublished; treat the $3,600 figure as unverified; window closes periodically.

sunset_notes: No free offer was sunset in 2025-2026, but several materially changed: (1) Pro plan was restructured in 2025 ('Simpler Pricing' / Fluid compute era): it now carries a $20 included usage credit and plan limits are expressed in Fluid Active CPU hours / Provisioned Memory GB-hrs rather than old per-function allowances; Hobby's core limits (100 GB transfer, 1M CDN requests, 1M function invocations, 4 CPU-hrs, 360 GB-hrs memory, 200 projects) are unchanged from previously known values as verified on the official pages today. (2) Vercel for Startups: new 'Flexible Commitment' credit terms apply to startups accepted on/after August 6, 2026 - the credit amount became partner-negotiated (up to a $30,000 max) rather than a fixed amount, with a 50%-of-monthly-credit cap on AI Gateway usage. (3) v0 plan lineup was rebranded - the '$20 Premium' plan referenced by older student-program marketing no longer exists; v0 is now Free / Plus ($30/user/mo, $30 monthly credits) / Business ($100/user/mo), so the exact value of the 1-year free v0 for Students offer is unpublished. (4) AI Accelerator credit pools scaled up between cohorts: $4M+ (2025) -> $6M+ (Feb 2026 cohort, apps due 2026-02-16) -> $8M+ on the current page. (5) v0 for Students launched Oct 2025 with 5 schools (Stanford, Harvard, MIT, Princeton, UC Berkeley) and has since expanded to 15; the .edu-only verification has not been loosened as of Jan 2026. (6) Vercel Remote Cache became free (changelog item, 2025-2026 era), adding to the Hobby free offering.

findings.claim: Create a Render account (no card), click New > Web Service (or Static Site/Postgres/Key Value), choose the 'Free' compute plan, deploy. Free web services: spins down after 15 min of idle (HTTP+WebSocket) and takes ~1 min to wake; all 750 hours shared across every free web service in the workspace; hours reset monthly with no rollover; exhaustion suspends all free web services until next month.
findings.detail: Free web service instance: $0/mo, 512 MB RAM (pricing table lists Free as '$0/month, 512 MB RAM, plan id free'; CPU share not stated on pricing page, third-party trackers cite 0.1 vCPU). 750 free instance hours per workspace per calendar month, shared by all free web services; spun-down services do not consume hours. Features kept: custom domains, managed TLS, service previews, log streams, rollbacks to 2 most recent deploys. Limits: single instance, no persistent disk, no SSH, no autoscaling, no one-off jobs, no reserved ports 18012/18013/19099, no private-network inbound traffic; outbound SMTP ports 25/465/587 blocked since 2025-09-26; local filesystem wiped on spin-down/restart/redeploy; Render may restart or suspend a free service 'at any time'.
findings.eligibility: Any new Render account; no credit card, .edu email, or region requirement stated; region chosen at creation (US/Europe/Asia).
findings.expiry: Perpetual; 750 hours reset on the 1st of each calendar month, unused hours do not roll over.
findings.gotchas: Official docs: 'Do not use them for production applications.' Free web services and static sites count against the Hobby workspace's 5 GB included bandwidth and 500 included pipeline minutes; exceeding them with no payment method on file suspends all Free services for the rest of the month (new builds disabled for pipeline minutes). A pinger defeats the point: keeping one service awake ~744/750 hours a month.
findings.name: Free web services (Free tier)

findings.claim: New > Postgres, choose the Free compute plan. One per workspace (individual and team accounts).
findings.detail: One free Render Postgres database per workspace: 256 MB RAM, 1 GB SSD storage, 100 connections. No backups of any kind, no managed connection pooling. Expires 30 days after creation, then a 14-day grace period; afterwards Render deletes the database and all its data. After expiry you may create a new free database. Paid upgrade starts at $6/mo (0.1c-256mb).
findings.eligibility: Any account; no credit card required; no .edu requirement.
findings.expiry: 30 days from creation + 14-day grace period, then data deleted.
findings.gotchas: Despite being called 'free', this is effectively a 30-day trial: it is the only free datastore with a hard expiry. Since 2024-05-20 the expiry was cut from 90 to 30 days. No backups means the 14-day grace period is the only recovery window; export data before day 30.
findings.name: Free Postgres database

findings.claim: New > Key Value, choose the Free plan.
findings.detail: One free Key Value (Redis-compatible) instance per workspace: 25 MB in-memory, ~50 simultaneous connections. In-memory only — data is lost on every restart and also when the instance is upgraded to a paid plan. No continuous on-disk persistence.
findings.eligibility: Any account; no credit card required.
findings.expiry: Perpetual as long as the instance exists; data itself is never durably stored.
findings.gotchas: Useful only for cache/queue experiments, not durable state; a restart silently wipes keys. 2026-10-01: Render added two new paid Key Value plans (3 GB up to 3,000 connections; 50 GB up to 50,000 connections) and lowered prices on 1 GB+ plans — free tier unchanged.
findings.name: Free Key Value instance

findings.claim: New > Static Site, deploy from Git; no compute plan selection needed.
findings.detail: Static sites are free to deploy on Render (HTTPS, global CDN). They count against the workspace's monthly included outbound bandwidth (5 GB on Hobby) and build pipeline minutes (500/mo on Hobby).
findings.eligibility: Any account; no credit card required.
findings.expiry: Perpetual; usage limits reset monthly.
findings.gotchas: Bandwidth overage: $0.15/GB if a payment method is on file; otherwise services are suspended for the remainder of the month. Note the 2026 Hobby bandwidth cut (100 GB -> 5 GB) applies to static-site egress too.
findings.name: Free static sites

findings.claim: Nothing to claim — every new Render account starts on the $0 Hobby plan automatically.
findings.detail: Hobby workspace plan: $0/mo + usage-based compute/storage. Included: 5 GB outbound bandwidth (then $0.15/GB), 500 build pipeline minutes/month (then $5 per additional 1,000), up to 25 services (all types incl. suspended), 2 custom domains (then $0.25/domain/month), 1 team member. Pro is $25/mo flat (seat fees removed, unlimited members/services, 25 GB bandwidth, 1,000 pipeline minutes). Scale $499/mo. If a Pro/Scale workspace has no services and no activity, the subscription fee is waived for that month.
findings.eligibility: Any account; no credit card required to use the Hobby plan; egress/build-minute overages require a payment method or free services are suspended.
findings.expiry: Perpetual; usage quotas reset monthly. New workspaces got the new plans on 2026-04-23; existing workspaces auto-migrated on 2026-08-01.
findings.gotchas: The 2026 restructure narrowed the free offer: Hobby bandwidth went from 100 GB to 5 GB/month and services are capped at 25 (legacy Hobby was unlimited). Free-instance specs themselves were unchanged. Egress billing widened in 2025-08 to service-initiated outbound, WebSocket responses and Private Link traffic.
findings.name: Hobby workspace plan ($0/mo + usage)

findings.claim: Create a Render account (Step 1 'Start'), complete the short application on the startups page referencing your Render instance (Step 2 'Apply'); on approval credits are applied to the account (Step 3 'Launch'). Build/Scale/AI tiers: apply through your enrolled accelerator/VC's partner link. Contact: startup-program@render.com.
findings.detail: Render startup credits, valid 12 months from approval. Tiers: Prototype — $500, open to any qualifying new customer; Build — $2,500 (majority of partner programs) up to $5,000 (select partners, e.g. Aurelia Ventures' $5K program); Scale — $10,000 (startups with < $1M funding) or $25,000 ($1M+ funding) with top-tier VC funding; AI — $100,000 (AI-native/data-heavy products) plus 1:1 onboarding, 1-year dedicated support Slack, co-marketing. Perks: startup-specific onboarding resources and exclusive startup events on partner tiers.
findings.eligibility: New Render customer; Series A or earlier; less than $50M raised total; company < 4 years in operation (< 5 years for Scale tier). Prototype: minimum $25K seed funding. Build/Scale/AI: must apply through an enrolled partner accelerator/VC; AI additionally requires at least $2.5M funding from an enrolled top-tier VC. No .edu or student path; no equity ask stated; geography global.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months from time of approval.
findings.gotchas: This is a funded-startup program, not a student offer — the free tier is Render's student path. Not open to existing Render customers. The /startups page is JS-rendered; the tier figures above were read from the live official page via the search index today and corroborated by partner pages (Aurelia $5K; COMPOUND, builtfirst marketplace 'up to $100,000'). Verify exact tier numbers on the live page before applying.
findings.name: Render Startup Program credits (Prototype/Build/Scale/AI)

findings.claim: Not claimable through Render directly — credits are granted by the event organizer at registration (e.g., Atria Summer of Code Hack Days, hacks.osatria.in).
findings.detail: Event-specific, not a standing program. Render is the official deployment partner for Hack Days by Atria Summer of Code (announced 2026-06-04): $50 in Render platform credits to every participant plus additional credits for winning teams, with OSCode (MLH network) as a partner. Render's startup-program page also says it partners with 'accelerators, incubators, educational institutions, and startup programs to help students and founders' — such partner programs can surface credits for students at events, but there is no standing education license.
findings.eligibility: Students via event organizers (hackathon registration); no .edu email requirement stated for the credits themselves; availability tied to specific 2026 events.
findings.expiry: Event-specific; not a recurring offer.
findings.gotchas: Do not expect these to recur or generalize; check the specific event's page. No .edu pricing, student discount, or academic license exists anywhere on Render's site (no education link in navigation).
findings.name: Hackathon/education partner credits (event-specific)

provider: Render (Free web services — Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment)
sunset_notes: No Render free offer was fully sunset in 2025-2026, but several were materially narrowed: (1) 2026-04-23 'Better pricing for fast-growing teams' (auto-migration completed 2026-08-01): Hobby bandwidth cut from 100 GB to 5 GB included/mo, overage now $0.15/GB, Hobby capped at 25 services (was unlimited) and 2 team-member environments became unlimited projects x 2 environments; Pro moved from $19/member to $25 flat; free-instance specs (512 MB web / 256 MB Postgres / 25 MB KV / 750 hours) were explicitly unchanged. (2) 2025-09-26: free web services block outbound SMTP ports 25/465/587 (changelog 2025-09-16). (3) 2025-08-01: bandwidth pricing halved ($30 -> $15 per 100 GB, now per-GB) and egress billing expanded to service-initiated outbound, WebSocket responses and Private Link traffic (changelog 2025-07-01). (4) 2026-02-24: free web services now stay awake while receiving WebSocket messages (previously only HTTP prevented spin-down). (5) Context: free Postgres expiry was cut from 90 to 30 days on 2024-05-20. Education: Render has never offered a standing student/education license or .edu pricing; the only student-facing free offers are the general free tier plus event-specific hackathon credits (e.g., Atria Summer of Code Hack Days, June 2026, $50/participant). Related but not student/startup: Render also advertises 'up to $10K migration credits' for production infrastructure migrations. Known-so-far claims verified: 750 instance-hours/mo, 512 MB free web instance, 30-day free Postgres expiry, no-card signup — all confirmed on the official pages today.

provider: Databricks Lakebase (serverless Postgres, ex-Neon Postgres product family) — Databricks Data + AI Platform

findings.name: Databricks Free Edition (perpetual, no-credit-card, student/hobbyist tier)
findings.detail: Perpetually free 'limited Databricks account with no expiration for personal use'. Exactly 1 serverless workspace, no access to classic compute, 'limited compute size and usage' with daily fair-use limits (no exact DBU/storage numbers published on the page; a doc link 'community-edition-limitations' exists but is not rendered publicly with figures). Sign up with a personal email; no credit card or payment required. Free access to the unified Data + AI platform: notebooks, dashboards/Genie, agents, scheduled data workflows, plus free self-paced Databricks Academy training. FAQ: 'Free Edition is built for students, hobbyists, and aspiring data and AI professionals... not for production or commercial use.'
