'Get Free Edition' routes to /signup/free-edition (provider=DB_FREE_TIER).
findings.eligibility: Any personal email (no .edu verification, no enrollment proof). Personal use only — commercial use explicitly barred. Region: all supported Databricks cloud regions; tier is account-level.
findings.claim: 1) Go to databricks.com/learn/free-edition (or /signup/free-edition). 2) Sign up with a personal email. 3) You get one serverless workspace instantly; no cloud provider account or card needed. Databricks Academy courses are free at customer-academy.databricks.com using the 'Customer and Prospects' sign-up.
findings.expiry: No expiration ('perpetually free'). Daily usage limits apply. Legacy Community Edition accounts: 'access will continue to be available for the remainder of this year' (2026) — the older CE tier is being wound down in favor of Free Edition.
findings.gotchas: Lakebase is LOCKED in Free Edition — the trial-page comparison lists 'Locked features (no GPUs, clean rooms, Lakebase, enterprise admin etc.)'. So the free tier does NOT include the Postgres product. Also: no production/commercial use, one workspace, no classic compute, fair-use daily caps with no published quota, no support SLA.

findings.name: 14-day free trial with up to $400 in usage credits (includes Lakebase 'try for free')
findings.detail: 'Full Databricks platform access for two (2) weeks used for business evaluation', 'up to $400 in free usage' credits, 'No credit card is required to start your Databricks free trial'. Express signup (email only, immediate serverless workspace) or AWS Marketplace signup (serverless + optional classic workspace in your own account). Docs confirm credits are 'valid for 14 days after you start your trial', non-transferable, trial ends when credits are exhausted, then the account 'switches to a pay-as-you-go model' (payment method: card, Marketplace, or commit contract). Personal-email trials are capped: max one SQL warehouse per workspace at 50 DBU/hr, serverless notebooks/jobs/Lakeflow capped at 50 DBU/hr, CPU only (no GPUs), one AI Search endpoint capped at 1 search unit. Lakebase: its pricing page states 'Pay as you go with a 14-day free trial' — i.e., Lakebase Postgres is reachable during the standard 14-day trial; the Lakebase product page's 'Try for free' CTA routes to the same signup. Lakebase create-flow: New project in workspace region (12 AWS regions listed), production branch, scale-to-zero enabled by default with a 24-hour inactivity timeout.
findings.eligibility: Work email 'recommended for full trial benefits' (business trials are unrestricted evaluation; personal email gets the 50-DBU/hr caps). No age/funding rules; no published per-person cap or region restriction on the trial itself, but Lakebase availability is limited to supported regions (12 AWS regions incl. us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-central-1, ap-northeast-1; Azure Premium = AWS/GCP Enterprise tier; 'displayed pricing does not guarantee product availability in that region').
findings.claim: 1) databricks.com/free-trial -> 'Try Databricks' (/signup/express) with an email; or AWS Marketplace signup with existing AWS account. 2) Create a Lakebase project from the Lakebase Postgres app in your workspace (Autoscaling -> New project). 3) Connect with psql/PG drivers via OAuth (postgresql://user@databricks.com@ep-....databricks.com). 4) Upgrade before day 14 to keep remaining credits (they survive an upgrade).
findings.expiry: 14 days, no renewal of the same trial; credits expire with the trial unless upgraded to paid. After the trial, a payment method is required to continue.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: this is an evaluation trial, not a perpetual tier — Lakebase's only 'free' on-ramp is this trial; it is NOT available in the perpetual Free Edition. $400 is 'up to', not guaranteed; after expiry you're on pay-as-you-go with storage quotas (per-branch, adjustable on request) and possible egress/transfer costs (no public free egress allowance found). Credits cannot be combined with promotions or negotiated terms.

findings.name: Databricks Startup Program: up to $200K in credits for Databricks and Neon
findings.detail: Official startup page: qualifying startups receive 'up to $200K in credits for Databricks and Neon' (Neon = the serverless Postgres product behind Lakebase). Credits cover the Databricks Data + AI Platform incl. 'Database – Postgres for data apps and AI agents' (Lakebase) plus four 'solution accelerators' (recommendations, onboarding, LLM search, time-series forecasting with GenAI). No credit window, per-product split, or age/funding caps are published on the page.
findings.eligibility: Startups 'not founded... ' — no published eligibility criteria on the official page: no stated company age, funding-raised cap, revenue limit, or region. Two paths: apply directly (Google Sites form at sites.google.com/databricks.com/startup-program-apply; form fields not publicly readable), or be nominated by an investor — listed VC partners: Andreessen Horowitz, Battery, General Catalyst, Insight Partners, Menlo Ventures, NEA, among others.
findings.claim: 1) Apply via the 'Apply now' form (Google Sites) with company details, OR 2) ask a partner VC to nominate you into the program. No public review-timeline; no published cap on number of credits beyond 'up to $200K'.
findings.expiry: Not published (no credit-usage window or program end date on the page; footer copyright 2026, content dated 2026-04).
findings.gotchas: Amount is a ceiling ('up to'), not a guarantee; exact allocation and duration are decided per-approval. The $200K spans two product families (Databricks + Neon) — split undisclosed. Eligibility caps are hidden in the application form. Startup credits don't replace the pay-as-you-go base: unused commitment after credit exhaustion bills normally.

findings.name: University Alliance / education program (educators + students)
findings.detail: For educators: 'perpetually free Databricks experience for learning and experimentation' (Free Edition), dedicated online community, dedicated educator/student badges, free teaching resources and sample notebooks ('Get free resources' -> /resources/teach; 'Access Free Edition' -> /learn/free-edition). For students (via /resources/student-resources and /university/student-fellows): free Free Edition access, free self-paced Databricks Academy courses, University Alliance Student badge (LinkedIn-ready), and students who complete a course 'qualify for a 25% discount on Databricks certifications' (exam fee, not platform credits). Student Fellows sub-program: by invitation only ('invited for their exceptional contributions'), grants free Free Edition access plus 'free or discounted' certification vouchers, on-campus communities, and internship pipeline; application via Airtable form with a T&C PDF; no stipend or credit hours stated.
findings.eligibility: No .edu email requirement or enrollment verification is stated on any page. Free Edition portion: personal email, personal use only, any region with the tier. University Alliance: faculty/educators invited via the program; Student Fellows: invitation-only, no published geography or funding limits.
findings.claim: Students: 1) sign up for Free Edition (provider=DB_FREE_TIER). 2) take free Academy courses at customer-academy.databricks.com ('Customer and Prospects' login). 3) earn the badge after finishing a course; claim the 25% certification discount after course completion. Fellows: apply through the Airtable form linked from /university/student-fellows. Educators: use 'Access Free Edition' / 'Get free resources' on /university.
findings.expiry: Perpetual for Free Edition and badges; no expiry stated for the 25% certification discount or Fellows vouchers. No renewal needed.
findings.gotchas: This is NOT a platform-credit grant: the education offer is Free Edition access (which locks Lakebase out) + free training + a 25% exam-fee discount, so students get no money-credits and no Lakebase under this program. .edu email is not verified, so anyone can use it; Fellows details (term, counts, countries) live only in the T&C PDF. Free Edition caps: 1 serverless workspace, fair-use daily limits, personal use only.

sunset_notes: Community Edition sunset/rebrand (2025-2026): Databricks' legacy 'Community Edition' (the free, Spark-learning tier) has been replaced by the expanded 'Free Edition' — 'designed and extended to include full access to the Data + AI Platform'; the Free Edition page states 'Access to legacy CE accounts will continue to be available for the remainder of this year' (page footer © 2026), i.e., legacy CE is being sunset by end of 2026 and users are steered to Free Edition. Startup program now explicitly bundles Neon credits ('up to $200K in credits for Databricks and Neon') on the 2026 page — older program versions referenced Databricks credits alone. Lakebase positioning: no perpetual free Lakebase tier exists; the only free on-ramps are the 14-day trial (Lakebase explicitly listed among Free Edition's locked features) and startup credits. No other Lakebase-specific trial/free-offer changes were visible in 2025-2026 pages; Lakebase docs (last updated Oct 21, 2026) show no GA/preview badge on the core service, with 'store Postgres changes as Delta tables' still marked Public Preview. One caveat: WebSearch was unavailable this run (session budget), so the 2025-2026 change summary relies only on official pages fetched today plus the pages' own footers/dates.

findings.name: Free plan ($0/mo, $1/mo usage credit, permanent)
findings.detail: Permanent $0/month plan with $1 of non-rollover usage credits each billing cycle. Limits: max 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB per service, 1 replica, 3-day log history, 1 project, 3 services, 1 member per project, 500 MB max volume, 0 custom domains, 1 concurrent build. Metered rates beyond the $1: CPU ~$20/vCPU-month, memory ~$10/GB-month, egress $0.05/GB, volumes ~$0.15/GB-month; stopped services cost nothing. Restored Aug 27, 2025 after the free plan was deleted years earlier (blog: 'enough to run a small app for free in perpetuity').
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone (students and startups alike), no .edu, no CC required for the free tier, no stated region limits. No application.
findings.claim: Sign up at railway.com (click 'Login'); new accounts land in the Trial, then automatically revert to the Free plan when the $5 trial credit expires (30 days). Nothing else to claim; no form.
findings.expiry: Perpetual. The $1/mo credit resets each billing cycle and does not roll over.
findings.gotchas: $1/mo is tiny (roughly 36 vCPU-hours or ~$1 of egress); usage beyond it is billed per-second on a metered basis even on the free plan, so a busy app or data-heavy app can incur charges — set a billing limit in dashboard. 0 custom domains and 1 member/project; only 3 services. Egress ($0.05/GB) and volumes are not covered by a free allowance on this plan.

findings.name: Free trial: $5 one-time credit, 30 days, no credit card
findings.detail: One-time $5 credit valid 30 days, no credit card required. Trial limits: up to 2 vCPU / 1 GB per service (shared vCPUs), 2 replicas, 7-day logs, 2 projects, 5 services, 3 members/project, 500 MB volume, 1 custom domain, 3 concurrent builds. Two trial flavors: Full Trial (verified GitHub account) and Limited Trial (unverified) — Limited restricts outbound network access to a limited port set; verification is automated (GitHub account age/activity) and Railway does not respond to verification requests (can retry at railway.com/verify). After 30 days or $5 spent, the account reverts to the $1/mo Free plan.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone, no .edu or startup proof, no CC required. Unverified GitHub accounts get the Limited Trial with network restrictions instead of full features.
findings.claim: Click 'Login' at railway.com to start the trial (no CC). Alternative entry: no account needed — run `ssh railway.new` to get a free anonymous Linux VM (2 vCPU / 2 GB, 60-minute build window, 24-hour claim window, max 3 boxes per IP per day; unclaimed boxes and their files are deleted; claim link moves the box into your account).
findings.expiry: 30 days or $5, whichever comes first. If you upgrade while a balance remains, it carries over to the paid plan but may not be applied to the first billing cycle (applied as a discount to subsequent charges after a successful payment).
findings.gotchas: Limited Trial (unverified) = restricted outbound networking/ports; code deploys work but egress to arbitrary hosts may be blocked. Railway deletes stateful volumes tied to Trial accounts 30 days after the credit expires, so persistent data requires upgrading in time. Anonymous ssh railway.new boxes are region-capped under high demand and unclaimed work is destroyed.

findings.name: Startup program: $5,000 credits (LAUNCHED Apr 2024, now CLOSED)
findings.detail: Railway's official Startup Program (announced in the Apr 26, 2024 changelog and Apr 18, 2024 LinkedIn post) offered up to $5,000 in Railway credits. Original criteria: $2M–$25M in outside funding, founded in 2020 or later, new to Railway or under $100 lifetime platform spend; decisions promised 'within a few days'. No longer active as of late 2026: the program's dedicated page is gone (startup.railway.app returned 404 per a status-code audit on 2026-08-05; railway.com/startups also 404s today), staff told station users in Nov 2025 that 'railway does not have any startup programs' (only Free/Hobby/Pro), and a third-party tracker (noizz, checked 2026-09-23) lists Railway as having no startup program.
findings.eligibility: At launch (2024): VC/angel-funded startups with $2M–$25M outside funding, founded 2020+, <$100 lifetime Railway spend. Bootstrapped startups were explicitly excluded in v1 ('likely to expand down the line' — that expansion never materialized).
findings.claim: Was application-based (apply via the program link, review in days). The application path no longer exists; do not rely on it.
findings.expiry: Sunset: program page 404 as of Aug 2026; staff denials on Railway's own support station Nov 2025 and Dec 2025. Exact end date between 2024-04 and 2025-11 (unknown).
findings.gotchas: Treat the $5K offer as historical only. Remaining adjacent third-party channel: JoinSecret marketplace lists '$240 credit on the Hobby plan for 1 year' for 'selected startups' via a unique affiliate promo path (third-party, last checked 2026-10-01; promo credits apply only to new signups via that path) — low-confidence, not a first-party program. A 2026-10-10 station question asking for startup credits has no staff answer yet.

findings.name: Education / student program: NONE exists (students use the general trial)
findings.detail: Railway has never run a .edu student program or education license. Staff statements on Railway's support station: 2023/2024 — 'Railway does not currently run any programs like that'; Dec 29, 2025 — 'Railway doesn't have a program where we distribute credits for students' (instead pointed to template kickback/bounty earnings, which are revenue-share, not grants). The 'Student ID validation' feature request was closed by staff Mar 28, 2025: 'we have retooled our Trial to be general access. We may consider adding a free plan back in the future' (the free plan did return Aug 27, 2025). Third-party student-deal sites (studentoffers.co, student-perks) merely re-market the general $5/30-day trial as a 'student offer' — Railway lists it as 'Open to All'.
findings.eligibility: n/a — no student verification, .edu email, or GitHub Student Pack integration exists. The only free path for students is the open-to-all trial ($5/30 days) + Free plan ($1/mo).

provider: Cloudflare — Workers Free plan (Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment)

findings.name: Cloudflare Workers Free plan ($0/mo, no credit card)
findings.detail: $0/month. Core Worker: 100,000 requests/day; 10 ms CPU time per invocation, no charge for duration; max 100 Worker scripts per account (500 on paid); 128 MB memory per isolate; static assets free and unlimited requests (up to 20,000 files per Worker version, 25 MiB per file); no charge for data transfer (egress/bandwidth). Free included data stores on the same plan: KV (100,000 reads/day, 1,000 writes/day, 1 GB), D1 (5 GB total, 5M row reads/day, 100K row writes/day), R2 (10 GB-month, 1M Class A ops/mo, 10M Class B ops/mo, free egress), Durable Objects (100,000 requests/day, 13,000 GB-s/day), Queues (10,000 ops/day), Workflows (100,000 req/day, 10 ms CPU, 1 GB-month storage), Hyperdrive (100,000 queries/day), Vectorize (5M stored dimensions, 30M queried dimensions/mo), Workers Logs (200,000 events/day, 3-day retention). Containers: N/A on Free. Paid Workers plan starts at $5/mo (10M requests/mo, +$0.30/M; 30M CPU ms/mo, +$0.02/M CPU ms; unlimited egress).
findings.eligibility: Any person/company — create a free Cloudflare account at dash.cloudflare.com. No .edu email required, no regional restriction, no startup age/funding criteria, and no credit card required (Cloudflare's developer-facing messaging: 'Start building for free — no credit card required'). No application or approval.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a free Cloudflare account. 2) Go to Workers & Pages in the dashboard, or deploy locally with `npx wrangler deploy`. 3) Free plan is the default — no selection or billing setup needed. Limits apply automatically; exceeding them triggers the pay-per-use option ($5/mo minimum) only if you add a billing profile.
findings.expiry: No expiry/sunset date for the free plan; daily quotas reset at 00:00 UTC. Ongoing as of 2026-10-22 (pricing page last updated 2026-10-02; limits page 2026-10-12).
findings.gotchas: 10 ms CPU per invocation is a hard cap on Free (long jobs need Paid at 5 min cap); 100,000 requests is a per-DAY cap (≈3.1M/mo max), not monthly; static-asset 'unlimited' is bounded by 20,000 files/25 MiB per file; Durable Objects on Free are SQLite-only (no container DOs); Workers Logs free tier (200K events/day) migrates to Cloudflare Observability pricing on 2026-12-01; Durable Objects SQLite storage billing begins Jan 2026; no-charge-for-egress applies to CDN delivery, but connecting metered third-party services can incur charges on their side.

findings.name: Cloudflare Pages free plan (frontend hosting)
findings.detail: $0/month, available on the Free plan: 500 builds/month, 1 concurrent build, 20-minute build timeout; 100 projects (sites) per account (limit not routinely increased); up to 20,000 files per site, 25 MiB per file; 100 custom domains per project; unlimited preview deployments; unlimited users; no egress charges; no credit card required. New-project creation is rate-limited during the first 48h of account age.
findings.eligibility: Any Cloudflare account; no .edu, no credit card, no regional restriction. Domain must use Cloudflare nameservers for custom domains.
findings.claim: 1) Free account at dash.cloudflare.com. 2) Connect a Git repo (GitHub/GitLab) under Pages or upload manually; build+deploy is automatic. No application.
findings.expiry: No expiry; 500 builds reset monthly. Current as of 2026-09-05 (last updated on limits page).
findings.gotchas: Pages is in a migration/maintenance posture: Cloudflare docs actively direct users to Workers static assets ('Workers supports most Pages use cases and offers a broader feature set'; a dedicated 'Migrate From Pages' guide exists, updated 2026-10-12), so new features are landing on Workers, not Pages. Pages has no published aggregate storage cap (file-count cap instead of MB cap). To host >100 sites, Cloudflare pushes Workers for Platforms (paid product).

findings.name: R2 free tier (object storage with free egress)
findings.detail: Free every month: 10 GB-month storage, 1 million Class A operations, 10 million Class B operations, and egress is free (R2 charges no egress at any tier). Paid Standard: $0.015/GB-month, $4.50/M Class A, $0.36/M Class B. Added 2026: R2 SQL free tier 10 GB data-scanned/mo (billing enabled 2026-08-03); R2 Data Catalog free tier 1M catalog ops + 10 GB compaction/mo (billing enabled 2026-08-03).
findings.eligibility: Any free Cloudflare account; no credit card required; no .edu or regional limit.
findings.claim: Create an R2 bucket in the dashboard (or via `wrangler r2`); free tier is automatic — no application.
findings.expiry: No expiry; monthly free allowances reset. Verified on R2 pricing page last updated 2026-10-01.
findings.gotchas: Free tier applies to Standard storage only — Infrequent Access storage is NOT covered; R2 SQL minimum 10 MB scanned per query; unauthorized (401/403) requests are not billed; connecting R2 to other metered services may be charged by those services.

findings.name: D1 free tier (serverless SQLite)
findings.detail: Free: 5 GB total storage, 5,000,000 row reads/day, 100,000 row writes/day, $0. Paid: first 25B rows/mo reads, 50M rows/mo writes, first 5 GB included, then $0.75/GB-mo storage.
findings.eligibility: Any free Cloudflare account; no credit card; no .edu or regional restriction.
findings.claim: `wrangler d1 create my-db` or dashboard; included automatically in the Workers Free plan.
findings.expiry: No expiry; daily quotas reset at 00:00 UTC. Limits as of pricing page updated 2026-10-02.
findings.gotchas: Quotas are per-DAY, not per-month (daily reads cap = up to 150M/mo, writes = 3M/mo); D1 is designed for Workers bindings — it adds no egress cost.

findings.name: Durable Objects free tier (stateful coordination)
findings.detail: Free: 100,000 requests/day and 13,000 GB-s of duration/day; SQLite-backed storage is the only DO storage option on the Free plan. Paid: 1M requests/mo (+$0.15/M), 400,000 GB-s/mo (+$12.50/M GB-s).
findings.eligibility: Any free Cloudflare account; no credit card; no .edu or regional restriction.
findings.claim: Deploy a Worker with a DO class via `wrangler deploy`; free allowances automatic.
findings.expiry: No expiry; daily reset at 00:00 UTC.
findings.gotchas: Containers-backed DOs are NOT available on Free (listed N/A) — container DO billing is on the $5/mo paid plan; DO SQLite storage billing began January 2026 (target 2026-01-07 per changelog on the pricing page).

findings.name: Workers KV free tier
findings.detail: Free: 100,000 key reads/day, 1,000 writes/deletes/lists/day, 1 GB stored data; limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC. Paid: 10M reads/mo (+$0.50/M), 1M writes (+$5.00/M), 1 GB (+$0.50/GB-mo).
findings.eligibility: Any free Cloudflare account; no credit card; no .edu or regional restriction.
findings.claim: Create a KV namespace in the dashboard / `wrangler kv`; automatic.
findings.expiry: No expiry; daily reset. KV legacy API routes (/accounts/.../workers/namespaces/*) are deprecated — migrate to /storage/kv/namespaces/* before 2026-10-15.
findings.gotchas: The write cap (1,000/day) is the binding constraint for most apps; legacy API route deprecation deadline 2026-10-15 (past due as of 2026-10-22, so use the new routes).

provider: Cloudflare Pages (Free) — Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment

findings.name: Cloudflare Pages Free plan (free tier)
findings.detail: $0/mo, permanently free, no application. Static hosting: unlimited requests and unlimited bandwidth ('Requests to static assets are free and unlimited' — Workers platform pricing doc). Monthly/structural limits: 500 builds (deploys) per month, 1 concurrent build, 20-minute build timeout; up to 100 projects per account (limit 'not routinely increased'; new-project creation throttled for first 48h of a new account); 100 custom domains per project (free; Pro 250, Business/Enterprise 500); 20,000 files per project on Free (paid plans get 100,000 via env var PAGES_WRANGLER_MAJOR_VERSION=4); 25 MiB max per file; unlimited preview deployments; unlimited dashboard users; _headers 100 rules (2,000 chars/value); _redirects 2,100 total (2,000 static + 100 dynamic). No region limits stated in the limits doc. Docs last updated Sep 5, 2026; overview doc also states '500 deploys per month on the Free plan'.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Cloudflare account; no .edu, no company, no approval. No credit card required for the free plan in practice (dashboard sign-up is cardless) — this is not explicitly stated on the docs pages I read today, so treat the no-card sub-claim as medium confidence; the official limits/pricing docs simply never gate the Free plan on payment.
findings.claim: Create a free account at dash.cloudflare.com (no card), then deploy a Pages project via Git integration, C3 CLI, or direct upload. Project lands on the Free plan automatically; add a custom domain in the project's domains tab if needed.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier, no expiration or renewal. Quotas reset monthly (builds) or daily (Workers-side quotas).
findings.gotchas: (1) Pages Functions are billed as Workers: free Workers plan = 100,000 requests/day and 10 ms CPU time per invocation, plus free quotas for KV (100k reads/1k writes, 1 GB), D1, Queues, DO — functions that exceed these fall under the paid $5/mo minimum or overage rates. Static-asset traffic stays free and unlimited regardless. (2) Large assets (>25 MiB) don't fit — use R2 public buckets instead. (3) 100-project cap is effectively a hard limit; beyond that Cloudflare points to Workers for Platforms. (4) Strategic shift 2025–2026: Pages was folded into the Workers platform — docs now say 'Start new projects with Workers' and 'Workers supports most Pages use cases'; Pages itself is not being sunset but new features land in Workers. (5) Paid plan column in the limits doc (Pro/Business) corresponds to the Workers platform pricing (from $5/mo min) — Pages alone has no standalone paid subscription; '100 custom domains/project' on Free is per-project, multiplied across up to 100 projects.

findings.name: Cloudflare for Startups (startup credit program)
findings.detail: Official program page read today: up to $350,000 in credits for early-stage companies, tiered: Tier 3 = $10,000 credits (bootstrapped/self-funded, under $1M raised, no minimum funding, benefits: community/Discord/docs); Tier 2 = $100,000 (under $5M raised, funded by an affiliated partner; account manager case-dependent + expert sessions); Tier 1 = $350,000 ($5M+ raised, funded by an affiliated partner; account manager, priority support, bi-weekly Solutions Architect office hours). Credits cover usage-based services incl. Pages: Workers, Workers for Platforms, Durable Objects, Workflows, Workers AI, KV, D1, Queues, Vectorize, R2 (capped $10,000), Pages, Images and Stream, Cache Reserve, Argo Smart Routing. Product caps: Workers AI $2,500 (T3)/$10,000 (T2)/$50,000 (T1); R2 $10,000; AI Gateway temporarily NOT covered. Included at no cost in all tiers: 3 enterprise domains, unlimited Business and Pro plans, DDoS/bot protection, WAF with 1,000 custom rules, SSL, CDN+DNS, LB (2 origins), Rate Limiting (1 rule), 100% SLA. Excluded from credits: registrar fees, Enterprise add-ons, Magic Transit, Enterprise Spectrum, Dedicated IPs, China Network.
findings.eligibility: ALL must be met: for-profit business; incorporated/founded within the last 10 years; funded up to Series B (within last 12 months); actively building a technology product; publicly accessible live website; public presence on LinkedIn, X or GitHub; first-time applicants only; business email matching your domain (no personal email). Explicitly excluded: educational institutions, personal blogs, consultancies, service-based agencies, MSPs, resellers. No .edu (students use the free plan instead). No geographic restriction stated (China Network excluded and needs a dedicated contract).
findings.claim: Apply via the landing page linked from cloudflare.com/startups (form at /lp/startups): fill out the application describing product and team; review typically within 48 hours; activation confirmation by email; questions to startups@cloudflare.com. A valid payment method must be uploaded on file as part of the program.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 1 year or until fully consumed, whichever comes first; Cloudflare states it cannot approve extensions. After expiration, the credit card on file is billed for usage unless a prepaid contract is signed.
findings.gotchas: Credits are for usage-based services only — the free Pages plan is $0 to begin with, so the program only pays for your overage/paid-plan consumption; 'no cost' bundle (3 enterprise domains, WAF, SLA) is the real structural win. CREDIT CARD / payment method IS required (unlike the free plan). Funding caps matter: Tier 1 needs an affiliated-partner round, not just any $5M+. The older regional sub-pages (en-gb/en-ca /forstartups/) still show the pre-2026 four-tier $5k/$25k/$100k/$250k structure — the main cloudflare.com/startups page is authoritative.

findings.name: Student / education offer
findings.detail: No student-specific free offer exists for Pages or the Cloudflare developer platform. The official education page (read today) lists no academic license, no student credits, and no .edu-based benefit; the only quantified education program is 'Project Cybersafe Schools': free cloud email security and DNS filtering (CIPA-compliant) for small US K-12 public school districts — a security offering, not hosting, and not available to individual students/educators. Cloudflare's startup program explicitly excludes educational institutions. Individual students are served by the universal $0 Pages Free plan (no card, no application), which is the same as the general public's free tier; free developer courses/community exist but carry no hosting entitlement.
findings.eligibility: Students: no dedicated eligibility — they use the general Free plan (any account, no card). Project Cybersafe Schools: small US public K-12 districts. No .edu requirement anywhere; .edu email grants no special Cloudflare benefit.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim for students beyond the standard free plan. For K-12 districts: contact Cloudflare education team via the contact form on cloudflare.com/education.
findings.expiry: N/A — absence of a student program; free plan is permanent.
findings.gotchas: Search budget in this session was exhausted, so I could not exhaustively rule out ad-hoc student partnerships (e.g., accelerator/course-specific credit drops like the historical Workers Launchpad, which is partner-gated, not student-gated). Confidence is medium: I read the official education page today but student programs, if any, could live under partner/launchpad names I didn't fetch.

sunset_notes: 2024-2026 changes: (1) Startup program was revamped Sep 2024 from a one-size $500k-era offer to a credits system capped at $250,000 (3 tiers). April 11, 2025: expanded to four tiers — $5,000 (bootstrapped/stealth, founded last 5 yrs), $25,000 (funded to $1M), $100,000 ($1M-$5M + approved VC/accelerator), $250,000 (Tier-1 VCs / AI / Workers Launchpad) — with a 5-year founding window and a 'BOOTSTRAPPED' promo-code path. The current 2026 page replaced this with three tiers ($10k/$100k/$350k), a 10-year founding window, 'funded up to Series B within the last 12 months', a hard payment-method-on-file requirement, and per-tier Workers AI caps. Old $250k/$5k-$250k four-tier copy still lingers on stale localized sub-pages (en-gb, en-ca) — treat cloudflare.com/startups as current. (2) Pages platform shift 2025-2026: Pages was consolidated into the Workers platform; docs now steer new projects to Workers ('Start new projects with Workers'; Pages Functions billed exactly as Workers), but Pages is not sunset — Free plan numbers stand as verified Sep 5, 2026 doc: $0, unlimited static requests/bandwidth, 500 builds/mo, 100 projects, 100 custom domains/project, 20,000 files (raised from the prior 10,000 cap; paid tiers unlock 100,000 via PAGES_WRANGLER_MAJOR_VERSION=4), 25 MiB max asset. (3) No student/education program was created or sunset in this window; 'Project Cybersafe Schools' (free K-12 email security + DNS filtering, US districts) remains the only education-facing free offer. No trial-credit program (e.g., a $500 API-credit trial) is currently advertised on the official pages I read.

findings.name: Developer Sandbox — always-free plan (2 services + 2 cron jobs + 1 database)
findings.detail: Free 'Sandbox' plan (aka Developer Sandbox / Free Developer Projects since Nov 2021): 2 free services, 2 free cron jobs, 1 free database/addon (Postgres, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ), up to 1 BYOC cluster, always-on compute with no sleeping or cold starts. Includes free SSL + custom domains, UI/API/CLI, logs and metrics, secret management. No cash credit is granted — 'credits' on Northflank are prepaid purchases ($50 minimum), so there is no trial-credit offer. Paid reference rates for what you hit beyond free: $0.01667/vCPU-hr, $0.00833/GB-hr memory, $0.15/GB-month disk, $0.06/GB egress (ingress free); GPUs start at $0.80/hr (L4) and require a $50+ credit purchase to unlock. Docs state the free tier 'should not be used for production applications'.
findings.eligibility: Open to any user; no .edu, age, funding or region restriction published. A payment method IS required on every plan (docs: 'all users must add a payment method to start creating resources on Northflank, regardless of plan selection') — for the free plan the card is only verified ('when you enter a card we only verify the card'; Northflank states you won't be charged unless you upgrade to a paid plan).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at app.northflank.com (GitHub/GitLab/Google/email). 2) Select the free Sandbox plan when creating the team/organization. 3) Add a payment method when prompted (verification only for Sandbox). 4) Create a project and deploy up to 2 services, 2 cron jobs, 1 database add-on (from Git or container image). Free forever; upgrade to Pay-as-you-go any time, keeping existing resources.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal stated — permanently free. Logs/metrics retained ~1 month per docs. If you upgrade and later downgrade, your team must contain no more resources than the target plan allows.
findings.gotchas: Payment method required even on the free plan (rank risk: card is verified, not charged, on Sandbox; charge only on paid plans, billed at end of billing cycle with configurable billing alerts). Quotas are per account, not per project. BYOC on Sandbox keeps the Northflank orchestration free but your cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure/Oracle/CoreWeave/Civo/bare-metal) still bills you for underlying infra. Northflank does not publish free-tier egress/HTTP-request/log/metric quotas — third-party trackers estimate ~10 GB egress but that is unconfirmed by Northflank; not-intended-for-production warning; a third-party atlas notes a project-count discrepancy (pricing lists 2 projects, setup docs list 1). No 15-minute sleep: compute is explicitly always-on, unlike Fly.io/Render-style free tiers.

findings.name: Student Developer Pack — doubled free tier (4 services) + student support
findings.detail: Northflank's education offer: the standard free tier (2 services, 2 cron jobs, 1 database) is increased to 4 services plus student support for verified students. Program has existed since Jan 2022 (announced in changelog). No .edu-exclusive rule is stated in the cached page copy — it asks you to email 'via a valid student email'.
findings.eligibility: Students (group projects, assignments, side projects). Requires emailing from a valid student/academic email; recognized student address needed for the upgrade to be granted. No region limits published.
findings.claim: Email students@northflank.com from your student email requesting the Student Developer Pack (standard offer: 4 services + student support); Northflank 'will be in contact' to verify and apply it. Note: the payment-method requirement of the base Sandbox plan still applies.
findings.expiry: No official expiry or renewal date published; implicitly valid while a student. Offer terms not officially re-stated on any live Northflank page as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: MAJOR: the official page https://northflank.com/student-developer-pack returned HTTP 404 when fetched 2026-10-22 (also /education is 404). The offer text above comes from the search-engine cached copy of that page plus third-party directories (studentoffers.co, open-awesome.com) that still list it, so the program may have been quietly retired or the URL changed in 2025-2026. Verify by emailing students@northflank.com before relying on it. Not part of any GitHub Student Developer Pack-style automated claim — it is manual email review.

findings.name: Startups: no Northflank-branded startup program or trial credits — BYOC + third-party cloud credits instead
findings.detail: Northflank has no published startup program, startup credit grant, or funded-startup discount of its own. The Pay-as-you-go plan is simply marketed toward 'Early stage startups'. Instead Northflank's 2026-03-30 blog documents how startups burn existing third-party credits on BYOC: AWS Activate Founders ($1,000 AWS credits + $350 dev-support credits, <10 employees, <$1M revenue/funding, no VC/accelerator affiliation, no prior Activate credits), YC Startup School ($2,500), Stripe Atlas ($5,000 auto-included for US incorporation), FounderPass (up to $5,000, $99/yr membership), VC/accelerator partner referrals ($10k–$100k+); credits typically last 12 months from issuance. With BYOC, those credits pay the cloud provider; Northflank charges its own flat per-cluster/vCPU/GB platform fees on top (or $0 platform fee within the Sandbox plan's 1 BYOC cluster).
findings.eligibility: Depends on each third-party program, not Northflank: AWS Activate Founders = bootstrapped, <10 employees, <$1M annual revenue/funding, no VC/accelerator affiliation; YC Startup School = open application; Stripe Atlas = founders incorporating a US entity; credits via accelerator/VC = enrollment in a recognized program. No Northflank-side age/funding cap exists because Northflank grants nothing.
findings.claim: 1) Obtain credits from AWS Activate / accelerator / Stripe etc. 2) Create a Northflank account (free Sandbox plan, card verified). 3) Connect your AWS/GCP/Azure account as a BYOC cluster. 4) Deploy on Northflank so compute runs on your credit-bearing cloud account; Northflank bills only its platform fee (free for 1 cluster on Sandbox).
findings.expiry: Underlying cloud credits expire (AWS: typically 12 months from issuance; 'credits last 12 months' per Northflank blog). The BYOC setup and Sandbox plan have no expiry; platform fees apply if you exceed Sandbox's 1 BYOC cluster.
findings.gotchas: These are not Northflank credits — a directory listing Northflank under 'free credits for startups' would be wrong; Northflank explicitly has 'no cash credit; free Developer Sandbox plan' (third-party tracker, checked 2026-09-02). BYOC still incurs Northflank's flat platform fees per cluster/vCPU/GB unless inside Sandbox. Aifree.dev's 'startups verification required: confirm your company details (age, funding, or website) to claim' refers to the directory's own verification of claims, not a Northflank program. Free Sandbox BYOC includes up to 1 cluster; more clusters requires upgrading.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22: (1) The official Student Developer Pack page (northflank.com/student-developer-pack) returns HTTP 404 — the program appears retired or URL-changed in 2025-2026 even though third-party directories still list 'free tier doubled for students' (4 services + student support via students@northflank.com); treat as unconfirmed pending email verification. (2) No Northflank-branded startup program or free trial-credit offer exists or was sunset — the startup route is BYOC with third-party credits (AWS Activate et al.). (3) 2025-2026 pricing changes: 11 Dec 2025 — network pricing cut 60% to $0.06/GB egress and new Tokyo + Melbourne regions (changelog); 2025-2026 releases added GPUs (B200, Granite Rapids), unified jobs, BYOC microVMs/sandboxes, object storage — none changed the free Sandbox quota of 2 services / 2 cron jobs / 1 database / 1 BYOC cluster, which has been stable since the Nov 2021 'Free Developer Projects' launch. No known sunset of the free tier itself; it remains always-on and free with card verification at signup.

findings.name: Fly.io Free Trial (2 VM hours / 7 days)
findings.detail: Every new account gets a trial grant of 2 total VM hours of machine runtime OR 7 days of access, whichever comes first. Trial limits: up to 10 machines, 20GB of volume storage, machines up to 2 vCPU / 4GB RAM. Trial machines auto-stop after 5 minutes of runtime (relevant when no billing is on file). NOT included: dedicated IPv4 addresses and performance-optimized vCPUs. Metering: machine runtime (incl. memory) per second; volume storage and machine count per hour. Visible under 'Trial Status' in the dashboard. After the trial: apps halt; you cannot launch new machines, attach volumes, or deploy changes until a payment method is set up. Adding a credit card from the dashboard ends the trial early and billing starts immediately. Pay-as-you-go then runs from ~$2.19/mo for the smallest always-on app (shared-cpu-1x, 256MB), plus dedicated IPv4 $2.00/mo and egress $0.02/GB (NA/EU).
findings.eligibility: Any new user who creates a Fly.io account — no credit card required to start, no .edu email, no student/startup restriction, no funding cap, no stated region limit. Open to the general public, not a student or startup program.
findings.claim: Sign up at fly.io/app/sign-up/ — the trial is attached automatically at account creation, no separate activation step. Monitor remaining time/hours under 'Trial Status' in the dashboard. To continue past the trial, add a payment method (Stripe) in Billing.
findings.expiry: Expires at 2 total VM hours or 7 days, whichever comes first; earlier if you add a card (trial ends, billing begins). Not renewable; no stated extension path.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs. free: this is a metered trial, not an ongoing free tier — when it ends without billing, all apps stop and deploys are blocked. With no card on file, trial machines auto-stop after just 5 minutes of uptime. The 2 VM hours are shared across all machines and include memory; a single 256MB shared-CPU machine running 24/7 already burns ~half the grant in 3 days. After trial, stopped-but-kept machines still accrue storage ($0.15/GB-mo on rootfs), and same-region transfer is free but internet egress is $0.02/GB. Pre-auth holds are usually under $10 and can show for up to 10 business days.

findings.name: Always-free allowances on paid plans (no free compute tier)
findings.detail: After the trial, there is no free compute tier: no free VM hours, memory, or machine minutes. What is free for any account: first 10GB of volume snapshots per month; a shared IPv4 and unlimited Anycast IPv6 for every app; same-region data transfer; and community support. Cheapest running states: shared-cpu-1x 256MB preset $2.19/mo; stopped machines bill $0.15/GB-mo of rootfs; volumes $0.15/GB-mo; Managed Postgres Basic $38/mo; dedicated IPv4 $2.00/mo; egress $0.02/GB (NA/EU); support from $29/mo.
findings.eligibility: Any Fly.io account. Note a credit card is required by most accounts to deploy multiple apps or public images (abuse prevention); alternative if you can't add a card: purchase account credits, minimum $25 (prepaid cards can fund credit purchases but not serve as the saved method). No student/startup-specific terms on this page.
findings.claim: Automatic for every account on sign-up; snapshot allowance and network allowances apply without opt-in. Credits purchased in the dashboard Billing section.
findings.expiry: Ongoing, not time-limited. The 10GB snapshot allowance resets monthly; free allowances do not expire and do not renew/stack beyond that.
findings.gotchas: 'Free' here means snapshots/IP/networking/community support only — compute, storage of running or stopped volumes, Postgres, and internet egress all bill. Volumes in pending_destroy state do not accrue charges. Free Postgres from the old shared-CPU days is gone: managed Postgres now starts at $38/mo.

findings.name: Fly.io Startup Program (up to $15,000 in credits)
findings.detail: fly.io/startups offers up to $15,000 in credits for eligible early-stage startups. Credits apply across Machines, Sprites, Managed Postgres, volumes, and bandwidth, but exclude support plans, compliance packages, and Machine reservations. Credits expire 1 year after they are added to the organization. Applicants are invited to a Slack channel with the Fly team. After credits are exhausted, apps keep running at standard pay-as-you-go (billed by the second). Application takes ~2 minutes; a human reviews it and replies by email within about a week. Fly may verify funding via a quick email intro to the investor or accelerator.
findings.eligibility: Seed- or Series-A-stage startups backed by a venture firm or an accelerator. Must NOT have received Fly.io startup credits before (one-time). No startup-age cap, revenue cap, team-size cap, .edu requirement, or stated region restriction — funding-stage/VC-backing is the gate, not time since founding.
findings.claim: Fill out the application at fly.io/startups/ (fields: name, work email, company, website, funding stage, lead investor/accelerator, Fly.io org name, description of what you're building). A human reads it; response by email within ~1 week.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 1 year after being added to the organization. The program itself has no listed deadline. No renewal: startups that already received Fly startup credits are ineligible, so this is a one-time grant per startup.
findings.gotchas: 'Up to $15,000' — the page does not publish a fixed grant amount or tiering. Credit card requirement is not stated on the page. Credits do not cover support, compliance, or reserved machines. If funding cannot be verified, the application may be rejected.

findings.name: Education / student program: none exists (former free tier with student eligibility is gone)
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 there is no Fly.io education license, student program, .edu email offer, or free academic compute tier. fly.io/education returns HTTP 404; docs.fly.io/about/education returns HTTP 404; the docs home, learn hub (40 technical explainers), and pricing page contain no education/student/academic offer. The legacy free plan — which historically offered free shared-CPU machines to students, educators, researchers, and artists — has been removed: the old reference page fly.io/docs/reference/free-faq now redirects to docs.fly.io/reference/free-faq, which returns HTTP 404 (page deleted). The only free entry point is the general 2-hour/7-day trial, open to everyone without card.
findings.eligibility: n/a — no current education offer exists. Historically the retired free tier targeted students/educators/researchers/artists with no stated .edu verification on the surviving pages.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Students get exactly the same 2 VM-hour / 7-day trial as any other user; there is no separate application, license, or student pricing to request.
findings.expiry: n/a (no offer). The old free tier's successor (the trial) has its own 7-day/2-hour expiry as documented in finding 1.
findings.gotchas: Do not assume the old student-friendly free shared-CPU tier still exists — the reference docs are deleted and the pricing page lists no free compute. Anyone citing 'free Fly machines for students' is using pre-sunset information.

sunset_notes: Legacy free tier (free shared-CPU machines, historically eligible for students/educators/researchers/artists) has been sunset: the old FAQ at fly.io/docs/reference/free-faq now 404s at docs.fly.io/reference/free-faq, fly.io/education and docs.fly.io/about/education 404, and today's pricing page shows no free compute tier — replaced by the 2-VM-hour / 7-day no-card trial plus pay-as-you-go from ~$2.19/mo. Free Postgres on the old free plan is also gone (Managed Postgres Basic starts at $38/mo). Web search was unavailable in this session (budget exhausted), so I could not pin the exact sunset date of the old free tier (my prior knowledge suggests the free tier was retired in 2024 and replaced by the trial); that date should be confirmed separately. The $15,000 startup-credit figure and the 1-year credit expiry come from the live fly.io/startups page (copyrighted 2026), so the program is current as of 2026-10-22; no material 2025-2026 change was visible on the official pages themselves. No evidence today of any current education license or student program.

provider: Deno Deploy (Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment)

findings.name: Deno Deploy Free plan (new platform, $0/mo)
findings.detail: Free plan of the new Deno Deploy (GA Feb 3, 2026). As listed on the official pricing page today: $0/mo; 1M inbound HTTP requests/mo; 10 active CPU-hours/mo; 20 GiB egress/mo; 10 GiB revision storage; 10 concurrent apps (deployments); 1 concurrent build; 15 builds/hour; 5 custom domains (no wildcard subdomains); 3 team members; 150 GiB-hr memory time; KV: 1 GiB storage, 1,000,000 KV read units/mo (4 KiB), 500,000 KV write units/mo (1 KiB); log/trace retention 1 day; app metrics history 1 month; log streaming API included; NOT included: sandboxes, volume storage, email support, SLA, SOC2 Type 1/DPA. Targeted at 'personal use and smaller projects'.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone; sign-up free at console.deno.com. No .edu email required, no startup age/funding cap (this is a general free tier, not an education or startup program). No credit card requirement is stated anywhere on the pricing page (CTA is simply 'Start free'); the docs' usage/limits page adds that orgs can set alert thresholds and hard spending limits in the console (controls available as of Sept/Oct 2025). Regions: new Deno Deploy platform serves only 2 regions (us, eu) plus self-hosting via deployd; Classic (6 regions) is sunsetting. No other regional restriction stated.
findings.claim: No application or activation needed: create a free account at console.deno.com, create an org/app, deploy code (deno deploy / Git integration); the free plan is the default starting tier. Upgrade to Pro/Builder/Enterprise in-console when limits are exceeded.
findings.expiry: Ongoing monthly free tier; does not expire or require renewal. Free limits reset monthly. No sunset date announced for the new platform's free plan (in contrast: Classic sunsets 2026-07-20).
findings.gotchas: (1) CPU billing is only while code actively runs; idle apps auto-shutdown in ~20-30 s, so 10 active CPU-hours is roughly equivalent of one always-busy app for ~10h. (2) Egress excludes inbound request data; 20 GiB/mo is a hard cap for Free. (3) The Free column lists no overage rates — Pro/Builder overage is $2/M requests and $0.20/GiB egress, so staying on Free means hitting caps, not paying overage. (4) The Feb 2026 GA blog describes the free tier as '1M requests, 100 GB egress, 15 CPU hours' — the current pricing page (fetched today) shows 20 GiB egress and 10 CPU-hours, i.e., the free allocation appears to have been cut since GA; trust the live pricing page. (5) No wildcard subdomains; only 5 custom domains; 3 team members; KV free bucket is small (1 GiB). (6) WebSearch was unavailable in this session (budget exhausted), so program checks relied on fetching deno.com pages directly today.

findings.name: No free trial credits for paid plans found
findings.detail: The official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22) contains no mention of a free trial of Pro/Builder/Enterprise (no trial duration, no $ credits). No 'trial' or 'credit' program appears on the homepage, /deploy product page, blog index, or docs. A trial may exist inside the console, but it is not documented or advertised on any official page checked.

findings.claim: Nothing to claim; no application URL found.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Don't assume 'Start free' = a time-limited trial of paid plans; it is a perpetual free tier. Any console-gated trial could not be verified without an account, so treat as unconfirmed/low confidence.

findings.name: No startup program or education license found
findings.detail: Deno has no documented startup-credit program, student program, or education license for Deno Deploy. deno.com/startups and deno.com/education are both 404; the blog index (2024-2026 entries) has no post announcing such a program; the pricing, product, and docs pages contain no 'education', 'student', 'startup', or 'academic' offers. Closest adjacent items: free database provisioning from the dashboard for Pro (Prisma partnership, mentioned in the GA post — not a startup-specific offer) and enterprise 'Deno for Enterprise' (paid support, not free).
findings.eligibility: N/A — no documented offer.
findings.claim: N/A.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: If a student/startup wants more than the free tier, the only documented path is paid Pro/Builder/Enterprise; no .edu verification or startup application flow exists on deno.com as of today.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: (1) PLATFORM MIGRATION — Deno Deploy was rebuilt: the new platform hit GA on Feb 3, 2026 and 'Deno Deploy Classic' plus the subhosting v1 API shut down on 2026-07-20 (date past as of today); Classic stopped onboarding new users/orgs earlier. deployctl CLI is sunset, replaced by the 'deno deploy' subcommand; KV queues were removed; regions dropped from 6 (Classic) to 2 (us, eu) on the new platform. Existing Classic free-plan users had to migrate to console.deno.com before 2026-07-20. provider: GitHub Pages (Frontend hosting / PaaS & app deployment) — GitHub, Inc.

findings.name: GitHub Pages free hosting tier (GitHub Free plan)
findings.detail: $0/mo flat-free hosting, no credit card required. Limits: up to 1 user or organization site per account plus unlimited project sites; recommended source-repo limit 1 GB; published site size capped at 1 GB; soft bandwidth limit of 100 GB/month; soft build limit of 10 builds/hour (this cap is waived when you build/publish via a custom GitHub Actions workflow); deployments time out after 10 minutes. Sites that hit rate limits return HTTP 429. Custom domains and HTTPS are supported at no cost. Pages on public repos is available on GitHub Free; hosting Pages for private repos requires GitHub Pro/Team/Enterprise (or the free student tier).
findings.eligibility: Any personal or organization GitHub account. GitHub Free is $0 with no credit card. Public Pages sites work on GitHub Free (public repos). Private-repo Pages requires GitHub Pro/Team/Enterprise (paid plans) OR free GitHub Education student status. No founding-age, funding, or geographic restriction on the free tier.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free GitHub account (no card). 2) For a user/org site name the repo <user>.github.io or <org>.github.io; for project sites use any project repo. 3) Add an entry file at the source root (index.html / index.md / README.md). 4) In repo Settings > Pages, choose the publishing source (branch/folder or a custom Actions workflow). 5) Click 'Visit site' to see the live deployment; add a custom domain + HTTPS under Pages settings if needed.
findings.gotchas: 1 GB site size and 100 GB/mo bandwidth are SOFT limits, not hard caps: exceeding them can cause the site to stop being served or trigger an email asking you to reduce server impact. 10 builds/hour is a soft cap and 10 min is a build timeout. No separate egress/data-egress charge on the free plan beyond the soft bandwidth cap. On GitHub Free, the repo hosting the Pages site must be public; private Pages pushes you to a paid plan unless you have free student status.
findings.expiry: Indefinite: part of the free GitHub plan; no expiry while the account/plan stay active. GitHub can change limits at any time without notice; no 2025-2026 sunset of the free tier observed.

findings.name: GitHub Education / Student Developer Pack (education license)
findings.detail: Verified students get GitHub Pro FREE (unlimited private repos with advanced collaboration tools), free GitHub Pages hosting (incl. for private repos), GitHub Copilot Student (free access to Copilot and its premium features), GitHub Codespaces up to 180 core hours/month with Pro-equivalent storage (~20 GB Codespaces storage and ~2 GB Packages storage), ~3,000 GitHub Actions minutes/month, and roughly 80 third-party 'Student Developer Pack' partner offers (e.g., a free domain, ~$100 Azure credit, JetBrains, 1Password). Student validation lasts 2 years.
findings.eligibility: 13 years or older; enrolled in a degree- or diploma-granting program (high school, college, university, or homeschool; bootcamps qualify only if part of GitHub's Campus Program). Requires a personal GitHub account. Verify with a school-issued email OR dated proof of enrollment (school ID photo, class schedule, transcript, or affiliation/enrollment letter showing a date and current status) — a .edu email is NOT strictly required. No credit card required. No GitHub-imposed regional cap, though individual third-party partners may add their own age/region limits. Teachers/faculty/staff get free/discounted GitHub but are NOT eligible for the Pack.
findings.claim: 1) Sign in to the personal GitHub account you want benefits on. 2) Add/verify your school email under Settings > Emails (or rely on uploaded enrollment proof if your school issues no email). 3) Make your profile name match your documents. 4) Go to Settings > Education benefits, under 'GitHub Education' click 'Start an application'. 5) Fill the form, select your school, upload dated proof of enrollment, submit. 6) After approval (usually a few days), open the GitHub Education portal / Student Developer Pack page and claim each offer individually. No credit card needed.
findings.gotchas: The third-party partner offers (free domain, Azure credits, JetBrains, 1Password, etc.) are the de-facto 'trial credits' — they churn, pause, or are removed at the partner's request (the 2024-10 partner list already removed Netwise, Typeform, and a .Tech email offer). You cannot re-redeem a time-limited offer by re-verifying student status; some partners disallow stacking. Individual partners may impose age/country limits. The 180 Codespaces hours/month are for your personal account; Codespaces usage in GitHub Classroom assignment repos is billed to the classroom org, not you. The free-domain offers are typically time-limited (often 1 year). GitHub Pro/Pages/Copilot/Codespaces access lapses when student status lapses.
findings.expiry: Student validation lasts 2 years, then must be re-validated. GitHub Pro, Pages, Copilot Student, and Codespaces access continue only while you remain a verified, enrolled student. Each third-party partner offer carries its own terms and duration.

findings.name: GitHub for Startups (startup program) — $10,000 Enterprise credits
findings.detail: Partners (VCs, accelerators, incubators) refer early-stage startups to receive $10,000 in GitHub credits usable across the Enterprise platform for up to 12 months, covering GitHub Copilot, GitHub Advanced Security, GitHub Actions (with 50k included minutes), and GitHub Packages. Also includes tailored onboarding, office hours, technical best-practice guidance, and entry into the GitHub startups community (~40,000 startups and 1,000+ ecosystem partners). This is NOT a free Pages hosting tier — Pages is already free to everyone; this grants Enterprise-platform credits. Program page carries © 2026 GitHub, Inc., so it is current as of 2026.
findings.eligibility: Must be referred/affiliated with a GitHub for Startups partner (VC, accelerator, or incubator; any such org can submit a partner application). Must have received outside funding up to Series B or earlier (non-equity credits do not count). Must be NEW to GitHub Enterprise (no Enterprise plan in the prior 6 months and no prior GitHub credits or Enterprise licenses). Enterprise Cloud on github.com only (Enterprise Server and Data Residency excluded). No founding-age cap, no company-size cap, and no geographic restriction stated. A payment method IS required (an authorization charge is expected within weeks of onboarding). One-time offer: previously credited accounts are ineligible.
findings.claim: 1) Get referred by a VC / accelerator / incubator that is a GitHub for Startups partner (or have that org submit a partner application). 2) Alternatively reach out via the page's 'Contact sales' link. 3) Approval email arrives in ~2-3 business days. 4) Onboard to GitHub Enterprise Cloud on github.com and add a payment method (authorization charge expected). 5) Spend the $10,000 Enterprise credits across Copilot / Advanced Security / Actions (50k min) / Packages within 12 months. This is partner-gated (not open self-signup), requires a payment method, and is a credits grant, not free Pages hosting.
findings.gotchas: Not a free-forever frontend hosting tier: it is a $10k Enterprise-credits grant. Partner referral is mandatory (not open application). A payment-method authorization charge is required despite the credit coverage. After credits are consumed or 12 months elapse, active products automatically transition to standard paid billing. Downgrading before the credits are exhausted forfeits the remaining credits AND bars reapplication. Enterprise Cloud on github.com only — not Enterprise Server or Data Residency. Funding cap: Series B or earlier. One-time offer only.
findings.expiry: Credits valid up to 12 months from approval — they expire on full consumption or at the end of the 12-month period, whichever comes first. Program active as of 2026 (© 2026 GitHub, Inc.).

sunset_notes: No sunset of the GitHub Pages free tier in 2025-2026: the limits page is current and the flat-free model (1 user/org site + unlimited project sites, 1 GB site, 100 GB/mo soft bandwidth, 10 builds/hr, 10-min build timeout, custom domains + HTTPS) is unchanged, and Pages remains $0 with no credit card on public repos. There is no separate 'free trial credit' offer specific to Pages hosting. The third-party Student Developer Pack partner list churns (the 2024-10 partner snapshot removed Netwise, Typeform, and a .Tech email offer) — those partner offers are not the core GitHub offer and can pause or be removed. The verifiable startup program is 'GitHub for Startups' at github.com/enterprise/startups ($10,000 Enterprise credits, Series B funding cap, partner-referral, Enterprise Cloud only, active as of 2026); I could not confirm any separately-branded 'GitHub Accelerate' hosting-credits offer this session. No region-based or egress-cost sunset dates were announced for Pages hosting; the only data-cost concern is the 100 GB/mo SOFT bandwidth cap, not a priced egress charge.

provider: Upstash (Managed Databases & Data Platforms) — as of 2026-10-22

findings.name: Upstash Free Tier (all products: Redis, QStash, Workflow, Vector, Box, Blob) — the de facto free offer for students and startups
findings.detail: Permanent $0 plans, open to everyone (no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap). Redis: $0/mo, 500K commands/mo, 250 MB data, 10 GB bandwidth, up to 10 free databases (1 DB per plan row in comparison table; FAQ says up to 10 free DBs, $0.50/DB after, max 100), 10K cmd/s, 1 index (10K docs/index), 10 MB request / 100 MB record size; no Multi-Zone HA, no uptime SLA, no IP allowlists, no encryption at rest, no SOC-2/HIPAA, no Prod Pack, regions on AWS/GCP/Vercel (no FLY). QStash: 1,000 messages/day, 50 GB bandwidth, 1 MB message, 1 URL group (100 endpoints), 10 queues, 10 schedules, 7-day max delay, DLQ+log retention 3 days. Workflow: 1,000 steps/day (soft limit), 10 concurrent steps, 1 MB message. Vector: 200M vectors x dims, 1536 max dims, 10K queries/day, 1 GB data+metadata, 10 indexes free, top-k default 1000; regions LIMITED to N. Virginia (AWS), Ireland (AWS), Iowa (GCP). Box (serverless compute): 10 concurrent boxes, 5 CPU hours/mo, $1 LLM token budget/mo (400 after cap; BYOK allowed), AWS us-east-1 only. Blob (S3-compatible object storage): 1 GB storage, 10K simple ops/mo, 2K advanced ops/mo, 10 GB egress/mo, global CDN (no region choice), 'free plan is never charged'; overage = requests stop until 30-day window rolls (hard cap, no bill). No credit card required on any: adding a card upgrades the resource to pay-as-you-go.
findings.eligibility: Anyone: sign up free at console.upstash.com (GitHub/Google/email). No student verification, no startup criteria, no credit card. Region limits apply per product (Vector 3 regions; Box us-east-1 only).
findings.claim: 1) Create free account at console.upstash.com (no card). 2) Create a database/queue/index/box/bucket — it lands on the Free plan automatically. 3) Use it; each product's free allowance renews monthly/daily forever.
findings.expiry: No expiry: free plans renew indefinitely (daily allowances for QStash/Workflow/Vector reset daily; monthly for Redis/Blob/Box).
findings.gotchas: Redis 'retry' semantics: QStash FAQ says 'each delivery attempt counts as one message', so failed-retried deliveries eat the 1,000/day; Workflow retries and parallel/context calls consume extra billed steps (context.call/invoke = 2 steps each). Blob stops serving (not billed) when caps hit. Adding a credit card silently moves you to paid PAYG ($0.20/100K Redis commands, $0.25/GB storage, 200 GB/mo bandwidth free on PAYG). Free tier lacks HA/SLA/SOC2/encryption-at-rest — fine for student projects, not production compliance. Up also offers ad-hoc free trials/PoC on request via support@upstash.com.
findings.source_url: https://upstash.com/pricing/redis.md (free plan + FAQ); also /pricing/qstash.md, /pricing/vector.md, /pricing/workflow.md, /pricing/box.md, /pricing/blob.md, all read 2026-10-22

findings.name: start-redis instant trial database (free trial credit, no signup)
findings.detail: POST https://upstash.com/start-redis returns a ready, free Redis database with credentials, quickstart and a console claim-link — no signup, no credit card, no API key. Unclaimed databases are deleted after 3 days; an agent is expected to send a User-Agent identifying itself (optional Idempotency-Key makes retries return the same DB).
findings.eligibility: Anyone, including AI agents; no account or card needed.
findings.claim: curl -X POST https://upstash.com/start-redis (send a User-Agent header); open the console URL in the response to claim it into an account before the 3-day deletion.
findings.expiry: Trial DB expires/deleted after 3 days if not claimed; once claimed it lives on the normal Free plan.
findings.gotchas: It is a trial, not the free tier: data is lost at 3 days unless claimed. Claiming drops it into the standard Redis free limits above.
findings.source_url: https://upstash.com/redis and https://upstash.com/pricing/redis.md ('For AI Agents' section)

findings.name: Upstash Open Source Program — up to $1,000/month credits for OSS projects (CLOSED to new applications)
findings.detail: $1,000/month credit: 'We cover all Upstash-related costs up to $1,000 per month. Build on any Upstash product(s) without worrying about billing.' Perks: direct technical support, priority support 'just like our Pro customers', co-marketing/technical articles. Credit renews monthly with no fixed end date. Eligibility is 'open-source projects building on Upstash' — no star count or license criteria published. As of the page read on 2026-10-22: 'The open-source program is currently closed and not accepting new applications.' Questions go to program lead @joshtriedcoding.
findings.eligibility: Open-source project maintainers/builders (individual devs qualify, not just startups); program currently closed, so no one can claim new applications right now.
findings.claim: No application URL while closed: follow Upstash / email program lead (@joshtriedcoding) to hear about reopening.
findings.expiry: Credits are monthly while in the program; program intake currently closed.
findings.gotchas: Third-party lists still advertise it as open ($1,000/mo grant) — the official page says closed today; verify before relying on it. No student-specific program exists; students get the general free tier instead.

findings.name: Upstash Postgres / Kafka free metered tiers (previously 'free to start') — NO LONGER LISTED AS PRODUCTS
findings.detail: The task's premise includes Postgres and Kafka metered free tiers, but as of 2026-10-22 neither appears anywhere on upstash.com: the pricing page lists only Redis, QStash, Workflow, Box, Blob; /pricing/postgres, /pricing/kafka, /postgres, /kafka all 404; docs only mention Kafka as the open-source broker (QStash comparison page); docs search confirms no Postgres or Kafka product exists. Kafka survives only in blog content (including 'kafka-connectors-deprecation'), and QStash/Workflow now serve the messaging use case. No Postgres/Kafka free-tier limits can be quoted from official sources today.
findings.eligibility: n/a — offers not present on the official site.
findings.claim: n/a — nothing to claim.
findings.expiry: Sunset from the product lineup by 2026-10-22 (messaging replaced by QStash/Workflow).
findings.gotchas: Treat any current listing of Upstash Postgres or Upstash Kafka free tiers as stale. If you need Kafka-like streaming on free, use Upstash QStash (1,000 msgs/day free) or Workflow.
