findings.detail: Third-party deal site SaaSOffers lists '$500 in credits' for startups using serverless Redis/Kafka ('Verified October 2026'). No official Upstash page substantiates it: no /startups or startup-program page exists (404s), the homepage nav and pricing pages contain no startup program link, and the Redis free-tier FAQ has no startup section.
findings.eligibility: Allegedly early-stage startups on a new account; criteria unknown.
findings.claim: Unknown — no official application path found; would require contacting sales@upstash.com.
findings.expiry: Unknown.
findings.gotchas: Third-party aggregator claim only; possibly an old promo, possibly a confused entry (Upstash also historically ran startup perks via partner programs). Low confidence — do not plan on it without written confirmation from Upstash sales.
findings.source_url: https://saasoffers.tech/offers/upstash (third-party; official absence verified at https://upstash.com)

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes: (1) Upstash Postgres and Upstash Kafka (both previously free-to-start metered products) no longer exist on upstash.com — pricing, product pages, sitemap and docs all omit them as of 2026-10-22; messaging is now QStash/Workflow (docs only reference Kafka as the open-source broker). (2) The Upstash Open Source Program ($1,000/mo credits) is currently closed to new applications per the official page. (3) No official education/student program exists: /education 404s, the Redis FAQ has no education entry; third-party 'student deal' pages (Modelverse, ToolBridge) merely describe the general free tier and cite outdated figures (10,000 commands/day, 256 MB) vs today's official 500K commands/month, 250 MB. (4) A widely circulated 'Upstash $500 startup credits' claim (SaaSOffers) has no corresponding official page — no /startups, no startup section in pricing or FAQs. (5) Free Redis numbers changed from the old 10K/day+256MB form to 500K/month+250MB with 10 free databases; Vector is region-capped (N. Virginia, Ireland, Iowa) and Box runs only in AWS us-east-1.

provider: Hugging Face Spaces (Free) — Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment

findings.name: Free static Spaces hosting (unlimited)
findings.detail: Static Spaces (plain HTML, or built React/Svelte/Vue) are $0, free for everyone, unlimited in number, with no hardware charge and no card required. Default per-Space limits: 2 vCPU / 16 GB RAM / 50 GB non-persistent disk; CPU Basic (2 vCPU / 16 GB) has 'no hourly cost' but as of mid-2026 creating a compute Space (Gradio or Docker, incl. CPU Basic) requires a paid plan (PRO $9/mo personal; Team $20/Enterprise $50 per user for orgs). Static SDK Spaces never require a paid plan. All free for anonymous visitors too; no egress fee noted for Spaces.
findings.eligibility: Any account, free; no credit card, no age/region limit stated for static Spaces. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Create a Space with the Static SDK at huggingface.co/spaces -> 'Create new Space', push your site; it deploys free forever. Zero setup cost, card only needed if you later add paid hardware.
findings.expiry: Indefinite while account exists; auto-rebuild on each push. Space goes to sleep when idle.
findings.gotchas: As of ~July 2026 free accounts can no longer create Gradio/Docker compute Spaces (incl. free CPU Basic) — static only; CPU Basic downgrade from ZeroGPU also requires PRO. Non-persistent 50GB disk, 16GB RAM ceiling. PRO is $9/mo card-only; free tier has no hourly charge but compute creation is gated.

findings.name: ZeroGPU free GPU demos (host up to 2 Spaces + free usage quota)
findings.detail: ZeroGPU dynamically allocates NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell (half = 48GB VRAM 'large', full = 96GB 'xlarge', xlarge costs 2x quota). Free personal accounts 'in good standing' (verified email, account older than 30 days) can HOST up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces at $0. Visitors get daily GPU quotas: unauthenticated 2 min, free account 5 min, PRO 40 min (8x), Team 40 min, Enterprise 60 min; quota resets exactly 24h after first usage. Default per-call runtime 60s; over-quota usage $1 per 10 min, but only PRO/Team/Enterprise can extend (pre-paid credits). No card required for the free tier.
findings.eligibility: Free personal accounts: email verified + account >30 days old; Gradio SDK only; PyTorch-first (transformers/diffusers best). No .edu or startup requirement; no card required.
findings.claim: Create a Gradio Space with ZeroGPU hardware selected, decorate GPU code with @spaces.GPU, push; hosting is free for up to 2 such Spaces. Usage by any visitor is free within their daily 5-min (free account) quota.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; daily quota resets every 24h. PRO is $9/mo (card required) for 10 Spaces, 40 min quota and overage billing.
findings.gotchas: Free accounts cannot buy over-quota credits (paid tiers only). xlarge (96GB) burns 2x quota (45s task = 90s quota). After 2026 hardware migration some workloads auto-fell back to xlarge, doubling effective quota consumption (forum reports May 2026). Queue priority rises as your remaining daily quota falls. Gradio-only; Docker Spaces can't use ZeroGPU. Historically an undocumented run-count limit (~3 runs/day, staff-confirmed April 2026) may still apply on top of the 5-min time quota. A forum answer (July 2026) suggests new free accounts see ZeroGPU as the only creatable runtime — CPU Basic now PRO-gated.

findings.name: Community GPU grants (in-kind, rolling)
findings.detail: HF offers 'community GPU grants' for side projects: in-kind dedicated GPU hardware that ZeroGPU can't cover (non-PyTorch heavy init, models >96GB VRAM, always-on serving) or an extra Gradio Space beyond the free 2-Space cap without needing PRO. No dollar amount, duration or pool size published; decisions can take days; approved hardware attaches automatically (Static Spaces just flip SDK to gradio).
findings.eligibility: Public, open use cases — 'open research demo, hobbyist project, educational tool, institutional showcase' — that 'can't pay for the hardware'. No funding-cap or age limit; free account works; card not needed for the grant itself.
findings.claim: 1) Build your Space (ZeroGPU or Static). 2) Post a Community Tab discussion titled 'Apply for a GPU community grant: <Personal|Company|Academic> project' with a one-paragraph description + justification (default: 'Public open-source demo, can't cover the hardware cost'). 3) Wait for approval; hardware attaches automatically.
findings.expiry: Rolling, no published deadline; no published grant duration.
findings.gotchas: In-kind only, no cash; approval is discretionary and slow (days+); not a formal startup program; don't rely on a guaranteed quota.

findings.name: Hugging Face for Classrooms (free education workspace)
findings.detail: Free classroom-organization offering: teachers set up a shared workspace where students upload datasets, models and ML demos 'for free', with version control and student access controls (admin/read/write), teaching materials and support. 'Everything is free' per the page; no numeric repo/storage/GPU caps published.
findings.eligibility: Any classroom — students and teachers; no .edu verification gate stated, no card required, no institution-type minimum.
findings.claim: Create free at huggingface.co/classrooms ('Create a classroom for free', routed to /organizations/new?orgType=classroom); students join and host demos/datasets in the org workspace at $0.
findings.expiry: Indefinite while the classroom org exists.
findings.gotchas: Compute (GPU) is not part of the free classroom bundle — it's storage/hub hosting of repos, datasets, models and static demos; hardware upgrades are separate paid services. Limits not published, so heavy use could hit general free-tier storage limits.

findings.name: Academia Hub (education license — PAID, free only at partner universities)
findings.detail: Institution-level education plan: from $10/seat/month with volume discounts; minimum 250 annual seats; includes 1TB private + 1TB public storage per seat, $2/month/seat of compute credits (Inference Providers, Inference Endpoints, upgraded Spaces hardware, Jobs), higher daily ZeroGPU priority, SSO/SCIM/SOC 2. Students get nothing for free as individuals — HF staff confirmed there is no student Pro plan (Oct 2025 forum). Partner universities (e.g., ESCP, 12,000+ students) negotiate free access for their community.
findings.eligibility: University IT/procurement must initiate from a university email; individual .edu email is NOT enough. Free only at partner institutions that have negotiated a deal.
findings.claim: Contact HF from your university's IT/procurement team to negotiate; or at a partner university, your admin provisions your seat — then you get PRO-equivalent features + $2/mo compute credits free of personal cost.
findings.expiry: Subscription term, renews automatically; per-institution negotiation.
findings.gotchas: Not free for most students; the $2/mo compute credits are for paid seats the institution funds; minimum 250 seats excludes most small departments (Team plan suggested instead).

findings.name: Startup program: none first-party (third-party 'free PRO for startups' claims unverified)
findings.detail: No startup program exists on any Hugging Face owned page (checked Sep 2026 by a tracker; pricing/enterprise pages list only PRO/Team/Enterprise with no startup discount or application path). The well-known 2024 '$10M of GPUs' was a one-off commitment at ZeroGPU launch (its free quota persists, the $10M pool did not). Third-party perk marketplaces (creditforstartups, saasoffers, perq.sh) advertise 'up to $108 free PRO via partner perks' or '$1,000 in GPU credits' for HF — none of these could be verified against an HF-owned page; treat as unverified aggregator claims. The old '50% off Enterprise in year one' startup offer is no longer verifiable anywhere on HF's sites.
findings.eligibility: N/A for a first-party program; third-party perks claim pre-seed–Series A AI startups worldwide, referral from partner investor/accelerator, but terms aren't published by HF.
findings.claim: There is nothing to claim directly. Startups should use: free static Spaces + 2 free ZeroGPU Spaces per team member, the community GPU grant (in-kind), and generic cloud startup programs (AWS Activate, Google/Microsoft for Startups) for compute instead.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Beware unverified marketplace 'credits' (amounts unverifiable, may require equity/referral, may be expired promos). Meta x Hugging Face x Scaleway AI Startup Program (EU accelerator, 2nd cohort Sep 2024–Feb 2025) is now discontinued.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 material changes: (1) Mid-2026 (docs PR merged 2026-07-21; forum reports from 2026-07-09): creating compute Spaces — Gradio or Docker, including formerly-free CPU Basic — now requires a paid plan (PRO $9/mo personal, Team/Enterprise for orgs); free personal accounts were pushed to 'Static only, or up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces'. This materially shrank the free tier that previously let anyone run a free CPU Gradio Space. (2) 2026-06-29: ZeroGPU hosting formalized a free tier — 'accounts in good standing' (verified email, >30 days old) host up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces; PRO up to 10; paid orgs up to 50. Before this the free hosting cap/wording changed repeatedly. (3) December 2025: H100 / 8x H100 removed from the Spaces hardware lineup. (4) ZeroGPU hardware migrated from A100 (2024 launch) to NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell by 2026; post-migration some workloads silently fall back to xlarge, doubling quota consumption (forum reports May 2026). (5) No student plan has ever shipped; HF staff confirmed in Oct 2025 that Academia Hub is the only education path. (6) The $10M GPU pledge (May 2024, ZeroGPU launch, via A100s) was a one-off commitment — the durable free offer is the ZeroGPU daily quota, not a $ pool. (7) Payment gotcha: PRO is credit-card-only; India-issued cards are not yet supported (use AWS/Google Cloud Marketplace billing workaround). Free account and all free-tier usage require no card. No region limits on free usage found.

findings.name: Koyeb Startup Program — up to $30,000 in free compute credits
findings.detail: Up to $30,000 in free credits usable on Standard CPU and GPU instances (the application form also mentions Postgres databases per third-party trackers). Extras: solutions-engineer onboarding, dedicated Slack channel for priority support, white-glove migration, early access to new features, and extra resources/features/regions for startup accounts; the 2024 launch post also listed exclusive swag. Launched 2024-06-21 (Day 5 of Koyeb Launch Week). Still advertised on the official pricing page as of 2026-10-22 ('Early stage startup: Get up to $30k in credits...').
findings.eligibility: Seed-stage companies. Prioritized: (a) part of a Koyeb partner accelerator (new cohorts onboarded regularly) or (b) raised $1M-$5M from VCs. Bootstrapped / just-started companies are encouraged to apply and are reviewed case-by-case. No .edu requirement, no age cap, no stated region limit (global). No credit card required to apply; however, to use credits you need a Koyeb account, and new Koyeb signups must have a valid payment method and subscribe to a paid plan (Pro/Scale/Enterprise) since Feb 2026.
findings.claim: 1) Open the official program page (linked from koyeb.com/pricing) and click apply; the application form is at tally.so/r/w4kzad. 2) Fill in company website, founding year, funding, region, and how you plan to use Koyeb. 3) Koyeb's Startup Program team reviews and responds 'within the week.' 4) On approval, credits are applied to your Koyeb account for Standard CPU/GPU instances; you get solutions-engineer onboarding and a dedicated Slack channel.
findings.expiry: One-time credit grant on approval; the official page states no credit validity period or expiry date; program is ongoing and was verified still advertised on the official pricing page on 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: $30,000 is a ceiling — the actual amount is decided case-by-case after review. Program launched under standalone Koyeb (June 2024); Koyeb entered a definitive agreement to join Mistral AI on 2026-02-17, so terms/partners may change — re-check the official page before applying. Third-party trackers state new Koyeb users must be on a paid plan (Pro or above), i.e. credits ride on a paid account; the official post does not state this. No published credit expiry — rely on terms received at approval.

findings.name: Free Starter plan + 1 free 512 MB instance — grandfathered to existing organizations only
findings.detail: One free web Service per organization: 512 MB RAM, 0.1 vCPU, 2 GB SSD, deployable only in Frankfurt or Washington, D.C. It auto-scales to zero after 1 hour of no traffic (wakes in seconds on next request). Restrictions: cannot be used as a Worker Service, no custom scaling configuration, no persistent Volumes. The Starter plan itself is $0 pay-per-use: you're charged only for resources used beyond the free allowances (FAQ: outbound bandwidth 'not charged yet', 100 GB/mo free, then $0.04/GB — billing 'ahead of time' notice promised; custom domains free on paid plans). Since the Feb 2026 Mistral AI agreement, the Starter plan is closed to new signups; the pricing page lists only Pro ($29/mo + compute), Scale ($299/mo), and Enterprise ($1,000/mo+); new users sign up on Pro with a credit card and pro-rated charge. Existing Starter organizations keep their current terms.
findings.eligibility: Existing Koyeb organizations already on the free/Starter plan (grandfathered). NOT available to new accounts as of Feb 2026 — new signups require a credit card/payment method and a paid plan (Pro/Scale/Enterprise). No .edu requirement. Region-limited: free instance only in Frankfurt or Washington, D.C.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim — existing Starter orgs keep their free instance automatically. New users cannot obtain it: sign-up defaults to Pro with a $29 pre-authorization card hold plus pro-rated Pro charge; the docs FAQ still says Pro 'can be downgraded to the Starter plan at any time', but the post-Mistral FAQ flow restricts new signups to paid plans.
findings.expiry: No published sunset date for grandfathered free instances. Koyeb's own announcement says the platform will transition into a core component of Mistral Compute 'in the coming months'; third-party reporting (Aug 2026) quotes the FAQ as saying the Starter plan will be 'removed soon / in the coming months'. Export anything you'd miss; do not build long-term dependency.
findings.gotchas: Free instance limits: 1 per org, 1 of 2 regions, 512 MB RAM / 0.1 vCPU / 2 GB SSD, scale-to-zero after 1h idle, no Workers/volumes/custom scaling. Free outbound egress is 'not charged yet' (100 GB/mo allowance; $0.04/GB after) — can start with notice. Paid-plan extra bandwidth: $0.02/GB EU/US, $0.04/GB Asia. New signups: credit card mandatory ($29 pre-auth, immediate pro-rated Pro charge) — so the free tier is effectively no longer free-to-start for anyone new. Many 2024-2025 articles still describe a sign-up-able 'Hobby' free tier: stale. The old $5.50/mo free credit was already removed 2024-02-01.

findings.name: Free Serverless Postgres tier ('Free 5h'): $0/hr, 0.25 vCPU / 1 GB RAM / 1 GB storage, ~5 h active per day
findings.detail: Koyeb's Serverless Postgres has a free option priced $0/hr and $0/mo: 0.25 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 1 GB storage. The pricing page's activity schedule for it is 'Dev/Staging/CI environments (4h/day)' with scale-to-zero on inactivity; the docs FAQ describes it as 'one free PostgreSQL database limited to 5 hours of active time and 1 GB of storage.' 100% Postgres-compatible. Additional storage billed at $0.50/GB/month (the 1 GB attached to the free tier is included). One free Postgres is listed as included with plans.
findings.eligibility: Available with Koyeb plans (FAQ: free Postgres 'included with all plans'). In practice, new accounts today must sign up for a paid plan (Pro $29/mo + compute at minimum) with a valid credit card/payment method, so the free Postgres is effectively gated behind a Pro account for new users. No .edu requirement, no region limit stated.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for Koyeb (GitHub/Google SSO, passkey, or email; add a credit card — $29 pre-auth hold, pro-rated Pro charge). 2) Create a Serverless Postgres database and select the free / 'Free 5h' option ($0/hr). 3) Set the activity schedule to Dev/Staging/CI (4 h/day) so it pauses outside active hours.
findings.expiry: Ongoing as of 2026-10-22; no expiry stated on official pages. The database auto-pauses after the daily active hours (4-5 h/day); you get one free Postgres per org.
findings.gotchas: Explicitly for dev/staging/CI, not production: only ~4-5 hours of active time per day. New users need a credit card and pay the Pro base fee ($29/mo + compute) even to use the $0 Postgres — it is not a no-card, no-cost onboarding path for new accounts. Egress beyond plan allowance is billed ($0.02/GB EU/US; $0.04/GB Asia). The 0.25 vCPU/1 GB tier is small — heavy dev DBs will be latency-bound.

findings.name: Student / education offers — none exist (absence confirmed)
findings.detail: Koyeb has no education license, student program, or .edu-based offer. The official pricing page, pricing FAQ, and docs contain no education section or student discount; student-perks trackers (e.g., freEDU) do not list any Koyeb student offer. Students get the same terms as any user: new accounts require a credit card and a paid plan (Pro/Scale/Enterprise); the only zero-cost options are the grandfathered free 512 MB instance (existing orgs only) and the $0 Postgres tier (requires CC + paid plan for new users). The Startup Program is the only real free credit program, and it is company-level (early-stage startups), not school-affiliated.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no student offer exists. .edu email confers nothing at Koyeb.
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Anyone advertising 'Koyeb free for students' is citing stale or fabricated terms; verify only against koyeb.com official pages.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: (1) 2026-02-17: Koyeb entered a definitive agreement to join Mistral AI (Mistral's first acquisition, undisclosed price; Koyeb's 3 co-founders + 13 employees joined Mistral's engineering team in March 2026). The Koyeb platform continues operating and is transitioning to become a core component of 'Mistral Compute'. Material consequence: new users can only sign up for paid plans (Pro $29/mo + compute, Scale $299/mo, Enterprise $1,000/mo+) with a valid payment method; the free Starter plan was closed to new signups and Koyeb's FAQ says it will be removed 'soon / in the coming months' (no date published). Grandfathered free instances for existing orgs remain in effect as of 2026-10-22, but the official wording ('in the coming months') makes this a sunset-pending offer — export workloads. (2) 2025-03: free instances changed to automatically scale to zero after 1 hour of inactivity (cost-sustaining change). (3) The $30k Startup Program has NOT been publicly sunset; it was verified still advertised on the official pricing page on 2026-10-22, but its terms (partner accelerators, credit amounts, response SLAs) were set pre-acquisition and may change under Mistral AI — treat as at-risk. (4) Context from before 2025: the old $5.50/month free credit was removed from all accounts 2024-02-01 and replaced by the free instance type; GPU prices were cut up to 24% on Nov 7, 2025 (A100/H100/L40S). Sources: https://www.koyeb.com/blog/koyeb-is-joining-mistral-ai-to-build-the-future-of-ai-infrastructure , https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/17/mistral-ai-buys-koyeb-in-first-acquisition-to-back-its-cloud-ambitions/ , https://www.koyeb.com/changelog , https://www.koyeb.com/blog/koyeb-for-startups-accelerate-with-credits-for-high-performance-infrastructure , https://www.koyeb.com/pricing , https://www.koyeb.com/docs/faqs/pricing , https://www.koyeb.com/docs/reference/instances

findings.name: Free Starter tier (no subscription, no claim needed)
findings.detail: Replit's free plan is called the Starter tier. Per official docs: 1 free published app (Lite build or Design Canvas) whose link automatically goes down after 30 days; daily Agent/AI chat credits 'up to a monthly cap' (exact numbers not published); monthly cloud credits covering databases, object storage, and publishing; 0 active background tasks; 0 collaboration seats; Lite build only (full builds require Core); 'Made with Replit' badge cannot be removed; third-party connectors, AI integrations, Plan Mode and non-web/mobile artifact types require Core/Pro. The /edu/students marketing page lists the free tier as 'Unlimited public apps, Replit AI basic, community support, build on any device' — note this conflicts with the docs' 1-published-app limit. Current paid reference points (replit.com/pricing, read today): Core $20/mo ($18/mo billed annually), Pro $100/mo ($90/mo billed annually).
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a free Replit account; no student/startup status required; no credit card requirement is stated on the plan docs or pricing page.
findings.claim: Sign up free at replit.com; the Starter tier is the default. No verification or application needed.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; published free app links auto-take-down after 30 days; AI agent chat is on a daily cap with a monthly cap; cloud credits reset monthly.
findings.gotchas: The single free published app expires after 30 days and requires Core ($20/mo) to publish additional/longer-lived apps. Once included Agent credits are exhausted, usage-based (effort-based) pricing and credit packs apply — pay-as-you-go overages, not a hard stop. Data transfer, databases and compute are billed usage-based on top of monthly cloud credits (docs: Publishing and Database Billing). Marketing 'unlimited public apps' vs docs '1 published app (30-day)' is a real discrepancy to verify in-account.

findings.name: Student discount: 50% off Replit Core (~$10/mo vs $20/mo) with verified .edu email
findings.detail: Official /edu/students page (text via search index; page is JS-rendered): 'Free to start. 50% off Core with your .edu email.' Core is $20/mo, so students pay ~$10/mo, auto-applied at checkout when the account email is recognized as academic — no coupon, no GitHub Student Pack, no document upload. Core unlocks 10x more AI compute, faster builds, more CPU/RAM, private projects, and priority support on top of Starter. Launched Sept 19, 2025; early reports described it as '$10/mo for the first six months', but the current official page states no time cap or renewal requirement.
findings.eligibility: Currently enrolled student with a valid academic email (.edu or equivalent institutional domain); .edu convention is US-centric — non-US students may need to confirm with Replit support. Discount is tied to the account email, so existing accounts must add/switch to the student email. No funding/age restrictions (it's a student, not startup, program). No credit card requirement stated for verification; a payment method is of course needed to pay for Core.
findings.claim: 1) Visit replit.com/edu/students (or sign up at replit.com/signup using your .edu email). 2) Create/sign in to a Replit account with the academic email. 3) Verify the email via the confirmation link. 4) Go to replit.com/pricing, choose Core — the 50% student price (~$10/mo) is auto-applied at checkout.
findings.expiry: No end date or duration stated on the official page as of late 2026; discount reportedly was 6 months at launch (Sept 2025) and is now advertised without a time cap. Re-verify eligibility at renewal; the school must keep issuing the academic email.
findings.gotchas: Discount applies to Core only, not to extra credit packs or Pro. September 2026 community reports (replit.discourse.group) of .edu-verified accounts NOT getting the discount at checkout, and a support form that requires an active paid subscription — a closed loop. Not combinable in writing with yearly billing (the pricing page does not say yearly + student stack). Region: .edu verification is US-centric; non-US academic domains may fail auto-detection.

findings.name: Replit Startup Program: up to $25,000 in Replit credits; free year of Replit Pro for other venture-backed founders
findings.detail: Official replit.com/startups page (FAQ JSON-LD read today): 'Startups backed by a Select Partner (e.g. a16z, Khosla, SVB) qualify for up to $25,000 in Replit credits. If your fund isn't listed yet, you can still apply — we review every application.' Page meta: 'Startups backed by a Select Partner qualify for up to $25,000 in Replit credits; other venture-backed founders get a free year of Replit Pro. Apply in minutes.' Credits cover compute, deployments, Replit Agent (AI-assisted development) and all Pro features. A free year of Pro (currently $100/mo) is worth ~$1,200. Confirmed in the FAQ: credits are valid 12 months from approval; Pro subscription remains active as long as the partnership is in effect. For VC/accelerator funds: partnering with Replit is free; a partner application form exists on the page.
findings.eligibility: Venture-backed startups (no stated age, funding-cap or headcount limit). 'Select Partner' status (fund listed in the page's logo grid, e.g. a16z, Khosla, SVB) => up to $25K credits; other venture-backed founders => free year of Replit Pro. Unlisted funds can still apply and are reviewed case by case. No credit-card requirement stated (page says apply in minutes). Region limits: not stated.
findings.claim: 1) Go to replit.com/startups. 2) Check the Select Partner logo grid for your investor. 3) Submit the application form ('Apply to the Replit Startup Program', targets replit.com signup) — takes minutes. 4) Replit confirms eligibility at application approval; credits land on the account. Funds can apply via the VC partner form instead.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months from date of approval. Pro subscription (for the free-year tier) stays active as long as the startup–partner fund relationship is in effect. No published program end date.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free trap: if you already have an existing Core or Pro subscription, you receive the equivalent in credits INSTEAD of the free trial (FAQ). 'Up to $25K' — actual amount per approval, not guaranteed to every Select-Partner startup. Credits expire 12 months after approval. The Select Partner list is on the JS-rendered page and can change; verify your fund is actually listed before assuming $25K.

findings.name: Replit for Education: free Replit for verified educators + credits for students (teacher/education license)
findings.detail: Official replit.com/edu page: 'Teach the AI generation. Free Replit for verified educators. Credits for your students. Curriculum, templates, and 1:1 onboarding.' Also: 'Run Replit on your campus' — host events, earn commissions on signups, direct access to the Replit team. Page meta (read today): 'Replit equips students, educators, and campus leaders to build real apps with AI — no setup, no busywork. Free to start, trusted by top universities.' The exact plan tier given to verified educators (presumed free Core or Pro) and the amount of student credits are not published on the page (JS-rendered; body not extractable), so specifics must be confirmed via the education application flow.
findings.eligibility: Educators (teacher verification implied); students of those educators receive program credits. No .edu requirement stated for educators on the page; 'verified' process handles it. No credit card required for the free educator tier.
findings.claim: 1) Visit replit.com/edu. 2) Apply for educator access (verified-educator flow, plus curriculum/templates/1:1 onboarding offered). 3) Students in the program get credits; campus programs earn commissions on signups.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal terms published on the page.
findings.gotchas: Amounts are not publicly quantified — do not assume $120/yr or a specific plan tier; confirm at application. This is a separate offer from the .edu 50% student discount (a student with a .edu email gets the 50% Core discount regardless; an educator's classroom 'credits for your students' is a distinct programmatic offer).

findings.name: One-time free Agent checkpoint (trial credit for new accounts)
findings.detail: Per official AI billing docs: 'All subscribers receive one-time free Agent checkpoints.' This is Replit's only documented trial credit: new users get their first Agent work checkpoint free, after which effort-based (usage-based) pricing applies — simple tasks cost less than complex builds, one checkpoint per request, and third-party model calls (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) are billed at provider public API rates, deducted from Replit credits.
findings.eligibility: Any new Replit account/user (no student or startup status needed). No credit card requirement stated in the docs.
findings.claim: Just start Replit Agent on a new account — the first checkpoint is free automatically; nothing to apply for.
findings.expiry: One-time per account, not renewable.

findings.name: Puter.js user-pays developer offer: $0 infrastructure, no API keys
findings.detail: docs.puter.com and developer.puter.com (read 2026-10-22): developers pay $0 for infrastructure regardless of end-user count ('Whether your app has 1 user or 1 million users, it costs you zero to run'). End users cover their own AI/cloud consumption via their Puter account; 'each user gets pre-allocated resources' and every user 'starts with a free monthly allowance' (amount shown in usage dashboard, resets monthly, no rollover; purchased credits never expire). SDK exposes 500+ AI models (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok, etc.), cloud storage (puter.fs), serverless NoSQL KV (puter.kv), auth, serverless workers — via one script tag (https://js.puter.com/v2/), no API keys. Claims 80K+ developers, 130K+ apps, 400K+ installations. Matches the known baseline of in-browser IDE + instant live URL + user-pays model.
findings.eligibility: Any developer can use Puter.js free; no credit card, no company age/funding cap, no .edu requirement. Abuse is handled user-side ('abusers pay for themselves'), not via developer-side CAPTCHA or developer-side rate limits.
findings.claim: Add <script src="https://js.puter.com/v2/"></script> (or npm @heyputer/puter.js) to your app; auth, storage, KV, AI and worker deployment work under the user's Puter account at $0 cost to you.
findings.expiry: No stated end date; free developer cost is architectural (user-pays), not a time-boxed trial.
findings.gotchas: Not a fixed credit grant: the free allowance amount is only visible per-user in the dashboard, not published. Free-tier caps apply to each end user's account (see quotas finding) — heavy users will hit limits or need paid plans themselves. Developer 'infra $0' claim excludes nothing else (e.g. no SLA stated).

findings.name: Free-tier quotas & rate limits (Puter.js accounts) — exact published numbers
findings.detail: docs.puter.com/rate-limits-and-quotas/ (read 2026-10-22). Free (per user, per minute unless noted): AI 30 req/10s, 3 concurrent; KV get/set 400/10s, list 120/min, key 1 KB, value 400 KB; filesystem quota 100 MiB, write 120/min, stat 600/min; sites/workers: subdomain create 60/min, worker deploy 80/min, 5 concurrent workers; email 600 sends/min (but sendTransactional() paid-only); teams: 1 team/account, 3 free seats for owner; live connections 200/account; relay tokens 30/min; handler chain 4 runs. Free->paid deltas exist (e.g. AI 30->200 req/10s, concurrency 3->20, live connections 200->400). Usage credit: free monthly allowance resets monthly, no rollover; purchased credits never expire.
findings.eligibility: All free Puter.js accounts; same free allowance regardless of tier per docs.
findings.claim: No claim step beyond creating a free Puter account; limits apply automatically and are documented at docs.puter.com/rate-limits-and-quotas/.
findings.expiry: Ongoing published schedule; credit portion resets monthly, no rollover.
findings.gotchas: Numbers are rate limits, not volumes — a 100 MiB free FS quota vs 25 MB on the marketing pricing page is a metering discrepancy (plan storage vs JS quota) that can confuse budgeting. Paid-only: transactional email, anyone-with-link shares. Event delivery has micro-cent costs (broadcast 10 µ¢/delivery, single 100 µ¢) and no-credit backlogs are deleted after 1 h.

findings.name: Val Town Free plan — unlimited public vals at $0/mo
findings.detail: Perpetual $0/mo free tier. Verified today on val.town/pricing and docs.val.town/faq: unlimited public vals, 100,000 runs/day, 15-min cron intervals, 1-min wall clock time per run, 3 days log retention, no custom domains, 'email yourself', MCP integration, CLI (vt), and a SQLite database + S3 blob storage (every val got a database on 2026-01-23). docs.val.town/vals/limitations adds: max 1,000 files per val, max 100 branches per val, 0 private/unlisted vals on Free (Pro: unlimited private). Paid context: Pro $25/mo or $21/mo billed yearly; Business $200/mo or $167/mo billed yearly. No egress/bandwidth cap is published for any plan; no per-user seat cap stated for Free. For comparison, free Pro trial: none found.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone; no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no region limits stated on any official page. No credit card required for the free plan (free signup is via GitHub/Google/email at val.town/auth/signup; the page itself returned 403 to the fetcher, so this is inferred from the FAQ's 'you can start using Val Town on a Free account' and the absence of any billing step on the free column — Pro checkout is Stripe-based).
findings.claim: Sign up free at https://val.town/auth/signup (no billing step), then deploy serverless JS/TS vals to a val.town subdomain (yourname.val.town) with one-click forking of existing vals, or run `npx vt` / the MCP server. Free plan is automatic; no code or application needed.
findings.expiry: No expiry; perpetual free plan. Logs retained only 3 days on Free. No renewal step — free stays free until downgraded/changed by Val Town.
findings.gotchas: Free users get 0 private/unlisted vals — everything is public; private vals require Pro ($21-25/mo). 1-min wall clock per run and 100k runs/day are hard caps. No bandwidth/egress numbers published (limits page exists for 'granular details' per the pricing page but docs pages fetched gave no egress figures). Val Town runs built-in AI per-user-pay (see separate finding). Free tier is user-pays for AI, not a trial — it is genuinely $0 with no time limit.

findings.name: Free tier includes $1/mo Townie (AI) credit; AI usage is pay-per-use after
findings.detail: As of the June 11, 2025 'Townie Credits' post, Val Town's built-in AI coding agent (Townie) is pay-per-use with a 50% markup over raw LLM cost (example: $10 of Townie spend -> $6.66 to Anthropic, $3.33 to Val Town), decoupled from the Pro subscription. The Free plan includes $1/mo of Townie credit; Pro includes $10/mo; Business $100/mo (confirmed today on docs.val.town/faq and docs.val.town/guides/prompting/townie). A 2026-07-02 changelog states 'Townie 5x cheaper'; 2026-01-22 'Townie v5' runs on Val Town MCP with Claude 4.5 (and newer model list includes Opus 5, GLM, DeepSeek variants). Check spend via the /cost and /context slash commands.
findings.eligibility: Everyone on the Free plan gets the $1/mo credit automatically; no .edu, no application, no credit card needed for the $1 included amount. Additional AI use is pay-per-use (user pays), so effectively a $1/mo free allowance on top of the $0 hosting tier.
findings.claim: Automatic: sign up free, open Townie in the val editor; the $1/mo credit is applied. Top-up/purchase flow for more credits is not documented on the official pages I could reach.
findings.source_url: https://docs.val.town/guides/prompting/townie (credit amounts corroborated: https://docs.val.town/faq; pay-per-use mechanics: https://blog.val.town/townie-credits/)
findings.expiry: $1 credit renews monthly while on the Free plan; pay-per-use has 'no limits' per the 2025 post but costs real money beyond the included credit. Model availability changes over time (Townie v5, 2026 model list).
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free nuance: the $1/mo is a standing free allowance, not a one-time trial. Once it's exhausted, AI calls bill the user at ~1.5x raw LLM cost — a free user hammering Claude Opus can rack up spend. 'No custom domains' and the 1-min run wall clock also constrain what the free AI-built app can do.

sunset_notes: No education license and no startup program exist on Val Town as of 2026-10-22: /students, /education, and /startup on val.town all 404; docs.val.town's sitemap (fetched today) contains no pricing/education/student/credit pages; the FAQ and pricing page mention no student/startup discounts; the full blog archive (blog.val.town, fetched today) has zero education/student posts. Nothing was sunset in 2025-2026 that I could find. Material changes that did happen: (1) 2025-06-11 Townie switched to pay-per-use 'Townie Credits' at a 50% markup over raw LLM cost and was decoupled from the Pro plan (previously Townie access came with Pro); (2) 2026-07-02 changelog 'Townie 5x cheaper'; (3) 2026-01-22 Townie v5 (MCP + Claude 4.5) and 2026-01-23 every val gets its own database; (4) Plan pricing: Pro $25/mo ($21/mo yearly), Business $200/mo ($167/mo yearly). Caveat: the session's web-search budget was exhausted, so this absence check relied on the official site's own pages (sitemap, pricing, FAQ, limitations, townie guide, full blog archive) rather than a global search; a niche startup program announced only in social media would not have been caught. WebFetch of val.town/auth/signup was blocked (403), so the no-credit-card-for-free claim rests on the FAQ wording and the pricing page's free-column structure, not direct observation of the form.

provider: DigitalOcean (VPS / startup credits; fronts: VPS, bare-metal & dedicated)

findings.name: DigitalOcean Startups program (formerly Hatch) — startup credits
findings.detail: 12 months of DigitalOcean credits; amount 'varies' per startup/partner and is stated only in the onboarding email, with a general $10,000/month consumption cap (usage beyond the cap in a month is charged at published prices). Credits cover nearly all DO services (Droplets/VPS, App Platform, Kubernetes, Spaces, managed databases, CPU bare metal) but as of 2026-05-13 EXCLUDE: GPU Droplets, NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, Dedicated Inference, Serverless Inference, third-party AI models outside DO infrastructure (incl. Anthropic/OpenAI), Paperspace Machines, Cloudways, and pass-through third-party charges. GPU credits are a separate, by-invitation benefit ('Early-Stage Boost'). Also includes 15 months of free Standard-tier paid support, expert 1:1s with DO PMs/engineers, Marketplace access, and a Welcome Kit partner perks: Stripe Atlas 20% off, Shortcut 2 months free, Cloud66 $500, Ovvy 90 days free, QuickNode up to $5,000, Bolster $1,000, Mercury $500 cash on $50k deposit, Airtable $2,000, Notion $1,000, HubSpot up to 90% off year one, Miro $1,000, Chargebee free until $1M revenue, 100ms $2,500. Migration assistance/credits for moving customers from other clouds (amounts unpublished).
findings.eligibility: Must have raised $10M or less total funding; product/digital startups only (service-based businesses: agencies, consulting, web/app dev firms are not eligible); AI-native startups are prioritized but AI is not required; corporate website with a matching company-domain email required (personal email fails); a registered DigitalOcean team account (company email, not personal) required; applicants must be new to DO credits (no prior DO credit use); a valid credit card must be on file; no geographic restrictions published (global). No .edu or enrollment requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Create a DO team account with a company email and valid credit card. 2) Apply at digitalocean.com/startups (about 10-minute application; if unaffiliated with a partner organization, select 'Other'), or via an approved partner (VCs, accelerators, incubators — Techstars is a 2026 premier partner). 3) Acceptance at DO's sole discretion; your credit amount arrives in the onboarding email; benefits are distributed through approved partners.
findings.expiry: Credits end exactly 12 months from acceptance; unused credits are forfeited and are not transferable; no extensions, no renewal mechanism (program term fixed at 12 months per ToS, last updated 2026-05-11). DO may change or discontinue the program at any time. Termination events (crypto mining, IPO, insolvency, prohibited change of control) end all benefits immediately and any fees owed become due.
findings.gotchas: Headline credit amount is not published ('varies') — the Jan 2025 Hatch press release claimed up to $100,000 in compute credits, but the current page no longer advertises any total; budget against the $10,000/month cap, not a headline number. GPU/inference/third-party AI models are excluded as of 2026-05-13 — a major gotcha for AI workloads. Overage beyond the monthly cap and beyond Droplet bandwidth allowances is billed. Powered-off Droplets still bill. Egress beyond the included bandwidth allowance costs extra. No free trial exists for bare-metal or dedicated servers; they are covered only if your credits apply and usage stays under the monthly cap (bare-metal CPUs eligible; bare-metal GPUs excluded).

findings.name: New-account signup credit ($5 / 90 days)
findings.detail: New team accounts automatically receive a $5 credit applied to the first team; valid for 90 days after signup. The pricing page states your card will not be charged until the credit is exhausted or the 90-day window lapses (e.g., spending $3 in the window means no charge).
findings.eligibility: All new DigitalOcean accounts; no .edu, student or startup requirement; no region limit published; a payment method (card) IS required before creating resources — so this is a trial credit, not a no-card free tier.
findings.claim: Sign up for a DigitalOcean account, add a payment card; the $5 credit is applied automatically to the first team. No application needed.
findings.expiry: 90 days from signup.
findings.gotchas: Card required (not free-tier in the no-CC sense). $5 covers roughly 1-2 months of the cheapest $4/mo Droplet; anything beyond it bills immediately. Historically larger trials (e.g. $100-$200/60-day offers) are not shown on the current pricing page as of 2026-10-22.

findings.name: Always-free tier items (no perpetual free VPS)
findings.detail: Perpetually free with any account: 3 free static sites on App Platform (~1 GiB outbound/mo each); 90,000 GiB-seconds/mo free on DO Functions with no charge for invocations; Container Registry free with 1 repository and 500 MiB storage; unlimited VPCs at no cost with free ingress data transfer to VPCs; Droplets include free outbound data transfer starting at 500 GiB/mo; free reserved IPs when assigned to a Droplet; free DNS; free Cloud Firewalls; free basic monitoring/alerts; 1 uptime check/mo; free email support tier. Managed databases and basic Droplets are NOT free (start at $15/mo and $4/mo respectively). No free-trial offer for bare metal or dedicated servers appears anywhere on the pricing page.
findings.eligibility: All DigitalOcean account holders; no .edu, no startup requirement; payment method still required for any billable resource.
findings.claim: Included automatically with any account; no application or claim step.
findings.expiry: No expiry (ongoing free allowances).
findings.gotchas: Droplets themselves are never free — so there is no free VPS; 'free outbound transfer starting at 500 GiB/mo' scales with the Droplet plan. Static-site free tier egress is ~1 GiB/mo per site; larger traffic bills. VPC peering between datacenters is $0.01/GiB (intra-DC free). Powered-off Droplets continue to bill.

findings.name: Ad-hoc university partnership grants (case-by-case, not a general education license)
findings.detail: DigitalOcean makes individual university grants: e.g. the University of Arizona Eller MIS Department (announced July 2025) partners with DO to provide unlimited cloud resources to students in one master's-level cloud computing class for the duration of the semester. This is a bespoke grant, not a claimable .edu program.
findings.eligibility: Only students in specific partner classes/programs, at the discretion of the DO-teacher partnership; no general .edu email or student verification pathway exists as of 2026-10-22 (the old GitHub Student Pack credit is gone — see sunset notes).
findings.claim: No public application; arises only when a professor/department negotiates with DigitalOcean.
findings.expiry: Per-partnership (e.g., one semester in the Eller case).
findings.gotchas: Not renewable, not generally available, not tied to .edu emails; the former blanket student offer ($200 via GitHub Student Developer Pack) was discontinued.

sunset_notes: Major 2025-2026 changes: (1) HATCH RETIRED — the Hatch brand was retired and replaced by the "DigitalOcean Startups" program; the Hatch ToS now only point to a prior version of the Startups ToS (Startups ToS last updated May 11, 2026; third-party guides place the brand retirement on May 11, 2026). The Jan 2025 Hatch offer of "up to $100,000 in compute credits + up to 3 months free GPU usage" (announced Jan 22, 2025) is no longer the current offer — the current page says credit amount 'varies' with a $10,000/month cap and unpublished totals. (2) STUDENT CREDIT ENDED — DigitalOcean exited the GitHub Student Developer Pack; students were told around July 1, 2026 that DO was "winding down the program" and "ending their participation in the GitHub Student Developer Pack"; ALL Student Pack promotional credits, including ones already redeemed that had run a full year, expired universally on July 31, 2026 (retroactive cutoff). From June 8, 2026 the credit had already excluded GPU Droplets, H100 Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, DO Inference, third-party AI models, Paperspace and Cloudways. There is no replacement DigitalOcean student/education license as of 2026-10-22. (3) CREDIT COVERAGE NARROWED — as of May 13, 2026 the Startups program credits explicitly exclude Dedicated/Serverless Inference, third-party AI models, Paperspace Machines, Cloudways and Bare Metal GPUs (in addition to the earlier GPU Droplet/H100 exclusions), and the page now states the $10,000/month cap. (4) A limit reduction was recorded around 2026-04-07 (narrowed signup-credit terms; low confidence, from a third-party changelog). (5) No free bare-metal or dedicated-server trial, no perpetual free VPS tier, and no no-credit-card offer exists as of 2026-10-22 — a payment card is required for every DO offer above.

As of 2026-10-22, no active official free offer (trial credit, free tier, education license, or startup program) for Hetzner Cloud / VPS / dedicated servers could be verified on any official page; the historically reported ~EUR 20 new-customer cloud trial (promo-code based, no credit card to start) appears to have been sunset: (1) https://www.hetzner.com/cloud/trial — the URL now serves the generic Hetzner Cloud landing page (SPA fallback), with zero mention of a trial, credit, or promo code; (2) https://www.hetzner.com/cloud/education, /cloud/startup, and /cloud/promo all render the same general landing page — no dedicated education or startup program pages exist; (3) https://www.hetzner.com/community/trial is a hard 404; (4) docs.hetzner.com (top-level and overview pages) contain no trial/credit/education/startup content. The landing page's only pricing statements today are catalog floors: Cost-Optimized from EUR 5.99/mo, Regular Performance from EUR 6.49/mo, General Purpose from EUR 43.49/mo (excl. VAT), locations Germany/Finland/Singapore/USA — i.e., no permanent free tier. The ~EUR 20 trial is likely discontinued (not just undocumented), since its canonical URL is dead; however, web search was unavailable in this session (shared 200-call budget exhausted by sibling agents), so any 2025-2026 sunset announcement date could not be pinned down — confidence in the exact end date is low, confidence that no active official free offer is currently advertised is high (read every candidate official page today). Caveat: Hetzner has run occasional time-boxed promo campaigns in the past (referral/affiliates, console banners); an ephemeral campaign could exist without a dedicated page, but none is advertised anywhere on hetzner.com today.

provider: Replit (Starter free tier) — Frontend hosting, PaaS & app deployment

findings.name: Starter free plan (current as of 2026-10-22)
findings.detail: $0/mo, no dollar figure listed ('available at no cost'). Includes: (1) daily-reset Agent credits with a monthly cap (no public numbers — check Settings → Usage); (2) monthly credits for production databases, object storage, and publishing (autoscale/static) that reset each month and do NOT roll over; (3) exactly 1 free published app that auto-expires 30 days after publishing and carries a 'Made with Replit' referral badge (badge removal requires Core); app can be re-published; (4) 'Lite build' only — Full build (autonomous agent), design-to-artifact backend conversion, third-party connectors (Google, Stripe, Replit AI Integrations), Plan Mode, and non-web/mobile artifact types all require Core/Pro. Resource facts: development databases are free on every app with 20 GiB free dev storage (50 GiB on Pro/Enterprise); production PostgreSQL storage capped at 1 GiB on Starter; static hosting is free but outbound transfer bills at $0.05/GB; autoscale is $2/mo base + $0.60/million compute units + $0.40/million requests once credits run out; object storage $0.015/GiB/mo + $0.05/GiB transfer + $0.0004–0.005/thousand ops with a 7-day minimum billing floor; 'Made with Replit' referrals earn credits only after upgrading to a paid plan.
findings.eligibility: Any Replit account (email or Google/GitHub OAuth signup); no .edu email, no student status, no region limit stated in docs. Credit card: NOT stated on any current official page — free-plan signup has historically required no card; a card/payment method is only involved when you buy credit packs or subscribe to Core/Pro. Treat 'no card required' as true-but-unconfirmed-in-current-docs.
findings.claim: Create a free account at replit.com — you are on Starter automatically, no card step. Publish up to 1 app; view live credit caps in Settings → Usage; upgrade via replit.com/settings/billing when you hit limits.
findings.expiry: Agent credits reset daily; monthly cloud credits reset each month (no rollover); the free published app goes down 30 days after publishing (re-publish to extend; each republish resets the window).
findings.gotchas: Legacy numbers circulating for Starter (1,200 agent/dev minutes per month ≈ 40/day, 100 AI completions, 0.5 vCPU / 1 GB RAM / 2 GB disk) no longer appear on any official page I read today — the platform moved to a credits + Free Mode system in 2025–2026, so those figures are likely stale. Egress/autoscale/object-storage can produce real charges if your free app gets traffic (outbound data $0.05/GB has no stated free allowance). Routines and heavy agent work need paid credits. 'No card' is not explicitly documented today.

findings.name: Free Mode on the free Starter plan (launched 2026-08-18, OpenAI partnership)
findings.detail: Free Mode is a no-cost Agent mode using 'intelligent model routing' (model picked by Replit; per the announcement, powered by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Luna). It is available on Starter, Core, and Pro. Core users get 'up to 30 hours per month of chat' in Free Mode and up to 60 projects in Free Mode; Pro gets even larger allowances; the allowance on Core/Pro 'refreshes every five hours'. On the free Starter plan Free Mode also applies but Replit publishes no number — the docs say only 'Your Free Mode limits depend on your plan' and point to Settings → Usage. Routines cannot run in Free Mode (they need a per-run paid budget). Free Mode replaces everyday work that previously consumed credits: 'everyday tasks will no longer use credits'; the older Economy Mode was renamed Power Mode at the same cost.
findings.eligibility: All accounts including the free Starter plan; no card needed for Free Mode itself; no regional or education gating stated.
findings.claim: It is the default Agent experience — just chat/build; when the 5-hour or daily allowance is exhausted Replit warns you before a request shifts to a paid mode (Power/Max). Monitor the counter in Settings → Usage.
findings.expiry: Allowance refreshes every 5 hours (Core/Pro) and daily (Starter); Free Mode shipped Aug 18–19, 2026 and is ongoing.
findings.gotchas: No model picker in Free Mode (auto routing only); Starter's exact allowance is not public; Free Mode excludes Routines, Plan Mode (Core-only), and third-party AI integrations (paid, billed at provider API rates from your credits).

findings.name: Replit Startup Program — 'Up to $25K in Credits'
findings.detail: A live official page exists at replit.com/startups with the title 'Startup Program: Up to $25K in Credits | Replit'. The page body is client-rendered: two independent fetches on 2026-10-22 returned only the <title> with no body text, so I could NOT confirm eligibility (company age, funding cap, headcount), the credit breakdown, the program's duration, or the application form. Nothing in the docs index (llms.txt) or the blog sitemap references the program. Headline claim from the title alone: up to $25,000 in Replit credits for qualifying startups.
findings.eligibility: Unconfirmed. Almost certainly early-stage startup-focused (page is a gated application), but age/funding/employee caps were not readable today. No .edu component visible.
findings.claim: Apply via the form at replit.com/startups (page loads in a normal browser; details are JS-rendered, so a WebFetch/markdown reader sees nothing). Verify current terms in the rendered page before relying on the $25K figure.
findings.expiry: Unknown — no duration or sunset date visible on the page.
findings.gotchas: Page has no server-rendered content, so any details beyond the title are unverified; credits (not cash) are what's offered, and credit packs purchased on Replit expire 6 months after purchase — check whether program credits share that rule. Trial-vs-free: these are credits, not a free plan.

findings.name: Education / student and teacher program — not found (likely sunset)
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 Replit has no publicly offered education-specific free offer: replit.com/education and replit.com/classroom both return HTTP 404; the docs index (llms.txt) contains zero 'education', 'student', 'teacher', 'classroom', 'startup' or 'trial' paths; and replit.com/pricing has no education or startup discount section. The only education-adjacent asset is learn.replit.com, a free self-serve course platform (e.g., 'AI foundations' 30 min/7 lessons, 'Enterprise foundations' 30 min/6 lessons, two courses 'coming soon') with no .edu gate, no free paid seats, and no teacher/classroom entitlements. Historical context: Repl.it's classrooms product and 'student overview' teacher-dashboard features (closed beta ~2016, docs updated Oct 2023) are no longer represented on current official pages.
findings.eligibility: n/a — nothing claimable as a student/teacher offer today; learn.replit.com courses are open to anyone, no .edu email required.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim: sign up at learn.replit.com for free courses if the courses themselves are the goal.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Absence-based finding: 404s + missing docs entries + unannotated pricing page, checked today. Replit's old teacher/student classroom program (free paid-tier seats for teachers) appears to have been retired or folded into the credit-based plans; if you still need .edu perks, Replit currently does not publish any.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes (all verified against official pages fetched 2026-10-22): (1) Effort-based (usage-based) Agent pricing replaced flat per-unit Agent billing for new signups 2025-06-18, rolled out to everyone ~2025-07-02; each Agent checkpoint now costs by resources consumed (from ~$0.06 to multiple dollars). This is why the legacy Starter figures (1,200 agent minutes/mo, 100 AI completions, 0.5 vCPU/1GB RAM/2GB disk, "40 min/day") no longer appear on official pages — that system is effectively superseded by daily Agent credits + Free Mode. (2) One-time migration gift: $10 in free Replit credits was auto-applied to all active accounts that used the new pricing model (July 2025) — a one-off, not a recurring trial; also the docs still say "all subscribers receive one-time free Agent checkpoints" (quantity not published). (3) Paid lineup was rebranded to Core ($20/mo, $18 annual, $20/mo model credits) and Pro ($100/mo, $90 annual, $100/mo model credits) + Enterprise; the old "Builder"/"Team" naming is gone. (4) 2026-08-18: Free Mode launched with an OpenAI partnership (GPT-5.6 Luna); Economy Mode renamed Power Mode; Core Free Mode capped at ~30 hours chat/month, refreshing every 5 hours. (5) Education: /education and /classroom now 404 and no education/teacher/student paths exist in the docs index — the dedicated Repl.it classrooms/teacher program is no longer published (likely sunset or rebranded); what remains is free self-serve courses at learn.replit.com. (6) Startup program is live (replit.com/startups, "Up to $25K in Credits") but its details could not be machine-read; no sunset date published. Also note: unused monthly credits do not roll over, purchased credit packs expire 6 months, and free published apps expire after 30 days.

findings.name: 30-day free trial with $400 in credits (new Cloud orgs, incl. Continuum)
findings.detail: Every new CockroachDB Cloud organization gets a 30-day trial with $400 in credits; all usage (compute, storage, backups, data transfer, add-ons) draws down the $400 pool. Trial ends at 30 days or when the credit is exhausted, whichever first. New organizations created on/after Sep 15, 2026 land on the new 'Cockroach Continuum' pricing (Standard and Mission Critical editions, billed per vCPU-hour: Standard from $0.057/vCPU-hr on shared infra, 99.99% SLA; Mission Critical from $0.162/vCPU-hr on dedicated infra, 99.999% SLA). After the trial, clusters pause; a 30-day grace period follows (throttled, config changes restricted) during which adding a payment method restores clusters; after that, all clusters are permanently deleted and cannot be restored. Email milestones to Org Admins/Billing Coordinators at 50% and 75% credit consumption, trial end, <24h and grace end.
findings.eligibility: Only a user's FIRST organization qualifies; users invited to an organization do not get additional credits; organizations billed by invoice are excluded. No .edu or startup eligibility involved. No credit card required to start on the Standard edition (legacy Basic/Standard plans also card-free); Mission Critical REQUIRES a credit card because it runs on dedicated infrastructure. Region/provider limits on the card-free tier: Standard is AWS/GCP only (shared infra); Mission Critical adds Azure. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at cockroachlabs.com (cloud console) — 'Create a free Continuum Cloud organization'. 2) The $400 trial credit is applied automatically to the new organization (no coupon or form). 3) Deploy a cluster (Standard edition = no credit card). 4) Optionally add a payment method (console, or via AWS/Google Cloud Marketplace) before the trial ends to keep running.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free tier: this is a one-time credit, not a perpetual free tier; it ends when EITHER 30 days pass or $400 is used. Standard: no CC needed; Mission Critical: CC required. Data/egress: same-region traffic between cluster nodes is free; cross-region and public-internet egress are billed at the cloud provider's list price and will consume the $400. After grace period, cluster deletion is irreversible. New deployments after Sep 15, 2026 are on Continuum pricing, not the legacy RU plans.
findings.expiry: Trial: 30 days or $400 exhaustion, whichever is first; then 30-day grace period, then deletion. One trial per user's first organization only; does not renew.

findings.name: Basic plan free tier: 50M RUs + 10 GiB storage free per month (~$15/month free resource credit) — legacy CockroachDB Cloud plans
findings.detail: The Basic plan starts at $0/month and includes 50 million Request Units and 10 GiB of storage free every month; on-demand compute/storage scale to zero. Billing docs describe the same benefit as the first $15 of monthly resource consumption 'credited back on the monthly invoice'. Basic targets smaller/bursty workloads up to ~30K RU/sec (~60 vCPUs), multi-region on AWS & GCP (select regions), 99.99% SLA. This is the only recurring free tier in the product line.
findings.eligibility: Applies to pay-as-you-go CockroachDB Cloud organizations; customers on annual or multi-year contracts are explicitly NOT eligible for the monthly free resource benefit. A payment method (credit card or cloud Marketplace subscription) must be on the account to receive the free credit. CAVEAT as of 2026-10-22: the RU-based plan pages state these prices 'apply to pay-as-you-go and committed-use customers with clusters created prior to September 15, 2026' and 'Such pricing is no longer available for purchase' — new orgs get Cockroach Continuum, which lists no free tier. So the free tier is effectively live only for pre-cutover / existing pay-as-you-go orgs.
findings.claim: Sign up for CockroachDB Cloud pay-as-you-go, add a payment method in the console (or subscribe via AWS/Google Cloud Marketplace), deploy on the Basic plan; the first 50M RUs + 10 GiB each month are credited back on the invoice automatically. No coupon needed.
findings.gotchas: Credit is monthly, not cumulative; it is a credit-back on invoice, not a hard cap — going over costs money, and a payment method is required to get the benefit at all. Annual-contract customers lose it. Under the Sep 15, 2026 cutover to Continuum this plan structure is no longer available for new purchases, so its practical value in 2026 is limited to existing pay-as-you-go orgs. Backups on Basic are daily and not configurable; IOPS and data transfer are bundled into RUs.
findings.expiry: Ongoing while the Basic plan is active for pay-as-you-go orgs; effectively sunset for new customers at the Sep 15, 2026 Continuum cutover.

findings.name: Free self-hosted use: CockroachDB Software License (CSL) limited non-production carve-out + legacy MIT-licensed releases
findings.detail: Since Nov 18, 2024 (v24.3 and later major series), the CockroachDB server is no longer MIT-licensed: it ships under the proprietary 'CockroachDB Software License' (CSL), a key-gated license. The CSL permits use without a paid License Key only for 'Limited Non-Production Use' (design, prototyping, testing, development in non-production environments) or a database running solely on a single node. Multi-node production self-hosting requires a purchased License Key. Older releases remain available under their original licenses (MIT), so a genuinely free production-grade self-hosted path still exists for those versions.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (no .edu, no CC); the free carve-out covers non-production use of any size and single-node production. Region limits: none (self-hosted).
findings.claim: 1) Download a legacy MIT-licensed release (pre-Nov 2024, e.g. v24.2-series) for free production self-hosting, or 2) download the current v24.3+ build for free development/testing or single-node use; no registration or key needed for the carve-out. For multi-node production on current releases, purchase a License Key from Cockroach Labs.
findings.gotchas: The license text forbids operating multi-node production without a key, restricts benchmarking, mandates telemetry unless a key disables it, and is non-sublicensable/non-transferable. This is a 2024 license change, not a trial: it is a permanent free tier for non-production/single-node use, not a dollar credit and it covers no managed service or support. If you need the latest release in production, budget for the key.

findings.name: Startup program / education license: verified absent
findings.detail: No startup-credits program and no education (student/.edu/academic) free-license program was found on the official site as of 2026-10-22. /startup-program/ and /company/startup-program/ return 404; /resources/startup/ redirects to the homepage; /education/ is 404; the marketing sitemap (scanned in full today) contains no 'education', 'student', 'academic' or startup-program URLs — only marketing blog posts/webinars and a free 'Unicorn Lessons' architecture ebook for startups (no credits or discount). The 'education-first' blog is a customer case study, not a program. 'CockroachDB University' (free training, launched Nov 2019) is still referenced in the site footer at learn.cockroachlabs.com (fetch bot-blocked, HTTP 403); even when active it was free education/training only, with no free Cloud license or credits for students or educators.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no offer to claim.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; the only free access for students/startups is the generic 30-day/$400 trial and (for pre-cutover orgs) the Basic free tier.
findings.gotchas: Absence verified via official 404s/redirects and a full marketing-sitemap scan today, but the session's web-search budget was exhausted, so I could not cross-check press releases or partner pages for an off-site program. Startup/education deals, if any, would come only via sales (account team), not public self-serve claims.

sunset_notes: 1) Sep 15, 2026 cutover: Cockroach Labs moved new deployments to 'Cockroach Continuum' (Standard/Mission Critical editions, per-vCPU-hour pricing). The legacy RU plans (including the $0/month Basic free tier with 50M RUs + 10 GiB free monthly) are 'no longer available for purchase' for new orgs; existing customers stay on old pricing unless they opt in. Continuum lists no recurring free tier — only the one-time 30-day/$400 trial. 2) Nov 18, 2024 relicensing: CockroachDB server moved from MIT to the proprietary, key-gated CockroachDB Software License (v24.3+); free self-hosting is now limited to non-production use or single-node deployments, while pre-Nov-2024 releases remain MIT. 3) Sep 26, 2024: the old 'Serverless'/'Dedicated' product names (which carried the original 'free for everybody, scales to zero' serverless framing) were absorbed into CockroachDB Cloud, per a reader's note on the serverless blog post. 4) No startup program and no education license are publicly offered today; Cockroach University (free training) is still footer-linked but bot-blocked (403) and never included a free database license. 5) WebSearch was unavailable this session (shared budget exhausted), so verification was done against official pages fetched 2026-10-22 (marketing pricing, docs.cockroachlabs.com, GitHub LICENSE) rather than press/news coverage of 2025-2026 changes.

findings.name: AWS Free Tier (2025 revamp) — Free account plan: up to $200 credits, 6 months no-cost
findings.detail: Since July 15, 2025, new AWS accounts get $100 USD in credits immediately at sign-up, and can earn up to $100 more (5 activities x $20: launch/terminate an EC2 instance, RDS basics, Lambda function URL, Bedrock text playground, AWS Budgets) = up to $200 total. The Free plan incurs no charges for up to 6 months or until credits are exhausted, whichever comes first; the account then auto-closes unless converted to a Paid plan (upgrade must happen within 90 days of expiry notice or AWS permanently deletes account content/resources). 30+ services remain 'Always Free' on both plans. Not available in GovCloud (US) or China regions. A new sign-up experience launched October 2026 (credits tracked in Settings Portal instead of Billing console).
findings.eligibility: All new AWS customers (no prior/existing AWS account). No .edu required, no funding cap, no minimum funding; explicitly aimed at students, developers and early entrepreneurs. Payment method/credit card NOT required to sign up for most new customers (AWS may request one for identity verification in some cases). Free plan excludes 'hardware purchases' and services that would rapidly burn credits; enrolling the free account in AWS Organizations upgrades it to Paid and forfeits Free Tier credits.
findings.claim: Create a new AWS account, choose the Free account plan (or Paid plan, which also gets the $200 credits), $100 is credited automatically; complete the five 5-activity tasks in the 'Explore AWS' widget to earn the remaining up to $100; upgrade to Paid at any time one-click. No application, no CC needed.
findings.expiry: Free plan period ends 6 months after account creation or when credits are used up. Terms state Free Tier credits expire 12 months from account opening; Free Tier FAQ says credits expire 6 months — treat 6 months (Free plan) as the practical window; on the Paid plan unused credits remain usable up to 12 months from sign-up. 'Always Free' offers never expire.
findings.gotchas: Legacy 12-month tier (750 hrs/mo t2.micro/t3.micro, 30 GB EBS, 100 GB egress/mo) applies ONLY to accounts created before July 15, 2025. Credits cannot be combined with other promotional offers, one account only, not transferable. Exceeding Always-Free limits auto-applies credits; beyond that you must be on Paid plan. Free plan accounts are 'for evaluation purposes, not for sensitive data'. Unused monthly allowances don't roll over; AWS may reclaim resources idle for 3 months on 30 days' notice. EC2 free-tier-eligible instance types under new model are t3.micro/t3.small/t4g.micro/t4g.small/c7i-flex.large/m7i-flex.large — no bare-metal (e.g. c7i-metal) or dedicated-host free offer exists; those are billable to credits only. No separate VPS product: the VPS front is covered by EC2 micro/small instances charged against credits rather than the old 750-hour cap.

findings.name: AWS Activate Founders (self-funded startups): $1,000 credits, up to $5,000
findings.detail: Activate Founders package grants $1,000 USD in AWS Activate Credits; 'select participants may qualify for additional credits up to $5,000' total over time. Credits are USD, governed by the AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs, and can offset 200+ AWS services including Amazon Bedrock third-party models. Decision within 5-10 business days of submission.
findings.eligibility: Self-funded (bootstrapped) startup; founded in the past 10 years; fully functioning company website; new to AWS Activate Credits; pre-Series B by definition (no external round). No .edu email requirement, no published HQ-country restriction. Must hold an AWS account on a Paid plan to receive credits.
findings.claim: 1) Create/verify an AWS Builder ID (personal email). 2) Complete the one-time AWS Activate profile using your business email (matching startup domain). 3) Choose the Founders tier on the credits application page. 4) Provide product/funding details, link your AWS account, submit; track status on the Credit Application Status page. Apply at aws.amazon.com/startups/join?destination=/credits/apply. A new 'apply using your AI agent' path also exists.
findings.expiry: Validity window not stated on the current official credits page (deferred to Promotional Credit T&Cs). Historical materials: 2-year validity windows for pre-seed tiers in 2024 AWS Japan materials; CNBC (June 2024) reported the legacy $100K tranche expired in 1 year vs 3 years for the $200K. Verify at grant time.
findings.gotchas: Requires a paid AWS account (payment method implications), so the 'no credit card' property of the Free Tier does not carry over. Inaccurate funding info can cause denial. Credits are one-way: amount is fixed once selected (per 2024 materials). Support plan fees (Developer/Business) have historically been credit-eligible per AWS materials, while partial/all-upfront Reserved Instances are NOT eligible.

findings.name: AWS Activate Portfolio (VC/accelerator-backed): up to $200,000 credits
findings.detail: Activate Portfolio grants up to $200,000 USD in credits to provider-backed startups. The ceiling was $100,000 and was doubled to $200,000 in June 2026 (confirmed by the redesigned live credits page and awslabs/startups content update, June 2026). Credits offset infrastructure, data services and AI/ML models; redeemable on third-party foundation models in Amazon Bedrock. AWS has provided over $7-8B in Activate credits since 2013 to 350,000+ startups.
findings.eligibility: Associated with an AWS Activate Provider (VC, CVC, accelerator, angel, e.g. a16z, Greylock, Sequoia, YC, Brex, Carta) and holding that provider's Organizational ID; has not previously received AWS Activate Credits of equal or greater value; pre-Series B with the most recent funding round within the last 12 months (if funded); founded in the past 10 years; fully functioning company website; AWS account on a Paid plan. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Founder creates/verifies AWS Builder ID. 2) Complete AWS Activate profile with business email. 3) Choose Portfolio tier and enter the provider's Org ID. 4) Provide startup/funding details, link an existing or new AWS account, submit; decision in 5-10 business days. If funded after a pre-seed grant, top-up to the higher tier is possible (historically the system grants the difference, validity reset per terms).
findings.expiry: Not published per-tier on the official page (governed by Promotional Credit T&Cs). CNBC (June 28, 2024) reported the $200,000 tranche valid for 3 years vs 1 year for the old $100,000 — treat as indicative only. June 2026 cap doubling is documented on the live page (© 2026) and in the awslabs/startups repo changelog.
findings.gotchas: The June 2024 CNBC report ('$200K for Series A funded in past year, effective July 1, 2024') was not reflected in 2025 official materials (which still said 'up to $100,000'); the official cap only moved to $200,000 in June 2026. Credits cannot be applied to partial/all-upfront Reserved Instances; some services are excluded. No self-service: you need a provider Org ID — cold-start founders without VC ties get Founders ($1k-5k) only.

findings.name: AWS Credits for AI Startups (invite-only, above Activate)
findings.detail: A new tier announced alongside the June 2026 credits-page redesign: 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' offering $200,000+ in AWS Credits, invite-only, for AI startups 'ready to scale post Activate Portfolio.' Access is via your AWS Account Manager; no public application form. Amount has no stated cap.
findings.eligibility: AI startups that have completed/exhausted the Activate Portfolio tier and are scaling beyond it; engagement is AM-driven (invite-only). Implied pre-Series B / within Activate program terms, but no published caps.
findings.claim: No self-serve path: talk with your AWS Account Manager (or request via the AWS Startups team) to be referred for the AI startup credit offer. Application still anchored on the AWS Builder ID + Activate profile.
findings.expiry: Not published (invite-only, per-account). Governed by AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs like all Activate credits.
findings.gotchas: Amounts not disclosed publicly; eligibility is at AWS's discretion; 'apply using your AI agent' from the IDE (AWS Startup Advisor) is a new 2026 convenience but the >$200K tier itself requires AM engagement.

findings.name: Kiro Startup Credits: up to 1 year of free Kiro Pro+ (2-30 users)
findings.detail: Kiro (AWS's agentic IDE) offers early-stage startups up to a 1-year's worth of free Kiro Pro+ usage credits in three tiers: Starter (up to 2 users), Growth (up to 10 users), Scale (up to 30 users). Credits are delivered to the AWS account and expire one year after issuance; when depleted the account auto-switches to standard Kiro Pro+ billing. Not refundable, re-issuable, transferable or sellable; can be shared among authorized users of the same company.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage to Series A startups; matching business-domain email and corresponding AWS Account ID required; companies with ACTIVE AWS Activate Credits are excluded from this promotion (though Activate credits can still be applied to Kiro usage); a list of excluded countries/regions applies (not itemized on the page).
findings.claim: Sign in at kiro.dev/startups with your AWS account, select a tier (2/10/30 users), submit; review on rolling basis with follow-up email; approved credits are added automatically to your AWS account. Use Kiro via AWS IAM Identity Center (not Builder ID or social login).
findings.expiry: Credits expire 12 months after issuance to the AWS account; tier caps usage seats, not dollar amount.
findings.gotchas: If your startup already holds AWS Activate Credits, you are not eligible for this Kiro promo — plan which benefit to take. 'Kiro' is a tool-specific credit, not general AWS infrastructure credit.

findings.name: AWS Impact Accelerator (launched April 2025): $125,000 cash + up to $100,000 AWS credits
findings.detail: Under a >$30M, three-year commitment, each qualifying startup receives $125,000 cash plus up to $100,000 in AWS credits (up to $225,000 combined), an 8-week personalized program with AWS startup experts, mentoring, investor networking and Amazon-leader introductions. Runs in founder-demographic tracks: Black Founders (inaugural cohort, June 2025, US-based), Women Founders (H2 2025, US-based), with Latino and LGBTQIA+ tracks following.
