findings.eligibility: High-potential, pre-seed early-stage startups led by Black, women, Latino, or LGBTQIA+ founders (track-dependent); US-based cohorts at launch. No .edu or funding-stage exception beyond pre-seed.
findings.claim: Apply through the program's dedicated application page when a track opens (inaugural Black Founders track applied via aws-startup-lofts.com, linked from the AWS announcement). Cohort-based: application windows are per track, not rolling.
findings.expiry: Program commitment spans three years from the April 2025 launch; individual cohort windows open/close per track. Whether tracks remained open in 2026 could not be re-verified (web-search budget exhausted this session).
findings.gotchas: Competitive cohort selection, not a self-serve credit grant. Cash leg ($125k) is separate from the AWS-credit leg. Demographic eligibility narrows applicant pool vs generic Activate.

findings.name: AWS Generative AI Accelerator (GAIA): up to $1,000,000 AWS credits (cohort program)
findings.detail: GAIA is AWS's flagship cohort accelerator for generative-AI startups. The official 'What's New' page states the 2025 cohort 'will receive unmatched benefits designed to accelerate both technical growth and market traction, including up to $1 million in AWS credits' (per-startup figure cited by third-party trackers; the official page only states 'up to $1 million in AWS credits' for the cohort). Includes hands-on AI expertise, GTM resources, and investor/mentor connections. 80 startups were selected for the 2024 program.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage generative-AI startups; cohort is competitive/selected (applications open in cycles; 2025 cohort applications were open at time of the What's New entry). No .edu requirement. No public funding cap stated.
findings.claim: Apply during open application windows on the GAIA program page (linked from AWS Startups news; the deep URL I attempted returned 404, so use the AWS Startups 'What's New' / Generative AI Accelerator landing when live).
findings.expiry: Cohort-based; 2025 cohort cited; a 2026 cycle likely but not verified in this session (search budget exhausted). Credit validity per-grant not published on fetched pages.
findings.gotchas: The exact per-startup dollar figure (commonly reported as up to $1M for top cohorts) is not confirmed on the pages I could load; cohort status for 2026 unverified.

findings.name: AWS education / student offers: free learning (no .edu required), no student-specific credits
findings.detail: AWS has no student-specific free credit program and no 'education license' VPS offer. Free offers for students are: (1) the standard AWS Free Tier (up to $200 credits, 6 months, explicitly marketed to students — no .edu email and no credit card required for most new customers); (2) free digital training / courses and certification-voucher programs (AWS Academy resources, AWS Educate-style free self-paced content); (3) institutions can get 'special pricing for education customers' via sales (discounts, not free). The education page confirms 17,000+ education customers but lists no student credit dollar amounts.
findings.eligibility: Students: same as general Free Tier — new AWS account, no .edu requirement, no CC for most customers. Institutions: separate education customer pricing negotiated via AWS sales. No funding caps (N/A).
findings.claim: Students: sign up for AWS Free Tier (Free or Paid plan) at aws.amazon.com/free and complete the credit-earning activities. Training: enroll in free AWS digital courses / Academy resources (free signup, no .edu). No application steps for credits themselves.
findings.expiry: Free Tier: 6-month plan / 12-month credit expiry (see Free Tier finding). Free training content has no expiry. Education-institution special pricing has no published sunset.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse 'AWS Academy' (partner-facilitated, some paid programs) with 'free digital training'. There is no dedicated .edu-gated offer; a school email is NOT required anywhere in the AWS free stack. Any 'student voucher' deals are ad-hoc campaign offers, not standing programs.

provider: AWS (Amazon Web Services) — fronts: VPS (EC2 micro/small instances), bare-metal & dedicated (no free front; credit-eligible only)
sunset_notes: Major 2025-2026 changes: (1) July 15, 2025 — AWS replaced the long-standing 12-month Free Tier (750 hrs/mo t2.micro/t3.micro + 30 GB EBS + 100 GB egress, 30+ always-free services) with a credit-based model for NEW accounts: $100 sign-up credits + up to $100 earned = up to $200, with a 6-month no-cost Free plan that auto-closes. Legacy 12-month benefits remain ONLY for accounts created before July 15, 2025. Also, since the revamp, a credit card/payment method is no longer required to sign up for most new customers (previously mandatory). A new sign-up experience (Settings Portal credit tracking) launched October 2026. (2) June 2026 — AWS Activate Portfolio credit ceiling doubled from $100,000 to $200,000; the Founders tier was standardized at $1,000 with an 'up to $5,000' extension for select participants; a new invite-only 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' tier (>$200K) was introduced (confirmed by the redesigned aws.amazon.com/startups/credits page © 2026 and the awslabs/startups repo content update June 16, 2026). Note: CNBC's June 28, 2024 report that Series A startups got $200K from July 1, 2024 was NOT reflected in 2025 official materials (which still said 'up to $100,000'); the cap only officially moved to $200K in June 2026. (3) April 2025 — AWS launched the $30M Impact Accelerator (new program, not a sunset). (4) No VPS/bare-metal/dedicated specific free offer was sunset, because none existed as a standalone front: bare-metal and dedicated hosts have never had free tiers and remain credit-eligible under Activate/Free Tier credits only. (5) GAIA 2025 cohort status and Impact Accelerator 2026 track openings could not be re-verified this session (shared web-search budget exhausted); confidence ratings above reflect that.

provider: Scaleway (scaleway.com — VPS / bare-metal / dedicated servers, France/EU)

findings.name: New-account free trial: €100 credit (Business/Professional account)
findings.detail: Create a Business account (older pages say Professional) and get €100 free credit across cloud services. The trial does not auto-apply: if eligible, a voucher code is emailed within 24 hours and the trial starts when you redeem it. Credit expiry is not officially stated. Payment method is required: ordering resources needs a valid credit card (€1 authorization is placed and auto-reimbursed within 2 days); virtual prepaid cards are not accepted; KYC identity verification is part of the account process.
findings.eligibility: New Business/Professional customers with a valid payment method who have NEVER had an invoice issued by Scaleway (a €0 invoice counts as an invoice and disqualifies you). Not advertised for Personal accounts. No .edu or startup-status requirement; effectively open to any new account.
findings.claim: 1) Create an account at console.scaleway.com, choosing a Business (formerly 'Professional') organization type. 2) Add a valid credit card (Visa/MasterCard/CB/UnionPay/Amex; SEPA with a physical card on file). 3) Wait for the voucher-code email (within 24h of qualifying) and redeem it in the console to activate the €100 trial.
findings.source_url: https://www.scaleway.com/en/scaleway-vs-aws/ (trial FAQ + '€100 free credit' banner; mirrored on https://www.scaleway.com/en/generative-apis-signup/ and https://www.scaleway.com/en/scaleway-vs-digitalocean/)
findings.expiry: Official expiry not stated; voucher must be redeemed (emailed within 24h). Credit not cash-outable.
findings.gotchas: Any prior Scaleway invoice (even €0) disqualifies — a forgotten test account silently blocks the offer. Virtual/prepaid cards rejected. GPU is not excluded from the credit, but new-account quotas may limit larger GPU types. Dedicated-server and some products bill separately; egress/data transfer rules vary per product.

findings.name: Startup Program — Founders tier: €1,000 credit, 12 months
findings.detail: Entry tier of Scaleway's Startup Program for startups migrating to Scaleway or doing an initial build. €1,000 in cloud credits valid 12 months, not renewable; support is self-serve (no dedicated CSM); benefits include collective onboarding, private Slack with peers/alumni, product betas, masterclasses, co-marketing, and VC-network access. Application review takes under 21 business days; admission is rolling.
findings.eligibility: Entity under 5 years old; fewer than 50 employees; must NOT already be a Scaleway customer. No funding-stage or location cap stated. Open regardless of vertical.
findings.claim: Apply via the Startup Program application (scaleway.com/en/startup-program/ or email startup-program@scaleway.com). Committee reviews applications; program dates are set per cohort (6 or 12 months after credits activation).
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months; non-renewable. Overage beyond the voucher is billed.
findings.gotchas: Being an existing customer (even a trial account) disqualifies you — coordinate with the €100 trial so an invoice isn't issued first. No funding cap published, but committee discretion applies; 'up to €1,000' vs '€1,000' phrasing differs between the nav and the benefits block.

findings.name: Startup Program — Early Stage tier: €1,500/month x 6 = up to €9,000
findings.detail: For startups going to market at pre-seed to seed stage. €1,500 per month of cloud credits over 6 months (total €9,000), with community support, co-marketing, and technical guidance from a CSM on request. Implied consumption floor of €500/month (the FAQ states this tier starts at '500€/month consumption').
findings.eligibility: Less than 5 years old, fewer than 50 employees, not yet a Scaleway client; pre-seed to seed stage. Cannot move from Early Stage directly into Growth Stage.
findings.claim: Same rolling application as the program (scaleway.com/en/startup-program/, or startup-program@scaleway.com); selected startups join a cohort running 6 months from credit activation.
findings.expiry: 6-month credit window; overage beyond the voucher billed.
findings.gotchas: Consumption floor (~€500/month) means this is a ramp-up grant, not a small grant; usage below the floor is not expected. Page says 'up to €9,000' and '1 500€ per month for 6 month'.

findings.name: Startup Program — Growth Stage tier: €3,000/month x 12 = up to €36,000
findings.detail: For seed-to-Series-A startups scaling up. €3,000 per month of cloud credits over 12 months (total €36,000), with dedicated CSM, 24/7 technical support (page typo '27/7'), co-marketing, events, and VC-network access. Implied consumption floor of €1,500/month.
findings.eligibility: Less than 5 years old, fewer than 50 employees, not yet a Scaleway client; seed to Series A stage. An Nvidia-dedicated variant has conditions similar to Growth.
findings.claim: Apply via scaleway.com/en/startup-program/ (rolling admission; a page FAQ says the committee reviews weekly/monthly — see gotchas). 12-month cohort from credit activation.
findings.expiry: 12-month credit window; overage billed.
findings.gotchas: Highest exposure — floor of ~€1,500/month; the €36,000 only materializes if consumption matches the monthly tranche. Program FAQ wording conflicts internally on review cadence (weekly on the main page, monthly on the Founders page FAQ, 'under 21 business days' on Founders).

findings.name: Object Storage trial: 750 GB free for 90 days (new users)
findings.detail: New users get 750 GB of free storage total, splittable between Standard Multi-AZ and Standard One Zone classes, across all regions, for 90 days. If you exceed 750 GB during the trial, only the excess is billed. Trial is activated from the Object Storage section of the console and cannot be paused/restarted once started; after 90 days regular pricing applies.
findings.eligibility: New users who had never used the Standard Multi-AZ class before 30 Nov 2023 23:59:59 (stated in the official FAQ). No card needed specifically for the trial itself, though ordering resources generally requires a valid payment method.
findings.claim: Activate in the Scaleway console under Object Storage. Free quota applies to buckets in your Organization across regions.
findings.expiry: 90 days from activation; one-shot (cannot deactivate and resume).
findings.gotchas: The 2023 cut-off eligibility date is a hidden disqualifier for older accounts. Marketing pages say '750 GB/h free for 90 days' (GB per hour of trial, not 750GB/hour sustained) — it is 750 GB total. Data egress after trial follows regular pricing.

findings.name: Ongoing free tiers: serverless monthly quotas, free Kapsule control plane, 1M free Generative API tokens
findings.detail: Recurring per-account free quotas on the official Serverless pricing page: Functions — 1,000,000 requests/month and 400,000 GB-s/month free; Containers — 400,000 GB-s/month and 200,000 vCPU-s/month free; Jobs — 400,000 GB-s/month and 200,000 vCPU-s/month free. Kapsule (managed Kubernetes) control plane is free (dedicated control-plane option is paid). Generative APIs: every new customer gets 1,000,000 free tokens (pay from the 1,000,001st). Docs billing concepts confirm free tiers on select products have no expiration date but may change.
findings.eligibility: Account-level: applies per account, resets monthly for the serverless quotas (Provisioned/warm resources have NO free tier and bill from the first second). No .edu requirement; Generative API token grant targets new customers.
findings.claim: No application — quotas apply automatically to each account; Kapsule control plane is simply free when you create a cluster (nodes are billed from ~€0.027/h).
findings.expiry: Ongoing monthly resets (serverless), token grant is a one-time 1M-token welcome allowance; 'no expiration date but subject to change' per docs.
findings.gotchas: Free quotas cover compute/consumption only — data transfer (egress), provisioned instances, and storage attached to serverless workloads are billed. Prices are ex-VAT. These are not free VPS: the smallest Learning ('Stardust') instance is a paid ~€4.47/month box.

findings.name: Education / students: no real free credit program found
findings.detail: No .edu-based free credit or education license program exists on Scaleway's official site as of today. The closest offerings are: (1) 'Learning Instances' (Stardust class: 1 shared vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 10 GB storage, 100 Mbps; available only in FR-PAR-1 and NL-AMS-1, max 1 per AZ, limited monthly supply) — cheap, not free; (2) Scaleway Learning — paid certification (€300 ex-VAT exam, badges valid 2 years). No university agreement or student voucher surfaced on official pages.
findings.eligibility: None education-specific. A student with a normal account gets the same offers as everyone (€100 trial requires Business type, 750 GB/90-day storage trial, monthly serverless free tiers).
findings.claim: No student-only claim path exists; students use the standard new-account offers above.
findings.source_url: https://www.scaleway.com/en/scaleway-learning/ ; https://www.scaleway.com/fr/new-stardust-instances/ (English equivalent: pricing for Learning Instances under Virtual Instances)
findings.gotchas: Third-party 'student' listings (e.g., StudentPerks) only point back to the general startup program, not a student tier. Don't cite .edu eligibility that isn't documented.

sunset_notes: URL drift / rebrand: the task's starting point https://www.scaleway.com/en/cloud-startup/ now returns 404. The startup offer was restructured into a three-tier Startup Program at https://www.scaleway.com/en/startup-program/ (Founders €1,000/12mo; Early Stage €1,500/mo x 6 = €9,000; Growth €3,000/mo x 12 = €36,000, with ~€500 and ~€1,500 monthly consumption floors respectively). The old single 'Scaleway for Startups' page copy is gone. Account model changed from Personal/Professional to Personal/Business: the €100 trial is now marketed to 'Business' accounts (older vs-DigitalOcean page still says 'Professional'). The Elastic Metal loyalty voucher (refund-of-commitment-fee credit after 12 months) is no longer available for NEW subscriptions as of 1 April 2026 (existing subscriptions keep it). The ViVaTech '3 months of credit' campaign ended in 2025 (results announced end of July 2025). Review-cadence copy is inconsistent across program pages (weekly vs monthly vs 'under 21 business days') — treat as committee-discretion. No material change was found to the €100 trial, the 750 GB/90-day Object Storage trial, or the monthly serverless free quotas between 2025 and 2026; all remain live on official pages read today (2026-10-22).

provider: AWS — Free Plan (ex-12-month Free Tier) + AWS Startups/Activate + Education

findings.name: AWS Free Plan (new accounts, since Jul 15 2025): up to $200 credits, 6-month free plan
findings.detail: New AWS customers get $100 USD in credits immediately at signup and can earn up to $100 more by completing five 'explore' activities ($20 each: launch/terminate an EC2 instance, launch an RDS database, build a Lambda web app with a function URL, run a Bedrock prompt in the text playground, and create an AWS Budgets cost budget). Total up to $200. Choosing the Free account plan (the default at signup) means zero charges: 'no surprise bills', access to 90+ services for up to 6 months. The account auto-closes 6 months after opening or when credits run out, whichever is first. AWS suspends the account at expiry, retains your data 90 days, then permanently deletes account + content. Free plan includes Basic Support. Free plan cannot receive other promotional/incentive credits (e.g., AWS Activate), cannot buy hardware, and some 'large enterprise' services are unavailable; upgrade to Paid plan anytime (credits then remain valid until 12 months from signup).
findings.eligibility: All new AWS customers (anyone creating a brand-new AWS account); students and startups qualify exactly like everyone else — no .edu email, no student verification required. A credit/payment method is NOT required for most new customers (FAQ: 'A payment method isn't required to sign up for most new customers'; AWS may still request one or other identity info for verification in some cases). Excludes accounts that already have (or ever had) an AWS account; one Free Tier credit grant per person. Excluded regions: AWS GovCloud (US) and China (Beijing/Ningxia) regions; all other commercial regions GA.
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://aws.amazon.com/free/ and create a new AWS account, selecting the Free account plan during sign-up. 2) $100 credit appears automatically. 3) In the AWS Management Console, complete the 5 explore activities (shown in the 'Explore AWS' widget / Credits page in Billing & Cost Management console; credits may take up to 10 minutes to post). 4) Track balance/expiry on the Credits page; AWS emails reminders as expiry approaches. 5) To keep using AWS after the 6-month free window, upgrade to Paid plan within the 90-day data-retention window (Settings portal > Payment > Upgrade).
findings.expiry: Free plan period: 6 months from account creation or credit exhaustion, whichever is first — no extension possible. Credits expire 12 months from account creation (if you upgrade to Paid, unused credits stay valid to that 12-month mark). After free-plan expiry: 90 days of data retention, then permanent deletion. A new sign-up experience is noted to launch in October 2026 (FAQ).
findings.gotchas: This replaces the old free 750 h/month EC2 VPS: on the new plan EC2 usage is credit-based (eligible instance types changed — t2.micro no longer listed; free-tier-eligible types are t3.micro, t3.small, t4g.micro, t4g.small, c7i-flex.large, m7i-flex.large), so a running VM burns your $100-$200 credits. Credits are non-transferable and non-stackable with any other AWS promo (Activate/Partner) credit. Enrolling in AWS Organizations or a Control Tower landing zone voids remaining explore activities and extra credits (account auto-upgrades to Paid). Resources unused for 3 consecutive months can be reclaimed on 30 days' notice. Go beyond always-free monthly caps on the Free plan and remaining credits are auto-deducted; once depleted you must upgrade to Paid. Free plan is intended for evaluation and 'should not be used for processing sensitive data'.

findings.name: Legacy 12-month Free Tier (accounts created before July 15, 2025)
findings.detail: Accounts created before 15 Jul 2025 still hold the old 12-month offers: EC2 free-tier-eligible instances t2.micro and t3.micro (the classic 750 h/month 'free VPS'), plus legacy per-service 12-month allowances (e.g., RDS db.t3.micro/db.t4g.micro for MySQL/PostgreSQL/MariaDB/SQL Server Express; S3, Lambda, etc. per the old terms, last updated Aug 14, 2018). Usage past limits is billed pay-as-you-go during the 12 months. This is now strictly legacy: the cutoff date is 15 Jul 2025 — new accounts cannot obtain it.
findings.eligibility: Only AWS customers who created their account before July 15, 2025. Not claimable by new accounts under any circumstances.
findings.claim: Already enrolled automatically for pre-cutoff accounts; nothing to do. For new accounts: not claimable.
findings.expiry: 12 months from account creation (legacy terms, last updated 2018-08-14); after that, standard pay-as-you-go. Legacy RDS/other service offers follow their own per-service legacy pages (e.g., https://aws.amazon.com/rds/free/ shows 'Legacy Free Tier' for accounts activated before Jul 15, 2025).
findings.gotchas: Any 2024-era guide saying 'free t2.micro for 12 months' is stale for new signups — since 15 Jul 2025 there is no hours-based EC2 free tier for new accounts; new accounts are on the credit-based Free Plan instead. Exceeding legacy monthly limits before the 12-month end triggers pay-as-you-go charges.

findings.name: Always Free tier (30+ services, monthly caps, indefinite, both plans)
findings.detail: 30+ AWS services remain 'always free within monthly usage limits' on both the Free and Paid plans, indefinitely. Verified example today: AWS Lambda free tier = 1,000,000 requests + 400,000 GB-seconds per month, free 512 MB ephemeral storage, first 6 MB streamed response per request free (100 GB/month streamed bytes). Other long-standing always-free allowances across the catalog (e.g., S3 storage, DynamoDB, CloudFront egress) live on individual service pricing pages; the /free/ page now routes per-service limits to those pages. Usage is aggregated across all regions; unused monthly amounts do not roll over.
findings.eligibility: All AWS customers (new AND existing) — including Paid-plan customers who skip the free plan. No credit card required for the always-free usage itself; no region/industry exclusions stated.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim — automatically applies to any account on eligible services within the monthly caps. Monitor via service dashboards/Billing console.
findings.expiry: No expiry; perpetual monthly allowances. Amounts do not roll over between months. AWS may reclaim resources unused for 3 months (30-day notice) and may terminate any offer at any time.
findings.gotchas: On the Free plan, overflow beyond always-free caps automatically consumes your remaining Free Tier credits (and once credits are gone, you must upgrade to Paid to keep resources running). On the Paid plan, overflow is billed at standard rates. Concrete always-free numbers for each of the 30+ services must be checked per-service (today's /free/ page no longer prints them); only the Lambda figures above were re-verified on an official page today. Lambda provisioned concurrency has NO free tier.

findings.name: AWS Activate / AWS for Startups — up to $200,000 in credits + partner offers
findings.detail: AWS for Startups (includes the former AWS Activate): headline is 'up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits' (credits offset infrastructure, data services, and AI/ML model costs, and are redeemable on third-party models on Amazon Bedrock). The /free/offers/ page states the Activate grant as '$1,000 to $100,000 in AWS credits' (tier-dependent) plus 'access to 80+ exclusive offers' in third-party products, memberships, and education programs, valued at up to $800,000. 'AI startups ready to grow may be eligible for additional credits beyond Activate' (no amount published). A separate 'Kiro credits' offer for startups is referenced (amount not published). Application is processed in 7-10 business days; an 'AWS Startup Advisor' can scaffold architecture and apply from an IDE.
findings.eligibility: Startup must be self-funded or externally funded up to and including Pre-Seed, Angel, Seed, Debt Finance, or Series A; must have a company website or public company profile; must have been founded in the past 10 years. No .edu/student track is published — student/educator access is via the general new-account Free Plan (above) or, as a new customer, AWS Free Tier + activation.
findings.claim: 1) https://aws.amazon.com/startups/ → 'Join now' (/startups/join); for credits specifically: /startups/join?destination=/credits/apply. 2) Submit application (company details, public website); AWS reviews in 7-10 business days; decision by email. 3) Important: an account on the Free Plan is NOT eligible for Activate/promotional credits — you must be on the Paid plan (the new-account $200 Free Tier credits exist but the Free Plan 'cannot receive' other incentives).
findings.expiry: Per-tier credit durations are not published on the pages read today (legacy program historically allowed credits over 12-36 months depending on stage; not verifiable today due to web-search budget exhaustion — treat durations as unconfirmed). Credits governed by AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions.
findings.gotchas: Cannot combine with the Free Plan: AWS Promotional Credit terms bar combining Free Tier credits with other promo/incentive offers, and the Free Plan FAQ says Free-plan accounts can't receive other promotional credits like AWS Activate — so to collect Activate you must run a Paid plan and rely on standard pricing. Amounts: the public range is $1,000-$100,000 (Activate tiers) with a program headline of 'up to $200,000' plus unspecified extra AI credits. 80+ partner offers are third-party value, not AWS dollars. Kiro credits banner references an AI IDE credit program whose amount isn't disclosed on the pages read.

findings.name: Education: no standalone free student/educator VPS or credit program published (AWS for Students/Faculty)
findings.detail: The AWS education pages publish no student- or educator-only free instance/VM program and no .edu-gated credit offer. What exists: (1) students get the same universal new-account AWS Free Plan ($100 + up to $100 credits, 6 months) as anyone — no .edu verification; (2) free hands-on training content (AWS Training & Certification: self-paced digital courses, free digital certificates via the Skill Builder / free-course paths); (3) institutions: 'special pricing for education customers' by contacting public-sector sales (/government-education/contact/), on-campus training, and an education catalog on AWS Marketplace. The former dedicated AWS Activate portal for students/educators (historically up to $100k/$150k credits for verified students/faculty and accelerators) is no longer at its old URL — /activate/ now serves the AWS for Startups program page. No per-service 'education license' free-tier (like GitHub Education's free cloud credits) exists on AWS pages read today.
findings.eligibility: Students: standard new AWS account requirements (no .edu email required, no payment method required for most). Institutions/faculty: engage AWS public-sector sales for education pricing; free courses open to anyone via AWS Training.
findings.claim: Students: create an account at https://aws.amazon.com/free/ (same as any new customer) to get the $100-$200 Free Plan; take free courses at https://aws.amazon.com/training/. Educators/institutions: request education pricing through /government-education/contact/; no self-serve credit application exists.
findings.expiry: N/A — no published education-only credit program to expire. Universal Free Plan rules apply (6 months/credits, 12-month credit expiry) to student accounts exactly as to all new accounts.
findings.gotchas: Do not expect a perpetual free VPS for students from AWS: the old 'free for 12 months' EC2 offer is gone for new accounts of any kind (15 Jul 2025 cutover). AWS has no .edu-verified free-credits program on its public pages today; the startup-track (Activate/Startups) is the only published large-credit program and it targets companies, not individuals (a solo founder's startup can qualify if it has a public company profile and fits the 10-year/ Series-A funding caps). Web search budget was exhausted mid-research, so absence-of-offer claims reflect the official pages fetched today, not an exhaustive search of AWS announcements.

sunset_notes: Sunset/changed in 2025-2026: (1) 15 Jul 2025 (announced AWS Summit NY, 15-16 Jul 2025): the 12-month Free Tier was retired for NEW accounts and replaced by the credit-based Free Plan ($100 signup credit + up to $100 explore credits, 6-month auto-closing plan, 90-day post-expiry data retention); pre-cutoff accounts keep their legacy 12-month offers until each one's own expiry. (2) EC2 free-VPS offer sunset: t2.micro (and hours-based t3.micro 750 h/mo) free tiers no longer apply to new accounts; new free-tier-eligible EC2 types are t3.micro, t3.small, t4g.micro, t4g.small, c7i-flex.large, m7i-flex.large, consumed via credits. (3) AWS Activate was folded into AWS for Startups: /aws.amazon.com/activate/ now serves the startups program (startups.aws.com); headline credit figure is 'up to $200,000' with published tiers $1,000-$100,000, 80+ partner offers valued up to $800,000, plus undisclosed extra AI-startup credits and Kiro credits — replacing older multi-year $1M total caps and old student/faculty Activate tiers (up to $100k/$150k) which no longer appear on official pages. (4) The Free Plan explicitly cannot combine with any other promotional/incentive offer, and joining AWS Organizations/Control Tower auto-upgrades to Paid and voids remaining explore credits. (5) AWS signals a new sign-up experience in October 2026 (FAQ note); Free Tier Terms last updated 9 Jul 2025. Note: session web-search budget was exhausted, so 2025-2026 change verification relied on WebFetch of official AWS pages (free/, free/offers/, free/free-tier-faqs/, free/terms/, startups/, education/, EC2 docs, Lambda pricing, RDS free page, what's-new Jul 2025 entry, AWS blog 15 Jul 2025) rather than broader search.

findings.claim: Order any VPS plan (e.g. VPS S+ at $2/mo, 3-mo intro, 1-yr term), use it up to 30 days, cancel for a full refund.
findings.detail: The 'Free VPS Trial' on IONOS's US site is a 30-day money-back guarantee, not a no-cost trial: you pay for the VPS up front (current VPS+ lineup: S+ $2/mo, M+ $5/mo, L+ $8/mo for 3 months with a 1-year term; older 'VPS' line from $2-4/mo on 3-year terms) and IONOS refunds 'no questions asked' if you cancel within 30 days. VPS includes unlimited traffic up to 1 Gbps, NVMe storage, wildcard SSL, KVM root access, Linux (AlmaLinux/Debian/Rocky/Ubuntu) or Windows Server 2022/2025. Not a perpetual free tier; renews into the paid term after the window.
findings.eligibility: New consumers/businesses; any customer. No .edu email, no startup age or funding cap. Payment card (credit card) IS required to start. US storefront sells into US, UK, German, Spanish data-center locations; other IONOS country sites (CA, UK, NZ) run the same 30-day trial with local pricing (e.g., CA adds a $15 setup fee; CA prices $3-6/mo).
findings.expiry: 30 days from order/activation; cancel inside the window for full refund. After that the 1-year term (or 3-year for older VPS line) applies with list prices.
findings.gotchas: Trial = refund offer, NOT free: CC charged immediately and refund processing is required; sales tax/state tax applies; Windows OS, extra IPv4 ($5/mo), Plesk ($6/mo US) and Cloud Backup (~$0.065/GB/mo) are add-ons that also factor into the effective cost; 'unlimited traffic' is only up to a 1 Gbit/s connection; US data-center availability is the practical region limit for the .com offer.
findings.name: IONOS VPS '30-day free trial' (30-day money-back guarantee)

findings.claim: Create an IONOS account, order a cloud server (Cube) sized so expected 30-day consumption stays under the $200 credit; no minimum contract, cancel anytime; if credit is exceeded you are billed only the difference.
findings.detail: IONOS US 'Free Cloud Server Trial': packages contain starting credit of $200 (UK: £200) entitling the user to 30 days of free cloud-server hosting as long as booked resources don't exceed the credit. Cloud cubes are pay-as-you-go, billed down-to-the-minute: Basic Cube XS $5.76/30d, S $10.08/30d, M $18.72/30d, L $34.56/30d, XL $65.52/30d; Memory cubes $13.68-90.00/30d. Cubes available in EU data centers and Newark, NJ, USA. 'Free server hosting' marketing also appears on ionos.com/servers/free-server-hosting. HostingAdvice (updated Aug 2026) additionally describes $100 first-month credits for Compute Engine, S3 storage and Managed Kubernetes plans.
findings.eligibility: New IONOS cloud customers; no student/.edu requirement, no startup age or funding cap. Credit card required for the account (pay-as-you-go billing). Data-center locations: EU + Newark NJ for cloud cubes; other regions via IONOS CLOUD enterprise sales.
findings.expiry: 30 days or credit exhaustion, whichever first; account then converts to production billing automatically. Extensions only by contacting the account manager.
findings.gotchas: This one is genuinely free up to the credit (unlike the VPS refund trial) but the CC gets charged automatically if you exceed $200 or run past 30 days; Windows Server licenses (from ~$0.0072/vCPU/hr, i.e. ~$5.18/30d/vCPU) and RHEL licenses add on top of the base cube price; outbound traffic is metered; traffic/Windows/backup/object-storage usage is not shown in the dashboard and must be watched via the Billing API; no data-egress free allowance stated.
findings.name: $200 IONOS Cloud server credit ('free server hosting' trial, 30 days)

findings.claim: Apply via IONOS CLOUD sales (phone +49 30 57700 840 or beratung@cloud.ionos.de); private-cloud/bare-metal trial by speaking with the sales department; trial converts to production account automatically at expiry.
findings.detail: Official IONOS CLOUD trial conditions: every customer can test the production environment. Default trial resources: 8 cores, 20 GB RAM, 600 GB HDD + 600 GB SSD Standard/Premium, 1 static IP; trial limited to 30 days OR maximum resource consumption of EUR 500. Account creation requires company + credit card details and phone verification; the CLOUD sales team calls within 24h on working days. Private cloud (VMware on dedicated hardware, i.e. the closest bare-metal/DCC-free trial) can also be tested free for 30 days 'contact IONOS CLOUD sales directly.' Trial accounts auto-convert to production with billing at expiry or when resources are exhausted.
findings.eligibility: Corporate/enterprise prospects ('every customer' may test); trial signup asks for company details and a credit card. No student or .edu path through this program. Region: IONOS CLOUD data centers incl. US (Las Vegas/DC-region mentions in docs), EU (Karlsruhe, Frankfurt); EU-only CLOUD regions possible.
findings.expiry: 30 days or EUR 500 consumption, whichever first; extensions require the account manager.
findings.gotchas: CC required and used for billing after conversion; resources, not just time, cap the trial (500 EUR); traffic, Windows licenses, backups, S3 storage aren't itemized in the dashboard - watch via Billing API; data must be deleted before trial end or it becomes billable production data; this is a separate enterprise funnel from the consumer VPS/cube trials.
findings.name: IONOS CLOUD 30-day trial account (up to EUR 500 of resources), incl. private cloud/bare-metal via sales

findings.claim: Contact IONOS CLOUD sales (beratung@cloud.ionos.de / +49 30 57700 840) to apply; no self-serve portal found on ionos.com.
findings.detail: IONOS's official CLOUD FAQ confirms: 'Do you offer discounts on contracts? ... Does IONOS CLOUD have special offers for students, freelancers, or startups? We have special offers for students, freelancers, and startups. For more information, see IONOS CLOUD Startup Program.' The dedicated startup-program URL on ionos.com returned 404 today, so exact credit amounts, company-age or funding caps, and application steps are not publicly documented. Treat amounts as unknown/confirm-with-sales.
findings.eligibility: Per the FAQ, aimed at students, freelancers and startups; no .edu-only requirement stated publicly. Credit card likely required as with all IONOS CLOUD accounts. No published funding cap or company-age limit found.
findings.expiry: Unknown - not publicly documented.
findings.gotchas: Details (credit size, duration, renewal) require direct contact with IONOS CLOUD sales; region likely EU (the program sits on IONOS CLOUD, sold via German sales team); third-party 'IONOS startup credit' claims should be treated as unverified.
findings.name: IONOS CLOUD Startup Program (special offers for students, freelancers, startups)

findings.claim: Watch IONOS storefronts (ionos.com/special-deals, coupon-codes) and third-party deal aggregators; offers are time-boxed and rotating.
findings.detail: IONOS has historically run rotating bundle promos such as 'VPS free for 12 months with a purchase' (typically a paid web hosting or domain purchase making the VPS free for its first year). No such 1-year-VPS bundle was visible on the pages fetched today (2026-10-22); the special-deals page currently shows 1-year-term deals (Website Builder $1/mo, WordPress $1/mo, Web Hosting $6/mo) but no free-12-month VPS bundle. Status: possibly inactive right now or gated behind checkout/coupon codes.
findings.eligibility: New customers; no student restriction; CC required; US storefront.
findings.expiry: Time-boxed promo; check the deals page for current codes.
findings.gotchas: 'Free 1-year VPS' in these bundles usually means 12 months at $0 on top of a paid anchor purchase (hosting/domain), often with a longer-term commitment on the paid item afterwards; verify the promo's T&C at checkout, as IONOS rotates and expires these frequently.
findings.name: Rotating promos: free 1-year VPS with purchase / coupon-driven deals

findings.claim: No .edu free tier or education license exists; students get the same consumer trials plus third-party UNiDAYS/coupons.
findings.detail: No IONOS education license or .edu-gated free tier was found. IONOS appears in UNiDAYS (GB) as a student-discount partner, but the partner page lists generic IONOS discounts (domains, hosting, servers) without a quantified student offer; major coupon sites (Cybernews, HostAdvice, updated 2026) explicitly state 'IONOS does not provide a dedicated student discount' and sell unverified generic coupon codes (e.g. up to 94% off web hosting, up to 18% off VPS).
findings.eligibility: Anyone; UNiDAYS listing nominally targets students but no verified .edu requirement on any IONOS offer found. No funding-cap or startup-age condition applies to the standard trials.
findings.expiry: N/A - no perpetual student program; generic trials apply as above.
findings.gotchas: Treat third-party 'student coupon' claims as marketing, not IONOS policy; do not expect .edu verification to unlock a VPS free tier - the only student-adjacent path is the IONOS CLOUD Startup Program's 'special offers for students' via sales contact.
findings.name: Student/education: no dedicated .edu free tier; UNiDAYS listing + generic coupons only

sunset_notes: No verified sunset of the core free offers in 2025-2026: the VPS 30-day money-back trial, the $200/£200 cloud-server starting credit, and the IONOS CLOUD 30-day trial account (8 cores/20GB RAM/600GB storage, EUR 500 cap) were all present on official pages/docs as of 2026-10-22. (2) The VPS lineup was refreshed: a new 'VPS+' generation (Dell enterprise hardware, S+ $2/mo, M+ $5/mo, L+ $8/mo for 3 months on 1-year terms) now fronts the .com VPS pages, while the older 'VPS' line (from $2-4/mo, 3-year terms, $4/mo anchor price) persists at cloud-vps.html; pricing pages show both, so renewals can land on higher list prices than the intro deal. (3) The rotating 'free 1-year VPS with purchase' promo was not visible on any fetched page today and may be between rotations - do not rely on it without a live coupon. WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted after ~4 searches, so 2025-2026 press on sunsets was not exhaustively covered; a startup-program URL returned 404 on fetch.

findings.name: US$100 promotional credit trial (the successor to the "Linode $100 free trial")
findings.detail: New-customer promotional credit of US$100 applied automatically at signup; the current Akamai Cloud pricing/FAQ gives the window as 60 days ("if you received a $100 credit for 60 days..."). Credit covers Compute, Object Storage, Block Storage, and NodeBalancers; GPU plans are excluded. After the credit is exhausted or the window expires, the card on file is charged for remaining balance at standard rates; unused credits expire automatically. One promo code/redemption per business; transferred codes cause account termination.
findings.eligibility: New customers only ("not yet signed up for a free trial"). A valid payment method is required — Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, or PayPal (Google Pay with associated card); a card/PayPal backup is mandatory up front and a pre-authorization may be sent, but you are not charged during the trial. No .edu requirement. No region limit stated on the page (offer localized into 9 languages; Linode data centers still available). No free-CC path: credit card or PayPal IS required.
findings.claim: 1) Go to login.linode.com/signup (via the 'Try Akamai Cloud with US$100 in credits*' banner on akamai.com/cloud/pricing, or directly to https://www.akamai.com/lp/free-credit-100). 2) Sign up with Google SSO, GitHub SSO, or email. 3) Add a valid payment method (not charged during trial). 4) Agree to ToS; the US$100 credit is applied automatically to the new account. Fine print lives in the 'Promotion Redemption Rules & Conditions' linked from the asterisk.
findings.gotchas: It is a trial/credit, not a perpetual free tier — card gets charged for any active service after the credit window; no published extension/renewal. The 60-day figure comes from the pricing-page FAQ example; the LP page itself does not state a fixed day count (the legal rules page is a generic promo-code document: 'Credit amounts are nonstandard and granted at the sole discretion of the Akamai sales team', 'Promo codes expire after one year'). Older Linode links (linode.com/trial) now 404 — the offer only runs through the Akamai Cloud pages/signup. Promo codes don't apply to Marketplace/third-party services.
findings.expiry: 60-day credit window per current FAQ example (standard promos historically 30–60 days; always check the exact period shown in your signup/confirmation). Promotional codes themselves expire after one year per the legal rules page; promo is new-customers-only with no published end date.

findings.name: Rise start-up program (Akamai Cloud start-ups)
findings.detail: 3-year start-up program. Year 1: 'between $500 and $120,000 in cloud credits' (tiered, decided case-by-case; no published formula). Years 2–3: continued discounted cloud services (no published percentage). Includes architecture/migration consulting (valued ~$250/hour), prioritized 24/7 support, dedicated account management. First-year credits do not roll over month-to-month or to subsequent years; overage in a month is billed that month. Contact: startups@akamai.com.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage, for-profit company fewer than 7 years old; at least one of: paid staff beyond founders, active non-affiliated users, initial revenue, or VC backing; must commit to a concrete infrastructure scaling plan and use Akamai Cloud as a primary provider. Must register a commercial account with a corporate email on a matching domain plus a valid credit card. Existing Akamai customers cannot join; managed hosting firms, MSPs, system integrators, and resellers excluded; SaaS, media, and gaming prioritized.
findings.claim: 1) Complete the intake form on https://www.akamai.com/cloud/start-ups/rise (or email startups@akamai.com). 2) Internal review with status update within ~2 weeks. 3) Brief discovery call for qualified applicants. 4) Onboarding — credits loaded onto your account and next steps set with a program coordinator.
findings.gotchas: Credit amount is highly variable ($500–$120,000) and sales-discretionary — most applicants will get far less than the max; monthly credit allotments burn down per month with no rollover. Not a free tier: you're expected to pay for overage. 'Discounted' years 2–3 have no published discount level. Corporate email + card required; individual/education applicants don't qualify.
findings.expiry: Program runs 3 years; year-1 credits expire monthly (no rollover). No published application deadline — rolling intake.

findings.name: Partner start-up program (VCs / accelerators / investors)
findings.detail: Enrollment for VCs, accelerators, and investors, on behalf of portfolio companies. Credits 'up to $3,000/month for a year' for qualified new Akamai Cloud customers (i.e., up to ~$36,000 total per portfolio company). Also technical enablement workshops and a path for strong portfolio companies into Akamai's Tech Partner Program. Developers in a partner's portfolio can start using credits immediately.
findings.eligibility: The partner (fund/accelerator/investor organization) must apply; credits are restricted to 'qualified new customers' of Akamai Cloud (existing Akamai customers excluded). No fund-size or stage thresholds published.
findings.claim: Fill out the 'Become a partner' form on https://www.akamai.com/cloud/start-ups/partner, or email startups@akamai.com — Akamai contacts you to discuss the partnership; portfolio companies then get credits loaded.
findings.gotchas: This is an investor-channel program, not something an individual startup can apply to directly — a startup without VC/accelerator sponsorship should use the Rise program instead. Monthly cap ($3,000) means large month-1 spikes bill to the company; 'qualified' is not defined on the page.
findings.expiry: Credits: up to 12 months at $3,000/month. No published deadline — rolling partner enrollment.

findings.name: Enterprise cloud credits (up to US$5,000) — context only, not a student/startup offer
findings.detail: Akamai Cloud's main cloud page promotes 'up to US$5,000 in cloud credits' for new AND existing enterprise customers, requested via a contact/apply form (in-page '#request-credits'). Per the promo rules, credit amounts are nonstandard and granted at Akamai sales team discretion; one redemption per business; codes expire after one year. Included here for completeness because it's the only other published dollar-amount credit; it targets enterprise sales motion, not students or early-stage startups.
findings.eligibility: Enterprise customers (new and existing), sales-driven; no .edu or startup-age criteria; a valid payment method on account is a standing requirement of the Master Services Agreement.
findings.claim: Use the 'request credits' apply link on https://www.akamai.com/cloud (or Akamai sales); credits are provisioned by the sales team, not self-service.
findings.gotchas: Amount is discretionary (up to $5,000, not guaranteed); no self-service claim; don't confuse with the self-serve $100 new-customer promo.
findings.expiry: Promo codes expire after one year; enterprise grants have no published duration beyond code expiry.

findings.name: Education/Academy: no free student hosting tier exists; free learning content moved to Akamai Academy
findings.detail: No perpetual free-tier VPS plan, and no free student/educator hosting license was found on any current page. linode.com/education, linode.com/linode-education and the old Linode trial/education URLs all 404 today. The free learning asset that remains is the (former) Linode Academy, now Akamai Academy at training.akamai.com/learn (Cloud Computing Foundations and other free courses; certification is separate). Academy = free courses, NOT free hosting. I verified no education program is linked from the Linode homepage or the Akamai Cloud homepage (only 'Cloud Computing Foundations Certification' under training).
findings.eligibility: Anyone can take Academy courses for free; no .edu email requirement found. No hosting entitlement attaches to it.
findings.claim: Visit https://training.akamai.com/learn for free courses. (Note: this site is a JS app; I could not extract course/certification pricing today, so treat certification cost as unverified.)
findings.source_url: https://www.linode.com/ (no education link present); https://www.akamai.com/cloud (no education program present)
findings.gotchas: Old Linode student-facing pages are gone post-rebrand; do not rely on pre-2025 Linode 'education' or 'student trial' claims found in third-party blog posts. If a source cites a Linode student free tier, it is outdated.
findings.expiry: n/a — no such free hosting offer is currently published; verify only via the official pages above.

sunset_notes: 2025 changes (verified against live pages on 2026-10-22): (1) Rebrand — Linode is now 'Akamai Cloud' following Akamai's 2025 acquisition of Linode; linode.com/pricing (and the whole marketing site) now 301-redirects to akamai.com/cloud, and signups still run through login.linode.com. The old standalone 'Linode $100/30-day trial' link (linode.com/trial) now 404s — the trial is now the 'US$100 in credits' promo on Akamai Cloud pages, with the FAQ example stating a 60-day window (older promos were 30 days; ~30-60 days is the right mental model, but the exact window is per your signup/confirmation). (2) No perpetual free VPS tier has ever existed at Linode — the only recurring 'free' element on the pricing page is Object Storage's monthly free outbound egress allowance before overage (quantity not quantified on the page). (3) learn.linode.com (Linode Academy) no longer resolves (DNS ENOTFOUND) — training content moved to training.akamai.com/learn; there is no student/educator free-hosting license at Akamai Cloud today, so any 2025/2026 source claiming a 'Linode free student plan' is outdated. (4) WebSearch was unavailable in this session (budget exhausted), so corroboration relied on official pages fetched today; the $100 offer's exact day count remains a FAQ example rather than a hard-published policy figure.

findings.name: 30-day $100 Free Trial (VPS)
findings.detail: Free 30-day trial with cloud services worth up to $100: 1 cloud server (custom CPU/RAM/storage config) valued up to $100/month, plus 1 TB cloud block storage, 1 TB traffic (inbound+outbound), full platform access, scaling within the $100 config, technical consultation and 24/7 support. Trial clock does NOT start at signup - it starts when the first server is created; account stays on hold until then. Trial ends after 30 days, then standard billing begins; account may be placed in 'deposit mode' requiring a minimum deposit to stay active. Overages during the trial (beyond 1 server/$100 config or 1 TB traffic) trigger an email alert; unadjusted overage is charged pro-rata to the card and credited against the first monthly invoice. A small validation charge (~$1-2) may be taken on card; a fully-refundable deposit (e.g., $10) can be requested when unusual billing activity is detected.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone - no .edu email, region limit, or user-type restriction stated. Credit card NOT optional: a valid credit/debit card is required to activate the trial; if the card is not accepted, a pre-paid refundable deposit via PayPal is allowed instead. One account and one 30-day free trial per customer - multiple trials via multiple accounts is explicitly prohibited. Password must be 8+ chars with lowercase, uppercase and number.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at kamatera.com/free-trial with email + compliant password; 2) verify email; 3) complete Billing profile in console (personal info, phone verification, card entry); 4) card validation charge may occur; 5) create first server - trial starts; 6) within limits no charge; to exit, terminate servers - no charge.
findings.expiry: 30 days from creation of first server; no renewals - after 30 days it converts to a paid account (deposit mode applies if no valid payment). No sunset date published; page carries (c) 2026.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free: this is a limited trial, not a perpetual free tier. CC (or PayPal deposit) is required even though nothing is charged within limits. 1 TB traffic includes BOTH directions. Server with 'powered off' state still incurs small hourly storage/IP charges. First invoice after trial generated on 1st of the month cycle. 1-server cap.

findings.name: RiseUP Cloud Start-Up Program - up to 24 months of infrastructure credit
findings.detail: Startup program at startup.kamatera.com: 'Twenty-four months of runway, on us.' Up to 24 months of infrastructure services credit (dollar cap per month NOT disclosed on the page) plus, all 24 months: a personal account manager, a dedicated cloud consultant, a business consultant on request (Tech/Sales/Marketing/Finance/HR), and marketing & PR access through Kamatera's partner network. Available across Kamatera's 25 datacentres / 21 locations / 4 continents. Applying is free and non-binding; the team reviews and contacts applicants to 'discuss your options.' Page is live with (c) 2026.
findings.eligibility: All five required: (1) within the first 5 years of the company's funding, (2) a company website - live or in development, (3) an active LinkedIn page - live or in development, (4) 'the intention to become a unicorn', (5) a signed Start-Up Program agreement. If close on one criterion, the page invites applying anyway and explaining in the message. No .edu/student path; no funding cap amount stated beyond the 5-year-from-funding window.
findings.claim: Fill the application form at startup.kamatera.com (name, email, phone with 8+ digits, company name, company website, optional free-text), submit; Kamatera's team reviews and follows up. Corporate office phone listed: 074-70-50-340.
findings.expiry: Credit runs from month 0 to month 24 ('first 24 months of credit'). No renewal/extension terms disclosed on the page.
findings.gotchas: No dollar figure or per-month cap published - 'credit' is opaque; program terms are set via a signed agreement and individual review, so actual allocation is discretionary. No CC/billing mechanics disclosed on the page. Program is targeted at startups (companies), not individual students/hobbyists. Program appears newly launched in the 2025-2026 period (could not independently date the launch - see sunset_notes).

findings.name: No dedicated student/education program, no perpetual free tier (students use the generic trial)
findings.detail: Kamatera publishes no .edu-verified student program, no education license, and no perpetual 'free tier' for VPS. Students are served by the same $100/30-day trial, which third-party student-hosting roundups (ProBlogGuru, HostAdvice, LinuxBuz 2026 lists) recommend to students precisely because no student ID is required. Kamatera is a VPS/IaaS-only provider - it has no bare-metal/dedicated-physical-server line, so its offers cover virtual servers only (dedicated vCPU configs available inside the trial).
findings.eligibility: Students: same as generic trial (anyone with a credit card). No .edu email, no student verification, no regional restriction stated.
findings.claim: Same claim path as the $100 trial; no separate student application exists.
findings.expiry: n/a - absence of an offer; generic trial remains live as of 2026-10 (page (c) 2026).
findings.gotchas: Third-party 'Kamatera student' content is repackaged trial marketing, not a distinct product. Do not treat any '1MONTH300'-style promo codes quoted in blogs as current without verifying in the console.

sunset_notes: No Kamatera free offer found closed or materially changed in 2025-2026. The $100/30-day trial has been continuous: Kamatera's own Jan 2025 YouTube ad and the 2026 official page both carry the identical $100/30-day/1TB terms, and third-party 2026 roundups still list it. The RiseUP startup program (24 months of infrastructure credit, startup.kamatera.com, page copyright 2026) appears to be a NEW 2025-2026 program; the older generic 'Cloud Solutions for Tech Startups' marketing page (kamatera.com/solutions/use-cases/startups, last seen 2023) contained no concrete free credit. Could not independently date the RiseUP launch: the session's shared WebSearch budget was exhausted before verifying launch history.

findings.name: Automatic $5 / 90-day signup credit (new accounts)
findings.detail: Per official docs: 'When you create your first team, DigitalOcean automatically applies a $5 signup credit.' No promo code required. The credit applies to all products except SaaS Add-Ons — so it covers Droplets (VPS), bare metal and dedicated servers, App Platform, etc. A valid payment method must be on file before you can create resources; your card is charged only after the credit is exhausted or the 90-day window expires ('if you received a $5 credit for 90 days, then that $5 credit is automatically applied to your account' — pricing FAQ). Credit expires 90 days after signup; it cannot be transferred to other teams. Governing 'Promotional Credit & Discount Terms' (last updated Jun 7 2024): no cash value, non-transferable, no stacking with other promotions, exclusions for Marketplace/Support/crypto mining, voiding for accounts created solely to obtain credits. Docs page last verified 15 Jul 2026.
findings.eligibility: All new accounts — any person/company's first DigitalOcean team. No student or startup status needed, no .edu email. A credit card or other valid payment method (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Discover, PayPal, Google/Apple Pay) is required on file, so it is NOT a no-credit-card offer; billing only happens after credit exhaustion or the 90-day expiry. No region limits stated on the page.
findings.claim: Automatic: create your first team; the $5 credit is applied with no code and no application. Add a payment method first. Claim: free on everything non-SaaS Add-On up to $5.
findings.expiry: 90 days from account signup; no renewal; one-time only (first team only, non-transferable to later teams).
findings.gotchas: Payment method required (trial-style, not card-free). Amount is small ($5) vs the wound-down former $200/60-day trial. 'All products except SaaS Add-Ons' still covers bare metal and dedicated, but DO Marketplace products and DO Support are excluded from promotional credits per the legal terms. Overage beyond $5 (or any spend after day 90) bills normally; free outbound bandwidth allowance (e.g., 500 GiB/mo on small Droplets) and free reserved IP/DNS are separate product inclusions, not credit. Fraud/accounts created solely for credits are voided.

findings.name: DigitalOcean Startup Program (startup credits via partner networks)
findings.detail: Official program page (fetched today): rolling 12-month platform-credit window; credit amount 'varies' and is determined through approved partner organizations/accelerators; participants 'are entitled to a $10,000 monthly limit' beyond which standard charges apply. GPU credits exist separately for select applicants after review. Enrolled startups also get free access to Standard-tier paid support for 15 months and discounted third-party perks (e.g., Stripe Atlas 20% off, QuickNode up to $5k, Airtable $2,000, Miro $1,000). As of May 13 2026, credits explicitly EXCLUDE: GPU Droplets, NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, Dedicated Inference, Serverless Inference, third-party AI models (Anthropic, OpenAI), Paperspace Machines, Cloudways, and pass-through third-party charges; crypto mining and excessive resource consumption prohibited; credits non-transferable. Co-branded with Y Combinator, Techstars, a16z, Backstage Capital, etc. 'The DigitalOcean Startups program does not grant extensions' and unused credits are 'forfeited'.
findings.eligibility: Startups only: must have raised $10m or less; a company website with a matching corporate email; registered DO team account on a business (not personal) email; program targets 'new startups that have not used prior credits with DigitalOcean' and 'prioritizes AI-native startups'; service-based companies (consulting, web/app dev services, marketing agencies) are NOT eligible. No company-age floor, employee cap, or geographic restriction stated. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Two paths: (1) if backed by a partner/accelerator on the portfolio list, route through that partner's program manager; (2) otherwise fill out the application via the Typeform on the /startups page and select 'Other' as the affiliated partner. Once accepted, perks are delivered via the 'Welcome Kit'. The partner determines the actual credit amount (undisclosed publicly; $10k/month cap on usage).
findings.expiry: Rolling 12-month credit window from enrollment; no extensions granted; unused credits forfeited at window end; no calendar application deadline published (rolling eligibility).
findings.gotchas: Exact credit amount is undisclosed ('varies' by partner) — treat any figure circulating ($10k–$250k historically) as unverified. GPU and bare-metal-GPU products and third-party AI model spend are excluded from credits (as of May 13 2026), so this program does NOT reliably fund GPU/dedicated AI hardware. Non-transferable, no stacking with the signup credit is addressed in the Promo Credit terms. 15-month support perk is Standard tier only.

findings.name: Wavemakers Program (community chapter leaders — open, not student/startup-specific)
findings.detail: DigitalOcean-supported local community chapters; leaders 'Get access to DO credits to use on our platform' (no dollar amount or duration published), plus exclusive swag, invite-only events/workshops, and web/social features. Leaders must host at least four events per year (one per quarter, virtual or in-person), serve as the main point of contact, use the designated event platform, and stay in touch with DO. FAQ: open to 'tech enthusiasts, community builders, and influencers from all backgrounds' and worldwide (U.S. not required).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone who wants to lead a local DO community chapter — not restricted to students or startups. No .edu or company requirement; global.
findings.claim: As member: join via the linked Meetup. As chapter leader: (1) fill out the quick application (Google Form), (2) DO team reviews and contacts you with next steps, (3) receive a welcome packet including a community leader toolkit; credits arrive through DO's side once established.
findings.expiry: No application deadline, credit expiry, or duration published on the page; ongoing rolling program.
findings.gotchas: Credit amount, duration, and product scope are NOT disclosed — low value certainty; it's primarily a community commitment (4 events/year). Do not treat this as a budget-grade credit source.

findings.name: Always-free product tiers and add-ons (all accounts, incl. VPS customers)
findings.detail: From the official pricing page (fetched today): 'Build and deploy 3 static sites for free' (App Platform static sites); 'One Uptime Check/month included with every account'; Kubernetes: 'Free control plane, free bandwidth allowance' (node plans from $12/mo); free VPCs (unlimited, intra-DC peering free); free reserved IPs when attached to a Droplet, free DNS, free cloud firewalls; Container Registry: 'Free container registry with 1 repository and 500 MiB storage'; Functions free tier as printed on the pricing page: 'Use 90,000 GiB-seconds per month for free with DigitalOcean Functions' and 'no additional charges for function invocations'; Droplets include free outbound transfer starting at 500 GiB/mo (overage $0.01/GiB). NOTE: there is no free Droplet/VPS tier — the $5/90-day signup credit is the only standing free-usage grant for VPS.
findings.eligibility: All accounts, no application, no student/startup status. No .edu requirement; no region limit stated. No credit card required to hold the free add-ons (a free-tier-only usage of, e.g., a static site or registry can be exercised without spend).
findings.claim: Inherent: provision the resources in the control panel (static site on App Platform, registry, VPC, K8s free control plane); nothing to apply for.
findings.expiry: Perpetual; no published expiry or renewal cycle.
findings.gotchas: The Functions '90,000 GiB-seconds' figure is exactly as printed on /pricing/ today but could not be cross-checked against a /functions/ product page (404 at fetch time) — medium certainty on that number. Free static sites: 3 sites cap; app (dynamic) sites on App Platform are not free. Free K8s control plane still requires paid nodes (from $12/mo). The often-cited '$5/mo for 250 GB Spaces' is a paid entry price, not a free offer. Free egress allowances attach to specific Droplet sizes; bare metal/dedicated have their own plans (no free tier).

findings.name: Education / student or educator programs — none currently published (negative finding)
findings.detail: No education license, student program, or educator discount is published on DigitalOcean's site as of today: /education/, /educators/, /community/education/, docs /platform/education/, and blog tag /education/ all return HTTP 404 (verified by fetch today). The pricing page FAQ contains no student/education offers, and the legal index shows no education-specific credit terms. The only standing free grant for new users (any user) is the $5/90-day signup credit.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no current education offer to be eligible for. .edu email would not unlock anything specifically.
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim; students effectively get the same $5/90-day signup credit as any new account (and Startup/Wavemakers programs if they meet those programs' criteria).
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Absence verified by direct URL checks today, but WebSearch was unavailable in this session (budget exhausted), so I could not confirm via third-party news whether an education program existed in 2025 and was quietly removed.

sunset_notes: Sunset/change notes for 2025–2026: (1) The former $200/60-day new-user trial is wound down — the old trial landing pages (/free-trial/ and /trial/) now 404 (verified today), and it has been replaced by the small automatic $5/90-day signup credit applied to the first team (docs page last verified 15 Jul 2026). (2) Startup Program: effective May 13 2026, credits were re-scoped to EXCLUDE GPU Droplets, NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, Dedicated Inference, Serverless Inference, third-party AI models (Anthropic/OpenAI), Paperspace and Cloudways — so startup credits no longer fund GPU/bare-metal AI hardware; program also explicitly grants no extensions and forfeits unused credits. (3) Wavemakers is DigitalOcean's current community-chapter program (replacing/continuing the older 'DigitalOcean Community Chapter' branding) with unpublished credit amounts. (4) No evidence of any education/student program in the 2025–2026 official site; the Promotional Credit & Discount Terms page is unchanged since June 7 2024. Method caveat: WebSearch was unavailable for this session (shared budget exhausted), so the '2025-2026 changes' cross-check relied solely on WebFetch of DigitalOcean's official pages; third-party press coverage was not verified.

findings.claim: Sign up at azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free → verify phone + card (temporary $1 hold) → $200 credit active for 30 days → within 30 days move to pay-as-you-go (portal: Subscriptions → Upgrade subscription) to keep the 12-month free amounts; otherwise services are disabled at day 30.
findings.detail: New Azure customers get $200 credit usable for 30 days (or until credit is exhausted), plus the 12-month free service amounts and 65+ always-free services on top. After 30 days / credit exhaustion the account and services are DISABLED (not auto-converted); you must move to pay-as-you-go to continue. Unused credit stays available for the full 30 days from creation. Credit cannot be applied to Azure Marketplace offers or Azure Spot VMs. Sovereign cloud products in US Government, Azure China, and Azure Germany are excluded. No $100 12-month credit is listed on the current pages — the standard trial is $200/30 days only.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only (one free account per new customer). Requires phone number, a credit or debit card (non-prepaid), and a Microsoft or GitHub account. A temporary ~$1 authorization is placed on the card and reversed on verification; the card is not otherwise charged. Only credit cards accepted in Hong Kong and Brazil. Offer unavailable in countries not on Microsoft's list; 'If your country is not listed, the offer is not available in your region.'
findings.expiry: Credit: 30 days from account creation (unused credit lost). Free service amounts: 12 months after sign-up for the trial account. Renewal: none — after 12 months, used services bill at PAYG rates.
findings.gotchas: VPS angle: the 12-month free VM allowance covers B1s, B2pts v2 (ARM) and B2ats v2 (AMD) burstable VMs only — 750 hours each per month. That is roughly 24h/day for one VM; larger/Standard VMs are NOT covered. Data transfer/egress beyond free allowances and storage beyond free quotas bill at PAYG rates even in the trial. Account is disabled (not billed) if you do nothing — but resources are inaccessible until upgrade.
findings.name: Azure free account: $200 credit, 30 days

findings.claim: No separate claim — included automatically when creating any Azure account (free trial or PAYG, new customer). Create resources via the 'Free services' page in the Azure portal with free tiers selected to avoid accidental billing.
findings.detail: Free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months: VMs 750 hours/month each of B1s, B2pts v2 (ARM-based), B2ats v2 (AMD-based) burstable VMs; Azure Container Registry: 1 Standard registry, 100 GB storage, 10 webhooks; PostgreSQL Flexible Server: 750 hours Burstable B1MS + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup; MySQL Flexible Server: same 750 hours B1MS + 32 GB + 32 GB; Azure SQL Managed Instance: 720 vCore hours of 4 or 8 vCore General Purpose (64 GB data + 64 GB backup); Azure Vision (Foundry Tools): 5,000 transactions per S1/S2/S3 tier. Can be consumed in any region where the service is available and split across instances (e.g. 5 VMs × 150 h). Services in use after 12 months continue running and bill at PAYG.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only — 'not previously had an Azure account or received 12 months of free services.' NOT currently available to customers who sign up directly for pay-as-you-go in China and India. Trial signups must move to pay-as-you-go within 30 days to keep receiving them.
findings.expiry: 12 months from account creation; unused monthly amounts do not roll over; after 12 months everything in use bills at PAYG rates. No renewal.
findings.gotchas: For a free VPS: 750 h/month is the total shared across B1s/B2pts v2/B2ats v2 — a single always-on B1s VM works for ~12 months, but nothing above B-series burstable is free. 'Always-free' services (65+) do NOT include VMs, so a pure PAYG account beyond 12 months has no free compute; only the free service tiers listed remain. Egress/storage beyond free quotas bill.
findings.name: 12-month free service amounts (new customers)

findings.claim: Automatic with any Azure account; create resources on the free tiers. This is the realistic 'always-free tier' for lightweight workloads (serverless/PaaS) — but NOT for VPS: no free VM tier exists in the always-free set.
findings.detail: Permanent free monthly amounts for every Azure account: App Service (10 web/API apps, 1 GB storage, 1 hour/day compute), Functions (1 million requests), Container Apps (180,000 vCPU-s, 360,000 GiB-s, 2M requests), Static Web Apps (0.5 GB/app, 100 GB bandwidth/subscription), AKS cluster management (nodes bill), Cosmos DB (1,000 RU/s + 25 GB), Azure SQL serverless (100,000 vCore-s + 32 GB/month), DocumentDB (32 GB cluster), Azure Data Factory (5 low-frequency activities), API Management Consumption (1M calls/month), Logic Apps Consumption (4,000 actions), Notification Hubs (1M pushes), IoT Hub (8,000 msgs/day), AI/Foundry services (Speech 0.5M chars, Translator 2M chars, Document Intelligence 500 pages S0, AI Search 50 MB/10k docs/3 indexes, Vision/Content Safety tiers), Azure DevOps (5 users), Azure Machine Learning (free, egress may apply), plus free/unlimited management services (Monitor control plane, Arc, Advisor, Migrate, Cost Management, Lighthouse, etc.).
findings.eligibility: All Azure customers, no verification beyond having an account; no credit card needed if usage stays within free amounts.
findings.expiry: No expiry while the account exists; monthly allowances reset each month. Cloud Shell's 5 GB free storage in Azure Files lasts 12 months only.
findings.gotchas: App Service '1 hour per day' makes it usable as a very small always-on worker but it's not a VM. Egress, premium storage and anything above free tier limits bill. AKS is 'free' only for cluster management — node VMs bill.
findings.name: Always-free services (65+, all accounts)

findings.claim: Sign up at azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students with your school email (no card) → $100 credit + free tiers active → renew annually while still a student by re-verifying with the school email (reminder emails ~30 days before anniversary). Track remaining credit in the Azure Sponsorships portal.
findings.detail: $100 in Azure credit usable within 12 months, plus 20+ 12-month free service amounts and 65+ always-free services; includes Azure OpenAI/Foundry access and free dev-tool downloads via the Azure Education Hub (Visual Studio, SQL Server, Windows Server, etc.). Unused credit cannot carry over between months/subscriptions. If the $100 runs out early the subscription is disabled; you get a 90-day window after the free period to upgrade to PAYG, otherwise products are decommissioned. One subscription per person, non-transferable, cannot combine with other offers. Not available for MOOCs or for-profit training. Credit cannot be applied to Azure Marketplace offers.
findings.eligibility: Full-time students at an accredited, degree-granting two-year or four-year institution; must be 18+; verified through the institution's email (school/.edu address). No credit card required at sign-up. Limited supply — available while supplies last; Microsoft may terminate the offer at its discretion.
findings.expiry: Credit valid 12 months from sign-up (whichever first, credit or time, disables the subscription). Renewable each year while a student — renewal grants a fresh $100; unused credit does not carry over.
findings.gotchas: The 12-month VM allowance here is the same B1s/B2pts v2/B2ats v2 750 h/month — fine for a small always-on VPS, but only burstable tiers. A Microsoft Q&A thread confirms $100 exhaustion disables the subscription (in markets where the credit converts to local-currency spend, e.g. ~₹8,500 in India). Student accounts are for education/non-commercial use; production commercial workloads violate terms. No .edu email → ineligible (use Students Starter or the standard trial instead).
findings.name: Azure for Students: $100 credit, 12 months, renewable yearly

findings.claim: Sign up at azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students (Start free) choosing the Starter variant; verify school email; no card. Upgrade via Azure portal → Subscriptions → Upgrade when ready.
findings.detail: A second education offer: 'Azure for Students Starter' — academic email verification, no credit card, access to selected free Azure services (e.g. App Service free tiers) without the $100 credit. It is the fallback for academic users not eligible for the full Azure for Students offer; from a Starter account you can upgrade to an Azure free account (getting $200 credit + 12-month free services) if eligible, or to pay-as-you-go.
findings.eligibility: Academic users with a verifiable school email who do not qualify for the full Azure for Students offer (full-time student of an accredited institution); no credit card required. Country coverage follows where Azure is commercially available.
findings.expiry: Free service amounts run while the subscription is active (12 months for the new-customer amounts). No stated credit because there is no credit pool.
findings.gotchas: Exact per-service Starter allowances are not itemized on the current /free/students page (Microsoft's academic content describes it as 'use select Azure products like App Services for free') — treat specific limits as unconfirmed. Not a substitute for the $100 credit; best used as a path to the standard free account ($200/30 days).
findings.name: Azure for Students Starter (no-credit-card, no-$100 tier)

findings.claim: No application: create an Azure account under the Azure for Startups offer (linked from azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students and microsoft.com/startups) → $1,000 credit active for 90 days → complete business verification → additional up to $4,000 for 180 days.
findings.detail: The self-service startup credit offer (open track of the two-track system introduced July 1, 2025): $1,000 in Azure credits instantly, no application required, valid 90 days; up to $4,000 more (total $5,000) unlocked after business verification, valid 180 days. Full Azure catalog access up to credit limits; after expiry/usage the account moves to pay-as-you-go. No dedicated support — self-serve.
findings.eligibility: Startups that are NEW to Azure (new Azure customers only). Business verification = confirmation the startup is a registered legal entity. A credit card is required only for identity verification and for usage beyond the credits.
findings.expiry: Initial $1,000: 90 days. Post-verification $4,000: 180 days. Then PAYG. No renewal; cannot combine with other offers unless Microsoft permits.
findings.gotchas: This is the post-July-2025 self-service track — it replaced the old unfunded-startup tiers (former L1-L4 up to $150k). Note the marketing card says $1,000 instant, while the Microsoft for Startups program application (separate, see other finding) starts at $200 — they are different entry points.
findings.name: Azure for Startups (self-service credit offer, up to $5,000)

findings.claim: Go to startups.microsoft.com (or microsoft.com/startups) → Get started → submit application → starter credits available during review (~3 business days) → business verification → grow workloads to unlock higher tiers; credits managed in the Microsoft for Startups portal in the Azure portal (primary experience for those who joined after May 29, 2026).
findings.detail: Current (2026) milestone structure from the official getting-started doc (updated 2026-08-05): apply at startups.microsoft.com → M1 $200 (sign up + personal-LINKEDIN identity verification, no business accounts), M2 $5,000 (business verification — registered legal entity), M3 $25,000 (5+ Azure workloads active ~60 days), M4 $50,000 (7+ workloads ~60 days), M5 $150,000 (10+ workloads + ~$3,000/month Azure usage sustained ~60 days).
