Milestones can be skipped; at $25K you get a one-time two-year credit-use extension. Workload = a distinct actively-used Azure service (VMs, AI models, databases, hosting). Investor-network track (introduced July 2025): startups referred by an affiliated investor/accelerator/university start at $100,000 with dedicated support. Pegasus (invitation-only CSM support) continues unchanged.
findings.eligibility: Startups applying through the program; no publicly stated startup-age or funding cap in the current 2026 docs (the older program required companies founded <2 years — that explicit criterion is not on the current page). Personal LinkedIn at M1; registered legal entity for M2.
findings.expiry: 2-year use window at the $25K milestone (one-time extension). Higher-tier availability requires sustained ~$3,000/month usage for 60 days — credits subsidize, not replace, that spend. No stated hard expiry for the top tier.
findings.gotchas: Every workload must stay above $1 spend for the full 60-day window or the count resets. 'Up to $150k' effectively requires ~$3k/month real spend across 10+ services — it is not free infrastructure for a small VPS. GPU availability has been reported as chronically constrained by participants. Program rules have changed 3 times since 2025 (see sunset notes) — re-verify before planning.
findings.name: Microsoft for Startups program: milestone credits up to $150,000 (2026 structure)

findings.claim: Apply through Microsoft's nonprofit program (microsoft.com/en-us/nonprofits / Tech for Social Impact portal); upon approval the $2,000 Azure grant is credited and can renew each year while the organization stays eligible.
findings.detail: Registered nonprofits receive a $2,000 Azure grant annually, plus broader Dynamics 365 / Microsoft 365 grants and discounts. Amount confirmed on the Azure offers page and the Azure free account offer-terms page read today ('a $2,000 Azure grant annually'); deeper eligibility is mediated through Microsoft's tech-for-social-impact program (TechSoup partnership).
findings.eligibility: 501(c)(3)-equivalent registered nonprofit organizations; individuals not eligible; organizational verification required.
findings.expiry: Annual grant; renews yearly. Not a trial — it is a recurring sponsorship.
findings.gotchas: Not relevant for personal VPS use; listed because it is a distinct standing free/low-cost offer on the Azure side. Grant mechanics (channel, exact process) are confirmed at headline level only.
findings.name: Azure for Nonprofits: $2,000 grant annually

findings.claim: Contact Microsoft / apply via the Azure Accelerate page; credits allocated case-by-case.
findings.detail: Azure Accelerate offers free Azure credits 'to help offset migration costs and fuel your cloud transformation and AI journey,' with expert access. It is a program for existing/migrating customers rather than a sign-up free offer for new accounts; the offers page does not publish a fixed credit amount today.
findings.eligibility: Organizations migrating to Azure; qualification-based (no published dollar figure on the offers page read today).
findings.expiry: Not stated on the offers page.
findings.gotchas: Treat as supplementary/uncertain — no concrete amount verified today; useful only for migration scenarios, not for a free VPS.
findings.name: Azure Accelerate (free migration credits for existing customers)

provider: Microsoft Azure Free Trial (VPS / cloud VM)
sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes to be aware of: (1) The legacy '12-month free services + $100 credit' structure in the STANDARD free account no longer appears on the current official pages — the trial is now $200 for 30 days plus 12-month free amounts; the '$100 12-month credit' noted in 'known so far' appears outdated (medium confidence on the removal; not visible on /free or /pricing/free-services read today). (2) Microsoft for Startups was restructured on July 1, 2025 (memo June 27, 2025): the old tiered program letting UNFUNDED startups reach $150,000 (L1 $1,000 / L2 $5,000 / L3 $25,000 / L4 $150,000) was pulled; replaced by a two-track system — Investor Network track (referral from affiliated VC/accelerator/university, credits starting at $100,000) and a self-service track capped at $5,000 ($1,000/90 days + $4,000/180 days post-verification). Activated legacy credits remained valid until expiry. (3) The program changed again: for anyone who joined Microsoft for Startups after May 29, 2026, the Azure Portal becomes the primary experience and credits are milestone-based ($200 → $5k → $25k → $50k → $150k based on workload count and ~$3,000/month usage over 60 days; docs updated 2026-08-05), effectively re-opening the $150k ceiling via usage milestones rather than investor referral. (4) 'Azure for Teachers' ($1,000 credit for educators) has no current offer page — it was sunset years ago; faculty now use the standard $200/30-day free account (card required) or institution-level Microsoft Learn for Educators (MSLE, which channels the $100 student credit). (5) The 'Azure 6 months free for Visual Studio subscribers' developer offer page (azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/visual-studio) returns 404 — that offer appears discontinued as of today. (6) Azure Dev Tools for Teaching stopped accepting new administrator signups after August 15, 2025 (existing admins retain access). (7) Pegasus (invitation-only startup support) was explicitly unchanged by the 2025 restructure. (8) Many 'Foundry Tools' lines reflect the 2025–2026 Azure AI rebrand (Azure AI Services → Azure AI Foundry); amounts themselves are unchanged.

findings.name: GCP Free Trial — $300 credit, 90 days
findings.detail: New-customer Welcome credit of $300, valid 90 days from signup, in a preloaded Free Trial billing account; not billed unless the $300 is exhausted; trial access to products may be limited to prevent abuse. During the trial the customer also has access to the Always Free tier. Verified on the official docs page read 2026-10-22: 'The Free Trial gets you a $300 Welcome credit to spend over 90 days... you won't be billed' and 'preloaded with $300 in free Welcome credit which is valid for 90 days'.
findings.eligibility: Must have never been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase, and must not have previously signed up for the Free Trial (effectively one trial per person/company; students qualify the same way). A credit card or other valid payment method IS required at signup (bank-account verification may also be needed in some countries). No .edu requirement, no region stated on the page. The 'credit card NOT required' claim is FALSE for the trial: signup docs state 'you must provide a credit card or other payment method that is valid for the period of the Free Trial'.
findings.claim: 1) Go to cloud.google.com/free (or Console) and start the Free Trial; 2) add a valid payment method; 3) $300 is preloaded into the trial billing account; 4) optionally upgrade to a Paid billing account during the trial — unused credit is then retained until 90 days from signup.
findings.expiry: Credit expires 90 days from signup. If you do not upgrade to a Paid billing account before 90 days, or spend the whole $300, the Free Trial billing account is closed and all its projects/resources are stopped (i.e., your VPS dies and you lose unspent credit). Free Tier access continues afterwards only with an active billing account.
findings.gotchas: Card required even if usage is $0 (temporary authorization hold on signup). Trial end = account closure + stopped resources, not a silent conversion. $300 counts toward the '<$5,000 previously received GCP credits' cap of the startup program. One trial per customer (never a paying GCP/Maps/Firebase user).

findings.name: GCP Always Free tier — free VPS (e2-micro) + 20+ products
findings.detail: Free-forever monthly quotas (no expiration, subject to change). VPS-relevant Compute Engine: 1 non-preemptible e2-micro VM per month in us-west1 (Oregon), us-central1 (Iowa) or us-east1 (South Carolina), plus 30 GB-months standard persistent disk, plus 1 GB/month outbound egress from North America (excl. China/Australia). VM limit is by time, not instance count; GPUs/TPUs are never free. Other verified quotas: Cloud Run 2M requests/mo + 360,000 GB-seconds memory + 180,000 vCPU-seconds + 1 GB North America egress; Cloud Run Functions 2M invocations + 400,000 GB-seconds + 5 GB egress; Cloud Shell 5 GB persistent disk; Cloud Source Repos 5 users/50 GB; BigQuery 1 TiB query + 10 GiB storage; Cloud Build 2,500 build-minutes; Artifact Registry 0.5 GB; Firestore 1 GiB storage + 50k reads/20k writes/20k deletes per day + 10 GiB egress; GKE 1 free Autopilot or zonal Standard cluster per month (credit excludes compute/networking); Pub/Sub 10 GiB messages; reCAPTCHA 10k; Cloud Vision 1,000 units; Cloud Natural Language 5,000 units; Cloud Monitoring API 1M time series; Cloud Storage 5 GB-months Standard (free-tier benefits only in the 3 US regions); Datastream 100 GiB CDC (AlloyDB/Spanner→BigQuery only).
findings.eligibility: Active billing account (Paid OR Free Trial) in good standing, and no negotiated pricing contract. A payment method is effectively required because the billing account comes from card signup (trial) or a paid account; no .edu or age requirement. No per-country limit stated, but free Compute/Storage capacity is limited to the 3 US regions.
findings.claim: Sign up for GCP (Free Trial or paid account), create a project, launch an e2-micro VM in us-west1/us-central1/us-east1 with ≤30 GB standard pd-SSD — usage within the quotas is never billed. No separate activation step.
findings.expiry: No expiry; quotas refresh monthly and 'do not expire, but are subject to change'. Free VM regions are fixed (us-west1, us-central1, us-east1 only).
findings.gotchas: e2-micro is a 2 vCPU / 1 GB burstable micro instance — hobby VPS, not production. 30 GB disk + 1 GB egress are small; egress beyond 1 GB/month is billed. Stopped-VM disk still consumes the 30 GB-months quota. Free GKE cluster credit does not cover node compute or networking. No free bare-metal or dedicated-server option exists at GCP at all — the e2-micro (or Cloud Run) is the only 'free server'.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program — up to $350,000 GCP credits over 2 years (AI & non-AI tiers)
findings.detail: Successor to the old 'Cloud Startups' program, verified on startup.google.com/cloud (read 2026-10-22): headline 'up to $350,000 in Cloud credits over two years'. AI startups: Year 1 = 100% of GCP spend up to $250,000; Year 2 = 20% of Year-2 spend, up to an additional $100,000 in credits. Non-AI startups: Year 1 = 100% up to $100,000; Year 2 = 20% up to $100,000. Third-party model spend (e.g. Anthropic models on Vertex) is billed directly and NOT covered. Credits may only be used by the original applicant — no sharing/splitting/reselling. Non-credit benefits in the program: 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no cost (domain must not have had a paid Workspace plan in the prior 31 days), monthly Google Maps Platform credits (separate application), Google Skills training, dedicated Startup Success Managers/Customer Engineering, and Google Cloud Marketplace co-sell.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Seed to Series A stage; founded within the last 3-5 years; previously received less than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits; digital-native startup with a scalable proprietary product, a working MVP, and a verified company domain; company email matching the public website; valid GCP account + Billing ID required. Excluded: companies that IPO'd or were acquired, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs, dev shops/consultancies/agencies, crypto mining. No US-registered-entity or .edu requirement is stated on the current page (the legacy program was US-centric).
findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup/apply with your company email that matches your website; have a GCP account + Billing ID ready; pass program review; credits are applied to your billing account and usable for the Year-1 window plus the Year-2 top-up.
findings.expiry: Two-year structure: 100% coverage window in Year 1 (up to the tier cap), then a Year-2 top-up of 20% of spend up to $100,000. Unused Year-1 credit is not carried into Year 2.
findings.gotchas: The '<$5,000 previously received GCP credits' cap means heavy trial/legacy-program users can be disqualified. 'Founded within the last 3-5 years' is tier-dependent — older startups may not qualify. Third-party (non-Google) model spend is out of scope. Credits cannot be resold or shared with partners.

findings.name: Gemini API free tier (Google AI Studio) — no credit card required
findings.detail: Free tier of the Gemini API / Google AI Studio, verified at ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits (2026-10-22): qualification = 'Active project or free trial' (i.e., no billing account and no credit card needed) with no spend cap; paid tiers are Tier 1 ($250 cap, active billing account), Tier 2 ($2,000 cap, $100 + 3 days from first payment), Tier 3 (higher, $1,000 + 30 days). Free usage is rate-limited per model on RPM (requests/min), TPM (input tokens/min) and RPD (requests/day, reset midnight PT). Available to students and to bootstrapped/self-funded startups — the startup program also advertises 'free access to the Gemini API in Google AI Studio' on its Prototype track. Not a VPS offer, but a distinct card-free free tier.
findings.eligibility: Any Google account that creates a GCP project; no payment method, no .edu, no startup status required. Students: same access.
findings.claim: Sign in at aistudio.google.com (or use the API key from AI Studio) — free-tier rate limits apply automatically; no billing setup.
findings.expiry: No expiration; limits are per-minute/per-day and may change by model. Exact per-model free RPM/TPM/RPD numbers are in a JS-rendered table I could not extract today — treat specific figures as unverified.
findings.gotchas: Free tier excludes batch/long-context features of paid tiers; spend-based limits only protect paid accounts. Do not confuse 'free tier' with the $300 trial (which does require a card).

findings.name: Product-specific free trials (GKE, Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, Bigtable)
findings.detail: On cloud.google.com/free (read 2026-10-22), new-customer product trials beyond the $300 credit: GKE — 90 days, full capabilities, no fee (fleet-based team management, GitOps config, GKE on hybrid/multicloud); Cloud SQL — 30-day trial of an 8 vCPU Enterprise Plus instance, 64 GB memory, 100 GB storage; Spanner — 90-day trial instance with 10 GB storage; AlloyDB for PostgreSQL — 30-day trial, 8 vCPU basic primary instance, up to 1 TB storage capacity; Bigtable — 10-day trial, 1-node SSD cluster, up to 500 GB. Each states 'new Google Cloud customers get $300 in free credits on signup' alongside.
findings.eligibility: New Google Cloud customers (same trial-eligibility rules: never a paying GCP/Maps/Firebase user; card required for the underlying account). No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Create the product instance from the product's console quickstart / the 'Free Trial' callouts on cloud.google.com/free; the trial period runs from instance creation.
findings.expiry: Fixed per-product windows (10-90 days) as listed; after expiry the instance converts to standard pay-as-you-go billing.
findings.gotchas: These are trial periods on paid products, not free tiers — after the window you are billed in full. GKE trial cluster is a different thing from the '1 free GKE cluster per month' Always Free allowance (that one is free forever but excludes compute/networking charges).

findings.name: Education / student offers: no dedicated GCP compute credits or education license
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22, GCP has no student-only free compute credits or education license: students get the same $300/90-day trial (card required), the Always Free tier, and the card-free Gemini API free tier. Google's education-related cloud offering is Google Cloud Skills Boost (free skills/training platform referenced by partner pages; the startup program's perk list says 'training via Google Skills'). NOTE: the historical domain skills.cloud.google.com failed to resolve (DNS) today, suggesting it was renamed or retired — the free-learning offering now appears to live under 'Google Skills' / cloud.google.com/learn; not fully verified.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no .edu-gated GCP compute offer exists.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim beyond the standard trial/free-tier/Gemini-API routes above.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse free 'learning' access with free 'compute' access; certification fee waivers (when offered) are unrelated to VPS usage.

sunset_notes: Legacy "Cloud Startups" program materially changed: the long-standing terms of "up to $200,000 in GCP credits, typically 12-month terms, mostly US-based startups" (the prior known baseline) no longer appear on the current program pages. As read today (2026-10-22), cloud.google.com/startup and startup.google.com/cloud both present the restructured "Google for Startups Cloud Program": up to $350,000 over two years, split into AI (Year-1 $250K) and non-AI (Year-1 $100K) tiers, eligibility "Pre-Seed to Series A, founded within the last 3-5 years, <$5,000 previously received GCP credits", with no US-entity requirement stated on the page. Exact 2025/2026 transition dates could not be news-verified today (this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted; the session user may raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION to allow that), so the "replacement" characterization is based on the live pages rather than a dated announcement — medium confidence on timing, high confidence on the current terms. Also current-state notes: (1) the $300/90-day trial and Always Free quotas are unchanged on today's official pages; (2) GKE's permanent free cluster is now phrased as "one free Autopilot or zonal Standard cluster per month" with compute/networking explicitly excluded; (3) GCP offers no free bare-metal or dedicated-server capacity at any tier — the only free "server" is the e2-micro micro-VM (3 US regions) and Cloud Run; (4) the Skills Boost domain no longer resolves — the education-facing free offering is now bundled under "Google Skills".

findings.name: Public Cloud Free Trial (global, www.ovhcloud.com) — US$200 / 1 month
findings.detail: US$200 free trial credit (displayed in local currency of the account's market/country, ex-VAT) valid for one month, activated when the first Public Cloud project is created. Applies to any Public Cloud service in the catalogue across all regions where Public Cloud is offered, incl. GPU/AI: the page's worked example covers 35 hours of AI1-1-GPU AI Notebook and 5 hours of AI Training on 4 AI1-1-GPU nodes. One voucher per natural or legal person (even across multiple NIC handles). Non-refundable, non-transferable, no combining with other offers; if the credit outlives on another NIC handle OVHcloud may terminate services; amounts covered by the voucher are excluded from SLA calculation. Offer live since 30 Jun 2022.
findings.eligibility: Any OVHcloud customer (new or existing) who has NEVER created a Public Cloud project (active or past). A valid payment method (credit card/bank) must already be saved in the account before starting — a card IS required, contrary to some listings. No .edu/education email requirement. Available in all regions where Public Cloud is offered. One per person/entity.
findings.claim: 1) Create/log in to an OVHcloud account (ovhcloud.com). 2) Ensure a payment method is saved. 3) In the Control Panel open Public Cloud and create your first project — the FREETRIAL voucher activates on project creation. 4) Deploy resources; the US$200 is auto-deducted from that project's bills for one month. 5) After the month or when the credit runs out, the saved payment method is billed for further usage.
findings.expiry: Voucher valid 1 month from project activation; non-renewable, non-exchangeable. After expiry the account reverts to standard pay-as-you-go billing.
findings.gotchas: It's a trial credit, not a free tier — payment method required and unused credit vanishes after 30 days. VPS and bare-metal/dedicated servers are NOT covered (Public Cloud only); the trial page's own examples show GPU AI notebooks/AI training. Third-party trackers (agentdeals.dev) recorded a terms tightening on 2026-04-01 and a 2026-10-01 price change (Gen3 B3/C3/R3 instances now bill local storage and a public IPv4 as separate lines, raising total bills 1.4–21.9% for small instances), which makes the US$200 burn faster on Gen3 instances.

findings.name: Public Cloud Free Trial (OVHcloud US, us.ovhcloud.com) — up to $300 / 90 days
findings.detail: US$200 credit when creating the first US Public Cloud project PLUS an additional $100 credit for creating the first Managed Database service — up to $300 total. Credits valid 90 days from the date they are applied (applied automatically; operational target 2 business days, contractual outer bound 30 days after OVHcloud receives the required $0.99 purchase). Cover Public Cloud only: compute (VMs, Cloud GPU, Local Zones), Block/Object/File storage, network, Managed Kubernetes, managed databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Valkey, Kafka, OpenSearch, Grafana), AI & ML (AI Notebooks, AI Training, AI Deploy) and security/ops services. Do NOT cover bare metal, VPS or Hosted Private Cloud.
findings.eligibility: US datacenters only; customers who have not previously purchased Public Cloud services from OVHcloud. Must purchase at least $0.99 of Public Cloud services to trigger; a payment method with a $0.99 fee must be added when creating the first project — i.e. a card is required (though effectively cost-free via the $0.99 charge). No promo code, no .edu requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for an OVHcloud US account (us.ovhcloud.com). 2) Create your first Public Cloud project in the Control Panel — add a payment method ($0.99 fee applies). 3) Launch your first resource ($0.99 purchase triggers eligibility). 4) The $200 credit auto-applies within 2 business days; buy your first Managed Database service to unlock the extra $100. 5) Check balance in the account's Payment Methods > vouchers tab.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 90 days after being applied to the account. No renewal/extension; unusable balance is void. After expiry the account bills at standard rates via the default payment method.
findings.gotchas: The page's header says 'one-month free trial' but the terms state 90-day validity — treat 90 days as contractual. Charges continue automatically once credits are exhausted/expired via the card on file. US-only infrastructure: US regions with Public Cloud availability qualify. The $100 Managed-DB bonus is the part most easily missed.

findings.name: OVHcloud Startup Program — Start level: €10,000 credits / 12 months (EU; $12,000 US)
findings.detail: 12-month membership: €10,000 in free cloud credits (US program: up to $12,000; Canada site shows $14,000) usable on Public Cloud and Hosted Private Cloud, plus 6 hours of free 1-on-1 engineering consultation, regional manager access, free social visibility ('Shine On'), Showcase events with VCs, mentoring. Credits are vouchers valid 12 months; unused vouchers are lost at the end. Voucher-eligible products: Public Cloud compute (instances incl. GPUs — only V100, V100s and RTX5000 GPU instances, all other GPUs excluded), Block/Object/Cold Archive storage, Managed K8s, managed databases, AI & ML (AI Notebooks, AI Training, AI Deploy, AI Endpoints), Quantum Notebooks; Hosted Private Cloud VMware/Nutanix. Not eligible: VPS, dedicated/bare-metal servers, Web Cloud, telecom. Also: quantum emulators get 'free credits via the Startup Program or free trial offer' per the QPU product page. No equity taken, no exclusivity (competing programs allowed).
findings.eligibility: Selected pre-seed and seed startups with at least a Proof of Concept or MVP deployable on OVHcloud, and a professional startup/business activity. Excluded: NGOs, associations, resellers/integrators, crypto mining, black-hat SEO, gaming bots, companies that already joined the program (incl. former Digital Launch Pad). No published company-age cap and no published funding cap for Start (OVHcloud decides the tier; any prior funding round 'improves chances' but isn't required; pre-revenue and revenue-generating both apply). Geographic: apply on the country site matching your business address; US infrastructure companies use the separate US program with a US account; generally one program membership (country of incorporation/operation). No .edu email; individual students aren't the target — it's company-level.
findings.claim: 1) Pick the right country site at startup.ovhcloud.com (or us.ovhcloud.com/startup-program for US). 2) Click Apply and link an existing OVHcloud customer account or create a new one (use a business account, not personal). 3) Answer company questions; you may get an email requesting more info. 4) Decision within ~7 days. 5) On acceptance sign the program contract in the Control Panel; vouchers arrive within ~48 hours; a regional program manager onboards you. Spend vouchers on eligible services during the 12 months.
findings.expiry: Vouchers must be used within 12 months of the contract; remaining balance is automatically invalidated. No renewal; one membership per company, ever (re-applying after exit not allowed).
findings.gotchas: Credits can't pay for VPS or dedicated servers — the 'fronts: VPS' angle only works through Public Cloud instances/Bare Metal Cloud (Bare Metal Cloud IS listed eligible in OVH docs' eligible-products table, while classic 'Dedicated Servers' and 'VPS' are not). GPU access under the program is limited to V100/V100s/RTX5000 instances. Trial-vs-free: this is a selective, application-based credit grant, not self-serve. Application must be honest — false/vague info gets it rejected. If you order non-eligible products by mistake they bill your regular payment method.

findings.name: OVHcloud Startup Program — Scale level: up to €100,000 credits / 12 months (EU; up to $120,000 US)
findings.detail: 12 months for Series A (and beyond) funded startups/scaleups: vouchers sized by OVHcloud's assessment of your expected 12-month infrastructure spend, capped at €100,000 (US: up to $120,000), plus up to 20 hours of 1-on-1 engineer time, Business-tier support, personalized quotes via Sales, personal visibility and market/funding event access. Same voucher eligibility rules as Start level (Public Cloud + Hosted Private Cloud; GPU only V100/V100s/RTX5000; no VPS/dedicated servers; AI Notebooks/Training/Deploy and Quantum Notebooks eligible). 'Enabler' route: accelerators/incubators/VCs that are OVHcloud partners can bring members to the same ceilings (up to €100k/20h); an event code is only mandatory when the support structure is a Premium partner.
findings.eligibility: Startups/scaleups that have raised Series A or later (funding stage is the main discriminator vs Start; OVHcloud makes the final tier decision). Same exclusions as Start level (NGOs, non-business projects, resellers, contentious activities, prior program members). Company site matching business address; US program requires a US OVHcloud account.
findings.claim: Same as Start level: apply online at startup.ovhcloud.com (country site per your address) or us.ovhcloud.com/startup-program, link/create a business OVHcloud account, respond to follow-up, ~7-day decision, sign contract in Control Panel, vouchers within ~48h, manager onboarding.
findings.expiry: Vouchers valid 12 months from contract; unused balance lost. Participation capped at 12 months per level.
findings.gotchas: 'Up to' — actual amount is set by OVHcloud from your projected spend, not guaranteed at the cap. Series A+ requirement means most seed-stage teams get the €10k Start level instead. No exclusivity with other cloud providers' programs. GPU instances other than V100/V100s/RTX5000 aren't voucher-eligible even at Scale level.

findings.name: Public VCF-as-a-Service first month free (US promo, code VCFTRIAL)
findings.detail: Limited-time promotion on OVHcloud US homepage: first month of Public VCF-as-a-Service (VMware Cloud Foundation workloads on shared infrastructure) free for new OVHcloud customers, using code VCFTRIAL at checkout. Standard Starter Pack only. This is a VMware-hosted private-cloud offering, not a GPU/VPS/dedicated-server product.
findings.eligibility: New OVHcloud US customers only; first 50 customers or until October 31, 2026, whichever comes first (i.e. it ends ~9 days after the 2026-10-22 reference date). No .edu requirement; payment at checkout after the free month.
findings.claim: 1) New OVHcloud US account. 2) Order Public VCF-as-a-Service Standard Starter Pack. 3) Enter code VCFTRIAL at checkout to waive the first month.
findings.expiry: Offer limited to first 50 customers or 31 Oct 2026. After the free month, standard pricing auto-renews unless cancelled before the promotional period ends.
findings.gotchas: Auto-renews to paid — cancel if you don't want it. Strict customer cap (50). The promo is US-only and VMware-specific; unrelated to the $200/$300 Public Cloud trial or the Startup Program (don't assume it can be stacked — page says 'additional terms apply').

findings.name: Student/education offer: free access to OVHcloud quantum notebooks (Qualifying Students program)
findings.detail: Announced with the Quandela MosaiQ QPU inauguration (2024; rooted in the 2023 C12 notebook release): selected students from higher-education/research institutions (incl. QuanTEdu-France consortium members such as Telecom Paris) receive free access to OVHcloud's full quantum notebook range (Alice & Bob, C12, Eviden, Pasqal, Quandela, later Qiskit) and to the Quandela QPU via the cloud — original press announced 80 hours of notebook access per selected student. OVHcloud's current QPU product page says free emulation credits are 'available... particularly for startups, researchers or innovative companies — via the OVHcloud Startup Program or the free trial offer', i.e. students effectively ride the Startup Program/trial credits rather than a dedicated self-serve .edu offer.
findings.eligibility: Students at qualifying higher-education/research institutions; selection by application review (2024 program cited QuanTEdu-France/Telecom Paris). No .edu self-serve tier is published on ovhcloud.com today. Adjacent non-free education channel: OCRE 2024 framework (awarded to OVHcloud by GÉANT, 5-year agreement running since Feb 2025) gives research/education institutions in 9 European countries (BE, FR, DE, IT, NL, PL, PT, ES, UK) simplified procurement access to OVHcloud Public Cloud — negotiated framework terms, not free credits.
findings.claim: No self-serve claim path published. Route: get your student/employer enrolled as an OVHcloud customer (e.g. via a startup/researcher account or OCRE-eligible institution) and use the US$200 Public Cloud free trial or apply to the Startup Program; request access to quantum notebooks/emulators in that account.
findings.expiry: No published expiry; the 2024 '80 hours' figure was per selected student. OCRE 2024 framework runs ~5 years from Feb 2025.
findings.gotchas: Low confidence this is still actively recruiting individual students — it was an announced ecosystem initiative, not advertised on current ovhcloud.com marketing pages as of 2026-10-22. Quantum notebook access is metered per-minute like other AI notebooks unless covered by trial/program credits. Don't count on a free .edu tier for VPS/dedicated servers — none exists.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22: (1) The legacy offer in the task's 'known so far' — 'US$200 free trial on new dedicated servers & VPS, 2-month, no commitment (refundable)' — is GONE: https://www.ovhcloud.com/en/free-trial/ returns 404; the only live trial is the Public Cloud US$200/1-month trial (and up to $300/90 days in the US). No dedicated-server or VPS trial credit is advertised anywhere on ovhcloud.com or us.ovhcloud.com. (2) 2026-04-01: third-party changelog (agentdeals.dev) records OVHcloud narrowing the free-trial terms; and on 2026-10-01 OVHcloud restructured Gen3 Public Cloud instance pricing — local storage and public IPv4 on B3/C3/R3 are now billed as separate lines (~€109/TB/mo storage, ~$1.97/mo IPv4), raising bills 1.4–21.9% (largest for small instances), which consumes trial credits faster. (3) VPS pricing: VPS 2026 list prices were raised 36–49% effective 2026-04-01 (e.g. VPS-1 €4.49→€6.49/mo); the new 'VPS 2027' range launched (VPS-1 2027 from ~$4.54/mo per www.ovhcloud.com/en/vps/). No VPS free tier/trial exists. (4) Bare metal: Kimsufi budget range was discontinued and replaced by the 'Eco' range (~$30/mo, us.ovhcloud.com/deals); bare-metal prices rose 9–11% for new deployments post-April 2026. (5) The VCFTRIAL first-month-free VMware promo is a sunset-in-9-days offer (ends 31 Oct 2026 or after first 50 customers). (6) No dedicated .edu/students free tier and no 'education license' for VPS/dedicated servers was found; the only education-adjacent channels are the qualifying-student quantum notebook program (2024, low visibility now) and the OCRE 2024 GÉANT procurement framework (institutional, negotiated, not free). 7) Startup Program structure is unchanged in substance (€10k Start / up to €100k Scale, 12 months) but currency values differ by country site (US $12k/$120k, CA $14k).

findings.claim: 1) Register at signup.upcloud.com (name, email, phone required). 2) Log into the Control Panel; trial does not auto-start. 3) Verify identity with credit card + billing info to enter the trial. 4) Start trial within 365 days of registration or the account is removed. 5) Optionally pay min 10 one-time deposit to keep/upgrade; request longer trials from sales.
findings.detail: All new users get a 7-day trial starting at the moment of activation, NOT a fixed credit pot. Trial quotas (official docs): Cloud Servers 2 cores / 4 GB RAM (all OSes except Windows); Block Storage 60 GB each of Archive, Standard and MaxIOPS; Networks 2 IPv4 + 2 IPv6; NAT/VPN Gateway x1 (Development or Standard plan); Managed Object Storage 1 instance up to 250 GB; Managed Databases 1 DB / 1 node (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Valkey, OpenSearch); Managed Load Balancer 1 Development plan, 1000 sessions; Managed Kubernetes 1 cluster on Development plan. Not available: Windows servers, GPU servers, Private Cloud. Firewall is locked to standard web ports (HTTP/HTTPS open both ways; SSH in only; RDP in only; SMTP 25 blocked both directions; NTP/DNS out only). You can redeploy within quotas as often as you like. Upgrade minimum is a one-time deposit of 10 in account currency; when the trial ends without a deposit, deployed services are removed and new deployments are blocked (account stays active). Data egress is free (zero-cost egress is a standard UpCloud feature since the 2025 'UpCloud Essentials' change).
findings.eligibility: All new users, no .edu, no region limit beyond UpCloud's sanctioned-region restrictions (Russia, Belarus, Crimea, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Syria excluded). Credit card + billing info ARE required to activate the trial (0 or 1 EUR/USD temporary authorization, card not charged before/during/after). No card-free trial.
findings.expiry: 7 days from activation (longer only via promotion). Promo credits from signup codes are valid 60 days after signup per bonus-credits docs; trial credits for the standard trial effectively expire with the 7-day window. Accounts not started within 365 days of registration are deleted.
findings.gotchas: This is a quota trial, not money: the 'small ~$25 free trial credit' often cited for UpCloud does not match current docs - the baseline trial has no dollar credit at all. CC mandatory for activation. Windows/GPU excluded. After expiry your resources are deleted if you haven't deposited at least 10. SMTP port 25 blocked; outbound SSH restricted. 14-day and 30-day figures floating around are leftover promos, not the standard.
findings.name: Standard 7-day free trial (quota-limited, no dollar credit)

findings.claim: Upgrade the trial account with a minimum 10 one-time deposit in Billing, use services for up to 30 days, request a refund from Customer Support within the window if unhappy.
findings.detail: The first payment made at/after trial upgrade carries a 30-day money-back guarantee of up to 500 EUR / 500 USD; contact support for refund. Not an independent offer - it attaches to the first one-time deposit (minimum 10).
findings.eligibility: Any new customer making their first payment; no .edu or startup requirements; same CC/sanctioned-region rules as the trial.
findings.expiry: Refund window = 30 days from first payment, capped at 500 EUR/USD of the first payment.
findings.gotchas: Only the FIRST payment is covered and only up to 500; does not stack on top of promo credits. It is trial-vs-free: you must have paid to claim it.
findings.name: 30-day money-back guarantee on first payment (up to 500 EUR/USD)

findings.claim: 1) Create an UpCloud account. 2) Open the Startup Program page and use the on-page 'Apply now' application form. 3) Submit company details; wait 5-10 business days for review. 4) On approval, credit is attached to your account (usage details in the welcome email).
findings.detail: Official program page (read directly today): Tier 1: up to 25,000 EUR free credit, valid 24 months, for startups in the UpCloud ecosystem (partner VC, incubator or accelerator) that have raised more than 5M EUR. Tier 2: 5,000 EUR free credit, valid 12 months, for startups founded within the last 24 months in FI, SE, NO, DK or IS (Nordics). Tier 3: 1,000 EUR free credit, valid 12 months, for startups founded within the last 24 months in non-Nordic EU, EEA, UK or CH. Credits usable across compute, storage, networking and managed databases; GPU Servers are excluded from credit usage (UpCloud may enable them at its discretion post-onboarding). Also includes 24/7 human support, startup events/forum, solution-architecture consultations, and a startup spotlight on UpCloud channels. Since March 2026 the program is run in partnership with Maria 01, the Helsinki startup hub. Applications reviewed in 5-10 business days; you may be asked for proof of company registration, valid VAT ID, funding-round documentation (Tier 1) and accelerator/VC/incubator affiliation proof (Tier 1). After credits expire, services continue at standard pricing and you are notified beforehand.
findings.eligibility: New UpCloud customers only; UpCloud account required before applying; company registered in EU, EEA, UK, Ukraine or CH; valid VAT ID; founded within the last 24 months (Tiers 2 and 3). Tier 1 additionally requires partner-ecosystem affiliation and >5M EUR raised. No .edu / student angle. No funding cap for T2/T3 (bootstrapped OK). Region-locked to Europe (Nordic advantage).
findings.expiry: Tier 1 credits valid 24 months; Tier 2/3 valid 12 months from approval; program itself is ongoing (Maria 01 partnership announced March 2026).
findings.gotchas: Credits are denominated in EUR on the official page (site displays in euros; third-party trackers sometimes restate them in USD - treat EUR figures as canonical). 'Up to' Tier 1 means the final amount is UpCloud's discretion within the cap. GPU excluded. Must be a NEW customer - existing UpCloud users are ineligible. VAT ID is mandatory, so individuals/students without a company cannot use it. After expiry you pay standard prices with no cliff.
findings.name: UpCloud Startup Program - up to 25,000 EUR credits in 3 tiers

findings.claim: Register at signup.upcloud.com and enter a valid promo code in the 'Promo code' field at signup (only one code, only at signup). Check which code is live before relying on it - none are advertised on the default page today.
findings.detail: UpCloud layers time-boxed promos on the baseline trial: Aug 2025 'upcloud500' gave 500 USD for 30 days plus first-payment matching (max 100 USD, forever) and looser trial quotas (16 CPU / 32 GB / 1024 GB storage / 5 IPs), ending 2025-09-30; later 'boost500' offered 500 EUR or 500 USD valid for the first 30 days with GPU excluded. As of TODAY (2026-10-22) I verified on the live signup page that the boost500 code returns 'Promo code boost500 is inactive' and the default offer is the 7-day trial with an optional promo-code field. Affiliate codes for 250/500 credits also circulate but none are live on the default page. Per official bonus-credits docs: one promo code, only at signup, promo credits valid 60 days after signup, and promo-credit accounts need manual support activation to deploy GPU products.
findings.eligibility: New trial accounts; same CC-verification rules as the trial. No student/startup distinction - it is a general new-user promo.
findings.expiry: boost500: INACTIVE as of 2026-10-22 (verified on signup page). upcloud500: ended 2025-09-30. Generic rule: promo credits valid 60 days after signup.
findings.gotchas: Inactivity of boost500 verified today; historical amounts/durations come from UpCloud's own social posts (Mastodon/Nostr) and third-party trackers, so treat the code details as second-hand. Codes expire without notice - recheck the signup page before claiming.
findings.name: Signup promo-code trial credits (historically up to 500 EUR/USD for 30 days) - currently INACTIVE

findings.claim: 1) Get an existing customer's personal referral code/link. 2) Sign up with it. 3) New user receives 25 credit on the account. 4) Make at least two one-time payments and keep the account active 28+ days to unlock the referrer's 50.
findings.detail: Per official bonus-credits docs (read today): a new user signing up via a referral receives 25 EUR / 25 USD free credits spendable on any service; the referrer earns 50 EUR / 50 USD on their account. Referral credits do NOT expire. Conditions: the referred new user must make a minimum of two one-time payments and stay active for at least 28 days for the referrer to receive the 50. So the new user's 25 requires two paid one-time deposits - effectively a paid-account perk, not free-for-forever.
findings.eligibility: Any new UpCloud user referred by an existing customer; no .edu or startup requirement; no stated funding/age cap; same sanctioned-region rules apply.
findings.expiry: Referral credits do not expire (official docs).
findings.gotchas: You must actually pay (2 one-time deposits) - not pure free. One promo/referral code per signup, no stacking described. GPU deployment on bonus-credit accounts needs a support ticket to activate.
findings.name: Referral program: 25 EUR/USD to the new user, 50 EUR/USD to the referrer

findings.claim: No public claim path. A professor/instructor contacts UpCloud sales/support to request sponsored credits for their class (per the Stony Brook example).

The only education-related activity is ad-hoc: UpCloud has sponsored university cloud courses (case study: Stony Brook University's cloud computing class - the professor emails UpCloud each semester and UpCloud 'donates credit' to sponsor the whole class; documented 2023, not a published program with eligibility). Third-party coupon sites claim 'student discounts' but the FAQ they quote is generic filler, not an official offer.

provider: UpCloud (VPS / cloud servers, bare-metal & dedicated incl. GPU clusters)
sunset_notes: 1) The task's starting URL https://upcloud.com/try/ now serves a 404 'Page Not Found' (verified 2026-10-22) - UpCloud has sunset the dedicated trial landing page; trial info now lives in the docs (upcloud.com/docs/getting-started/free-trial/) and the signup flow. 2) The '500 EUR/USD for 30 days' signup promo chain (upcloud500 in 2025, then boost500 active into Sept 2026) is dead: the live signup page today shows boost500 as 'inactive' and defaults to the plain 7-day quota trial. So any listing advertising a standing $500/30-day free trial (e.g. 'UpCloud for Startups: $500' directory entries) is outdated as of 2026-10-22. 3) The previously circulated 'small ~$25 free trial credit' assumption is wrong for current terms - the baseline trial is quota-based with no dollar credit; 25 EUR only appears via the referral program. 4) The Startup Program is the main 2025-2026 structural change: it now runs a three-tier EUR system (up to 25k/5k/1k, 24/12/12-month validity) gated on VAT ID + 24-month company age + EU/EEA/UK/UA/CH registration, formalized in a March 2026 Maria 01 (Helsinki) partnership; third-party trackers restate tiers in USD - the official page prices in EUR. 5) Since June 2025, 'UpCloud Essentials' made zero-cost egress, Kubernetes control planes, load balancers, NAT/VPN gateways and a daily backup plan permanently free for all users - not a trial offer, but it removes the usual egress-cost gotcha. 6) Unverified third-party claim (notes.aflukasz.pl, May 2025): 5,000 EUR for European businesses with a VAT ID, usable over 3 months - not corroborated on the official site; treat as a lapsed enterprise promo. 7) Region limits: UpCloud does not serve sanctioned regions (RU, BY, Crimea, IR, KP, CU, SY) and validates payment origin/geo - all offers above are subject to that.

findings.name: OCI Always Free tier (VPS: 2 AMD micro VMs + 2 OCPU/12 GB ARM Ampere A1 pool + storage/DB/networking)
findings.detail: Perpetual ('life of the account') Always Free resources, home region only: (1) up to 2 VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro AMD instances, each 1/8 OCPU (~200 MHz, burstable) + 1 GB RAM, 1 VNIC, 1 public IPv4, up to 50 Mbps internet / 480 Mbps intra-region; (2) Ampere A1 ARM (VM.Standard.A1.Flex): a monthly pool of 1,500 OCPU-hours + 9,000 GB-hours = equivalent to 2 OCPUs and 12 GB total, usable as one instance or up to two 1-OCPU instances (min boot volume 47 GB/instance); (3) 200 GB block volume total (boot + data, home region) with 5 volume backups; (4) object storage: 20 GB combined Standard+Infrequent Access+Archive for free-only tenancies (10 GB per tier while trial/PAYG is active); (5) 10 TB/month outbound egress; (6) 2x Autonomous AI Database (20 GB storage each, 1 Oracle CPU, serverless Exadata, 20 max concurrent sessions); (7) MySQL HeatWave standalone single-node cluster, 50 GB data + 50 GB backup storage; (8) NoSQL: 133M reads + 133M writes/mo, 3 tables x 25 GB (Phoenix region only); (9) 2 VCNs, 1 Flexible Load Balancer + 1 Network Load Balancer, 50 IPsec site-to-site VPN connections, 5 CAs + 150 certificates, 3,000 emails/mo Email Delivery, plus free APEX, Resource Manager/Terraform, Monitoring/Logging, Bastion, Vault (software keys unlimited; 20 HSM key versions), Security Advisor, Content Management Starter. NO free bare-metal or dedicated-server shapes exist — OCI bare metal (BM.Dense/BM.Standard, incl. 80-core Ampere bare metal) is paid-only.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone who signs up (one free trial/Always Free account per person; one cloud account per email). Credit or debit card REQUIRED at signup: major-network cards (Visa/Mastercard/Discover/Amex) that do not require a PIN; virtual, prepaid, single-use and PIN-debit cards are rejected. A mobile phone number is needed for most users. Available in all regions where commercial OCI is offered (Free/Always Free NOT available in US Government Cloud regions); '$300 credit' part is 'available in select countries'. .edu email NOT required for the free tier. Startup age/funding caps: none for the free tier.
findings.claim: Sign up at https://signup.oraclecloud.com (linked from https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/): select country, enter name + valid email, verify email (link valid 30 min), set password (8-40 chars, complexity rules), optionally enter company name, create a cloud account name, pick Home Region (irrevocable; Always Free compute + ADB can only be created in the home region), enter address + phone, add credit/debit card as payment-verification method (you may see a small temporary ~$1 verification hold that auto-reverses), accept ToU, 'Start my free trial'. Always Free resources are usable immediately with no upgrade; $0 charged unless you upgrade to PAYG. No separate claim form for the Always Free tier itself.
findings.expiry: Perpetual — 'available for an unlimited period of time, for the life of the account.' Trial portion: $300 credits expire 30 days after signup. No renewal needed.
findings.gotchas: HOME-REGION LOCK: Always Free compute and ADB provision only in home region; use in other regions bills at PAYG rates. IDLE RECLAMATION: Always Free VMs (and bare metal) can be reclaimed when over any 7-day window CPU p95 < 20% AND network < 20% (AND memory < 20% for A1 shapes). Accounts idle 30+ days may be deemed abandoned and suspended/terminated. 2026 ARM CUT-ENFORCEMENT: since 2026-08-18, A1 instances exceeding 2 OCPU/12 GB are auto-terminated; once an existing oversized instance is terminated it 'may not be possible' to recreate it above the new limit. Capacity: free-tier accounts frequently hit 'out of host capacity' on A1/micro shapes in US regions; PAYG upgrade generally provisions more reliably. Eligible OS images limited (Oracle Linux/Ubuntu/CentOS for micros; Oracle Linux/Ubuntu + Oracle Linux Cloud Developer for A1, latter needs >=8 GB). No SLA and no Oracle Support unless a paid account. If trial ends with more A1 OCPUs/memory than 2/12, excess instances are disabled then deleted after 30 days unless you upgrade. Paid resources made with trial credits are deleted (unrecoverable) if you don't upgrade.

findings.name: OCI Free Trial: US$300 cloud credit for 30 days (all eligible OCI services, on top of Always Free)
findings.detail: One-time US$300 in cloud credits valid up to 30 days from account creation, spendable on all eligible OCI services (compute beyond free limits, GPU, K8s, analytics, up to ~8 instances / 5 TB storage while credits last, per the trial marketing). Credits are consumed at discounted trial rates. Unused credits expire at 30 days. After trial: 30-day grace to upgrade; paid resources are otherwise reclaimed/deleted; Always Free resources persist. Upgrading carries a ~$100 card authorization. Extensions/additional credits possible only via an Oracle sales representative (console Upgrade page).
findings.eligibility: Same as free tier signup: one per person; credit/debit card (major network, no PIN required) + phone number for identity verification; US$300 credit 'available in select countries' per the FAQ asterisk. No .edu, no startup-age requirement — this is a general trial, not a special program.
findings.claim: Automatically granted at https://signup.oraclecloud.com — no separate claim. Steps: country -> name -> email (verify within 30 min) -> password -> optional company -> cloud account name -> Home Region -> address/phone -> add card verification (small temporary ~$1 hold) -> ToU -> 'Start my free trial'. Upgrade to PAYG at any time via Console > Billing & Cost Management > Upgrade and Manage Payment.
findings.expiry: Credits: 30 days from signup or $300 exhaustion, whichever first. Trial resources: 30-day grace after expiry to upgrade before deletion. Always Free portion: no expiry.
findings.gotchas: Card IS required (contrary to 'no credit card' marketing assumptions): FAQ says credit cards and PIN-less debit cards only; virtual/prepaid/single-use cards rejected; periodic re-validation holds possible. 'Some special Free Trial offers' (e.g., email-invite promotions): after expiry the account is suspended for 30 days then permanently deleted — they do NOT convert to an Always Free account. No SLA/support once credits gone. Billing begins after trial if you upgraded (credit balance preserved until trial period ends). No downgrade from paid back to free. Data in trial-created resources is unrecoverable after reclamation.

findings.name: Oracle Startup Program (startup cloud credits)
findings.detail: UNVERIFIABLE TODAY. findings.name: Education offer: no dedicated .edu cloud-credit program; free tier open to students/academics + free Oracle University training/certifications (Oracle Learning Explorer)
findings.detail: No .edu-gated OCI VPS license found on official pages as of 2026-10-22. Free education/training: (a) Oracle Learning Explorer — free entry-level training courses and accreditation across Oracle's product portfolio; (b) Oracle University 'Free Foundations training' — free training and certifications for OCI, Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications and AI (oracle.com/education/training, 'New free Foundations training... free training and certifications'); (c) a promo on that page: 'Free certification on OCI, AI, multicloud, and data services — Now through October 31, join the Race to Certification 2025' (note: page footer is © 2026, the 'Race to Certification 2025' banner looks like stale promotional copy — the offer may have already expired on 2025-10-31; do not count on it without re-checking).

findings.claim: Cloud: standard signup at signup.oraclecloud.com (any special education offer is surfaced there via the email eligibility check). Training: enroll at mylearn.oracle.com / oracle.com/education/training ('Explore free training and certifications'); Learning Explorer via oracle.com/education ('Start learning for free').
findings.expiry: Free Foundations training: ongoing/promotional ('New free Foundations training' as of the page's © 2026). Race to Certification: 'through October 31' (year unclear — likely already ended 2025-10-31; stale banner).
findings.gotchas: Oracle University free tier is training-only, no infrastructure credits; the 'free' training does not include the full exam voucher unless the specific Foundations course lists it; verify 'Race to Certification' status in the console/marketing site before assuming it's live; no .edu-only benefits exist in OCI as of this check.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes: (1) ALWAYS FREE AMPERE A1 HALVED, SILENTLY — Oracle's docs changed without a public announcement so that the A1 pool went from 3,000 OCPU-hours + 18,000 GB-hours/month (equivalent to 4 OCPU / 24 GB, i.e., 'up to four Ampere instances' as the older MySQL-free page still claims) to 1,500 OCPU-hours + 9,000 GB-hours/month (= 2 OCPU / 12 GB total, 'one or two instances, 2 OCPUs total'). Per InfoQ (2026-07-03) the docs change took effect 2026-06-15 with no blog post or customer notice; hard enforcement (auto-termination of over-limit instances) began 2026-08-18 per a customer email quoted by CNELECAR. Ambiguity remains: Oracle support reportedly told PAYG tenancies the old 4/24 limits still apply free, while the docs say 'All tenancies get the first 1,500 OCPU hours...' — unconfirmed either way. Once an oversized A1 instance is terminated it likely cannot be recreated above the new limit. AMD micros, 200 GB block, object storage, 10 TB egress, and 2x20 GB ADB limits are unchanged. (2) $300/30-DAY TRIAL — unchanged through 2025-2026; card still required at signup. (3) STARTUP PROGRAM — not verifiable this pass (bot-blocked global page); no evidence it was sunset, but no official docs corroborate it either. (4) BARE-METAL / DEDICATED-SERVER FRONT — Oracle has no free bare-metal or dedicated-server offer at any tier; bare-metal/dedicated is paid-only (PAYG or Always-Free-exempt). (5) EDUCATION — no .edu-gated program currently advertised; free Foundations training/certifications remain available per the ©2026 Oracle University pages.

provider: Cursor (Anyspheres / cursor.com — Dev Tools, IDEs, Git & CI/CD)

findings.name: Free plan ($0/mo) — standing free tier, no trial
findings.detail: Official pricing page lists a Free plan at $0/month with 'Limited AI usage': 'Limited agent requests' and 'Limited Chat requests' (no numeric caps published; the docs page marks free included-usage as simply 'Limited'). Free tier includes 'Post, reply, and follow'; Grok Chat/Imagine/Build are 'Limited'; third-party models, Grok API, cloud agents, code hosting, AI code reviews are not available ('—') on Free. Usage allowance refreshes weekly ('one heavy day never wipes out your whole month'); when exhausted, users 'can keep going with top-offs, or wait for your allowance to refresh'; remaining usage visible in settings. No free trial or starter credits are advertised anywhere on the current pricing page.
findings.eligibility: Anyone can sign up; no .edu email, no proof of affiliation, and no credit card required for the free tier (page states only that self-serve paid plans support major credit/debit cards). No region limits stated on the page. Prices exclude tax (VAT).
findings.claim: Fetched https://cursor.com/pricing and https://cursor.com/docs/models-and-pricing today (2026-10-22): Free plan $0/mo, limited agent/chat requests, weekly refresh, top-ups optional, no trial or CC requirement stated; paid tiers Plus $8 / Premium $30 / Super $100 / Ultra $200 per month.
findings.expiry: Indefinite free tier; weekly usage refresh; no expiry date, no trial clock.
findings.gotchas: Exact request limits are not published on the page (only 'Limited') — plan accordingly. Third-party model usage is billed separately at API list price even on paid tiers; 'Plus ($8/mo) is Grok-models-only', so cheapest paid tier is deliberately restricted. There is no advertised free-trial of paid plans, so free users get less than historical promo/credit offers. Cancellation policy: cancel at least 24h before renewal to avoid charges.

findings.name: Campus Leads program — free 6 months of Cursor Ultra for student community leaders
findings.detail: Cursor's 'Campus Leads' program (run twice yearly, fall and spring) accepts current university students who commit ~5 hours/week to building the campus community (workshops, hackathons, meetups, partnering with clubs, product feedback). Benefits: all-expenses-paid trip to Cursor's San Francisco office for kick-off, custom swag, travel reimbursement to one hackathon from a verified list, early access to new features, invitation to a private Slack with the Cursor team, funding/resources to host on-campus events, and 'Access to 6 months of Cursor Ultra' — the top tier, worth $200/mo per the pricing page (~$1,200 value, plus travel). Eligibility criteria: current university student, completed application, accepted Code of Conduct, 5h/week commitment.
findings.eligibility: Must be a current university student (no .edu stated as a check method, but student status required). Selective admission — application + Code of Conduct required. No funding-cap or startup-age criteria (this is a student/community program, not a startup program). No credit card mentioned for acceptance.
findings.claim: 1) Go to cursor.com/campus-leads. 2) Fill out the interest Typeform (hosted by Anysphere) to be notified when applications reopen. 3) Apply when the cycle opens; accept the Cursor Community Code of Conduct (linked Notion). 4) Direct questions to students@cursor.com. Note the page says 'Applications reopen in January' — i.e., the spring intake window.
findings.expiry: Program runs on two cycles per year (fall/spring); the Ultra access lasts 6 months per cycle. Applications reopen in January for the spring cycle; fall cycle via the interest form.
findings.gotchas: Only accepted Campus Leads get the free Ultra — it is not a blanket student license; general students still use the free 'Limited' tier. Perks are program-bound (renewal means staying an active lead / re-entering the next cycle). The 6-month Ultra benefit plus travel is the entirety of the free-value offer; no monetary refund or seat sharing is mentioned.

findings.name: Student discounts/promotions (on-campus & online events, fall cycle) — amounts not fixed
findings.detail: The dedicated students page (cursor.com/students) confirms 'Anyone can get started with Cursor for free' and, in its FAQ, says: 'To upgrade your access, look out for promotions at our on-campus and online events starting this fall.' A linked Typeform sign-up advertises 'early access to upcoming events, exclusive discounts, and beginner guides.' No dollar amount, percentage, tier, seat count, code or credit amount is published on the page; the concrete student benefit available today is the Campus Leads Ultra benefit above.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone who signs up for the free tier (no .edu required for free start). Event-based student promotions target on-campus/online participants (students/educators at institutions); no explicit .edu verification stated. No credit-card requirement stated for the free start.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for Cursor free (no card). 2) Subscribe to the Typeform newsletter on cursor.com/students for event early access and discount offers. 3) Attend on-campus/online events (fall cycle) to receive promotions. 4) Optionally apply to Campus Leads for the 6-month Ultra benefit.
findings.expiry: Tied to the fall/spring event calendar ('starting this fall'); promotions are event-specific with no published expiry or renewal terms; the newsletter early access persists.
findings.gotchas: No exact discount figures, dates or limits are published — do not treat 'exclusive discounts' as a known amount. The event-based promotion is not a standing license; it may differ from the Campus Leads benefit. Verify current event terms at each event, since pages say 'look out for' rather than commit to a price.

sunset_notes: No startup program found: cursor.com/startups returned only a page title with no program, credits or eligibility content, and neither the pricing page nor the models-and-pricing docs reference any startup offer, funding cap or startup-age criterion. No trial-credit offer is advertised: the current official pages list no free trial of paid plans and no starter credits (historical new-user trial/promo-credit offers from 2024–2025 are absent from the pricing/docs pages as of today; I could not run web searches this session to confirm sunset dates, so this is 'not listed on official pages today' rather than a verified end date). Material 2025–2026 structural changes observable on the current pages: tier lineup and pricing are now Plus $8/mo, Premium $30/mo, Super $100/mo, Ultra $200/mo (Teams $30/$100/$200 per seat; Enterprise custom), with pools expressed as multiples of Plus and a weekly refresh; the Free plan's exact request counts are unpublished ('Limited'); third-party models are billed at API list price with spending caps, and Teams/Enterprise add a $0.25/million-token 'Cursor Token Rate' on eligible third-party usage. A model promo (e.g., GPT-5.6 'Promotional pricing through November 21, 2026') appears in the docs, but it is a pricing promo, not a student/startup offer.

findings.name: Figma Starter plan (free tier, open to everyone incl. students and startups)
findings.detail: Permanent free plan: unlimited draft files shareable with unlimited viewers; co-editing with unlimited users limited to 3 files (3 pages per file); UI kits and templates; 150 AI credits/day capped at 500 AI credits/month; Figma Buzz beta available. 'We do not have any discounts for non-profits. Anyone is welcome to use Figma's free plan.' No free trials of paid plans exist; Figma directs all startups to this free Starter plan.
findings.eligibility: Open to all individual users, no verification. No .edu email, no funding cap, no application. No credit card is mentioned or required for a free account (payment methods listed only for paid plans). No stated region limits. Credit-card requirement: not required for the free plan (FAQ silent; sign-up is email-only).
findings.claim: Create a free account at figma.com (email signup). No claim step, no form, no partner referral. Account lands on Starter automatically.
findings.expiry: No expiry; limits (3 co-edit files, 3 pages/file, 500 AI credits/mo, 150/day) apply continuously. AI credits reset monthly and do not roll over.
findings.gotchas: Freemium, not unlimited: >3 co-editable files or >3 pages/file forces upgrade; advanced Dev Mode inspection, team libraries, MCP server and Figma Make workflows are paid-plan features (Starter gets basic access only). AI credits: 150/day daily cap + 500/month cap, no purchase option on Starter — hitting the cap blocks paid-tier AI features until the next month. This is the fallback Figma recommends to startups whose dedicated program was discontinued.

findings.name: Figma for Education: free Professional plan for verified students & educators (age 13+)
findings.detail: 'Figma & FigJam are 100% free for students, educators and schools.' Higher-ed, approved bootcamps, and secondary/high school students and educators get free Professional-tier access: unlimited files/projects, team-wide design libraries, advanced Dev Mode inspection and MCP Server. AI: 'Eligible education users get full access to Figma's AI toolkit, including Figma Make and AI-powered tools on the canvas' — but AI tools, the Figma agent, and Figma Sites are restricted to higher-ed and bootcamp Education users (not K-12/high-school); Education seats get 3,000 AI credits/month (per person, monthly reset, no rolver). Figma Sites: each eligible user may publish one self-created Site file; custom domains not available. No way to purchase extra AI credits on the Education plan — overage requires upgrading to paid Professional.
findings.eligibility: Current student or educator in a structured classroom (high school, university, post-grad, trade school, polytechnic, college, select curriculum-based online courses/bootcamps/workshops, design & coding academies); must be old enough to consent personally (13+ self-serve path); school-issued email REQUIRED — 'Non-school emails will be auto-rejected'; not strictly .edu (any school-issued email; personal accounts must switch to the school email before applying). Higher-ed verification goes through SheerID; bootcamp/online-course users cannot self-verify — the bootcamp admin applies as a trusted partner and submits user lists. Excluded: school staff in non-teaching roles, self-directed learners, startups/edtech companies, non-profits, and programs whose parent org's primary purpose is not educational. 'Figma for Education is only available in select regions and may not be accessible everywhere' (no published country list).
findings.claim: 1) Have/switch Figma account to a school-issued email; sign up selecting School > role (Student/Educator) > institution type (High school / Higher Education / Bootcamp or online course). 2) 'Verify your status' under the Professional plan card at Figma.com/education/apply — high school: agree to terms and submit; higher ed: complete SheerID form; bootcamp: admin applies on your behalf. 3) A free Education team is created. K-12 districts / under-13 use instead: school contacts Figma and signs school terms (apply at /education/k-12/#contact).
findings.expiry: Per official validity table: high-school students 1 year; high-school educators 2 years; higher-ed students 1 year; higher-ed educators 2 years; bootcamp students 6 months; bootcamp educators 2 years; K-12 set by the domain administrator. Renewal: reapply for education status at term end. On lapse, team members drop to view-only and the team converts to a free Starter team (locked if it holds 4+ files) until re-verification or paid upgrade.
findings.gotchas: Education status is tied to the verified email — changing the account email revokes it. AI tools/Figma Make/Figma Sites unavailable to K-12 and high-school Education users (higher-ed and bootcamp only); even eligible users lack some AI features (e.g., visual search in editor). 3,000 AI credits/month is a hard per-person cap with no top-up on Education — hitting it blocks credit-based AI features until monthly reset. UK/Japan note: Figma may only be used by students above the age of consent; younger students require the district process. Data hosted on US servers; only email + name collected. Bootcamp educators stay free 2 years while students only 6 months.

findings.name: Figma for Education: free Enterprise plan for K-12 districts (under-13 path)
findings.detail: K-12 districts 'qualify for free access to the Enterprise tier' — the most premium plan: custom team workspaces, design system theming and APIs, SCIM seat management, enterprise-level security. Provided at no cost via school-signed terms, replacing paid Enterprise (listed at $90/mo Full seat for commercial customers).
findings.eligibility: K-12 schools/districts intending to use Figma with students under 13; the school must be the applicant — individual self-serve not available. In UK and Japan, Figma 'may only be used by students above the age of consent', so under-13 use there requires this district route.
findings.claim: School/district contacts Figma and signs the terms for schools; started via the form linked at /education/k-12/#contact ('Apply for K-12 program'). Domain administrator then manages the K-12 education status. Optional supports: bi-weekly free live training sessions and free on-site PD sessions for schools.
findings.expiry: K-12 education status duration is 'set by the domain administrator' — institution-controlled, not a fixed consumer term.
findings.gotchas: Not self-serve; K-12 users do NOT get AI tools, Figma Make, or Figma Sites (higher-ed/bootcamp only). The Education FAQ answers COPPA/FERPA/GDPR compliance by restating the age gate and school-signature process rather than a flat 'yes' per jurisdiction — compliance review needed for districts. US data residency; Figma deletes personal data within 30 days of request; Google Workspace/Microsoft Education SSO and classroom integration (FigJam Classroom add-on) available for managed rollouts.

findings.name: Figma for Startups program — DISCONTINUED; no live offer as of 2026-10-22
findings.detail: The dedicated startup program (historically: free Organization plan for 24 months for VC-backed/accelerator-referred startups, or '$1,000 in Figma credits' per aggregator listings; one listing described 'up to 100% off Professional for 1 year, or 50% off for 6 months, new customers that raised under $10M') no longer exists on Figma-owned surfaces. figma.com/startups returns HTTP 404 (verified by direct fetch on 2026-10-22); no application form, no help-center article, and no startup mention in the pricing pages or pricing FAQ. Third-party trackers confirm: 'We could not verify this program on any Figma-owned page as of September 13, 2026' and 'No. Figma has no startup program: figma.com/startups is a 404, and Figma points everyone to its free Starter plan' (checked 2026-10-14).
findings.eligibility: None currently. Historical eligibility (per aggregators, now stale): VC-backed or accelerator-affiliated startup, referral by an approved Figma startup partner, new Organization-customer, Series A or below, <50 employees, raised under ~$10M. Note: early-stage startups are explicitly excluded from the Education plan ('Figma does not provide free Education teams for: Early stage Startups').
findings.claim: No active claim path. Startups' only official free route is the unlimited free Starter plan. Accelerator/VC perk books may still republish the old offer, but no working application link exists on Figma-owned domains as of today.
findings.expiry: N/A — program discontinued; figma.com/startups 404 as of 2026-09-13 and re-verified 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: Aggregator sites (foundery.space, creditforstartups.com, startupintros.com, startup-perks.com) still list 'Figma for Startups' as Active with old terms — those listings are stale, not evidence the offer exists; always confirm on figma.com. Figma discounts do not stack — historically the largest single qualified discount applied. No nonprofit discount of any kind (FAQ: 'We do not have any discounts for non-profits'), so aggregator claims of '40-80% off nonprofit' are also stale.

sunset_notes: Figma for Startups: sunset/paused — figma.com/startups 404, no application form, no help-center article, confirmed unverified by multiple independent trackers Sept-Oct 2026; the program previously offered ~24 months of the free Organization plan (or ~$1,000 in credits) for VC/accelerator-referred startups and should not be counted as a live offer. Related 2025 sunset: Figma's affiliate program was deprecated in early 2025 (no new applications). Material 2025-2026 changes: paid plan pricing and seat structure changed (now Full/Dev/Collab seats: Professional $16/$12/$3 per month per seat, Organization $55/$25/$5, Enterprise $90/$35/$5 annual billing; Professional was ~$18/editor and Organization ~$35 pre-restructure) — do not quote old per-editor prices. AI credits are now built into every plan/seat (Starter 500/mo with 150/day cap; Pro Full 3,000/mo; Org Full 3,500/mo; Enterprise Full 4,250/mo; all other seats 500/mo) and Figma explicitly states there are no free trials of paid plans and no nonprofit discounts. New products included in seats (Figma Make, Motion, Sites, Buzz, Specs) are beta on paid seats. The Education program itself is live and current: free Professional for 13+ verified students/educators, free Enterprise for K-12 districts, 3,000 AI credits/month for higher-ed and bootcamp education seats, with 1-year (students) / 2-year (educators) / 6-month (bootcamp students) validity terms.

findings.name: Free plan (Cloud)
findings.detail: Permanent free tier on CircleCI Cloud: 30,000 credits/month (= up to 6,000 build minutes on small Docker at 5 credits/min; ~3,000 min on medium Docker at 10 credits/min). Up to 5 active users/month; 30x concurrency (Docker, Linux VM, Arm, Windows VM) but only 1 macOS concurrency; 5 concurrent self-hosted runner tasks. Includes 2 GB storage + 1 GB network transfer; excess network/storage draws from your monthly credits at ~420 credits/GB. 1,000 Smarter Testing test atoms/month free. Free plan has no GPU classes and no X-large/large+ resource classes (Docker capped at Large; macOS M4 Pro Large and all GPU classes are paid-only).
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no .edu email, no application, no credit card required (page states 'No credit card required'). New signups land on Free plan. From 2025-12-01 each unregistered commit author counts individually toward the 5 active-user limit (previously counted as one).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at circleci.com/signup (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Cursor Origin), 2) connect a repo and add project, 3) builds run automatically on the Free plan — no plan selection or payment step needed.
findings.expiry: Recurring monthly; the 30,000 free credits expire at end of each billing month with no rollover. No sunset date. When credits hit 0, personal builds are blocked until the next month's refill.
findings.gotchas: Small-Docker framing makes it look like 6,000 min but on medium Docker you get ~3,000 min; on macOS M4 Pro (200 credits/min) the 30k pool lasts only ~150 min. 5-user cap bites if many contributors push to private repos. Credits are non-refundable; unused paid credits forfeit on cancellation (Free credits simply don't roll over).

findings.name: Open source build pool (free OSS program)
findings.detail: Free-plan orgs building public repos get up to 400,000 credits/month for Linux, Arm, and Docker OSS builds (= up to 80,000 build minutes on small Docker) on top of the 30,000-credit personal pool, plus 30,000 credits/month for macOS and Windows OSS builds. Includes enterprise-grade features (Docker layer caching, SSH debugging, flaky-test detection, self-hosted runners). OSS builds keep running even when your personal 30k pool is exhausted, and unregistered OSS contributors (e.g., PR authors) do not count toward your seat limit.
findings.eligibility: Free-plan organizations whose repository is public (GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket) and meets open-source licensing; OSS must be enabled in the project settings. No application, approval, or credit card; no .edu required; not region-limited. Docs note the OSS credit availability/limits are not visible in the web app.
findings.claim: 1) Create the account on Free plan, 2) keep the repo public on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, 3) enable open source in project settings (per CircleCI staff guidance in the Dec-2025 billing change thread) — the extra pool then applies automatically, no form needed.
findings.expiry: Recurring monthly (400k refreshes each month), no rollover, no end date. The official open-source page states 30,000 credits for macOS/Windows, but a May 2026 support article states 25,000 credits for macOS — treat the macOS/Windows sub-pool as 25k–30k pending CircleCI confirmation.
findings.gotchas: OSS credit pool is invisible in the UI; if you're blocked from building you must open a support ticket. Windows/macOS OSS capacity is tiny vs Linux/Arm/Docker. The official macOS number is inconsistent across CircleCI's own pages (30k on pricing/open-source vs 25k in support docs), so plan around the lower figure.

findings.name: Startup Program (CircleCI for Startups)
findings.detail: Up to $20,000 of free compute credits (at the $0.0006/credit rate, roughly 33M credits) usable on Docker, Linux, Arm, macOS, and Windows, spread over up to 24 months free, plus free Starter Support normally valued at $249/month, plus guided onboarding/migration support. Exact credit amount and program length vary by startup stage and location; it ends when the credits are exhausted or the promotional window closes, whichever comes first.
findings.eligibility: All must hold: (1) new to CircleCI or on the Free plan (no current paid customers), (2) Pre-Seed through Series A (Series B+ excluded), (3) founded within the last 5 years, (4) part of a recognized accelerator or VC, or otherwise proof of at least $500K USD raised (minimum threshold; no revenue cap or headcount cap stated). No .edu; no explicit region exclusion, but amounts/duration vary by location. No credit-card requirement is mentioned on the page.
findings.claim: 1) Fill out the application form on circleci.com/startup-program/ (HubSpot form), 2) or email startups@circleci.com (accelerators/VCs can enroll portfolio companies there), 3) CircleCI decides your tier on application; a representative contacts you as credits run low; after the window you move to standard pricing with volume discounts, config/history carry over with zero disruption.
findings.expiry: Promotional period: up to 24 months or until credits are fully consumed, whichever comes first. Program itself has no stated sunset date. Unused credits are program-scoped, not refundable/cashable.
findings.gotchas: 'Up to' figures — the actual tier (credit count and months) is assigned by CircleCI, not chosen by you, and varies by location. If you burn the pool early you transition to paid; the 'more credits than standard Performance' pitch still leaves you on a billable plan afterward. Not available to companies already paying for CircleCI or founded 5+ years ago.

findings.name: Education license / student offer — none active (Academy sunsets)
findings.detail: CircleCI has no student-specific free offer or .edu-based license: students simply use the standard Free plan (30,000 credits/month) with a personal account. The former free education platform, CircleCI Academy (free courses and the Associate Developer certificate, once accessible with code public-2020), is no longer available — CircleCI's support 'Educational resources' collection states 'CircleCI Academy is no longer available' and offers all 17 former courses/certificates only as downloadable SCORM files (course + exam links via Google Drive) that you can import into your own LMS or run locally. Third-party 2026 discount roundups (CostBench, Erkan Saka) confirm no CircleCI education terms are published.
