findings.eligibility: Formerly: anyone (public-2020 access code) for Academy courses. Now: course/exam downloads are public; no .edu email or enrollment proof needed for anything. There is no student pricing, discount, or license program to apply for.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim for a student license. For the learning content: go to the 'Educational resources' collection on support.circleci.com and download the SCORM courses; for actual CI compute, just sign up for the Free plan or the OSS pool with a public repo.
findings.expiry: CircleCI Academy is already sunset (confirmed as of 2026-10-22; no end date published). The SCORM downloads remain available. Free plan / OSS pool have no end dates.
findings.gotchas: Treat any cached third-party pages advertising 'CircleCI for students' as stale. A support article (May 2026) still says macOS OSS gets 25,000 credits vs the pricing page's 30,000 — documentation is slightly out of sync. Certificate no longer issued, only self-study downloads.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes and absences: (1) No free trial credits on paid plans currently exist — the pricing page (read 2026-10-22) lists no trial duration, trial credit pool, or CC-for-trial offer, and an independent 2026-10-14 tracker (PulseSignal) records "Free trial: None listed"; the trial-circleci model has been superseded by the permanent 30,000-credit Free plan. (2) CircleCI Academy (free courses/certificate, formerly the closest thing to an education program) has been sunset — the support collection now says "CircleCI Academy is no longer available"; only SCORM downloads of the 17 former courses remain; no end date was published, but it was already gone by 2026-10-22. (3) Effective 2025-12-01, CircleCI changed unregistered-user billing: every unregistered user now counts individually toward the monthly active-user total (previously all unregistered users counted as one); the Free plan keeps 5 included active users at the same price, and OSS-enabled projects are exempt (unregistered OSS PR authors don't count as seats). (4) The Free plan's 30,000-credit monthly allowance has been stable through 2025–2026 (no observed change; PriceVersion shows $0/30,000 credits recorded as current from 2026-10-04); the 400k OSS Linux pool and 30k macOS/Windows OSS pool are also still live per the official open-source page, though the support doc (May 2026) still lists macOS OSS at 25,000 credits — a documentation inconsistency worth confirming with CircleCI support. (5) Related non-offer sunsets: Bitbucket Data Center support retired 2026-10-01 and Self-Hosted Runner Bitbucket Cloud retires 2026-11-12 (VCS deprecations, not pricing); Xcode image retention is rolling off older versions each month.

provider: Windsurf (Codeium), now Devin Desktop under Cognition — Dev Tools, IDEs, Git & CI/CD fronts

findings.name: Devin Free plan ($0, perpetual)
findings.detail: Free tier at $0 on devin.ai/pricing: 'Light quota to code with agents', 'Limited model availability', 'Unlimited inline edits', 'Unlimited Tab completions', concurrent sessions capped at 10, Slack/Teams integrations, premium-model throughput marked 'Slow'. Docs (docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve.md) confirm Free grants 'Limited Devin usage' plus Devin Review and DeepWiki access, with usage allowance that refreshes on a daily and weekly basis; no dollar-value quota is published for the Free tier. Free sign-up: docs say users 'can sign up for free!'; no credit card is mentioned anywhere on the pricing or getting-started pages. No trial period or trial credits are offered — docs explicitly state 'Free trials of paid plans are not currently offered.'
findings.eligibility: Open to any individual, no .edu or startup requirements, no credit card required (not stated as required; free download/Signup link). No region limits stated on the pages read.
findings.claim: Register at devin.ai (Download free / Sign up for free). Free plan is $0; upgrade to any paid plan anytime via Settings > Plans. No email domain, funding, or age requirement stated.
findings.expiry: Perpetual free tier; no expiry stated. Quota refreshes daily/weekly; purchased on-demand credits never expire and roll over.
findings.gotchas: Agent quota is 'Light' with no published session or dollar amounts, so heavy agent use is quickly capped. Premium models are slow on Free; the page recommends mini models. The historical ~$10/mo Windsurf credit allowance is NOT stated anywhere on the current official pages. Overages on paid tiers bill at on-demand API pricing — Free simply has a limited quota. Free trials of paid plans do not exist.

findings.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) Free tier — IDE agent
findings.detail: The Windsurf IDE was renamed Devin Desktop ('Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf' — devin.ai/desktop FAQ). Free tier: $0 with direct Download link, unlimited inline edits and unlimited Tab completions (from the devin.ai/pricing Free row), 'Light' agent quota and 'Limited model availability'. Plans/extensions/settings carry over from old Windsurf accounts automatically via over-the-air update; Windsurf for JetBrains (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm) still downloadable. Docs (desktop/accounts/usage) say model credits are metered per agent prompt ('default message costing 1 credit') with per-model multipliers; no numeric free-plan credit allowance is published today.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no .edu, no startup gate, no credit card stated as required. Not student/startup-specific — same free tier as the Devin plan.
findings.claim: Download Devin Desktop (devin.ai/desktop, Free tier, $0) or keep the Windsurf JetBrains plugin; sign up free; the historical Windsurf account/credits/settings migrate automatically.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated for the free tier; daily/weekly refresh quotas apply.
findings.gotchas: 'Cascade' (the old Windsurf agent name) no longer appears in any current docs or release notes — agent usage is now metered under Devin Desktop ACU/credit mechanics; the historically quoted ~$10/month free credit allowance is not confirmed on any current official page. Free = no Devin Cloud/API access, no shared/collab features (those start at Pro/Teams).

findings.name: Devin Startup Program (startups)
findings.detail: Official program at devin.ai/startup (rolling review, apply via form): $15K in Devin credits loaded to your account on approval, plus a $50K matching grant — 1:1 dollar match on your next $100K of usage ('You spend $50K, you get $100K'), totaling $65K value. Also: unlimited seats (whole team in collaborative sessions), exclusive events (founder meetups, early-access previews), and a Devin swag pack for accepted startups. Social proof on page: NVIDIA, Cloudflare, Modal, Mercor, OpenRouter, Gamma, Exa, Profound.
findings.eligibility: Marketed to 'early-stage' startups. The page states NO funding cap, company-age limit, headcount limit, revenue requirement, or geography restriction; review is rolling with no hard deadline. No public terms/ToS link or credit-expiry window is published.
findings.claim: Fill out the application form at devin.ai/startup describing your startup; on approval $15K credits load immediately and the $50K 1:1 match applies to your next $100K of usage.
findings.expiry: No credit expiry or usage deadline published; matching grant applies to 'your next $100K of usage'. Program availability not dated.
findings.gotchas: All eligibility guardrails are off-page (in the application/review process) — a startup not deemed 'early-stage' could be rejected. The offer is Devin cloud-agent credits, not a free IDE tier for the team; unlimited seats are about collaborative Devin sessions, not free seats in the paid Desktop/Teams product. No region limits stated, but nothing either guarantees service availability in your country.

findings.name: Teams 'Flex seats' (free seats inside a paid team)
findings.detail: On the Teams plan ($80/mo minimum, up to 200 users, $40/mo per full developer seat), Flex seats are listed as 'Free': they carry no per-seat charge and draw 'entirely from the team's shared pool of on-demand credits'; no separate limit on flex seats, but every member (full or flex) counts toward the 200-user cap. Under the $80 minimum, 0 full seats = $80 of on-demand credits, 1 full seat = $40 credits, 2+ full seats = $0 bundled credits.
findings.eligibility: Not student/startup-specific — any organization buying Devin Teams. A free seat only exists inside a paid team plan; there is no standalone free team.
findings.claim: Buy a Devin Teams plan ($80/mo minimum) and add Flex seats at $0/seat, billing their usage from the shared on-demand credit pool.
findings.expiry: Included purchased credits never expire and roll over month-to-month; auto-refill can be configured (default monthly budget cap $160, in $120 increments of 1,000 pooled credits per docs.devin.ai desktop usage page).
findings.gotchas: Flex seats have no included quota — every agent action bills the shared pool, so a large flex team can burn the credit pool fast; not a genuine zero-cost offer (the $80/mo team minimum is mandatory).

sunset_notes: EDUCATION: No active student/education license found as of 2026-10-22. Official checks today: devin.ai/education returns 404, cognition.ai/education redirects to cognition.com/education which returns 404, and the full docs.devin.ai index (llms.txt) contains no education/student page; no student or classroom offer appears on devin.ai/pricing. Any earlier Devin/Windsurf/Codeium student pilot therefore appears to have been sunsetting-era or simply not published as a current program — I could not independently confirm its history because the session's web-search budget was exhausted, so treat the historical student-pilot detail as unverified (medium-low confidence). RENAME: 'Windsurf' the IDE was rebranded to 'Devin Desktop' by Cognition; docs.windsurf.com now 307-redirects to docs.devin.ai/desktop, the 'Cascade' agent name is gone from current docs/release notes (2025 and 2026 releases), and the historically quoted ~$10/month free credit allowance is not stated on any current official page. TRIALS: docs explicitly state 'Free trials of paid plans are not currently offered' — so the only free offers are the perpetual $0 Free tier, the Devin Startup Program, and free Flex seats inside a paid Teams plan. Note: official pages do not publish exact Free-tier quota numbers; 'Light quota' is all that is stated.

provider: GitHub Actions (GitHub / GitHub Education) — Dev Tools, IDEs, Git & CI/CD

findings.name: GitHub Actions Free plan (available to everyone, incl. students & startups)
findings.detail: Verified today at docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions and github.com/pricing. Private repos: 2,000 CI/CD minutes/month and 500 MB artifact storage (pooled with GitHub Packages) on the Free plan; Pro is 3,000 min/1 GB, Team 3,000 min/2 GB, Enterprise Cloud 50,000 min/50 GB; cache 10 GB/repo. Public repos using standard GitHub-hosted runners: minutes are free/unlimited ('GitHub Actions usage is free for self-hosted runners and for public repositories that use standard GitHub-hosted runners'). Self-hosted runners: free. GitHub Pages and Dependabot runs: free. No credit card required for the free tier. Startups: there is no separate startup program — any startup just gets this free tier.
findings.eligibility: Everyone with a GitHub Free account; no .edu email, no age/region limit (min account age standard). Credit card NOT required.
findings.claim: Already active by default on any GitHub Free account — no application needed. Usage is charged to the repo owner/billing account, not the workflow trigger.
findings.expiry: No expiry; allowance resets monthly. Larger runners and excess usage beyond 2,000 private min are billed per minute (e.g. Linux 2-core $0.006/min, macOS $0.062/min) once you exceed the quota.
findings.gotchas: Standard-runner public-repo minutes are unlimited; larger/custom runners are always charged even in public repos. Artifact storage is a shared pool with GitHub Packages. Minutes charged to repo owner, so a team/organization shares the 2,000 min per account, not per person. One github.com/pricing rendering I fetched suggested 'Unlimited public repo minutes — Students only; all other users 2,000 min/mo public', which contradicts the docs fetched the same day ('public repositories ... free', no student-only language) — trust the docs and treat public-repo minutes as free for all.

findings.name: GitHub Education for students (Student Developer Pack): free Copilot, Codespaces hours, free Pro
findings.detail: Verified today at docs.github.com/en/education/.../about-github-education-for-students, the apply page, the Student Developer Pack T&C page, and github.com/education. After verification: free GitHub Copilot 'Student' tier ('Verified students get free access to Copilot and its premium features'); GitHub Codespaces up to 180 core hours/month for personal accounts; Student Developer Pack with 80+ partner offers (cloud hosting to dev platforms to premium content, 'use professional tools at no cost'); the github.com/pricing education section lists free GitHub Pro for students/educators plus the same Codespaces/Copilot/pack benefits. GitHub Pro duration is not itemized in the current docs (historically 1 year; T&C do not restate it).
findings.eligibility: Student or faculty at an accredited educational institution, or enrolled in a degree/diploma-granting program (high school, college, university, or homeschool). Proof of enrollment: school ID with current date, class schedule, transcript, or enrollment verification letter. If your institution issues academic emails, you must add and verify one on your GitHub account (i.e. .edu/academic email where applicable; otherwise supply official documentation). Own a personal GitHub account; age 13+. No credit card required.
findings.claim: Settings → Education benefits (github.com/education) → 'Start an application' under GitHub Education → fill form (proof of enrollment) → submit; verify academic email first. Check first whether your institution is already a GitHub Campus Program partner. Benefits appear in the Education portal after approval.
findings.expiry: Student validation lasts 2 years, then revalidation required. Offers cannot be redeemed multiple times (including via new accounts). Third-party partners can change or remove offers at will; GitHub says it will try to notify in advance. Codespaces 180 core hours is a recurring monthly allowance; Pro offer (historically) 1 year.
findings.gotchas: The current docs 'About' page no longer itemizes free GitHub Pro or Actions minute allowances — only Copilot, Codespaces 180 h, and the pack; free Pro was confirmed from the pricing page's education section, not the docs (medium confidence there). Pack is partner-dependent: offers vary, no stacking of promos, terms are student-vs-partner. Faculty/teachers get a separate track; a school club can get a free GitHub Team with unlimited users + private repos for free.

findings.name: GitHub Campus Program (education license for schools): free GitHub Enterprise
findings.detail: Verified today at docs.github.com/en/education/.../about-github-campus-program. Schools get GitHub Enterprise Cloud and GitHub Enterprise Server free of charge, free for one year with automatic annual renewal, 'so long as you continue to operate within the terms of the agreement'. The license bundles 50,000 GitHub Actions minutes and 50 GB GitHub Packages storage. This is the main 'education license' offer — it benefits students at partner schools by making Enterprise tooling available campus-wide.
findings.eligibility: Any school that grants degrees, diplomas, or certificates. Application must be signed by a school employee with authority to adopt technology school-wide (CTO/CIO, Dean, Department Chair). Internal IT, research groups, and other departments may use the licenses provided they do not profit from them. Students themselves do not apply.
findings.claim: Apply through the Campus Program (referenced from the GitHub Education docs; application via the official Campus Program site / GitHub Education Resource Guide). Check institution status on the education docs before any individual student applies.
findings.expiry: Free for 12 months; auto-renews annually as long as terms are met.
findings.gotchas: For institutions, not individuals — individual students can't claim it. If your school is already a Campus partner, students at that school should not submit a separate individual application. Enterprise Server deployment implies self-managed infrastructure; no cost but operational burden on the school.

sunset_notes: Startup: GitHub has no dedicated startup program, no startup-credit offer, and no trial-credit offer for GitHub Actions as of 2026-10-22; startups only receive the general Free plan (2,000 min + 500 MB). No GitHub startup program ever existed on GitHub's public docs/pricing, so there is no 2025-2026 sunset of one to report. No sunsets or material changes to the student offers were noted on the official pages read today: the 2,000 min / 500 MB free tier is unchanged; Codespaces 180 core hours/mo for students and free Copilot (now branded 'GitHub Copilot Student') remain; the 2-year student validation period is confirmed. Two caveats: (1) the current docs 'About GitHub Education for students' page no longer itemizes free GitHub Pro or free Actions minutes — free Pro now appears only in github.com/pricing's education section (medium confidence; historically Pro was 1 year, duration no longer restated in docs T&C, which instead cite a 2-year validation and 80+ partner offers); (2) the web-search budget for this session was exhausted, so 2025-2026 news-level changes (announcements outside the official docs) could not be verified — confidence in 'no changes' rests on the docs/pricing pages fetched today only.

2025-2026 changes: (1) Aug 12, 2025 - JetBrains rebranded/relaunched the student program as the "JetBrains Student Pack" (blog.jetbrains.com post); license duration wording is now "completely free and remain valid as long as you're a student, but must be renewed annually" (replaces the old "1-year, renewable" framing). Promo: verify by Sep 12, 2025 to enter a prize draw (MacBook Pro, iPad Pro, reMarkable Paper Pro) - now expired. (2) Bootcamp student-coupon program is being retired: official sales FAQ (updated 30 Sep 2026) states "no new coupons are being issued after October 1, 2026"; short-term/bootcamp students were never eligible for free educational licenses (only long-term programs >1 year qualify). (3) Jul 18, 2025 - IntelliJ IDEA moved to a unified distribution starting with 2025.3: the separate Community Edition installer is gone; the single IDE keeps more free features than old Community for everyone, and an expired subscription degrades gracefully to the free feature set instead of locking out. Perpetual fallback license (last major version after a year of uninterrupted subscription) still applies. (4) The startup offer is now a 50% discount plan (caps over 5 years), not the older "up to 12 free licenses for 1 year" program that ran for years - free startup licenses survive only in the incubator/accelerator/VC partner track (6 months, up to 10 licenses). The 40% / 2-year graduation discount listed in the task's "known so far" could not be re-verified today: jetbrains.com student/estore pages are Cloudflare-gated to this fetcher and /shop/eform/students, /estore/graduates, /for-startups, /startup all 404'd; treat it as likely still real but unconfirmed (no official page read today).

findings.name: JetBrains Student Pack - free full IDE licenses for students
findings.detail: Free, non-commercial licenses for the paid IDEs while you stay enrolled; must be re-verified (renewed) annually with a reminder email. Products named in the Aug 2025 blog: IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, CLion, Rider, PhpStorm, DataGrip, RubyMine, RustRover, DataSpell, GoLand (11 IDEs). Also includes the JetBrains Academy plugin (100+ courses), IDE Features Trainer, and Code With Me. Non-commercial use only.
findings.eligibility: Student at an accredited educational institution (university/college; program longer than one year - bootcamps/short courses NOT eligible). Verify via: official university (.edu-like) email, ISIC/ITIC student ID, GitHub Student Developer Pack account, or uploaded official enrollment document (student ID/enrollment letter, <=4MB, not older than 6 months; China can use chsi.com.cn report; review up to 2 weeks). Minors need a parent/guardian email for consent. No credit card required. GitHub Student Developer Pack is a first-class application route (GitHub is a 'trusted partner').
findings.claim: 1) Apply at jetbrains.com/estore/students (or the academy student-pack page) using a GitHub Student Developer Pack account, university email + ID, or official documents; 2) email verification link; 3) after approval, log in to a JetBrains Account, download any IDE in the list - license activates automatically; installation instructions arrive by email.
findings.expiry: Valid as long as you remain a student; renewal annually (JetBrains reminds by email; resubmit proof of enrollment). The Sep 12, 2025 prize-draw deadline has passed.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial only - no commercial work. Free educational licenses exclude short-term/bootcamp programs (official FAQ, updated 30 Sep 2026). Annual re-verification required or access lapses. The 11 IDEs are individual products; the All Products Pack-style full bundle is what the pack effectively grants across them. AI tools are NOT included free - see separate finding.

findings.name: JetBrains Teacher Pack - free IDEs for teachers/educators
findings.detail: Free access to 10 JetBrains IDEs - 'the full versions of IntelliJ IDEA and PyCharm, plus GoLand, PhpStorm, and others' - plus course creation (JetBrains Academy) and 'classroom-wide AI control, deployed and managed from one place'. Licenses are valid one year with an automatic email reminder before expiry to renew/re-apply. No percentage discount tier is shown on the page; the pack is free, and institutional projects beyond classroom use go to commercial licensing.
findings.eligibility: Two tracks: (a) classroom track - representatives of accredited schools/colleges/universities, verified by 'a letter from school officials or a copy of your staff ID'; (b) individual track - teachers and IT staff at accredited institutions with programs longer than one year, verified by a university email address or valid ISIC card. No credit card required. Apply through the JetBrains shop e-form.
findings.claim: Apply via the 'Apply' link on the Teacher Pack page (JetBrains shop e-form), pick classroom or individual track, submit verification document or ISIC/university email, license arrives in the JetBrains account after review.
findings.expiry: Licenses valid 1 year; automatic email reminder before expiration to renew or re-apply (renewable while still teaching).
findings.gotchas: Classroom use is the intended scope; internal/institutional commercial projects must use commercial licenses. 'Full versions' means paid-tier IDEs, not just Community features.

findings.name: JetBrains for Startups - 50% Startup Discount Plan
findings.detail: 50% off JetBrains developer, team and learning tools plus AI, for up to 10 IDE subscriptions, 10 paid team/learning tool subscriptions, and 10 JetBrains AI subscriptions (AI Pro/AI Ultimate, which include Junie) over a five-year window. Plugins: unlimited different plugins, up to 10 licenses each. TeamCity capped at 10 build agents; YouTrack at 250 users/subscription. Licenses can be spread across the 5 years; 50% off applies automatically at checkout; cannot be stacked with other discounts; no team/floating licenses; personal (non-commercial) licenses excluded.
findings.eligibility: Company privately owned; established within the last 5 years (provable with a document, <=4MB); has a website or other discoverable online presence. No funding cap, revenue cap, or headcount cap stated (teams of 50+ are redirected to business sales). One application per organization; subsidiaries of an already-approved org are ineligible; discount granted only once. Review takes up to 48 hours.
findings.claim: Apply at jetbrains.com/startups (form: jetbrains.com/shop/eform/startup): choose products, submit company info + founding-date proof; if approved you get a quote email and 50% off automatically applies at checkout within the caps for 5 years.
findings.expiry: Discount lapses 5 years after the approval confirmation or when the purchase caps (10+10+10 subscriptions) are exhausted, whichever first. Company can receive the discount only once.
findings.gotchas: This is a discount program, not free licenses - the older 'up to 12 free startup licenses' model is gone (see sunset notes). No free tier for direct startup applicants; the free-license route now only exists via the partner track: incubators/accelerators/VCs with >=10 portfolio startups get six months of free access to up to 10 licenses, then the standard 50% for the remaining ~4 years; a partner-network startup must use the partner's free period first and cannot hold a direct discount at the same time. Credit card not needed to apply.

findings.name: JetBrains AI Free access - Junie Lite + AI Free plan (AI tools)
findings.detail: Free AI layer for individuals: 'Junie Lite' is a free model, 'always on, in every JetBrains account' - 'a free AI layer, no trial, no card', plus BYOK (bring your own API key, provider-rate pricing, zero markup, supports local models). The Aug 2025 student-pack post says students should 'Test-drive JetBrains AI tools during your trial, and then switch to the AI Free plan or upgrade anytime'. Paid tiers for reference: AI Pro $8.33/user/month (10 AI credits per 30 days + top-ups); AI Ultimate $25/user/month (35 AI credits per 30 days + top-ups, recommended for Junie).
findings.eligibility: Any JetBrains account gets Junie Lite free (no card, no trial). AI Free plan available to individual users, including students after their trial. Paid tiers need a subscription. No region limits stated.
findings.claim: Sign in to any JetBrains account / open Junie in terminal or IDE -> free model is available immediately. For AI Assistant: click the AI icon in the IDE top-right, complete trial, then select the AI Free plan; upgrade to Pro/Ultimate via the JetBrains subscription purchase links.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated for the free tier; 'always on, in every JetBrains account'.
findings.gotchas: Free tier is model- and rate-limited ('AI usage billed separately' caveat on the page); heavy Junie agent use hits the free-model or credit limits, which is why Ultimate is 'recommended for Junie'. Naming is in flux: product page says 'Junie Lite', student blog says 'AI Free plan' - the free tier's exact credit numbers were not published on the pages fetched. CC NOT required for the free tier.

findings.name: Free IDEs for anyone - non-commercial use & unified IDEA free tier
findings.detail: Several JetBrains products are free outside the student program: RustRover is listed on the products page with download only (no Buy CTA); Datalore is 'Get it for free'; YouTrack has a free tier plus paid; dotPeek is a free .NET decompiler; Gateway, Hub and Toolbox are free downloads. Since the July 2025 unified distribution (from 2025.3), IntelliJ IDEA ships as ONE installer: all Ultimate features need a subscription, but without one 'the IDE will remain fully functional, free to use for both commercial and non-commercial projects, and will include more features than the current Community Edition ever had'.
findings.eligibility: Nobody in particular - free for anyone: RustRover, Datalore, YouTrack (free tier), dotPeek, Gateway, Hub, Toolbox; IDEA's free feature set is usable even for commercial projects. Community Edition as a separate product no longer exists.
findings.claim: Download directly from jetbrains.com/products (or the per-product pages); for IDEA, install the single unified IDE and use the free feature set without any license.
findings.expiry: No expiry; ongoing. (Per-product 'free for non-commercial use' tiers for WebStorm/GoLand-class IDEs are commonly cited but were not re-verified on today's pages - unconfirmed here.)
findings.gotchas: Unified IDEA still gates the full Ultimate feature set behind a subscription; when a paid IDEA subscription lapses, the IDE degrades to the free feature set instead of locking out; a perpetual fallback license (last major version from your uninterrupted-subscription year) still applies. Don't confuse free personal use of these IDEs with the student pack, which grants full paid IDEs to students.

findings.name: 30-day free trials for paid JetBrains products
findings.detail: All paid products (IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate features, WebStorm, CLion, DataGrip, Rider, TeamCity, etc.) offer a 30-day free trial, and the student-pack post explicitly points students to 'test-drive JetBrains AI tools during your trial' before moving to the AI Free plan.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a JetBrains account; no eligibility beyond creating an account.
findings.claim: Download a paid product from its product page, start the IDE, choose the 30-day trial when prompted at license selection.
findings.expiry: 30 days per product (longer combined window when products are downloaded together).
findings.gotchas: Trial is not free-forever; CC not required for the trial itself. Do not mistake trials for the free student/teacher licenses.

findings.name: 40% graduation discount for 2 years (unverified today)
findings.detail: The task's known-baseline says '40% graduation discount for 2 years' - graduated students can keep cheap licenses for their first two years after finishing studies. This could NOT be re-verified today: jetbrains.com/estore pages are behind a Cloudflare check to this fetcher, and /shop/eform/students, /estore/graduates, /shop/eform/graduates, /for-startups all returned 404/403. No official page read today contains the figure.
findings.eligibility: Per the old program: recent graduates who held a student license; claimed through the students e-store with proof of graduation/completion.
findings.claim: Unconfirmed today - check jetbrains.com/estore/students or the JetBrains sales FAQ directly for the live terms.
findings.expiry: Believed to apply for up to 2 years after graduation; unconfirmed.
findings.gotchas: May have been folded into the Student Pack / estore flow after the Aug 2025 relaunch; do not quote the 40%/2-years figures without re-checking the official page.

provider: Google Cloud (VPS / cloud VM front: Compute Engine e2-micro; trials, free tier, startup credits, education credits)

findings.name: GCP Free Trial: $300 Welcome credit for 90 days
findings.detail: Free Trial billing account is preloaded with a $300 Welcome credit, valid for 90 days, spendable on any Google Cloud products (including Compute Engine VMs as VPS). You are not billed for any usage during the trial. If you upgrade to a Paid billing account you keep unused credit until it expires 90 days from signup; if you neither upgrade nor spend the $300, the trial billing account is closed and all associated projects/resources are stopped.
findings.eligibility: New customers only: you must never have been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase, and must not have previously signed up for the Free Trial. One trial per person/payment method. A valid credit card or other payment method is REQUIRED at signup (plus bank-account verification in some countries) even though you aren't billed during the trial.
findings.claim: 1) Go to cloud.google.com/free (or console.cloud.google.com/freetrial). 2) Create a Google account + GCP project. 3) Add a credit card/payment method and complete identity verification. 4) Trial starts after verification; $300 credit and 90-day clock begin. No card is charged during the trial.
findings.expiry: Credit and trial both last 90 days from signup. Unused credit expires 90 days from trial signup even if you convert to paid. After that, account is closed (projects stopped) unless converted to a paid account before expiry.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (unlike AWS, you cannot get the GCP trial without a payment method; Google runs an authorization hold to validate it). $300 burns fast on VMs (e.g. an e2-micro VPS for 90 days costs only ~$10-15, but anything bigger eats it quickly). Trial ends -> resources stopped, data at risk: upgrade before day 90 or export/stop instances. The trial credit does NOT cover Always-Free tier usage; after trial, usage outside the Free Tier is billed.

findings.name: Compute Engine Always-Free tier: 1 e2-micro VM + 30 GB disk, perpetual (no card required)
findings.detail: Free Tier, no expiration, available to all GCP customers: 1 non-preemptible e2-micro VM instance per month (1 vCPU / 1 GB RAM), time-based limit - free until cumulative hours equal the total hours in the month; usable in us-west1 (Oregon), us-central1 (Iowa), or us-east1 (South Carolina), used combined across those regions. 30 GB-months standard persistent disk. 1 GB/month outbound egress from North America to all destinations except China/Australia. Related free items on the same page: Cloud Storage 5 GB regional storage, Cloud Run 2M requests/mo, App Engine F1 + 9 h/day B1, Cloud Build, Cloud Functions. GPUs/TPUs are never free.
findings.eligibility: Any GCP customer (including trial users, post-trial, or accounts that skip the trial - the Free Tier applies as long as you use products within the monthly limits). A billing account must exist; the Always-Free usage itself does not consume trial credit. Region lock-in: e2-micro free limit only in the 3 US regions; you can still place a paid VM anywhere.
findings.claim: Create a GCP project (billing account, no card needed if you stay within free tier; a trial or a card is only needed the moment you exceed limits), go to Compute Engine -> Create VM, pick e2-micro in us-west1/us-central1/us-east1, attach a 30 GB or smaller standard PD, and run it - compute+disk+1 GB egress stay $0 each month indefinitely.
findings.expiry: No expiration - Free Tier has no stated end date, limits reset monthly. Google reserves the right to change/eliminate usage limits with 30 days' notice.
findings.gotchas: The '1 TB egress/mo' in the task's known-info is WRONG: official limit is 1 GB/mo outbound from NA (China/AU excluded). The limit is by hours, not by instance - running multiple e2-micros in parallel still costs $0 up to full-month hours. Disk must be STANDARD type, 30 GB or less. Egress >1 GB, GPU/TPU, larger disks, non-US regions for e2-micro, and any usage over the time limit bill at standard rates. A billing account without a payment method: free tier usage is permitted, but exceeding it will suspend service until a card is added.

findings.name: GKE Free Trial: 90 days of full Kubernetes Engine capabilities at no fee
findings.detail: Separate from the $300 trial: a GKE trial card on cloud.google.com/free - 'Try GKE with the full set of product capabilities for 90 days for no fee', deep-linked to console.cloud.google.com/freetrial?redirectPath=/kubernetes/overview. Use it to run a managed Kubernetes cluster (worker VMs) free for 90 days; useful as a VPS/container-hosting front.
findings.eligibility: GCP account holders (trial signup path); subject to abuse prevention - 'Access to products may be limited to prevent abuse'. New-customer trial rules apply for the $300 companion credit.
findings.claim: From cloud.google.com/free, click the GKE Free Trial card (or console.cloud.google.com/freetrial?redirectPath=/kubernetes), complete trial signup with a card, and create a GKE Autopilot/Standard cluster for 90 days without paying.
findings.expiry: 90-day window from signup; after that standard GKE pricing applies (control-plane fee, node hours).
findings.gotchas: Requires the same card-verified trial signup; GKE Autopilot still charges per-node-hour for the 90-day trial at list price after the window; the free GKE *tier* (always-free cluster) also exists but only the cluster fee, not compute/networking. If your real goal is a cheap VPS, raw Compute Engine e2-micro is simpler than GKE.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program (rebranded/expanded GCP for Startups): $2K Start tier, $200K-$350K Scale/Scale AI tiers
findings.detail: Official page cloud.google.com/startup ('Google for Startups Cloud Program'). Tiers: Start = $2K in credits for startups founded within the past 2 years with a working MVP, clear business model, and plans to seek VC funding. Funded tiers 'Scale' and 'Scale AI' range $200K-$350K in GCP credits for growing startups with verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding, founded within the last 3-5 years. Footnote structure on the page: AI startups - Year 1: 100% coverage up to $250,000 GCP credits; Year 2: 20% coverage up to an additional $100,000. Other startups - Year 1: 100% up to $100,000; Year 2: 20% up to an additional $100,000. Also includes Startup Success Managers, Customer Engineering support, and AI/DeepMind build benefits; a separate Maps Platform benefit exists (separate application).
findings.eligibility: Startups: founded within 2 years (Start) or 3-5 years with Pre-Seed to Series A funding (Scale/Scale AI). Exclusions: companies that have IPO'd or been acquired, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content, dev shops, consultancies/agencies, cryptocurrency mining companies, or token-distributing companies. Acceptance at Google's sole discretion. No .edu email or revenue cap stated - 'funding stage' (Pre-Seed to Series A) is the cap. No funding needed for the $2K Start tier.
findings.claim: Apply via the 'Apply to the program' button on cloud.google.com/startup (links to cloud.google.com/startup/apply). Fill in company info, stage, funding, website. Stealth (funded) founders: get your accelerator/VC to verify/referral you; unfunded stealth founders must wait to apply until product launch with a live website. If accepted, credits apply to a GCP billing account; check 'Billing -> Cloud Credits' in console for balance/expiry. Third-party (partner) model usage is billed directly, not covered.
findings.expiry: Year-1 credits (100% coverage up to the tier cap) then Year-2 credits at 20% up to $100K additional. A separate footnoted rule: your company domain must not have been on a paid Google Workspace plan within 31 days of applying. Exact per-tier dollar caps beyond '$200K-$350K' and credit validity windows are not spelled out on the page I read - treat specific amounts as up-to tier cap.
findings.gotchas: The page's marketing ('Up to $350k') and the footnote caps ($250K AI / $100K non-AI Y1 + 20%/$100K Y2) don't fully reconcile - confirm the exact amount in your acceptance. Credits are for GCP products, not cash; third-party model calls bypass the credit. Not available to your own personal account - must be the startup's billing account. Old 'GCP for Startups' URLs (cloud.google.com/programs/startup, /boost) 404; use cloud.google.com/startup (gcp-startups still resolves, 200).

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education - Faculty Teaching Credits: up to $100/staff + up to $50/student
findings.detail: From cloud.google.com/edu/faculty + edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching: eligible faculty (university faculty, not students) can apply for GCP credits to give students hands-on experience: up to $100 in Google Cloud credits per teaching staff member and up to $50 in Cloud credits per student, for up to 3 courses per application. Intended for classroom use; students cannot apply directly - they must be given credits by their faculty. Complementary: Google Cloud Career Launchpad (free coaching through GCP Certificates).
findings.eligibility: Faculty only, at accredited institutions in approved countries (country/state dropdown on the form; US has state list). Requires an official school email with a valid edu domain (or a nominated email - credits attach to it and are non-transferable) plus a link to your faculty directory profile. Must state course name, start date, abstract, expected student + TA counts.
findings.claim: 1) Faculty apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching/ (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/faculty 'Apply for teaching credits'). 2) Submit course details; approval via CloudEduGrants@google.com. 3) After approval, credits redeem to the school domain; share with students (who log in with their school email). 4) Pool individual student credits for group projects per the guide on the faculty page.
findings.expiry: Course start must be <=1 year from application. Once approved, credits are redeemable starting up to 16 weeks AFTER the course start date and are valid up to 1 year after the course start date. Re-submitting the form only reviews the latest submission.
findings.gotchas: Credit card NOT required for these credits. Credits are locked to school email domains and non-transferable - students can't move them to a personal account. US-only for some sub-benefits; check the country list. There is a dedicated PDF ('cloud edu free trial warning') telling faculty to keep students OFF the $300 free trial (which forces a credit card) and on to these credits instead. The faculty page also links 'Manage Google Cloud credits' and 'redeem education credits' guides.

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education - Research Credits: $5,000 GCP research credits
findings.detail: From cloud.google.com/edu/researchers + edu.google.com/programs/credits/research: apply for $5,000 in Google Cloud research credits (hero CTA 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'). Separate GPAR (Google Public Sector - Program for Accelerated Research) benefit is currently US-only. Related non-credit: on-campus research day, Google Skills training.
findings.eligibility: Faculty, PhD students, and postdoctoral researchers from accredited higher-education institutions and eligible nonprofit research institutions, in approved countries. Form asks institution, department, researcher type (Postdoc etc.), faculty/researcher directory link, project proposal (<=250 words), funding source, prior cloud/GCP usage, a GCP Pricing Calculator estimate + URL, and a GCP Billing Account ID. PhD students and postdocs can apply (faculty alone does NOT have to be the applicant).
findings.claim: 1) Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research/ (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/researchers 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'). 2) Create a GCP billing account first (needed to receive credits - ID up to 25 chars). 3) Submit proposal + pricing calculator estimate. 4) Once approved, credits land on your billing account.
findings.expiry: Credits are valid for 1 year from award (form explicitly asks how you'll fund the project 'after your credit expires in 1 year').
findings.gotchas: You MUST have a GCP billing account to receive research credits - it's where credits attach, not a card-charge requirement by itself (you can hold a billing account without a card until you exceed free usage). Credits are for research GCP products, non-transferable, tied to your institutional email/account. Country-locked - not available in all regions. $5,000 is the standard research figure; large AI/HPC projects may be pitched through partners or GPAR (US-only) instead.

findings.name: Google Cloud for Students: 200 free Google Skills training credits + free GCP Certificates/badges (NOT GCP compute credits)
findings.detail: From cloud.google.com/edu/students: students get 200 free Google Skills credits (Google Cloud Skills Boost / certification training) that 'expire one year after they are issued', requested via a form. PLUS free: Google Cloud Certificates (shareable digital credentials), skill badges from hands-on labs, Google Skills Arcade (gamified learning with prizes/swag), free online labs, Developer Student Clubs, Cloud OnAir events. IMPORTANT: this is TRAINING credit, not a GCP infrastructure/VM credit - students who want an actual VM use the $300 trial or credits granted by their faculty (faculty program above).
findings.eligibility: Students (and those preparing for entry-level cloud roles). The page does not state a .edu-email hard requirement for the training-credits form, but the request form (services.google.com/fb/forms/googlecloudskillsbooststudenttrainingcreditsapplication) and program context (student community, DSC, Cloud OnAir) are aimed at students; use your school email where offered. No credit card required for any of these.
findings.claim: 1) At cloud.google.com/edu/students, click 'Request credits' -> the Google Skills Boost student training-credits application form. 2) For credentials, complete Google Cloud Certificates / skill-badge lab paths (free, no prerequisites, no cost). 3) Join a Developer Student Club or Cloud OnAir events free.
findings.expiry: The 200 training credits 'expire one year after they are issued'. Certificates/badges/Skills Arcade have no expiry stated.
findings.gotchas: Do NOT confuse '200 Google Skills credits' (course/cert training, $-value on courses) with GCP compute/VM credits - the student page grants no e2-micro-style infrastructure credit. To actually run a VM for free as a student, use (a) the $300/90-day trial, or (b) credits your faculty applied for under the faculty program. The faculty page explicitly warns students to avoid the trial if their school has applied for education credits.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, no core offer was sunset: the $300/90-day trial, the Always-Free e2-micro VM tier, and the startup + education programs are all live and verified on official pages today. Verified structural notes (no web-searchable 2025-2026 change history available because this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted - conclusions below rest on page reads only, not on diffed changelogs): (1) The startup program now presents a THREE-tier structure - 'Start $2K' for unfunded startups founded in the last 2 years, plus funded 'Scale' and 'Scale AI' tiers ($200K-$350K) - a new/expanded format vs. the older single 'GCP for Startups' ($1M, founded-within-5-years, up-to-50-FTE) model that was widely documented pre-2025; old URLs cloud.google.com/programs/startup and cloud.google.com/boost now 404, and the current page is cloud.google.com/startup (cloud.google.com/gcp-startups still serves, 200). The Scale AI tier + 'Build with Google DeepMind' AI-credits framing (AI startups 100% to $250K Y1 / 20% to $100K Y2) reflects a post-2025 AI-first program redesign. (2) Education credits are now routed through edu.google.com forms (teaching credits, $5,000 research credits, 200 student training credits) and the 'cloud.edu free trial warning' PDF, a current setup. (3) GPAR (researcher fast-track) is flagged 'Currently only available in the United States'. If you need a 2025-2026 changelog (exact dates the startup tiers were reshaped or the trial terms edited), that requires a fresh WebSearch - this session's 200-call budget was consumed before the change-history could be verified; all amounts/durations above were read directly from the live official pages on the date of the report.

findings.name: Copilot Free (no-credit-card free tier, all individual users)
findings.detail: $0 tier: 2,000 completions per month, 'an allowance of GitHub AI Credits' (page says 'Limited chat and agent usage'; no fixed credit number published on the marketing page; 1 AI credit = $0.01 USD). Auto model selection only (as of 2026-06-24 the only model-selection experience on Free/Student); agents 'Limited'; Copilot Chat skills not available; no app modernization, no cloud agent, no code review. New signups remain open even when paid plans were paused. Open to everyone at github.com/sign-up.
findings.eligibility: Individual developers who do NOT already have Copilot through an organization/enterprise. No credit card required, no trial. No region limit stated on the pages fetched.
findings.claim: Sign up for GitHub -> choose Copilot Free (no card). Available from github.com/features/copilot/plans; IDEs/CLI/GitHub mobile included.
findings.gotchas: Marketing page wording: 'No credit card required' appears on the Free card at github.com/features/copilot. Free users are 'limited to 2,000 completions and access to entry level models per month' — entry-level model access despite the full model list being shown in the table. If you have an org-provisioned Copilot you can't use Free on the same account.
findings.expiry: No expiry; monthly rolling limits. (Free tier itself: none published.)

findings.name: Copilot Student (free plan for verified students via GitHub Education)
findings.detail: Dedicated free 'Copilot Student' plan (introduced 2026-03-12/13, replacing the old 'free Copilot Pro for students' benefit): unlimited code completions + 200 monthly included GitHub AI credits (credit allowance added 2026-06-01) + agent mode; auto model selection ONLY (manual premium model choice removed; auto routes across OpenAI/Anthropic/Google 'subject to plan restrictions'; GPT-5.3-Codex dropped from picker 2026-04-27; (Preview) labels retired 2026-06-24). Excludes third-party agents. Replaces the old free-access entitlement that had unlimited premium models.
findings.eligibility: Verified student in GitHub Education (accredited school; school-issued email and/or official dated proof of enrollment; Student Pack age floor is 13+ per education page). GitHub reevaluates eligibility every MONTH. No credit card. New Student signups were paused 2026-04-20 and reopened from ~2026-06-16/17; as of 2026-10-22 signups are open.
findings.claim: github.com/settings/education/benefits -> apply as student; after approval, 'Free GitHub developer resources for students and teachers' -> Learn more -> activate Copilot Student (activation can lag verification by days; direct URL github.com/github-copilot/free_signup). No action was needed for existing students at the 2026-03 transition.
findings.gotchas: '200 monthly AI credits' figure comes from the official community discussion of the transition, not a docs table — medium confidence on that number specifically. Monthly re-verification means losing eligibility (graduation) drops the benefit; the plan is not a paid subscription, so 'free plan runs out the moment you graduate'. Existing premium-request-unit (PRU) entitlements for pre-existing students were kept at transition. Student tier no longer includes premium-model manual selection — the biggest 2025->2026 change.
findings.expiry: Rollover: monthly re-evaluation; 200 credits/month (community-discussion figure); unlimited completions.

findings.name: Copilot Pro free for verified teachers/educators
findings.detail: GitHub Copilot Pro (normally $10/mo; 1,000 base + 500 flex = 1,500 AI credits/mo on the $10 price; base-credit pool quoted on marketing page as $15/mo worth) is free for verified educators. Also free: GitHub Teams account (unlimited private repos) for teachers.
findings.eligibility: Currently employed educator at an accredited educational institution. Verification requires an official institutional email plus supplementary proof (faculty ID or employment verification letter). No credit card mentioned anywhere on the page. No region limit stated.
findings.claim: Apply via the GitHub Education for Teachers portal (github.com/settings/education/benefits). If rejected: ensure clear academic email + employment documentation, update info and reapply. Copilot Pro then appears as the included plan.
findings.gotchas: Teacher verification is document-based, not just .edu-email. Docs (plans page) phrase it as 'Verified teachers... may be eligible for free access to Copilot Pro' — a benefit, not a guaranteed signup. Pro signups were briefly paused (2026-04-20 to ~2026-06-16) during the billing restructure; free-for-teachers activation follows the same plan plumbing. Opus models were removed from Pro (2026-04-20) even in the free-teacher grant.
findings.expiry: Tied to ongoing educator verification (GitHub reevaluates education eligibility monthly); no published sunset date.

findings.name: Copilot Pro free for maintainers of popular open-source projects
findings.detail: GitHub's open-source benefits: 'Copilot Pro is free for open source maintainers of popular projects and verified students'; GitHub cites 280,000+ maintainers with program access. Free Pro = 1,000 base + 500 flex = 1,500 AI credits/mo (paid-plan equivalent; $15/mo worth base pool on marketing page).
findings.eligibility: Maintainer of a 'popular' project — the current pages do NOT document the popularity threshold (no stars/followers number published on github.com/open-source or the plans docs page; historically tied to project popularity, e.g. high star/follower counts). Claim is through the normal Copilot sign-up, where eligible accounts get Pro instead of paid checkout.
findings.claim: Sign up via github.com/features/copilot ('Sign-up for Copilot' CTA from the open-source page); eligible maintainers' accounts receive Pro-tier access; users who get Pro 'through... an existing verified OSS, student, faculty, or MVP account may elect to use Free instead' (features/copilot FAQ).
findings.gotchas: Exact 'popular project' criteria are not documented on any page fetched today — verify case-by-case at signup; don't claim a specific star threshold as fact. Benefit is not a paid subscription, but Pro plan mechanics (model restrictions, e.g. Opus removed from Pro 2026-04-20) apply. Pro signups were paused 2026-04-20 to ~2026-06-16.
findings.expiry: No published expiry; tied to maintaining a popular project; not monthly like student status per pages fetched (unverified).

findings.name: GitHub for Startups program ($10,000 GitHub Enterprise Cloud credits, incl. Copilot)
findings.detail: Eligible startups receive $10,000 in GitHub credits applied to their Enterprise Cloud account, valid up to 12 months (expire on full consumption or 12-month end, whichever first). Credits cover Enterprise licenses, Copilot licenses/premium models/agentic capabilities, Advanced Security, Actions, and other metered offerings; includes 50k included Actions minutes under Enterprise tier. The page notes a PREVIOUS startup offer has been discontinued and is no longer available.
findings.eligibility: Must be tied to an approved partner (VC, accelerator, incubator); received outside funding 'up to Series B or earlier' (stage cap, non-equity credits don't count as funding); NEW to GitHub Enterprise — not on an Enterprise plan within the past 6 months and no prior credits/licenses; GitHub.com Enterprise Cloud only (no Enterprise Server/Data Residency). Pages fetched state NO founding-age cap, no dollar funding ceiling, and no geographic restriction.
findings.claim: 1) Get referred/apply through a GitHub for Startups partner (partner directory + partner-application form on the page). 2) Submit the Enterprise application; applicant's primary email gets a reply within 2-3 business days. 3) Complete onboarding INCLUDING adding a payment method. A valid payment method (credit card) IS required — 'Failure to have an authorization... will result in your account being locked.'
findings.gotchas: Payment method required (unlike all the offers above). One-time redemption; after credits expire/12 months, products 'automatically transition to standard paid billing'; violations can have credits revoked. No specific seat counts/Codespaces hours published on the page — the old 'X free seats' style offer was discontinued. Partner-gated: you cannot self-serve without a partner referral.
findings.expiry: Credits: 12 months or full consumption; program: no end date published.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 material changes verified via changelog/docs: (1) 2026-03-12/13: the legacy free student entitlement (previously 'free Copilot Pro features for verified students') was replaced by a dedicated, deliberately more limited 'Copilot Student' plan — manual premium-model selection removed, auto-only routing; 200 AI credits/month added 2026-06-01; GPT-5.3-Codex dropped from student model picker 2026-04-27; auto-only model selection enforced 2026-06-24. (2) 2026-04-20: new signups for Student/Pro/Pro+/Max PAUSED and usage limits tightened (Opus removed from Pro, Pro+ >5x Pro limits; refund window closed 2026-05-20); signups gradually reopened from 2026-06-16/17 — as of 2026-10-22 open. (3) 'Premium requests' terminology is gone across pages fetched; plans now use GitHub AI Credits (1 credit = $0.01; overage $0.01/credit) after usage-based billing went live 2026-06-01 — so older docs citing e.g. '50 premium requests' on Free are outdated. (4) GitHub for Startups: the previous startup offer was explicitly 'discontinued and is no longer available'; current offer is the $10k Enterprise-cloud credit. (5) No region restrictions found on any fetched page; student offer is global via GitHub Education verification. One caveat: the session's web-search budget was exhausted, so verification relied on WebFetch of official pages; 'popular OSS project' threshold remains undocumented on official pages (medium confidence).

findings.name: GitHub Codespaces Free plan (all users)
findings.detail: Personal Free accounts include 120 core-hours of codespace compute + 15 GB of codespace storage per month (renew each billing cycle). A 2-vCPU codespace burns 2 core-hours per active hour, so 120 core-hours = 60 hours on 2 cores, 30 hours on 4 cores ($0.36/hr), 15 hours on 8 cores ($0.72/hr). 16/32-core sizes cost $1.44/$2.88 per hour. Storage overage: $0.07/GB-month; compute overage only if you add a payment method and raise the spend limit. Free accounts (github.com/pricing) have a $0 spend limit by default, so no CC is required and charges cannot accrue unless you opt in. No free quota exists for organization/enterprise accounts on the Free plan.
findings.eligibility: Any GitHub account on the Free plan (personal accounts only; 'GitHub Free for organizations' includes none). No credit card, no verification.
findings.claim: Create a free GitHub account; codespaces work immediately in a web/VS Code session. Check usage at github.com/settings/billing (Codespaces section) or github.com/codespaces. No application or enrollment needed.
findings.expiry: Quota renews automatically each monthly billing cycle (based on personal billing day). No sunset of the free tier announced as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: When the 120 core-hours or 15 GB run out, creating/opening new codespaces is blocked unless you add a payment method and set a budget. Storage accumulation is cumulative within the cycle: deleting codespaces does not claw back current-month storage. Stopped codespaces auto-delete after ~30-day retention but count toward storage until then; prebuilds are disabled once storage is exhausted. Dev containers using default images do not count toward storage. Orgs on the Free plan have 0 included core-hours — a common trap.

findings.name: GitHub Free for students (free Pro via Student Developer Pack) — 180 core-hours + 20 GB
findings.detail: Verified students get GitHub Pro free for the duration of their student status, which carries Pro-level Codespaces: 180 core-hours/month + 20 GB codespace storage (the Pro included-quota values read today from the Codespaces billing docs; students map to Pro, not a separate student codespace quota). Also included at no cost: full GitHub Pro plan, GitHub Copilot for students ('unlimited code completions + GitHub AI credits, limited chat/agent, auto model selection'), GitHub Pages limits, plus third-party partners (Azure $100 credit, JetBrains, Datadog, 1Password, etc.).
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students; verification through GitHub Education (education.github.com/pack). Typically a school-issued email (.edu or equivalent) or proof of enrollment; school/issuer photo ID may be used. No credit card required. No stated region limit. Teachers: verified academic faculty get GitHub Team free for teaching/research (separate offer, see sunset notes for plan-table changes).
findings.claim: Sign in at education.github.com/pack -> verify student status with school email/ID -> pack benefits apply automatically account-wide (Pro plan + Codespaces Pro quota). No separate codespaces enrollment.
findings.expiry: Lasts 'while you are a student' (pack states the Pro benefit persists during enrollment; re-verification happens when status changes, effectively each school year). Included codespace quota resets monthly with the billing cycle.
findings.gotchas: The old dedicated 'Free for students' codespace tier (120 core-hours/15GB distinct from Pro) is no longer documented — students now receive Pro's 180 core-hours/20GB, so the figures are read via the Pro row. Pro included usage does not cover metered add-ons (Copilot usage, GHAS, etc.) — plan discounts don't apply to usage-based billing. Copilot student tier is 'limited' chat/agent — agent-heavy use exhausts quickly. Pack partner offers (Azure, Datadog) are trial/credit-based, not perpetual.

findings.name: GitHub for Startups program — $10,000 credits (education/startup front: startup program)
findings.detail: Current startup offer (verified on github.com/enterprise/startups today): eligible startups get $10,000 in GitHub Enterprise platform credits usable across Enterprise, Copilot, Advanced Security, Actions (50,000 included Action minutes) and other metered add-ons (i.e. codespaces compute billed to the Enterprise org) for up to 12 months. Includes onboarding/office hours. This is a credits program on Enterprise Cloud, not a free codespaces tier for startups.
findings.eligibility: Company must have outside funding up to Series B or earlier (non-equity credits excluded); must be new to GitHub Enterprise (no Enterprise plan in prior 6 months and never received GitHub credits or Enterprise licenses); must apply through an approved partner (VC, accelerator, or incubator); GitHub Enterprise Cloud on github.com only (no Enterprise Server/Data Residency); one-time redemption.
findings.claim: Go via a partner: browse github.com/enterprise/startups/partners (or the partner you are affiliated with applies on your behalf). Ineligible companies get a free Enterprise trial instead (github.com/get_started?with=enterprise). Support: ticket under 'Credit Offers - GitHub for Startups'.
findings.expiry: Credits valid for up to 12 months from approval or until fully consumed, whichever comes first; single redemption, no re-entry after a prior redemption.
findings.gotchas: A card authorization charge hits your payment method within weeks of onboarding (a failed charge locks the account) — so unlike the free tiers, this program effectively requires a payment method. Downgrading before credits are consumed forfeits the balance and bars re-application. All program/billing notices go to the primary account email. No free Pro/Team plan for startups is offered anymore — value is credit-based only.

findings.name: GitHub Team free for verified academic faculty (education license)
findings.detail: Verified academic faculty can apply for GitHub Team free 'for teaching or academic research' — unlimited private repos and unlimited collaborators, per the discounted-plans docs. Team is a metered/usage-based plan, so faculty-driven codespaces on Team are usage-billed (no free core-hours included), making this more an IDE/CI license than a codespaces offer.
findings.eligibility: Verified academic faculty (school-affiliated accounts via GitHub Education); institutions/nonprofits route through the education/nonprofit portals.
findings.claim: Apply through the GitHub Education benefits/verification flow (linked from docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/discounted-plans); faculty Team grant is account-level, no CC required on the free grant itself.
findings.expiry: Tied to active academic status (school year / employment).
findings.gotchas: No codespaces core-hour allocation with the free Team grant — codespaces usage bills against usage-based billing; nonprofit/library variant is free Team or 25% off Enterprise Cloud via nonprofits.github.com.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes observed while verifying (as of 2026-10-22): (1) GitHub's 'Accelerate' marketing page (github.com/enterprise/accelerate) now 404s and github.com/accelerate is just an org profile — the startup program is now branded 'GitHub for Startups' and is credit-based ($10K/12 months) rather than the older free-Team-plan/accelerate structure; I could not re-read the pre-change Accelerate page, so historical free-Pro-for-founders details are not confirmed (low confidence on the prior shape). (2) Billing docs were restructured: docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/billing-plans-and-billing-limits-for-individuals and the old /billing/managing-billing-for-github-codespaces/pricing-for-codespaces URLs are 404; plan/usage data now lives under /en/billing/concepts/product-billing/* and /en/billing/reference/product-usage-included. (3) The product-usage-included table no longer lists a separate 'Free for students' row — students receive Pro-plan entitlements (180 core-hours/20 GB) instead, which is why student figures come from the Pro row. (4) Student Copilot benefit wording changed to 'unlimited completions + GitHub AI credits + limited chat/agent usage' (the pre-2025 '2,000 completions' framing is gone), and a new partner (Camber: 40 CPU hours, 5 GPU hours, 50 GB storage) joined the pack. No termination of the Free or student codespaces tiers was announced.

provider: Azure DevOps / Microsoft Azure (Dev Tools, IDEs, Git & CI/CD) — verified 2026-10-22

findings.name: Azure DevOps Basic plan (free tier, perpetual)
findings.detail: All facts read from https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/devops/ today. 'Stakeholders (Free)' tier: free read-only participants. 'Basic' plan: first 5 users free, then $6/user/month; 1 Microsoft-hosted CI/CD parallel job with 1,800 build minutes/month; 1 self-hosted parallel job with unlimited minutes; extra Microsoft-hosted parallel job $40/month; extra self-hosted parallel job $15/month (unlimited minutes); Azure Artifacts 2 GiB free per org, then $2/GiB (2-10), $1/GiB (10-100), $0.50/GiB (100-1k), $0.25/GiB (1k+); unlimited private Git repos; Azure Boards work-item tracking and Kanban included. 'Basic + Test plans' is $52/user/month with a 30-day free trial (adds test planning/tracking/execution, browser tests, UAT, centralized reporting). Visual Studio subscribers get free Azure DevOps access and don't count against the 5 free users; Azure DevOps Basic is included in GitHub Enterprise; 'Basic' also carries a 'free offer' from Individual Services.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no credit card required for the Basic plan; per-org free allowance. Region: no restriction stated on the pricing page.
findings.claim: Create an Azure/Microsoft account, go to dev.azure.com, create an organization: first 5 users + 1 MS-hosted job (1,800 min/mo) + 2GB artifacts activate automatically; buy extra users/jobs as needed. For Test plans, start the 30-day trial then $52/user/mo.
findings.expiry: No expiry; the Basic free allowance is perpetual and build minutes reset monthly. Paid Test-plan trial expires after 30 days.
findings.gotchas: 1,800 MS-hosted minutes do not roll over monthly; the free 2GB artifact cap is per organization; extra MS-hosted parallel jobs are $40/month (big jump); Basic + Test plans is $52/user/month after the 30-day trial; as of 2025-2026 the page adds GitHub-hosted Mac agents (per-minute, no parallel job) and 'GitHub AI Credits for Azure DevOps' (Copilot autofix, code review) billed per credit; 99.9% SLA applies to paid users only.

findings.name: Azure Free Account trial (new-customer credits + 12-month free services)
findings.detail: Read from https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/ today: $200 credit usable within 30 days for new customers, PLUS free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months (e.g., 750 hours each of B1s, B2pts v2 (Arm) and B2ats v2 (AMD) VMs; 750 hours PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server B1MS with 32 GB storage; Standard Container Registry 100 GB + 10 webhooks; 720 vCore-hours SQL Managed Instance), PLUS 65+ always-free services (Azure Functions 1M requests/mo; Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s provisioned + 25 GB; AKS cluster management free; Azure SQL 100,000 vCore-seconds + 32 GB serverless). This credit/always-free coverage spans Azure consumption services including Azure Pipelines/DevOps compute beyond the free 1,800-min Basic allowance.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only; limit of one free-services+$200-credit account per customer. Requires a phone number and a credit or non-prepaid debit card plus a Microsoft or GitHub account. Not available for sovereign clouds (US Government, Azure China, Azure Germany).
findings.claim: Sign up at azure.com/free with a Microsoft/GitHub account, pass phone verification, add a card (a temporary $1 authorization may appear and is reversed), then the $200 credit and free monthly service amounts are active; spend the credit on any eligible Azure service.
findings.expiry: $200 credit expires 30 days after signup; 12-month free amounts end after 12 months; then pay-as-you-go (no fee to keep the account; cancel anytime).
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (contrast with the student offer); account auto-converts to pay-as-you-go after credit expiry — any unused credit is lost; 65+ always-free services have per-service monthly caps (excess is billed); sovereign-cloud regions excluded; this is a trial-credit offer, not a perpetual free tier.

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit + education dev-tools licenses (Azure Dev Tools for Teaching)
findings.detail: Read from https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/ today: $100 Azure credit usable within 12 months for new Azure customers, plus 12 months of free monthly amounts of 20+ services and 65+ always-free services (free Azure DevOps for 5 users with unlimited private Git repos is in the always-free list). Bundled education licenses via the Azure Dev Tools for Teaching program, downloaded from the 'Azure Education Hub': Visual Studio (Agents, Code, Community, for Mac), SQL Server Developer and Standard, Windows Server, Visio Professional, Azure DevOps Server, R Client/R Server, Remote Tools for VS, System Center, Skype for Business Server. Also free student access to Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, AI Search, Content Safety, and 1,700+ foundation models.
findings.eligibility: Full-time university students only. Verification is via your school email (no separate .edu gate stated — school email is the eligibility check; out-of-school users are not covered). No credit card required. One account per person.
findings.claim: Sign up at azure.com/free/students using your school email (no card), verify, then the $100 credit + 12-month free amounts activate; download the dev-tools bundle from the Azure Education Hub in the portal.
findings.expiry: $100 credit valid 12 months; 12-month free amounts end at 12 months. Students can 'renew your subscription annually and continue to get free access to Azure as long as you're a student' (credit/renewal via school email while enrolled). After credit exhaustion, email notice and choice of pay-as-you-go (keeping free monthly tiers) or disable.
findings.gotchas: The $100 credit CANNOT be applied to Azure Marketplace offers; dev-tools bundle licenses are NFR (no redistribution); per the VS credit-eligibility doc, the 'Visual Studio Enterprise - Azure Dev Tools for Teaching' license does NOT carry a monthly Azure credit ($150/mo credits are for paid VS Enterprise; VS Community and VS Code are free to everyone anyway); some services/regions may still be unavailable depending on where Azure offers are commercial.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — up to $150,000 startup credits (single-entry, milestone-based, as of 2026)
findings.detail: Read from current official Learn docs (updated 2026-08-05 and 2026-10-09): single entry point at startups.microsoft.com. On signup you get $200 in 'Startup credits' immediately (investor-referral path: $1,000 immediately); then automatic milestone unlocks up to $150,000: Milestone 1 $200 = Azure signup + personal-Linkekin identity verify; M2 $5,000 = business verification (registered legal entity); M3 $25,000 = 5+ distinct Azure workloads in active use over ~60 days; M4 $50,000 = 7+ workloads ~60 days; M5 $150,000 = 10+ workloads plus ~$3,000/month Azure usage sustained ~60 days. The 60-day clock requires every counted workload to stay above $1 spend for all 60 days; milestones can be skipped (qualify directly for higher tiers). At the $25K milestone you get a one-time two-year extension to use your credits. Investor Network (VC/accelerator/university) 10-character referral codes unlock higher-tier benefits earlier and expanded/third-party perks. Credits cover eligible Azure consumption (incl. AKS and eligible Microsoft Foundry model usage); GitHub usage not covered out of the box. Other benefits: Azure AI/Foundry access, Microsoft Marketplace co-sell, dedicated program support; review within ~3 business days.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage B2B software/AI/tech startups: pre-seed through Series B funding; NOT Series C or later; privately held, for-profit; own your software (not licensed-in); HQ in a country/region where the program operates; fewer than $350,000 lifetime free Azure credits received; excluded: educational institutions, government, consultancies/agencies/dev shops, crypto mining. Applicant needs a personal consumer Microsoft account with no prior Azure account, personal (non-school/work-domain) email, phone, LinkedIn (personal account, identity verify), and payment/credit card info at Azure account creation (credit card IS required for the sponsored subscription).
findings.claim: Go to startups.microsoft.com (or the www.microsoft.com/en-us/startups landing 'Get started now'); sign in with a personal MS account; optionally enter your investor's 10-character referral code; complete the 3-step Azure account creation (profile/address/payment) to unlock $200 (or $1,000 on the investor path); application review ~3 business days; credits activate in the portal.
findings.expiry: Credits have program-defined durations (one-time 2-year extension at the $25K milestone); the sponsored subscription auto-converts to pay-as-you-go when credits are exhausted or expire. Existing activated credits from the old 2025 programs remained valid until they expired after the 2025-07-01 change.
findings.gotchas: Workload-count trap: any of the 5/7/10 workloads dropping below $1/month spend during the 60-day window resets that milestone; $150K requires ~$3K/month real spend anyway; lifetime $350K free-credit cap blocks repeat users; credits don't cover Marketplace, support plans, or GitHub (needs Azure linked as GitHub payment method); country/region chosen at signup can't be changed later and some countries are ineligible; personal email only — school/company domains rejected; LinkedIn personal account required (no business accounts).

sunset_notes: 2025-07-01: Microsoft retired the old "Founders Hub" tiers of Microsoft for Startups — the former up-to-$150,000-in-credits-plus-benefits program (Founders Hub levels 1-4: $1,000/$5,000/$25,000 Azure credits bundled with 50 M365 Business Premium seats, Dynamics 365 licenses, Power BI/Power Apps/Power Automate users, 20 GitHub Enterprise seats, 5 Visual Studio Enterprise seats, and third-party perks; up to $20K extras reported at level 4) — replacing it with a two-track model (investor-affiliated track starting at $100,000 in credits; self-serve track up to $5,000 total: $1,000 for 90 days + $4,000 for 180 days after business verification; no dedicated support on the self-serve track). Existing activated credits kept running until expiry (per The Register 2025-07-01 and Microsoft Q&A threads). 2026: the program was restructured again into the current single-entry "Microsoft for Startups": $200 starter credits ($1,000 with investor referral) and automatic milestone unlocks up to $150,000 based on workload adoption/usage (per current Learn docs, updated 2026-08/10, and the microsoft.com/en-us/startups page). No changes found to the Azure DevOps Basic free tier (1,800 MS-hosted minutes, 5 free users, 2GB artifacts still as of today's pricing page), though the pricing page now lists 2025-era additions: 'Basic + Test plans' at $52/user/month with 30-day trial, GitHub-hosted Mac agents (per-minute), and GitHub AI Credits for Azure DevOps. No changes found to Azure for Students ($100/12 months, no CC, school email) or the new-customer $200/30-day free account as of today's pages. Pegasus (invitation-only) was retained through the 2025 transition. The 'Pegasus' dedicated-CSA program survives; note the partner-network 'Founders Hub benefits guide' (partner.microsoft.com) still lists the old Level 1-4 credits table — treat that as a legacy page.

findings.name: Free plan (always-free tier)
findings.detail: $0 forever. Unlimited members, up to 2 teams, 250 active issues (unlimited archived issues), 10 MB file uploads per attachment, Google SSO, core issue tracking plus Agent platform and Linear Agent. This is the de-facto 'trial' for everyone — Linear runs no separate paid-plan trial; sign-up itself is free.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, worldwide, no account-age, funding or headcount limits. Sign up with email, Google or GitHub — credit card NOT required. No .edu needed.
findings.claim: 1. Go to linear.app and sign up (free). 2. Create workspace; you get 2 teams / 250 issues immediately. 3. Add unlimited teammates for free. No application, no approval.
findings.expiry: None published; free-plan limits (unlimited members, 2 teams, 250 issues, 10MB uploads) unchanged across every archived pricing page 2024-10-2026.
findings.gotchas: 250 active-issue cap (new issue creation blocks at cap, archived issues exempt); only 2 teams; 10MB upload cap; AI-credit-dependent features (Coding Sessions, Loops, agent automations) are metered separately on paid tiers — free tier has no paid AI features. Sales tax now applies in specific US states + DC (as of Jan 2026) on paid plans, not free.

findings.name: Startup program — up to 6 months free Business plan (partner referral only)
findings.detail: Startups affiliated with an official Linear partner (VC, accelerator or startup community; 500+ partners incl. a16z, Sequoia, Index, Techstars, Antler, Bessemer, 500 Global) get up to 6 months of free access to the Business plan (normally $16/user/mo annual). At redemption the account automatically renews at the standard rate unless you switch plans or cancel.
findings.eligibility: Must be affiliated with a partner (dedicated partner link/code). Hard cap: fewer than 50 employees AND non-paying Linear user (new paid customers only). No funding cap, company-age cap or revenue cap published. Bootstrapped/unaffiliated founders: NOT eligible — the page explicitly says only partner-affiliated companies can participate; >50 employees: contact sales instead.
findings.claim: 1. Find your investor/accelerator/community in the partner list on linear.app/startups (ask them to join if missing). 2. Ask the partner for their dedicated redemption link. 3. As workspace admin, follow the link or enter the partner code to redeem; offer applies to a new workspace. No codes to manage on the startup side.
findings.expiry: Program open-ended (no sunset date published); each grant lasts up to 6 months, then auto-renews at standard Business rate unless cancelled/switched.
