Older third-party listings mentioning 'Standard and Plus plans' are stale (2024 plan names) — current grant covers Basic or Business.
findings.gotchas: Referral-only: no self-service application and no bootstrapped path. 50-employee cap and 'non-paying users only' are the effective gates. Duration not precisely published per grant ('up to 6 months'). AI-credit-gated features (agent automations, Loops, Code Intelligence) may incur extra AI-credit charges on top of the free seats. After the free window, workspace drops to paying Business rate for all users, not just admins.

findings.name: Education program — students: 1 year free (100% off Basic or Business)
findings.detail: Full-time students at colleges/universities get 100% discount (free) on Basic ($10/user/mo annual) or Business ($16/user/mo annual) for ONE YEAR, for student-led programs, clubs and educational activities (non-commercial). No credit card required to claim (a $0 charge at checkout is mentioned by aggregators).
findings.eligibility: .edu email required to apply. Must be full-time; high schools, for-profit and online-only institutions excluded. Proof of full-time enrollment required — student IDs are NOT accepted (enrollment letter / proof of enrolled courses). Optionally attach proof of institutional accreditation to speed approval. Not for commercial/business use. No region limits published (non-.edu academic domains possible but undocumented — ask support).
findings.claim: 1. Create a Linear workspace (name it — needed for the application). 2. Email support@linear.app FROM your .edu address, including your workspace name and the email on the Linear account. 3. Attach proof of full-time enrollment (not a student ID) and optionally accreditation proof. 4. Wait for manual approval (no self-service portal); discount is then applied to Basic or Business.
findings.expiry: Free period = 1 year per grant. Renewal/re-verification rules NOT published — unclear if renewable; check the approval email.
findings.gotchas: Applies to Basic/Business only, NOT Enterprise. Covers student/educational use only — commercial side projects out of scope. Approval is at Linear's sole discretion and can change terms. If the workspace exceeds free-tier caps on any paid downgrade/cancellation, new issue creation blocks. Third-party value quotes ($120/yr Basic, $192/yr Business per seat at 2026 prices) reflect the post-Nov-2025 price hike.

findings.name: Education program — university staff: 75% off Basic/Business (ongoing)
findings.detail: Staff and employees at qualifying academic institutions (colleges and higher-level institutions) get a 75% discount on Basic and Business paid plans. Discount is ongoing per approval (no published end date, unlike the 1-year student grant).
findings.eligibility: .edu/school email + proof of employment at an eligible college or university. Same institutional exclusions as the student track (no high schools, for-profit or online-only institutions). At Linear's sole discretion.
findings.claim: Email support@linear.app from your institutional .edu address with workspace name, account email and proof of employment; optionally attach proof of your institution's accreditation. Discount applied on approval.
findings.expiry: No sunset published; discount runs with the subscription. Enterprise plan excluded (75% applies to Basic and Business only).
findings.gotchas: You still pay 25% of seat price (2026: $2.50/user/mo Basic, $4/user/mo Business equivalent). Excluded from discount: Enterprise tier and any AI-credit add-ons (metered separately).

findings.name: Non-profit program: 75% off Basic/Business
findings.detail: Registered non-profits get 75% off Basic and Business plans (not Enterprise). Apply via support@linear.app with proof of non-profit status; eligibility determined at Linear's sole discretion.
findings.eligibility: Standard 501(c)-style registered non-profit status proof. Explicitly EXCLUDED: legislative/political bodies, churches and religious groups, schools and colleges, government offices, opinion-influence groups, hospitals/health-insurance entities, and private foundations.
findings.claim: Email support@linear.app with proof of non-profit status (registration docs); discount applied on approval.
findings.expiry: No sunset published; runs with the subscription. 75% covers Basic/Business only.
findings.gotchas: Discretionary approval; a long list of org types is excluded even if formally non-profit; AI credits remain a separate metered cost.

findings.name: No standalone free trial / trial credits for paid plans
findings.detail: Linear offers no time-boxed trial of Basic/Business and no trial credits anywhere in 2025-2026. The free plan is the only always-free access; paid access comes via the partner-startup grant or the education/non-profit discounts above.
findings.eligibility: N/A — absence confirmed on pricing page, docs and startup page as of 2026-10-22.
findings.claim: Not claimable.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Don't confuse partner startup grants (up to 6 months free Business) with a general trial — they require partner affiliation. Anyone else paying gets Basic $10/user/mo annual (no published monthly-billing price) or Business $16/user/mo annual.

findings.name: Postman Free plan (free tier)
findings.detail: Official Free plan on postman.com/pricing (read 2026-10-22): 1 user; 1,000 API monitoring requests/month (per team); unlimited automated API testing via Collection Runner; Mock Servers (cloud and local) with no stated cap; 25 Automation Flows credits/month; Context Graph ingestion free (24h refresh) and 1,000 Context Graph queries/month then $0.01/query; up to 5 integrations; 10,000 calls/month to Postman's own platform API; collection recovery window 1 day; Postman-branded API docs. Not included on Free: RBAC, SSO, cloud performance testing, private NPM packages, SDK generation, custom domains, monitor reports, API Catalog, private runners. Card lists '100 AI credits' but the comparison table row 'Postman AI credits' shows '50 / month' for Free - a live discrepancy on the same page; known data (100 AI credits/mo) matches the plan card. Paid reference prices (annual billing): Solo $9/user/mo, Team $19/user/mo, Enterprise via sales.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone - individuals, students, startups; no .edu email, age, funding, or region requirement stated. Free account creation (email or SSO login) with no payment method on the page; credit card is not part of the free sign-up (official page does not say 'no credit card required' - medium confidence on that detail). Free desktop app + CLI: 'Download Postman | Get Started for Free', 'Create a free account and you are in.'
findings.claim: Go to postman.com/pricing -> 'Get Started'/'Sign Up for Free' to create a free account; the API client, CLI, and platform features at Free limits are immediately available. Download app at postman.com/downloads.
findings.expiry: Perpetual free tier; no trial clock or renewal. Free features stay until user adds a paid plan; downgrades keep the account usable at Free limits.
findings.gotchas: Only 1 user on Free (a free team workspace with collaborators requires a paid plan). The pricing page self-contradicts on AI credits (100 on plan card vs 50/month in the table) - verify before relying on 100. Usage-based charges can still hit a Free account: Context Graph overage $0.01/query beyond 1,000/month, and cloud perf testing / AI overage are paid features gated to paid plans. Basic and Professional plans are gone for new customers, so older student-startup offers built on those tiers no longer exist.

findings.name: Postman Academy (free education/certification platform)
findings.detail: academy.postman.com (read live 2026-10-22): 'Master APIs with Postman Academy' - free on-demand self-study learning modules and learning paths (e.g., API Testing Path v12, API Collaboration Best Practices), free live webinars ('Sign up for free, live sessions led by Postman trainers'), and course-completion badges/certifications. Stats shown: 150k+ learners, 250+ workshops, 95% satisfaction. Content can be filtered by persona and Postman license type. Enterprise training (private workshops, custom-branded academy, LMS reporting) is a paid/Enterprise offering, not part of the free offer.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone - no .edu email, region, or startup requirement stated; access via a free Postman account. No credit card required.
findings.claim: Sign in to Postman at academy.postman.com, pick a learning path or course, complete it; badges are issued automatically after course completion (now via Credly).
findings.expiry: Perpetual free access; no stated expiration. Badging migration: from 21 Jul 2026 badges move from Badgr to Credly; previously earned Badgr badges are NOT revoked; reissuance of old badges only on request to academy@postman.com.
findings.gotchas: Free tier is the self-study/live-webinar content; instructor-led private workshops and custom-branded academies are enterprise/commercial. Not a free Postman product license - it is free learning content. The 'new learning platform' LiftOff (postman.com/liftoff) is Postman's 2026 successor-style track alongside Academy.

findings.name: Postman LiftOff (free hands-on learning, new in 2026)
findings.detail: postman.com/liftoff (read live 2026-10-22): 'Interactive, hands-on learning modules with real-time API validation', 'Powered by Postman'. Currently 5 Learning Paths and 21 Modules; progress steps per module (e.g., '0/20 steps completed'); users can 'earn your rank'. Sign in with Discord to save progress; browse without signing in. No pricing, paid tier, or limits stated anywhere on the page - free.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone ('Start your API journey here'); no student/startup-specific targeting, no .edu or region requirement; Discord sign-in optional.
findings.claim: Browse paths at postman.com/liftoff, sign in with Discord to track progress, connect Postman when ready to validate against real APIs.
findings.expiry: No expiration stated; free with a Postman account.
findings.gotchas: No certifications or credentials issued on the LiftOff page itself (unlike Academy badges); small catalog so far (5 paths / 21 modules) - content is being built out. 'Real-time API validation' consumes runs against your Postman account limits (Free plan applies).

findings.expiry: No active program; old pages soft-404 to the app shell, /learn/education/ hard-404s.
findings.gotchas: Treat any third-party page or archive claiming a 'Postman for Students' free Professional license as outdated; Professional is not offered to new customers. If a school previously had an education license, it would be legacy Basic/Professional and is migrated to Team over time per Postman FAQ.

findings.name: Startup program / startup discount (not found)
findings.detail: No public 'Postman for Startups' program exists on official pages as of 2026-10-22: https://www.postman.com/startups/ returns 200 but serves the same generic app SPA shell as other nonexistent marketing routes; the pricing page and FAQ contain no startup discount, funding-cap, or company-age terms; the only 'trial' wording is 'Teams can trial Enterprise features to evaluate advanced collaboration, security, and governance before upgrading' (Enterprise evaluation via sales, not a public self-serve startup offer). findings.expiry: N/A.

findings.name: Docker Personal plan — $0 free tier for individual developers (incl. students)
findings.detail: Docker Personal is $0/user/mo with no stated time limit (self-serve at app.docker.com/signup). Includes: Docker Desktop (Engine + built-in Kubernetes, CLI, Compose), Docker Hub (unlimited public repos, 1 private repo, 100 image pulls/hr per authenticated user; 10 pulls/hr per IP unauthenticated), Docker Scout (1 Scout-enabled repo with continuous vulnerability analysis), Docker Debug, and 100 Testcontainers Cloud runtime minutes/month. Cap: 1 user. Free account gives 7-day trials of Docker Build Cloud and Testcontainers Cloud.
findings.eligibility: Open to any individual (no .edu email or student verification required). 'For individual developers who need the essential tools to build and deploy containers.' Does not cover company/team use except the small-company Desktop carve-out below. Government entities may not use Docker Desktop free without a subscription. No region limits or credit-card requirement stated on the official pages.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free Docker Personal account at https://app.docker.com/signup 2) Download Docker Desktop from desktop.docker.com (Windows/macOS/Linux installers) 3) Log in with the Personal account — Docker Hub/Scout/Debug entitlements apply automatically. No application, no .edu proof, no CC wording required.
findings.expiry: No expiry — permanent $0 tier; entitlements 'remain free but still subject to licensing terms' (Docker plans FAQ).
findings.gotchas: 1 user only; 100 pulls/hr and 1 private repo are tight for class-group work (unauthenticated 10 pulls/hr/IP). Personal excludes Docker Pro extras (synchronized file shares, 2 Scout repos, unlimited Hub pulls, 100 Testcontainers min are the Personal/Pro boundary). If your company grows past the small-startup carve-out you must buy Team ($16/user/mo monthly, $15 annualized, up to 100 users) or Business ($24). Trial vs free: Build Cloud and Testcontainers Cloud are 7-day trials on Personal; only the 100 Testcontainers runtime minutes/month are permanently included.

findings.name: Docker Desktop free for early-stage startups (<250 employees AND <$10M revenue)
findings.detail: Per the Docker plans FAQ: 'For small companies with fewer than 250 employees AND less than $10M in revenue, Docker will continue to offer free usage of Docker Desktop only' — for (i) non-commercial open source projects and/or (ii) commercial use with <250 employees and <US$10,000,000 (or local-currency equivalent) annual revenue. This is a carve-out on top of the $0 Personal plan: the tool is free; the account entitlements are still the Personal ones.
findings.eligibility: Startup/company with <250 employees and <$10M USD (or equivalent local currency) annual revenue. Government entities excluded. No formal application, funding cap, or age cap stated — the caps are employee count and revenue. No region limits stated.
findings.claim: No claim step beyond normal use: sign up at app.docker.com, install Docker Desktop (desktop.docker.com), and use it under the small-company terms. Self-declaration; keep company size/revenue under the caps and you remain free for Docker Desktop.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry; the carve-out 'will continue' per the current FAQ. It is revocable — crossing either cap means Docker Desktop is no longer free and a paid subscription (Team/Business) is required.
findings.gotchas: 'Docker Desktop only': no free entitlements for paid Hub features, Testcontainers Cloud minutes, Build Cloud, or support SLAs — the startup team still gets Personal-tier limits (100 pulls/hr/user, 1 private repo, 1 Scout repo). The 250-employee / $10M-revenue test can be outgrown mid-year with no grace period stated. Team plan starts at $16/user/mo once you exceed the carve-out.

findings.name: 7-day free trials: Docker Build Cloud and Testcontainers Cloud (via free Personal account)
findings.detail: Docker plans FAQ: 'Docker Personal users who want to start or continue using Docker Build Cloud may trial the service for seven days' and 'Docker Personal users may also trial Testcontainers Cloud for 7 days.' Without a paid subscription, a free Personal account gives the trial. Testcontainers Cloud is bundled into paid tiers (Pro 100 min/mo, Team 500, Business 1500 runtime minutes; overage buy-more at $3 per 100 min prepaid or $4 per 100 min on-demand). Open-source Testcontainers libraries (Java, Go, .NET, Node.js, Python, Rust, Ruby, PHP, etc.) remain free and open source.
findings.eligibility: Any individual with a free Docker Personal account (no .edu needed, no company requirement). No region limits stated.
findings.claim: 1) Free Personal account at app.docker.com/signup 2) Sign up for Testcontainers Cloud trial at https://app.testcontainers.cloud/signup (or the in-product trial path) 3) Trial Build Cloud from Docker Desktop. 7-day windows; no stated duration limits beyond the 7 days.
findings.expiry: Trials last 7 days. No stated credit-card requirement on the official pages fetched (not mentioned).
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: only 100 Testcontainers Cloud runtime minutes/month are permanently included in Personal; the 7-day trial unlocks full service access, not the 100-min allotment. After trial, extra minutes cost $3-4/100 min. CI runs also consume runtime minutes — test-parallelism can burn minutes fast.

findings.name: Docker Hardened Images (DHI) Community tier — free for every developer
findings.detail: Docker pricing page lists DHI 'Community' at $0: 'Free for every developer' — hardened minimal container images, near-zero CVEs, verifiable SBOMs, Apache 2.0 catalog. Paid tiers: DHI Select from $5,000 per repo (FIPS/STIG variants, critical-CVE fixes <7 days, up to 5 customizations) and DHI Enterprise (contact sales, unlimited customizations, +5-yr ELS updates). A 'Start Free Trial' CTA points to /products/hardened-images#getstarted.
findings.eligibility: Any developer/student/startup — no eligibility test, no .edu required, no CC requirement stated. 'Secure, transparent, and no-cost for everyone.'
findings.claim: Pull DHI Community images from the Docker catalog, or start the DHI free trial via the 'Start Free Trial' link on the Hardened Images product page. No application.
findings.expiry: Community tier has no stated expiry. Trial of paid DHI has no stated duration on the pricing page.
findings.gotchas: Free tier is only the hardened image catalog (supply-chain tooling for the images themselves); it does not include Scout repo analysis beyond Personal's 1 repo, or the Select/Enterprise CVE-fix SLAs ($5k/repo).

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, Docker has NO active student-specific program, education license, or startup program on its site. (1) 'Docker for Student Developers' (historically the .edu-verified student program, applied via docker.com/dsdev) now 404s and is not linked anywhere on docker.com — it appears sunseted/removed; the 404s are observed today, but no official end date was found (medium confidence it is dead, low confidence on when it ended). (2) The Y Combinator startup partnership (docker.com/ycombinator and /partners/y-combinator both 404 today) is not listed on the current /partners/ page, which now lists only Channel, Alliance, Extension, and Docker Trusted Content programs — so Docker's YC/startup deal is not publicly available (medium confidence). (3) Legacy 'Free Team' tier (up to 3 seats, 100 pulls/hr/user, no Build Cloud/Testcontainers Cloud) is referenced in the pricing FAQ with an upgrade path dated Dec 10, 2024; the current Personal plan is a 1-user $0 tier. (4) No trial credits in dollars, no funded startup accelerator benefits, and no classroom/educator license exist; Docker's free 'education' is limited to self-guided docs learning paths and free YouTube content (the LinkedIn Learning Docker Foundations Professional Certificate requires a paid LinkedIn subscription). Note: WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so 2025-2026 change verification relied on official docker.com and testcontainers.com pages fetched today; confidence in sunset claims is therefore capped at medium.

findings.claim: Sign up at retool.com; the Free plan is applied automatically with no card entry. Keep the org on the Free plan (up to 5 users) and use 500 runs / 20 agent-hours / 250 AI credits per month at no cost.
findings.detail: Permanently free plan, $0/mo. Unlimited web & mobile apps; up to 5 users; 500 workflow runs/month; 5GB data storage; up to 20 agent-hours/month plus 250 AI credits/month. AI credits are account-level and monthly with no rollover; bonus credits 'may change over time'; agent execution pauses when free agent-hours are exhausted. Page states no credit-card requirement and no time-limited trial; this is a standing tier, not a trial. No region limits stated on the page.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no .edu, no funding-stage, no region limit stated. Credit card NOT required for the Free plan.
findings.expiry: No expiry; renews indefinitely at $0 while the org stays on the Free plan.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: none — this is a free tier, not a trial. Agents bill by the hour separately from the AI-credit pool and pause at 20 h/mo. Free plan lacks Team/Business features (public apps, release versions, staging, granular permissions). AI-credit allowances (20 agent-hrs + 250 credits) are a recent 2025-era addition to the Free tier, not a legacy free-tier value.
findings.name: Retool Free plan (cloud)

findings.claim: Install the Retool self-hosted edition (builds from retool.com; Free license, no card); self-hosting is opt-in on any plan tier — no claim form needed.
findings.detail: All four tiers (Free, Team, Business, Enterprise) support self-hosting. Free self-hosted keeps the 5-user cap and adds 'unlimited database management' on top of the cloud-free limits. Team/Business self-host cap at up to 100 users; Enterprise self-host adds multi-instance deployments and bring-your-own-PostgreSQL. You run and operate your own infrastructure (no cloud hosting; agent-hour/AI-credit entitlements are not documented for self-hosted Free).
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no card, no .edu, no region limit stated. Requires your own Postgres/infrastructure.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry; the Free tier is standing.
findings.gotchas: Data/egress costs are yours: infrastructure, hosting, maintenance. The 5-user cap applies even when self-hosted (matches the cloud Free tier). Feature parity for Agents/AI on self-hosted Free is not stated on the pricing page.
findings.name: Retool self-hosted Free edition

findings.claim: Steps: (1) create a free Retool org; (2) upgrade to the monthly Team or Business plan via plans & billing — card info required but not billed immediately; (3) submit the Startup Program application (HubSpot form linked in the docs and at retool.com/startups); (4) acceptance email; the 100% discount auto-applies to the first invoice at end of first billing cycle. No reply after a week: email startups@retool.com.
findings.detail: Year 1: 100% off coupon for one year on a monthly Team or Business plan, value up to $60,000. Year 2: 25% off coupon on the paid plan. Year-1 Agents: up to 50 hours / $125 of free usage per month; Year 2: up to 20 hours / $50 per month; usage beyond that is billed out-of-pocket (year 2 with the 25% coupon applied). VCs/accelerators/incubators can add Retool to their deal books via the partner channel.
findings.eligibility: All of: bootstrapped, angel-funded, debt-funded, pre-seed, seed, or Series A; total funding raised under $10M; founded within the last 10 years; new Retool customer on a MONTHLY Team or Business plan (no annual plans, no Enterprise). Excluded: customers already on a paid plan for multiple billing cycles, and any org previously enrolled (one-time only, no re-application). No region limit stated.
findings.expiry: 100% discount lasts exactly 1 year from approval date, then 25% off in year 2, then full price (graduates). No extensions are granted. If nothing changes, Retool automatically continues the current plan and charges the card on file. Downgrade to the Free plan at any time via plans & billing.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required at signup for the paid plan (though not billed immediately and invoices are $0 under the 100% off). Monthly-only program — annual contracts and Enterprise are ineligible. Overage Agents usage charges out-of-pocket. Card on file is charged at discount expiry if you stay on the plan.
findings.name: Retool for Startups program (100% off year 1, up to $60k value)

findings.claim: Steps: (1) create a free Retool organization using your education email; (2) submit the Education Program application (Typeform linked from the Discount Programs docs page) with the same education email; (3) on acceptance, upgrade to a monthly Team or Business plan via plans & billing. Applications are typically processed in under a week.
findings.detail: 100% off discount for any MONTHLY Team or Business plan — i.e., free Business-tier access for the duration of eligibility (third-party aggregators such as StudentPerks quote ~$120/yr value; official docs give no dollar cap). No agent-hour/AI-credit add-ons are specified for this program. No stated region limits; an education email is the eligibility signal. Exclusions: admin/back-office/operational staff at educational institutions, former students/educators who merely retained a .edu, edtech companies and education-adjacent service providers.
findings.eligibility: Current students or individual educators; education (e.g., .edu) email address required. One program per org (if accepted to another discount program, you cannot apply to this one).
findings.expiry: Runs for the duration of student/educator status. When you graduate or lose eligibility, 'you'll be notified by our team and given a timeline for exiting the program' — no automatic downgrade/charge-off terms are spelled out.
findings.gotchas: Standard card-on-file billing applies when you subscribe to the plan; if the discount fails to apply (multiple accounts or currency mismatch between account and credits), the card may still be charged — contact support. Monthly Team/Business only (no annual, no Enterprise). Former students with a lingering .edu are NOT eligible.
findings.name: Retool Education program (free Team/Business for students & educators)

findings.name: Tally Free plan (unlimited forms & submissions)
findings.detail: Free tier with no hard numeric cap: unlimited forms, unlimited submissions, conditional logic, calculations, signatures, payment collection (Stripe), file uploads (10 MB per-file limit on free), custom Thank You page, redirect, password protection, 45+ languages, and integrations incl. Google Sheets, Notion, Airtable, Zapier, Make, Slack, Discord, n8n, Linear, Webhooks, API and MCP access. All subject to the fair-use policy. Paid tiers: Pro €20/mo (≈$29/mo, or $24 annual-equivalent; annual = 2 months off / 17% off) for branding removal, custom domains, unlimited team seats, partial submissions, custom CSS, respondent emails, analytics; Business €65/mo (≈$89/mo) adds data-retention controls, email verification, 90-day version history. Billing currency USD or EUR based on IP. No region limits stated; data hosted in the EU (Belgium-based, GDPR).
findings.eligibility: Everyone: any user, individual, student or startup. No .edu email, no age/funding criteria, no signup barrier noted for basic use; no credit card required for the free plan (credit card is only used when upgrading to Pro/Business, billed upfront).
findings.claim: Go to tally.so, create an account or start a form directly (no signup required for basic form creation); free features are on by default. Paid upgrade is via sidebar 'Upgrade plan' with a (prepaid) credit card. Fair-use overage: Tally contacts you to build a custom plan with quarterly invoicing; if you decline, they give transition time to migrate.
findings.expiry: No expiry, no duration, no renewal — perpetual free tier with fair-use guardrails. Fair-use 'extensive usage' reference thresholds (Tally says they will contact you if consistently exceeded for 3-4 straight months): 50,000 submissions/month; 100 GB/month or 500 GB total file-upload storage; 50,000 email notifications/month. Paid subscriptions auto-renew monthly/yearly; cancel anytime via Settings → Billing, access continues to end of prepaid period; no refunds for unused time.
findings.gotchas: Free is 'unlimited' only within fair use — the thresholds above are the de-facto cap and overage triggers a paid custom plan (quarterly invoice), not an immediate paywall. 10 MB/file upload limit on free (unlimited uploads only on Pro). Removing Tally branding, custom domains, team seats/workspaces, partial submissions, GA/Meta Pixel, and 30/90-day version history all require paid plans. Pro/Business subscriptions may not be shared outside the registered organization (suspension risk). Trial-vs-free: Tally explicitly does NOT offer free trials of paid plans — the free plan itself is the always-free base, so there is no trial-conversion trap, but there is also no free trial of Pro. Payment failures on education/nonprofit discounts permanently block reactivation of the discount.

findings.name: Tally for education (student/educator Pro discount)
findings.detail: 30% off Tally Pro for 1 year, for a student or educator in a structured classroom. Exact prices: monthly $29 → $20; yearly $290 → $203. Eligible settings: high schools, universities, post-graduate institutions, trade schools, colleges, online bootcamps, design and coding academies (virtual or in-person). This is a discount, not a free license — there is no fully free education plan.
findings.eligibility: Students or educators in structured classroom programs (as listed above). No .edu email requirement stated on the page; no funding/age criteria. Discounts are for NEW customers only — existing or previously terminated Pro subscribers are excluded.
findings.claim: Open https://tally.so/help/tally-for-education and use the 'Apply here' link on the page (application/approval flow; no public email address or exact form fields documented). Discount applies to Tally Pro purchase only.
findings.expiry: Discount lasts 1 year and is explicitly non-renewable: 'Discounts cannot be renewed and are only applicable to new customers.' Discounts cannot be reactivated after failed payments. No sunset date stated.
findings.gotchas: Not free: it cuts Pro from $29 to $20/mo, so you still pay. New customers only — no stacking on existing plans. Single-use: the 30% rate ends permanently after 12 months. If the first payment fails, the discount is void and cannot be reactivated. No .edu verification method is documented, so approval likely happens via the application flow.

findings.name: No free trials or startup program at Tally (explicit absence)
findings.detail: Tally's billing help page answers 'Do you offer free trials?' with: "We don't offer free trials but are happy to answer any questions about Tally Pro or Tally Business." Their stated philosophy (help/plans-and-pricing): instead of traditional discounts, Tally focuses on giving ~99% of features free and keeping Pro/Business cheap; the only discount programs on the site are 'Tally for education' and 'Tally for non-profit'. No startup program, trial credits, or startup-age/funding-cap offer was found on any official Tally page.
findings.eligibility: n/a — absence of offer. Non-profit (separate, not startup) gets a permanent 30% Pro discount ($29→$20/mo, $290→$203/yr), new customers only, via https://tally.so/help/tally-for-non-profit.
findings.claim: n/a. For any startup-specific deal, Tally's stated path is contacting support (hello@tally.so / contact form).
findings.expiry: n/a.
findings.gotchas: Startups simply use the same free plan as everyone else; there is no startup-tier lock-in or trial credit to claim. Third-party listings (G2, TrustRadius, formbricks/formbuilder blogs) disagree on Pro/Business prices ($29/$89 'per user' vs $24/$74 flat vs €20/€65) — trust tally.so/pricing (flat team-wide price, currency by IP), not review-site widgets.

sunset_notes: No Tally free offer was sunset or materially changed in 2025-2026 per official pages read 2026-10-22: the free tier (unlimited forms/submissions under fair use), the 1-year 30% education discount, and the permanent 30% non-profit discount are all live, and Tally still explicitly offers no free trials. Pricing pages now display EUR (Pro €20, Business €65) with USD shown as $29/$89; annual billing gives 2 months off (17%). Only caveat: third-party review sites publish stale or per-user pricing (e.g., TrustRadius lists Pro/Business as per-user) that contradicts Tally's flat team-wide pricing. Note: WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-research; findings are based on direct WebFetch of official Tally pages (pricing, fair-use-policy, plans-and-pricing, tally-for-education, tally-for-non-profit, billing-and-payment-info) plus search snippets captured earlier, so official-source confidence is high.

findings.name: Kaggle Notebooks free GPU weekly quota (30 h/week, P100 or T4)
findings.detail: Official docs state Kaggle 'provides free access to NVIDIA TESLA P100 GPUs' and that the GPU quota 'resets weekly and is 30 hours or sometimes higher depending on demand and resources'. T4s (16 GB) were added as a GPU option alongside P100 in the 2023 notebooks update ('New GPU (T4s) options & more CPU RAM'). V100/A100 are not in the free pool. No credit card required; a free account suffices. Quota resets weekly (community tracking: Friday/Saturday midnight CET); the float above 30 h is not predictable. Interactive sessions have a 60-minute idle timeout (confirmed on the official GPU-usage tips page); batch (commit) sessions may run longer.
findings.eligibility: Any free Kaggle account (email/Google/Facebook sign-up). No .edu requirement, no CC. Phone verification (one-time SMS/voice call) gates accelerator access per secondary sources (medium confidence). Some regions have historically had restricted/intermittent accelerator availability (e.g., prior EU/UK data-sovereignty restrictions; exact 2026 state unverified — low confidence).
findings.claim: Sign up at kaggle.com -> create/open a notebook -> Settings tab -> Accelerator dropdown -> select 'GPU' (or 'GPU T4') -> session runs against the 30 h/week pool; remaining hours shown in notebook sidebar / kaggle.com/notebooks / settings. No claim steps needed — quota is automatic on every account.
findings.expiry: Quota never expires; resets weekly (historically Sat 00:00 UTC / Fri midnight CET). Per-session: 60 min idle timeout for interactive sessions.
findings.gotchas: Quota counts session wall-time with accelerator attached, not actual GPU utilization — a T4 session parked open burns hours. Quota 'sometimes higher' is not in advance and can differ by region/demand. Phone verification required to enable accelerator. Free storage: ~20 GB notebook temp + 200 GB user datasets (secondary source, medium confidence).

findings.name: Kaggle Notebooks free TPU weekly quota (~20 h/week, v2/v3 8-core)
findings.detail: Kaggle offers free 8-core TPU access (TPU v2/v3 '8' nodes; v5e/v5lite available on request but intermittent). Widely documented quota is 20 TPU hours/week for TPUs, with a 9-hour max per session (task's known-so-far figure matches this). The TPU docs page at kaggle.com/docs/tpus 404'd during this check, so the 20 h figure is from pre-2026 documentation/secondary sources rather than a re-verified official page — treat as medium confidence and re-verify in-browser.
findings.eligibility: Any free Kaggle account; TPU access (especially v5e/v5lite) may need an email request to Kaggle support; availability is intermittent and region-dependent. No credit card.
findings.claim: Notebook -> Settings -> Accelerator dropdown -> 'TPU v2/v3 8-core' (or request v5e/v5lite). 20 h/week pool shared across notebook sessions; check remaining hours in settings/usage panel.
findings.expiry: Resets weekly with GPU quota; 9 h max per TPU session.
findings.gotchas: Quota is shared per-week with no carryover; 9 h session cap is shorter than some GPU batch sessions; TPU pool availability fluctuates — your run can be queued or no-accelerator if pool is full; idle timeout still applies to interactive sessions.

findings.name: Kaggle free CPU notebook time (~60 h/week)
findings.detail: Notebooks also give a free weekly CPU allowance, commonly documented at 60 hours/week for 2-core / 13 GB RAM / 20 GB temp storage runs (secondary figure, not re-verified on an official page today — medium confidence). No CC required.
findings.eligibility: All free accounts; no phone verification typically needed for CPU-only sessions.
findings.claim: Automatic on any account; select 'None' accelerator in notebook Settings.
findings.expiry: Resets weekly with the other pools.
findings.gotchas: CPU hours are tracked separately from GPU/TPU; 60 h figure has varied historically — verify in the in-app usage panel.

findings.name: No separate Kaggle student or startup free-offer
findings.detail: Kaggle does not run a distinct free student program, .edu-verified education license, or startup credit program for notebooks compute. Students and startups get the identical free Notebook quotas described above by virtue of a free account; Kaggle's education offering (courses, micro-credentials) is a separate thing and does not change compute quotas. If a startup-program search intended 'Kaggle startup credits', no such official program was found as of this check.
findings.eligibility: n/a — no distinct offer to claim.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; sign up free and use the general free quotas.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse Kaggle with GitHub Student Pack-style programs; Kaggle has no age/funding-cap or .edu-gating for compute access.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes/notes: (1) The historical 'floating quota' era (2020–2021, 36–43 h/week) settled back to a stated 30 h floor 'or sometimes higher depending on demand' — the current official docs still use that floating-quota language. (2) T4s and larger CPU/RAM options were added in the 2023 notebooks update; the accelerator menu now offers P100 and T4. (3) No material 2025–2026 changes to the 30 h GPU / 20 h TPU quotas were verifiable in this check: search budget was exhausted mid-check (200-call shared limit), kaggle.com/docs/tpus returned 404, and several Kaggle pages render client-side so WebFetch saw only titles — TPU and CPU figures above are therefore medium confidence and should be re-verified in a browser at kaggle.com/docs/notebooks. (4) Secondary 2026-04 sources (yangmao.ai, aifree.dev) still describe Kaggle at 30 GPU h/week (T4 x2 or P100), 9 h session cap, phone-verification gating accelerators — consistent with the official page, no sunset found. (5) V100/A100 free access was never part of the standard pool and no paid 'Kaggle quota boost' for free users exists; paid accelerator access is only via competition/enterprise deals.

findings.name: Self-hosted open-source Gitea (free tier)
findings.detail: The core Gitea release is open source under the MIT license and is free to run: 'Full control, unlimited users and repositories.' Bundles code hosting, issue tracking, pull requests, project management, Gitea Actions (GitHub-Actions-compatible CI/CD), and a package registry. Free features listed on the pricing page: code hosting, issue tracking, PRs, project management, Gitea Actions, packages, rapid updates, active contributions, community support. No repo/user/storage cap is published — you are limited only by your own infrastructure. This is the primary free path for students and startups: replace paid GitLab/GitHub tiers at $0 license cost.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone: individuals, students, startups, and companies. No .edu email, startup-age or funding cap, and no credit card required. You must supply your own host (VPS/bare metal/K8s) and bear your own compute/data/egress costs.
findings.claim: No application needed. Download the free binary or Docker image (gitea.com products page / github.com/gitea) and install on your own Linux/Windows server or VPS; configure a DB (SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL). Unlimited users/repos forever. Enterprise extras (SAML SSO, audit logs, K8s autoscaling runners, SLA support) are NOT in the OSS build.
findings.expiry: None — perpetual MIT license, no sunset date.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: this is a genuinely free, permanent license (not a trial). Self-hosted = you pay your cloud provider for CPU/egress; Gitea's license is free but the box is not. No managed CI runners are provided — OSS Gitea Actions requires you to run your own runners. Enterprise-only features absent; support is community-only.

findings.name: gitea.com — free first-party hosted Gitea instance
findings.detail: Gitea operates gitea.com, a free public first-party Gitea instance: anyone can register a free account and host repositories on Gitea's own infrastructure at no charge. The sign-up form (gitea.com/user/sign_up) has only username/email/password plus OAuth (GitHub/GitLab/Google/OpenID) — no credit card or payment field. It is described as a 'free public first-party instance' hosting public repos (59 public repos on the Gitea org). No repo/storage cap is published on the page.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone (individuals, students, startups). No .edu requirement, no startup/funding cap, no credit card required. Free to register.
findings.claim: Register at gitea.com/user/sign_up, then create repos/projects. Hosts Gitea.org's own public open-source code (gitea/gitea, runner, tea CLI, etc.).
findings.expiry: Ongoing free service, subject to Gitea's terms; no published sunset date.
findings.gotchas: Free CI runners are NOT available on gitea.com (as of Nov 2025, maintainers confirmed there are no free managed runners; Gitea Actions needs a self-hosted runner or paid Gitea Cloud managed runners). The gitea.com root now 303-redirects to about.gitea.com (marketing); use gitea.com/<org>/<repo> for actual hosting. Exact repo/storage caps and private-repo policy are not published — treat as a public/mirror-friendly instance, not a guaranteed production private-code host. Source on no-free-runners: https://forum.gitea.com/t/how-to-make-gitea-actions-work-on-gitea-com/11793

findings.name: Gitea Cloud — 30-day free trial (managed Git hosting)
findings.detail: Gitea Cloud is a fully managed, dedicated, single-tenant Gitea instance where you choose provider and region (incl. Frankfurt EU for data residency). A 30-day free trial is offered ('Start your 30-day free trial'); after it ends, it becomes pay-as-you-go (no permanent free hosted tier). Managed Gitea Actions CI/CD runners are included automatically. Unlimited network traffic: incoming traffic is free & unlimited; once the high-speed egress quota is hit, a speed cap applies only to outgoing traffic. A recurring 50% discount is available on most plans (Extra/Max/Ultra unlimited-user tiers excluded). Instances provision in ~2 minutes; public repos can allow anonymous access; 2FA supported.
findings.eligibility: Open to individual developers, startups, and enterprises — no .edu requirement and no dedicated startup program. No published funding/age cap. Payment is pay-as-you-go after the trial (credit card likely required at checkout; the 30-day trial itself is advertised without a stated CC requirement — not confirmed on the pages read).
findings.claim: Go to cloud.gitea.com/signup → 'Start your 30-day free trial' → choose provider/region and a plan (S/M/L or Extra/Max/Ultra) → provision → use fully managed Gitea for 30 days → pay-as-you-go thereafter (apply the 50% discount where offered).
findings.expiry: Trial lasts 30 days, then pay-as-you-go. No published free-tier renewal; the 30-day trial is one-time.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a permanent free tier — costs begin after 30 days (pay-as-you-go; add-on object storage is extra). Egress: high-speed quota then speed-capped outgoing (incoming free). 50% discount does not cover Extra/Max/Ultra tiers. Exact $/month per plan tier and the CC-required policy for the trial are not published in the pages read (Cloud site is an SPA). No free managed CI runners outside the trial.

findings.name: Gitea Enterprise — 30-day free trial (self-hosted enhanced edition)
findings.detail: Gitea Enterprise is the enhanced, closed-source edition (SAML SSO, audit logs, Kubernetes AutoScaling Runners, mandatory 2FA, IP allowlist, enterprise themes, priority SLA support, installation/upgrade assistant, emergency remote support). A 30-day free trial is offered via the customers portal with full Enterprise features. List price is $19/user/month, with a recurring 50% discount shown as $9.50/user/month; a 1-year commitment is required with online payment. Licenses are user-count based and can be resized at any time; after a trial you can keep paying or revert to open-source Gitea (fully data/config compatible).
findings.eligibility: For companies/enterprises (and 'small companies' — discounts available for non-profits and small companies; FAQ notes discounted or even free quotes for education/non-profit on request). Not a dedicated free startup program. No .edu requirement for the trial itself; paid tier needs online payment (credit card) with a 1-year commitment.
findings.claim: Go to customers.gitea.com → sign in with an organization account → 'Request Trial' → specify desired user count → a 30-day trial license is auto-issued → download license.key → in Gitea Enterprise admin: Site Administration → Enterprise License → Upload License. During the trial all Enterprise functions are free.
findings.expiry: Trial = 30 days. Paid licenses run for the committed term (typically 1 year, resizable), renewable; if unpaid after trial the instance falls back to open-source Gitea behavior (no data loss).
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-paid: free only for 30 days, then $19/user/month list ($9.50 with the 50% recurring discount) on a 1-year commitment. Exceeding the user count just blocks new sign-ups (resize for free). Resale of Gitea Enterprise is prohibited. Non-profit/small-company discounts and even free quotes require contacting Gitea — they are not self-serve.

findings.name: Gitea Education Program — free 12-month Gitea Enterprise license (institutions)
findings.detail: Eligible non-profit K-12 and higher-education institutions receive a no-cost Gitea Enterprise license for 12 months, self-hosted, with community technical support only (no commercial support / no SLA). Renewable annually after an eligibility review. Covers coursework, labs, capstones, student group projects, non-commercial academic research, and internal school collaboration tied to the academic mission.
findings.eligibility: Institution-level, NOT individual students. Eligible: non-profit K-12 schools, colleges, and universities officially recognized/authorized/accredited/licensed or otherwise approved by the relevant education authority. Applications must come from full-time faculty/staff using an institutional email. Excluded: for-profit training firms, commercial bootcamps, private coaching, unrecognized/unaccredited organizations, and requests from students, alumni, or external consultants. Use is limited to academic/non-commercial — no commercial software delivery, paid hosting, or revenue-generating services. A .edu address is not strictly required, but an institutional email from a recognized non-profit institution is; proof of recognition/accreditation is required.
findings.claim: Apply via the contact form at about.gitea.com/contact/form/?program=education. Provide: institution name/website/country, a link or document showing education-authority recognition/accreditation, non-profit confirmation, applicant name/role/institutional email, expected user count + short usage summary, and acknowledgement that only community support is included. Every request is manually reviewed; on approval you get a tailored 12-month Enterprise license.
findings.expiry: 12 months, renewable annually after re-confirming eligibility and usage scope. Notify Gitea if eligibility or usage changes.
findings.gotchas: Students cannot apply directly — they benefit only via their school's license. Community support only (no commercial/SLA support). Non-commercial academic use only; commercial/resale/revenue use is prohibited and could void the license. No fixed seat count — scoped to the institution's expected users.

sunset_notes: try.gitea.io — the free hosted "try" instance listed in the known-so-far notes — no longer resolves (DNS getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND on two attempts as of 2026-10-22), indicating it has been retired or repurposed; no current official page or terms could be found. Treat it as defunct. gitea.com's root domain now 303-redirects to about.gitea.com (marketing site); the free first-party public instance still serves orgs/repos under gitea.com/<org>/<repo>, but gitea.com no longer offers free managed CI runners (confirmed by a Gitea maintainer on the forum, Nov 2025 — Gitea Actions on gitea.com needs a self-hosted runner or paid Gitea Cloud managed runners). No dedicated Gitea startup program with free credits exists as of 2026-10-22 (startups' free path = self-hosted OSS Gitea + the Gitea Cloud 30-day trial). Recurring 2024→2026 changes still in effect: Gitea Cloud added a Frankfurt (EU) region, add-on object storage, unlimited network traffic (incoming free, outgoing speed-capped past a high-speed quota), and a 50% recurring discount on most plans; Enterprise lists at $19/user/month with a 50% discount to $9.50/user/month on a 1-year commitment. The Education Program (free 12-month Enterprise license for non-profit institutions) is current and live on about.gitea.com/education. Note: WebSearch budget was exhausted, so verification relied on WebFetch of official Gitea pages (about.gitea.com products/pricing/education, gitea.com, docs.gitea.com/enterprise, cloud.gitea.com) plus one forum confirmation.

findings.name: ZeroGPU free GPU inference (Spaces)
findings.detail: Shared NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs allocated on demand to Gradio Spaces. 'large' = half card, 48GB VRAM (1x quota); 'xlarge' = full card, 96GB VRAM (2x quota). Daily GPU quotas: unauthenticated 2 min; free account 5 min; PRO/Team 40 min; Enterprise 60 min; paid plans can extend via pre-paid credits at $1/10 min. Quota resets exactly 24h after first daily GPU use. No credit card required for the free tier; no stated regional limits. Free accounts host max 2 ZeroGPU Spaces (PRO: 10; orgs: 50). Gradio SDK only; @spaces.GPU decorator, default 60s function runtime (extendable via duration=...); no torch.compile (use PyTorch AOT, torch 2.8+).
findings.eligibility: Any free HF account in good standing: verified email address and account older than 30 days. No .edu required, no startup status, no credit card, no stated region limits. Using (visiting) existing ZeroGPU Spaces is free for everyone, even unauthenticated (2 min/day).
findings.claim: Sign up at huggingface.co (free), verify email; create a Gradio Space and select ZeroGPU hardware in Space Settings (free accounts: up to 2 such Spaces, allowed only after account is 30+ days old); import spaces and decorate GPU functions with @spaces.GPU (default size large; size='xlarge' for 96GB at 2x quota cost); deploy and use within the 5 min/day free quota.
findings.expiry: Quota renews daily (resets 24h after first use). Hosting cap (2 ZeroGPU Spaces) persists while account stays in good standing; no sunset date published for the program.
findings.gotchas: Gradio-only (Docker/static cannot use ZeroGPU); xlarge doubles quota consumption and queue wait; free tier cannot buy quota extension ($1/10-min credits only for PRO/Team/Enterprise); model must be loaded to 'cuda' at module level (CUDA is emulated outside @spaces.GPU functions); remaining quota determines queue priority, so idle free users queue behind paid ones; as of 2025-2026 creating new CPU Gradio/Docker Spaces now requires a paid plan - the 2-Space ZeroGPU exception is the only free Gradio path.

findings.name: Static Spaces + free Hub tier (free hosting, no GPU)
findings.detail: Static HTML Spaces are free for everyone on any plan. CPU Basic hardware (2 vCPU/16GB, no accelerator) is $0/hour. Free personal accounts get 100GB private storage (public storage 'best-effort' free), unlimited public models/datasets repos, and free CPU Spaces. No credit card needed. Inference Endpoints/Jobs (paid GPU) are NOT free - there is no free notebook/training offering.
findings.eligibility: Any free HF account, worldwide, no verification beyond the account itself; static Spaces need no email-verified/30-day status the way ZeroGPU hosting does.
findings.claim: Create a free account, create a Space with SDK 'static HTML' (or CPU Basic Gradio/Docker if already on a paid plan); no payment setup required.
findings.expiry: Ongoing free tier; no expiry stated. Note the 2025-2026 change: new Gradio/Docker Spaces (even on free CPU Basic) now require PRO (personal) or Team/Enterprise (orgs) to create or duplicate - only Static Spaces remain free for free accounts.
findings.gotchas: The marketing page /classrooms still says demos are 'hosted for free', but the Spaces docs explicitly require a paid plan for new Gradio/Docker Spaces; duplicating a Gradio/Docker Space follows the same paid rule (ZeroGPU exception only). Free spaces sleep when idle; protected/private visibility requires PRO/Team/Enterprise. Free private storage capped at 100GB, overflow is billed.

findings.name: Community GPU grants (free dedicated GPU hardware for Spaces)
findings.detail: Case-by-case grants that cover Space hardware upgrade costs (dedicated GPU, or ZeroGPU slots beyond the free 2-Space cap) for public-facing community use cases: open research demos, hobbyist projects, educational tools, institutional showcases; company projects may apply ('Company project' option). No fixed dollar amount - the grant attaches the needed hardware to the Space. Official docs link to applying 'using the link in the Settings tab of your Space'. No credit card; no stated startup age/funding caps.
findings.eligibility: Qualifying public, non-commercial-leaning Space use cases where the user 'can't pay for the hardware' (open source, research, educational, institutional). Private/commercial/closed-source projects are steered to PRO instead. No .edu required for company grants.
findings.claim: Build the Space (as ZeroGPU if you still have a free slot, else a free Static Space with ZeroGPU-ready code), then open a Community Tab discussion on the Space titled 'Apply for a GPU community grant: <Personal|Company|Academic> project' with one paragraph on what the app does and one on why it should run on free GPU; wait days for review; approved grants attach hardware automatically (Static holding Spaces must flip sdk to gradio). The entry point is also the 'apply for a community GPU grant' link in the Space Settings tab.
findings.expiry: Grant covers the attached hardware while the Space/project qualifies; no published renewal term. The old public application page (huggingface.co/community-grants) is reported dead as of 2026-Q2; the current channel is the per-Space Settings tab link / Community discussion.
findings.gotchas: Approval takes days and is discretionary ('see if yours makes the cut'); open public demos typically approved, commercial ones not; grant docs come mainly from the official huggingface/skills repo rather than a dedicated marketing page, so policy can shift without announcement; no guarantees on hardware size.

findings.name: Hugging Face for Classrooms (free education workspace)
findings.detail: Free classroom organization on the Hub for educators: free hosting of class datasets, models and demos, git version control, admin/read/write access controls per student, private or public visibility, plus free HF courses (NLP, Deep RL, Gradio). Students only need a free account to join; no seat cap. No institutional verification, no .edu email, no credit card.
findings.eligibility: Any user can create a classroom (org type 'classroom'); no educator verification or application required; available worldwide per official page.
findings.claim: Create a free HF account, open huggingface.co/classrooms, click 'create a classroom for free', set name/visibility/permissions, invite students by username or email.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no expiry or renewal stated.
findings.gotchas: It is a Hub workspace, not compute: the Classrooms page still says demos are 'hosted for free', but the current Spaces docs say new Gradio/Docker Spaces require a paid plan (Team/Enterprise for organizations) and list no classroom exception - so classroom demos are free as Static Spaces (or ZeroGPU for invited free individuals under their own accounts), not as new CPU Gradio Spaces. Storage follows the free tier (100GB private).

provider: Hugging Face (Spaces ZeroGPU inference hosting; front-end: GPU / ML training & Notebooks free compute)
sunset_notes: No free education license or startup program: Hugging Face's education offering is Academia Hub, a PAID institutional plan ($10/seat/month, min 250 annual seats, incl. $2/seat/month compute credits and higher ZeroGPU priority) — institutions like ESCP (Aug 2025) pay for it; there is no self-serve .edu free program and no dedicated free startup program (no application form, no funding-cap criteria found; community GPU grants are the closest equivalent and accept 'Company project' cases). No free ML training/notebook compute exists: HF Jobs and Inference Endpoints are on-demand paid, and the only free inference-side compute is ZeroGPU's 5 min/day plus CPU Basic $0/hr. Material 2025-2026 changes: (1) new Gradio/Docker Spaces now require a paid plan (PRO personal / Team-Enterprise org) — previously CPU Spaces were free for all; free accounts retain only Static Spaces + up to 2 ZeroGPU Gradio Spaces (verified in the spaces-overview doc, 2026-10-22). (2) ZeroGPU hardware is now shared NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (48/96GB slices) replacing the earlier A100/A10G-based shared fleet; the original program (May 2024, ~$10M commitment, The Verge) survives in this form. (3) The former public community-grants application page (huggingface.co/community-grants) is reported 404 as of 2026-Q2; grants are now requested per-Space via the Settings tab link / Community discussion. (4) A May 2026 press item (CBW News) claims ~$5/month free GPU credits for all accounts; this does not appear on huggingface.co/pricing or the official docs and is unverified (low confidence). Free-account 100GB private storage, best-effort public storage, and 'protected' visibility gating to paid plans also confirmed 2026-10-22. WebSearch session budget was exhausted after 2 searches, so sunset/change claims rest on the official pages fetched today plus third-party changelogs (aifree.dev, perq.sh, The Verge, ESCP).

findings.name: Modal Starter Plan — $30/month free compute credits (free tier)
findings.detail: Starter plan: $0/mo base + pay-as-you-go compute, with $30/month of free compute credits included, billed per second with no minimums. GPU list prices per second: B300 $0.001972/s (~$7.10/hr), B200 $0.001736/s (~$6.25/hr), H200 SXM $0.001261/s (~$4.54/hr), H100 SXM5 $0.001097/s (~$3.95/hr), RTX PRO 6000 $0.000842/s, A100 80GB $0.000694/s, A100 40GB $0.000583/s, L40S $0.000542/s, A10 $0.000306/s, L4 $0.000222/s, T4 $0.000164/s (~$0.59/hr). So $30 ≈ ~50 T4-hours, ~12 A100-hours, ~7.6 H100-hours, ~6.6 H200-hours, ~4.8 B200-hours. CPU $0.0000131/core/s (min 0.125 cores/container), memory $0.00000222/GiB/s, volumes $0.09/GiB/mo with 1 TiB/mo free, egress $0.04/GiB with 1 TiB/mo free on Starter. Signup is OAuth (GitHub/Google/SSO) — no credit card required to sign up; a payment method is only needed if you exceed $30. Credits reset monthly, no rollover. No published sunset date.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — no .edu email, no funding proof, no credit card for signup (GitHub/Google/SSO OAuth). No region limit stated on the pricing page. Limits: up to 3 seats, 100 containers, 10 GPU concurrency, 200 deployed apps, 5 cron jobs, 1-day log retention. Team plan (paid, $250/mo) includes $100/mo compute credits, unlimited seats, 5000 containers, 50 GPU concurrency, 10 TiB/mo egress.
findings.claim: Go to modal.com/signup → 'Continue with GitHub/Google/SSO' → workspace is created instantly with $30/mo free compute; install Python SDK (`pip install modal`, then `modal setup`) and deploy. Credits apply automatically to all billed compute.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: $30/mo is a recurring free tier, not a one-time trial. If usage exceeds $30 without a payment method on file, workloads stop (or you add billing) — no quiet overcharge, but a card/ACH is needed for anything above the free pool. Sandboxes + Notebooks CPU/memory are billed at non-preemptible 3x list ($0.00003942/core/s). Shared Endpoint LLM tokens are billed separately and NOT covered by the $30. Region selection multiplies base prices 1.15–1.75x. 1-day log retention and no deployment rollbacks on Starter. Volume storage beyond 1 TiB/mo and egress beyond 1 TiB/mo bill at list.

findings.name: Modal for Startups — one-time free compute credit grants (VC-backed startups)
findings.detail: Two tiers, application-based, one-time grants: (1) Seed to Series A: 'Free credits for rising startups' — eligible if raised ANY amount of VC funding from Modal's partner network (Y Combinator, a16z, Sequoia, Khosla, Neo, HF0, Pear, Lux Capital, plus others in FAQ) OR raised >$1M VC from any fund; (2) Scaling / Series B+: 'Custom' grants for AI-native companies that raised >$30M or are post-Series B with a partner-network VC. Official page says 'thousands of free GPU credits' but does not publish exact dollar amounts; third-party trackers and Modal's own restructure history indicate the Seed–Series A tier is up to $25,000 in credits valid for 12 months (was $50,000 before the Q4 2025 cut). Also includes direct access to Modal's engineering team, GTM amplification on launches/raises, and an exclusive founder community.
findings.eligibility: Must be NEW to Modal (no existing paid use). Seed–Series A: any funding from a Modal partner fund, or >$1M VC from any fund. Series B+: >$30M raised or post-Series B, with partner-network VC. No company-age cap and no explicit employee-count cap on the official page; no equity taken. No .edu requirement. Global (no region limit stated).
findings.claim: Sign up for Modal, create a team (shared) workspace, then at modal.com/startups click 'Apply Now' (modal.com/startups#apply) → submit company/funding details + proof of funding + use case → review takes ~3–14 days → credits are provisioned to your workspace; check status in Usage & Billing.
findings.gotchas: Payment method is required on file for the program (per the startup FAQ and trackers). Credits are a one-time grant per tier — you may NOT reapply once you received credits in a tier. Exact credit amounts and expiration/reinstatement policy are not published on the official page (FAQ says credits last a period and may be reinstated if expired; trackers say 12 months from issuance). 'Thousands of free GPU credits' on the official page is deliberately vague; the $25K figure comes from third-party trackers + PricingSaaS's Q4 2025 change record ('Modal Reduces Startup Credit Grant from $50k to $25k for Early-Stage Startups'). Personal workspaces reportedly not eligible — use a shared/team workspace. Common rejections: Series C+ stage, already a paying customer, mismatched Crunchbase data.

findings.name: Modal for Academics — up to $10,000 free compute credits (student/researcher program)
findings.detail: Modal for Academics gives graduate students, labs, and researchers 'up to $10k' of free compute credits on Modal. Benefits: run workloads on B200s/H100s without requesting quota, autoscaling GPUs, and direct access to Modal's engineers/PhDs for research support. Spun out as its own program in the October 2025 restructure of the formerly unified '$50k for startups and academic researchers' grant. No expiry date or renewal policy is published; no statement whether the $10k is one-time or recurring.
findings.eligibility: Intended for graduate students, labs, and researchers (e.g., ARC Prize collaboration, MIT/Cornell team). The official page does not state an explicit .edu email requirement, university-affiliation proof, or deadline — eligibility is determined by application. No region limit stated.
findings.claim: At modal.com/academics, click 'Sign up to hear about our grant programs' (modal.com/academics#apply) or the 'Contact us' Pylon form to request the grant; researchers are contacted for a partnership/review before credits are issued.
findings.gotchas: High = I read the official page today, but the page itself is thin: 'up to $10k' is the only number; the program is invitation/application-driven (Modal contacts applicants), so approval time is uncertain and amounts are discretionary ('up to'). No published credit expiry, no published renewal. The separate $30/mo Starter free tier also applies to academic accounts; the $10k grant is additive. The pricing page's 'Credit grants for academics' blurb also cites 'up to $10k'.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes (from PricingSaaS Pulse captures of modal.com): (1) Oct 5, 2025 — Modal restructured its credit grants: the single unified 'up to $50k for startups and academic researchers' grant was split into 'Credit grants for startups' (then up to $50k) and 'Credit grants for academics' (up to $10k); cloud marketplace committed-spend also expanded from AWS-only to AWS + GCP (+Azure/OCI in that capture). (2) Q4 2025 — Modal cut the early-stage (Seed–Series A) startup credit grant from $50k to $25k. (3) Q2 2025 — H200 GPU option added at $0.001261/sec; (4) Mar 2026 — RTX PRO 6000 added at $0.000842/sec; B300 now listed at $0.001972/sec (the task's known H200/B300 range is confirmed live). No offer was fully sunset: the $30/mo Starter free tier, the startup grants, and the academics grants all remain active as of Oct 22, 2026. Team plan is now $250/mo including $100/mo of compute credits. Sources: https://modal.com/pricing , https://modal.com/startups , https://modal.com/academics , https://modal.com/signup , https://pricingsaas.com/companies/modal/diffs/2025Q3 , https://sidehustletools.app/free-credits/modal-for-startups , https://perkbook.co/vendor-directory/modal/ , https://creditforstartups.com/companies/modal , https://grabaicredits.com/en/deals/modal-for-startups , https://aifree.dev/offer/modal-startup-program

findings.name: Datadog Free Plan (Infrastructure monitoring)
findings.detail: Free monitoring plan at $0: up to 5 hosts, 1-day metric retention, 5 containers per host (FAQ says '5 or 10 containers free for each host license'), unlimited user accounts, 'core collection and visualization features', 1,000+ integrations. The current pricing table does NOT show custom-metric/custom-event allotments in the Free column; its FAQ attributes '100 custom metrics/500 custom events per host' to Pro and '200/1000' to Enterprise — so the previously advertised 100-metric/500-event free allotment is no longer explicitly granted on the Free tier as displayed today. Paid reference points: Infrastructure Pro $15/host/mo (annual, 15-month retention), Enterprise $23/host/mo.
findings.eligibility: Open to any new Datadog account holder; no .edu email, no startup proof, no credit card stated for the free plan; no region restriction stated. Data region chosen at signup cannot later be migrated.
findings.claim: Sign up at app.datadoghq.com/register (no credit card required) -> choose data region -> the 5-host Free plan applies automatically to the account; no application or referral needed.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; no expiration or renewal. 1-day metric retention means data older than 1 day is purged; plan limits (5 hosts) are fixed.
findings.gotchas: 1-day retention vs 15 months on paid plans; container allotment (5 or 10 per host) is a soft cap; over 5 hosts or over 10 containers/host requires a paid plan; the 100 custom metrics/500 custom events per-host allotments appear tied to paid Pro/Enterprise in today's pricing FAQ, so verify current free-tier custom-metric behavior in-product. 'Unlimited alerts' and 'unlimited users' are not explicitly printed in the Free column on today's page (they appear under Pro/Enterprise rows).

findings.name: Agent Observability (LLM Observability) Free Tier
findings.detail: Per today's pricing page: Free tier gives 'Up to 40K LLM spans / month', '15-day trace retention', 'Unlimited context & evals', 'Full feature access', positioned 'For individuals and small teams', and the FAQ states 'up to 40K LLM spans per month with 15-day retention ... no credit card required.' Paid contrast: Pro 'Starting At $160 per month' includes 100K LLM spans/month; overage 'Additional spans: $3.50 per 10K LLM spans'.
findings.eligibility: Any Datadog account holder; individuals and small teams; no .edu or startup proof; no credit card required; no region limit stated.
findings.claim: Included with a standard Datadog account (sign up free, no CC) -> connect LLM/agent telemetry via OpenTelemetry OpenInference integrations or supported LLM SDK integrations -> spans are tracked up to 40K/month with no application.
findings.expiry: 40K LLM-span allowance resets monthly; 15-day rolling trace retention; no end date. Exceeding 40K spans on the free tier pushes you to the paid Pro tier pricing.
findings.gotchas: Renamed from LLM Observability to Agent Observability; 'full feature access' is on the free tier but the product was recently GA-transitioned, so some features may be in preview; 15-day retention is short vs 15-month metric retention on paid infra plans; span overages are not billed on free — they are the trigger to upgrade; egress/scanning costs (e.g., AI Guard at $0.80/1M tokens scanned) are separate paid line items if enabled.

findings.name: 14-day Free Trial (metrics, APM/traces, logs, Synthetics)
findings.detail: Official trial page: '14 days of unlimited monitoring' covering 'metrics, traces, and logs', log search/analysis, APM request tracing, and Synthetic-like monitoring of 'applications and API endpoints via simulated user requests', plus anomaly/outlier/forecast alerts. 'No credit card required' is stated on the page. 'Unlimited' during trial means no host limit for the trial window; at trial end the account drops to plan-based limits (free plan for infra).
findings.eligibility: Any new Datadog user; no .edu email or startup proof required; no credit card; region choice at signup is binding ('You can't migrate data between regions').
findings.claim: Click any 'Start Free Trial' CTA (or datadoghq.com/trial) -> create account with no CC -> pick data region -> monitoring is live immediately for 14 days; no application, no sales call.
findings.expiry: 14 days from signup; not renewable as a trial (one trial per account in practice). After it ends, only the free-plan limits (e.g., 5 hosts) and the 40K LLM-span tier apply; paid products require a plan.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free confusion: 'unlimited' applies only during the 14 days; post-trial you keep the free plan, not unlimited monitoring. No post-trial behavior is stated on the page (data retention/downgrade specifics not published). Region cannot be changed later. Trial does not include all products (e.g., Cloud SIEM/Security add-ons have separate trial offers).

findings.name: Datadog for Startups (DDFS) — up to $100K credits
findings.detail: Official startup page: 'up to a year of free access to the full Datadog platform — up to $100k in credits', hero states 'a year of free Datadog Pro'. Coverage: complete GA product suite (Observability: infrastructure/APM/logs/data; Security: code/cloud/SIEM; Digital Experience; Software Delivery; Service Management; AI modules) with 'No watered-down tiers, no hidden limits'; preview products 'if space permits'. Extras: optional Technical Engagement Manager, documentation access, customer-success rep after several months.
findings.eligibility: (1) Funding stage 'Series A or earlier' (the page's cap is funding-stage based, no explicit employee/revenue figures published); (2) 'New to Datadog' — no current/prior Datadog customers and no prior DDFS credits; (3) 'Referred by one of our partners' (VCs, hyperscalers, accelerators) — applications without a partner referral are not accepted. No .edu component.
findings.claim: Get a referral from a partner (VC/hyperscaler/accelerator) -> submit the application at datadoghq.com/startups describing your team -> start a Datadog trial while it is reviewed -> acceptance notified in ~3-5 business days -> activate within 30 days after acceptance or credits are forfeited.
findings.expiry: Credits valid up to 1 year from acceptance/activation; activation window is 30 days post-acceptance; inactive accounts (3 months without usage) get a 30-day warning before removal; unused credits do not roll over.
findings.gotchas: Partner-referral-only — no direct application path, which excludes bootstrapped/unaffiliated startups; 'up to $100k' is a ceiling, actual awards vary; credits apply to services, not products you can't resell; starting a trial during review is required by the process; three-month inactivity rule can void remaining credits.

findings.name: Student/education license (status: no public offer found as of 2026-10-22)
findings.detail: No public Datadog education program, student license, or .edu-based free tier was found on the official site today: datadoghq.com/education/ returns 404; /solutions/education/ is a sales page aimed at selling Datadog TO institutions (Harvard Medical School, University of Chicago, Coursera as customers), with no free seat grants; /learn/ offers a free 'Learning Center' (hands-on course platform for all users, free of charge) but no student/educator account or seat grants, no .edu email requirement, and no classroom environment program is advertised (the older 'Datadog Classroom' URL structure is no longer live).
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — no public application process. The general 14-day trial and 5-host free plan are open to students/educators like anyone else (no CC required for trial; no CC stated for free plan), and free learning courses at /learn/ are open to all users.
findings.claim: N/A — no education application exists. Nearest path: use the general free trial (no CC) + 5-host free plan for coursework; use free /learn/ courses for certification-style study.
findings.expiry: N/A for the (absent) program; free plan and trial terms as in their own findings.
findings.gotchas: Students have no dedicated .edu offer or classroom org grants discoverable today; do not assume a 'Datadog Classroom' free lab still exists; confirm with Datadog sales/academics if a class agreement is needed — any such access would be custom, not public.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22 (all figures from official pages fetched today; the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted in this session so third-party 2025-2026 change reports could not be cross-checked — confidence in 'what changed' below is medium, based on comparison with previously advertised terms): (1) EDUCATION: no public student/educator license or .edu program remains on datadoghq.com (/education/ is 404; the /solutions/education/ page only sells to institutions; the once-public 'Datadog Classroom' free course/lab offering is no longer advertised at its old URL — treat a standing free education license as sunsets/unadvertised; Datadog's only free education-adjacent asset is the free Learning Center at /learn/). (2) FREE INFRA PLAN SCOPE: the free tier no longer publicly lists the '100 custom metrics + 500 custom events per host' allotments that were previously associated with the free plan; today's pricing FAQ ties 100/500 to Pro and 200/1000 to Enterprise, so free-plan custom-metric/event entitlements appear reduced or unpublished (verify in-product). (3) STARTUP PROGRAM: currently advertised as 'up to $100k in credits / up to a year of the full GA platform', a material increase over earlier publicly advertised credit amounts (roughly $35k-50k in prior years — exact prior figures could not be re-verified today due to search budget). Eligibility has tightened to partner-referral-only (VC/hyperscaler/accelerator) with Series A-or-earlier and new-to-Datadog conditions; no sunset of DDFS itself was found. (4) LLM/AGENT OBSERVABILITY: renamed from LLM Observability to Agent Observability; 40K LLM spans/month free tier is live and no CC required; Pro floor is $160/month with 100K spans included. No announced sunset of the free tiers; 5-host free infra plan and 14-day no-CC trial remain active with no termination notice.

findings.name: Starter plan (free tier)
findings.detail: $0, no time limit. Daily Agent credits that reset daily, capped by a monthly cap (exact credit count is NOT published by Replit; Settings > Usage is the source of truth). Monthly cloud credits for production databases, object storage, and publishing (autoscale/static) that reset monthly (no dollar figure published). Lite build only (Full build requires Core). Exactly 1 free published app: the link auto-goes offline 30 days after publish (you can re-publish), and it carries a mandatory 'Made with Replit' badge with your referral link. Includes Design Canvas + Visual Editor and web & mobile app projects.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no credit card required; no .edu required; no region limit stated; no funding cap. Not gated on startup backing.
findings.claim: Sign up free at replit.com; Agent usage and remaining allowance show in Settings > Usage; publish one app via Lite build or Design Canvas.
findings.expiry: No time limit; daily Agent and monthly cloud allowances reset daily/monthly; the single published app goes offline after 30 days.
findings.gotchas: Exact credit amounts are not published (check Settings > Usage). 'Free Mode' is NOT a standalone free plan (see below). As of 2026 the public pricing page (replit.com/pricing) no longer lists a free Starter card - it now opens on Core ($18 billed annually / $20 monthly); a third-party pricing tracker reports the free Starter plan was dropped from the pricing page between Aug 28 and Sept 11, 2026. Docs still list Starter as an active free tier, so it remains available but is no longer the advertised self-serve entry point (a new signup now lands on paid Core). Referral credits from your badge only vest after you upgrade to a paid plan. Connectors (Google/Stripe), Replit AI Integrations, Plan Mode, artifact types beyond web/mobile, badge removal, and 2nd+ published apps all require Core.

findings.name: Free Mode (no-cost Agent allowance inside plans)
findings.detail: Launched Aug 18, 2026. No-cost Agent usage within each plan's allowance. Core: up to 30 hours/month of chat on Free Mode and up to 60 projects on Free Mode; marketing claims up to 30x more creation vs before. On Core/Pro the Free Mode allowance resets every 5 hours and has a weekly limit; Starter keeps its own daily limits. Paid modes: Power (mid-tier, formerly 'Economy') and Max (top-tier, formerly 'Power').
findings.eligibility: Subscribers to Starter, Core, or Pro. No extra eligibility; Replit picks the model in Free Mode (no manual model choice). Not available on Enterprise.
findings.claim: Open a new Agent chat - it starts in Free Mode by default; a paid mode only runs after your explicit one-time confirmation per request.
findings.expiry: Core/Pro Free Mode allowance resets every 5 hours with a weekly cap; Starter uses daily limits.
findings.gotchas: Replit's help page states explicitly that Free Mode 'is not a free plan on itself' - it is an allowance bundled into paid Starter/Core/Pro. A paid escalation (Power/Max) applies to that one request only, then returns to Free Mode. After the Aug 2026 restructure the genuinely free entry point is effectively the Starter plan, and Free Mode is framed around the $20 Core subscription.

findings.name: Replit for Startups (up to $25K credits / free Replit Pro)
findings.detail: Launched live April 23, 2026.
