Two tiers: (1) Up to $25,000 in Replit credits for startups backed by a 'Select Partner' fund or accelerator - a partner offer (SVB) lists $25K credits with 6-month validity plus a dedicated onboarding call, priority support community, and co-marketing. (2) Free Replit Pro for startups backed by any other recognized fund/accelerator in the broader 'Partner Network' - a partner offer (JPMorgan) lists 1 year of Pro (free for the duration of the partnership): $100/month credits, access to the most powerful models, private deployments, up to 15 collaborators and 50 viewers, 28-day database restore, premium support. No fixed company-age or funding cap is stated publicly; partner pages say 'eligible at any funding stage' - the gate is being backed by a partner fund/accelerator, not a headcount/dollar threshold.
findings.eligibility: VC / fund / accelerator-backed startups (not .edu-based). Backed by a Select Partner fund -> up to $25K credits; backed by any other Partner Network fund/accelerator -> free Pro tier. Requirements: apply with a professional (work) email + company domain; one application per company. Unbacked founders may still apply and are reviewed; Replit may add your fund to the Partner Network.
findings.claim: Apply at replit.com/startups with a professional email + domain, complete the application, and redeem via the partner link. If your fund is not listed, use replit.com/startups/fund-not-listed to request it be added, then apply.
findings.expiry: Credits: ~6-month validity on the $25K tier (per partner offer). Free Pro: 'for the duration of the partnership' (1 year on partner offer).
findings.gotchas: CC not required to receive the perk, but a Replit account is needed to redeem. The $25K tier is reserved for 'Select Partners' only - most funds land in the free-Pro tier. Exact specs differ by fund partner (SVB vs JPMorgan pages disagree on term length). Program existence + cap + apply-anyway path are confirmed high-confidence on Replit's own pages; the tier breakdown / validity / Pro specs came from third-party partner offer pages, so treat those specifics as medium. Unbacked/solo founders are NOT the target (use Race to Revenue instead).

findings.name: Race to Revenue (builder program: $10K credits + $25K cash prize)
findings.detail: Pilot launched Dec 9, 2025. 8-week structured program; 20 builders per cohort (pilot cohort ~21 founders across 4 continents). Each selected builder receives $10,000 in Replit Agent + Cloud credits. The winner gets a $25,000 CASH prize at the 2-day Final Showcase capstone in San Francisco. Zero equity. Partner perks: Ramp (corporate cards/expense tools), Stripe Atlas (free incorporation ~$500 value + $2,500 Stripe credits + up to $50K partner perks), Linear 6 months free, Rippling 6 months free, ElevenLabs 12 months free (600+ hrs), HubSpot 90% off, Make Industry toolkit, Gunderson Dettmer legal.
findings.eligibility: Solo builders and early-stage/bootstrapped founders who are building on or deeply integrating with Replit. No prior revenue required to apply; no funding/backing requirement. Must commit to full 8-week participation (miss >1 week = dropped) and travel to SF for the showcase; international applicants allowed (travel logistics on them).
findings.claim: Apply at replit.com/racetorevenue: provide name/email/location/team size, what you're building + ICP, a traction signal, whether you build on Replit, 6-week availability + SF travel, and a 2-minute video explaining the project and why you're the one to build it.
findings.expiry: Cohort-based, 8 weeks; explicitly a pilot/iterating program. Credits and prize allocated per cohort.
findings.gotchas: You are FILMED (it is a documentary series) and you pitch live on camera in SF. The $10K is Replit-platform credits, not cash; only the winner receives the $25K cash prize. Partner perks are limited/subject to partner terms. It is a competitive selection, not an open grant.

findings.name: Replit for Education (students & educators)
findings.detail: Replit runs an education program for students and educators; the pricing docs FAQ confirms it and describes it as offering 'discounted access to eligible students,' noting the education page is the source of truth. The live page is replit.com/edu (title 'Replit for Education'). Exact terms - free vs discounted, .edu requirement, credit amounts, and enrollment steps - could NOT be read this run: the page is JS-rendered (WebFetch returned only its title) and the session web-search budget was exhausted.
findings.eligibility: Students and educators; a .edu email is likely required but unconfirmed this run. Which roles (K-12, higher-ed, teachers vs students) and exact eligibility are unconfirmed.
findings.claim: Enroll at replit.com/edu (terms are gated behind the live page).
findings.expiry: Unknown (page not readable this run).
findings.gotchas: Do not assume specific credit amounts - Replit's docs state education eligibility/discounts 'may change' and defer to the education page. Historical 'free Core for students/teachers' terms were not verifiable today. Re-verify by reading replit.com/edu directly before citing numbers.

findings.name: No time-limited free trial for Core/Pro (clarification)
findings.detail: Replit's pricing docs state explicitly that there is no time-limited free trial for Core or Pro; the free Starter plan is the 'no-cost, no time limit' on-ramp. Third-party partner channels do run limited-time Core promos (e.g., a 'Startup Grind x Replit Core' page advertising 3 months of Core free for new accounts only), which are separate, time-boxed, new-account-only partner offers - not a standing free tier.
findings.eligibility: Clarification, not a grant. Partner Core promos require a new Replit account; professional (non-personal) email required on some partner forms.
findings.claim: For a no-cost start, use the free Starter plan. Partner Core promos are claimed only via the specific partner link while the promo is live.
findings.expiry: N/A for the docs statement. Partner Core promos are time-boxed (e.g., 3 months) and new-account-only; confirm current availability.
findings.gotchas: Don't conflate Free Mode with a free plan (it is a paid-plan allowance). Startup Grind-style '3 months Core free' offers are limited partner promos, not a recurring program - verify they are still live before relying on them.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes: (1) The free Starter plan was removed from the public replit.com/pricing page between ~Aug 28 and Sept 11, 2026; the page now opens on Core ($18 billed annually / $20 monthly), so new self-serve entry is paid. The free Starter tier still exists in Replit's docs (docs.replit.com/billing/plans/starter-plan) and remains $0/no-time-limit, but it is no longer the advertised entry point. (2) Agent modes were restructured on Aug 18, 2026 with the launch of Free Mode: paid modes renamed 'Economy'->'Power' and 'Power'->'Max'; free Agent work is now framed as a paid-plan allowance (Core: up to 30 hrs/month chat, 60 projects; resets every 5 hrs + weekly limit). (3) 'Replit for Startups' launched April 23, 2026 (up to $25K credits for Select-Partner-backed startups, free Pro for the broader Partner Network), superseding earlier ad-hoc startup perks. (4) 'Race to Revenue' pilot launched Dec 9, 2025 ($10K Replit credits per builder + $25K cash prize). (5) Plan-structure change per a third-party pricing tracker: Feb 2026 the Pro plan launched, Core dropped to $20, and the old 'Teams' plan was sunset; Aug 2026 Core's credit wallet was trimmed to $20 and Pro annual set to $90 (medium confidence - tracker, not Replit). Net: no generic free trial exists today; the genuinely free options are the Starter plan (unadvertised on the pricing page since late 2026) plus the grants in Replit for Startups and Race to Revenue. Data caveat: this run hit the session web-search budget, so education-page specifics and JS-rendered program bodies could not be fully read; confidence ratings reflect that.

findings.name: GitLab.com Free plan (permanent free tier)
findings.detail: Ongoing $0/month plan requiring no credit card. Included: 400 CI/CD compute minutes/month, applied per top-level group ("The quota will be applied to a group, no matter the number of users in the group or the number of users in the subscription"); initial 10 GiB limit per project on Git repo + LFS storage, which is "adjustable" (extra storage purchasable); 5 users per top-level group with private visibility ("The 5-user limit is applicable only to users of the Free tier of the GitLab.com offering in a top-level group with private visibility"). Basic security features on all tiers: SAST, secret detection, container scanning. No GitLab Duo credits included on Free (add-on, $1/credit on-demand; monthly commitment pools available to Free top-level group namespaces but not personal namespaces; compute-minute top-ups $10 per 1,000 minutes).
findings.eligibility: Anyone can sign up on gitlab.com, no CC required, no age/institution requirement. Public groups, paid tiers, and community-program users are exempt from the 5-user cap.
findings.claim: Create a gitlab.com account (sign up at gitlab.com/users/sign_in), the group sits on the Free plan automatically; purchase add-ons (storage/minutes) via group billing settings.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no sunset date published. Overage add-ons bill monthly (storage $5/mo per 10 GiB on paid tiers; minutes $10/1,000).
findings.gotchas: 400 minutes is a hard per-group per-month cap for CI/CD on shared runners; public groups are the main workaround for the 5-user cap; Duo/AI features are paid add-ons even on Free; self-managed GitLab CE (open-source edition, $0) has no user cap and no 400-minute cap (BYO runners/storage) — see https://about.gitlab.com/install/.

findings.name: GitLab for Education (free Ultimate license for educational institutions)
findings.detail: Complimentary GitLab Ultimate license, SaaS or self-managed, with UNLIMITED seats and 50,000 compute minutes/month included (extra minutes purchased separately). 1-year duration, renewed annually; renewal requires re-verifying the renewer's employment via the Proxi.id partner, and the original applicant must be the one to renew (ownership transferable via support ticket). Multiple self-managed instances can run on the same license key. Community-level support only (GitLab Community Discord); paid support no longer offered as an add-on on this license. 1,000+ institutions and ~3M people participate; the program spans 65 countries.
findings.eligibility: Institution must be: accredited by a local/state/provincial/federal/national authorized agency, primarily focused on teaching enrolled students, actively granting degrees/diplomas/certificates, and not-for-profit (for-profit institutions ineligible). Institutions enrolling students under 13 are ineligible for SaaS (self-managed still available). Applicant must be a FULL-TIME faculty or staff member applying with the institution's email domain; GitLab explicitly cannot issue licenses directly to students — students must find a faculty/staff sponsor or use the Free tier. GitLab, Inc. does not issue licenses to institutions in China (JiHu separate entity). Use restricted to instruction and non-commercial academic research — not running/administering the institution's own IT services.
findings.claim: Faculty/staff apply through the GitLab Customer Portal at customers.gitlab.com/subscriptions/community_program/coupons/new?program=EDU (linked from about.gitlab.com/solutions/education/join/), verify via institutional email, receive redemption instructions; re-apply/verify annually for renewal.
findings.expiry: License valid 1 year, renewed annually; access lapses when employment/renewal verification fails; graduates lose access because licenses are issued to the institution.
findings.gotchas: NO student-issued licenses — individual students with .edu emails are NOT automatically enrolled; a faculty/staff sponsor is required. 'Apply with the institution's email domain' (institutional domain, not necessarily .edu). No credit card required. No storage allotment is stated. Students are funneled to https://about.gitlab.com/community/ (Free tier) instead. China excluded; for-profit colleges excluded.

findings.name: GitLab for Startups (free/reduced Ultimate program)
findings.detail: Two tiers by funding: SEED — Pre-Seed or Seed stage with up to $5M in external funding, new customers only: Year 1 = free GitLab Ultimate license (SaaS or self-managed) up to 20 seats; Year 2 = 50% discount on any tier, up to 20 users. EARLY — Series A or Series B with up to $20M in external funding, new customers only: Year 1 = 50% discount on any tier (up to 20 users); Year 2 = 25% discount (up to 20 users). Program spans two years; GitLab contacts teams before year one ends to discuss renewal. No company-age or headcount threshold is stated. Support is NOT included; self-managed recipients must enable usage and analytics features. Additional seats beyond 20: email startups@gitlab.com for an add-on quote.
findings.eligibility: Externally funded startups only — self-funded companies are excluded ("The program is currently available for externally funded companies only"). Must be a new GitLab customer. Seed: <= $5M external funding; Early: Series A/B, <= $20M. Applicants must provide a Crunchbase, Pitchbook profile, or VC/accelerator webpage proving current funding status; otherwise the application "will not be considered". New customers only.
findings.claim: Submit the in-page application form on https://about.gitlab.com/solutions/startups/ (#form anchor; all fields required; may be asked for more info to verify eligibility). Questions: startups@gitlab.com. No credit card requirement stated.
findings.expiry: Two-year program (Year 1 entitlement, then Year 2 discount); after year two the company "will have the flexibility to choose from our offerings"; program "offered at the sole discretion of GitLab and is subject to change". Applications not processed during U.S. holidays.
findings.gotchas: The current official page does NOT list 50,000 compute minutes or any storage allowance for startups (the pricing page's line bundling "qualifying open source projects, educational institutions, and startups" under "free Ultimate licenses, along with 50K compute minutes/month" is ambiguous — confirm with GitLab whether SaaS compute minutes ship with the seed license). 20-seat cap. Paid support excluded. Seed stage gets the only genuinely free license; Early stage is a discount, not free.

findings.name: GitLab for Open Source (free Ultimate features for qualifying projects)
findings.detail: Features of GitLab Ultimate free to qualifying open source projects, self-managed or SaaS, plus 50,000 compute minutes "calculated at a program-specific cost factor." Seat allocation uses a concurrent-seat model (max users enabled at once; every occupied seat counts, including the owner's, except Guest-permission members). No support included, and purchasing GitLab Credits for the Duo Agent Platform is not available on community subscriptions.
findings.eligibility: Every project in the namespace must be published under an OSI-approved open source license; the organization must not seek to make a profit (donations OK; selling services/enhancements not); group and source code must be publicly visible and available; personal namespaces ineligible (must be a group; only free-tier groups you own appear in the application dropdown).
findings.claim: Steps: (1) verify qualification against the requirements list, (2) create a GitLab account (Free tier or Ultimate trial), (3) GitLab.com: fill out the Customers Portal form to confirm the group meets requirements — you then receive an email with a coupon code and provisioning instructions; self-managed: submit the form with project details and a clear justification; (4) enroll via the Apply link. Renew annually by resubmitting the form; renew up to 3 months early, start at least 1 month before expiration — failing to renew means the account is downgraded.
findings.expiry: Annual membership, renewed by re-applying; downgraded to Free tier if not renewed. No CC required.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial requirement rules out monetized/mixed projects; Guest seats don't count toward the concurrent cap; self-managed applications are not processed during holidays; 50K minutes are billed internally at a "program-specific cost factor" rather than standard rates.

findings.name: 30-day GitLab Ultimate free trial (SaaS and self-managed)
findings.detail: "Start your 30-day GitLab Ultimate trial" covering "nearly all features of our Ultimate tier" plus Duo Agent Platform access. 30 days for both GitLab.com (hosted) and self-managed. GitLab.com trial limits: 400 compute minutes/month, 24 Duo Agent Platform credits/user, one project token only (group tokens excluded), no external-API features. Self-managed trial: requires GitLab 18.0+ and an internet connection, support excluded at any level, Duo Agent Platform (24 credits/user) starts with GitLab 18.9. A credit/debit card is NOT required for customers who do not use GitLab.com CI/CD (BYO runners or shared runners disabled); enabling shared runners triggers a $1 authorization (no charge transfers). New and existing users can start; at trial end you stay on the Free tier or upgrade, and "You will lose access to GitLab Duo Agent Platform and any remaining credits from the trial period." Included 12/24 Duo credits on paid tiers are a limited-time promotional offer.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, including students and startup founders; no CC required unless shared runners are used; one trial flow via gitlab.com/-/trials/new or the free-trial page; no per-account trial-count cap or fixed expiry date is stated on the page.
findings.claim: Go to https://about.gitlab.com/free-trial/ (or gitlab.com/-/trial_registrations/new), choose hosted or self-managed, sign up / log in.
findings.expiry: 30 days per trial; Duo Agent Platform access and remaining trial credits are forfeited at trial end.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: the 30-day Ultimate trial is separate from the permanent Free tier; post-trial you fall back to Free (with its 400-min/5-user caps) unless you pay. The marketing JSON-LD schemas on the /solutions/ pages still advertise a "60-day free trial" — the dedicated official trial page says 30 days; treat 30 days as current. Shared-runner use triggers a $1 card hold.

sunset_notes: Restructured/changed in 2025-2026 (per official pages read 2026-10-22): (1) Trial duration — the dedicated free-trial page states 30-day GitLab Ultimate trials for both hosted and self-managed, while JSON-LD schema metadata on the marketing /solutions/ pages still says "60-day free trial"; the 30-day figure is the current authoritative one. (2) GitLab for Startups is now a two-tier (Seed <=$5M / Early Series A-B <=$20M) structure capping benefits at 20 seats, with Seed = free Ultimate year one + 50% year two and Early = 50%/25% discounts; self-funded startups are excluded and the current page no longer lists 50,000 compute minutes or a storage allowance for the startup program (the pricing page's "50K compute minutes/month" sentence bundles open source, education, and startups without clarifying which still get it — verify with startups@gitlab.com). (3) Education: seats are unlimited with 50,000 compute minutes/month included, but the license is institution-only via full-time faculty/staff — GitLab explicitly cannot issue licenses directly to students, so there is no standalone "GitLab for Students" free program; students are routed to the Free tier or a faculty sponsor. (4) Duo AI features: no free credits are bundled on the Free plan (paid GitLab Credits add-on, $1/credit); the 12/user/mo (Premium) and 24/user/mo (Ultimate) included-credits lines are flagged as a limited-time promotional offer, so those "free" AI credits can sunset. (5) Trial is Ultimate-only; no standalone Premium trial offer appears on the current trial page. No program was announced as fully sunset as of this check; open-source program renewals lapse to the Free tier if not resubmitted annually.

findings.claim: Go to colab.research.google.com, sign in with any Google account, open/create a notebook, then Runtime > Change runtime type > Hardware accelerator = GPU or TPU. No signup form or payment.
findings.detail: Browser-hosted Jupyter notebooks, free of charge, with CPU-only and free GPU + TPU runtime options. Free sessions run for at most 12 hours; idle VMs are deleted after inactivity. No fixed/published compute quota — Google states the specific GPU and TPU types available "vary over time" (community-reported free GPU is commonly an NVIDIA T4, 16 GB; official FAQ does not name a guaranteed model). No credit card required — sign in with a Google account. Free (no compute-unit balance) runtimes are shared/preemptible and prohibit: file hosting, torrent/P2P, remote shells & desktops, bypassing the notebook UI, remote proxies, crypto mining, DoS, password cracking, multi-account abuse, deepfakes, distributed-compute workers, and containerization to evade anti-abuse checks.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Google account. No .edu email required, no region restriction stated in the FAQ, and no credit card required.
findings.expiry: No subscription expiry. Each session is capped at ~12 hours; idle VMs are deleted. Notebooks/models persist only if saved to Google Drive (Drive free-tier 15 GB shared).
findings.gotchas: Free GPU/TPU are shared and intermittently unavailable (no guaranteed quota; may be interrupted under high demand). T4 vs TPU specifics not officially fixed. Paid products (Colab Pro / Pro+ / Pay-As-You-Go, billed on a compute-unit balance; Pro+ up to 24 h continuous with enough units) are separate from free — do not conflate. Free runtimes carry the anti-abuse restrictions above.
findings.name: Colab Free Tier (Notebooks) — free CPU/GPU/TPU runtimes

findings.claim: No longer claimable for new users. Existing verified education users retain access until their 1-year subscription end.
findings.detail: Formerly a FREE 1-year Colab Pro subscription for students and faculty of US-based universities (more compute than the free tier). Per the official FAQ it is now CLOSED: "no longer available for new signups at this time." Previously-verified education users keep access until their 1-year anniversary.
findings.eligibility: Was: US-based university students/faculty (typically .edu verification). Now: new signups not accepted.
findings.expiry: Existing subscriptions expire at the 1-year mark; new signups are closed. Upgrading to a paid personal plan permanently unsubscribes the free education benefit.
findings.gotchas: Sunset offer. Do not pay for a personal Colab Pro/Pro+ assuming it replaces the education benefit — doing so terminates the free edu subscription permanently.
findings.name: Colab Pro for Education (students & faculty)

findings.claim: Not claimable for Colab. To use the credits you run self-hosted GCP workloads (Vertex AI / GKE / GCE) instead of Colab.
findings.detail: There is no Colab-specific startup program and no free Colab trial-credit offer. The adjacent offers are Google Cloud ones: a Startup Program (tiered credits, roughly $500 up to ~$100K) and a new-account Free Trial (historically ~$300 over ~90 days, credit card typically required). These credits apply to GCP services (GCE, Vertex AI, GKE, BigQuery, etc.), NOT to Colab's free tier or to Colab Pro/Pro+ subscriptions.
findings.eligibility: Startup Program: for-profit company, founded within the last ~3 years, raised under ~$50M, in a supported region. Free Trial: new GCP account (CC historically required). Neither grants free Colab.
findings.expiry: Startup credits valid ~3 months from issuance; free trial ~90 days.
findings.gotchas: Could not re-verify live GCP figures today (cloud.google.com/programs/startup returned 404; /free and /colab/pricing were truncated/JS-rendered) — treat the credit amounts and caps as approximate/low-confidence. Colab free tier itself needs no CC and no credits.
findings.name: No Colab-specific startup program or Colab trial credits (GCP credits do NOT apply)

sunset_notes: Sunset / materially changed (2025–2026): (1) COLAB PRO FOR EDUCATION — the formerly free 1-year Colab Pro subscription for US university students/faculty is now CLOSED to new signups (official FAQ, read 2026-10-22); only pre-verified users keep access until their 1-year anniversary, and upgrading to a paid personal plan terminates it permanently. (2) NO COLAB-STARTUP OFFER — there is no Colab-specific startup program or free Colab trial-credit; the only \"credits\" are Google Cloud Startup Program / new-account Free Trial, which do NOT apply to Colab. Method note: web-search budget was exhausted this session, so 2025–2026 change-detection relied on the official FAQ fetched today plus best-effort GCP fetches; GCP credit amounts/eligibility could not be re-verified live (target pages 404'd or truncated), so treat those figures as approximate.

findings.name: Startup Program — Starter Tier: $1,000 free credits for pre-Series A startups
findings.detail: Read runpod.io/startup-program on 2026-10-22. Starter tier grants $1,000 in free credits with full platform access (Pods, Serverless, Clusters, Public Endpoints, Storage), self-serve onboarding, and 'Direct Support' from the Runpod team. Credits have no product-type limitations. Best fit stated as 'Pre-Series A startups with working products and near-term GPU needs.' The program is explicitly selective ('we can't accept every applicant').
findings.eligibility: Pre-Series A (earlier-stage) startups with a working product and near-term GPU needs. Page 'strongly prefers' venture backing (Seed–Series B+) with active investors validating traction/runway; pre-funding or bootstrapped applicants are steered to the self-serve platform instead. Must be new to Runpod (program 'primarily designed for new customers onboarding for the first time'), ready to onboard now (not 'in 6 months'), and have infrastructure as a current bottleneck. No .edu requirement, no stated region limit, no credit-card requirement stated on the page, and no published company-age cap (stage language only: 'Pre-Series A').
findings.claim: Click 'Apply now' on https://www.runpod.io/startup-program (self-serve form). Existing Runpod customers below the Growth threshold should contact their account manager or sales@runpod.io; rejected/non-applicant users can simply sign up for pay-as-you-go self-serve without applying.
findings.expiry: No stated expiration for Starter credits on the page (only the Growth tier's 12-month agreement is referenced). One-time program; no credit reload mentioned for Starter. Verify expiry in writing when the credits are granted — treat as finite, likely loaded as account credit.
findings.gotchas: Not for existing customers unless via account manager. 'Strongly preferred' VC backing means bootstrapped/pre-funding startups may be told to just use self-serve pay-as-you-go instead. Once credits run out it's pure pay-as-you-go with storage/effective costs: volume disks bill ~$0.10/GB/mo running and $0.20/GB/mo idle; stopped (not terminated) pods still bill container disk. Credits are platform-wide but not infinite runway — $1,000 covers e.g. ~300h on an H100 SXM at $3.99/hr.

findings.name: Startup Program — Growth Tier: $25,000 bonus credits on $50,000 committed spend (credit match, NOT free)
findings.detail: Depositing up to $50,000 towards a committed contract earns $25,000 in bonus credits ($75,000 total), usable across Pods, Serverless, or Clusters. 12-month agreement with dedicated onboarding call, enterprise-grade uptime/SLA options, and a 'Warm handoff to sales' Enterprise Path. Target: 'Series Seed–B+ startups spending (or ready to spend) $5K–$25K+/mo on GPU infrastructure.' Credits load immediately alongside the deposit; bonus is one-time, explicitly 'no credit reload.'
findings.eligibility: VC-backed Seed–B+ startups, new to Runpod, ready to onboard now, 'pre prepared to invest upfront for credit match,' open to enterprise conversation. No .edu or region requirements stated.
findings.claim: Same 'Apply now' CTA on https://www.runpod.io/startup-program; existing customers contact their account manager or sales@runpod.io.
findings.expiry: Credits loaded under a 12-month agreement; one-time bonus with no reload/renewal. No separate renewal track published.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free caveat: this is a 50% credit match on $50k committed spend, not a free offer — do not count it as free compute. Commitment is upfront and contracted. One-time only.

findings.name: No public student/.edu free offer — Academic Research program is institutional and sales-led
findings.detail: The pricing page (read 2026-10-22) shows no free tier, sign-up bonus, trial credits, or student discount anywhere. The Academic Research program targets universities, departments, and labs: lab/department-level projects prioritized, individual students/solo researchers only 'on a case-by-case basis,' access via institutional enrollment with university SSO integration, billing via custom invoicing aligned to academic calendars/grants/shared lab accounts, and manual application review with follow-up in 7-10 business days then a discovery call. No free GPU hours, no dollar-amount education discount, and no .edu sign-up-and-go tier is published.
findings.eligibility: Institutions (university SSO, grant/department funding) rather than individuals. No .edu free allocation; individuals only on a case-by-case basis.
findings.claim: Contact form or phone +1 (888) 478-6012 via https://www.runpod.io/academic-research ('Get in touch' / 'Request a demo').
findings.expiry: N/A — no published free/discounted terms to expire.
findings.gotchas: If the goal is free student compute, RunPod is a weak option versus Kaggle (free P100 notebook quota), HF Spaces, or Modal's up-to-$10k academic credits. Any education discount is negotiated, not self-serve; expect no public number.

findings.name: Partner/event-sponsored free compute (secondary, non-self-serve offers)
findings.detail: Several one-off free-compute offers around RunPod exist but are not standing self-serve programs: (1) Santa Cruz Accelerates 2025 cohort via Santa Cruz Works — eligible accelerator founders can apply for three tracks: up to 1,000 free H100 GPU hours, up to 1,000,000 free Serverless requests, or up to 750 free multi-node H100 compute hours (partner announcement, Jul 31, 2025). (2) $100 free GPU credits for ARC-AGI-2 participants (RunPod LinkedIn post, Mar 2025, application form, event-limited). (3) TreeHacks 2026 (Stanford, Oct 2026): RunPod donated $20k+ in credits to hackathon teams — sponsorship, not claimable by the public. Hackathons/events like these recur but each is separate and time-boxed.
findings.eligibility: Santa Cruz: founders enrolled in the Santa Cruz Accelerates 2025 cohort (apply through Santa Cruz Works or mention them on the referral form). ARC-AGI-2: participants of that specific challenge. TreeHacks: hackathon teams only.
findings.claim: Santa Cruz: apply through Santa Cruz Works (santacruzworks.org) or the RunPod referral form mentioning Santa Cruz Works. ARC-AGI-2: via the event application link. General: watch runpod.io/blog for current sponsorships.
findings.expiry: All time-boxed/cohort-specific (2025 cohort, 2025 challenge, 2026 event). Not renewable; likely expired or past for 2025 items as of 2026-10-22 unless re-run.
findings.gotchas: These do not constitute a recurring student/startup free tier; amounts are per-cohort/per-event and require the external partner's program eligibility, not just a RunPod account.

sunset_notes: No 2025-2026 sunset or material change of the RunPod Startup Program was found: the official page was live and verified on 2026-10-22 with the Starter $1,000 / Growth $25,000-match tiers matching prior public claims. No public sign-up bonus credits for regular users ever appeared on the pricing page, so there is nothing in that lane to sunset. Event-based free offers ($100 ARC-AGI-2 credits, Mar 2025; Santa Cruz Accelerates 2025 cohort; TreeHacks 2026 sponsorship) are time-boxed and effectively closed by 2026-10-22 unless re-announced. The second web-search on change-tracking hit the session search budget and did not complete, so pre-2026 history of the startup program's tiers is not independently cross-checked beyond the official page; re-verify tier amounts on the official page before relying on them.

findings.name: Starter free plan — $30/month free compute credits (no monthly fee)
findings.detail: Starter plan is "$0 + compute / month" and includes "$30 / month free credits" covering GPUs, CPUs and memory (per-second billing; e.g. H100 ~$0.001097/sec, L4 ~$0.000222/sec, CPU $0.0000131/core/sec). Included limits: 3 seats, 100 containers, 10 GPU concurrency, 5 deployed crons, 200 deployed apps, 1-day log retention, 1 TiB/month free network egress. $30 is roughly ~7.5 h H100 or ~37 h L4 GPU time. Usage above the credit is billed per second; nothing is billed at scale-to-zero. No one-time signup/trial credit exists — the $30 is the only free allotment (recurring monthly).
findings.eligibility: Everyone, no .edu or startup requirement, no funding/age caps. Region limits: none stated on the pricing page. Caveat: per official docs a payment method on file IS required to use Modal at all, so a card/paypal must be added even for the free tier (contradicts any 'no credit card' assumption).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at modal.com (GitHub, Google or SSO) — new workspaces start on Starter at $0/month. 2) Credits apply automatically to usage. 3) Optionally set a $30 spending limit to stay free. 4) Add a payment method in account settings (required by Modal docs).
findings.expiry: Recurring monthly allowance ('$30 / month'); page does not state rollover or a fixed expiry date.
findings.gotchas: Credit card/payments required on file even for free tier. Overage billed per-second; volumes >1 TiB cost $0.09/GiB/mo; egress >1 TiB costs $0.04/GiB; region pinning costs 1.15–1.75x base; non-preemptible execution 3x base; containers billed for 60s after last input. As of 1 Sep 2026 Shared Endpoints are billed per token from the first request (previously had a free-token allowance) — a 2026 change that adds costs on an otherwise free account. Containers minimum 0.125 cores / 128 MiB.

findings.name: Modal for Academics — up to $10,000 free compute credit grant (students/labs/researchers)
findings.detail: Official pricing page: "Graduate students, labs, and researchers can get up to $10k free compute credits". The academics landing page: "Unlock up to $10k of credits" to "Run workloads on B200s, H100s, and more without requesting quota", plus "Direct access to the Modal team of engineers and PhDs for research support". Award size is discretionary ('up to', not guaranteed); used for training/experiments on Modal's pay-per-second platform. Real-world use: cited by academic papers (e.g., the Forge/TMLR paper thanks Modal for academic credits).
findings.eligibility: Aimed at graduate students, academic labs, researchers (pricing-page audience line). The page itself states no hard .edu-only clause, no funding/age cap, no region limit; a valid academic email is the practical claim path (a third-party guide describes .edu/institutional email in the apply form — unverified on the official page, so treat .edu requirement as likely but not officially confirmed).
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://modal.com/academics. 2) Click 'Sign up to hear about our grant programs' (anchor /academics#apply) — this is a mailing-list/apply form (fields not rendered in the fetched page). 3) Modal contacts eligible applicants for the next grant cycle; a modal.com account (with payment method on file, per docs) is needed to use the credits. Educators can also email partnerships@modal.com for course integration (per third-party guide).
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page — no grant-cycle dates, deadline, or credit-expiry window is published. A third-party tracker (Token Thrift) lists 'no expiry date' but that is not official. Treat award duration as unknown and confirm at award time.
findings.gotchas: This is a grant Modal selects, not a self-service education license: eligibility is 'decided by Modal'. 'Up to $10k' — actual amount varies. No official statement that .edu email is required; the apply form is a waitlist-style signup. Payment method still required on the Modal account. Stacking behavior with the $30/month Starter credits or startup credits is not documented.

findings.name: Modal for Startups — tiered one-time free compute-credit grants (seed→Series A and Series B+)
findings.detail: Official startups page: two tiers, one-time credit grants for customers new to Modal. Tier 1 (Seed to Series A): eligible if you 'Raised any amount of VC funding from our VC partner network' OR 'Raised VC funding >$1m from any fund'. Tier 2 (Scaling / Series B+): 'Custom for rapidly growing AI-native companies' — 'Raised VC funding > $30m or post-series B' and the VC must be in Modal's partner network. The page says 'Unlock thousands of free GPU credits' but does not publish per-tier dollar amounts (the '>$1m' figures are funding thresholds, not credit caps). VC partner network listed: Y Combinator, a16z, Sequoia, Khosla Ventures, Neo, HF0, Pear VC, Lux Capital. Extras beyond credits: 'Direct access to Modal's engineering team for technical support and GTM amplification on launches and raises' and a founder network with online/in-person events.
findings.eligibility: Must be a new-to-Modal customer meeting a funding-stage criterion (Tier 1: any VC funding from the partner network, or >$1m VC from any fund; Tier 2: >$30m or post-Series B with partner-network VC). No startup-age cutoff, total-funding cap, or region limit is stated on the page.
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://modal.com/startups. 2) Click 'Apply Now' (form at /startups#apply; form fields not rendered in the fetched page). 3) VC funds can separately apply to join the partner network via a dedicated form. 4) Credits are applied to your Modal account; a payment method must be on file per docs.
findings.expiry: Credits are 'a one-time grant and you may not reapply once you have received credits in a given tier' (reapplication across tiers is not explicitly ruled out). A FAQ heading 'How long do my credits last? Can they be reinstated if they expire?' exists but its answer is not rendered on the fetched page, so the expiry window is unpublished.
findings.gotchas: Dollar amounts are discretionary and unpublished — 'thousands of' credits, not a fixed number. No reapply within the same tier. The FAQ on credit duration/reinstatement is not publicly readable in page text; ask Modal at application. Credits offset compute usage but CPU/memory/egress/volume multipliers (3x non-preemptible, 1.15–1.75x region pinning, $0.04/GiB egress beyond allowance) still apply. Separate AWS Activate add-on credits may stack (see next finding).

findings.name: AWS Activate partnership — additional Modal credits for eligible startups
findings.detail: From the official pricing-page FAQ: 'we have a special partnership with AWS that allows eligible startups to unlock additional Modal credits if they are part of AWS Activate.' No dollar amount or eligibility beyond AWS Activate membership is stated on the page.
findings.eligibility: Startups that are part of AWS Activate; final eligibility 'decided by Modal' per the pricing page's program section. No .edu, age, or region limits stated.
findings.claim: 1) Be/qualify for AWS Activate (AWS's own program). 2) Apply via Modal (startups page or by contacting Modal) — the pricing FAQ does not publish a separate form URL; /startups#apply or support are the paths. 3) Credits appear on your Modal account.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page.
findings.gotchas: Amounts unpublished and discretionary; confirm with Modal that they stack with the startup-tier grant. AWS/GCP/Azure credits of the cloud providers themselves 'cannot be applied towards your Modal usage' (pricing FAQ) — only Modal-issued credits count.

findings.name: Team plan — $100/month free credits on a $250/month paid plan (context, not a student offer)
findings.detail: Team plan: '$250 + compute / month' and includes '$100 / month free credits', 5000 containers, 50 GPU concurrency, unlimited crons, 30-day log retention. Listed for completeness of every free-credit mechanism; it is a paid plan, so not a free offer for students/startups unless funded by a grant.
findings.eligibility: All paying customers; no student/startup-specific eligibility. Not a free offer in itself.
findings.claim: Upgrade a workspace to Team in the dashboard; the $100/month credit is included automatically in the $250 base fee.
findings.expiry: Recurring monthly; base fee charged even in quiet months.
findings.gotchas: The $100 credit does not offset the $250 base fee — it only covers usage beyond plan limits; a third-party guide (Codeables) even misstates this, so rely on the official pricing page. Enterprise plan is custom and adds volume discounts rather than free credits.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22 no student/startup free program was found to be sunset: the $30/month Starter free credits, the up-to-$10k academic grant, the tiered startup credit program, and the AWS Activate add-on are all live on official pages read today. Changes found: (1) Shared Endpoints moved to per-token billing from the first request, effective 1 Sep 2026 (pricing page) — this removes a former free-token allowance and is the most material 2026 change for free-tier users; (2) 2025–2026 changelog page 1 (Sep–Oct 2026) shows no credit-tier, startup-program, or academic-program changes or sunsets. Not verified (could not rule out): a one-time signup/trial credit — no such credit appears on any official page today; a third-party guide's claim of '$1 at signup + $29 after adding a payment method, $0.50 one-time fee' is unverified and contradicts the official '$30/month' wording, treat as unreliable. Also unverifiable from fetched pages: exact academic grant cycle timing/expiry, per-tier startup credit dollar amounts, and whether .edu email is formally required for the academic grant (likely in practice, not stated on the official page).

provider: Lightning AI (Studios / AI Studio) — Free plan

findings.name: Free plan: 1 free CPU Studio + up to 30 one-time free credits (~80 GPU hours on interruptible machines)
findings.detail: $0/mo tier aimed at "students, researchers, hobbyists." Included: 1 free active CPU Studio (up to 32 cores; runs 24/7 but requires a restart every 4 hours), 32-core CPU Studios, single-GPU Studios (L40S, A100, H100, H200, T4, L4, RTX PRO 6000), up to 2 concurrent GPUs, 80% discount on interruptible (spot) instances, unlimited inactive Studios, unlimited background execution, connect any local IDE or SSH, multiplayer live collaboration, secrets management + E2E encryption, 15 req/min and 120,000 tok/min to Lightning model APIs. Credits: "You get 5 free Lightning credits upon registration. Add a card for 25 more" (1 credit = $1 USD) = up to 30 free credits, which the pricing page says "gets you ~80 GPU hours on interruptible machines." Per-GPU free-hours table on pricing page: T4 75, L4 31, A100 40GB 10, A100 80GB 5, L40S 5, RTX PRO 6000 2; H100/H200 show no free hours. Persistent storage: official pricing table lists a 200 GB limit for Free (third-party checks still say 50 GB — see gotchas). All GPUs across AWS/GCP/Lightning/Nebius/Lambda/NScale.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone. No credit card required for the base tier, but 25 of the up-to-30 credits are only unlocked by adding a card. A phone number is required at signup ("to prevent abuse of the platform"). Region: official docs state "Lightning AI is not available in every country"; no published country list.
findings.claim: 1) Create an account at lightning.ai (email, Google, GitHub, or SSO) — no card needed. 2) Verify your phone number; this is what unlocks the free credits/GPU hours (docs: "Verify your phone number to receive up to 80 free GPU hours to start"). 3) Start a Studio — it boots on a free CPU instance by default; install deps there, switch to GPU only when needed. 4) Optional: add a payment card to receive the extra 25 credits (up to 30 total).
findings.expiry: The credit grant is a one-time registration grant (5 on sign-up, 25 after adding a card); unused credits expire 12 months from issuance (purchased credits also expire 12 months from purchase). The free CPU Studio's 4-hour restart cycle repeats indefinitely — no end date published.
findings.gotchas: "Known so far" said "30 free credits/month" — the official page today does NOT say monthly; it is up to 30 one-time credits (5 + 25-with-card). Some third-party sources (codeables.dev 2026-03, a GitHub doc) still claim 15 credits topped up monthly on the free plan; the billing FAQ now describes free credits only as "promotional, non-transferable, and do not accumulate," with no quantified monthly amount. Beyond the credits everything is pay-as-you-go (GPUs billed per second, storage per day). Free GPUs are interruptible/preemptible. Free-tier API caps: 15 req/min, 120k tok/min. Session caps: A100/H100/H200 sessions limited to 4h; T4/L4/L40S unlimited. Storage limit inconsistent between sources (official table: 200 GB; aifree.dev person-verified 2026-10-12 and AILookup: 50 GB) — verify in-dashboard. Free credits are "promotional" and Lightning "may change or limit free credit grants, eligibility, usage rules, or expiration terms at any time." No multi-node training, no multi-GPU per Studio, no SAML/SSO, no uptime SLA on Free.

findings.name: Academic tier (education license): 80% off list price for first 48 months, requires academic email
findings.detail: Lightning AI offers a discounted academic Pro tier: "80% off the list price for your first 48 months, billed annually." Standard Pro is $50/month; academic pricing shows ~$9.99–$10/month billed annually, with 100 annual credits, 30 req/min and 150,000 tok/min model-API limits, unlimited background execution, multi-node training and up to 4 concurrent GPUs (per third-party listings). Students ALSO keep the full free tier: "All verified users get free credits for GPU workloads plus a free CPU studio." If your class/lab's institution already pays for Lightning AI, the org admin can assign you one of its academic seats instead of buying your own.
findings.eligibility: Requires an academic email address on your account (e.g., .edu or institutional email). No funding/age constraints — it is an education license, not a startup program. No credit card needed to use the free tier, but the academic Pro tier itself is a paid plan (billed annually).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up / sign in to lightning.ai with your academic email (faster verification per docs). 2) On the pricing page, toggle 'Academic pricing' to see the discounted tier, or contact support to apply. 3) Alternatively, ask your instructor to create a Lightning organization for the class and add seats/credits there — "most universities have cloud credits and budgets they can use for classes through Lightning AI."
findings.expiry: Discount lasts the first 48 months, billed annually; the docs do not state whether the same rate renews after 48 months. Credits attached to plans (incl. the 100 annual academic credits) expire after 12 months. The 4-hour free CPU-Studio restart mechanism has no stated cap.
findings.gotchas: This is a DISCOUNT, not a free offer — Academic Pro still costs ~$10/mo billed annually. The dedicated marketing page lightning.ai/academia currently returns HTTP 404; the offer lives in the docs (docs/platform/overview/setups/academia and .../students) and the pricing page's 'Academic pricing' toggle. Exact monthly price varies slightly across sources ($9.99 vs $10/mo). A 2023 forum thread shows free credits were sometimes not auto-deposited for .edu accounts (had to be manually sorted by support) — if the 5 signup credits don't appear, contact support@lightning.ai.

findings.name: Startup program: free-to-start orgs + partner offers (Y Combinator $5K credits, NVIDIA Inception 80% off)
findings.detail: Official startup docs: creating a Lightning organization costs nothing ("There is no cost to create a new organization"), pay-as-you-go from the first second, each member gets a free CPU Studio and a free teamspace, and orgs can connect their own AWS/GCP accounts to run on their own startup cloud credits (free BYO-credits path). The pricing page states "Startup and academic pricing available" (by contact; no published startup-credit amount). Y Combinator partner page: YC program members get 3 Enterprise-tier seats (stated $30K value), $5,000 in Lightning AI compute credits ($5K value), and $5,000 of platform onboarding/support ($5K value) — BUT this "requires $20K annual contract," so it is a discounted paid deal, not a free grant. NVIDIA Inception partnership (announced by co-founder William Falcon, 2025-03-25): 80% discount on the Enterprise tier for NVIDIA Inception member startups (example given: $50K subscription for $10K) plus expert access.
findings.eligibility: Official startup docs state NO published requirements — no funding cap, no company-age limit, no VC-backing requirement; any startup can create a free org and pay as it goes. Third-party directories (startupperks.co, aifree.dev) additionally claim startups must "verify company details (age, funding, or website)" — this is NOT stated on the official startups docs page, so treat it as unverified. YC offer: must be a Y Combinator program member; NVIDIA offer: must be an NVIDIA Inception member.
findings.claim: Free path: 1) Create a Lightning AI organization (org title in top-left sidebar > 'New Organization' — takes under 10 minutes, free). 2) Invite team members; each gets a teamspace. 3) Optionally add a private AWS/GCP cloud account to consume your own startup cloud credits (AWS Activate / GCP for Startups credits). 4) For extra startup pricing/credits, contact Lightning AI via the pricing page's 'Startup and academic pricing available' link. YC offer: apply through YC partner channel and 'log in to claim'; NVIDIA Inception: claim via the Inception program portal.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no sunset date published for the free-to-start org model or the partner offers. YC and NVIDIA Inception deals are subject to each program's own renewal terms (not published on Lightning's pages).
findings.gotchas: The headline YC '$5K in compute credits' is conditional on a $20K annual contract — effectively a 20%-of-cost rebate, not free. No public, no-string-attached dollar-amount free-credit grant for startups exists on official pages (unlike free-tier users' 5/30 credits). "Startup pricing" means discounted paid plans by inquiry, not published free credits. Free-tier caveats still apply to any startup account (4h Studio restarts, interruptible GPUs, pay-as-you-go beyond credits).

sunset_notes: 1) The \"Known so far\" figure of \"up to 30 free credits/MONTH\" is no longer what the official pricing page says (checked 2026-10-22): credits are a one-time grant of 5 at registration + 25 after adding a card (up to 30 total), expiring in 12 months. The older \"15 monthly Lightning credits included\" free-plan model (visible in the Sept-2024 SaaSworthy snapshot and 2023 forum threads) was a monthly allowance; the billing FAQ now describes free credits only as \"promotional, non-transferable, and do not accumulate\" without a monthly amount, and some 2026 third-party write-ups (codeables.dev, a GitHub repo doc) still claim 15/month — that monthly figure is unconfirmed on any official page read today. 2) Storage: \"50 GB persistent storage\" (known-so-far and still the figure on aifree.dev, person-verified 2026-10-12, and AILookup) conflicts with today's official pricing table, which lists a 200 GB persistent-storage limit for the Free plan — possibly a 2025-2026 change or a limit-vs-included distinction; verify in-dashboard. 3) The dedicated education marketing page lightning.ai/academia now 404s; the academic offer was consolidated into the docs tree (lightning.ai/docs/platform/overview/setups/academia[/students]). 4) No region limits are published beyond \"Lightning AI is not available in every country\". 5) lightning.ai was showing a global-outage banner (status.lightning.ai) at read time; all pages above still returned content. No startup free-credit grant was found to have been sunset — Lightning has no public fixed-amount startup credit program to begin with; the closest offers (YC $5K + $30K seats contingent on a $20K contract; NVIDIA Inception 80% Enterprise discount) are partner deals, not free programs.

findings.claim: Sign up free at paperspace.com ('Sign up free', or via the Notebooks page 'Sign up with Google/GitHub'), open a private workspace (individual plan), create a Gradient Notebook, choose a pre-built runtime template, select the Free GPU (M4000) machine type, and launch. No payment step.
findings.detail: Open free tier on Paperspace Gradient: $0/month, includes 'Basic' free instances — Free GPU (M4000, 8 GB VRAM, 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM, Maxwell/2015, $0.45/hr if billed) and Free CPU (C4). Docs (verified 13 Jul 2026): free machines can only be used for Notebooks in private workspaces; Free plan includes 5 GB persistent storage. Free-tier auto-shutdown max is 6 hours per the official docs (the pricing page shows 'Auto-shutdown (12 hour limit)'); only 1 free machine runs at a time; free capacity is a shared, non-guaranteed pool (free notebooks can sit Pending in queue). Public projects/notebooks only — no private projects on the Free plan. Upgrade path: Pro $8/mo individual (adds Free P4000/P5000/RTX4000/RTX5000/A4000, 15 GB storage) and Growth $39/mo (adds Free A5000/A6000/A100-80G, 50 GB storage).
findings.eligibility: Open to all new users; no .edu email, student status, or startup criteria; no credit card required for the Free plan (official sign-up says 'Create a free account'; card only needed for paid instance usage or paid plans). Not student/startup-specific — a general consumer free tier.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal — the Free plan is permanent at $0 while account is active. Overage model, not a trial: storage over $5 GB is billed $0.29/GB/month; running paid instance types bills hourly. Free-plan cap applies; upgrade to Pro/Growth to unlock more free GPU SKUs.
findings.gotchas: M4000 is a 2015 Maxwell card — slow for serious training; 8 GB VRAM. Free notebooks are public only (no private projects), 1 running free notebook at a time, capacity is best-effort (queue/Pending possible), session auto-shutdown max 6h per docs (pricing page says 12h — treat as ~half-day sessions). 'Free' is free-tier, not trial-with-expires: paid instances and storage overage are real charges, and the platform has no refunds. No capacity guarantee and free-tier storage is exclusive per region. Free-machine use is limited to Notebooks, not raw Machines/Deployments.
findings.name: Gradient Free plan — free GPU notebook (M4000) for any new user

findings.claim: Create a free Gradient account, start on the $0 team T0 plan via the pricing page ('Start Now'), invite collaborators to the team to use the 10-notebook allowance.
findings.detail: Free team-tier plan: $0 base + utilization on paid instance types. 10 total notebooks, max 1 running at a time, 'Low' instance types only, public notebooks only, 10 GB persistent storage included ($0.29/GB/month overage), 12-hour auto-shutdown limit. Private workspace and team(s) are billed separately.
findings.eligibility: Any small team; no education/startup restrictions noted on the pricing page. Free sign-up; card needed only for paid utilization.
findings.expiry: No expiry/renewal; ongoing $0 base with pay-per-use overage. Cancellable any time from console settings.
findings.gotchas: No free GPU entitlement is documented for T0 — the listed 'Low' instance types map to the paid 'Low' tier (C5/C7 CPU, P4000/RTX4000/A4000 GPU), which is card-on-file territory, so T0 mostly gives free CPU/low-tier access; the free M4000 GPU is tied to individual Free/Pro/Growth G-plan workspaces. Overage storage at $0.29/GB adds up; public notebooks only; no refunds on the platform.
findings.name: Gradient T0 Team plan — $0 team notebook workspace (10 notebooks)

findings.claim: Apply through an affiliated accelerator/incubator/VC if listed in their partner program, otherwise complete the application on the DigitalOcean Startups page (TypeForm, select 'Other' as affiliated org); on acceptance a 'Welcome Kit' delivers the credits.
findings.detail: Startups receive DigitalOcean cloud credits for a 12-month period; the amount varies by partner/tier, with a $10,000 monthly credit-usage cap (overage billed), plus 15 months of free Standard support. Credits flow through an approved partner (accelerator/incubator/VC on their partner list) or a direct application via their TypeForm with 'Other' organization. Partner perks add up (e.g. Stripe Atlas 20% off, QuickNode up to $5k, Cloud66 $500). Program now prioritizes AI-native startups; unused credits are forfeited, no extensions.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage company, $10M or less raised total; must have a company website, a matching corporate email, and a registered DigitalOcean team account with a valid credit card. Service-based startups (agencies, consultancies) excluded. Not aimed at students; no .edu requirement.
findings.expiry: Credits usable for 12 months from grant; $10k/month cap; unused credits forfeit at end of period. No renewals.
findings.gotchas: Critical for this task: the program FAQ explicitly EXCLUDES Paperspace Machines (and GPU Droplets, H100 GPU Kubernetes, bare-metal GPUs, inference, third-party frontier models) from 'Qualifying Program Services' — GPU credits are a separate, non-guaranteed benefit. So Hatch does NOT reliably buy free Paperspace compute; it credits DigitalOcean core services (Droplets, Spaces, etc.). Card required on the DO team account; no crypto mining; no transfer of credits.
findings.name: DigitalOcean Startups ('Hatch') program — cloud credits, but Paperspace GPUs excluded

Historically Paperspace's education story was fast.ai course runtimes inside free-tier notebooks; that is a feature, not a funded license.
findings.eligibility: n/a — no program exists to claim. Students get the same open Free plan as any user (free M4000 GPU notebook, no card, no .edu verification).
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Do not treat the general Free plan as an 'education license' — it has the same non-guaranteed free capacity and public-only notebooks for everyone. If an edu program existed it would be a distinct finding; it does not appear to currently.

provider: Paperspace (DigitalOcean) — Gradient Free Plan, Notebooks & GPU Compute
sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: (1) No Paperspace-specific 2025/2026 program changes found — the public changelog (updates.paperspace.com) shows no 2025-2026 entries on the landing page (last visible 2023-12) and the docs are current as of 2026-07-13 with the Free-tier M4000/GPU+ offering still listed, so the Gradient Free plan appears still live. (3) DigitalOcean's Startups/Hatch program has repositioned to prioritize AI-native startups but continues to EXCLUDE Paperspace Machines from qualifying services — so even though the task frames 'startup program' for Paperspace free compute, the only startup-credit vehicle is generic DO credits that do not cover GPU/Paperspace usage. (4) The old Paperspace referral program (free GPU hours for friend referrals, linked in older page footers) has no live page — paperspace.com/referral is 404; treat as sunset. findings.name: llama.cpp itself — free open-source local engine (no hosted offer)
findings.detail: llama.cpp is an MIT-licensed C/C++ library for LLM/VLM inference and training. It is $0 to use with unlimited local use and commercial use; there is NO free tier, trial credits, startup program, or education license, because llama.cpp is a self-hosted library, not a cloud/compute provider. The only cost is the hardware you run it on (consumer GPU/CPU; GPU backends CUDA/ROCm/Vulkan/Metal) plus any cloud GPU you rent to host it. This is the accurate core answer to 'does llama.cpp offer free compute to students/startups?' — the software is free, but no hosted free-compute offer exists from it.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, no account, no .edu, no credit card, no region limit; bounded only by your own hardware. No student/startup-specific program exists for the llama.cpp project.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Download a prebuilt binary or build from source at github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp (or Docker). License text: github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/LICENSE (MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2023-2026 The ggml authors').
findings.gotchas: Costs shift to hardware: 20–100GB+ model storage, GPU compute, electricity; idle always-on cloud GPUs still bill (~$400–450/mo T4 at startup scale per third-party analysis). Free software does not mean free compute. No training-notebook front is hosted by llama.cpp.

findings.name: Meta Llama Startup Program (adjacent — for the Llama MODEL, not llama.cpp)
findings.detail: Meta's program reimburses early-stage US startups for using Meta's open-weight Llama models via hosted APIs on cloud inference providers: up to $6,000 USD/month for up to 6 months = up to $36,000 total, plus hands-on technical support from the Llama team. This is a REIMBURSEMENT of actual Llama API spend, not a grant, and it funds the Llama model ecosystem — it is distinct from the llama.cpp library.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups incorporated in the United States; raised less than $10M USD; at least one developer on staff. Target industries: tech/software, financial services, healthcare/life sciences, telecom, retail/eCommerce. US-only (no EU/Canada). No .edu required (not a student offer).
findings.claim: Apply via the Meta Llama Startup Program page (go.fb.me / lnkd.in links from the 2025-05-21 announcement). Selected members receive monthly reimbursements up to the $6K cap over up to 6 months.
findings.expiry: Initial-cohort applications closed 2025-05-30 (6:00pm PT); first cohort announced 2025-06-17 (~1,000+ applications). Per-member reimbursement window is up to 6 months. As of 2026-10-22 there is NO official confirmation the program has reopened; a third-party aggregator (grantedai.com) lists it 'Active / check source'.
findings.gotchas: Reimbursement only for hosted Llama API costs (not on-prem/llama.cpp self-host, not training infra) — so it does not offset llama.cpp local runs. Monthly cap is 'up to' $6K, not guaranteed. US-only and <$10M funded; no new-cohort confirmation found for late 2026. Feedback on Llama is implicitly expected in exchange.

findings.name: AWS + Meta 'Building with Llama' program (adjacent — Llama model on AWS)
findings.detail: A 6-month virtual program co-run by AWS and Meta for ~30 promising US startups building with Llama. Offer: up to $200,000 in AWS promotional credits, plus office hours with Meta/AWS engineers, dedicated Meta Discord, AWS Solution Architect access, and model customization/inference guidance. Distinct from the smaller Meta Llama Startup Program and from llama.cpp.
findings.eligibility: US-based startups that have raised money, less than 10 years old, available for a 6-month virtual program. Selected startups must enroll in AWS Activate to draw the credits. No .edu (startup, not student, offer).
findings.claim: Apply through the AWS Startups 'Building with Llama' landing page; selected startups sign up for AWS Activate and receive up to $200K promotional credits over the 6-month build window.
findings.expiry: Announced 2025-07-21; applications due 2025-08-08, AWS notified selectees by 2025-08-29; a single cohort of ~30 US startups. Landing page still live but this was a cohort-specific program; no confirmed 2026 re-open.
findings.gotchas: Credits are AWS promotional (consumable against AWS usage, not cash), require AWS Activate enrollment, and are gated by selection (30 spots). The direct AWS page could not be re-fetched today (network block); terms verified via official page snippet + Meta blog. Credits expire per AWS promotional-credit terms; does not fund self-hosted llama.cpp compute.

sunset_notes: llama.cpp (the named provider) has NOT sunset and is not a compute vendor: it remains free, MIT-licensed, with unlimited local use; there is no free tier, trial credits, student/education offer, or startup program to sunset — those categories simply do not apply to a self-hosted library. The 'free-compute' offers people associate with the 'Llama' name in 2025-2026 belong to Meta's Llama model and its cloud partners, NOT to llama.cpp: (1) Meta Llama Startup Program ($6,000/mo up to 6 months = $36K reimbursement) — initial cohort closed 2025-05-30; no official confirmation it reopened as of 2026-10-22 (third-party aggregators list it 'Active, check source'). (2) AWS + Meta 'Building with Llama' (up to $200K AWS credits, 6-month, ~30 US startups) — cohort applications due 2025-08-08, a cohort-specific offering. Both are startup (US, funded/<$10M or <10 yrs old) programs tied to the Llama model ecosystem, not llama.cpp; neither is a .edu student offer. Key disambiguation to carry forward: llama.cpp = local engine; the credit programs = Meta Llama model via cloud APIs/GPU, so they do not reimburse local llama.cpp runs. AWS 'Building with Llama' page was network-blocked today, so its current enrollment status is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: Apply via the TypeForm linked on https://lambda.ai/research ("Apply for a grant" / "Apply now"), form ID form.typeform.com/to/Wn8YWMIj. No account or payment info is asked at the form level as far as the public page shows; Lambda contact/sales ("Talk to our team") handles the rest.
findings.detail: Lambda Research Grant: up to $5,000 in Lambda cloud (GPU) credits for developing and showcasing research work on Lambda Instances. Rolling, competitive; select accepted projects get featured on lambda.ai. The page markets the grant as backing named research efforts ("Breakthroughs backed by Lambda"). Official pages read today: https://lambda.ai/research (amount + application link), https://lambda.ai/pricing (no other free offers), https://lambda.ai/instances (no startup/student program), https://lambda.ai/legal/terms-of-service (credit terms).
findings.eligibility: Page states only "qualifying researchers" — no explicit .edu requirement, student-vs-postdoc distinction, startup criteria, funding cap, or region limits are published on the page. Selection is competitive/discretionary. The "Startups and Researchers" nav label on the homepage simply routes to /instances; it is a product audience segment, not a program with benefits.
findings.expiry: No application deadline or program end date published (rolling intake). Per Lambda Cloud Terms of Service, issued credits expire 12 months from issuance unless the credit instrument states an earlier date, and Lambda may revoke or expire credits at any time for any or no reason.
findings.gotchas: Credits have no cash value, are non-transferable, and can be revoked early (ToS §3d). A payment method is required on the account generally (ToS Hardware §7.2: valid credit card or accepted payment method), so the grant is compute offset, not a card-free account. Mentorship mentioned in prior notes is NOT stated on the current public page — only "featured on our website" is promised. Web search was unavailable in this run, so 2025-2026 program changes/sunsets of any earlier Lambda startup program or trial-credit offers could not be independently verified; only live-page evidence is reported.
findings.name: Lambda Research Grant (up to $5,000 GPU cloud credits for researchers)

findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Event giveaways are one-off and attendee-restricted; the only standing free compute path for students/researchers is the Research Grant.
findings.detail: Verified absence of standing free offers: the pricing page lists only on-demand per-GPU-hour rates (e.g., H100 SXM $3.99/GPU-hr, B200 $6.69/GPU-hr, A100-40GB $1.99, A10 $1.29, "plus applicable sales tax/VAT/GST") with no free tier, trial credits, education license, or startup credit program. /startups, /education, /labs all return HTTP 404. Sign-up (cloud.lambda.ai) is app-rendered and blocked direct inspection (403); no promotion is advertised on the homepage or pricing page. The only "free" mechanisms found: (a) ToS-permitted Beta Services offered "at no additional charge" while designated beta (trial expires at the earlier of 1 year or Lambda's written date), and (b) one-off event giveaways on lambda.ai (AI Infra Summit Giveaway 2026, 2026 GTC Berlin Giveaway, 2025 Microsoft Ignite Cloud Credit Giveaway) — attendee/contest-style, not standing programs for students or startups. Free educational resources (deep learning curriculum, Open-Sora/diffusion notebooks, Lambda Stack software) are content, not compute credits. Marketing note: instances advertise "no egress fees", which is a cost perk, not a free offer.
findings.eligibility: n/a — this finding documents that no free tier, trial credit, startup program, or education license exists as of 2026-10-22 outside the Research Grant.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Beta-service free access ends when a feature leaves beta or at the 1-year trial cap. Event giveaway pages may be stale by the time you read them. Because search was unavailable, if a legacy startup program existed pre-2025 I could not confirm its status; the 404s on /startups and /labs plus the absence on pricing indicate it is not currently offered.
findings.name: No standing free tier, trial credits, startup program, or education license (verified absence)

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, the only standing free compute offer on lambda.ai is the Research Grant (up to $5,000 credits, rolling/competitive). No dedicated startup program, student/education program, or free tier is currently published: /startups, /education, and /labs all 404, and pricing/instances/homepage show no audience-specific discounts. \"Startups and Researchers\" is only a navigation label to /instances. One-off event credit giveaways exist (2025 Microsoft Ignite, 2026 GTC Berlin, AI Infra Summit 2026) but are contest/attendee events, not standing student/startup programs. Caveat: the web-search budget was exhausted during this run, so historical sunsets of any earlier Lambda startup or trial-credit programs in 2025-2026 could not be independently confirmed; the absence conclusion is based on live official pages read today plus the 404s. Per ToS, all Lambda credits (including grant credits) are non-cash, non-transferable, revocable, and default to a 12-month expiry from issuance unless stated earlier.

findings.name: Camber Student plan via GitHub Student Developer Pack (monthly free compute)
findings.detail: Free Camber Student plan while enrolled: 40 CPU hours/month, 5 GPU hours/month, 50 GB storage, 50 agent messages/month. Runs on Camber's agentic AI data-science platform (connect Postgres/Trino/S3, build agents, run from Cursor or Claude Code via Camber MCP server). Verified verbatim on the official pack page today ([education.github.com/pack](https://education.github.com/pack)) and in the [SDP changelog](https://github.com/github-education-resources/Student-Developer-Pack-Current-Partners-FAQ/blob/main/SDP-changelog.md) entry of 2026-08-20. Claim: (1) verify in GitHub Education (school-issued email and/or dated proof of enrollment, 13+, enrolled in a degree/diploma program); (2) open [Camber's student pack page](https://www.cambercloud.com/github-student-pack); (3) click 'Sign-up with GitHub' (→ app.cambercloud.com/login/github) using the GitHub account that holds the verified pack; (4) confirm the Student plan quotas in the dashboard. Camber's own page repeats the offer but not the numbers — the numbers come from GitHub's pack page.

findings.claim: Verify GitHub Student Developer Pack → visit cambercloud.com/github-student-pack → 'Sign-up with GitHub' with the verified account → Student plan activates with the monthly quotas.
