findings.name: Free desktop app (LM Studio + Bionic) — unlimited local inference at $0
findings.detail: Official pricing page (lmstudio.ai/pricing, verified 2026-10-22): Free tier at $0 includes Bionic Agent, running local LLMs via llama.cpp and MLX, offline voice transcription, LM Link for up to 5 devices, and 'limited web search.' The classic LM Studio app also serves an OpenAI-compatible local server on port 1234 (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, etc.), so local inference is unlimited and $0. Paid tiers are Bionic+ $20/mo (US-hosted open models: Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4 Flash; discounted bulk tokens; full web search + page extraction) and Pro $100/mo (5x usage limits, early access). Cloud models beyond plan allowances are prepaid 'cloud credits' billed per million tokens, roughly $0.13–$15.00/M tokens depending on model (per-model rates, e.g., DeepSeek V4 Flash $0.13 in/$0.26 out; Kimi K3 $3 in/$15 out).
findings.eligibility: No .edu email, no startup age or funding cap, no application of any kind. No account and no credit card are required for local models or LM Link remote-model use (docs: 'Local and LM Link models do not use Bionic cloud credits, and can be used without an LM Studio account'). Cloud models require a signed-in account with billing set up. No region limits on local use; cloud inference is US-hosted with Zero Data Retention.
findings.claim: Download from https://lmstudio.ai/download (homepage link 'Download LM Studio Bionic'). No sign-up for the local workflow. For cloud models: Settings → Account → Sign in, then add credits under Cloud Inference on the LM Studio Hub. Plan changes managed from the dashboard.
findings.expiry: No expiry — free terms effective since the 2025-07-08 terms change; renewal is automatic (nothing to renew). Free web-search allowance on the Free plan is 'limited' with no published cap; the forthcoming 'Bionic Pass' (announced, pricing unpublished as of Oct 2026) may alter cloud allowances.
findings.gotchas: Free = software fee only: you still pay for hardware, GPU/RAM, and electricity for local inference. 'Limited web search' cap is not quantified. 'Bionic' public download currently lists Windows; a Linux Bionic build is unconfirmed on LM Studio's own pages (LM Studio proper supports macOS/Windows/Linux, 16GB+ RAM and 4GB+ VRAM recommended). Paid Teams/Enterprise features (SSO, model/MCP gating, private collaboration) are not in the Free tier; team billing is via paid organization credits.

findings.name: Free for work and school — de-facto free startup/education license (terms change 2025-07-08)
findings.detail: LM Studio removed the requirement that companies/organizations obtain a separate commercial license. Since 2025-07-08 the app terms allow free use at home, work, school, or anywhere, so startups and academic institutions can adopt it with no procurement, no form, and no license purchase. Fortune 500 companies and universities are already on the paid Enterprise track, but standard app use needs nothing.
findings.eligibility: Any individual, company, startup, or school — no minimum/maximum company age, no funding cap, no .edu verification, no region limits.
findings.claim: Automatic — nothing to claim. Just download the app; the updated app terms apply on use.
findings.expiry: Indefinite under current terms; no sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Covers the app; redistribution/rehosting and team control features (SSO, gating, private collaboration) are the paid Enterprise/Teams boundary. Model licenses (open-weight models downloaded via the app) still need their own license review.

findings.name: Free public Hub organization for teams (2025-07)
findings.detail: Announced alongside the free-for-work change: teams can create a public Hub organization to share LM Studio 'stuff' (models, presets, MCPs, configurations) for free, usable at work or school. Private/team-only sharing of artifacts is the paid boundary ('simple self-serve Teams plan' announced for late 2025; as of the 2026-10 pricing page, teams use centralized billing via organization inference credits and 'Subscription plans for teams [are] coming soon').
findings.eligibility: Any team size; no funding/age caps stated; no .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Create a public Hub organization in the LM Studio Hub (hub.lmstudio.ai / account after signing in).
findings.expiry: No expiry published for public organizations.
findings.gotchas: Public orgs are visible; private collaboration, SSO and model/MCP gating are Enterprise (sales-priced, no public rate card).

findings.name: No startup program, no education license, no trial credits (absence finding)
findings.detail: There is no dedicated student plan, academic discount, startup credits program, or free trial of cloud inference from LM Studio. The official pricing and enterprise pages carry no education/startup tier. The only free offer is the app itself (unlimited local inference + limited free web search). A third-party tracker (noizz.io, 'LM Studio for Startups', checked 2026-09-23) explicitly states 'No startup program'; hokai.io (checked 2026-10-05) confirms Free/Bionic+($20)/Pro($100) with free local use and no quotas on local runs.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no program exists to be eligible for. For cloud inference there are no free trial credits; paid prepaid credits are required (cheapest hosted model DeepSeek V4 Flash from ~$0.13/M input tokens).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Students/startups get the same Free plan as everyone else; the 'free offer' is the app.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: If the expectation was a hosted free tier (like a 12-month startup credit at a cloud GPU provider), it does not exist here — the 'free compute' is the user's own hardware. Cloud overage/egress: prepaid cloud credits, per-model per-token rates, US-hosted ZDR; Bionic Pass pricing unpublished.

sunset_notes: No LM Studio program was sunset or removed in 2025–2026; the opposite happened: on 2025-07-08 the paid commercial-license requirement for workplace use was REMOVED (previously: free personal use + separate commercial license for companies), making the app free for startups, schools, and companies. In 2025-07 the free public Hub organization and a paid Teams plan were added; the Bionic agent app launched 2026-07-16 with paid Bionic+ ($20/mo) and Pro ($100/mo) plans plus pay-as-you-go cloud credits, while keeping local inference free and unlimited. Note on task framing: LM Studio has never offered 'GPU / ML training & notebooks — free compute' fronts — it is a local-inference desktop app, not a GPU cloud; 'free compute' means the user's own hardware. The Teams plan is still not fully rolled out: the 2026-10 pricing page says team subscriptions are 'coming soon' with centralized org billing via paid inference credits. No student/education license or startup credit program exists (confirmed by third-party checks 2026-09/10); the free tier + free-for-work terms is the complete free offer.

findings.name: Student Credits — $20 free credit (A6000/L40 only)
findings.detail: Official /students page (read 2026-10-22): sign up with your student email to get $20 of free Thunder Compute credit, added automatically after signup ('no application and no waiting'). Credit is restricted to RTX A6000 and L40 GPUs — at listed on-demand rates (A6000 $0.35/hr, L40 $0.79/hr) that is ~57 A6000-hours or ~25 L40-hours. Not usable on H100 SXM ($3.20/hr) or A100 80GB ($1.09/hr).
findings.eligibility: Students enrolled at US universities only ('Only students enrolled at US universities qualify'). Must sign up with a university email; the system 'verify your email domain automatically'. No other credential (not even strictly .edu, though the company's own blog FAQ phrases it as 'verified .edu email') is stated. No credit card or payment method is mentioned as required to claim the credit; after it is exhausted, standard pay-as-you-go billing applies.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at console.thundercompute.com/signup using your university email; 2) email domain is verified automatically and the $20 credit is added to the account right after signup; 3) use the credit on A6000 or L40 instances. No application, no waiting.
findings.expiry: No expiration date, renewal cycle, or re-eligibility window is stated on the /students page. After the credit is spent, usage continues at normal pay-as-you-go rates.
findings.gotchas: US-institution-only; credit locked to A6000/L40 (cheapest GPUs in their lineup, not the H100/A100 most workloads need); fraud or abuse 'may result in credit removal or account suspension'. One account/student implied by the auto-verification; no stated way to re-claim. WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted), so a 2025-2026 history of the offer (e.g., whether it was ever larger or previously also covered A100) could not be verified.

findings.name: Referral Program — 3% of referred customers' lifetime spend, paid in credits
findings.detail: Official /referrals page (read 2026-10-22): 'Earn 3% in credits on the lifetime spend of every customer you refer to Thunder Compute.' Example given: refer $10,000 in spend -> $300 in credits. Recurring/ongoing, not one-time. Referring 25 users who spend money unlocks affiliate status. No dollar cap or per-referral limit is stated beyond the illustrative example.

findings.claim: Share your referral link; each referred paying customer generates 3% of their lifetime spend as credit to your account.

findings.gotchas: Credits only, not cash. 'Fraud or abuse of the referral program may result in credit removal and/or account suspension.' You need referrals who actually spend; a referred free-credit-only student account generates no referral value unless they top up. Not a startup program — it's a generic growth incentive.

The company's own 'Free Cloud GPU Credits in 2026' blog directory attributes to Thunder Compute only the $20 student credit and the 3% referral program — no startup-tier entry. So there is no evidence a startup program ever existed or was sunset; the only distinct free offers are the student credit and the referral credits above. Caveat: WebSearch's session budget was exhausted, so 2025-2026 change history was verified by reading official pages only, not by news search.

findings.name: Ollama local inference runtime (free, open source)
findings.detail: Download Ollama's desktop app or CLI and run open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Mistral, Gemma, gpt-oss, DeepSeek, etc.) on your own CPU/GPU at $0. No account, no API key, no per-token billing; local usage is unlimited and it works fully offline / air-gapped. Permissive open source: the repo LICENSE file is MIT (the 'known so far' note said Apache-2.0 — that is outdated). Scale per ollama.com homepage: 9M+ monthly installs, 1B+ model downloads, 200T+ tokens served. This is the core 'free compute' angle for students/startups: you pay for hardware, not for the runtime.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, worldwide — no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card, no region limits. Identical for students and startups as for everyone else.
findings.claim: Download from ollama.com (desktop app or CLI), install, then `ollama run <model>` (e.g. `ollama run llama3`). Models pull from ollama.com's registry. No signup required for local use.
findings.expiry: None — permanent, no time limit or renewal, for as long as Ollama is maintained.
findings.gotchas: You pay for your own hardware (RAM/VRAM + electricity + depreciation) — that is the real cost surface; no free GPU or free training compute is bundled. Ollama is an inference/serving runtime, not a notebook/training platform; fine-tuning needs separate tooling. License is MIT, not Apache-2.0. No egress/egress-style fees locally (data stays on your machine).

findings.name: Ollama Cloud Free tier ($0 hosted GPU inference)
findings.detail: Ollama Cloud's Free plan is $0/mo and includes a small 'Starter usage credits' allowance (a modest monthly usage pool for a set of 'starter models'; no dollar figure is published). 1 concurrent request. Zero data retention, hosted in the US/Europe (some Qwen models route to Singapore); prompts are never logged or trained on. No service fees, no subscription. Model pay-as-you-go rates range ~$0.015/M cached-input (nemotron-3-super) up to $15/M output (kimi-k3); off-peak half-pricing applies on some models outside 12:00–18:00 UTC weekdays and all weekend. Free tier structure (monthly starter credits, no 5-hr/weekly caps) effective Aug 31, 2026.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who creates a free account at ollama.com — no .edu, no startup age/funding cap, no region gate. Credit card is NOT required for the free tier; a payment method is only needed if you opt in to add pay-as-you-go credits to unlock all models.
findings.claim: Create a free Ollama account at ollama.com → in the CLI run `ollama signin` → run a cloud model (e.g. `ollama run qwen3-coder:480b-cloud`, `gpt-oss:120b-cloud`) or call Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. Starter usage is included; add credits to go beyond it.
findings.expiry: Free tier has no expiry; starter credits refresh monthly. No time limit on the $0 tier.
findings.gotchas: Starter-credit amount is not published (no dollar figure). Concurrency capped at 1; requests beyond are queued (a full queue rejects new requests). Overage = pay-as-you-go at published per-token rates (real cost). It is inference only — no free notebooks, no training GPU. This is a permanent free tier, not a trial/credit drop.

findings.name: No Ollama startup program, student/education discount, or nonprofit offer
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 Ollama offers NO dedicated startup program, NO student/academic discount, and NO nonprofit tier. ollama.com/pricing lists only Free / Pro / Max / Team / Enterprise — no discounted or special student/startup/edu/nonprofit plan. Discount aggregators (costbench, aitoolsatlas) print generic 'startup/education/nonprofit program' templates but explicitly state no Ollama-specific terms are verified. A third-party 2026-09-04 review confirms: 'Ollama has no student or academic discount' — the pitch is that the core software is already free and unrestricted, so there is nothing to discount.
findings.eligibility: N/A — none of these programs exist. The only free offers available to students/startups are the general ones above (local runtime + Cloud Free tier), which need no special eligibility.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; use the general Free tier / local runtime.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Treat auto-generated 'Ollama student discount / startup program / nonprofit discount' pages (costbench, aitoolsatlas, nozz's paid Founding-Member upsell, trytrick) as unverified, not official Ollama programs; confirm anything on ollama.com before relying on it.

sunset_notes: LICENSE CORRECTION: the 'known so far' note said Ollama is Apache-2.0 — the repo's LICENSE file is actually MIT (permissive open source; free and unrestricted). MATERIAL PRICING CHANGE: Ollama Cloud pricing was overhauled on Aug 31, 2026 to transparent monthly usage-credit pools. Legacy mechanics — 5-hour session limits + 7-day weekly caps, and the 'Pro = 50x Free / Max = 5x Pro' framing — are gone; new structure: Free (starter credits, 1 concurrent) / Pro $20/mo ($200/yr ≈ $16.67/mo, $60/mo credits, 3 concurrent) / Max $100/mo ($300/mo credits, 10 concurrent, early access to newest models) / Team $500/mo (early access, $1,000/mo shared credits, unlimited users) / Enterprise (custom, volume pricing). Cloud (hosted inference) models first launched in preview Sep 19, 2025; Team plan opened Aug 31, 2026. NOTHING FREE WAS SUNSET: the free local runtime and the Cloud Free tier remain $0 — only the free tier's usage-limit mechanism changed (session/weekly → monthly starter credits). ADJACENT / THIRD-PARTY 'free GPU + Ollama' offers that appear in search are NOT Ollama's own programs: UCloud CompShare (10 hours free RTX40-series GPU after signup + ID verification; 5% discount + compute subsidy for academic/enterprise certification; hosts Ollama images) and Brown CCV 'Oscar' HPC (800+ NVIDIA GPUs, Ollama preinstalled as a module, 100+ shared open models, free to Brown accounts). Ollama provides no free notebooks or free ML-training compute — its cloud is inference-only and the local runtime is for inference/serving; training/fine-tuning requires separate tooling.

findings.name: Baseten AI Startup Program ("Baseten for Startups") — up to $25,000 credits (Dedicated Inference/Training) + up to $2,500 (Model APIs)
findings.detail: Per-application grant, not automatic: 'Up to $25,000 in credits for Dedicated Inference or Training' plus 'Up to $2,500 in credits for Model APIs'. Credits are non-cash, applied to Baseten Inference and Training Services under Baseten T&C. Acceptance is at Baseten's sole discretion; the amount awarded is set per applicant. Extras with admission: support starting at response times 'within a few business hours', shared Slack channels and Zoom calls, cross-cloud autoscaling, GTM amplification for launches/raises, invitations to Baseten-hosted networking events. Page fetched live 2026-10-22; terms unchanged since the legal disclaimers' last update (October 7, 2025).
findings.eligibility: Early-stage AI-first startups: 'artificial intelligence needs to be core to your primary products or solutions'; funding stage Seed to Series A; started less than 5 years ago; 'VC funded' framing on the page (criteria do not hard-require VC backing — bootstrapped AI startups appear possible but must confirm at application). Net-new customers only: never received any Baseten credits, and the company domain must not have been subscribed to a paid Baseten Service plan within 31 days of applying. Excluded: IPO'd or acquired companies, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content, dev shops, consultancies, agencies, crypto mining companies. No .edu requirement (students are not the target), no region limit stated. No credit card required to apply; no equity requested.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a Baseten account (login.baseten.co/sign-up). 2) Apply via baseten.co/startup-program/ → 'Join the program' → baseten.co/talk-to-us/startup-program/. 3) Wait for manual review (third-party trackers report ~2–10 business days; acceptance is discretionary). 4) On acceptance, credits are applied to your account. Do NOT burn any paid plan or use more than the default signup credits before applying — net-new status (no Baseten credits ever) and the 31-day paid-plan rule are the main disqualifiers.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 6 months from grant date ('used within 6 months of their grant date and will expire if not consumed after 6 months'); no stated end date or renewal for the program itself.
findings.gotchas: 'Up to' amounts — award size is per-applicant, not guaranteed maximum. Net-new rule: receiving the default signup credits or a paid trial before applying can disqualify you. 31-day paid-plan rule (legal disclaimer #2, last updated 2025-10-07). Credits cover inference/training compute and Model API usage only; after the 6-month window unused credits vanish. Support SLA is 'business hours', not 24/7. JPMorgan's tracker lists tech support response at max 48h via dashboard UI. Common rejection reasons per trackers: personal email instead of company domain, thin/placeholder website, application data mismatched with Crunchbase/PitchBook.

findings.name: New-account signup ('starting') credits — unannounced amount, no application
findings.detail: Official pricing FAQ (fetched 2026-10-22): 'Do you offer free credits to get started? Yes, new Baseten accounts come with credits so you can get to know the UI and experiment with deployments for free.' Baseten's billing docs (docs.baseten.co/organization/billing) add: 'New workspaces receive credits for testing and deployment. Baseten applies credits to the current invoice before charging a payment method; you do not need to redeem them.' No exact dollar amount is published by Baseten. Third-party trackers (pricepertoken.com, infrabase.ai, Perkstack, aicredits.dev — per their notes the figure traces to Baseten's changelog announcement of usage-based pricing) report the amount as $30 per new workspace; treat $30 as plausible but unconfirmed (the live balance in a new workspace's billing dashboard is authoritative). One-time, per-workspace grant; not recurring.
findings.eligibility: Any new Baseten account/workspace, no application, no funding/age/status requirement. No credit card required to receive the starting credits.
findings.claim: Sign up at app.baseten.co (email, Google, or GitHub), verify email, create a workspace. Credits are attached automatically — nothing to redeem. They offset all usage (dedicated GPU time, Model API calls, training) and are deducted before any payment method is charged; balance visible on the billing dashboard. If you don't see them, Baseten's docs say to contact them.
findings.expiry: No published expiry for the starting-credits balance; docs say 'Baseten doesn't offer a separate free tier or perpetual free plan' — beyond the starting credits you pay standard per-minute / per-token rates. When credits run out with no payment method on file, Baseten deactivates your models until one is added.
findings.gotchas: Exact amount is unannounced by Baseten (the $30 figure is third-party/changelog-sourced — verify in your billing dashboard). This signup credit counts toward 'never received any credits from Baseten before', so it affects Startup Program net-new eligibility — apply for the program before spending/using paid features. No idle-time billing (scale-to-zero supported). Model API rate limits on the Basic plan are defaults, not a free allowance.

findings.name: Education / student offer — none exists (negative finding)
findings.detail: Baseten has no education license, .edu program, or student credits. Official support KB (support-legacy.baseten.co, article last updated ~1 month before 2026-10-22): 'We don't have a self-serve credits program for individual students or projects, so we can't grant credits from a support request — sorry to be the bearers. What does exist: Startups may qualify for the Baseten Startup Program.' The Startup Program's legal disclaimers explicitly exclude 'educational institutions'. Occasional one-off hackathon sponsorships (e.g., shared endpoints at HackMIT 2024, ad-hoc extra credits on request) are the only student-facing touches; none are standing offers.
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — no standing student/education offer. .edu email confers no benefits. Educational institutions are ineligible for the Startup Program.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. If you are a student or academic, your only paths are the generic new-account starting credits, or forming an AI-first early-stage company to apply to the Startup Program.

sunset_notes: 1) "Fall into Inference" campaign (ended): baseten.co/talk-to-us/fall-into-inference/ previously offered new Baseten customers 'up to $10,000 of free inference credits' (multi-cloud inference, with cloud partners and NVIDIA), valid 'Until December 20, 2025'. Fetched 2026-10-22 the URL now serves a generic 'talk to us' contact page with no campaign language — consistent with the campaign closing ~2025-12-20. 2) 2025–2026 status of standing offers: the AI Startup Program's $25,000 + $2,500 structure, Seed-to-Series-A / <5-years / net-new criteria, 6-month credit expiry and 31-day paid-plan rule are all live and unchanged as of 2026-10-22; the legal disclaimers page was last updated October 7, 2025, and no material change was found in today's page fetches or in third-party verification runs dated 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-22. 3) No perpetual free tier has ever existed at Baseten ('Baseten doesn't offer a separate free tier or perpetual free plan' — official billing docs), so the only recurring free benefit is the one-time, unannounced-amount starting credit for new workspaces.

provider: Airplane (Airplane Labs, Inc., internal-tools platform at airplane.dev; acquired by Airtable Jan 2024)

findings.name: Free plan ('Start using Airplane for free')
findings.detail: Final form (2023-2024, last archived official pricing page 2024-03-10): Free $0/user/month with unlimited users, unlimited objects, 2 environments, 3 days of activity history. Limits evolved: 2021 early access was $0/mo unlimited tasks+users; Mar 2022 free tier was up to 5 users + up to 5 runbooks/tasks + 3-day activity log; Sep 2022 was up to 5 users + up to 50 objects; by Sep 2023 it was unlimited users/objects + 2 environments + 3-day history (the widely-cited '5 internal tools, unlimited users' line is an intermediate 2022-era limit, not the final state). 'Objects' = internal apps (UI/API serverless functions).
findings.eligibility: Anyone (personal or company). No .edu email, no startup stage/funding requirement. No credit card requirement documented on any archived page; sign-up was GitHub-login based ('Sign Up' button), Free tier had a 'Get started' CTA.
findings.claim: Sign up at airplane.dev with GitHub, choose the Free plan ($0) - no form, no credits to redeem. Paid Team ($10/user/mo) and Business ($40/user/mo) tiers were marked 'Try for free'.
findings.expiry: EXPIRED - service sunset 2024-03-01 (acquisition by Airtable); new signups closed 2024-01-03. No offer exists as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: the free plan was genuinely perpetual while live, but the whole platform was sunset so nothing persists. Data: 3-day activity-history cap on Free; self-hosted agents, group permissions and env/embed features were paid-only. Self-hosted agents were the only data-egress mitigation; no public egress/egress-fee schedule on Free. The live URL now redirects in a 301 loop on a Squarespace parking backend - any link to airplane.dev/pricing in old articles is dead.

findings.name: Airplane for Startups - up to $10,000 in credits
findings.detail: Program ('Scalable tools for fast-moving teams'): eligible startups could redeem up to $10,000 in Airplane credits, valid for a year. Page was live from at least 2023-03 through its last 200 capture 2024-02-29, and already returning 404 by 2024-05-16. Intro blog post 'introducing-airplane-for-startups' appeared 2024-01-04.
findings.eligibility: Three stated requirements: (1) fewer than 50 employees, (2) Series A or earlier (stage cap - no explicit dollar funding figure), (3) not a current paying customer. Work email required on the form (no .edu angle, it was a startup program); no region limits stated.
findings.claim: Fill out the form on airplane.dev/startups ('Redeem your credits'): name, work email, company name, and an optional 'Anything specific you want to use Airplane for?' field; approval was manual. No credit card required. Program was dead once Airplane itself shut down.
findings.source_url: https://www.airplane.dev/startups (dead; archived copies read today: https://web.archive.org/web/20240229194024/https://www.airplane.dev/startups ; FAQ/announcement: https://web.archive.org/web/20240104062134/https://www.airplane.dev/blog/introducing-airplane-for-startups)
findings.expiry: EXPIRED - program ended with platform sunset 2024-03-01; /startups 404 by 2024-05-16. $10,000 of credits for a year is unredeemable and the platform it applied to no longer exists.
findings.gotchas: Credits were Airplane-platform-only (valueless post-sunset). The 'up to $10,000' was a cap, not a guaranteed amount. 'Series A or earlier' is the only funding/stage gate. No student/education variant of this program ever existed.

findings.name: Free trials on paid plans (Team 'Try for free', Business 'Try for free')
findings.detail: Team at $10/user/mo and Business at $40/user/mo carried 'Try for free' CTAs on the 2023-2024 pricing page; trial duration and post-trial billing terms were not published on the page. (Enterprise was custom, 'Book demo'.)
findings.eligibility: Anyone signing up; no startup/stage restrictions; no .edu requirement. No credit-card requirement documented on the archived page (sign-up via GitHub login).
findings.claim: Click 'Try for free' on the Team or Business tier at airplane.dev/pricing.
findings.expiry: EXPIRED - all signups closed 2024-01-03; platform sunset 2024-03-01.
findings.gotchas: Trial terms (duration, CC capture) were not published and cannot be verified; treat as non-existent now.

sunset_notes: FULLY SUNSET - nothing live as of 2026-10-22. Timeline (verified today via DNS, live probing and Wayback): (1) 2024-01-03: Airtable announces acquisition of Airplane in official blog 'Airtable acquires Airplane' (archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20240310140454/https://www.airplane.dev/blog/airtable); same post states 'we will unfortunately be sunsetting the Airplane platform on March 1' and that new signups had already closed. (2) 2024-03-01: platform sunset date. (3) 2024-05-16: /startups already returning 404. (4) No 200-status HTML captures of any airplane.dev page (incl. subdomains) exist after mid-March 2024; all 2025-2026 captures are 301s. (5) As of 2026-10-22 the domain itself is lapsed/parked: authoritative Googledomains NS shows apex A-record 198.49.23.145 (NSI-style parking IP) and NXDOMAIN for www.airplane.dev; www paths serve self-referential 301 loops behind a 'Server: Squarespace' header, apex 301s to www - a broken-redirect parking loop, so even the parked page won't render. GitHub orgs 'rethink-dev' and 'getairplane' both 404. The team was absorbed into Airtable; Airtable did not continue Airplane as a standalone product on that domain. No education/student offer existed at any point: no /education, /students, or /student-programs pages in the archive and zero 'student'/'.edu' mentions on archived pricing/startup pages. Note the sunsetting happened in 2024, not 2025-2026; during 2025-2026 the domain simply went from dead to parked - no offer changes. All claims above therefore rely on archived copies of the official pages (read today), not on live ones, since the live pages no longer exist.

findings.name: SGLang open-source inference engine (Apache-2.0) — permanently free
findings.detail: SGLang is a fully open-source LLM/VLM/diffusion serving engine (RadixAttention prefix caching, structured generation, speculative decoding) under Apache-2.0: $0 license, no subscription, no per-token/seat fees, unlimited usage, indefinite. 'Free' here means the software; you still pay for your own GPU compute (e.g., ~$3.39/hr median on-demand H100 as of Sep 2026). The commercial backer RadixArk (launched May 2026, $100M seed at $400M valuation) sells managed services, but the open engine remains free. No free tier, trial, education license, or startup program exists on SGLang's official site (verified sglang.io 2026-10-22: no pricing page, no student/startup program; only 'enterprise adoption/consulting/sponsorship' contact at sglang@lmsys.org).
findings.eligibility: Anyone, anywhere — no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card, no region limits. Open-source license is unconditional (Apache-2.0). Students get the identical free software as enterprises.
findings.claim: git clone or pip install/uv sglang (or Docker image) from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang; run on any supported GPU/TPU/NPU/CPU (A100/H100/H200/B200/MI300X/TPU v6e-v7/Apple Silicon etc.). No account, no signup, no key.
findings.expiry: Permanent (open-source license; no expiry). Ecosystem sub-projects (SGLang Diffusion, SGLang-Omni, SpecForge, HiCache/Mooncake) are in the same repo/organization and open-sourced too.
findings.gotchas: The $0 software does NOT cover compute: GPU rental is the real cost (on-demand H100 ~$3.39/hr; below ~2.5-3B tokens/mo a per-token API is usually cheaper). Model weights for served models come from other labs — some models (e.g., certain gated LLMs) require their own license acceptance. Third-party 'pricing' sites (costbench, aiindigo, aitoolsatlas) describe a '$0 free tier' but aitoolsatlas's 'education pricing available' claim is generic boilerplate, not a real SGLang program. The 'median contract $51,500/yr' figure on costbench refers to RadixArk commercial managed deals, not the free engine.

findings.name: AMD Developer Cloud free MI300X credits (~$100 / ~50 hrs) via SGLang partner guide
findings.detail: AMD Developer Cloud has offered free MI300X GPU access to developers, and SGLang's own project posted (2026-03-17) a guide to run a full stack (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 served via SGLang in one Docker command, selectable in OpenClaw's onboarding CLI) 'at zero cost' on a single MI300X, quantified as ~$100 AMD Developer Cloud credits (~50 hrs of MI300X). AMD replied to the post confirming the guide. This is partner-sourced free compute, not an SGLang program.
findings.eligibility: AMD Developer Cloud account holders (developer sign-up); guide is aimed at any developer/student/startup building an agent stack — no .edu requirement stated, no funding cap. US-based cloud (AMD data centers); account verification typically required.
findings.claim: Sign up at devcloud.amd.com, apply for the free MI300X trial/credits, then follow SGLang's published guide (shared 2026-03-17 on the SGLang LinkedIn, shortened link lnkd.in/g2UZFehh) to deploy Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 via SGLang in one Docker command.
findings.expiry: Credits are promotional and time-boxed; ~50 hrs / $100 figure is from the Mar 2026 post — exact expiry window not confirmed (AMD's pages are JS-only and I could not read official terms today; search budget exhausted).
findings.gotchas: Not an SGLang-owned program — terms/limits/credits can change or be revoked by AMD; capacity on MI300X instances is limited and often queued; data egress/model-download costs may apply; 'free' applies only while credits last, after which MI300X time is metered. Verify current credit amounts at devcloud.amd.com before relying on this.

sunset_notes: No SGLang-specific free offer was sunset or materially changed in 2025-2026: there is no SGLang free tier, trial credit, startup program, or education license to sunset — the 'free offer' is the Apache-2.0 software itself, which is permanent. Material 2025-2026 context: (1) the commercial entity RadixArk launched May 2026 ($100M seed, $400M valuation) with managed-inference/managed-training services on top of the open core — at this date it has announced no startup or education program, so nothing free exists on that front to claim; (2) SGLang joined the PyTorch ecosystem during 2025; (3) a free-compute path via partner AMD Developer Cloud (MI300X, ~$100/~50 hrs) was highlighted by the SGLang project in March 2026, but AMD's official terms could not be read (JS-only pages) and web-search budget was exhausted, so treat that figure as unverified current. Third-party discount sites claiming SGLang 'education pricing' (e.g., aitoolsatlas.ai) are auto-generated generic text, not a real program.

provider: GPUStack (gpustack.ai — self-hosted AI inference/runtime platform; note: task's starting URL https://gpustack.co does not resolve — DNS not found; official site is https://gpustack.ai)

findings.name: Free open-source self-hosted runtime (the only real free offer; available to students and startups alike)
findings.detail: GPUStack core is free, open-source, Apache 2.0 licensed (NOT MIT as the task's 'known so far' said — both gpustack.ai and the GitHub repo state Apache 2.0 today). One-line Docker install (server: sudo docker run -d --name gpustack -p 80:80 --volume gpustack-data:/var/lib/gpustack gpustack/gpustack; worker: separate privileged Docker command with --server-url and a generated --token). Includes Ollama-style local web UI + OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API, model deployment, and supports heterogeneous accelerators (NVIDIA; AMD/ROCm, Ascend, Hygon, MetaX, Moore Threads, Cambricon, Iluvatar, T-Head PPU per the site). Free forever, no expiry. No hosted free tier, no trial credits, no student/education offer, no startup program exists on the official site (verified /, /enterprise, /blog, GitHub, docs quickstart on 2026-10-22; /cloud/ and /pricing/ are 404). Sources read today: https://gpustack.ai, https://gpustack.ai/enterprise, https://gpustack.ai/blog/, https://gpustack.ai/blog/introducing-gpustack/, https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack, https://docs.gpustack.ai/latest/quickstart/
findings.eligibility: Anyone — students, startups, enterprises, individuals. No .edu email, no account, no company age or funding-cap requirements, no region limits. Credit card NOT required; no commercial license, no login/account to set up (local 'admin' user with a system-generated password).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim or sign up for: clone/download the open-source code (https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack) and run the Docker one-liners from https://docs.gpustack.ai/latest/quickstart/. Worker nodes need Linux + at least one GPU (docs quickstart covers NVIDIA; site advertises AMD/ROCm and Chinese accelerators too; macOS/Windows can host the server via Docker Desktop, workers are Linux-only; Windows via WSL2).
findings.expiry: Indefinite — Apache 2.0 license is perpetual; no sunsetting date for the open-source product.
findings.gotchas: The 'free compute' is BYO-hardware: you pay for your own GPU, electricity, and (for model pulls from hub sources) data egress; there is no GPUStack-hosted free GPU pool. Workers are Linux-only — no macOS worker nodes. RBAC, SSO (OIDC/SAML/LDAP), token quotas, metering & billing, white-label, HA and multi-tenancy are Enterprise features sold via 'Talk to Sales'/'Book a Demo' (https://gpustack.ai/book-demo) with no published pricing — do not assume free. The June 2026 'Introducing GPUStack' blog repositions the product as an 'enterprise AI infrastructure platform' with 'MaaS and GPUaaS under one control plane' (https://gpustack.ai/blog/introducing-gpustack/), so a commercial hosted GPUaaS is signaled, but no public self-serve page, pricing, or free tier for it was found (gpustack.ai/cloud and gpustack.ai/pricing return 404). WebSearch was unavailable this session (session budget exhausted), so third-party sources (funding news, off-site discount resellers) could not be checked.

findings.name: GPUStack Enterprise (paid, sales-led — NOT a free offer; listed so it is not confused with a free tier)
findings.detail: Enterprise adds high availability, multi-tenancy, RBAC/SSO, token quotas, rate limits, audit logs, metering & billing, white-label. No dollar figures, no tiers, no trial credits, no self-serve purchase anywhere on gpustack.ai; the only CTA is 'Talk to Sales' → /book-demo. A free trial or evaluation sandbox may be negotiated via sales but is not publicly published. Sources: https://gpustack.ai/enterprise, https://gpustack.ai/book-demo
findings.eligibility: Enterprise/sales channel; no public self-serve. No student or startup eligibility criteria published.
findings.claim: Book a demo at https://gpustack.ai/book-demo/ to request evaluation or pricing; nothing claimable online.
findings.expiry: n/a (no published free component)
findings.gotchas: Verify what is actually free vs. Enterprise-locked before self-hosting in production; the metering/billing and white-label features are on the paid side of the line.

sunset_notes: No student, education, or startup program existed to sunset, and no trial-credit program was closed, in 2025-2026 — GPUStack has run exclusively as (a) a free Apache-2.0 self-hosted runtime and (b) a sales-led Enterprise product, with no published pricing pages (/pricing/ and /cloud/ are 404 as of 2026-10-22). Material 2025-2026 changes to note: (1) the task's 'known so far' claim of an MIT license is wrong — both the official site and the GitHub repo say Apache 2.0 today; (2) November 2025 'v2' and March 2026 'v2.1' releases added faster inference, Alibaba T-Head PPU support, a model gateway with routing, and a community backend marketplace (per https://gpustack.ai/blog/ listing; individual release details not fetched, so medium confidence on the specifics); (3) in June 2026 GPUStack repositioned as an 'enterprise AI infrastructure platform' marketing 'MaaS and GPUaaS under one control plane' (https://gpustack.ai/blog/introducing-gpustack/) — a hosted GPUaaS is signaled but had no public self-serve page, pricing, or free tier as of 2026-10-22. The original https://gpustack.co domain does not resolve; gpustack.ai is the live official domain. Caveat: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so all 'no program exists' conclusions rest on official-page fetches done today only; an off-site program (e.g., a partner marketplace discount) could not be ruled out via search.

provider: Azure Free Account (free VMs) (Cloud trial) — Microsoft Azure, as of 2026-10-22

findings.name: Azure Free Account — $200 credit for 30 days + 12-month free services (B1S / B2pts v2 / B2ats v2, 750 hrs/month)
findings.detail: Confirmed today on official pages: $200 credit (in your billing currency) usable for 30 days on any Azure service except third-party Marketplace purchases. From signup up to 12 months: free monthly amounts of ~25+ services, including 750 hours/month EACH of the three free burstable VM SKUs — B1S, B2pts v2 (ARM-based), B2ats v2 (AMD-based), Linux or Windows. 750 hours can be split across instances (e.g. 5 VMs x 150h) and created in any region where B-series is available. After day 30 only the free-limited services remain free; unused $200 credit is lost at day 30 unless you upgrade to pay-as-you-go before 30 days (then credit stays usable for the full 30-day window). Must move to pay-as-you-go within 30 days or account/services are disabled. 12-month offer is new-customers-only (never had an Azure account / 12-month benefits before) and NOT available to customers who sign up directly for pay-as-you-go in China and India.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers. Credit card or debit card (non-prepaid) + phone number REQUIRED at signup ($1 temporary auth hold, reversed; credit cards only in HK and Brazil). No .edu needed. Not available to existing PAYG signups in China/India for the 12-month benefit.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at azure.microsoft.com for 'Azure Free Account' with phone + card. 2) In portal, use the 'Free services' page (go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=859151) so free tiers are preselected. 3) Create resources within 750h/month VM limits; convert to pay-as-you-go before day 30 to keep the 12-month free tier.
findings.expiry: Credit: 30 days from account creation (lost if unused unless early PAYG upgrade). Free services: 12 months from account creation, then services decommission/subscription disabled; no renewal of the trial itself.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (unlike student offers). Free VM hours exclude egress over free bandwidth, public IP and disk charges — classic surprise-bill source. Don't create resources outside the 'Free services' page: free tiers are not default-selected elsewhere, you get billed. After day 30 without PAYG upgrade the whole account is disabled; resuming requires PAYG. HK/Brazil prepaid cards rejected.

findings.name: 65+ always-free Azure services (incl. notebook/ML-adjacent: Synapse Spark, Databricks, AI/ML categories)
findings.detail: The free-services overview page (read today) states '65+ always-free services with an Azure account' with 'free monthly amounts... for as long as you have an Azure account', spanning AI/ML, compute, databases, IoT, management. The per-service limit tables on that page are JS-rendered and could not be extracted today, so the specific figures below are the long-standing published limits, unconfirmed in today's fetch: Azure Synapse Spark SQL pool DW1000c 250 hrs/month, Azure Databricks 32 SQL DBU/month, Data Factory 5,000 slicing units/month, App Service 1 shared instance + 60k req/day, Functions 1M req + 400k GB-s, Storage 5 GB LRS + 5 GB premium, Cosmos DB 500 RU/s + 400 GB, 100 GB egress/month, App Insights 5 MB ingest/day. Always-free is available with ANY account, including pay-as-you-go accounts — you do not need the trial.
findings.eligibility: Any Azure account (free or paid); no card required to exist, but creating resources needs a valid billing profile. No student/startup status needed.
findings.claim: Sign up for any Azure account; create services via the 'Free services' page in portal selecting the free tier. No separate application.
findings.expiry: Indefinite — free monthly amounts continue for life of account; amounts reset monthly; exceeding limits triggers PAYG billing.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free confusion: the 12-month tier is a separate, larger allotment that expires at 12 months; the always-free tier persists. Free Spark/Databricks limits are small — fine for notebook experiments, not sustained GPU/ML training. Outbound data and data at rest beyond free storage bill separately. Per-service figures above were not re-verifiable today (JS-rendered table), treat exact numbers as medium-confidence until checked at azure.microsoft.com/pricing/free-services in a browser.

findings.name: Free GPU / ML-training & notebooks compute: what actually exists
findings.detail: Azure has NO free-tier GPU VMs and no free Azure Machine Learning compute in the free account. The only free paths for GPU/ML work: (1) the $200 trial credit (30 days) can buy any compute incl. GPU VMs (e.g. NC/NV/A-series) — a few hours of a mid GPU VM is typical of what $200 buys, exact durations vary by SKU/region; (2) always-free notebooks/data engines: Synapse Spark SQL DW1000c 250 hrs/month and Databricks 32 SQL DBU/month (medium confidence, see above) — CPU-based, not GPU; (3) 750 hrs/month B-series burstable VMs for light CPU training/inference. For sustained GPU/ML training the realistic free routes are the startup credits (up to $150K, finding 8) or Azure Spot/standard pricing — there is no recurring free GPU offering at Azure as of 2026-10-22.
findings.eligibility: Same as each underlying offer: new customers for the $200 credit; any account for always-free Spark/Databricks.
findings.claim: Use the $200 credit within 30 days on GPU VMs; enable always-free Spark/Databricks via the 'Free services' page in the portal.
findings.expiry: Credit: 30 days. Spark/Databricks free amounts: monthly, indefinite.
findings.gotchas: GPU hours under the credit are finite and CPU-free tiers can't replace them; egress and managed-disk I/O billed; Databricks free DBUs cover SQL warehouse only, not full DBU workspace runs; don't confuse trial (30d) with always-free.

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit for 12 months, no credit card required
findings.detail: Confirmed today: $100 in Azure credits usable within the first 12 months (non-rollover), plus 'select free services' (FAQ states the offer includes 25+ free services incl. compute/network/storage/databases). Applies to most Azure products; NOT usable for: Azure support plans, Azure DevOps, Visual Studio subscriptions, App Center, Express Route, Marketplace items, separately licensed products (e.g. Entra ID Premium). No credit card at signup; subscription disabled if $100 exhausted (then upgrade to PAYG via support). One subscription per person, non-transferable, cannot combine offers. Renewable annually (Microsoft emails near the anniversary; re-signup). 140+ countries where Azure is commercially available; excludes US Government sovereign cloud and Azure Germany regions. Inactive >90 days: Microsoft may remove compute resources (with notice).
findings.eligibility: Age 18+, FULL-TIME student at an accredited degree-granting 2- or 4-year institution; verify via your organization's (school) email address — not strictly '.edu'; MOOCs and for-profit professional training excluded. (Faculty/teachers: not on this offer; see Dev Tools for Teaching instead.)
findings.claim: 1) Go to the 'Apply now' link on the offer page (go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2244463). 2) Register with school email to verify academic status. 3) No card needed. 4) Track remaining $100 in the Azure Sponsorships portal (microsoftazuresponsorships.com).
findings.expiry: Credit and free-service window: 12 months from signup; renew once more by re-signup if still a student. 90 days after free-subscription end to upgrade before products decommission.
findings.gotchas: If credit runs out, subscription disables — nothing kept running for free; you must upgrade to PAYG (which requires a payment method). Credits cannot buy Marketplace/DevOps/support. One sub per person — a second school email won't work around it. Not valid in US Gov/Germany regions.

findings.name: Azure for Students Starter — free-tier services, no credit card, no time limit
findings.detail: Confirmed today (Learn FAQ, updated 2026-08-03): free tier of Azure App Service, Azure Functions, Azure Notification Hubs, Azure Database for MySQL, Application Insights, and Azure DevOps Services — no cost, no commitment, no time limit, and no credit card required. Upgrade to PAYG at any time to unlock all services.
findings.eligibility: Verified students: 13+ in the US, 16+ elsewhere; verify academic status via organization email or Shibboleth. MOOCs/for-profit training excluded. One subscription per person, non-transferable, no offer stacking.
findings.claim: Sign up via the Azure Education Hub in the portal (aka.ms/azure4students / Education Hub > offers) with school email; no card.
findings.expiry: Indefinite while account exists; services capped at free-tier levels forever.
findings.gotchas: Very small service set (no VMs, no databases beyond MySQL free tier, no GPU/ML) — useful for always-on web/hosting, not training workloads. Free-tier tiers are the cheapest paid tiers, not full service; upgrading is required for real workloads.

findings.name: Azure Academic Grant / Azure Sponsorship (course credits) — 100% discount for approved-course students
findings.detail: Confirmed today (Learn FAQ): students enrolled in approved courses (e.g. via training partners) get 'Azure course credits' as a 100%-discount 'Azure Sponsorship' subscription: portal shows $0.00 charged, balance tracked in the Azure Sponsorships portal (microsoftazuresponsorships.com/balance). Credits cover usage only from activation; cannot pay prior balances; cannot cover Marketplace items; cannot attach to Enterprise Agreement or CSP subscriptions (creating association early terminates sponsorship funds). Course credits can be moved between accounts via support.
findings.eligibility: Students of approved courses/partners; verify with the sponsoring program; one activated 'Azure Sponsorship' offer (ms-azr-0143p) subscription.
findings.claim: Activate the 100% discount button in the sponsorship approval email, or have support convert an existing subscription; associate course credits to the entitled account.
findings.expiry: Set by the course sponsorship period (varies by partner; not stated on the FAQ page).
findings.gotchas: Sponsorship + EA/CSP association kills the funds; Marketplace purchases still hit the card; $0 balance display is a discount, not a stored dollar balance.

findings.name: Azure Dev Tools for Teaching — education license: free dev software, NO cloud credits
findings.detail: Confirmed today: academic institutions with a Microsoft Volume Licensing agreement (Education Solutions/Open Value/School Agreement) enroll via a promo code from the license welcome email and get free, unlimited (noncommercial) access to dev tools: Visual Studio Enterprise/Code/Community, SQL Server Developer & Standard, Windows Server, Windows 10/11 for Education, SharePoint/R Server, System Center, Visio Professional, Hyper-V, Azure DevOps Server; students download via the Education Hub Store with school credentials; faculty install on personal PCs. Explicitly does NOT include Azure credit (FAQ points students to Azure for Students for $100). Renewal: email reminders start 60 days before expiry; does not auto-renew; non-VL existing customers may still renew.
findings.eligibility: K-12/academic institutions under a Volume Licensing agreement; 140+ countries where Azure is commercially available; noncommercial educational use; students may not commercially sell products built with the tools (Windows Store apps excepted).
findings.claim: Institution admin enrolls with the promo code from the VL welcome email at azureforeducation.microsoft.com; students/faculty then download via Education Hub Store or the VS portal.
findings.expiry: Subscription term per institution license; renews manually via admin.
findings.gotchas: Zero cloud/ML value — it's an on-prem/dev-tools license bundle; don't count it as free compute; no Office included.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — base $1,000 (90 days) + $4,000 (180 days) Azure credits; up to $150,000 via investor referrals
findings.detail: Confirmed today on Learn (page dated 2026-05-21/22) and the marketing landing page: single-entry program at startups.microsoft.com. (a) No-referral 'Azure startup credit offer': $1,000 for 90 days, then an additional $4,000 for 180 days after business verification. (b) Investor offer (referral code from a partner in the Microsoft for Startups Investor Network — investor, accelerator, incubator, angel network, or similar): most startups begin with $100,000 in Azure credits with the opportunity to earn more; program 'unlocks up to $150K in Startup credits over time' as verified progress/adoption/sustained usage; landing page advertises 'up to $150,000 in credits'. Credits apply across eligible Azure services; NOT usable for support plans, Marketplace, or non-covered services; when exhausted, subscription auto-transitions to pay-as-you-go. Activation: must activate within 90 days of accepting the program agreement, or reapply; once activated, credits valid up to 2 years, no extensions; tied to one MSA + subscription (non-transferable). Dedicated MFS point of contact available for eligible startups; go-to-market/discounts on GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn Premium Business, M365 Business Premium, VS Enterprise, Dynamics 365, Power Platform included in the investor offer. Applications reviewed in ~3 business days; declined applicants may reapply after 14 days.
findings.eligibility: Company: develops a software-based product/service it owns; privately held, for-profit; HQ in a country where Azure is available; NOT an educational institution/government/consultancy/agency; no cryptocurrency mining; has not raised Series C or later; has not received more than $350,000 in lifetime free Azure credits. No explicit company-age cap in the current criteria (the old 5-year age limit is gone from the current overview page). CC is required for credit activation (identity verification + transition to PAYG).
findings.claim: 1) Apply at startups.microsoft.com ('Get started'). 2) Optionally enter an Investor Network referral code for the $100K+ tier. 3) Wait ~3 business days for approval email. 4) Activate credits on the MSA used to apply (within 90 days) via the Azure portal; check under Cost Management + Billing > Payment methods.

Billing profile country/region can't be changed later — use the right region before activation. Auto-transition to PAYG when credits run out = unexpected bills. Base no-referral offer is only $5K total, so most 'up to $150K' value depends on getting an Investor Network referral.

provider: Grafana Cloud Free (Grafana Labs) — Observability, Monitoring, Uptime/Synthetics, k6, Frontend Observability

findings.name: Grafana Cloud Free tier (free forever, no credit card)
findings.detail: Official Grafana Cloud Free plan, read today (2026-10-22) on grafana.com/pricing and grafana.com/products/cloud/free-tier. Exact limits: 10k active metric series/month; 50 GB logs/month; 50 GB traces/month; 50 GB profiles/month; k6 limited to 500 virtual user hours/month; Synthetics (uptime) limited to 100k API test executions + 10k browser test executions/month; Frontend Observability 50k sessions/month; Grafana Assistant 3 active AI users (40M tokens/user/month) plus 25M tokens/month for service-account usage; Grafana Visualization 3 active users; IRM 3 active users; 14-day retention for metrics, logs, traces, profiles & k6 tests; community support. 'Free forever', 'No charges ever', 'No credit card required' — stated on each service block. Note: the commonly cited '100K k6 executions' is outdated; k6 is now capped in virtual user hours, while the 100k figure applies to Synthetics executions.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — no .edu email, no student status, no startup status, and no credit card required. Free tier page markets it as 'perfect for personal projects, exploring new ideas, and early-stage startups'. No region restriction mentioned; stacks can be created in Grafana's public-cloud regions. Total user count is capped at 3 active users on the free tier.
findings.claim: Sign up free at grafana.com (Create free account → grafana.com/auth/sign-up/create-user/?cta=free). Create an organization and a stack in your chosen region; all services above are available within the stated limits at $0. No credit card or payment method is asked. Upgrade to Pro (from $19/month + usage, 13-month metric retention / 30-day log-trace retention) or Enterprise (from $25,000/year spend commit) anytime if you outgrow the limits.
findings.source_url: https://grafana.com/pricing/ (limits table read 2026-10-22; corroborated by https://grafana.com/products/cloud/free-tier/ and https://grafana.com/auth/sign-up/create-user/?cta=free&pg=graf&plcmt=pricing-card)
findings.expiry: No expiry or sunset stated; marketed as 'Free forever'. Limits shown are current as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: 1) Total seat cap of 3 active users — a team larger than 3 cannot all use the free tier. 2) As of April 20, 2026, Grafana disabled alerting and reporting for NEWLY created free/trial stacks (email alerts/reports restricted to users inside your own instance; Cloud Alertmanager access disabled) as an anti-abuse measure — existing free accounts keep full functionality (third-party mirror of the Grafana status incident; medium confidence). 3) As of Jan 1, 2026, Grafana Assistant became billed on active users; free plan includes 3 AI users with a 40M tokens/user/month message cap, and paid plans charge $20 per additional active user beyond 3. 4) Free tier data is 14-day retention only; exceeding volume limits means downsampled/dropped data or upgrade — no egress-charge surprise, but no billing above limits on free (hard caps, not overage billing). 5) 'Adaptive Telemetry' and AI features included on free are allotment-limited, not unlimited.

findings.name: Grafana Labs Startup Program (up to $100,000 in Grafana Cloud credits)
findings.detail: Announced at ObservabilityCON on 2024-09-25; program page still live as of 2026-10-22 (© 2026 footer, ObservabilityCON 2026 banner; terms mirror the original launch). Awards up to $100,000 in Grafana Cloud credits, valid for 12 months or until the startup's next funding round (whichever comes first). Credits apply to ANY Grafana Cloud service: managed metrics/logs/traces backends, k6 performance testing, profiling, incident response & management, frontend/application observability, and synthetic monitoring. Additional perks for accepted startups: all Enterprise data source plugins, 24x7 Grafana support, guaranteed 20% discount off list price after credits or the 12-month window end (plus further consumption-based discounts), and access to Grafana's integrations team.
findings.eligibility: Open to all new customers — explicitly including existing Grafana Cloud Free-account holders and Grafana OSS users migrating to managed cloud; students with a startup can apply too. Ideal profile: raised less than $10 million and under 25 employees, but the page says 'apply even if you do not meet these guidelines'. No stated company-age cap, no .edu requirement, no region limit. Admission is at Grafana Labs' sole discretion (not first-come-first-served). Accepted startups must agree to be a reference customer and may be asked to participate in marketing (guest blogs, event speaking). No credit card required to apply.
findings.claim: Fill out the 4-question application form: https://grafana-labs.typeform.com/to/cSI7ohks (linked from the official blog post). Wait for Grafana Labs' discretionary decision; if accepted you receive the credit allocation plus the perks listed above.
findings.expiry: No published sunset date as of 2026-10-22. Each award lasts 12 months or until the company's next funding round; the guaranteed 20% discount continues after credits end. No 2025-2026 amendments to the program structure are stated on the page.
findings.gotchas: 1) Discretionary selection — 'apply' does not mean 'get in'; no SLA on decisions. 2) Obliges reference-customer and marketing commitments. 3) Credits offset usage-based billing; they are not free hosting — if usage exceeds the credit value you must pay (at the 20% discount). 4) Program is startup-company-oriented, so a solo student project with no company may be a weak application. 5) The $100k figure is 'up to' — actual credit amounts vary per acceptance.

findings.name: Free Plan (50 monitors, forever free)
findings.detail: Official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22): $0/month. 50 monitors; 5-minute check interval; HTTP/website, keyword, ping, port, API, UDP, dependency, location-specific, slow-response, DNS and SSL/domain-expiry monitor types; 1 basic status page (UptimeRobot subdomain, no custom domain/white-label); 3-month data retention; only 5 integrations allowed; no login seats, no notify seats; monthly email reports only first 3 months; no SMS/voice credits included (pay-per-pack, from $3 one-time for 10). No credit card required. Free for any use including commercial and business use under current terms.
findings.eligibility: Everyone: no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no region limit, no credit card. Commercial use allowed again per terms updated 2026-05-26; governed by a Fair Use Policy (no coordinated multi-account circumvention, no automation patterns straining shared infrastructure; enforcement discretionary).
findings.claim: Register free at uptimerobot.com (pricing page 'Register now'); no credit card. Paid upgrades optional via 'Upgrade' in header/My Settings.

findings.name: CloudWatch / X-Ray / Synthetics Always-Free offers (Monitoring + Uptime)
findings.detail: Unlimited-duration, per-account monthly allowances confirmed on the CloudWatch pricing page today: 10 custom or Detailed Monitoring metrics; 1M CloudWatch API requests/month (excluding GetMetricData, GetInsightRuleReport, GetMetricWidgetImage, which are always charged); CloudWatch Logs 5 GB/month covering ingestion + archive storage + Logs Insights data scanned, plus 1,800 Live Tail minutes/month, 1 Contributor Insights rule/month and first 1M matching log events/month free; 3 custom dashboards referencing up to 50 metrics each (all Automatic Dashboards free); 10 alarm metrics (Standard resolution, direct metric listing, no Metrics Insights queries); Synthetics 100 canary runs/month (uptime checks); X-Ray first 100,000 traces recorded/month and 1,000,000 traces retrieved/scanned/month; RUM one-time trial of 1M web events; Application Observability: 3-month trial per account OR caps of 100 GB ingested / 1M X-Ray trace-summary spans / 100M signals, whichever first. The 'known so far' amounts (1M API requests, 10 metrics, 5 GB logs, 100 canaries, 3 dashboards, 10 alarms, 100K X-Ray traces) are all still correct today.
findings.eligibility: All AWS customers, new and existing, indefinitely; no .edu email, no startup status, no funding cap, no credit card required for most sign-ups (payment method may be requested for identity verification in some cases). Not available in China (Beijing/Ningbo) or AWS GovCloud (US) regions; limits are aggregated across all regions per account, no monthly rollover.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim or activate: create a normal AWS account (Free plan at sign-up gets zero charges) and usage under these caps bills as $0 automatically. Verify in Billing console > Free Tier page; CloudWatch Free Tier usage alerts fire at 85% of a limit.
findings.expiry: Always-free: no sunset, caps reset monthly, do not roll over. Under the new Free plan (accounts after Jul 15 2025), Always-Free offers are the only offers active on the Free plan; on the Paid plan, overage past these caps is automatically covered by remaining Free Tier credits, then standard pay-as-you-go.
findings.gotchas: GetMetricData / GetInsightRuleReport / GetMetricWidgetImage API calls are ALWAYS charged even within the 1M limit; High/Composite alarms, Container Insights observations, OTel metrics ingestion ($0.50/GB), Metrics Streams and Anomaly Detection alarms cost extra; exceeding a cap on the Free plan suspends the account once credits run out (no overage bills possible, but your monitoring dies); 3-month Application Observability trial starts on first use.

findings.name: AWS Free Tier credit model (up to $200 credits, 6-month Free plan)
findings.detail: As of Jul 15, 2025 the 12-month free tier for NEW accounts was replaced by a credit model: $100 credit at sign-up + up to $100 more earned via 5 activities in the Explore AWS widget (EC2 launch/terminate, RDS config, Lambda web app, Bedrock prompt, AWS Budgets budget = $20 each), max $200. Free plan: no charges ever, expires at earlier of 6 months or credit exhaustion, then account is suspended with a 90-day window to upgrade to Paid before AWS permanently deletes the account and data. Paid plan: same credits but pay-as-you-go after they run out; new customers on Paid can still redeem promotional credits (e.g. AWS Activate). 30+ always-free services remain on both plans.
findings.eligibility: All new customers worldwide, students included; no .edu email required; new AWS customers ONLY — anyone who has ever had an AWS account is ineligible; payment method not required for most new customers (social sign-in via Google/GitHub/Apple/Amazon supported since the Oct 2026 new sign-up experience); excluded from China (ZHY/BJS) and GovCloud regions.
findings.claim: Create account at aws.amazon.com (or new sign-up flow) choosing Free or Paid plan; complete the 5 activities within 6 months to earn the extra $100; upgrade to Paid within 90 days of suspension to keep resources and remaining credits.
findings.expiry: Free plan: 6 months from account creation or credit depletion, whichever first; 90-day post-suspension grace then permanent deletion. Credit expiry is inconsistent across AWS pages: FAQ says base $100 expires 6 months and earned credits 12 months from account creation (upgrade to Paid shifts remaining credits to a 12-month window per Jul 2025 terms), while the Jul 9 2025 Terms say 12 months — plan on the EARLIER date and check the Credits page / Settings Portal in your account.
findings.gotchas: Free plan accounts are NOT eligible for promotional/Activate credits and cannot purchase paid offers — startups needing Activate credits must run a Paid plan; joining AWS Organizations or a Control Tower landing zone instantly upgrades Free to Paid and you stop earning credits; on Free plan only the ~90 services on the restricted list are available and overage on always-free items consumes your credit pool; no credit transfer between accounts; Free plan is for evaluation only (no sensitive data).

findings.name: AWS Activate Credits for startups (Founders up to $5K, Portfolio up to $200K)
findings.detail: Two tiers read from aws.amazon.com/startups/credits today: (1) Activate Founders — self-funded/seeded: $1,000 at start, select participants up to $5,000 total; (2) Activate Portfolio — must use an Organization ID (Org ID) from an Activate Provider (accelerator/VC/angel, e.g. Y Combinator, Sequoia, a16z, Brex, Carta, Rho): up to $200,000. Credits apply to 200+ AWS services, third-party foundation models on Amazon Bedrock, Kiro, and eligible Support plans. An invite-only 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' tier offers $200,000+ post-Activate via your Account Manager. Application turnaround 5-10 business days.
findings.eligibility: Startups: pre-Series B (most recent funding round within last 12 months, if applicable), founded in the last 10 years, fully functioning company website, AWS Account on Paid Tier Plan required, and must be new to Activate Credits or requesting more than previously received; no .edu email involved; no hard 'funding cap' — stage gates it. Portfolio tier additionally requires being affiliated with an Activate Provider and holding their Org ID.
findings.claim: 1) Create/verify an AWS Builder ID (personal email); 2) complete the AWS Activate profile (use your business-domain email); 3) pick tier — Founders directly, or Portfolio with your provider's Org ID; 4) link your AWS account and submit; AWS responds in 5-10 business days and credits are applied to the account.
findings.expiry: Promotional-credit expiry by size (since Jun 2024): $100K-class credits expire in 1 year, $200K-class in 3 years from receipt; confirm exact dates on the Credits page. The program itself is ongoing, not a trial; repeated applications are allowed only when requesting more than previously received.
findings.gotchas: AWS Account must be on a Paid plan (so a real billing payment method is effectively required — the Free plan cannot hold Activate credits); Free-plan accounts get none of this; credits do not cover AWS Marketplace purchases, RI upfront, training/cert fees or professional services; AWS has final say even with a provider vouch; multiple startups per founder or equal/higher prior credits can make a startup ineligible; credit exhaustion auto-switches to pay-as-you-go.

findings.name: Kiro Startup Credits (AI IDE, for early-stage startups)
findings.detail: Relaunched Apr 7, 2026: up to 1 year of Kiro Pro+ (agentic AI IDE by AWS) across three tiers — Starter (up to 2 users), Growth (up to 10), Scale (up to 30). Approved credits are deposited into the startup's AWS account and bill Kiro usage for free until exhausted or expired, then standard Kiro Pro+ billing starts automatically on the card on file. The original v1 (launched Dec 3, 2025 at re:Invent, up to 100 users, pre-seed to Series B, apply by Dec 31, 2025) is closed and was replaced.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage to Series A startups; current promotion states VC-backed; official business email whose domain matches the startup's company website AND an AWS Account ID using that same email; 18+; excludes residents of Argentina, Belarus, Brazil, China/GCR, Cuba, France, Germany, Iran, Italy, Mexico, North Korea, Poland, Russia, Spain, Syria, Crimea, DNR, LNR, UAE. Startups with ACTIVE AWS Activate Credits are NOT eligible (Activate credits can instead be used to pay for Kiro; Kiro first, then Apply to Activate is allowed).
findings.claim: Apply at aws.amazon.com/startups/credits/kiro (window Apr 7 – Dec 31, 2026, rolling review, email notification). On approval: enable IAM Identity Center in AWS (required first step), create users/groups, activate the Kiro subscription in the AWS console, and sign developers in to Kiro via the org identity (Builder ID or Google/GitHub sign-in will NOT redeem the credits).
findings.expiry: Application deadline Dec 31, 2026; credits expire exactly 1 year after issuance to the AWS account; non-refundable, non-reissuable, one subscription per startup; overage past your tier's user count or upgrade above Pro+ incurs charges.
findings.gotchas: Team members must cancel their individual paid Kiro accounts after setup or they get double-billed; choosing the wrong region when enabling IAM Identity Center causes silent sign-in auth failures; credits activate on provision, not on your schedule — claim only when you'll use it within the year.

findings.name: AWS Educate + Student Rewards on AWS Builder Center (students)
findings.detail: AWS Educate is now a free, self-paced learning platform (labs for S3/EC2/VPC/RDS + job board) open to anyone 13+ with just an email address — no credit card needed, no .edu required, and no universal credit grant (institute credit grants were discontinued Feb 2023; some member institutions still run their own grants, e.g. $100/yr per student, refreshed until graduation; legacy qwikLABS 'Starter Account' gave $75 credits no-CC). The new student money program is Student Rewards (launched Aug 2026, part of a $500M commitment): verified university students 18+ get 12 months Skill Builder Premium (900+ courses/labs, $449 value) for a complete profile, $10 AWS credits at 7 badges, $20 at 14 badges, and a $100 AWS Foundational exam voucher at 21 badges — up to $579 total per student. Credits redeem as promo codes in the Billing console and apply to eligible AWS services (not Marketplace, exam fees, RI upfront, or Pro Services).
findings.eligibility: Student Rewards: verified higher-ed enrollment via SheerID (enrollment check, not a .edu email), 18+; open to students worldwide in 60+ countries. Educate: anyone 13+ with an email (verified), no payment method; institutional grant variants require enrollment at a participating school.
findings.claim: Sign in to AWS Builder Center, complete SheerID student verification, fill the profile (unlocks Skill Builder premium), then earn badges by publishing articles/comments/engagement to unlock the $10 + $20 credit codes and the $100 exam voucher; redeem codes in AWS Billing & Cost Management > Credits.
findings.expiry: Skill Builder access lasts 12 months from unlock; the program is ongoing (no published end date; rolling); institutional grants renew annually until graduation where the school still participates.
findings.gotchas: The $30 in credits is modest — the real value is Skill Builder + exam voucher; to redeem into a standalone AWS account, AWS may still ask for a credit card on file; do NOT plan a project around Educate credits that no longer exist; legacy 12-month and pre-Jul-2025 free tier limits are gone — use the Free Tier credit model instead.

findings.name: CloudFront Free plan (CDN/Uptime front)
findings.detail: CloudFront now ships a standing $0/month 'Free' plan tier (alongside Pro/Business/Premium/Custom): 100 GB of data transfer out per month + 1M requests/month, 'no overage charges', 5 GB of S3 Standard storage credits, default WAF/DDoS/TLS with 5 WAF rules. This is the successor presentation of the classic 'always-free 100 GB/month CloudFront' allowance. Missing from Free tier: Uptime SLA, logging, bot management, advanced DDoS, private origins, origin failover, high-speed origin routing, and >5 WAF rules.
findings.eligibility: All AWS customers indefinitely (standing plan tier, not a trial or 12-month offer); no .edu or startup status; no credit card required for most sign-ups; same region/policy constraints as standard CloudFront.
findings.claim: Create a CloudFront distribution and leave it on the Free plan (default); upgrade to Pro/Business/Premium/Custom when you need the missing features — overage does not exist on Free, you simply upgrade.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; no sunset date. 'May not be combined with other offers, promotions, or discounts.'
findings.gotchas: No Uptime SLA or CloudWatch access logs on Free (your monitoring/dashboards that rely on them lose data — relevant to the Uptime & CDN fronts); 5-WAF-rule cap; the S3 'credit' is a 5 GB storage allotment, not $ value; if your distribution outgrows 100 GB you must move to a paid plan, which has its own egress pricing.

findings.name: AWS Academy (accredited-institution education license)
findings.detail: For AWS-accredited universities/institutions: free instructor-led curriculum (Cloud Foundations, ML Foundations; Associate level adds Cloud Development/Architecting/Cloud Operations/Data Analytics), free lab environments, a 50% discount exam voucher for AWS certification exams for students, and labs provisioned with up to US$100 of AWS credits per student per lab (budget provided by the institution, not a universal student grant).
findings.eligibility: Students and faculty at AWS-accredited institutions; faculty must complete AWS Academy instructor accreditation for Associate-level courses; no individual self-serve enrollment — it is an institution license, so eligibility is effectively 'your school must be an AWS Academy partner.'
findings.claim: Institution becomes AWS Academy accredited; faculty enroll students into class; students access learning + lab environment with institution-provisioned credits.
findings.expiry: Institution license term; the 50% exam voucher is one-time per license grant; lab credits refresh per lab as provisioned.
findings.gotchas: Not a universal student offer — if your institution is not accredited, there is no personal grant; credits are per-lab, not a standing balance; exam discount is 50%, not free.

findings.name: AWS Education Equity Initiative (education-focused orgs)
findings.detail: Part of a $100M commitment of AWS technology: edtech companies, non-profits, governments and CSR teams building digital learning solutions for underserved learners can apply for up to $10,000 USD in AWS credits plus technical advising from AWS Solutions Architects (advice/demos only — no build service). Applications reviewed on a rolling basis, responses ~3 weeks; typically each organization is supported once.
findings.eligibility: The ORGANIZATION applying (edtech/startup/non-profit/government), not individual students; pro-social enterprises welcome; new-to-AWS orgs self-serve the application; existing customers with an Account Manager go through the AM.
findings.claim: Submit the application form (or ask your AM), describe underserved audience + quantified reach + proposed solution; credits + SA advising issued on award.
findings.expiry: Ongoing program; credits are standard AWS promotional credits (subject to AWS Promotional Credit T&Cs).
findings.gotchas: Not monitoring/observability-specific and not a student offer — included only because it sits under the education front; advising is guidance, not implementation; 'we typically support organizations once.'

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes (all verified against AWS pages today, 2026-10-22): (1) Jul 15, 2025 — the legacy "12 months free" tier was replaced for NEW accounts by a credit-based Free Tier: $100 sign-up credit + up to $100 earned, 6-month Free plan; every legacy 12-month offer on pre-Jul-15-2025 accounts (including legacy CloudWatch 12-month items) has now fully lapsed. (2) Oct 2026 — AWS launched a new sign-up experience: social sign-in (Google/GitHub/Apple/Amazon), no credit card needed for most customers, and credit tracking moved from the Billing console to a Settings Portal for accounts signed up after the rollout; the Free Tier FAQ now states base credits expire 6 months (vs. 12 months in the Jul 9, 2025 Terms) — a live contradiction AWS hasn't harmonized, so treat 6 months as the safe planning horizon. (3) Dec 3, 2025 — Kiro Startup Credits v1 launched (up to 100 users, pre-seed to Series B, apply by Dec 31, 2025) and closed; relaunched Apr 7, 2026 with 2/10/30-user tiers, early-stage to Series A (VC-backed per the current promotion), apply by Dec 31, 2026; startups with active AWS Activate credits are excluded from the Kiro promo. (4) Jun 2024 (context) — AWS doubled Portfolio credits $100K to $200K and extended expiry 1 year to 3 years; still the structure in effect. (5) Feb 2023 (context) — AWS Educate stopped issuing universal/institutional credit grants; it is now free learning only, and student credits now flow through Builder Center Student Rewards (up to $579 incl. $30 credits + $100 exam voucher, launched Aug 2026). (6) CloudFront's classic "100 GB/month always-free" line is now presented as a standing $0 "Free" plan tier with 100 GB + 1M requests + 5 GB S3 storage credits and no overage charges — not sunset, but restructured.
