No CloudWatch/observability offer was sunset; the known limits (10 metrics, 1M API requests, 5 GB logs, 100 canaries, 3 dashboards, 10 alarms, 100K X-Ray traces) all still apply as ALWAYS-FREE allowances. There is no CloudWatch-specific startup or student grant beyond the general AWS Free Tier credits and Activate credits, which can offset CloudWatch usage on a Paid plan.

provider: Better Stack (betterstack.com) — Observability, Monitoring, Uptime & Status Pages

findings.name: Better Stack Free Plan ("Free for personal projects")
findings.detail: $0/month forever tier (verified on official pricing page fetched 2026-10-22, plus pricing.md copy and a PulseSignal change-history snapshot verified 2026-10-20). Exact free allowances: 10 monitors and 10 heartbeats combined; 1 public status page (1,000 status-page subscribers included; custom sub-domain on a betterstack subdomain or your own CNAME sub-domain listed in the feature set); 100,000 exceptions/month for error tracking; 5,000 session replays/month; 3 GB logs/month retained 3 days; 3 GB traces/month retained 3 days; 30 GB metrics; 3 GB web events/month retained 3 days; Slack and e-mail alerts only (no phone/SMS on free); on-call scheduling and basic single-channel Slack/Teams integration listed as included; 3-minute minimum check interval on free (30-second requires a paid Responder). Team member (Telemetry access) roles are $0/month — unlimited dashboard-only viewers free.
findings.eligibility: No student-specific or .edu requirement, no region limit: the free plan is open to anyone who signs up (e-mail/Google sign-up at betterstack.com/users/sign-up), but the plan is explicitly labeled "Free for personal projects" — signaling personal/non-commercial intent. No credit card is listed as required for the free plan (only the 60-day money-back guarantee, which applies to paid plans).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up free at betterstack.com/users/sign-up (no CC step advertised). 2) In the dashboard create up to 10 monitors + 10 heartbeats. 3) Create the included status page and attach monitors. 4) Add up to 3 GB/month logs, 30 GB metrics, 100K exceptions, 5K session replays under the free caps.
findings.expiry: No expiry — it is a permanent $0/month plan, not a trial. Paid plans carry a 60-day money-back guarantee; that does not apply to or alter the free tier.
findings.gotchas: 1) Labeled for personal projects — commercial/startup production use may fall outside the stated intent of the free plan (no explicit commercial prohibition published on the pricing page). 2) Alerts on free are Slack + e-mail only; phone-call, SMS and unlimited push require a Responder license ($29/mo annual, $34/mo monthly billed). 3) Free check interval is 3 min vs 30 s paid; 4) log/trace/web-event retention is only 3 days; 5) status-page upgrades are steep (white-label, SSO, IP allowlisting $250/page/mo; custom CSS/JS $15/page/mo; extra page $15/mo). 6) Additional monitors cost $25/mo per 50-pack (monthly) and heartbeats $20/mo per 10-pack — the free plan is not a trial of paid volume.

findings.name: Free Telemetry team seats (and new "Free responder access" entry, added 2026-10-06)
findings.detail: On the official pricing page, the "Team member (Telemetry access)" role is $0/month with no stated seat cap, so any number of dashboard-only viewers is free. A third-party price tracker (PulseSignal, verified 2026-10-20) records that on 2026-10-06 the plan previously named "Free" was renamed "Free for personal projects" and a new plan entry "Free responder access" ($0) was added — i.e., Better Stack has recently added free responder-tier access for at least some users. I did not see a "Free responder access" row in today's pricing fetch, so treat the exact scope (all accounts vs. one free responder per account) as unconfirmed.
findings.eligibility: Free for any Better Stack account (team-member roles); the new free-responder entry's qualification rules are not published where I could read them.
findings.claim: Invite extra team members as Telemetry-access members ($0 each). Check the plan picker at betterstack.com/pricing for the "Free responder access" option and select it when creating a team.
findings.expiry: No published expiry on the free roles; the free-responder entry is brand new (2026-10-06) and its terms may still be evolving.
findings.gotchas: Telemetry members cannot receive phone/SMS alerts or be on-call; anything on-call-capable is a paid Responder. The 2026-10-06 change means older third-party comparisons describing Better Stack's free offer are one revision stale.

findings.name: Startup deal via third-party aggregators ("6 months free Pro" on SaaSOffers; 25% off annual via Freelance Stack) — NOT a vendor-run startup program
findings.detail: betterstack.com/startups returns 404 and the pricing page contains no startup program. SaaSOffers (aggregator, self-labeled 'verified October 2026') advertises a '6 months free Pro' deal for startups (~$300 claimed value, 'accelerator-backed startups' eligibility described with generic template language); Freelance Stack advertises an 'additional 25% off annual plans' Better Stack partner promo for new customers. Neither is a Better Stack-published program with stated eligibility (funding cap, company age, headcount).
findings.eligibility: As documented by the aggregators only: SaaSOffers says qualifying/accelerator-backed startups, no referral needed, apply via the aggregator; no .edu or funding-cap criteria published by Better Stack itself. Region: global.
findings.claim: SaaSOffers path: create a free SaaSOffers account (no CC) -> open saasoffers.tech/offers/betterstack -> click 'Claim Deal' and follow the activation steps to apply the discount to a new Better Stack paid plan. Freelance Stack path: sign up through their deal link, subscribe to a new account, then request cashback/discount per their instructions.
findings.expiry: Third-party deals; no vendor-published end date. '6 months' is the deal value itself, not a program duration; both aggregators note offers change frequently.
findings.gotchas: These are affiliate/deal-aggregator offers, not an official Better Stack startup program — eligibility and mechanics are enforced by the aggregator, not the vendor. No funding cap or age cap is documented anywhere on betterstack.com. A paid subscription is required to benefit, so this is a discount/trial-credit path, not a permanent free offer; if you outgrow the free plan, the free tier remains available independently.

findings.name: Education/student program: none found (explicit negative)
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22 there is no Better Stack education license or student offer: betterstack.com/education is 404, the pricing page lists no student/education tier, the official docs FAQ mentions no education discount, and two independent price trackers explicitly mark Better Stack education terms as 'not verified/unknown'. Students can only use the general 'Free for personal projects' plan (finding 1). A nonprofit plan does exist ('We're happy to support non-profit organizations... apply for our non-profit plan' in the official docs FAQ) — adjacent, but not a student/startup offer.
findings.eligibility: n/a — no eligibility rules exist because no program exists.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim for students. A student's only free options: the standard free plan (betterstack.com/users/sign-up) or the third-party aggregator deals (finding 3).
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Absence confirmed by negative evidence (404s + trackers saying 'not verified') as of 2026-10-22; Better Stack could introduce an education offer at any time. Do not cite SaaSOffers' '6 months free Pro' as a student offer — its stated audience is startups.

findings.name: Non-profit plan (out of scope for students/startups, noted for completeness)
findings.detail: Better Stack's official docs FAQ states: 'We're happy to support non-profit organizations. Learn more about our non-profit plan and how to apply on this page' (link on the FAQ page not fully retrievable in this pass). No amounts or eligibility details were visible on the page I read.
findings.eligibility: Non-profit organizations only; not students or startups.
findings.claim: Apply via the link on the official docs FAQ page (betterstack.com/docs/uptime/frequently-asked-questions/) or contact hello@betterstack.com.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Details unconfirmed; treat as a lead to follow up with the vendor directly.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes, none of which sunsetting the free plan: (1) 2026-10-06 — the plan previously named "Free" was renamed "Free for personal projects" and a new "Free responder access" ($0) entry appeared (PulseSignal change history, vendor page verified 2026-10-20). (2) 2026-09-11 — Responder monthly price rose from $29/mo to $34/mo (annual rate stayed $29/mo) per FrontDeskReview's correction log. (3) 2026-08-01 — telemetry pricing was restructured into per-region bundles (US / Europe / Singapore) with old "Bundle" plan names removed. (4) 2026-08-25 — a standalone "Transaction Monitoring" plan was removed; transaction (Playwright) monitoring moved to per-minute usage pricing, and "1 responder included in the starting offer" was added to Responder terms. (5) Macro pivot 2025-2026: after an $18.6M Series A (led by Creandum), Better Stack stopped selling monitor-count tiers (old "Freelancer/Small Team/Business" names seen in third-party articles are stale) and now prices per Responder seat plus telemetry bundles — so third-party pages still showing "$24 Basic / $45 Freelancer" pricing are outdated. (6) The free-tier telemetry allowances have grown over time: secondary 2026 early-year sources cite 1 GB logs free; the current official page lists 3 GB logs, 3 GB traces, 30 GB metrics — no limits were removed, only expanded. (7) Rebrand context: Better Uptime + Logtail were merged into the "Better Stack" platform (2022-2023 press post); pricing survived the merge unchanged. (8) An adjacent non-profit plan exists per the official docs FAQ but no student or formal startup program ever existed on betterstack.com (betterstack.com/education and /startups both 404 as of 2026-10-22).

provider: New Relic (Observability / Monitoring / Uptime — no CDN product; "uptime" front is covered by synthetic monitoring)

findings.name: Perpetual Free Tier (all accounts; no .edu or startup requirement)
findings.detail: Free forever plan verified on newrelic.com/pricing as of 2026-10-22: 100 GB data ingest/month (account-wide, not per user), 1 full-platform user with access to all 50+ platform capabilities (APM with distributed tracing, infrastructure monitoring, error tracking, digital experience monitoring), unlimited basic users (view custom non-quickstart dashboards, query, alert), 500 synthetic checks/month, unlimited hosts/agents/containers/devices/AWS Fargate tasks/cloud functions, default data retention at least 8 days, default log obfuscation. Explicitly no data egress or hydration charges. Overage: if you exceed 100 GB in a month, data ingest ceases and you lose platform access until you upgrade or the 1st of the following month (auto re-enables). Paid contrast for context: Pro full user $349/user annual or $418.80/month; Core user $49; overage $0.40/GB standard or $0.60/GB 'Data Plus' add-on; EU data-center storage +$0.05/GB/month.
findings.eligibility: Anyone: no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card required ('No credit card required to start' per pricing FAQ), no stated region limits.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free New Relic account at newrelic.com (no credit card). 2) Free tier is active immediately with the 100 GB/mo + 1 full user + 500 synthetic checks. 3) Overage suspends ingest until the 1st or an upgrade — never billed.
findings.expiry: Perpetual; no expiry date. Monthly limits reset on the 1st of each month.
findings.gotchas: Exceeding 100 GB halts ingest AND platform access for the month (not a bill, but you go dark). Only 1 full-platform user is free — team collaboration relies on unlimited basic users (restricted access). The '10,000 synthetic monitors' figure that appears in a pay-as-you-go FAQ is a different (paid-edition) benefit, not the free 500 checks. No separate time-boxed free trial is advertised — the perpetual tier is the trial replacement.

findings.name: New Relic for Students (education program)
findings.detail: Verified on newrelic.com/students as of 2026-10-22: 500 GB data ingest per month and 3 full-platform users (vs. 100 GB / 1 user on the standard free tier), plus access to 30+ platform capabilities, a monthly newsletter, exclusive certifications/workshops, potential sponsorships, and office hours with New Relic staff. Benefits are gated behind linking an education partner account.
findings.eligibility: Students (and select technical-bootcamp students) at accredited colleges, universities, or technical schools; 'proof of current student status is required'. Two routes: (a) GitHub Education — students in the GitHub Student Developer Pack, verified via GitHub; (b) Platzi — open to Spanish/Portuguese-speaking learners in Latin America and beyond, but Platzi's side requires a monthly course subscription. Select bootcamps only; others email students@newrelic.com. No .edu-email-only shortcut is documented.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free New Relic account (no credit card). 2) Have an active account with a partner: GitHub Education (verify student status in GitHub) or Platzi. 3) GitHub path: in New Relic go to Help icon → 'New Relic for Students' → 'GitHub Education' → 'Authorize with GitHub'. Platzi/other-partner path: submit the form with your 7-digit New Relic account number; benefits land in 5–10 business days. 4) Non-eligible bootcamp students email students@newrelic.com for manual verification.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page. No renewal date, cap, or grace period is published; presumably reverts to the standard 100 GB/month free tier if student status is lost.
findings.gotchas: Perks only activate after linking a partner account. Platzi route: the New Relic tier is free but Platzi itself costs a subscription. Graduating or losing student status has no documented re-enrollment or grace language — expect to drop to the base free tier. 3 full users is for 'collaborative projects' (class group work).

findings.name: New Relic for Startups program
findings.detail: Verified on newrelic.com/startups as of 2026-10-22: 5 full-platform users plus 'generous data ingest per month, free' — the exact GB figure is not published on the page. Full platform 'from day one — no gating, no tool switching' (AI Monitoring, APM, Logs), explicitly 'not just bankrolled with credits'; also includes a New Relic engineer alongside launch, office hours, and quarterly architecture reviews.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups; the page itself publishes NO startup-age cap, funding cap, headcount cap, or region limit — thresholds are applied during application review. No credit-card requirement mentioned (consistent with the no-CC free signup).
findings.claim: 1) Submit the multi-step 'New Relic for Startups Registration' form on newrelic.com/startups. 2) 'Our team will reach out shortly, to process your application, and to confirm your place and next steps' — benefits are confirmed post-review rather than instantly granted.
findings.expiry: Not disclosed on the page (no program length, renewal terms, or end date).
findings.gotchas: Key numbers (monthly GB allotment, program duration, funding/age caps) are not public — the page is a marketing/registration funnel, so treat the exact benefit as 'confirmed after application'. Do not assume 100 GB: that figure on the site belongs to the standard free tier, not the startup program. If not accepted, you fall back to the perpetual free tier.

sunset_notes: No New Relic free offer was sunset or materially changed in 2025-2026 per pages fetched today (2026-10-22): the perpetual free tier (100 GB/month, 1 full user, unlimited basic users, 500 synthetic checks) is still advertised on newrelic.com/pricing, the site navigation still shows '100GB/month free' / 'New Relic Free Tier', the students program (500 GB/mo, 3 users) is live at newrelic.com/students, and the startups program is live at newrelic.com/startups. No separate time-boxed 'free trial' is currently advertised — the perpetual free tier with no credit card is the entry point. Note: WebSearch could not be run this session (search budget exhausted), so 2025-2026 change-verification relied on fetching official pages and the blog index rather than searching; the blog index (Oct 2026 posts) shows no pricing/plan sunset announcements. Also: New Relic has no free CDN offer at all (CDN is not a New Relic product); the 'Uptime' front maps to the 500 free synthetic checks in the free tier. 'Observability for Good' (nonprofits) exists but is out of scope (not a student/startup program).

findings.claim: 1) cloud.google.com/free → select the free trial. 2) Create a Google Cloud account and enter a credit card (verification only; $0.00–$1.00 auth hold, not charged during trial). 3) A new GCP project is created; the $300 applies to eligible pay-as-you-go products for 90 days. 4) Before day 90, upgrade to a paid billing account to keep the account open.
findings.detail: One-time $300 welcome credit valid for 90 days; the account is a non-billable free-trial account during that window. If the $300 is spent or 90 days pass without upgrading to a paid billing account, the account auto-closes; a 30-day grace period then allows recovery of stopped resources/data before permanent deletion. GPUs/TPUs cannot be added on a non-billable trial account; the $300 cannot pay Gemini API-in-AI-Studio costs or managed generative-AI partner-model (Model-as-a-Service) usage. Verified on the official trial docs (served from docs.cloud.google.com) on 2026-10-22.
findings.eligibility: Never been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase, and never signed up for the Free Trial (one per person). Credit card / payment method IS required at signup. No .edu or company email requirement.
findings.expiry: Credit valid 90 days from account creation, not renewable; 30-day grace period after expiry; the always-free tier continues indefinitely on the account's products.
findings.gotchas: CC required despite the free label; GPUs/TPUs not allowed on the non-billable trial account; Gemini API costs and managed partner AI models excluded from the $300; unused credit lapses at 90 days; after the grace period resources are stopped and data deleted.
findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial: $300 credit, 90 days (one-time, new customers)

findings.claim: No claiming step: free-tier allotments apply automatically to eligible products/regions; create a GCP project and stay under the caps. For e2-micro: pick one of us-west1 / us-central1 / us-east1, instance e2-micro, standard persistent disk ≤30GB total, one external IP.
findings.detail: Indefinite, no-card free allotments across 20+ products; no end date but Google can change limits with 30 days' notice; unused monthly limits do not roll over. Compute Engine: 1 e2-micro (non-preemptible, 2 shared vCPU / 1 GB RAM) per month + 30 GB-months standard persistent disk + 1 external IP free + 1 GB outbound transfer/month — only in us-west1 (Oregon), us-central1 (Iowa), us-east1 (South Carolina); all eligible hours across those 3 US regions are free up to the month's total hours. Cloud Storage: 5 GB-months regional storage (US regions only), 5,000 Class A + 50,000 Class B operations, 100 GB outbound from North America to any region except China/Australia. Cloud Run: 2M requests/month, 360,000 GiB-s memory, 180,000 vCPU-s compute, 1 GB outbound. Cloud Functions (1st gen): 2M invocations/month, 400,000 GB-s, 5 GB outbound. BigQuery: 1 TiB queries/month free. GPUs and TPUs are explicitly NOT in the free tier — 'you are always charged for GPUs and TPUs that you add to VM instances.' Verified 2026-10-22.
findings.eligibility: Any Google Cloud account (including trial accounts); no credit card required for the free allotments themselves. Region limits: free Compute VM and GCS storage are US-3-regions-only; egress exclusions apply to China and Australia destinations.
findings.expiry: No expiry (indefinite); monthly caps reset each month with no rollover; Google may change limits with 30 days' notice.
findings.gotchas: Only 1 free e2-micro per account per month, only in the 3 US regions; any other machine type, region, GPU/TPU, or extra disk is billed; outbound beyond 1 GB/100 GB quotas is billed; the GCP project still has a billing account with a payment method attached, so a cent over any cap hits the card — set budgets/alerts. Free tier is 'always free'; the time-limited product trials below are separate.
findings.name: Google Cloud Always-Free tier (free forever, no credit card, no trial needed)

findings.claim: From a GCP project, enable/try the product (e.g., Cloud SQL) during its trial window via the console; the trial covers normal usage for the stated days; ensure a billing account with a payment method is in place beforehand.
findings.detail: Separate, time-boxed product trials listed alongside the free tier: Spanner 90-day, Cloud SQL 30-day, AlloyDB 30-day, Looker 30-day; they require a billing account (unlike the always-free allotments which don't). These cover database/BI experiments for 30–90 days without per-use cost. The broader 'free $300 and 20+ free products' hub is cloud.google.com/free. Note: I read these durations from the official free-tier docs today; per-product trial terms (auto-renew, conversion) were not individually re-verified — treat specifics as medium.
findings.eligibility: Requires a Google Cloud billing account (payment method on file). One trial per product/account.
findings.expiry: Spanner 90 days; Cloud SQL/AlloyDB/Looker 30 days each; not renewable (re-apply rules vary per product).
findings.gotchas: After the window, full pay-as-you-go applies; Cloud SQL/AlloyDB can get expensive (instance + storage + egress), so terminate or set budgets before expiry; trials need a billing account where the free-tier items don't.
findings.name: Time-limited product trials bundled with the free tier (Spanner 90d, Cloud SQL 30d, AlloyDB 30d, Looker 30d, etc.)

findings.claim: 1) Prepare the 18-character GCP billing account ID, a business email whose domain matches the company website domain, and a live, non-placeholder company website. 2) Apply at cloud.google.com/startups ('Apply now'), pick tier (Start $2k, or Scale/Scale AI if funded; stealth founders via investor/VC referral). 3) Wait 5–7 days for the automated accept/reject email (check spam). 4) Credits deposit into the selected billing account; request the Workspace and Maps benefits separately.
findings.detail: Successor of the old 'Google Cloud Startup Program'. Tiers per the live page (fetched 2026-10-22): Start tier = $2,000 credits for startups founded in the past 2 years with a working MVP and plans to seek venture funding. Funded tiers = Scale and Scale AI, $200K–$350K total credits, for startups with verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding (founded within the last 3–5 years). Footnoted math: AI startups get 100% of GCP spend up to $250,000 in Year 1 and 20% (matching) up to an additional $100,000 in Year 2 (max $350K); non-AI startups get 100% up to $100,000 Year 1 and 20% up to $100,000 Year 2. Perks also include credits for frontier models like Gemini and Gemma (third-party models in Model Garden/Marketplace billed directly), Google Skills training, Startup Success Managers + Customer Engineering, and 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no cost (separate application; company domain must not have had a paid Workspace plan within 31 days before applying; a separate Maps application is required for monthly Google Maps Platform credits). Credits cover most Google-owned pay-as-you-go GCP products; subscription/prepay products and 3P Marketplace/Model Garden items are excluded. Acceptance is discretionary (funding stage/type, business model, founder experience, product usage, vertical, age, growth); response in 5–7 days. Non-VC funding (private equity, bank loans, government programs, grants, crowdfunding, friends & family) does not qualify for the funded tiers; re-application is allowed if prior credits went unused and current-year criteria are met.
findings.eligibility: For-profit, digital-native company; not IPO'd/acquired; excludes educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content, dev shops, consultancies, agencies, crypto-mining companies, and token distributors in violation of local regulation; must operate in a region where GCP is GA and self-service. Funded tiers: verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding from a known investor, founded within the last 3–5 years. Requirements: GCP billing account ID (18 chars), business email whose domain matches the company website domain, active website (heavily AI-generated content screened and may be rejected). The application itself is free and needs no credit card, but a GCP billing account — which normally carries a payment method — is the delivery vehicle for the credits. Credits are non-transferable and cannot be shared, split, or resold; doing so terminates enrollment.
findings.expiry: Credits granted over 2 years: Year 1 100% (up to $250K AI / $100K other), Year 2 20% matching up to an additional $100K; Workspace benefit = 12 months; program qualifications change annually and previous enrollment does not guarantee re-enrollment.
findings.gotchas: Funded tiers require VC/known-investor funding — non-venture money disqualifies you from Scale; company email domain must equal the website domain or extra proof is requested; third-party models and subscription-billed products are excluded; past GCP credit usage is a (discretionary) acceptance factor; don't expect the generic $300 trial to auto-upgrade into this program — it is a separate application; AI-generated-heavy websites are screened and can cause rejection.
findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program (up to $350,000 GCP credits over 2 years + 12 months Google Workspace Business Plus + monthly Google Maps Platform credits)

findings.claim: 1) Faculty complete the form at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/faculty). 2) Provide the official school email, faculty directory link, institution + department. 3) Per course (up to 3): course name, expected start date, abstract + how credits will be used, a URL that proves you teach the course, student email domain(s), expected student/TA counts. 4) Submit; only the most recent submission is reviewed; on approval, credits attach to the institution's email domains.
findings.detail: Faculty of accredited institutions can apply for GCP credits for themselves and students so students get hands-on classroom experience. Verified numbers from cloud.google.com/edu/faculty: up to $100 per teaching staff member and up to $50 per student in Cloud credits. Terms (from the official application form, read today): up to 3 courses per application; course start date no later than 1 year from application; credits redeemable from approval until 16 weeks after the course start date, and valid up to 1 year after the course start date; confirmation emails come from CloudEduGrants@google.com (whitelist that alias); group projects can pool students' individual credits. Related: 'Career Launchpad Program' gives students access to Google Cloud Certificates/credentials content.
findings.eligibility: Faculty only (students should have their faculty apply) at an accredited institution; official school-issued email with a valid .edu/.ac domain required (a nominated alternate email is possible — credits attach to it and are non-transferable); available only in the listed ~65 countries (incl. US, UK, EU, India, Japan, Brazil, others). No credit card required — these are promotional education credits, distinct from the paid-card $300 trial.
findings.expiry: Credits valid up to 1 year after the course start date; must be redeemed by 16 weeks after course start (from approval); non-transferable, educational use only.
findings.gotchas: Google's own faculty docs explicitly warn: keep students off the $300 Free Trial (it requires a credit card) — use these course credits instead; country list is closed; resubmitting a form replaces the previous submission (the most recent is the one reviewed); multiple sections of the same course in the same period count as one course.
findings.name: Google for Education faculty ('teaching') credits: up to $100 per teaching staff + up to $50 per student, for classroom use

findings.claim: 1) Fill the form at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/researchers). 2) Provide job title (faculty/postdoc/PhD/IT admin), organization, directory or candidacy link, project name + start date, a 250-word proposal (Google Doc link or paste) covering problem, GCP tools, timeline, milestones, and future GCP use, a field of research, a pricing-calculator estimate with its URL, a GCP billing account ID, and your post-credit funding plan. 3) On approval, redeem within 60 days of the project start date.
findings.detail: For accredited higher-education and eligible nonprofit research institutions: up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits (cloud.google.com/edu/researchers says 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'). Terms from the official application form (read today): credit must be activated within 60 days of the project start date; it expires 365 days from the coupon redemption date or when the amount is fully used; non-transferable, no commercial value or commercial use; faculty accept on the institution's behalf, PhD students only for the described project. Related: GPAR (Google Public Sector — Program for Accelerated Research) gives expert/researcher collaboration from Google + partners and on-campus research days (a services program, not a credit pool).
findings.eligibility: Faculty, PhD students, and postdoctoral researchers from accredited higher-education institutions or eligible nonprofit research institutions, in the approved-country list (~65 countries; undergrad/master students are NOT eligible for research grants). Institution email preferred. No credit card required for the credits themselves (a GCP billing account ID is still needed to receive them).
findings.expiry: Redeem within 60 days of project start; valid 365 days from redemption or until $5,000 used, whichever first; renewal not guaranteed.
findings.gotchas: Credits are for the described project only — no personal or commercial use; you must declare how you'll fund the project after the credit expires; proposals without a GCP cost estimate get bounced; GPAR is a separate expert-collaboration program, not a second credit pool.
findings.name: Google for Education research credits ('Academic Research Grants'): up to $5,000 in GCP credits for 1 year; plus GPAR collaboration program

findings.claim: 1) Go to cloud.google.com/edu/students → 'Request credits' for the 200 Google Skills credits (learning-platform credits; expire 1 year after issue). 2) Use Google Skills to open the free hands-on labs and earn skill badges. 3) Join/apply to a Developer Student Group or attend Cloud OnAir events (both free). 4) For real GCP compute in coursework, use your faculty's teaching credits or a campus institutional agreement.
findings.detail: cloud.google.com/edu/students (read today): students can request 200 free Google Skills credits which expire one year after issue; no-cost access to hands-on labs; skill badges (complete a lab series + challenge-lab final assessment for a shareable credential); Google Cloud Certificates (preview free on YouTube, no prerequisites); Google Skills Arcade by Google Cloud (gamified learning, swag rewards); free Developer Student Groups (join or create a campus chapter); free Cloud OnAir events and YouTube tutorials. There is no .edu-gated GCP compute-credit pool for individual students — students' actual GCP compute comes from faculty teaching credits, the generic $300 trial (CC required), or institutional agreements; the notebook/lab front on GCP therefore runs through faculty credits or trial, while self-serve free lab environments come from Google Skills' sized sandboxes. Confidence is medium on exactly what 200 Skills credits purchase: the page does not publish a per-course price list.
findings.eligibility: Open to students (no .edu email explicitly required to request the Google Skills learning credits or badges; DSGs are campus-based). The $300 trial and free tier remain available to students but the trial needs a card. Google's own faculty docs steer students toward faculty-issued credits instead of the trial.
findings.expiry: Skills credits expire 1 year after issue; labs/badges are free as long as offered.
findings.gotchas: '200 Google Skills credits' are learning-platform credits, not GCP $-credits — don't conflate with the $300 trial; Skills GCP sandboxes are time-boxed/limited; there is no free GCP GPU/TPU access for students (GPUs/TPUs are explicitly outside the free tier).
findings.name: Free student learning offers: 200 Google Skills credits + free hands-on labs, skill badges, Google Cloud Certificates (preview), Google Skills Arcade, Developer Student Groups

findings.claim: 1) Sign in at aistudio.google.com (or colab.research.google.com for notebooks). 2) Create/select a project, generate an API key, pick a model — free-tier quotas apply automatically. 3) Check per-model free limits in the AI Studio rate-limit dashboard; exceeding them moves you to paid tiers (which require a billing account).
findings.detail: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits (read today; page 'Last updated 2026-10-15 UTC'): usage tiers are Free, then paid Tiers 1–3 (with $10/$50/$200 rolling 10-minute spend caps and escalating limits). Free tier qualification: 'an active project or free trial' — no active billing account required, in contrast to Tier 1+ which require a linked billing account. Per-model free RPD/RPM/TPM numbers are not published on that page; they are shown per-project in the Google AI Studio rate-limit dashboard. Batch API free-tier table starts at Tier 1 (no free batch numbers shown). No free fine-tuning/training credits are listed on the page. Related: the GCP $300 trial credit cannot pay Gemini API-in-AI-Studio costs (trial docs), and the startup program's 'prototyping/Start' offering gives pre-funded builders instant AI Studio access (API keys + Gemini, Gemini Omni, Nano Banana, etc.) plus 'credits for frontier models like Gemini and Gemma' in funded tiers, while third-party partner models are billed directly. Google Colab remains the classic free notebooks front (CPU and quota-limited TPU runtimes), but its current exact quotas could not be re-verified in this session (web-search budget was exhausted) — treat remembered Colab numbers as low confidence.
findings.eligibility: Any Google account; the Gemini API free tier needs no credit card and no billing account (Tier 1+ does). GCP trial users: AI Studio Gemini costs are excluded from the $300 trial credit.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry for the free tier (ongoing, subject to Google's policy changes).
findings.gotchas: Free-tier rates are per-project, per-model and can change; the dashboard is the source of truth; no free batch API at the Free tier; no free fine-tuning stated; Colab TPU sessions are quota/time-limited — don't assume old Colab quotas are current; past free limits, paid tier 1 applies its $10 rolling spend-cap structure rather than unlimited use.
findings.name: Gemini API / Google AI Studio free tier (the ML-inference + notebooks front; no credit card)

provider: Google Cloud (Google) — Free Trial + Always-Free tier + Startups + Education
sunset_notes: 1) Startup program renamed/restructured: the legacy 'Google Cloud Startup Program' (commonly cited as up to $200K/2-year funded track plus a YC-alumni track) is gone; cloud.google.com/startups/program and cloud.google.com/programs/startup-program now 404. The live offer (2026) is the 'Google for Startups Cloud Program': Start tier $2k; Scale/Scale AI $200K–$350K over 2 years, with AI startups capped at $250K Year 1 (100% match) + $100K Year 2 (20% match), other startups $100K Y1 + $100K Y2; new 12-month Google Workspace Business Plus benefit and monthly Google Maps Platform credits added. 2) Trial: current official terms are $300/90 days (not the 30/60-day figures seen in third-party summaries, including some of today's truncated page renders); a 30-day recovery grace period after expiry is now documented. 3) Trial restrictions are explicit and new-ish: GPUs/TPUs cannot be added on non-billable trial accounts; the $300 cannot pay Gemini API-in-AI-Studio or managed partner-model costs — so the 'GPU/ML-training' front on GCP trial means CPU (e2s) + free-tier e2-micro, with real GPU/TPU access requiring a paid account. 4) Docs domain moved: cloud.google.com/free/docs/* now 301-redirects to docs.cloud.google.com/free/docs/*. 5) Method caveat: WebSearch was unavailable for this run (shared session search budget exhausted), so 2025–2026 change-detection relied on the live official pages themselves; items I could not re-verify (Colab free quotas, Google Skills credit prices, per-product trial renewal rules) are marked medium/low confidence rather than carried from memory. 6) No evidence found this session that the always-free e2-micro or the education faculty/research grants were sunset — all confirmed live on 2026-10-22.
label_name: Google Cloud Free Trial + Free Tier

findings.claim: No claim step: git clone / download, run the Docker image louislam/uptime-kuma (or bare-metal Node.js >= 20.4 with PM2) on any server; no sign-up, no account, no credit card. A full install via Docker Compose takes ~5-15 minutes. Optional community plugins via the built-in plugin marketplace.
findings.detail: Uptime Kuma is free open-source (MIT) self-hosted monitoring: $0 license, no tiers, no vendor, no monitor caps. Unlimited monitors, multiple public status pages, ~20-second check intervals, 90+ notification channels (Slack, Discord, Telegram, email, webhooks, Pushover, Apprise), 2FA, SSL certificate expiry alerts. Free identically for students, startups, and enterprises. The only cost is hosting: a small VPS (~$5-20/mo per third-party pricing pages) or $0 on an existing always-on box. No .edu email needed, no region limits, no credit card. Funding of the project itself is via GitHub Sponsors/Open Collective (noted special sponsor Atlas Cloud, USD 400/month) - this is optional support, not a purchase requirement. Verified on the official repo today: the page mentions no pricing page, no commercial tier, no cloud service, no education or startup program.
findings.eligibility: Universal - any person or company, including students and startups; no .edu email, no age/funding cap, no region restriction, credit card NOT required (nothing to purchase).
findings.expiry: Perpetual; MIT license grants rights without time limit. No renewal, no trial countdown. Note v2.0.0 (released 2025-10-20) was a major breaking upgrade (rootless Docker images, removed legacy JSON backup/restore, LiquidJS templating) - existing instances must migrate; the software remains free.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: there is no trial - the entire product is permanently free; the paid components are third-party hosting/support, never the software. Data/egress: you pay your VPS host, and misconfigured shared cloud (e.g. Oracle Cloud always-free idle policy, which took down the maintainer's own instance in 2023) can silently stop the monitor. Operational cost: TLS, backups, upgrades, and security are on you; a single self-hosted instance monitors from one location and cannot monitor its own host. NFS filesystems are not supported. The public demo at demo.kuma.pet is temporary (data wiped every 10 minutes) and is not a hosted offering.
findings.name: Uptime Kuma software itself: free MIT license, unlimited monitors & status pages (self-hosted)

findings.claim: Generic (not student/startup-specific) trials: sign up at the host, deploy the Uptime Kuma instance from its catalog. E.g. Elestio: create instance, use $20 trial credits over 3 days (then pay hourly credits; level-1 support free). Stellar Hosted: 14-day free trial on the 100%-money-back-guarantee plans. DANIAN: 7-day free trial, no credit card, then from EUR 9/mo. Enzonic: permanent free tier (812 MB RAM / 100% CPU / 10 GB SSD, no card) that runs Uptime Kuma always-on, subject to availability - the closest thing to a $0 hosted path.
findings.detail: No Uptime Kuma first-party hosting exists, so any 'hosted free Uptime Kuma' comes from third-party PaaS/VPS vendors offering generic free tiers or short trials: Elestio (managed, $20 in trial credits valid 3 days, then hourly credit billing, free level-1 support), Stellar Hosted (14-day free trial; paid plans EUR 49-199+/mo in Amsterdam EU), DANIAN (7-day free trial, no credit card, from EUR 9/mo, 21 regions), Enzonic (free 'Wood-adjacent' tier: 812 MB RAM, 100% CPU, 10 GB NVMe, no credit card, always-on, subject to availability). Kuma Engine (kumaengine.com, third-party LLC, terms updated 2025-07-01) offers fully-managed Uptime Kuma at US$4/mo or US$24/yr with 5 GB block storage, 5 GB monthly transfer, and 5,000 SMTP email notifications - NO free tier. None of these target students or startups with special eligibility.
findings.eligibility: Generic end users; none require .edu email, startup age, or a funding cap. Age 18+ per Kuma Engine ToS. No region limits on Elestio/DANIAN; Stellar is EU (Amsterdam). Credit card NOT required on Enzonic free tier, DANIAN trial, and Elestio trial; Kuma Engine requires prepaid payment.
findings.expiry: Trials: Elestio $20 credits valid 3 days; Stellar 14 days; DANIAN 7 days. Enzonic free tier: 'free forever' but subject to capacity availability. Kuma Engine: none - paid only, auto-renewing, non-refundable.
findings.gotchas: These are hosting offers, not Uptime Kuma offers - terms change with the host, not the project. Enzonic's free tier is capped at ~812 MB RAM and can be reclaimed; Elestio credits expire after 3 days and you keep paying hourly after; Kuma Engine's 5,000 SMTP email cap and 5 GB egress can throttle heavy alerting. Do not confuse the temporary public demo (kuma.pet) with a free hosted instance. All third-party plans disclaim SLA unless explicitly stated.
findings.name: Third-party managed-hosting free tiers/trials for Uptime Kuma (not student/startup programs)

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, Uptime Kuma has no student-specific, education, or startup offers, and never has - it is MIT-licensed software with a $0 license for everyone, so no vendor cap, trial, or discount program exists to sunset. 2025-2026 changes: (1) v2.0.0 shipped 2025-10-20 as the project's biggest release - breaking changes (rootless Docker images, LiquidJS SMTP templates replacing regex-based ones, removed legacy JSON backup/restore, UI refresh); the 2.3.x line (through v2.3.2, 2026-05-03) added OracleDB monitor support and SQLite-locking fixes, and 2.5.x extends push-interval limits beyond ~24 days - still all free. (2) No first-party cloud/managed service launched; 'Uptime Kuma hosting' listings are third parties (Kuma Engine LLC since at least 2025 at $4/mo per-instance with no free tier; Stellar Hosted, DANIAN, Elestio, Enzonic, ElfHosted, DreamHost pre-installed VPS). (3) Project funding remains volunteer-based: GitHub Sponsors / Open Collective, with Atlas Cloud as a noted special sponsor (USD 400/month). (4) No free-hosting sunset in 2025-2026 detected; the oldest known host-side gotcha is Oracle Cloud's always-free idle-instance policy (2023), which still affects Kuma self-hosters on that tier. The official site (uptime.kuma.pet) blocks automated fetchers (403), so pricing/program verification relies on the GitHub repo plus third-party pages. Confidence: high on absence of official offers (read the official repo today); medium on third-party trial details (from host pages, not tested).

findings.claim: Sign up free at https://sentry.io/signup (create org, add projects, paste DSN into apps). No credit card, no trial needed, no eligibility gate.
findings.detail: Sentry's 'Developer (Free)' plan is free forever: 5,000 errors/mo, 5,000,000 spans/mo, 50 session replays/mo, 5 GB logs/mo, 5 GB application metrics/mo, 1 uptime monitor, 1 cron monitor, 20 metric monitors, 10 custom dashboards, 1 GB attachments, 100 Size Analysis builds, 30-day data retention/lookback, unlimited projects, data residency available. NOT included on this tier: UI Profiling, Continuous Profiling. Pricing page tagline: 'Start free on the Developer plan forever.' Free plan is one of four tiers: Developer (free), Team, Business, Enterprise.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (open registration, no .edu email or startup status required — students and startups qualify on equal footing with everyone else). Hard cap: 1 user. No region limits stated; data residency offered. Credit card NOT required.
findings.expiry: Never — explicitly 'forever' on the pricing page; no sunset clause published.
findings.gotchas: Monthly quotas are hard caps: events/attachments over quota are simply not accepted (silent data loss, e.g., a single crash bug can blow 5K errors in a day). 1 user = any teammate needs Team ($29/mo or $26/mo annual) or Business ($89/mo or $80/mo annual). If you trial Business and don't upgrade, you are silently downgraded to this tier with limits on features.
findings.name: Sentry Developer Plan (Free) — perpetual free tier

findings.claim: Just create a new Sentry account (sentry.io/signup). All new accounts get it automatically; no application or credit card. Upgrade via Settings > Billing if you choose to stay on Business ($89/mo monthly, $80/mo annual).
findings.detail: Per docs.sentry.io/pricing: 'All new Sentry accounts come with a 14-day free trial period' — the initial trial is the Business plan ('the initial 14-day Business trial'). During it you have Business-plan features (unlimited users, unlimited dashboards, SAML/SCIM, 90-day retention, etc.). Pricing page: 'try Business for 14 days with no credit card.' No dollar trial credits exist — it is a time-boxed plan trial, not a credit balance.
findings.eligibility: Every new Sentry org/account, one time. No .edu, startup, or region conditions stated; credit card explicitly NOT required.
findings.expiry: 14 days from account creation. After it ends: 'Users who haven't upgraded by the end of their free trial will remain on the free Developer plan with limited features.' No auto-billing since no card is on file.
findings.gotchas: Trial is 14 days of Business features, then downgrade to the 1-user/5K-error Developer caps — if your app is error-heavy, expect dropped events post-trial. New accounts can only request the separate one-time product trial on day 15 (after this trial ends).
findings.name: 14-day Business free trial for all new accounts

findings.claim: Request from the org (Settings > Billing/plan area, 'request a product trial'; Seer via 'Start Trial' in Settings). Free accounts: any time; new accounts: day 15; existing Team/Business: any time for products not in their plan.
findings.detail: Sentry offers a one-time 14-day trial of individual products not already in your plan. Docs: 'During your 14-day product trial, you'll be able to send us an unlimited number of events' and 'You won't be billed for any data you've used during the 14-day trial period.' This includes add-on/subscription products (e.g., Seer AI debugger trial — the docs reference a dedicated Seer trial, with no published duration/eligibility beyond the general rules; Seer itself is a paid subscription, current pricing $40/active contributor/month after legacy pricing was sunset Jan 2026). No dollar-value trial credits exist.
findings.eligibility: Per product, once per org ('each org can only trial each product once'). Free (Developer) accounts may request at any time; new accounts from day 15; Team/Business for products outside their plan. No credit card requirement stated; no .edu/startup conditions.
findings.expiry: 14 days per product trial; strictly one-time per product per org — a second request is not possible.
findings.gotchas: 'Unlimited events' applies only inside the 14-day window; afterwards the product is paid or unusable. Trial-vs-free gotcha: this is a time-boxed add-on trial, not a free plan. Seer-specific trial terms aren't fully published (see sunset notes re: Seer pricing change).
findings.name: One-time 14-day product trials (incl. Seer AI debugger) — unlimited events during trial

provider: Sentry (sentry.io) — Developer Plan (free tier) + trials; fronts: Observability, Monitoring, Uptime & CDN
sunset_notes: No Sentry-specific education, student (.edu), startup, or nonprofit discount program was found on any official page checked today: sentry.io/education/, sentry.io/startups/ and sentry.io/nonprofit/ are not real program pages (machine-UI 404s), and neither the current pricing docs (docs.sentry.io/pricing) nor the legacy pricing docs mention any such program. The free offers for students/startups are therefore the general-purpose ones above (Developer free plan + 14-day trials), which carry no special eligibility. 2025-2026 changes: (1) Legacy Seer pricing ($20/month + $25 event credits) stopped being offered as an add-on as of January 2026; current Seer is $40/active contributor/month — so the 'Seer free credits' offer is gone. (2) The entire pre-June-11-2024 pricing structure (including legacy 'Performance Units' for spans) was replaced by per-product quotas (errors/spans/replays/logs/metrics as separate lines) — a 2024 change, kept as context. No 2025-2026 changes to the Developer free plan or the 14-day trials were found on the current pages (verified 2026-10-22). Paid reference points: Team $29/mo monthly or $26/mo annual (50K errors/mo, 90-day retention, unlimited users); Business $89/mo monthly or $80/mo annual; Enterprise custom. Note: web search was unavailable this session (budget exhausted), so the 'no education/startup program' conclusion rests on direct page checks of sentry.io + docs.sentry.io rather than a full web sweep.

findings.name: Metabase Open Source / Community Edition — free, unlimited, self-hosted
findings.detail: Perpetually free and unlimited: unlimited users, unlimited questions & dashboards, 20+ supported data sources, MCP server, AI on your own model, unlimited transforms when self-hosted. License is AGPL (GitHub repo lists AGPL + commercial MCL files). No sign-up, no credit card, no region limits. You pay only for your own infrastructure (Docker/JAR on your host). No support, backups, or managed upgrades — those are what the paid/cloud tiers sell.
findings.eligibility: Everyone — no .edu email, no startup-age or funding-cap requirement, no application process.
findings.claim: Self-service: deploy the official Docker image from Docker Hub or download the JAR and point it at your database (metabase.com/start/oss). Alternatively 'Get started' on the homepage routes to the paid cloud checkout at store.metabase.com/checkout.
findings.expiry: None — perpetual, no renewal, no sunset date stated.
findings.gotchas: Free edition excludes commercial features (SSO, required 2FA, row/column permissions, auditing, white-label embedding are Pro/Enterprise-only). No included support: 'All of Metabase's plans include support' means support is a paid-bundle item; self-hosters use community forums/discourse. Hidden cost is your hosting, not Metabase. AI is 'on your preferred model' (BYO) in the OSS path, so LLM API costs fall on you.

findings.name: Metabase Cloud 14-day free trial (any plan: Starter / Pro / Enterprise)
findings.detail: 14-day free trial of Metabase Cloud, available on any plan. Starter is $100/mo ($90/mo billed yearly, $1,080/yr; 5 users incl., extras $6/user/mo); Pro is $575/mo ($517.50/mo yearly, $6,210/yr; 10 users incl., extras $12/user/mo); Enterprise custom, 'from $20,000/yr'. Cloud trial includes automatic backups/restore/upgrades, managed PostgreSQL (AWS RDS), preconfigured SMTP, SSL, SOC 2 Type II, multi-zone HA, unlimited engineer support by email. Homepage CTA: 'Try Metabase Cloud free'.
findings.eligibility: Open; no student/startup criterion mentioned. Trial is time-limited (14 days), presumably for new accounts. Regions at signup: US East, Frankfurt, São Paulo, Singapore, Sydney (changeable later).
findings.claim: Sign up via the 'Get started' / 'Try Metabase Cloud free' button, which routes to https://store.metabase.com/checkout; pick a hosting region at signup.
findings.expiry: Trial ends after 14 days; continued use requires conversion to a paid plan. No renewal of the free period is stated.
findings.gotchas: This is a TRIAL, not a free tier — there is no perpetual free Metabase Cloud plan. The official page does not state whether a credit card is required for the trial; checkout goes through a store, so card capture is plausible but unconfirmed. Usage-based extras after trial: AI (Metabase-hosted) $3.75/1M tokens with 1M tokens included; Transforms 1,000 runs included then $0.01/run (Advanced $0.02 BI / $0.01 EA); storage first 1M rows free then $2/1M rows. Data-residency limits: only the 5 listed regions; air-gapped or HIPAA needs go to self-hosted/Enterprise.

findings.name: Education / student program — does not exist
findings.detail: No student or education license is offered. metabase.com/education and metabase.com/startups both return HTTP 404. The pricing page, homepage, cloud page, GitHub repo and blog index contain no education discount, .edu requirement, or student offer. The only 'free' paths are the perpetual OSS self-hosted edition and the 14-day Cloud trial.
findings.eligibility: N/A — program not found; nothing to claim.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Students use the same free OSS self-hosted edition (unlimited users) as anyone else.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Absence confirmed on the official site today, but 'no program' cannot be guaranteed if one were announced off-site; the free OSS edition is the de facto student offer (no .edu email needed, no seat caps — unlike typical SaaS student tiers that cap seats or features).
findings.source_url: https://www.metabase.com/ (404s at /education and /startups; homepage + pricing + blog scanned today)

sunset_notes: No dedicated free Cloud tier with limited questions/users currently exists on the official site — the 'known so far' item (Metabase Cloud free tier, limited questions/users) appears to describe either the 14-day trial or a plan that was never a perpetual free tier; as of 2026-10-22 the free offerings are only (a) the unlimited self-hosted OSS/Community Edition and (b) the 14-day Cloud trial. No 2025-2026 sunset of a student or startup program was found: /education and /startups are 404 and no pricing-change or program-anniversary posts appear in the blog index (closest historical posts: 'Announcing Metabase Cloud' and 'An Enterprising Opening'). Caveat: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so third-party/press cross-checks of 2025-2026 changes (e.g., plan renames, tier limit tweaks) could not be done; confidence in absence-claims rests solely on the official pages fetched today. The OSS repo README describes the cloud offering strictly as a 'free trial', with no perpetual free tier.

findings.name: Honeycomb Free plan (free forever)
findings.detail: Free plan verified on today's pricing page: up to 20M events/month AND up to 100M metrics (time-series) data points/month, 2 triggers, 0 SLOs, no Service Map. Included features: Distributed Tracing, BubbleUp, OpenTelemetry support, Team Query History, query result permalinks, Honeycomb Metrics, Canvas AI Copilot, Hosted MCP, Agent Timeline, Honeycomb Intelligence. Marketing states 'Unlimited seats' and 'Unlimited querying'. No trace-count cap, dashboard cap, or retention window is printed on the pricing page today; the 60-day high-resolution retention figure is the historical figure from the plan's docs (not re-verified today, docs were restructured). Optional add-on Telemetry Pipeline (extra ingest, OTel processing) starts at $0.10/GB; Pro starts at $150/month for 50M events (up to 750M).
findings.eligibility: Anyone (no .edu, no startup criteria, no funding cap). No region limits stated. No credit-card requirement is stated anywhere on the pricing page (unconfirmed; page is silent).
findings.claim: Sign up at https://ui.honeycomb.io/signup ('Start for free') — free plan is the default plan; no sales gate on this tier. Then send events via OTel SDKs or API key.
findings.expiry: No expiry — explicitly 'free forever'. Upgrade trigger: exceeding 20M events/month (or 100M data points) requires Pro, starting at $150/month.
findings.gotchas: Genuinely free tier, not a time-boxed trial. Only 2 triggers free (no SLOs, no Service Map) — alerting beyond 2 triggers is paid. Retention not printed on today's pricing page (60-day figure carried over from historical plan docs, unconfirmed). Optional Telemetry Pipeline add-on is metered at $0.10/GB and adds cost on top of free ingest. CC requirement unverified without running the signup flow.

findings.name: Honeycomb for Builders — Pro Bronze (academic / nonprofit / open-source)
findings.detail: Official builders program (verified today on honeycomb.io/honeycomb-for-builders): 'Pro500 for qualifying open source, non-profit, and academic projects in perpetuity' — complimentary Pro plan at the Pro500 volume tier (≈ up to 500M events/month; Pro's max tier per pricing page is 750M, so Pro500/Pro750 denote event-volume tiers, not seats). Includes all Pro features, community onboarding sessions, office hours, and Honeycomb swag. Free in perpetuity.
findings.eligibility: Academic projects/organizations, non-profits, and open-source projects. No .edu-email requirement published; eligibility is vendor-determined via application. Individual students are covered only through their academic organization or OSS project — there is no student-specific tier.
findings.claim: Apply via 'Talk to us' on https://www.honeycomb.io/honeycomb-for-builders (routes to /get-a-demo; third-party listings say the application form is embedded on that page). No published review timeline; approval at vendor discretion.
findings.expiry: In perpetuity for qualifying projects — no renewal trigger or end date published; implicitly revocable if the project stops qualifying.
findings.gotchas: The tier is for projects/organizations, not named individuals — a student must apply on behalf of their academic org or OSS project. Third-party directories note award timing/duration are not published. Pro500's ~500M events/month allowance dwarfs the free tier — most valuable academic offer.

findings.name: Honeycomb for Builders — Pro Silver (early-stage startup discount)
findings.detail: Official builders program (verified today): 'Pro750 at 50% off for 1 year, available to early stage startups (Pre-seed, Seed round, Early series A)'. Pro750 = Pro plan at the 750M events/month volume tier (Pro's top tier; base Pro starts at $150/month for 50M events, so Pro750 is a high-volume custom-priced configuration — 50% discount applies to that configuration, absolute $ not public). Includes all Pro features, onboarding sessions, office hours, swag.
findings.eligibility: Startups at Pre-seed, Seed, or Early Series A stage; no age cap published beyond funding stage. No accelerator requirement at this tier. A third-party directory (StartupCreds) notes bootstrapped founders as eligible — not stated on Honeycomb's own page.
findings.claim: Same application path: 'Talk to us' form at https://www.honeycomb.io/honeycomb-for-builders. Vendor-side approval; not self-serve.
findings.expiry: 1 year at 50% off; no renewal/extension terms published — after 12 months presumably full (custom) Pro pricing unless re-approved.
findings.gotchas: Discount, not free — do not confuse with Pro Gold. Pro750 list price is not public, so '50% off' cannot be converted to dollars from public pages. No numeric funding cap (e.g., <$X raised) stated beyond the 'Early series A' ceiling.

findings.name: Honeycomb for Builders — Pro Gold (accelerator startup free year)
findings.detail: Official builders program (verified today): 'Pro750 free for 1 year for qualifying startups', two required conditions: (1) 'Active in a recognized startup accelerator (including Y Combinator and accelerators supporting underrepresented founders)' and (2) 'Actively using or building with OpenTelemetry'. = full Pro plan at the 750M events/month volume tier at $0 for 12 months, plus all Pro features, community onboarding sessions, office hours, swag. No purchase or commitment required.
findings.eligibility: Startup must (a) be active in a recognized accelerator — Y Combinator explicitly named, plus accelerators supporting underrepresented founders — and (b) actively use or build with OpenTelemetry. No .edu requirement, no separate funding cap published. YC's own 'YC AI Stack' free-credits pack (Fall 2025, $25k+ in credits) does NOT include Honeycomb — YC teams still apply via the builders form; nothing auto-redeems through deals.ycombinator.com.
findings.claim: Apply via the 'Talk to us' form at https://www.honeycomb.io/honeycomb-for-builders; approval vendor-side. Third-party trackers (Sourcey) list it open to applicants meeting both conditions, no payment required.
findings.expiry: Free for exactly 1 year. No renewal, extension, or post-expiry pricing terms published; team expected to convert to paid Pro after expiry.
findings.gotchas: OpenTelemetry usage is a hard condition — teams not instrumenting with OTel are ineligible. 1-year term with no published renewal path. One third-party directory marked the offer 'stale' in a crawl, but the official page still lists it as of today — treat the official page as authoritative.

sunset_notes: No Honeycomb free offer was sunset or materially changed that I could find for 2025–2026. The free plan numbers in the known-so-far brief (20M events/month, up to 100M metric data points, 2 triggers, free forever) all match today's pricing page — no change detected. Notable adjacent developments: (1) docs.honeycomb.io was restructured — the old /manage-honeycomb/plans-pricing URL now 404s and docs no longer host plan/retention details, which is why the 60-day retention figure is now unconfirmed from official pages; (2) YC's 2025–2026 'YC AI Stack' student free-credits program (Fall 2025 start, Jan 16 2026 announcement, ~$20–25k+ in credits) does NOT include a Honeycomb benefit — students get AWS/Azure/OpenAI/Anthropic credits instead. There is no dedicated .edu student-only license or student trial-credit program from Honeycomb itself; students' free paths are the universal Free plan and, for academic projects, the builders Pro Bronze tier.

findings.name: Self-Hosted Open Source Edition (free forever)
findings.detail: AGPL-3.0 open-source build (single Rust binary / Docker) with the full observability stack: logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts, RUM, multi-tenancy, HA. No usage charges, no per-seat/host fees, unlimited ingestion. Cost = your own infra (object storage like S3/MinIO + PostgreSQL). Latest release Oct 2026.
findings.eligibility: Anyone - students, startups, enterprises; no .edu email, no company registration, no credit card, no region limit. Self-managed updates; community support only.
findings.claim: 1) Download binary or use Docker from https://openobserve.ai/downloads/ 2) Set ZO_ROOT_USER_EMAIL/PASSWORD and run, or run the container 3) Point agents (OTel, Fluent Bit, Vector, Prometheus) at it 4) GUI at localhost:5080. Zero-cost to start.
findings.expiry: No expiry - free forever. No renewal needed.
findings.gotchas: AGPL-3.0 (not Apache 2.0 since Nov 2023): if you modify and offer it as a service, source-disclosure obligations can apply; unmodified self-hosted use is fine. You run your own HA/storage - ops cost is on you. Enterprise features (SSO, RBAC, federated search, QoS, audit) are not in the OSS build - those come via the free 50GB/day Enterprise self-hosted tier below.

findings.name: Self-Hosted Enterprise Free Tier (50 GB/day)
findings.detail: Enterprise Edition (SSO, RBAC, federated search, query management, workload QoS, audit trail, sensitive-data redaction) is free up to 50 GB/day (~1.5 TB/month) of ingestion per legal entity, with no license key required, and includes full commercial use. This is a genuine free-forever tier, not a trial.
findings.eligibility: Any legal entity (B2B license; personal/household use excluded). No funding cap, no .edu requirement, no credit card, no region limit. Aggregated across all deployments of the same legal entity.
findings.claim: Download the O2 Enterprise build from https://openobserve.ai/downloads/ (v1.1.x, all OSes) and run it - it works without requesting a license up to 50 GB/day. No sign-up or license key needed for the free tier. Above 50 GB/day you must request a paid license via sales.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; no stated sunset date. Free-tier allowance is part of the EULA (last updated 2026-09-05), not a time-boxed promotion.
findings.gotchas: Spike buffer: you may exceed 50 GB/day up to 3 times per month; after the 3rd excess, search queries are BLOCKED until volume drops back under the limit or you buy a license. 'Daily Ingestion' is counted uncompressed, per 24h UTC day. EULA is B2B-only - a student's side-project company is fine, but purely personal/household use is out of scope. Monitoring/usage telemetry is enabled under the EULA.

findings.name: OpenObserve Cloud 14-day free trial (no credit card)
findings.detail: 14-day trial on the Pay-As-You-Go (Professional) cloud plan: $0.50/GB ingested + $0.01/GB queried, unlimited users, logs/metrics/traces/RUM/session replay; included retention: metrics 15 months, logs/traces/RUM 30 days. No credit card required to start (pricing page + ToS Free Trial section). Available in 4 regions (US-West-2 Azure, US-East-2 AWS, EU Central AWS, AP South 1 AWS).
findings.eligibility: Anyone creating a new Cloud org - students/startups alike; no .edu requirement, no CC required to begin. No region restriction beyond the 4 offered cloud regions. Signup: https://cloud.openobserve.ai/web/login?mode=signup
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at cloud.openobserve.ai 2) Create org - 14-day trial starts automatically (code defaults trial_ends_at to 14 days) 3) Ingest/query trial features free 4) Add a payment method to continue - after 14 days the org's ingestion/search/alerts/billing endpoints return 403 until you move to Pay-As-You-Go.
findings.expiry: Trial ends after 14 days; no extension stated; after expiry you must switch to usage-based billing (or terminate). No CC required before trial ends.
findings.gotchas: This is a TRIAL, not a free tier - the cloud free tier no longer exists (killed 2025-06-02, see sunset notes). At trial end you're billed $0.50/GB ingested + $0.01/GB queried for everything ingested during the trial usage model; extra non-metrics retention is $0.02/GB per additional 30-day period. Synthetic/uptime monitoring is still beta; RUM and error tracking carry separate per-unit fees in the underlying pay-as-you-go model.

findings.name: AI features: 20 free credits in preview (AI SRE Agent + AI Assistant)
findings.detail: AI-powered features (Incident Management / AI SRE Agent and AI Assistant) are free during preview; each account gets 20 credits, consumed per AI operation.
findings.eligibility: Any Cloud account (per pricing.md); no .edu or startup requirement; credits are per account. No stated region limit.
findings.claim: Create any OpenObserve Cloud account (or use the 14-day trial) and use AI SRE Agent / AI Assistant - 20 credits are preloaded; free while in preview.
findings.expiry: Tied to preview status - when preview ends, standard Enterprise add-on pricing applies; 20 credits are finite and do not renew automatically.
findings.gotchas: AI features are listed under the Enterprise feature set, so full production use may require Enterprise plan access; 'free during preview' can end without per-user advance notice. Credits are a play-quota, not a discount.

findings.name: OpenObserve Startup Program (50% -> 25% Cloud discount, 12 months)
findings.detail: Sign a 1-year OpenObserve Cloud contract and pay 50% off for the first 6 months, 25% off for the next 6 months. Discount is contingent on the 1-year contract; no cash value; cannot be extended, transferred, or renewed; standard pricing applies automatically after the 12 months. Program may be modified/terminated on 30 days' notice.
findings.eligibility: ALL of: total funding raised < $10M; ARR <= $1M; anticipated ingest > 100 GB/day; actively VC-backed or in a recognized accelerator program. Global (no region limit). No .edu involvement - a company program, approval at OpenObserve's sole discretion, documentation may be requested. One application per company.
findings.claim: Apply on the 'Apply Now' form at https://openobserve.ai/startup/ (be ready to confirm investor/accelerator backing; a company email on your own domain). On approval, sign the 1-year Cloud contract and the tiered discount applies from the approval date.
findings.expiry: Discount valid for 12 months from approval (6 x 50%, 6 x 25%); not renewable. Not free - it is a discount, useful when ingest >100GB/day (at $0.50/GB that's ~$1.5k+/mo list, so real dollar value).
findings.gotchas: This is NOT a free offer - minimum 100GB/day ingest requirement excludes most students and pre-revenue startups; the 1-year commitment is the cost. Resale/abuse triggers termination. After month 12, full price applies unless you terminate. Verify current terms before applying - program terms can change on 30 days' notice.

findings.name: Education / non-profit 'special pricing' via sales (no published program)
findings.detail: OpenObserve states: 'Discounts available for eligible startups, non-profits, and educational institutions' - applied through openobserve.ai/contact-sales. There is NO published education license, student tier, .edu requirement, or fixed discount amount anywhere on the official site; no dedicated /education page exists. The Enterprise EULA is explicitly B2B-only ('business, commercial, or organizational purposes only, not consumer for personal, family, or household use'), so a purely individual student gets no licensed free offer; students' realistic free path is the self-hosted OSS or 50GB/day Enterprise free tier, plus the 14-day cloud trial.
findings.eligibility: Institution-level (university, research lab, non-profit) via sales negotiation; criteria not published. No .edu-only free product found.
findings.claim: Contact openobserve.ai/contact-sales describing the institution and use case; expect a custom quote/quote-level discount, not a self-serve free offer.
findings.expiry: No program, so no expiry; offers are ad-hoc quotes.
findings.gotchas: Because the EULA is B2B, even a favorable education quote likely binds an institution, not a student. Do not confuse this with a student free tier - none exists.

sunset_notes: SUNSET: OpenObserve Cloud's free tier was DISCONTINUED effective 2025-06-02 (announcement: https://openobserve.ai/blog/june-25-pricing-policy-updates/). Moving to fully usage-based Pay-As-You-Go with no minimums; existing free-tier cloud customers got a 30-day exemption (until ~2025-07-02) and then required a valid credit card on file for usage charges. New customers instead get the 14-day no-CC trial. PR #6922 (merged 2025-07-10) confirms the code: orgs default to a 14-day trial and the free plan was removed from the billing UI. So any 'OpenObserve Cloud free tier' seen in pre-June-2025 articles is stale. PRICING CHANGE: ingestion price moved from $0.30/GB (June 2025) to $0.50/GB on the current Professional plan (pricing.md, updated 2026-09-04) - trial/usage costs are higher than 2025 docs suggest. ALSO: uptime/CDN front - OpenObserve has no CDN; uptime/synthetic monitoring (HTTP/TCP/TLS/SSH + Playwright browser checks) is in BETA in Cloud as of Aug 2026 with no separate free tier found, and RUM/session replay on cloud carry per-unit pay-as-you-go fees; nothing in the current material is a permanent free monitoring/uptime/CDN offer - the permanent-free value is entirely in the self-hosted OSS build and the 50GB/day self-hosted Enterprise free tier.

findings.name: PostHog Free Plan (universal monthly free tier) — Observability & Product Analytics
findings.detail: Every PostHog product ships with a monthly free allowance that resets each month; same allowance whether or not a card is on file; usage stops at the limit so you cannot be overcharged. Exact free limits (US Cloud, current as of 2026-10-22): Product Analytics 1,000,000 events; Session Replay 5,000 web + 2,500 mobile recordings; Feature Flags 1,000,000 requests (Experiments billed with feature flags); Error Tracking 100,000 exceptions; Surveys 1,500 responses; Data Warehouse Sources 1,000,000 rows + free historical syncs; Destinations 10,000 trigger events + 1M rows; AI Observability (ex-LLM Analytics) 100,000 events; PostHog AI 500 credits (~$5); Logs 10 GB ingested; Replay Vision 2,500 credits (~$25); PostHog Desktop 2,000 credits (~$20); Workflows 10,000 messages/channel; Inbox Beta 3 PRs; Emails 10,000. Free plan = 1 project, 1-year data retention (session recordings kept ~1 month), unlimited team members, community support, SSO (Google/GitHub/GitLab), API access.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone — students and startups included. No .edu email required, no credit card required, no region restriction (US Cloud default; EU Cloud available). Not a trial: it is a perpetual free tier that 'renews every month... forever.'
findings.claim: Sign up at app.posthog.com or posthog.com/pricing ('Get started – free'); install SDK / add tracking code. Free allowance auto-applies every month, no application or card step needed.
findings.gotchas: It is explicitly 'not a trial, no credit card' — a true perpetual free tier, not a 14-day trial. Free plan is capped at 1 project; adding a card (Pay-as-you-go) unlocks 6 projects and 7-year retention, not a higher free tier. Beyond the free caps you pay usage-based, and you can set per-product billing limits to prevent surprise bills. Logs custom retention beyond the free allowance is charged ($0.05/GB-month).
findings.expiry: Perpetual; the free allowance renews every month. No expiry or annual review on the base free tier.

findings.name: Error Tracking free tier (Monitoring front)
findings.detail: Generous free tier of 100,000 exceptions/month, GA (out of beta April 2025). No credit card required; you can set billing limits. After the free 100K: tiered pricing 100k–325k $0.000370/exception, 325k–10M $0.000140/exception, 10M+ $0.000115/exception. Bill is driven by ingested $exception events (suppression rules drop future matching exceptions pre-ingestion and are not billed).
findings.eligibility: Anyone on the PostHog free tier — students/startups, no .edu or card required.
findings.claim: Included automatically in the free tier once error tracking SDK is enabled; no separate application.
findings.gotchas: Exception autocapture on by default can over-capture; you can trim captured types client-side. Merging/resolving/suppressing existing issues does not reduce the bill; suppression only saves on future matching events.
findings.expiry: Perpetual monthly free allowance; renews each month.

findings.name: PostHog for Startups — $50,000 in free credits
findings.detail: $50,000 in free PostHog credits for 12 months for early-stage teams (page headline: '$50K in credits for early-stage teams'). Official eligibility stated on the pricing page: company younger than 2 years and total funding raised under $5M. Credits are applied on top of/within a pay-as-you-go account so usage can far exceed the free tier.
findings.eligibility: Startup (not education): founded <2 years ago, <$5M total funding raised. No .edu requirement; aimed at VC/startup founders.
findings.claim: Apply at posthog.com/startups ('Get started – free' → app.posthog.com/signup). The page's application/claim steps were not fully readable in this fetch; apply via the startups page. Note: the base free tier needs no card, but redeeming $50K of usage credits effectively puts you on a pay-as-you-go account (card requirement for that account not explicitly confirmed on the page).
findings.gotchas: Credits are for 12 months (time-boxed), not perpetual. The eligibility caps (<2 yrs, <$5M raised) mean a more mature startup is not eligible. Do not confuse with the separate Y Combinator offer below.
findings.expiry: 12-month credit window.

findings.name: Y Combinator Startup Program — $50,000 free credits/yr, renewable
findings.detail: Y Combinator-backed companies get $50,000 in free PostHog credits per year, renewable while the company's total funding raised stays under $25M (separate, YC-specific program listed on the pricing page).
findings.eligibility: Y Combinator companies (or a company that raised via YC); total raised must stay < $25M to keep the renewal. No .edu.
findings.claim: Applied through PostHog's YC/startup program (posthog.com/startups and pricing page); YC-backed teams claim the annual $50K.
findings.gotchas: Renewal is gated on the $25M raised ceiling — once raised funding exceeds $25M the renewable credits stop. Distinct from the general <2yr/<$5M startup program.
findings.expiry: Renews annually while raised < $25M.

findings.name: Non-profit discount (adjacent to student/startup audience)
findings.detail: Registered non-profits receive 15% off purchases under $25k; an additional 5% stacks on top of standard volume discounts in the $25k–$100k range. This is a discount (not a free tier), but is one of PostHog's stated offers alongside the startup discounts.
findings.eligibility: Registered non-profit organization (no .edu, no startup age cap).
findings.claim: Noted on the pricing page; apply the discount when setting up a paid account.
findings.gotchas: It is a percentage discount on spend, not free usage; the free tier (finding 1) already covers most non-profit baseline needs at $0.
findings.expiry: Ongoing discount; no expiry stated.

findings.name: Education / student license — no dedicated program found
findings.detail: No dedicated PostHog education, student, or .edu license/program exists in the official site. A direct fetch of posthog.com/education returns 404 (no page), and the FAQ/pricing pages do not list a student-only offer. Effectively, the 'education' front is served by the universal free tier: students can use all products free (1M events, 5K replays, 100K exceptions, 10GB logs, etc.) with NO .edu email and NO credit card, so classroom/student projects are covered at $0.
findings.eligibility: No .edu email required, no institutional agreement, no special license — the free tier is open to any student. (No evidence of a distinct education-specific benefit.)
findings.claim: Same as the free tier: sign up at app.posthog.com; no separate education application exists to claim.
findings.gotchas: Because there is no dedicated education program, there is no .edu-verified perk or extended data-retention for students; students get the same 1-project / 1-year-retention free tier as everyone else.
findings.expiry: n/a (no dedicated program; rides on the perpetual free tier).

findings.name: Uptime & CDN fronts — no dedicated PostHog product
