findings.detail: PostHog does not sell a standalone uptime-monitoring service or a CDN, so there is no free offer specifically in those two fronts. Its 'monitoring' coverage comes through the free tier's Observability stack: Error Tracking (100K exceptions free), Logs (10 GB free), Web Vitals / performance capture, and alerts. 'Monitoring' in the uptime-sense (ping/SLO uptime checks) and any CDN/edge delivery are out of scope of PostHog's product list (analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, error tracking, logs, surveys, workflows, AI observability, data warehouse, destinations, inbox, PostHog AI).
findings.eligibility: n/a — no uptime or CDN product to claim.
findings.claim: n/a. For uptime/CDN you would need a different vendor; PostHog's free value is in error tracking + logs + analytics, not uptime pings or a content/edge network.
findings.gotchas: Don't list a 'free uptime monitoring' or 'free CDN' as a PostHog offer — none exists. Web-vitals/performance data inside analytics is the closest monitoring feature, and it is covered under the 1M-event free analytics allowance.
findings.expiry: n/a.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes that matter for the 'free offer' claims: (1) In 2025 PostHog raised several free-tier limits — a third-party (metacto, updated 2025-10-24) reports Surveys free allowance increased from 250 → 1,500 responses/month, and Data Pipelines free quota changed to 10K events + 1M rows (previously 1M events). These 'after' values match today's official pricing page (1,500 surveys; 10K destination trigger events + 1M rows); the 'before' values are third-party (medium confidence). (2) A new AI/LLM product launched in 2025 with 100K free events/month, initially named 'LLM Analytics' (per the 2025 metacto article) and now shown on the 2026 pricing page as 'AI Observability' — i.e., the 100K free-events figure is a 2025 addition / rebrand, not part of the original 2024 free tier. (3) Context from 2024: PostHog cut session-replay and analytics-event prices, and in 2025 cut data-pipeline and survey prices — so the free tier has generally been expanding, not shrinking. (4) Error Tracking went GA (out of beta) around April 2025 with its 100K free-exceptions tier; before that it was a beta. (5) No student/education program or startup/YC program was sunset in 2025-2026: the $50K startup program (<2yr, <$5M), the YC $50K/yr program (<$25M raised), and the 15% non-profit discount all remain live on the current pricing page. (6) Tangential: 2025 self-hosting guidance changed (support for new Kubernetes/Helm installs ended) — affects self-hosted users, not the cloud free tier. Net: every 'known so far' claim (free error tracking, session replay, logs, 1M events, no credit card) is CONFIRMED and current; nothing in the free-offer set was removed, only some limits were raised.

findings.name: Hosted Hobbyist Free Plan (permanent free tier)
findings.detail: The hosted service's Hobbyist plan is $0/month with no time limit: monitor 20 jobs (cron jobs / heartbeats), 100 log entries kept per job (oldest entries evicted when the cap is hit — a job pinging every 5 minutes retains only ~8 hours of history; a weekly job retains ~2 years). No SMS/WhatsApp/phone-call credits on the free tier; email, webhook, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Pushover, Signal, ntfy, Matrix, GitHub Issues and other web-based alert channels work. Paid tiers for comparison: Supporter $5/mo (same limits, donation only), Business $20/mo (100 jobs, 1000 log entries, 50 SMS/WhatsApp + 20 phone credits, email support; $16/mo billed annually), Business Plus $80/mo (1000 jobs, 500 SMS/WhatsApp + 100 phone credits, priority support; $64/mo annual, 20% annual discount).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (including students and startups): sign up with just an email address via magic-link; no credit card, no .edu address, no region restriction, no funding or company-age criteria. Not a trial — a permanently free tier. Running multiple accounts to exceed the 20-job cap is explicitly labeled abuse by Healthchecks.io.
findings.claim: Go to healthchecks.io, click Create Free Account / sign up for the Hobbyist plan with an email address (magic link), no payment details. Then create up to 20 checks (ping URLs or cron expressions) and have your job curl the ping URL on each run.
findings.expiry: No expiry; free forever. Author has publicly stated (July 2024 blog post) that he is not planning to tighten free-plan limits or raise paid prices.
findings.gotchas: No phone/SMS/WhatsApp alerts on the free tier (paid only). 100-entry log cap means short retention for fast jobs. Inactive accounts receive 'Inactive Account Notification' emails; long inactivity may affect the account. Capping out at 20 jobs means upgrading to Business at $20/mo. Payments when you do pay run via Braintree (PayPal division); no card data stored on Healthchecks.io servers.

findings.name: Self-Hosted Open-Source Healthchecks (free, unlimited)
findings.detail: Healthchecks is open source under the BSD license (code on GitHub, developed in the open). Self-hosting the full product on your own infrastructure is free with no check-count limits — 'unlimited checks on your own infrastructure', which is the offer referenced for students building on cheap/homelab or university cloud credits. You run the entire service (web app + PostgreSQL + object storage for ping bodies) and every feature is available, minus the hosted service's ops guarantees (Hetzner bare metal, hot standby, daily S3 backups).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone — no account, no credit card, no .edu, no region limit. Costs shift to you: you need hosting, and you become the operator (backups, upgrades, failover). The about page states plainly: 'Healthchecks is free software, and can be self-hosted.'
findings.claim: Clone the BSD-licensed GitHub repo (github.com/healthchecks/healthchecks), run the Django app + PostgreSQL per its docs, point your cron jobs at your own instance's ping URLs.
findings.expiry: No expiry — BSD license is permanent; the project is accepting contributions and the author (one-person SIA Monkey See Monkey Do, Latvia) keeps it maintained as of 2026 (11 years in business per the About page).
findings.gotchas: You pay for your own infrastructure and all ops burden (database failover is manual even on the hosted version, and a single operator handles it); no 'free' in the sense of zero cost — only zero license cost. Feature parity with the hosted version can lag or differ; you don't get the hosted reliability track record (99.9%+ since 2015).

findings.name: Free Business Plan for Open-Source Projects and Nonprofits
findings.detail: Healthchecks.io offers the Business plan free of charge for open-source projects and nonprofits — worth $20/month — including 100 monitored jobs, 1000 log entries per job, 50 SMS/WhatsApp credits and 20 phone-call credits, plus email support. It is not a student or startup program; the eligible categories are OSS projects and nonprofits. The About page tracks ~106 such accounts (OSS + nonprofit) vs ~1,236 paying.
findings.eligibility: Open-source projects and registered nonprofits only. No .edu email, no student license, and no dedicated startup program exists on the official pages. No published funding caps or age criteria; eligibility is judged by the team on request. No region limit stated. No credit card required (plan is free).
findings.claim: Email contact@healthchecks.io (listed in the FAQ) asking for the free Business plan as an open-source project or nonprofit; they set the account up. It is not self-serve — you must ask.
findings.expiry: No published expiry or renewal date; it is a standing program (listed on the pricing-page FAQ and FAQ as of today, 2026-10-22).
findings.gotchas: Not available to for-profit startups or individual students — claiming it as a commercial startup would be misusing the program. It's manual/e-mail based with no SLA on response; the Free tier (20 jobs) already covers most personal/student use cases. SMS/WhatsApp/phone credits are consumed by alert volume; when they run out you'd need a paid upgrade to top up.

sunset_notes: No student/education-specific license, startup program, or trial-credit offer exists at Healthchecks.io as of 2026-10-22; the only concessions are the permanent Hobbyist free tier (20 jobs), the BSD-licensed self-hosted build, and the free Business plan for open-source projects and nonprofits. Nothing was sunset in 2025-2026: the tier structure ($0/$5/$20/$80, 20→100→1000 jobs) matches the limits stated in the 2024 blog post, and a third-party price tracker (Outmano) captured the official pricing page on 2026-09-24 with 'no change recorded yet'. The author explicitly stated in 2024 that he is not planning to tighten free-plan limits or raise prices, and has been publicly committed to that stance since. One caveat: the session web-search budget was exhausted, so the second confirmation search did not run; findings marked 'high' confidence are based on pages fetched today from healthchecks.io directly. No data/egress cost gotchas: self-hosted requires your own DB/object-storage, and the hosted free tier has no bandwidth charges to you as user.

provider: Microsoft for Students (Dev Tools, IDEs, Git & CI/CD fronts: Microsoft 365, GitHub, Azure, Store)

findings.name: Azure for Students: $100 credit + 12-month free services + always-free services (no credit card)
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22: $100 in Azure credit valid for 12 months (new Azure customers only); free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months (e.g., 750 hrs each of B1s/B2pts v2/B2ats v2 burstable VMs; Container Registry 1 Standard tier with 100 GB + 10 webhooks; Azure SQL 100,000 vCore-sec serverless/mo with 32 GB; PostgreSQL/MySQL 750 hrs Flexible B1MS with 32 GB data + 32 GB backup; SQL Managed Instance 720 vCore-hrs of 4/8-vCore GP with 64 GB data + 64 GB backup); plus 65+ always-free services (DevOps: 5 users with unlimited private Git repos; Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB; Functions 1M requests/mo; App Service up to 10 web/API apps w/ 1 GB storage; Static Web Apps 100 GB bandwidth; AKS cluster mgmt free; IoT Hub 8,000 msgs/day). Renew annually while a student. One account per person. After credit: email offers pay-as-you-go or disable.
findings.eligibility: Full-time university students only (page asterisks full-time requirement); sign up with school email to verify student status; .edu or equivalent institutional email; not a trial — no credit card required. Region-limited services apply (always-free/12-month SKUs differ by Azure region); available in most Azure regions.
findings.claim: 1) Go to azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students. 2) Sign up with a Microsoft account + school email. 3) Student status verified automatically from email (no CC). 4) Claim $100 credit and apply; browse always-free/12-month services in portal. 5) Renew yearly while enrolled.
findings.expiry: Credit: 12 months from account creation; 12-month services: 12 months (new customers); always-free services: indefinite. Annual renewal while a student re-extends the free amounts. No published sunset date.
findings.gotchas: Credit card NOT required, but services beyond free amounts/credit bill you once credit is gone (pay-as-you-go). 'Always-free' has hard monthly caps (egress >100 GB/mo always-free is billed; data egress costs apply). Student plan is for learning/non-commercial; commercial workloads are ineligible. One account per person; re-verification may be requested.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack: free GitHub Pro, free Copilot, 80+ partner dev-tool offers (JetBrains, CI/CD)
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22 (pack page footer '© 2026'): free GitHub Pro account while a student (unlimited private repos; 3,000 Actions minutes/mo; 180 Codespaces hours/mo; 2 GB Packages + 20 GB Codespaces storage), free GitHub Copilot Student tier ('unlimited code completions, an allowance of GitHub AI Credits, plus limited chat/agent usage'), free Microsoft 365 offer in the pack ('with AI built in, 1 TB cloud storage, advanced security'), Microsoft Azure in the pack: '$100 in Azure credit + 25+ Azure services' (students 18+; a separate 13–17 offer: free App Service, Functions, Notification Hubs, MySQL, App Insights, Azure DevOps). Partner offers incl. JetBrains 'free subscription for students, renewed annually', Heroku $13/mo credit for 24 months, 1Password free 2 years, Datadog Pro (10 servers) 2 years, MongoDB $50 Atlas credit + $150 certification, GitKraken & GitLens free 6 months then up to 80% off while a student, Travis CI private builds while a student, Codecov free public+private, BrowserStack 1 year, Sentry (50K errors) 1 yr renewable, Requestly Pro ($270 value) 1 yr. 83 partner entries total (page says '80+' style count).
findings.eligibility: Students aged 13+ enrolled in a degree- or diploma-granting course of study; school-issued email address and/or official, dated proof of enrollment. .edu preferred but international equivalents accepted via verification. One pack per student. Free; no credit card for GitHub itself (some partner trials may ask for a card on their side).
findings.claim: 1) github.com/education/students (or education.github.com/pack). 2) 'Get verified': sign in, verify school email or upload enrollment proof. 3) Claim Student Developer Pack; individual partner offers are accepted one by one in the pack page. Renewal: re-verify yearly while enrolled.
findings.expiry: Pack entitlement lasts while student status is verified; renews annually. Individual partner offers have their own terms (1 week–24 months; e.g., Heroku $13/mo x 24 mo). 'Always' items: GitHub Pro, Copilot Student, Codespaces pro tier.
findings.gotchas: GitHub Actions minutes/Codespaces hours are tied to the free Pro student tier, not a one-time grant. Copilot 'limited chat/agent usage' caps apply. Partner lineup churns (e.g., Gitpod/Replit/DigitalOcean no longer listed in 2026; JetBrains still listed but now as 'free subscription, renewed annually'). Microsoft 365 offer in the pack is the discounted/free M365 deal, not a new entitlement.

findings.name: Office 365 A1 free for students, faculty & staff (desktop + web), donated to eligible institutions
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22: 'Educators and students with an eligible education email address can get Office 365 A1 for free' — Microsoft donates Office 365 A1 for Education to eligible institutions at no cost. Desktop Office apps install on up to 5 PCs/Macs + up to 5 tablets/phones per user; includes web apps, OneDrive for Education, Teams for Education. If your school already licenses A3/A5, you get that tier instead. Validity: 'as long as you are working at, or enrolled in, a qualified educational organization; eligibility may be re-verified at any time.'
findings.eligibility: Eligible education email at a qualified institution (.edu or equivalent; individual verification possible for schools without an org license: automated check 'instantaneous', or up to a month for institution verification; individuals without eligibility get a 30-day trial path).
findings.claim: 1) Use your school email at office.com / 'get Office 365 A1 for free' (aka.ms/office-a1-hero-button). 2) Verify with institutional email (30-day trial fallback if school not yet in a qualifying org). 3) Desktop install via your account on 5 PCs/Macs + 5 tablets/phones.
findings.expiry: No fixed expiry while enrolled/employed; plan ends (apps drop to reduced-functionality mode; online services stop) on departure/expiry. Eligibility can be re-verified at any time.
findings.gotchas: This is the school's license flowing to the individual — not a personal subscription; you lose access on graduation/leaving. Doesn't include full Microsoft 365 Personal (e.g., Word desktop on a personal account). Free Office on the web remains separately available to anyone.

findings.name: 50% student discount on Microsoft 365 Personal with Copilot (Word/Excel/PPT/OneNote/Outlook + Copilot, 1 TB OneDrive)
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22 (offer cards on MS education hub and store/education page): 'Use your college email to save 50% on Microsoft 365 with Copilot included' — Microsoft 365 Personal with Copilot at 50% off the list price, includes desktop apps with Copilot, 1 TB OneDrive, Defender security. Offer card title on store page: 'Students save 50% on Microsoft 365 Personal'. This replaced/superseded the old '50% off' Office 365 University offer.
findings.eligibility: Full-time and part-time enrolled university/college students at accredited institutions; verification of student status + a valid Microsoft account (personal MSA, NOT the .edu address, for the subscription itself). .edu/college email used to verify. Available in the markets where the student deal is offered (US-first, expanded in Oct 2025 'to more markets around the world').
findings.claim: 1) microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/college-student-pricing. 2) Create/sign in with personal Microsoft account. 3) Add payment info (a payment method IS required to subscribe). 4) Provide EDU email for verification. 5) Email with completion link arrives at the student mailbox; subscribe at 50% off.
findings.expiry: Recurring subscription: auto-renews at the discounted monthly/annual price while verification holds; eligibility can be re-checked (Microsoft periodically re-verifies student status; account downgrades when no longer eligible).
findings.gotchas: Payment method required (unlike Azure for Students). It's a personal MSA subscription, not a school license. Trial vs free: the discounted plan is a paid subscription from day one — the free 12-month variant (below) is the no-cost path where available.

findings.name: Free 12 months of Microsoft 365 Personal (with Copilot) for US college students — announced Sep 4, 2025; 50% off afterward
findings.detail: Per Microsoft's White House AI Education commitments announcement (2025-09-04): 'Microsoft 365 Personal free for 12 months to every college student in the United States', incl. community college students; Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote, Outlook with Copilot built in; sign-up opened immediately 'through October 31, 2025 (valid university email address required)'. After the free year: eligible for 50% discount to continue (list ~$99.99/yr before discount). Microsoft's Oct 1, 2025 announcement 'expanding the limited-time student offer to more markets around the world'. The education Office page (2026-10-22) still shows a 'Free for students: Our ultimate AI and productivity subscription' section pointing to college-student-pricing, but the live page could not be read today (JS/timeout), so current (post-Oct-2025-window) availability is unconfirmed.
findings.eligibility: US college students (incl. community colleges) at launch; later expanded to more markets. Valid university email required; signup on a personal Microsoft account. No credit card for the free year is advertised; a payment method is required for post-expiry continuation at the discounted price.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up via the M365 student offer (college-student-pricing / 'Free for students' card on education pages). 2) Verify with valid university email. 3) Use M365 Personal free for 12 months; set a reminder before the free year ends to switch to 50% discount or cancel.
findings.expiry: Free period = 12 months per claim; original US signup window closed Oct 31, 2025 (international expansion Oct 2025). Status of the offer in Oct 2026 could not be confirmed from the live page today.
findings.gotchas: Limited-time offer: likely lapses or narrows between promo windows; check the page before relying on it. Auto-billing kicks in after the free year unless cancelled. 1 TB OneDrive included; Copilot usage limits apply.

findings.name: Microsoft Store 10% student/parent discount on select devices
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22: 'Students and parents can get 10% off on select devices, including Microsoft Surface' (education hub) — store FAQ wording: 'Use the Microsoft student discount to get 10% off select physical products, including select Surface devices, as well as select student laptops, and PC accessories'. Ongoing, not time-boxed.
findings.eligibility: Students: school-issued email 'provided by the school (for example, contoso.edu) that can receive external email, be of legal age to sign up for an online offer'. Parents discount is the separate parent-verification variant of the same program. US storefront.
findings.claim: 1) microsoft.com/en-us/store/b/education. 2) Sign in, verify student (school email) or parent status. 3) 10% applied to eligible SKUs at purchase.
findings.expiry: Ongoing while eligible; no stated end date.
findings.gotchas: Only 'select' SKUs; Microsoft 'reserves the right to verify an eligible retailer's advertised price and availability'. Physical products only (no M365 subscription discounts here).

findings.name: Azure Dev Tools for Teaching (Azure Education Hub) — free professional dev tools, IDEs & Git/CI tooling for students and faculty
findings.detail: Free, non-credit offering: Windows 11/10 Pro, Visual Studio, SQL Server, Windows Server, Project Professional, Visio Professional (title list confirmed by UTEP's Feb 2026 catalog and U of I WebStore listing; full list in the Microsoft FAQ) plus GitHub Student Developer Pack integration on campus. 'Software is acquired ... only for instructional and research purposes'; commercial use prohibited (except free Windows-store apps). Office is NOT included. No expiry while enrolled — re-verifying student/faculty status keeps access; the 2016 'no expiry date' model continues.
findings.eligibility: Students and faculty/staff of accredited institutions; student status verified with the university email via the Azure Education Hub (institutional SSO). Region: worldwide, campus-by-campus agreements.
findings.claim: 1) Open the Azure Education Hub student-verification portal (linked from your campus IT page). 2) Sign in with your university email (SSO where available). 3) After verification, browse 'Software' in the hub and download titles (license terms per title).
findings.expiry: Licensed for as long as enrolled/employed at the qualifying institution; no personal expiry date; access lapses on verification failure/graduation. Titles change with Microsoft's licensing agreements.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial, instructional/research use only — cannot run departmental infrastructure or commercial products. Microsoft's own page (azure.microsoft.com/en-us/education) now funnels to Azure-for-Students content; program details live in the hub FAQ. Credit: no Azure credit in the hub — the $100 student credit is separate (Azure for Students).

findings.name: Azure for Startups (new 2025/2026 credit program) — $1,000 instant credits, up to $5,000 total; card required for identity
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22 on the Azure-for-Students page (a new tier now advertised alongside the student offer): 'Azure for Startups: $1,000 in Azure credits instantly — no application required; unlock up to $5,000 in total credits with business verification; credits valid for 90 days (initial) and 180 days (post-verification); access to full Azure catalog up to credit limits; spending protection — credit card required only for identity verification and services beyond credit; no upfront commitment — cancel anytime; move to pay-as-you-go after credits expire or are used.'
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers starting a startup (any new business customer can get the $1,000 instant tier; the extended tier requires business verification). Not age/funding-capped like the legacy Founders Program. Worldwide where Azure is available.
findings.claim: 1) Create a new Azure account; select the Azure for Startups plan (ad on the Azure free/students pages). 2) No application for the instant $1,000 — card added for identity verification. 3) Complete business verification to unlock up to $4,000 more (total $5,000). 4) Set spending limits; credits burn down 90 days (initial) / 180 days (post-verification).
findings.expiry: Credits expire on fixed clocks: 90 days (initial $1,000) and 180 days (post-verification pool). After expiry: pay-as-you-go unless cancelled.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (identity + beyond-credit charges) — unlike Azure for Students. 90/180-day validity is far shorter than legacy Founders Program credits. Not a 'trial': unused credits are forfeit, not refunded.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups Founders Program — 'up to $150,000' Azure credits marketing (legacy big program)
findings.detail: As read 2026-10-22: the Microsoft for Startups landing page still advertises 'up to $150,000 in credits' — 'Credits can be applied across eligible Azure services', with AI tools ('scalable AI tools that help cut costs'), technical resources, and the startup network. The 'Get started now' CTA now routes to the Azure Portal startup home view (portal.azure.com/?homeview=startup) rather than a standalone Founders Program application page; /startups/founders 404s. No numeric eligibility thresholds (funding cap, startup age, region) are published on the current page — detailed terms now live behind the portal flow. Legacy Founders Program historically: early-stage startups, < $30M raised, multi-month credit validity, plus training/mentorship/benefits; those specifics are not confirmable on the live pages today.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups building on Microsoft tech (funding cap and age limits historically: < $30M raised; regions with Azure availability). No current live-page confirmation of caps today.
findings.claim: 1) microsoft.com/startups → 'Get started now' (fwlink resolves to portal.azure.com/?homeview=startup). 2) Start in the Azure Portal startup flow / register via the startup program portal; larger credit pools historically required application + investor/partner referral; the new instant tier is the Azure for Startups $1k/$5k above.
findings.expiry: Credit validity depends on the specific granted pool (legacy grants were ~6–12 month usability); not published on the landing page today.
findings.gotchas: The $150K figure is a marketing maximum (historically: up to $150K Azure credits including base grants); most startups receive far less, tiered by review. The classic application-based Founders flow appears to have been consolidated into the portal 'Azure for Startups' tiers; treat the $150K as aspirational ceiling, not entitlement.

findings.name: College PC bundle promo (2026) — 1 yr Microsoft 365 Premium + 1 yr Xbox Game Pass Ultimate + controller; promotion ENDED
findings.detail: Offer valid 4/15/2026–8/31/2026, redemption deadline 9/30/2026 (per official FAQ read 2026-10-22: 'This promotion has ended'): eligible US college students buying a new eligible Windows 11 PC got 1 year of Microsoft 365 Premium (ARV $199.99), 1 year Xbox Game Pass Ultimate (ARV $275.88), and an Xbox Design Lab controller (ARV $79.99) — '$500+ in added value'. One PC per student/account; refurbished PCs excluded; controller US shipping only.
findings.eligibility: US college/university students at accredited US institutions with a valid .edu email; eligible new Windows 11 PC purchase; M365 Premium: new subscribers or Personal/Family upgraders; Game Pass: new subscribers only.
findings.claim: Ended: (1) buy eligible PC by 8/31/26; (2) verify .edu status via on-PC prompt or email at the Microsoft Academic Verification page; (3) claim subs + controller promo code by 9/30/26 11:59pm PT. findings.name: AWS Free Plan (credit-based Free Tier, 2025 revamp) — up to $200 in trial credits, 6 months
findings.detail: New customers get $100 in AWS credits immediately on signup, plus up to $100 more earned by completing 'Explore' activities in key services (Explore AWS widget); total up to $200 usable over up to 6 months. Covers access to 90+ services on the Free plan for up to 6 months (the start-here page says 100+ services, incl. EC2, S3, DynamoDB, Lambda, Bedrock, SageMaker AI). Going beyond always-free monthly limits or using paid features is auto-covered by remaining credits. No charges unless you convert to the Paid plan. New customers on the Paid plan are also eligible for up to $200 in credits; the Paid plan offers limited free trials of selected services and a monthly spend limit starting at $20 (alerts at 50/75/90%, workload paused at limit).
findings.eligibility: All new customers; NOT eligible if you have ever had an AWS account before. No credit card required to start for most new customers (AWS may run a fraud check that places a USD $1 hold for 3-5 days, no charge). Region limits: credits not available in China (ZHY) and China (BJS) or in AWS GovCloud (US) except certain services (e.g., Lambda for GovCloud). Credits apply across global regions, calculated monthly in USD.
findings.claim: Create a new AWS account (Fast sign-up with Google/GitHub/Apple/Amazon login creates an 'AWS Builder ID' personal profile; or advanced account creation for region control) at aws.amazon.com/free or signin.aws.amazon.com/signup?request_type=builderId — Free plan auto-enrolled, $100 credit lands in the billing console; earn the second $100 within 6 months by completing Explore activities (may take up to 30 minutes to appear).
findings.expiry: Free plan lasts the EARLIER of 6 months from account creation or credit exhaustion; account then auto-closes, cannot be extended. On expiry AWS suspends the account; data retained 90 days, then permanently erased. You can upgrade to Paid within the 90-day window; remaining credits roll onto Paid bills (FAQ states they expire 12 months after account creation, while the Advanced-Features section states 6 months — treat as 6-12 months, check billing console). No downgrade back to Free plan.
findings.gotchas: Free plan is a LIMITED subset of services (Bedrock AgentCore is Paid-plan exclusive) and excludes services that would immediately consume the whole credit amount or require hardware purchases. Free-plan accounts are INELIGIBLE for promotional/incentive credits (e.g., AWS Activate) — startups need a Paid-plan account. Joining an AWS Organization/Control Tower or activating Advanced Features (multi-region, enterprise services) makes you ineligible to earn extra Explore credits and credits then expire 6 months after account creation. Credits are not transferable. GPU/ML note: no GPU-specific free allotment; GPU instances (EC2 P-series, SageMaker GPU notebooks) are payable with the $200 credits rather than always-free.

findings.name: Always Free layer — 30+ services free within monthly usage limits, indefinite
findings.detail: Separate from the 6-month credit-based Free plan: '30+ AWS services are always free within monthly usage limits on both the Free and Paid plans.' Applies to ALL customers (new and existing), no application. If usage exceeds the monthly limits, remaining Free Tier credits automatically cover the cost (on Free plan). The hub page (aws.amazon.com/free) lists flagship services (EC2, S3, Aurora, RDS, DynamoDB, AWS Transform, Bedrock, SageMaker AI) as available on both plans but does NOT publish the per-service monthly quota numbers on the page fetched today; per-service limits live on each product pricing page.
findings.eligibility: All AWS customers on Free or Paid plan; not restricted by region except the same China/GovCloud caveats as the Free plan.
findings.claim: Automatic — no signup step beyond having an AWS account; available on aws.amazon.com/free.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; no renewal, no sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Quota figures (hours/GB/requests) are not on the free-plan hub; verify per-service numbers on each service pricing page before relying on a specific limit. Egress/data transfer beyond limits and any charged feature draws on credits (Free plan) or bill (Paid plan).

findings.name: Amazon SageMaker free notebook allowance (ML notebooks front) — 250 hours sc.t3.medium, first 2 months
findings.detail: Per the SageMaker pricing page (SageMaker Unified Studio era): AWS provides 250 hours of sc.t3.medium notebook instances during the FIRST 2 MONTHS of a new account, for Amazon SageMaker notebooks. Also always-free monthly items for the SageMaker Catalog (built on DataZone): 20 MB metadata storage, 4,000 API requests, and 0.2 compute units per account per billing month; plus 'always-free' core Unified Studio requests (IdC-based domain setup, user/project management, policy grants). SageMaker Data Agent (new) is pay-as-you-go at $0.04 per credit, no free allowance. Non-GPU only (sc.t3.medium); GPU notebook/training instances (p3/p4/p5, Trainium) are paid and can be covered by Free Plan credits or Activate credits.
findings.eligibility: New AWS account, first 2 months only; available to Free and Paid plans (notebook hours) per the pricing page; notebook service 'honors your current AWS Free Tier allocations'.
findings.claim: Create a SageMaker notebook (Unified Studio) on a new account within the first 2 months; the 250 sc.t3.medium hours apply automatically; no separate application.
findings.expiry: 250-hour notebook allowance: first 2 months of account, no renewal. Catalog always-free allowances: recurring monthly, indefinite.
findings.gotchas: This is a material shrink vs the legacy free tier's 750 hours/month of ml.t3.medium for 12 months (old figure from the pre-revamp page, not re-verified today). Storage (S3), EKS clusters, endpoints, and GPU instances cost extra; SageMaker usage through Unified Studio is billed per underlying service. Data/prep jobs are not listed as free in the section fetched.

findings.name: AWS Activate (AWS for Startups) credits — Founders up to $5,000, Portfolio up to $200,000, AI startups $200,000+
findings.detail: Three tiers on the current credits page: (1) Activate Founders (self-funded/bootstrapped): start with $1,000 in credits, earn up to $5,000 total; apply directly. (2) Activate Portfolio (VC/accelerator/angel-group backed, use the provider's Organization ID): up to $200,000 in credits. (3) AWS Credits for AI Startups: $200,000+ for 'AI startups ready to scale', invite-only, via your AWS account manager. All credits in USD, redeemable on AWS services including third-party models on Amazon Bedrock. Beyond credits: mentorship (ex-founders, CTOs, VCs, angels), technical/business guidance, co-build/co-market/co-sell, AWS Marketplace listing, and the new 'AWS Startup Advisor' (IDE-integrated cost tracking and credit applications). The separate offers page still lists the program as '$1,000 to $100,000' plus '80+ exclusive third-party offers valued at up to $800,000' — figures now inconsistent with the credits page (up to $200,000).
findings.eligibility: Founded in the last 10 years; pre-Series B stage (offers page says funded up to Series A); company website required; needs an AWS account ON THE PAID plan; must be new to Activate credits or requesting more than previously received. Apply with a Builder ID using a professional (company) email. No funding-amount cap is printed; no credit-card detail stated (Paid plan implies a payment method).
findings.claim: 4 steps from aws.amazon.com/startups/credits: 1) create AWS Builder ID with professional email; 2) pick tier — Founders (self-funded, apply directly) or Portfolio (with provider's Activate Org ID); 3) provide product, funding-stage, company details; 4) link an AWS Paid-plan account and submit. Response within 5-10 business days (credits page; offers page says 7-10).
findings.expiry: No renewal mechanism published; credits are one-time grants (duration-of-use window not stated on page fetched today).
findings.gotchas: Free-plan accounts are INELIGIBLE for Activate (FAQ confirms Free plan excludes promotional/incentive credits) — you need a Paid account, i.e., the Free Plan's 6-month account that auto-closes is the wrong vehicle; startups should stay on Paid. Kiro Startup Credits are mutually exclusive with active Activate credits. The '/free/offers' page figures ($1K-$100K, 7-10 days) look stale versus the dedicated credits page ($5K/$200K, 5-10 days) — trust the credits page.

findings.name: Kiro Startup Credits (separate, non-Activate track, 2025/2026 new)
findings.detail: Up to one year of Kiro Pro+ credits (Kiro is AWS's agentic IDE) delivered in three tiers: Starter — up to 2 Kiro users; Growth — up to 10; Scale — up to 30. Credits are automatically added to the linked AWS account on approval. Not AWS infrastructure credits — covers Kiro Pro+ subscription only.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage through Series A startups, global, but EXCLUDED: Argentina, Belarus, Brazil, China/GCR, Cuba, France, Germany, Iran, Italy, Mexico, North Korea, Poland, Russia, Spain, Syria, Crimea, DNR, LNR, UAE. Requires a business email matching the startup's domain and an AWS Account ID tied to that email. Startups with active AWS Activate Credits are excluded (Activate credits can still be spent on Kiro separately).
findings.claim: Submit the form at kiro.dev/startups (or the AWS Startups Kiro credits page); reviewed on rolling basis, follow-up email; one application at a time per startup; redeem via Kiro using AWS IAM Identity Center sign-in (not Builder ID or social login).
findings.expiry: Credits expire one year after issuance to the AWS account. Not refundable, re-issuable, transferable, or sellable; shareable across authorized users of associated accounts in the same company. Once depleted, standard Kiro Pro+ billing applies.
findings.gotchas: Only relevant if you build in Kiro; does not fund GPU/ML compute. Heavy region exclusions (many of the EU, LatAm, ex-USSR).

findings.name: AWS Educate (education license / student path) — free digital training and credentials, no .edu email required
findings.detail: Free, curated learning paths and hands-on labs (starter labs in Storage, Compute, Networking, Databases, Cloud Operations); earn shareable digital badges (Credly network). Job board access for learners 18+. Recruiter accounts for employers to source talent. No institutional enrollment needed: 'open to any individual'.
findings.eligibility: Any individual — NO .edu email required; learners as young as 13 can register with just an email address; 'No credit card needed'.
findings.claim: Register at aws.amazon.com/education/awseducate with any email address; take labs; earn digital badges. No application or license to claim.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; no renewal or sunset noted. (A historical faculty/classroom-licensing front: aws.amazon.com/education/awsclassroom returns 404 — no public classroom-license page found today; institutions are instead directed to contact AWS for 'special pricing for education customers', i.e., not a public free offer.)
findings.gotchas: This is learning content, not compute: no GPU/ML training credits; no AWS account credits. The education landing page is high-level; program details live on the awseducate page. AWS Academy/partner-institution programs are separate and not free-publicly.

sunset_notes: Major 2025-2026 changes verified on official pages today (2026-10-22): (1) The legacy 12-month Free Tier is gone — the old 'free for 12 months' language no longer appears on aws.amazon.com/free; it has been replaced by the credit-based Free Plan ($100 signup + up to $100 explore = up to $200 over 6 months), after which the account auto-closes (data kept 90 days, then erased). (2) The classic 'Always Free' list was narrowed in messaging to '30+ services' with monthly limits (legacy tier had 60+ services); per-service quota numbers are no longer published on the hub. (3) SageMaker notebook free allowance shrunk to 250 hours of sc.t3.medium for the first 2 months (vs legacy 750 hours/month ml.t3.medium for 12 months). (4) AWS Activate tiers renamed/revalued: 'Activate Community' no longer appears on the current credits page — it is now 'Activate Founders' (up to $5,000, start $1,000) alongside 'Activate Portfolio' (now up to $200,000, previously up to $100,000) plus a new invite-only 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' ($200,000+); a new Kiro Startup Credits track (up to 1 year of Kiro Pro+, 1/10/30 users) was added. The stale /free/offers page still shows old $1,000-$100,000 figures and 7-10 day processing, inconsistent with the current credits page ($5,000/$200,000, 5-10 days) — treat the credits page as authoritative. (5) WebSearch was unavailable during this run, so no third-party press confirmation of announcement dates was possible; all claims above are from the official AWS pages fetched today.

provider: NVIDIA Inception Program — GPU / ML Training & Notebooks — Free Compute (verified 2026-10-22)

findings.name: NVIDIA Inception Program (startups) — free membership & core benefits
findings.detail: Free, no-equity program: free self-paced NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute courses, discounted expert-led workshops, free cloud credits from NVIDIA and partners, preferred pricing (rebate on select hardware/software), NVIDIA Developer Forums access, Inception Capital Connect (VC exposure), badges/co-marketing. No application fees, deadlines, or cohorts. Note: the task's entry URL nvidia.com/en-us/ai-catalog/inception/ now 404s; the live official page is nvidia.com/en-us/startups/ (verified today).
findings.eligibility: Company must be officially incorporated, less than 10 years old, actively operated by at least one founder, with a clear NVIDIA technology use case; any funding stage including bootstrapped; global, no stated region limit. Excluded: consulting/outsourced-dev firms, crypto-related companies, cloud service providers, resellers/distributors, public companies. NOT a .edu program — no student individual track, a legal entity is required.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at nvidia.com/en-us/startups/ (portal: programs.nvidia.com/phoenix/application). 2) Company is reviewed; keep profile/product details current in the portal to remain eligible. 3) Request benefits (cloud credits, partner offers, courses) from the Inception benefits catalog; partners approve individually. No credit card required for membership.
findings.gotchas: 'Free cloud credits' is a per-benefit request, not a fixed grant — amounts depend on which partner benefit you request. Preferred pricing is a rebate via suppliers, not a discount NVIDIA can guarantee. Membership can lapse if the portal profile goes stale.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry for membership; credits have partner-defined validity (e.g., Yotta 24 months, GCP 2 years).

findings.name: NVIDIA DGX Cloud credits — up to $100,000 for H100 capacity (Inception members)
findings.detail: Announced at GTC 2025 (March 2025 press release 'NVIDIA Expands Cloud Benefits for Startups'): NVIDIA offers qualified Inception members up to $100,000 in NVIDIA DGX Cloud credits for dedicated NVIDIA H100 GPU capacity, plus expert office hours. The figure still appears on NVIDIA's official Cloud Partners page as of today (2026-10-22), but the Inception main page does not list the benefit and 'qualified' criteria are unpublished; current availability not reconfirmable today.
findings.eligibility: Inception members (see base program: incorporated, <10 yrs old, any funding stage). 'Qualified members approved by NVIDIA after requesting the benefit in the portal' — qualification criteria are not public. No student path.
findings.claim: As an Inception member, request the DGX Cloud credit benefit in the Inception benefits catalog; NVIDIA reviews and may approve up to $100,000. No CC required by NVIDIA itself.
findings.gotchas: Gated request, not automatic; no dollar amount promised at membership; criteria unpublished; if NVIDIA has wound this down, it was quietly — the Cloud Partners page still advertises it (stale-risk).
findings.expiry: Not published.

findings.name: NVIDIA Cloud Partner free credits via Inception — Nebius up to $150K (+$10K inference), Yotta up to $50K, plus Lambda/Scaleway/Lintasarta
findings.detail: GTC 2025 (April 2025) expansion: Nebius 'AI Lift' — up to $150,000 in Nebius AI Cloud credits (NVIDIA GPUs) plus $10,000 specifically for inference workloads; first 3 months of the program also gave priority Blackwell access. Yotta — up to $50,000 in credits in three tiers ($10K/$15K/$25K), valid 24 months (confirmed on Yotta's official program page today). Lambda and Scaleway offer credits; NVIDIA said these partner/ISV offers total ~$300,000 in credits and discounts combined. Each partner sets its own amount/terms and approves the request.
findings.eligibility: NVIDIA Inception or NVIDIA Connect members who request the specific partner benefit in the Inception portal and are approved by that partner. Global; partner-specific terms apply (Yotta's $15K/$25K tiers need more detail about your NVIDIA-platform usage).
findings.claim: 1) Join Inception. 2) In the benefits catalog, request the desired partner (Nebius/Yotta/etc.). 3) Partner reviews and issues credits on its platform; Yotta credits valid 24 months.
findings.gotchas: Amounts are partner-defined, not NVIDIA's; partner approvals can be slow. Yotta tiers require describing how you use NVIDIA SDKs/platform. The $300K 'total' NVIDIA headline is a marketing aggregate, not stackable credits.
findings.expiry: Yotta: 24 months from grant; others partner-defined.

findings.name: AWS Activate via Inception (NVIDIA-issued Org ID) — Portfolio up to $200,000; self-funded Founders up to $5,000; invite-only AI tier $200,000+
findings.detail: Official AWS Activate page (verified today): Activate Portfolio = up to $200,000 in credits (pre-Series B, requires Org ID from an Activate provider; NVIDIA is an approved provider via Inception). Activate Founders (self-funded/bootstrapped) = start with $1,000, up to $5,000 total, apply directly without Org ID. New 'AWS Credits for AI Startups' = $200,000+, invite-only for scaling startups via account manager. A new 'Kiro Startup Credits' track also appears. Credits are redeemable on third-party models on Amazon Bedrock; 'AWS Account on Paid Tier Plan' is required. NVIDIA developer forums (2025–2026) show members previously receiving $10K/$25K tiers and up to $75K–$100K Scale-tier approvals, plus persistent Org-ID handoff issues between Inception and AWS.
findings.eligibility: Founded within the last 10 years; Pre-Series B (Portfolio); most recent funding round rules apply on AWS's side; bootstrapped founders use the Founders tier directly; for Inception-referred applicants: Inception membership + NVIDIA-confirmed AWS benefit + NVIDIA Org ID. AWS paid-tier account (credit card on file) required.
findings.claim: Inception route: 1) Join Inception, request the AWS benefit in the portal. 2) NVIDIA confirms eligibility and issues an AWS Activate Org ID. 3) Apply on AWS Activate (startups.aws.com) using the Org ID; AWS reviews (5–10 business days per AWS; community reports months). Direct route (self-funded): apply directly to Activate Founders, no Org ID. No .edu/student track (individuals just need an AWS account; students have AWS Free Tier separately).
findings.gotchas: Official tiers were restructured — the older member-reported $10K/$25K/Scale-up-to-$100K offers no longer appear on AWS's current page; the handoff (NVIDIA Org ID → AWS) has documented 3–15 month delays and auto-rejections ('already received credits at same or greater amount', 'provider has not confirmed affiliation'). Paid-tier account = CC required. Bedrock third-party model usage consumes credits.
findings.expiry: Activate credits validity is set by AWS promotional terms (typically 12 months from grant) — not restated on the page today.

findings.name: Google Cloud for Startups Cloud Program — up to $350,000 credits over 2 years (AI track)
findings.detail: Official GCP page (verified today): 'Up to $350,000 in Cloud credits over two years', plus credits for frontier models (Gemini/Gemma), technical/product training. Tier structure (footnotes on the page): AI startups — Year 1: up to $250,000 at 100%; Year 2: up to an additional $100,000 at 20%. Other startups — Year 1: up to $100,000 at 100%; Year 2: up to an additional $100,000 at 20%. 'Most tiers require verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding.' Third-party models are billed directly, not covered by credits. This program is a stated Inception partner benefit (NVIDIA↔GCP collab since April 2024 offered the up-to-$350K path through Inception).
findings.eligibility: Incorporated startup, verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding for most tiers; AI track requires the product to be AI-focused; apply at cloud.google.com/startup/apply. Inception members get an accelerated onboarding path (partner deal). No .edu requirement; not open to individuals/students. Card policy not restated on the page today (GCP account required; standard GCP trials normally take a card on file).
findings.claim: 1) Apply at cloud.google.com/startups (Apply to the program). 2) Verify funding stage / company details. 3) If Inception member, use the partner fast-track. 4) Draw down: AI — up to $250K year 1; +up to $100K at 20% (i.e., up to $20K effective in year 2 per footnote wording). 5) Credits cover Google-built models; third-party model inference is billed separately.
findings.gotchas: 'Year 2: 20% up to an additional $100,000' means only 20% of year-2 usage up to $100K is credited, not the full amount — real max over 2 years is less than a naive $350K + $100K read. Third-party (e.g., non-Google) model API calls are excluded. Pre-Seed–Series A gate excludes bootstrapped/late-stage companies (unlike AWS's pre-Series B).
findings.expiry: Credits usable over 2 years as structured above.

findings.name: Google Cloud free trial + always-free tier — $300 / new customers (open to students & individuals)
findings.detail: Official page (verified today): 'New customers get $300 in free credit to try Google Cloud products and build a proof of concept. You won't be charged until you activate your full paid account.' Plus 20+ always-free products with monthly limits ('$300 in free credits and 20+ free products'), free trial instances for GKE, Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, Bigtable, plus Gemini Enterprise Plus free trial. This is the individual/student-reachable free GPU/cloud front of the ecosystem (GCP A-series GPU instances can be run on the $300 trial).
findings.eligibility: New GCP customers; open to anyone with a Google account (students with .edu or personal both qualify); no funding/age requirements; global. Standard signup takes a credit/debit card on file (not restated in today's page text — historical standard).
findings.claim: Sign up at console.cloud.google.com/freetrial; $300 credit is valid for 90 days under standard terms; always-free quotas apply regardless. Use on A3/A100/A100M GPU instances or Vertex AI for ML training jobs.
findings.gotchas: Trial is a 90-day time-boxed trial, not perpetual free compute; if the paid account activates after trial expiry, standard pay-as-you-go applies; card required (verify current signup). GPU availability for A100/A3 is region-limited.
findings.expiry: $300 trial: 90 days (standard terms); always-free tier: indefinite, monthly limits.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — 'up to $150,000 in credits' on Azure + free AI tools & GitHub credits
findings.detail: Official hub (verified today): 'Access cutting-edge AI models, developer tools, and up to $150,000 in credits' — a large 2025/2026 expansion vs the legacy $1,200/year Azure + $1,200 GitHub framing. Credits apply to eligible Azure services on a sponsored subscription; Microsoft Learn (today) documents credit-aware use across GitHub (Copilot, Actions, billing connected via the Azure subscription), Microsoft Foundry models, Fireworks models, and AKS (AKS usage on a sponsored subscription is auto-covered). Tier details and eligibility are gated behind the application flow, not published on the marketing page.
findings.eligibility: Incorporated startups; Microsoft's own 'Microsoft for Startups' application decides tier/amount; Inception members can apply independently (no NVIDIA Org ID involved). No .edu/student track — it is a startup program. Exact funding/age caps not stated on the pages verified today.
findings.claim: 1) Apply via Microsoft for Startups (www.microsoft.com/en-us/startups → apply/claim benefits). 2) Claim 'Startup credits' into a sponsored Azure subscription. 3) Optionally connect that subscription as GitHub's payment method so GitHub Copilot/Actions metered usage bills against the credits. No CC required for the sponsored credits themselves (standard Azure account still needed).
findings.gotchas: 'Up to $150,000' is a marketing ceiling — the bulk of recipients get far less; published tier table not found on marketing pages. Partner/community models on Foundry are billed separately from Microsoft-sold models. Legacy $1,200 figure no longer appears — check the application flow for what you will actually be offered.
findings.expiry: Not published on verified pages; Microsoft historically used 12-month renewal windows for Azure startup credits.

findings.name: NVIDIA Inception Innovation Lab — 60 days of hands-on NVIDIA GPU access (selected members)
findings.detail: Inception benefit: 60 days of hands-on NVIDIA GPU access on a self-serve platform with pre-optimized environments and expert support, run in cohorts; NVIDIA provides the cloud instance (no dollar value published). Reported in the current (2026) Inception benefits summary; it is a selected-member benefit, not automatic.
findings.eligibility: Selected NVIDIA Inception members (cohort-based); same base Inception eligibility (incorporated, <10 yrs, NVIDIA use case).
findings.claim: Join Inception, then be selected into an Innovation Lab cohort; request via the benefits catalog.
findings.gotchas: Cohort selection — approval not guaranteed; time-boxed 60 days; no published dollar value; availability fluctuates.
findings.expiry: 60 days per cohort.

findings.name: build.nvidia.com — free NIM inference for open models incl. Nemotron (open access, incl. students)
findings.detail: Official build.nvidia.com (verified today): 'Free inference with leading models' — free API endpoints for Nemotron models (and other open models, e.g., DeepSeek) plus pre-built agentic capabilities and blueprints. Open sign-up (no startup status or .edu stated as a requirement), so this is the individual/student-reachable 'free ML compute' front, but it is inference API, not GPU training or notebooks. Community reports a default RPM cap around 40; Inception members can request higher RPM for research workloads (forum, Oct 2026).
findings.eligibility: Any NVIDIA developer account; Inception members may request raised rate limits. No funding/institution gate documented. No CC stated for inference use.
findings.claim: 1) Sign in at build.nvidia.com. 2) Use the model's API endpoint / key to run inference free within rate limits. 3) Inception members: request higher RPM via the Inception portal / developer forums for research benchmarks.
findings.gotchas: Inference-only — cannot train or host notebooks here; rate-limited; free-tier availability of specific models can change; heavier workloads require paid or partner-cloud (Inception credit) routes.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry; free tier subject to change.

findings.name: NVIDIA education angle — free self-paced DLI courses; no dedicated student GPU-compute program found
findings.detail: NVIDIA's student/education-free offer is educational, not compute: free self-paced Deep Learning Institute courses (course codes distributed via Inception membership; public DLI catalog is also free), discounted instructor-led workshops, free CUDA Toolkit/NGC developer downloads. No NVIDIA 'education license' or .edu GPU quota program (e.g., Colab-style notebooks) was found in the Inception or NVIDIA education pages as of today; student GPU compute in this ecosystem effectively comes through the partner free trials (GCP $300/90-day + free A-series eligibility, AWS Free Tier, Azure) or via starting a company and joining Inception.
findings.eligibility: Individuals/students: free DLI courses, build.nvidia.com inference, partner free trials (no .edu email specifically required by NVIDIA; .edu mainly matters at third parties like Google's student pricing elsewhere). Startups: Inception (incorporated entity).
findings.claim: Students: enroll in DLI courses / use build.nvidia.com free inference / claim GCP $300 trial and AWS Free Tier on a personal account. Startups: apply to Inception for the partner-credit stack above.
findings.gotchas: Do not conflate 'free trials' (time-boxed, card on file, pay-as-you-go after) with 'free' — only DLI, build.nvidia.com inference (rate-limited), and partner credits are genuinely free.
findings.expiry: N/A (courses free; trials per partner terms).

findings.name: Personal free plan (permanent free tier)
findings.detail: Free forever Personal plan: 500 GB/month data-loading (ingest) compute, 10 GB-hours query compute, 25 GB storage, 30-day retention. Includes full APL access and all integrations; community support. Soft limits on datasets / fields per dataset / query concurrency that 'can be lifted on request'. No hard numeric caps published for those. Verified on the official pricing page on 2026-10-22: '500 GB load / 10 GB-hours / 25 GB storage, free forever' is also restated on the Startups solution page.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone, including students and early startups. No credit card required (pricing page: 'No credit card required'; quickstart: 'No schema, no credit card'). No .edu email required, no age/funding/region limits stated.
findings.claim: Sign up at axiom.co (no payment method), create a dataset, ship logs via OTel or Axiom SDKs (5-minute quickstart at /docs/getting-started). No application needed. Request soft-limit lifts via support (axiom.co/support) if needed.
findings.expiry: Permanent ('Permanent' on pricing page; FAQ calls it 'free forever with a generous allowance'). No expiry or renewal.
findings.gotchas: Only 30-day retention and 25 GB storage on free tier — long-term archives need paid Axiom Cloud (customizable/Forever retention). The free plan is a real perpetual tier, not a trial. Soft limits on dataset counts/concurrency can bite heavy users. Previously-seen '5 GB ingest + $10 credit' figures are stale — see sunset_notes.

findings.name: Axiom for Startups program (compute discount + platform-fee waiver)
findings.detail: For qualifying startups: 30% off Data Loading and Query Compute, 'up to $10,000 in compute savings' over 'up to 12 months' (whichever comes first), plus the $25/mo Axiom Cloud platform fee waived for 12 months. The always-free included usage (first 1 TB load + 100 GB-hours query per month, 100 GB storage) still applies. Worked example on page: 10 TB load + 2,000 GB-hrs query/mo saves ~$5,340/yr including the fee waiver. Verified on official page 2026-10-22.
findings.eligibility: Startup stage 'between Seed and Series A'. Must be NEW to paid Axiom Cloud — free-tier users may apply; existing paid customers are NOT eligible. Company must not have received an Axiom startup benefit before. No startup-age, funding-dollar-cap, or location restrictions stated beyond the Seed–Series A stage.
findings.claim: Submit the form at https://axiom.co/axiom-for-startups: describe your company, how you found the program, and provide a funding announcement, investor portfolio page, or accelerator profile (or an access code / confirming contact if private). Axiom reviews and replies by email. Once approved the program is enabled on your org; the 12-month clock starts when you upgrade to Axiom Cloud (which requires a credit card on file).
findings.expiry: 30% compute discount lasts up to 12 months OR until $10,000 in savings, whichever comes first (hitting $10k ends the discount early but the fee waiver runs its full 12 months). After 12 months, standard pricing including the $25 platform fee resumes. No renewal path is described. No program sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Not self-serve: application must go through a participating accelerator, investor, or startup community and requires proof. Cannot combine with committed-use pricing or another promotional compute discount. Storage and add-ons (SSO $100/mo, Directory Sync $100/mo, RBAC $50/mo, Audit Logs $50/mo) stay at standard pricing. Axiom Cloud itself needs a card on file. Billing caps pause (not bill) overage, which can interrupt queries/monitors at the cap.

findings.name: Axiom Cloud 'always free' allowance baked into the $25/mo plan (startup-adjacent offer)
findings.detail: Axiom Cloud: $25/month platform fee, no minimum commitment, with an always-free allowance of 1 TB (1,000 GB) data loading + 100 GB-hours query compute + 100 GB storage per month; usage beyond is credit-based (1 credit = $1 by default; data loading from 0.12 credits/GB down to 0.06 at high volume; committed-use pre-purchase up to ~47% off at 2.5M credits/yr on 36-month term; pre-purchased credits 'never expire'). A hard spend cap can be set in the Console — overage is paused rather than billed (cap feature introduced 2025-09-22). Useful for students/startups who need more than the Personal tier but want a cost ceiling: worst case is the $25 fee.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who upgrades to Axiom Cloud; credit card required (card on file). No age/funding/education restrictions. Students can use it with a spend cap to guarantee max cost = $25/mo.
findings.claim: Upgrade from Personal at axiom.co/pricing (add card), optionally set a monthly spend limit in the Console; claim the Axiom for Startups program instead if you qualify for the 30% discount + fee waiver.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; allowance renews monthly with the plan. No expiry date published.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required (differs from the free Personal plan). Hitting the spend cap PAUSES usage (queries/monitors stop) until next cycle — 'may cause service interruptions'. Overage beyond the 1TB/100GB-hr free block can still add cost within the cap. Add-ons (SSO, RBAC, audit logs, Directory Sync) are extra $50–100/mo.

findings.name: Education / student program: none found
findings.detail: No dedicated Axiom education license, student program, or .edu-based offer exists on the site as of 2026-10-22: /education returns 404, the sitemap has no education/student/campus/trial URLs, the pricing page, FAQ, and 2025–2026 blog index contain no student or academic pricing. Students' effective free offer is the credit-card-free Personal plan (finding 1); startups' is the Axiom for Startups program (finding 2).
findings.eligibility: N/A — no program to be eligible for. Students use the general Personal free plan (no .edu email required, no credit card).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim separately; students simply sign up at axiom.co for the free Personal plan.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Absence was verified via sitemap, 404 checks on /education, and blog index, but WebSearch budget was exhausted so I could not sweep press/third-party sources for a partner-run student deal; confidence medium rather than high on the negative.

sunset_notes: 1) The previously known '5 GB ingest/month + $10 signup credit' is STALE. On 2025-04-21 Axiom 'Reimagined pricing' (blog/reimagining-pricing): the old ingestion-focused Personal/Team/Enterprise tiers were replaced by credit-based Axiom Cloud pricing ($25/mo platform fee, 1 credit = $1, always-free 1TB/100GB-hr/100GB block) plus a new credit-card-free Personal free tier now at 500 GB load/mo (current pricing page), 10 GB-hrs query, 25 GB storage, 30-day retention. 2) The $10 signup credit no longer appears on the pricing page, FAQ, or 2025–2026 blog; it is not a documented current offer (treat as discontinued/unverified). 3) 2025-09-22 changelog added compute-credit pre-purchase discounts and spend caps (overage pauses rather than bills) — a material change for cost safety. 4) Axiom's docs moved from docs.axiom.co to axiom.co/docs in 2026. 5) No 2025–2026 sunset of the startup program found — /axiom-for-startups is live with current terms as of today's fetch.

provider: Prometheus (CNCF, self-hosted OSS) — Observability/Monitoring front, plus managed-Prometheus hosts with free offers: Grafana Cloud, AWS AMP, Datadog, Cloudflare, GCP

findings.name: Prometheus self-hosted (open source)
findings.detail: Core offer: Prometheus is 100% open source under Apache 2.0, a CNCF graduated project. Free, unlimited, self-contained time-series DB; no pricing, tiers, or per-metric limits exist for the OSS server. Pairs with Grafana OSS (also free) for dashboards and Alertmanager for alerting. No account, no claim, no expiry; the only cost is the infrastructure you host it on (cloud compute/egress).
findings.eligibility: Universal: anyone (students, startups, enterprises, noncommercial or commercial). No .edu, no funding cap, no credit card.
findings.claim: No claim needed. Download binary/Docker from prometheus.io/download or your package manager; deploy and point Grafana at it. Optionally use k8s (kube-prometheus-stack).
findings.expiry: None — Apache 2.0 license, indefinite.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: there is no trial, it is simply free. Watch your hosting/egress costs, retention (local disk is finite), HA setup (thanos/cortex/remote write adds complexity), and scale limits of a single node. Managed tiers below exist precisely to offload ops.

findings.name: Grafana Cloud Free plan (managed Prometheus metrics)
findings.detail: Per grafana.com/pricing (read today): 3 active users; up to 10k active metric series/month; 50 GB ingested/month across logs/traces/profiles; 14-day retention for metrics/logs/traces/profiles; 100k synthetics API executions + 10k browser test executions/month; 500 k6 vUser-hours; community support. No credit card required. Pro starts at $19/mo platform fee + usage (e.g., $6.50/1k series for metrics).
findings.eligibility: Universal, no education/startup status needed. CC explicitly not required on the free plan.
findings.claim: Sign up at grafana.com (Grafana Cloud), choose the Free plan, then configure your Prometheus to remote-write to the Grafana cloud ingestion endpoint — free managed Prometheus with no card.
findings.expiry: Indefinite free plan; no expiry, no auto-conversion.
findings.gotchas: Free is capped at 10k active series and 50 GB ingest/month — overage pushes you to paid. Retention is short (14 days; Pro gives 13 months metrics/30 days logs). 'No credit card required' is the page's claim — verify at signup, Grafana has occasionally asked for a card in promos.

findings.name: Grafana Labs Startup Program (Grafana Cloud credits for Prometheus logs/traces/metrics)
findings.detail: Per the official blog (read today): up to $100,000 in Grafana Cloud credits for 12 months OR until the next funding round, usable on any Grafana Cloud service (logs, traces, metrics incl. managed Prometheus, k6, synthetics, IRM). Ideal profile: < $10M raised and < 25 employees, but larger startups are encouraged to apply. Admission at sole discretion; accepted startups agree to be a reference customer and possible marketing collaboration. After credits expire: guaranteed 20% discount off list pricing. Announced at ObservabilityCON, 25 Sep 2024.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups (ideal: <$10M raised, <25 employees, open to exceeding guidelines); all new Grafana Cloud customers incl. free-tier users, and Grafana OSS users moving to managed. Not aimed at students/education. Discretionary acceptance.
findings.claim: Complete the 4-question application (Typeform link published in the official blog post; program web pages grafana.com/startups and grafana.com/startup-program both 404'd today — use the blog post's link or contact Grafana sales to apply).
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months or until next funding round, whichever first; renewal beyond that is the 20% list-price discount, not more credits.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: this is a credits program, not a permanent free tier — after burn, you pay (less). Reference-customer/marketing strings attached. Verify the live application URL before assuming the program is still open (web page 404 today; program is 2+ years old as of 2026).

findings.name: AWS Managed Service for Prometheus free tier
findings.detail: Per aws.amazon.com/prometheus/pricing (read today): free tier includes 40M ingested metric samples/month, 200B query samples processed/month, and 10 GB of stored metrics — 'you can get started with Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus for free (in supported AWS Regions)'.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with an AWS account (new-account free tier terms apply); no student/education or startup status required; no CC claim beyond normal AWS account setup.
findings.claim: Create a Prometheus workspace in a supported AWS region; free tier applies automatically, no enrollment.
findings.expiry: Free tier is ongoing (not a 12-month trial) subject to AWS free-tier policy; limits are monthly.
findings.gotchas: Only available in 'supported AWS Regions' — check region coverage. Limits are per-sample, so a high-cardinality scrape job can burn 40M samples fast; overage bills per sample/GB, and the 200B query-sample cap can surprise. This sample-based structure differs from the 100 GB/month + custom-label-sets limits third-party trackers historically reported for AMP (see sunset_notes).

findings.name: Datadog Free plan (including Prometheus monitoring)
findings.detail: Per datadoghq.com/pricing (read today): Free tier = up to 5 hosts, unlimited user accounts, 100 custom metrics allotted per host, 500 custom events/host, 5 containers per host, out-of-the-box dashboards, unlimited alerts; full-resolution data retention shown as 1 day on the current page. Prometheus is covered via Datadog's Prometheus integration (APM/infrastructure monitoring); Prometheus is not named on the pricing page's free-tier table.
findings.eligibility: Universal (students/startups/anyone); no .edu requirement. Credit-card policy is not stated on the page — Datadog's signup historically asks for a payment method even for the free plan, so do not assume no-CC.
findings.claim: Sign up at datadoghq.com, select the Free plan, install the Datadog agent or point Prometheus at Datadog's endpoint.
findings.expiry: Free plan is perpetual; no expiry.
findings.gotchas: Current page states 1-day full-resolution retention on Free (historically 14 days) — materially thinner than older marketing. The 'Start Free Trial' CTA wording conflates the Free plan with a trial; verify you're on the Free plan, not a trial with clock. CC policy unverified on the page.

findings.name: Cloudflare for Startups (CDN/uptime front; credits + free tier)
findings.detail: Per cloudflare.com/startups (read today): up to $350,000 in credits, valid 1 year or until consumed (no extensions), across three tiers — Tier 3: $10,000 (bootstrapped or <$1M raised, no partner needed); Tier 2: $100,000 (<$5M raised, funded by an affiliated partner, gets an account manager); Tier 1: $350,000 ($5M+ raised, partner-funded, bi-weekly architect hours + priority support). Credits cover usage-based services (Workers, Durable Objects, Workflows, Workers AI [AI capped at $50k in T1], R2/KV/D1/Queues/Vectorize [R2 capped at $10k], Pages, Images/Stream, Cache Reserve, Argo Smart Routing). Core CDN/DNS/SSL/DDoS/WAF/load-balancing are free-included in every tier regardless.
findings.eligibility: Startups: incorporated within last 10 years, funded up to Series B within the last 12 months, building a tech product with a live public website, active on at least one public social channel, for-profit company email matching the domain; first-time applicants only. Excludes educational institutions, consultancies, MSPs, resellers, personal blogs — not a student offer.
findings.claim: Apply via the program's application page at cloudflare.com/lp/startups; review typically within 48 hours; email startups@cloudflare.com for case-by-case tier upgrades (existing members under old caps).
findings.expiry: Credits: 12 months or until consumed, whichever first; not extendable; upgrades don't reset the clock. Free CDN/uptime tier itself is indefinite.
findings.gotchas: Overages bill the card on file after credits run; AI Gateway is temporarily not credit-eligible; premium products (Magic Transit, China Network, etc.) need separate contracts. Students get nothing here — Cloudflare's plain Free plan (CDN/DNS/SSL for 100 zones) is the indefinite, no-CC, free-for-all baseline.

findings.name: Google Cloud Startup Program credits (usable on Managed Service for Prometheus)
findings.detail: Per cloud.google.com/startup/ai content surfaced in search today: up to $350,000 GCP credits over 2 years — Year 1: 100% of first $100,000 (up to $250,000 for AI-first startups), Year 2: 20% of up to an additional $100,000; includes Gemini/Gemma access and expert webinars. These general credits cover GCP's Managed Service for Prometheus ingest/query costs, which is the closest thing to a GCP 'managed Prometheus' free offer.
findings.eligibility: VC-funded startups: pre-seed/seed raised within last 5 years, Series A within last 12 months, founded within last 5 years, not yet received more than $5,000 in GCP credits; eligibility at Google's discretion. Not a student offer (Google Cloud's $300/60-day free trial is the general alternative).
findings.claim: Apply via Google Cloud's startup program application (cloud.google.com/startup) or an affiliated YC/accelerator partner; credits land as GCP billing credits usable on any service incl. Cloud Monitoring / Managed Prometheus.
findings.expiry: Credits structured over 2 years (Y1 100%, Y2 20%); GCP free-trial alternative: 60 days.
findings.gotchas: Third-party models billed directly, not covered by credits; 'up to $5,000 in GCP credits already received' gate; Y2 discount rate drops to 20%. Specific GCP Managed-Prometheus free-tier numbers could NOT be verified today (pricing pages truncated/redirecting/404) — treat any per-sample free allowance figures as unconfirmed.

findings.name: No student/education license exists for Prometheus (negative finding)
findings.detail: Prometheus has no education license, student program, or .edu offer: prometheus.io (read today) carries no pricing, education, or partner pages at all — it is an Apache-2.0 CNCF project, so the 'student offer' is simply that the software is free and unlimited for students. No Grafana, AWS AMP, Datadog, or Cloudflare education-specific tier tied to Prometheus was found on the official pages read today. Azure's Managed Prometheus service exists (GA 2025) but its pricing page would not load today, so any Azure free-tier figures are unverified rather than reported.
findings.eligibility: n/a — absence finding. Anything claiming a 'Prometheus education discount' (e.g., boilerplate rows on discount-tracker sites) is generic vendor-template content, not a real offer.
findings.claim: n/a. For students: just self-host Prometheus OSS (free) or use Grafana Cloud Free / Cloudflare's no-CC Free plan.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Discount-aggregator pages (e.g., costbench) publish 'Education Discount / Startup Program' boilerplate for Prometheus that they themselves mark as unverified — do not treat those as real programs.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 changes & verification gaps: (1) AWS AMP's free tier is now expressed as 40M ingested samples/mo + 200B query samples/mo + 10GB stored, replacing the 100 GB/month + custom-label-sets formulation that trackers like costbench still list — a pricing-model change; no sunset announcement found, but the old figures are stale. (2) Datadog's Free plan now shows 1-day full-resolution data retention (down from the long-standing 14 days) — a material reduction. (3) Grafana Labs Startup Program ($100k credits) details come from the Sep 2024 blog; the program web pages grafana.com/startups and grafana.com/startup-program both 404 today, so the application link moved — verify before assuming the program is open; credits remain subject to '12 months or next funding round' expiry. (4) Cloudflare for Startups was raised in 2025–2026: Tier 1 up from $250k to $350k, Tier 3 up from $5k to $10k; T1 credit AI cap $50k, R2 cap $10k; AI Gateway excluded from credits. (5) GCP Managed Service for Prometheus and Azure Managed Prometheus free-tier numbers could not be verified today (truncated/404/redirecting pages, and the session's web-search budget is exhausted) — anything specific about them here is unconfirmed rather than verified. No Prometheus offer was fully sunset: the OSS remains free-and-unlimited, and every managed free tier above still exists.

findings.name: Elastic Cloud 14-day free trial (Observability incl. logs, APM, metrics, traces, RUM, synthetics/uptime)
findings.detail: 14-day trial of Elastic Cloud (Hosted and Serverless) covering the full Elastic Observability suite: log monitoring, APM, infrastructure monitoring, AIOps/generative AI, digital experience monitoring (RUM, synthetics, uptime), OpenTelemetry, plus AutoOps. Official pricing FAQ states the trial 'includes a cluster with 8GB of RAM and 240GB of storage'; the Observability trial page says 'Get up to 360GB of storage during your trial' (figures differ between pages). No credit card required to sign up; after the trial you only pay if you add a card, pay-per-use with no long-term commitments.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, any email — no .edu, no company stage, no funding cap, no region limit (deploys in AWS/Azure/GCP regions; note sign-ups routed through Azure/GCP marketplaces get the 7-day marketplace trial instead).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at cloud.elastic.co (email/Google/Microsoft), 2) choose a cloud provider, 3) create a deployment — up and running in <5 minutes. Trial clock starts when the first cluster is created.
findings.expiry: 14 days from cluster creation. No extension or renewal; deployments/data persist afterward but using them beyond the trial requires adding a credit card.
findings.gotchas: Trial is not free-forever: post-trial, adding a card converts you to a paid subscription and billing begins. Official pages disagree on storage cap (240GB in pricing FAQ vs 'up to 360GB' on trial page) — actual limits may vary by provider/region. Azure/GCP-marketplace sign-ups get a 7-day trial, not 14.

findings.name: AWS Marketplace / GCP Marketplace 7-day trials (no credit card to Elastic)
findings.detail: Subscribing via AWS Marketplace gives a 7-day free trial (single deployment, not charged for first 7 days) during which you automatically get an Enterprise-level subscription; you pay Elastic via your AWS bill with no separate card to Elastic. GCP Marketplace: 7-day trial, one deployment plus three projects; usage-based billing starts automatically after 7 days; one Elastic Cloud org per GCP billing account; if you unsubscribe, the trial ends immediately and cannot be resumed even after resubscribing.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with an AWS or GCP account (billing account used for the marketplace purchase). No .edu or startup requirement.
findings.claim: AWS: Elastic Cloud on AWS Marketplace > View purchase options > sign in > use; billing starts automatically after day 7 unless you delete deployments. GCP: subscribe on the GCP Marketplace Elastic page, link/create an Elastic Cloud account, verify email; delete resources to stop charges.
findings.expiry: 7 days; automatic conversion to usage-based billing on the marketplace bill (Elastic Cloud billed through AWS/GCP, egress/snapshot charges metered in US East for AWS).
findings.gotchas: Billing starts automatically after 7 days — delete deployments to avoid charges. These are separate from the 14-day direct trial; a marketplace subscription replaces/links to the trial account, it does not extend it.
