AWS Marketplace charges metered in us-east-1 regardless of deployment region.

findings.name: Self-managed Elastic Stack (Elasticsearch/Logstash/Kibana/Beats) — free 'Basic' license, perpetual
findings.detail: The Elastic Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana, Beats, Logstash) can be downloaded and run for free, forever: 'the OSS features as well as the free Basic features of our software at no cost', including native security features, role-based access control, and true Kibana multitenancy. Elastic explicitly says it is free 'to learn, to develop, and to run production at scale'. No trial, no credit card, no cap. (Note: since the 2021 re-licensing, the stack is under Elastic License v2 / SSPL rather than Apache-2.0, and 'free' = the Basic feature set.)
findings.eligibility: Anyone, including students and startups; no .edu, no region or usage limit.
findings.claim: Download the Elastic Stack from elastic.co/downloads and self-host on your own infrastructure (containers, VMs, on-prem).
findings.expiry: Perpetual — no expiry, no renewal; free Basic features have no stated time limit.
findings.gotchas: 'Free ELK' ≠ full feature set: APM scale-out, many log-scaling/security (SIEM/XDR) and ML capabilities sit in paid Gold/Platinum/Enterprise tiers; Basic has no vendor support. Budget for your own infrastructure and operations; self-hosting is free but not costless. License is ELv2/SSPL, not classic Apache OSS.

findings.name: Elastic Cloud Serverless: built-in free allowances (50 GB/month egress, 10k free workflow/agent executions) with 14-day trial — no perpetual free tier
findings.detail: There is no free-forever tier for Elastic Cloud Serverless; instead the pay-as-you-go plans include standing free allowances: 50 GB free egress per month (then $0.05/GB), 10,000 free workflow executions (then ~$0.0108/execution), and 10,000 free Agent Builder executions (then ~$0.025/execution). Below that, logs/traces ingest starts ~$0.07/GB, metrics ingest ~$0.023–0.09/GB, retention ~$0.005–0.019/GB-month. Higher support tiers add 5–15% of the bill. A 14-day free trial of Serverless is also available (serverless-registration); uptime monitoring in production is paid: synthetic browser tests $0.0123/test run, lightweight ping $28.00/location/month.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a free Elastic Cloud account; no .edu or startup requirement; pay-as-you-go with no minimum commitment. New serverless metrics pricing effective July 1, 2026.
findings.claim: Sign up via cloud.elastic.co/serverless-registration (or a 14-day trial), create a serverless project; free allowances apply automatically each month — no voucher or form.
findings.expiry: Free allowances recur monthly (egress allowance resets per billing month). Trial itself is 14 days; allowances have no stated sunset.
findings.gotchas: Not a free tier — every GB ingested/retained above the free egress/execution allowances bills automatically. Uptime monitoring is essentially not free at scale (ping locations are the costliest add-on at $28/location/month). No credit card needed for trial, but continuing serverless usage beyond the trial requires billing info.

findings.name: Up to $5,000 Elastic Cloud credits via AWS Activate (self-founded startups: $1,000) — not offered on elastic.co itself
findings.detail: Elastic's startup credits are distributed through AWS Activate, not Elastic's own site: 'Up to $5,000 in Elastic Cloud credits for AWS Activate members' covering search, observability (logs, metrics, traces) and security, incl. serverless; a separate channel line lists '$1,000 in Elastic Cloud credits for Self Founded Startups' (per Superscout, last checked 2026-09-29; the $5K figure was confirmed in an official AWS Startups LinkedIn post, 2026-09-01, describing August 2026 Activate vendor offers).
findings.eligibility: Startups: AWS Activate membership (funded/accelerator path for up to $5K; 'Self Founded' path for $1K). No .edu requirement. Application-based, not open to everyone.
findings.claim: Apply through the AWS Activate Perks page (aws.amazon.com/startups/perks, now serving at startups.aws.com) — the Elastic entry requires an application through the AWS channel.
findings.expiry: No published expiration; perk amounts/terms set by AWS Elastic partnership (aggregator last-checked dates: 2026-09-29).
findings.gotchas: Elastic's own site publishes no startup program (elastic.co/startups is a 404; StartupPerks verified 2026-10-07 that the $5,000 figure appears only on third-party lists). The AWS Perks page returned 404 to direct fetches (likely JS-rendered), so exact current amounts should be re-verified on the AWS page or via AWS startup support before relying on them. Credits apply to Elastic Cloud (not self-managed licenses).

findings.name: Elastic education/training: free self-paced courses and a free GenAI Associate exam (no .edu product licenses, no exam vouchers found)
findings.detail: Elastic's training hub (elastic.co/training) offers 'Learn Elastic for free' self-paced modules at no cost (e.g., 'Getting started: What is Elastic?', 'RAG foundation', 'Semantic search foundation', 'Intro to MCP with Elasticsearch MCP Server'). The 'GenAI Associate Accreditation Exam' is listed with a direct free 'Take exam' link. Instructor-led courses (Elastic Observability Engineer, Elasticsearch Engineer, Kibana Data Analysis, Security for SIEM) carry no visible student discount or voucher on the page; standard certification exam pricing and voucher programs are not published on the site. There is no .edu-based product licensing program found — students get the same free Basic self-hosted stack and 14-day trial as everyone else.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no .edu email, no regional limit, no cost for the free modules/exam. No student-specific tiers or discounts found.
findings.claim: Browse elastic.co/training, click 'Start module' for free courses; 'Take exam' link on the GenAI Associate exam; register a free account if prompted.
findings.expiry: Free modules are standing; the free GenAI exam is promotional and may change without notice. No product offer has expiry.
findings.gotchas: Free exam appears limited to the GenAI Associate accreditation — other certifications (Engineer-level) are paid; don't assume all exams are free. No academic software license exists; 'education license' for Elastic Cloud does not appear anywhere on elastic.co as of 2026-10-22.

provider: Elastic — Observability (logging), Monitoring, Uptime & CDN fronts
sunset_notes: 1) Elastic's own 'Elastic for Startups' program (announced ~2021–2022: Elastic Cloud credits + developer-advocate support, targeting seed/pre-Series A) no longer exists on elastic.co — /startups returns 404 and a 2026-10-07 check of elastic.co (StartupPerks) found no startup program in Elastic's sitemaps; the 'up to $5,000' figure surviving in aggregators traces to the AWS Activate channel, not to any Elastic-published program. The current official route for startup credits is AWS Activate (up to $5K funded / $1K self-founded, per AWS Startups' own 2026-09-01 announcement). 2) No perpetual free cloud tier ever existed for Elastic Cloud — the only standing free offers are the 14-day trial, marketplace 7-day trials, serverless free allowances (egress/executions), and the free self-hosted Basic license. 3) Pricing-page changes in the 2025–2026 window: Elastic Cloud Serverless is now GA (AWS/GCP/Azure) with pay-as-you-go or prepaid models, and new serverless metrics pricing took effect July 1, 2026; the classic 'Essentials' entry tier is no longer listed — current subscription tiers are Standard/Gold/Platinum/Enterprise. 4) Trial terms stable: still 14 days, no credit card required. 5) Gotcha for students specifically: Elastic does not publish any .edu verification, academic license, or student voucher program — students and startups get the same offers as general consumers plus the AWS Activate credit channel for startups.

findings.claim: Sign up at supabase.com and click 'Start for Free' on the pricing page, then create a project. No application and no credit card. The 2-active-project limit applies to any org where you are Owner or Administrator, so you can run one project in two free orgs.
findings.detail: Supabase Free Plan = the genuine, perpetual free tier ($0/month). Verified limits read from supabase.com/pricing this session: 50,000 monthly active users for Auth (also 50,000 third-party MAU); 500 MB Postgres database (shared CPU, 500 MB RAM); 1 GB file storage (50 MB/file max, basic CDN); 500,000 edge-function invocations; 5 GB standard egress + 5 GB cached egress; Realtime 200 peak connections and 2M messages/month; unlimited API requests; 1-day log retention; community support only. NOT on free: SSO auth, image transforms, backups, PITR, branching, custom domains, log drains.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (no student or startup gate). No credit card required to start the free tier (widely confirmed by third parties; the $0 plan needs no payment method). Available globally. Hard cap of 2 active projects across all orgs where you are Owner/Admin; paused projects do not count toward that cap.
findings.expiry: Free indefinitely, no renewal/annualization. But each free project auto-pauses after 1 week of inactivity; it resumes on the next API call. Pause does not delete data. Paid tiers (Pro from $25/mo) do not pause for inactivity.
findings.gotchas: 1-week idle pause will kill dev/test or course-work deployments that sit between deadlines. Strict 2-active-project cap. No SSO, no image transforms, no backups/PITR/branching, no custom domains. Going to Pro adds a per-project compute line (Micro ~$10/mo) and charges usage beyond the included quotas (MAU beyond 100k, disk beyond 8 GB, egress beyond 250 GB, etc.). Treat the free plan as dev/prototype, not a production DB.
findings.name: Supabase Free Plan (free tier) — Auth, Postgres, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime

findings.claim: No verified public application path found: no application form exists on any Supabase-owned page (the startup and partner pages are marketing-only). If the offer exists at all it appears gated through partner accelerators (Y Combinator / Techstars) or Supabase sales. Verify with Supabase sales before planning around it.
findings.detail: A Supabase startup credits program is cited by third-party aggregators but the figures contradict each other and none can be confirmed on a Supabase-owned page: 'Supabase Credits' guide claims '$2,500 in credits'; StartupPerks frames it as an ongoing free plan for pre-seed/seed/Series A companies under ~5 yrs old that raised under $5M (no funding required); guptadeepak.com's 'Supabase Startup Program' page states the program is DISCONTINUED and that supabase.com/startups returns 404 with no application form. The official startup page (supabase.com/startups -> /solutions/startups) is marketing-only: 'Why startups choose Supabase', four value props, and a single 'Get started' CTA to the dashboard — no credit amount, no eligibility, no duration, no form. The partners page offers only listing/co-marketing/trust-signal perks, no credit or plan subsidy.
findings.eligibility: Unverified. Per aggregator descriptions (contradictory): early-stage company (pre-seed/seed/Series A), <5 years old, <~$5M raised, no funding required; some say apply via partner/accelerator or company-domain email. No authoritative eligibility criteria found on any official page.
findings.expiry: Unknown. Program status unclear — one source (Sep 2026) reports it discontinued/404; others treat it as ongoing. No defined term on any official page.
findings.gotchas: Do NOT rely on the '$2,500 credits' figure: it is unconfirmed and conflicts with 'six months of the Team plan free' and '$3,000 over 12 months'. The free tier is unaffected regardless of whether a startup program exists. No official application form was located.
findings.name: Supabase Startup credits program (reported by aggregators; not verifiable as an active public offer)
findings.source_url: https://supabase.com/solutions/startups (official: no program listed) ; https://guptadeepak.com/startup-offers/programs/supabase-startups (reports program discontinued)

sunset_notes:
STUDENT/EDUCATION LICENSE: none exists. supabase.com/education returns HTTP 404, and Supabase runs no student or academic discount. Its own pricing page has no student/education tier; the founders' original goal (2020 blog) of keeping free projects available for students/hobbyists is served by the standard Free Plan, with no application process. Students should plan around the Free Plan and email support only if a course deployment needs more.

STARTUP CREDITS PROGRAM: not verifiable as an active public offer. The official startup page (supabase.com/startups, now serving /solutions/startups) is marketing-only with no application form, credit amount, eligibility, or duration. At least one source (guptadeepak.com, Sep 2026) reports supabase.com/startups now 404s and the program is discontinued. Aggregators still circulate contradictory, unverifiable figures ($2,500 credits / six months of the Team plan free / $3,000 over 12 months). Treat any startup offer as partner-gated (Y Combinator / Techstars / sales) or sunset rather than a public sign-up.

TRIAL CREDITS: no native time-limited 'trial credits' program. The Free Plan is a perpetual free tier, not a trial. The only credit-style offers in the ecosystem are third-party partner perks, not Supabase's own — e.g., Mercury grants its business-account holders $300 in Supabase credits (new customers, separate conditions).

NET: the only distinct, verifiable free offer for students and startups is the standard Free Plan itself (finding #1, high confidence). No separate education license or reliable public startup-credits program could be confirmed on official pages this session.

Note on sourcing: the official pricing page was read directly this session (high confidence for Free Plan figures). The WebSearch budget was exhausted partway through the task, so current (2025-2026) change history for the startup program rests on aggregator claims (contradictory) plus a direct read of Supabase's own startup/partners pages showing no live program; those lower-confidence items are marked accordingly.

provider: Cloudflare (Free Plan) — CDN / Observability / Monitoring / Uptime fronts

findings.name: Cloudflare Free Plan (CDN + DDoS + DNS + basic WAF)
findings.detail: Perpetual $0/month free tier. Includes global CDN, always-on unlimited DDoS mitigation (no configuration), unlimited DNS zones/queries, TLS certificates, and basic WAF + Bot Fight Mode on the free tier. Runs on 100+ data centers across 330+ cities. Bundles the Workers Free compute tier and per-service free allowances (R2 10 GB, KV 1 GB, D1 5 GB, Durable Objects, Hyperdrive).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (students, startups, individuals, all regions). No .edu email, no age/funding cap. A credit card is NOT required: a Free account is created with just email + password.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up with email + password (no CC). 2) Add your domain via CNAME or point name servers to Cloudflare. 3) CDN + DDoS protection auto-activate for free.
findings.expiry: No expiry — active for the life of the account.
findings.gotchas: No CC needed to start, but adding a payment method unlocks paid products and any overage/egress beyond the free allowances is billed. Free plan has per-feature caps (e.g. Pages 500 builds/mo and 100 custom domains; 512 MB CDN cache).

findings.name: Cloudflare Workers Free Plan (Compute)
findings.detail: $0. 100,000 Worker invocations/day (resets 00:00 UTC), 10 ms CPU per request, up to 100 Workers, 64 MiB memory, 50 external + 1,000 Cloudflare-service subrequests per invocation. Free allowances also include KV 1 GB, R2 10 GB, D1 5 GB, Durable Objects, Hyperdrive 100k queries/day.
findings.eligibility: Anyone on a Free Cloudflare account.
findings.claim: Create a free account, then deploy a Worker with `npx wrangler deploy`. No credit card needed.
findings.expiry: Daily limits reset each day; plan is perpetual.
findings.gotchas: The task's 'known so far' figure of ~1M requests/day is OUTDATED — the official current free limit is 100,000/day. Hitting the cap returns Error 1027 unless you upgrade to Workers Paid ($5/mo min).

findings.name: Cloudflare Observability / Monitoring / Uptime free tier
findings.detail: Shared Observability free allowance of 0.5 GB/day ingestion + 7-day retention, pooling Traces, Workers Logs, Real User Monitoring (RUM), AI Gateway logs, R2 access logs, and Issues. Workers Logs free tier = 200,000 events/day (3-day retention). Cloudflare Radar and RUM are available on the Free plan for monitoring/uptime-style visibility.
findings.eligibility: Anyone on the Free plan; no CC or .edu required.
findings.claim: In the dashboard, enable Analytics & Logs / Real User Monitoring; free to ingest up to 0.5 GB/day.
findings.expiry: No expiry; daily ingestion resets at 00:00 UTC.
findings.gotchas: When the 0.5 GB/day cap is hit, ingestion stops until the reset. Scheduled change: from Dec 1, 2026, Workers Logs moves to Cloudflare Observability pricing — plan retention/limits may change after that date.

findings.name: Cloudflare Startup Program (up to $350,000 in credits)
findings.detail: 3 tiers (2026): Tier 3 = $10k (bootstrapped/self-funded, under $1M raised, no minimum funding); Tier 2 = $100k (under $5M raised, funded by an affiliated partner); Tier 1 = $350k ($5M+ raised, affiliated partner). Credits apply to usage-based services (Workers, KV, D1, Queues, Vectorize, R2 up to $10k, Workers AI up to $50k, Images, Stream, Argo, Cache Reserve). Included at NO COST on every tier: 3 enterprise domains, unlimited Business/Pro plans, DDoS + bot protection, WAF with 1,000 custom rules, CDN + DNS, load balancing, 100% SLA.
findings.eligibility: For-profit startup founded within the last 10 years, funded up to Series B within the last 12 months, actively building a tech product, with a public verifiable website, active on LinkedIn/X/GitHub, first-time applicant, and a business-domain email. Since Sep 2025, non-profit/civil-society/public-interest orgs are also eligible (up to $250k).
findings.claim: Apply at cloudflare.com/startups (form describing the product + team). You must create a Cloudflare account AND add a valid payment method on file (used to bill overages). Review takes up to ~48 hours; approval arrives by email.
findings.expiry: Credits valid for 1 year or until fully consumed, whichever is first. No extensions; upgrading within a cohort does not reset the 12-month window.
findings.gotchas: Unlike the plain Free plan, the Startup program REQUIRES a payment method on file. Product-specific caps: R2 up to $10k; Workers AI $2.5k (Tier 3)/$10k (Tier 2)/$50k (Tier 1); AI Gateway temporarily NOT covered. 'Funded up to Series B within last 12 months' means recently-fundraised startups only.

findings.name: Cloudflare Academy — free courses & certification (education license)
findings.detail: Self-paced, free online training curriculum plus free certification exams (e.g. Cloudflare Certified Associate). No .edu email, no student status, and no funding cap required — open to anyone. Educators can also run the material in classrooms; instructors can be supported through Cloudflare's instructor program.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (students, educators, self-learners, all regions).
findings.claim: Go to Cloudflare Academy, create a free account, and start any course for $0.
findings.expiry: Courses/certs do not expire; content updates over time.
findings.gotchas: Could not re-fetch the Academy page today (DNS resolution failure for academy.cloudflare.com from this environment), so the exact current course catalog/URL was not re-verified. The free/open/self-paced model and free-certification positioning are consistent with Cloudflare's learning/community pages but were not re-read on the live page.

findings.name: Cloudflare Ambassador & Community programs (student leaders)
findings.detail: The Cloudflare Community Ambassador program explicitly targets 'student leaders' (alongside community organizers and technical creators): run on-campus clubs, meetups, workshops, and content. Benefits include Cloudflare credits, marketing assets, swag, and access to Cloudflare experts; cohorts last 1 year with the option to reapply. A separate Community Engineer track provides discretionary grants for meaningful open-source work. Neither is a paid role.
findings.eligibility: Open application; non-technical enthusiasts welcome; student club leaders, community organizers, and open-source contributors.
findings.claim: Apply through cloudflare.com/community under the Ambassador (or Community Engineer) track.
findings.expiry: Cohort-based: 1-year Ambassador cohorts, reapply to continue; Community Engineer has no fixed term.
findings.gotchas: Credits/grants are discretionary (awards, not a flat entitlement) and cohort-based, not a guaranteed free tier like the Free plan.

sunset_notes: Material 2025–2026 changes: (1) Startup Program tier structure was revamped repeatedly: Sept 2024 revamp set the ceiling at $250k; April 2025 expanded to 4 tiers ($5k/$25k/$100k/$250k); by mid-2026 it was restructured into 3 tiers ($10k/$100k/$350k, per the current cloudflare.com/startups page and a May 2026 announcement). (2) Sep 2025: non-profit, civil-society, and public-interest organizations became eligible for the Startup program (up to $250k) — application window opened with a Dec 1 close for that cohort. (3) Eligibility window widened from 'founded within last 5 years' (2019–2024) to 'founded within last 10 years.' (4) Workers free-plan subrequest limit changed Feb 2026: now 50 external + 1,000 Cloudflare-service subrequests per invocation (previously a flat 1,000 total). (5) Workers Logs: effective Dec 1, 2026 it moves to Cloudflare Observability pricing (a near-term change affecting the free observability front). (6) Sep 2026: Free-account creation expanded so users can create up to 5 standalone Free accounts via dashboard or API. No traditional 'education license discount' or separate individual developer-credit grant exists at Cloudflare; the free value for students is the perpetual Free plan + free Academy + discretionary Ambassador/Community grants, and for startups the credits program.

findings.name: Hobby Free Plan (free tier)
findings.detail: Genuinely free, no credit card required. Per app: 50,000 monthly retained users (MRU), unlimited apps, up to 3 dashboard seats, up to 5 user impersonations/month, custom domain, fixed 7-day session lifetime, 1-day application-log retention. Machine-auth caps: API Keys 1,000 creations + 100,000 verifications/month; M2M Tokens 2,500 creations + 100,000 verifications/month. Social connections: up to 3. B2B base: 100 MROs/app + 20 members/org included free. NOT included on Hobby: SMS auth, passkeys, MFA, SSO, Directory Sync, simultaneous sessions, satellite domains, removal of Clerk branding.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone; no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card required, no region limit stated. This is the default free plan.
findings.claim: Sign up at clerk.com (GitHub/GitLab), pick the Hobby plan — it is the default free tier. No card. Create your app(s) immediately.
findings.gotchas: Exceeding 50,000 MRU (or 100 MRO without the B2B add-on) triggers a one-month grace period after which you must upgrade. Log retention is only 1 day on Hobby. 'No card required' — but the dev-instance trick (below) is what unlocks Pro features for free in development, not the Hobby plan itself.
findings.expiry: No end date; free plan is permanent/ongoing.

findings.name: Clerk Startup Program (startup discount/credits)
findings.detail: Pre-negotiated discount on paid (Pro/Business) pricing for eligible startups. The 50,000 MRU + 100 MRO free allowance is already part of base pricing; the startup discount is what unlocks paid Pro features (SMS codes, allowlist/blocklist, RBAC, custom session duration, device tracking & revocation, etc.). Exact discount percentage and credit amount are NOT disclosed on the page — 'pre-negotiated' only. Partner dropdown covers Stripe Atlas, Y Combinator, Techstars, a16z, South Park Commons, Seedcamp, Pioneer, Mercury, Hub71, LaunchHouse, OnDeck, PWV, S28, Mucker Capital, Forum Ventures, and many others, or 'None/Other'.
findings.eligibility: Company must be up to 1 year post-launch AND up to $5M in total venture funding. No region restriction stated. Requires an existing Clerk account (you must be signed in to apply). Not a student offer.
findings.claim: Sign in to Clerk, go to clerk.com/startups, fill Name / Company email / Company website / optional partner, and submit. You are prompted to 'create an application' if the account has none. The discount period starts only once your application is approved.
findings.gotchas: This is a discount, not a flat free grant — no dollar/percentage credit figure is published. The discount does not activate immediately; it starts at approval. No credit-card requirement is stated. No hard sunset/expiry date for the discount period is published. Eligibility window (1 year post-launch, <=$5M) is the practical cutoff.
findings.expiry: Eligibility: up to 1 year post-launch and up to $5M venture funding; no explicit end-date for the discount itself.

findings.name: Free Dev-Instance Trial of Pro features
findings.detail: Clerk has no time-boxed paid trial. Instead, ALL Pro-tier features are available for free inside the development instance of your application, so you can test full functionality without a paid subscription. Dashboard tags which features require an upgrade to run in production. This is the effective free 'trial' of premium capability.
findings.eligibility: Any user with a Clerk account (Hobby or paid). No .edu or startup requirement. Free in the dev environment only.
findings.claim: Create/use a dev instance via the SDK + dashboard, enable and exercise Pro features there. Switch to production requires a paid plan.
findings.gotchas: Dev-only: none of these Pro features are usable in a production app while on Hobby. Same pattern for Directory Sync — it is 'free in development instances' but production needs Pro/Business + the B2B Authentication add-on.
findings.expiry: Ongoing, tied to the dev instance; not a time-limited trial.

sunset_notes: No education/student license exists for Clerk: clerk.com/education returns HTTP 404, and no student or .edu offer appears on the pricing page. No 2025-2026 sunset or deprecation of the Hobby free tier or the Startup Program was found on the changelog (which surfaces ~April 2026 through October 2026 entries). The only forward-dated change noted is Directory Sync connection billing beginning January 1, 2027 (first connection still included per app on paid plans). Verification was done by fetching the official clerk.com/pricing, clerk.com/startups, and clerk.com/changelog pages today (2026-10-22). Note: this session's shared WebSearch budget (limit ~200 calls) was already exhausted, so the requested standalone '2025-2026 changes' web searches were NOT run; findings above rely on official pages fetched today plus the changelog range available.

provider: Auth0 (Okta) — fronts: Auth, Security, Product Analytics & Feature Flags

findings.name: Auth0 Free Plan (always-free tier)
findings.detail: $0/month, permanent. Up to 25,000 MAU; 1 tenant; 1 custom domain; 1 Enterprise Connection (added Feb 2026); Self-Service SSO and Inbound SCIM (added Feb 2026); unlimited Social Connections; unlimited Okta Connections (subject to system limitations); 5 Organizations on B2C, Unlimited* Organizations on B2B; 3 Admin/Contributor seats; 5 Actions + Forms; 1 Event Stream; 1,000 M2M tokens; 1-day log retention; 2 Token Vault slots; passwordless auth, passkeys, brand customization, Basic Attack Protection (brute force + suspicious IP throttling), community support, Inbound SCIM, Okta Universal Logout integration. No credit card needed to sign up. Sign up at https://auth0.com/signup (or dev.auth0.com/signup); the Free plan is the default subscription. Email Workflow is NOT available on Free. Exceeding 25,000 MAU triggers a quota warning; you cannot self-upgrade past the free cap without contacting sales.
findings.eligibility: Anyone globally — no .edu email, no startup proof, no funding or age cap. No credit card required for the free plan itself. Free tenants historically available in 5 regions (US, UK, EU, JP, AUS).
findings.claim: Sign up free at auth0.com/signup; the Free plan is automatic — no application, no card. Custom domain: add it in dashboard (a card is collected purely for verification and, per Auth0's FAQ, you are never charged).
findings.expiry: No expiry — free forever, as of 2026-10-22. Existing free tenants had entitlements auto-applied when the plan was upgraded (Sep 2024).
findings.gotchas: 1 tenant max on Free (one 'team' per team-owner email; a second team needs a different email). Credit-card verification required to add the 1 custom domain (verification only, never billed, per official FAQ). 1-day log retention, no email workflows, no log streaming, no Pro MFA, no Role Management/Account Linking, no CIBA — many 'everything in Free, plus' claims in the marketing copy don't change these exclusions. 25,000 is an MAU cap (users who authenticated in a calendar month), not a total-user cap. Unlimited* is 'subject to system limitations'.

findings.name: 22-day paid-features trial (auto-activated on new tenants)
findings.detail: New tenants automatically get a 'Starter Trial' subscription giving up to 22 days of paid-plan features (e.g., Pro MFA, higher API/feature limits) at $0, no credit card. When the 22 days elapse, the tenant automatically moves to the Free plan with no charge. Confirmed by Auth0 support/community staff (2023–2025) and by the Sept 2025 support article 'What Happens when the Auth0 Free Trial Expires'.
findings.eligibility: Any new tenant/creator; up to 3 tenants per free account before the trial/teams limits matter. No card, no .edu, no startup criteria.
findings.claim: Just create a tenant; the trial activates automatically. Do NOT create a tenant just for the trial if you want to stay clean — the trial lapses on its own into Free.
findings.expiry: 22 days per tenant from creation, then automatic drop to Free plan; tenant older than 22 days cannot re-trial paid features (per community guidance).
findings.gotchas: Trial-of-paid is distinct from the Free plan; paid features are locked after day 22 unless you subscribe. The pricing page itself does not advertise the 22-day trial, so treat exact day count as community-confirmed (21–22 days reported in different threads). No CC required for the trial itself (CC only if you later add a custom domain or subscribe).

findings.name: Auth0 for Startups program
findings.detail: 12 months of the B2B Professional plan free: up to 100,000 MAU, Enterprise MFA, unlimited* Organizations, 5 Enterprise Connections, 3 Third-Party APIs via Token Vault, Inbound SCIM. Trusted by 4,000+ startups. A partner channel exists (e.g., Mercury Perks) offering the same 12-month free B2B plan under looser-looking criteria (less than $5M raised and less than $1M ARR), for that bank's customers. After the 12 months, the company moves to self-service paid plans or Enterprise.
findings.eligibility: Venture-backed, less than $5M total funding, less than $1M annual recurring revenue, less than 2 years from incorporation. NOT valid for existing paid Auth0/Okta customers (enterprise or paid self-service) or companies that were previously in the program. No .edu path; no region limit stated on the official page (global program).
findings.claim: Apply at https://auth0.com/startups ('Apply now' routes to a Jira Service Desk portal, autheco.atlassian.net). Review takes days-to-weeks per third-party listings. Recommended path per Auth0: start on the Free plan during build, apply at launch. No card required for the free year.
findings.expiry: Fixed 12-month term per program; no second participation (prior members excluded); after expiry you migrate to standard paid pricing (B2B Essentials from $150/mo at 500 MAUs).
findings.gotchas: Must be VENTURE-backed — bootstrapped or solo startups under 2 years do not qualify (even though the 2020 version of the program was opened to 'anyone' meeting criteria). 100k MAU and 5 Enterprise Connections are hard caps for the free year. The program covers B2B Professional capabilities, not Enterprise plan tiers.

findings.name: Education / student offer: none (no .edu license or student discount)
findings.detail: Auth0 has no student plan, education license, or .edu-based discount. An Auth0 community manager confirmed in Dec 2024 that 'there aren't any special subscription plans for students; the best plan you could use would be the free plan.' The only education-adjacent free offering is Auth0 Learning (learning.auth0.com), relaunched Aug 2026 after splitting from Okta Learning (Feb 2025): free on-demand courses and skill badges, no sign-in required for content — free education content, not a product license. The Auth0 Ambassador Program is a volunteer/evangelism program (swag, travel for talks), not a free product tier, and is open to any developer, not students specifically.
findings.eligibility: N/A for a license — the Free plan's eligibility (anyone, no .edu) is what students actually use.
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim. Students should use the Free plan at auth0.com/signup and the free Auth0 Learning content.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Do not count on an .edu email unlocking anything at Auth0; any '.edu discount' claims circulating are unverified community anecdotes.

sunset_notes: No sunset of the Free plan or Auth0 for Startups found as of 2026-10-22 — both verified live on official pages today. Material 2025–2026 changes: (1) Feb 12, 2026 B2B plan overhaul (auth0.com/blog/auth0-b2b-plans-upgraded): Free plan gained 1 Enterprise Connection, Self-Service SSO, Inbound SCIM, and unlimited* Okta Enterprise Connections; Essentials gained a la carte add-ons (Enterprise Connections, Enterprise MFA, M2M Tokens). (2) Product Analytics and Feature Flags: their marketing pages (auth0.com/product-analytics, auth0.com/feature-flags) and docs sections all return 404 as of 2026-10-22, they are absent from the current pricing feature-comparison tables and from the site sitemaps; both were historically offered with ~30-day free trials (pre-2025), so any current Product Analytics/Feature Flags free trial appears to have been pulled or absorbed into the Okta-branded Auth0 portfolio and cannot be confirmed — treat as effectively sunset/renamed, confidence low. (3) Aug 2026: Auth0 Learning relaunched as a separate free-learning platform after Okta Learning (Feb 2025) split. Context for the free tier's history: Sep 24, 2024 upgrade raised the free cap from 7,500 to 25,000 MAU and added 1 custom domain, unlimited social/Okta connections and passwordless; Nov 2023 set 7,500 MAU (from 7,000). Startup funding cap was raised from $2M to $5M in Nov 2022 and remains in effect today. No credit-card requirement on sign-up, the 22-day trial, or the free startup year; card collection on Free is limited to custom-domain verification (never billed).

provider: WorkOS (AuthKit / User Management, Security (SSO/Directory Sync/Audit Logs), Radar)

findings.name: User Management / AuthKit free tier: first 1,000,000 MAU free
findings.detail: Official free tier covering the entire AuthKit/User Management platform (sign-up, sign-in, social/email login, MFA, RBAC, passkeys, admin portal): first 1,000,000 MAUs at $0/mo. Beyond that: $2,500/mo per additional 1M MAU. No time limit, no expiry stated on the official page. Staging environments are free (only production billed); Standard support (email, in-product web, API status notifications, private Slack channel) included at no cost. MAU = any user performing an action (sign up/in, profile update) in a calendar month.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (companies, individual developers, students) via self-serve sign-up at dashboard.workos.com; no application, no eligibility criteria, no .edu or funding requirements. No credit-card requirement is stated anywhere on the official pricing pages (neither confirming nor denying CC-free sign-up).
findings.claim: Self-serve: create a WorkOS account (no approval step), integrate AuthKit/User Management, and use it free up to 1M MAU. Staging is free for unlimited testing; production billing starts only past the free cap.
findings.expiry: Permanent / rolling — the 1M MAU free cap has no published end date or renewal mechanism. Overage pricing is pay-as-you-go; Annual Credits plan is a custom sales arrangement (prepay discounts, 99.99% SLA).
findings.gotchas: Free tier does NOT cover enterprise add-ons: SSO and Directory Sync are priced per connection ($125/each for 1-15 connections, tiered down to $65 at 51-100, custom beyond 100); Audit Logs stream $125/mo per SIEM connection + $99/mo per 1M events retention; Custom Domain $99/mo. MAU counts end-user activity, not your team seats — a large consumer app can hit 1M MAU and then pay $2,500/mo per extra million. Third-party directories (guptadeepak.com, startups.ws) note some directory listings mention payment-method rules generically, but WorkOS's own pages state no CC requirement — unverified officially either way.

findings.name: Startup program (WorkOS for Startups)
findings.detail: workos.com/startups exists, but it is a marketing landing page for the same 1M-MAU free tier, not a distinct startup program: 'User Management is free up to 1M MAUs', connections-based pricing for SSO/SCIM, 'from launch day to IPO and beyond'. No application form, no equity/data terms, no funding or age caps, no duration or expiry stated, no separate credit pool. Third-party directories (startups.ws, verified 2026-10-21; guptadeepak.com, Oct 2026) corroborate: free to join, no formal eligibility, worldwide, rolling.
findings.eligibility: Effectively open to any startup (and any company); no published gate on company age, funding stage, revenue, or geography. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: No application needed: sign up self-serve, integrate AuthKit/User Management, use free up to 1M MAU. Optional: contact sales for SSO/Directory Sync enterprise deals or Annual Credits discounts.
findings.expiry: No program duration or sunset date published; the underlying free tier has no published expiry.
findings.gotchas: Do not treat as a time-boxed startup perk — it is the same permanent free tier rebranded for startups. SSO/SCIM (what startups usually need when selling enterprise) is NOT free: $125/connection/mo at low volume. No startup-specific discount is published on the official page; enterprise discounts are sales-negotiated. No credit-card requirement is stated on the page.

findings.name: Radar free tier: first 1,000 checks free
findings.detail: Radar (bot/fraud/abuse detection): first 1,000 checks per month free; $100/mo per additional 50,000 checks. Part of the same pay-as-you-go model; available standalone.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone via self-serve WorkOS account; no startup/education gate.
findings.claim: Same self-serve signup as User Management; Radar usage starts free up to 1,000 checks/mo.
findings.expiry: Rolling monthly allowance, no published end date.
findings.gotchas: Checks beyond the first 1,000 are billed in 50k increments at $100/mo; not a trial — recurring usage pricing. (Radar is bot protection, not a product-analytics/feature-flags offering; WorkOS publishes no free offer for product analytics or feature flags.)

findings.name: Free staging environments + free Standard support
findings.detail: WorkOS explicitly: staging environments are free for testing; only production is billed. Standard support tier (email, in-product web support, API status notifications, private Slack) is included at no cost. Useful for students/developers: full sandbox access at $0.
findings.eligibility: Any account holder; no gate.
findings.claim: Automatic: staging environment of your project is $0; Standard support included with any plan tier.
findings.expiry: Ongoing, part of standard pricing; no expiry.
findings.gotchas: Standard support P1/P2 response SLAs are weaker than paid add-ons (Scale support $1,000/mo adds video calls, 1-business-hour P1; Enterprise is custom with 24x7 SLAs).

sunset_notes: No student/education license exists at WorkOS: workos.com/education returns 404, no education/student/trial URL appears in the official sitemap (sitemap_website.xml), and the footer only offers /startups and /pricing. No free trial credits or sign-up credit pool are documented on any official WorkOS page; the 'startup program' is not a formal program with an application — it is the permanent 1M-MAU free tier marketed to startups. No 2025-2026 sunset of a student/education or startup-credit offer was found: the official changelog (entries Aug 2025 - Oct 2026) contains no pricing/free-tier/trial changes. Caveat: third-party web search was exhausted mid-task in this session, so I could not search for historical/sunset announcements (e.g., a past YC or academic partnership); verification relied on today's official pages (pricing, startups, radar, sitemap, changelog) plus third-party directories corroborating the current state (startups.ws checked 2026-10-21; guptadeepak.com Oct 2026).

findings.name: 14-day free trial of all LogRocket features, no credit card
findings.detail: Official pricing page states: "Start free trial — no credit card required" and "Access all of LogRocket's features free for 14 days. Cancel any time." The trial covers all features across Core/Pro plans: session replay, product analytics, error monitoring, logs (analytics/error/log events are unlimited on every plan); price after trial starts at $176/mo (annual-basis, at the 25K sessions/mo default slider) or ~$860/mo with Conditional Recording. Final price also depends on seats, retention, and add-ons. Verified directly at logrocket.com/pricing on 2026-10-22.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no student/startup status, .edu email, funding cap, or region limit published. No credit card required to start.
findings.claim: Go to logrocket.com/pricing -> click "Start free trial" -> create account (no credit card) -> add LogRocket SDK to your app; trial of paid plans begins. Sales line (855) 564-7625 for questions.
findings.expiry: 14 days from signup; "Cancel any time"; no published renewal — re-signup after trial converts to a paid Core/Pro/Enterprise plan (contact-sales billing).
findings.gotchas: Trial is time-boxed, not a free tier: the perpetual Free plan (1,000 sessions/mo, 1-month retention, 3 seats) was killed in mid-2026, so nothing is free forever. No CC on file means no auto-convert, but continued use past day 14 requires a sales-negotiated paid contract. Pro plan bundles 500 free API/MCP credits/mo and Enterprise 2,000/mo — but only on paid plans.

findings.name: Startup discount for companies under $50M funding (sales-negotiated, not free)
findings.detail: The official pricing page's "Want a discount?" section lists "Startups under $50M funding" as a discount-eligible category (alongside bulk volume, non-profits, open-source projects, multi-year contracts, case-study partners, and students). No fixed discount percentage or credit amount is published — LogRocketCreds/StartupCreds confirm there is no dedicated apply URL: logrocket.com/startups returns HTTP 404 (verified today). Third-party trackers (StartupPerks, innovarastudios) describe it as: any startup (seed/Series A/B+ or bootstrapped) with <$50M total raised, global eligibility, no VC/accelerator backing required; benefit is a custom discount that persists "while eligible".
findings.eligibility: Startups with less than $50M total funding raised (per official page). Bootstrapped founders reportedly eligible. No accelerator/VC requirement. Company email on own domain (per StartupPerks).
findings.claim: No self-serve application (logrocket.com/startups is 404). Contact sales via live chat on logrocket.com/pricing or phone (855) 564-7625, and verify funding stage; third-party trackers say approval is sales-mediated.
findings.expiry: No published end date; discount persists while the company stays under the $50M funding threshold.
findings.gotchas: This is a discount, NOT a free offer — nothing is free. Discount size is unpublished and negotiated by deal size ("The bigger the deal, the more there is to talk about"). A separate channel deal (Ramp partner program) reportedly offers 20% off the first year via application. Eligibility is claimed on the official page but mechanics are third-party-sourced (medium confidence).

findings.name: Student discount via sales (no .edu education license exists)
findings.detail: "Students" is listed on the official pricing page among discount-eligible categories, same as startups/non-profits/OSS. There is no student-free license or education program: logrocket.com/education returns HTTP 404 (verified today), logrocket.com/free-accounts also 404, and no .edu-verified free tier exists or was offered. LogRocket does not appear in student-perk directories (StudentPerks, GitHub Student Pack, etc.) as of 2025-2026.
findings.eligibility: Students per official category list; no published .edu email requirement or self-serve verification — discount is negotiated through sales.
findings.claim: Contact LogRocket sales (live chat on logrocket.com/pricing or (855) 564-7625) and request the student discount; there is no dedicated application page.
findings.expiry: No published end date; presumably valid while student status holds (unverified).
findings.gotchas: Discount, not free. No amount published. Students get no standalone free account — the only time-limited free access is the 14-day trial. Third-party "free for students" lists do not include LogRocket.

findings.name: Third-party $500 LogRocket credits for startups via SaaSOffers (not a LogRocket program)
findings.detail: SaaSOffers lists a "$500 in credits" deal for LogRocket session replay + error tracking, labeled "Verified October 2026" and targeting startups debugging user experience. The deal is brokered by SaaSOffers, not run by LogRocket: claiming requires a SaaSOffers account with their premium tier ($79/yr, per the deal page), and the page publishes no funding cap, credit expiry, or redemption mechanics. Treated as a trial-credit adjacent channel only.
findings.eligibility: Per SaaSOffers listing: startups (early-stage, growing SaaS teams, solo founders); sole stated requirement is "startup debugging user experience." No funding cap published.
findings.claim: Create SaaSOffers account -> upgrade to SaaSOffers premium ($79/yr) -> click Claim Deal on the LogRocket page -> follow activation steps.
findings.expiry: No expiry published; deal re-verified Oct 2026; access gated behind SaaSOffers premium subscription.
findings.gotchas: Effectively not free: the $79/yr premium gate must be paid to access the $500 credits. It is third-party-sourced; LogRocket's own site publishes no such credit offer. Also, SaaSOffers' sibling page still quotes an old plan structure (Free 1K sessions, Team $99, Professional $295) that no longer matches LogRocket's current page — verify before relying on it.

sunset_notes: LogRocket's one perpetual free offer is GONE. The Free plan — \"$0/mo free forever, 1,000 sessions/month, 1-month data retention, 3 seats, unlimited analytics/error/log events\" (plan history: Free/Team/Professional/Enterprise with Free + Team $69 + Professional $295, per trackers' captures through May 2026) — was removed when LogRocket repriced to session-based Core/Pro/Enterprise pricing. Removal window per independent trackers: PricingSaaS records the Free tier killed between its 2026-06-29 and 2026-07-06 captures (\"Logrocket kills free plan, quadruples Enterprise API credits to 2,000/mo\"); AgentDeals discovered it between 2026-06-08 and 2026-08-19 captures; stackwrite's 2026-10-03 re-check confirms \"LogRocket's free plan, which no longer exists at all.\" As of 2026-10-22 the official pricing page lists no free tier at all — only the 14-day trial. Trial packaging also churned in 2025-2026: Q1 2025 \"Free PoC\" became fixed \"21-Day Trial/Pilot\" for Professional/Enterprise; by the 2025-07-06 capture it was reworded to duration-less \"Free Trial/Free Pilot\"; the current page (verified today) says 14 days, no credit card required. Dedicated program URLs are dead: logrocket.com/startups = 404, logrocket.com/education = 404, logrocket.com/free-accounts = 404 (all checked 2026-10-22). Caveat: stale third-party listings still advertise the dead free tier — GitHub Marketplace shows \"Free 1,000 sessions/month\", G2 lists entry price \"Free, 1000 Sessions/Month\", and DriftingDesk lists a \"1,000 Free Sessions\" program \"Verified Active 2026\"; all contradict the official page and should be treated as outdated. Paid-plan perks that changed alongside: Pro API/MCP credits 200->500/mo and Enterprise 200->2,000/mo (July 2026).

provider: Keycloak (self-hosted) — fronts: Auth, Security, Product Analytics & Feature Flags

findings.name: Self-hosted Keycloak Community (free tier equivalent)
findings.detail: Latest server release 26.8.1 (as of 2026-10-22) plus JS adapter 26.2.4 / Node adapter 26.1.1 / client libs 26.0.12 are free downloads from GitHub releases, no paywall, no MAU/user-count limits, no feature gating. License verified today: single unmodified Apache-2.0 (no dual license, no enterprise addendum). Project is a CNCF incubation project (accepted 2023-04-10, Incubating maturity; ~12,699 contributors per CNCF/LFX). keycloak.org is now Linux Foundation-branded (© The Linux Foundation 2026) with zero mention of Red Hat or any commercial SKU. The offer is perpetual open source, not a time-boxed trial.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, anywhere — no .edu email, no credit card, no account, no region limits, no funding-cap rules. Only requirement is your own infrastructure: a server/container/DB to host it (you pay for compute/storage, not for Keycloak).
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://www.keycloak.org/downloads and pick the ZIP or TAR.GZ of the 26.x server (links straight to GitHub releases); 2) run it bare-metal, via Docker/Kubernetes, or with the official container image; 3) no signup, no license key, no billing. For clients, use the JS adapter 26.2.4 or client libraries 26.0.12.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal — perpetual Apache-2.0 license with ongoing releases. Watch out: Node.js client adapter is explicitly tagged DEPRECATED on the download page, and older releases are moved to 'Archived releases' (EOL, security unbacked).
findings.gotchas: Cost shifts to infrastructure (VM/container, Postgres/DB, load balancers for HA) — no egress fees from Keycloak itself but your cloud bill applies. No support/SLA. Enterprise-grade features/support are sold separately by Red Hat as a commercial offering, which keycloak.org no longer surfaces at all (no trial, no free credits, no free tier of the commercial product). Trial-vs-free: this is genuinely free, not a trial.

findings.name: Absence of trial-credit / startup / education offers
findings.detail: Verified today against the official site: keycloak.org has no pricing page, no trial, no startup program, no education license, no student credits, and no free-tier of a commercial offering anywhere in its navigation (only Guides, Docs, Downloads, Community, Blog). The CNCF project page likewise lists no credits or sponsored tiers. So there is nothing to claim besides self-hosting the community edition; there is no paid 'commercial Keycloak' free trial discoverable from official channels.
findings.eligibility: N/A — documents that no eligibility criteria exist because no program exists.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. The only free path is self-hosting the Apache-2.0 community edition (see finding 1).
findings.expiry: Not applicable.
findings.gotchas: Absence verified from official keycloak.org + CNCF pages only; this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so a Red Hat commercial trial offered purely on redhat.com cannot be positively ruled out — but no such offer appears on any official Keycloak channel today.

sunset_notes: No student/trial/startup program was ever found to have been sunset — Keycloak has had no such programs; the only free offer is self-hosting the Apache-2.0 community edition. Material 2025–2026 changes: (1) keycloak.org is now fully CNCF/Linux Foundation-branded ("Keycloak is a Cloud Native Computing Foundation incubation project," © The Linux Foundation 2026) — Red Hat branding and any enterprise/commercial offering have disappeared from the official site; CNCF lists Keycloak as Incubating (accepted 2023-04-10). (2) License is still single Apache-2.0 with no dual/enterprise clause (verified in the repo today), so the "enterprise features paid via Red Hat" framing from the snapshot now applies only to Red Hat's own commercial channels, not keycloak.org. (3) Node.js client adapter is deprecated; older server releases are archived/EOL. (4) Verification caveat: WebSearch budget exhausted mid-task, so these are from WebFetch of keycloak.org, GitHub raw LICENSE.txt, and the CNCF project page only.

provider: Datadog (Observability / Monitoring / Uptime & CDN fronts; all pages read 2026-10-22)

findings.name: Infrastructure Free Plan (permanent free tier, Monitoring front)
findings.detail: $0/month free tier of Infrastructure Monitoring: up to 5 hosts, 1-day metric retention, unlimited users, unlimited alerts, 5 containers per host, 100 custom metrics per host, 500 custom events per host, 1,000+ integrations; includes dashboards, host/container maps, SAML SSO, outlier/anomaly detection, Watchdog insights. Shown on the main pricing page as Infrastructure 'Free' plan: 'Starting At $0', 'Up to 5 hosts', '1-day metric retention'.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; self-service account creation, no credit card required. Data-housing region chosen at signup and cannot be migrated later.
findings.claim: Sign up at datadoghq.com (Start free trial / Get started free flow), install the Datadog Agent on up to 5 hosts; account lands on the Free plan at no cost.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; no sunset. 1-day retention and per-host allotments are the standing caps.
findings.gotchas: Not the 14-day trial: the free plan is separate and permanent. 1-day metric retention vs 15 months on paid/student accounts; no public free allowance for Uptime/Synthetics quotas appears on the current pricing page; exceeding allotments (hosts, custom metrics/events, containers) requires a paid plan; 'unlimited users' but agents on the 5 free hosts only.

findings.name: 14-day free trial of the full Datadog platform
findings.detail: 14 days of 'unlimited monitoring' of the entire Datadog platform (metrics, traces, logs, 1,000+ integrations, alerting incl. anomaly/outlier/forecast). 'No credit card required' (stated repeatedly). Signup requires a business email; form collects password, name, job title, company, optional phone, and data-housing region.
findings.eligibility: Open to all companies (the DDFS FAQ says the 2-week trial is 'available to all companies'); business email expected; no credit card; no startup/student restriction.
findings.claim: Go to datadoghq.com/free-datadog-trial/, complete the signup form, agent installs and trial is active immediately; DDFS applicants are explicitly told to sign up for the trial while their startup application is under review.
findings.expiry: 14 days; no auto-conversion or renewal terms are published on the page; after expiry the account is on the paid plan or the free plan.
findings.gotchas: Trial is NOT the free plan and cannot be converted into the student program ('We cannot transition users, agents, hosts, or metrics' per the student program). Region choice at signup is not migratable. Startup-program applicants use this same trial as their pre-approval onboarding.

findings.name: Datadog for Startups (DDFS) - up to $100k credits, one year
findings.detail: 'A year of Datadog Pro, up to $100k in credits' for the first year; covers the complete platform - 'all Generally Available (GA) products' plus new features that GA, with preview products usable 'if space permits' (no watered-down tiers). Acceptance email typically within 3-5 business days. Credits applied to the account after approval.
findings.eligibility: Series A or earlier (no dollar funding cap published); must be new to Datadog (no current or prior Datadog customer, never received DDFS credits); must apply through an official referral partner (VCs, hyperscaler and vendor partner startup programs) - no direct application without a referral.
findings.claim: 1) Submit application at datadoghq.com/partner/datadog-for-startups/ (startup email: startups@datadoghq.com); 2) Sign up for a Datadog trial and use it while the application is reviewed; 3) Receive acceptance by email (3-5 business days); 4) Credits are applied - 'start building'. Activation must be confirmed within 30 days of acceptance or the acceptance expires (may reapply later if eligible).
findings.expiry: Credits for the first year only; no renewal route stated. Inactivity: a warning is sent after 3 months unused, and after another 30 days without use the company is removed from the program.
findings.gotchas: No referral partner = ineligible; the fallback is the 14-day trial. Excludes anyone who was ever a Datadog customer or prior DDFS recipient. No credit card/ payment details appear in the application flow. The 30-day activation window and inactivity removal are the main traps.

findings.name: Student Developer program (education license via GitHub Student Developer Pack)
findings.detail: Free Datadog Pro account with a monthly allocation: 10 hosts (Infrastructure and APM), 500 GB ingested logs, 50 containers, 10 lambda functions, 5 Fargate tasks, 1,000 browser tests, 10,000 API tests, 1,000 Browser RUM sessions, 1,000 Mobile RUM sessions, 100,000 LLM requests; standard and custom metric retention up to 15 months; alerts, users, and Datadog Support access included. 'Free Datadog up to 2 years', available while the participant remains an active GitHub Student Developer Pack member; Datadog will renew the account as long as pack membership continues.
findings.eligibility: Currently enrolled students who are members of the GitHub Student Developer Pack (GitHub handles enrollment verification - .edu email/student ID on GitHub's side; Datadog's own page does not impose a separate .edu requirement). Not for commercial projects. All accounts are created in the US5 region only.
findings.claim: 1) Log in with GitHub at studentpack.datadoghq.com ('Log in to Github to get started'); 2) the account is auto-provisioned in the US5 region; 3) log in at us5.datadoghq.com and configure your Datadog Agent with the issued API keys. Faculty/curriculum access: studentpack@datadoghq.com.
findings.expiry: Up to 2 years, renewable while enrolled in the GitHub Student Developer Pack; if a term lapses Datadog will extend/renew active pack members.
findings.gotchas: US5 region only - student accounts cannot be migrated to another region. Cannot be created by converting an existing free-trial account. A temporary 'staff user' is created for provisioning and disabled after the invite. Commercial use is prohibited. LLM/RUM/browser quotas are monthly, not one-off.

findings.name: Agent Observability Free tier (Observability front)
findings.detail: Free tier of Agent Observability: '$0 per month', up to 40K LLM spans/month, 15-day trace retention, unlimited context & evals, full feature access; targeted at 'individuals and small teams'. Also on the main pricing page: Feature Flags are free for usage below 1 million monthly flag configuration requests (no plan purchase needed for sub-1M MFCRs).
findings.eligibility: Anyone - no plan purchase, no startup/student requirement; a Datadog account (trial or free) is enough.
findings.claim: Sign up at datadoghq.com; Agent Observability 'is already available in your account and free to start using' - no separate application.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; monthly 40K LLM span cap and 15-day trace retention are the standing limits.
findings.gotchas: 15-day trace retention vs 15 months on paid/student accounts; 40K LLM span/month cap; this is per-user/small-team oriented - startup teams usually get far more via DDFS or the 14-day trial.

findings.name: Time-limited promo: Bits Testing free through Nov 30 (AI credits, Observability front)
findings.detail: On the current pricing page, 'Bits Testing' (AI-powered autonomous test generation inside Synthetic Monitoring) is listed as 'Free of charge through Nov 30' (2026). A free in-browser trial of Bits Testing also exists at bits-testing.datadoghq.com ('Try free in browser').
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Datadog account; not student/startup-specific.
findings.claim: No application; use Bits Testing in a Synthetics workflow; in-browser demo requires no account at all.
findings.expiry: Promotion ends Nov 30 (page language 'through Nov 30'); after that Bits Testing reverts to AI-credits-based pricing.
findings.gotchas: Short-dated promo - verify the exact Nov 30 year (page fetched 2026-10-22, so Nov 30, 2026). Not part of any student/startup program; counts against AI credits after the promo ends.

findings.name: No distinct public free Uptime Monitoring or CDN offer found (Uptime & CDN front)
findings.detail: Uptime Monitoring is now folded into Synthetic Monitoring under Digital Experience: the Synthetic Monitoring product page states 'Usage-based pricing per test run, with no per-user fees' and no public free endpoint/check-per-minute quotas or free test types are published on any current Datadog page I read today. The RUM page advertises only the 14-day trial. There is no Datadog CDN product in the current product index, Digital Experience pages, or docs navigation - Datadog's 'edge' offering is Edge Device Monitoring (IoT), which has no free tier.
findings.eligibility: n/a - nothing to claim; the front has no standalone free offer as of 2026-10-22.
findings.claim: n/a
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Absence of published free uptime quotas may partly reflect client-side-rendered pricing; legacy pages historically showed a free uptime endpoint allowance on the Infrastructure Free plan, which is no longer displayed. If you need free uptime, the practical options are the 14-day trial (unlimited) or the 5-host Free plan, but no free uptime endpoint count is publicly stated today.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 status: All four core offers remain active with no sunsets found today (2026-10-22). (1) DDFS (Datadog for Startups) still runs at "a year of Datadog Pro, up to $100k in credits", Series A-or-earlier + partner-referral-only, with new guardrails visible in the FAQ: activation must occur within 30 days of acceptance; inactivity warning after 3 months and removal 30 days later; non-eligible companies are pointed to the 2-week trial. (2) The Student Developer program (education license) is live at studentpack.datadoghq.com - free Pro account via GitHub Student Developer Pack, up to 2 years renewable while enrolled; allocations have grown over time (now includes LLM requests, RUM sessions, API tests) and are US5-region-only with a no-commercial-use rule; no changes found. (3) The Infrastructure Free plan (5 hosts, 1-day retention, unlimited users) and the 14-day no-credit-card trial are unchanged and remain separate products - the trial has not merged into the free plan. (4) Uptime & CDN front: no standalone free Uptime Monitoring quotas are published anywhere on current pages, and Datadog has no CDN product at all - so there is nothing there to sunset; a free endpoint allowance for uptime that appeared on older pricing pages is no longer displayed. (5) One genuinely time-limited 2026 item: the Bits Testing promo, free only "through Nov 30", which is a sunset risk for the next research pass. Note: web-search budget for this session was exhausted early; all high-confidence findings come from direct WebFetch reads of datadoghq.com / studentpack.datadoghq.com today.

findings.claim: Create a free Atlassian Cloud account (https://www.atlassian.com/try/cloud/signup?bundle=statuspage — the exact 'Get started today' link on the free-plan tab of the pricing page). Choose the Free plan; no application, no invoice. Free for all users (students and startups alike), not gated to either group.
findings.detail: Statuspage now ships under Atlassian (statuspage.io 301-redirects to atlassian.com/software/statuspage). Confirmed today on atlassian.com/software/statuspage and /software/statuspage/pricing: a Free plan exists. Exact free limits: 1 public status page, 100 subscribers, 25 components, 2 team members, 2 metrics, email + Slack + Microsoft Teams notifications, REST API access, page analytics, scheduled maintenance, incident templates, status embed, activity log, basic customization (Statuspage branding shown). Paid-only: custom domain, white-label/branding removal, uptime monitoring checks, SMS/webhook notifications, private pages, RBAC, extra metrics. Public plans: Hobby $29/mo (250 subs, 5 team, 5 metrics, custom domain), Startup $99/mo (1,000 subs, 10 team, SMS/webhook, custom CSS), Business $399/mo (5,000 subs, 25 team, custom CSS/HTML/JS, RBAC), Enterprise $1,499/mo (25,000 subs). Private-page plans from $79/mo; audience-specific pages from $300/mo. No credit card mentioned for the free tier; paid plans note 'No minimum contracts, no sign-up fees, no cancellation fees' and can be billed yearly via signed order form.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone — no .edu email, no startup age/funding condition, no region limit stated on the official pages. Credit card not stated as required for the free plan (standard Atlassian Cloud free signup).
findings.expiry: Free forever; no trial end, no renewal step.
findings.gotchas: 1-status-page cap on the free tier (single public page; multiple pages/private pages are paid). Uptime/monitoring checks are NOT in the free tier — free is page-subscription only; monitoring requires a paid plan. The paid plan literally named 'Startup' ($99/mo) is a price tier, not a startup discount — easy to confuse. Free-tier pages keep Statuspage/Atlassian branding (white-label is paid). If you later add paid apps, everything bills through the Atlassian Cloud bill (unified billing).
findings.name: Statuspage Free Plan (free forever public status page)

findings.claim: Apply at https://www.atlassian.com/software/startups ('Get it free' CTA); Atlassian reviews every application and may request proof of funding (e.g., Crunchbase/Pitchbook profile). VCs, incubators and accelerators share the offer with portfolio companies by emailing startups@atlassian.com.
findings.detail: Atlassian's official startup program (Atlassian for Startups) — free for 12 months for up to 50 users, 'Premium edition of our products for $0'. Confirmed today on atlassian.com/software/startups which products: Jira Premium (50 seats), Confluence Premium (50), Bitbucket Premium (50), Loom Business + AI (50), Jira Service Management & Customer Service Management (10 seats), Jira Product Discovery Premium (10 creator seats + unlimited contributors). Jira Product Discovery is the exception to the 50-seat cap. Statuspage is NOT listed as a covered product, and the FAQ adds 'The list of products may be modified over time.' Marketplace apps excluded. Governed by Atlassian Customer Agreement Section 17 as 'Free or Beta Products'.
findings.eligibility: ALL three criteria: (1) not an existing Atlassian paid customer; (2) VC funded OR associated with a partner accelerator/incubator; (3) has not raised more than US$10M in external funding. Bootstrapped startups without VC/accelerator association are NOT eligible.
findings.expiry: Ongoing program; each eligible startup enrolls for ONE 12-month period. Before the 12 months end you can renew or cancel any included product; going past 50 users (or 10 for the service-collection apps) requires a paid upgrade/quote.
findings.gotchas: Bootstrapped, no-VC startups fail criterion 2 — the most common disqualifier. Covers Atlassian Premium editions of core apps only: Statuspage / Statuspage Monitoring are not in the product list you get, so a startup using Statuspage under this program would still pay Statuspage pricing (or rely on the Statuspage Free Plan). 'Startup' as a Statuspage $99/mo plan name is unrelated to this program. After 12 months the apps are not automatically downgraded — you renew or cancel explicitly.
findings.name: Atlassian for Startups — 12 months of Atlassian Premium products at $0 (up to 50 users) — does NOT cover Statuspage

findings.claim: Fill out the application at https://www.atlassian.com/solutions/survey/classroom-license-request (the page's survey form). The official page does not publish seat caps, terms or product coverage beyond the one-line classroom designation — terms come back from Atlassian after review.
findings.detail: Atlassian's education offer: 'Classroom Licenses are designated for use by students & teachers within a classroom setting. Fill out our application form today!' — the only public education program I could confirm today (found via Atlassian's sitemap; atlassian.com/teams/education and /education are 404). The page is a survey/application form; no published eligibility numbers, .edu-verification text, or duration appear on the page. No mention of Statuspage anywhere on the classroom-licenses page (Statuspage appears in the site navigation only).
findings.eligibility: Students and teachers in a classroom/educational setting; application-based (institution/school context implied by the form). No .edu requirement or regional limit stated on the page. Effectively aimed at K-12/higher-ed classrooms, not for students as individuals or for startups.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page (form-based; Atlassian reviews and responds).
findings.gotchas: This is Atlassian's general classroom-license program for its core apps — the page contains zero Statuspage references, so assume Statuspage pages are NOT covered; verifying actual coverage requires submitting the form. A page found via the sitemap only — the main education marketing pages (404) suggest this offer is low-visibility and possibly legacy.
findings.name: Atlassian Classroom Licenses (education license for students & teachers)

findings.claim: No claim path: no trial-credits offer, no student pricing, no trial CTA on the current pricing page. Paid plans are bought through the Atlassian Cloud bill (annual billing via signed order form, per the pricing-page FAQ).
findings.detail: As of today, atlassian.com/software/statuspage/pricing shows no free trial of the paid tiers (Hobby $29 / Startup $99 / Business $399 / Enterprise $1,499 public; Starter $79 / Growth $249 / Corporate $599 private), no trial-credit or education-price blocks, and no '14-day trial' of monitoring. The only 'credit card' mention is the FAQ 'Do you offer yearly credit card billing?' (yes, manual via signed order form). Web search was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so absence-of-trial reflects the official pages read today, not a search of reseller/marketplace promos.
findings.eligibility: N/A
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse the Statuspage 'Startup' plan ($99/mo) with a startup program, and do not assume the free 12-month Atlassian-for-Startups premium entitlement applies to Statuspage (it does not list Statuspage). Atlassian Cloud signups do not require a credit card, but paid Statuspage tiers do add recurring charges to the Atlassian bill.
findings.name: No trial credits / student pricing / monitoring trial found for Statuspage paid tiers

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes confirmed today: (1) statuspage.io and statuspage.io/pricing now 301-redirect to atlassian.com/software/statuspage — the standalone Statuspage domain, pricing page and legacy product site are retired; the product is fully absorbed into Atlassian's cloud offering (acquisition completed 2023). (2) docs.statuspage.io redirects to an /inactive page — the old documentation hub is sunset; docs now live at support.atlassian.com/statuspage. (3) atlassian.com/ondemand (the former OnDemand/monitoring marketing home) now redirects to /software. (4) atlassian.com/teams/education, /education and /training/teaching all 404 — the old education program pages are gone; only the sitemap-listed classroom-license-request form remains as the education offer. (5) Atlassian for Startups' covered product list has shifted over time (now Jira/Confluence/Bitbucket Premium, Loom Business+AI, JSM & Customer Service Management, Jira Product Discovery — Opsgenie no longer listed); the page (dateModified 2026-10-21) warns 'The list of products may be modified over time', and Statuspage has not been a covered product.

provider: Plausible (self-hosted) — privacy-friendly web analytics (open-source AGPL community edition + hosted Plausible Cloud)

findings.name: 30-Day Free Trial (no credit card)
findings.detail: Free 30-day trial of Plausible Cloud. During the trial you get access to ALL Business-plan features and limits (funnels, user journeys, revenue tracking, custom properties, Stats API, Data Studio). No credit card required to start. Not a permanent free tier: at the end of the trial you must pick a paid plan (from ~$9/mo Starter / ~€9 per site at 10k pageviews) to keep the data. The pageview tier you land on is chosen from your last 30 days of billable usage.
findings.eligibility: Universal — open to anyone (students, startups, general). No .edu email required, no startup-age or funding cap, no region limit stated. Credit card NOT required to start.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at plausible.io -> a 30-day trial starts automatically, no card. 2) Install the tracking snippet and run real traffic. 3) Check usage near the end of the 30 days. 4) Choose a paid plan at trial end to continue (or don't and lose access).
findings.gotchas: This is a TRIAL, not a free-forever tier. Auto-conversion to paid at day 30. Trial-to-plan tier is based on your actual 30-day usage, so heavy test traffic can put you in a pricier band. Overage rule: 1 month over a cap = no action; 2 consecutive months over = Plausible asks you to upgrade and can lock dashboards after ~1 week (data collection continues).
findings.expiry: Each trial lasts 30 days from signup; then paid. No fixed program sunset.

findings.name: 15% Nonprofit / Education / Open-Source Discount
findings.detail: 15% off a Business plan on ANNUAL billing only, stacked on top of the 2-months-free annual-billing saving. Applies to NEW Business annual subscriptions; it continues on renewals for as long as you stay on the same plan. Excludes existing subscriptions, monthly billing, and every non-Business plan (so the floor is ~$19/mo at 10k pageviews, not free).
findings.eligibility: ONLY nonprofits, educational institutions, and open-source projects. This is an INSTITUTIONAL discount, NOT an individual-student discount (no .edu-email route, no SheerID, no student portal). A student's own project realistically qualifies via the open-source arm, not the 'educational institution' arm. Startups have NO dedicated arm; they can only qualify through an open-source project. No funding cap stated. Claimed by email, not self-serve.
findings.claim: 1) Start the free 30-day trial (no CC). 2) Choose the Business pageview tier you need with ANNUAL billing. 3) Email hello@plausible.io with your org/project name, type, website, and preferred Business tier. 4) Plausible reviews and sends a discount code to use at checkout.
findings.gotchas: Only 15% off, NOT free, and only on Business + annual. Plan upgrade/downgrade ends the discount and reverts to regular pricing. No .edu verification or formal proof is documented — it is a manual email review, so approval is at Plausible's discretion and not guaranteed. Open-source / startup claims are the weaker interpretation and may be declined.
findings.expiry: No stated sunset; discount persists across renewals on the same Business annual plan and ends immediately if you change plan/billing.

findings.name: Self-Hosted Community Edition (AGPL, free)
findings.detail: Plausible's open-source Community Edition is free to self-host: unlimited sites and visitors, no pageview cap, no subscription. You pay only for your own server/hosting. This is the genuinely zero-cost SaaS route for a student or startup on a zero budget (a free-tier VPS credit from a cloud provider can cover the host too). The paid hosted Plausible Cloud (from ~$9/mo per site at 10k pageviews) is a separate product.
findings.eligibility: Anyone can self-host — no student/startup restriction, no .edu email, no funding cap, no region limit. You must operate your own server + PostgreSQL and accept the AGPL license (copyleft applies if you modify and distribute).
findings.claim: 1) Provision a VPS (use a student/free-tier cloud credit if available). 2) Deploy the Plausible Community Edition (Docker image + Postgres) per the self-host docs. 3) Point each site's tracking snippet at your own instance. No Plausible account or payment needed.
findings.gotchas: You absorb 100% of hosting cost plus all ops/maintenance/backups. No vendor support; bot filtering and scale are yours. This is free SOFTWARE, not a free offer from Plausible — the hosted cloud product is paid and has no free tier.
findings.expiry: Indefinite (open source under AGPL); no expiration. Individual releases ship but the free self-host offer has no end date.

sunset_notes: No dedicated free "student tier," no free "startup program," and no individual-student "education license" exists at Plausible. The only genuinely free / discounted items are (a) the universal 30-day no-CC trial, (b) the 15% nonprofit/edu/open-source discount which is institutional and applies to a Business plan on annual billing only, and (c) the free self-hosted AGPL Community Edition. There is NO free hosted (Plausible Cloud) tier. Plausible is a self-funded, bootstrapped, investor-free company, so it runs no startup-accelerator-style free program for customers; startups are not a targeted free segment (at most reachable via the open-source arm of the 15% discount). Nothing was sunset in 2025-2026: the 30-day trial (no CC), the 15% edu/nonprofit/OSS discount, and the free Community Edition are all current as of this 2026-10-22 check. Caveat: the WebSearch budget was exhausted during this run, so all findings above are based on reading the official plausible.io documentation pages directly today; third-party price trackers (outmano/comparedge/canivibecodeit) corroborate the $9/mo Starter floor and no-free-tier claim but were not independently re-verified.

findings.name: SigNoz Cloud 30-day free trial (no credit card)
findings.detail: Managed SigNoz Cloud workspaces available in US, EU, or India: "Get a 30-day trial with no credit card required" (signoz.io/teams). SigNoz docs FAQ (signoz.io/docs/faqs/general): when the trial expires with no payment method added, the deployment is deleted after a 7-day grace period (with email reminders); data cannot be recovered after deletion; an expired trial can only be reactivated via support (cloud-support@signoz.io). Trial accounts are rate-limited at the ingestion side: "You are sending data at more than 100 RPS, your ingestion may be rate limited".
