Post-trial pricing: Teams plan from $49/month including $49 of usage; overage at $0.30/GB logs or traces and $0.10/million metric samples; retention 15 days logs/traces, 1 month metrics on base plans (longer retention: 15/30/90/180 days or 1 year for logs/traces, 1/3/6/13 months for metrics, via support, affects pricing); Enterprise from $4000/month.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone who signs up (no .edu, no startup criteria, no credit card during trial). Workspaces served from US, EU, India data centers. No student-only or startup-only trial variant found.
findings.claim: Sign up at signoz.io/teams ("Get Started - Free" CTA): create account, choose a data source, instrument with OpenTelemetry and visualize. To keep the workspace after day 30, add a credit card under Settings > Billing before the trial or 7-day grace period ends.
findings.expiry: 30 days from signup, then a 7-day grace period; after that the workspace and all data are deleted (irrecoverable; reactivation only via support). Trial does not renew automatically.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a perpetual free tier. No trial ingestion cap in GB is published on any official page I fetched today - the previously circulated "~50 GB ingest" limit could NOT be confirmed; the only documented trial cap is the ~100 RPS ingestion rate limit. Adding a credit card "does not charge you during the trial period" (docs FAQ), but a card becomes required to continue use. Cancelling a subscription deletes the workspace and its data with no restore. Each additional workspace bills separately; no consolidated billing across workspaces.

findings.name: SigNoz Startup Program - $19/month for 12 months
findings.detail: Eligible startups pay $19/month for SigNoz Cloud for the first 12 months instead of the $49/month Teams minimum, and that $19 includes $19 of telemetry usage each month; consumption beyond the included amount is billed at standard published rates ($0.30/GB logs or traces, $0.10/million metric samples). Roughly $19 of usage equals ~63 GB of logs or traces per month. No end date or sunset is stated on the page; the program was live as of 2026-10-22.
findings.eligibility: All three must hold: company less than 3 years old, fewer than 30 employees, and less than $6 million raised. No .edu/student eligibility; no credit-card requirement stated; no region limit stated. The page does not document how eligibility is verified (self-declared at signup vs. reviewed).
findings.claim: Go to signoz.io/startups and click the "Start your free trial" CTA (routes to the signoz.io/teams signup). The $19 rate applies for the first 12 months of an eligible company's SigNoz Cloud subscription. Confirm the startup rate on your first invoice; contact support@signoz.io if the discount is not applied.
findings.expiry: The $19/month rate lasts 12 months, after which standard pricing applies (Teams from $49/month including $49 of usage). Program itself has no published expiry or sunset date.
findings.gotchas: Includes only $19 of usage/month - a startup shipping more telemetry will get bill overages at standard rates. The startup price is anchored to the $49 Teams minimum, which was cut from $199/month to $49/month in May 2025 (see sunset notes), so the effective discount relative to the old baseline is much larger than $30/month. No documented review process or appeal path; eligibility claims are not machine-verifiable.

findings.name: Self-Hosted Community Edition - free open-source observability
findings.detail: SigNoz is an open-source, OpenTelemetry-native platform (metrics, traces, logs in one datastore, out-of-box APM dashboards) that you can self-host free of charge: "Get started with Community Edition" (signoz.io/pricing). Install via Docker Compose/Swarm, Linux install, or Kubernetes/Helm (including AWS, GCP, AKS, DigitalOcean guides; see signoz.io/docs/install/docker, /install/kubernetes). The pricing-page FAQ "What is the difference between SigNoz Cloud (Teams) and Community Edition?" frames the difference as: self-host the community edition yourself vs. Cloud adds managed operation plus SSO & SAML support and help configuring dashboards/alerts. There are no published data caps on the self-hosted edition - you provide your own infrastructure (ClickHouse storage, OTel collector resources are your cost). Retention is configurable per-workspace in Settings > Retention Controls. The docs product FAQ describes SigNoz as a "full-stack open source APM tool" and open source alternative to SaaS APMs. OSS license name could not be verified today (GitHub pages were unreachable from this environment).
findings.eligibility: No eligibility requirement: no .edu email, no credit card, no company age/funding cap - anyone, including students and startups, can self-host. Practically it requires your own server/container infrastructure (Linux/Mac/containers; the team does not support Windows installs per docs FAQ, so use containers on Windows).
findings.claim: No account or payment: download/deploy via Docker Compose or the Helm chart per signoz.io/docs/install/; point OpenTelemetry SDKs/collectors at your endpoint (gRPC 4317 / HTTP 4318, no ingestion key needed, TLS off by default).
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal - community edition is an ongoing open-source project; no sunset date published. Ongoing cost is your infrastructure (compute/storage), not a license fee.
findings.gotchas: "Free" means no software license fee; you bear infrastructure, storage, query-performance and ops cost, and any egress you arrange. The OSS license text could not be re-verified today (GitHub fetches returned 404 from this environment) - verify the repo license before commercial use if that matters. Self-hosted build lacks Cloud-only add-ons like SSO/SAML and managed help; long-term retention and high RPS are constrained by your own hardware. To leave SigNoz later, OpenTelemetry-native data makes exporting out easier, but a self-hosted-to-Cloud migration is a supported (one-way) path.

sunset_notes: 1) Teams price cut (May 2025): SigNoz cut the SigNoz Cloud Teams minimum from $199/month to $49/month, with $49 of usage now included at that price (blog: "Cloud Teams Plan Now at $49", with 2025/05 asset in page; per-unit rates unchanged at $0.30/GB logs/traces, $0.10/mn metric samples; the $19 startup price sits off this new baseline). 2) The previously cited free-trial figure of "~50 GB ingest" could NOT be found on any official page fetched today (signoz.io/pricing, /teams/, docs FAQs, cost-control docs); the only trial limit documented today is the ~100 RPS ingestion rate threshold - treat any "~50 GB" claim as unverified. 3) No student/education license or program exists on signoz.io as of 2026-10-22 (checked pricing, homepage, /startups/, docs FAQs, and the corporate sitemap, which lists no education/academic page). 4) No perpetual free SigNoz Cloud tier - "Get Started - Free" is the 30-day trial. 5) No standalone free Uptime/CDN offering found: uptime monitoring in SigNoz is a dashboard-template feature, not a separate free SaaS tier. 6) Method note: search-engine cross-checks were unavailable this session (shared WebSearch budget exhausted); verification was done directly against official signoz.io pages, docs .md endpoints, the corporate/product sitemaps, and SigNoz's own blog. GitHub (for the OSS license name) was unreachable from this environment and is the one claim left unverified.

provider: Mixpanel (product-analytics; frontends: Auth, Security, Product Analytics & Feature Flags)

findings.name: Mixpanel Free Plan (free-forever tier)
findings.detail: Verified on mixpanel.com/pricing today: 1,000,000 events/month, 10,000 session replays/month (30-day replay retention), unlimited seats, 5 saved reports per user, Experiments up to 1,000 MEU/month, up to 10 active feature flags. $0, no credit card, "free forever", no trial. Excludes on Free: saving cohorts (can create, not save), lookup tables, custom/borrowed properties, permissions, multi-touch attribution, group analytics, alerts, anomaly detection, root-cause analysis, data-warehouse connectors, query API, SSO/SCIM, HIPAA. Default data retention 2 years.
findings.eligibility: Everyone — no .edu or organizational verification, no region limits stated, no credit card required. Usable as-is by students, educators and academic institutions.
findings.claim: Sign up at mixpanel.com/register; Free Plan applies automatically. Autocapture setup takes <2 minutes. Nothing else to redeem.
findings.gotchas: Exceeding 1M events/month does NOT cost money but report access is blocked for the rest of that month (ingestion continues; support-confirmed Jul 2025). Cohorts can't be saved, and 10K replay cap is low — session-replay-only users may prefer Growth-at-$0.
findings.expiry: No expiry; free indefinitely. 30-day replay retention; 90-day audit-log retention.

findings.name: Growth plan "Starts at $0" — first 1M events/month free
findings.detail: Repriced Feb 4, 2025 ("Mixpanel Events 2.0"), confirmed on the pricing page read today: Growth starts at $0 with the first 1M events/month included free, up to 20M events/month, per-event overage pricing per the official yearly table (e.g. 10M events = $840/mo billed annually; ~$0.28 per 1,000 events), volume discounts available. Includes unlimited saved reports (vs 5 on Free), 20K session replays/mo in base (configurable to 500K), Experiments 5K MEU/mo included (up to 100K MEU/mo purchasable), 50 active feature flags in base (up to 500 with add-on MEU), 5 alerts, saved cohorts, data dictionary, APIs. Docs state: "Growth plans purchased after February 2025 include the first 1M events free."
findings.eligibility: Anyone (no startup age/funding rules, no .edu check). Effectively no minimum commitment: pay $0 if you stay under 1M events/month. Credit card only needed when your bill exceeds the free volume (not explicitly documented).
findings.claim: Use the plan builder at mixpanel.com/pricing → Growth → "Start for Free". Pick event volume; the first 1M events/mo are in the base price; you only pay the per-event rate on overage.
findings.gotchas: Not a 30-day trial — it is an ongoing usage-based plan where events 1–1M/mo are simply $0. Overage replays are paywalled and heavy over-ingestion means replays get dropped (support-confirmed). A $0 Growth org is functionally MORE capable than the 1M-cap Free plan (unlimited reports, saved cohorts), which is the common complaint about the Free tier.
findings.expiry: No expiry; renews monthly/annually with no time limit. No trial window.

findings.name: Mixpanel for Startups — first 12 months free on the Startup Plan
findings.detail: Verified today on mixpanel.com/startups/ and docs.mixpanel.com/docs/pricing/startup-program: 12 months of the full product suite at $0 — 1 billion events/year, 1M Session Replay recordings/year, Experiments 1.2M MEU/year, Feature Flags 50 flags + 120M FF API requests/year, plus all four add-ons (Data Pipelines, Group Analytics, Warehouse Connectors, Session Replay), unlimited seats, 24/5 support, Mixpanel University access, and a private Startups Slack community. Marketing states "$145,000 value, costs $0" (Jan 2025 launch post said $150,000+). No credit card required; "no vendor lock-in, no surprise billing". 11K+ startups listed as having chosen Mixpanel.
findings.eligibility: Incorporated <5 years ago; total funding raised ≤ $8M USD; never been on a Mixpanel paid plan; haven't redeemed any other Mixpanel offer (incl. the free-plan exclusives). VC/accelerator affiliation is NOT required but a referral partner can be selected on the application. If Mixpanel learns criteria aren't met it can transition you to paid, suspend, or terminate the account.
findings.claim: Apply at https://mixpanel.com/startups-apply/ ("Join Now" on mixpanel.com/startups). On acceptance your account is provisioned with the Startup Plan for a fixed 12-month term; you MUST begin sending data within 90 days of acceptance or you are removed and prohibited from rejoining. If usage exceeds 1B events/year you may upgrade to paid Growth/Enterprise or downgrade to the Free plan (Mixpanel contacts you in advance).
findings.gotchas: No second free year — after month 12 you move to Free/Growth/Enterprise; the Startup Plan cannot be bought standalone and doesn't support BAAs/MSAs. Misrepresenting eligibility (age/funding) risks suspension/termination. The 90-day data-send requirement is the classic trap: applying early without implementation burns the one-shot chance.
findings.expiry: Fixed 12-month term starting at application approval; no program end date announced. Not renewable — no year-2 free option exists.

findings.name: Education / student license — does not exist (closest substitutes noted)
findings.detail: No .edu-gated education license, student discount, or academic-institution program exists or is advertised on Mixpanel's official sites. The current pricing page (read today) mentions no education/student offer, and no mixpanel.com/education page is linked. Closest free substitutes: (1) the standard Free Plan, which students/educators/universities can use with no verification; (2) Mixpanel University (university.mixpanel.com), a free self-paced training/certification platform — open to everyone since its Nov 2025 launch, free, but it is learning content, NOT a software license; (3) a 2018 nonprofit program (10K MTU free + 80% discount) no longer advertised on the current site — for nonprofits, not students.
findings.eligibility: n/a — nothing to claim. Free Plan requires no eligibility proof; Mixpanel University requires only an account.
findings.claim: Nothing to redeem for .edu users; sign up at mixpanel.com/register for the Free Plan, and use university.mixpanel.com for free coursework/training.
findings.gotchas: Confidence is medium only because absence was verified, not because an offer was read: official pages plus two 2026 discount aggregators confirm no Mixpanel-specific education terms exist; undisclosed sales-side academic deals cannot be ruled out. Don't confuse "Mixpanel University" (training) with a free analytics license.

sunset_notes: Jan 21, 2025: Mixpanel for Startups was REVAMPED — the legacy credit-based track (up to $50,000 in credits, with the card on file charged for renewal/overage) was replaced by 100%-free first year on the Startup Plan (1B events/yr). Docs still reference the legacy credit-based track's renewal-billing language. Feb 4, 2025: "Mixpanel Events 2.0" repricing — Growth restructured to a $0 floor with first 1M events/month free (~100x cheaper; old plans had per-MTU minimums that could DOWNGRADE an upgrader's included volume); docs rule: only Growth plans purchased after Feb 2025 get the 1M free events. No free-plan limit changes since Feb 2025 (1M events/mo, 10K replays/mo, 1K MEU experiments, 10 flags unchanged as of today's page). No education/student program exists to sunset. The 2018 nonprofit offer (10K MTU free + 80% discount, discover.mixpanel.com/nonprofit.html) is no longer advertised on mixpanel.com as of today and appears dormant. Nothing on mixpanel.com/startups or /pricing indicates a 2025–2026 sunset of the startup program; it is active with 11K+ claimed participants.

provider: Amplitude (product analytics) — official pages fetched 2026-10-22: https://amplitude.com/pricing, https://amplitude.com/scholarships, https://amplitude.com/tech-for-black-founders

findings.name: Amplitude Free Plan (permanent free tier, not a trial)
findings.detail: 2M events/month FREE FOREVER; 10,000 session replays/month with 1-month replay retention; 2,000 AI feedback records; 5,000 agent sessions/month; AI Agents & MCP included; Product Analytics + Agent Analytics; one-time cohort syncs; limited experiments/guides/surveys. Also: unlimited seats, up to 10 saved charts/org, 1 collaboration space, 1-year data access, no customer support. Explicitly 'No Credit Card required' and 'You can use Amplitude for free as long as it fits your needs' — no time limit.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (individuals/explorers and companies). No .edu requirement, no funding cap, no credit card, no stated region limit. Claims: sign up at amplitude.com (workspace), select Free plan at pricing page — self-serve, no application.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a free Amplitude account at amplitude.com/signup. 2) Integrate product/mobile/web SDK and start sending events. 3) That's it — 2M events/month accrue automatically with no card and no application.
findings.expiry: Never — '2M Events/month forever'. No renewal needed.
findings.gotchas: Hard cap at 2M events/month: overage is not billed, it forces a paid upgrade (data handling above cap is plan-gated, not metered free). 1-year data access only (Plus gives 2). No support. 10 saved charts and 1 collaboration space limit team use. Free tier is not a trial: it is a permanent tier, so 'trial credits' as such do not exist in the offer.

findings.name: Plus plan 'Starts at $0' — first 2M events/month free on a paid plan
findings.detail: Plus 'Starts at $0': 'First 2M Events/month free', scales up to 70M events / 700K MTU. Beyond free-tier extras: custom events/formulas, 20 behavioral cohorts, alerts, heatmaps, 2-year data retention, unlimited saved charts, 3 collaboration spaces, online support, 2-year replay retention. 'Credit Card required. Estimate bill.'
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no application. A CARD IS REQUIRED even for the first 2M free events (this is the key difference from the Free plan). No .edu/funding/region conditions stated.
findings.claim: 1) At amplitude.com/pricing choose Plus. 2) Add a credit card (bill estimated — $0 while under 2M events/month). 3) You keep Plus features at no charge while usage stays under 2M events/month.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; free while usage <= 2M events/month. Monthly invoice can become nonzero automatically when events exceed 2M — usage-based sliding scale up to 70M events. Not a fixed trial; no stated end date.
findings.gotchas: TRAP: 'starts at $0' does NOT mean no card — a live card is on file and overage bills automatically. Trial-vs-free distinction: Free plan = cardless forever; Plus-$0 = card-on-file, metered above 2M. To stay free, downgrade to the Free plan (your data/dashboards are kept).

findings.name: Startup Scholarship (Early-Stage Startup Plan) — 1 year of Growth plan free
findings.detail: Year 1: 100% off the FULL Growth plan — 'Every feature, unlimited teammates, no credit card'; advertised value '$60,000' including '100M events a month' (about 200K MTUs). Year 2: 40% off annual Plus plan. Marketing claims: 'Most startups are approved instantly' and '96% of startups who apply get in.'
findings.eligibility: Raised LESS THAN $10M in funding AND FEWER THAN 20 employees. No company-age cap stated on the page. No credit card required. No .edu requirement. No explicit region limit stated (application is in-app).
findings.claim: 1) Create an Amplitude account. 2) Submit the scholarship application FROM INSIDE YOUR WORKSPACE (in-app application link from the Scholarships/Startups page). 3) Approval is typically instant; onboarding support follows. Extension requests: email scholarship@amplitude.com.
findings.expiry: 1-year grant, then converts to 40%-off Plus (not free). Amplitude sends a usage-based quote for year 2 sixty days before it ends. You may 'Drop to the free 2M-events/month plan and keep your data and dashboards. No penalty.' No automatic renewal of the free year.
findings.gotchas: Year 2 is discounted, not free — budget it. Losing Growth features at conversion unless you pay; downgrading to Free forfeits Growth feature set (but keeps data). Funding cap is 'raised < $10M' — total raised, so check current cap table before applying.

findings.name: Tech for Black Founders Scholarship — Growth plan free in perpetuity while eligible
findings.detail: Free, unlimited access to the Growth plan (the Startups page also phrases it as the 'full Startup Plan'): advanced analytics, experimentation, governance, dedicated onboarding; coverage up to 500K Monthly Tracked Users; 'for as long as you are eligible' / 'in perpetuity as long as you continue to meet the criteria.' Offered jointly with Braze.
findings.eligibility: US-HEADQUARTERED (explicit region limit); raised LESS THAN $30M in venture capital; FEWER THAN 150 employees; led by one or more Black founders. Early-stage ventures only. Founders must apply personally; no application fee; no credit card stated.
findings.claim: 1) Go to amplitude.com/tech-for-black-founders. 2) Complete the application form (founder applies personally, 'in-app' link available from the Startups page). 3) 'Our team will be in touch to get you started' — human review, not instant approval.
findings.expiry: No fixed end date; runs 'in perpetuity' while all criteria keep holding. Exits: exceed $30M raised, exceed 150 employees, founder-ownership change, or leave US base — free tier stops applying (terms for post-eligibility billing not stated on page).
findings.gotchas: Identity criteria ('led by one or more Black founders') disqualify many startups — check founder composition, not just company demographics. 500K MTU cap on the free grant; above that, pricing. 'Unlimited' refers to the Growth plan feature set, not event volume.

findings.name: Venture Partner Program (VC/accelerator channel into the free Startup Plan)
findings.detail: VCs and accelerator programs that 'invest in or run a program for startups' can partner so they 'give every company you back the Startup Plan free, plus partner-only perks.' For a startup, this is an alternative route to the same 1-year-free Growth plan as the Startup Scholarship. General partner-referral deals also add 'additional discounts' beyond the standard Startup Plan.
findings.eligibility: The VENTURE FIRM is the applicant (firm must invest in or run a program for startups). Startup recipients are those backed by/within that partner firm's portfolio; standard Startup Plan criteria (<$10M raised, <20 employees) presumably apply. No .edu requirement; no credit card stated; no region limit stated.
findings.claim: 1) VC/accelerator applies at /venture-partner on Amplitude's Startups page. 2) Partner gets a mechanism to grant the free Startup Plan to its portfolio companies ('partner-only perks' for the firm). 3) A startup in the portfolio claims through the referring partner.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page; the underlying grant has the same 1-year-Growth-free / 40%-off-Plus structure as the standard Startup Scholarship.
findings.gotchas: Detail was read second-hand from the Startups page, not a dedicated program page — treat perk specifics as approximate. If you are the startup, your route is via your investors/accelerator, not direct.

findings.name: YC / Bookface deal (Y Combinator-affiliated startups)
findings.detail: Amplitude's Startups page states: 'We have a separate deal for YC folks - check out Bookface.' Bookface is a YC-ecosystem deals platform where YC startups claim partner offers; the deal is described as distinct from the standard < $10M / < 20-employee Startup Plan. The exact Amplitude offer terms (plan, event volume, duration) could NOT be verified: bookface.com (the domain I fetched) is an unrelated books marketplace, and the Amplitude deal page returned 404.
findings.eligibility: Y Combinator-affiliated startups (presumed in addition to/instead of standard criteria). No other details verifiable.
findings.claim: Unverified path: YC startup goes to Bookface's Amplitude deal page and applies/claims in-app; YC network access required.
findings.expiry: Unknown — not verifiable from the sources I could fetch.
findings.gotchas: Treat all specifics as unverified. If you are YC-backed, locate Bookface's correct domain and the Amplitude deal card before relying on this; it may duplicate or extend the Startup Scholarship.

findings.name: Education / student license: NOT FOUND
findings.detail: No Amplitude education or student program exists on its public site as of 2026-10-22. Verified: amplitude.com/education, /students, /solutions/education, /solutions/higher-education all 404; the Resources library (/resources/education) contains no student/edu offer; the pricing page states no education discount. Students/universities are covered only by the general Free plan (2M events/month, cardless) or Plus-$0 (card on file). No .edu email gate anywhere — because no edu offer exists to gate.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no dedicated program. Open access via the standard Free plan: no .edu email, no credit card, no region limit.
findings.claim: Students claim the generic Free plan at amplitude.com/signup. For institutional or educational pricing, contact Amplitude sales (no public application path found).
findings.expiry: Free plan never expires; no license to renew.
findings.gotchas: Absence-of-evidence caveat: I confirmed the main public pages but could not exhaustively crawl every Amplitude URL (web-search budget was exhausted in this session). A limited/invitational edu program could exist off-site; treat 'none found' as 'none on public pages'.

sunset_notes: Coverage note: WebSearch was unavailable in this session (shared budget exhausted), so 2025-2026 change history was NOT independently verified; all 'high' confidence items are Amplitude's own pages fetched 2026-10-22. What today's pages confirm vs. 'known so far' (all consistent, no sunset detected): (1) 2M events/month free forever on the Free plan; (2) 10,000 session replays/month free; (3) new AI allowances now bundled on the FREE plan — 2,000 AI feedback records, 5,000 agent sessions/month, AI Agents & MCP — indicating the free tier was expanded in the 2025-2026 AI repositioning rather than cut; (4) Plus 'starts at $0' with the first 2M events free is a 2025-era restructuring (older Amplitude tiers did not have a $0 entry point) — it requires a credit card, so it is a free-allowance-with-card, not trial credits: Amplitude does not appear to offer fixed trial credits. Startup program current terms: <$10M raised + <20 employees = 1 free year of Growth ('$60,000 value', 100M events/month), then 40% off Plus in year 2 (a material change vs. the older '2 years free' model that some earlier iterations of the Amplitude startup program advertised — if that is what 'known so far' assumed, the current public page shows year 2 is discounted, not free). Tech for Black Founders (<$30M, <150 employees, US-HQ, Black-led) is in perpetuity while eligible. No education license found on any public page — if one existed pre-2025, it is not advertised today. YC/Bookface deal is referenced on the official page but its terms are unverifiable from the domains I could fetch (bookface.com currently resolves to an unrelated books site; Amplitude deal page 404s). No data/egress fees are advertised on any free offer; the recurring cost risk is automatic metered billing once Free-plan users upgrade to Plus-$0 with a card on file.

findings.name: Free plan (hobby tier), free forever
findings.detail: Free plan at $0/€0 'Free forever', targeted at side projects and blogs. Exact limits read today: 1 user, up to 5 websites, 1-month data history ('the last 30 days'). Unlimited pageviews subject to a fair-use policy. Exclusions: no events, no goals, no Stats API access. A Simple Analytics badge must remain in the site footer (customizable at /badges); badge checks start ~14 days after the site's first analytics visit and run roughly every 30 days — a missing badge gives a 14-day warning, then locks dashboard data, API, exports, public dashboards and embedded charts while event collection continues. Paid plans do not require the badge; upgrading removes the obligation.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no credit card required, no region limits, no student/startup status needed. For hobby sites, not commercial use in practice.
findings.claim: Sign up at simpleanalytics.com (#signup / pricing page) and select the Free plan; no card, no payment. Generate and embed the badge from the /badges builder, keep it visible and linking back to Simple Analytics on every page.
findings.expiry: Indefinite ('Free forever'); the badge is the funding mechanism — the badge page states it keeps the Free plan available, so the offer is tied to continued badge display.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: this is a permanent free tier, not a trial. No CC required. Gotchas: mandatory badge with lockout (data/API/export locked, collection continues) if removed; only 30 days of history; 1 user / 5 websites; events, goals and APIs are paid features only; 'unlimited' pageviews are capped by an unquantified fair-use policy.

findings.name: 14-day free trial of paid self-serve plans, no credit card
findings.detail: Self-serve paid (Simple) plans: usage-based tiers by combined pageviews + events/month. pricing.md (USD): $15/mo ≤20k, $20/mo ≤100k, $30/mo ≤250k, $40/mo ≤500k, $60/mo ≤1M, $80/mo ≤2M, $120/mo ≤5M, $160/mo ≤10M, then +$16 per extra 1M. Yearly billing = 10× monthly (2 months free). 1 user included, +$20/mo per extra user, up to 10 websites, 3 email reports, 3 years (1,096 days) of data retention. 14-day trial with no credit card required and 'advanced features' unrestricted; payment details only after the trial.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no card required to start the trial. Paid plans are for production/commercial use (free tier is for hobby).
findings.claim: Start from the signup/pricing page, pick a paid tier, complete the 14-day trial (no CC), then add payment. Annual plans: pay 10× monthly for 2 months free.
findings.expiry: Trial is fixed 14 days; no auto-renew during trial; cancel any time, access retained through paid period.
findings.gotchas: It's a trial, not a free tier — CC/payment is required after 14 days. Usage-based overage: fees follow pageviews+events volume; for yearly plans data points reset after a year and excess emails a notice. Numbers differ between the HTML page (shown as €20/mo base with a 100k–2.5M slider) and pricing.md (USD tiers from $15/mo, up to 10M+) — likely currency display vs. the machine-readable list; treat pricing.md as the exact tier schedule. Bitcoin payment adds +10% surcharge (yearly only); bank transfer bills ≥€500 add +10%.

findings.name: No student, education, or startup program exists

findings.claim: Nothing to claim; both candidate URLs 404 and no signup path, email offer or discount code is advertised.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: If a student/startup offer was ever rumored, it is not present on the site as of 2026-10-22; do not assume .edu discounts (no education license found).

findings.name: Enterprise 30-day free proof-of-concept (assisted)
findings.detail: Enterprise tier (custom pricing) offers a free 30-day assisted POC run alongside GA4 — setup support, proxy and custom-domain assistance included, campaign comparisons, API & BI access. Not self-serve: it is arranged by booking a demo. Also available as a free evaluation path, though aimed at larger organizations rather than students/startups.
findings.eligibility: Organizations pursuing Enterprise; arranged via demo/consultation, not self-serve; no student/startup-specific criteria published.
findings.claim: Book an Enterprise demo; the 30-day POC runs in parallel with GA4 with assisted setup at no cost.
findings.expiry: Fixed 30 days; after POC, custom-pricing engagement.
findings.gotchas: Not a free tier: post-POC pricing is custom/procurement-based, and security/compliance/SSO workflows (Okta, Microsoft Entra) sit in Enterprise docs.

sunset_notes: No 2025–2026 sunset of any student/startup/education program found: the Free plan is marketed as 'Free forever' and no such program page exists (/startups, /education both 404; no mention in pricing, pricing.md, docs or homepage). No plan-structure change announcements appear in the blog index page 1 fetched 2026-10-22 (its 2025 posts cover EU consent/GDPR topics, not pricing). The notable 2025–2026-era structure visible today is the usage-based self-serve tier ladder in pricing.md ($15–$160/mo by pageviews+events, yearly = 10× monthly) versus the HTML pricing page's €20/mo base display — a currency/display discrepancy rather than a confirmed price cut; if exact EUR numbers are needed, check the live pricing page in EUR locale. Verification caveat: live web search was unavailable for this run (session search budget exhausted), so all verification was done by fetching the official site's pages directly on 2026-10-22; no third-party or archive corroboration was possible.

findings.name: Countly Lite (Community Edition) — free self-hosted
findings.detail: Countly Lite is 'Free-Forever Product Analytics': open-source, self-hosted server (countly-server on GitHub, MongoDB+Node.js) with 20+ plugins covering core analytics (dashboards, session/event tracking, mobile/web/desktop SDKs). Official /lite page: free, no trial sign-up, no payment required; community support only (Discord/GitHub). Licensing: repo is AGPL-3.0 with a modified Section 7; README describes Lite as 'Free to use under an open-source, non-commercial license' — commercial use of your users' data effectively requires a paid Enterprise agreement. Feature gating vs paid editions: advanced/engagement capabilities (funnels, retention, drills, push at scale, A/B, cohorts, AI agent 'Cee', SSO/SLA) sit in the paid Flex/Enterprise capability bundles; SDKs are identical across editions.
findings.eligibility: Anyone can download and self-host; license intended for individuals, small teams, and non-commercial use. No .edu, no age/funding cap, no credit card, no stated region limits. Commercial products (e.g. tracking users of a paid app) are outside the non-commercial license.
findings.claim: Download countly-server from github.com/Countly/countly-server and self-host on your own VM/container; no signup. For commercial use, contact Countly sales for an Enterprise license (custom pricing, annual).
findings.expiry: Free forever; no stated sunset. Enterprise split (Lite non-commercial vs commercial license) is structural, not time-limited.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial license restriction is the big one: a startup's commercial app likely cannot track users on Lite. Self-hosting cost is on you (MongoDB/Node/Nginge infra, ops). No vendor support; feature set is the reduced core.

findings.name: Countly Flex 14-day free trial (managed private cloud)
findings.detail: Flex (managed private cloud) starts at $175/month (Tier 5K = 5,000 MAUs, 5M data points/month; higher tiers up to 1M MAUs at $16,444/month on flex.countly.com pricing table). A 14-day free trial is offered on Tier 5K only (per the flex pricing table). Official Flex page states: 'You can start with a trial to explore Countly Flex and its core analytics capabilities. A credit card is required to begin the trial.' Trial includes Advanced Analytics suite (real-time analytics, event tracking, sessions, user profiles, dashboards); Adaptivity/Intelligence are paid add-on bundles. US GCP regions included; other regions carry a monthly surcharge; 6 months data retention included (longer retention is paid). Pay monthly, cancel anytime.
findings.eligibility: All organizations (self-serve, no stated student/startup/region restriction beyond GCP region choice). Credit card IS required to start the trial — this contradicts the official marketing FAQ's silence on the matter.
findings.claim: Sign up at flex.countly.com ('Start free trial' on countly.com/flex or countly.com/pricing), add a card, create a server (tier 5K, region, cloud provider), trial lasts 14 days; then standard Flex billing applies unless cancelled.
findings.expiry: Trial ends after 14 days; no stated program expiry. If you go over a tier's MAU threshold, the server is locked until upgrade (per Countly support FAQ).
findings.gotchas: CC required (trial is not no-CC). Trial is only on the smallest tier. Data lives in Countly-managed GCP private cloud (not your infra). Add-on bundles (Intelligence from $44/mo, Adaptivity from $62/mo at Tier 5K) and region/retention surcharges stack up quickly; fully loaded Flex can be very expensive at scale.

findings.name: Countly Academic Program (CAP) — institutional education license (not free, $500/yr)
findings.detail: Official academic program: 'simple, fixed, non-volume based pricing ... annual fee of $500.' Grants accredited institutions a Countly Enterprise site license for instructional and non-commercial research purposes: discounted Enterprise server packages you install and supervise yourself, full SDK source code for students to examine/modify, unrestricted access to knowledge base/docs/updates, and Enterprise-grade support terms. Not a free student license and not aimed at individual students.
findings.eligibility: Institutions (not individuals) that grant a degree via 2-6 year programs or equivalent; technical schools offering distance education also eligible. License must be used solely for instructional/non-profit research, never commercial; hardware/VMs must be under the institution's IT supervision; Countly works only with an institution staff admin (not a student/TA); EULA signed between Countly and the institution. No .edu email requirement stated — it's an institutional agreement.
findings.claim: Institution applies via countly.com/academic-program, signs a CAP EULA, pays the $500 annual fee; Countly supplies Enterprise server packages for on-prem or institution-supervised cloud install.
findings.expiry: Annual fee, EULA-based; license not transferable outside the institution; renew per the signed agreement. Page content verified via search snapshot of the official page today; a direct fetch bounced to a generic education-solutions page, so details are as of that snapshot.

findings.name: No official Countly startup program or trial-credit program found

Startup options are only the general 14-day Flex trial (CC required) or the free non-commercial Lite self-host. No vendor-specific startup age/funding caps exist because no program exists.
findings.eligibility: n/a — offer does not exist on official channels.
findings.claim: n/a.
findings.expiry: n/a

findings.name: Open-Source self-hosted edition (free forever, no caps)
findings.detail: Free open-source edition: session replay, DevTools, product analytics, co-browsing, Spot bug reports, heatmaps. No hard caps on events, recordings, users or retention — storage, RAM, vCPUs and retention are 'self-managed'; scalability labeled 'low traffic'. Support is community-only (GitHub, Slack). The live pricing page comparison table lists this tier simply as 'Free' (Open-Source column) and the FAQ says 'Open-Source is free — you host it on your own infrastructure.' No .edu email, no application, no startup program needed — anyone (students, startups, anyone) can self-host it free. License: AGPL-3.0 (openreplay/openreplay on GitHub).
findings.eligibility: Universal — no application, no .edu email, no age/funding caps, no region limits. Student or startup just self-hosts on any infrastructure.
findings.claim: No claim step: clone openreplay/openreplay, deploy via Docker on any host/cloud (docs.openreplay.com); or build free in-repo. Community support only.
findings.expiry: Indefinite (free-forever, open-source). No renewal.
findings.gotchas: You pay your own infrastructure (VM, storage, bandwidth/egress) — 'free' software but not free hosting; low-traffic scalability means you must size your own hardware; no SLA, no managed updates; AGPL-3.0 obligations apply to modified redistributed versions; data retention you manage yourself.

findings.name: 7-day free trial of cloud Dedicated (no credit card)
findings.detail: Dedicated managed cloud instance: 'Start 7-day trial', 'No credit card required', 'a fully-provisioned instance to evaluate before committing'. After trial, Dedicated starts at $199/mo (O1: 8GB RAM, 2 vCPUs, 120GB disk; billed hourly at $0.276/hr; 'stopped instances are still billed a small amount based on disk size'). O2/O3 sized instances go up (vendor's own llms.txt lists O2 $399/mo up to 200K sessions and O3 $799/mo up to 500K, but the live pricing page shows only 'from $199/mo'). 50 regions (AWS/GCP/Azure/BYOC), 2-day automated backups, SSO/SCIM, SOC 2 Type II.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (student or startup) — sign up required, no .edu email requirement stated, no startup-age or funding cap stated, credit card explicitly NOT required, no region limit for the trial signup.
findings.claim: Pricing page → 'Try Cloud' / Dedicated card → 'Start 7-day trial' → OpenReplay provisions a full Dedicated instance; no card, no commitment.
findings.expiry: 7 days; at expiry the instance no longer runs for free — converting to paid requires a plan ($199/mo+ or BYOC flat rate).
findings.gotchas: Trial is trial-only, not a free tier: nothing persists free after 7 days; billing is hourly from the moment you subscribe, and stopped instances still incur small disk-storage charges; BYOC is billed at a flat monthly rate; O1 estimated $199/mo assumes ~full-month runtime.

findings.name: Serverless usage-based cloud (per-session pricing; free-cloud-tier claim unverified)
findings.detail: Cloud 'Serverless' plan is usage-based: pay only for recorded sessions; OpenReplay's own 2025 blog post and its llms.txt price it at $5.95 per 1,000 sessions (O1-cap ~50K sessions/mo figure appears in O1 Dedicated sizing), and a 2025 blog post states the cloud offering 'includes a 7-day free trial.' The vendor's llms.txt also claims a 'Free cloud tier (1,000 sessions/mo, 2 users)' with 30-day retention — but that tier does NOT appear on the live pricing page as fetched today (only Open-Source 'Free', Dedicated, Enterprise are shown; the page's 'Try Cloud Free' CTA may point to a signup flow). The pricing page today shows no per-session figure, so the $5.95/1K figure is from vendor-secondary pages, not the live pricing page.
findings.eligibility: Cloud plan, so universal signup (no .edu/age caps stated). If a true free cloud tier (1,000 sessions/mo, 2 users, 30-day retention) exists as llms.txt claims, eligibility would just be account signup.
findings.claim: Start with 'Try Cloud' on openreplay.com; confirm at signup whether a free Serverless tier with 1,000 sessions/mo is offered, since the live pricing table omits it.
findings.expiry: If the 1,000-session free tier exists: renewable monthly up to 1,000 sessions and 2 users; 30-day data retention; overage $5.95/1,000 sessions per llms.txt. Unconfirmed — verify in the signup flow.
findings.gotchas: llms.txt vs live pricing page conflict — treat the free cloud tier as unverified; per-session billing means cost scales with traffic; 30-day retention on cloud tiers (self-managed on OSS); 'no hard event caps' claim applies only to self-hosted open-source edition.
