provider: PostHog (product analytics / feature flags platform, posthog.com)

findings.name: PostHog Free Tier — monthly free allowances on every product
findings.detail: Free tier, no credit card required, not a trial: Analytics 1M events/mo; Session replay 5,000 recordings/mo (PostHog's Feb 2026 comparison page breaks this as 5,000 web + 2,500 mobile); Feature flags 1M requests/mo (experiments billed with flags); Error tracking 100K exceptions/mo; Surveys 1,500 responses/mo; Data warehouse Sources 1M rows + free historical syncs, Destinations 10K events + 1M rows; AI Observability 100K events/mo; PostHog AI 500 credits (worth $5); Inbox (beta) 3 PRs; Workflows 10K messages/channel; Logs 10 GB ingested/mo; Replay Vision 2,500 credits (worth $25); PostHog Desktop (beta) 2,000 credits (worth $20). Free plan: unlimited team members, 1 project, 1-year data retention, community support. Posting on the page: 'No credit card required… Same allowance whether or not you have a card on file… Your free allowance renews every month. Yes, for everything. Yes, forever.' Usage stops at the free limits so no surprise bills.
findings.eligibility: Anyone/any company (no .edu requirement, no age/funding cap, no region limit stated). No credit card required. 1 project max on the free plan; add a card to create more projects.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up free at app.posthog.com/signup (or posthog.com/pricing 'Get started – free'). 2) Install the PostHog snippet/SDK (JS, Python, Node, mobile). 3) Use — free allowances apply automatically; set billing limits; no card on file needed.
findings.expiry: Free allowance resets every month indefinitely ('forever'). Data retention is 1 year on the free plan (7 years once paid).
findings.gotchas: Experiments and Evaluations have no standalone free allowance — they bill against their parent product (flags / AI observability). Free plan = 1 project; a second project requires adding a card (Pay-as-you-go plan keeps the same free tier, then charges overage). 5,000 replays is the stated cap; the web/mobile split appears only in comparison copy. Paid add-ons (platform packages, onboarding calls) are not covered by the free tier.

findings.name: PostHog for Startups — $50,000 in platform credits for 12 months
findings.detail: $50,000 in PostHog credits valid for 12 months, usable across nearly all products (analytics, replays, flags, error tracking, surveys, warehouse; page says ~950M events or 6M+ replays if spent on one product). Plus ~$12,000 in partner perks: $1,500 off Incident.io teams plan, 50% off Speakeasy for 6 months, $5,000 Depot credit, and 50% off Mintlify for 6 months (Stripe Atlas variant of the deal), plus exclusive founder merch (one welcome pack) and a founder newsletter.
findings.eligibility: Company <2 years old AND <$5M raised; company email domain required (applications from free/disposable domains like gmail.com/outlook.com are auto-rejected; if you lack a company domain you stay on the monthly free allowance and apply once you get one); PostHog signup on/after Jan 1, 2023 (earlier signups can join the program perks but not the credits); apply from a PostHog account using the company domain. Applications are auto-approved then manually reviewed. YC teams are excluded from this track (separate YC deal; programs don't stack).
findings.claim: 1) Create a PostHog account with the company email. 2) Sign up to a paid plan (usage-based; free tier still applies; no minimum spend). 3) Fill the application form at posthog.com/startups; the credit is applied automatically if eligible and you get an email when accepted.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 12 months after grant. After expiry you move to a normal plan and keep program perks (events/newsletter). Small open-source projects without corporate backing and <$200k annual revenue can contact support to have the 12-month expiry waived.
findings.gotchas: From September 14, 2026, credits can NO LONGER be used on AI tools (PostHog Desktop, PostHog Slack app, Replay Vision, PostHog AI, Inbox); teams who joined before that date can still use credits for usage incurred before the cut-off. Credits cannot cover a BAA under the Boost plan, nor onboarding calls/service packages. Going over $50k means moving to another plan. No refunds.

findings.name: PostHog for Y Combinator — $50,000 per year, auto-renewing
findings.detail: Similar to the startups program but for YC teams: $50,000 in credits per year — register once and it renews automatically while eligible; up to 4 founder merch packs (different pack than the startups program); access to Hogpatch (PostHog's YC-founder space) for the duration of the batch; partner benefits with Speakeasy and Incident.io; priority support. YC credits can be used for BAA in the Boost package (unlike the standard startups credits).
findings.eligibility: Must be a YC company (any batch, proven with a YC verification link via Bookface), <$25M raised in total, company email domain. Not available to YC alumni who started a new company (those can use PostHog for Startups instead) nor to YC companies acquired by a non-YC parent.
findings.claim: Register once on the YC Bookface page (the internal YC deal listing; PostHog team manages the copy there). Auto-renews while the team stays eligible (<$25m raised). Teams whose earlier deal expired must re-register.
findings.expiry: Renews annually while eligible (<$25M raised); no one-time 12-month expiry like the startups program.
findings.gotchas: Same September 14, 2026 AI-tools credit exclusion applies to YC credits. Programs don't stack with PostHog for Startups. Details come from PostHog's company handbook (official but internal-marketing doc); I could not re-fetch the full page body today (page fetch truncated), so treat specifics (4 merch packs, Hogpatch access) as reported, not re-verified against the live YC Bookface listing.

findings.name: PostHog for Students — campus events + $2,000 in hosting perks (NOT credits or an education license)
findings.detail: PostHog for Students is an in-person campus events program, explicitly 'about events, not credits': free in-person mixers each semester with a PostHog team member (food, drinks, merch covered), AMAs/talks and 1:1 mentorship. Students or student orgs who host an event get a $1,000 cash grant (food/drinks) + $1,000 in PostHog merch = $2,000 total, plus a PostHog speaker. A few times a year, students are invited to 'Startup School' in SF at Hogpatch (apply via the page). There is no student discount, no student credit grant, and no course/certificate (explicitly 'no coursework, no grades, no certificate').
findings.eligibility: Open to Bay Area universities and UC campuses across California; schools outside that list can apply but the program 'can't commit to extending further'. A school-issued email (a .edu or other university-associated domain) IS required to apply — personal emails are not accepted. No company or finished idea required; no region limit beyond the .edu-style email check and current campus focus.
findings.claim: 1) You (or your student org/club) apply via the form at posthog.com/students (name, school email, school, optional LinkedIn, event description). 2) PostHog pairs you with a team member and schedules the event each semester. 3) Free attendance; hosting grants are per event.
findings.expiry: Semester-based events; the $1,000+$1,000 hosting grant is a one-time per-hosted-event award, not a recurring credit. No credits to expire.
findings.gotchas: If a student is building a company <2 years old with <$5M raised, the page routes them to PostHog for Startups ($50k credits) instead — the student program gives no platform credits. The broader student program is still an open RFC internally (GitHub RFC #503, Mar 2026), so it may expand; a third-party tracker (Modelverse) describes a '365-day student grant' for the free tier, but that's just the standard monthly free tier, not a student-specific offer.

findings.name: Non-profit discount (adjacent offer, not student/startup)
findings.detail: PostHog offers discount options for non-profits: after signing up, contact the sales team to discuss a discount. No public fixed amounts are listed. Also mentioned on the pricing page: 'We also offer discounts for startups and non-profits.'
findings.eligibility: Registered non-profits; no .edu or funding caps — case-by-case via sales.
findings.claim: Sign up for PostHog, then contact PostHog sales/support to arrange the non-profit discount.
findings.gotchas: Not a self-serve offer and not quantified publicly; treat as a discount negotiation, not a free tier.

findings.name: Self-hosted PostHog open source (MIT) — free for anyone who can run infrastructure
findings.detail: PostHog is open source, MIT licensed; you can self-host the full stack in your own organization at no per-event license cost. The pricing page positions it for 'a big organization that isn't ready to move to PostHog Web yet'. This is a separate free path from the cloud free tier and available to students/startups who have the infra budget.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no account, no card, no .edu. You must host and maintain it yourself (k8s/Docker, Postgres, ClickHouse).
findings.claim: Deploy from github.com/PostHog/posthog (MIT) following the self-host docs; no signup or billing.
findings.gotchas: Self-hosted does not include PostHog cloud services (e.g., hosted context warehouse/cloud-only products); you pay your own infra and maintenance costs. Cloud free-tier allowances (1M events etc.) are a cloud-only concept and don't apply to a self-hosted install.

sunset_notes: Verified against live official pages today (posthog.com/pricing, /startups, /students fetched and read in full; handbook/startups content from the official handbook via search snippet): (1) From September 14, 2026, both the PostHog for Startups and Y Combinator programs' credits can NO LONGER be applied to AI tools (PostHog Desktop, PostHog Slack app, Replay Vision, PostHog AI, Inbox); pre-cutoff teams can still burn credits for usage incurred before that date. (2) The free-tier allowances listed in the task baseline (1M events, 5,000 session recordings, 1M flag requests, 100K exceptions, 10GB logs) are confirmed unchanged and current on the pricing page; PostHog states no loss-leader products that will later be retired, and 'No credit card, not a trial' — there is no separate trial program (docs: 'no trial needed'). (3) PostHog notes price cuts in 2024 (session replay, analytics events) and 2025 (data pipelines, surveys) per its Feb 2026 comparison page — these were paid-rate cuts, not free-tier changes. (4) No student/education license or student credit program exists: the student offer is events-only; the YC deal is the more generous credits variant ($50k/yr auto-renewing vs $50k one-time). Sources: https://posthog.com/pricing · https://posthog.com/startups · https://posthog.com/students · https://posthog.com/handbook/marketing/startups · https://posthog.com/docs/billing/common-questions · https://github.com/PostHog/requests-for-comments-public/issues/503 · https://posthog.com/startups/stripe-atlas · https://posthog.com/compare/posthog-vs-pendo

findings.name: Free (forever) plan — transactional + marketing email
findings.detail: 3,000 transactional emails/month with a hard cap of 100 emails/day (UTC calendar day, resets midnight UTC). Includes 3 verified domains, 3 inboxes, 10,000 automation runs/mo, 5 AI credits/mo, 1 webhook endpoint, 30-day data retention, ticket support, open/click tracking. Marketing (Broadcasts): unlimited sends to up to 1,000 contacts/mo, 3 segments. Overage billing not available on Free — sending pauses at the quota. No credit card required to sign up; paid plans accept major credit cards only.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone (students, startups, anyone). No .edu email, funding cap, or startup age requirement. No credit card required on Free. No region limits found. Free-forever, not a trial.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at resend.com (no CC needed). 2) Add a custom domain and paste the generated DKIM/SPF/DMARC DNS records for verification. 3) Generate an API key / use SMTP relay and start sending immediately. Free marketing contacts are managed via the Broadcasts feature in the same dashboard.
findings.expiry: No expiry — recurring free plan, limits renew monthly. No renewal steps.
findings.gotchas: Inbound (received) emails count against the 3,000/mo and 100/day quota — spam hitting free inboxes consumes it. The daily cap is not bankable (each UTC day is independent). Hitting quota pauses sending until the next billing cycle; paid tiers instead bill overage ($0.90/1,000, capped at 5x quota). Extra domains ($20/mo add-on) and extra inboxes ($1/mo) require a paid plan. API rate limit is 10 req/s on all plans. No annual billing option.

findings.name: YC deal — startup credits for Y Combinator companies
findings.detail: $25,000 in credits for the current YC batch, valid for 12 months; $15,000 for YC alumni. Perks beyond credits: dedicated Slack channel with Resend founders and engineers, optional company feature as a use case on Resend's website, direct access to the CEO's phone (WhatsApp/text). Signing up before Demo Day also earns an exclusive gift from the Resend team.
findings.eligibility: Y Combinator companies only: current-batch founders get the $25k tier, YC alumni the $15k tier. Verified through the official YC verification link (ycombinator.com/verify). Not open to non-YC startups; no .edu or funding-cap criteria — batch/alumni status is the gate.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at resend.com before your batch's Demo Day. 2) From resend.com/yc, use 'Get your YC verification link' (ycombinator.com/verify) to authenticate your YC status. 3) 'Claim deal' on the YC page; credits and perks attach to your verified account. No credit card is required to receive credits.
findings.expiry: Credits valid for 12 months (stated for current batch; alumni window not explicitly stated, assumed same). Offer is per YC batch cycle — claim before Demo Day for the bonus. No renewal/extension policy published.
findings.gotchas: This is the ONLY remaining Resend startup offer: the open startup program page (resend.com/startups) returns 404 as of 2026-10-22. No per-sender caps or volume limits are published on the page. Third-party directories (techscoop, creditforstartups) add unverified exclusions (e.g., 'not for Series C+'); the official page states only the batch/alumni tiers.

findings.name: Resend Insiders — ambassador program with free Pro subscription
findings.detail: Select insiders receive a free Resend Pro subscription ($20/mo value = 50,000 transactional emails/mo tier, no daily limit) plus early access to new features, limited-edition swag, featuring on Resend's official channels, direct access to founders/DX/engineering teams, and a private builders community.
findings.eligibility: Application-based, 'Resend's most invested users': content creators (blogs/videos), power users who improve docs, open-source contributors. No .edu, funding, or age requirements. No credit card required. First cohort is described as a small, selective group — acceptance is not guaranteed.
findings.claim: 1) Open resend.com/insiders. 2) Fill out the application form (name, email, city/country, languages, motivation, technical skills; GitHub and X/Twitter optional). 3) If selected for the cohort, the Pro subscription and perks are granted.
findings.expiry: No stated term, renewal, or end date. Perks appear to last while the person remains an Insider; no public re-application cycle.
findings.gotchas: Selective — most applicants will not be accepted. Perks are individual (not company/team-wide volume entitlements like the YC deal). No credit amounts, usage caps, or sunset date are published. Do not confuse with the discontinued open startup program.

sunset_notes: No education/student offer: Resend's pricing FAQ explicitly states 'We do not offer education pricing' — no .edu-based license or student discount exists (as of 2026-10-22). No free trial either: the FAQ answers 'No, but we provide a free-forever plan.' Open startup program sunset: resend.com/startups returns 404 as of 2026-10-22; the only remaining startup offer is the YC deal at resend.com/yc (independently confirmed checked Oct 2026 by third-party directories). 2025-2026 structural changes: pricing was restructured around two tracks — transactional (3,000/mo Free) and marketing Broadcasts (free tier now includes 1,000 marketing contacts, unlimited sends to them); inboxes were added (3 free inboxes; extra inboxes $1/mo on paid plans). An earlier 2024 'New Free Tier' change had cut free domains to 1 and moved multi-region sending to Pro; the current Free plan lists 3 domains. Core limits (3,000/mo, 100/day; Pro $20/50k) were confirmed unchanged by May 28, 2025 price snapshots and today's page. No annual billing or annual discount exists for self-serve plans; a 50% nonprofit discount exists but is not a free offer and outside the students/startups scope. Third-party 'student discount' and 30% promo-code listings (hotdeals.com, paradox.engineer, costbench.com) are unverified and contradict the official FAQ — treat as noise. Fronts note: Resend is email-only (API, SMTP, SDKs, Broadcasts); it has no SMS, push-notification, or chat API, so the SMS/Push/Chat fronts of this task have no Resend offers.

provider: Flagsmith (Bullet Train Ltd) — feature-flags, fronts: Auth, Security, Product Analytics & Feature Flags

findings.name: Free Cloud Plan (permanently free tier)
findings.detail: $0/mo. Up to 50,000 API requests/month; up to 100,000 users in experiments; 1 team member; 1 project; unlimited feature flags; unlimited environments; unlimited identities and segments; API access; fair-usage policy applies. Overage billing 'starts at $50 per million per month and decreases with volume'. Free-plan users who exceed limits get 7 days to upgrade before 'any action is taken'. Verified on official pricing page 2026-10-22: numbers match the known baseline (50k requests; Start-Up $45/mo, $40 annual, 1M requests, 3 members).
findings.eligibility: Anyone, any size/region/education status; self-serve signup ('Start for Free' / 'Get Started!'). No .edu email requirement, no startup age or funding cap, no published region limits. No explicit 'no credit card required' statement appears on the pricing page — signup is account-based; CC requirement unverified.
findings.claim: 1) Go to flagsmith.com/pricing and click 'Get Started!' / 'Start for Free' on the Free tier -> 2) Create an account on app.flagsmith.com -> 3) Use within 50k requests/month and 1 team member. No application, no invoice.
findings.expiry: Permanently available free tier; no stated expiry. Fair-usage policy is the only caveat.
findings.gotchas: Fair-usage policy applies (undefined). No 2FA, no scheduled flags, no A/B & MVT testing, no 3rd-party integrations, no roles/audit logs — all Start-Up or higher. Exceeding 50k requests: 7-day upgrade window, then enforcement; overage pricing from $50/1M. Single team member + single project make it solo-dev, not team, oriented. Credit-card requirement for sign-up not stated on the page.

findings.name: 14-Day Free Trial of paid plans (Start-Up / Scale-Up)
findings.detail: Both Start-Up ($45/mo monthly, $40/mo billed yearly; 1,000,000 requests/mo; 500,000 experiment users; 3 team members; 2FA, A/B & MVT, scheduled flags, integrations, email support) and Scale-Up ($300/mo monthly, $250/mo yearly; 5,000,000+ requests/mo; up to 20 team members, extra members $50/mo; SAML/SSO, governance, audit logs, BYO experimentation warehouse) offer a '14 Day Free Trial' as listed on the pricing page.
findings.eligibility: Open signup; no startup-age or funding criteria stated; no .edu requirement; CC requirement for the trial not stated on the pricing page.
findings.claim: 1) Select Start-Up or Scale-Up on flagsmith.com/pricing -> 2) click the 14-day trial start -> 3) provisionally get full paid-plan features; decide to pay within 14 days or lose access.
findings.expiry: 14 days from trial start; then plan becomes paid at $45/mo (Start-Up) or $300/mo (Scale-Up) unless cancelled/downgraded (downgrade path not stated on page).
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free confusion: the trial is a paid-plan preview, not an extension of the free tier; after 14 days billing presumably starts unless you cancel or switch to the free plan. Overage grace: a paid plan exceeding its request limit (within 200% of limit) for the FIRST time gets a 30-day grace period before billing; Start-Up overage is $7/100k requests. Annual plans: 12 months paid up front.

findings.name: Free self-hosted Open-Source edition (Community build)
findings.detail: Free, 'always open' self-hosted build of the Flagsmith platform under BSD-3-Clause ('one of the most permissive open-source licences available — no restrictions on commercial use'; core repo states 'majority of our platform is open source under the BSD-3-Clause'). Includes unlimited feature flags, segments & targeting (incl. multivariate flags), remote config, server-side evaluation, 15+ open-source SDKs, A/B & MVT testing, kill switches, edge proxy, integrations (Grafana, Slack, Amplitude, New Relic), and NO API request limits on self-hosted deployments. Gated to paid Enterprise: audit logs, role-based access control / change requests / approvals, SAML/SSO, advanced governance, enterprise-grade support, on-prem/air-gapped support and optional on-prem installation.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — students, students' course projects, startups; no .edu email, no CC, no request caps, no team-size caps stated. Self-host on-premises or in your own cloud (GCP/AWS/Azure).
findings.claim: 1) Clone/deploy the open-source Flagsmith stack via Docker or Kubernetes + Helm (charts published by Flagsmith) -> 2) run it on your own infra -> 3) use indefinitely with no flagsmith.com account needed. Enterprise features add via a paid license 'without migrating platforms'.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; 'Core will always be open' per the page; no sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: You own all ops (hosting, updates, backups) — no managed free hosting. Governance/security features (audit logs, RBAC, SSO, change requests) are Enterprise-gated, so startups needing SAML/SSO must pay. Self-hosted MCP Server is 'soon' (not yet available there). License nuance: main repo is BSD-3 per WebFetch; 'a small number of repositories are under the MIT license' — check the specific repo you deploy. No official SLA/support on the free build.

findings.name: Discounted plan for open-source / not-for-profit / charity projects
findings.detail: The pricing FAQ answers the question 'We're an Open Source/Not for profit/Charity project. Do you offer discounts?' with '100% Yes! Please get in touch and we can set you up on a discounted plan.' No discount percentage, no eligibility checklist (no .edu requirement, no startup age, no funding cap) is published — it is a discretionary, contact-gated concession, not a formal program. Related: annual-payment discounts are offered on all plans, and bespoke tiers between Start-Up and Enterprise can be arranged via the contact form.
findings.eligibility: Stated for open-source, not-for-profit, or charity projects (startups doing OSS may qualify). No .edu-email criterion mentioned; education/student-specific licensing does NOT exist — /education, /startup-program and /faq all 404 as of 2026-10-22. No region limits stated.
findings.claim: 1) Go to flagsmith.com/pricing FAQ -> 2) contact Flagsmith (contact-us / sales) describing your project -> 3) receive a custom discounted paid plan. No self-serve application.
findings.expiry: No expiry, renewal or sunset terms published; discount is bespoke per negotiation. Terms (percentage, duration, renewal) are not public.
findings.gotchas: Discount % and plan shape are unpublished — always negotiate in writing. This is NOT an education license: no student/academic tier or .edu requirement exists. The free OSS self-hosted build already gives most of the value for free, so the discount only matters if you want managed cloud + governance features. 'Get in touch' means sales lead time; the free cloud tier and 14-day trial remain the instant paths.

sunset_notes: No formal Flagsmith startup program, student/education license, or trial-credit offer exists as of 2026-10-22 — dedicated pages /education, /startup-program, /faq all return 404; the only concessions are the permanent free tier, 14-day paid-plan trials, the free BSD-3 open-source self-hosted build, and the contact-gated open-source/non-profit/charity discount. Current published figures exactly match the known baseline (Free: 50,000 requests/mo, unlimited flags/environments, 1 team member; Start-Up: $45/mo monthly / $40/mo yearly, 1M requests, 3 members), indicating no material pricing change is visible on the official page today. Caveats: (1) the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so 2025-2026 change history could not be independently verified via search engines — I verified the live official pages only; (2) the Flagsmith blog page (Sep–Oct 2026 posts) shows no pricing-change announcements on its first page; (3) one possible 2025-2026 change: the core repository now advertises a permissive BSD-3-Clause license ('no restrictions on commercial use') where Flagsmith historically used a Business Source License — I could not verify the license-change date (history was not searchable); if the repo was BSL before, that re-licensing is a material, favorable change for commercial self-hosting.

findings.name: Firebase Spark plan — free, no credit card
findings.detail: The free 'No-cost (Spark plan)': Authentication no-cost up to 50,000 MAUs with standard methods (email/password, social, magic link, email link, etc.), and no-cost up to 50 MAUs for SAML/OIDC. Also no-cost on Spark: Analytics, App Check (App Security; quotas/limits vary by attestation provider), A/B Testing, App Distribution, Cloud Messaging, Crashlytics, In-App Messaging, Performance Monitoring, and no-cost usage quotas for paid products (e.g. Firestore 50K reads/20K writes per day, Cloud Functions 2M invocations/mo, Hosting 10GB, RTDB). No stated expiry — free forever. Confirmed on the live pricing page today (2026-10-22).
findings.eligibility: Any new Firebase user. No credit card / payment method required. No .edu email, no region limit stated. Feature Flags is NOT listed as a product on the pricing page (docs URLs 404 — see sunset_notes).
findings.claim: 1) Go to console.firebase.google.com and start onboarding with the Spark option (link purchaseBillingPlan=no-cost), or in an existing project: Project settings → Billing tab → select 'No-cost (Spark plan)'. No payment info entered.
findings.expiry: No expiry (permanent no-cost plan).
findings.gotchas: Exceeding a no-cost allocation shuts that product OFF for the rest of the month across all apps in the project (hard cap, no silent overage billing on Spark). Phone Auth is not part of the free offering on Spark (N/A). SAML/OIDC is only 50 MAUs free — enterprise IdP sign-in quickly costs. No-cost amounts can differ between Spark and Blaze per product.

findings.name: Firebase Blaze plan no-cost tier (pay-as-you-go with free daily quotas)
findings.detail: Blaze shows the same no-cost lines: Authentication 'no-cost up to 50K MAUs' (standard) and 'no-cost up to 50 MAUs' (SAML/OIDC), calculated daily; beyond no-cost, pay-as-you-go. Also adds: Firestore no-cost daily quotas, Cloud Functions no-cost tier, access to paid GCP products (Cloud Run, Pub/Sub, BigQuery streaming), and 'If eligible, get $300 in free credit' via the GCP trial sign-up path.
findings.eligibility: Requires a linked Google Cloud billing account with a payment method (major credit cards or other accepted methods). Not a no-CC offering.
findings.claim: Sign up for Blaze in the Firebase console (link purchaseBillingPlan=metered); create/link a GCP billing account (this auto-upgrades the project to Blaze).
findings.expiry: No expiry for the plan; no-cost usage recalculated daily; pay-as-you-go beyond quotas indefinitely.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required — real billing risk once no-cost usage is exceeded; Phone Auth on Blaze is billed per SMS sent (no longer free). Set GCP budgets/alerts before relying on Blaze.

findings.name: Google Cloud $300 free trial (90 days)
findings.detail: New GCP sign-ups get a $300 welcome credit usable for 90 days, plus access to 20+ always-free products. A valid credit/debit card is required at signup (small temporary authorization hold, not an actual charge). Credits cannot fund Gemini API in AI Studio costs or managed generative-AI partner models; GPUs/TPUs, Cloud Marketplace, Windows Server VMs and VMware Engine are excluded.
findings.eligibility: New customers only: never signed up for the GCP Free Trial and never a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform, or Firebase. No .edu requirement; effectively one trial per person/payment identity.
findings.claim: 1) Go to cloud.google.com/free → create account → add credit/debit card (hold ~$0.00-1.00). 2) $300 credit auto-applies; use 90 days. 3) Before trial ends, upgrade to paid to keep resources; otherwise trial account auto-closes, then a 30-day grace period, after which resources are permanently deleted.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 90 days from signup (kept if you upgrade to paid). Without upgrade: account auto-closes, 30-day grace, then resources permanently deleted.
findings.gotchas: Trial is NOT free-tier: after 90 days (or credit exhaustion on paid resources), standard billing applies — delete unused resources and set budget alerts. Trial credit explicitly excludes Gemini API costs. Docs page last updated 2026-10-20.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program — up to $350,000 GCP credits
findings.detail: Live program (as of the page fetched 2026-10-22): 'Start' tier = $2,000; 'Scale' = 100% up to $250,000 credits in Year 1 + 20% up to an additional $100,000 in Year 2 (up to $350,000 over two years); 'Scale AI' = 100% up to $100,000 in Year 1 + 20% up to $100,000 in Year 2. Includes credits for frontier models (Gemini, Gemma; third-party models billed separately), monthly Google Maps Platform credits, 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus at no extra cost, Startup Success Managers and Customer Engineering support.
findings.eligibility: Scale tiers: verifiable Pre-Seed to Series A funding from a known investor; company founded within the last 3-5 years (tier-dependent). Start tier: founded within the past 2 years, working MVP, clear business model, plans to seek venture funding. Non-VC money (private equity, bank loans, grants, crowdfunding, friends & family) does not qualify for Scale. Excluded: IPO'd/acquired companies, educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs, dev shops/consultancies/agencies, crypto mining. Must be in a region where GCP is GA and self-serve purchasable; AUP must be met.
findings.claim: Apply self-service at cloud.google.com/startups ('Apply now' → 'Apply to the program'): have your 18-character GCP billing account ID ready (credits are issued directly to it); company email domain must match the website domain; active non-AI-generated website required; stealth companies can be referred by their VC/accelerator; Workspace Business Plus is a separate application (domain must not have been on paid Google Workspace within 31 days of applying).
findings.expiry: Credits issued/usable over two years (Year 2 at 20% rate). Program eligibility changes annually; previous participation does not guarantee re-enrollment — re-applications are possible if still eligible. Credits non-transferable, no sharing/reselling.
findings.gotchas: Credits only apply to eligible GCP pay-as-you-go products (not subscription products, not Marketplace/third-party, not Google Workspace/Ads). Acceptance at Google Cloud's sole discretion; rejection is common without VC funding. Do not confuse with the defunct launchcloud.withgoogle.com portal (404).

findings.name: Google for Education — research credits (up to $5,000)
findings.detail: GCP credits grant for research at accredited higher-education / eligible nonprofit research institutions in approved countries: 'Apply for up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits' (stated on cloud.google.com/edu). Credits must be activated within 60 days of the stated project start date, then expire 365 days from coupon redemption or full use, whichever first; non-transferable; may not be used for commercial purposes. No credit card required — but a Google Cloud Billing Account ID must be provided on the application.
findings.eligibility: Faculty, PhD students, and postdoctoral researchers only (job titles on the form). Institutional account email preferred; .edu/.ac domain in practice; limited to the listed approved countries (other countries can only 'express interest'). PhD students qualify on this track; undergrads/taught students do not.
findings.claim: 1) Fill the research-credits form at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research: personal/org details, project proposal (up to 250 words), field of research, expected costs (estimate via the GCP pricing calculator), billing account ID, and a plan for funding after the credits run out. 2) If approved, activate the credit within 60 days of project start.
findings.gotchas: Exact award per application is set at review (cap $5,000); unused credits after 365 days are lost; not available in all countries; 'Institution account preferred' may steer awards to a campus billing account rather than your personal one.

findings.name: Google for Education — teaching credits
findings.detail: GCP credits for faculty teaching with GCP; apply for up to 3 courses per submission; expected course start no later than 1 year from today's date; credits redeemable from approval until 16 weeks after course start and good for up to 1 year after course start; non-transferable and tied to the applicant's email. No dollar amount is published on the page. No credit card requirement stated — it is a grants-style application.
findings.eligibility: Faculty only — students cannot apply directly. Requires an official school email with a valid edu domain. Program limited to a listed set of countries (70+); unlisted countries can only express interest. Only the most recent submission is reviewed.
findings.claim: Fill the teaching-credits form at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching: personal details, institution, up to 3 courses, school email domains, and a faculty-directory profile link; submit and await approval.
findings.expiry: Credits good up to 1 year after course start; must be redeemed by 16 weeks after course start.
findings.gotchas: Per-course dollar amount is not disclosed publicly — check the award email when approved. Faculty-only means it does not help students directly (students can only use the free trial/free tiers or faculty-provisioned classroom projects).

findings.name: Google Cloud always-free tier (20+ products)
findings.detail: Independent of the $300 trial: a set of always-free monthly quotas across 20+ GCP services (the page markets it as 'Google Cloud free tier — explore products with free monthly usage', and 'Google Cloud Free Program — $300 in free credits and 20+ free products'). Typical always-free SKUs include e2-micro compute, Cloud Run requests, Cloud Storage, BigQuery processed/storage allowances, and Cloud SQL free instance. Works alongside Firebase Spark no-cost quotas for Firestore/Hosting/Functions.
findings.eligibility: Any GCP account; no credit card needed for the always-free usage itself. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Create a GCP account; always-free quotas apply automatically to eligible SKUs — no enrollment step.
findings.expiry: Permanent (recurring monthly quotas).
findings.gotchas: Exact per-product quota figures were not verified on the live page today; quotas differ by SKU/region and Google has periodically restructured free-tier SKUs. Free SKUs do not cover everything (e.g., most GPU/TPU shapes are paid).

findings.name: Firebase App Check (App Security) — no-cost on both plans
findings.detail: App Check (bot/attestation protection for Security Rules and API requests) is listed as a no-cost product on both the Spark and Blaze plans: 'No-cost, subject to quotas and limits that vary based on attestation provider'. No credit card needed on Spark. This is the free 'Security' front: security rules + App Check are free; there is no paid security product in Firebase pricing.
findings.eligibility: Any Firebase project; no CC required on Spark; on Blaze a GCP billing account exists but App Check usage itself is no-cost within quotas.
findings.claim: 1) In Firebase console, App Check → register your apps (Android Play Integrity, iOS, Web reCAPTCHA, or DeviceConfig providers). 2) Add corresponding Security Rules enforcement. No separate enrollment or payment step.
findings.expiry: No expiry (permanent no-cost offering).
findings.gotchas: Quotas/limits vary by attestation provider (e.g., reCAPTCHA Enterprise quotas); exceeding them can break app attestation — check per-provider quota limits in the App Check docs.

All Firebase Feature Flags URLs checked today 404 (firebase.google.com/docs/feature-flags, /docs/feature-flags/overview, /docs/feature-flags/pricing, /product/feature-flags, /pricing/feature-flags) and 'Feature Flags' has no line on the official pricing page — the product/doc set appears to have been restructured or sunset out of developer preview; treat as not-free-until-verified. findings.name: Free plan (permanent free tier, Email)
findings.detail: $0/month forever: 6,000 emails/month with a hard cap of 200 emails/day, 1,000 contacts (primary + subaccount combined, exclusion list included). Includes Send API, SMTP Relay, Webhooks (event API), MJML, drag-and-drop Advanced Email Editor, email templates, GDPR subscription forms, basic statistics, form builder, email tracking consent, up to 1 subaccount. Ongoing overages beyond the monthly allowance are billed in 1,000-email blocks; unused credits expire each billing cycle.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, no age/funding limits; no credit card required at sign-up (official FAQ: 'No, there is no credit card required for the free plan at sign up'). No .edu email requirement. Free ticket support only in the first month.
findings.claim: Sign up at mailjet.com (signup page -> pick Free plan). No CC. Then add/validate a sender address or domain and set up SPF/DKIM to send.
findings.expiry: Indefinite — no sunset date on the Free plan. Inactivity policy: re-engagement emails at 2/6/9/12 months of inactivity, 30-day deletion notice at 12 months, permanent deletion at ~400 days of inactivity (all data gone).
findings.gotchas: 200/day cap: excess emails queue up to 3 days then are PERMANENTLY dropped — unusable for time-sensitive sends >200/day. Campaigns can target max 200 recipients at once. Exceeding 1,000 contacts (anywhere in the account, incl. exclusion list) triggers an automatic send hold on both primary and subaccount until trimmed or upgraded. Since Oct 6, 2025 the contact cap dropped to 1,000 and template download (HTML/MJML) is no longer available on Free. No A/B testing, automations, segmentation, landing pages, dedicated IP. Mailjet logo stays in footer.

findings.name: 30-day Free Premium trial (auto on new signups)
findings.detail: Every new account gets Premium features free for the first 30 days: Brand Kit, AI Templates (1 free test), advanced image editor, saved & linked/prebuilt sections, dynamic content, collaboration tools, labels, version history, landing pages (create only, not publish), segmentation, A/B testing, advanced analytics, email automation, bot-activity detection, preference center. NOT in trial: AI Assistant, email validation, custom landing-page domains, inbox email previews, template downloads, account sharing.
findings.eligibility: All new Mailjet signups (students, startups, anyone). No credit card required — after the 30 days you are automatically moved to the Free plan, not billed.
findings.claim: Just sign up at mailjet.com; trial is automatic. Upgrade in-account before day 30 to keep Premium features.
findings.expiry: 30 days from account creation, then auto-downgrade to Free plan (features lock). Existing plan limits still apply during trial: Free-plan accounts keep the 200 emails/day cap during the trial.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: during the trial your sending limits are still those of your plan (200/day on Free), so the trial unlocks features, not volume. Several Premium-only features are unavailable even in trial. The trial is marketing-positioned as 'free premium trial' but the account default is the Free plan — no charge on expiry.

findings.name: Startup program (Premium free-window) — UNVERIFIED third-party claim
findings.detail: Third-party deal aggregator claimstartupgrants.com describes an application-based Mailjet startup program giving qualifying early-stage companies 'an extended stretch of its paid Premium tier at no cost' (headline ~$300 value), with case-by-case approval. No corresponding page exists on mailjet.com or in the Mailjet Help Center (searches for 'startup program' surface only generic startup-marketing landing pages). A similar unverifiable 15%-off-startup/nonprofit code circulates on coupon sites.
findings.eligibility: As claimed by the aggregator: early-stage/startup companies, approval case-by-case via submitted company details. No official eligibility criteria published by Mailjet.
findings.claim: If it exists, per the aggregator you apply through their deal page (subscription-gated promo code + steps). No official Mailjet application flow found.
findings.expiry: Unknown; aggregator lists it as a 2026 deal; no official dates.
findings.gotchas: Not confirmed by any official Mailjet source found today; treat as rumor unless verified directly with Mailjet sales. The reliable startup path is the permanent Free plan + 30-day Premium trial.

findings.name: Education/student license — NOT offered
findings.detail: No student or .edu-based free license/credits exist for Mailjet. Searches of mailjet.com and the Help Center found no education program; the only education-adjacent deal is an unverified ~10% 'student discount' on a coupon site (marketingtools.discount) that claims Mailjet 'isn't known' for reliable codes. findings.eligibility: N/A — no student eligibility criteria published by Mailjet. Non-profit status required for the non-profit discount (not student/education).
findings.claim: N/A for students — use the Free plan / 30-day Premium trial. Non-profits: contact Mailjet support with documentation for the discount.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Don't budget around the rumored 10% student code; it is not corroborated by official sources.

findings.claim: Go to launchdarkly.com/pricing, click 'Get started free' under the Developer plan, create an account (email/password or SSO); no credit card asked; SDKs immediately usable in one project.
findings.detail: LaunchDarkly Developer plan: $0/mo, 'forever'. Limits read today from the official pricing page: unlimited feature flags; unlimited seats (no per-seat pricing); 1 project and 3 environments; 5 service connections; 1K client-side MAU/mo; 10M logs + 10M traces/mo; 5K session replays and 5K errors/mo (ingestion stops at 5K, no overage billing on this tier); 100K experimentation MAU/mo at no charge; 5,000 AgentControl AI runs/mo included with 14-day data retention. Docs add: free up to 1,000 users/contexts/mo and 10,000 experiment keys. All plans include SSO/SAML; Developer includes 2FA. No region limits stated. The plan was renamed from 'Personal Use' to 'Developer'.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (individuals, students, startups, teams). No .edu email, no funding/age cap, no credit card required ('No credit card required' shown on the Developer plan). No region limits stated on the page.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal; the Developer tier is free indefinitely. 2025-09-08 terms update does not change the free tier.
findings.gotchas: It's a free tier, not a trial: free forever, but strict caps. Usage beyond caps = ingestion stops (errors/replays), not billed overage. 14-day AgentControl data retention vs 30/100+ on paid tiers. 1 project/3 environments only. In-progress guarded rollouts from a trial complete, but no new guarded rollouts without Enterprise+Guardian. 'No per-seat' means whole team can use it, but the usage caps are account-wide, so a busy team burns 1K MAU / 5 service connections fast. Foundation pay-as-you-go (first 5 service connections included, then $10/SC/mo; $8.33 per 1K client-side MAU/mo; $5 per additional 1K AI runs; billed yearly) is the upgrade path, so plan egress/usage before upgrading.
findings.name: Developer plan (free tier, renamed from 'Personal Use')

findings.claim: Sign up at launchdarkly.com ('Sign up for a free trial'); 14-day trial starts immediately; nothing to do afterward — it auto-converts to the free Developer plan. Optionally upgrade to Foundation/Enterprise during the trial.
findings.detail: 14-day free trial covering 'all of the LaunchDarkly Enterprise and Guardian features'. Official getting-started docs: after 14 days the trial 'automatically converts to a developer tier plan' free up to 1,000 users/contexts/mo and 10,000 experiment keys. Plans docs: no credit card is required for the free Developer tier; the trial itself has no stated card requirement. Enterprise also offers a 'Get Enterprise trial' path on the pricing page.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who can create an account. No .edu, no funding cap, no stated region limits. Trial does not advertise a credit-card requirement.
findings.expiry: 14 days per trial. At expiry the account auto-converts to the free Developer plan (or you upgrade to paid Foundation/Enterprise). Not renewable as a free offer.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free tier: trial includes ALL Enterprise + Guardian features; after conversion those features become read-only — LaunchDarkly retains the data but you cannot interact with it (Guardian guarded rollouts, custom roles revert to base roles, offline Relay Proxy still works but cannot download new flag rules; in-progress guarded rollouts complete, new ones blocked). The free tier's hard caps apply immediately post-trial. You cannot stay on 'Enterprise features for free' — the trial is a 14-day window, not a renewable offer.
findings.name: 14-day free trial (full Enterprise + Guardian features, auto-converts to Developer)

findings.claim: Visit academy.launchdarkly.com, select 'Sign In' → 'Sign Up' (guest account); no payment info is requested. Existing LaunchDarkly customers can use their login instead.
findings.detail: LaunchDarkly Academy (academy.launchdarkly.com): free self-guided courses and public virtual classes, free LaunchDarkly certification, no payment information required at signup, guest accounts available. It is a free education/training resource (not a classroom license for product use): FAQ confirms courses free, no card required. Confidence medium because the official support FAQ page blocked direct fetch (HTTP 403 to bots); content comes from the official support site's FAQ as surfaced today.
findings.eligibility: Open to all (guests, students, educators, partners). No .edu required; no fee. Not an institutional product license: it covers training content, not free classroom SaaS accounts.
findings.expiry: No expiry; account-based, no renewal. Courses reviewed/refreshed quarterly.
findings.gotchas: Free tier covers self-guided content and public virtual classes only; 'private paid-engagements' cost extra. Academy access is separate from the product free tier — you still need the Developer plan for actual flags. Do not share one Academy account among students per FAQ guidance. Third-party 'education discount' entries for LaunchDarkly are unverified templates, not real offers.
findings.name: LaunchDarkly Academy (free training/certification, no payment info)

findings.claim: Not applicable — no current offer found. Verified via launchdarkly.com/pricing and docs 'Subscriptions and plans' (fetched today); /education and /startup return 404; no application path exists on official pages.
findings.detail: No publicly available free student/university license or startup credits program as of 2026-10-22. launchdarkly.com/education and launchdarkly.com/startup both return 404. The official 'Subscriptions and plans' docs and pricing page mention zero education or startup programs; the blog listing has no startup-program posts. LaunchDarkly's only standing free offers are the Developer plan and the 14-day trial. Costbench's 'Education Discount' / 'Startup Program' rows for LaunchDarkly are generic template entries the site itself flags as unverified.
findings.eligibility: n/a — offer does not currently exist
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Any claim of 'LaunchDarkly free startup credits' without an official page is unverified. The de-facto free route for startups/students today is simply the free Developer plan + 14-day trial.
findings.name: Education license / startup program: no active public offer found (pages 404)
