provider: Statsig (feature flags / experimentation / product analytics; now part of the Amplitude family since May 5, 2026)

findings.name: Statsig free tier ("Developer" / free self-service tier)
findings.detail: $0/month, explicitly 'no credit card required'. Includes: 2M Metered Events/month; unlimited flag & config checks; 50,000 session replays/month; unlimited seats; A/B tests, feature flags, product/web analytics, session replays; analytics data retention 1 year; session-replay retention 30 days. Metered Events = exposures + log events + ingested metrics + custom metrics, deduped per user/feature (60-min window on client SDKs, 1-min on server SDKs). The pricing page states ~90% of customers 'start for free'.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — no .edu email, no startup age/funding caps, no application, no credit card, no stated region limits.
findings.claim: Self-serve: click 'Sign up for Free' (console.statsig.com/sign_up) from statsig.com/pricing; the free tier is provisioned immediately. 'Test Drive Now' (console.statsig.com/demo) is a separate demo flow.
findings.expiry: Ongoing/indefinite; no stated end date or renewal conditions. If you exceed 2M events/month you are prompted to add a card to upgrade; if you decline, 'gate and config targeting will continue to work, but Metric Lift computations will stop'.
findings.gotchas: (1) Card prompt only triggers at the 2M event cap; if exceeded, metric-lift/A-B computations degrade while flag serving continues. (2) 'Metered Events' aggregates exposures, log events, ingested + custom metrics, so the 2M allowance burns faster than '2M tracked users' implies. (3) Free tier has 1-year analytics retention and 30-day replay retention (Pro: unlimited analytics, 100K replays/mo). (4) Overages on Pro are billed next period (Jan overages hit Feb invoice) — free tier has no overage billing, just degradation. (5) 'Statsig Lite' in the site nav is NOT the free tier; it is a separate free experiment calculator (see other finding).

findings.name: Statsig Lite (free self-serve experiment calculator)
findings.detail: A free tool, distinct from the platform's free tier: upload two CSVs (an assignments CSV and a metrics CSV, each ≤10MB), name the experiment, and Statsig analyzes the results with its stats engine; results are delivered by email. No account, no platform usage (no flags, no analytics, no replays), no credit card. Sign-up CTAs on the page: 'Sign up for Free' → console.statsig.com/sign_up; 'Test Drive Now' → console.statsig.com/demo.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who provides a business email to receive results. No .edu requirement, no funding caps, no card, no stated region limits.
findings.claim: Go to statsig.com/lite, complete the 4-step flow (upload assignments CSV, upload metrics CSV, name experiment, enter business email); results emailed when ready.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry; no credit card involved; one-shot analysis per upload (CSV size capped at 10MB each).
findings.gotchas: This is only an A/B results calculator, not the feature-flag/product-analytics platform; it cannot replace the free Developer tier for flag serving or dashboards. File-size cap 10MB per CSV. The /lite entry in the site nav is easy to confuse with a free 'Lite plan' — it is not one.

findings.name: Statsig Startup Program
findings.detail: For 12 months: access to all Enterprise-tier features (feature flags, product analytics, experimentation), 1 billion events (page describes this as worth '$50k+'), usable for flags, A/B tests, analytics or any mix, plus Pro-level support (Slack + email, responses by next business day).
findings.eligibility: Company founded <5 years ago; < $50M total funding; 'best suited for companies with over 25K MAU that are scaling fast'. The page's FAQ steers brand-new or small startups to the free Developer tier instead. No .edu requirement (not an education program); selection-based, not auto-approved.
findings.claim: Apply via the 'Apply to Startup Program' button on statsig.com/startups, which submits a Google Form (forms.gle/9toPnV3kkE8skn2T8). Acceptance is at Statsig/Amplitude discretion.
findings.expiry: Benefits last 12 months from program start; afterwards you 'graduate to Statsig's Enterprise Tier, Pro Tier, or Free tier'. No published sunset date for the program itself.
findings.gotchas: The '$50k+' value claim is marketing, not a credit balance. Program eligibility emphasizes funding caps (<$50M) — highly-funded or >5-year-old companies do not qualify. After the May 5, 2026 Amplitude acquisition the page is still live with no stated changes, but Amplitude has not re-announced the program in press materials, so treat continued availability as unconfirmed; the Google Form may have moved. Do not confuse with the free tier: the program targets scaling, VC-backed companies with high event volume.

findings.name: Trial credits / education (student) license
findings.detail: No separate trial-credit offer exists: the pricing page lists no paid trial, no dollar credit, and no time-boxed Pro trial — the free Developer tier is the stated entry point (~90% of customers 'start for free'), and 'Test Drive Now' is a demo console, not a trial. No student/education program exists on statsig.com: /education is a 404, the site navigation and homepage have no student/education entry point, and 'Statsig University' (footer/Resources) is a certification/learning resource, not an .edu discount or free access.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no trial-credit eligibility beyond self-serve free signup; no .edu-email or academic eligibility criteria found anywhere on the official site.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim beyond the free Developer tier signup (console.statsig.com/sign_up) and the Startup Program application for VC-backed early companies.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Absence verified on the official site only (homepage, pricing, nav, /lite, /startups, docs landing, blog) as of 2026-10-22; a web-search sweep of 2025–2026 change history could not be run in this session (search budget exhausted), so off-site announcements (e.g., Amplitude press releases, X posts) were not independently checked.

sunset_notes: 2025–2026 corporate changes: (1) The original Statsig team is now at OpenAI — per Statsig's own announcement blog (statsig.com/blog/statsig-amplitude-phase-1), OpenAI 'walked us through the platform, codebase, operations, and roadmap'; Statsig was acquired by OpenAI in 2025 (date/price not re-disclosed on the official pages I could read). (2) Statsig 'joined the Amplitude family on May 5 (2026)' — the product/company is now maintained by a ~50-person team led by Amplitude's VP of Product Chris Yu; Amplitude says it will keep investing in Statsig, with Phase 1 priorities (governance, AI-native workflows, data-pipeline scale) and Phase 2 deeper Amplitude+Statsig interoperability 'by the end of Q3' 2026. (3) No sunset found: as of 2026-10-22 the official pricing page still shows the free Developer tier (2M events/mo, no card) and the /startups page still offers the Startup Program; no blog post (Oct 2026 archive reviewed) or site notice mentions closing the free tier, the startup program, or any migration/forced-migration. No student/education offer was ever found on the official site. Amplitude's press page shows no Statsig-specific press release in the Oct 2025–Oct 2026 range I could read (load-more not fetchable), so the exact terms of the May 2026 Amplitude deal were not verified from Amplitude's side. Verification caveat: WebSearch was unavailable for the back half of this task (shared session budget exhausted), so claims are based on statsig.com pages fetched today; anything not on those pages (e.g., Google Form status, Amplitude press releases) is marked medium/low confidence.

provider: Mailchimp (Intuit) — email marketing, Marketing/Transactional APIs, SMS

findings.name: Free email plan ("free forever" tier, not a trial)
findings.detail: Official free plan as of 2026-10-22: limit of 250 contacts, max 500 email sends/mo or 250/day; 1 audience, 1 seat; limited pre-built templates, 300+ integrations, popup forms included. Excludes: email scheduling, automation flows, custom/branded templates, dynamic content, role-based access, custom reports, remove-Mailchimp-branding. Email support for first 30 days. If contact or send limit is exceeded, sending is paused (no overage billing on free). The page is region-gated; US and EU variants both show 250/500.
findings.eligibility: Any new user, no .edu or age/funding requirements; account via mailchimp.com sign-up. Sign-up has not required a credit card for the free plan (site does not state CC explicitly for free; medium confidence on this sub-point). Region: available in standard Mailchimp-supported countries.
findings.claim: Sign up at mailchimp.com/signup → Free plan is automatic; nothing to request. Upgrade to Essentials/Standard/Premium when you exceed 250 contacts or 500 sends/mo.
findings.expiry: No expiry — perpetual free tier. Trial support ends at 30 days.
findings.gotchas: This is a free tier, not a trial: no CC, no auto-upgrade. The 250-contact/500-send limit is the post-2025 reduction (older docs said 500 contacts/1,000 sends — that data is now stale). No email scheduling or A/B on free; over-limit sends are paused, not billed. Branding (Mailchimp footer) cannot be removed on free.

findings.name: 14-day free trial of paid Essentials / Standard plans
findings.detail: 14-day free trial of Essentials (US entry $13/mo at 1,500 contacts) and Standard (US entry $20/mo) marketing plans. Eligibility: you must be a new Mailchimp customer OR an existing Free plan customer whose account was created within the last 90 days. Valid payment information (credit card) is required at enrollment. One trial per account; not stackable with other offers. After the trial the plan starts at the paid rate.
findings.eligibility: New customers or free-plan accounts <90 days old; one trial per account; card required up front — so this is NOT no-CC free usage, it is a trial. No education/age/funding caps.
findings.claim: From mailchimp.com/pricing, start the Essentials or Standard trial, provide a card, cancel before day 14 to avoid charge.
findings.expiry: 14 days, then auto-converts to paid subscription at the standard rate; cancel before trial ends to stay free.
findings.gotchas: Credit card mandatory — accounts that are new-eligible and cardless cannot use it. The 90-day age rule on existing free accounts is the main trap. Trial is not stackable; one per account. Marketing plan features (campaign sends, seats) apply; if you only want API/transactional access, Standard is the minimum plan that supports it.

findings.name: Premium plan 1-month free trial (sales-assisted)
findings.detail: Pricing page lists a "Free Trial of Premium for 1 Month" available to qualified new customers, obtained by contacting Sales (premium includes 15% off first 12 months for 10,000+ contacts, unlimited users/audiences, Enterprise SSO, dedicated onboarding specialist). This is separate from and not combinable with the self-serve 14-day Essentials/Standard trial.
findings.eligibility: "Qualified new customers" via Sales — implies new Mailchimp account; card required at conversion. No published eligibility thresholds beyond 'new customer'; region-limited to Sales coverage.
findings.claim: Contact Mailchimp sales from mailchimp.com/pricing (or sales form) and request the 1-month Premium trial.
findings.expiry: 1 month, then Premium at the standard rate (US entry ~$350/mo for the small-contact tier with 15% intro discount; much higher at scale).
findings.gotchas: Sales-gated, not self-serve; do not conflate with the 14-day Essentials/Standard trial; Premium is a large bill at conversion — only worth it if you need predictive segmentation, multivariate testing, SSO, or 200,000+ contact high-volume plan.

findings.name: Transactional Email API (formerly Mandrill): free send credits — and SMS has no free tier
findings.detail: Transactional Email (Mandrill successor): "New users receive up to 500 free email sends to their verified domain" (restrictions apply). Paid pricing is block-based: 25,000-email blocks at $20 (1-500k), $18 (500k-1M), $16 (1M-2M), $14 (2M-3M), $12 (3M-4M), $10 (4M+) — i.e. $0.80 down to $0.40 per 1,000 emails; 50% off 1M+ emails for first 12 months for qualifying new customers; dedicated IP +$29.95/mo. SMS: transactional SMS shares credits with SMS marketing in one pool, credits do not roll over, and a Mailchimp-approved phone number is required; no free SMS quota is listed. No push-notification or chat API product exists in the Mailchimp/Intuit suite reviewed.
findings.eligibility: Transactional Email is an add-on that requires a Mailchimp Standard or Premium marketing plan (or legacy Monthly Plan); Essentials is explicitly ineligible — so the 500 free sends are effectively gated behind a paid marketing plan, not a standalone no-CC free API tier. A verified domain is required for the free sends.
findings.claim: Sign up at login.mailchimp.com/signup/?entrypoint=mandrill, verify your domain, and claim the free 500 transactional sends; purchase 25k blocks as volume grows.
findings.expiry: Free 500 sends are a one-time new-user allowance (per the page's wording); unused purchased blocks expire each billing cycle (no rollover). 50%-off promo: first 12 months.
findings.gotchas: Read 'add-on to Standard/Premium' carefully: you cannot run transactional email on the free marketing plan alone, so the 'free tier' is really 500 credits for new users who will pay for the hosting plan — treat as trial credits, not a permanent free API. SMS and transactional SMS draw from one shared credit pool. No push/chat equivalents to claim.

findings.name: Nonprofit/charity 15% discount (adjacent, not free)
findings.detail: Mailchimp offers a 15% discount to nonprofits and charities. It is a discount on paid plans, not a free tier: sign up free, then contact the Billing team with your username and a link to your organization's website. No .edu/student license or startup program (no /for/students/ or /startups/ page exists — both 404) was found on official pages. There is also a general 'Save 15% on 10,000+ contacts' intro discount for the first 12 months on Essentials/Standard/Premium for businesses at that scale.
findings.eligibility: Registered nonprofits/charities (typically 501(c)(3)-equivalent); applied after a free sign-up. No student or startup program exists to claim — if your goal is a .edu license, there is none.
findings.claim: Create a free account, email Mailchimp's Billing team with username + org website; for the 10k+ intro discount it applies automatically at 10,000+ contacts on the plan's first 12 months.
findings.expiry: Nonprofit discount: ongoing while nonprofit status applies (per Billing team). 10k intro discount: first 12 months; can be kept when moving up a tier.
findings.gotchas: Do not cite Mailchimp as having a student or startup program — none exists on official pages as of 2026-10-22. The 15% figures are discounts, not free usage.

sunset_notes: Major 2025 change: the free email plan's limits were reduced from the previously-known 500 contacts / up to 1,000 emails per month to 250 contacts / max 500 sends per month (250/day) — the live pricing page (US and EU variants) confirms the 250/500 limits as of 2026-10-22, so the "known so far" figure is stale. The Customer Journey Builder was rebranded to Marketing Automation Flows effective June 2025. No student/education (.edu) license program and no startup program exist on official pages (/for/students/ and /startups/ both 404; no program mentions on pricing, developer, or nonprofit pages). No free SMS allowance, and no push-notification or chat API product exists to claim. Transactional Email's free offering is a one-time 500-send new-user allowance gated behind a paid Standard/Premium plan, not a standalone free API tier. One verification gap: this session's web-search budget was exhausted, so corroboration beyond official Mailchimp pages (press posts about the 2025 free-plan reduction, third-party comparisons) was not possible; all facts above come from live official pages fetched today, with the Premium sales trial and the 500-free-sends transactional allowance the only medium-confidence items.

findings.name: Free Plan (standing, no credit card required)
findings.detail: Per official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22): $0/mo, up to 250 active subscribers, 2,500 emails/month, 3 active automations (5 steps each), 3 active forms, 2 user seats, 1 website + 1 landing page, 1 digital product/booking, all 3 email editors, 100+ integrations, MCP for Claude/ChatGPT, knowledge-base support only. Explicitly 'No credit card required'. API/MCP/Webhooks are 'Limited' on Free (no API sending). No stated time limit — standing tier.
findings.eligibility: Anyone worldwide; no credit card required; no .edu or org proof. Region limits not documented on the page.
findings.claim: 1) Go to mailerlite.com and sign up (email-based, no CC). 2) Account lands on Free plan automatically. 3) Import/capture up to 250 subscribers via forms; send up to 2,500 email campaigns/automations per month.
findings.expiry: None — Free plan is a permanent tier, no expiry date documented.
findings.gotchas: Do not use the legacy numbers '1,000 subscribers / up to 12,000 emails/mo' — superseded; current Free is 250/2,500. MailerLite logo remains on email; no report exports, no custom domain permissions, KB-only support. Automation cap is 3 active x 5 steps. API/MCP access is limited on Free and excludes sending.

findings.name: 14-day Premium trial (no credit card required)
findings.detail: Every new MailerLite account gets 14 days to try premium features (Comfort/Power-level features: 50 automations, more forms/sites, paid-plan features). No credit card required. When the trial ends, premium features lock but 'none of your data including subscribers, automations, forms, sites will be removed'. Paid plans start at $12/mo (Comfort, $25/mo Power; annual billing saves 10%).
findings.eligibility: All new accounts; no CC required; no documented region or org limits.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a new account — trial applies automatically, nothing to request. 2) Use premium features for 14 days. 3) If not upgrading, account reverts to Free plan limits.
findings.expiry: 14 days from account creation; then premium features unavailable unless upgraded.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a free tier — after 14 days you drop to Free (250 subs / 2,500 emails/mo) or must pay. Data is retained, not deleted. No CC required at start; upgrade later can add billing.

findings.name: API front: Limited on Free, sending paid-only; no free API credits; no SMS/Push/Chat product
findings.detail: Pricing FAQ: 'Email sending via the API and MCP server is available on paid plans' and 'On Free, API and MCP access is limited and doesn't include sending'. Free users can still make API/MCP/webhook requests (e.g., manage subscribers) within limits. Paid plans from $12/mo. MailerLite's only messaging front is email — no SMS, push, or chat product/API exists, so 'SMS, Push & Chat APIs' fronts have no offer here. API docs at developer.mailerlite.com sit behind login. No free tier of API sending credits exists.
findings.eligibility: API key available on all plans; API sending requires a paid plan (Comfort $12/mo+). No CC required for Free (read/manage only).
findings.claim: 1) Create an API key in the account (see help article 'MailerLite API key, Group ID, and documentation'). 2) Free plan: read/manage endpoints only. 3) To send email via API/MCP: upgrade to paid.
findings.expiry: n/a — follows plan; no credit expiry since no free send credits exist.
findings.gotchas: Do not assume the 2,500 free email sends can be dispatched via API — sending via API/MCP is paid-only. 'Limited' is not quantified on the public page (rate limits live in login-gated docs).

findings.name: No student/education license (verified absence)
findings.detail: No education offer found on the official site: mailerlite.com/education returns HTTP 404; the pricing page and help center index contain no student, educator, or .edu discount of any kind. There is no .edu email requirement or education license to claim — students get only the standard Free plan (250 subs / 2,500 emails/mo).
findings.eligibility: n/a — no program exists.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim; a student should sign up for the standard Free plan.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Absence verified on official surfaces only; this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so a third-party student-discount portal cannot be fully ruled out.

findings.name: No startup program (verified absence)
findings.detail: No startup offer found: mailerlite.com/startup returns HTTP 404; no startup discount, funding cap, or application form on the pricing page or help center. The only discount programs MailerLite documents are: 30% nonprofit discount (proof required, e.g., US IRS certificate or EU government NGO document; only one discount at a time) and 10% off annual billing. A startup simply uses the standard Free plan or paid plans; the nonprofit 30% discount is out of scope for students/startups.
findings.eligibility: n/a — no program exists.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim for startups.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Nonprofit 30% is the closest org-type program but is not free and not for startups/students; discounts don't stack.

findings.name: Adjacency (out of scope): 30% nonprofit discount + 10% annual-billing discount
findings.detail: For completeness: nonprofit organizations get 30% off paid plans — indicate nonprofit status during the approval application and submit proof (US IRS certificate or EU government document) via support. Annual billing saves 10%. 'We can only apply one discount at a time.' Neither is a free offer and neither targets students or startups.
findings.eligibility: Registered nonprofit (US/EU proof); not for students/startups.
findings.claim: Contact support with nonprofit proof; select annual billing.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Not a free offer; single-discount rule; proof required.

sunset_notes: The previously circulated free-tier numbers — 1,000 subscribers and up to 12,000 emails/month — are outdated. MailerLite restructured its plans (old Growth-plan era) so the current Free tier is 250 active subscribers / 2,500 emails/month / 3 active automations, confirmed on the official pricing page on 2026-10-22. No education license, startup program, or free API-send-credit program exists for MailerLite as of 2025-2026; /education and /startup URLs 404 and nothing is mentioned on the pricing or help-center pages. MailerLite has no SMS/Push/Chat front — email only. Caveat: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-research, so absence claims rest on direct inspection of official MailerLite pages (pricing, help index, 404 checks) rather than a full web sweep; a small third-party student-discount listing cannot be completely ruled out.

findings.name: Free Developer plan (permanent free tier, auto-assigned on signup)
findings.detail: Every new Postmark account starts on a free 'Developer' plan: 100 emails/month, $0/mo, no overages allowed on this plan, never expires, no credit card required. Full API/SMTP access, transactional + broadcast message streams, webhooks, analytics. Paid plans start at Basic $15/mo for 10,000 emails (overages $1.80/1k); Pro $16.50/mo ($1.30/1k) and Platform $18/mo ($1.20/1k) for more streams/domains/inbound. Verified directly on the live pricing page today.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; automatic at signup at account.postmarkapp.com. No .edu, no startup status, no card. Sender signature or domain verification (DNS DKIM) required before sending. No published region limits.
findings.claim: Sign up at account.postmarkapp.com → confirm email → verify a sender signature or domain → you are on the free Developer plan automatically; 100 emails/month usable indefinitely.
findings.expiry: No expiry; the plan is permanent. Upgrading requires entering a credit card; downgrading back to free is allowed at end of billing cycle.
findings.gotchas: No overages on the free plan — hitting 100 emails stops sending (unlike paid plans where overages are billed). 100 emails/mo is test-only (~3/day), not viable for production. Postmark is transactional-first: marketing/bulk mail must go through Broadcast streams and mixing marketing content into transactional streams gets accounts suspended. Default data retention 45 days on all plans; custom retention is a paid add-on from $5/mo.

findings.name: Bootstrapper credit — $75 one-time account credit for bootstrapped startups
findings.detail: One-time $75 account credit. Official eligibility: product fully launched, actively charging for it, and no outside investment/funding taken (i.e., strictly bootstrapped — VC/angel-funded startups do NOT qualify). Support FAQ notes the $75 'typically covers your next five payments of $15 each'. Applied to account after support verifies eligibility.
findings.eligibility: Bootstrapped, fully launched, revenue-generating product. No .edu. No funding cap other than 'no outside funding' at all. No age limit published. No region limit published.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for Postmark (lands on free Developer plan). 2) Message Postmark Support stating you are applying for the Bootstrapper credit. 3) Include a link to your live pricing page as proof you charge customers. 4) Support confirms eligibility and applies the $75 credit.
findings.expiry: Rolling, evergreen offer (page live as of 2026-10-22; support article published 2025-11-04 and last updated 2026-10-19). No published expiry date on the credit itself; one-time only. No renewal.
findings.gotchas: No self-serve form — manual via support, vendor discretion on approval. Funded or pre-launch/stealth products are ineligible. ~$75 is only ~5 months of the $15/mo Basic plan. Postmark does not offer annual plans or invoices/PayPal — credit sits against monthly card billing.

findings.name: Friend & Family referral — both accounts get one month free
findings.detail: Any paying Postmark customer can refer another paying customer; when verified, each account receives one month of Postmark usage for free. Claimed by messaging support with the referred (or referring) account's email address. Both accounts must be active paying customers and the referral must be genuine (no duplicate/fake accounts).
findings.eligibility: Both parties must be paying Postmark customers; no .edu or startup-age requirements.
findings.claim: Existing paying customer messages Postmark Support including the email address of the referred account (or the account they were referred by); support applies the free month to both accounts after verification.
findings.expiry: Rolling; no deadline published. One free month per verified referral.
findings.gotchas: Requires paying accounts on both sides — not a free on-ramp for new users. No published cap on how many referrals one user can make.

findings.name: Legacy free signup credits (25,000 credits) and old time-boxed trial server — retired
findings.detail: Historically new signups received 25,000 free credits on the credit-based plan, and Postmark previously ran a time-boxed free trial server (the 'known' ~100,000-emails trial). Both are gone: credit-based plans were retired effective July 5, 2023, and no time-boxed trial appears on the current pricing/docs — the FAQ now describes the 'trial with no expiration date' as the free Developer plan (100 emails/mo).
findings.eligibility: n/a — no longer claimable.
findings.claim: n/a.
findings.expiry: Credit-based plans retired 2023-07-05; legacy customers were migrated to monthly plans. Current model (as of 2026-10-22) = permanent 100-email/mo Developer plan + $75 Bootstrapper credit.
findings.gotchas: Old third-party pages comparing Postmark to competitors may still quote 100k-email trials or 25k signup credits — ignore those; they predate the current pricing model. Also note postmark.com now 301-redirects to postmarkapp.com (domain/branding change post-ActiveCampaign acquisition).

sunset_notes: No student/education offer exists: no .edu discount, education license, or student plan anywhere on postmarkapp.com; /for/education returns 404. No SMS, Push, or Chat API front: Postmark's current product is email delivery only (SMTP + REST, transactional and broadcast streams, inbound email) — the pricing page and docs list no SMS/Push/Chat products, so no free offers on those fronts. Sunset/change notes for 2025-2026: (1) The legacy free 25,000 signup credits (credit-based plans) were retired 2023-07-05 — still a 'legacy' footnote in docs but no longer offered. (2) The time-boxed trial-server model previously known (~100k emails, no card) is no longer published; it has been replaced by the permanent free Developer plan (100 emails/month, no expiry, no card) — the exact old duration/limits of the trial server (3 months vs the ~6 months in our notes) could not be confirmed on current official pages. (3) Bootstrapper $75 credit is unchanged through the 2025-11-04 support-article publication and 2026-10-19 update. (4) Domain rebrand: postmark.com 301-redirects to postmarkapp.com. Caveats: web-search budget was exhausted mid-task, so absence-of-education-offer and absence-of-SMS/Push/Chat rest on the official pricing page, 404 check, and the home page's explicit 'email delivery via SMTP and REST' positioning rather than exhaustive site crawl; the Friend & Family finding was read from an official support FAQ snapshot, not fetched directly today.

provider: Loops (official site loops.so; operating company Astrodon Corporation, YC W22) — email API/platform (marketing + transactional + workflows) for software companies. IMPORTANT: the task's starting URL https://loops.com/pricing/ is a DIFFERENT company: loops.com now 301-redirects to Loopsbeauty.com (beauty e-commerce). Loops also does NOT offer SMS or push/chat channels — email only — so the task's "SMS, Push & Chat" fronts have no free offer here.

findings.claim: Self-serve, no application. 1) Sign up free at app.loops.so/register ("Start for free" CTA on loops.so/pricing); no credit card required. 2) Create/verify a sending domain (Loops generates MX/SPF-TXT/DKIM records, Settings -> Sending domain). 3) Generate an API key (Settings -> API) and send via REST API/SDKs, or build campaigns/workflows in the dashboard. No student/startup verification, no .edu email required, no startup age/funding cap, no region limits stated.
findings.detail: Free plan at $0: unlimited contact storage; up to 4,000 total marketing AND transactional sends combined per rolling 30-day window, delivered to your first 1,000 subscribed contacts; rate limit 10 emails/second (over-limit emails queued, not rejected); all features included (campaigns, workflows, transactional API); "Powered by Loops" footer branding on free emails; no per-seat fees (unlimited team seats); a person can belong to up to 3 free teams. Official pricing-page footnote: "Free stores unlimited contacts and includes 4,000 total marketing and transactional sends per rolling 30 days to your first 1,000." Docs (loops.so/docs/account/billing): free plan available to anyone with fewer than 1,000 subscribed contacts; "You can stay on the free plan indefinitely." Marketing copy: "A free tier that doesn't expire." No changes to this free tier in the 2025-2026 window; the last change was 2024-12-10 when the free plan doubled from 2,000 to 4,000 sends/month and transactional sends became free/included on all paid plans.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no region limits stated). No credit card required: "Loops is free to start, with no credit card required." Free plan requires fewer than 1,000 subscribed contacts.
findings.expiry: Never expires - no time limit on the free plan. Persists while under 1,000 subscribed contacts; passing 1,000 does not lock the account or stop contact uploads, but campaign/workflow sends to contacts beyond the first 1,000 are restricted (transactional sends keep working within the 4,000 pool). You are prompted to upgrade past 1,000. Paid plans are never auto-downgraded to Free; to leave a paid plan, cancel from the Billing page (app.loops.so/settings?page=billing), which returns you to Free. Contact count changes can take up to 24h to reflect.
findings.gotchas: (1) The 4,000-send rolling-30-day pool is SHARED by marketing and transactional email - password resets, OTPs and receipts spend the same budget as campaigns, and a heavy launch week keeps counting for 30 days afterward. (2) Only your first 1,000 subscribed contacts receive campaign/workflow email; extra contacts are stored free but don't get those sends. (3) 10 emails/sec on Free vs 1,000/sec paid; over-limit emails queue. (4) "Powered by Loops" footer remains on free emails. (5) Max 3 free teams per person - join more only by upgrading one team or deleting/leaving a team. (6) Ambiguity: the official footnote says "first 1,000" while several Oct-2026 third-party articles describe it as the "1,000 newest" contacts - verify in-product which contacts actually receive sends past 1,000. (7) No trial credits, no student/education license, and no startup program exist; the paid-plan "Start for free" CTAs simply land you on this same free plan (Growth starts at $49/mo, priced by subscribed contacts). (8) Loops is email-only - no SMS or push offered, so nothing free on those fronts.
findings.name: Loops Free plan - permanent free tier ($0; called "Early Stage" in some third-party/marketing copy)

sunset_notes: URL correction: https://loops.com/pricing/ no longer belongs to the email provider - loops.com 301-redirects to Loopsbeauty.com (beauty retailer, verified 2026-10-22); the email API provider's pricing is at https://loops.so/pricing. Disambiguation: on 2026-10-12 Salesforce/Tableau announced a definitive agreement to acquire an UNRELATED analytics company also named "Loops" (loops.ai, AI KPI analytics, CEO Tom Laufer) - not this email provider (Astrodon Corp); do not conflate. No student/education offers, startup programs, or trial-credit programs exist for Loops (email) as of 2026-10-22; none were sunset either (none ever advertised). The only material free-offer change on record: 2024-12-10, when the free plan doubled from 2,000 to 4,000 sends/month and transactional email became free/included on all paid plans (previously metered at $1 per 2,000 transactional sends). No 2025-2026 changelog entry touched free-tier limits (2025-2026 entries - split testing, Guardian, double opt-in, Workflows, Goals, CLI/Skills, ChatGPT listing - were feature releases only). The permanent free tier above remains the only genuine free offer from this provider.

provider: SendPulse (multichannel: Email, SMS, Web Push, Chatbots, CRM, Transactional/SMTP)

findings.name: Email Marketing Free Plan (free-forever)
findings.detail: Free tier: up to 500 subscribers, up to 15,000 emails/month, 3 sender addresses, 250 MB image storage, 5 automated flows (50 elements/flow, 1 event), 100 email-address verifications, multichannel subscription forms, full analytics, integrations (Make, Zapier, WordPress, Shopify, Creatio), API and webhooks. 24/7 email/help-desk support; live chat support only 30 days from registration. Paid entry: Standard $9.60/mo billed annually. Correction to the 'known so far' note: the cap is 500 subscribers (not 15,000); 15,000 is the monthly email volume, not a 150/day figure.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, worldwide; no student or startup requirement. Single-user plan (no team seat on Free).
findings.claim: Sign up at sendpulse.com: 'Create a free account. No credit card required.' Free plan is the default plan automatically on the account; nothing to activate. No CC, no phone required.
findings.gotchas: Free-tier emails carry SendPulse branding; no A/B testing, no scheduled sending, no payment processing in emails, no reengagement emails, no tags/dynamic segmentation. As of Sep 2025: max 5 mailing lists, only the default subscription-confirmation (double opt-in) template, and no new custom tracking domains (existing ones grandfathered). Chat support drops off after 30 days; email support remains.
findings.expiry: Permanent free plan; no expiry. Support window: 30 days of live chat from registration.

findings.name: Transactional Email / SMTP Free Tier
findings.detail: Separate free meter: 12,000 transactional emails/month, 50 emails/hour, 2 authenticated domains, DKIM/SPF/DMARC records, SMTP relay and API sending. 'On the SMTP Test plan, you can add 1 authenticated domain' — free test entry before the free plan. No time-boxed trial; this is the ongoing free (Basic) tier.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no CC required ('No credit card required' on the SMTP pricing page).
findings.claim: Create account (no CC) and use SMTP/API under the free Basic plan automatically. Paid: Pro 100k/mo $59.88/mo billed annually; pay-as-you-go from $15 per 10,000 emails (valid 12 months).
findings.gotchas: Free SMTP is throttled to 50 emails/hour and free-plan emails must be <=1 MB; separate meter from the 15,000-email bulk campaign free tier — you pay for both meters if you use both. 30-day chat support only.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; no expiry.

findings.name: Web Push Notifications Free (Basic) Plan
findings.detail: Free Basic web-push plan: up to 10,000 push subscribers, unlimited web push notifications, HTTP/HTTPS support, RSS-to-push, automated message series, personalized messages. No credit card required; 30 days of chat support.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a website/app; no student or startup requirement.
findings.claim: Sign up for free (no CC) at sendpulse.com and add the web push tool to your account; Basic is the default free tier. Pro: $24/mo ($19.20/mo billed annually) for 30,000 subscribers.
findings.gotchas: Free plan is branded; 10k-subscriber cap; no API access, segmentation, A/B testing or Automation 360 integration on free; chat support ends at 30 days.
findings.expiry: Permanent free plan; 30-day chat-support window only.

findings.name: Chatbot Builder Free (Basic) Plan
findings.detail: Free Basic chatbot plan (messenger bots: Facebook, Telegram, etc.): up to 500 subscribers, up to 10,000 messages/month across all bots, 3 chatbots, 10 variables, 10 triggers, unlimited flows, limited API access, premade templates. No credit card required.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no student or startup requirement.
findings.claim: Sign up free (no CC); chatbot tool's Basic plan is the default free tier. Pro from $9.60/mo billed annually removes message caps.
findings.gotchas: Message caps are shared across all 3 bots; WhatsApp/Viber campaign sends are billed at operator rates and are excluded from grants; 30-day chat support only.
findings.expiry: Permanent free plan; 30-day chat-support window only.

findings.name: CRM Free Plan
findings.detail: Free SendPulse CRM: account owner plus up to 4 invited users, up to 2 sales pipelines, up to 2 boards.
findings.eligibility: Anyone on a SendPulse account; no CC required to create the account.
findings.claim: Available in-account on the free tier automatically (documented in SendPulse's official knowledge base, 'Pricing plan basics').
findings.gotchas: Documented in the knowledge base rather than the main pricing page; limits are small (4 team users, 2 pipelines/boards).
findings.expiry: Permanent free plan; no expiry.

findings.name: SMS Free Trial (10 test SMS) — pay-as-you-go model
findings.detail: No free SMS plan or subscription: bulk SMS is pure prepaid pay-as-you-go ('There are no pricing plans for the SMS service'). New signups get 10 test SMS free ('Sign up and send 10 test SMS for free!'). Per-message rates per country (e.g. US $0.024, DE $0.086, PL $0.031; 200 countries). Optional SMS Bot add-on: $3.50 setup + $3.50/mo + $0.024 per outgoing message.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no credit card required to register (prepaid top-ups accept Visa/Mastercard/PayPal).
findings.claim: Register (no CC) and click 'Add funds'; the 10 free test SMS are available to new accounts for evaluation.
findings.gotchas: After 10 test messages, every SMS costs money — it is a trial sample, not an ongoing free tier. SMS marketing is explicitly excluded from the startup grant. SMS Bot add-on has separate recurring costs.
findings.expiry: 10-SMS trial is one-time on registration; prepaid funds expire per SendPulse policy (12 months for purchased email credits; SMS top-ups similar).

findings.name: Startup Program: $5,000 Credit Grant ('Offer for Startups')
findings.detail: SendPulse startup grant: $5,000 in SendPulse marketing credits loaded into the account's bonus balance, usable for any SendPulse tool over 12 months, EXCEPT email verifier, SMS marketing, and WhatsApp/Viber campaigns. Review takes 1-3 business days; unused credits expire after the year. No funding cap, headcount cap, or region limit is stated on the page (team size is collected as a form field: <5 to >50). Accelerators/startup hubs have a partner channel (inquiries ok@sendpulse.com).
findings.eligibility: All four required: (1) launched within the past 3 years; (2) offers an innovative product; (3) NOT an eCommerce project/online business; (4) no history of using paid SendPulse plans. No .edu or student criterion. No credit card required for signup or the grant form.
findings.claim: Submit the form at sendpulse.com/startup: startup name, website, applicant name, team size, country of registration, SendPulse account email, optional accelerator, short comment. 1-3 business day review, then the $5,000 is credited to your bonus balance.
findings.gotchas: The $5,000 is marketing-tool credit, not cash or a discount — it buys SendPulse services only and does not cover SMS marketing or WhatsApp/Viber. The 3-year company-age rule excludes most funded/later-stage startups; eCommerce is explicitly excluded. Unused balance is forfeited at the 12-month mark. Page carries 2026 copyright; no announced 2025-2026 changes to amount or terms.

findings.name: Brevo Free plan (free forever): 300 emails/day + up to 100,000 contacts, no credit card, no time limit
findings.detail: Confirmed as of 2026-10-22 from the official help-center article 'About Brevo's pricing plans' (id 208589409, fetched today via API) and the pricing page FAQ. Limits: 300 email sends/day (reset daily; unused sends do NOT roll over); up to 100,000 stored contacts; 1 marketing seat / 1 user; marketing automation limited to 2,000 unique contacts entering active automations; 50 open deals, 1 pipeline, 1 connected calendar/inbox, 1 deal currency (free sales features); basic reporting only; 'Sent with Brevo' sticker cannot be removed; 2 languages; email support; outbound webhooks; Aura AI assistant. Included API/transactional surface: transactional emails and SMS are part of the Free plan (same 300/day cap; once the daily cap is hit, up to 1,000 extra transactional emails wait in a retry queue, then dropped; campaigns to >300 recipients deliver 300/day and require manual Requeue). SMS campaigns exist on Free but SMS messages are a paid add-on (credits sold separately; prepaid SMS/WhatsApp credits 'never expire'). Web/mobile push notifications, landing pages, A/B testing, popups, WhatsApp, dedicated IPs, sales workflows, Instagram DM/Facebook Messenger, and phone support are NOT in the Free plan (official FAQ lists them as excluded).
findings.eligibility: Anyone worldwide — individuals, solopreneurs, students, startups. No .edu email, no company-age or funding requirement, no region limit. Credit card NOT required (pricing page FAQ: 'No. We only need your email address to sign up'). Must pass account verification and sender (DKIM/domain) approval before the 300/day sending limit unlocks.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at brevo.com (email only, no card) — you land on the Free plan automatically. 2) Verify your account and authenticate a sending domain (SPF/DKIM). 3) Import up to 100,000 contacts; send up to 300 emails/day (marketing or transactional). 4) Use SMTP/REST APIs on the same account for transactional email; SMS requires purchasing message credits.
findings.expiry: No expiry — 'completely free forever... no time limit' (official). CAVEAT: Free plan accounts with no use for 4 months are automatically DELETED (official help-center article 'About the deletion of inactive Free plan accounts'), with 4 email reminders at 30/15/7/1 day before; data is unrecoverable. Any automated activity (automations or transactional sends) counts as 'active' and prevents deletion. Paid-plan accounts are exempt.
findings.gotchas: The 'trial' of Brevo IS the free plan — Brevo explicitly answers 'Can I try Brevo before purchasing a plan?' by pointing to the automatic Free plan (no time-boxed trial exists for paid plans). Branding sticker always on. Campaigns >300 recipients take multiple days to reach everyone. Daily cap blocks same-day rescheduling. 'Sent with Brevo' + basic stats only. 4-month inactivity deletion of free accounts (GDPR) — export data first. SMS/WhatsApp/WhatsApp-verified numbers cost real money; the free plan includes the channel only, not the messages.
