Historical context (SaasTrack price history, third-party but consistent with Ably's 2024 plan restructure): on 2024-06-18 Ably removed the old 'Developer', 'Self Service', and 'Enterprise' plans and introduced the current Free ($0), Standard ($29), Pro ($399) structure — the old Developer plan (3M->4.8M messages/mo in 2022) is what older sources cite. (2) 2025-2026 changes: Standard/Pro billing model churn (tiered<->flat flips recorded around 2025-08-06, 2025-10-12, 2025-12-05, both flat $29/$399 as of the 2026-04-11 snapshot); the Free package limits shown on the official site as of 2026-10-22 are 6M messages/mo, 200 conc. connections, 200 conc. channels, 500 msg/s. (3) No sunset of the Free package found; no official startup program or education license exists as of 2026-10-22 (ably.com/startups and ably.com/education both 404), so nothing was closed in 2025-2026 that I could confirm — the $500-credit entries in aggregators appear to be third-party listings, not an Ably official program. Caveat: the shared session web-search budget was exhausted mid-task, so 2025-2026 change detection relied on official page fetches plus one search that surfaced SaasTrack/aggregator history; a second search pass could not run.

findings.name: Pusher Channels — Sandbox free tier
findings.detail: Free, no time limit, self-serve. Limits: 200,000 messages/day and 100 concurrent connections, Standard support, Functions included. A 'message' = every API publish received plus one delivery to each connected client (one publish to 50 subscribers = 51 messages), so fan-out burns the daily quota fast. A 'connection' = one live user; how many channels that user subscribes to does not increase the count. Next paid tier is Startup at $49/mo (1M msgs/day, 500 CC).
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone — no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no application, no stated region limits. Free sign-up from the dashboard; the official page does not state a credit card is required, and the third-party tracker freetier.wiki (checked 18 Oct 2026) records 'Card required: No', hard cap: no, resets: daily.
findings.claim: Create a Pusher account (dashboard.pusher.com), create a Channels app in the dashboard, copy app_key/app_secret from App Keys — the app starts on the free Sandbox plan with no application or approval step.
findings.expiry: No expiry or duration limit; it is an always-free tier. Upgrade/downgrade/cancel at any time from the dashboard, prorated by day. Pusher emails you when you approach plan limits; the page says plans have 'headroom for spikes' but does not publish a hard overage rate or cut-off behavior (the legal quotas page says hard limits are enforced and apps can be disabled for failing to upgrade).
findings.gotchas: Daily (not monthly) caps: 200k msgs/day can mean up to ~6.2M/month but a single busy day can exhaust the quota. The known-earlier figure of '~5,000 channel pushes/month' is the pre-2023 old free plan and no longer exists. No SLA on free tier (SLAs only for select enterprise customers). Standard support only. 'Startup' on this page is a paid tier name ($49/mo), not a startup program. Free tier is for prototypes/low-traffic; the next step is $49/mo flat (no usage metering — plans are ceilings, overages rate-limit rather than bill).
findings.source_url: https://pusher.com/channels/pricing/ (official page read 2026-10-22; corroboration: https://freetier.wiki/services/pusher/, https://pusher.com/legal/quotas/)

findings.name: Pusher Beams — Sandbox free tier (mobile/web push)
findings.detail: Pusher Beams (the push-notification product covering iOS/Android/web push; Pusher itself has no email or SMS offering — the footer notes Pusher is part of MessageBird, whose separate product covers email/SMS). Beams free Sandbox: up to 1,000 subscribers, Standard support. Next paid tiers: Startup $29/mo (10,000 subscribers), Pro $99/mo (50,000), Business $199/mo (115,000), Premium $399/mo (250,000).
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone; 'Sign up for free' via the dashboard, no application. No .edu requirement or stated region limits. The official page does not state whether a credit card is required for the free tier.
findings.claim: Create a Pusher account and create a Beams app in the dashboard; it runs on the free Sandbox plan (1,000-subscriber cap) with no trial-approval step.
findings.expiry: No stated duration limit on the free tier; the cap is a standing subscriber ceiling (1,000 registered device/subscriber tokens), not a monthly send allowance. No per-plan message/throughput caps are published on the page.
findings.gotchas: 1,000 is a subscriber (device-token) cap — once you have 1,000 registered subscribers you must pay $29/mo even if send volume is tiny. No trial of the paid tiers is listed. The '$29 Startup' Beams tier is a flat plan name, not a startup program.

findings.name: No trial credits, startup program, or education license found (negative finding)
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22: (1) No free trial of the paid Channels/Beams plans is listed on any official page (third-party pricing checks list 'Free trial: None listed'). (2) No startup program: pusher.com/startups/ returns 404; 'Startup' is only the name of the entry paid tier on both Channels and Beams. (3) No education/student license: pusher.com/education/ returns 404; no student program or .edu discount is mentioned on the Channels or Beams pricing, product, or docs pages read today.
findings.eligibility: n/a — absence of offers. Both Sandbox free tiers above are the only free offers and are open to students and startups on the same terms as anyone else.
findings.claim: n/a
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: The session's shared WebSearch budget was exhausted, so this negative result rests on the official pages fetched today (pricing/product/docs, plus 404 checks of /startups/ and /education/) and search-result snippets already retrieved, not on exhaustive site-wide search.

sunset_notes: 1) The old Pusher Channels free plan (~5,000 channel pushes/month, ~100 concurrent connections — the figure in the 'known so far' note) was retired when Pusher introduced the quota-based Sandbox plan (announced 20 Jan 2023, https://pusher.com/blog/pushers-sandbox-plan/): 200,000 messages/day + 100 concurrent connections, free, no card. It is not the same as the old monthly-pushed figure (200k/day ≈ up to 6.2M/month). 2) The Channels pricing lineup changed on 2026-03-26 per PulseSignal's pricing history ('Plan removed / pricing unit changed'); the page as read today lists 8 fixed tiers (Sandbox, Startup $49, Pro $99, Business $299, Premium $499, Growth $699, Plus $899, Growth Plus $1,199) + Enterprise; the specific plan removed on that date could not be confirmed from official sources today. 3) No 2025-2026 sunset of any free offer was found: both Sandbox free tiers (Channels 200k msgs/day + 100 CC; Beams 1,000 subscribers) are live on the official pages as of 2026-10-22. 4) No dedicated Pusher education, student, or startup-credits program exists at the URLs checked; Pusher (a London company, part of MessageBird per its own footer) has no email/SMS product of its own — email/SMS would come from the MessageBird/Infobip side, outside Pusher's free offers.

provider: Stream (getstream.io) — Chat (plus Feeds, Video & Audio, AI Moderation); fronts: in-app chat, push notifications (APNs/FCM/Web Push), Webhooks. No email/SMS front.

findings.name: Free 'Build' tier for Chat (always-free developer tier)
findings.detail: Read on the live official pricing page today (2026-10-22). Build = $0/mo, 'No Credit Card Required', 'Makers get higher limits' cross-note. Includes: 1,000 MAU/month, 100 concurrent connections, up to 1M total API calls/mo, up to 100K Query-Channel calls/mo, up to 10 GB API bandwidth/mo; all core Chat features (1:1 DM, group channels, threads, reactions, presence, offline support, push notifications, URL enrichment, Giphy, polls, basic moderation, global edge network) with Community Support. Paid plans for comparison: Start $399/mo (annual) / $499 monthly for 10K MAU; Elevate $599/mo (annual) / $675 monthly.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, no application, no .edu requirement, no startup age/funding caps, no credit card required, no stated region limits. Just sign up.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at getstream.io (email, Google or GitHub). 2) Create a Chat app in the dashboard. 3) Build tier is the default; nothing further to activate. Can build immediately.
findings.expiry: No expiry; renews monthly; hard caps — exceeding them requires upgrading (or a Maker Account), no auto-billing occurs without a paid plan. Overage rates when on paid plans: MAU $0.09/user, concurrent $0.99, stored messages $5.00/1M, channels $100/1M, API calls $7/1M, QC calls $2.50/100K, API bandwidth $0.40/GB, CDN $0.17/GB egress / $0.07/GB storage.
findings.gotchas: The previously-known free dev tier (up to 50K MAU / 1M messages/mo) no longer exists — live page caps the free tier at 1,000 MAU (50x cut) and storage/channel limits are 'Limits Apply' (hard caps, not published numeric overage on Build). Build excludes multi-tenancy/Teams, SAML/SSO, HIPAA, AI moderation, campaigns, auto-translation. Push delivery itself is included, but you must wire your own APNs/FCM credentials and third-party egress can add CDN bandwidth cost. Free tier is community support only.

findings.name: Maker Account — free 'startup program' for small teams ($100/mo free credit for makers)
findings.detail: Read on the live official maker page today (2026-10-22): 'Stream is free/gratis/complimentary' when you meet all requirements. What you get: Chat — modified Start Plan with ALL Start capabilities but capped at 2,000 MAU and 100 concurrent connections; Activity Feeds — Start Plan; Video & Audio — Build Plan; AI Moderation — Pay-as-you-go with $100 monthly credit; Vision Agents — open source; 'Hard limits - no surprise bills'. Page warns 'availability is limited'. Blog (updated 2025-08-19) adds older concrete figures: Chat 2,000 MAU/mo, Feeds 125K API calls/mo, Video 333K participant-minutes/mo, AI Moderation $100 credits, no credit card required.
findings.eligibility: All three: five or fewer team members; less than $100k in funding (cumulative raised); less than $10k/month revenue. No .edu or student requirement (solo students qualify as <=5-person 'companies'); no credit card required; no stated region limits, but slots are 'limited' (first-come/availability, not guaranteed).
findings.claim: 1) Create a Stream account (or new account along the way). 2) Sign in to the Stream dashboard and open getstream.io/maker-account ('Apply Now' routes to dashboard login with ?next=/maker-account). 3) Fill out the brief application form. 4) You can start building immediately while it is reviewed; a 30-day free trial auto-activates and converts to the Maker Account on approval.
findings.expiry: No published expiration or renewal cycle; benefits are tied to continuing eligibility (team size, funding, revenue). If the company grows past the caps, the free status no longer applies and a paid plan is expected. 30-day trial bridges application review.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free confusion: during review you run on a 30-day trial, not the maker account, until approval. The modified Chat Start plan keeps only 100 concurrent connections even though MAU doubles to 2,000 — heavy real-time apps will hit the concurrent cap fast. Hard limits mean no overage billing but also no headroom. 'Availability is limited' means approval is discretionary; $100 moderation credit is per-month, not a lump sum; after the credit, AI Moderation is pay-as-you-go.

findings.name: 30-day free trial of paid plans (no credit card)
findings.detail: Stream's maker-account blog (updated 2025-08-19) states: applying 'will automatically activate a 30-day free trial (no credit card required) that will be converted to the Maker Account upon approval.' The case-study corpus (e.g., Student+, 2020) also references a Stream 'trial period' for paid products. The dedicated /chat/trial/ URL now 301-redirects to the dashboard signup (dashboard.getstream.io/signup/?product=chat), so the trial is claimed through signup rather than a standalone trial page.
findings.eligibility: Any new Stream account; no credit card required per the official blog; no .edu requirement; no stated region limits.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at getstream.io / dashboard.getstream.io. 2) The 30-day trial of the product plan starts on sign-up/application. 3) On trial end, either the account converts to an approved Maker Account (if eligible) or moves to a paid plan / free Build tier.
findings.expiry: 30 days from activation; converts to Maker Account upon application approval. No auto-renewal stated for the trial itself.
findings.gotchas: The live marketing pages I read today (pricing, maker) no longer print '30-day trial' language, so the duration comes from the official blog (Aug 2025) rather than a page re-read today — hence medium confidence. Trial != free forever: post-trial you are expected to either be approved for the Maker Account or pay. Credit-card-free claim is stated for the maker/trial path; paid plans generally require payment on checkout.

findings.name: Student / education license: none exists
findings.detail: No .edu-based student program, education discount, or academic license was found on Stream's official pages as of 2026-10-22. The ed-tech solutions page is sales-oriented (for education companies, 'a member of our sales team will be in touch'). Students effectively use the same offers as everyone else: the free Build tier (1,000 MAU) or the Maker Account (students/solo builders qualify: <=5 people, <$100k funding, <$10k/mo revenue). Stream's own June 2025 case study describes a university student shipping an award-winning app on 'free Stream chat APIs' via a plain free account.
findings.eligibility: N/A — not a distinct offer. Students access the free Build tier (no eligibility) or the Maker Account (same startup/maker caps; no .edu required).
findings.claim: N/A — use the Build tier signup or the Maker Account application (dashboard -> getstream.io/maker-account).
findings.expiry: N/A — follows the underlying Build tier (no expiry) or Maker Account (no published expiry).
findings.gotchas: Do not expect a .edu login, student discount, or academic pricing; any education deal would be a sales/enterprise conversation, not a self-serve program.

sunset_notes: 1) The "known so far" figure (free developer tier up to 50K MAU / 1M messages/mo) is STALE: the live official Chat pricing page read today shows the free Build tier at 1,000 MAU / 100 concurrent / 1M API calls / 100K QC calls / 10 GB bandwidth. Stream restructured Chat pricing into Build/Start/Elevate/Enterprise (Start now $399/mo annual at 10K MAU, Elevate $599/mo annual), and the old high-limit free developer tier was cut. I could not pin the exact sunset date of the 50K MAU free tier because the session's web-search budget was exhausted mid-run; no archive fetch was performed. 2) 2026 pricing-page changes tracked by PricingSaaS (third-party, medium confidence): May 25, 2026 — Start/Elevate API bandwidth raised 10 GB -> 500 GB/mo, stored-message overage $5 -> $6/1M; Sep 21, 2026 — channel overage doubled to $100/1M (from ~$0.05/1K) while stored-message overage fell back to $5/1M; Oct 12, 2026 — Chat Enterprise column dropped stated minimums (1,000,000+ MAU / 750,000+ concurrent -> "Custom"). None of these touched the free Build tier or the Maker Account. 3) The dedicated /chat/trial/ page no longer exists as a marketing page — it 301-redirects to dashboard signup (trial claimed via signup; blog documents the 30-day, no-CC trial). 4) Maker Account terms seen today (2,000 MAU Chat cap, <=5 team / <$100k funding / <$10k-mo revenue, "$100 monthly credit") match a third-party record of the page as of 2026-09-12, so the maker offer appears unchanged in 2025-2026; no sunset found. 5) No student/education license has ever been a distinct self-serve program on the official pages found today; ed-tech is sales-led.

provider: Amazon Web Services (AWS) — Amazon SES (email), AWS End User Messaging (SMS/push/chat, formerly Amazon Pinpoint), AWS Free Account, AWS Activate

findings.name: AWS Free Account: up to $200 in Free Tier credits covering Amazon SES (new signup experience, live ~Oct 2026)
findings.detail: New AWS accounts get a credit-based free tier: $100 in credits immediately at sign-up, plus up to $100 more for completing 'Explore AWS' activities = up to $200 total. Credits are redeemable on eligible services, explicitly including Amazon SES (replaces the old per-service SES allowance of 3,000 emails/month). Sign-up is a choice between a Free plan and a Paid plan; Free plan lasts 6 months after account creation and the account auto-closes '6 months after you open it or when your credits run out, whichever comes first'. On the Free plan, 'no charges incurred unless you upgrade to a Paid plan or activate paid-only services'. Base credits expire 6 months from account creation; if you upgrade to Paid, remaining credits keep applying to bills and expire 12 months from account creation. After the Free plan ends, AWS retains your data 90 days before deletion. A separate 'always free' bucket of 30+ services with monthly limits continues on both plans, with credits covering overages. A payment method is NOT required for most new customers ('AWS may still ask for one to verify identity in some cases').
findings.eligibility: Any new AWS account under the new sign-up experience (rolled out October 2026). No credit card required in most cases; no .edu or startup status needed. No region limit stated on the credits themselves.
findings.claim: Create a new AWS account at the new sign-up flow, choose the Free plan (or Paid and let credits apply to bills), and use SES/SMS/push messaging within the $100-$200 credit envelope; upgrade to Paid if you want to continue past 6 months. Credits apply automatically to new eligible charges.
findings.expiry: Free plan: 6 months from account creation (account auto-closes). Base credits: 6 months; credits on Paid plan: 12 months from account creation. Data retained 90 days post-closure.
findings.gotchas: The old per-service 12-month free tiers (incl. SES 3,000 emails/month) are no longer listed on the official pages — they were replaced by this credit model. Free Plan auto-CLOSES the account, so anything not migrated by month 6 is gone after the 90-day data retention. Credits apply to new eligible charges only, not retroactively.

findings.name: Amazon SES pricing/plan model (2025-2026): new accounts default to 'Essentials' plan from July 21, 2026; à-la-carte $0.10/1,000 emails
findings.detail: SES pricing is 'per account per region per month'. À-la-carte outbound email is $0.10 per 1,000 emails (matching the 'then $0.10/1K' figure) and inbound $0.10/1,000; attachment data $0.12/GB; dedicated IPs $24.95/IP/month; Mail Manager email processing $0.15/1,000. NEW: 'New SES accounts and account x region combinations with no metered SES activity since June 1, 2025 will start on the Essentials plan beginning July 21, 2026'. Plans: Essentials $0.16/1K (0-10M), no monthly fee; Pro $0.22/1K with $105/mo fee; Enterprise $0.23/1K with $500/mo fee (all with virtual deliverability manager; volume tiers drop to $0.14/$0.17/$0.18 at 10-100M and $0.11/$0.12/$0.13 above 100M). 'You can upgrade or switch to à-la-carte pricing at any time'; downgrades take effect at the next billing cycle.
findings.eligibility: All SES users in commercial regions (per-account-per-region pricing; GovCloud/sovereign clouds excluded from some features). No card/edu/startup requirement — a standard AWS account (which under the new model may need no card for 6 months on Free plan).
findings.claim: Just start sending in the AWS console or via API; new/inactive accounts are put on Essentials by default from 2026-07-21 — if you want the cheaper $0.10/1K à-la-carte rate, switch to à-la-carte pricing in the console; Free Account credits (up to $200) offset early usage.
findings.expiry: No expiry; pricing structure. Note the old 3,000 emails/month SES free allowance is no longer published on the pricing page — it is superseded by the $200 credit model and the Essentials/à-la-carte structure.
findings.gotchas: Gotcha: the default Essentials rate ($0.16/1K) is ~60% MORE than à-la-carte ($0.10/1K) — switch deliberately, downgrades lag a billing cycle. Extra metered costs alongside SES: S3 storage for message transfer, SNS notifications, CloudWatch custom metrics/dashboards. Regional price differences apply per account per region.

findings.name: Push notifications free tier: first 1,000,000 push notifications per month free (AWS End User Messaging)
findings.detail: On the AWS End User Messaging pricing page: 'You pay $0 for the first 1,000,000 push notifications that you send each month', then $0.000001 each. No time limit or region restriction is stated on the page (language is recurring 'each month'), implying a standing allowance for End User Messaging. This is the successor to Amazon Pinpoint's push channel: AWS 'will end support for Amazon Pinpoint on October 30, 2026'; console and Pinpoint resources (endpoints, segments, campaigns, journeys, analytics) end, while 'APIs related to SMS, voice, mobile push, OTP, and phone number validate are not impacted' and continue under AWS End User Messaging. (Legacy Pinpoint console also offered $0 for 1M pushes/month and $0 for first 100M events collected, first 5,000 targeted endpoints, first 15,000 in-app message requests.)
findings.eligibility: Any AWS customer sending push notifications through End User Messaging (post-Pinpoint APIs). No card/edu requirement beyond normal AWS account rules (new accounts can be card-free for 6 months on Free plan). No region limit stated.
findings.claim: Use the End User Messaging mobile push API; the first 1M pushes/month are $0 automatically — nothing to redeem. Migration users: keep API usage (APNs/FCM/WNS) intact past 2026-10-30 since campaigns/journeys/console state in Pinpoint does NOT survive the sunset.
findings.expiry: Standing monthly allowance, no stated expiry. Hard date to act on: 2026-10-30 Pinpoint support ends — move off Pinpoint console/journeys before that.
findings.gotchas: Post-1M pushes cost $0.000001 each. Push is one channel of EUM; SMS/voice/email in the same app are billed separately (email via SES; no free SMS). Inbound/egress data and any EC2/S3 behind your app add cost.

findings.name: SMS (End User Messaging): no free SMS quota published — pay-per-message with carrier surcharges
findings.detail: The End User Messaging pricing page lists NO free SMS/MMS/voice message allowance (unlike push's 1M free). SMS: 'price varies by destination country and, in some cases, carrier within a country' (e.g., Canada toll-free: $0.00581 AWS + $0.00705 carrier). MMS (US/Canada outbound): $0.02 base + $0.01 carrier. Voice (outbound): US $0.013/min, requires a dedicated voice-enabled long code. OTP: $0.045 per successful verification plus the SMS price. Phone Number Validate: $0.006/request. Add-ons: SMS Protect Monitor/Filter $0.01/message; Notify managed feature $0.030-$0.045/message volume-tiered plus channel fee; phone number leasing $1-$995/mo; short codes US setup $650 + $995/mo. The legacy '100 free SMS/month in US regions' SNS free tier is no longer published anywhere on the current End User Messaging/SNS pricing pages — likely absorbed into the $200 Free Account credit model.
findings.eligibility: Any End User Messaging customer. No free tier to claim; new accounts' up-to-$200 Free Account credits can offset early SMS spend. No card needed during the 6-month Free plan.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim for SMS specifically — usage is metered; if you need zero-cost SMS, rely on the up-to-$200 new-account credits or an AWS Activate credit grant.
findings.expiry: No free tier, so no expiry question; pricing is standing. Legacy 100-msg US free tier: no longer listed as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: High gotcha surface: carrier fees are passed through on top of AWS fees (so 'real' per-SMS cost is higher than the AWS number); promotional SMS in many markets is heavily regulated; OTP and Phone Number Validate are separate paid features; scaling past 'Notify' requires dedicated phone numbers + brand verification (US 10DLC etc.), which cost money.

findings.name: Chat APIs (WhatsApp & RCS via End User Messaging): no free tier — metered with Meta/carrier surcharges
findings.detail: WhatsApp: AWS fee $0.005 per outbound message globally (except India Authentication/Utility at $0.002), $0.001 per inbound globally; WhatsApp voice calling $0.005/min outbound (India $0.003), $0.001/min inbound; Meta's separate message fees are added on top and vary by country/message type. RCS (US): Rich RCS outbound $0.007/segment AWS + $0.00494/segment carrier; Rich Media RCS $0.020/message AWS + $0.00949 carrier. 'Businesses are only charged when a message is successfully delivered.' No free messages for WhatsApp or RCS.
findings.eligibility: Any End User Messaging customer; no free tier to claim. No card requirement during the new-account Free plan window.
findings.claim: Use EUM WhatsApp/RCS APIs; expect cost from message #1 unless you hold AWS credits (Free Account $200 or Activate grants).
findings.expiry: Standing metered pricing; no trial stated.
findings.gotchas: Double billing: AWS fee + Meta fee (WhatsApp) or AWS fee + carrier fee (RCS); 'only charged on successful delivery' cuts both ways for delivery-failure accounting.

findings.name: AWS Activate Founders tier: $1,000 in AWS credits (up to $5,000 over time) for early-stage, self-funded startups
findings.detail: Founders tier (current as of the June 2026 applying guide): $1,000 in AWS Activate Credits; 'select startups may qualify for up to $5,000 over time'. Eligibility: new to AWS Activate Credits, self-funded, fully functioning company website, founded in the past 10 years. Credits expire within 1-2 years depending on package and are applied monthly to new eligible charges only (never retroactive). Processing 7-10 business days. Credits are redeemable across 200+ AWS services, including third-party foundation models on Amazon Bedrock (OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Meta, etc.). No credit-card requirement mentioned for the program itself. Re-applying is allowed for a larger tier; you receive the difference up to a lifetime cap; submitted applications can't be edited (cancel + unlink + resubmit).
findings.eligibility: Startup founders (individuals applying on behalf of a company): self-funded (no institutional funding), company < 10 years old, working company website required, first-time Activate recipient, business email matching the startup domain. Applies to startups of any funding stage at or before Pre-Series B.
findings.claim: Create/sign in to an AWS Builder ID (personal email) → complete one-time Activate profile (business email) → choose Founders tier → enter company + funding details → link your primary AWS account (root/admin) → verify in console → submit. Credits land on the linked AWS account and automatically offset SES/SMS/push spend.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 1-2 years from grant depending on package; no stated renewal — you can re-apply when you qualify for a bigger tier.
findings.gotchas: Self-funded only — a small funding round or accelerator affiliation pushes you to the Portfolio tier instead. Credits cover new usage only; pre-existing debt on the account is not credited. $5K 'over time' is discretionary/select.

findings.name: AWS Activate Portfolio tier: up to $200,000 in AWS credits for provider-backed startups (pre-Series B)
findings.detail: Portfolio tier: 'up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits'. Eligibility: associated with an AWS Activate Provider (accelerator/VC/ecosystem org, 'thousands worldwide') and hold their Organizational ID; Pre-Series B (most recent funding round within last 12 months, if funded); founded in the past 10 years; working company website; no prior AWS Activate Credits of equal or greater value. Beyond $200K, 'AI startups ready to grow may be eligible for additional credits' via an Account Manager. Credits redeemable on 200+ services incl. Bedrock third-party models; expire within 1-2 years; applied monthly to new eligible charges. Program stats: 350,000+ startups, $8B+ in promotional credits since 2013. Note: an older marketing page (startups.aws.com LP) still advertises 'up to $100,000' — the June 2026 guide and main page confirm $200,000 as the current ceiling; also a new 'Kiro credits' offer for startups exists (kiro.dev/startups).
findings.eligibility: Startup companies affiliated with an Activate Provider (Org ID), pre-Series B funding cap (most recent round <= 12 months old), < 10 years old, working website. Not for individuals or non-startup businesses; no .edu involved (student startups go through their university's provider agreement — see Educate finding).
findings.claim: Obtain your provider's Org ID → AWS Builder ID + Activate profile (business email) → choose Portfolio tier → submit funding/company details → link primary AWS account → wait 7-10 business days; credits apply monthly to new eligible usage.
findings.expiry: Grant-to-expiry 1-2 years per package; re-application gives the difference vs previously held credits up to the lifetime cap.
findings.gotchas: The headline number moved from $100K to $200K (some pages stale); 'most recent round within last 12 months' is a hard timing rule; credits are new-charge-only; wrong/funding details = denial (inaccurate info results in denial).

findings.name: AWS Educate: student program at partner institutions (credits ~$100/yr; some universities offer up to $5,000 for student startups)
findings.detail: AWS Educate (successor to AWS Academy's classroom content) is offered through enrolled institutions: students get free self-paced courses, labs, and a promo credit (commonly ~$100/yr, redeemed by code in Billing & Cost Management -> Credits). Some university startup programs (e.g., AWS Activate partnerships at universities like Syracuse's Blackstone LaunchPad) extend student-startup eligibility to up to $5,000 in credits valid ~2 years plus 1 year of AWS Business Support. Note: the official Educate landing page could not be fetched today (404/DNS), so dollar amounts are from university-published pages updated in 2025; treat as approximate.
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students/faculty at a partner institution; the ~$5,000 startup path requires the university's Org ID and meeting Activate Portfolio-style requirements (website, funding stage). Verification via the institution's enrollment, not a .edu email alone.
findings.claim: Register through your school's AWS Educate portal, complete the AWS Educate application, then redeem the emailed credit code in AWS Billing & Cost Management; for student startups, apply through the university's Activate provider page (Org ID) for the larger grant.
findings.source_url: https://support.sou.edu/kb/articles/amazon-web-services-educate-program (institutional reference; official page https://awsacademy.com/amazon-educate/ was unreachable today)
findings.expiry: Educate credits typically annual per-enrollment; university startup grants ~2 years. Verify current numbers with the school's page.
findings.gotchas: Credit codes are account-bound (redeem on the account you'll use, they don't transfer); some schools cap or restrict production use (learning-only policies, e.g., UC Berkeley's disclaimer that these are sandbox resources, not for launching a business).

findings.name: AWS Builder Center student rewards: free Skill Builder year + badge-earned credits, no credit card required
findings.detail: Verified students at accredited higher-education institutions (verified via SheerID with name, college name, and school email — .edu domain NOT strictly required) get: 1 year of AWS Skill Builder (900+ courses, labs, cert exam prep, game-based learning) just for completing a profile; badge-based rewards — 7 badges = $10 AWS credits, 14 badges = $20 AWS credits, 21 badges = $100 AWS Certification voucher; plus free workshops/courses/community, explicitly 'No credit card'. Student Builder Groups (student-led campus communities) also exist.
findings.eligibility: Students (or staff) of an accredited higher-education institution, verified by SheerID (most checks minutes; up to 24-48h with extra docs). No startup/funding rules.
findings.claim: Sign in with an AWS Builder ID at builder.aws.com → complete SheerID student verification → complete profile (unlocks Skill Builder) → earn badges (articles, comments, streaks) to unlock the $10/$20 credits and $100 voucher. Credits apply to AWS usage (incl. messaging services) if you have/created an AWS account.
findings.expiry: Skill Builder benefit is 1 year; badge credits/voucher have no expiry stated on the page; program is ongoing.
findings.gotchas: Rewards are small ($10-$20 credits, $100 voucher) — meaningful but not a production budget; the cert voucher is a voucher, not exam free passage; no card needed but actual AWS production usage still requires a billing account.

sunset_notes: 1) Amazon Pinpoint sunset (HARD DATE): AWS ends support for Amazon Pinpoint on October 30, 2026 — console access and all Pinpoint resources (endpoints, segments, campaigns, journeys, analytics) terminate that day; only the messaging-channel APIs (SMS, voice, mobile push, OTP, phone number validate) continue under the rebranded "AWS End User Messaging" service. Anyone relying on Pinpoint journeys/campaigns must migrate before 2026-10-30. 2) Legacy per-service Free Tier replaced: the old model — e.g., "SES: 3,000 emails/month free for the first 12 months, then $0.10/1K" and "SNS: 100 SMS/month free, US regions" — is no longer published; as of the October 2026 sign-up experience, new accounts instead get up to $200 in Free Tier credits over 6 months (Free plan auto-closes at 6 months or when credits run out). The "then $0.10/1K" figure survives, but as the à-la-carte SES price, while NEW SES accounts default to the more expensive Essentials plan ($0.16/1K) starting July 21, 2026. 3) The formerly permanent "3,000 emails/month free (US regions, no purchase of sending capacity)" SES allowance is not listed on today's official pricing page — treat it as superseded by the credit model for new accounts; legacy account behavior not verifiable (docs pages didn't render). 4) The legacy 100-free-SMS/month US-regions tier also no longer appears on End User Messaging pricing; SMS is now fully pay-per-message. 5) AWS Activate credit ceiling was raised to $200,000 (some pages still show the old $100,000 figure — a 2025-2026 program change, not a sunset).

provider: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap geocoding, nominatim.openstreetmap.org, operated by the OpenStreetMap Foundation)

findings.name: Free public Nominatim API (the only offer; there is no student/startup tier, trial credit, or education program)
findings.detail: Nominatim offers exactly one access mode: the free public service at nominatim.openstreetmap.org, run by the OSMF Operations Working Group on donated servers. No API keys, no signup, no billing. Limits (verified on the official policy page today): absolute maximum 1 request/second per application/website (sum of all your end users, not per user); long-running (>1 day) or recurring bulk scripts throttled to 4 requests/minute; bulk jobs single-machine single-thread, no distributed scripts; no auto-complete; no systematic queries (grids, full postcode/POI lists); no scraping of /details; no reselling of geocoding output (services whose primary function is geocoding — package/vehicle tracking, API resellers — must host their own instance); LLMs may only point to the service if they prominently surface the policy, and no-code/low-code/vibe-coding platforms are barred from wiring it in as a generic geocoding feature. You must send a valid identifying User-Agent or Referer (library defaults banned) and display OSM attribution. Data is ODbL (share-alike).
findings.eligibility: Universal: any individual, student, researcher, or startup anywhere in the world. No .edu email, no startup age or funding cap, no credit card, no region limits — you simply call the API. The constraint is use-pattern, not user type: heavy/bulk use is prohibited regardless of who you are.
findings.claim: No claim needed — it is open and unkeyed. To use: (1) call https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=... or /reverse?lat=..&lon=.. (format=jsonv2/json/geojson); (2) set a descriptive User-Agent or Referer for your app; (3) pace to <=1 req/s in aggregate; (4) cache results on your side (a proxy is strongly recommended); (5) display '© OpenStreetMap contributors' attribution. OSMF may change the policy without notice and revoke access at any time; apps must be able to switch providers without a software update.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal: it is a permanent free public service (still live as of 2026-10-22; Nominatim 5.2.0 shipped 2025-10-29). No sunset date is published, but OSMF explicitly reserves the right to change policy or block clients without notice, so treat the free tier as revocable fair-use capacity, not an SLA.
findings.gotchas: This is the classic 'free but not for production scale' offer: the public instance is deliberately kept small, and exceeding it means 403/IP blocks, not bills. Bulk geocoding, high-volume API serving, or embedding into a commercial geocoding product are forbidden — for those you must self-host or pay a commercial provider (MapTiler, LocationIQ, Geocode Earth, Stadia Maps, OpenCage, Geoapify — all third-party, none OSMF-run; their free tiers are a different provider and out of scope here). The LLM/vibe-coding and no-code restrictions are 2025-vintage additions; AI-generated boilerplate that hits the public endpoint for users may itself violate policy. ODbL share-alike applies to the underlying data even though the service is free. There is no student discount program, no startup program, no trial credits, and no education license at OSMF/Nominatim — absence, not a hidden program, is the finding.

findings.name: Self-hosted Nominatim (open source, the sanctioned alternative for students/startups needing more than the free public instance)
findings.detail: Nominatim itself is free open source (GPL v3+; latest release 5.2.0, 2025-10-29) and running your own instance carries zero project-imposed rate limits, zero fees, and zero approval — this is what the OSMF policy explicitly directs bulk users and commercial geocoding services to do. Practical costs: a worldwide install needs roughly 1 TB storage plus a PostgreSQL/PostGIS stack; country extracts fit much smaller boxes (a real-world 3M-point Swiss project in 2025 was successfully served from a WSL Ubuntu box). It is the only genuinely 'free for students and startups' path to scalable geocoding under the Nominatim umbrella.
findings.eligibility: Universal — anyone, any region, any age, no funding cap, no CC, no email gating. The only conditions are your own infrastructure cost and ODbL compliance for OSM data.
findings.claim: No claim. Download from https://github.com/osm-search/Nominatim (or nominatim.org install docs), install per platform (Docker/Waydroid/WSL paths documented), import a planet/country OSM extract into PostgreSQL+PostGIS, expose the same REST API. Note self-hosting also shifts you out of the public-instance usage policy, which 'does not apply to nominatim services run by yourself or other organisations'.
findings.expiry: None. Open source under GPL; free indefinitely. The software line continues (5.x current as of late 2025).
findings.gotchas: Free software, not free compute: RAM/CPU/storage and 1TB-class disk for global data are real egress/infra costs. ODbL share-alike still governs OSM data (published derivatives must be shared). The /search.php endpoint is deprecated in favor of /search and will be removed in future releases — pin/upgrade deliberately. No support or SLA; the community supports it on the OSM forum.

findings.name: Commercial Nominatim front-ends with their own free tiers (OSMF corporate members / listed third parties)
findings.detail: The OSMF-maintained Nominatim wiki lists companies offering hosted Nominatim-style geocoding: Geofabrik, OpenCage, Stadia Maps, LocationIQ, plus Geoapify, Geocodify, Maps.co and Europe-oriented 'Geocoding API' services. These are distinct providers — NOT Nominatim/OSMF — and any free tiers, trial credits, or startup programs belong to those vendors and must be researched under their own provider entries (several, e.g. OpenCage and MapTiler-style free tiers of 50k–50k calls/month, are commonly advertised). For Nominatim/OSMF itself: none.
findings.eligibility: Per-external-vendor, not verifiable from OSMF pages; not claimed here.
findings.claim: n/a — not a Nominatim/OSMF offer.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: Counting these as Nominatim offerings would conflate the free OSMF service with commercial resellers the usage policy actively steers you toward for bulk volume.

sunset_notes: No student, startup, trial-credit, or education program existed at OSMF/Nominatim, so none was sunset in 2025–2026. What DID materially change in 2025–2026: (1) the OSMF Nominatim Usage Policy was tightened — bulk scripts now hard-capped at 4 req/min (single machine, single thread, >1-day or recurring jobs), with repeated-identical-query clients classified 'faulty' and blockable; (2) a new 'Usage in LLMs' clause: LLMs may only suggest the service if they prominently surface the policy, and no-code/low-code/'vibe-coding' platforms are prohibited from embedding the public API as a generic geocoding feature — aimed squarely at AI-generated app stacks; (3) explicit ban on reselling/repackaging geocoding output, naming package/vehicle tracking and API resellers, and a warning that commercial users may have access revoked 'without notice'; (4) software releases: Nominatim 5.2.0 on 2025-10-29 (wiki, accessed 2026-09), and /search.php deprecated in favor of /search. Nothing was closed; the free public service remains live as of 2026-10-22 (policy page fetched today).

findings.claim: Create a free RapidAPI developer account (no card). Open any free-API listing from https://rapidapi.com/collection/list-of-free-apis; for 'Free' category APIs you call endpoints directly or generate an API key with no subscription and no credit-card step.
findings.detail: Thousands of public APIs on the RapidAPI hub offer a free tier requiring no credit card and no subscription. Every 'Free API' plan is hard-capped at 1,000 requests/hour AND 500,000 requests/month; exceeding either returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. Usage above that cap must move to a paid plan. The 500K/month cap is the platform-wide max a zero-price plan may allow: any plan exceeding 500K requests/month must charge at least $0.00003 per call (minimum-price floor, so e.g. a 2M-call plan must cost at least $45/month).
findings.eligibility: Any RapidAPI consumer account. No .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no documented region restriction, and credit card NOT required for the 'Free' API category. Caution: freemium APIs DO require a credit card even for their $0 free plan, and Pay-Per-Use/Paid APIs require a card — so 'free' only means the Free category.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; free plans persist while the API provider keeps them enabled. Providers can disable/modify pricing plans at any time (existing subscribers keep the old plan version).
findings.gotchas: (1) Trial-vs-free: a 'free' plan on a freemium API still demands a credit card — check the API's category before relying on no-card access. (2) Since December 2025 a Bandwidth Platform Fee applies to each subscription (including free plans): 10 GB/billing cycle free, then $1 per additional 1 GB (~$0.001/MB), charged to the consumer with no free-plan carve-out — a high-bandwidth consumer of a $0 plan can still be billed. (3) 429 hard-stop at the caps; no overage billing on free plans, just rejection. (4) Daily-quota plans reset 24h from subscription time, not midnight.
findings.name: Free API plans (no credit card): 1,000 req/hour, 500,000 req/month hard caps

findings.claim: Nothing to claim — applied automatically to every API subscription (including $0 plans) starting December 2025.
findings.detail: RapidAPI's 'Connecting to an API' docs state: 'Starting December 2025, each subscription will include 10 GB of bandwidth per billing cycle at no cost. After that limit, a fee of $1 per additional 1 GB of traffic will apply, calculated proportionally based on total usage. This fee will be charged to the consumer.' Reference figure: average request ~2 KB, so ~100GB ≈ 50M requests before any charge.
findings.eligibility: All RapidAPI consumer subscriptions, free or paid.
findings.expiry: In effect since December 2025; ongoing as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: This is a cost add, not a benefit: even a $0 Basic plan can accrue a consumer bill above 10 GB/month; free plans receive the same 10 GB grant but the docs show no carve-out from the $1/GB overage.
findings.name: Bandwidth platform fee: 10 GB/month included free per subscription, $1 per additional GB (Dec 2025)

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22 there is NO RapidAPI student, education, or startup program: no .edu licensing, no startup credit/trial-credit offer, no startup-age or funding-cap eligibility — the official docs/FAQ pages (updated through mid-2025) contain no mention of any such offer, and no 2025-2026 announcement of one was found. The only material 2025-2026 change is consumer-side: the December 2025 Bandwidth Platform Fee (10 GB free/cycle, then $1/GB charged to the consumer), which partially erodes the 'free' story for free plans. The core free offer stands: no-credit-card free API plans capped at 1,000 req/hour and 500K req/month (confirmed on the official monetization docs). Note: the session's web-search budget was exhausted partway through; findings above are based on official docs pages fetched today (high confidence), while the absence of student/startup programs is asserted from the official pages' silence (medium confidence that none exists on a dedicated marketing page that was not reachable).

provider: Firebase / Google Cloud — Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) push; plus GCP/Firebase platform free offers (trial, startup, education)

findings.name: FCM No-Cost Free Tier (Spark & Blaze plans)
findings.detail: FCM is listed as 'no-cost' on both the free Spark plan and the pay-as-you-go Blaze plan. No per-message charge and no monthly cap on message count — unlimited sends in principle. The only constraint is a rate quota: the HTTP v1 API default is 600,000 downstream messages/minute per project (HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED above it). Payload up to 4096 bytes per message (2048 bytes for topic messages). Works on Android, iOS and web.
findings.eligibility: Universal — open to anyone (student, startup, or enterprise). No .edu email, no startup age/funding test, and NO credit card required on the Spark plan. Not region-limited for the free tier.
findings.claim: Create a Firebase project (defaults to the no-cost Spark plan, no billing account or card needed). Send push via the console Notifications composer, the server SDKs, or the FCM HTTP v1 API. Upgrade to Blaze only if you need to exceed quotas or enable other paid services.
findings.expiry: No expiry — always free; quotas are 'subject to change' but no renewal is required.
findings.gotchas: 600k msg/min rate quota returns 429 when exceeded; client errors (HTTP 400-499, excluding 429s) also count against quota; quota windows are not clock-aligned (bursts can still throttle). Collapsible messages are capped at 20 bursts/app/device. Topic fan-out to large audiences is slow (minutes, not seconds) and messages are best-effort with no delivery guarantee. The backend you run to dispatch (e.g., Cloud Functions) is billed on its own terms, not free. To raise the quota you must show >=80% usage for 5 consecutive min/day and a <5% client-error ratio; temporary/launch spikes are handled via Firebase Support (max 2 temp events/yr, <=30 days total). FCM is push-only: it offers no email or SMS (Firebase Auth phone sign-in is billed per SMS, not a free tier).

findings.name: Google Cloud / Firebase $300 Free Trial credit (90 days)
findings.detail: New Google Cloud customers get a $300 'Welcome' credit valid for 90 days, plus access to the Always Free tier during the trial. The credit can be applied to ANY Google Cloud / Firebase service, including ones that are not free (Cloud Functions, Firestore beyond free limits, Hosting bandwidth, App Hosting, etc.). A credit/debit card is required at signup solely for identity/fraud validation — you are not charged unless you explicitly upgrade to a paid account. One-time and non-renewable. NOTE: the period is 90 days, not 30.
findings.eligibility: Must have NEVER been a paying Google Cloud / Google Maps Platform / Firebase customer AND never signed up for the Free Trial. A corporate card is not required (a personal card is fine). New customers only; US/MX government entities excluded.
findings.claim: Sign up for the GCP Free Trial ($300 / 90 days) and create a Cloud Billing account (card entered for validation only). In the Firebase console, link that billing account to a project to move it to the Blaze plan — the $300 then applies across Firebase. As of March 2025, eligible users are routed straight into the Free Trial signup from the Firebase console.
findings.expiry: Ends when the $300 is spent or 90 days elapse, whichever comes first; unused credit expires at 90 days. Non-renewable. If you do not upgrade to a paid account by day 90, resources are stopped and data may be deleted.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required (unlike the FCM free tier, which needs none). FCM itself is free, so this credit only helps with the non-free services around it. During the trial you cannot: create Cloud VMware Engine resources, use Windows Server images, add GPUs to VMs, or request allocation increases (all need a paid account). No SLA/indemnity applies during the trial and it is not meant for production. Auto-closes at 90 days or on credit exhaustion.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program (GCP credits for startups)
findings.detail: A startup program offering Google Cloud credits plus tools/mentoring, delivered partly through a partner network of accelerators, incubators and VCs. Historically up to ~$150,000 in GCP credits for qualifying early-stage companies (accelerator/VC-linked tracks can receive more), typically valid ~12 months. NOT FCM-specific — credits apply across GCP. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: live 2026 figures could not be read from the page (the page is JS-heavy and returned truncated content; the paths /programs/startups, /transform/startups and /startup returned 404 or only the title 'Google for Startups Cloud Program'), so the exact tiers, funding cap and founding window are UNCONFIRMED.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startup: founded within a recent window (commonly ~3-4 years), below a funding cap, HQ in a supported country, registered legal entity. A vetted program, not a free tier.
findings.claim: Apply at the Google for Startups Cloud program page (cloud.google.com/startup), either directly (self-service application) or through a partner accelerator/incubator/VC.
findings.expiry: Credits ~12 months from acceptance (unconfirmed for current cohort).
findings.gotchas: Could not confirm current credit amounts, funding cap, or founding window from the live page today (WebSearch budget exhausted; URLs moved) — treat all figures as historical/approximate and re-verify on the live page before applying. GCP Marketplace third-party SKUs typically do not draw from program credits.

findings.name: Google Cloud credits for students / teachers (education)
findings.detail: Google Cloud has offered education-focused credits for students and teachers. The live specifics (exact credit amount, whether a .edu email or a teacher-license verification is required, and duration) COULD NOT be confirmed today: the education developer portal (edu.dev) failed to resolve (DNS ENOTFOUND) and the GCP /edu page would not render its content. Historically these are comparatively small credits (on the order of hundreds to ~$1,000) for students via an academic/.edu email and for verified teachers. NOT FCM-specific — FCM is free to everyone regardless of this.
findings.eligibility: Students: academic/.edu email or institutional verification. Teachers: verified teacher status (license/employer proof). Exact current requirements unconfirmed.
findings.claim: Sign up via the Google Cloud education credits page using a .edu email (students) or teacher verification (educators); credits deposit to a GCP project. (Unverified flow — confirm on the live page.)
findings.expiry: Unconfirmed (historically ~12 months).
findings.gotchas: Could not verify the live amount or eligibility today (low confidence) — do not assume a specific dollar figure or a hard .edu requirement until confirmed on the official page. The FCM free tier does not depend on any of this.

sunset_notes: No FCM free offer was sunset in 2025-2026. FCM remains 'no-cost' on the Spark and Blaze plans (always free, no per-message charge; the only limit is the 600,000 msg/min rate quota, which is a throttle, not a billing cap). The GCP/Firebase Free Trial remains $300 for 90 days — a '30-day' figure that surfaced during research was a fetch error, not a real change; the official T&Cs, GCP docs, and the Firebase blog all confirm 90 days. I could not verify the LIVE 2026 figures for the Google for Startups Cloud Program or the education-credits program (program URLs have moved, the pages would not render, edu.dev failed DNS, and the session WebSearch budget was exhausted), so findings 3 and 4 are reported as low-confidence, historical/approximate, and need re-verification on the live pages. One minor 2025 change observed (not FCM-related): the Blaze plan's App Hosting added a no-cost allowance of up to 10 GiB/month of outgoing bandwidth starting Aug 1, 2025. Note on scope: FCM is a push-only service and offers no free email or SMS tier; the 'Email/SMS front' in the task framing does not exist within FCM (Firebase Auth phone sign-in is billed per SMS, not free).

provider: Twilio SendGrid (Email), fronts: Email, SMS, Push & Chat APIs

findings.name: Twilio SendGrid free trial (Email API + Marketing Campaigns)
findings.detail: 60-day trial at $0/mo starting from signup. Email API: up to 100 emails/day. Marketing Campaigns: up to 100 marketing emails/day and up to 100 contacts. No credit card required to start ('Your card won't be charged at this time'). Trial is one-time only; upgrading immediately terminates it and it cannot be restarted. After expiry you must upgrade to keep sending or use the Marketing tab. New accounts must, before upgrading: enable 2FA, complete domain authentication (or 'Send to a Coworker'), and add a payment method. Paid: Email API Essentials from $19.95/mo, Pro from $89.95/mo, Premier custom; Marketing Basic from $15/mo, Advanced from $60/mo, Custom via sales. Overage charges may apply on paid plans.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone creating a SendGrid account; no .edu or startup requirement stated; no region limit stated on the trial itself.
findings.claim: Sign up at https://signup.sendgrid.com/; trial begins at sign-up (60 days, 100 emails/day). Upgrade via Settings -> Account Details -> Your Products -> Change Plan.
findings.expiry: 60 days from sign-up; one-time; unused capacity is lost at expiry.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs free: the Email API has NO persistent free plan after the 60 days — you must pay ($19.95+/mo) or stop sending; 100 emails/day on trial, not 100/month; the old 'free 100/day forever' framing is gone. For accounts that want marketing, see the separate persistent free Marketing tier below. New-account upgrade prerequisites (2FA + domain auth + payment) are often missed. Docs page last modified 2025-09-25.

findings.name: SendGrid Marketing Campaigns permanent free tier
findings.detail: Twilio's Marketing Campaigns pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22) states 'We also offer a Free Marketing Campaigns Plan' distinct from the 60-day trial: store up to 2,000 contacts and send 6,000 free emails/month, plus A/B testing, sign-up forms, automation, and email-testing credits; and a free SMTP layer of 100 emails/day. Paid starts at Basic $15/mo (Basic 5K: 5,000 contacts / 15,000 emails, overage $0.0040/email) or Advanced $60/mo. No credit card required to start the free trial.
findings.eligibility: Any SendGrid account; no .edu/startup requirement stated. (Page does not explicitly state the free tier survives after the 60-day trial lapses, but it is presented as a separate named plan.)
findings.claim: Sign up free at SendGrid; Marketing free plan is available in-product under Marketing Campaigns; upgrade is optional.
findings.expiry: Ongoing (no stated end date).
findings.gotchas: Free marketing tier (100 contacts/100 emails/day during the 60-day trial) is tighter than the free plan (2,000 contacts/6,000 emails/mo); overage pricing applies beyond plan limits; 'free trial' marketing copy on landing pages can obscure which offering you are in.

findings.name: Twilio platform free trial (SMS/Push/Chat fronts): per-product free units, 30 days
findings.detail: New Twilio accounts get a 30-day free trial with no credit card: product-specific free units instead of a dollar balance — 100 SMS messages, 100 WhatsApp messages, 3,000 emails, 75 voice minutes (monitored via the Console's 'Free units tracker'). Trial ends 30 days after sign-up. Restrictions: you can call/message only verified recipients (up to 5 per account; sign-up number auto-verified), SMS/voice limited to your sign-up country, email limited to your sign-up address, Twilio-provided templates only (no custom message/email/WhatsApp content), and trial numbers are assigned, not chosen. After upgrading (add payment details + address + starting balance) you get 'post-upgrade free units' for eligible products. Per the Twilio pricing page (current as of Aug 2026): Flex/Video start with 5,000 hours free; TaskRouter first 100 tasks/mo free; Functions 10,000 free invocations; Serverless Assets free tools access; Connections 14-day free trial; Twilio for Salesforce 30-day trial then $15/seat/mo. Pay-as-you-go rates: SMS/RCS from $0.0083/message, WhatsApp from $0.005/message, Twilio Email from $0.0013/email, voice from $0.0085/min inbound.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; requires verifying a personal phone number at sign-up. Push service and Conversations (Chat) have NO trial 'Try-out' flows listed — trial try-outs cover SMS, Voice, Email, WhatsApp only; Push/Chat are pay-as-you-go after upgrade.
findings.claim: Sign up at twilio.com/try-twilio (verify email, verify personal phone, describe project); free units are deducted before any charges; upgrade via the Trial banner in Console.
findings.expiry: Trial expires 30 days after sign-up; upgrade required to continue; disposition of unused units after expiry is not documented on the page.
findings.gotchas: No credit card, but real pay-per-use starts after the 30 days or after free units are consumed post-upgrade — SMS at $0.0083/message adds up; recipient (5 max), country, and template restrictions make trial useless for production A2P or custom content; Push/Chat users get no trial units.

findings.name: Twilio Startup program ('Grow with Twilio')
findings.detail: Active program for early-stage companies: free educational resources (developer hub tutorials, docs, videos) and the standard account trial credit ('a small trial credit when you sign up for your Twilio account'). Contact path: 'Complete the form below to get in touch with the Twilio Startups team.' No company-age cap, funding cap, or revenue ceiling is published on the page.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage companies per Twilio's own wording; no explicit funding/age limits; no .edu requirement.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes observed: (1) The Twilio trial was restructured from a shared dollar-credit model (historically the widely documented $10 trial balance) to per-product FREE UNITS (100 SMS / 100 WhatsApp / 3,000 emails / 75 voice minutes) — the current docs state units are given 'instead of a shared dollar balance' — and now has a hard 30-day expiry ('Trial accounts expire after 30 days'), replacing the previously open-ended trial-until-upgrade model. (2) SendGrid is rebranded under Twilio: sendgrid.com 301-redirects to twilio.com/en-us/sendgrid, and the master pricing page lists 'Twilio Email starts at $0.0013/email' (page marked current as of Aug 2026); SendGrid's 60-day trial and persistent free Marketing tier (2,000 contacts / 6,000 emails/mo) remain. (3) The Twilio startup program no longer grants startup-specific credits: official page states 'We do not offer additional credits to startups at this time' — the old standalone startup-credit program, if it ever stood as such, is materially reduced to resources + standard trial. (4) No education license found; if one existed previously, no trace on official pages. Note on method: WebSearch budget was exhausted for this session, so all facts above come from official Twilio/SendGrid pages fetched on 2026-10-22 (high-confidence items) rather than searches; exact sunset dates for the trial revamp are not published on the pages I could reach.

findings.claim: Sign up at signup.mailgun.com/new/signup (or app.mailgun.com/signup); account starts on the Free plan automatically. No separate claim flow.
findings.detail: Standing $0/mo tier: 100 emails/day (~3,000/mo), 1 custom sending domain, 2 API keys, 1 user per account, 1 day log retention, 1 inbound route, ticket support only. No expiry; it is the permanent entry tier. Overage/extra pricing starts on paid Basic ($1.80/1,000 emails, from). Page states 'It's free to sign up and easy to get started'; signup page is titled 'Sign Up Free', but the page does not explicitly say 'no credit card'.

findings.expiry: Never expires; 100 emails/day cap is permanent. Log retention only 1 day.
findings.gotchas: Daily cap: sending is limited past 100/day with no overage on Free. 1 user, 1 domain, 2 API keys. Higher volume requires the paid 'free 30-day trials' (Foundation/Scale below). Paid plans bill monthly in arrears (after the first partial month, charges are at the start of each month for the previous month). Card requirement for the Free plan not explicitly confirmed on the page.

provider: Kit (formerly ConvertKit) — email platform; fronts: Email, SMS, Push & Chat (API at developers.kit.com)

findings.name: Kit Free plan (standing free tier, Email)
findings.detail: $0/mo permanent free tier: up to 10,000 email subscribers; 'unlimited email broadcasts' and 'unlimited landing pages & forms' per the live pricing page (no monthly email cap is stated on any official page — the '1,000 emails/mo' figure from known-so-far is not confirmed on current official pages); 1 user seat; audience tagging/segmentation; 2-subject-line A/B; digital products & subscriptions with 3.5% + 30c transaction fee; Creator Network with 5 Smart Recommendation slots; 'API access' and free Kit App Store apps (paid apps excluded). Excluded: visual automations, email sequences, rules & RSS campaigns, AI connectors, SMS marketing, Paid Recommendations (23.5% fee), Kit MCP, subscriber engagement scoring, deliverability reporting, custom tracking domain, 24/7 support. Support answered within 24h in receive order.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with an email address — no .edu required, no region limit stated. No credit card required (signup button is 'Try Kit for free'; the pricing page's no-CC language applies to the trial, and the free tier is the default account state). Free 'for as long as you stay under 10,000 subscribers'; crossing 10,000 forces upgrade to a paid plan to keep sending. No expiry date.
findings.claim: 1) Go to kit.com and click 'Try Kit for free' / 'Get started'. 2) Complete signup — new accounts start on the Free plan. 3) Optionally verify via Dashboard > Billing to confirm plan type. No application, referral, or code needed.
findings.expiry: Permanent; no renewal date. Exits only when user exceeds 10,000 subscribers (upgrade required) or cancels the account.
findings.gotchas: (1) Pricing page says 'unlimited email broadcasts' on Free but the help article says cancel/downgrade 'moves your account... to our free plan, which has fewer features and a lower sending limit' — treat Free as a reduced-cap plan; verify the live cap in-app for your account. (2) 'Unlimited' broadcasts come with a 3.5%+30c fee on commerce (incl. Kit's 0.6% of fees). (3) Downgrading a paid account stops automations/sequences from running until re-upgrade. (4) API/email-stats retention is now clamped to 5 years (API change 2026-10-15). (5) Features like 'apps/integrations' presence varies: Free gets API access + free apps but NOT paid App Store apps, paid Recommendations, or SMS.

findings.name: 14-day free trial of paid plans (Creator & Pro)
findings.detail: 14-day free trial of Creator and Pro plans with full paid features (Creator: unlimited subscribers, unlimited visual automations/sequences/RSS, 2 users; Pro: everything + unlimited users, 5-subject-line A/B + content A/B, SMS marketing, Kit MCP, Subscriber Signals, Growth Concierge). Post-trial pricing: Creator '$33/mo' billed yearly at '$390 billed yearly — Save $78 per year' (monthly tier $39/mo at 1,000-subscriber tier per billing help article; $59/mo at 3,000-subscriber tier); Pro '$66' listed with 'EXTRA 25% OFF FIRST YEAR' promo at '$50/mo — $593 billed first year, Save $355 first year; footnote: discount applies only to first year, plan renews at standard rate. Free migrations offered alongside the trial.
findings.eligibility: New accounts (trial users); no .edu, no startup age/funding cap, no region restriction stated. Credit card NOT required to start ('No credit card required. Cancel anytime').
findings.claim: 1) On kit.com/pricing click 'Start 14-day free trial' under Creator or Pro. 2) Sign up without a card. 3) To stay paid after 14 days, add a payment method (Stripe runs a $1 verification charge that reverses in ~7 days when a card is added/changed); otherwise the account falls back to the Free plan with reduced limits.
findings.expiry: Trial lasts 14 days from signup; the Pro 25% discount lasts only the first year of Pro. API exposes trial state (on_trial, trial_lapse_date, renews_at) since 2026-07-09, confirming trial lapse is date-based.
findings.gotchas: (1) This is a trial, not a free tier — after 14 days you are billed at the chosen (yearly/monthly) rate unless you cancel or lack a saved payment method. (2) Trial price is quoted at the 1,000-subscriber tier; price scales as your list grows. (3) Annual billing = '12 months for the price of 10', no refunds beyond standard 30-day policy. (4) 'Discount applies only to your first year of Pro' — renews at standard $66 rate. (5) Pro trial is where SMS/Push/Chat features unlock — there is no standalone free SMS/Push/Chat trial separate from the plan trial.

findings.name: Developer / API access on Free plan (Email API v4, webhooks, App Store)
findings.detail: The Free plan help article lists 'API access' as an included extra, alongside free (non-paid) Kit App Store apps. Kit's developer platform (developers.kit.com) provides V4 REST API (api.kit.com/v4: broadcasts, subscribers, sequences CRUD, forms, webhooks 2.0, OAuth for apps, MCP docs server, V4 sandbox added June 2025) plus App Store publishing and OAuth (/v4/oauth, DCR RFC 7591 since 2026-05-20). API keys are test-only; OAuth is required to go live. No per-plan rate limits or quota tables are published. SMS, Push, and Chat: no SMS/push/chat API docs exist in the developer index (llms.txt) — the SMS marketing feature itself is paid-only (excluded from Free), so 'free SMS/Push/Chat API' does not exist as an offer.
findings.eligibility: Any plan is 'eligible for use with the API, apps and legacy integrations' per the API overview (it defers specifics to the pricing page); Free-plan help docs explicitly include 'API access', so Email-API usage is available on Free. No card, no .edu. No region limit. Gating detail (which endpoints differ by plan) is not publicly documented — free plan cannot install PAID Kit App Store apps.
findings.claim: 1) Create a Kit account on Free plan. 2) Generate an API key (test) or register an app via OAuth to access api.kit.com/v4 endpoints for free. 3) To ship an app, follow developers.kit.com/kit-app-store (OAuth required to go live). No separate signup or application for API access.
findings.expiry: Ongoing while account exists; Free API access ends if the account is cancelled. No stated sunset.
findings.gotchas: (1) 'API access' on Free is asserted by the help article but the developer docs only say the plan must be 'eligible' — plan-tier endpoint differences and rate limits are undocumented; verify empirically. (2) Paid App Store apps are not available on Free. (3) Email-stats retention is clamped to 5 years as of 2026-10-15 (older requests return 400). (4) Legacy v3/v4 webhooks are kept but Webhooks 2.0 (endpoint-based, signed, batched) shipped 2026-08-27 — plan code around the legacy format accordingly.

sunset_notes: No student/education license and no startup program exist for Kit as of 2026-10-22: kit.com/education and kit.com/startups return 404, the pricing page has no student/startup offer, and the help center's 14 collections (incl. 'Getting Started', 'Managing Your Account', 'Creator Network', 'Kit Studios') contain no education/students or startup-discount items. Kit's actual programs — Kit Expert program, Creator Network (5 free Smart Recommendation slots on every plan incl. Free), and Kit Studios (paid session-booking service) — are creator/consultant programs, not free student/startup offers. 2025-2026 material changes: (1) Kit executed its 'first price increase in 12 years' in 2025, effective after Oct 15, 2025, with 30-day notice (per help billing article) — paid plans became more expensive (Creator $39/mo monthly at the 1k tier; the Free plan's core offer — 10,000 subscribers, 1 user, no card — was not changed by this). (2) The '1,000 emails/mo' free-plan cap circulating in prior notes is NOT confirmed on any official page fetched today; the live pricing page says 'unlimited email broadcasts' for Free — treat 1,000/mo as unverified/outdated. (3) API/data policy: email-stats retention clamped to 5 years (2026-10-15); Webhooks 2.0 launched 2026-08-27 with legacy webhooks retained. (4) Historical: ConvertKit rebranded to Kit (2023) — older 'ConvertKit free plan' sources (300-subscriber cap era) do not apply to current offers.

findings.name: Vonage "Try it free" developer trial (free credit, no credit card required) — covers SMS, Voice, Verify, Email, Chat/Conversation APIs
findings.detail: Every Vonage Communications API marketing page (e.g. https://www.vonage.com/communications-apis/pricing/, /communications-apis/email/, /communications-apis/verify/pricing/) carries the CTA: 'Try it free — Start developing now with free credit. The exact free-credit dollar amount and trial duration are NOT stated on any public page I could read today; the amount is visible only inside the dashboard after signup. No .edu email required; open to anyone who creates a developer account.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no student/education requirement, no startup criteria, no credit card required (explicit on-page). Credit card is only needed later to pay for real usage; free test numbers are used to develop without charge.
findings.claim: Go to https://www.vonage.com/en-us/pricing/ (redirects content at /communications-apis/pricing/) or any product pricing page, click 'Try it free', create the account at ui.idp.vonage.com/sign-up/dashboard with no credit card; trial credit is applied in the dashboard (amount/duration not published on the web page).

findings.gotchas: (1) Marketing says 'free credit' but the public pages never state how much or for how long — treat any third-party figure (e.g. legacy $500 Nexmo trial) as unverified. (2) It is a trial, not a free tier: production messages, numbers, and real recipients cost money per unit after the credit runs out; there is no perpetual free tier for the APIs. (3) The www.vonage.com/en-us/pricing/ URL now 403s/404s for most fetchers — the live pricing content lives under /communications-apis/pricing/. findings.name: Vonage for Startups program — up to $75,000 in Vonage API credits + tailored support
findings.detail: Official page https://developer.vonage.com/en/startups: 'Vonage for Startups helps burgeoning brands with tailored support and up to $75,000 Vonage API credits.' Benefits: LEARN (technical workshops, 1:1s with Vonage product managers, custom solutions), RECEIVE TAILORED SUPPORT, BUILD (use credits to build MVP), CONNECT (Vonage startup community). FAQ confirms: 'This includes technical workshops, 1:1s with Vonage product managers, and any other support — such as up to $75,000 in Vonage API credits.'
findings.eligibility: Technology-agnostic; VC/incubator/accelerator backing NOT required. Hard criteria to be considered: early-stage (Pre-Seed to Series A), founded within the past 5 years, has a company website + associated emails, has a Vonage API account, and is not an existing managed customer. Existing customers may apply unless they already have an assigned Vonage account manager. No .edu email; not limited to any region on the page. Recommended before applying: public LinkedIn company page, public product signal (demo/waitlist/docs/GitHub repo), and a clear GTM plan tied to communications APIs.
findings.claim: Click 'Apply Now!' on https://developer.vonage.com/en/startups (form at https://wkf.ms/3YpFywo, MarketWIRED form), submit company details; selection is discretionary — credit amount up to $75,000 is negotiated, not guaranteed to every accepted applicant. No credit card required to apply.
findings.expiry: No program end date published on the page; cohort-based startup program, so terms/credit amounts may change per cohort.
findings.gotchas: 'Up to $75,000' is a cap, not a promise — actual awards vary; 'up to' wording means no fixed amount. Must hold a Vonage API account first. Managed-account customers are excluded. The credit is for Vonage APIs (communications), not a general cloud spend.

findings.name: Free Developer plan (forever-free chat tier)
findings.detail: Official chat pricing page read 2026-10-22. MAU 'Up to 1,000'; peak concurrent connections 'Up to 20'; messages/month 'Unlimited'; message storage 'Unlimited'; retention '6 months' (longer retention is an Enterprise add-on); feature set 'All Pro features'; support 'Community support'; 'No overages allowed'; 'No credit card required'. findings.claim: Sign up at sendbird.com/signup; in the subscription management page select the free Developer plan (you can switch to it at any point during the trial). Stays free and active as long as the account owner logs into the Sendbird dashboard at least once a year.
findings.expiry: Indefinite / free forever. Account is kept active by logging into the dashboard once a year; otherwise it can be deactivated.
findings.gotchas: 'No overages allowed': exceeding the soft MAU/PCC cap blocks new chat until quotas reset at the start of the next calendar month. 6-month message retention only. Community support only. The '2 apps' figure from prior notes is not explicitly published for this tier (page says 'multiple apps under one organization' but gives no numeric cap). 10K MAU in prior notes is stale; current cap is 1,000 MAU.

findings.name: 30-day free trial (Pro feature set)

findings.claim: Create a free account via the free-trial form (sendbird.com/form/free-trial). You get ~30 days of Pro features; to stay free, select the free Developer plan from the subscription management page at any point during the trial instead of a paid plan.
