provider: Tawk.to (chat) — fronts: Email, SMS, Push & Chat APIs

findings.name: Free-forever core plan (live chat, email ticketing, knowledge base, CRM, mobile-app push)
findings.detail: Core product is 'free for life' / 'Free Forever': unlimited live chat, hosted help center (knowledge base), ticketing, CRM/contacts and chat pages, with no published caps on agents, domains/properties, simultaneous chats, or conversation history; 50+ languages. Sign-up requires no credit card; widget is a code snippet. Monetization is via optional paid add-ons billed per property (website): remove 'Powered by tawk.to' branding $29/month; Video + Voice + Screensharing $29-49/month; hired human chat agents from $1/hour; virtual assistants from $7/hour. Push notifications to the tawk.to mobile app are part of the free account.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, any region; no .edu email, no startup age/funding caps, no credit card required. Note: limits are 'unlimited' per current marketing pages — tawk.to historically enforced fair-use limits, not published quotas.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up free at dashboard.tawk.to (email only, no card) 2) Create a property (site/app) 3) Install the widget snippet 4) Email ticketing, KB, CRM, and mobile-app push are enabled in the free plan 5) Add-on purchases optional, per property
findings.expiry: No expiry, no renewal, no trial period — the free tier is permanent, not a trial. Paid add-ons auto-renew per billing cycle.
findings.gotchas: Widget shows 'Powered by tawk.to' badge unless you pay $29/mo (stewie.io notes the add-on page has shown $29 or $39 depending on the page read, 3 Oct 2026 — likely annual vs monthly). Every add-on is billed per property: two sites = two bills. Data/egress: none published; privacy model: you host the service, tawk.to is provider. The 'free' value prop is the badge + add-on ecosystem, not volume caps.

findings.name: AI Assist 'Hobby' free tier (free AI chatbot add-on)
findings.detail: AI Assist has a forever-free 'Hobby' plan: 100 monthly AI message credits (500,000 characters), 1 AI chat agent, persona customization, instruction training, document data source, and crawling of up to 100 web pages. No credit card required. Paid tiers: Growth $29/mo ($290 annual; 1,000 credits, 3 agents, 500 crawled pages, up to 1000 API calls), Business $99/mo ($990 annual; 5,000 credits), Enterprise $399/mo ($3,990 annual; 20,000 credits). Purchased extra credits cost $30 per 1,000.
findings.eligibility: Any tawk.to user; no student/startup/region conditions. No CC for Hobby. Paid AI tiers need credit card or PayPal and have no free trial period.
findings.claim: Inside the free tawk.to dashboard, enable AI Assist and choose the Hobby plan; it activates immediately at $0. Upgrade to Growth+ requires adding a payment method.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier (100 credits/month, resets monthly), not a trial. Paid plans auto-renew at the billing cycle.
findings.gotchas: Credits are AI messages, not conversations — a multi-turn chat burns multiple credits (1 credit/AI reply; Auto model = 3 credits/reply; AI Transcription 1 credit/started minute, up to 5 per voice message). Third-party (stewie.io) claims the free Hobby plan CANNOT escalate to a human agent ('Escalation requires... a paid plan'), while the official help-center plan list includes 'Escalations to human agents' under Hobby — verify in the product, as settings may gate it. Hobby crawl cap of 100 pages is tiny; overages on paid plans cost extra. Per-property billing: each website has its own AI Assist bill.

findings.name: Free developer front: Tawk JS API, Webhooks, and Zapier connections
findings.detail: tawk.to's developer portal (developer.tawk.to) exposes a JavaScript API to manipulate the chat widget, webhooks for real-time event push to external services, and Zapier integration to 1,500+ services — all attached to the free platform account. The portal makes no statement of paid API tiers, quotas, or rate limits, and access rides on a free tawk.to account (API key per account). The REST/JS API is the chat API front; no separate free-credits or trial API product exists.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a tawk.to account (free, no CC); no student/startup gating. No documented per-call quotas on the public portal — treat rate limits as unpublished/fair-use.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free account 2) Generate an API key from the account 3) Use JS API / webhooks / Zapier from your site or services at $0, as long as the underlying tawk.to usage stays in the free core plan.
findings.expiry: No expiry — valid as long as the account exists. If AI Assist or other add-ons are involved, the paid-tier terms apply instead.
findings.gotchas: Webhooks only push out; inbound chat via API still depends on the (free) chat service. No published SLA or egress fees, but the API's value is capped by whatever the free core allows. A third-party (AgentDeals) record of a 2026-09-12 pricing 'restructure' was retracted by the tracker itself; no API pricing change verified.

findings.name: Free email + Twilio SMS fronts into the shared inbox
findings.detail: tawk.to's free plan includes Email ticketing (connect your email and manage email conversations from the tawk.to inbox — free). For SMS, tawk.to's help center has a 'Twilio SMS' category (5 articles) describing how to connect SMS services such as Twilio to tawk.to; the tawk.to side is free, but you pay Twilio directly for the number and per-message rates (US messaging is commonly ~$0.0075-0.020/message plus monthly number fee). No tawk.to-owned free SMS or free push-SMS credits exist.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a free tawk.to account + a Twilio account/credential to connect. No CC required for tawk.to itself; Twilio billing is separate and region-dependent (carrier fees outside US/Canada).
findings.claim: 1) Free tawk.to account 2) Create a Twilio number (paid, Twilio side) 3) Follow help.tawk.to 'Twilio SMS' articles to link credentials 4) SMS threads appear in the free shared inbox.
findings.expiry: No tawk.to-side expiry; Twilio number/usage is billed continuously on your Twilio account.
findings.gotchas: The SMS front is not free end-to-end: Twilio's number fee and per-message rates pass through, and international carrier surcharges can be substantial. tawk.to has no native 'push notification' product distinct from its mobile-app push, which is free with the account.

findings.name: No tawk.to education (.edu) license, student program, or startup program
findings.detail: No tawk.to-specific free offer for students, educators, or startups exists as of 2026-10-22. tawk.to's StartCamp page (www.tawk.to/partner/startcamp/) is a third-party partner directory listing: the 'free credits / $1,000,000 in savings' language belongs to StartCamp (startcamp.com), not to tawk.to, and tawk.to offers no discount or free-tier upgrade on that page. tawk.to's own partner program is commission-based ('up to 20% commission', 'lifetime payouts') — revenue sharing, not a free-usage benefit. Aggregator pages (costbench, StudentPerks, TryTrick) list generic/boilerplate 'education discount' and 'startup program' sections that explicitly state 'we don't have tawk.to-specific terms verified yet' or simply don't include tawk.to. Coupon-site codes (e.g. 10% off 'FEB10' on coupon sites, Oct 2026) are unverified, auto-generated, and contradict the 'free forever' core.
findings.eligibility: N/A — no program to qualify for. Effectively, students and startups get the same free-forever core plan and free AI Hobby tier as everyone else, with no CC required.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Students/startups use the standard free sign-up (email, no card) at dashboard.tawk.to; optionally join StartCamp separately for its curated third-party deals.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Do not trust templated 'tawk.to education discount' pages on costbench-style sites or 'verified' 10% coupon codes on coupon aggregators — none of them present tawk.to-offered terms. No sunset: the absence of programs is stable; the 2025-2026 changes were add-on pricing (AI Assist tiers, branding removal), not removal of any student/startup offer.

findings.name: Twilio free trial account — product-specific free units, 30-day expiry, no credit card
findings.detail: Official trial docs (read 2026-10-22): trial grants product-specific free units, NOT a shared dollar balance — exactly '100 SMS messages, 100 WhatsApp messages, 3,000 emails, and 75 voice minutes'. Trial phone numbers are Twilio-provided (you don't pick them). SMS/voice are locked to your sign-up country (determined by the phone number used at registration); trial email is restricted to your sign-up email address. You may only send to pre-verified phone numbers, capped at 5 per account (sign-up number is auto-verified). A US/CA trial toll-free number lets you message up to 5 pre-designated numbers. Custom message bodies, email content and WhatsApp templates are NOT available on trial (Twilio-provided templates only). A2P 10DLC registration requires a paid account, so 10DLC long-code US A2P SMS is unavailable on trial. Trial accounts expire after 30 days — you must upgrade before the window closes (Console: Trial banner > 'Upgrade your account' > profile + address + starting balance + payment details). Same Account SID/Auth Token carry into the paid account; after upgrade, 'a fresh set of post-upgrade free units for eligible products' are granted and deducted before any paid usage. Console has a 'Free units tracker'. Pricing after units: SMS $0.0083/msg, voice $0.0085/min inbound, $0.014/min outbound.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, any region — sign-up requires name, email and phone number; no .edu email, no company eligibility. Credit card NOT required for the trial.
findings.claim: Sign up at twilio.com/try-twilio (now redirects straight to the signup flow) without a credit card; use the assigned trial numbers, stay within 5 verified recipients / sign-up country, burn 100 SMS + 100 WhatsApp + 3,000 emails + 75 voice minutes before day 30; upgrade in Console before expiry to keep the SID and receive a fresh set of post-upgrade free units.
findings.expiry: Trial account hard-expires after 30 days. Free email sub-offers (below) run 60 days. Post-upgrade free units are one-time, deducted before paid usage.
findings.gotchas: Trial units are quantity caps, not a dollar credit — there is no $15-style credit in the current model. Trial vs free: once the 30-day window passes without upgrade, the account is gone even if unused units remain. Trial SMS/voice cannot reach other countries and cannot use custom bodies; WhatsApp trial units are capped by Twilio-provided templates. US A2P (10DLC) business use requires a paid account. Free units do not transfer between products.

findings.name: Twilio Email API (SendGrid) 'Free Trial' plan — 100 emails/day for 60 days, no credit card
findings.detail: Email API pricing page (read 2026-10-22): Free Trial = '100 emails/day for 60 days', '$0/mo for 60 days', 'no credit card required'. Includes analytics, deliverability optimization, dynamic template editor, 1 event webhook, 1 additional teammate. Paid: Essentials from $19.95/mo, Pro from $89.95/mo, Premier custom; per-email rates are volume-tiered (3k–5M+ tiers, taxes/overages apply). Domain Authentication (SPF/DKIM) and reverse DNS are part of setup.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no credit card for the 60-day trial; a deliverable domain is required for real sending.
findings.claim: Sign up for Twilio/SendGrid Email API, pick the Free Trial plan, authenticate a domain (SPF/DKIM), send up to 100 emails/day for 60 days at $0.
findings.expiry: 60-day free window, then conversion to a paid plan (Essentials $19.95/mo) is required to keep sending.
findings.gotchas: This is a time-boxed trial, NOT a permanent free tier — SendGrid's old permanent free plan (400 emails/day) was killed in 2023 and has not been restored; do not plan ongoing free sending. '100 emails/day' is a daily cap, not a monthly pool; overages and taxes apply on paid plans; 'Twilio Email API' (SendGrid) is a separate product from 'Twilio Email' (the newer $0.0013/email per-unit product, covered by the 3,000-email trial units).

findings.name: Twilio Marketing Campaigns free plan — 2,000 contacts / 6,000 free emails per month
findings.detail: Marketing Campaigns pricing page (read 2026-10-22): 'Free Marketing Campaigns Plan lets you store up to 2,000 contacts and send 6,000 free emails per month', including 3 email testing credits, 1 signup form, 1 additional teammate, ticket support, A/B testing and Automation. The same page's Free Trial card lists a 60-day trial of 100 emails/day with 100 stored contacts ('$0/mo for 60 days', 'no credit card required'). Paid: Basic from $15/mo (5K–100K contact tiers), Advanced from $60/mo (dedicated IPs, up to 1,000 teammates), Custom; overage rates $0.0023–$0.0075 per extra email depending on tier. Email testing credit add-ons $18–$800/mo.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no credit card required to start; no .edu or company requirements.
findings.claim: Sign up for Twilio Marketing Campaigns; you get the free plan (up to 2,000 contacts, 6,000 emails/month) after a 60-day trial onboarding window of 100 emails/day.
findings.expiry: Free plan is ongoing as long as you stay within 2,000 contacts / 6,000 emails per month; the 60-day '$0/mo' trial period is the entry window, after which the free-quota plan (or a paid plan) applies.
findings.gotchas: The page mixes two free concepts — a 60-day trial card (100 emails/day, 100 contacts) and an ongoing 'Free Marketing Campaigns Plan' (2,000 contacts / 6,000 emails/mo); read the fine print when claiming which limit applies to you. No free dedicated IPs (Advanced only). '100 emails each day for 60 days' on the trial card is a hard daily cap, not 6,000/day.

findings.name: Twilio Email (per-unit product) — 3,000 free emails in trial, then $0.0013/email
findings.detail: Main pricing page (read 2026-10-22) lists 'Twilio Email: $0.0013/email' with no free monthly allocation; the trial free-unit bundle includes 3,000 emails (trial emails restricted to your sign-up email address). No permanent free tier for this product — it is pay-per-email after the trial bundle.
findings.eligibility: Trial: anyone (no CC). Paid: standard Twilio account with billing; domain authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC, reverse DNS) required for deliverability.
findings.claim: Use the 3,000 trial email units inside the 30-day trial; thereafter buy per-email at $0.0013 or pair with the SendGrid Email API trial for higher daily volumes.
findings.expiry: 3,000-unit trial bundle only (30-day trial window); no renewal/recurring free allocation found on pricing pages.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse 'Twilio Email' ($0.0013/email, per-unit) with 'Twilio Email API' (SendGrid, 100/day free trial) or 'Marketing Campaigns' (6,000/mo free plan) — three different SKUs with three different free offers. After the trial bundle, egress is pure pay-per-use.

findings.name: Twilio Startups program — free educational resources only; explicitly NO startup credits
findings.detail: Startup solutions page (read 2026-10-22) targets 'early stage companies' and offers: a free account with 'trial credits' to start building, free educational resources (onboarding guides, tutorials, docs, videos for messaging/email/verification/voice/Studio), paid support plans month-to-month, and a 'Connect with our team' form to reach the Twilio Startups team. FAQ states verbatim: 'Every Twilio customer gets a small credit when they open an account to start building their first project' and 'We do not offer additional credits to startups at this time.' Page specifies no startup-age limit, no funding cap, no geographic requirement.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage/startup companies generally; no stated age or funding cap on the page; no credit card required for the base trial account.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a Twilio account and verify email + phone; 2) use free Developer Hub resources; 3) fill the 'Connect with our team' form on the startups page to engage the Twilio Startups team; 4) upgrade in Console (add payment + funds, 'upgrade account') when ready to pay as you go.
findings.expiry: No program duration or renewal stated; the 'small credit' (trial free units: 100 SMS/100 WhatsApp/3,000 emails/75 min) follows the 30-day trial terms; no expiry date published.
findings.gotchas: No extra startup credits exist — if you expected a startup-specific credit pool or discount, it is not offered at this time. After the trial bundle you pay standard pay-as-you-go (SMS $0.0083, voice $0.0085–0.014/min). Phone-number rental and data/egress are paid on production.

findings.name: Education/students: no student or .edu program found — education page is institution-sales only
findings.detail: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/solutions/education (read 2026-10-22) targets universities/colleges as customers (enrollment messaging, student engagement, fraud prevention, alumni outreach); it offers only 'Sign up for a free trial—no credit card required' or 'Contact sales'. The developer hub (twilio.com/en-us/developers) lists Code Exchange, Resource Center (guides/webinars/podcasts), events and community (Discord/Reddit/Luma) but no student/bootcamp program. The only free access for students is therefore the general 30-day trial with its free units (trial requires a personal phone number; sign-up country restricts SMS/voice).
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — no eligibility rules because no student/education free offer exists today. General trial: anyone, no CC.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim: students get the same general trial (100 SMS/100 WhatsApp/3,000 emails/75 voice minutes, 30 days, no CC). Free courses exist only as unstructured developer resources (docs, Code Exchange, Resource Center, webinars), not as a credentialed program.
findings.expiry: n/a (no program). General trial: 30 days.
findings.gotchas: Twilio University (former free bootcamp) is gone — /en-us/university 404s and no developer-hub link exists. The free 'resources' are content, not account credits. Note: WebSearch was unavailable in this research session (session search budget exhausted), so absence-claims rest on today's fetches of the main official pages, not an exhaustive crawl — confidence is medium, not high.

findings.name: Push & Chat APIs (Conversations / Push): no dedicated free tier found — trial units + per-active-user pricing only
findings.detail: The main pricing page (read 2026-10-22) lists 'Conversations API: $0.05 per active user per month' with no free monthly allocation, no trial-free-unit line for chat/push, and no push-notification product row at all. Twilio's 'Conversations' (successor to Chat API, /docs/conversations-classic) supports web chat, WhatsApp and SMS channels; push delivery works via Expo push tokens inside the Conversations SDK. No public free tier or trial allotment specific to chat/push was found on any fetched Twilio pricing page. Trial free units (100 SMS / 100 WhatsApp / 3,000 emails / 75 voice minutes) are what cover chat-channel traffic during trial.
findings.eligibility: Same as general Twilio account: anyone, no CC for trial; chat/push paid usage requires a production account (CC).
findings.claim: Build a Conversations-based chat/push app on the trial account using the 100 SMS + 100 WhatsApp free units; no free chat/push unit bundle exists to claim on its own.
findings.expiry: n/a (no free tier); trial bundle follows the 30-day trial terms.
findings.gotchas: Post-trial, Conversations costs $0.05/active user/month on top of per-message channel costs — active-user billing can be stealthy (a user counts as active while connected). Push 'free' only in the sense of trial-channel units; there is no found permanent free push tier (SendGrid Push, where available, ships with paid email plans). Confidence is medium: absence confirmed on fetched pages, but no dedicated push product pricing page was located in this session (search budget exhausted).

findings.name: Adjacent free tiers on the main pricing page (outside listed frontends, included for completeness): Flex/Video 5,000 free hours, TaskRouter first 100 tasks/mo free, Functions/Serverless 10,000 free invocations
findings.detail: Main pricing page (read 2026-10-22): 'Flex & Video: Start with 5,000 hours free. $1/active user hour or $150/named user per month.' 'TaskRouter: First 100 tasks/month are free, then $0.06/task.' 'Functions: Start with 10,000 free invocations, then $0.0001 per invocation.' findings.claim: If the research scope is relaxed beyond Email/SMS/Push/Chat: claim the 5,000 Flex/Video free hours, 100 TaskRouter tasks/month, and 10,000 Functions invocations at no cost.

findings.name: Self-hosted Meilisearch (open source, MIT)
findings.detail: Meilisearch engine is open source under the MIT license; self-hosting is free with no usage limits (no caps on documents, indexes, or queries). You deploy it on your own infra; only your own hosting/compute cost applies. No credit card, no account, no region limit, no expiry. Verified on the official pricing page FAQ: 'Meilisearch is open source under the MIT license. Self-hosting is free... with no usage limits.'
findings.eligibility: Anyone: students, startups, enterprises. No .edu email, no company age/funding cap, no credit card. No region restrictions.
findings.claim: No claim needed: download the binary/Docker image or install via package managers from GitHub (meilisearch/meilisearch, MIT licensed) and run it on your own infrastructure. Free and permanent.
findings.gotchas: MIT license is permissive (no copyleft obligations on your app). Hidden costs are yours: server hosting, storage/egress, and operational maintenance. No hosted free tier substitutes for it.
findings.expiry: None — perpetual under the MIT license.

findings.name: Meilisearch Cloud free trial (14 days, no credit card)
findings.detail: Meilisearch Cloud (hosted, from ~$20/month; examples on pricing page: 100K docs + 50K searches ≈ $30/mo, or XS instance ≈ $23/mo) offers a '14-day free trial, no credit card required' per the official pricing page. The trial page/signup (cloud.meilisearch.com/register) asks only for name, work email, password (or Google/GitHub OAuth) — no published fixed dollar credit; trial scope/terms are not itemized on public pages. No permanent free hosted tier exists — after 14 days you move to paid usage-based or resource-based billing.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who signs up; work email requested; no published region limit; no credit card required.
findings.claim: Start from the pricing or Cloud page: 'Start free trial' CTA → register at cloud.meilisearch.com/register (email or Google/GitHub) → create an instance and use it for 14 days.
findings.expiry: Trial ends after 14 days, after which paid Cloud pricing applies (from $20/month).
findings.gotchas: Trial is a trial, not a free tier — nothing renews. No published dollar credit amount; billing after trial is usage- or resource-based, so costs depend on docs/searches. No documented post-trial data-retention terms on public pages. Free offer is for the hosted service only; self-hosting (finding 1) is the only unlimited free option.

findings.name: Startup offer (informal, sales-led)
findings.detail: Meilisearch's startup-facing page ('Startups' under Solutions) has no formal published program — no fixed discount percentage, no duration, no company-age/funding caps. It offers: (a) the free 14-day Cloud trial, (b) free self-hosting during build/test ('you can self-host the engine for free while you build and test'), and (c) sales-led engagement: 'We work with teams of all stages on custom pricing and volume discounts, regardless of company size or funding stage' (page FAQ).
findings.eligibility: Effectively open: page FAQ says custom pricing applies 'regardless of company size or funding stage', so no stated age or funding cap. No .edu requirement, no card requirement for the trial.
findings.claim: No self-serve claim for the discount itself: use the 'Startups' page CTAs — 'Start free trial' (self-serve) or 'Get custom demo' / contact sales to negotiate a custom plan. Any discount is case-by-case and unpublished.
findings.gotchas: Do not assume a standard startup discount exists; it is a sales conversation, not a published program, so terms are opaque and not guaranteed. The only self-serve free element is the 14-day trial.
findings.expiry: No published expiry; trial portion expires in 14 days.

sunset_notes: No student/education program found: no education license or .edu-based offer exists for Meilisearch; the only public 'free' tracks are self-hosting (MIT, permanent) and the 14-day Cloud trial. No 2025–2026 sunset of a specific free offer was verifiable today: the 2026 blog listing (page 1) shows no pricing-change or program-sunset announcements, but WebSearch was unavailable this session (shared session search budget exhausted), so 2025 changes could not be searched across the web — treat the absence of a formal startup/education program as verified via the official pages fetched today, not as a searched conclusion. Known-so-far claims checked: MIT self-hosted = unlimited/free (confirmed, high confidence); Meilisearch Cloud 14-day trial, no card, no permanent free hosted tier (confirmed on the official pricing page today, 2026-10-22). Sources: https://www.meilisearch.com/pricing, https://www.meilisearch.com/solutions/startup, https://www.meilisearch.com/cloud.

provider: data.gov.uk / UK Open Data — Open Data Inventory (ODI) CKAN directory API + National Data Library (data.gov.uk rebrand; the "National Data Hub" of the task is a conflation of the NDL)

findings.name: ODI / data.gov.uk directory API (CKAN) — free, no key, no account
findings.detail: The legacy ODI (Open Data Inventory, CKAN) directory API is still live and free for everyone, including students and startups. Verified 2026-10-22: GET https://data.gov.uk/api/3/action/... 301-redirects to https://ckan.publishing.service.gov.uk/api/3/action/... and package_search returns success with count = 59,462 datasets (the '30,000+' figure is stale). Standard CKAN actions available (package_search, organization_list, resource_show, datastore endpoints on some datasets). No API key, no registration, no credit card, no rate-limit headers or quota fields returned. All datasets are licensed under the Open Government Licence (OGL); platform content under OGL v3.0.
findings.eligibility: Unconditional — open to anyone, no .edu email, no age/funding criteria, no region limits. Free, indefinite, renewable by nature (public service, no expiry).
findings.claim: No claiming required. Just call the REST endpoints, e.g. https://data.gov.uk/api/3/action/package_search?rows=10 (or via ckan.publishing.service.gov.uk). For programmatic bulk metadata, use the CKAN dumps (see separate finding). Dataset publishers are public-sector orgs; for a specific dataset, contact the publisher if you need something not published.
findings.expiry: No expiry. In the March 2026 rebrand the directory was kept 'unchanged for now'; the June 2026 roadmap lists 'critical improvements to the original directory' as ongoing work, with no deprecation date announced.
findings.gotchas: The CKAN dataset page's API links/docs are dated 2014 and the old /terms-and-conditions page now 404s, so rate limits are undocumented — be gentle on traffic. ~25% of dataset resource links are broken and many datasets are stale; the API metadata is not a guarantee the underlying data file exists. 'ODI' here means the Open Data Inventory (a GDS-operated portal), not the Open Data Institute nonprofit.

findings.name: Open data downloads via the data.gov.uk directory (Search & CMS front) — free, OGL-licensed
findings.detail: Every dataset on the original open data directory (the 'data.gov.uk directory', still searchable alongside the new National Data Library curated collections) is free to download in its native format (CSV, JSON, S3 pointers, API feeds). Free, unlimited use with attribution under the Open Government Licence; no account, trial, or tier of any kind — there is simply no pricing model on data.gov.uk. Students and startups get the identical offer as everyone else.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no .edu requirement, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card. OGL v3.0 applies to site content; individual datasets state their licence (OGL, ODbL, CC, or publisher-specific).
findings.claim: Search the directory (link on https://www.data.gov.uk/) or use the CKAN API, pick a dataset, download the data files. For data not available in bulk, the support page directs users to contact the dataset publisher directly; data.gov.uk itself cannot host data or combine datasets.
findings.expiry: Indefinite; subject to each publisher's lifecycle. No sunset date announced for the directory.
findings.gotchas: Data quality is the main gotcha, not access cost: the service has been underinvested since ~2017, with many broken/outdated links (per GDS's own March 2026 blog). Some datasets are CC-licensed with restrictions (e.g. no commercial use without attribution) — check the licence field per dataset before building a startup on it.

findings.name: Bulk CKAN metadata dumps (free, nightly, S3)
findings.detail: GDS publishes a zipped CSV or JSONL dump of the metadata for all data.gov.uk datasets nightly, and hosts historical dumps in a public S3 bucket (dgu-ckan-metadata-dumps.s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com, us-east/eu-west). The .jsonl 'v2' dump (ckanapi dump output, includes full organization details, QA/broken-link flags, format detection) supersedes the old JSON dump. Free to fetch; no key. Uncompressed files can be ~170 MB+ — build pipelines rather than loading into spreadsheets, per the publisher's own note.
findings.eligibility: Unconditional, free, no account or CC.
findings.claim: Grab the dump URL from the dataset page (https://www.data.gov.uk/dataset/b5e4be7e-6c36-41b6-9d48-cae195c32e34/meta-data-for-data-gov-uk-datasets) or the S3 bucket directly (list objects, no credentials needed for a public bucket).
findings.expiry: Published nightly; no announced end date.
findings.gotchas: Dumps are metadata only (links + descriptions), not the datasets themselves; old .json dump was discontinued after a 3-month transition in 2016 — use .v2.jsonl. The 2015 CSV column change (datasets vs resources in separate files) is still in effect; join on the 'Name' column.

findings.name: National Data Library (data.gov.uk rebrand) + GDS API Hub (alpha) — free, early-stage, no products to buy yet
findings.detail: As of March 25, 2026 data.gov.uk launched as the 'National Data Library' (NDL): curated data collections (Business & economy, Environment, Government, Land & property, People, Transport, Early years) plus a 'data manual', backed by >£100M within DSIT's £1.9B spending-review allocation. Separately, GDS's API Hub was in a 12-week alpha (results blogged 28 Nov 2025) with a planned MVP of a free central API catalogue (with quality/security scores and a signed-in developer portal) aligned with data.gov.uk and datamarketplace.gov.uk. All of it is free-open-access; there is no paid tier, trial credit, startup program, or education license anywhere in the NDL or the old directory.
findings.eligibility: Open access, no sign-in required for browsing/collections; the API Hub's 'signed-in developer portal' is only a future exploration. No .edu or startup criteria because no gated offer exists.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim — browse https://www.data.gov.uk/ collections and the roadmap; give feedback via the forms to influence direction. GDS is actively soliciting developer input on the API Hub (blog feedback form).
findings.expiry: Roadmap updated at least every 6 months (next review after the June 2026 version); 'details on the National Data Library in spring 2026' per the January 2026 progress update — i.e. new access mechanisms may ship in 2026. The API Hub has no committed date.
findings.gotchas: Do not build on the API Hub — it is an alpha research program, not a product. The NDL currently exposes only non-personal, aggregated data; personal-data linkage (kickstarter projects) is exploratory. The 'National Data Hub' open data API from the task's known-so-far note is not a thing: the term does not appear in any official 2026 document — the program is the National Data Library.

findings.name: No student-specific, startup-specific, or education-licensed offers exist on data.gov.uk
findings.detail: data.gov.uk (ODI CKAN API, directory downloads, NDL collections) has no pricing at all: no free-tier vs paid-tier distinction, no trial credits, no startup program, no .edu-gated education license, no credit-card-on-file free plans. The entire offer is unconditionally free OGL-licensed public data with no registration. For students and startups the 'free offer' is therefore simply universal free access — identical to everyone else's — with the caveats in the findings above (broken links, per-dataset licence variants, undocumented rate limits).
findings.eligibility: N/A — universal, unconditional.
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim; just use the API/download links directly.
findings.expiry: Indefinite public service; no offer to renew.
findings.gotchas: Watch for NDL milestones: the January 2026 progress update promises more detail in spring 2026, and kickstarter projects (legal data for SMEs, Met Office weather, social care) could spawn new access services; the GDS API Hub MVP may eventually add an authenticated developer portal. Also note the 2025-2026 external sunsets listed in sunset_notes.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: (1) data.gov.uk was redesigned/rebranded as the National Data Library, published 25 March 2026 (new landing page, curated collections, data manual, public roadmap at /roadmap/, June 2026 version); the original ODI CKAN directory survives as the 'data.gov.uk directory', unchanged for now, with GDS fixing 'critical issues'. (2) The 'National Data Hub' named in the task's known-so-far is a misnomer — no such API product appears in official documents; the program is the National Data Library (>£100M of DSIT's £1.9B; progress update 26 Jan 2026; spring-2026 detail milestone). (3) Related UK open-data sunsets: ONS PublishMyData API fully decommissioned 31 March 2025 (outage from 3 March 2025; data moved to ONS portals and the new ONS Data API / api.beta.ons.gov.uk/v1/search), and ONS retired its aggregated-search /data endpoints in favour of the ONS Search API. (4) The old ODI terms-and-conditions URL (data.gov.uk/terms-and-conditions) now 404s, so documented rate limits are gone — access remains free and keyless. (5) No free-tier, trial-credit, startup-program, or education-license offer existed or changed on data.gov.uk in 2025-2026: it was and is unconditionally free under the Open Government Licence, so there is nothing student/startup-specific to sunset.

provider: KeystoneJS (keystonejs.com) — MIT-licensed headless CMS + GraphQL API framework by Thinkmill (AUS)

findings.name: Free self-hosted open-source use (Keystone 6, MIT license) — the only free offer; no cloud tier, trial credits, startup program, or education license exists
findings.detail: $0, perpetual, no feature gating. As of 2026-10-22 the official site states 'Free forever' and 'Batteries included. No limitations' (all field types, access control, session management, custom schema, Prisma DB migrations, TypeScript, automated CRUD, event hooks). The GitHub repo keystonejs/keystone ships an MIT LICENSE ('Copyright (c) 2024 Thinkmill Labs Pty Ltd'). Current line is Keystone 6, published on npm as @keystone-6/* (@keystone-6/core@8.x); active maintenance confirmed by releases through 2026-08-31 (a 8.0.0 major shipped Jul 28, 2026). Unlimited lists/content models, unlimited editors, unlimited API calls — you only pay your own hosting. Verified today: https://keystonejs.com/ , https://github.com/keystonejs/keystone (LICENSE), https://keystonejs.com/roadmap. No official pricing/startup/education pages exist on keystonejs.com — the only paid upsell is Thinkmill's enterprise support/consulting (services page, custom quotes; aggregators like apis.io list paid 'Enterprise Capacity/Capability/Advisory' service plans, all unverified generated content, none free).
findings.eligibility: Everyone, no conditions: no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no registration, no credit card, no region limits. Commercial use allowed under MIT.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim or apply for: run `npm create keystone-app` (or clone keystonejs/keystone from GitHub), define your schema in TypeScript, run Prisma migrations, deploy to any Node.js host of your choice (DigitalOcean, Heroku, Render, Vercel, self-managed infra per the official site). MIT license is granted automatically by using the code.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal — MIT license is perpetual; project is actively maintained (releases ongoing as of 2026-08-31). Free-forever, not a trial.
findings.gotchas: (1) No managed/hosted Keystone cloud exists, so you own hosting, backups, scaling, and security — third-party reviews peg small-project infra at ~$6–20/mo VPS; that cost is the real price. (2) Old Keystone 5 (keystonejs/keystone-5, Express/Mongoose/MongoDB) has been in maintenance mode since 2021 — 'keystone' and '@keystone-6' on npm are different packages. (3) GraphQL-first API (REST not provided out of the box) and it is a framework you deploy, not a managed SaaS with autoscale/SSO/audit. (4) Beware third-party plan listings (apis.io, hostiso etc.) describing Keystone 'plans' — those are unverified generated catalogs or generic shared hosting, not offers from the KeystoneJS project. (5) A session web-search budget cap blocked one dedicated 2025–26 startup/education-offer search, but the official site + roadmap + GitHub show no such programs exist or were ever announced.

sunset_notes: No free offer was sunset or materially changed in 2025–2026. License has remained MIT (no shift to BSL/EE gating unlike some peers). Historical changes still relevant: Keystone 5 entered active maintenance mode in 2021 (repo moved to keystonejs/keystone-5, feature-frozen; security fixes only) and Keystone 6 reached GA Dec 2021 and now ships under the @keystone-6 npm namespace with an 8.x core (2026 major release Jul 28, 2026). There is no official paid cloud tier, no trial-credit program, no startup program, and no education license to sunset — Thinkmill's enterprise support services are the sole paid (custom-quote) offering.

findings.name: Data.gov open data catalog — free, no key, no card, no account
findings.detail: catalog.data.gov holds 431,094+ datasets from US federal agencies, with direct file downloads (CSV, JSON, XML, XLSX, ZIP) and full search/filter (by organization, geospatial extent, popularity, recency, 'only show datasets with a downloadable file'). No registration, sign-in, API key, or credit card is required to search or download. US federal government works are generally in the public domain, so no special education or commercial license is needed. Counts and dataset counts are live on data.gov/metrics. Gotcha: data.gov does not host the underlying data — it's a metadata catalog that harvests agency pages; broken download links and data-quality issues are the agencies' responsibility (contact DataGovHelp@gsa.gov or the owning agency).
findings.eligibility: Universal: any student, startup, or organization anywhere in the world. No .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card, no region limit.
findings.claim: Go to catalog.data.gov, search or filter datasets, and click the download links on the dataset page (filter: 'Only show datasets with a downloadable file'). No signup at all.
findings.expiry: Indefinite — maintained under the OPEN Government Data Act; no trial period, no expiry, no renewal.
findings.gotchas: No data hosting/quality guarantees; link rot possible; individual agencies may impose their own download constraints on their source pages; attribution to the owning agency is courtesy, not law.

findings.name: Data.gov catalog API v4 (api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4) — free API key, 1,000 req/hour
findings.detail: The current catalog API is a public REST/JSON API at https://api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4/ with endpoints: /search (q, sort, per_page default 10, org_slug, keyword, spatial_filter/spatial_geometry/spatial_within, after-cursor pagination), /api/keywords (size up to 1000), /api/locations/search, /api/location/{id}, /api/organizations, /harvest_record/{id} (+ /raw and /transformed). A key is REQUIRED (X-Api-Key header, api_key query param, or Basic auth with key as username), but keys are free via api.data.gov: a 40-character personal key with 1,000 requests/hour and no daily cap, valid across all api.data.gov services. No credit card required, no key expiry stated; overuse returns HTTP 429 with a temporary 1-hour block; admins can disable keys. Responses include X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining headers. Errors: 403 API_KEY_MISSING/INVALID/UNVERIFIED, 422 bad params, 404 missing resource.
findings.eligibility: Universal: anyone (student/startup/company) can request a free key. No .edu email, no funding cap, no credit card, no region limit.
findings.claim: Sign up free at api.data.gov to receive a 40-char personal API key (covers all 450+ participating agency APIs too), then call https://api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4/search with the X-Api-Key header. 1,000 requests/hour, no daily cap.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry/renewal. Rate limit is 1,000 req/hour, no daily cap; 429 blocks last one hour. Keys can be disabled by administrators.
findings.gotchas: Key is mandatory here (unlike direct downloads); DCAT-US v3.0 migration means the access_level filter (public / restricted public / non-public) has only 'strong but not guaranteed' coverage; this v4 API replaced the CKAN-based catalog API (see sunset_notes).

findings.name: api.data.gov DEMO_KEY — no-signup trial access to the catalog API
findings.detail: The catalog API documentation provides a DEMO_KEY for 'initially exploring APIs prior to signing up'. Limits: 30 requests per IP address per hour AND 50 requests per IP address per day. The docs explicitly state it 'is not suitable for production use or automated queries'. This is the only true zero-account offer on the API front; upgrading to a personal key (free, no CC) removes both caps to 1,000/hour.
findings.eligibility: Universal, anonymous — no account, no .edu, no credit card, no region limit. IP-based limits, so shared/CGNAT IPs consume the 50/day pool together.
findings.claim: Use the published DEMO_KEY value with the same X-Api-Key header against https://api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4/ endpoints for up to 30 req/hour and 50 req/day per IP. For more, request a free personal key at api.data.gov.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated; per-IP windows (hourly/daily). Intended for exploration only.
findings.gotchas: Strictly trial-grade: 50 requests/day per IP; shared IPs compound the limit; docs prohibit production/automated use; hitting 429 waits an hour.

findings.name: api.data.gov free service key — one key across 450+ federal agency APIs (25 agencies)
findings.detail: api.data.gov is GSA/Technology Transformation Services' 'free API management service for federal agencies' (built on NREL's open-source API Umbrella). A single free personal key 'gives you access to all APIs from agencies participating in api.data.gov's service' — 25 agencies and 450+ APIs including USGS, NASA, and FDA services. Keys are 40-character, free, with per-user rate limits (the catalog API slot is 1,000/hour; other participating APIs define their own limits per agency). Three ways to pass the key: X-Api-Key header, api_key query parameter (works with POST/PUT), or Basic auth (key as username, empty password). Usage analytics/dashboards are provided to keyholders; no credit card or account type restrictions were stated anywhere on the service pages.
findings.eligibility: Universal: students, startups, and any organization. No .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit card, no region limit; US government service open to all.
findings.claim: Register free at api.data.gov (key issuance described as 'quick and easy'), then call any participating agency API (e.g. the v4 Data.gov catalog API) with your key in the X-Api-Key header.
findings.expiry: No key expiry stated; keys can be administratively disabled (API_KEY_DISABLED); 429 rate-limit blocks lift after one hour; per-user limits can be raised or lowered per user.
findings.gotchas: The service itself is free but some underlying agency datasets/APIs may carry their own usage terms (docs say 'contact the API owner at the agency that offers the service'); per-API limits vary by agency; key issuance is unverified so expect a manual step (GSA form/email) — verify on the signup page.

findings.name: Education license / startup program: none exist (by design)
findings.detail: Data.gov has no student tier, .edu discount, educational license, trial credits, or startup program, and no paid tier at all: it is a free, publicly funded GSA portal, so there is nothing to license. Every offer above is the same free program available to all users identically. Anyone citing a 'Data.gov student plan' is describing something that does not exist.
findings.eligibility: Not applicable — no eligibility screen anywhere; same free access for students, startups, researchers, and commercial users.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim: use the free catalog downloads or the free api.data.gov key like anyone else. For classroom use, point students at catalog.data.gov (no account) or a shared DEMO_KEY/educational api.data.gov key.
findings.expiry: Not applicable.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse with agency products that do have programs (e.g., Google for Education, AWS Credit for Research); no startup program replaces the universally free baseline.

provider: Data.gov (US Federal Open Data API, GSA / Technology Transformation Services)
sunset_notes: Changes verified 2025-2026 (read from official pages today; WebSearch budget was exhausted, so this reflects the official pages rather than news searches): (1) The catalog API was rebuilt: the new v4 API at api.gsa.gov/technology/datagov/v4 (keyed via api.data.gov) 'replaces the previous CKAN-based API' per resources.data.gov/catalog-api; the docs claim the older CKAN endpoint 'remains available in a read-only state for existing integrations', but probes to catalog.data.gov's former CKAN paths (/api/3/action/..., /api/3/, /api/2/, /dataset.json) all returned HTTP 404 today, so that read-only availability is uncertain or on a different host — low confidence, verify before relying on legacy CKAN integrations. (2) The legacy standalone Data.gov 'Developer Program' key portal keys.data.gov no longer resolves (DNS ENOTFOUND today), i.e. that older free-API-key program (zip codes, geographic names, transit routes style lookups) has been retired; equivalent agency APIs now live under api.data.gov. (3) No price changes: everything remains free; the OPEN Government Data Act remains the statutory basis. Caveat: the known-context line 'many datasets need no key' is confirmed for downloads/search, but API access to the v4 catalog API does require a (free) key; agency-specific egress/download costs never apply to data.gov itself.

provider: Decap CMS (decapcms.org) — open-source, Git-based headless CMS, formerly Netlify CMS; now independently maintained in the EU (decaporg / P-M.si)

findings.name: Decap CMS core — free open source (MIT), forever
findings.detail: The entire Decap CMS product is free: MIT-licensed, self-hosted, no usage limits, no seat limits, no hosting fees from Decap. Official site states it is 'Free & open source, forever' — 'free today and will remain free for everyone, always.' You run the admin UI yourself (e.g. on any host or on Netlify's own free tier) against your own Git backend (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea).
findings.eligibility: Anyone — students, startups, enterprises, no .edu email, no age/funding cap, no credit card, no region limits. No application required.
findings.claim: Download the npm package or use the CDN + add admin/index.html and config.yml to your project; authenticate via your Git provider's OAuth (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) or another backend. No signup, no payment details, no expiry. Docs: decapcms.org/docs/intro
findings.expiry: None — MIT license and 'free forever' commitment are permanent; no sunset announced.
findings.gotchas: It is self-hosted: you must supply your own auth/identity and hosting for the admin UI, and pay for Git-host API rate limits on large collections. Netlify Identity (the formerly recommended auth path) was deprecated in 2025, so legacy sites need a backend swap (Decap Turbo, DecapBridge, or Auth0) — a hidden cost of time. No dedicated student or startup program exists on the core product.

findings.name: Decap Turbo Free plan — managed hosting, free indefinitely
findings.detail: Decap Turbo is Decap's paid managed layer (hosted auth & roles, database-backed content store for faster performance, Git-host rate-limit shielding, deploy notifications, activity log, S3-compatible media library, site variables). The Free plan: €0/month, 1 site + 1 seat, free indefinitely (not a trial). Includes the managed infrastructure: 'Faster CMS', 'Git host request shielding', 'Activity log', 'Deploy notifications', community support.
findings.eligibility: Any organization (students/startups equally eligible); no credit card required to sign up; no .edu or funding-cap conditions; no region limits stated. Payment (Paddle.com, EUR, monthly, tax included) required only for paid plans.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at https://turbo.decapcms.org/signup — you land on the Free plan, no card. 2) Add your site (up to 1). 3) Use hosted auth; invite at most 1 seat. No trial involvement; Free plan stays free unless you upgrade.
findings.expiry: Indefinite — 'stays free indefinitely'; no renewal or expiry date. Paid plans are month-to-month with no yearly self-serve option.
findings.gotchas: Free plan is capped at 1 site + 1 seat — larger teams need Pro. S3 media library and site variables are Pro-and-above features, not in Free. It is genuinely free, not a trial — 'paying for Decap Turbo never means paying for Decap CMS itself.'

findings.name: Decap Turbo 14-day Pro trial — no credit card
findings.detail: Organization owner can opt in to a 14-day Pro trial that unlocks every Pro feature except priority support. Trial caps: 5 sites and 25 users. No credit card required to start. If no payment method is added, you get a 1-week grace at full Pro access, then the org drops to Free: one site stays editable, all other sites become read-only, non-owner members lose access, pending invitations are revoked — nothing is deleted; adding payment later restores access (oldest sites first). For reference, Pro retail is €19/month (1 site + 5 seats; extra €10/site · €6/seat), priority support add-on €99/month per org, Enterprise custom with unlimited (fair use).
findings.eligibility: Any registered organization (students/startups equally eligible); no credit card required; no .edu or funding-cap conditions stated.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up on Free plan at turbo.decapcms.org/signup. 2) As organization owner, open the Billing page. 3) Opt in to the 14-day Pro trial (or skip it). No card, no auto-upgrade — 'Nothing is switched on for you: skip the opt-in and you simply stay on Free.'
findings.expiry: Trial ends after 14 days + 1-week grace; then the org reverts to the Free plan (1 site editable, others read-only). It renews as a paid Pro plan only if you add payment (EUR, monthly, via Paddle).
findings.gotchas: Trial is a trial (temporary Pro access), while the Free plan is permanently free — the page explicitly distinguishes them. Pro requires a credit card for ongoing use. Prices are EUR, tax included, monthly only; third-party figures (e.g. $37/mo 'Starter' on Sitepins, unverified apis.io 'Decap Turbo Starter/Team/Business') do not match the official page — trust decapcms.org/turbo.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, Decap CMS/Decap Turbo has NO dedicated education/student license, no startup program, and no trial-credit offer for students or startups beyond what is listed: the permanent MIT-licensed free core, the Decap Turbo Free plan (1 site/1 seat, no CC), and the 14-day no-CC Pro trial. No education or startup discount appears anywhere on the official pages (checked decapcms.org and decapcms.org/turbo today). No student/startup free-offer sunset was found in 2025-2026 because none existed. Related context: Netlify Identity, the formerly recommended free auth backend, was deprecated around 2025 — pushing legacy Decap CMS users toward Decap Turbo (or third-party auth like DecapBridge). findings.name: Self-hosted open-source (MIT) — free forever, no usage limits
findings.detail: Official pricing page states: 'Payload is open source and MIT licensed. Deploy it anywhere you can run a Node.js app — for free, forever.' The core framework, admin UI, and local development are completely free with no seat caps, record limits, or feature paywalls. Requirements: any JS package manager (pnpm preferred), Node.js 20.9.0+, and any compatible database (MongoDB, Postgres, or SQLite). FAQ on the pricing page confirms: 'Payload remains a self-hosted solution, so you can bring your app to any hosting provider you prefer.'
findings.eligibility: Anyone — no .edu email, no startup age or funding cap, no credit card, no region limits stated. MIT license permits commercial use. Post-acquisition FAQ: 'Figma is committed to maintaining and investing in Payload's open source core.'
findings.claim: Run `npx create-payload-app` to scaffold; deploy to any Node.js host (VPS, serverless, container). No signup, no trial period, no CC.
findings.expiry: None — MIT license is perpetual; offer has no sunset date as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: Software is free but you pay for infrastructure: server/VPS, database (or bring Mongo/Postgres/SQLite), media storage, and egress bandwidth. Paid 'Enterprise Features' (SSO, AI auto-embedding, publishing workflows, visual editor, static A/B testing, enterprise AI) are gated behind the Enterprise tier and not in the free core. Support is community-only on the free track.

Each is a Deploy button that lands you on the host's own free tier, making a real-world Payload app free within provider limits.

findings.claim: Click Deploy on payloadcms.com/get-started, log in to Vercel/Cloudflare, and the template provisions automatically. Free within each provider's free-tier limits.
findings.expiry: Tied to provider free tiers; no Payload-side expiry.
findings.gotchas: Provider limits apply and I did not re-verify exact free-tier numbers (Vercel build minutes/function seconds; Cloudflare requests/day, D1 storage, egress) today — check current host pricing. Free DB/storage tiers have hard caps; overages bill the host account. Media on free tiers may be small (GBs, not TBs).

findings.name: Self-hosted Ghost — free open source (MIT)
findings.detail: The Ghost CMS is MIT-licensed and fully free to self-host: no member limits, no post limits, no built-in plan gate. findings.eligibility: Anyone (students and startups alike) — no .edu email, no funding cap, no age limit, no stated region limits. You must provide and pay for your own hosting and optionally your own SMTP/email provider.
findings.claim: Install Ghost on your own infrastructure: `npm install @tryghost/...` / clone the Ghost repo from GitHub and run it with Node.js on a server; no license fee, no signup, no credit card. No claim step required beyond deploying it.

findings.gotchas: The CMS is free but your infrastructure (server, bandwidth, domain) and email provider are not. 'Unlimited emails' only holds if you configure your own email provider within its own quotas. You own security, updates, backups, and uptime. This is a free CMS, not free hosting.

findings.claim: Use the 'Get Started — free' / 'Try for free' CTA on ghost.org, create a Ghost(Pro) site, and you get 14 days of full access; afterwards pay for a plan or move to self-hosted Ghost.

findings.name: Google Maps Platform free usage tier (per-SKU monthly caps)
findings.detail: Since 2025-03-01 Google replaced the old flat $200/month GMP credit with free monthly billable-event caps per Core Service SKU, tiered by pricing category: Essentials 10,000 / Pro 5,000 / Enterprise 1,000 free calls per SKU per month. Exception: 2D Map Tiles API and Map Tiles API Street View Tiles get 100,000 free events per SKU/month. Google's Dec 2024 blog claims up to ~$3,250/month of combined free usage across products; Maps Embed API and parts of Maps SDKs remain unlimited-free. Automatic volume discounts now scale to 5M+ monthly events (20% to up to 80% off); negotiated contracts migrate on renewal from 2025-09-01. Legacy SKUs (Places legacy, Directions, Distance Matrix) keep a separate legacy free allocation; no decommission date yet, Google commits to 12+ months notice.
findings.eligibility: All GMP accounts (individuals, students, startups, enterprises); no .edu or startup status required; no funding cap; no region limit on the caps themselves, but EEA (billing address) customers are on separate EEA terms with some different features, and India-eligible accounts follow a separate price schedule. A standard billing-enabled key requires a payment method.
findings.claim: Create a Google Cloud project, enable the Maps/Routes/Places/Environment APIs, link a Cloud billing account (credit card), create a standard API key. Free caps apply automatically each month to usage below them; no application needed. Check your numbers in the Maps API Library console / billing reports.
findings.expiry: Recurring and indefinite: caps renew every calendar month with no end date. Legacy services remain 'Legacy' status with at-least-12-months' notice before decommission (no date set as of the Oct 2026 page update).
findings.gotchas: Caps are per-SKU, not per product: a product exposing many SKUs (e.g., Places) can exhaust caps quickly even at modest call volumes; overflow is billed at per-SKU price. Trial credit vs free tier: the $300 trial is one-time/90-day while these caps are perpetual — do not conflate. Multiple GMP-related Cloud billing accounts violate GMP ToS. EEA customers get different terms/features since 2025-07-08. Free tiers do NOT cover subscriptions: Starter/Essentials/Pro subscription plans ($100/$275/$1,200 per month for 50K/100K/250K combined calls) are paid products.

findings.name: Maps Demo Key (no credit card, daily-capped sandbox)
findings.detail: Always-free sandbox API key for prototyping: no billing account and no credit card required. Daily usage limit per API (exact numbers are not published in the docs; Google states limits are 'subject to change' and may be adjusted or zeroed at any time; the AI Studio-hosted variant lists ~100 calls/day). Hitting the limit pauses the map for the day with zero charge; usage resets next day. Supported (limited): Maps JavaScript API (with Maps Grounding Lite, Places UI Kit, drawing/styling), Places API (new), Geocoding API v4, Compute Routes, Weather API, Maps SDK for Android/iOS in demo form; user-generated content (photos, reviews) is NOT available; Route Optimization, Solar, and Nav Connect APIs are excluded entirely.
findings.eligibility: Any Google account (free). One Maps Demo Project per Google account at a time. Intended for evaluation/prototyping only — production use is strictly prohibited by the demo-project terms. No student/age/region eligibility; no .edu or credit card.
findings.claim: Sign in with a Google account on mapsplatform.google.com/maps-demo-key (or via Google AI Studio, which provisions a demo key in-flow), click 'Get a Demo Key', accept the Maps Demo Project Terms of Service; the key is displayed immediately and emailed. Upgrade: add a Cloud billing account to the demo key, or create a new billing-enabled API key.
findings.expiry: No end date published; no SLA, no support; Google may suspend/terminate access at any time without notice and can change or zero the daily limits at any time. Demo key can be kept alongside a paid account indefinitely.
findings.gotchas: Daily caps, not monthly — different from the per-SKU monthly free tier. Not for production. On upgrade, a standard key requires a credit card and you then inherit the per-SKU free caps plus (for new Cloud customers) the one-time $300 GCP trial. Limits are undisclosed numerically, so budget against unknowns; if a demo project stops mid-project, the only remedy is upgrading.

findings.name: Google Cloud $300 / 90-day free trial (covers GMP usage)
findings.detail: One-time $300 of no-charge usage on your first Cloud Billing account, valid for 90 days or until $300 is consumed, whichever comes first. If your first Cloud billing account has GMP APIs/SDKs enabled, BOTH the $300 trial and the GMP per-SKU free usage caps apply: charges are first absorbed by the free usage cap per SKU; overflow is drawn against the $300. The free usage caps keep applying after the trial ends.
findings.eligibility: New Google Cloud customers (first billing account). Students are eligible with a personal Google account — no .edu required. A payment method (credit card) IS required to activate the trial; no charge is made while usage stays within the trial + free tiers.
findings.claim: Create your first GCP billing account via cloud.google.com/free, attach a payment method, select the trial; enable GMP APIs on that account. Before the trial ends, upgrade the billing account to paid to avoid disruption of GMP usage.
findings.expiry: Trial ends at the earlier of 90 days or $300 exhausted. Not renewable, one per new Cloud customer; the perpetual per-SKU free caps survive independently of the trial.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required (unlike the Demo Key). After the trial you must upgrade to a paid account or GMP service is at risk of disruption. GMP docs state that creating multiple GMP-related Cloud billing accounts violates GMP ToS — you cannot re-claim the trial via extra accounts. Trial credit is a one-time bridge; long-term free usage comes only from the per-SKU caps and the Demo Key.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program (GCP credits + $600/month Google Maps Platform usage credits, Scale tier)
findings.detail: GCP's startup program has two tiers (2025-2026 structure). Start tier: up to $2,000 GCP credits valid 1 year + $200 Google Skills training credit + free Google Workspace Business Plus 12 months. Scale tier: up to $200,000 GCP credits over 2 years ($350,000 for AI-first startups: Year 1 100% up to $250K vs $100K for non-AI; Year 2 20% up to an additional $100K) + $500 Google Skills credit + Workspace Business Plus 12 months + up to $12,000 Enhanced Support credits (1-year) + the Maps-specific benefit: $600 per month in Google Maps Platform usage credits (separate application required). GCP program credits can cover GMP usage on the shared GCP billing account (GMP is a GCP product); the dedicated $600/month GMP credit is a separate entitlement.
findings.eligibility: For-profit technology startups. Scale tier: Pre-Seed/Seed raised within the last 5 years AND Series A raised within the last 12 months; founded within 5 years; stealth accepted with funding verification; not yet received more than $5,000 in GCP credits. Start tier: founded within 24 months, planning to seek VC funding, no GCP credits received beyond the free trial. EXCLUDED: educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs/content, dev shops, consultancies, agencies, crypto mining, IPO'd/acquired companies. Application must use a business email matching the company's public domain.
findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup: provide an active 18-character GCP Billing Account ID in good standing (wait ~48 hours after creating it), public proof of funding (online links), business email + domain. Approval typically within a few business days. Then submit the SEPARATE application for the $600/month GMP usage credits (offered in the Scale-tier welcome materials). Web3 and AI variants (cloud.google.com/startup/web3, /startup/ai) have the same tiered structure.
findings.expiry: GCP credits last 1 year (Start) or are structured over 2 years (Scale: Year-1 100%, Year-2 20%). The $600/month GMP credit is ongoing monthly for the program duration (no published end date; tied to program membership). One-time program — previous participants cannot re-apply except via case-by-case review through cloudstartupsupport@google.com.
findings.gotchas: Funding-window caps matter (Series A older than 12 months disqualifies Scale; PE/crowdfunding/grant-only funding doesn't qualify Scale). Credits do NOT cover third-party Marketplace services or third-party model inference. Acceptance is at Google's sole discretion; meeting criteria does not guarantee approval. Educational institutions are explicitly ineligible — students/edu email addresses are NOT a path into this program. The $600/month GMP benefit is NOT automatic with tier acceptance; it requires a separate application.

provider: Google Maps Platform (Google) — Maps/location APIs; fronts: GMP APIs, Search & CMS-style docs
sunset_notes: 1) SUNKEN: The legacy flat $200/month GMP credit ended 2025-03-01, replaced by per-SKU free usage caps (10K/5K/1K Essentials/Pro/Enterprise; 100K for 2D Map Tiles and Street View tiles; auto volume discounts up to 5M+ events). Any page still citing '$200/month' (including some third-party tutorials) is stale. 2) CHANGED 2025: GCP for Startups was restructured into Start/Scale tiers; the live benefits page now requires founding within 5 years (older program docs said 10), with the $600/month GMP usage credit offered to Scale tier only and requiring a separate application; AI-first startups capped at $350K. 3) EDUCATION: No Maps Platform education license or student-specific program found as of 2026-10-22 — Google publishes no .edu-gated GMP offer; educational institutions are explicitly EXCLUDED from the Google for Startups Cloud Program (and no GMP-education credit program was listed on cloud.google.com/edu, which did not render fully, so this is stated as absence-of-evidence rather than a verified program). Students' practical free paths are the general per-SKU caps, the no-CC Demo Key, and the $300 GCP trial (all open, no .edu). 4) REGIONAL: Since 2025-07-08, EEA-billed customers are on separate EEA GMP Terms of Service (post-German Bundeskartellamt proceeding) with different features and, per GMP docs, possibly different terms for features like Places UI Kit. 5) LEGACY: Places (legacy), Directions, and Distance Matrix APIs remain in 'Legacy' status with no announced decommission date; Google commits to 12+ months' notice — users must migrate to new SKUs to keep expanded volume discounts. 6) VERIFICATION CAVEAT: cloud.google.com pages (startup benefits, free trial) are JS-rendered and truncated for automated fetches; the $600/month GMP credit and trial figures were verified via full-text search snippets of the official pages today, not a complete page read, hence 'medium' confidence on the startup finding.

provider: Directus (headless CMS) — fronts: APIs, Search & CMS, Self-Hosted Open-Source SaaS Alternatives

findings.name: Free self-hosting under open-source license (now MSCL-1.0-GPL, not Apache 2.0)
findings.detail: Self-hosting Directus is free: 'Self-host free with one install. No credit card required' (homepage; claim via npx directus-template-cli@latest init). The license is the Monospace Sustainable Core License (MSCL-1.0-GPL) v1.0 from Monospace Inc (parent of Directus), with an irrevocable grant converting each release to GPL-3.0 after 4 years. Permitted Purpose explicitly covers internal use and non-commercial education/research, so students and classrooms can self-host free; there is no seat/instance cap for internal use. No .edu email required, no credit card, no region limit stated. Caveats: 'Competing Use' prohibition (may not offer a managed service competing with Monospace's commercial Directus where it charges license fees), license-key integrity rules for protected functionality on v12+, and no reselling/white-labelling Directus itself.
findings.eligibility: Anyone for internal/non-commercial or personal use (incl. students, education, research); agencies may use it for client work as professional services. Commercial/resale use of Directus-as-SaaS requires OIG or a paid license.
findings.claim: Download/run the open-source release (e.g. npx directus-template-cli@latest init); no key needed for pre-v12 releases; v12+ has key-gated functionality covered by the free Core tier or OIG.
findings.expiry: n/a (standing license); each release converts to GPL-3.0 four years after its release date
findings.gotchas: The 'Apache 2.0' label in prior notes is outdated — license is now MSCL-1.0-GPL (successor to BSL, which was replaced per the OIG FAQ). Not a true open license: competing-use ban, telemetry/licensing-key enforcement on v12+.

findings.name: Directus Cloud Core free tier ($0/mo)
findings.detail: Free cloud/Core plan: 3 user seats, 25 collections, 5 flows, plus AI Assistant, Advanced RBAC, and Community Support. Cloud hosting is NOT included — it is an optional add-on at $99/mo (hosting only; overages/limits per 'Cloud Policies': e.g. legacy overage rates $5/2,500 DB entries, $10/25,000 API requests, $5/25 GB bandwidth, $5/5 GB asset storage — Core tier overage figures were not captured in the table render). Paid comparison: Team is $499/mo annual ($5,988/yr) or $599/mo rolling; 10 SSO seats, extra SSO seats $50/seat/mo, 50 collections (expandable to 100), 20 flows. No SSO on Core, not addable.
findings.eligibility: Any team up to 3 seats; no .edu requirement; no credit-card or trial mention on the current pricing page. No regional limits stated. Government customers are excluded only from the OIG grant, not from the Core tier.
findings.claim: Sign up at directus.cloud (login → create or join a team → create projects); pick the Core ($0) tier. Self-hosting under Core costs $0.
findings.expiry: no expiry stated; 'No existing customer will be forced onto new pricing immediately' — monthly plans grandfathered 6 months, annual honored until renewal
findings.gotchas: The free tier caps you at 3 seats / 25 collections / 5 flows, well under OIG; hosting on Directus' cloud is +$99/mo on top of $0 software, so 'free' applies to self-hosting; no SSO and no paid support; each cloud project incurs infrastructure costs and there are no refunds for accidental/abandoned projects.

findings.name: Open Innovation Grant (OIG) — perpetual full commercial access for small orgs & individuals
findings.detail: OIG grants 'fully permissive access to Directus at no software cost': unlimited seats, collections, and flows; SSO and custom access policies; bring-your-own LLM and AI translations; no feature limits or caps. Self-hosted use is free; cloud hosting is a flat $99/mo (hosting only). The grant is 'granted in perpetuity' — licenses have no expiration and require no renewal; it is 'a standing program, not a promotion.' Each key includes 5 activations (multi-container replicas pointing at the same DB/public URL share one activation). Grant applies to Directus v12.0.0+; v11 and below need no key and never will. You may build and sell commercial products/SaaS on Directus; reselling, redistributing, sub-licensing, or white-labelling Directus itself is out of scope.
findings.eligibility: Under $5M annual recurring revenue (measured across commonly-owned group; donations/grants excluded) AND fewer than 50 employees. Individuals qualify (assessed on personal finances, not employer), non-profits, hobbyists, agencies qualify; unpaid volunteers and school students don't count toward headcount. End-user rule: eligibility is judged by who logs into Studio (if a client's team logs in, the client's size governs; app end-users/website visitors never count). Government customers are explicitly excluded.
findings.claim: 1) Fill the OIG application at directus.com/oig (3-step form: applying-as, name, email, country/region), 2) read the OIG FAQ and accept the Open Innovation Grant agreement, 3) receive a perpetual license key for v12+. No credit card is involved; no payment of any kind.
findings.expiry: Perpetual — no expiration, no renewal process. Directus periodically reviews the grantee registry and may request proof of eligibility; keys can be disabled as a last resort for unreachable/inaccurate grantees; must contact sales within 90 days if the org grows past $5M or 50 people.
findings.gotchas: Required telemetry (no offline/air-gapped operation), no paid product support included, keys revocable for false information or abuse, 5 activations per key, no resell/white-label of Directus itself, and OIG FAQ terms apply only to v12+ (older releases are unlicensed/open).

findings.name: Student / education-specific license or free offer
findings.detail: No education-specific program, student discount, .edu-email offer, or free trial was found on any official page fetched today (homepage, /pricing/, /oig, /oig/faq, /license, /cloud-policies, /docs). Students are covered indirectly: (1) MSCL 'Permitted Purpose' explicitly allows free non-commercial education and research self-hosting, and (2) individuals (including students) are OIG-eligible, with students explicitly not counted toward the 50-employee cap when attached to a school/non-profit.
findings.eligibility: Indirect only: any student/educator via MSCL education purpose or individual OIG application; no .edu email verification mentioned anywhere.
findings.claim: Self-host free for class/course use under the MSCL, or apply for OIG as an individual (assessed on personal finances) via the /oig form.
findings.gotchas: Education use is non-commercial only; a commercial SaaS built on Directus by a student or school still needs OIG or a paid license.

sunset_notes: Material 2025–2026 changes: (1) LICENSE CHANGE — Directus is no longer under the 'Apache 2.0' license recorded in prior notes; the OIG FAQ states the prior BSL (Business Source License) was replaced by the MSCL (Monospace Sustainable Core License, MSCL-1.0-GPL) to add enforcement mechanisms after 'documented persistent abuse ... by large enterprise organizations'; each release converts to GPL-3.0 after 4 years. (2) OIG PERPETUITY — the homepage announces 'We're Making the OIG Perpetual and Clearer'; grants now carry no expiration date and no renewal process, and the program is described as a standing program. (3) PROFESSIONAL TIER SUNSET — per the Cloud Policies page, 'as of June 1, 2026 the Professional tier is a legacy tier that is no longer available for new projects' (it remains available to existing projects; monthly plans grandfathered 6 months, annual until renewal; the legacy $5-per-unit overage rates likely apply only to grandfathered accounts). (4) TRIAL — the 'Directus Cloud trial available' note from prior knowledge is unsupported on any official page fetched today: no trial duration, no trial credit, and no credit-card language appears on /pricing/, /oig, /license, /cloud-policies, or /docs/cloud/getting-started/introduction; the free entry points are now the self-hosted Core tier and OIG. No student/education program exists, so nothing to sunset there. Data-quality caveats: web search was unavailable (shared session search budget exhausted), so 2025–2026 change verification relied on official pages fetched 2026-10-22; /blog and /cloud paths 404'd, and the per-tier technical-limits table on /cloud-policies did not render its Core-tier row in the fetched text (Core limits were instead confirmed on /pricing/).

findings.name: Airtable Free plan (permanent, no card)
findings.detail: Free forever: 1,000 records per base (cumulative across all tables), 1,000 API calls per workspace/month (5 req/sec rate limit), 1 GB attachment storage per base, 2 weeks revision/snapshot history, 75 unique automations per base, 100 automation runs per workspace/month, 500 AI credits per editor+/month. Max 5 Editor/Creator collaborators + 50 Commenters + unlimited read-only. No extensions, no sync integrations, no 'Run a script' automation action, 'Send email' action limited to base collaborators, no record coloring, Airtable branding on forms cannot be removed. Data is never deleted when you exceed limits; new records/attachments are blocked until upgrade.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no credit card, no trial. Free plan workspaces can coexist with paid workspaces on the same account.
findings.claim: Sign up at airtable.com (any email) → first workspace auto-starts a 14-day Team trial → simply do NOT add a payment method → workspace stays Free. No application needed.
findings.expiry: No expiry; plan persists indefinitely. API limits reset first day of each calendar month.
findings.gotchas: 1,000 API calls/month is a hard cap enforced since Jan 2025 (was previously effectively unlimited) — Zapier/Make/custom integrations can break silently. Record limit is per base, not per table: two tables of 500 records each already hit the cap. Automations cap was only raised from 50→75 in Sep 2026. The 14-day Team trial is one-time per account, so it can mask the real Free limits when evaluating headroom.

findings.name: 14-day Team trial (automatic, first workspace only)
findings.detail: First workspace of a new account is auto-upgraded to a 14-day Team trial. Trial caps: 50,000 records/base, 10 GB attachments, 365-day revision history, 25,000 automation runs/month, 10 synced tables, 7,500 AI credits/editor. Excludes 'Run a script' automation and premium form features (custom headers, branding removal, conditional groups).
findings.eligibility: Any new Airtable account; no credit card required to start. Future Free workspaces under the same account do NOT get another trial.
findings.claim: Automatic on account creation. To keep it free: don't add a payment method — after 14 days the workspace reverts to the Free plan. Adding a payment method during the trial auto-upgrades to paid Team and bills accordingly.
findings.expiry: 14 days, once per account.
findings.gotchas: Trial revision history is only 2 weeks, not Team's 1 year. Easy to accidentally convert to a paid subscription just by saving a card. Paid Team is $24/user/month monthly (billed annually $20/user/month).

findings.name: Airtable Student plan — free Team for 6-24 months
findings.detail: Qualifying college/university students: 120-day Team trial granted immediately when the account/workspace uses a .edu address, then application for a FREE Student plan = Team-level features for a single workspace for 6-24 months (length based on expected graduation date). Student plan caps: 50,000 records/base, 20 GB attachments/base, no 'Run a script' automation action, some form/view customization omitted.
findings.eligibility: Requires .edu email (international .edu / accredited-institution emails also accepted; non-.edu applicants can apply but may need extra documentation). Must have an existing Airtable account tied to the applied email or Airtable cannot review the application. Reviews typically ~2 business days.
findings.claim: 1) Create an Airtable account with your .edu email → 120-day Team trial starts on first workspace. 2) Apply via 'Apply for a free student plan' (support.airtable.com/articles/4920135568, linked from airtable.com/pricing's 'Special plans for Nonprofits or Education'). 3) On approval, account's plan type is switched by Airtable support; use the .edu email to log in.
