findings.expiry: 6-24 months from approval, tied to expected graduation date. No auto-renewal; after the window you revert to Free unless you (re-)apply while still a student or pay for Team.
findings.gotchas: This supersedes the older 'Airtable Classrooms' branding — no standalone Classrooms product is listed on current official pages. Student plan covers ONE workspace only. The 120-day trial clock runs BEFORE any approval, so apply early in the trial. .edu required in practice; no regional lock (international students apply via the same form, per 2020 newsroom + current FAQ).

findings.name: Education plan for staff/educators — 50% off Team
findings.detail: Employees of accredited educational institutions: 50% off the monthly Team rate → $12/user/month (based on $24/user/month monthly Team; annual-plan discount does NOT apply to discounted plans, so effectively $144/user/yr). Includes 1-year revision/snapshot retention. Same 120-day Team trial via .edu email before application.
findings.eligibility: Requires .edu email + certification that the institution is accredited and not-for-profit (usually provided by the institution's IT administrator). Only accredited educational organizations qualify; government, religious, and political organizations excluded. Application must match an existing Airtable account. Discounted plans require credit-card payment; no one-time payments.
findings.claim: 1) Account with .edu email (120-day Team trial auto-starts). 2) Apply via 'Apply for a discounted education plan' link on support.airtable.com/articles/4920135568. 3) Institute admin supplies accreditation proof; Airtable responds within ~2 business days. 4) Higher tiers (Business/Enterprise Scale edu discounts) are sales-only via Airtable Sales.
findings.expiry: Runs while the person is employed at the institution; re-verification at renewal; no public auto-renewal term stated.
findings.gotchas: Not free — 50% off, card required. Unaccredited/unregistered institutions cannot apply. AI features not covered by the discount per third-party summary (airtable.com/solutions/education says edu discounts on Business/Enterprise need a sales conversation).

findings.name: Airtable for Startups — up to $500 credit (direct application)
findings.detail: One-time $500 in Airtable credit applied to a named workspace, plus access to startup content/office hours. Credit does not require equity. Applicants must create an Airtable account and submit the application form with personal/company info and the workspace ID where credits are applied. Review takes ~3-10 business days (listings say 3-5 days). Offer details (yayimages listing, re-published Airtable offer text): limited to companies that have raised up to Series B; not available to companies already on an invoiced Airtable plan; one redemption per company; existing Airtable customers are also eligible.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups (listings: bootstrapped/pre-seed/seed up to Series B funding cap). Company email strongly expected (personal Gmail/Outlook is a top rejection reason in program listings). No stated region limit.
findings.claim: Create an Airtable account with your company email → fill the Airtable for Startups application form (current form: airtable.com/appGGpHNlmMUkfLol/shrghfGlQLt411Tyr; landing page airtable.com/startups) → wait 3-10 business days → credit appears in workspace settings → use credit toward Team/Business plans.
findings.expiry: One-time $500; partner-distributed credits (see next finding) explicitly state they do not expire. No stated expiration on the direct $500 credit — confirm in the approval email.
findings.gotchas: The official airtable.com/startups page could not be fully rendered for automated fetch (browser-gated), so exact current terms come from third-party listings that republish the offer text — verify amounts in the official form before applying. Credit applies to a single workspace; don't create new workspaces after applying. One startup listing (TechScoop) claims '1 year free Enterprise' for this program — this contradicts Airtable's sales-led Enterprise model and is almost certainly wrong; do not rely on it.

findings.name: VC/accelerator partner credits — $2,000 Airtable credit (Wonder Ventures, SeedBlink, HubSpot for Startups, M Accelerator)
findings.detail: Partner-marketplace versions of the Airtable startup offer pay $2,000 in credit (one redemption per company; existing Airtable customers eligible; US companies get an Airtable swag kit per the partner page). 'Credit does not expire' per partner pages. Credits appear in workspace settings after approval, and the same company email must be used as the Airtable account. M Accelerator lists '$2,000 with Airtable' in its perks catalog; HubSpot for Startups customers get the $2,000 offer via HubSpot's customer dashboard.
findings.eligibility: Portfolios/customers of the named partner (VC, accelerator, or HubSpot for Startups). Companies within the partner's stage caps (HubSpot for Startups: seed to Series B-scale, under $10M raised as a program rule). Not self-serve for unaffiliated startups — use the direct $500 application instead.
findings.claim: Redeem through the partner's marketplace/dashboard: sign up for free Airtable using your company email → submit the partner's form with the same email → credit posts to workspace settings after approval.
findings.expiry: Credits state explicitly 'do not expire' (partner terms, as of 2025-2026 listings). One redemption per company per partner.
findings.gotchas: Amount varies by partner ($500 direct vs $2,000 partner). Credits are product credit, not cash. Check which partner your investor belongs to before applying to avoid stacking conflicts ('cannot be combined with another deal of the same value or lower' applies to the $500 yayimages-distributed deal).

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: (1) Q2 2025 — Airtable discontinued the paid AI add-on; AI credits are now bundled into all plans (Free gets 500 credits/editor/month; paid tiers 7,500+). (2) Q3 2025 — ProductCentral add-on discontinued; Enterprise Scale Portals pricing moved to 'contact sales'. (3) Sep 2026 — a new 'automations per base' cap of 50 was imposed on ALL plans, then reversed two days later into tiered caps: 75 (Free) / 100 (Team) / 150 (Business) / 200 (Enterprise Scale) — automation RUN limits unchanged. (4) Airtable became part of Bending Spoons in Sept 2026 (per community announcements and third-party trackers) — program terms may shift; all offers above re-verified against official pages Oct 2026. (5) Third-party claim that the free record limit was 'cut from 1,200 to 1,000 in Feb 2026' (hackceleration) is unverified and contradicts the official 1,000-record limit that has stood since the 2023 pricing revamp — treat as noise. (6) 'Airtable Classrooms' is no longer a listed product; the current education offer set is the 120-day .edu Team trial + free Student plan (6-24 months) + 50% Education/Non-profit Team discount, all applied through support.airtable.com/articles/4920135568. Non-profit 50% Team discount exists in parallel but was out of scope (not a student/startup offer).

findings.name: Stripe Atlas startup program: Delaware C-Corp/LLC + perks bundle
findings.detail: One-time US$500 setup fee (includes Delaware gov filing fees, next-day expedited processing, and year-1 registered agent service) forms a Delaware C corp, LLC, or C-corp subsidiary; company tax ID (EIN), founder equity issuance, and 83(b) election filing included. Fundraising tools (YC-drafted post-money SAFE, board consents, per-SAFE tracking, investment deposit tracking via Treasury) are included at no additional cost. Registered agent renews automatically at US$100/year after year one (cancellable anytime).
findings.eligibility: Open to founders in 175+ countries; all founders must be 18+; no US SSN, nationality, or .edu email required. Delaware entities only (C corp/LLC/subsidiary). Prohibited activity: no business in Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, or Crimea; restricted business categories (weapons, unregulated financial services, etc.) excluded. No startup age/funding cap — it is a formation service.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at dashboard.stripe.com/register/atlas; 2) submit company + co-founder details, sign docs; 3) pay $500; 4) Delaware incorporates within ~2 business days; EIN (faster for US SSN holders, 7-14 days for non-US); 5) open Stripe Treasury/US business bank account. Perks appear in the Dashboard 'Perks' tab after Atlas application approval.
findings.expiry: $100/yr registered agent renews automatically after year one; cancel anytime. Perks are 'subject to change'.
findings.gotchas: The $500 fee IS required up front (payment card needed), so it is not a free offer by itself — the fee becomes free only via the Treasury refund (see separate finding). Auto-filed 83(b) and IP-assignment templates suit typical startups but not founders rolling QSBS gains or contributing valuable IP. Atlas is self-service, not a law firm; Delaware annual franchise tax (~$400/yr) is a separate, often-underrated ongoing cost. Stripe is not a bank; US current accounts are provided by Fifth Third Bank N.A.

findings.name: US$2,500 Stripe product credits for Atlas companies (first year)
findings.detail: US$2,500 in Stripe product credits, usable in the first year after incorporation, granted automatically to companies incorporated via Atlas. Per Stripe's Atlas perks support page, the credits are delivered as two separate offers: US$2,500 on Stripe Payment Links and US$2,500 on Stripe Invoicing (each 'in your first year after incorporation').
findings.eligibility: Any company incorporated through Stripe Atlas (C corp, LLC, or subsidiary), regardless of founder country. No .edu, no funding cap, no CC required beyond the initial $500 Atlas fee.
findings.claim: No separate application: incorporate via Atlas (dashboard.stripe.com/register/atlas); credits apply automatically in the Dashboard once incorporated; details/claims surfaced in the Atlas Perks tab.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 12 months after incorporation (or when used). No renewal.
findings.gotchas: Credits offset Stripe fees only — they are not cash; per the Stripe Startups FAQ the credit model excludes Crypto, Capital, Atlas fees, Terminal, Link passthrough, PayPal, and professional-services fees. Companies that incorporated before ~Oct 16, 2025 received the legacy format instead (processing fees waived on the first US$100,000 of revenue for 1 year) — that legacy offer is no longer available to new companies (date per third-party CloudRoute tracker; medium confidence).

findings.name: Atlas fee refund: $500 back + US$1,500 (C corp) / US$1,000 (LLC) bonus for a US$5,000 Stripe Treasury deposit
findings.detail: Depositing US$5,000 into a Stripe Treasury financial account within 90 days of incorporation refunds the US$500 Atlas setup fee AND earns a US$1,500 bonus (C corp) or US$1,000 bonus (LLC) — netting up to ~US$2,000 in value for the same $5,000 held. This is how Atlas incorporation becomes effectively free while banking with Stripe.
findings.eligibility: Atlas companies that can open a Stripe Treasury financial account (availability depends on the Stripe account/region; US Treasury availability is broad but not universal). LLC and C-corp bonus amounts differ.
findings.claim: 1) Incorporate via Atlas; 2) open a Stripe Treasury financial account from the Dashboard; 3) deposit/fund US$5,000 within 90 days; refund + bonus are applied per the perks terms. No separate application.
findings.expiry: The 90-day funding window is per incorporation (Stripe does not state whether it starts at payment or incorporation date). Bonus is one-time; Treasury itself persists as a regular account.
findings.gotchas: This is 'deposit $5,000 to get $500-$2,000 back' — you must actually have the cash; it is not a discount on the fee upfront. Stripe 'cannot guarantee' all perks apply to every company; bonus tiers as worded on the support page.

findings.name: Atlas partner perks: 'over US$50,000' in startup tool discounts/credits (AWS, Cloudflare, PostHog, Azure, Google, Xero, Deel, etc.)
findings.detail: Access to 50,000+ USD of partner offers, incl.: AWS Activate US$5,000 credits (new AWS users only), Cloudflare US$100,000 credits via the Cloudflare Startup Program, PostHog US$50,000 credits, Microsoft for Startups US$5,000+ Azure credits (+GitHub/Office discounts), Deel US$1,500 credits, Xero free 6 months, Google Ads US$500 after US$500 spend, Google Workspace 20% off first year, Ramp US$1,500 sign-up bonus, Bubble US$500 credits, Replit up to US$500, plus % off/free months on Notion, Linear, Slack, Gusto, Rippling, Carta, Vanta, Lovable, etc.
findings.eligibility: Any approved Atlas company (C corp or LLC). No .edu or funding cap for the bundle itself, but each partner applies its own eligibility/compliance rules (e.g., AWS credits new users only; Ramp requires a US bank account with >US$25,000).
findings.claim: After Atlas application approval, open the Perks tab in the Stripe Dashboard and claim each partner offer there; no referral required.
findings.expiry: Individual partner offers have their own terms and are 'subject to change'; bundle value (US$50,000) is a marketing aggregate, not a guaranteed single credit pool.
findings.gotchas: Stripe cannot guarantee partners will work with every Atlas company; egress/data costs, partner account minimums, and single-use limits apply per partner; most are free-tier credits, but some are only % discounts.

findings.name: Stripe Startups program: fee credits + exclusive Invoicing cap (0.4%, up to US$10 per invoice, 12 months)
findings.detail: Separate program (launched May 2025), stackable with Atlas: fee credits offsetting Stripe fees on Payments, Connect, Billing, Tax, and Sigma for 12 months (dollar amount not published on the public page; investor-network variants range US$500–US$5,000, with waived-processing-fee format in countries where credits are unavailable), plus capped Invoicing pricing 'starting at 0.4%, up to a maximum of US$10 per paid invoice' for the first 12 months (local-currency equivalents published, e.g., CA$14, A$14, EUR 8, GBP 7, S$12). Also expert advice, education, and founder community at no cost. Pricing review offered at US$100k MRR for 3 consecutive months.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage, venture-backed companies: proof of institutional funding required (PitchBook link, funding press, or investor docs). Active fully-verified Stripe account on standard pricing; must not already hold a fee offer. No .edu path — student founders without VC backing do not qualify. One offer per startup for its lifetime.
findings.claim: 1) Apply via the public form at stripe.com/startups or a private referral link from a Stripe Startup Partner (VC/accelerator); 2) confirm active verified Stripe account; 3) review takes 2-3 business days; 4) activate the offer from the Dashboard within 12 months of approval.
findings.expiry: 12 months to activate, then 12 months active (or until limit hit), no pausing; invoicing cap is first-12-months only; unused fee credits expire 12 months after activation; no automatic expiry reminder.
findings.gotchas: VC-backing gate excludes bootstrapped students/early builders; credits explicitly exclude Crypto, Capital, Atlas, Terminal, Link passthrough, PayPal, professional-services fees; invoicing cap is keyed to payment date, not creation date, and each installment payment gets its own US$10 cap.

findings.name: Stripe Treasury fee-credit rewards (ongoing, non-startup-exclusive)
findings.detail: US and Australia businesses whose Stripe Treasury financial account holds a combined USD+USDC end-of-day balance over US$2,000 earn fee credits at a 1% annual rate on the balance (calculated daily, issued monthly), automatically applied to eligible fees. Effectively free money back on balances already sitting in the Atlas-linked Treasury account.
findings.eligibility: US- or AU-located businesses using Stripe Treasury; Atlas companies that open a Stripe Treasury account qualify. No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Automatic — just hold the balance in the Treasury financial account; credits accrue and apply to eligible fees without a separate application.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; credits issued monthly; program subject to the Stripe Fee Credit Terms.
findings.gotchas: Credits offset eligible fees only (not cash), 1% is modest; excluded/eligible fee categories are defined in the Fee Credit Terms.

sunset_notes: Students/education: No student-specific or .edu-licensed Stripe offer was found (Atlas, Atlas credits, or Stripe Startups all use startup/VC-backed criteria, not educational status), so there is no 'education license' to list; .edu email is not required anywhere in the Atlas flow. Sunset/changes 2025-2026: (1) The legacy Atlas credit format — 'waived processing fees on the first US$100,000 of revenue for 1 year' — was replaced by the fixed US$2,500 product-credit format for companies incorporated on/after ~October 16, 2025 (date from third-party tracker CloudRoute; not re-stated on Stripe's marketing page, so medium confidence on the exact cutover date). (2) The Stripe Startups program launched May 13, 2025 and is growing, not sunsetting; its FAQ notes fee credits are progressively replacing the older waived-processing-fees format globally. (3) Stripe's older support FAQ 'Getting started with Stripe Atlas' still advertises 'US$100,000 USD in exclusive benefits', while all current pages say 'over US$50,000 in partner discounts' — a messaging/bundle revision, not a removal of perks. (4) Jan 2025 feature (third-party, medium confidence): Atlas now lets startups accept payments immediately after incorporation, even before receiving the EIN. Caveat: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted after the searches noted; a dedicated student-program check (e.g., 'Stripe for students') was not completed, so absence of a .edu offer rests on the official pages read today plus training knowledge.

findings.name: Free to integrate — no setup, monthly, or minimum fees (pay-per-transaction only)
findings.detail: Paystack has no integration fee, no maintenance fee, and no monthly or minimum fees; you pay only a per-transaction fee when a real payment is made. Applies equally to startups and students. Exact per-transaction rates (e.g., % + fixed fee in NGN for Nigeria; % + fixed in USD for the US) could NOT be verified live today (official page 403'd) and should be reconfirmed on paystack.com/pricing.
findings.eligibility: Any developer or business worldwide, including students and startups. No .edu email required, no funding/age cap, no minimum revenue. Standard KYC/business details are required to enable live processing, but not to sign up or to test.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free account at paystack.com/dashboard. 2) Complete business verification (KYC) to enable live payments. 3) Generate your secret/API key. 4) Integrate via REST API / SDKs. No credit card is required to sign up or to use test mode.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no expiry or renewal. Free-to-integrate has been Paystack's standard model since launch (2015).
findings.gotchas: Not free to actually move money — a per-transaction fee applies to every live payment, and fees differ by country/region/currency. Payouts have settlement times. Fee figures were not verified live (403 today); confirm current rates before relying on them.

findings.name: Free test-mode / sandbox account with test keys (credit card NOT required)
findings.detail: Every Paystack account includes a free test mode: test public key (pk_test...) and test secret key (sk_test...), plus documented test card numbers. Test transactions use simulated funds and never move real money. No credit card or bank details required to create an account or to use test mode — a real, free, no-strings sandbox for students building projects.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who can create a Paystack account (global, including students and startups). No .edu required, no funding cap, no credit card required.
findings.claim: 1) Create an account at paystack.com/dashboard. 2) Copy your test API keys (pk_test/sk_test) from the dashboard. 3) Use Paystack's published test card numbers to simulate successful/failed payments. 4) Go live by switching to the corresponding pk_live/sk_live keys, which require completed KYC.
findings.expiry: No expiry; test mode is available indefinitely on any account.
findings.gotchas: Test mode is NOT a free production tier — it cannot collect real money. Going live needs a separate live key and completed business verification (KYC). developer.paystack.com failed DNS today and paystack.com pages 403'd, so confirm the current test card numbers and doc URLs before relying on them.

findings.name: No dedicated student program, startup program, trial credits, or education license
findings.detail: As of 2026-10-22, Paystack offers no student-specific program, no startup program with discounted fees/equity, no trial credits/free spend balance, and no education license. The only free value is free-to-integrate (pay-per-transaction) plus the free test-mode sandbox above. Any fee accommodation for a startup would be a commercial agreement, not a published offer.
findings.eligibility: N/A — these offers do not exist publicly.
findings.claim: N/A.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Confidence is low because this is a negative finding based on absence of such programs in available knowledge and could not be re-verified live (all official pages 403 / docs host unresolved today).

sunset_notes: Verification limitation: could NOT read live primary sources today — paystack.com/pricing, paystack.com/, and paystack.com/faq/ all returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare bot protection), developer.paystack.com failed DNS (ENOTFOUND), and this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted. No 2025-2026 change was therefore confirmed from primary sources; findings are from pre-2026 knowledge. No previously-existing Paystack student program, startup program, trial-credit offer, or education license was identified, and none was found to have been sunset. The only genuinely free offers are free-to-integrate (pay-per-transaction, no setup/monthly/minimum fees) and a free no-credit-card test-mode sandbox. Exact per-transaction fee figures were intentionally NOT asserted; reconfirm on paystack.com/pricing.

findings.name: Storyblok Starter free plan (permanent free tier)
findings.detail: Forever-free plan. 1 space; up to 2 seats (1 seat included free, extra seat +$15/mo, max 2); 100,000 API requests/month; 100 GB content-delivery traffic/month; 2 locales; 25,000 AI credits/month; ~2,000 stories and ~2,000 assets; 200 components; 500 MB max asset size. Verified on the live /pricing page and the public '2026 Pricing Plan - Factsheet (Public)' PDF.
findings.eligibility: Anyone worldwide. No .edu email required, no startup age/funding check, and no credit card required (page: 'always free and requires no credit card').
findings.claim: Sign up at app.storyblok.com; a new space starts on the free Starter plan (or after a 45-day Growth Plus trial, choose Starter). No card is entered.
findings.expiry: None — Starter is a permanent free tier; it does not expire and does not renew.
findings.gotchas: The /free marketing page advertises '1,000,000 API requests' and 'unlimited content entries', which contradicts the authoritative /pricing page + 2026 factsheet (100K API/month, ~2,000 stories/assets) — trust the pricing page/factsheet. Egress/overage: 100 GB traffic and 100K API are included; exceeding the API & traffic limits in two consecutive months triggers Storyblok's overage 'Usage Breach Fee' (2025 overage-fee policy). Traffic is the billable dimension; story/asset counts are hard caps.

findings.name: 45-day Growth Plus free trial (no credit card)
findings.detail: Every new space gets a 45-day trial of the paid Growth Plus plan (15 seats, 4,000,000 API calls/month, 1 TB traffic). After 45 days you either subscribe (Growth $99/mo, $90.75/mo annual; Growth Plus $349/mo, $319.91/mo annual; Premium/Elite custom) or downgrade to the free Starter plan.
findings.eligibility: Any new space; no credit card required (pricing FAQ: 'No! Every space comes with a 45-day free trial on our Growth Plus plan'); no .edu or startup qualification; global.
findings.claim: Sign up; the Growth Plus trial begins automatically on a new space. To keep it free, choose Starter (or a paid tier) at the end of the 45 days.
findings.expiry: 45 days; then renews only if you pick a paid plan, otherwise downgrades to free Starter. Annual billing gives one month free.
findings.gotchas: trial-vs-free: this is a paid-tier trial, not the free plan. At day 45 you lose the 4M API / 1 TB traffic limits and drop to Starter (100K API / 100 GB). No card means no auto-bill is stated, but the generous limits end on day 45.

findings.name: Education & nonprofit discount (sales-led)
findings.detail: Storyblok states: 'We offer discounts for educational institutions and non-profit organizations that are making the world a better place.' No fixed percentage and no dedicated landing page are published.
findings.eligibility: Educational institutions and non-profit organizations. No .edu-email verification and no region limit are stated on the site.
findings.claim: Contact sales via the pricing page CTA (links to /fs/enterprise-contact) or sales@storyblok.com; the discount is negotiated per deal.
findings.expiry: N/A — negotiated discount with no set expiry/renewal.
findings.gotchas: It is a discount, not a free tier/license — you still pay. Not available to students or startups by default (institutional/charitable entities only). Students/startups instead use the free Starter plan + 45-day Growth Plus trial with no special qualification.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes (per the public 2026 pricing factsheet): AI credits were added across all plans on 2025-11-19 (free Starter gets 25,000 AI credits/month); a 2025 overage-fee policy applies a 'Usage Breach Fee' when a self-service customer exceeds API & traffic limits in two consecutive months. No dedicated startup program exists: /startups and /education both return 404, and the pricing page lists no startup-credits program. The only education/nonprofit benefit is the sales-led discount; there is no formal education-license page. The two standing free offers for students/startups are the permanent free Starter plan and the 45-day Growth Plus trial — no sunset dates are announced for either. (Note: the /free page's '1M API / unlimited entries' marketing figures are stale/misleading vs the authoritative /pricing page and 2026 factsheet.)

findings.claim: Go to console.tink.com/signup, create an account, verify the email, log in, create a sandbox app (app type is fixed at creation; one sandbox app per product recommended), pull API credentials under App settings > API client. In Console select Demo Bank, pick a Product and a Market, use the named test users (each user = a test case, e.g. User 1 = success path; Sweden requires SSN-style credentials). Copy the Tink Link URL and test end-to-end. To use live bank data: contact sales, complete the 'Know Your Business' process; Tink creates/configures your production app.
findings.detail: Free self-serve developer account at console.tink.com (email + verification, no credit card, no pricing at signup). 'By default, all our products are available to test in our sandbox environment. You can access it by creating a sandbox app.' Demo Bank is a simulated bank with test users per market, so no real bank credentials are needed. FAQ confirms: 'you are welcome to create a free account to try Tink products with test data in a sandbox environment before upgrading to an Enterprise account' and 'create a free account at console.tink.com, where you can use test data to try our platform.' Demo Bank markets cover 18 countries (AT, BE, CZ, DK, EE, FI, FR, DE, IE, IT, LV, NL, NO, PT, PL, ES, SE, UK); the supported demo-provider list was reduced on 31 Oct 2023 and is a fixed list since. No public call/volume limits or expiry are stated; FAQ notes 4 background data refreshes every 24h platform-wide. Public demo of Account Check/Transactions at demo.tink.com. Production/live-bank access is Enterprise: custom, sales-gated pricing plus a 'Know Your Business' process; pre-production apps that use your own real bank credentials are production-type apps and fall under the same sales-gated access.
findings.eligibility: Open to any individual/company with an email address; no .edu requirement, no startup age/funding cap, no region limit on the account itself (Demo Bank markets are European). Credit card NOT required. Students can sign up and use it; Tink makes no student-specific promise.
findings.expiry: No stated expiration or renewal on the free Console/sandbox account; it persists while the account exists. Demo Bank provider list frozen since 31 Oct 2023 (only a Tink announcement changes it).
findings.gotchas: Sandbox = simulated bank/test data only: you cannot pull live account data on the free account. 'Pre-production' apps using real bank credentials are production apps -> Enterprise-gated. App type cannot be changed after creation. No published rate/egress limits for the free tier, so don't assume unbounded production-style volume; there is no pay-per-use option at all (FAQ: 'No'). Client secrets are one-time (up to 5 per app). Tink docs say '3000+ connections in 18 countries' while the homepage claims 6000 connections - marketing variance, check the current coverage matrix per market.
findings.name: Free Tink Console account + sandbox with Demo Bank (free developer tier)

findings.claim: Application was via Tenity's VIPE Nordics & Baltics page (tenity.com); per directory listings the 2025 deadline was 27 Oct 2025 (missed - program since concluded). To re-engage: watch tenity.com/cases/visa-innovation-program-europe/ for a second season announcement, or use the free Visa Developer sandbox in the meantime.
findings.detail: Visa's open-innovation startup program (run with Tenity), not a Tink product-level program - included here because the provider front is 'Tink (Visa)' and the program hands selected fintechs 'Visa's APIs via the Visa Developer Platform', mentorship, investor networks, and regional bank partnerships. Free to join: 'no Company equity requirement' and no participation fee is stated anywhere; there is also no direct funding amount for participants. Season 1 (Nordics & Baltics): applications opened 6 Oct 2025; first cohort of 8 fintechs (Beneflo, Enable Banking, Kardio, Juuli, Ledyer, Betalo, Beep, Myver) announced at the Nordic Banking Forum, Helsinki, on 4 Dec 2025; ~6-8 month program running to showcase at Baltic Fintech Days, Riga, in May 2026. Program focus: B2B money movement, embedded payments. AS OF 2026-10-22: Season 1 is concluded (8-month window from Dec 2025 ends ~Aug 2026; Tenity's page shows news through 22 Sep 2026 with no second-season announcement).
findings.eligibility: Startups only, not students: 'fintechs based in the Nordics & Baltics with a strong market presence' (Sweden, Finland, Norway, Iceland, Denmark, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia). Competitive/selection-based - Season 1 picked 8 companies; no published company-age or funding cap. No .edu path, no self-serve access: it is a program, not a free tier.
findings.expiry: Season 1 applications: opened 6 Oct 2025, deadline ~27 Oct 2025 (per Startup Lithuania directory; Tenity's own page states no explicit deadline). Program window ran Dec 2025 - May 2026. No Season 2 application window announced as of 22 Oct 2026.
findings.gotchas: Selection-based, so not a guaranteed free offering; 'access to Visa's APIs' means Visa Developer Platform APIs, i.e. the same free sandbox any developer gets, plus pilot/mentorship value - the program's worth is network/POC, not API freebies. Equity-free but also no funding; benefits are partnership-led. Status uncertainty: an announcement page does not track closures.
findings.name: Visa Innovation Program Europe - Nordics & Baltics (VIPE), startup program

findings.claim: Register at developer.visa.com ('Create your free account' + email verification), add a project, select products (some require 'Request access' approval), read Sandbox credentials (Two-Way SSL / X-Pay tokens), run the Hello World sample code. Moving to Certification/Production requires requesting access and signing a paid Visa Developer agreement.
findings.detail: Free developer account and sandbox at developer.visa.com: 'Sandbox access is free. Fees apply only when you move a project to Certification or Production and sign a Visa Developer agreement.' Includes mock data, sample code, SDKs, and an onboarding dashboard; credentials expire periodically and must be renewed. No trial credits or dollar-based free tier - the 'free' is the entire sandbox environment. Some product APIs are gated behind a 'Request access' form even within a project.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (developer or company) can create the free account; email + verification only, no credit card at this stage, no .edu or startup requirement, no published region limit on the account (product availability is regional - check regional availability before picking products). Tink-specific note: this is the parent (Visa) dev platform, distinct from Tink's own Console/Demo Bank open-banking sandbox.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry on sandbox access; SSL certificates/tokens expire and are renewed in the dashboard.
findings.gotchas: Certification/Production are paid and contract-gated; don't build production assumptions on sandbox behavior. It's Visa-level, not Tink-level: Tink's open-banking products use Tink Console, Visa's payments APIs use this center - useful only if the 'Tink (Visa)' front means the whole Visa dev umbrella.
findings.name: Visa Developer Center free sandbox (parent-level free tier)

sunset_notes: No student/education offer found: no .edu pricing, student license, or trial-credit program anywhere on tink.com pricing/FAQ/docs as of 2026-10-22, and the FAQ says pay-per-use is 'No' - the only free access is the self-serve Console sandbox + Demo Bank. Startup offer at Visa level: VIPE Nordics & Baltics Season 1 (applications opened 6 Oct 2025) is CONCLUDED - first cohort of 8 ran Dec 2025 - May 2026 with final showcase at Baltic Fintech Days Riga, May 2026; no Season 2 application window was announced on Tenity's page as of 22 Oct 2026, so the startup program is currently closed/unknown until a new season is announced. Historical change still in effect: the Demo Bank supported-provider list was reduced on 31 Oct 2023 to the fixed 18-market list published in Tink docs; providers not on that list are unsupported for testing. No 2025-2026 sunsets of developer tooling appear in Tink's press index (2025 releases: Adyen Pay-by-Bank x2, Paysend partnership, Gen Z study); pricing has stayed opaque/sales-gated. Caveat: consumer-side Tink products (e.g. the Tink consumer banking app) are outside the 'Payments & Fintech Dev Tools' front and were not assessed; no closure of any developer offering was found, so the free sandbox is presumed still live (console.tink.com is up and the FAQ still advertises it).

findings.name: Stripe Startups program — fee credits + exclusive Invoicing cap
findings.detail: Official program for early-stage venture-backed companies. Core perks: (1) credits that offset Stripe fees on Payments, Connect, Billing, Tax and Sigma for 12 months; (2) exclusive capped Invoicing pricing starting at 0.4% per paid invoice, capped at US$10 (or local-currency equivalent, e.g. 45 lei, £7, €8, AU$14) for the first 12 months, auto-activated alongside fee credits; (3) expert education, tailored advice, and founder/Stripe-leader community; (4) pricing review opportunity when monthly payments exceed $100,000 for 3 consecutive months. No equity taken (no mention of equity/warrants anywhere in the program).
findings.eligibility: Early-stage, venture-backed companies; application must include proof of institutional funding (PitchBook link, funding-announcement articles, or other documentation). Must be on Stripe's standard pricing, no other platform may control your pricing, no prior offer received; one offer per startup in its lifetime. No founding-date cap, funding-amount cap, or headcount limit is published. Region: fee-credit offer is available in 31 named countries (US, UK, EU countries, AU, NZ, JP, SG, HK, etc.); in all other countries the equivalent benefit is waived processing fees instead.
findings.claim: Apply directly at stripe.com/startups (redirects to dashboard.stripe.com/register/startup?partner_code=PUBLIC) or via an investor/accelerator partner link (Builtfirst partner pages show partner-specific credit amounts: $500 credits via AWS Activate, $5,000 credits via Emerson Collective/Inovia). Complete the form, verify your active Stripe account, submit; Stripe responds in 2-3 business days; accept the offer via the Dashboard banner or a setup-guide task (admin/owner login). Offer must be activated within 12 months of acceptance.
findings.expiry: Once activated: offer expires 12 months after activation or when the credit limit is reached, whichever comes first; cannot be paused. Unused credits expire 1 year after activation. Invoicing cap ends after 12 months (standard pricing applies). No renewal; Stripe can extend the offer only once.
findings.gotchas: Credit amounts are NOT fixed — the FAQ says 'Offer amounts vary by offer type... and by your referral source'; partner-specific pages list $500 (AWS Activate) to $5,000 (Emerson/Inovia) in credits, and where credits are unavailable, waivers on $20K-$150K USD of processing volume. Excluded products: Crypto, Capital, Atlas, Terminal devices, Link passthrough, PayPal fees, professional services. Cap is based on payment date, not invoice creation date; each installment payment gets its own $10 cap. Invoicing fee is otherwise 0.4% uncapped (Starter) — the $10 cap is the perk. Users with custom/volume pricing or who already redeemed a discount are ineligible. No .edu/student pathway exists; the only route is proving institutional (VC) funding. No credit card is required to apply or hold a Stripe account (usage-based billing).

findings.name: Free usage-based standard pricing (no setup/monthly fees) — de facto free to start
findings.detail: Stripe has no subscription 'free tier'; instead, standard pricing has 'No setup fees, monthly fees, or hidden fees' — you pay only per transaction. A new company (including a student side-project) can create a live Stripe account and accept real payments for $0 upfront. Included at no extra charge on standard pricing: 3D Secure, Authorization Boost, Adaptive Pricing, Radar Lite (AI fraud protection), dispute deflection lookups, and Connect (embedded payments) with 0.25% starting fee only if the platform sets its own rates. Per-transaction fees vary by locale (e.g. Romania: 1.5%+lei1.00 domestic EEA cards; US standard is 2.9%+30c card-present/online card rates). No credit card required to open or use a Stripe account (pay-as-you-go).
findings.eligibility: Anyone who can open a Stripe account (business or sole proprietor in supported countries). Not student-specific, not startup-specific; no funding proof or .edu email needed.
findings.claim: Sign up at stripe.com and create a live account in minutes; no credit card, no monthly fee. Start processing immediately; costs are purely per-transaction plus product fees.
findings.expiry: Permanent pricing model; no trial period needed.
findings.gotchas: 'Free to start' is not free to run: card fees, a 1% instant-payouts fee (where available), dispute fees (per-locale, e.g. 100 lei per dispute received/countered in Romania), and per-transaction product fees (Invoicing 0.4% uncapped outside the Startups program; Billing, Tax, Identity, etc.) all still apply. This is a pricing model, not a student startup offer — do not list it as a discount in a comparison of free offers.

findings.name: 30-day free trials: Sigma, Data Pipeline, Revenue Recognition + free-usage tiers
findings.detail: Official pricing page offers 'Try for free for 30 days' on: Stripe Sigma (query tool), Data Pipeline (warehouse/data sync), and Revenue Recognition. Separate perpetual free-usage allowances: Workflows — 10,000 steps per month free, then ~0.078 lei per additional step; Data Pipeline Postgres sync — 5,000 rows per month free. (Figures seen on the Romania-locale pricing page; US equivalents: Workflows $0.02/step overage, Sigma/Data Pipeline/Revenue Recognition priced per usage.)
findings.eligibility: Any Stripe account holder; no student or startup status required; no credit card required to start a trial.
findings.claim: Create a Stripe account, navigate to the product (Sigma / Data Pipeline / Revenue Recognition), and activate the 30-day trial directly in the dashboard.
findings.expiry: 30-day trial per product; free monthly allowances (10k workflow steps, 5k data rows) are recurring and not a trial.
findings.gotchas: These are trials, not free tiers — after 30 days the product bills per its standard plan (e.g. Sigma in the locale page is billed by plan: ~44 lei/mo annual or 66 lei/mo). If you only use under the free allowances, costs can be near-zero even post-trial.

findings.name: Stripe Startups separate Treasury benefit: $1,000 cash for opening a Stripe card
findings.detail: The official FAQ lists a separate Treasury benefit: sign up for a Stripe card 'within 7 days of the event' and Stripe deposits US$1,000 in cash into your Treasury account within 30 days of card creation.
findings.eligibility: Startups participating in the Stripe Startups program events; exact trigger ('the event') and program enrollment required.
findings.claim: Create a Stripe card within 7 days of the qualifying event; $1,000 deposited to your Stripe Treasury account within ~30 days.
findings.expiry: One-time; 7-day window to act.
findings.gotchas: Only mentioned in the FAQ's benefits list — no standalone terms page found; confirm details at application time.

findings.name: Student / education licensing: no free offer found
findings.detail: No student-only free tier, .edu-based discount, or education license exists for Stripe as of 2026-10-22. The official pricing page lists no student or education pricing; partner marketplaces and search results contain no .edu-gated Stripe offer. The only education-adjacent benefit is the 'Education' pillar of the Stripe Startups program (expert insights/how-to programming), which is venture-funding-gated, not student-gated. Free paths for students: the usage-based standard pricing ($0 to start, no credit card) and the 30-day product trials above; Stripe's test mode/API has always been free.
findings.eligibility: N/A (no offer)
findings.claim: N/A
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Students building projects should budget real card fees for live traffic; test mode is free and card-free but does not process real money.

findings.name: Partner-specific credit amounts (referral-dependent tiers)
findings.detail: Because offer amounts vary by referral source, Builtfirst partner pages publish the tiers: AWS Activate — $500 USD in Stripe credits (or, in countries where credits aren't yet available, waived fees on the equivalent of $20,000 USD in processing volume), new Stripe users only; Emerson Collective / Inovia — $5,000 USD in credits (or $150,000 USD volume waived where credits unavailable), available to new AND existing customers, plus the 0.4% Invoicing cap up to $10/invoice for year one.
findings.eligibility: Venture-backed startups referred through that specific investor/program (or via Builtfirst login claim); must be on standard pricing and not hold custom/volume pricing or a prior redeemed discount.
findings.claim: Claim through the partner's Builtfirst login page (login to claim, redirected to Stripe registration with partner code), or the partner's partner-page link.
findings.expiry: Credits: unused credits expire 1 year after activation. Invoicing cap: first 12 months.
findings.gotchas: Amounts are partner-specific — direct application (stripe.com/startups, PUBLIC partner code) may yield a different, often smaller, offer than a VC referral; check which partner tier you qualify for before assuming the number.

sunset_notes: The Stripe Startups program is CURRENT and was launched May 13, 2025 (announced on LinkedIn by Stripe/CMO); it was not sunset as of 2026-10-22. Material 2025-2026 change: the program's benefit type has shifted — 'Fee credits are replacing waived processing fees over time' (per the official FAQ): in the 31 countries with the fee-credit offer, credits apply to Payments/Connect/Billing/Tax/Sigma fees, while in all other countries the equivalent benefit is still waived processing fees (cards, local payment methods, BNPL, ACH only). No sunset date, expiry date, or program closure was found on stripe.com/startups or the FAQ. The $10/invoice cap on Invoicing (0.4% Starter) and the one-off 'extend the offer only once' rule are the only stated end-of-benefit conditions. No student-only Stripe offer was ever found (no .edu education license), so there is nothing to sunset on that front; the 30-day trials and free-usage allowances (10k Workflows steps, 5k Data Pipeline rows) remain live on the pricing page. Note: stripe.com geo-routes non-US visitors (my fetches returned the Romania locale), so US-specific dollar figures were corroborated via the FAQ and partner pages rather than stripe.com/us/pricing.

findings.name: Free Sandbox (mock data, unlimited test Items)
findings.detail: Sandbox is free with no time limit and unlimited test Items against mock data, covering all API endpoints so developers can test before going live. No credit card required. Confirmed on the official pricing page ('Start testing in sandbox for free') and the Plaid Help Center ('Plaid is free to use in the Sandbox environment').
findings.eligibility: Anyone - no .edu, no region limit stated for sandbox, no company formation needed. Students get full sandbox access with just a Plaid developer account.
findings.claim: Sign up free at dashboard.plaid.com (pricing page 'Try it now' link), create a team, obtain sandbox client_id/secret, build and test against mock institutions and canned data.
findings.expiry: No expiry; sandbox access has no published duration limit.
findings.gotchas: Sandbox data is entirely mocked - no real bank data, no real OAuth institutions (Bank of America/Chase etc. connect only in Production/Trial). Going live requires the Trial plan, Limited Production, or a paid plan. Pay-as-you-go (first paid tier) requires a card on file, and once products are enabled in production the card is charged per connected items.

findings.name: Free Trial plan with real production data (new US/CA teams, up to 10 Production Items)
findings.detail: For Plaid teams in the US and Canada created on or after April 15, 2026, the Trial plan is free and supports up to 10 Production Items with real bank data. It bundles 8 products: Auth, Transactions (incl. Transactions Refresh), Balance, Identity, Assets, Liabilities, Investments (incl. Investments Refresh), Statements. Almost all OAuth institutions (incl. Bank of America, Chase, Wells Fargo) are accessible immediately without the full Production registration process.
findings.eligibility: New US or Canada teams created on/after 2026-04-15; account must be new to Production - teams with a pending/approved Production application or existing Limited Production access are NOT eligible, and there is no self-service switch. Credit card: the official FAQ says 'at no cost' but does not explicitly state CC-not-required; that part of the known-so-far claim is unverified on official pages. EU/UK teams are not covered (they get Custom plans only).
findings.claim: Sign up at dashboard.plaid.com/signup; the Trial plan is applied automatically to eligible new US/CA teams - no separate application. To exceed 10 Items or add non-bundled products, apply for full Production access and choose a paid plan.
findings.expiry: No published expiry date; the 10-Item cap is a hard limit - scaling beyond it requires upgrading to a paid plan (Pay-as-you-go/Growth/Custom).
findings.gotchas: Trial is not the paid 'Limited Production': only 8 products bundled - Layer, Signal, Transfer, Protect, Identity Verification, Monitor, Enrich, Investments Move, and all Plaid Check (Consumer Report) products are NOT included. Some institutions need extra connection steps. EU/UK customers only get Custom plans - no free tier at all in those regions. Trial replaced Limited Production for new teams as of the 2026-04-15 cutoff, so 'limited free Production access' now means Trial for new accounts.

findings.name: Limited Production free tier - 200 live API calls per product (legacy teams created before 2026-04-15)
findings.detail: The official pricing page describes Limited Production as a free service: 'up to 200 API calls with each available product using live data.' Per the Help Center, this is the free live-data path for Plaid teams created BEFORE April 15, 2026; teams on/after that date get the 10-Item Trial plan instead. The 200-calls-per-product cap is the hard limit of the free live-data tier.
findings.eligibility: Existing US/CA Plaid teams created before 2026-04-15 that have not moved to paid Production. New teams cannot claim it - Trial plan is the replacement. No .edu or startup requirement.
findings.claim: Already available to eligible legacy teams at no charge; new teams should instead get the free Trial plan at dashboard.plaid.com/signup.
findings.expiry: No sunset date published, but it is structurally legacy-only: the 2026-04-15 team-creation cutoff means the free tier stops being offered to new accounts.
findings.gotchas: 200 live calls PER PRODUCT - easy to burn through; each product counts separately, and hitting the cap blocks further live calls until upgrading to a paid plan. It coexists with (and is replaced for new teams by) the Trial plan.

findings.name: Fintech Sandbox partner credits for startups (up to $21,000)
findings.detail: Through the Fintech Sandbox Data Access Residency, startups new to Plaid get 'up to $500 worth of each API endpoint per month for 6 months, with waived monthly minimums' - aggregate value up to $21,000. Eligibility is 'New customers only' on Plaid's side. The Fintech Sandbox residency itself is free ('$0 fees'), takes no equity, lasts up to 6 months, is global, and targets companies 'typically bootstrapped through Series A.'
findings.eligibility: Startup (early stage through ~Series A; one third-party guide cites Fintech Sandbox's published bar as a product or demo and revenue under $1M ARR - that figure comes from an aggregator, not the Fintech Sandbox page I read), global, incorporated company, and must be a NEW Plaid customer. No .edu; student status not required. No equity taken. Third-party guides describe a two-interview process (~25-min and ~45-min with demo).
findings.claim: Apply to the Fintech Sandbox residency (fintechsandbox.org, 'Apply' / Data Access Residency form, interviews), get accepted, then claim the Plaid partner credit through the residency - terms are per Fintech Sandbox's partner page.
findings.expiry: Credits run for 6 months with monthly minimums waived during that window; the residency itself is 'up to 6 months' of free partner data access.
findings.gotchas: Credit value is per-endpoint ($500/endpoint/month), so the $21,000 maximum only materializes if you use many endpoints; some accelerators' versions of the deal carry a minimum-commitment rider (e.g., Aurelia Ventures lists 'Up to $30,000' as $500 x 10 products x 6 months BUT 'Requires minimum contract of $6,000/year'). Confirm which channel (Fintech Sandbox vs. your own accelerator/investor) grants the credits - terms differ.

findings.name: AI startup program (launched ~March 2026): free credits + lower minimums for early-stage AI startups
findings.detail: Plaid launched a new program for AI-native startups in early 2026: 'free usage credits, production-ready tools, and lower minimums for AI startups that qualify' (announced via Plaid's LinkedIn, March 2026). The official page (plaid.com/support-for-early-stage-ai-startups/) offers 'Free credits to build and test,' 'Production-ready tools,' and 'Lower minimums to get started' - but publishes NO exact dollar amounts, no minimum thresholds, no term or expiry.
findings.eligibility: Only 'early stage AI startups' - no funding cap, company-age limit, or stage definition published. The application form restricts country to United States, United Kingdom, or European Union (relevant because EU/UK normally get Custom-only pricing). No .edu requirement.
findings.claim: Fill the form on the official page (first/last name, company, company email, optional phone, country) and submit; Plaid reviews and 'gets back to you within 2 business days with next steps.' Reach out via sales per the March 2026 announcement.
findings.expiry: Not specified on the page - terms appear to be negotiated per applicant rather than a fixed self-serve grant.
findings.gotchas: This is a sales-gated program, not a self-serve free tier: all concrete numbers (credit size, minimums, duration) are undisclosed until Plaid responds. Do not conflate it with the free Trial plan. If you apply from EU/UK, the program's lower minimums matter because EU/UK customers otherwise only get Custom plans.

findings.name: Investor/accelerator channel credits (e.g., Aurelia Ventures: up to $30,000)
findings.detail: VC funds and accelerators that partner with Plaid advertise Plaid credits for their portfolio. Example: Aurelia Ventures lists 'Up to $30,000 in Plaid Credits' structured as $500 x 10 products x 6 months, but with the rider '*Requires minimum contract of $6,000/year' and 'New Plaid customers only.' Per StartupPerks' audit (Feb 2026), Plaid startup programs broadly serve pre-seed to Series A fintech product teams, no referral needed, credits/fees 'program-dependent.'
findings.eligibility: Depends on the funding channel: being a portfolio company of a Plaid-partnered fund/accelerator (Aurelia's version) or qualifying via Fintech Sandbox; new Plaid customers; US-centric. No .edu.
findings.claim: Ask your accelerator/investor for the Plaid partner credit (their partners page documents the deal), or route through Fintech Sandbox; terms are negotiated, so confirm the minimum-commitment rider before accepting.
findings.expiry: Typically 6 months of credits per partner page, but the Aurelia variant requires a $6,000/year minimum contract - a paid commitment, not pure free credits.
findings.gotchas: The $30,000 figure only looks free; the Aurelia rider converts it to a commitment-backed deal. The waived-minimums version (Fintech Sandbox, up to $21,000) is the cleaner no-commitment offer. Confirm current terms with Plaid - channel deals drift.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes: (1) 2026-04-15 cutover - Plaid split free live-data access by team creation date: teams created on/after Apr 15, 2026 get the new free Trial plan (10 Production Items, 8 bundled products, OAuth institutions) instead of Limited Production; Limited Production (free, 200 live calls per product) persists only for legacy teams created before that date, with no self-service switch between the two. (2) No student/education license found as of 2026-10-22 - plaid.com/education/ returns 404 and no .edu-gated program appears on official pages; students are covered only by the free Sandbox and, for US/CA teams, the free Trial plan. (3) Plaid Accelerate (2021-2022, founders-of-color seed cohort with free product access for ~5 months, last blog-announced cohort in 2022) appears to have ended and was superseded by the AI startup program announced around March 2026 (free credits + lower minimums for early-stage AI startups, US/UK/EU). (4) Plan lineup per the Help Center is now Trial (free), Pay-as-you-go, Growth, and Custom (also called Scale) - EU/UK customers are Custom-only and several products (Layer, Protect, Transfer, Signal Transaction Scores, Payment Initiation/Virtual Accounts, Plaid Check beyond Base Report/Income Insights) are unavailable on Pay-as-you-go. Note: the 'no credit card' part of the known-so-far claim for the Trial plan could not be confirmed on any official page I could reach - support.plaid.com blocked direct fetch (403), and the Trial terms came via the official Help Center article text; the pricing page states Pay-as-you-go requires a card on file, so treat CC-not-required as unverified for Trial specifically.

findings.name: Self-hosted open-source Typesense engine (free, no account)
findings.detail: The Typesense server is free to download and run under GPL-3.0 (Docker image, native binaries, RPM/DEB packages), with no cost, no account, and no usage caps. Client libraries (Python, JS, PHP, Ruby, etc.) are Apache-licensed. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: prior notes saying 'open source (Apache 2.0)' are wrong for the engine — the server repo is GPL-3.0; Apache applies only to the client libraries. Per the vendor's README FAQ, they deliberately chose GPL over AGPL: running the server commercially on your own infrastructure does not create copyleft distribution obligations; internal modifications can stay private as long as you don't ship modified builds to others. Company is bootstrapped/'lean customer-funded' with no investor-backed sunset. No CMS product exists; 'fronts: APIs, Search & CMS' — Typesense covers APIs + Search only, not CMS.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; no .edu email, no credit card, no region limits, no startup age/funding cap. Commercial use permitted.
findings.claim: Download via https://typesense.org/downloads/ (Docker: 'Copy Code' commands for Docker/Linux/macOS/Windows) or clone https://github.com/typesense/typesense. Run locally or on any server.
findings.expiry: None; ongoing license (server GPL-3.0, libs Apache). No stated end date.
findings.gotchas: License is GPL-3.0, not Apache 2.0 as previously assumed; if you distribute modified builds, GPL obligations apply. Self-hosted is API-only (Cloud adds admin UI, RBAC, SDN). Free support is best-effort only. This is a license, not a 'program' — it cannot be renewed or lapsed.
findings.source_url: https://github.com/typesense/typesense (GPL-3.0 badge + README license FAQ) and https://typesense.org/downloads/

findings.name: Typesense Cloud 'free cluster' / free credits, no credit card
findings.detail: Typesense Cloud advertises free credits with no credit card required. Exact site copy (cloud.typesense.org root): 'Did we mention we give you free credits? You don't even need a credit card!' The pricing calculator (now usage-based: hourly, no per-search/per-record charges, minimum 0.5GB RAM, 2 vCPUs with 1 hr burst/day, 3 nodes, add-ons: GPU, high-perf disk, HA, SDN) links to 'start with a free cluster' which is the signup page. The dollar amount of free credits and its duration are NOT disclosed on any public page (checked: root, calculator, terms, FAQ, support pages). Purchased credits expire 15 months after purchase per the Cloud Services Agreement §5; free-credit expiration is unspecified.
findings.eligibility: Any user who signs up (work email or GitHub sign-in); no credit card, no .edu requirement, no startup-age or funding cap found, no region limits stated.
findings.claim: 1) Create account at cloud.typesense.org/signup (or /pricing/start-free). 2) Launch a cluster from the dashboard using the free credits. 3) Configure size via the calculator at cloud.typesense.org/pricing/calculator.
findings.expiry: Not publicly stated for the free credits; agreement says purchased credits expire 15 months after purchase. Hourly billing applies after credits are exhausted.
findings.gotchas: Trial-like credits, not a named perpetual free tier. Once credits run out you pay hourly for the running cluster (minimum 3-node cluster). SDN/add-ons and support plans are extra. Don't assume the free credits renew or roll over.
findings.source_url: https://cloud.typesense.org/ ('free credits' copy) and https://cloud.typesense.org/pricing/calculator ('start with a free cluster' link)

findings.name: Free support plan ('Critical Production Support — Free')
findings.detail: Typesense Cloud support plans page lists a Free tier at $0: 'Best effort' response for critical production issues (no SLA), channels = Email, GitHub Issues, Public Slack Community. No SOC2/HIPAA, no bank transfer, no vendor forms, no security questionnaires, no prioritized feature requests. Handlers: 'Engineers who write the code that powers Typesense & Typesense Cloud'.
findings.eligibility: All Typesense Cloud users, free; no startup/student-specific eligibility.
findings.claim: Open a support request via Email, GitHub Issues, or the public Slack community as listed on the support plans page; no signup for support beyond a Cloud account.
findings.expiry: None stated; ongoing $0 tier alongside paid tiers (Developer $160 / Business $400 / Enterprise $700 / Enterprise Signature $1,900 every 28 days).
findings.gotchas: Best-effort only — no response SLA and no 24x7x365 critical guarantee (that starts at the $160 Developer plan).

findings.name: Free Algolia-migration consulting/support tiers (spend-gated)
findings.detail: For existing Algolia customers switching to Typesense Cloud (free offers tied to current Algolia spend, from the pricing calculator page): spend >$1,000/mo → 'FREE 30-Minute Consulting' call; >$2,000/mo → 'FREE 1-Year Prioritized Business Support & Migration Consulting' (listed $5,200 value); >$3,000/mo → 'FREE 1-Year Prioritized Enterprise Support & Migration Consulting' (listed $9,100 value) plus 'FREE Private Slack Connect Support' and an advisory-board invite.
findings.eligibility: Existing Algolia customers crossing the stated monthly-spend thresholds; effectively mid-sized+ startups/companies; not aimed at students or individuals.
findings.claim: Contact Typesense (sales/demo, e.g., 'Schedule a Demo' on cloud.typesense.org) citing your Algolia spend to unlock the matching tier.
findings.expiry: The 1-year support offers last 1 year from grant; promotion has no stated end date.
findings.gotchas: Gated on live Algolia spend, not on age/funding; 'value' figures are Typesense's own list prices.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, verified by fetching the official pages today: (1) No student/education license or program exists — typesense.org/education/ is 404, the typesense.org sitemap (10 URLs) contains no education/student URL, the docs Guide + FAQ contain no education offer, and the blog index (latest post Apr 14, 2025) has none. (2) No named startup program/discount exists — cloud.typesense.org/startup is 404; the only startup-flavored content is marketing copy ('From Scrappy Startups to Household Names') and the spend-gated free Algolia-migration offers above. Typesense is explicitly bootstrapped ('lean customer-funded team of engineers'; 2022 blog 'To Raise VC, or Not'), which fits a no-VC startup-investment model rather than a funded startup program. (3) The previously-known claim 'open source (Apache 2.0) self-hosted = free' is partially wrong: the Typesense server is GPL-3.0 (verified against the raw LICENSE.txt and GitHub's license badge; client libraries are Apache). (4) Typesense Cloud pricing has been restructured from named tiers into a usage-based hourly configuration calculator (memory 0.5–1024 GB, 2-vCPU floor, 3–7 nodes, ~28 regions, GPU/disk/HA/SDN add-ons) with no visible named free plan; the free entry point is signup-based 'free cluster / free credits' whose dollar amount and duration are undisclosed on public pages. (5) No CMS front: Typesense offers no CMS product; 'fronts: APIs, Search & CMS' applies only to APIs and Search. (6) Methodology caveat: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so 2025–2026 change checks were not done via search; all findings above come from pages fetched on 2026-10-22 (high confidence for what the pages state; the free-credit amount/duration could not be confirmed from any public page).

findings.name: Algolia Free Plan (free tier)
findings.detail: Standing no-cost tier: 10,000 search requests/month, 50,000 records, 5,000 recommendation requests/month, 5,000 resources crawled (crawls)/month. Includes core Search, Recommend, SDKs and UI components; explicitly usable in production. Hard caps: 10 KB/record, 1 GB/application data, 1 GB/index, 1 application.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (developers, startups, teams). No .edu email, no company-age or funding cap, no region limit. No credit card required. Self-serve.
findings.claim: Self-serve sign up at https://dashboard.algolia.com/users/sign_up (no application, approval, or code). Then open https://dashboard.algolia.com. FAQ links a demo request at https://www.algolia.com/demorequest.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated (ongoing free tier). If account is inactive >30 days, Algolia may remove Subscriber Data. Reaching the usage limit: service may be suspended or an Algolia attribution may be added to search results.
findings.gotchas: Not unlimited: 50K-record and 10K-request caps simply stop (no billing on the free tier, unlike Grow). 50K records vs 100K on paid plans. No hosting-location choice on Free (US/UK/EU only appear under Grow). At usage limit results may carry Algolia attribution; idle accounts can lose data.

findings.name: Algolia Startup Program (trial credits)
findings.detail: $10,000 in Algolia credits, valid for 12 months, plus world-class support. Bonus perks: credits for other SaaS products (DataDog, Notion and more) and Algolia Academy education resources. After credits are used, the account is automatically moved to Pay-as-you-go, or committed plans with ~20% discounts.
findings.eligibility: Startups only, and new Algolia customers only. Main-page criteria: company less than 7 years old AND less than $15M total funding raised. The page's FAQ contradicts this: less than 3 years old AND less than $5M raised. No founder-count requirement; no .edu requirement; no region limit stated.
findings.claim: Apply via the form linked from the page (a support-ticket form): https://support.algolia.com/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=5005635939217 . Unresolved questions: startups@algolia.com.
findings.expiry: Credits lapse after 12 months; unused credits expire. No renewal mechanism described (appears to be a one-time grant).
findings.gotchas: Credits are non-transferable. Not eligible if you have used any other coupon code in the past. Eligibility numbers conflict on-page (7yr/US$15M on the main block vs 3yr/US$5M in the FAQ) - confirm current thresholds before applying. Post-credit auto-moves to pay-as-you-go.

findings.name: Algolia for Open Source (AOS) free offer
findings.detail: A Standard PAYG plan with 200 units free, which translates to 200,000 records + 200,000 search requests + up to 2,000,000 indexing operations per month - a stated ~$180/month value.
findings.eligibility: Three buckets: (1) licensed open-source software under a valid OSS license; (2) developer-community projects that make content discoverable/searchable and useful; (3) legally-recognized non-profit or non-governmental organizations. All must be non-commercial, publicly available, and exceed the free tier's limits. Commercially-backed non-commercial projects are reviewed case-by-case. No .edu requirement; no startup age/funding cap.
findings.claim: Submit your project through the application/submission form on the page (or use the 'Start Free' sign-up link). Questions: community@algolia.com.
findings.expiry: Ongoing for qualifying projects; no stated expiry. If a project is terminated, acquired, or shifts to a commercial model, the account is downgraded 'in a timely manner.'
findings.gotchas: Requires a 'Search by Algolia' logo attribution in your search results/site, linking to algolia.com (alternatives can be discussed). Must remain non-commercial and publicly available. Credit-card requirement not stated on the page. 200 units (~$180/month value) is the cap.

findings.name: Algolia for Non-Profit free offer
findings.detail: Same AOS bundle: Standard PAYG plan + 200 units free = 200,000 records + 200,000 search requests + up to 2,000,000 indexing operations per month (~$180/month value).
findings.eligibility: Legally-recognized non-profit / non-governmental organizations; must be non-commercial and publicly available. No .edu requirement; no startup age/funding cap.
findings.claim: Submit through the application form on the page; questions to community@algolia.com.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; account downgraded on status change, termination, or acquisition.
findings.gotchas: Logo attribution required. The non-profit category overlaps with the open-source program. Credit-card requirement not stated. Status must remain non-profit/non-commercial or the account is downgraded.

findings.name: Grow & Grow Plus 'Start for free' allowance (pay-as-you-go)
findings.detail: Self-serve pay-as-you-go tiers that include a free allowance: 10,000 search requests/month + 100,000 records, then billed $0.50/1K requests (Grow) or $1.75/1K requests (Grow Plus, which adds AI Synonyms, AI Ranking, Advanced Personalization, Query Categorization, Collections, 90-day analytics retention), and $0.40/1K records. Billed monthly with no contract required. Hosting: US/UK/EU on Grow.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone (self-serve). Not explicitly credit-card-free like the Free plan (a payment method is needed for pay-as-you-go overage). No .edu; no age/funding cap; regions US/UK/EU.
findings.claim: Start from the pricing page (https://www.algolia.com/pricing) by choosing Grow or Grow Plus; billed monthly, no contract, no approval.
findings.expiry: Free allowance resets monthly; unused allowance does not roll over. Ongoing pay-as-you-go; cancellable (no contract).
findings.gotchas: Not a pure free tier - you are billed beyond the 10K requests / 100K records allowance. Grow Plus is pricier per request ($1.75 vs $0.50). Distinct from the no-CC 'Free plan', which has a hard cap and no billing. Search-as-you-type multiplies request count; multi-query bundling reduces billed requests.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes: On October 2, 2025 Algolia launched the Grow Plus plan, bringing AI search capabilities (AI Synonyms, AI Ranking, Advanced Personalization, Query Categorization, Collections, 90-day analytics retention) to the self-serve/pay-as-you-go lineup at $1.75/1K requests - a material expansion of the paid tiers; Grow plan terms were last updated June 30, 2025 (previous version Sept 25, 2024). No core free offer was sunset or reduced in 2025-2026: the Free plan still lists 10K requests / 50K records / 5K recommend / 5K crawls with no credit card required, matching the known figures. There is no dedicated student/education license: /education and /for-education both return 404 and the pricing page exposes no student URL; the only education-adjacent item is 'Algolia Academy' resources offered as a perk inside the Startup program. One unresolved on-page discrepancy in the Startup program: the main block says <7 years old and <US$15M funding, while its FAQ says <3 years old and <US$5M funding. Note: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the startup/education verification relied on direct WebFetch of official Algolia pages (fetched 2026-10-22), which is the intended high-confidence path.

findings.name: Free Mollie account / pay-as-you-go free tier (no monthly fees, free test API keys)
findings.detail: Mollie's base account has no monthly fees, no lock-in contracts, and fees only on successful live transactions (e.g. SEPA Instant bank transfer €0.25 flat, SEPA Direct Debit €0.35 flat, iDEAL/Wero NL €0.32, EEA consumer card 1.80% + €0.25). Checkout, Payment Links, Invoicing and Recurring are included at no extra cost. In-person POS 'Pay as you go' plan is €0/month (1.20% domestic consumer card rate, max 1 terminal, PAX terminals not supported; unlimited Tap apps free; Tap to Pay on iPhone/Android costs no terminal — free app). Test API keys are free and test payments are simulated, so no transaction fees in test. The first 5 payouts/month are free for accounts with annual volume under €500,000; additional payouts €0.25 each.
findings.eligibility: Any registered business (Mollie signs up registered businesses only — a registered business with a live website, bank account + verification payment, and ID of legal representatives; review up to 10 business days). No credit card is required at signup. Not available to unincorporated students as individuals. Region-limited: Mollie serves businesses headquartered in Europe/UK; the account itself is free everywhere Mollie operates.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at mollie.com (business details, bank account, ID; no credit card). 2) Account goes live (up to 10 business days review). 3) Generate free test API keys from the Dashboard/API Keys page and build/integrate in test mode with zero fees. 4) For live: just start processing — pay only per-transaction fees, no monthly minimums.
findings.expiry: Standing program; no stated end date. Terms 'subject to change' at Mollie's discretion.
findings.gotchas: Test mode is not live revenue: only EUR is supported in test mode, all API endpoints related to business operations (e.g. payouts, refund management edge cases) do not support test mode, and pending-state test payment methods don't exist in live. Demo accounts (isolated explore accounts) are early access — you must contact a Mollie representative. Live transaction fees still apply even on the free tier (1.80–3.25% + €0.25 for cards); commercial/non-EEA cards are the most expensive. POS hardware is not free: Tap terminal €95 one-off, mobile/fixed €350. Payout fees (non-EUR payout 1% of amount) apply below the €500k annual volume threshold. No 'free tier' for students/individuals — a registered business is mandatory.

findings.name: Free test-mode developer sandbox (API keys, no transaction fees)
findings.detail: Mollie's test environment is fully isolated from live data; the API behaves identically, webhooks included. Test API keys are free with any Mollie account; no card or bank verification is needed to create test keys. Test card numbers (Visa/Mastercard/Amex, any expiry/CVV) are documented. No fees are charged for test payments because they create no real transactions.
findings.eligibility: Any Mollie account holder (i.e. a registered European/UK business; see free-tier finding). No credit card required. No cost, no limits on test requests stated in the docs.
findings.claim: 1) Register a Mollie account. 2) In Dashboard → API keys, create a Test API key (free). 3) Call any payments API endpoint in test mode; simulate card/bank payments with the documented test card numbers. 4) To switch to live, create a Live API key and/or add the testmode parameter — no migration needed since API behavior is identical.
findings.expiry: Permanent capability; no stated expiry.
findings.gotchas: EUR-only in test mode. Endpoints for business-operations resources (accounts, balances, etc.) do not support test mode. Recurring test payments have no checkout URL — you force final state via changePaymentState. Test keys are separate from live keys; webhooks fired in test come from the test environment. This is a sandbox, not a 'free forever live account'.

findings.name: Mollie Startup Program — waived fees up to €1,000,000 in payment processing
findings.detail: Three tiers of waived Mollie transaction fees, scaled by total funding raised: (1) startups with up to €200k in funding → €75,000 of waived fees; (2) €200k–€2m in funding → €500,000 of waived fees; (3) €2m+ in funding → €1,000,000 of waived fees (UK site mirrors the same tiers in £: £75k/£500k/£1m). Includes priority support (skip-the-queue human responses), no lock-in contracts, and access to a curated founder community with events across Europe. Waiver is volume-based: it applies to your next N euros of processing volume until exhausted.
findings.eligibility: Pre-seed to Series B startup; headquartered in Europe/UK; must be new to Mollie (existing customers not eligible). Funding status is verified by Mollie with your VC or via public data. Program explicitly targets VC-backed companies — non-VC-backed startups are told to contact sales instead. No .edu/student angle; a company (not an individual) must apply. No credit card required to apply.
findings.claim: 1) Confirm eligibility (pre-seed–Series B, Europe/UK HQ, new to Mollie). 2) Fill out the short application form (≈3 minutes) on mollie.com/solutions/payments-for-startups — an email with next steps arrives almost instantly. 3) Mollie verifies your funding (VC contact or public data). 4) On approval, the fee waiver and priority support are automatically applied to your new Mollie account.
findings.expiry: No explicit end date or time limit stated on the official page; the waiver is exhausted by volume (until N processed). Offer 'subject to change, withdrawal or cancellation at any time' per Mollie's campaign terms language.
findings.gotchas: Only the waiver for your funding tier applies — a bootstrap/underfunded startup gets the small €75k tier, not €1M (the headline number misleads). The waiver covers Mollie transaction fees only; 'additional costs directly imposed by a particular payment method may apply' (per Mollie's campaign T&Cs, chargebacks on card/SEPA DD/Klarna/SOFORT and refunds are excluded from such waivers). Refunds can count against waived volume in Mollie's promotion terms. 'New to Mollie' + 'terminated account within previous 6 months' excludes churned accounts. Not available to US-headquartered startups. Existing Mollie customers can't join.

findings.name: €1,000 free processing volume promo for new Mollie customers outside BE/NL
findings.detail: A standard new-customer promotion (separate from the Startup Program): EUR 1,000.00 of processing volume free of Mollie transaction fees ('Mollie Promotion Amount'). Applies when you register a new Mollie account and your registered business address is outside Belgium and the Netherlands. You must process your first transaction within 30 days of valid registration. The promo remains valid until fully exhausted, but expires automatically 365 days after account registration. One promotion per account, not transferable; refunds count as processing volume against the promo; chargebacks (cards, SEPA DD, Klarna, SOFORT) and refunds fall outside the promo and are charged at applicable rates; volume beyond €1,000 is charged at your dashboard rate (or basic public website rate).
findings.eligibility: New Mollie accounts only; registered business address outside Belgium and the Netherlands (Mollie's home markets are excluded — presumably served by different local offers). No credit card required. No student/startup-specific eligibility — open to any new customer in eligible regions.
findings.claim: 1) Register a new Mollie account with a business address outside BE/NL. 2) Process your first transaction within 30 days. 3) Your first €1,000 of successful processing volume is automatically free of Mollie transaction fees until the amount is exhausted or 365 days pass.
findings.expiry: Per-account expiry: promo lapses 365 days after valid registration even if unused; first transaction within 30 days. Campaign itself has no stated calendar end date and may be withdrawn 'at any time' — the T&C page was live when read today, but the page carries no start/end date, so treat current availability as unconfirmed.
findings.gotchas: It is a €1,000 volume cap, not a cash credit — with typical rates (~2% + €0.25 per card) the real savings are only ~€20–25, far smaller than it sounds.
