sunset_notes: No Razorpay startup/student program was sunset in 2025-2026; the changes were additive: (1) NEW as of 1 Jul 2026 - the 90-day new-merchant welcome offer (up to Rs 5 lakh of domestic payment value fee-free, new merchants only, one redemption per PAN/bank account, KYC fee of Rs 199 + tax may apply). (2) May 2025 - MeitY Startup Hub partnership added the MSH-credits track (PG zero fees up to Rs 1 lakh / 6 months, banking 3 months + 40% off, payroll free <5 employees). (3) 25 Mar 2026 - DPIIT MoU + 'Startup Sahayak' platform added zero-professional-fee incorporation and credits for DPIIT-recognised startups. (4) US promo - 'first year free up to $50,000 transaction volume' was in Razorpay's machine-readable US pricing reference (updated May 2026) but is absent from the live US pricing page as of 22 Oct 2026; treat as unverified or sunset unless confirmed with Razorpay US sales. (5) No student/education license or student free tier has ever existed at Razorpay - there is nothing to sunset on that front; the only student program is the recurring (September) AI Buildathon internship in Bangalore. (6) Baseline 'free' items (0 setup, 0 AMC, 0 integration/support fee, free REST API/SDKs/webhooks, pay-per-transaction 2% domestic + up to 3% international + 18% GST) remain unchanged in the current pricing page. All startup-perks credits are first-come-first-served and valid only 3 months from activation (or until the cap is hit), so the practical constraint is expiry, not sunset.

findings.name: Startup Program — $1M free Billing
findings.detail: Chargebee's official startup offer: 'Bill your first $1M of usage and subscriptions for free.' Chargebee Billing is at zero cost (stated as 'zero dollars, no fine print') until cumulative invoiced revenue through Chargebee reaches $1M, plus free data migration and 24/7 email support, access to 40+ gateways, and the modular stack (CPQ, tax, revenue reporting). After crossing $1M (cumulative, not ARR/MRR), the account transitions to a pay-as-you-go plan with no annual commitment, with advance notice. Companies that have raised over $5M are not excluded: the form has a '$5M+ funding' option and Chargebee proposes a custom offer. Amounts are USD; non-US thresholds adjust for current FX rates. No public sunset/end date found on the page.
findings.eligibility: All three conditions required: (1) NEW Chargebee customer, not already on a paid plan; (2) company belongs to a partner Accelerator or VC portfolio network (the key gate — no founding-date or revenue cap otherwise listed); (3) total funding raised below $5M. No .edu/student route.
findings.claim: Apply via the 'Apply now' form on https://www.chargebee.com/startups/ (choose the '$5M+' option if funding exceeds $5M so the team tailors terms), or email startups@chargebee.com / use on-site chat. A representative reviews the application and follows up within 2-3 business days to get you set up.
findings.expiry: No published end date; individual free period ends when cumulative invoiced revenue hits $1M, then pay-as-you-go (no annual commit) begins automatically.
findings.gotchas: The partner-accelerator/VC-portfolio requirement is easy to miss — independent bootstrapped startups with <$5M funding do not qualify on the letter of the offer. '$1M free' is cumulative lifetime billing, not ARR/MRR, and not a forever-free tier: after $1M you are on standard usage pricing. This is the only genuinely free-for-new-customers offer on the site; the $0 add-ons (Growth Starter, CPQ Lite) are gated behind an active paid Billing plan.

findings.name: Growth Starter ($0 Growth add-on)
findings.detail: The Growth module's 'Starter' plan is priced at $0: pricing tables, hosted checkout, self-serve portal, no-code cancel pages, 1 growth experiment; single-brand; aimed at 'teams with hundreds of subscribers'. It is a free add-on, not a free platform tier.
findings.eligibility: ANY Chargebee Billing customer — the page states 'Exclusively for Chargebee Billing customers' and Billing itself has no free tier (entry plan is usage-priced Flow: $0 + 0.80% of monthly invoiced volume up to $500K/mo, breakeven ~$66K vs $99 + 0.65% above $500K). So in practice you need an active paid billing relationship (or the startup program) before this is usable.
findings.claim: Included at $0 once you are a Chargebee Billing customer; no separate enrollment. Claim path: start on a Billing plan (e.g., via the startup program or Flow plan), then enable the Growth Starter module.
findings.expiry: No expiry noted; $0 while Growth Starter conditions hold.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free trap: $0 price does not mean $0 total cost — the required Billing plan bills usage (0.80%+ of invoiced). Do not count this as a free tier for new startups.

findings.name: CPQ Lite (first 50 quotes free)
findings.detail: The CPQ 'Lite' module is 'Free for the first 50 quotes': quote creation and immediate amendments; paid add-on for CPQ for Salesforce/HubSpot. Free beyond 50 quotes or full CPQ requires a paid/enterprise arrangement ('Talk to sales').
findings.eligibility: ANY Chargebee Billing customer ('Available exclusively for Chargebee Billing customers'), i.e. same paid-billing gate as Growth Starter. No student/education angle.
findings.claim: Available at no cost on the free 50 quotes once a Billing plan is active; full CPQ or extra gateway integrations go through sales.
findings.expiry: The free portion is capped at 50 cumulative quotes, not time-limited.
findings.gotchas: The 50-quote allowance is cumulative; 'free' quotes still presume the paid billing relationship that is the module's precondition. No egress/data export on the free modules — data export to GCS/S3/Snowflake and higher API/webhook limits are paid add-ons.

findings.name: Free trial (marketing trial, details unpublished)
findings.detail: Every Chargebee page carries a 'Start Free Trial' CTA leading to the signup form at /trial-signup/ (US/EU/AU data residency selection, ToS/privacy consent). However, the trial duration and credit-card requirement are NOT stated on the pricing page, the signup page, or the homepage as of 2026-10-22. Historically Chargebee ran a ~30-day trial with no credit card, but I could not re-verify that on any official page today, so treat those specific parameters as unconfirmed.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone who signs up at /trial-signup/; no student or startup condition stated.
findings.claim: Go to https://www.chargebee.com/trial-signup/, pick a data center, and complete the sign-up form.
findings.expiry: Trial terms (length, auto-conversion) not published on the pages read; confirm in the signup flow or with Chargebee support.
findings.gotchas: A trial is not a free tier: without publishing trial terms, verify whether a card is required and whether it auto-converts to the usage-priced Flow plan at the end. Do not quote '30 days, no CC' as current fact.

sunset_notes: (1) Education/student license: NONE found — as of 2026-10-22, chargebee.com has no education page (/education/ and /for-education/ do not host a student program; the 'e-learning' section is a vertical marketing page FOR e-learning companies like Study.com), no .edu/email-verified student offer anywhere on the site, no footer or nav link to an academic program, and no trial credits of any kind. (2) Free-tier sunset: the pricing page now lists only two Billing plans — 'Flow' ($0 + 0.80% up to $500K/mo invoicing, $99 + 0.65% above $500K/mo, ~$66K breakeven, 100M usage events/mo included) and 'Enterprise' (custom) — so there is no free core-Billing tier for new users; the old-style free entry plan (Basic) is no longer offered. What remains free is: the $1M-cumulative startup program (with partner-network eligibility), the 50 free CPQ quotes and $0 Growth Starter (both gated behind an active paid Billing relationship), and the marketing trial whose terms are no longer published on-site. (3) Methodology caveat: the official pages (https://www.chargebee.com/pricing/, /startups/, /trial-signup/, homepage) were read directly on 2026-10-22 (high confidence for those); the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-task, so 2025-2026 change history (e.g., prior startup-offer versions, trial-terms changes) could not be independently verified — statements about prior-plan lineup above rest on pre-existing knowledge and are medium confidence.

findings.name: Free test/sandbox environment & test-mode API access (no credit card, no real money)
findings.detail: Adyen's self-service developer offer: a free test Customer Area (ca-test.adyen.com), test API + test Client API keys, and Adyen-published test card numbers and test payment-method credentials to simulate payments, tokenization, fraud/3DS2 without real money. Adyen charges NO setup fee and NO monthly fee (confirmed on adyen.com/pricing: 'Pay per transaction, with no setup or monthly fees'; 'We do not have monthly fees, set-up fees, integration fees or closure fees'). Production is per-transaction (e.g., cards ~US$0.13 + Interchange++ + 0.60%; ACH ~US$0.37; Amex ~3.95%), and Adyen has a per-industry 'minimum invoice' (one 2025 review cites ~US$120/mo; Adyen states it varies and fees on the public page are 'indicative', not guaranteed).
findings.eligibility: No .edu / student status, no company verification, no funding cap, and NO credit card required to use the test environment (self-service email + MFA signup). Open to any developer, student, or startup. Global (Adyen supports acquiring in 45+ markets; specific methods/currencies vary by region).
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for a free Adyen test account at ca-test.adyen.com (email + MFA). 2) In the test Customer Area, generate a test API key and a test Client API key for a test application (or use Adyen's pre-supplied test credentials). 3) Use Adyen's published test card numbers / test payment-method credentials to simulate transactions. 4) Build and test your integration against the test endpoint. To go live: contact Adyen sales, apply for a live account, sign a contract, and re-create the test setup in the live Customer Area.
findings.expiry: No published expiry for test accounts/credentials (Adyen may close very long-inactive test accounts; test credentials stay valid until regenerated). Live account terms/renewal are per-contract and require ongoing Adyen sales engagement.
findings.gotchas: Test mode moves no real money and CANNOT accept real payments/payouts - that needs an approved live account (sales + contract + per-industry minimum invoice). There is NO perpetual 'free production tier'; production is per-transaction and published fees are indicative, not guaranteed. Adyen for Platforms, Capital, and Issuing/Balance products are 'contact us' and priced separately (not self-service). Prices/minimums vary by industry and region.

findings.name: Adyen Accelerator program (impact / social startups)
findings.detail: A week-long accelerator (public editions in 2021 and 2022; the 2022 edition ran June 13-17). Benefits: dedicated Adyen business mentors, workshops/talks, investor networking, a pop-up 'impact market' at Adyen's offices to trial Adyen technology, and a demo day pitching to impact-focused investors and Adyen board members. No participation fee, credit amount, or monetary stipend was published. This is a mentorship/visibility program, not a free-credit or pricing offer.
findings.eligibility: EMEA-based, direct-to-consumer social/impact startups with a launched MVP and a clear impact aligned to a UN Sustainable Development Goal (SDG). Not for general commercial startups, not student/education-facing; no funding or age cap stated.
findings.claim: Fill out the application form linked from Adyen's press release (2022 cycle closed mid-March for a June program). Selection is by application/review - no direct self-serve enrollment.
findings.expiry: Ran on an annual cadence in 2021-2022. No 2025 or 2026 cohort is publicly confirmed on Adyen's site as of this check (page footer is '© 2026 Adyen' but the content is the 2022 edition), so the program appears dormant/sunset.
findings.gotchas: Not a financial 'free offer' - no credits, fee waivers, or guaranteed discount; value is mentorship/visibility/investor access. EMEA/impact-only. Status unclear - treat as likely discontinued and verify with Adyen before relying on it.

findings.name: 'Adyen for Startups' integration credits (unverified)
findings.detail: A third-party startup-credits directory (StartupFlow AI) lists 'Adyen for Startups' as 'discounted global payment-processing integration credits for early-stage startups,' eligible at pre-seed/seed, 'global, subject to the provider's eligibility and approval,' with no funding limit stated and no referral needed. The directory explicitly says it 'has not confirmed a direct application page' and only links to Adyen's main site. Adyen's own site and full developer-docs sitemap contain no confirmed public startup-credits program, no stated credit amount/limit, and no dedicated application URL.
findings.eligibility: Reported (unconfirmed) as pre-seed/seed, global, no stated funding cap, no .edu requirement, no self-serve page - 'subject to Adyen approval.' Treat as unverified.
findings.claim: No confirmed official application flow. Best effort: contact Adyen sales/partnerships to ask about a startup program or credits; no public self-serve form was found.
findings.expiry: Unknown; no public start/expiration dates. Directory entry last verified 2 Aug 2026 but only against Adyen's main site.
findings.gotchas: Low confidence / unverified: not confirmed by Adyen, no amount or limits published, no application URL - could be a generic directory placeholder. The only verifiable free developer surface Adyen offers is the test/sandbox environment.

sunset_notes: For Adyen (Payments & Fintech Dev Tools), of the four requested categories only the free test/sandbox environment + test-mode API access is a genuine, currently-available free offer. Verifications (all done via WebFetch of official Adyen pages + Adyen's docs sitemap + two third-party directories; the second WebSearch hit was blocked because the session web-search budget was exhausted): (1) No perpetual FREE production tier - adyen.com/pricing is per-transaction (cards ~US$0.13 + Interchange++ + 0.60%), 'no setup fee / no monthly fees,' with a per-industry minimum invoice; published fees are indicative, not guaranteed. findings.name: Explore plan — free tier (US)
findings.detail: US pricing page (read today) lists Explore at $0 per user/month with NO deposit/balance threshold in the fine print: multi-currency accounts in 20+ currencies, up to 10 free Spend users, free batch transfers to 120+ countries, unlimited multi-currency corporate cards with zero international fees, up to 2% cashback on local USD spend, 3.44% on USD with Yield, domestic USD & CAD transfers free, invoicing free. No credit card required to open (business KYC onboarding only). Business/legal-entity account required — no personal/student accounts exist.
findings.eligibility: US-registered business (any size). New sign-up via airwallex.com/en-us/signup; KYC/onboarding required. No funding stage, no .edu, no minimum balance listed on the US page. findings.claim: Sign up free at airwallex.com/en-us/signup (no CC, no deposit on US page); plan is ongoing while you remain a customer.

Marketing 'free' claim in US changed over 2025: previously threshold-based ($0 if $5K/mo deposit or $10K balance, else $29). Legacy customers who signed up before June 1, 2025 were placed into Explore with no monthly fee as of July 1, 2025.

findings.name: Free sandbox / developer tools (Payments & Fintech Dev Tools)
findings.detail: Airwallex developer docs (airwallex.com/docs, API reference at /docs/api) include a 'Sandbox environment' developer tool to 'simulate transactions before going live'. Docs confirm existence of a self-serve sandbox; doc sub-pages are JS-rendered so exact 'no production account / no real money / no CC required' wording could not be re-verified today — treat those specifics as medium confidence. No per-call API pricing is published; production Platform APIs / Embedded Finance are custom-priced ('contact sales').
findings.eligibility: Any Airwallex customer/developer; sandbox simulates transactions with test data — no real money. A registered business account for full production use.
findings.claim: Open an account via airwallex.com/en-us/signup, enable developer tools, generate test/API keys in sandbox mode; docs at airwallex.com/docs.

findings.name: Airwallex for Startups (US) — startup program with fee credits
findings.detail: US marketing page (read today): $150K in fee credits usable across FX, payments, payouts and platform fees for 12 months; no FX fees on your first $50,000 in transfers; no monthly global-account fees for the first 12 months (60+ countries); 6 months of t0 AI-CFO access; up to 2% cashback/fee savings on your first $800K when investors join the partner network. Partner-stack credits: Google Cloud $250K in credits, Nebius US$100,000 AI compute credits, 6 months of Notion Business (with Notion AI) free, 20% off first-year Carta subscription + waived onboarding, 20% off Deel first year. T&C (last updated Sept 9, 2026): card cashback = 10% rebate on eligible transactions for first 90 days of the Promotion Period, 2% thereafter (non-withdrawable, must offset future card spend/fees); a fee-waiver option of up to 'USD 25,000,00 equivalent' payments volume or 'USD 10,000,00 equivalent' FX volume (figures appear garbled in the fetched text — likely USD 250K / USD 100K volume caps; verify in a real browser). Rewards post by the 2nd of the following month; refunds/chargebacks reverse rewards.
findings.eligibility: Venture-backed US-registered startups, pre-seed through Series A, having raised at least USD 500,000 in venture capital; Series B or later or valuations over USD $1B disqualify; NEW Airwallex customers only (existing customers explicitly not eligible per marketing page); enrollment via a direct Airwallex invitation link, acceptance at Airwallex's sole discretion. No .edu; no credit card required; company age not stated (funding stage is the filter).
findings.claim: Apply/enroll on the Airwallex for Startups page (airwallex.com/en-us/startups) — no promo code for the US; sign up at /en-us/signup through the startup invitation flow. T&C at airwallex.com/en-us/terms/airwallex-for-startups-promotion.
findings.expiry: Application window closes 31 December 2027, 23:59 PST (extendable/shortenable at Airwallex's discretion). Benefits run 12 months (fee credits/monthly fee waiver) or 6 months (t0 AI CFO); unused waiver capacity auto-expires; participation may be revoked at any time.
findings.gotchas: Marketing-page figures ($150K fee credits, $50K FX waiver, $800K cashback base) do not line up cleanly with the fetched T&C text (garbled 'USD25,000,00'/'USD10,000,00' caps) — confirm exact caps before relying on them. Cashback is non-withdrawable and excludes card-present transactions, cash/ATM, gift vouchers, balance transfers, gambling, crypto/investments, government payments. Promotion cannot be combined with other Airwallex offers. Series B+/>$1B valuation and existing Airwallex customers are out.

findings.name: Airwallex for Startups — regional offers (AU/NZ, UK, Singapore)
findings.detail: Refreshed global program launched 29 Oct 2025 (Singapore first, then global), three pillars: stage-appropriate financial infrastructure, Startup CFO Expert Panel mentorship, and an AI Sandbox track. AU/NZ: pre-seed = 3 months free on Explore tier; seed = 3 months free on Grow tier + waived fees on first AUD$100,000 of payments + fee-free FX on first AUD$100,000 of conversions + Airwallex Yield on AUD/USD; Series A+ = contact sales; redeem code AIRWALLEX2 when enquiring via partner Scendar; requires AU ABN or NZ NZBN and venture backing. UK: pay 0% payment-method fees on first £10,000; zero FX fees on first £10,000 of conversions; 2% cashback on first £10,000 of card spend. Singapore (via SMU IIE incubatees): cashback on card spend, free FX conversions, waived collection fees and 50% off annual fees on up to S$800,000 of usage; activate perks by making an S$1 deposit or transaction; sign up via partners.airwallex.com/SMUIIE.
findings.eligibility: Venture-backed startups with a business entity registered in the program's region (AU/NZ: ABN/NZBN required; 'focused on' that region for now). UK page directs to startups@airwallex.com. No .edu requirement; no CC required.
findings.claim: AU/NZ: apply on airwallex.com/en-au/startups and redeem AIRWALLEX2 with partner Scendar (or via approved accelerator/VC partner links; Series A+ only via VC partner links). UK: register interest on airwallex.com/en-uk/airwallex-for-startups or email the startups team. SG: open account through the SMU IIE referral URL.
findings.expiry: No calendar end date published; tier offers (3-month Grow/Explore) are time-boxed to 3 months; AU terms document updated Oct 2025. Each company may redeem only one offer after Seed stage.
findings.gotchas: Regional coverage is at Airwallex's discretion and varies by market; pre-seed AU applicants must be incorporated in Australia within 12 months before account activation and be building a technology product; eligibility/stage reclassification at Airwallex's discretion; requires an active Airwallex account and completed KYC.

findings.name: Partner Rewards catalog — free trials and credits for customers
findings.detail: airwallex.com/en-us/rewards: free trials/credits from 25+ partners for Airwallex customers, incl. 6 months free Zendesk, Zegal 1 year free unlimited signing (or 2 months Standard), Pencil first 3 months free, Qwilr $90 free credits (3 months), A2X 20% off first 4 months (code AirwallexA2X), HelloTax 15% off (code AIRWALLEX), Oyster 20% off first 12 months, Amaka 100% free plan/14-day premium trial, Sostocked 30-day trial, Borderless360 up to 150 free shipments, Shipbob $300 shipping credit, Payability $250 sign-on bonus, Kickfurther 50% off first month, Klarna up to 20 bps off standard pricing, JoeLister 30-day trial, Zonguru 7-day trial + 10%, Lawpath up to 35% off, Reviews.io 30%, Linktree 1-month trial, Seller Candy $200 off (LAUNCHCA), TransImpact 60-day free audit.

findings.name: Student / education offers — none public; education-adjacent programs only
findings.detail: No .edu-based free tier, student license, or student discount exists: Airwallex is B2B-only (no personal accounts; a registered business + KYC is required), and /en-us/education and /en-us/students do not exist (404). What does exist (education-adjacent, mostly AU): (1) Airwallex Impact (Nov 2024, Pledge 1%): 1% of company equity pledged to philanthropy (~US$56M at pledge), funding scholarships/training/incubators; 43 University of Melbourne scholarships (up to A$30K each) via an A$3M 2022–2025 partnership (now extended with a further ~A$2M donation, announced 24 Apr 2026); 'discounted Airwallex product for select non-profits' was planned for mid-2025. (2) Latitude 37 (launched 30 Apr 2026): A$100,000 EQUITY-FREE grants to 10+ Australian AI founders under 25 each year, plus Airwallex network access and an SF/Singapore immersion tour; applications opened late May 2026 (window likely closed by Oct 2026 — verify). (3) UNSW Sydney Founders community perk: bonus A$100 credit plus free multi-currency account, no monthly fee — open only to UNSW Founders and requires an active ABN.
findings.eligibility: Scholarships: University of Melbourne IT students (alumni program, not self-serve). Latitude 37: Australian AI founders under 25 (post-grad), grant-based. UNSW perk: UNSW Founders community members with an ABN. No .edu email pathway to a free Airwallex account for individual students.
findings.claim: No self-serve student claim path. University programs are administered by the partner institutions (contact via the universities or sarah.kenny@unimelb.edu.au for UoM); Latitude 37 via its application window; UNSW perk via founders.unsw.edu.au/airwallex.
findings.expiry: UoM 'Opportunity Fund' bursary closed (funding capacity reached); initial 2022–2025 partnership term ended, extended April 2026; Latitude 37 applications opened late May 2026.
findings.gotchas: These are grants/scholarships/partner perks, not product free tiers — a student cannot simply open a free Airwallex business account as an individual; 'discounted product for nonprofits' (mid-2025) applies to non-profits, not students, and no percentage is published.

(2) STARTUP PROGRAM REFRAMED (29 Oct 2025): the global 'Airwallex for Startups' program was relaunched in Singapore with three pillars (stage-appropriate infrastructure, CFO Expert Panel, AI Sandbox) before expanding to the US/UK; the prior version's 'win a $10,000 local-currency business acceleration grant in select regions' was replaced by the current per-stage perk structure (US: $150K fee credits etc.). US program T&C last updated Sept 9, 2026, application window open through 31 Dec 2027. (3) LATITUDE 37 (30 Apr 2026): new A$100K equity-free grant for under-25 Australian AI founders — applications opened late May 2026, likely closed by today's date. (4) UoM partnership extended 24 Apr 2026 with a further ~A$2M; its 'Opportunity Fund' bursary has reached funding capacity and is closed. No Airwallex free offer for students was sunset, because none ever existed as a public product tier.

findings.name: Free developer account + free sandbox/test environment
findings.detail: Signup at app.flutterwave.com/register grants a 'free test environment where you can simulate your preferred transactions' with mock data: 8 success + 7 failure test cards (Mastercard, Visa, Verve, Afrigo) with test OTP/PIN, Access Bank test accounts 0690000031-0690000041 (+blacklisted 0690000036), any mobile-money number with OTP 123456, Capitec test numbers, BVN test values, mock wallets and virtual cards. Transfers default to PENDING and update after 10 minutes (overridable per-transaction with _PMCK / _PMCK_ST_F / DU_{minutes} suffixes). Webhooks: 60s timeout, 3 retries at 30-minute intervals; testing is done by pointing your endpoint at webhook.site (no native in-platform webhook simulator). No fees, volume caps, or paid tiers for the test environment are stated anywhere in the docs.
findings.eligibility: Open signup - no .edu email, no credit card, no startup age/funding cap, and no stated region limit for test mode. KYC verification is only required to enable LIVE transactions; test mode works with unverified accounts. Any OTP in test transactions passes validation (5548/6648 simulate specific failures).
findings.claim: Register at app.flutterwave.com/register, receive test API credentials from the dashboard, and build against the test endpoints using the published mock cards/accounts. Contact support for mock data tied to a specific flow. Go-live requires completing KYC, after which settings can be transferred from the test environment to the live account.
findings.expiry: No expiry, renewal, or sunset date stated for the test environment; it is a standing free capability of every account.
findings.gotchas: The previously reported '30-day test-data retention' could NOT be confirmed in the current docs (testing.md, quickstart.md, api-basics.md) - treat as unverified/possibly outdated. Webhook testing relies on external webhook.site, not a built-in simulator. Checkout test URLs must use localhost:port (127.0.0.1 errors). Transfer integration testing requires IP whitelisting of your calling servers. Test receipts are emailed to your business email, not to customers. Live transactions cost per-transaction fees (e.g. NGN: 2% local = 1.4% + 0.6% platform, 4.8% international; transfers NGN 10/25/50; fees subject to 7.5% VAT), so the free part ends at going live.

findings.name: Free Store / free e-commerce website (Flutterwave Store, SME)
findings.detail: Official Store page FAQ: 'It's totally free to setup a store.' Marketing copy: 'Create a free ecommerce website and start selling worldwide with just a few clicks' and 'Create a free online store that helps you find customers, and accept payments globally.' Included: multiple products & variants, mobile store management, low-stock notifications, delivery-fee charging, customer discounts, multiple payment options, and listing on Flutterwave Market ('Africa's fastest growing marketplace'). No setup charge stated; transaction fees apply per the country pricing schedule.
findings.eligibility: General merchant/SME - no student, .edu, or startup-specific restrictions stated. Region: site localized (e.g. /us/store); no funding/age caps published.
findings.claim: Primary CTA on the page is 'Contact sales' (/us/contact-sales); the standard flow per the page's own steps is: create account, set up store with product photos/specs, share the store link and start selling. Footer also points 'Create a free account' at the contact-sales flow.
findings.expiry: No expiry or limits stated on the free store itself; fee schedule has no published effective date.
findings.gotchas: No product caps, tier limits, or fee schedule disclosed on the store page - live charges follow the per-country pricing (e.g. Ghana: 2.6% local cards, 4.8% international cards; NGN 2%/4.8%). Setup is free but setup may be routed through sales rather than self-serve.

findings.name: No recurring subscription - live fees are purely per-transaction (verified Nigeria & Ghana schedules)
findings.detail: Server-rendered country pricing pages confirm there is no subscription, setup, or seat fee: fees are per-transaction. Nigeria: local collections 2% per transaction (1.4% transaction + 0.6% platform), international 4.8%; transfers to bank/Mobile Money NGN 10 (<=5k), 25 (5,001-50k), 50 (>50k); all transaction fees subject to 7.5% VAT. Ghana: local cards 2.6%, local bank transfer & wallets/mobile money 2%, international cards 4.8% (settled in local currency by default); transfers GHS 10 (bank) or 1.5% (mobile money); pricing excludes VAT; next-day settlement for local payments. No free-transaction allowance (e.g. 'first N free') appears on these pages.
findings.eligibility: Applies to all live accounts; no student/startup discount tiers found on the official pricing pages.
findings.claim: No separate claim - this is the fee baseline: after the free test environment, costs accrue only per live transaction; there is no paid plan to subscribe to.
findings.expiry: No effective dates or sunset notices shown on the pricing pages; figures verified today (2026-10-22).
findings.gotchas: The US pricing page (/us/pricing) is JS-rendered and its fee table could not be extracted via fetch - US rates unverified in this pass. VAT/tax excluded from displayed rates. 'Why you got charged' link now redirects to a separate dispute subdomain (dispute.flutterwave.com).

findings.name: Flutterwave MFB (Meridian Bank) business account - waitlist, unquantified
findings.detail: Flutterwave holds an MFB license (FinCEN-reg Flutterwave Payments LLC, NMLS ID 2391594). The /us/bank page is a waitlist/announcement page: consumer banking inside SendApp ('get your own account number', wallets, Tap-to-Pay coming soon) and business banking ('open a business account', multi-currency, payroll/mass payouts, working-capital loans 'powered by real transaction data'). Compliance: PCI DSS Level 1, SOC 1 & SOC 2.
findings.eligibility: Not student/startup-specific; aimed at consumers and businesses. No amounts, minimum balances, eligibility thresholds, or free-account terms published yet - the page contains zero exact monetary figures.
findings.claim: Join the waitlist at flutterwave.com/us/bank; features not all live yet (Tap-to-Pay 'coming soon', 'coming soon' items present).
findings.expiry: Roadmap/waitlist stage; no published dates or limits.
findings.gotchas: Do not count on a 'free bank account' offer - no fee schedule or free-tier terms are stated; lending/treasury features are described without caps or APRs.

sunset_notes: No distinct startup program, student/education license, or trial-credit offer exists on Flutterwave's official front pages as of 2026-10-22: /startups, /us/students, /us/programs, and /campus-tech all return 404, and the site navigation (Enterprise/SME/Personal/Developers/Resources/Company menus), footer, and blog category pages list no such programs. Historically Flutterwave ran 'Campus Tech' (Nigerian campus promoter program), but it has no current official page - treat as sunset/unavailable unless a new announcement appears. The previously known 'test data retained 30 days' detail and native 'webhook simulation' could not be re-verified: current docs describe webhook testing via external webhook.site and state no data-retention period, so those specifics may have changed or been removed. Trial-credit or education-discount offerings: none found. Verification method: all facts above come from official pages fetched today; the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no third-party/news confirmation of 2025-2026 program sunsets was possible, and the JS-rendered /us/pricing fee table could not be extracted (US rates unverified; Nigeria and Ghana rates verified on server-rendered regional pages).

provider: Paddle (Payments & Fintech Dev Tools) — paddle.com, Merchant of Record billing platform

findings.name: No fixed costs: pay-as-you-go only (no monthly, setup, or migration fees)
findings.detail: Paddle's billing platform charges only 5% + 50¢ per Checkout transaction — 'No monthly fees, migration fees, or hidden extras.' The rate includes payments, checkout, billing, global tax/regulatory compliance in 130+ countries, fraud protection, chargeback handling, and buyer support (Paddle is merchant of record). 'No lock-in periods' and customer data is '100% yours'. Custom/enterprise pricing exists only for high-volume businesses via demo; bespoke pricing available on request for products under $10.
findings.eligibility: Any business that signs up (B2B; no student-specific path). No credit card required to sign up; no region-specific pricing — 5% + 50¢ applies globally.
findings.claim: Self-serve: sign up at login.paddle.com (no demo required). No claim steps, codes, or applications.
findings.expiry: Standing pricing, no expiry or sunset date published as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: Not actually free per-transaction: every revenue dollar costs 5% + 50¢ (and volume pricing for high-growth startups is negotiated, not published). Paid add-on 'Premium Advisory' for large SaaS volumes. No trial credits or trial period on the billing platform itself.

findings.name: Paddle Metrics (ProfitWell Metrics) — 100% free subscription analytics
findings.detail: Standalone subscription-analytics product described as 'completely free' / 'Real-time subscription analytics, 100% free'. Included free: out-of-the-box KPIs (MRR, churn, upgrades/downgrades, LTV, active customers, revenue per customer), health scores, churn alerts, benchmarking against 30,000+ companies, advanced segmentation (cohorts, segments, plan data) enriched with Clearbit and FullContact data, and customizable alerts. Integrates with Stripe, Chargebee, Braintree, Zuora, Recurly, and Paddle's own stack. GDPR and CCPA compliant. No paid tier, add-on, or numeric caps stated on the page.
findings.eligibility: Aimed at 'subscription and SaaS companies' (business, not student-specific). No .edu email or institutional license. No credit-card requirement mentioned.
findings.claim: Click 'Get ProfitWell Metrics free' → signup at www2.profitwell.com/signup/start. For Paddle customers it integrates 'one click'. Live demo link also offered.
findings.expiry: Presented as permanently free; no trial expiry, renewal date, or sunset stated as of 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: Free product is analytics only — it does not waive Paddle billing fees or provide a free tier of the billing platform. No seat/API/data-retention caps published. Data is enriched via third parties (Clearbit, FullContact) — review privacy implications. Sign-up lives on profitwell.com (Paddle's acquired ProfitWell brand), not paddle.com.

findings.name: Developer sandbox — free test/evaluation environment (no live billing, no payment card in the flow)
findings.detail: Separate sandbox account for testing and evaluation of the Paddle API/dashboard: point code at https://sandbox-api.paddle.com, sandbox API keys contain '_sdbx', client-side tokens prefixed 'test_'. Test cards only (e.g. 4242 4242 4242 4242; sandbox rejects real card numbers, live rejects test cards). Webhook delivery limited to 3 attempts within ~2 minutes (vs up to 60 in live). Refund adjustments auto-approve every 10 minutes; cancellation flows work; checkout shows a 'Test Mode' watermark. No payouts or monthly statements in sandbox; credentials, products, prices, and customers are not shared with a live account.
findings.eligibility: Any developer; signup asks only 'personal and business details' — no payment method step and no .edu/institutional requirement. Sandbox sign-up is separate from a live account (you need one even if you already have a live account).
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://sandbox-vendors.paddle.com/signup, 2) enter personal/business details, 3) click Continue. Docs: developer.paddle.com/sdks/sandbox.md; quickstart mentions sandbox tokens start with 'test_'.
findings.expiry: Standing developer tooling; no expiry or sunset stated. 'Free' is inferred (no charge/payment step in the documented signup flow) — the page does not print the word 'free'; go-live later requires a separate live account where 5% + 50¢ applies.
findings.gotchas: Mixing sandbox and live credentials against the wrong API endpoint returns 'forbidden'. Sandbox email delivery is limited to addresses on your registered domain. Payment Recovery and Term Optimization work only on live accounts. No refunds/payouts in sandbox, so it cannot validate real money movement.

findings.name: Paddle for Startups — solutions positioning, no published startup discount or credits
findings.detail: The 'Paddle for Startups' page (solutions/startups, 'Billing Infrastructure for Startups') is marketing/solutions content, not a fee program. It confirms the standard 5% + 50¢ all-in rate vs '~7% and above' for assembling separate PSPs, 'no hidden fees, no paying for add-ons', and 'Volume pricing available for high growth startups' (negotiated via demo/enterprise path — amounts unpublished). Trusted-by examples: n8n, DataforSEO, Runna. No trial credits, no startup-only fee waiver, no funding-cap or age cap, no application form.
findings.eligibility: Startups of any age/funding level can simply sign up at the standard rate; volume pricing requires a booked demo. No credit card, .edu, or region requirements.
findings.claim: Standard rate: self-serve sign-up at login.paddle.com. Volume pricing: 'Book a demo' (/demo). No application or discount code mechanism described.
findings.expiry: No program expiry; 'volume pricing' terms are opaque, set per deal.
findings.gotchas: 'Startup program' here ≠ fee discount: a startup with high volume pays negotiated custom pricing, not a published discount. Don't assume startup status changes the default 5% + 50¢.

Paddle's free offers that do exist are the two standalone items above (free Metrics, free sandbox) plus zero fixed fees.

findings.claim: Not claimable. Nearest free items: Metrics (profitwell.com signup) and developer sandbox (sandbox-vendors.paddle.com signup).

findings.gotchas: Paddle is a B2B merchant-of-record platform for businesses selling software/digital goods; an individual student building a side project would be priced like any other business (5% + 50¢, no fixed fees). Do not confuse paddle.com with other 'Paddle' brands.

sunset_notes: No student/startup/education program was found that closed or changed in 2025-2026 — because none is published. Observed structural changes instead: (1) Paddle's developer docs moved from docs.paddle.com to developer.paddle.com (301 redirect, current as of 2026-10-22); sandbox signup is at sandbox-vendors.paddle.com with sandbox-api.paddle.com as endpoint. (2) The free analytics product remains branded 'ProfitWell Metrics' under Paddle, with sign-up still on profitwell.com. (3) WebSearch for 2025-2026 news was unavailable in this session (shared session search budget exhausted), so this verification relied exclusively on the official pages read today: paddle.com/pricing, paddle.com (homepage nav), paddle.com/solutions/startups, paddle.com/profitwell-metrics, developer.paddle.com (llms.txt, get-started/quickstart.md, sdks/sandbox.md, and the sandbox-account page). All 'high' confidence items were read from official pages on 2026-10-22. Nothing on those pages indicates a sunset date for the free Metrics product, the sandbox, or the no-fixed-fee pricing model.

provider: Microsoft (Azure / Microsoft for Students, Microsoft for Startups, Dev Tools for Teaching)

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit + free monthly service allowances
findings.detail: Verified today on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students: $100 Azure credit usable on most Azure products within 12 months; free monthly amounts on 20+ popular services for 12 months (new customers only), e.g. 750 hrs B1s/burstable VMs (Linux & Windows), 750 hrs PostgreSQL/MySQL Flexible Server B1MS + 32 GB storage + 32 GB backup, 720 vCore-hrs Azure SQL Managed Instance, 1 Azure Container Registry (Standard, 100 GB), 5,000 transactions of Azure Vision in Foundry Tools; free monthly amounts on 65+ always-free services with no time limit, e.g. Azure Functions 1M requests/mo, App Service 10 web/API apps + 1 GB storage, Cosmos DB 1,000 RU/s + 25 GB, AKS cluster management free (node charges apply), API Management 1M calls/mo (Consumption), AI Search 50 MB storage / 10,000 docs / 3 indexes, Static Web Apps 100 GB bandwidth, Logic Apps 4,000 built-in actions, DevOps 5 users, IoT Hub 8,000 msgs/day, plus Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Foundry model access. After the 12 months or credit exhaustion, Microsoft emails you to choose pay-as-you-go or have the subscription disabled; if you convert, free monthly amounts continue.
findings.eligibility: Full-time university students only; sign up with a school (.edu) email; one account per person; NO credit card required (explicitly stated on the page). No minimum age stated on the page, but the Azure-for-Students credit offer in the GitHub pack is 18+ (younger students get limited access). No country list published on the page (US-locale content).
findings.claim: 1) Go to azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students, click 'Start free' (go.microsoft.com/fwlink link id 2062405). 2) Sign up with your school email; verification is via the school email — no card. 3) The $100 credit and free monthly allowances are granted immediately. 4) After account creation, download free dev tools from the Azure Education Hub. Renew yearly while enrolled.
findings.expiry: Credit usable within 12 months of account creation; free monthly allowances: 12 months for the 'popular services' set, ongoing (no limit) for the 65+ always-free set. Subscription renewable annually while still a full-time student. No sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: The $100 credit is a cap, not cash; once exhausted you must pay unless you stay within the free-allowance limits. Free-tier caps (e.g., VMs 750 hrs, not 730) are hard limits — overage is billed. Data egress, storage over 32 GB on DBs, and premium-tier usage are not covered. You must convert to pay-as-you-go to keep running after credit expiry. The AI free allowances are rebranded under Microsoft Foundry ('Foundry Tools'/'Control Plane') in 2025-2026 — same services, new names. One account per person; no stacking with the Azure Free account's $200.

findings.name: Azure Free Account (standard tier, non-student) — $200 credit / 30 days + 12-month free services
findings.detail: Verified today on azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free: $200 credit usable on Azure services within 30 days (one per new customer; unused credit stays valid for the full 30 days), free monthly amounts on 20+ popular services for 12 months, and 65+ always-free services ongoing (same lists as the student page: 750 hrs VMs, 1M Functions requests, Cosmos DB 1000 RU/s + 25 GB, etc.). A phone number plus credit/debit card (non-prepaid; credit cards only in HK and Brazil) is required at signup, with a temporary ~$1 authorization that is reversed.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only; one free account with the $200 credit per person. Credit card required (unlike the student track). No funding or company requirements — open to individuals.
findings.claim: 1) Go to azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free, 'Get started'. 2) Sign in with a Microsoft or GitHub account. 3) Provide phone number + credit/debit card for identity verification. 4) $200 credit activates immediately; 12-month free service amounts apply to new-customer services.
findings.expiry: Credit: 30 days from account creation. 20+ free monthly amounts: 12 months (new customers). 65+ always-free services: ongoing. After expiry, Microsoft emails you; if you don't convert to pay-as-you-go, the account and services are disabled.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required here (not for students). After 30 days the $200 lapses; only the free monthly allowances survive. The $25/75-day extension that older guides mention is no longer advertised on the current page. Spending protection applies only while on the free account; convert to PAYG and all usage is billed.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — single-path program, $200 immediate credits, up to $150,000 via milestones (current 2026 structure)
findings.detail: Verified today on learn.microsoft.com (page updated 2026-08-05; June 2, 2026 Microsoft blog 'a clearer path from AI development to enterprise growth'): startups apply directly at startups.microsoft.com and immediately get up to $200 in Startup credits (sign up for Azure + verify identity with a personal LinkedIn account; business accounts rejected at this step). Credits grow via automatic milestones: $5,000 after business verification (registered legal entity); $25,000 after 5+ active Azure workloads sustained ~60 days (one-time 2-year credit-use extension granted at this tier); $50,000 at 7+ workloads; $150,000 at 10+ workloads AND ~$3,000/month sustained usage. You can skip tiers; a 10-character investor referral code (from a Microsoft for Startups Investor Network VC/accelerator/partner university) unlocks higher tiers faster, a dedicated Microsoft point of contact, and extra credits. Includes Azure AI/Foundry model access, Marketplace/co-sell benefits, expert guidance.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage B2B software startups: pre-seed through Series B (no Series C funding or later), privately held for-profit, building a software product you own, HQ in a country where Azure is available; NOT more than $350,000 lifetime free Azure credits; no educational institutions/government/consultancies; no crypto mining. Apply with a personal consumer email (school/work emails rejected). Decisions typically within 3 business days.
findings.claim: 1) Go to https://startups.microsoft.com, click 'Get started now'. 2) Sign in with a personal Microsoft account (create if needed). 3) Choose path: enter your 10-character investor referral code, or 'Continue without a code'. 4) Verify with LinkedIn to 'Unlock $200 in Azure credits', then complete the 3-step Azure account setup (profile, billing address, payment info). 5) Credits appear in the MFS portal / Azure portal (joins on or after May 29, 2026 activate through the Azure portal; earlier joins used the MFS portal).
findings.expiry: Credits usable over the program period; at the $25K milestone you receive a one-time 2-year extension on using credits. Higher tiers require sustained ~60-day workload usage (each workload must stay above $1 spend for all 60 days; the clock starts once the required number of workloads each have >=$1 spend). No fixed sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: A credit cap, not cash: money is only 'free' while inside the ceiling, and exceeding it moves you to pay-as-you-go. Payment info/card is required at activation (won't be charged unless you exceed credits and stay on PAYG). Milestone credits are conditional on real sustained usage, not activation — many startups stop at $5K. School/edu emails are explicitly rejected for signup (contrast with the student program). The $150K figures on the still-live Founders Hub signup page and the $10K/$350K caps reflect different (legacy vs current) rules — the Learn program docs are authoritative. Pegasus (invitation-only) program continues separately.

findings.name: Azure for Startups self-service credits — $1,000 (90 days) + up to $4,000 after business verification
findings.detail: Listed on the current Azure for Students page (fetched today) as a separate sign-up tier: $1,000 instant Azure credit valid 90 days, plus up to $4,000 more that remain available for 180 days after business verification. This is the self-serve track of the July 2025 MFS restructure (replacing the old $150K/$10K Founders tiers for un-backed startups), which Microsoft further streamlined in 2026 into the milestone model ($200 start -> $5K verified -> $25K/$50K/$150K milestones).
findings.eligibility: Early-stage startups without investor backing, new to Azure; credit card required for identity verification (only charged if you move to pay-as-you-go beyond credits). Business verification = registered legal entity. Same MFS constraints apply (for-profit, software product, HQ in an Azure-available country, funding/credit caps per current program docs: no Series C+, <=$350K lifetime free Azure credits).
findings.claim: Sign up for the 'Azure for Startups' tier from azure.microsoft.com (offered alongside the students and free accounts), or apply at startups.microsoft.com and complete business verification to unlock the additional $4,000. Identity-verification card required.
findings.expiry: Base $1,000 credit: 90 days from signup. Additional $4,000: available for 180 days after business verification. Existing credits from before the July 2025 program change remained valid until their original expiry.
findings.gotchas: No dedicated support on the self-serve track (self-service only) — the dedicated-Microsoft-POC/support path requires an Investor Network referral. Card required (unlike the student tier). The $4,000 is gated on actually completing business verification within the window. Note the 2026 milestone docs show some tiers now framed as $200/$5,000 gates, so the $1K/$4K structure coexists with the milestone model — check which offer is presented at signup.

findings.name: Azure Dev Tools for Teaching / Visual Studio Academic Program — free education licenses (Visual Studio, SQL Server, Windows Server, Visio, Office, GitHub benefits)
findings.detail: Verified today via the Azure for Students page, which states that after creating the student account you 'download free dev tools from the Azure Education Hub' through the Azure Dev Tools for Teaching program. The page's DFTT bundle lists: Visual Studio (Community, for Mac, plus Agents/Remote Tools), Azure DevOps Server, R Client/Server, SQL Server Developer/Mobile Report Publisher/Standard, System Center, Visio Professional, Windows Server, Skype for Business Server. Schools (accredited institutions) get the teaching licenses; students get the student-side dev licenses for non-commercial, educational use while enrolled.
findings.eligibility: Accredited educational institutions (faculty) and enrolled students; claimed through school-issued email / institutional account for the teaching side; the student side rides on the verified Azure for Students account. Non-commercial educational use only.
findings.claim: 1) Verify with your school email on the Azure for Students page (no card). 2) After account creation, open the Azure Education Hub linked there and download the dev-tool licenses. 3) Institutions obtain teaching kits via the Microsoft Academic Program (historically partner.microsoft.com/academic-program; that page returned 403 to today's fetch).
findings.expiry: Licenses last while you remain an enrolled student / faculty member; renewed yearly with the student subscription. No fixed sunset.
findings.gotchas: Dev-tools licenses are non-commercial — shipping a paid product with them breaches terms. The exact SKU list on the partner.microsoft.com DFTT page couldn't be fetched (403), so treat the granular list as 'per the students page snapshot today'. Office/M365 is generally delivered through the school's campus license (M365 Education) rather than a personal free download.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack (Microsoft-subsidized offers inside the pack: $100 Azure credit, GitHub Pro, Copilot, Codespaces)
findings.detail: Verified today on github.com/education: verified students (13+, enrolled in a degree/diploma-granting program, school email or dated proof of enrollment) get free GitHub Pro (unlimited private repos, 3,000 Actions minutes/mo, 180 Codespaces hours/mo, 2 GB Packages storage), free GitHub Copilot for Students (300 premium requests/mo class allowance per current plan), plus 80+ partner offers. Microsoft's own offers inside the pack: $100 Azure credit (18+; separate limited access for 13-17), and a 'Microsoft Azure (for ages 13-17)' offer; partner offers include JetBrains, Heroku $13/mo x 24 months, MongoDB $50, domains. Student validation lasts 2 years, then revalidation required. Offers can't be reset by re-verifying; partner terms can limit age/country.
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students 13+ with school-issued email or enrollment proof; separate validation from the .edu-only Azure for Students program (documents accepted: ID, transcript, class schedule, verification letter). No credit card for the GitHub side; some partner offers require a card on their own site.
findings.claim: 1) Go to github.com/education/students (or education.github.com/pack). 2) Start an application under Education benefits settings in your GitHub profile. 3) Submit proof of enrollment; approval lands in the GitHub Education portal. 4) Claim Microsoft offers (Azure $100 credit 18+, etc.) from the pack page.
findings.expiry: Valid while student status holds (revalidated every 2 years; the pack is typically held until end of 4th year of study). Individual partner offers have their own durations (e.g., Heroku 24 months, GitKraken 6 months + 80% off).
findings.gotchas: Offers are partner-controlled and change or drop out (see changelog: DigitalOcean's $200 credit sunset July 31, 2026; Bump.sh offer ended Dec 9, 2025; 1Password expanded to 2 years in Oct 2026). The $100 Azure credit is the SAME offer as Azure for Students (claim one, not both — one per person). Copilot student entitlements 'are evolving in 2026' per the official discussion; check the live allowance on activation. This is a GitHub program — included here because the Microsoft offers (Azure credit, and DFTT-tied tooling) flow through it.

sunset_notes: MAJOR 2025-2026 CHANGES (all verified via official pages/articles fetched today): (1) Microsoft for Startups: the old multi-tier Founders program (up to $150K for funded/AI startups, $10K base tier) was abruptly retired effective July 1, 2025 (June 27, 2025 memo) and replaced with a two-track system: an Investor Network track ($100,000+ credits, requires referral from affiliated VCs/accelerators/universities) and a self-serve track ($1,000 for 90 days + $4,000 after business verification = up to $5,000, no dedicated support). (2) The program was re-restructured again in 2026 (single application path; Learn docs updated May 27, 2026 and Aug 5, 2026; Microsoft blog June 2, 2026): all startups now apply directly, start with up to $200 in credits after personal LinkedIn verification, and unlock up to $150,000 over time via automatic milestones ($5K verified -> $25K at 5 workloads -> $50K at 7 -> $150K at 10+ workloads + ~$3K/mo usage); activation moved to the Azure portal for joins on/after May 29, 2026. (3) The still-live Founders Hub signup page (foundershub.startups.microsoft.com) shows legacy marketing ('up to $150,000', 'no funding required', $10K prior-credit cap, 'not Series D+') that conflicts with the current Learn docs (no Series C+, $350K lifetime free-credit cap) — treat Learn as authoritative. (4) The Pegasus invitation-only program was explicitly NOT changed. (5) Azure AI services were rebranded under Microsoft Foundry (2025-2026): the free allowances are now described as 'Foundry Tools' / 'Foundry Control Plane' (Speech, Vision, Translator, Content Safety, Document Intelligence) — same limits, new names; old guides citing 'Azure AI Studio/Cognitive Services' free tiers may be stale. (6) GitHub Student Developer Pack sunsets 2025-2026: DigitalOcean $200 student credit ended after July 31, 2026; Bump.sh offer removed Dec 9, 2025; Thinkful offer paused Oct 25, 2025; GitKraken offer changed to 6 months + 80% discount; 1Password offer extended to 2 years (Oct 2026). (7) Azure for Students core terms ($100/12 months, no credit card) are UNCHANGED on the current page — no 2025-2026 reduction found; no sunset dates published. (8) The standard Azure Free account no longer advertises the former $25/75-day extension; current page shows only $200/30 days + 12-month service allowances. Minor: the standard free account's 12-month free-service count is now phrased as '20+ popular services' / '65+ always-free services' rather than the older '55 services for 12 months' wording.

findings.name: Square Sandbox (free test environment)
findings.detail: The Square developer docs describe the Sandbox as 'a free, isolated server environment' at base URL https://connect.squareupsandbox.com, provisioned per application in the Developer Console. The page states: 'Use of the Sandbox environment is free of charge' and you can make 'an unlimited number of free Sandbox API calls.' Cards are never charged ('payments are never actually processed by a live bank'), and the Sandbox 'doesn't accept real credit cards or payment methods' — you use designated test card numbers/tokens. Functional limits: up to 10 additional test accounts beyond the default; Square hardware (POS terminals) not usable; Square for Restaurants, POS, Invoices, Snippets, Sites and Reader SDK are unsupported in the Sandbox; the Sandbox dashboard lacks receipts, refunds issuance, email, and banking features; real PII must not be stored in Sandbox.
findings.eligibility: Open to any Square developer: create a free Square account, register an app in the Developer Console, and the Sandbox is provisioned for that app. No .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, and no credit card required. Region: docs are US-oriented (developer.squareup.com); sandbox availability not region-gated in the docs I read.
findings.claim: Sign up at squareup.com, create a Square account and an app in the Developer Console (developer.squareup.com), then use the sandbox base URL (connect.squareupsandbox.com) with test card values — no credit card or live seller account needed; sandbox API calls are free and unlimited.
findings.expiry: No expiration, time limit, or sunset date is documented for Sandbox access as of 2026-10-22; 'unlimited free Sandbox API calls' per the docs.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free gotcha: the Sandbox is permanently free, but moving to production (live mode) is NOT free — in live mode cards are actually charged by a live bank and Square's pay-per-transaction processing fees apply (context: ~2.9% + 30c per card via the payments APIs; ACH per transfer). No hardware in Sandbox; several product lines unsupported; must not store real PII; test disputes/sandbox entities are invisible in the Developer Console or Dashboard.

findings.name: Free developer access — no monthly/annual developer fees, no per-API-call fee advertised (pay-per-transaction live model)
findings.detail: Square's developer platform has no advertised monthly/annual developer subscription and no per-API-call charge. The Square pricing page leads with 'Your complete business toolkit, starting at $0' and 'Only pay when you take a payment.' The developer landing page (developer.squareup.com) and docs hub make no cost claim beyond that; the Get Started flow is 'Create an account and make your first Square API call in minutes.' No trial credits, no prepaid credit pool, and no developer-tier free-usage bucket exist on any page I could read (2025-2026 changes could not be checked via search — search budget exhausted this session).
findings.eligibility: Open to all developers/merchants who sign up at squareup.com (developer signup routes to app.squareup.com/signup?v=developers). No .edu requirement, no startup age or funding cap, no credit card required for account or app creation. Not a student-only or startup-only offer; it is the default model for everyone.
findings.claim: Sign up free at squareup.com, create an app in the Developer Console, build and test in the free Sandbox; going live costs only standard per-transaction processing fees on payments you take (context: 2.9% + 30c online card; ACH per transfer) — no platform fee and no card required to sign up.
findings.expiry: No expiry; standing pricing model as displayed on 2026-10-22. Exact live-mode rates were not numerically confirmed on the page (rates render via JavaScript); the 2.9% + 30c figure is from task context, not re-verified today.
findings.gotchas: The $0 entry point covers software/toolkit ('Square Free' plan: POS app, online site, item library, invoicing, booking, checking & savings accounts, $0/mo); processing fees on live payments are separate and are the real cost. 'Plus' plan is a paid tier with 'lower processing fees' and a rendered 'Try free for N days' trial button (day count not rendered in the page text) — a trial, not a free tier.

findings.name: Square 'Free' plan (the $0 software plan) — not student/startup-specific
findings.detail: On squareup.com/us/en/pricing, 'Square Free' starts at $0 and includes: 'POS app for any payment', 'Online site' (ordering profile, basic website, or booking site), 'Item library', 'Invoicing', 'Booking', and 'Checking and savings accounts'. Page states 'Only pay when you take a payment' and 'No hidden fees or locked-in contracts. Cancel or switch anytime.' A second specific number on the page: for Plus text marketing, 'The first 500 texts are free, then pay 3¢ per text.'
findings.eligibility: Any business/seller; no .edu email, no startup age/funding cap, no credit-card requirement stated for the free plan itself. Available generally, not a student or startup program.
findings.claim: Sign up for Square at no monthly cost and use the included POS app, online site, invoicing, booking, and banking features for $0/mo; you only pay per-transaction processing fees when you take payments.
findings.expiry: No stated end date; 'Cancel or switch anytime' per the page, so no lock-in. Verified 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: This is a merchant-softwar plan, not a developer tier; 'free' excludes card/ACH processing fees on live payments, which are the main cost of the platform. The paid 'Plus' tier can undercut Free on processing rates but is a subscription — do not conflate the $0 plan with Plus's 'lower processing fees' perk.

findings.name: Square App Partner Program — free open base tier; selective enhanced tier (no startup-only perks found)
findings.detail: The App Partner program (squareup.com/us/en/partnerships/app-partner) lets developers build and publish on the Square App Marketplace ('3.4 million views' cited). Base participation appears free and open: 'Don't wait on us to get started — dive into building, launch your integration, and reach out once it's live.' Even a declined enhanced-tier application leaves you free to 'build with our open platform.' The enhanced tier requires a form (personal/company details, Square App ID, industry, target markets AU/CA/FR/IE/JP/GB/ES/US, customer counts, app description) and is explicitly selective. Benefits of the enhanced tier: dedicated partner manager, 'profit-share eligibility' ('Create new revenue streams by sharing in profit generated through the app partnership' — no percentages, minimums, or fee structure disclosed), and co-marketing/sales enablement. No startup-only discounts, grants, or accelerated review appear anywhere on the page.
findings.eligibility: Open base tier: any developer who registers an app; no .edu email, no startup age or funding cap, no credit card required. Enhanced tier: application-based and selective, favoring 'highest impact' apps with 'strong enough demand'; target markets limited to AU, CA, FR, IE, JP, GB, ES, US.
findings.claim: Build and publish your Square app for free (no fee to list), then apply via the app-partner form for the enhanced tier with a dedicated partner manager and profit-share eligibility.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated for base participation; enhanced-tier terms are individually negotiated. Verified 2026-10-22.
findings.gotchas: 'Profit-share eligibility' is an opportunity, not a guarantee, with no disclosed percentages or fees — do not treat it as free money. The program is selective; rejection from the enhanced tier does not revoke free access to the open platform. No student-specific or startup-specific benefit was found on the page or the partnerships hub.

sunset_notes: No student- or startup-specific free offer exists for Square Developer as of 2026-10-22: no .edu education license, no startup credit pool, no trial credits, and no startup age/funding-capped program were found on developer.squareup.com, the Square pricing page, or the partnerships hub (us/en/partnerships lists only App Partner and Developer Platform tracks; no education, reseller, or startup programs). Square's free offers are model-based and open to everyone (free Sandbox; no developer subscription; $0 'Square Free' software plan; free app-marketplace base tier), so nothing appears to have been sunset in 2025-2026 under a student/startup name. Caveats: (1) WebSearch was unavailable for this session (budget exhausted), so 2025-2026 change announcements (e.g., news of rate changes like the 2.9%+30c figure, which the pricing page renders via JS and could not be numerically re-confirmed) could not be independently checked; rate-level claims are carried from task context, not re-verified today. (2) Square Plus carries a 'Try free for N days' trial button whose day count is a template variable and did not render — a trial, not a free tier, and not student/startup-scoped.

provider: Adobe Creative Cloud for Students (Education & Student Programs)

findings.name: Adobe Express Free Plan
findings.detail: Free tier of Adobe Express, no expiration, no credit card required. Includes 100,000+ templates, 1M+ royalty-free Adobe Stock assets, 4,000+ fonts, standard photo/video/document editing, 5 GB cloud storage, 10-day version history, 10 PDF Quick Actions/month, videos up to 30 min, and limited free generative AI: 'free daily generations' for insert/remove objects, 5 lifetime uses of Generate Presentations, and 2 lifetime uses of 5-second video generation. Export limited to JPEG/PNG/PDF/GIF/PPT (no transparent-background PNG). Paid Premium is US$9.99/mo (30-day free trial) with 250 monthly generative credits, 100 GB storage, 4K export, 3 accounts per social network.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a free Adobe account; no .edu email, no student status, no credit card required. Available worldwide (page shown in US locale; region-specific bundles exist, e.g., Airtel India, IM3 Indonesia). K-12 US educators can create free classroom accounts via Google Workspace for Education.
findings.claim: 1) Go to adobe.com/express 2) Sign up with a free Adobe account (email or social sign-in) 3) Use Express web/app free; do not select the Premium plan. Students may already have free Express Premium via school .edu login (per page FAQ).
findings.expiry: No expiry; free tier has no time limit. Trial of Premium is 30 days; trial converts to paid (US$9.99/mo) unless cancelled.
findings.gotchas: Generative AI on the free tier is heavily capped (lifetime uses, not monthly) and 'free daily generations' are standard-model only; 250 monthly Firefly credits require the US$9.99/mo Premium plan. Free tier has no 4K export, no transparent PNGs, 5 GB storage cap.

findings.name: Student Spaces in Acrobat (AI study tools, free)
findings.detail: Adobe's free AI study feature: Student Spaces turns notes into flashcards and quizzes ('an AI study buddy'). The official landing page states 'Get started for free'. Listed on Adobe's education page among 'several free tools students can start using right away', alongside Adobe Express and Firefly. No Creative Cloud subscription is required.
findings.eligibility: Any student with a free Adobe account; no .edu email requirement stated on the page. No credit card required.
findings.claim: 1) Sign in at acrobat.adobe.com/studyspace/collection/create-new-project (link from adobe.com/education.html) 2) Upload notes or a document 3) Generate flashcards/quizzes in the free Student Spaces project.
findings.expiry: Ongoing, no published sunset date. Some advanced Acrobat features remain in paid Acrobat Studio/Pro plans; Student Spaces itself is free to start.
findings.gotchas: Landing page is thin on detail (title/headline only); confirm the full feature set (e.g., AI Assistant quotas, PDF import limits) in-app. Adobe's page copy ties it to Acrobat, so it may nudge toward paid Acrobat plans for heavy document workflows.

findings.name: 7-day free trial of Creative Cloud Pro (incl. Firefly)
findings.detail: Full 7-day trial of Creative Cloud Pro: 20+ apps (Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, After Effects, Lightroom, Acrobat, Firefly, Express, Fresco) on desktop and iPad. Payment method required at signup but you are not charged until the trial ends; billing converts automatically to Creative Cloud Pro on Day 8 (regular US$69.99/mo; promo US$34.99/mo for first 3 months, new subscribers). A 14-day money-back window after conversion allows cancellation for a full refund. Desktop suite and iPad app are downloadable during the trial; the trial is NOT available on phones.
findings.eligibility: Any Adobe account holder; only ONE 7-day CC Pro trial per person (trial already used = not eligible). Student/teacher front: eligible students can 'start a 7-day free trial' of the student plan before the paid student subscription (adobe.com/education/students/creativecloud.html).
findings.claim: 1) Go to adobe.com/creativecloud/free-trial.html (or the CC plans page) 2) Create/sign in to an Adobe account 3) Enter payment details (no charge until Day 8) 4) Download/install apps 5) To avoid paying: cancel via account page > Manage Plans > Cancel Plan within 7 days; if you miss the window you have 14 days post-trial to cancel for a full refund.
findings.expiry: Trial = 7 days, one-time only; refund window = 14 days after trial ends. If not cancelled, plan auto-renews monthly at US$69.99/mo (or promo US$34.99/mo x3 then $69.99).
findings.gotchas: Free-trial vs free-tier trap: this is a trial, not a free plan - a card/payment method is required on file and automatic billing starts on Day 8. One trial per person lifetime. Trial unavailable on phones (desktop/iPad only).

findings.name: Creative Cloud Pro for Students & Teachers (discount, not free) - verified at 71% (US) / 75% (EU)
findings.detail: The discounted education plan: US$19.99/mo for the first year, then US$39.99/mo as long as eligibility continues ('Save 71%' vs US$69.99/mo list). EU listing shows 75% off: 19.66 EUR/mo incl. VAT (first year, annual-billed-monthly) vs 79.30 EUR/mo list; Israeli listing shows NIS 88.99/mo year 1, NIS 179.99/mo year 2+. Includes 20+ apps, unlimited standard generative AI features (e.g., Generative Fill), 4,000 monthly generative credits for premium AI video/audio (e.g., Text-to-Video), Firefly Boards (unlimited), non-Adobe models in Firefly (Adobe, Google, OpenAI), Express Premium, Frame.io, 100 GB cloud storage. A 7-day free trial of the student plan is available first. Note: the '74% off' figure in the brief is not what current pages show - US says 71%, EU says 75%.
findings.eligibility: Students: 13+, currently enrolled at an accredited school/college/university or qualified online program; teachers: educators/staff at an accredited institution. Adobe verifies status and may request school-issued email, student/teacher ID, enrollment document, transcript, class schedule, pay slip, or offer letter from the current academic year. Purchase must be made by someone 18+ with a credit card. Renewal requires continuing eligibility (annual re-verification); year-2+ price doubles (US$19.99 -> US$39.99/mo).
findings.claim: 1) adobe.com/education/students/creativecloud.html 2) Select Creative Cloud Pro for Students, start 7-day trial or buy 3) Verify eligibility with school email/ID 4) If your school has a campus license, skip this entirely and use the institutional offer (see next finding). One subscription: sign-in on 2 computers, active use on 1.
findings.expiry: Discount lasts as long as eligibility is verified; price rises after year 1 (US$19.99 -> US$39.99/mo). Renewal re-verification required each year.
findings.gotchas: This is a paid discount, not free - 'free access' only via school institutional licensing. Year-1 vs year-2 pricing gap is the biggest trap. Requires age 18+ to pay; verification can be requested AFTER purchase. CC required for the full app suite; 100 GB storage does not cover heavy video projects (eject/egress: no public data-egress fees, but storage overage forces pay-as-you-go add-ons).

findings.name: Institutional / campus-wide Creative Cloud licensing (free for students at partner schools)
findings.detail: Many universities and K-12 districts purchase 'Creative Cloud for education institutions' (20+ apps, plan=edu_inst; pricing by phone/institutional sales). At partner schools, students and faculty typically get the full suite at no personal cost by logging in with their school account; the education page states 'some schools provide free access to the full Creative Cloud suite' and directs students to their IT department. K-12 and higher-ed dedicated pages exist (/education/k12.html, /education/higher-ed.html); higher-ed page emphasizes FERPA/COPPA compliance and 'no training on student content'.
findings.eligibility: Current students/faculty at institutions that hold an Adobe institutional or K-12 agreement (varies by country and school). Usually requires a school email/SSO; no personal credit card. No age/funding caps - it's per-institution, not per-startup.
findings.claim: 1) Check your school's portal / IT department / Adobe Admin Console login link 2) Sign in with your institution-issued Adobe account 3) Download CC apps - no purchase, no trial needed. If your school has no deal, fall back to the student discount plan above.
findings.expiry: Valid for as long as you are enrolled/employed at the institution; access ends at graduation/resignation. No per-student sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Availability is entirely school-dependent and varies widely - no self-serve redemption steps are published; institutional pricing is phone-only (US 888-649-2990). Students at schools without a deal must pay the discounted plan themselves.

findings.name: Startup program: none found
findings.detail: Adobe has no startup program, startup credits, or startup discount as of the verified pages: adobe.com/startups.html and adobe.com/small-business.html are 404, and adobe.com/business.html explicitly has no 'Startups' category - only Business, Students & Teachers, Home & Personal, Government, Nonprofits. A startup's only Adobe offers are the standard 7-day CC Pro trial, team plans (10-or-fewer-license 'small business' tier; e.g., Acrobat Pro teams US$28.98/mo annual-billed-monthly with free trial), and 30-day Adobe Stock trials.
findings.eligibility: No startup-specific eligibility (no company-age or funding cap exists because there is no program). General Adobe terms apply; team plans need a minimum of 1-2 licenses and a paying account.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim - use the standard 7-day trial (one per person) and team plans; nonprofit/government categories exist but startup does not.
findings.expiry: N/A (no program). Team-plan trials are 14 days with a cancellation fee of half the remaining annual commitment if cancelled 14 days after the trial.
findings.gotchas: Don't assume a 'Adobe for Startups' exists from third-party blogs; the official pages show no such front. Cancellation fee clause applies to team plans.

sunset_notes: 1) WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted), so all verification was done via direct WebFetch of official adobe.com pages (fetched today, 2026-10-22); helpx.adobe.com returned 403. 2) The brief's '74% off CC Pro' does not match current pages: US plan page says 71% off (US$19.99/mo yr 1, then US$39.99/mo) and the EU education page says 75% off (EUR 19.66/mo incl. VAT first year vs 79.30 EUR/mo list). 3) Firefly free tier: could not verify a standalone free Firefly plan or free monthly generative credits - adobe.com/firefly/pricing.html and /firefly.html are 404 and firefly.adobe.com/pricing renders no text content. Paid Firefly plans start at US$9.99/mo (2,000 credits) per the CC plans page; free AI generation is currently available through the Adobe Express free tier (daily generations + lifetime uses) rather than a confirmed standalone Firefly free credit pool. The Firefly homepage now markets '30+ AI models in one place' (Adobe + Google + OpenAI), indicating the 2025-2026 shift toward Firefly as a multi-model hub. 4) No startup program exists (checked 2026-10-22); nothing appears to have been sunset recently on that front - it simply was not advertised. 5) No sunset/expiry dates published for Express Free or Student Spaces; both are ongoing with no CC requirement.

findings.name: Free sandbox & test mode (no credit card)
findings.detail: Free isolated test environments: simulated payments, no real money movement, no card-network processing. Every Stripe account includes a test mode sandbox (shares some settings with live mode; cannot be deleted) plus up to 5 general sandboxes (fully isolated settings/data; recommended for new integrations; supports API v1 and v2 - test mode only supports v1 + partial v2). Stripe CLI can provision an anonymous sandbox with working API keys, no account registration required (`npm i -g @stripe/cli`, `stripe sandbox create`). No fees, no stated limits on test transactions. IC+ pricing cannot be tested in any sandbox. Docs, API reference and libraries are free.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, worldwide. No .edu email, no startup age/funding requirement, no credit card (anonymous CLI sandbox needs no Stripe account at all), no regional limit.
findings.claim: 1) Create a free Stripe account, 2) toggle test mode in the Dashboard (or create a general sandbox under the account picker), or 3) use Stripe CLI: `stripe sandbox create` for an anonymous sandbox.
findings.expiry: None - indefinite, no expiration; sandboxes can be created/deleted at will.
findings.gotchas: Test mode sandbox shares some settings with live mode, so Dashboard changes can leak into live mode (look for notification banners). Test objects are not accessible from live mode and vice versa. General sandboxes support API V2; test mode is the legacy path.

findings.name: Stripe Startups program (venture-backed startups): fee credits or waived processing fees, free community
