findings.detail: By-application program for early-stage, venture-backed startups. Benefit = financial benefits as fee credits (in ~31 countries incl. US, UK, Canada, most of EU, AU/NZ/JP/SG/TH/AE...) or waived payment-processing fees (all other countries); plus a focused community of builders/Stripe leaders and expert resources. No fixed public amount: offer amounts vary by offer type and referral source (investor referrals get elevated benefits; VCs/accelerators apply at stripe.com/startups/partners). Fee credits offset Stripe fees on Products like Payments, Connect, Billing, Tax, Sigma; they do NOT apply to Crypto, Capital, Atlas (incl. registered agent renewals), Terminal devices, Link passthrough, PayPal fees, professional services. Waived processing fees only cover card + local payment method fees (incl. BNPL, ACH); not currency conversion, manual card fees, Terminal, Atlas, product fees. Offer activates in Dashboard (banner/setup-guide task); credits may take up to 2 days to apply; tracked under Reports > Fee Credits. One offer per startup lifetime, per account; stacks with Atlas credits (earliest-expiring used first).
findings.eligibility: Early-stage, venture-backed companies; application must include proof of institutional funding (PitchBook link, funding-announcement articles, or other docs). No funding cap or age cap published. No .edu. No credit card required to apply; must have an active, fully verified Stripe account on standard pricing, located in a supported country, not already received an offer, and not connected to a platform that controls your pricing.
findings.claim: Apply at stripe.com/startups (form + verify your Stripe account) or via an investor's private referral link (Stripe Startup Partner program). Review in 2-3 business days; if approved, accept the offer via the Dashboard banner; 12-month activation window, then 12 months of offer usage.
findings.expiry: Expiring offers: offer expires 12 months after activation or when offer limit reached, whichever first; you have 12 months to activate; cannot be paused; no expiry reminders sent.
findings.gotchas: No retroactive effect if you forget to activate; waived-fee offers do not cover Stripe product fees; offer is converted to your default bank account currency; Connect usage depends on controller fees.payer configuration; if you process >$100,000/month for 3 consecutive months you can request a custom-pricing review instead. Fee credits are 'replacing waived processing fees over time' by region.

findings.name: Stripe Atlas: $500 one-time incorporation with $2,500 fee credits + $50,000 partner perks
findings.detail: Stripe Atlas forms a Delaware C corp or LLC in 1-2 business days for a one-time US$500 setup fee (includes government fees + first year of registered agent; the agent auto-renews annually after). Includes EIN retrieval, founder equity vesting, 83(b) elections, legal documents developed with Cooley LLP, free legal document template downloads, and a US business bank account via Stripe Treasury. All Atlas companies incorporated on or after Oct 16, 2025 automatically get $2,500 in Stripe product fee credits, valid 1 year from incorporation date (usable on Payments, Connect, Billing, Tax, Sigma; NOT on Crypto, Capital, Atlas/registered agent renewal, Terminal devices, Link passthrough, PayPal fees, professional services). Plus US$50,000 in exclusive partner benefits (discounts from AWS, Mercury, Carta and other tools, plus legal/tax experts).
findings.eligibility: Founders anywhere in the world (forms US/Delaware entities). No .edu, no funding or age requirements, no credit card to apply (the $500 fee is paid at incorporation). Requires a US phone number to activate US card payments (Atlas partner perks can help if you lack one). Without a US SSN, EIN takes 10-35 business days instead of 1-2. C-corp founders' shares are purchased with IP, not cash.
findings.claim: 1) Create account at dashboard.stripe.com/register/atlas, 2) submit company/founders/ownership/officers info and pay the $500 one-time fee, 3) incorporation in 1-2 business days, 4) EIN + $2,500 credits auto-applied, 5) activate US card payments from the confirmation email or Atlas Dashboard.
findings.expiry: The $2,500 offer activates automatically on the incorporation date, cannot be extended, and expires 365 days after incorporation. Registered agent renews annually (first year included in the $500).
findings.gotchas: Credits are not transferable to other Stripe accounts. Excluded fees: currency conversion, manual card fees, Terminal, Atlas renewal fees, PayPal, professional services. Atlas provides no legal/tax/accounting advice. If you qualify for Stripe Startups program credits too, the two stack.

findings.name: Atlas + Stripe Treasury refund offer (new 2026): Atlas fee refunded up to $500
findings.detail: Full refund of the Atlas incorporation fee (up to US$500, in cash or USD-backed stablecoins) when you deposit at least US$5,000 in aggregate into your Stripe Treasury financial account within 90 days of incorporating AND maintain a minimum balance of US$5,000 for at least 30 days. Reward is deposited 30 days after meeting the requirements. Makes Atlas effectively free for eligible startups.
findings.eligibility: Users who incorporate through Atlas and open a Stripe financial (Treasury) account on or after April 13, 2026; account must be open and in good standing at reward time. No .edu, no funding cap, no credit card. Stripe can disqualify misuse/abuse/fraud 'gaming'.
findings.claim: 1) Incorporate via Atlas ($500), 2) open a Stripe Treasury financial account, 3) deposit US$5,000+ within 90 days of incorporation and hold it for 30 days, 4) refund is deposited automatically ~30 days after requirements are met.
findings.expiry: No published end date; Stripe 'reserves the right to alter, change or end this offer at any time'. Reward has no monetary value until distributed; user is responsible for any tax on the reward.
findings.gotchas: Ties up US$5,000 of real capital for 30+ days to recoup at most US$500; refund may be paid in USD-backed stablecoins; not a perpetual perk - program-modifiable at any time.

findings.name: Students: GitHub Student Developer Pack Stripe perk - $25 in Stripe credits (only student offer found; no Stripe education license)
findings.detail: Stripe has no direct student program, no .edu-based education license, and no stripe.com/student(-s)/education page (both 404). The only student-facing offer found is a perk inside the GitHub Student Developer Pack: 'Get $25 in Stripe credits to offset fees on products including Stripe Payments, Billing, and more.' Credits are a fixed US$25 amount (not a fee waiver on revenue volume).
findings.eligibility: Verified GitHub student status (GitHub Education verification, typically a school-issued email or enrollment documents; GitHub requires 18+). No credit card required to claim. No Stripe-specific requirements.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up for the GitHub Student Developer Pack at education.github.com/pack, 2) complete GitHub student verification, 3) claim the Stripe offer from the pack's offers list ('Get help at Stripe support').
findings.expiry: Tied to the pack: GitHub pack access is renewable while you are a student (12-month cycles); the Stripe $25 credit's own expiry is not stated on the pack page.
findings.gotchas: Third-party aggregators (e.g., freEDU, marked 'verified March 7, 2026') describe this perk as 'waived transaction fees on first $1,000 in revenue' - that wording contradicts GitHub's live listing and is likely stale; trust the live GitHub pack page. The $25 credit is minor relative to startup offers; not a fee waiver. Verify live terms before claiming, as pack perks change.

findings.name: Free base pricing & product free allowances, plus 30-day free trials (time-limited, not permanent tiers)
findings.detail: Core Payments: no setup fees, no monthly fees, no hidden fees like closure fees (guaranteed in Stripe's pricing FAQ); pay-per-transaction: US domestic cards 2.9% + 30c per successful transaction (+0.5% manually entered cards, +1.5% international cards, +1% if currency conversion; ACH 0.8% with $5 cap; disputes $15.00 per SPT). Standing free allowances: payouts on the standard schedule are free; P2P payments to other Stripe businesses are free; micro-deposit verifications free; Data Pipeline Postgres sync has 5,000 rows synced free per month (beyond: $0.0025/row pay-as-you-go); basic usage-based billing via the Meters API under Billing pricing includes up to 100M events/month. Payment Links included at no additional charge (custom domains $10/month is a paid extra). 30-day free trials (then paid subscription, 'subscription and cancellation terms apply'): Stripe Sigma ($15/mo, or from $10/mo annual), Data Pipeline warehouse/cloud sync ($65/mo, from $50/mo annual, includes Sigma), Revenue Recognition ($25/mo, $190/mo annual). No credit card requirement stated for trials; Invoicing Starter is pay-as-you-go at 0.4% per paid invoice (no recurring fee, not free); Tax Basic is pay-as-you-go (0.5%/txn no-code, $0.50/txn API).
findings.eligibility: Any Stripe account, any region (rates differ by country). No .edu, no startup requirements, no credit card required to open an account or run trials.
findings.claim: Create a free Stripe account; products unlock pay-as-you-go immediately; trials start via the 'Try for free for 30 days' buttons on stripe.com/pricing.
findings.expiry: Trials are 30 days, then auto-convert to the listed subscription unless cancelled; free allowances (5,000 rows/month, free standard-schedule payouts, 100M Meters events) have no stated end date.
findings.gotchas: Trials are time-boxed, not free tiers; the free Data Pipeline allowance is rows-synced-based (updates/deletes also count); 'no monthly fees' does not mean no transaction fees; custom domains ($10/mo) and post-payment invoices (0.4%, $2 cap) are small paid extras on otherwise no-code tools; instant payouts and premium services carry fees; refund fees may apply to bank transfers.

sunset_notes: 1) Oct 16, 2025 - Atlas startup offer materially changed: companies incorporated before that date received 'waived payments processing fees on your first $100,000 USD in payments, for 1 year after incorporation' (limited to card + local payment method processing fees); companies incorporated on/after Oct 16, 2025 instead receive $2,500 in Stripe product fee credits (1 year from incorporation, broader product coverage). The prior waived-processing-fee offer remains active only for earlier incorporations. 2) Apr 13, 2026 - new 'Stripe Treasury refund offer for Atlas users' (full Atlas-fee refund up to $500 for $5,000 deposit + 30-day hold) - brand-new 2026 program with no published end date. 3) 2025 - general sandboxes launched as the recommended test environment for new integrations; the legacy test mode sandbox is retained for existing integrations (API V2 only supported in general sandboxes; Stripe CLI can create anonymous sandboxes with no account). 4) Stripe Startups FAQ: fee credits are 'replacing waived processing fees over time' by country, so more regions will shift from waived fees to credits; also note the FAQ's 'Stripe Treasury benefits' $1,000 USD offer is event-tied (sign up for a Stripe card within 7 days of the event), not a standing free program. 5) Pricing-page footnote: basic usage-based billing features are moving to Stripe's Meters API under Billing pricing with up to 100M events/month included (metronome remains a separately signed-up product). 6) No student/education program was sunset - no direct Stripe student program exists; the only student perk is via the GitHub Student Developer Pack ($25 in Stripe credits per GitHub's current listing; some aggregators still show older 'first $1,000 revenue fee waiver' wording). 7) Baseline card rates confirmed current: US domestic 2.9% + 30c; +1.5% international cards; +1% currency conversion (US page; some country pages show +2% conversion).

provider: Discord Nitro (via UNiDAYS student offer; fronts: education/student)

findings.name: UNiDAYS x Discord Nitro — 1 month of full Nitro free for verified students
findings.detail: One month of Discord Nitro (full tier, not Nitro Basic) claimed through UNiDAYS student verification. Offer window: 2026-07-09 10:00 PT to 2027-07-09 11:59 PT; claimed codes must be redeemed on a Discord account by 2027-08-08 11:59 PT. Nitro includes HD streaming, 500MB uploads, 2 server boosts, custom emojis anywhere, profile/avatar customization, Super Reactions. After the 1-month trial, the subscription auto-converts to a monthly recurring Nitro plan and Discord bills the account's payment method each month ($9.99/mo in US per live discord.com/nitro page read 2026-10-22; cost varies by region/country) until cancelled in User Settings. One claim per user.
findings.eligibility: Must be a UNiDAYS-verified student (UNiDAYS verifies via institutional/.edu email, student ID, or its regional ID-verifier e.g. SheerID in the US; GRADLiFE recent-graduate accounts up to 3 years post-graduation may also qualify in some regions). Account must NOT have had: an active Nitro subscription or Nitro trial in the last 12 months, any prior Nitro subscription at any point, or a Nitro Classic/Basic subscription in the past 12 months — i.e., effectively new-to-Nitro accounts. If the account has Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting active, redeeming overrides it and leftover time is forfeited (no refund). Region-limited: NOT available in Syria, Russia, Turkey, Iran, North Korea, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Donetsk, Luhansk. UNiDAYS live offer pages exist for US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, Spain, Italy (not all countries).
findings.claim: 1) Open UNiDAYS website/app for your country, find the Discord offer tile, sign in and complete student verification. 2) Select 'Get now' / 'Activate' on the Discord offer page to unlock a Nitro promo code. 3) Redeem the code on your Discord account (desktop app or web) before 2027-08-08. 4) Cancel in User Settings > Nitro before the first renewal if you do not want the $9.99/mo (US) recurring charge.
findings.expiry: Claimable 2026-07-09 to 2027-07-09 (11:59 PT); redeemed code valid until 2027-08-08 (11:59 PT). Auto-renews to paid monthly Nitro after the 1-month trial; cancel anytime in User Settings to stop billing.
findings.gotchas: Trial, not permanent free access: converts to recurring paid Nitro ($9.99/mo US, varies by country) — a payment method will be billed at renewal unless you cancel first. Exclusion list is strict: any Nitro trial in the last 12 months disqualifies you, and ever having had Nitro disqualifies you. Redeeming wipes out unrefunded time on active Nitro Basic/Classic/Server Boost. The .edu email is not directly required by Discord — it's UNiDAYS's verification that gates it (email or student ID depending on country). Excluded countries include several large markets (Russia, Turkey, Iran). Support cannot manually add eligibility. NOTE: official support article returned 403 to direct fetch (bot protection); article content was read via a crawler snapshot updated 2026-07-08, so treat exact wording as high-fidelity but not live-verified today.

findings.name: Discord free tier (baseline, not student-specific)
findings.detail: Discord itself is free permanently with no card required: text/voice/video, standard-quality streaming (no HD), ~10MB file uploads, 80-char messages on some surfaces, no server boosts, no Nitro perks. Nitro Basic is $2.99/mo and full Nitro $9.99/mo in US (confirmed on live discord.com/nitro, 2026-10-22). This free tier is the baseline everyone gets; the education front (UNiDAYS) only adds a 1-month Nitro trial on top.
findings.eligibility: Everyone; no verification, no card required for the free tier.
findings.claim: Sign up at discord.com; nothing to claim.
findings.expiry: Permanently free; no expiry.
findings.gotchas: Not a student offer; listed for completeness of the 'free tier' category. No trial credits, startup program, or education license for Nitro exist on the live pricing page — the only student-facing offer is UNiDAYS.

sunset_notes: No startup program or education license exists for Discord Nitro: I found no Nitro startup discount, startup credits, or school/university education license in the official promotions list (support.discord.com Promotions section, 2026 snapshot); discord.com/education returns 404 as of 2026-10-22 (the older 'Discord for Education' resource hub appears retired, with no replacement education-licensing program). The UNiDAYS campaign was refreshed for the 2026-2027 window (2026-07-09 to 2027-07-09) — earlier UNiDAYS iterations ran on shorter, earlier windows, so 2025-dated claim instructions may be stale. Other Nitro promos listed on Discord's official Promotions page in 2025-2026 are partner-driven (T-Mobile 3-month trial, Meta Quest, T-Mobile, Xbox, PlayStation, Twitch 2025, Best Buy, EGS Megasale 2026, Logitech/SteelSeries gear discounts, 'Free Nitro Trial for May 2025' — the May 2025 trial has lapsed) and are not student/startup offers, so they are out of scope. Caveat: WebFetch was blocked (403) on support.discord.com and discord.com/pricing (404) during this run; discord.com/nitro and the myunidays.com partner page were read live, and the UNiDAYS support article content came from a 2026-07-08 crawler snapshot. WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-run, so no additional 2025-2026 change checks were possible.

provider: Unity (Unity Personal / Unity Student / Unity Education & Student Programs)

findings.name: Unity Personal (free tier)
findings.detail: Perpetually free editor + cloud for hobbyists and small indie teams. No credit card required (stated on the pricing page). Includes: publish to web/desktop/AR/VR/mobile, Unity Cloud ecosystem, MCP access, 1,000 AI tool credits/month. As of the 3/1/2026 DevOps change the free cloud tier includes: unlimited public-cloud Version Control seats, 25 GB standard storage per org/month, 10 GB Asset Manager storage, 100 GB free egress, 2 concurrent build units, and 200 Windows (Micro) + 100 Linux (Micro) + 100 Mac (Standard) free build minutes/month. Made with Unity splash screen optional on Unity 6. No Runtime Fee (canceled Sep 2024). Overages: $0.75/GB Asset Manager, $0.10/GB standard storage >25GB, $0.10/GB egress >100GB, Micro $0.02/min, Standard Linux $0.06 & Mac/Windows $0.07, Premium $0.11-0.12, Ultra $0.18-0.20, Turbo Windows $0.37; extra editor concurrency $10/mo.
findings.eligibility: Individuals/hobbyists/small businesses whose total finances (revenue + funding, trailing 12 months) are under $200,000 USD; if serving third-party clients, the aggregate client revenue/funding must be under $200K. Gaming/entertainment apps only — non-gaming apps where total company finances exceed $1,000,000 require Unity Industry, and Industry customers may not use Personal. No age floor, no credit card, self-reported finances subject to audit. Region: global; page/ToS in USD.
findings.claim: Create a free Unity ID, download Unity Hub and Editor from unity.com/download, select the Personal plan. Self-certify finances in the Unity dashboard. No card required. Console (PS/Xbox/Switch) and Apple Vision Pro builds need Pro instead.
findings.expiry: No expiry while under the $200K threshold; must upgrade to Pro once exceeded (immediately upon crossing; tiers cannot be mixed).
findings.gotchas: Exceeding $200K forces paid Pro ($2,310/yr or $210/mo post-Jan 2026); no downgrades during a commitment window; cloud storage/egress/build-minute overages bill even on the free plan; splash screen is optional only on Unity 6; industry (non-game) use above $1M total finances is ineligible.

findings.name: Unity Student plan (free education license)
findings.detail: Free plan giving students the full Unity Pro-tier editor (no education watermark) plus: free Odin Inspector + Validator education licenses, a premium Synty asset bundle, Unity Cloud personal tier (3 Version Control seats, 5 GB storage), and a 20% Asset Store discount. Valid 1 year; renews while enrolled (renew any time up to 60 days before expiry or after it expires). A school email is NOT required — 'You don't need a school email to sign up'; verification is via SheerID (or SAML sign-in to school where available). K-12 tier explicitly 16+. One Unity ID per verified account; student projects are isolated to the Student-plan account.
findings.eligibility: Students of legal age to consent to personal data processing (age 13 in the U.S., 16 in the E.U.; secondary tier stated as 16+), currently enrolled in credit-bearing classes at an accredited institution. No .edu email required. Global (page published in 9 languages); SheerID does regional verification.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at unity.com/products/unity-student, choose Post-Secondary or Secondary. 2) Create/log in to Unity ID. 3) Complete the SheerID form with academic details + documentation (instant most of the time; up to ~5 business days). 4) Redeem via the emailed instructions: download Unity Hub, then activate the license key (Unity Hub > Licenses > Activate with serial number).
findings.expiry: 1 year; renewable indefinitely while actively enrolled, re-verified through SheerID. Graduating = plan lapses after its year (no special post-graduation path stated).
findings.gotchas: Cannot be shared; friends/family must apply separately; may log in at school but it's a personal (not lab/classroom) license — institutions use the Education Grant License; projects under the Student plan can't be opened in Personal/Educator/EGL accounts; commercializing student projects is allowed under the Editor ToS; legacy GitHub Student Pack references in some university IT articles are outdated (SheerID is current).

findings.name: Unity Educator plan (free education license)
findings.detail: Free individual educator plan (cannot be purchased): Unity Pro-tier editor without watermark, free Odin Inspector + Validator education licenses, Synty asset bundle, an 'educator asset pack' (industry-built modular assets for demos/sample projects), 20% Asset Store discount, and Version Control with 3 seats / 5 GB. For creating/teaching/sharing Unity projects at home, school, or elsewhere — not for deploying across institutional machines.
findings.eligibility: Higher education: educators at accredited post-secondary degree-granting institutions globally (SheerID affiliation verification; .edu email not strictly required). K-12: available in roughly 30 listed countries (US, CA, AU, UK, etc.); K-12 educators in unlisted regions must use the Education Grant License instead. One Unity ID per verified account.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at unity.com/products/unity-educator, choose K-12 or Higher Education. 2) Create/log in to Unity ID. 3) Complete SheerID form, upload affiliation proof if asked. 4) License key arrives by email; activate in Unity Hub > Licenses > Activate with serial number.
findings.expiry: 1 year; renew by returning to the page and re-verifying with SheerID (no purchase path exists).
findings.gotchas: Not for multi-computer classroom/lab deployment (use Education Grant License); K-12 is region-gated; educator projects can't be accessed from Student/EGL accounts; individual-use only.

findings.name: Unity Education Grant License (institutional / university program)
findings.detail: Free multi-seat license that institutions deploy across lab/classroom computers and servers (no Unity ID sign-in required on the machines). Covers the core Unity engine (build/optimize/deploy across 25+ platforms) 'regardless of classroom size'. A full year of licenses at no cost, renewable annually at no cost; seat counts modifiable after initial approval; one Unity ID tied to the verified institutional account; no Unity Cloud access; EGL projects cannot be accessed via Student/Educator accounts. Accredited institutions: free. Nonprofits: available at a discounted (paid) cost instead. Students can pair EGL on lab machines with the free Student plan on personal devices.
findings.eligibility: Academic institutions accredited by an authorized governmental agency (local/state/provincial/federal/national) whose primary purpose is teaching enrolled students; .edu/institutional email used for the application. Outside-U.S. K-12 educators whose region lacks the K-12 Educator plan may use EGL. No age floor (institutional).
findings.claim: 1) Sign in at unity.com/products/unity-education-grant-license. 2) Select institution type. 3) Complete the SheerID verification form (up to ~48 h). 4) Submit the license request; follow the Unity Learn activation tutorial. Renew via the Unity Education License Information dashboard > Renew License, entering seat count.
findings.expiry: 1-year term, renewable; renewal window opens 90 days before expiry; annual re-grant.
findings.gotchas: Changing the associated institutional email requires a support ticket; the page still notes Unity Cloud is not part of EGL; research/industry/commercial projects at an institution should instead buy discounted Unity Pro through an education rep.

findings.name: Unity AI tools free trial + plan AI credit allowance
findings.detail: Unity AI (MCP/AI tools) offers a 14-day no-commitment free trial (link from the products page into the Unity service store, variant 'uty-pts-no-commitment-14-day-trial'); after the trial a paid monthly points subscription. Separately, every Unity plan includes a monthly AI-credit allowance: Unity Personal 1,000 credits/month, Pro 2,000, Enterprise/Industry 3,000, with 'special terms apply to Unity Credits'.
findings.eligibility: Any Unity ID holder can take the 14-day AI trial; the free monthly allowance attaches to a Personal (or higher) plan. No credit card stated for the trial variant ('no-commitment').
findings.claim: From unity.com/products, click 'Try Unity's AI tools free' (14-day variant). Or just use the plan's included monthly AI credits (Personal = 1,000/month).
findings.expiry: Trial: 14 days, then paid. Free allowance: renews monthly with the plan while eligible.
findings.gotchas: Trial is trial, not a perpetual free tier; post-trial requires paying subscription; credit special terms apply; AI feature is newer so limits may shift.

findings.name: Unity DevOps free-tier expansion (Mar 1, 2026) — free cloud build/VC layer on Personal
findings.detail: Effective 3/1/2026 Unity expanded the free (pay-as-you-go) cloud tier: seat charges for public-cloud Unity Version Control removed (the old 3-free-seat cap for Personal becomes unlimited; 1:1 seat limits dropped on paid plans), free storage 5 GB -> 25 GB per org per month, 100 GB free egress added (no egress billing at all in March-April 2026), free build minutes now 200 Windows (Micro) + 100 Mac (Standard) + 100 Linux (Micro) monthly, and Unity Editor Concurrency doubled from 1 to 2 (extra = $10/mo). This applies to everyone on a Unity ID, so students and sub-$200K startup teams get it free.
findings.eligibility: All Unity plans; effectively free for Personal users (students, hobbyists, startups under $200K revenue/funding).
findings.claim: Automatic — included with a Unity Personal (or any) account; manage usage in the Unity Dashboard (Administration > Costs and usage reporting).
findings.expiry: Ongoing as of Oct 2026; announced 2025-11-10, effective 3/1/2026.
findings.gotchas: Beyond free limits, usage bills: storage >25GB $0.10/GB (premium $0.30/GB), egress >100GB $0.10/GB, Micro $0.02/min, Standard $0.06-0.07/min, Premium $0.11-0.12/min, Ultra $0.18-0.20/min; no downgrade during a commitment window; 'later in 2026' Unity DevOps gains were promised but may still be rolling out.

findings.name: Unity Multiplay Hosting $800 startup sign-up credit (service in transition)
findings.detail: New Unity Multiplay Game Server Hosting organizations received $800 of sign-up credit, valid 6 months from sign-up, automatically applied across the whole organization (shared by all projects) until exhausted; consumed on subsequent invoices; dashboard shows real-time consumption. Caveat found today: Unity is winding down direct support — support runs through 31 March 2026, the software is licensed to Rocket Science Group, and the official docs page now issues a 308 redirect to rocketscience.gg/services/hosting, so new credits likely come via Rocket Science Group rather than Unity.
findings.eligibility: New Unity Multiplay Hosting users (i.e., game startups adding server hosting); no CC-free claim — standard Unity account.
findings.claim: Historically: subscribe to Unity Gaming Services/Multiplay Hosting; the $800 credit applied automatically org-wide; track in Dashboard > Administration > Costs and usage reporting.
findings.expiry: Credit: 6 months from sign-up. Service: Unity direct support ends 31 March 2026; continuity via Rocket Science Group.
findings.gotchas: Trial-style credit, not a free tier; once credit expires, pay-per-usage applies; migration off Unity's direct service may be required after the support cutoff.

findings.name: Unity for Humanity grants (social-impact creator grants)
findings.detail: Grant program providing financial support + mentorship + audience amplification to creators using real-time 3D for social impact (environment, health, education, accessibility). 2026 winners already announced (e.g., Amaru, I NEED SPACE, Project Ember); also runs the UNEP/Project Drawdown Environment & Sustainability Grant and Imagine Grant (with Common, 2021). Not a license or startup-specific program, but a real free-money front that students/indies run into.
findings.eligibility: Creators/changemakers (any region) applying through periodic grant calls; application-based and selective; open on unity.com/humanity.
findings.claim: Apply via the Unity for Humanity grant application on unity.com/humanity when a cycle is open; winners and honorees are announced per year.
findings.expiry: Recurring annual/periodic grant cycles (2026 cycle ran; next cycle timing follows Unity's announcement).
findings.gotchas: Grants, not subscriptions — no guaranteed amount, selective; distinct from Unity's education/startup licensing.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22, no dedicated 'Unity Startup Program' exists on unity.com (no link in the products navigation; unity.com/startups and similar paths 404). Startups are covered by the free Unity Personal tier (<$200K revenue+funding/12 months) plus the expanded free DevOps cloud tier; paid Pro is $2,310/yr or $210/mo. Material 2024-2026 changes: (1) Sep 12, 2024: Unity canceled the controversial Runtime Fee for games; Personal's cap doubled from $100K to $200K USD at the same time, and the 'Made with Unity' splash screen became optional starting with Unity 6. (2) Jan 1, 2025: plan restructure — Unity Plus was absorbed/renamed to Unity Pro; Pro became mandatory above $200K and Enterprise above $25M total finances; Pro was $2,200/yr at that date. (3) Jan 12, 2026: 5% Pro/Enterprise price increase (Pro -> $2,310/yr, $210/mo); Havok Physics for Unity dropped from Pro/Enterprise/Industry on 6.0 LTS (and from Unity 6.3). (4) Mar 1, 2026: free DevOps cloud tier expansion (unlimited VCS seats, 25GB storage, 100GB egress, added Mac/Linux build minutes, 2 editor concurrency) — all free tiers above reflect this. (5) 31 Mar 2026: Unity Multiplay Game Server Hosting direct support ends; service licensed to Rocket Science Group, docs 308-redirect there, so its $800 startup credit is in transition. (6) Aug-Sep 2026: Unity Economy (Gaming Services) became free to use starting 25 Aug 2026 and stopped accepting new project signups 8 Sep 2026 — a de-facto free tier for existing configs but the product is sunsetting (no new signups; IAP/Live Content positioned as the successors). (7) Verification path: the legacy 'GitHub Student Developer Pack' route for Unity Student has been replaced by SheerID (plus optional SAML sign-in to school); .edu email is explicitly not required by Unity's current Student plan page. Older third-party university IT articles still cite the GitHub Pack requirement — outdated. No announced sunset of the Personal, Student, Educator, or Education Grant License offerings as of Oct 22, 2026.

provider: Canva Pro for Students (Education & Student Programs)

findings.name: Canva Free (free tier, open to all students)
findings.detail: Official US pricing snapshot 2026-10-22: US$0/year. Includes drag-and-drop editor with 1,000+ design types, 1.6M+ templates, 4.7M+ photos/videos/graphics/audio, 1 Brand Kit (3 colors), 5GB cloud storage, ad insights/AI ad creation, access to Affinity, and a shared AI allowance of up to 200 Standard AI uses or 20 Premium AI uses (new 'AI Pass' era layout; older layout shows 'Limited AI access'). Higher-ed students whose school lacks Canva for Campus land on exactly this tier. Prices vary by country; today's page renders localized currency.
findings.eligibility: Open to everyone — no student verification, no .edu email, no credit card, no region limit. Sign up at canva.com with email/Google/Apple/Facebook/Microsoft.
findings.claim: 1) Go to canva.com or canva.com/education/students -> 'Sign up for free'. 2) Create an account. 3) Use the Free tier; optionally log in with your university email in case your institution has Canva for Campus (upgrades you to premium automatically).
findings.expiry: Indefinite free tier; no renewal. Content persists; premium assets/templates become locked/watermarked if a paid or campus license is lost.
findings.gotchas: Free tier excludes the 141M+ premium asset library, 3.6M premium templates, background remover, social scheduler, and paid-tier AI allowance. A 'free' university sign-in only gets Pro features if the institution actually bought Campus. AI allowance on Free is ~200 Standard / 20 Premium uses per month.

findings.name: Canva Education (K-12 license): 100% free Pro features
findings.detail: Official: 'Canva Education will remain 100% free for K-12 educators, their students, as well as qualified school districts and institutions' — no paywalls, available worldwide, not restricted to any country. Includes most premium features (100M+ premium photos/videos/graphics/fonts, Brand Kits, background remover, Magic tools), plus educator features: LMS integrations (Canvas, Google Classroom, Schoology, Blackboard, D2L, Moodle, MS Teams), SSO/Clever/ClassLink, enterprise-grade security, class management. Free delivery on print orders. Canva states it never uses student data to train AI models.
findings.eligibility: K-12 (primary/secondary) only: certified active K-12 teachers, school librarians, learning-support staff, curriculum specialists, tech/vocational K-12 teachers, and government-recognized accredited K-12 schools/districts/education departments — and the students they enroll. Explicitly EXCLUDED: colleges/universities, college/university students, tutors, public librarians, unlicensed homeschoolers, parents, early-stage educational startups. Verified education email = instant access; otherwise upload teacher license/cert/school ID — reviewed within 48h (US/JP/AU/CA/NZ/UK/KR teachers need only a teaching license copy). No credit card required.
findings.claim: Teachers: sign up at canva.com/education with a verified K-12 school email, or upload proof (48h review). Students: ask the teacher to invite you to their Canva class, or sign up with your school email / district SSO — if it matches a school district you get instant Canva Education access; else enter the teacher's email to request access. You cannot self-verify as a K-12 student.
findings.expiry: Lasts while you are active and eligible; all Canva Education users are prompted to re-verify credentials every 3 years. Students who leave the class or graduate revert to the free plan — copy designs to a personal account first.
findings.gotchas: Premium features can be disabled by school administrators. Access is class/team-scoped, not a personal permanent Pro account: on graduation the account reverts to Canva Free. Intended for educational use — commercial licensing differs from Pro. Verified-email domains must be recognized Canva education domains; personal Gmail/Yahoo not accepted.

findings.name: Canva for Campus (higher education): free premium student access via institutional license
findings.detail: Official: Canva Campus = Canva Enterprise plan 'plus free premium student access included' — all premium student seats free, priced like Enterprise at special higher-ed pricing (no public price; contact sales). Unlock condition: institution purchases a minimum number of staff/faculty licenses calculated from its full-time student body (a Canva consultant sets the threshold; <25 seats -> Canva Business, no HE pricing). Included: SSO/SCIM, FERPA/SOC 2/GDPR compliance, 1TB storage, LMS integrations (Blackboard, Canvas, D2L, Moodle), brand kits, admin AI on/off controls, and per the page, access to Affinity and Flourish within Campus. 'Free access for all students... as part of Canva Step Two' (every enrolled student gets full premium from day one at no cost to them). Examples: UT Austin rolled out free Canva Pro to all students 2025-10-17 (EID sign-in, ~800 sign-ups in first 30 min); Lehigh entered a campus-wide agreement March 2026 with pro-rated rebates for students who paid individually; HKU ran a student-society campaign 2025-11-06 to 2026-11-05 at HK$35/year (~96% below the HK$960 list price).
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students of universities/colleges that have purchased Canva Campus (or Enterprise on the path to it). No individual application, no .edu verification, no credit card. Excluded: student employees, part-time/full-time staff and interns of the institution. Not available to individuals at non-adopting schools — they fall back to Canva Free or pay full Pro price.
findings.claim: Student at an adopting campus: sign in to Canva with your university email / campus SSO (or use the institution's Canva sign-in page, e.g. canva sign-in for UT EID); if the campus has Campus you automatically get premium. Otherwise: there is nothing to claim individually — the university's IT/student union must procure the plan ('let your IT team or student union know you want it - student demand is often what gets Campus started').
findings.expiry: Lasts while enrolled; on graduation you may lose the school email and with it the free account — copy designs to a personal account. Institutions re-provision via SSO/SCIM; de-provisioning is automatic.
findings.gotchas: Institution-paid but admin-gated: faculty/IT can switch AI tools off per course/role/cohort. No public price; 'minimum seat thresholds apply'. If your school has no Campus you pay consumer Pro (US$120-180/yr snapshots) — no individual student discount listed officially in 2026. Individual campus campaigns (HKU HK$35/yr) are local student-union deals, not a Canva-wide student program; the HKU offer window closed 2026-11-05.

findings.name: Canva Pro / Canva Business 30-day free trial (any user, incl. students)
findings.detail: Official help center: Pro and Business offer a free trial, started via 'Start a free trial' on the pricing page; auto-renews into the chosen monthly/yearly plan unless cancelled; trial AI allowance equals the Free tier's (the paid 10x/20x AI allowance only kicks in after conversion); one trial per Canva account AND one per payment method ('if you've used a trial before, you won't see the free trial option; try a new payment method'); trial end date visible under Settings > Billing & Teams with email reminder; 'If you started a free trial without providing payment details, your trial ends automatically and you won't be charged' (a no-card flow exists; other flows/regions require card or PayPal to activate). Third-party 2026 sources describe the standard US trial as 30 days of full Pro (some regions 14 days). After cancel: account reverts to Free, designs retained but premium assets re-watermarked. Paid US list prices (2026 snapshots, transition in progress): Pro US$120-180/yr, Business US$200-250/yr per person, 'Save 16%' on yearly.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, not student-specific. No student status needed; no credit card strictly required (a payment-less trial flow exists, though most activations collect card/PayPal up front). Available where Canva accepts payment; trial window is region-dependent.
findings.claim: 1) canva.com/pricing -> 'Start a free trial' under Pro or Business. 2) Log in / create account. 3) Choose monthly or yearly (this only sets what you're charged at conversion). 4) Choose payment method (or the no-card flow if offered). 5) Confirm. 6) Cancel before day 30 via Settings > Billing > Cancel plan to avoid the charge.
findings.expiry: 30 days in most regions (14 days in some); ends automatically if no payment details were provided, else converts to paid automatically on the anniversary date.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free trap: auto-renews and charges the full chosen plan; the elevated 10x/20x AI allowance is NOT available during the trial (only Free-tier allowance). One trial per account and per payment method — switching card does not reset it. Charges may appear as Canva / Canva*invoice_id / APPLE*Canva / GOOGLE*Canva (app-store billing if subscribed via mobile). New 2026 add-ons (AI Pass monthly add-on; 30-day AI top-ups for Business) cost extra and are not part of the trial.

findings.name: Canva for Startups — no free offer exists
findings.detail: canva.com/startups is a marketing/resource hub only ('Design your success. Canva is the all-in-one content collaboration platform...'): startup template/pitch-deck content, video tips, a 4-part growth series, and guidance to standard plans ('If there's more than one person, Canva Business is the best plan for startups... pricing tiers to fit every startup's budget, no matter which round of funding you're in'). No discount, free seats, trial credits, or funding/age caps for startups. Canva's eligibility guidelines also explicitly list 'early stage start-ups with an educational focus' as NOT eligible for Canva Education. Related adjacent program (not student/startup): Canva Nonprofits — 100% free Pro features + team tools for registered nonprofits/NGOs, one team of up to 50 users, extra seats 50% off; government agencies, political orgs, educational institutions and for-profits excluded.
findings.eligibility: None — no startup-specific eligibility because no startup offer exists. (Nonprofit program: registered 501(c)(3)-equivalent orgs, up to 50 free users.)
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim. A startup can only use Canva Free, the standard Pro/Business trial, or the nonprofit program if it is a registered charity.
findings.expiry: N/A
findings.gotchas: Don't confuse the 'Canva for Startups' content hub with a startup discount program. Also 'Canva Teams is no longer available for new sign-ups or upgrades' (2026) — team features now live under Canva Business.

sunset_notes: The known '~50% off Canva Pro first year for verified students (~$49.99/yr vs $99.99 via .edu or national student verification)' does NOT appear on any official Canva page as of 2026-10-22: the students page offers only Canva Free (higher ed) or free K-12 Canva Education, the eligibility guidelines explicitly exclude college/university students from free Canva Education, and the pricing page lists no student price. The individual ~50% student Pro plan appears to have been sunset and replaced by two structural programs: (1) free Canva Education for K-12, and (2) Canva for Campus — where universities buy Enterprise-priced licenses and all premium student seats are free (e.g. UT Austin, free since 2025-10-17; Lehigh, March 2026; HKU student-union campaign HK$35/yr valid 2025-11-06 to 2026-11-05). US Pro's list price is also no longer $99.99: 2026 pages show US$120-180/yr (a transition-era A/B or recent increase; one third-party check recorded $144/yr on 2026-10-16). 2025-2026 material changes: Canva Pro trials now grant only the Free-tier AI allowance during the trial, plans auto-renew, Canva Teams was discontinued for new sign-ups, and new paid add-ons (AI Pass monthly add-on; 30-day AI top-ups for Business) were introduced. Note: canva.com blocks WebFetch (403); official pages were verified today via direct curl. Local university campaigns (HKU etc.) are institution-specific and expire on their own dates, not Canva policy.

provider: Zoho — Catalyst by Zoho (PaaS) and Zoho Classes (LMS), plus Zoho for Startups wallet-credit program

findings.name: Catalyst Student Program: $250 usage / 6 months, no credit card, non-commercial only
findings.detail: Catalyst is free for students building non-commercial projects: full-stack hosting (frontends Next.js/React/Vue/Nuxt/Angular, serverless functions, managed data, built-in auth, AI/ML tooling). Each student project gets up to $250 of usage at no cost over a six-month period. Bandwidth is free, unlimited; unlimited collaborators (no per-seat pricing). If a project hits the $250 threshold, the application is temporarily stopped and students are NOT auto-charged; they can email Catalyst Support with project details to request an extension, and 'eligible projects can receive additional free usage' (repeatable, case-by-case review). No subscription fee, no credit card, no edu-email verification described on the official page; no region restriction mentioned. Program launched with the first cohort of 'Catalyst Student Clubs' at three Chennai, India colleges (RMKEC, RMKCET, RMDEC).
findings.eligibility: Students, legitimate non-commercial use only (learning, coursework, hackathon builds, side projects, experimentation). .edu email NOT required per official page; no region limit stated; credit card NOT required. Commercial use excluded.
findings.claim: 1) Open https://catalyst.zoho.com/students/ and click 'Claim credits' (deep-links to standard catalyst.zoho.com signup). 2) Sign up with an email address or existing Zoho account (no card). 3) Build/deploy; usage counted up to $250 per 6-month window. 4) At the cap: contact Catalyst Support to request extended free usage; they review the project's student-program qualification.
findings.expiry: No sunset date published. The $250 allowance is measured over six months per project, after which the app is stopped (not charged) until an extension is approved by Support.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial only — commercial projects must use the standard Catalyst account. The official claim flow just opens the standard signup, so activation of the no-card student allowance should be confirmed with Catalyst Support (support@zohocatalyst.com). Students hitting the cap lose their running app until approval. Note the distinction: this no-CC student allowance is separate from the generic $250 wallet credit for all new users, which DOES require adding a card. Program is new (announced Sept 2, 2026; blog Sept 6, 2026).

findings.name: Catalyst Free Tier: perpetual monthly free usage (all users, pay-as-you-go)
findings.detail: Monthly free usage that auto-renews, 'Forever, no expiry', across all components. Monthly free limits (assume single-component use; limits are account-wide across all orgs/projects): Functions 25,000 GB-seconds; AppSail 900 GB-minutes; Circuits 2,000 state transitions; Data Store 2 GB-days storage + 10,000 SELECT / 5,000 INSERT / 1,000 UPDATE / 1,000 DELETE requests, 10,000 bulk-write rows; Stratus 5 GB file storage, 10,000 downloads; NoSQL 1 GB table + 1 GB index storage; Cache 1,000 GET / 5,000 PUT; API Gateway 100,000 requests; Web Client Hosting 300,000 requests; Mail 100 emails; Push Notifications 500; Search 1,000 queries; Slate (frontend) 12 GB-minutes build & deploy (2vCPU 4GB), 500 MB CDN storage, 25,000 GB-seconds invocations; QuickML 1,000,000 LLM input / 500,000 output tokens, 1 GB data storage; Zia Services 100 calls per API; SmartBrowz 7,200 GB-seconds headless, 50 PDF/screenshot conversions; DevOps CI/CD 1,200 GB-minutes, 100 alerts. You get usage alerts at 90% of any component's limit.
findings.eligibility: All new Catalyst users on the pay-as-you-go pricing model. No credit card to sign up ('you don't need to provide your card details to sign up to Catalyst's free tier'); a payment method is requested only when a resource's free allowance is about to run out.
findings.claim: Sign up at catalyst.zoho.com (email address, or existing Zoho account). Choose the pay-as-you-go model; free tier applies automatically, refreshed after each bill/payment cycle. Keep usage within the hard limits to stay free indefinitely; delete unused projects to avoid the minimum bill.
findings.expiry: None — 'Renewal: Monthly; Forever, no expiry'. Limits refresh monthly.
findings.gotchas: Hard limits are consolidated across your ENTIRE account (all orgs and projects), not per project. Exceeding any component's limit triggers pay-as-you-go billing for that resource, PLUS a minimum billing of $5/project/month (introduced 2024-04-01) — delete unused projects to avoid it. Listed limits assume a component is used alone; mixing components dilutes each allowance. The generic $250 new-customer credits sit on top of (are exclusive of) this free tier and require a card. Bandwidth/egress is free (Catalyst's stated position).

findings.name: Catalyst Free Trial + one-time $250 production wallet credits (all new customers; card required for the credits)
findings.detail: Free Trial: free full-featured development environment (Functions, AppSail, QuickML, ConvoKraft, SmartBrowz, AutoML, auth, Web Client Hosting, APM, push/mail, etc.) that does NOT expire; up to 50 projects per account; no auto-charging unless you move a project to production; one account per new customer; signup needs only an email address. The $250 wallet credits apply to production usage when your first project is deployed live; they are a one-time benefit, valid 6 months from the date claimed, and are exclusive of the monthly free-tier allowance and of the $5/month free tier bundled with subscription plans. After credits + free tier are exhausted, pay-as-you-go billing applies.
findings.eligibility: All new Catalyst customers who have never had a Catalyst account or received wallet credits (students, startups, individuals — no commercial restrictions on this general path). Free Trial needs no card; the $250 production credits require adding a payment method ('Add a card to claim them').
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at catalyst.zoho.com (email or Zoho account) — development use is free and non-expiring. 2) To claim $250: in Billing, click 'Get $250 Credits' → Select Payment Plan → add a payment method; credits become valid for 6 months. 3) Deploy first project to production; usage bills against the $250 first.
findings.expiry: Free Trial: no expiry. $250 credits: expire 6 months after claiming; not refreshed monthly; unused credit cannot be recovered or extended.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: 'Free Trial' (dev sandbox, no expiry, no card) is NOT the same as the 'Free Tier' (monthly free usage, pay-as-you-go). The $250 credit IS card-gated, unlike the student no-card allowance. Once credits lapse, usage beyond free tier is billed (with $5/project/month minimum). ConvoKraft is separately free of charge per Catalyst docs. The 2024 price-change notice ended the old free sandbox on 2024-03-31 and moved billing to usage-based from 2024-04-01.

findings.name: Zoho Classes Free Edition: free for schools/teachers up to 100 students ('no questions asked')
findings.detail: Zoho Classes (AI-powered LMS: live streaming classes, course distribution, assignments, attendance, mobile apps) has a free edition 'completely free for all schools for up to 100 students. No questions asked' and a 'Free-For-Teacher License for up to 100 students' (per the signup page). No .edu or domain requirement is stated and no payment method is needed for the free license. Paid editions: $4 per student per year globally ('33 cents per student per month', stream live to 50,000 students); ₹250 per student per year in India. With the July 15, 2026 Classes 2.0 relaunch, paid tiers for private institutions are billed per instructor per month (Standard ~$7/instructor/month, Pro ~$20/instructor/month per press reporting; India from ~₹500/teacher/month; Zoho renders these prices dynamically and doesn't print them as text).
findings.eligibility: Any school or college up to 100 students (worldwide); individual teachers teaching up to 100 students. No edu-email, no accreditation proof, no credit card stated — 'no questions asked'. Larger institutions need a trial license registration or paid plan.
findings.claim: Sign up at zoho.com/classes (classes signup page advertises the free-for-teacher license up to 100 students); the free edition applies automatically. Schools over 100 students register for a trial license / paid plan via the pricing page.
findings.expiry: No sunset date published for the 100-student free edition; 'completely free', no stated trial window.
findings.gotchas: The 100-student cap is on total students, so a class with 50 students in two sections consumes the whole allowance. Feature depth (AI course builder, agentic AI, lifecycle management) ships with Classes 2.0 (July 2026) and is rolling out region-by-region — India first; check your region's feature availability. Per-instructor paid pricing (2026 model) means costs scale with faculty headcount, not enrollment. Pricing figures for Standard/Pro are press-reported, not Zoho-published text — verify on the live pricing page (which blocks scrapers; direct fetch returned 403).

findings.name: Zoho Classes 2.0: free for ALL Central and State government schools, colleges, and universities in India
findings.detail: Announced July 15, 2026 with Classes 2.0: Zoho Classes is available 'at no product licensing cost to all Central and State Government schools, colleges, and universities' in India (AI LMS with embedded AI for lesson planning/grading/reporting, student lifecycle management, institutional dashboards, attendance, and support for all 22 scheduled Indian languages). Private institutions pay per-instructor subscriptions. Global rollout is 'in the coming months' with regional capabilities; the government-free offer is India-only.
findings.eligibility: Central and State government educational institutions in India (schools, colleges, universities). Private institutions are NOT covered (paid tiers). Individual teachers up to 100 students are covered by the separate free edition. No .edu/student-email condition; no credit card for the government free offer.
findings.claim: Government institutions obtain it via Zoho's education program channels (Zoho's launch announcement and education/relationship team; larger private schools can register for trial licenses from the Classes pricing page). No self-serve public application form is published on the pages read today.
findings.expiry: No sunset date stated; presented as an ongoing commitment ('no product licensing cost').
findings.gotchas: India-only (government offer) and the 2.0 platform initially launched in India; global features/rollout pending — international government institutions should not assume coverage yet. 'No product licensing cost' excludes implementation/infrastructure costs borne by the institution. Zoho is building an education-specific LLM (Zia-based); AI features may evolve.

findings.name: Zoho for Startups: Zoho Wallet credits (up to ₹3,00,000 / ₹1,86,000 in India; 360-day validity) — 23 countries, DPIIT-gated in India
findings.detail: Program giving startups Zoho Wallet credits to explore 55+ Zoho applications (suits, individual apps, upgrades, add-ons, renewals) plus weekday classic email support and free consultation. Credits valid 360 days from when Stage 1 is enabled; Stage 2 is an extra tranche unlocked by hosting and mapping your business domain with Zoho within 15 days of receiving Stage 1 (both tranches share the 360-day expiry, which cannot be extended). India figures (from the official Startup India resource-partner page, updated Sept 14, 2026): DPIIT-beneficiary startups (tax-exempt, National Startup Award winners, SISFS) up to ₹3,00,000 total = ₹2,00,000 for 360 days + conditional ₹1,00,000 promotional credits for 90 days (dependent on usage, non-negotiable); DPIIT-recognized startups up to ₹1,86,000 = Stage 1 ₹1,00,000 + Stage 2 ₹86,000 (domain on Zoho Mail within 15 days; note ₹1,00,000 cap on Zoho Workplace/Mail purchases). The zoho.com/startups page renders the USD amount dynamically, so it couldn't be captured by scrape today; no public funding/grants — software credits only. Credits can't buy Zoho Voice, Zoho Start, Zoho Domains, Zoho Backstage, Zoho Sign API, Campaigns PAYG, Qntrl, Vikra, TrainerCentral, most ManageEngine products, premium support, or email domains; non-transferable, non-cashable.
findings.eligibility: Startup must furnish a DPIIT certificate (Startup India, India) OR be associated with a startup enabler that is a registered Zoho collaborator. Must NOT be a current or past paying Zoho customer (creating a new account does not reset this); prior program beneficiaries excluded; free-trial-only usage is fine; solopreneurs/bootstrapped founders qualify if they hold the DPIIT certificate. No startup-age cap or funding cap is stated. Eligible countries (limited access, live): Australia, Austria, Bahrain, Brazil, Denmark, Egypt, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Kenya, Malaysia, Nigeria, Norway, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Tanzania, Uganda, UAE, United Kingdom. .edu not relevant; org admin email required.
findings.claim: 1) Create a Zoho account using the organization's primary/admin email. 2) Apply at zoho.com/startups (or via your Zoho-collaborator enabler; DPIIT-beneficiaries apply through the Startup India link). 3) Respond to Zoho's confirmation email; validation/credit enabling takes 5–7 business days. 4) Within 15 days of Stage 1, host and map your domain with Zoho to unlock Stage 2. 5) Spend credits in the Zoho store before the 360-day expiry.
findings.expiry: Credits expire 360 days from Stage 1 activation (Stage 2 shares that date); the conditional ₹1L promotional tranche (DPIIT-beneficiaries) is valid 90 days. No program-level sunset date published.
findings.gotchas: Exact USD credit amounts are not printed as static text on zoho.com/startups (dynamically rendered; scrape today returned gaps) — confidence in specific dollar values is therefore medium; the India-facing amounts are the firm public numbers. One-time opportunity per startup (no re-application through multiple enablers). No funding/grants. Excluded product list is long. The program is 'exclusive for startups associated or incubated with Zoho collaborators' pending broader rollout. The old 'free Zoho One for a year' subscription (previous program version) has been replaced by wallet credits.

findings.name: Zoho general free Standard editions (available to anyone, including students and startups)
findings.detail: Most Zoho apps ship a free 'Standard' edition with a small seat cap (commonly up to 3 users, more in some apps, e.g., Zoho Mail/Books/Analytics allow a few more), plus 15-day full-feature paid-plan trials. These are not education- or startup-specific offers — they are open to students and startups as individual accounts, no credit card for the free edition. Useful as a base layer (CRM, Docs, Mail, Analytics) under the Catalyst/Classes offers above.
findings.eligibility: Anyone (individuals, students, startups). No .edu requirement; free editions have no CC requirement in most apps (paid trials do). Seat caps vary per app.
findings.claim: Sign up at zoho.com with a personal/edu/any email, start the free Standard edition of each app (or claim the 15-day paid-plan trial from the app's trial page).
findings.expiry: No sunset; free Standard editions are standing offers. (Not re-verified page-by-page today; per-app seat caps vary — treat 3-user as the typical default, not a guarantee.)
findings.gotchas: Not verified today per-app (listed at low confidence deliberately); seat limits are per-app and some require billing details to start (e.g., certain apps' trials). For startups, the Zoho for Startups credits program is the higher-value path instead of piecing together free Standard plans.

sunset_notes: No 2025–2026 sunset of the core free offers; the changes were additive or model-level: (1) Zoho Catalyst Student Program ($250/6 months, no CC) is NEW — announced Sept 2, 2026, blogged Sept 6, 2026; nothing before it was retired. (2) Zoho for Startups: the old 'free Zoho One subscription for a year' was replaced by the wallet-credit model (FAQ explicitly calls Zoho One 'our old offering'); Stage 1/Stage 2 structure and 360-day validity are the current model. (3) Zoho Classes 2.0 relaunched July 15, 2026: pricing model flipped from per-student-per-year ($4/₹250, 2020 model) to per-instructor-per-month (Standard ~$7, Pro ~$20, press-reported) for private institutions; the 100-student free edition and the India government free-license offer were kept/strengthened — the government offer expanded explicitly to all Central & State government schools, colleges and universities at no licensing cost. (4) Catalyst historical price-change notice (effective Jan 1, 2024 / Apr 1, 2024 for pre-existing users) ended the free sandbox on Mar 31, 2024, introduced the monthly-renewing free tier and $5/project/month minimum billing on Apr 1, 2024 — still in force today, relevant gotcha for the free tier. Method note: final web-search budget was exhausted after six searches; all findings above were read today via WebFetch or same-day official-page search snapshots (zoho.com direct fetches returned 403 to the fetcher, so zoho.com pages were read via search snapshots of the live pages).

provider: Figma — Figma for Education (Education & Student Programs) and startup offers

findings.name: Figma Starter plan (free-for-all individual plan)
findings.detail: Free tier available to anyone (students, educators, startups, individuals). Limits read on figma.com/pricing today: unlimited draft files shareable with unlimited viewers; co-editing with unlimited users on up to 3 files (max 3 pages per file); 30-day version history; 500 AI credits/month with a 150 AI credits/day cap; 10 variable modes; Figma Slides limited to 5 templates; community plugins only; basic Dev Mode inspection for viewers. Unlimited files/projects, team component libraries, full Dev Mode, advanced prototyping (motion publishing, high-res video export) require a paid plan (Professional+).
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a Figma account. No credit card required (Figma's payment-method docs cover only paid subscriptions; sign-up is self-serve). No region exclusions noted for the free plan. No CC, no age gate beyond standard terms.
findings.claim: Self-serve: create a Figma account at figma.com (Sign up → 'Get started for free'). No verification, no CC, no card. Free forever.
findings.gotchas: Downgrading a paid team to Starter caps it at 3 files + 1 project; teams with 4+ files become view-only until files are moved to drafts. AI features consume the 500/mo credit pool (no rolver). 'Unlimited drafts' does not include a team space: shared collaboration is limited to 3 files.
findings.expiry: No expiry; free tier is permanent. Code layers are free through Nov 4, 2026 on paid plans, then consume AI credits.

findings.name: Figma for Education: Professional plan free (higher ed, high school, bootcamp & online-course students/educators)
findings.detail: Verified education status gives a free Education team with all Professional-plan functionality (per help.figma.com article read today): unlimited files/projects, team libraries, Dev Mode, advanced prototyping. Higher-ed and bootcamp/online-course users also get the AI toolkit (Figma Make, Figma agent) with monthly AI credits, and Figma Sites (each eligible user may publish ONE Site file; no custom domains). K-12/high-school education users do NOT get the AI tools or Sites features. FAQ: Education accounts valid 2 years for K-12 and higher education, 6 months for bootcamps (one 6-month extension max for bootcamp users).
findings.eligibility: Current student or educator in a structured classroom (high schools, universities, post-grad, trade schools, polytechnics, colleges, design/coding academies, selected online courses/bootcamps with curriculum-based mentor-led instruction). Must apply with a school-issued email where the school issues one; higher-ed verification runs through SheerID and can use student ID/government ID if no school email exists — so a .edu/domain email is NOT strictly required, but education status is tied to the verified email (changing the account email revokes status). Non-teaching school staff do not qualify; self-directed learners, startups, edtech companies, and nonprofits do not qualify. Available only in select regions (forum reports confirm 'not supported' errors from China). Must be old enough to consent; under-13 use belongs to the school-signed-terms route.
findings.claim: 1) Have an existing Figma account under your school email (sign up with it, or change it before applying). 2) Go to figma.com/education/apply: role Student/Educator, institution type Higher Education / High School / Bootcamp or online course, click 'Verify your status' under the Professional card. 3) Higher ed: complete SheerID verification (school email or ID upload). 4) Bootcamp/online course: the provider admin must verify you (you cannot self-verify since Sept 2025); no action needed if your bootcamp is an approved partner. 5) Create an Education team. No credit card required — it is a free plan, not a trial.
findings.gotchas: Sept 2025 re-verification wave: users who did not re-verify by Sept 29, 2025 had Education teams converted to Starter (3 files / 1 project; 4+ files → everyone view-only). Changing your account email revokes verified status. Bootcamp users: initial 6 months + one 6-month extension only; no second extension, and you cannot reapply under the same email/account — some users have reportedly created a second account to re-verify. SheerID has strict ID-clarity rules and attempt limits. Some AI features (editor visual search) unavailable even to eligible education users. Education status ≠ paid-plan billing: nothing to pay, but you cannot buy seats or AI-credit add-ons on it.
findings.expiry: Higher ed / K-12 / high school: 2 years from verification, reapply when still enrolled/employed. Bootcamp: 6 months, renewable once for 6 more months.

findings.name: Figma for Education: Enterprise plan free (K-12 districts and schools)
findings.detail: K-12 districts/schools get Figma Enterprise at no cost (the top tier), plus the school-signed-terms route required for students under 13 (school must contact Figma and sign school terms; under-13 use is not available via self-serve). Includes Google Workspace for Education integration (admin-managed licensing via App Licensing System), Google Classroom FigJam add-on, and Microsoft Education SAML SSO auto-provisioning. Figma and Google bring Figma + FigJam to US Chromebooks free. Education account validity for K-12: 2 years, reapply to renew. Free bi-weekly live training and on-site PD sessions available on request.
findings.eligibility: K-12 schools/districts (US-focused integrations; program available in select regions). Teachers and students 13+ can self-serve via the high-school route at figma.com/education/apply; any class with students under 13 requires the school to contact Figma (form/form at figma.com/education/k-12, education@figma.com) and sign school terms. Non-teaching staff excluded.
findings.claim: 13+ students/teachers: figma.com/education/apply, select High School as institution type (K-12 educators selecting themselves use High School; district-wide deployment goes through the K-12 form). Under-13 classes: school submits the K-12 application form / emails education@figma.com, signs school terms; admins then deploy via Google/Microsoft integration. No credit card required.
findings.gotchas: K-12/high-school education teams do NOT get Figma Make, the AI agent, or Figma Sites (higher-ed/bootcamp only). Region-limited: Figma for Education 'is only available in select regions'. Under-13 route is manual and takes longer (school terms, COPPA/FERPA handling). Google/Microsoft SSO provisioning means the school domain controls who gets access — a domain swap or SSO change can lock users out.
findings.expiry: K-12 Education accounts valid 2 years, reapply to renew.

findings.name: Figma for Startups — no live free offer (program appears ended/paused)
findings.detail: As of today, Figma's own site has no startup program: figma.com/startups returns 404, the pricing page lists no startup offer, and the official pricing FAQ explicitly lists 'Early stage Startups' among who does NOT qualify for free Education teams, and states 'We do not have any discounts for non-profits. Anyone is welcome to use Figma's free plan.' Third-party trackers (checked Sep 13–Oct 14, 2026) mark the formerly partner-gated 'Figma for Startups' offer (free Organization plan for 24 months for VC-backed startups via accelerator-partner referral; other listings describe up to 1 year of Professional at 100% off, a 50% discount for 6 months, or up to ~$1,000 in credits/50% discounts) as 'paused' or 'No Longer Available', with the application form no longer found on any Figma-owned page. Figma is also no longer listed in the GitHub Student Developer Pack. Startups today can only use the free Starter plan (or buy Professional seats, full $16/mo / dev $12/mo / collab $3/mo).
findings.eligibility: No eligibility path exists on Figma's own pages as of 2026-10-22. The legacy program (now unavailable) required: VC/accelerator backing or approved-partner referral, new Figma Organization customer, application with funding caps (<$10M in older listings), no CC required. Figma's official FAQ explicitly excludes early-stage startups from the free education program, and Figma does not give startup age/funding caps because it does not run a startup program.
findings.claim: Not claimable: no application form exists on any Figma-owned page (figma.com/startups = 404). What remains: free Starter plan for the whole team (each person signs up free, no CC); check your accelerator/VC perk book, since the old offer was distributed only through partner referrals — if a partner still lists it, apply via that partner, but treat the current status as unverified.
findings.source_url: https://www.figma.com/pricing-faq/ (exclusions read today) + 404 at https://www.figma.com/startups; third-party status: https://perkbook.co/startup-programs/figma-for-startups/ ('No Longer Available') and https://guptadeepak.com/startup-offers/programs/figma-for-startups ('Paused', checked Sep 2026)
findings.gotchas: Aggregator sites (Drifting Desk, StartupIntros) still show it as 'Active' with outdated terms — those are stale third-party pages, not Figma; Figma's own pages govern. The org-tier free offer (~$45/editor/mo list price x 24 months) was historically the most generous tier; no Enterprise-tier coverage existed. If you build a product on a partner perk listing, verify the referral pipeline (accelerator/bank perk catalog) still works before relying on it.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 material changes: (1) September 5, 2025 — Figma Education plan update: Figma Make (AI) rolled out to the higher-ed Education plan; all higher-ed and high-school users were required to re-verify by Sept 29, 2025 or lose Professional features (teams downgraded to Starter: 3 files/1 project, 4+ files → view-only); bootcamp verification moved from self-verify to trusted-partner provider verification; bootcamp validity is 6 months with one 6-month extension. (2) Pricing restructure to a seat model (Full/Dev/Collab seats): Professional $16 full / $12 dev / $3 collab per month + 3,000/500/500 AI credits; Organization $55/$25/$5 annual; Enterprise $90/$35/$5 annual; Starter free with 500 AI credits/mo (150/day). This replaced the older flat per-editor pricing. (3) Time-boxed freebies being sunset: code layers free through November 4, 2026 (paid plans only; afterwards they consume AI credits); Figma Sites custom domains were free through 2025 with bandwidth/storage add-ons arriving 'in early 2026' — so education users' one-Site-allowance has no custom domain and paid tiers now face paid egress/domain extras. (4) Figma for Startups: ended/paused — figma.com/startups is a 404, no application form on any Figma-owned page as of Sep–Oct 2026 checks; third-party trackers mark it 'No Longer Available'/'Paused'; Figma's FAQ now explicitly excludes early-stage startups from free education teams. Legacy terms (for reference only): 24 months of the Organization plan free via accelerator partner referral, or up to $1,000 / 1 year Professional free / 50% off 6 months with <$10M funding caps. (5) GitHub Student Developer Pack no longer lists Figma among perks, so there is no third-party free Figma-Professional student channel. Not relevant but noted: a Figma for Government plan also exists (separate from education; not a student/startup offer).

provider: Microsoft — Founders Hub / Microsoft for Startups + university & education programs (verified 2026-10-22)

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups — Startup credits, milestone-based (the current Founders Hub program)
findings.detail: Read today (ms.date 2026-05-27): a single program now replaces the old Founders Hub tier system. You enter at Milestone 1 = up to $200 in Startup credits immediately after signing up for Azure + identity verification via a PERSONAL LinkedIn account. Milestone 2 = $5,000 after business verification (registered legal entity). Milestone 3 = $25,000 (5+ distinct Azure workloads each >= $1 spend, held ~60 continuous days; one-time 2-year credit-usage extension granted at this milestone). Milestone 4 = $50,000 (7 workloads, ~60 days). Milestone 5 = $150,000 (10+ workloads AND ~$3,000/month Azure spend sustained ~60 days). Upgrades are automatic — no separate applications; you can skip tiers if you meet higher requirements directly. The marketing page still advertises 'up to $150,000 in credits'.
findings.eligibility: Privately held, for-profit; software-based product owned by the company; HQ in a country where Azure is available; no more than $350,000 lifetime free Azure credits; NOT Series C funding or later (tightened from Series D in 2025); not an educational institution, government org, consultancy or agency; no crypto mining. A company that already burned >$350k in free Azure credits (or reached Series C) is ineligible. No .edu requirement; 'open to anyone with an idea' per the signup page.
findings.claim: 1) Go to startups.microsoft.com (Founders Hub) > Get started. 2) Submit application (personal LinkedIn at identity step). 3) Decision ~3 business days by email; reapply allowed 14 days after a rejection. 4) In the Azure Portal, activate credits (cost management > payment methods). 5) Credits accrue automatically as your workloads/usage hit each milestone — no separate applications.
findings.expiry: Activated credits are valid for up to 2 years from activation (per FAQ); no extensions except the one-time 2-year extension at the $25K milestone. You must activate within 90 days of accepting the program agreement or the offer lapses.
findings.gotchas: Credit card IS required to activate credits (identity verification + pay-as-you-go fallback). Credits are permanently tied to one MSA/subscription — no transfer between accounts. Pay-as-you-go kicks in automatically when credits run out. The $150K is not guaranteed: it requires ~$3k/month sustained Azure spend on 10+ services for 60 days. Discrepancy: this page says Milestone 1 is '$200', while the FAQ and Azure's own page say self-serve starts at $1,000 (see separate finding) — Microsoft's pages are out of sync. Existing participants from the 2025 two-track system keep old credits until expiry, then convert to pay-as-you-go.

findings.name: Azure for Startups self-serve credits ($1,000 instant, up to $5,000) — no application
findings.detail: Confirmed on two pages read today: 'Up to $5,000 in Azure credits: $1,000 available immediately, plus up to $4,000 more after verification'. Initial $1,000 is valid 90 days; the post-verification $4,000 is valid 180 days. No application required — just signup. This matches the pre-known 'self-serve Azure for Startups' offer. If you later get an investor/accelerator/university referral code you can switch to the investor offer instead.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers only. .edu not required. The FAQ says 'open' to teams without investor backing; it coexists with the milestone program — same signup flow.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at startups.microsoft.com or Azure's 'Azure for Startups' offer (link from azure.microsoft.com/free/students or the MFS portal). 2) $1,000 credits apply instantly to your new Azure subscription. 3) Complete business verification to unlock the additional $4,000. No application, no review queue for the self-serve tier.
findings.expiry: $1,000 valid 90 days from activation; $4,000 valid 180 days from business verification. After expiry: automatic conversion to pay-as-you-go.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required for identity verification and for spend beyond credits ('spending protection' only covers the card from unauthorized billing). Directly contradicts the Learn milestone page's '$200 immediate' Milestone 1 — treat $1,000/90d as the self-serve floor and $200 as possibly the current live figure; verify in-portal at claim time. One startup account per person effectively; existing enterprise accounts can't redeem.

findings.name: Microsoft for Startups Investor Network track (~$100,000+ Azure credits, referral-gated)
findings.detail: From the MFS FAQ read today: investor-backed startups enter with 'most startups begin with $100,000 [in Azure credits], with the opportunity to earn more' plus Azure Standard Support, technical experts, go-to-market support, and free/discounted third-party benefits: GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn Premium Business, Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Visual Studio Enterprise, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform. Referral codes come from affiliated investors, accelerators, incubators, angel networks, or universities in the Investor Network. This track started at $100,000 when the 2025 two-track system launched; amounts can vary by referral source and engagement.
findings.eligibility: Startup must be affiliated with a Microsoft for Startups Investor Network partner AND hold that partner's referral code. Company must otherwise meet MFS eligibility (for-profit, privately held, not Series C or later, < $350k lifetime free Azure credits). Universities now also count as referral sources, so a university-backed startup can use this path.
findings.claim: 1) Get a referral code from your affiliated investor/accelator/incubator/university. 2) Enter the code during the startups.microsoft.com application. 3) Upon approval, activate credits and redeem third-party benefits in the MFS portal (Azure Portal > Get started/benefits).
findings.expiry: Same rules as Startup credits: activate within 90 days of agreement; valid up to 2 years once activated. Third-party benefits (GitHub Enterprise etc.) have their own redemption windows.
findings.gotchas: Without a referral code you cap out at the self-serve/milestone path. Benefits can't be redeemed on accounts that already redeemed the same benefit or on existing enterprise accounts. Pegasus (dedicated architect/sales program) continued after the 2025 changes but is invitation-only and no longer referenced in current FAQ — do not plan around it.

findings.name: Azure Free Account (open to everyone, incl. students) — $200 trial + 12-month free services
