findings.detail: Read today at azure.microsoft.com/free: $200 credit usable within 30 days; free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months (e.g., 750 hrs each of B1s/B2pts v2/B2ats v2 VMs, 32 GB PostgreSQL/MySQL storage, 720 vCore-hrs SQL Managed Instance, 100 GB Container Registry, 5 GB Cloud Shell/Storage); plus 65+ always-free services (e.g., 0.5M Speech chars/mo, 500 pages/mo Document Intelligence, 50 MB AI Search, 5,000 Vision transactions/mo). One free account per person. Spending protection: card won't be billed while covered; $1 temporary authorization possible.
findings.eligibility: New Azure customers, worldwide (card policy varies: HK and Brazil accept only credit cards). Students can claim this too, but if you're a student the Azure for Students offer below is better (no card, annual renewal). Not for people who already have a paid Azure account.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at azure.microsoft.com/free with Microsoft account. 2) Add a phone number and a credit/debit card (non-prepaid). 3) $200 credit applies immediately; free monthly amounts auto-attach. 4) After 30 days you're notified to convert to pay-as-you-go or the account is disabled.
findings.expiry: $200 credit: 30 days (unused credit does not extend, even if you convert early). Free monthly service amounts: 12 months, then pay-as-you-go rates apply. Always-free tiers have no time limit but usage is capped.
findings.gotchas: Trial, not free: card required, and pay-as-you-go starts the moment the credit or the 12-month window ends. Free credit cannot be applied to Azure Marketplace offers, Spot VMs, or Hybrid Benefit. 6-month AI-services window previously advertised is no longer on the page — only the 12-month/always-free tiers are.

findings.name: Azure for Students — $100 credit for 12 months, no credit card (school email required)
findings.detail: Read today at azure.microsoft.com/free/students: $100 in Azure credit usable within 12 months, NO credit card required; free monthly amounts of 20+ popular services for 12 months plus 65+ always-free services; full service catalog up to free amounts; 'renew your subscription annually and continue to get free access to Azure as long as you're a student'. A 'Starter' tier for younger users gives free service access only (no credit). The GitHub Student Developer Pack also routes 18+ students to this $100 offer (ages 13–17 get a reduced service set instead: App Service, Functions, Notification Hubs, MySQL for apps, App Insights, DevOps).
findings.eligibility: Full-time university students; sign up with a school (.edu/institutional) email for verification. No card needed. One account per person. Age: the pack routes 13–17 to Starter; the $100 credit is for 18+. Third-party trackers (checked Oct 2026) list country restrictions — some regions only allow Starter; check the signup flow.
findings.claim: 1) Sign up at azure.microsoft.com/free/students using your school email (or via the 'Microsoft Azure' offer in the GitHub Student Developer Pack after verification). 2) Confirm student status. 3) $100 credit activates immediately; free service amounts attach. 4) Renew annually while enrolled.
findings.expiry: $100 credit valid 12 months from signup; annual renewal keeps the free services going while you remain a full-time student. 12-month free-service amounts reset with the renewal.
findings.gotchas: The $100 credit is the same offer the GitHub Pack grants — don't claim it twice (one Azure account per person; a second claim fails or voids the benefit). No card = no pay-as-you-go fallback: when the credit or free amounts run out, resources stop rather than bill you. Students who need more than free amounts should use the MFS self-serve $1,000 offer instead (which does need a card).

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack — free Microsoft/educator stack (GitHub + M365 + Azure + tools)
findings.detail: Verified today on education.github.com/pack: while verified as a student you get free GitHub Pro, free GitHub Copilot 'Student' plan (unlimited completions + monthly GitHub AI credits, limited chat/agent on auto-selected models), 3-month Microsoft 365 Education (Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Teams/1TB OneDrive — duration on the current page says 'free or discounted', historically 3 months), $100 Azure credit (18+), Namecheap free .me domain (1 year) + free SSL, Heroku $13/month for 24 months, free annual-renewable JetBrains licenses, and a GitHub Foundations/Copilot certification voucher via Microsoft Learn (resumed Sept 2025). Enrollment requires being 13+, in a degree/diploma program; under-18s get a reduced offer set.
findings.eligibility: Enrolled students: verify via school (.edu) email OR student ID + one proof-of-enrollment document (or a .edu email alone in some regions); 13+; some individual offers (Azure $100, Heroku) require 18+. No country limit stated for the pack itself.
findings.claim: 1) Apply at education.github.com/pack (or github.com/education) with school email or student ID. 2) Approval unlocks the pack page at github.com/features/benefits/students. 3) Redeem each partner offer individually (Azure, M365, Heroku, domain, etc.).
findings.expiry: Benefits last while you remain a verified student (GitHub Pro, M365, JetBrains renew annually/on graduation). Heroku credit: fixed 24 months. Domain/SSL: 1 year. Once you graduate, the pack stops renewing.
findings.gotchas: Partners churn: DigitalOcean ($200 credit) and Canva left the pack (DigitalOcean credits expire 2026-08-01), Bump.sh ended Dec 2025, Appwrite offer restructured to 6 months in Oct 2026. The Azure $100 in the pack IS the Azure for Students offer — one per person. 13–17-year-olds get no $100 credit, only a reduced service list.

findings.name: Microsoft 365 Education trial (30 days, schools) + free M365A license for institutions
findings.detail: Microsoft offers schools a free 30-day Microsoft 365 Education trial (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, OneDrive, Class Notebook/whiteboard, Copilot in education apps, no credit card) claimable by an institution admin, and a free Microsoft 365 A1 (M365A) license for eligible K-12 schools and universities — through which most university students already get M365A at no personal cost via their school. Individual students at non-licensed institutions can use the free Office web apps/Word/Excel at no charge. (Official Microsoft page served localized/JS content and timed out, so the trial details are from the well-known program terms rather than a page read today — hence medium confidence.)
findings.eligibility: Trial: K-12 and higher-ed institutions (admin-managed). Free M365A: eligible institutions (K-12 schools and universities in supported countries); individual students get it only through an institutional license. No .edu email needed to sign the school up for the trial.
findings.claim: 1) School: admin claims the 30-day trial from the M365 Education 'try it free' link on microsoft.com/en-us/education. 2) K-12: apply for the free M365A K-12 license via the Microsoft Education Store/partner flow. 3) Students: ask IT for the school's M365A license, or use free Office web apps with any email.
findings.gotchas: The trial is school-scoped, not individual: a 'free M365 for me' student offer does not exist standalone — students ride on institutional licenses or free web apps. Teams Education and Power Platform for Education trial similarly (30 days, institution-scoped).

findings.name: Azure AI / Microsoft Foundry always-free tiers (available to students and startups alike)
findings.detail: From the Azure Free and Azure for Students pages read today: monthly always-free AI service amounts included with any free/12-month account: Azure Speech in Foundry Tools 0.5M neural characters/month; Document Intelligence 500 pages/month (S0); AI Search 50 MB storage (10k docs, 3 indexes); Vision in Foundry Tools 5,000 transactions/month per S1-S3 tier; Content Safety 5,000 text records or images/month; Azure DevOps free for 5 users; PostgreSQL/MySQL serverless free tiers. These stack on top of credit programs — useful for AI workloads while credits burn out.
findings.eligibility: Any Azure account; free monthly amounts are new-customer 12 months (VMs/databases) or perpetual (always-free services). Students with no card still get these via Azure for Students.
findings.claim: No separate claim — free amounts auto-attach to eligible Azure services; monitor usage in Cost Management to stay under caps.
findings.expiry: Always-free: perpetual. 12-month amounts: until 12 months from account creation, then standard pricing.
findings.gotchas: Usage above the free amounts bills at normal rates (with no card, it just throttles/stops). Large AI inference (e.g., LLM tokens) is NOT in the always-free list — paid per token even in Foundry; budget accordingly.

sunset_notes: 1) July 1, 2025 (announced June 27, 2025): the classic Founders Hub multi-tier program (apply-then-upgrade to $100 → $5,000 → $25,000 → $150,000 with business-plan validation) was RETIRED and replaced by a two-track system: Investor Network track ($100,000+ starting credits, referral from affiliated investors/accelerators) and a self-serve track ($1,000 for 90 days + $4,000 for 180 days after business verification, cap $5,000 without investor affiliation). Existing activated credits of old participants stayed valid until expiry; unfunded participants' accounts converted to pay-as-you-go after expiry. Pegasus (invitation-only, dedicated Cloud Solutions Architect) continued but out of the new funnel. 2) 2026 restructure (MFS 2.0, docs dated May 2026): the program was rebranded 'Microsoft for Startups' with a single entry and automatic milestone upgrades: $200 immediate → $5,000 → $25,000 → $50,000 → $150,000, with the $150K tier gated on 10+ concurrent workloads and ~$3,000/month sustained Azure spend. Eligibility also tightened: funding cap moved from 'not Series D or later' to 'not Series C or later', and a $350,000 lifetime-free-Azure-credits cap was added. So the oft-quoted 'no funding required, up to $150K' is now true only in the narrow sense that early stages need no funding, but Series C+ companies are excluded and $150K requires heavy sustained Azure spend. 3) Legacy partner credits from the old Founders Hub ($2,500 OpenAI, Databricks, Twilio $10,000, Atlassian, etc.) are no longer listed in the current FAQ (read today); the signup-page snapshot still showed 'up to $150,000 in Azure credits, plus $2,500 of OpenAI credits' — treat OpenAI/Databricks/Twilio partner credits as unconfirmed/sunset unless shown in-portal; current investor-track benefits are GitHub Enterprise, LinkedIn Premium Business, M365 Business Premium, Visual Studio Enterprise, Dynamics 365, Power Platform. 4) GitHub Student Developer Pack: DigitalOcean's $200 credit offer left the pack (credits expire 2026-08-01); Bump.sh offer ended 2025-12-09; Appwrite restructured to 6 months (2026-10-02); GitHub Foundations certification voucher was paused 2025-10-25 then resumed 2025-09-30. 5) The Azure Free page no longer advertises the old '6 months free AI services' window — only 12-month free amounts and always-free tiers.

provider: AWS (Amazon Web Services) — Free Plan & Educate/Startup programs

findings.claim: 1) Create an AWS account, select Free plan (default). 2) $100 credit appears on the Credits page (up to 10 minutes to show). 3) Complete the five 'Explore AWS' activities in the AWS Management Console Home widget to earn up to $100 more. 4) Monitor balance/days remaining via the Cost & Usage widget or Settings Portal (new sign-up experience) / Credits page in Billing console (pre-Oct-2026 sign-ups). 5) Upgrade to Paid plan to continue after expiry.
findings.detail: As of the July 15, 2025 revamp (current structure, verified today): new customers get $100 in credits immediately on sign-up and can earn up to $100 more (5 console activities worth $20 each: launch an EC2 instance, create an RDS database, build a Lambda web app, try a Bedrock foundation model, set an AWS Budgets cost budget). Free plan = access to 90+ select services for up to 6 months with no charges and no surprise overages; you cannot exceed limits — remaining credits auto-apply. Upgrade to Paid plan any time; on the old sign-up experience unused credits stay usable up to 12 months from sign-up, but under the new sign-up experience (launched Oct 2026) the FAQ states Free Tier credits expire 6 months from account creation. Free plan accounts auto-enroll at account creation.
findings.eligibility: New AWS customers only (an existing or previously-had AWS account makes you ineligible). No .edu email or student status required — open to anyone worldwide. Credit card NOT required for most new customers (FAQ Q4: 'A payment method isn't required to sign up for most new customers. In some cases, we may request additional information, such as a payment method, to verify your identity'). NOT available in China (ZHY/Ningxia, BJS) regions or AWS GovCloud (US) regions (certain services such as Lambda excepted). Free plan + credits are NOT available through AWS Organizations: enrolling a Free plan account in Organizations upgrades it to Paid, and an Organization can benefit from offers via only one account (usage aggregated).
findings.expiry: Free plan expires at the earlier of 6 months from account creation or credit exhaustion (cannot be extended). After expiry AWS suspends the account and resources; data is retained 90 days, then the account and all content are permanently erased unless upgraded within 90 days. Credits expire 6 months from account creation on the new sign-up experience (FAQ); 12 months per the July 2025 Free Tier Terms for earlier sign-ups.
findings.gotchas: Suspended after expiry — move data/projects before the 90-day window or lose them. Free plan is 'evaluation only' per terms (sensitive data processing disallowed). Credits can't be transferred to other accounts. AWS may reclaim resources after 3 months of inactivity with 30 days' notice. Unused monthly free amounts don't roll over. Activating paid-only services upgrades you to Paid plan (bills on pay-as-you-go beyond credits). EC2/RDS/S3/API Gateway on new accounts are no longer fixed monthly free allowances — they consume the $200 credit pool; new free-plan-eligible EC2 types: t3.micro, t3.small, t4g.micro, t4g.small, c7i-flex.large, m7i-flex.large (t2.micro is legacy only).
findings.name: AWS Free Tier — Free Plan: up to $200 credits, 6 months, no charges

findings.claim: Automatic once you have an AWS account; no application.
findings.detail: All AWS customers (new and existing, Free and Paid plans) get over 30 'Always Free' services with monthly usage caps; usage is aggregated across all regions; excess usage automatically applies Free Tier credits (Free plan) or bills at standard on-demand rates (Paid plan). Representative always-free caps (per service docs and community verification, not all published on the /free/ page itself): Lambda 1M requests + 400,000 GB-seconds; DynamoDB 25 GB + 25 provisioned RCU / 5 WCU; SQS 1M requests; SNS 1M publishes; CloudWatch 10 custom metrics + 10 alarms + 1M API requests; CloudFront 1 TB data transfer out.
findings.eligibility: Any AWS customer — no .edu, no student status, no credit card required for the account itself. Available in regions where AWS operates (Always Free offers are region-broader than the Free Plan credits, which exclude China and GovCloud).
findings.expiry: No expiry while you hold an AWS account; monthly limits reset each month with no rollover. AWS may terminate any offer at any time.
findings.gotchas: Data transfer out (egress) beyond CloudFront's 1 TB and inter-region traffic are billable; paid add-on features auto-bill on Paid plans; individual service caps vary — check each service's pricing page before heavy use. The per-service figures above are medium-confidence (sourced from the EC2 docs and builder-community summaries, since the /free/ page lists service tiles without caps).
findings.name: AWS Free Tier — 30+ Always Free services (all customers, indefinite)

findings.claim: Activate the trial service from the console; track the trial end date yourself — AWS does not always notify when a trial ends.
findings.detail: Selected Paid-plan services can be 'tried' with limited free trials; the trial begins when you activate the service, and any eligible Free Tier credits automatically apply to usage beyond trial limits. Some offers are limited in duration or free-usage amount; on a Free plan, activating a paid-only service upgrades the account to Paid plan.
findings.eligibility: New AWS customers (per-service trials listed on aws.amazon.com/free/); no .edu required; same region caveats (Free Plan credits unavailable in China/GovCloud).
findings.expiry: Per-service trial windows; AWS may end any offer at any time.
findings.gotchas: Trial vs Always Free confusion: trial periods end and pay-as-you-go billing starts without a notification in some cases — delete trial resources before expiry. Egress/data-transfer and public IPv4 charges ($0.005/hr) commonly surprise trial users.
findings.name: AWS Free Tier — short-term trials on selected Paid-plan services

findings.claim: 1) Register at the AWS Educate sign-up page (promo code 'EducateLP' referenced on the page) or sign in to AWS Educate. 2) Choose a learning path (Cloud 101 recommended for new-to-cloud). 3) Complete labs/courses. 4) Claim digital badges on Credly. 5) Job board access at 18+.
findings.detail: Free, self-paced online cloud training 'designed for beginners': hundreds of hours of content incl. Getting Started with Storage (S3), Compute (EC2), Networking (VPC), Databases (RDS), and Cloud Operations + cost-estimation labs, a Cloud 101 pathway, and a Cloud Literacy interactive badge. Includes free hands-on labs in a sandboxed AWS Console environment (time-boxed, unlimited retries), shareable Credly digital badges, an invitation to the AWS Emerging Talent Community, and an AWS Educate Job Board (18+) with in-demand jobs and internships. No dollar-denominated AWS cloud credits — it is a learning program, not a credit grant.
findings.eligibility: Open to any individual regardless of education, experience, or career journey — NO .edu email or university affiliation required. Register with just an email address; no credit card needed. Minimum age: 'as young as 13' per the current page; the Educate FAQ says 14+ generally, with EU 16+; Algeria, Lebanon, Portugal 18+; not offered in China or Switzerland.
findings.expiry: No expiry; content and lab time limits update over time; lab attempts are time-boxed but retries are unlimited.
findings.gotchas: Labs run on shared sandboxes, not your own AWS account (does not stack with your Free Tier account). No monetary credits. Employer direct-messaging on the job board is US-only per the FAQ. Age minimum varies by country (higher in EU and some regions than the '13+' marketing). No certification exam included — AWS certifications remain paid (see AWS Academy vouchers).
findings.name: AWS Educate — free self-paced curriculum, hands-on labs, badges, job board

findings.claim: 1) Open AWS Skill Builder and sign in or create a free AWS Builder ID. 2) Enroll in any free digital course. 3) Score >=80% on the assessment to earn a badge. 4) Claim the badge via Credly.
findings.detail: AWS's Training FAQ: 'Self-paced digital training on AWS Skill Builder is free.' Free digital training includes 500+ on-demand courses in 17 languages (the /training/ page markets '600+ free digital courses'); free digital badges (knowledge, Cloud Quest) earned at >=80% on the associated assessment, claimable on Credly. Paid Individual/Team subscriptions add more content and labs; free webinars/Twitch training events also exist, while classroom training and certification exams cost money.
findings.eligibility: Anyone — no .edu or student status; sign in with a free AWS Builder ID (or APN credentials / company Team subscription if an org member). No credit card.
findings.expiry: No stated expiry for free access; subscription content changes with plans.
findings.gotchas: Only part of Skillbuilder is free — advanced lab-heavy content is behind paid Individual/Team subscriptions; certification exams are paid (vouchers only via AWS Academy pathways); don't confuse free digital badges with paid AWS certification badges.
findings.name: AWS Skillbuilder — 500-600+ free self-paced digital training courses

findings.claim: 1) Create a personal AWS Builder ID with a professional email. 2) Complete the AWS Activate profile. 3) Choose the Founders package. 4) Submit company/product/funding details (accurate info required; inaccuracies can be denied). 5) Link an AWS account and submit; decision in 7-10 business days by email, trackable in the console.
findings.detail: For self-funded, early-stage startups new to AWS Activate Credits: $1,000 USD in AWS credits (per AWS's gaming-startups page: 'Start with $1,000 USD in Activate Credits. Select participants may qualify for additional credits up to $5,000'). Credits redeem on 200+ eligible AWS services incl. third-party foundation models on Amazon Bedrock. Also includes technical support, business mentorship, co-build/co-market/go-to-market resources, free pre-built cloud templates, AWS Startup Advisor, AWS Support Plans eligible for credits, and access to 80+ third-party offers. New customers also get the AWS Free Tier when creating a new account.
findings.eligibility: Startup program — NOT an education/.edu program (student-founded startups can apply as startups). Criteria: self-funded (or pre-Series B per AWS's June 2026 guide), founded in the past 10 years, a fully functioning company website or public company profile, new to Activate Credits (or requesting more than previously received), and a business email matching the company domain. No student-specific grant exists.
findings.expiry: Credits are subject to the AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions (fixed validity from grant, not re-stated on these pages); not renewable at the same value without a larger request.
findings.gotchas: Without a functioning startup/website you won't qualify. AWS has final say; website professionalism is weighted heavily. Credits don't cover Marketplace third-party services, Route 53 domain registration/transfer, most support tiers, or Professional Services (except Bedrock third-party model charges). AWS offers generally not available in China regions.
findings.name: AWS Activate — Founders package: $1,000 credits (select participants up to $5,000)

findings.claim: 1) Enroll in a program with an AWS Activate Provider and get their Org ID/invitation. 2) Create an AWS Builder ID + complete the AWS Activate profile. 3) Choose the Portfolio package with your Org ID. 4) Submit details; link an AWS account; decision in 7-10 business days.
findings.detail: For startups affiliated with an AWS Activate Provider (accelerator, VC, incubator, or partner org — e.g., Y Combinator, a16z, nVIDIA, Carta): up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits per the main /startups/ page and AWS's June 4, 2026 step-by-step guide ('The Activate Portfolio tier offers up to $200,000 in AWS Activate Credits for provider-backed startups'); AI startups ready to scale can get additional credits beyond $200,000 via their Account Manager. Also: 80+ exclusive third-party offers/memberships valued up to $800,000, dedicated account managers, and solutions architects. Note: the /free/offers/ comparison page still lists the range as '$1,000 to $100,000' with eligibility 'funded up to and including Series A' — the $200k / pre-Series-B figures come from AWS's newer 2026 pages, indicating the cap and funding stage were raised in 2025-2026.
findings.eligibility: Must hold an Organizational ID from an AWS Activate Provider; pre-Series B (most recent funding round within the last 12 months, if applicable); founded in the past 10 years; a fully functioning company website; business email; must be new to Activate Credits or requesting more than previously received. Not open to direct application — provider affiliation is mandatory. No .edu/student path.
findings.expiry: Per the AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions (fixed validity from grant).
findings.gotchas: Provider gatekeeping (AWS has final say and gets pickier above $5,000). Official AWS pages conflict today on the cap: $100k on /free/offers/ vs $200k on /startups/ and the June 2026 guide — treat 'up to $200,000' as the current advertised max and verify at application. Legacy sub-tiers ($5k/$10k/$25k/$100k; YC's up to $250k) are no longer publicly listed.
findings.name: AWS Activate — Portfolio package: up to $200,000 credits (provider-backed)

findings.claim: 1) Institution applies to join AWS Academy (or is added to an existing membership). 2) CPOC nominates educators; educators complete the mandatory Getting Started course. 3) Educators teach courses; students use Learner Labs. 4) Educators/students claim exam discount vouchers per program rules.
findings.detail: AWS Academy 'provides higher education institutions with a free, ready-to-teach cloud computing curriculum' (aligned to AWS certifications) plus Learner Labs. FAQ: 'There is no cost to join.' Educators may request a 100% discount voucher on AWS certification exam cost; member institutions may request a 50% discount exam voucher that students redeem at 100% of the voucher's value; students in badge-eligible courses earn Emerging Talent Community points redeemable for rewards such as discounted AWS certification exam vouchers. This is AWS's closest university-scoped free offer.
findings.eligibility: Institutional, not individual: accredited higher-education institution offering degrees, diplomas, certificates, or continuing-ed programs, with an authorized Program Administrator or Central Point of Contact (CPOC). No .edu-email-only rule, but institutional membership is required; individual students/educators can't self-enroll.
findings.expiry: No expiry while the institution remains a member; voucher/reward programs are 'subject to change' per the FAQ.
findings.gotchas: Vouchers discount exam fees only — they are not AWS usage credits. Institutional onboarding can be slow; the free value to students is mainly the curriculum, labs, and exam discounts — hands-on AWS usage still comes from the regular Free Tier (which needs no Academy affiliation).
findings.name: AWS Academy — free participation for accredited higher-education institutions (+ exam vouchers)

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes (verified against official AWS pages on 2026-10-22): (1) Classic 12-month Free Tier sunset for NEW accounts on July 15, 2025 — replaced by the credit-based Free Plan ($100 + up to $100 earned = up to $200 over 6 months, auto-enrolled, no charges); accounts created before July 15, 2025 remain on legacy 12-month terms (750 hrs/mo t2/t3.micro etc.); legacy terms still published. (2) October 2026: AWS launched a new sign-up experience; the current FAQ now states Free Tier credits expire 6 months from account creation (vs 12 months under the July 2025 Free Tier Terms) and moved credit tracking to the Settings Portal — AWS's own FAQ is internally inconsistent between sections (6 vs 12 months), so treat credit expiry on the new experience as 6 months and verify per-account in the Settings Portal. (3) AWS Activate restructured in 2025-2026: old tiers (Starter $5k / Portfolio up to $100k / YC up to $250k / $5k-$100k sub-tiers) are no longer publicly listed; current structure is Founders ($1,000, up to $5,000 for select participants) + Portfolio (up to $200,000, cap raised from $100,000), with eligibility shifted from 'funded up to Series A' to 'pre-Series B, most recent funding round within the last 12 months', and the application flow now goes through the AWS Builder ID. AWS pages are inconsistent today: /free/offers/ still advertises '$1,000 to $100,000' while /startups/ and the June 4, 2026 AWS blog advertise 'up to $200,000'. (4) No education-only (.edu/student-email) free credits exist at AWS: no free offer requires a .edu or student email — AWS Educate is open to anyone 13/14+ with just an email, the Free Tier is open to any new customer, and AWS Marketplace 'education pricing' is a paid discount, not free. The only university-scoped free offer is AWS Academy (free institution participation + exam vouchers). (5) Free Plan/credits unavailable in China (ZHY, BJS) and GovCloud (US) regions, and not usable via AWS Organizations (auto-upgrades to Paid plan). (6) AWS Educate availability excludes China and Switzerland and raises minimum age in the EU (16) and Algeria/Lebanon/Portugal (18).

findings.claim: Sign in at github.com/settings/education/benefits -> Start a student application -> submit enrollment proof -> on approval the account is switched to Pro and benefits activate automatically.
findings.detail: The full personal GitHub Pro plan is free for the duration of student status. Current official limits per docs.github.com product-usage reference (fetched 2026-10-22): 3,000 GitHub Actions minutes/month, 180 GitHub Codespaces core hours/month + 20 GB Codespaces storage, 10 GB Git LFS, unlimited private repos, and Pro security/advanced features. No credit card required. NOTE: older 2024-25 materials state 5,000 Actions minutes and 50 GB Codespaces storage; those no longer match the current docs.
findings.eligibility: GitHub personal account + verified student status: enrolled in a degree-/diploma-granting program (high school, college, university, or homeschool), minimum age 13, proof of enrollment (school ID with current date, class schedule, transcript, or enrollment letter). A .edu/academic email is required only at schools where GitHub has detected recent applicants verified via academic email; otherwise documents suffice. Not a one-off trial — recurring benefit tied to student status.
findings.expiry: Student validation lasts 2 years, then re-validation is required; access lapses when no longer a verified student. Some sub-benefits (e.g. Copilot) are re-evaluated monthly.
findings.gotchas: Verify the current Actions figure (docs show 3,000/min, not 5,000). Excess Actions/Codespaces/LFS become metered pay-as-you-go. Teachers/educators are NOT eligible for this (separate teacher benefit). No-credit-card applies to the GitHub-side Pro tier.
findings.name: Free GitHub Pro plan (core student benefit)

findings.claim: Activated automatically with the free Pro plan; create/launch a codespace at github.com > Codespaces. Set a budget/stop-usage limit to avoid overage.
findings.detail: Pro-tier Codespaces included with the free Pro plan: 180 core hours/month and 20 GB storage (vs 120 core hours + 15 GB on the standalone Free plan). 'Core hours' is the post-2025 name for what was called 'premium hours'. Overage billed at compute rates from ~$0.18/hour (2-core) and storage ~$0.07/GB-month.
findings.eligibility: Same verified-student status as the free Pro plan. No credit card required for the included allowance.
findings.expiry: Allowance resets monthly; lapses when student status lapses.
findings.gotchas: Long-running, high-CPU, or large-storage codespaces burn through 180 core hours quickly and then cost real money (compute + egress/storage). '50 GB storage' from older sources is not current (docs show 20 GB).
findings.name: GitHub Codespaces (Pro tier, free for students)

findings.claim: github.com/settings/education/benefits -> Copilot 'Learn more' -> enable; do NOT complete a purchase (docs warn 'if only paid options appear, do not complete a purchase').
findings.detail: Copilot's premium features free for verified students: unlimited code completions plus a monthly allowance of GitHub AI Credits for chat/agent features and premium models. Pro-equivalent tier = 1,500 AI credits/month (1,000 base + 500 flex; 1 AI credit = $0.01 USD). Verified teachers and popular-OSS maintainers also get free Copilot Pro (same 1,500 credits). No credit card required; GitHub re-evaluates eligibility monthly. Note: 2025 restructure renamed the billing unit from 'premium requests' to 'GitHub AI credits' and added Pro+ ($39, 7,000 cr) and Max ($100, 20,000 cr) tiers; Pro is $10/month if not a student/teacher.
findings.eligibility: GitHub Education verified student (13+). No CC required. Separate from the general Free Copilot plan (Free = 2,000 completions/month, limited models).
findings.expiry: Tied to verified student status; eligibility re-evaluated monthly.
findings.gotchas: Completions are unlimited but chat/agent usage is capped by AI credits; the exact student-plan credit cap mirrors Pro (1,500) but the plans doc does not print a separate student number, so treat the exact student credit figure as medium-confidence.
findings.name: GitHub Copilot Student plan (free, Pro-equivalent)

findings.claim: Included automatically with the free Pro plan; no separate claim.
findings.detail: 3,000 GitHub Actions minutes/month included on the free Pro plan (vs 2,000 on the standalone Free plan; 50,000 on Enterprise). Public-repository runs are free/unlimited on Free; private-repo runs draw down the allowance. Overage is metered.
findings.eligibility: Verified student via free Pro plan. No CC required for included minutes.
findings.expiry: Resets monthly.
findings.gotchas: Current docs = 3,000 minutes, NOT the 5,000 assumed in the task's 'known so far'. Self-hosted runners have separate usage rules.
findings.name: GitHub Actions minutes (free, via Pro)

findings.claim: Pages available automatically; create a classroom at classrooms.github.com.
findings.detail: GitHub Pages free hosting: one user site per account/org plus unlimited project sites. GitHub Classroom is free for students and for verified teachers/educators to run courses and assignments.
findings.eligibility: Any GitHub account for Pages; verified student/teacher for Classroom. No CC required.
findings.expiry: Ongoing while account exists.
findings.gotchas: Pages traffic has fair-use limits and very high bandwidth can be metered/billed.
findings.name: GitHub Pages + GitHub Classroom (free)

findings.claim: github.com/settings/education/benefits -> apply as a teacher/educator.
findings.detail: Verified teachers/educators get: free GitHub Team (Teams) plan with unlimited users + private repositories; free GitHub Classroom; free GitHub Copilot Pro (~1,500 AI credits/month); plus a swag bag and access to education events. Teachers/faculty/staff are explicitly NOT eligible for the Student Developer Pack — this is the separate teacher track.
findings.eligibility: Verified teacher/educator status (in-class instructor or higher-ed faculty/staff). No CC required on the GitHub side.
findings.expiry: Tied to educator verification; re-validate periodically. No explicit duration stated on the doc page.
findings.gotchas: Team plan is org/teaching-scoped; no student-pack partner perks on this track.
findings.name: GitHub Education for teachers (free Team + free Copilot Pro)

findings.claim: settings/education/benefits -> Start an application (student) -> complete form -> Submit -> on approval, partner offers appear to claim individually.
findings.detail: The GitHub Student Developer Pack = 80+ resources (the 2026 catalog lists ~73 partner offers) PLUS the free GitHub Pro tier. Eligibility: enrolled in a degree-/diploma-granting program (high school to university, incl. homeschool), proof of enrollment, personal GitHub account, minimum age 13; some partner offers add their own age limits. Claim at github.com/settings/education/benefits. Student validation lasts 2 years then re-validation. Offers may not be redeemed more than once and partners may not 'stack' with a prior free trial. Third-party terms are between the student and the partner.
findings.eligibility: .edu/academic email only where GitHub detects recent school-level email verification; otherwise acceptable documents (school ID w/ current date, class schedule, transcript, or enrollment letter). No credit card required for GitHub-side benefits.
findings.expiry: 2-year student validation, then re-verify. Each partner offer has its own duration (from 1 week to 'while a student' to 'free forever').
findings.gotchas: Cannot re-claim an expired partner offer by making a new account/re-verifying. A partner free trial already used can block the pack version of that offer. Third-party partners can change offers; GitHub has no liability for partner products.
findings.name: Pack eligibility, claiming, and renewal (meta)

findings.claim: Via the pack partner link (Microsoft/Azure student portal) using your verified GitHub student account.
findings.detail: In the 2026 pack: 'Microsoft Azure (18+)': $100 Azure credit + 25+ cloud services, while a student, NO credit card. A separate '13-17' tier offers a limited set of Azure services (App Service, Functions, Notification Hubs, MySQL, App Insights, Azure DevOps) with no credit card. Also Microsoft 365 (productivity apps + 1 TB cloud storage) while a student.
findings.eligibility: Verified student; 18+ for the $100 credit tier, 13-17 tier separate. No CC required.
findings.expiry: While a student; credit offers carry partner expiry terms.
findings.gotchas: Some Azure services are region-limited; unused credit can lapse. No-CC applies to the $100 student offer.
findings.name: Microsoft Azure for Students (partner)

findings.claim: Via the pack partner link (Microsoft Dev Essentials).
findings.detail: 1-year offer: VS Community + Pluralsight training + '1 free year of Azure services with $200 credit for the 1st month'. The '$200' figure in older pack versions maps to this Dev Essentials Azure-credit offer (distinct from the $100 'Azure for Students' credit).
findings.eligibility: Verified student; some elements 18+. No CC required for the credit component.
findings.expiry: 1 year.
findings.gotchas: Distinguish the $200 Dev Essentials first-month credit from the $100 'Azure for Students' credit — they are two separate lines in the pack.
findings.name: Visual Studio Dev Essentials (partner, ~$200 first-month credit)

findings.claim: Via the pack partner link (MongoDB).
findings.detail: $50 in MongoDB Atlas credits, plus access to MongoDB Compass and MongoDB University (free certification, ~$150 value), while a student.
findings.eligibility: Verified student.
findings.expiry: While a student.
findings.gotchas: Credit is for Atlas usage; separate signup with MongoDB required.
findings.name: MongoDB Atlas (partner)

findings.claim: Via the pack partner link (Heroku).
findings.detail: Heroku at $13 USD/month for 24 months (a long discounted 'student' tier offered through the pack).
findings.eligibility: Verified student.
findings.expiry: 24 months.
findings.gotchas: Not fully free — it is a fixed low monthly rate for 24 months, so there is ongoing cost after the discount window unless cancelled.
findings.name: Heroku (partner)

findings.claim: Via the pack partner links (Namecheap / Name.com / .TECH).
findings.detail: Namecheap: 1-year free .me domain + 1 free SSL certificate. Name.com: a free domain from 25+ TLDs (.live, .studio, .software, .app, .dev) while enrolled. .TECH: one free .TECH domain for 1 year.
findings.eligibility: Verified student.
findings.expiry: Domain free period is 1 year (renewal after that is paid).

findings.name: Claude for Startups program (credits + VC top-up)
findings.detail: Program members access 'discounts and credits worth up to $45,000 from companies building with Claude' (offers from AI-native vendors across sales, design, data, meetings, engineering; each redeemed with a code in the Claude Console). Founders backed by a VC in Anthropic's partner network may receive up to $100K in ADDITIONAL first-party API credits, claimed through their VC. Members also get biweekly Applied AI webinars/AMAs and invites to Claude Startup events/hackathons.
findings.eligibility: Early-stage founders. Page states no explicit company-age cap, funding ceiling, minimum team size, .edu requirement, or region limit. The $100K is gated to founders whose VC is in the Anthropic partner network. CURRENT COHORT IS CLOSED: 'our current cohort is now full, and we're not accepting new applications right now' as of today.
findings.claim: Non-members: subscribe to the Claude Startup newsletter to be alerted when the next cohort opens. Existing members: sign in via Claude Console at platform.claude.com/claude-for-startups. The $100K VC credit is claimed through the VC, not the general application.
findings.expiry: No published expiry/validity window for member credits. Benefits run on a membership/cohort basis. Upcoming dated event: Claude Founder House, San Francisco, Oct 6-8, 2026.
findings.gotchas: Credits apply ONLY to the first-party Claude API via Claude Console and CANNOT be used on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or other third-party platforms. The program is cohort-based and applications are currently closed (must wait for the next opening). Trial-style, membership-gated, not a self-serve signup.

findings.name: Claude.ai Free tier (consumer, no startup needed)
findings.detail: Free Claude account: $0, 'Free for everyone'. Includes chat on web/desktop/mobile, web search, file creation, code execution, memory, Artifacts, Design, Slides, Docs. Projects capped at up to 5. Available models on Free: Sonnet and Haiku only (no Opus).
findings.eligibility: Everyone (no account prerequisites). No .edu required, no startup status required. No credit card required (listed 'n/a').
findings.claim: Sign up at claude.ai; select the Free plan.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; not a time-limited trial. Standard per-model usage limits apply (no fixed message count published; Anthropic links to a usage-limit-best-practices article).
findings.gotchas: No Opus access on Free. Distinct from the paid Pro ($17-20/mo) and Max ($100+/mo) plans which DO require a credit card. Consumer chat product, not API access.

findings.name: API free / trial credits
findings.detail: There is NO free API tier and NO standalone free API trial credits listed on the official pricing page today. API access is pay-as-you-go (e.g., Sonnet input $2/MTok, output $10/MTok). The $45K startup credits and the 'Team plan for scientists' are the free-ish routes to API usage.
findings.eligibility: API requires a paid account / credit card. Free API use is only via the startup program credits or the scientist plan.
findings.claim: Create an account in Claude Console (platform.claude.com) with a payment method; to use API without paying, qualify for the Claude for Startups program or the Team plan for scientists.
findings.expiry: n/a (no free tier to expire).
findings.gotchas: New API accounts need a card and are billed usage (data/egress/token costs apply). Anthropic historically offered a small free API trial credit for new accounts; that is NOT listed on the official pricing page as of 2026-10-22, so do not assume a fresh sign-up gives free API credit.

findings.name: Claude Team plan for scientists (free academic/nonprofit research seats)
findings.detail: Standard Team seats at $0/month (list $20; annual $0/$180 per seat); Premium seats $15/month (list $100). '10,000 scientists around the world can now get Claude at no cost to start.' 1-25 seats per group (contact for larger); Premium adds 5x usage; extra usage via the AI for Science grant program.
findings.eligibility: Principal investigators (or equivalent) at ACCREDITED UNIVERSITIES and NONPROFIT research institutes in natural sciences, math, CS, engineering and related fields. For-profit companies, CROs, and industry R&D teams are EXCLUDED.
findings.claim: Verify institutional affiliation at the 'Verify now' attestation link; confirm affiliation + brief research description; most applications reviewed within 5-7 business days; on approval admins add seats.
findings.expiry: Promotional $0 pricing lasts 12 months from sign-up, then seats renew at the then-current plan price; inactivity for 90 days may return the group to standard Team pricing; 'promotional pricing is not guaranteed, given limited availability.' No calendar dates published.
findings.gotchas: Requires an accredited-university / nonprofit-researcher affiliation (institutional, not just any .edu personal email). Cap on 10,000 scientists and limited availability. Renewal ends the free window after 12 months.

findings.name: Claude for Teachers (free K-12 educator access)
findings.detail: US K-12 educators and districts get FREE access to premium Claude features (teaching skills, evidence-based-curriculum connectors aligned to state standards, e.g., Learning Commons). Individual teacher account: free, premium features, extra usage limits apply, no numeric cap published. District tier: centrally managed accounts with RBAC/SSO, K-12 privacy agreement.
findings.eligibility: US K-12 educators and school/district leaders. Verified via claude.ai/teachers (individual) or claude.ai/k12districts (districts). US-focused.
findings.claim: Teachers: 'Verify now' -> claude.ai/teachers. Schools/districts: 'Get started' -> claude.ai/k12districts.
findings.expiry: Sign up by June 30, 2027 for a full year of free access; terms/price subject to change at Anthropic's discretion afterward.
findings.gotchas: US-only K-12. 'Extra usage limits apply' (no published numbers). Free annual window is tied to the June 30, 2027 sign-up deadline. Privacy: model training off by default for verified educators; FERPA/AFT Gold Standard oriented.

findings.name: Education / university license (institutional, not free self-serve)
findings.detail: A 'comprehensive university-wide plan' covering students, faculty, and staff at discounted (institutional) rates, with dedicated API credits and educational features for student learning, plus training/enablement. No specific dollar discount/seat count/percentage published; it routes to 'Contact our Education team' (/contact-sales/education-plan). Named partners include Dartmouth, UVA, U Pittsburgh, Northeastern, Syracuse, LSE, Champlain, Northumbria, USF.
findings.eligibility: Institutions purchasing an education plan (the .edu/affiliation benefit is institutional, not an individual free claim flow). No self-serve .edu sign-up or free student tier is offered on these pages.
findings.claim: Institution contacts the Anthropic Education team via /contact-sales/education-plan; there is no individual student free-claim flow.
findings.expiry: No published expiry. Ongoing commercial offer.
findings.gotchas: NOT a free self-serve license — it is a paid institutional plan (discounted), so it is not a free offer in the same sense as the Free tier or the scientist/teacher plans. No student-per-seat free access is published.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22 the Claude for Startups program has changed materially from its 2024-2025 form: it is now run in cohorts, and the current cohort is FULL with no new applications accepted, so the $45K/$100K credits are only claimable when the next cohort opens (newsletter sign-up is the only current action). No program is sunset, but two notes: (1) The Claude API no longer lists a standalone free trial-credit offer for new accounts on the official pricing page — free API usage is only via the startup credits or the Team plan for scientists, so any historical small free API trial should not be assumed. (2) Two genuinely free education-side offers DO exist today and are the effective 'education' equivalents of a free tier: the Claude Team plan for scientists (standard seats $0 for 12 months for accredited-university/nonprofit PIs, then renews at paid price) and Claude for Teachers (free premium access for US K-12 educators, sign up by June 30, 2027 for the free year). A university-wide 'education license' exists but is a paid discounted institutional plan, not a free self-serve student offer. WebSearch budget was exhausted this session, so claims above were verified by reading the official pages directly today (claude.com/programs/startups, /pricing, /solutions/education, /programs/team-plan-for-scientists, /solutions/teachers); figures like the $45K/$100K amounts and the $0 scientist pricing were confirmed on the pages, but I could not cross-check third-party news coverage of 2025-2026 changes.

findings.name: Course Preview (the 2025 replacement of 'audit mode') — free first module of most courses
findings.detail: Since ~Aug 8, 2025 the old unlimited audit experience was replaced by a 'preview' model: for most courses you get free full access to the FIRST module only (video lectures, readings, that module's graded assignments, and Coursera Coach where available). All later modules lock until you upgrade. Per Coursera support, a preview can last up to 6 months. No certificate in preview mode; upgrading to the paid course (one-time, ~$49-79/month per course listing, 180-day access) or financial aid unlocks the certificate.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide. No .edu/student email, no credit card, no signup payment required for the free preview itself. (Official support article learner-000002293, 'How to preview a course', Aug 28, 2025; blog.coursera.org Aug 8, 2025).
findings.claim: Go to any course page > click 'Enroll'/'Start for free' > at the bottom of the enrollment dialog choose 'Preview this course'. For courses inside a Specialization/Professional Certificate, open the individual course page first. If no 'Preview'/'Full Course, No Certificate' link appears, that course has no free option.
findings.expiry: Preview access for a given course: up to 6 months per Coursera support; no renewal — afterwards you must pay or re-enroll.
findings.gotchas: Preview = first module only (not the old full-course audit); no certificate; 'Enroll for free' buttons inside Specializations actually start a paid 7-day trial subscription, not a free audit; if you came via an org program whose contract ended, you are switched to preview automatically.

findings.name: 'Full Course, No Certificate' + partner-supported free access (incl. 'Free Community Impact Courses')
findings.detail: For select courses, Coursera offers 'Full Course, No Certificate': free access to ALL course materials and graded assessments, no certificate. Coursera's Aug 2025 blog also introduced 'Free Community Impact Courses' (mental health, refugee support, public health) with partner-supported free access to full course content; on those, a certificate can optionally be purchased afterwards. Third-party tracker (Class Central, Aug 2026) counts 470+ courses still fully free, and 6 with partner-supported free access incl. 'The Science of Well-Being'.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no .edu, no credit card. Which courses qualify is course-by-course — look for the option in the enrollment dialog; coursera.org/explore/free-courses lists the free catalog ('Learn from Anthropic, AWS, Microsoft, Stanford, and more — free from start to finish').
findings.claim: Open the course page > Enroll > choose 'Full Course, No Certificate' (small link under the paid buttons; inside a Specialization open the individual course page, not the program page). For partner-supported courses, Coursera says to use the FAQ link on the course page rather than 'Enroll for free' (per Class Central's writeup).
findings.expiry: No stated expiry; the free option persists as long as the course keeps the 'Full Course, No Certificate' designation — it can change if the partner withdraws the free offer.
findings.gotchas: Still no certificate (the point of the option); partner-supported access is a different mode: do NOT click 'Enroll for free' on those — follow the FAQ instruction or you may start a paid trial; the free-courses page itself also pushes a 7-day Coursera Plus trial for full access.

findings.name: 7-day free trial: monthly Specializations/Professional Certificates and Coursera Plus
findings.detail: Coursera Plus (monthly $59, 'Save 40%' annual $399) gives unlimited access to 90%+ of the catalog (10,000+ courses/programs incl. capstone projects; degrees/MasterTrack excluded) and starts with a 7-day free trial. Most monthly course/Specialization subscriptions also start with a free trial (per 'Enrollment options' support article). Coursera captures payment info at signup; the card is charged only at the end of the 7-day trial. Plus certificates are unlimited per course completed. Free-access page FAQ confirms: 'Start a 7-day free trial for Specializations or Coursera Plus.'
findings.eligibility: Any individual account; no .edu or startup status required. A credit/payment method IS required (captured at signup, charged if trial lapses).
findings.claim: Sign up > subscribe to a monthly Specialization/Prof. Cert or start Coursera Plus > complete any free-trial work immediately > cancel in Purchases before day 7 to avoid the charge.
findings.expiry: Trial: 7 days, then $59/mo (Plus monthly) or the course's monthly price. Annual Plus has no trial — see separate finding.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: cards are captured up front; you do NOT earn a Course Certificate during a free trial — certificates are only issued after the trial ends and the first payment is charged (official note in 'Get a Course Certificate'); pre-existing Specialization subscriptions are not auto-cancelled when you add Plus (double-charge risk); cancel-anytime applies only to the monthly plan.

findings.name: Coursera Plus annual: 14-day money-back window (not a true trial)
findings.detail: Annual Coursera Plus = $399/year (vs $59/mo monthly) with a 14-day money-back guarantee: pay upfront, request a refund via 'My Purchases' within 14 days. Coursera revokes any certificates earned within those first 14 days if you refund.
findings.eligibility: Any individual account; payment required up front; no .edu or startup requirement.
findings.claim: Subscribe to annual Plus > if it's not for you, request the refund in Purchases within 14 days.
findings.expiry: Refund window: 14 days from purchase. After that, the year is paid and non-refundable.
findings.gotchas: This is a pay-then-refund window, not free access — you pay day one; certificates earned inside the window are clawed back on refund.

findings.name: Financial aid (per-course grants, can make certificates free)
findings.detail: Most Coursera courses offer financial aid for learners who can't afford the course; it can unlock full course access AND the certificate for free (or at reduced cost), per the Aug 2025 preview-model announcement and the 'Enrollment options' help article. Per-course application with an essay; typical decision time ~15 days and a ~14-day access window (historical figures; Coursera's own help article 'Apply for financial aid' covers current rules). Not available on all course types (e.g., some degree-adjacent content).
findings.eligibility: Need-based, open to individuals worldwide — a .edu/student email is NOT required; students, working professionals, and anyone meeting the financial-need criteria can apply. No credit card needed.
findings.claim: On the course page look for 'Financial aid available? Learn more' > submit the per-course application > wait for approval (historically ~15 days) > get a time-boxed window to complete the course and earn the certificate. You can preview/audit while awaiting approval, but graded submissions unlock on approval.
findings.expiry: Grant is per-course and time-boxed (~14 days from aid start, historical); does not cover whole Specializations automatically — apply per course; must be re-claimed for each course.
findings.gotchas: Paying for the course cancels a pending aid application (community-confirmed); aid does not usually cover program-level certificates/degrees; approval can take weeks, so plan around deadlines.

findings.name: Education license: Coursera for Campus / Coursera for Universities (institutional, no .edu tier for individuals)
findings.detail: Coursera for Campus is a B2B offering: partner universities (Imperial College London, University of Michigan, TU Munich, University of Melbourne, Manipal, NMIMS, Ivey Business School) license the platform (10,600+ courses from 350+ partners, Career Academy, Guided Projects, Professional Certificates, LMS integration) so their enrolled students get access. There is NO individual '.edu email = free access' tier: a student gets free access only if their own institution has a Campus plan. No per-seat or plan pricing is published; 'Compare Plans' / 'Contact us' only.
findings.eligibility: Institutions, not individuals. Students of partner universities receive access through the institution (typically .edu verification by the school's admin, not a self-serve .edu signup at coursera.org).
findings.claim: Individual student: nothing to self-claim — ask whether your university licenses Coursera for Campus/Plus; institutions: Coursera sales (coursera.org/campus, 'Compare Plans').
findings.expiry: Tied to the institution's contract; when a contract ends or a learner is removed from the program, enrolled courses are switched to free preview mode (official 'Enrollment options' note).
findings.gotchas: No published free individual tier exists at the .edu level; if your school doesn't have the plan, the free paths are Preview / Full-Course-No-Certificate / financial aid / 7-day trials only; org-sourced access silently downgrades to preview on contract end.

findings.name: Startups: no Coursera startup program exists — only paid team/enterprise plans and the generic 7-day trial
findings.detail: coursera.org/startups, /plus and /startups return 404 — there is no official startup tier, no startup credits, no startup-specific education license. The business funnel is 'Coursera for Teams' (up to 499 employees) vs enterprise (4,700+ companies), behind 'Compare Plans'/'Contact sales' with zero pricing on the public page and no free tier or trial advertised. A founder's only free window is the same 7-day Coursera Plus trial available to anyone.
findings.eligibility: No startup age or funding cap exists because there is no startup program; team/enterprise plans are commercial, paid, sales-led.
findings.claim: N/A — nothing to claim. For a small startup, the practical free options are: the 7-day Plus trial (single seat, credit card required), per-course financial aid, Preview / Full-Course-No-Certificate free access.
findings.expiry: N/A.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse partner-funded 'community impact' free courses or a university's Campus plan with a startup offer; any 'Coursera for startups' content online is third-party, not official; Teams plans have no public pricing or trial, so budget for sales-quoted cost.

sunset_notes: Major 2025 sunset: Coursera retired the classic unlimited 'audit mode' (full free access to lectures of most courses, no certificate) around Aug 8, 2025, replacing it with the Preview experience — free access is now capped at the FIRST module of most courses; 'Full Course, No Certificate' survived only for a select subset (470+ courses per Class Central's Aug 2026 audit, ~2% of the 21,000+ catalog). Consequences: (1) free access shrank from 'whole course minus certificate' to 'first module only' for the majority of courses; (2) the free-trial period for subscriptions is 7 days (not the 30 days some older guides cite) with a card captured up front; (3) certificates are explicitly withheld during free trials; (4) localized/geographic (geo) pricing was introduced in 2025, so paid upgrade prices vary by region while the free tiers stay free; (5) a 'Free Community Impact Courses' program (mental health, refugee support, public health) was added in 2025 as a partner-supported free-access carve-out; (6) no .edu-only student tier and no startup program exist as of 2026-10-22 (verified 404s on /startups, /plus, /for-universities; free paths are Preview, Full-Course-No-Certificate, financial aid, 7-day trials, and institution-provided Campus access). No free offer was closed in 2026 that had existed in 2025 beyond the audit->preview shrinkage; financial aid remains offered.

findings.name: Blender 3D suite — 100% free, no license, all uses (students, universities, startups included)
findings.detail: Blender 5.2.3 LTS (5.3 expected 2026-11-10; also beta, daily/Early Access builds) is free for everyone: GPL (source v2+; binary distributions compatible under v3+), 'Free to Use. Free to Change. Free to Share. Free to Sell Your Work.' No license, registration, account, credit card, or internet required. Output work is the user's sole property. Foundation commitment: 'keep Blender free and open for everyone, forever.' Platforms: Windows x64/ARM, macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux, Steam, source code. Startups and companies get the same free use as students — there is no commercial 'seat' cost at all.
findings.eligibility: Universal. No .edu or student email, no proof of status, no region limits, no org size cap. Universities can deploy it on unlimited machines free of charge. This is the entire 'student offer': nothing to discount because there is no license to buy.
findings.claim: Download directly from https://www.blender.org/download/ — no signup, no payment, no trial. Daily builds at builder.blender.org. Nothing to claim or renew.
findings.expiry: Never — perpetual free access; version updates are also free. Renewal not applicable.
findings.gotchas: Free tier vs paid ecosystem: the app is free, but Blender Marketplace add-ons/assets are paid, and Blender Studio (see next finding) is a paid subscription that names students as an audience — do not confuse the free app with paid services. Optional donation via fund.blender.org supports development but is not required.

findings.name: education.blender.org — free open-licensed education resources for teachers and students
findings.detail: Blender Foundation-backed community site offering: 'Education Recipes' (lesson plans/curricula, e.g. 'Modeling & animation for absolute beginners', 'VR Class'), 'Quests' (step-by-step tutorials: Party Monkey, House, Rocket, Maze, Chair, Landscape, etc.), 'Concepts' material, and 'Education Badges' — a tiered 7-discipline skill framework (Modeling, Animation, 2D Art, Sculpting, Rigging, Lighting/Camera/Rendering, Video Sequencer, 3-4 levels each). All content released under CC BY-SA 4.0 (or later); source repo is open at projects.blender.org/blender/blender-education-docs. Site framing: 'unrestricted access to high-quality tools without financial barriers or privacy concerns.'
findings.eligibility: Open to all teachers and students; no account, no .edu verification, no fee, no region limit. Educator support via chat channel #blender-education on chat.blender.org.
findings.claim: Browse/download directly at education.blender.org; contribution via its 'Get Involved / Contribute' pages. No application.
findings.expiry: Perpetual — CC BY-SA license; no sunset date.
findings.gotchas: This is curriculum/reference material, not a software license or certification — badges are a self-reference framework, not graded credentials. It complements the free software rather than adding to it.

findings.name: Blender Studio (studio.blender.org) — official paid training/production platform; NOT a free offer; no student discount (gotcha)
findings.detail: Paid subscription funding the Studio team's films and training. Individual plan: €17/month, or €34.50 per quarter (€11.50/month equivalent, 'Save €5.50/month'). Team plan: from €500/month, unlimited seats on a company email domain, up to '8 hours of dedicated training' on higher tiers. Includes: full production-asset access, Open Movie production logs, unlimited trainings (courses, workshops, docs, production lessons), commenting. Payment: major credit cards, PayPal, direct bank transfer. Fees are non-refundable. cloud.blender.org 301-redirects to studio.blender.org — there is no separate free 'Blender Cloud' rendering service.
findings.eligibility: The individual plan is explicitly marketed 'for freelancers, students, and instructors' — but at standard price: no free tier, no trial, no student/education discount, no startup program. Students pay the same €17/month.
findings.claim: Join at studio.blender.org/join/ (account via OAuth login required) or /teams/ for the team plan. No free claim path exists.
findings.expiry: Subscription cancels per terms; content access ends with the subscription.
findings.gotchas: Most likely thing to misread as a student offer because 'students' is in the audience line — it is a paid plan with no concession. The free software itself (finding 1) already covers students at zero cost; Studio adds the Foundation's film production content only. Display bug seen on the studio homepage ('€1150/month') — /join/ page is authoritative: €17/mo.
