(4) market.blender.org (Blender Marketplace, paid add-ons/assets) did not resolve in this environment; no student pricing observed anywhere in the Blender ecosystem. (5) Historical note (low confidence): an early volunteer 'Blender Classrooms' educator-resource effort (mid-2010s) was wound down long before 2025; its role is now covered by education.blender.org, which remains free and active. WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-research, so 2025-2026 change detection relies on the official pages fetched today; the homepage's 'Free and Open Source, forever' language and unchanged download/license pages show no sunset of free access.

findings.name: Notion Free Plan (individual)
findings.detail: $0/yr. For a single-owner (1-person) workspace: unlimited pages & blocks. A free workspace with 2+ owners is capped at 1,000 blocks per workspace (3-day grace before enforcement). File uploads up to 5 MB each. Page/edit history 7 days. Up to 10 external guests on a single-member workspace. AI features (Notion Agent, Meeting Notes, Research Mode) are available only as a 'limited trial' with no published fixed free-credit allotment; extra Notion credits cost $10/1,000 (monthly) or $13/1,000 (annual), and Standard/Select AI credits are bundled only on Business/Enterprise.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no .edu email required, no credit card to sign up, no stated region limits.
findings.claim: Create a Notion account (web/desktop); you land on the Free plan by default. No card required.
findings.expiry: No expiry; the free tier is permanent. The AI 'limited trial' is not a recurring free entitlement and continued heavy AI use requires purchasing credits.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: AI on the Free plan is a limited trial, not a fixed free-credit pool — heavy AI use pushes you into $10/1,000 credits. The 1,000-block cap only triggers with 2+ workspace owners. Notion does not publish a total-storage figure; the cap is 5 MB per file.

findings.name: Notion for Education — free individual student/teacher plan
findings.detail: Free Education plan for a 1-member workspace (individual student or teacher): unlimited pages & blocks, up to 100 guests per workspace, unlimited uploads, 30-day edit history. No AI-credit amount is published. Genuinely free, not a trial.
findings.eligibility: Students/teachers at accredited colleges or universities listed in the World Higher Education Database (WHED). K-12 students and K-12 educators are NOT eligible. You must sign in with your institutional (.edu/college) email as the account's MAIN email (a secondary school email does not count). Notion does not accept student IDs or other documentation. Each school email claims it once, for one workspace.
findings.claim: Be on the Free plan with a single member. Settings -> 'Upgrade plan' -> 'Get free education plan'. If your school is in WHED, the upgrade is automatic once the institutional email is verified.
findings.expiry: No set end date. Re-verify your school email annually (unlimited re-verifications). Losing your valid school email downgrades the workspace (and all its content) to the Free plan. Upgrading to Plus/Business/Enterprise permanently ends Education eligibility for that workspace.
findings.gotchas: Upgrading to a paid plan is irreversible for Education eligibility on that workspace. Notion/AI credit counts and per-file size caps are not stated on the page. The individual claim is desktop/web only, not mobile.

findings.name: Notion for Education — free student-organization plan (unlimited members)
findings.detail: Free plan for a student-organization workspace with unlimited members: unlimited blocks/files, up to 100 guests, unlimited uploads, 30-day edit history.
findings.eligibility: Student organizations at accredited colleges/universities in WHED; one-time application (one application per organization). Same institutional-email verification as the individual plan.
findings.claim: Apply via the application link on the education help page; on approval the org workspace is granted. One application per organization.
findings.expiry: No set end date; annual re-verification; loss of a valid school email reverts the workspace to the Free plan.
findings.gotchas: One application/approval per organization; not stackable across multiple orgs.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack — Notion perk
findings.detail: Verified students receive 'everything in the Notion Education plan with additional AI responses' (i.e., the free Education-plan entitlements above plus extra AI responses; the exact AI quantity is not published). A separate 'Notion Template Collection' (course dashboards, hackathon tools, portfolio templates) is also in the pack.
findings.eligibility: Requires GitHub student verification (.edu email + verified student status via the GitHub Student Pack). No credit card required to claim the pack.
findings.claim: Verify student status on the GitHub Student Developer Pack, then claim the Notion perk; it links into Notion's Education-plan flow.
findings.expiry: Tied to GitHub student-verification validity; the underlying Notion education plan persists per its own annual re-verification.
findings.gotchas: The perk was historically 'free Notion Pro (annual)' for verified students; it is now reworded to the Notion Education plan + additional AI responses — the underlying plan type changed. 'Additional AI responses' quantity is unspecified.

findings.name: Notion for Startups — up to 6 months free Business plan (with Notion AI)
findings.detail: Eligible companies get free months on the Business plan (which bundles Notion AI). Tiers: 6 months for partner-affiliated startups (via AWS Activate, Stripe Atlas, HubSpot, Shopify, JP Morgan, etc.); 3 months for non-partner startups meeting criteria; 1 month for SMBs/small teams (<10 employees) or when verification fails. The 6-month track needs a valid Notion domain, a public company website, a company email, and <100 employees. Must be a new, non-paying Notion customer.
findings.eligibility: Startups building scalable tech-related products/services; partner route or non-partner route. No stated funding cap or minimum company age; headcount limits apply (6-mo: <100; 1-mo: <10). No region limits stated. No credit card requirement per the doc.
findings.claim: Partner route: get your partner's unique code, then submit the form at notion.so/startups-apply. Non-partner route: fill the same application form. Notion emails to confirm; the upgrade takes effect immediately. 3-5 business-day review. One redemption; multiple partners do not stack.
findings.expiry: The free window is fixed (1/3/6 months), after which the Business plan continues as a paid subscription unless downgraded.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free: after the free months you are on a paid Business plan — downgrade to avoid charges. Applies only to net-new Business plans (not Enterprise); no refunds for previously paid invoices. A failed/weak verification (inactive site, solo applicant, limited footprint) can downgrade a 3/6-month request to 1 month.

findings.name: Notion Business Plan 30-day trial (no credit card)
findings.detail: 30-day trial of the full Business Plan (includes Notion AI) at $0. No credit card to start; payment is collected only if you upgrade. Auto-renews at trial end if you added payment details; otherwise you are prompted to confirm the upgrade.
findings.eligibility: Requires a professional domain; educational and personal domains are excluded. Web/desktop only. No credit card required to begin.
findings.claim: Start the Business Plan trial from Notion's settings/billing on a workspace using a professional domain.
findings.expiry: 30 days, then auto-renew (if a card was added) or a prompt to confirm; canceling drops you to the Free plan (or back to Plus if the trial started on Plus).
findings.gotchas: Trial, not a free tier: if you add a card it auto-renews into a paid Business plan. .edu / personal / free email-provider domains are excluded. This is a gateway to a paid plan, distinct from the genuinely-free tiers above.

sunset_notes: Changes 2025-2026: (1) K-12 students and K-12 educators are NOT eligible for Notion's free Education plan — only students/teachers at accredited higher-ed institutions in the World Higher Education Database; K-12 users fall back to the general Free plan. This narrows the historical "free for all educators" posture. (2) The GitHub Student Developer Pack Notion perk, historically "free Notion Pro (annual)", is now listed as "everything in the Notion Education plan with additional AI responses" — the underlying plan shifted from Pro to Education, and extra AI is now metered. (3) AI is now usage-metered via "Notion credits" ($10/1,000 monthly; $13/1,000 annual); Standard/Select AI credits are bundled only on Business/Enterprise, and the Free/Education plans list AI as a limited trial with no published fixed free-credit amount. No core free offer was fully sunset in 2025-2026 — the free Education plan (higher-ed), the free student-org plan, the individual Free plan, the Startup program, and the 30-day Business trial all remain active as of 2026-10-22. Method note: web search budget was exhausted this session, so all findings above were verified by WebFetch of official pages (notion.com pricing, education/startups/trials/block-usage/credits help articles, education.github.com/pack) today; not a search-based synthesis.

findings.name: New-account free trial: $200 credit for 60 days
findings.detail: $200 in cloud credit valid for 60 days for new DigitalOcean accounts. Auto-applied at signup; usable across Droplets, App Platform, managed databases, Kubernetes, and Spaces. Marketplace/third-party integrations are excluded. Credits are consumed before the card is charged. After 60 days or when the credit is exhausted, standard pay-as-you-go billing applies and any unused credit is forfeited.
findings.eligibility: Open to new accounts in general - NOT restricted to .edu or students. Requires a valid credit card or PayPal for identity verification (no charge during the trial unless the credit is exhausted). One trial per person. No funding/age cap; not startup-specific.
findings.claim: Create a new DigitalOcean account (email, Google, or GitHub), add a credit card/PayPal, and the $200 credit is automatically applied to billing. Deploy workloads (Droplet/App Platform/DB/K8s). A referral or promo link can be used for the trial. Set a reminder before day 60.
findings.expiry: 60 days from account creation; unused credit forfeited at expiry; no renewal or extension.
findings.gotchas: A payment card IS required, so it is a card-required trial, not a no-card free tier. Trial-vs-free: every running resource becomes billable after 60 days. Egress beyond included allowances and all marketplace/third-party services are billed. Region availability of specific services varies. NOTE: the official /free-trial/ landing page returns a 404 today; the $200/60-day terms are corroborated by current (2026) third-party and first-party community sources, not a live official trial page.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack - $200 student credit (SUNSET / no longer listed)
findings.detail: Historically, students verified through GitHub (Student Developer Pack, typically .edu) could claim $200 of DigitalOcean credit. As of today's check, DigitalOcean is NOT listed as a perk in the current GitHub Student Developer Pack, and the dedicated DigitalOcean student page (/github-students) now redirects to the generic homepage. Community reports (May 2026) indicate the credit stopped applying after GitHub authorization + card. No active standalone .edu-only student-credit program could be confirmed. Practical effect: the only currently-usable student path is the general $200/60-day new-account trial above.
findings.eligibility: Previously .edu / verified GitHub student status; now appears unavailable. No live activation path found.
findings.claim: Previously: verify GitHub student status, then activate DigitalOcean from the Student Developer Pack. Now: no working activation path found - confirm on the live GitHub pack page before expecting any credit.
findings.expiry: Appears discontinued; no stated end date; the pack no longer lists DigitalOcean.
findings.gotchas: Do not rely on this offer. The 'known so far' $200 GitHub-pack student credit should be treated as outdated. If re-activated later, it would again likely require a card for account verification.

findings.name: DigitalOcean Startups program (credits for early-stage startups)
findings.detail: Participants receive a pre-determined credit amount (varies; spelled out in the onboarding email) subject to a $10,000 monthly spend ceiling, valid over a 12-month term (i.e., up to ~$120K of core credits). Credits apply to qualifying DigitalOcean services but EXCLUDE GPU Droplets, NVIDIA H100 GPU Kubernetes, Bare Metal GPUs, Dedicated/Serverless Inference, third-party/frontier AI models (including Anthropic and OpenAI), Paperspace Machines, Cloudways, and third-party pass-through charges. GPU credits are a separate, non-guaranteed invitation after review. Standard paid support is free for 15 months.
findings.eligibility: For new startups that have NOT used prior DigitalOcean credits. Must have raised $10M or less. AI-native startups prioritized; service firms (agencies/consulting) excluded. Requires a corporate/business email, a registered DigitalOcean team account, a valid credit card, and a public company website. No stated company-age or geographic restriction.
findings.claim: VC/accelerator-backed: confirm the partnership via DigitalOcean's portfolio partner list and ask your program manager. Independent founders: submit the application (Typeform) and select 'Other' for the affiliated partner organization. Perks are delivered in the 'Welcome Kit' on acceptance.
findings.expiry: 12-month program term; no extensions granted; unused credits forfeited; credits are non-transferable.
findings.gotchas: A credit card is required to be eligible. The widely-circulated 'up to $250K' figure is NOT what the current official page states - the current framing is a $10,000/month ceiling over 12 months with 'amount varies' (historically marketed as up to ~$200K including partner credits). Effective May 13, 2026 the eligible-service list broadened (core credits apply to more services, still excluding the GPU/AI-model/third-party list above). Prohibited uses include cryptocurrency mining and workloads with excessive network/CPU/disk I/O.

findings.name: Always-free services (free tier): static sites on App Platform + included add-ons
findings.detail: Up to 3 static sites can be built and deployed on App Platform for free with no expiration (~1 GiB outbound transfer per app; additional static apps cost $3/month). App Platform entry is listed as '$0/month'. Also always-free for all accounts: DNS management, Cloud Firewalls, monitoring & alerting, one free Container Registry repository (500 MiB), and free round-the-clock technical support.
findings.eligibility: All DigitalOcean accounts - not student/startup-specific. No .edu or funding requirements.
findings.claim: Sign up (with the $200 trial or a standard account); deploy static sites for free; the free add-ons are included automatically with a paid account.
findings.expiry: No expiration on the free static-site allowance; free add-ons are ongoing with a paid account.
findings.gotchas: Only STATIC apps are free - dynamic App Platform apps bill by resource units. Free static outbound transfer is capped (~1 GiB/app/month); egress beyond included allowances and third-party/marketplace services are billed. This free tier is separate from, and smaller than, the startup credits.

Community reports (May 2026) say the credit stopped applying after GitHub authorization + adding a card. Treat the 'known so far' $200 GitHub-pack student credit as outdated/unavailable; the only live student-accessible path today is the general $200/60-day new-account trial.

The $250K figure is unsupported by the current official page.

The official /free-trial/ landing page returns a 404 today, so the $200/60-day trial could not be read on a live official page; it remains corroborated by current (2026) third-party guides and first-party DigitalOcean community threads. No active .edu-only education license program was found.

findings.claim: Download n8n Community Edition from GitHub/npm/Docker and self-host on your own infrastructure — no signup, license, or application needed; free access is automatic. No card required.
findings.detail: Permanently free self-hosted edition with unlimited workflow executions, unlimited users and workflows, all integrations. Page states: 'A standard, self-hosted version of n8n is available on GitHub.' No execution cap, user cap, or feature restriction is listed. For the AI Assistant, self-hosters bring their own model API keys (BYOK), so no credit limits apply. You only pay for your own server/infra. Not student-specific — available to everyone.
findings.eligibility: No eligibility criteria; anyone can self-host. No .edu, age, funding, or region requirements. Not a student or startup-specific offer.
findings.expiry: None — perpetual free offering. No sunset announced.
findings.gotchas: You bear all hosting costs (VPS/cloud), updates, security, and maintenance. Enterprise/SSO, Git version control, multiple environments, queue-mode scaling, and extended data retention are Business/Enterprise features, NOT included in Community. No official support (community forum only). Trial-vs-free gotcha: this is the only genuinely free+unlimited tier — the cloud tier has no permanent free plan.
findings.name: Self-hosted Community Edition (free, unlimited executions)

findings.claim: Start the trial from the n8n Cloud sign-up (app.n8n.cloud) without entering a credit card; pick up any paid Starter/Pro plan when the trial ends. No application or .edu needed.
findings.detail: Free n8n Cloud trial with no credit card required: page states 'No credit card is required for the n8n Cloud trial.' Included: 1,000 workflow executions, 5 concurrent executions, 180-second execution timeout, 1 team project, Pro-level features (Global Variables, Insights dashboard with 14-day history, 5-day workflow history, advanced execution filters, unlimited evaluations, folders, Assistant), plus 800 Assistant credits + 100 AI credits. Excluded: Admin Roles, project Editor role, Named Versions, Workflow Diffs, and the n8n public API. No permanent free cloud plan exists — Starter is 20€/mo (billed annually) after the trial.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone creating an n8n Cloud account; no student/.edu requirement, no funding caps. No card required at start.
findings.expiry: Credits expire when the trial ends. Trial duration: the official page does not state an explicit day-count for the Cloud trial (the 14-day figure is stated only for the Business-plan trial); widely cited as 14 days — not explicitly confirmed on the page today. Downgrade/loss-of-data behavior after lapse not stated on the page.
findings.gotchas: Trial limits (1,000 executions, 5 concurrent, 1 project) are much smaller than the paid Starter tier (2,500 executions). Assistant/AI credits are one-time and expire at trial end. After the trial you either pay (Starter 20€/mo annual, 24€ monthly) or your workflows stop running on n8n's infrastructure — you can export workflows but hosted runs are not carried to Community. Card NOT required for Cloud trial (contrast: Business trial DOES require a card).
findings.name: n8n Cloud free trial (no credit card, 1,000 executions)

findings.claim: Sign up for the 14-day Business plan trial from n8n Cloud, with credit card on file.
findings.detail: Separate 14-day trial: 'full access to all Business features for 14 days.' Business plan is normally 667€/mo (billed annually; 800€/mo monthly), 40,000 executions, queue mode. This trial is for the Business tier (self-hosted-oriented features such as SSO/SAML/LDAP, admin roles, version control, environments).
findings.eligibility: Anyone; credit card IS required (unlike the Starter/Pro Cloud trial).
findings.expiry: 14 days, then converts to the paid Business plan (self-hosted) or as n8n defines at checkout.
findings.gotchas: Credit card required — risk of auto-conversion to a 667€/mo+ annual plan if you forget to cancel. Business plan is self-hosted only; 'Hosted by n8n?' is offered as a waitlist, so the hosted version of Business is not generally available. This is NOT free to keep — it is a time-boxed trial of a paid plan.
findings.name: Business plan 14-day trial (credit card required)

findings.claim: Check criteria (fewer than 20 employees, less than €5M total funding) → apply via the start-up offer link on n8n.io/pricing/startup-plan → subscribe → n8n generates a license key for your instance → enter the key in your instance's Settings to activate all Business-plan features.
findings.detail: 50% off the Business plan: 333€/mo billed annually (vs 667€/mo standard annual), for 40,000 workflow executions with unlimited steps. Includes 6 shared projects, SSO/SAML/LDAP, admin roles, version control (Git), multiple environments, queue-mode scaling options, global variables, 30 days of insights, forum support. Page FAQ states eligibility: 'Fewer than 20 employees', 'Less than €5M in total funding'. Duration: 'You can use the startup discounted plan for one year, or longer if you still meet the requirements.'
findings.eligibility: Startup-specific: fewer than 20 employees AND less than €5M in total funding. No explicit company-age or 'early-stage' date cap stated on the official page. No .edu. No region limits stated. Vendor reviews/approves the application. NOT free — it is a 50% discount on a paid license.
findings.expiry: Discount lasts one year and renews automatically for further periods only while the startup still meets the <20-employee and <€5M-funding criteria. Cancellation: Settings → Usage and plan → Manage Plan (Business plan section, not Start-up plan section). Monthly billing also available; 'cancel anytime on your monthly subscription.'
findings.gotchas: Not free — still 333€/mo (~4,000€/yr) and does NOT include hosting: 'The Business plan is currently available only for self-hosted deployments.' You pay your own infra, ops, and backups. Discount applies to license only. If funding crosses €5M or headcount crosses 20, the discount cannot be renewed. Self-hosted-only, so no cloud-hosted startup tier exists. For small projects, the 20€/mo Starter cloud plan may be cheaper than discounted Business even though Business has more features.
findings.name: n8n Start-up Plan (50% off Business, self-hosted)

findings.claim: Register at learn.n8n.io (free, no .edu or institution check), complete courses n8n101/102/103 + QS101 to earn the Foundations program certificate and verifiable badges; a timed certification exam is 'coming soon.'
findings.detail: n8n has NO education license, academic pricing, or student discount for the product. Its 'Education' footer link goes to the n8n Academy: 'Every course is free for everyone' — structured courses (Foundations program: n8n101, n8n102, n8n103 + quickstart), workflow templates, and docs. Free completion certificate + verifiable badge; finishing all Foundations courses yields a program certificate. A certification exam badge 'stays valid for two years' (exam itself is 'coming soon'). Self-paced, no enrollment windows.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone — no .edu email, no student verification, no region gate. Not a student-only offer and does not grant product access or discounts; it is free training/certification content.
findings.expiry: Courses are free with no stated end date. Certification badge validity: 2 years (once the exam ships).
findings.gotchas: Frequently confused with an education license: the Academy provides free learning, NOT a free or discounted n8n product license. Students still need the free Community Edition (self-hosted) or the cloud trial for the actual product. Badges/certificates are learning credentials, not workflow-execution entitlements.
findings.name: n8n Academy — free courses & certification (no .edu, open to all)

provider: n8n (Workflow automation, self-hosted open-source SaaS alternative to Zapier/Make)
sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22: no student/education product license or .edu-gated offer exists for n8n — only free open-access Academy courses (a learning platform, not a discount), the free unlimited self-hosted Community Edition, the card-free Cloud trial, and the paid 50% start-up discount. No permanent free cloud tier: cloud plans are paid (Starter 20€/mo annual, Pro 50€/mo annual; monthly 24€/60€ per Sept 2026 sources) and a free 14-day Business trial exists with card. Start-up Plan terms are current and unchanged (50% off, <20 employees, <€5M funding, 1-year renewable, self-hosted-only Business); the pricing page now shows Business 'Hosted by n8n?' as waitlist/self-hosted-only, so no hosted startup tier. findings.name: Cloud Free plan (perpetual)
findings.detail: $0 per builder/month. 2 builders, up to 50 end users, up to 10 apps, 100 AI credits/month with NO add-on AI credits available (unlike paid plans). ToolJet DB capped at 10 tables and 500 rows; external data sources unlimited. Predefined user roles, community support via Slack. Verified on the official pricing page today. No 2025-2026 sunset found.
findings.eligibility: Anyone; sign up at tooljet.com via 'Get Started'. No .edu email, no company type, no region limit stated. Credit card NOT required (free plan CTA is 'Get Started', no payment method mentioned anywhere on the page).
findings.claim: Sign up free at tooljet.com/pricing (Cloud tab, Free tier 'Get Started').
findings.gotchas: AI-credit add-ons (pay-as-you-go at $1/100 credits) are NOT available on the Free tier — 100 credits is the hard cap and credits reset each billing cycle with no rollover. DB limits (10 tables / 500 rows) make real apps impractical on Free. Third-party LLM keys: BYOK only on Enterprise.
findings.expiry: Perpetual free tier; no expiry date published.

findings.name: Self-Hosted Community Edition (open source, perpetual)
findings.detail: ToolJet core is open source under AGPL-3.0 (verified on the GitHub repo today): visual app builder, 90+ data sources, self-host via Docker/Kubernetes, run JS/Python in apps. The pricing page lists a $0 'Free' self-hosted tier: 2 builders, up to 50 end users, up to 10 apps, 100 AI credits/month, no AI add-on. Workflow Automation & Agent Builder are noted as 'Available on Self-hosted only'. Fully offline/air-gapped operation (including licensing) requires the paid Self-hosted Enterprise air-gapped add-on.
findings.eligibility: Anyone, unlimited — you host it yourself; no CC, no .edu, no region limit. AGPL-3.0: if you modify the server and offer it as a network service, the AGPL copyleft applies to your modified code. If you use an unmodified server build you have no AGPL obligations. No open-source commercial license tier is needed for private use.
findings.claim: Clone repo and self-host: https://github.com/ToolJet/ToolJet (Docker/Kubernetes). No sign-up required for the software itself.
findings.gotchas: Your only real cost is your own infrastructure (server, DB, LLM tokens if you wire up AI). Air-gapped/offline licensing is NOT free — Enterprise add-on. GitHub repo labels some AI features as 'ToolJet AI (Enterprise)'; the pricing page says Workflow Automation/Agent Builder ship with self-hosted (possibly tied to paid self-hosted Team), so confirm which agent features are CE vs Enterprise before relying on them. Open-source/non-profit projects are offered 'heavy discounts' on paid features per the pricing FAQ, but that is a discount, not free.
findings.expiry: Perpetual; AGPL-3.0.

findings.name: Team plan trial (self-serve 'Start Trial')
findings.detail: The Cloud Team tier ($199/builder/mo, 'Saved 20%' tagged) carries a 'Start Trial' CTA on the pricing page, implying a trial of the Team/Enterprise tiers. No trial length, conversion terms, or CC requirement is stated on the page; the official page did not publish details as of today.
findings.eligibility: Unpublished; sign up flow via 'Start Trial' on the Team tier.
findings.claim: Click 'Start Trial' on the Team plan at tooljet.com/pricing/.
findings.gotchas: Trial-vs-free trap: a trial converts to a paid plan; without published terms you don't know whether a CC is captured or when billing starts. Details unverified.
findings.expiry: Unpublished trial window.

findings.name: Stirring Minds partner startup deal ($2,000 credits) — likely stale
findings.detail: Partner program (Stirring Minds, Delhi, via its incubator network): $2,000 in credits for ToolJet Cloud Business plan + office hours with ToolJet's engineering team + 6 months free support for self-hosted Community Edition. Listed 2021-11-21; the deal page carried a © 2024 footer but no ToolJet-side confirmation of current availability.
findings.eligibility: Startups founded within the last 3 years; no funding cap stated; 'open to all organizations and startups'. Access is gated through Stirring Minds membership/its incubator.
findings.claim: Startups apply by filling out a form provided by Stirring Minds (to its members); services delivered after incubator approval. No direct application page on tooljet.com found.
findings.gotchas: Partner-channel deal from 2021 — may be lapsed or renegotiated; 'Business plan' naming suggests pre-2025 plan naming (ToolJet restructured tiers to Basic/Flexible/Team/Enterprise). Verify directly with Stirring Minds or hello@tooljet.com before relying on it.
findings.expiry: Unknown; listing undated beyond 2021 add date, site live to © 2024.

findings.name: ToolJet Academy (free learning + certification, not a license offer)
findings.detail: Self-paced learning platform launched 2025-04-24 (post updated 2025-12-31): project-first curriculum, quizzes, shareable digital certificate, 4-6 hour Developer track. Not a free ToolJet license or credit grant — it is an educational credential. The announcement does not state a price or student/educator discount; no eligibility restrictions are listed.
findings.eligibility: Anyone with an email; sign up at academy.tooljet.com. No .edu requirement stated; no evidence of a special student tier.
findings.claim: Sign up at academy.tooljet.com, complete the Developer track quizzes to earn the certificate.
findings.gotchas: Treat as free community/education content, not as a product offer; cost and certification status not explicitly confirmed as $0 on the announcement page.
findings.expiry: Ongoing program.

sunset_notes: As of 2026-10-22: ToolJet has no first-party student/.edu program and no dedicated startup program page on tooljet.com — the only startup credit offer found is the stale partner channel (Stirring Minds, 2021). The Cloud Free plan and self-hosted AGPL Community Edition remain the two genuinely free, perpetual offers; both verified on the official pages today. Plan structure changed since 2021: tiers are now Free/Basic/Flexible($79)/Team($199)/Enterprise with 'Saved 20%' discount tags; a third-party deals directory (aicodingdir.com, checked 2026-10-10) lists ToolJet cloud 'paid one at $99/month' (likely stale vs current $23 Basic). ToolJet Academy (2025-04 launch) is the only 2025-2026 addition to the free/education side; no major sunset of the free tiers was found. Note: WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-task, so verification relies on direct fetches of tooljet.com/pricing/, the ToolJet GitHub repo, the ToolJet Academy blog post, and the Stirring Minds listing plus prior search snippets; no official 2026 announcement of changes was located.

findings.name: Cloudflare Free (Network & CDN) plan — always-free
findings.detail: $0/month website/CDN plan: CDN, unmetered DDoS protection, Universal SSL, WAF with Free Managed Ruleset, DNS, SSO, Role-based Account Control; 70 WAF rules + 10K bulk redirects; bot mitigation limited to 'Simple bots'; community forums support only. Paid tiers for comparison: Pro $20/mo annual ($25 monthly), Business $200/mo annual ($250 monthly), Enterprise custom. Page targets 'personal or hobby projects'.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone worldwide; no .edu email, no student status, no credit card/payment method required for the Free plan (sign up at dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up, 'Start building for free' — payment method only needed later to enable paid products/services).
findings.claim: Create a free Cloudflare account (no payment method), add your domain as a zone, set nameservers to Cloudflare. Instant, perpetual, renews monthly at $0. The plan page (network-cdn) does not state a hard zone/site cap or bandwidth cap; Free has historically been unlimited-bandwidth with all sites/zones included.
findings.expiry: Permanent; no expiry. Free-plan feature sets can shrink/change with plan revisions.
findings.gotchas: Only 'Simple bots' mitigation and 70 rules on Free; WAF max payload and bot analytics are paid-plan features. Paid add-ons cost extra (e.g. Log Explorer $1/GB after 10 GB).

findings.name: Cloudflare Developer Free plan — Workers, R2, D1, KV, Pages, AI (perpetual, not a trial)
findings.detail: Perpetual free allowances (monthly unless noted): Workers 100,000 requests/day + 10 ms CPU/request (128 MB memory; 100 Workers; 5 cron triggers; 50 external subrequests/request); R2 10 GB-month Standard storage + 1M Class A + 10M Class B ops/month; D1 5 GB total storage + 5M rows read/day; Workers KV 1 GB storage + 100K reads/day; Pages 500 builds/month, 100 custom domains/project, 20K files, 20-min build timeout; Workers AI 10,000 neurons/day; Observability free: 0.5 GB/day ingestion, 7-day retention; Workflows 3,000 steps/day + 1 GB-month storage. No charge for egress/bandwidth on Workers and R2. Workers Paid plan is $5/mo minimum (includes 10M requests + 30M CPU ms).
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone; no .edu/student requirement, no funding/company status, and credit card NOT required to create a Free account — docs explicitly frame adding a payment method as a post-signup step to 'enable additional products and services'.
findings.claim: Sign up free at dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up; free allowances are included automatically on any new account — no application, no key, no card. Exceeding Workers quotas returns error 1027 (fail-open/closed), not a bill, on the Free plan; overages on R2/D1/KV etc. do bill, which requires a payment method on the account.
findings.expiry: Permanent free tier; daily limits reset at midnight UTC, monthly allowances reset each billing month. 2026 additions started charging for some add-ons (see sunset_notes).
findings.gotchas: R2 free tier covers Standard storage only (Infrequent Access is never free). New metered add-ons (R2 SQL, R2 Data Catalog billed 2026-08-03; AI Search billing from 2026-11-01 with 5M ingestion tokens, 10 GB-month, 1K semantic + 1K full-text queries/month included) can produce invoices on an otherwise-free account — monitor 'Billable Usage' and set spend caps. Workers AI Gateway is 'temporarily not covered' by startup credits.

findings.name: Cloudflare Startup Program — annual credits ($10K / $100K / $350K tiers)
findings.detail: Cloudflare's startup program (cloudflare.com/startup, apply at /lp/startups) offers credits valid 1 year or until consumed (extensions not granted). Tiers recently raised: Tier 3 $10,000/yr (was $5,000), 'no minimum funding required'; Tier 2 $100,000/yr + account manager; Tier 1 $350,000/yr (was $250,000) + Office Hours + priority support. Exclusions/caps: R2 capped at $10K credit; Workers AI capped at $2.5K/$10K/$50K by tier; AI Gateway temporarily not covered; domain registrar fees and premium network services (Magic Transit, Enterprise Spectrum, Dedicated IPs, China Network) excluded. Review typically ~48 hours, confirmation by email.
findings.eligibility: For-profit company only; incorporated no more than 10 years ago; funded up to Series B (funding within last 12 months, except Tier 3 needs no minimum funding); business email on the company domain — personal emails are rejected, so .edu/student emails are NOT eligible; must have a public website and public LinkedIn/X/GitHub presence; first-time applicant only; no region limit is stated on the page.
findings.claim: Apply via the form at https://www.cloudflare.com/lp/startups with company/business-domain email; if accepted you receive the tier's annual credit to offset Cloudflare spend. The startup program is for companies, so students/universities/sole .edu users effectively cannot claim it.
findings.expiry: Credits: 12 months from grant or until consumed, whichever first; no extensions. Active members near old caps may email startups@cloudflare.com for case-by-case tier upgrade (does not reset the 12-month window).
findings.gotchas: Business-entity + company-domain email rules make it unusable for individual students, classes, or nonprofit/university projects; 'funding within last 12 months' + up-to-Series-B cap means late-stage and >10-year-old companies are out; entry tier is now $10K not the $5K referenced in older sources.

findings.name: Education / .edu programs — no dedicated student or university program found
findings.detail: No .edu-only or student-exclusive Cloudflare offer was found today: no Cloudflare education license, no student credits, no university pricing page (cloudflare.com/academy and /lp/startups-education equivalents 404; academy.cloudflare.com did not resolve in this session; Cloudflare docs contain no 'academy/education' content). Cloudflare Academy (free courses/certifications for IT/security training, open to everyone — not .edu-gated) has existed in recent years, but its current status is unconfirmed from today's fetches. The only 'free' education-adjacent value is the general free developer plan plus free Radar data dashboards.
findings.eligibility: n/a — negative finding: no .edu/student-email program exists to claim; free platform is available to students exactly as to anyone else (no card required).
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Students get the standard Free developer plan (Workers 100K req/day, R2 10 GB, D1 5 GB, KV 1 GB, Pages 500 builds/month) with no special student terms; universities would have to use the startup program only if they fit its for-profit company rules, which they typically do not.
findings.expiry: n/a
findings.gotchas: If Cloudflare Academy has moved hosts (dead subdomain in this environment), re-verify before citing its free courses/certifications; treat any .edu-only claim as unsubstantiated.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes: (1) Startup program tiers were "recently updated" (undated on page, current as of 2026-10-22): Tier 3 raised $5,000→$10,000/yr and Tier 1 $250,000→$350,000/yr — older references to a "$5K credit" are stale; entry tier is now $10K. (2) No general-public time-boxed trial or one-off trial-credit offer exists; the only dollar-credit offer is the application-based startup program (perpetual free tiers are not trials and never expire). (3) New billable dimensions landed on the free platform in 2026: R2 SQL and R2 Data Catalog billing enabled 2026-08-03 for non-Enterprise accounts (free tier 10 GB scanned / 1M catalog ops / 10 GB compaction per month), AI Search billing begins 2026-11-01 (free: 5M ingestion tokens, 10 GB-month, 1K semantic + 1K full-text queries/month), and 2026-02-11 raised Workers subrequest limits (Free stays at 50 external/1,000 internal per invocation; Paid default 10,000, configurable to 10M) — free accounts can still accrue charges on metered add-ons, so set spend limits. (4) 2025-12-05 WAF max-payload change: Free zones already protected to 1 MB; paid plans need support ticket to enable. (5) Unbound/Bundled Workers plans are deprecated and unavailable to new accounts. (6) Education: no .edu-only program found and Cloudflare Academy's host (academy.cloudflare.com) did not resolve today — treat its current availability as unverified; if it was sunset in 2025-2026, no student/education free offer remains at Cloudflare.

provider: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) — Free Tier, 30-day trial, startup & education fronts

findings.name: OCI Always Free services (Free Tier — no expiry)
findings.detail: Always Free limits (oracle.com Free Tier service list, re-fetched live 2026-10-22): Compute = 2 AMD VMs (each 1/8 OCPU + 1 GB RAM) and ARM = 1,500 OCPU-hours + 9,000 GB-hours/mo (Ampere A1, ~2 OCPU / 12 GB RAM, usable as 1 or 2 VMs). Storage = 200 GB block (2 block volumes + 5 backups) + 20 GB object (standard+infrequent+archive combined) + 50,000 object API requests/mo. Networking = 10 TB/mo outbound egress, 2 VCNs, 1 Load Balancer (10 Mbps) + 1 Flexible NLB, 50 site-to-site VPN connections. Databases = up to 2 Autonomous DBs total (ATP/ADW/AJD/APEX), NoSQL (133M reads + 133M writes/mo, 25 GB/table up to 3 tables), 1 HeatWave (50 GB storage + 50 GB backup). Plus APEX 744 hrs/instance, Email 100/day, 5 Bastions, monitoring/logging within free quotas. Always Free services are usable for an unlimited period.
findings.eligibility: Open to any individual/account — no .edu or student-email requirement, no startup requirement. One Free Trial or Always Free account per person. Available in regions where commercial OCI is offered; some services (e.g., ARM, Autonomous DB) only in select/home regions.
findings.claim: Self-serve sign-up at oracle.com/cloud/free/ -> create a tenancy in a supported region -> provision Always Free shapes/services within the limits above. No charge while you stay within Always Free amounts. A credit/credit-like debit card is required at sign-up.
findings.expiry: No expiry / no renewal — Always Free has no time limit. Caveat: accounts idle for 30+ days may be deemed abandoned and suspended/terminated.
findings.gotchas: Card IS collected at sign-up for identity verification (a ~$1 temporary authorization hold is removed in 3-5 days; PIN, virtual, single-use and prepaid cards are NOT accepted). Do not conflate Always Free with the 30-day $300 trial. ARM is ~2 OCPU/12 GB (up to 2 VMs), NOT '4 micro VMs'; the 200 GB is the block-storage pool, not a per-VM figure. Autonomous DB capped at 2 instances; per-DB storage and region availability ('select regions') are not stated on the free page. Egress beyond 10 TB/mo and storage beyond free quotas are billed.

findings.name: 30-day Free Trial with US$300 credit (all OCI services)
findings.detail: Sign-up grants US$300 of credit usable on all eligible OCI services for 30 days, on top of Always Free. During the 30-day window you can also use the larger 'Trial' allowances listed on the page: Compute up to 4,500 hrs + 500 GB storage; Storage up to 7 TB block + 11 TB object; Autonomous DB up to 3,338 hrs + 2 TB Exadata; plus trial quotas for Functions, Kubernetes, WebLogic, HeatWave (5,000 hrs), Load Balancer, etc.
findings.eligibility: Any individual/account (students and startups alike) — no .edu or startup criteria. One Free Trial per person; a valid credit/credit-like debit card is required at sign-up for identity verification.
findings.claim: Same sign-up as the Free Tier (oracle.com/cloud/free/); the $300 trial credit attaches automatically to the new account. Spend it within 30 days. Optionally convert to Pay-As-You-Go at any point by adding a payment method.
findings.expiry: US$300 OR 30 days, whichever comes first; then the account drops to Always Free only (or Pay-As-You-Go if converted). Idle 30+ days may trigger suspension.
findings.gotchas: Card is REQUIRED at sign-up (temporary ~$1 auth hold; no PIN/virtual/prepaid cards). The $300 covers only the 30-day window — afterwards only Always Free remains unless you convert to Pay-As-You-Go. You are billed for data egress beyond 10 TB/mo, storage beyond free quotas, and any service not in Always Free. The live page shows US$300 (older marketing referenced a smaller figure; confirm $300, not $200).

findings.name: Oracle Startup program (application-based startup credit)
findings.detail: A separate, application-based credit program for startups, layered on top of the self-serve $300 trial. I could NOT read the live program page today: the legacy URL oracle.com/startupcloud/ returns 404 and oracle.com/startups/ is bot-gated (WAF 403) from this environment, so current credit amounts, duration, funding-cap and company-age criteria could not be independently confirmed.
findings.eligibility: Startups (application-based; typically partner/ecosystem criteria). Exact company-age / funding-cap limits not verifiable today.
findings.claim: Apply via the Oracle startup program portal (oracle.com/startups/ or a successor URL); on approval the startup receives cloud credit. Exact 2026 steps and limits unverified.
findings.expiry: Unknown — could not verify the live program terms today.
findings.gotchas: Do not rely on third-party numbers: the official page was inaccessible today (404/403), so re-verify amounts, funding cap, and duration in a normal browser. Distinguish this application-based program from the universal $300 trial / Always Free tier, which anyone can use.

findings.name: Education front — Oracle University (training) and Oracle Cloud Academy (appears sunset); no .edu-only free cloud offer
findings.detail: No distinct .edu-gated or student-email-only free cloud-credit program was found. The 'education' front is Oracle University (education.oracle.com), a free training/certification/skills-development portal (it confers no OCI cloud credit). The former 'Oracle Cloud Academy' (education.oracle.com/cloud-academy), which historically provided free OCI credits to learners/instructors, now returns a '404 / Oracle University' error page as of today, indicating that offering has been sunset or redirected.
findings.eligibility: No .edu requirement for any current Oracle free cloud offer. Oracle University is open (no student-email gate).
findings.claim: Students obtain cloud for free only via the universal Free Tier + $300 trial (a card is required). Oracle University courses are free at education.oracle.com but grant no OCI credit.
findings.expiry: Cloud Academy appears ended (its URL serves a 404/error page today).
findings.gotchas: Do not expect a student/.edu discount or dedicated student credit — use the standard sign-up. Some Oracle University certifications have paid components even though basic courses are free. Verify Cloud Academy status separately; as of 2026-10-22 its URL is an error page.

sunset_notes: Material 2025-2026 changes observed: (1) Oracle Cloud Academy (education.oracle.com/cloud-academy) — the last education-only free-credits front — now serves a '404 / Oracle University' error page as of 2026-10-22, i.e. it appears sunset; the education front is now just Oracle University (free training, no cloud credit). (2) Legacy startup program URL oracle.com/startupcloud/ returns 404; its successor oracle.com/startups/ is WAF/bot-gated (403) so live terms were unreadable today — treat startup-program figures as unverified. (3) The trial landing URL oracle.com/cloud/free/trial/ now 404s; the trial is folded into /cloud/free/. (4) Trial credit is US$300 for 30 days on the live page (older docs referenced a smaller credit). (5) ARM Always Free is ~2 OCPU/12 GB (up to 2 VMs), not '4 micro VMs' as in the task's known note (the 200 GB figure is the block-storage pool). Note: the oracle.com/cloud/free/ page carries a metadata 'Updated Date' of 2024-09-10, so the Always Free limits have not been re-edited since that date per the page metadata; values were re-fetched live on 2026-10-22. WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted), so all verifications were done by directly fetching official Oracle pages; the /startups/ and /startupcloud/ pages could not be read.

provider: edX; Google Cloud for Education (students, faculty, researchers); Google for Startups Cloud Program. Checked 2026-10-22.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial: $300 credit for 90 days (new customers)
findings.detail: $300 USD credit for new customers, usable for 90 days from sign-up. The trial ends at whichever comes first: credit spent or 90 days. Free Tier usage is not charged against the $300. During the trial, usage beyond the credit, beyond Free Tier limits, or on products outside the trial is charged to the payment method. The trial auto-closes at its end, resources stop, and there is a 30-day grace period to upgrade. Resources not moved to a paid billing account in that window are permanently deleted.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who has never been a paying Google Cloud, Maps Platform or Firebase user and has not previously signed up for the Free Trial. No .edu or student gate. A credit card or other valid payment method is REQUIRED at sign-up (the FAQ says it is a temporary authorization hold, not a charge). No region limit found in the text read.
findings.claim: Open cloud.google.com/free and click 'Get started for free'. Sign in with a Google account, accept terms, and add a payment method during sign-up. The trial period starts once the payment method is verified. Create projects under the trial billing account.
findings.expiry: Ends at $300 spent or 90 days after sign-up, whichever comes first. Then a 30-day grace period to upgrade.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a free tier: a card is required. Students who sign up by mistake will be charged for overage during the trial. The Google for Education teaching page itself warns students about this. Product-specific trials (see the next finding) are separate. Sources read today: cloud.google.com/free and cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-program-faqs.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Tier: always-free monthly quotas (no trial)
findings.detail: Monthly quotas that do not expire (the page says they are 'subject to change'). Compute Engine: 1 e2-micro VM per month. Cloud Storage: 5 GB-months Standard. BigQuery: 1 TB queries per month. Cloud Run: 2 million requests per month. Cloud Run functions: 2 million invocations per month. Pub/Sub: 10 GB messages per month. Firestore: 1 GB storage. Artifact Registry: 0.5 GB per month. Cloud Build: 120 build-minutes per day. Speech-to-Text: 60 minutes per month. Vision AI and Video Intelligence: 1,000 units each per month. Natural Language: 5,000 units per month. Workflows: 5,000 internal steps per month. Secret Manager: 6 secret versions per month. Cloud Shell: 5 GB persistent disk. GKE: one Autopilot or Zonal cluster per month. Agent Engine: first 180,000 vCPU-seconds (50 hours) and 360,000 GiB-seconds (100 hours) per month. Application Integration: 400 executions and 20 GiB per month. Cloud Source Repositories: up to 5 users. Datastream: 100 GiB of CDC per month.
findings.eligibility: Eligible customers only. Requires a Cloud Billing account that is active and in good standing, and no negotiated pricing contract or custom rate card (FAQ). Some quotas are stated per billing account. No student or startup gate. A card requirement for the free tier alone was not stated, but a billing account is needed.
findings.claim: Create a Google Cloud project on a billing account and stay inside the monthly limits. Nothing else to sign up for.
findings.expiry: Monthly limits reset each month. Not time-limited, but subject to change per the page.
findings.gotchas: Only the listed quotas are free. Usage above a limit is billed to the billing account. Earlier secondary summaries quoted different figures (for example Cloud Run 180,000 requests and Artifact Registry 50 GB). Those do not match the official page and were discarded.

findings.name: Google Cloud product-specific trials (in addition to the $300)
findings.detail: Spanner: 90-day free trial instance with 10 GB storage at no cost. Cloud SQL: 30-day free trial with an 8 vCPU Enterprise Plus instance, 64 GB memory and 100 GB storage. AlloyDB: 30-day trial instance. Looker: 30-day trial instance. GKE: full set of product capabilities for 90 days for no fee. Gemini Enterprise Plus edition: 30 days at no cost. The Spanner and Cloud SQL trial text also says new customers get $300 in credits on signup.
findings.eligibility: New Google Cloud customers. The FAQ section on product-specific trials has a sentence about what account is needed that was cut off in this run, so check each product page before starting.
findings.claim: Create the trial instance from the product's console page. FAQ wording: 'Create a 90-day Spanner free trial instance'.
findings.expiry: 30 or 90 days, per product. Post-trial behaviour was not verified in this run.
findings.gotchas: Trial instances are not the Always Free tier. Check each product's post-trial billing before leaving instances running. Also see https://cloud.google.com/free/docs/free-program-faqs.

findings.name: Google Skills student credits: 200 free credits (college and university students)
findings.detail: 200 Google Skills credits, usable on any lab in the catalog (hands-on labs, skill badges, courses). Credits expire one year after issue. Redeemable only for Google Skills educational content or Google Cloud certifications, and only for the institution's benefit. The form terms bar personal or hobby use and say credits are not a gift. They cannot pay for cloud infrastructure.
findings.eligibility: Currently enrolled college or university students at accredited institutions in eligible countries (the country list is on the form and was not captured in full). An institutional email is used to verify eligibility. The form does not say .edu specifically. The application is made on behalf of the institution.
findings.claim: From cloud.google.com/edu/students click 'Request credits'. The form is at services.google.com/fb/forms/googlecloudskillsbooststudenttrainingcreditsapplication/. Enter institutional email and country, accept terms and submit. Once approved, redeem on skills.google.com.
findings.expiry: One year after issue.
findings.gotchas: No payment step appears on the form, so no card is stated. Do not confuse this with the $300 trial, which needs a card. Form terms let Google share personal data with the institution and instructor. Country-limited.

findings.name: Google Skills Arcade: free gamified hands-on labs with badges and prizes
findings.detail: No-cost access to hands-on labs in a gamified space. Complete games and challenges, earn badges, and win swag and prizes. The page headline says 'earn prizes with Google Skills Arcade'.
findings.eligibility: Listed on the students page. Eligibility, age and country limits are not stated in the text read.
findings.claim: Follow the 'Explore Google Skills Arcade' link on cloud.google.com/edu/students (go.cloudskillsboost.google/arcade).
findings.expiry: Not stated.
findings.gotchas: Prize and swag terms were not read.

findings.name: Faculty teaching credits: up to $100 per teaching staff and $50 per student
findings.detail: Faculty can apply for Google Cloud credits: up to $100 per teaching staff member and up to $50 per student. Up to three courses per application. Credits are redeemable from approval until 16 weeks after course start, and are good for up to one year after course start. Course start must be within one year of applying.
findings.eligibility: Faculty only. Students cannot apply and are told to ask their professor. A school email with a valid .edu domain is required. Credits attach to that address, and only listed school domains can access them. Country list (about 80 countries, plus a US state list); other countries can only express interest. Needs a faculty directory link and a course URL showing the applicant teaches the course.
findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching/ (linked from cloud.google.com/edu/faculty). Provide school email, institution, faculty directory link, course name, start date, abstract of how credits will be used, course URL, school student domains and expected headcounts.
findings.expiry: Redeemable until 16 weeks after course start. Valid for up to one year after course start.
findings.gotchas: Not available to students directly. Course-specific and country-limited. No card step appears on the form.

findings.name: Research credits: $5,000 for faculty, PhD students and postdocs
findings.detail: The researchers hub advertises 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'. Terms: non-transferable and cannot be sold. Must be activated within 60 days of the project start date. Expire 365 days after coupon redemption or when fully used. GCP products only. Personal use is prohibited, and PhD students may use credits only for the project.
findings.eligibility: Faculty, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers at accredited higher-education institutions and eligible nonprofit research institutions in approved countries (country list on form). Institution email preferred. The application asks about external funding, prior cloud experience, and how the project will be funded after credits expire.
findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research/. Provide project name and start date, a proposal of up to 250 words (or a shared doc link), field of research, a pricing-calculator estimate link, and a Google Cloud Billing Account ID. Create the billing account first to redeem credits.
findings.expiry: Activate within 60 days of project start. Expire 365 days after redemption or when used up.
findings.gotchas: A billing account and a pricing estimate are required. Personal use is prohibited. Approval is discretionary. Whether a card is needed for the billing account is not stated on the form. Also see https://edu.google.com/programs/credits/research/.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program: Start tier (up to $2,000 credits and perks)
findings.detail: Up to $2,000 USD Google Cloud credits, valid one year. $200 Google Skills training credits. Google Workspace Business Plus free for 12 months for new sign-ups. AI webinars and content. Web3 perks (partner discounts from Quicknode, TRM, Allium and others).
findings.eligibility: Technology startup planning to seek venture funding soon. Founded within the last 24 months (per the benefits page). Not yet received Google Cloud credits beyond the free trial. Well-defined product roadmap. Acceptance is at Google's discretion. Excluded: educational institutions, government entities, nonprofits, personal blogs, dev shops, consultancies and agencies. Company email must match the company domain; personal email is not accepted (application guide). Workspace benefit: the company domain must not have had a paid Workspace plan in the 31 days before applying.
findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup ('Apply now' on the Start tier). Have a Google Cloud Billing ID (the application guide says to wait about 48 hours after creating it), a business email matching the domain, and a billing account owner on the same domain. Google matches the tier.
findings.expiry: Credits valid one year. Workspace 12 months from sign-up.
findings.gotchas: Official pages disagree on the founding window: 24 months on the benefits page, 'three to five years' on cloud.google.com/startup, and 10 years in an older application guide. Confirm on the application form. Third-party models (ex Anthropic) are billed directly and not covered by credits. Footnote: offer subject to change without notification.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program: Scale tier (up to $200,000 credits; $350,000 for AI startups)
findings.detail: Up to $200,000 USD Google Cloud credits over two years, or up to $350,000 for AI-first startups. Year 1: 100% up to $100,000 (AI-first: up to $250,000). Year 2: 20% up to an additional $100,000. Also: $500 Google Skills training credits; Google Workspace Business Plus free for 12 months for new sign-ups; $600 per month Google Maps Platform credits (separate application); up to $12,000 Google Cloud Enhanced Support credits for one year; a Startup Success Manager and Customer Engineers.
findings.eligibility: Pre-Seed or Seed raised within the last 5 years, or Series A within the last 12 months. Founded within the last five years. Not previously received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits. Qualifying funding is equity from institutional investors or VCs (SAFEs eligible; Web3 token raises and blockchain foundation grants accepted). Private equity, government innovation grants, prize funding, crowdfunding, angel and friends-and-family money do not qualify for Scale, but are evaluated for other tiers. Needs a working MVP, a roadmap, a verified company domain and publicly available proof of funding (application guide). Excludes educational institutions, nonprofits, government and agencies.
findings.claim: Apply at cloud.google.com/startup ('Apply now'). Provide a business email matching the public website, an active Google Cloud Billing ID owned by the same domain, and public proof of funding. Google reviews and matches the tier. Maps needs a separate application.
findings.expiry: Credits span two years. Enhanced Support for one year. Workspace 12 months.
findings.gotchas: The $350,000 headline is AI-first only; non-AI tops out at $200,000. Third-party models (ex Anthropic) are billed directly and not covered by credits. Workspace needs no paid Workspace plan on the domain within 31 days before applying. Startup terms excerpt says acceptance is at Google's sole discretion, including geographic region. Offer subject to change without notice.

findings.name: Google AI Studio: free Gemini API access for prototyping builders
findings.detail: Free access to the Gemini API in Google AI Studio for builders at the Prototyping stage, with instant access to a rapid prototyping environment, API key management, and access to Gemini and Gemma models. No credit amount or quota is stated on the pages read.
findings.eligibility: Startup pages describe the criteria as developers and builders working on small businesses, bootstrapped startups and self-funded ideas (no funding needed). Pre-funded builders and new Google Cloud customers are also named. No region limit found in the text read.
findings.claim: Use 'Start building in AI Studio' from cloud.google.com/startup and create an API key.
findings.expiry: Not stated.
findings.gotchas: Free quotas and rate limits were not read. The free-access statement came from a search excerpt of startup.google.com/cloud, not a full page read (https://startup.google.com/cloud/).

findings.name: edX audit track: free enrollment in most courses
findings.detail: Most edX courses can be audited for free before committing to the paid verified certificate track. Audit gives temporary access to select course content for the audit period. Graded assignments, exams and the certificate are not part of the audit track. The verified track is paid.
findings.eligibility: Any learner with a free edX account. Audit availability and access length are set per course (check the course page). No region or .edu limit found in the pages read.
findings.claim: On edx.org click 'Register for free' or 'Create your free account'. Open the course and choose 'Continue with audit track' or 'Select audit track'.
findings.expiry: Audit access is temporary. Length varies by course.
findings.gotchas: Audit is not a certificate, and graded work is locked. Financial assistance requires enrolling in the audit track first (see the next finding). Homepage: https://www.edx.org/.

findings.name: edX financial assistance: up to 80% off the verified-track fee
findings.detail: Eligible learners can get up to an 80% reduction on the verified-track fee for eligible courses. Maximum five approvals per 12-month period. Each course needs its own application. Assistance applies only to the course it was granted for and cannot be transferred. Decisions come by email, within up to four weeks. Apply before the course's published cutoff to upgrade to verified.
findings.eligibility: Financial need, judged on income, employment status and need. Course-by-course: not every course accepts assistance, and a list of non-qualifying courses is published. No .edu requirement and no region limit found in the page read. Degree programs can use federal aid (FAFSA) instead.
findings.claim: 1) Check the course homepage for assistance eligibility. 2) Enroll in the audit track. 3) Sign in to edX and complete the financial assistance application for that course. 4) Wait for the email decision (up to four weeks). 5) Upgrade to verified before the course's cutoff.
findings.expiry: Approval is per course. Cutoff varies by course. Five approvals per 12 months.
findings.gotchas: Cutoff dates vary, and missing one loses the discount. A denied application can be re-applied only if the error was in the submitted information. The homepage promo (code FALL2026, up to 20% off select courses and programs, 'for a limited time') is a discount, not a free offer.

sunset_notes:
Method: WebFetch on edx.org, cloud.google.com/edu and cloud.google.com/free returned truncated pages, so full page text was pulled with curl and read directly. WebSearch was exhausted after two searches (the session budget), so the 2025-2026 change scan rests on official pages fetched today plus two search excerpts (startup pages and the startup application guide). No sunset banner was found for the core offers: the $300/90-day trial, Always Free quotas, Skills student credits, faculty and research credits, and the Start and Scale startup tiers.

Changes and conflicts to watch: (1) The AI-first startup uplift ($250,000 in year 1, $350,000 total) appears on current official pages, while third-party copies (Innovation DuPage, Rho, a marketplace listing) still show a $200,000 maximum. This looks like a recent change; the effective date was not confirmed. (2) The Start-tier founding window conflicts: 24 months on /startup/benefits, 'three to five years' on /startup, 10 years in an older application guide, and 5 years in third-party copies. Treat as unresolved and confirm on the application form. (3) Rebrand: official pages now say Google Skills and Google Skills Arcade; third-party copies say Cloud Skills Boost. The amounts are the same (200 student credits; $200/$500 startup training credits). (4) edX: no free trial or membership was found. The edx-plus page embeds the text 'Our new subscription plan is not ready just yet' (medium confidence that it is user-facing). The homepage promo code FALL2026 shows no end date. (5) Discarded figures: earlier secondary WebFetch summaries (model memory, not on the pages) quoted Cloud Run 180,000 requests, Artifact Registry 50 GB, Cloud Storage Class A operations, '$325 student credits', '$1,000-$5,000 per faculty course' and 'per project' quotas. Official text read today: Cloud Run 2 million requests per month, Artifact Registry 0.5 GB per month, faculty credits $100 per staff member and $50 per student, and some quotas are per billing account. (6) Not verified in this run: Google Workspace for Education Fundamentals pricing (the Workspace page shows only a 'Sign up for Education Fundamentals free trial' button), Google AI or Gemini student plans, Google Cloud Certificate costs, data egress pricing, the full student country list, and the product-trial eligibility sentence that was cut off.

provider: MathWorks MATLAB and Simulink (student access, education programs, startup programs)

findings.name: Campus-Wide Access to MATLAB and Simulink (school-provided, free for students)
findings.detail: Students, faculty, staff and researchers at a school that holds a Campus-Wide license get unlimited use of MATLAB and Simulink desktop and online products, on and off campus and on any device (TAH support page). Students page: 'Your school provides free, unlimited access to MATLAB and Simulink.' The Campus-Wide product list covers the MATLAB and Simulink product families, toolboxes, MATLAB Grader, MATLAB Course Designer and Online Training Suite. Items marked with an asterisk need the license administrator to grant access. New academic products are added to the list automatically. This is an institution-level license with no student price.
findings.eligibility: Students at a school with Campus-Wide access only. Students must create a MathWorks Account using their student (school) email address. No individual application path for students at schools without the license appears on the fetched pages. No degree-level, region or .edu-only rule is stated beyond the school email. The 2,400+ school count in the brief was not verified.
findings.claim: 1) Confirm with school IT or the license administrator that the school has Campus-Wide access. 2) Open https://www.mathworks.com/products/matlab/student.html or https://www.mathworks.com/academia/students.html and click Get MATLAB. 3) Create or sign in to a MathWorks Account with the student email address. 4) Per the page, MATLAB can be used immediately once the school's Campus-Wide access applies.
findings.expiry: No end date or renewal term is stated on any fetched page. Access appears to follow the school's campus license term (inference, not verified).
findings.gotchas: School-dependent: students whose school lacks the license get nothing from this offer. The paid Student Suite (MATLAB, Simulink, Online Training, 60+ add-ons) is a separate purchase and not included. The expansion of the 'TAH' label was not found on the fetched pages.

findings.name: MATLAB Online basic (free tier for all MathWorks Account holders)
findings.detail: Free basic browser-based MATLAB Online: 20 hours per calendar month (page text: '20 hours per month of free use and access to 10 commonly used products'). Products: MATLAB, Simulink and nine toolboxes (per page summary). Continuous compute time 15 minutes; inactive idle timeout 15 minutes; MATLAB Drive storage 5 GB. Browser only, no desktop version. Support only via Help Center and MATLAB Central. The 20-hour window runs from the first to the last day of the calendar month and resets for the next month. At the cap, the current session can continue until sign-out or 15 minutes idle, but no new use until the next month. Self-paced online training and MATLAB Mobile reportedly do not count toward the 20 hours (page summary).
findings.eligibility: Any user with a MathWorks Account. The page says 'all users with a MathWorks Account will have access to the basic version of MATLAB Online by default.' No student status, purchase or license needed.
findings.claim: Create or sign in to a MathWorks Account through the login link on https://www.mathworks.com/products/matlab-online.html, then open MATLAB Online in the browser. No purchase step appears on the pages. Credit-card requirement not stated.
findings.expiry: No end date stated; this is a standing free tier. Hours reset every calendar month.
findings.gotchas: Not a trial, but capped: 20 hours per month, 15-minute continuous and idle limits, 10 products only (other toolboxes excluded), 5 GB storage. Linking an eligible license to your MathWorks Account upgrades you to full MATLAB Online: unlimited hours, 20 GB storage, 90-minute continuous compute and 60-minute idle timeout (the comparison table shows these figures). The eligible license list (including Campus-Wide and Personal Student licenses) and the Software Maintenance Service requirement are per page summary.

findings.name: 30-day free trial of MATLAB and Simulink (desktop and online)
findings.detail: Free 30-day trial with unlimited use for 30 days on desktop and online, including MATLAB, Simulink and 80+ products (trial page). FAQ: 'The trial period is 30 days'; to request an extension, contact Sales. The FAQ also says professors can get trials for their students.
findings.eligibility: No eligibility restrictions stated on the trial page or FAQ. Sign-in and a contact-information form are part of the Get MATLAB flow (page summary).
findings.claim: Open https://www.mathworks.com/campaigns/products/trials.html, click Get MATLAB, sign in or register with a MathWorks Account, complete the contact form, then install or open MATLAB.
findings.expiry: 30 days from start. Extension only by request to Sales.
findings.gotchas: A trial, not a free license: access ends after 30 days unless extended or purchased. Credit-card requirement is not stated on the fetched trial or FAQ pages (unknown; do not assume none). Do not confuse this with the free MATLAB Online tier, which is capped but ongoing.

findings.name: MATLAB Onramp free two-hour course and free online tutorials
findings.detail: MATLAB Onramp is 'a free two-hour, self-paced, interactive course that allows new users to learn how to use MATLAB effectively' (trial FAQ). The students resources page lists 'Free, Interactive Tutorials' with automatic-feedback exercises and full courses or single topics, linked to matlabacademy.mathworks.com (page summary, not raw-checked).
findings.eligibility: Described for new users; no eligibility restriction stated.
findings.claim: Open MATLAB Onramp from the link in the trial FAQ, or the online courses link on https://www.mathworks.com/academia/students/resources.html. No purchase or license step appears.
findings.expiry: None stated.
findings.gotchas: Training only; grants no software license. Whether course time counts toward the MATLAB Online 20-hour cap was not verified (page summary says self-paced online training does not count).

findings.name: Student competitions: complimentary software, training and mentoring
findings.detail: The students page states: 'MathWorks provides complimentary software, training, and mentoring' for its competitions, which include hackathons and student challenges (Simulink Student Challenge, AI Challenge and others on the competitions pages). No amounts, license durations or seat counts are stated on the students page. Prize details and per-competition rules were not read.
findings.eligibility: Students who enter a MathWorks-sponsored competition. Rules are set per competition and were not read.
findings.claim: Choose a competition from https://www.mathworks.com/academia/students/competitions.html and follow its registration page.
findings.expiry: Per competition; not stated on the students page.
findings.gotchas: Competition-specific, not a standing license. The quoted wording is verified, but how the software is delivered and for how long was not checked on the individual competition pages.

findings.name: MathWorks Accelerator Program: free in-kind licenses for startups at partner accelerators
findings.detail: Startups incubated at one of 500+ partner accelerators receive an in-kind software sponsorship: 'up to 10 user licenses for 12 months of free software' covering the MATLAB and Simulink suite of products. No cost or IT administration burden for the accelerator or the startup. Benefits per page summary: application-engineer support, local-language training options with a 50% training-credit discount, and co-marketing.
findings.eligibility: 'All startups incubated at a partner organization regardless of size or funding' (page text). Only startups at a partner accelerator qualify. The page has no direct self-serve application.
findings.claim: Ask your accelerator director whether your accelerator is already a partner and request access, per the page. Accelerators that want to join can contact MathWorks at startupaccelerators@mathworks.com (page summary; email not raw-checked).
findings.expiry: 12 months of licenses per the page; renewal terms not stated.
findings.gotchas: Not self-serve; depends on the accelerator being a partner. Capped at 10 user licenses per startup. This is a free in-kind sponsorship, not a discount. Terms after the 12 months are not stated.

findings.name: MathWorks startup suites (NOT free: discounted annual licenses)
findings.detail: Discounted 'Get Low-Cost Access to MATLAB and Simulink' tiers, both annual individual licenses: 'MATLAB Suite' (includes 40+ add-on products) and 'MATLAB and Simulink Suite' (includes 90+ add-on products). Suite holders get free access to the Online Training Suite Subscription. Prices render as unfilled template variables on the fetched page, so no dollar amount was confirmed.
findings.eligibility: Startups meeting all of: founded within the last 5 years; fewer than 15 engineers; less than USD 1 million annual revenue. 'Angel and venture capital funding levels are not criteria for acceptance' (no funding cap). No industry restriction stated.
findings.claim: Use the 'Apply now' or 'Request application' button on https://www.mathworks.com/products/startups.html to submit the application.
findings.expiry: Annual license; renewal terms and renewal pricing not stated.
findings.gotchas: Paid and discounted, not free. Price not visible in the fetched text. Startups sponsored through a partner accelerator get the free route instead (see the accelerator finding).

sunset_notes:
No sunset and no material 2025-2026 change was found on the official MathWorks pages read on 2026-10-22; the '(c) 1994-2026' footer is not a change. Pages were read as raw HTML via curl from mathworks.com (sitemap at https://www.mathworks.com/sitemap.xml used to locate pages) plus WebFetch summaries. Limits: the WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no news, changelog or forum check was possible. One DuckDuckGo query was attempted through WebFetch after the search-budget refusal, which the tool output had advised against; it returned a bot challenge with no results, and nothing from it was used.

Not found or not verified: free trial credits, cloud credits or per-student free licenses beyond the findings above; credit-card requirements (not stated for any offer); region limits for the free MATLAB Online tier (not stated; some pricing options show 'Not available in your region'); the 2,400+ campus-wide school count and the expansion of 'TAH'; MATLAB Mobile terms; the Student Suite price (not visible in fetched text). The brief's ~$675/yr student price is unconfirmed. The pricing page (https://www.mathworks.com/pricing-licensing.html) shows 'USD 940 per year' for an 'Individual License' with an intended-use selector (Standard, Startups, Academic, Student, Home), but the figure is not clearly tied to the Student option. Other academic license types (Academic Individual, Academic Teaching, Primary and Secondary School, Community College) appear on the pricing and versions pages; their prices and whether any are free were not verified.

provider: Google Cloud for Education and Students (Education and Student Programs), plus the Google for Startups Cloud Program and general Google Cloud free offers

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial: $300 credit for 90 days (new customers)
findings.detail: Signup creates a Free Trial billing account preloaded with a $300 Welcome credit valid for 90 days (cloud.google.com/free; signup FAQ). The trial ends at the first of: $300 spent, 90 days elapsed, or upgrade to a paid account (Free Trial Terms section 1.3, last modified 2026-02-12). Free Tier usage is not charged against the credit, and the credit can cover usage above Free Tier limits. On the trial, Compute Engine is capped at 8 concurrent cores (section 3.1) and some services are unavailable (section 3.3). Upgrading keeps unused credit, which still expires 3 months after the trial start (section 4.2). When the trial ends, access stops; there are 30 days to migrate data (except Compute Engine) or upgrade (section 5.2).
findings.eligibility: New Google Cloud customers only: never a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform or Firebase, and never previously signed up for the Free Trial (official docs). US and/or Mexican federal, state or local government entities are excluded unless Google agrees in writing (section 1.2). No .edu or student-email rule; a student qualifies as an individual.
