No startup age or funding rule applies. A payment method is required (see gotchas). Some countries also require bank account verification.
findings.claim: Open cloud.google.com/free and click Get started for free (or go to console.cloud.google.com/freetrial), sign in with a Google account, complete the Free Trial signup, add a valid payment method and verify identity, then create a project. The 90-day clock starts when the billing account is created. The Firebase console also routes eligible users into this signup (since March 2025).
findings.expiry: 90 days from billing account creation, or earlier at $300 spend or upgrade. Unused credit expires at day 90 (3 months after start if upgraded).
findings.gotchas: A credit card or other valid payment method is REQUIRED. It is not charged, but authorization holds can stay 1 to 14 business days. This is the key difference from the education credit programs, which need no card. Google may modify or terminate the trial at any time (section 3.6). An expired or invalid card can suspend the account (section 3.5). Faculty pages warn that this trial needs a card, so students should be steered to the education credits instead.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Tier: always-free monthly limits (20+ products)
findings.detail: More than 20 products have monthly free usage. The allowance does not expire but is subject to change, and it is not charged against the $300 trial credit (cloud.google.com/free). Examples from the current list: Compute Engine 1 e2-micro instance per month; Cloud Storage 5 GB-months Standard; BigQuery 1 TB of queries per month; Cloud Run 2 million requests per month; one GKE Autopilot or Zonal cluster per month; Cloud Run functions 2 million invocations per month; Pub/Sub 10 GB of messages per month; Firestore 1 GB storage; Cloud Build 120 build-minutes per day; Speech-to-Text 60 minutes per month; Vision AI 1,000 units per month; Natural Language API 5,000 units per month; Secret Manager 6 secret versions per month; Cloud Shell 5 GB disk; Artifact Registry 0.5 GB per month; Workflows 5,000 steps per month; Agent Engine 180,000 vCPU-seconds and 360,000 GiB-seconds per month. Compute Engine detail (official docs): the e2-micro is free only in us-west1 (Oregon), us-central1 (Iowa) and us-east1 (South Carolina); it includes 30 GB-months of standard persistent disk and 1 GB per month of outbound North America data; the limit is by time, not per instance; GPUs and TPUs are excluded. Cloud Storage free usage applies to US regions (the docs name us-east1, us-west1, us-central1).
findings.eligibility: Any Google Cloud customer; the trial is not required, and the docs say existing customers can use it too. No .edu or student requirement; no startup rules. Region limits: the e2-micro and Cloud Storage allowances apply only in the listed US regions.
findings.claim: Create a project and Cloud Billing account in the console, create resources only in the free regions, and stay within each monthly limit. Set a Cloud Billing budget with alerts so overages are noticed.
findings.expiry: No expiry. Monthly limits reset each month. Google says the limits can change.
findings.gotchas: Usage above a free limit is billed at standard prices. Creating the e2-micro outside the three US regions is billed. GPUs and TPUs are never free here. Egress beyond 1 GB per month is billed. Whether a card is needed for free-tier-only use was not verified in this run.

findings.name: Product-level free trials (GKE, Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB, Looker, Bigtable, Gemini Enterprise)
findings.detail: Trial offers listed on cloud.google.com/free: GKE, full capabilities free for 90 days with no fee; Spanner, 90-day trial instance with 10 GB storage; Cloud SQL, 30-day trial instance with 8 vCPU Enterprise Plus, 64 GB memory and 100 GB storage; AlloyDB, 30-day trial with an 8 vCPU basic primary instance and up to 1 TB storage; Looker, 30-day trial instance with standard features; Bigtable, 10-day trial with a 1-node SSD cluster and up to 500 GB; Gemini Enterprise Plus edition, 30 days at no cost. The Cloud SQL, Spanner, AlloyDB and Bigtable entries also say new customers get $300 credit on signup.
findings.eligibility: Set per product on each trial page; not verified one by one. No .edu requirement. Startup age and funding rules do not apply.
findings.claim: From cloud.google.com/free, open the product's trial link ('Explore more offers') and create the trial instance in the console.
findings.expiry: Trial instance periods are 10 days (Bigtable), 30 days (Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, Looker, Gemini Enterprise Plus) or 90 days (GKE, Spanner).
findings.gotchas: Trial instances end when their period ends; check each product page for what happens next. Card requirements and region limits for each trial were not checked individually. Trial instances are separate from Free Tier usage.

findings.name: Students: 200 Google Skills training credits
findings.detail: Currently enrolled college and university students can request 200 Google Skills credits for hands-on labs, skill badges and courses on Google Skills, the platform formerly called Google Cloud Skills Boost (cloud.google.com/edu/students). Credits expire one year after they are issued. The same page lists Google Skills Arcade (no-cost gamified labs) and a no-cost YouTube preview of Google Cloud Certificates.
findings.eligibility: Verified college or university students at regionally accredited institutions in the listed countries. The list is long and includes the US, UK, Canada, Germany, India, Japan, Brazil, Mexico, Australia and Singapore. For-profit institutions are not supported (support.google.com/google-cloud-higher-ed/answer/10322652). The help text does not spell out a .edu rule or the verification method. No card requirement is stated.
findings.claim: Submit the Google Skills training-credits application form (services.google.com/fb/forms/googlecloudskillsbooststudenttrainingcreditsapplication/) with your institutional details. Requests can take up to two weeks. For more credits, use the same form. Then use the credits on skills.google.
findings.expiry: One year after issue.
findings.gotchas: These are lab and training credits for Google Skills. The official pages do not describe them as Cloud Billing dollars, so they do not fund your own Cloud projects. The portal domain changed to skills.google in October 2025 (see sunset_notes).

findings.name: Google Skills no-cost Starter subscription: 35 credits a month
findings.detail: The Starter subscription costs nothing and gives learners 35 credits each month for hands-on labs in Google Skills (support.google.com/qwiklabs/answer/9139481). Google's Skills announcements and the Developer Program FAQ also cite 35 monthly credits for GEAR program participants and Google Cloud Innovators community members. Paid Monthly Pro and Annual Developer Premium plans sit above it.
findings.eligibility: Any learner with a Google account. Not limited to students, and no .edu rule. Innovators membership is joined through My Communities and Programs on the developer profile. The card requirement for the no-cost plan was not verified.
findings.claim: Sign in at skills.google, open the profile menu, go to Settings, then Subscriptions, and select the Starter (no cost) plan. For the Innovators or GEAR route, join through the program pages.
findings.expiry: Monthly allotment. Whether unused credits roll over was not verified.
findings.gotchas: Credits are for labs only. The exact reset and rollover rules, and whether the free plan asks for a card, were not checked directly.

findings.name: Google Career Launchpad: no-cost AI and cloud training for higher education
findings.detail: Career Launchpad gives higher-education institutions (and government and nonprofit workforce organizations) no-cost generative-AI and cloud training. It includes DeepMind's AI Research Foundations curriculum, Google Cloud Certificates, hands-on labs and Educator Guides. Faculty also get Google Skills credits to add labs to coursework. Google Skills Arcade is always-on and no-cost. Google Cloud Certificates carry an ACE recommendation of up to 10 college credits (page footnote). Career Dreamer is US-only. The page mentions a 50% certification discount for some learning-path completers; conditions were not checked.
findings.eligibility: Institutional program run by faculty facilitators at higher-education institutions. The page sets no .edu rule. Career Dreamer is US-only. The country list was not checked. No card requirement is stated.
findings.claim: Faculty apply through the Apply button on cloud.google.com/edu/faculty/career-launchpad (faculty form: services.google.com/fb/forms/googlecloudcareerlaunchpadapplication/).
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page. Expiry for the Skills credits within this program was not confirmed.
findings.gotchas: This is non-cash training, not a credit balance. The certification discount and ACE college-credit conditions were not verified.

findings.name: Education (teaching) credits: up to $100 per teaching staff member and $50 per student
findings.detail: Eligible faculty can apply for up to $100 in Google Cloud credits per teaching staff member and up to $50 in Cloud credits per student (cloud.google.com/edu/faculty). Approval issues coupons: faculty get codes for themselves and staff, plus a URL to send to students. Each course's credit is tracked in its own Cloud Billing account. Credits cover most Google Cloud products, and free-tier usage does not count against them (Cloud Billing edu-grants doc). Credits may not be used for course infrastructure, commercial use or personal use.
findings.eligibility: Faculty only; students cannot apply but can ask faculty to apply. Faculty must use an official school email on a valid .edu domain (or nominate another email if they have none). In the US the institution must be a regionally accredited program; outside the US it must be a higher-learning institution that awards degrees in an eligible country. For-profit institutions are excluded. The application form has a country list (includes the US, UK, Canada, India, Japan, Germany, Australia and Brazil). Up to 3 courses per submission, with course start no later than one year away. Students must confirm a school email to redeem. The support page says sign-up needs no credit card.
findings.claim: Faculty apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching (up to 3 courses, expected student and TA counts, school faculty-directory link). After approval, faculty get coupon codes and a student URL. Students verify their school email, then click Redeem now in the coupon email and accept the terms in the Google Cloud console. Questions go to CloudEduGrants@google.com.
findings.expiry: Redeemable from approval until 16 weeks after course start. Validity sources conflict: up to 1 year after course start (program page), 12 months after course start (help page), and 1 year after redemption (Cloud Billing docs). Confirm against the approval email.
findings.gotchas: The official amounts are per teaching staff ($100) and per student ($50). The '$100 per course' wording in the brief is not how the official page states it. Credits are non-transferable and tied to the school email. Google may revoke awards or change criteria at any time. Check spam for the confirmation email, which should arrive within 24 hours.

findings.name: Research credits: up to $5,000 for faculty, PhD students and postdocs
findings.detail: Researchers can apply for up to $5,000 in Google Cloud research credits (cloud.google.com/edu/researchers says 'Apply for $5,000 in research credits'; the application page text retrieved did not restate the figure). The credit must be activated within 60 days of the project start date on the application. It may be issued in increments and is for proof of concept, evaluation or comparison, workshops or training, and open-source development. The application asks for a funding plan for after the credit expires.
findings.eligibility: Faculty, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers at accredited higher-education institutions, plus eligible nonprofit research institutions, in approved countries (the list includes the US, UK, Canada, Germany, Japan, India, Australia, Singapore and South Africa). An institution account is preferred but not strictly .edu. PhD students may not use the credit for personal use. The GPAR program (Google Public Sector Program for Accelerated Research) is US-only and gives pricing co-investment, not credit. No card requirement is stated.
findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research. Provide personal and organization details, a project proposal (up to 250 words), the total from your pricing calculator with a link to it, a Google Cloud billing account ID, and a funding plan for after the credit expires.
findings.expiry: Expires 365 days after coupon redemption or when fully used, whichever comes first.
findings.gotchas: Non-transferable, with no sale or barter and no commercial use. The $5,000 headline comes from the researchers landing page. Confirm the cap on the form before relying on it, since 'up to' means awards can be smaller.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program, Start tier: up to $2,000 in credits
findings.detail: The Start tier gives up to $2,000 in Google Cloud credits valid for one year (cloud.google.com/startup/benefits). Also: $200 in Google Skills training credits; 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus free for new sign-ups (conditions apply); AI webinars and content; and Web3 partner perks for Web3 startups. This is the self-serve entry tier.
findings.eligibility: Technology startup with a working MVP, a clear business model and a well-defined product roadmap, that plans to seek venture funding soon. Founded within the last 24 months. Has not received Google Cloud credits beyond the free trial. The business email must match the company website domain, and the billing account must be owned and administered by someone on that domain. Not open to educational institutions, nonprofits, government entities, dev shops or consultancies, companies that have IPO'd or been acquired, or crypto mining. Google decides acceptance at its sole discretion. A Cloud Billing account is required; card requirement not stated.
findings.claim: Create a Cloud Billing account in the console and note its 18-character billing account ID, since credits attach to it. Confirm a business email on your website domain. Apply through the Apply now button at cloud.google.com/startup. On approval, credits are issued to the billing account named in the application.
findings.expiry: Valid one year (official page). Some third-party sites say two years; the official page does not.
findings.gotchas: Credits apply only to Google first-party pay-as-you-go or consumption products. Subscription, prepay and annual-license products are excluded, as are third-party Marketplace and Model Garden offerings. Third-party models (such as Claude) are billed directly. Credits cannot be shared, split or resold. Workspace is free only if the company domain had no paid Workspace plan in the 31 days before applying. Re-applying is possible if earlier credits went unused.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program, Scale tier: up to $200,000 (AI-first up to $350,000)
findings.detail: Scale tier: up to $200,000 in Google Cloud credits over two years. Year 1 covers 100% of spend up to $100,000; year 2 covers 20% of spend up to a further $100,000. AI-first startups: up to $350,000 (year 1 100% up to $250,000; year 2 20% up to $100,000 more). Also: 12 months of Google Workspace Business Plus free (separate application), $600 per month of Google Maps Platform credits (separate application), up to $12,000 in Google Cloud Enhanced Support credits for one year, Google Skills training credits (the benefits page lists $500 for this tier; verify), and a Startup Success Manager as you grow.
findings.eligibility: Venture-backed startups. Pre-Seed or Seed rounds within the last 5 years; if a Series A has been raised, it must be within the last 12 months. Founded within the last five years (benefits page; the program footnote says 3 to 5 years depending on tier). Has not received more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits before. Non-venture funding (private equity, bank loans, government grants, crowdfunding, friends and family) does not qualify. Stealth startups are accepted on investor or accelerator verification. The AI-first tier requires Gemini or Gemma as a foundation of the primary product (AI program page). Must be in a region where Google Cloud is generally available and sold through self-service purchasing. Acceptance is at Google's discretion, weighing funding stage and type, business model, founder experience, product usage, age, growth and total funding. No .edu rule. A billing account is required; card requirement not stated.
findings.claim: Have your funding round details, any investor or accelerator affiliation (enter these for stealth verification), billing account ID and website-domain business email ready. Apply at cloud.google.com/startup (Apply now). Credits are issued to the billing account after approval. Maps and Workspace benefits need separate applications.
findings.expiry: Credits run over two years in year-1 and year-2 tranches. The exact expiry of unused balances was not in the official text read.
findings.gotchas: Same first-party-only exclusions and third-party model billing as the Start tier. Credits cannot be shared, split or resold. Prior credits above $5,000 disqualify. Some third-party guides say the Scale tier is usually reached through a partner investor or accelerator; the official page does not say so. Approval is not guaranteed.

findings.name: Startups in prototyping: free Gemini API access in Google AI Studio
findings.detail: The prototyping track of the Google for Startups program gives free access to the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, with API key management, access to Google models such as Gemini, Gemini Omni and Nano Banana, and Build mode (cloud.google.com/startup and startup.google.com/cloud). This is product access, not a Cloud Billing credit.
findings.eligibility: Developers and builders at small businesses, bootstrapped startups and self-funded ideas, which are the stated criteria. No venture funding is required. No .edu rule. Card and regional requirements were not verified.
findings.claim: Use the Start building in AI Studio link on cloud.google.com/startup and sign in with a Google account to create an API key.
findings.expiry: Not stated. Free-tier quotas can change.
findings.gotchas: Rate limits and data-use terms for the free tier were not verified in this run. Third-party models are not covered by program credits.

sunset_notes: 2025-2026 changes and checks. (1) Google Cloud Skills Boost was renamed Google Skills in October 2025, and its domain moved from cloudskillsboost.google to skills.google (Google Cloud blog, 2025-10-09; a third-party blog covers the domain move). The 200 student credits and the 35-credit Starter plan now run on Google Skills. (2) The Free Trial Terms were revised on 2026-02-12, and that version is current. The $300, 90-day trial and the 3-month credit expiry are unchanged. The 8-core Compute Engine cap and the US/Mexico government exclusion appear in the current terms. The older 12-month trial applies only to trials started before 2020-08-17. (3) Since March 2025 the Firebase console routes eligible users straight into trial signup. (4) The Google for Startups Cloud Program was restructured in November 2024 (Start up to $2,000; Scale up to $200,000; AI-first up to $350,000). The official pages read today match that structure, and no 2025-2026 change to it was found. (5) No sunset was found for the Free Tier e2-micro (US regions only), the Cloud Storage free tier, the education teaching or research credits, the Career Launchpad, or the 200 student credits. Open items: the Career Launchpad credit expiry and the research application cap were not confirmed. Excluded as unverified or wrong: a 60-day trial (from unverified model memory; the official figure is 90 days), a $200 student credit ('historically up to $300'), a $150 exam voucher, a $2,000 Innovators credit, '500+ free modules', and a '$100 per course' instructor credit (official wording is $100 per teaching staff plus $50 per student). Out of scope or paid: Google Developer Program Premium ($299 per year), Google Workspace for Education, and the Maps Platform and Firebase free tiers (not verified in this run). Non-monetary items not counted as offers: Developer Student Clubs, Cloud OnAir events, Gemini Startup Forum, and equity-free accelerators. Limitation: the web search budget ran out before a 2026 news sweep, so 'no change' statements rest on the official pages read today, not on a full search of 2026 news. Some third-party sites say the Start tier is valid for two years; the official page says one year.
label_name: GCP for Education / Google Cloud for Stu

findings.name: Cloud Free plan (permanent $0 tier)
findings.detail: $0 on Appsmith Cloud, listed as 'Free' on the official pricing page. Limits per the official page: up to 5 users for cloud; 5 workspaces; Git versioning with 3 repos; 3 standard access roles; Google SSO (the comparison table also lists 'Google and GitHub OAuth', see sunset_notes); public apps only (table row 'Embed public apps'; private-app embedding is Enterprise); community support on Discord; 'Powered by Appsmith' branding stays on; backup/restore only when updating to a higher Appsmith version. Apps are listed as Unlimited in the comparison table. Not included on Free: Workflows, reusable packages, custom roles, audit logs, CI/CD, custom domains, SAML/OIDC, SCIM, managed hosting.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who opens a cloud account. No student, .edu, startup or funding check on any page read. No region limit stated.
findings.claim: Sign up at appsmith.com with an organization name (becomes orgname.appsmith.com). No payment step is described for the Free plan.
findings.expiry: None stated. The homepage says the core platform is 'free to use forever'.
findings.gotchas: The pricing page defines a user as any member added to a workspace, so viewers count toward the 5-user cap, not just builders. Going past 5 users means moving to Business at $15/user/month. The '10 apps' limit in the brief is not on Appsmith's official pricing (table says Apps: Unlimited); that figure matches ToolJet's free cloud plan (2 builders, 50 end users, 10 apps). The 'public apps only' restriction appears as the 'Public apps' bullet and 'Embed public apps' row; the page does not explicitly say login-protected apps are blocked on Free.

findings.name: Community Edition (free self-hosted, Apache 2.0)
findings.detail: Free open-source edition you run yourself. Official pricing page: 'Our open-source low code application platform, available for free.' Homepage: Community Edition is 'fully maintained, community supported' and the core platform is 'free to use forever'. License: Apache 2.0 (Terms section 2.1.1 and the GitHub repo). Install routes in the repo README: Docker (recommended), Kubernetes, AWS AMI. No user or workspace cap is stated for Community; the 5-user limit is labelled 'for cloud'. Community is not a column in the comparison table, so whether Business-only features (workflows, custom roles, audit logs, CI/CD) are available on Community is not stated.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. No account verification, student or startup check on the pages read. Runs on your own machine, private server or cloud VM.
findings.claim: 1) Pick an install route from the GitHub README (Docker recommended, Kubernetes or AWS AMI). 2) Follow the installation guide at docs.appsmith.com. 3) Only if you need Business features on your own server, use the self-hosted 15-day trial (see the trial finding) or buy a license.
findings.expiry: None stated for Community; the homepage says the core platform is free to use forever.
findings.gotchas: You carry the hosting costs (servers, storage, bandwidth), upgrades, backups and security patching; Appsmith publishes no estimate. Third-party site aitoolsatlas.ai says Community has 'unlimited users and apps'; this is not on Appsmith's own pages, so treat it as unverified. Business-only features are not documented as included in Community.

findings.name: Business Edition 15-day free trial (all new signups, cloud or self-hosted)
findings.detail: Official pricing page: 'All new signups receive a 15-day free trial of Appsmith Business, and there is no credit card required to start.' Docs intro: 'Try the Business Edition free for 15 days, then continue with Community Edition or upgrade to a paid plan.' Self-hosted route: a 'Start free trial (self-hosted)' button; self-hosted signups receive a license key with setup instructions. This is 15 days of Business features, not a credit pool; no trial credits were found on Appsmith's pages.
findings.eligibility: 'All new signups'. No student, startup or .edu requirement stated. No region limit stated.
findings.claim: Cloud: sign up at appsmith.com with an organization name and the trial starts. Self-hosted: click 'Start free trial (self-hosted)', receive the license key, follow the setup instructions and run the instance with that key.
findings.expiry: 15 days from signup. No renewal or extension stated. At the end you can activate Business or keep using the Free tier.
findings.gotchas: Activating Business bills monthly by credit card you provide at activation (per the pricing page). The pages do not say what happens to Business-only features, or to accounts above the Free 5-user cap, when the trial ends, so check before inviting users. The no-card wording comes from the pricing page; the docs page is silent on it, so confirm at signup.

findings.name: Appsmith Startup Program: $30,000 in credits valid 12 months
findings.detail: $30,000 worth of Appsmith credits, valid for 12 months once accepted, plus all Business plan features and access to Appsmith developer advocates. FAQ (summarised fetch): no restriction on usage hours or number of apps. Perks from the FAQ (medium confidence, summarised fetch): a 30% discount on upgrading to Enterprise as a program member; an extra 2 months free for each verified referral, requested by email to startups@appsmith.com. Credits are a platform credit, not cash; the page does not say how they are drawn down.
findings.eligibility: All four apply: (1) you plan to use Appsmith for your own startup; (2) you have raised less than $10M in funding; (3) you were incorporated less than 2 years ago; (4) you are looking to host Appsmith on your own infrastructure. Existing Community users can enrol if they meet the same criteria. Not stated: region or country limits, a credit card requirement, a cap on accepted startups, or a program end date.
findings.claim: 1) Check the four criteria on appsmith.com/startup-program. 2) Click 'Join now' and fill in the linked Google Form. 3) Appsmith's team schedules a call after you apply. 4) Questions go to startups@appsmith.com. Acceptance timing is not stated.
findings.expiry: Credits valid 12 months once accepted. Program end date and acceptance start date are not stated.
findings.gotchas: Hosting on your own infrastructure is a stated condition, so a cloud-only startup may not qualify; ask startups@appsmith.com. The $10M and 2-year limits are checkable. Arithmetic only, not program terms: at the $15/user/month Business list price, $30,000 equals about 2,000 user-months (about 167 users for 12 months). Third-party aggregators (sourcey.com, claimstartupgrants.com) list the same $30K offer; their eligibility text is secondary, so rely on the official page.

findings.name: Business Cloud 30-day free promo (limited time, June 2025)
findings.detail: From the June 2, 2025 Forge launch-week post, Day 5: 'For a limited time, we're offering 30 days of Business Cloud for free to new subscribers. Email discount@appsmith.com to claim your free offer and start building.' This is a 30-day trial of hosted Business, not a student or startup program.
findings.eligibility: 'New subscribers' (not defined on the page). Not restricted to students or startups.
findings.claim: Email discount@appsmith.com and ask for the 30-day Business Cloud offer.
findings.expiry: Unknown. The post says 'limited time' with no end date. Could not confirm the offer is still running in October 2026.
findings.gotchas: Probably lapsed since the June 2025 post; confirm by email before planning around it. Not a student or startup offer.

sunset_notes: Changes and gaps as of 2026-10-22. (1) Jan 2025 pricing overhaul (announced in Launch Week, Jan 12, 2025): moved from usage-based pricing (tracker cites $0.40/hour) to Business at $15/user/month; Free capped at 5 cloud users (previously unlimited) and 5 workspaces (new quota); Business capped at 99 users (previously unlimited); Enterprise $2,500/month for 100 users. Sources: https://www.appsmith.com/blog/appsmith-launch-week-1 and https://pricingsaas.com/companies/appsmith/diffs/2025Q1. (2) GitHub SSO: the tracker says it was removed from Free in 2025, but the official page shows both 'Google SSO' (bullet) and 'Google and GitHub OAuth' (table). Verify before relying on GitHub login on Free. (3) The brief's '10 apps' Free limit is not on Appsmith's official pricing; it matches ToolJet's free cloud plan. (4) Third-party comparison pages dated Aug to Oct 2026 (Softwr, 30 Aug 2026; Taskade, Sep 2026; Jetadmin, 26 Sep 2026; Awesomic, 8 Oct 2026) show the same Free (5 cloud users, 5 workspaces, 3 Git repos) and Business ($15/user/month) terms, so the plan terms look unchanged through October 2026 (medium confidence, secondary sources). (5) No education, student, teacher or academic license found, so no education finding is listed. Checked: the pricing page; appsmith.com/industry/education (only 'Start building for free' and sales@appsmith.com); the docs intro; the homepage; and the GitHub Student Developer Pack page (Appsmith not found there; the fetch may not have shown every offer). Institutions are routed to sales@appsmith.com. (6) Startup program: no end date or acceptance timeline is stated; aggregator record dates (Sept to Oct 2026) are not program start dates. (7) The Business Cloud 30-day promo is from June 2025, time-limited, and its current status is unconfirmed. (8) Search gap: the web search budget ran out during this run, so I could not search for other 2026 announcements, other startup or education programs, or the current status of the Business Cloud promo. Official pages were fetched directly instead. To run those searches, raise CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION and rerun.

provider: Google: Gemini API Free tier (Google AI Studio), Vertex AI express mode, Google Cloud Free Trial and Free Tier, Google for Startups Cloud Program, Google for Education and student AI offers (verified 2026-10-22)

findings.name: Gemini API Free tier (Google AI Studio): free-of-charge models
findings.detail: Free input and output tokens, Google AI Studio access, and 'limited access to certain models' (official pricing page, fetched 2026-10-22). Models marked 'Free of charge' on the Free Tier column include Gemini 3.8 Flash (confirmed in raw text), Gemini 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash, 2.5 Flash-Lite, 3 Flash Preview, 3.1 Flash-Lite and other Flash, Live, TTS, transcription, Embedding 2 and Gemma 4 entries (a third-party count says 23 of 35 pricing-page entries are free). Not free: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Gemini 4 Argon, Omni Flash, image models including 2.5 Flash Image, Veo 3.1, Lyria, 2.5 Pro Preview TTS, and grounding on Gemini 3+ models. Free-tier data: 'Used to improve our products' = Yes (paid tier = No). Numeric free-tier limits are NOT published in Google's docs: the rate-limits page says limits apply per project (not per API key), reset at midnight Pacific, are 'not guaranteed', and are shown per project in AI Studio (sign-in required). Third-party figures conflict (2.5 Pro 5 RPM / 100 RPD in several 2026 guides vs 50 RPD in a May 2026 guide; Flash-Lite 15 RPM / 1,000 RPD vs 30 RPM / 1,500 RPD). Treat numeric limits as unverified.
findings.eligibility: Any Google account to sign in to AI Studio. Official rate-limits table lists Free qualification as 'Active project or free trial'. No billing account or credit card is listed as required for Free tier; Tier 1 is the first tier that requires linking an active billing account. No .edu requirement, no startup age or funding cap. No country restriction appears on the captured pages (an older cached variant of the rate-limits page said 'Users in eligible countries'; unverified).
findings.claim: 1) Open aistudio.google.com and sign in with a Google account. 2) Create an API key (AI Studio creates or uses a Google Cloud project). 3) Call a free-tier model such as gemini-2.5-flash or gemini-3.8-flash without linking billing. 4) Read the project's live RPM/TPM/RPD limits in AI Studio.
findings.expiry: No end date published for the free tier. The model lineup changes with model lifecycle (see sunset_notes).
findings.gotchas: Free-tier prompts and responses may be used to improve Google products; do not send private or regulated data. Spend-based limit is N/A on Free, but RPM/TPM/RPD overages return 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. The $300 Google Cloud trial credit cannot pay Gemini API in AI Studio costs (official trial doc). Official billing tiers: Tier 1 = link active billing, billing tier cap $250; Tier 2 = $100 paid + 3 days, cap $2,000; Tier 3 = $1,000 paid + 30 days, cap $20,000 to $100,000+. Spend-based limits per rolling 10 minutes: Tier 1 $10, Tier 2 $50, Tier 3 $200. Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and Gemini 4 Argon are paid-only.

findings.name: Vertex AI express mode (now 'Agent Platform in express mode'): card-free 90-day free tier
findings.detail: Free tier for new Google Cloud users for up to 90 days, within specified quotas, with no billing information required. Rate limits in express free tier: gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-flash-lite and gemini-2.5-flash-image each max 10 requests per minute; gemini-3-pro-image, gemini-3.1-flash-image, gemini-3.1-pro-preview and gemini-3-flash-preview are 'Dynamic' (no fixed number published). Only the listed models are supported; dedicated Live API models (for example gemini-3.8-live) are not. Free-tier data source: Google Drive only. Separate from, and not available through, the Google Cloud Free Program or the $300 trial.
findings.eligibility: Developers with a @gmail.com Google Account. The 90-day free tier is for NEW Google Cloud users; existing Google Cloud users can sign up for express mode but use their existing billing account on the paid tier. No .edu requirement and no startup cap. Card-free in the free tier.
findings.claim: In the Google Cloud console, open Express Mode, sign in with a @gmail.com account and accept the sign-up (APIs are enabled automatically and an API key is issued), then follow the Vertex AI Studio or API express-mode tutorial.
findings.expiry: 90 days from sign-up. The free tier is removed if you are an existing Google Cloud user or after you enable billing (then standard pay-as-you-go limits apply).
findings.gotchas: Quotas are small (10 RPM on the 2.5 models; 3.x models have no published number). Product renamed: Vertex AI is now part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (official Vertex AI release notes); docs and console names changed. Enabling billing ends the 90-day free tier.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Trial: $300 Welcome credit for 90 days
findings.detail: $300 Welcome credit valid for 90 days from sign-up, spendable on most Google Cloud products including AI APIs, with Free Tier monthly limits available during the trial. Not charged during the trial unless you upgrade. The credit cannot pay Gemini API in AI Studio costs (use the Gemini API free tier or prepay) or third-party partner (MaaS) generative AI models.
findings.eligibility: Only if you have never been a paying user of Google Cloud, Google Maps Platform or Firebase and have not previously signed up for the Free Trial. A credit card or other payment method valid for the trial period is REQUIRED (not card-free); some countries also require bank-account verification; Google places an authorization hold typically released within a few days to a month. Country availability follows Google's supported-countries list (not fetched this run). No .edu requirement and no startup cap.
findings.claim: Go to cloud.google.com/free and click 'Get started for free' (or console.cloud.google.com/freetrial). Sign up, add a payment method and complete verification; a Free Trial billing account preloaded with $300 is created. Upgrade later from the console Welcome page via 'Activate'.
findings.expiry: 90 days from sign-up or until the $300 is spent, whichever comes first. Then the trial billing account closes, with a 30-day grace period before unrecovered resources are permanently deleted. Upgrading ends the trial; leftover credit keeps its 90-day expiry.
findings.gotchas: Not a card-free offer. Free Tier products require a billing account. The $300 trial does not disqualify you from the Start startup tier (that tier excludes only credits received beyond the free trial, per official wording). Free Tier overage during a trial is paid from the $300 credit, capped at $300 total.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Tier (Always Free monthly limits, 20+ products)
findings.detail: Free usage of select Google Cloud products up to specified monthly limits. Official cloud.google.com/free page: 'free usage of 20+ popular products, including Compute Engine and AI APIs'. Per-product monthly quotas were not verified in this run; earlier third-party quota figures were not confirmed.
findings.eligibility: A Google Cloud billing account is required to access the Free Tier (official docs). Paid billing accounts pay for any overage; Free Trial accounts draw overage from the $300 credit. No .edu requirement, no startup cap, no region limit captured.
findings.claim: Create a billing account (through the Free Trial or a paid signup) and use the products within their monthly limits; monitor usage in the Billing console.
findings.expiry: Ongoing; no expiry stated for Free Tier monthly limits.
findings.gotchas: A billing account is needed even for free usage. Exceeding monthly limits on a paid account incurs charges. Exact limits differ by product, so read each product's free-tier page before relying on them.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program: Start tier (up to $2,000)
findings.detail: Up to $2,000 USD in Google Cloud credits, valid for one year. Google Workspace Business Plus free for 12 months for new signups (listed in the official comparison). Official Start-tier description: digital-native startups with a working MVP, a clear business model, and plans to seek venture funding soon.
findings.eligibility: Founded within the last 24 months; not yet received Google Cloud credits beyond the free trial. The listed criteria do not require a funding round. No .edu requirement. A card requirement is not stated on the captured program page; region not captured. Applications are reviewed and approved against eligibility; approval is not guaranteed.
findings.claim: Click 'Apply now' on cloud.google.com/startup/benefits (/startup/apply) and complete the application. The form itself was not captured; third-party guides say it asks for a company website, a company-domain email and billing account details.
findings.expiry: Credits valid for one year.
findings.gotchas: Small pool. Credits received beyond the free trial make you ineligible. Scale later requires having received no more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program: Scale tier (up to $200,000, coverage-based)
findings.detail: Up to $200,000 USD in Google Cloud credits, coverage-based (credit applies only to eligible usage): Year 1 = 100% of eligible usage up to $100,000; Year 2 = 20% of eligible usage up to an additional $100,000. Program credits cover Google's models including Gemini and Gemma. Also Google Workspace Business Plus free for 12 months (new signups) and '$600 monthly credits in Google Maps Platform' (official list; duration text truncated in capture). Official description: VC-funded startups ready to grow and scale.
findings.eligibility: Funding: raised Pre-Seed or Seed within the last 5 years, or Series A within the last 12 months. Qualifying investment: equity from institutional investors and VCs; SAFEs are eligible; Web3 token raises and blockchain foundation grants are accepted. Private equity, government innovation grants, prize funding, crowdfunding, angel, and friends and family funding do NOT qualify for Scale (evaluated for other tiers). Company: founded within the last five years (official; several third-party sites say 10 years). Operating in stealth is supported upon verification of funding. Prior credits: not more than $5,000 in Google Cloud credits received. No .edu requirement; a card requirement is not stated on the captured page.
findings.claim: Apply from the official benefits page (/startup/apply) with funding round details (investor, round, date). Google reviews eligibility and approves at its discretion. Partner and accelerator routes are third-party guidance and unverified.
findings.expiry: Two-year coverage structure (Year 1 and Year 2 as above); no renewal stated.
findings.gotchas: Coverage-based, not a lump sum: you are not paid out for unused coverage, and Year 2 drops to 20% coverage. Third-party sources (Rho, Questd, getcloudcredits) give founding-age and tier amounts that differ from the official page; the official page is used here. Angel and friends-and-family money does not count for Scale.

findings.name: Google for Startups Cloud Program: AI-first track (up to $350,000)
findings.detail: Up to $350,000 USD in Google Cloud credits for AI startups: Year 1 = 100% of eligible usage up to $250,000; Year 2 = 20% of eligible usage up to an additional $100,000. Also dedicated AI training, resources and experts, and AI webinars and content (official benefits page).
findings.eligibility: Same funding and company rules as Scale. The official captured text does not define 'AI startup'; third-party guides say the startup must use or plan to use Vertex AI or Gemini as a foundation of its product (unverified). Startup age and funding cap as for Scale.
findings.claim: Apply through the same Google for Startups Cloud Program application (/startup/apply); the AI-first tier is a higher tier within the same program and Google assigns it on review.
findings.expiry: Two-year coverage structure as for Scale.
findings.gotchas: Credits apply only to eligible usage. Overclaiming AI-first may land you in a lower tier (third-party guidance, unverified).

findings.name: Google Cloud for Education (students): 200 free Google Skills credits
findings.detail: 200 free Google Skills credits for free online labs, skill badges and courses; credits expire one year after issue. Also free Google Skills Arcade labs, a no-cost preview of Google Cloud Certificates on YouTube, and Developer Student Club chapters. These are learning and lab credits, not Google Cloud billing credits.
findings.eligibility: Students ('students can request access'). The captured page does not state a .edu email requirement or a student-verification method, nor any startup cap or card requirement. Region not captured.
findings.claim: Open cloud.google.com/edu/students, click 'Request credits' (Google Skills), and sign up for the learning-program emails if desired; Developer Student Club chapters are listed on the page.
findings.expiry: Each credit expires one year after it is issued.
findings.gotchas: These are training credits for labs and courses, not billing credits for production cloud spend. Do not confuse them with the $300 Free Trial.

findings.name: Google Cloud Teaching credits: faculty-only course credits
findings.detail: Google Cloud credits for courses, redeemable from approval until 16 weeks after the course start date and usable for up to 1 year after course start. Up to 3 courses per application. The official form does not state a per-course amount on the captured page (an older Google support article uses a $50 worked example, which is not a grant amount). Credits are for student hands-on learning; not for commercial or personal use and not for course infrastructure; crypto mining prohibited (older support article).
findings.eligibility: Faculty only: students cannot apply directly but can ask faculty to apply. Available only in the countries listed on the official form (includes the United States and the United Kingdom among others). Older support article: US regionally accredited institutions plus degree-awarding institutions in eligible countries; for-profit institutions not supported. Expected course start date must be within 1 year of the application date. No .edu email rule stated; faculty status at an institution is required.
findings.claim: Faculty submit the application at edu.google.com/programs/credits/teaching: personal and institution details, course name, expected start date, course abstract, and how credits will be used. Up to 3 courses. Only the most recent submission is reviewed.
findings.expiry: Redeem within 16 weeks after course start; credits valid for up to 1 year after course start.
findings.gotchas: Students cannot apply directly. Approval is discretionary (older support article says Google may change criteria at any time). Credits may not be used for commercial or personal use.

findings.name: Google Cloud research credits (Academic Research Grants): up to $5,000
findings.detail: Up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits for research (official Cloud for Education listing: 'Apply for up to $5,000 in Google Cloud credits'). Credits provide computing power for research; they have no commercial value and may not be used for commercial purposes.
findings.eligibility: Faculty, PhD students and postdoctoral researchers at accredited higher-education institutions, and eligible nonprofit research institutions, in approved countries (list not captured). Application requires a link to your profile in the institution's faculty or researcher directory and a link showing candidacy status. No startup cap; no .edu email rule stated (an institutional directory link is used instead).
findings.claim: Apply at edu.google.com/programs/credits/research with personal information, department, the directory link and candidacy-status link. Only the most recent submission is reviewed.
findings.expiry: Term and expiry were not captured on the page.
findings.gotchas: Non-commercial use only. The approved-country list was not captured, so check it before applying.

findings.name: Gemini Academic Program: Gemini API credits and higher rate limits for researchers
findings.detail: Qualified academic researchers can apply to receive Gemini API credits and higher rate limits for research projects. Named priority areas include evaluations and benchmarks, scientific discovery (for example rare diseases, materials science, sustainability), and embodiment and interactions. The credit amount is not stated on the captured page.

findings.name: MIT-licensed Uptime Kuma software, free for anyone (no student or startup program)
findings.detail: Uptime Kuma is released under the MIT License (GitHub LICENSE: Copyright (c) 2021 Louis Lam). Downloading, using, modifying and self-hosting it cost $0 (Doolpa review, Pricing Starts At $0) and GBP 0 (uptimekuma.io licence line). The license imposes no paid tier, feature gating or monitor-count cap, and no monitor-count cap appears in the official sources read. Official Docker image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2. Minimum check interval: 20 seconds (README feature list; Doolpa review). Non-Docker install needs Node.js >= 20.4 and Git; pm2 is recommended for background running. Platforms per README: major Linux distros and Windows 10 x64 / Windows Server 2012 R2 or higher. README lists FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD, Replit and Heroku as unsupported, and NFS storage as unsupported.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. Checked for gates: no .edu or school email requirement, no startup age or funding cap, no credit card, and no region limits, because the MIT license and the official README contain none of these. It is not a student- or startup-specific program, so there is nothing to apply for.
findings.claim: No sign-up or claim step. Get the software from https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma and run it on your own server. Docker: docker run -d --restart=always -p 3001:3001 -v uptime-kuma:/app/data --name uptime-kuma louislam/uptime-kuma:2, or curl the repo compose.yaml and run docker compose up -d. Non-Docker: git clone the repo, run npm run setup, then node server/server.js or pm2 start server/server.js --name uptime-kuma.
findings.expiry: None. MIT has no expiry or renewal and applies to every copy of the software with no time limit.
findings.gotchas: (1) uptimekuma.io is NOT the project author's site. Its footer and licensing page name SMARTX TECHNOLOGIES Ltd (London), which sells paid managed hosting. The homepage shows a plan reported at 4.2 PLN per month (figure as summarized by the fetch tool, not independently checked). The homepage's free subdomain (uptimekuma.eu), free SSL and daily backups are bundled into that paid plan and are not a standalone free tier. Its 'unlimited monitored services' wording describes the paid plan, not the software. (2) uptimekuma.co is an unofficial fan site that disclaims affiliation with the author. GitHub metadata lists uptime.kuma.pet as the homepage; per the README it is a temporary demo server whose data is deleted after 10 minutes. It returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch. A demo is not an account, trial or credit. (3) Free means the software is free, not the hosting: you pay for the server, backups, updates and admin time. The uptimekuma.io March 2026 marketing article estimates GBP 5 per month for a small UK VPS and GBP 60 to 120 over 12 months for a self-hosted server. That is a vendor estimate, not an offer. (4) Because README lists Replit and Heroku as unsupported, those free app platforms cannot host it.

sunset_notes: No student, education, startup, free-tier or trial-credit offer was found in any source checked, so none was sunset or changed in 2025-2026. The only free item is the MIT license, which has no eligibility gate and no sunset. Coverage and gaps: (a) uptimekuma.io homepage, read 2026-10-22: only a paid managed-hosting plan (operator SMARTX TECHNOLOGIES Ltd); no free tier, trial, credits, education or startup program, sponsorship or donation option. Pro features (SSO/SAML, automated reminders, bulk send with CSV/XLSX import, conditional fields and formulas, payments, webhooks, PDF/DOCX/HTML template APIs, white-label logo, user roles, SMS verification, embedded form builder) need Pro at $240 per user per year ($20 per user per month billed annually). Server sizing for 10,000 signed documents: 1 vCPU and 1 GB RAM (smallest scenario) up to 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM (100 MB files); disk 6 GB to 4,500 GB; PostgreSQL recommended at 1,000+ documents per year.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who runs their own server. No student, startup or nonprofit eligibility rules are stated on the on-premises page or the pricing table. License: AGPL-3.0 with Section 7(b) additional terms, per the GitHub README.
findings.claim: 1) Get the code at https://github.com/docusealco/docuseal. 2) Run the Docker image docuseal/docuseal (port 3000, per the README) on your own server, or use the Heroku, Railway, DigitalOcean or Render deploy buttons in the README. 3) Point it at your own SMTP server (the open-source edition lists 'Own SMTP for emails'). 4) For 1,000+ documents per year, use PostgreSQL (server requirements page).

The self-signed certificate means signed PDFs are not backed by a commercial trust certificate. The 'without any limitations' marketing line conflicts with the feature gating in the pricing table; trust the table. No payment collection on this edition. AGPL-3.0 section 13 requires offering modified source to users who interact with a modified version over a network. The additional terms require keeping DocuSeal attribution in interactive user interfaces; this came from a summarizing fetch (medium confidence), so read LICENSE_ADDITIONAL_TERMS in full before rebranding or redistributing.

findings.eligibility: Must be tied to an approved partner (VC or accelerator). Outside funding required, 'up to Series B or earlier'; non-equity credits do not count. No Enterprise plan in the past six months and no earlier GitHub credits or Enterprise licenses. Must use Enterprise Cloud hosted on GitHub.com (Server and Data Residency excluded). findings.claim: Go through an approved partner listed on the site (investors can join as partners via a separate application). Approval email arrives within 2-3 business days at the primary address. Questions go to support as a ticket in the 'Credit Offers - GitHub for Startups' category.
findings.expiry: Up to 12 months after approval, ending early if credits run out. Credits are non-transferable and redeemable once. Downgrading early forfeits leftover credits and bars reapplying.

findings.name: Cloud 30-day free trial (no free cloud tier)
findings.detail: Pricing FAQ: 'When you create a team your first 30 days are free.' Each cloud plan (Starter, Team, Business) has a 'Start trial' link to app.getoutline.com/create (ref=starter, ref=team, ref=business). Homepage and compare pages advertise 'Cloud hosted, 30-day free trial'. The trial is time-based, not credits. After it ends, 'your knowledge base becomes read-only until a payment method is added'; all documents can be exported during read-only. Paid cloud prices on the same page: Starter $10/mo for 1-10 members, Team $79/mo for 11-100 members, Business $249/mo for 101-200 members; over 200 members means contacting sales. The page says annual pricing is available but shows no annual figure. Unlimited documents and revisions are stated; no storage, upload or region caps are stated.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who creates a team. The pricing page states no .edu email rule, no startup age or funding cap, no region limit and no student clause.
findings.claim: Open https://www.getoutline.com/pricing, click 'Start trial' under Starter, Team or Business, and create a team. The 30 days run from team creation. Export documents before day 30 if you will not pay.
findings.expiry: 30 days from team creation; then read-only until billing is added. It does not convert to a free plan.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial, not a free tier. Whether a credit card is required at sign-up is NOT stated on any page read, and the sign-up page did not render, so a card-free start is unverified. The 'until a payment method is added' wording suggests no card is needed during the first 30 days. The cloud price basis (flat per tier vs per member) is inferred from the plan cards.

findings.name: Community Edition: free self-hosted build ($0, limited features, no support)
findings.detail: Pricing page lists Community Edition at '$0 limited features, no support' with a Download button; it is the only $0 option on the page. Image: outlinewiki/outline on Docker Hub (linked from the pricing page). Hosting docs call Docker the 'preferred, supported' install method; a source build and a community-maintained Terraform/Ansible route for GCP (third-party repo) are also listed. Requirements: PostgreSQL 14 or later, Redis 4 or later, 512 MB RAM minimum (1 GB or more recommended), Unix-like OS only (not Windows Server), a dedicated domain or subdomain, and a compatible authentication provider, since Outline 'does not support email + password authentication natively'. Hosting docs say it 'requires dev-ops experience' to run in production. Support is GitHub Discussions only. Not included in Community Edition: AI question answering, guest users, extra security controls, SAML 2.0, structured data attributes, Confluence importer, security audit log, Glean integration, removal of Outline branding, and a support contract. SSO authentication is included.
findings.eligibility: No sign-up, seat cap, .edu, or startup condition is stated. The code is under Business Source License 1.1 (see gotchas). Internal production use by your own employees and contractors falls within the license's production grant, as read from the license text (not legal advice).
findings.claim: Pull outlinewiki/outline (or build from source), run it with PostgreSQL 14+ and Redis 4+ on a domain you control, connect a supported authentication provider, then follow https://docs.getoutline.com/s/hosting.
findings.expiry: No expiry stated for the edition. The license Change Date for Outline 1.11.0 is 2030-10-12, when that version converts to Apache 2.0.
findings.gotchas: License: BSL 1.1 is source-available, not OSI open source, until its Change Date, despite the homepage '10 years open source' badge. Additional Use Grant: 'you may not use the Licensed Work for a Document Service', where a Document Service is a commercial offering that lets third parties (other than your employees and contractors) create teams and documents they control. License restrictions page: 'selling, reselling, or hosting Outline as a service is a breach of the terms', and breach 'automatically terminates your rights under the license'. Costs are yours: server, PostgreSQL, Redis, domain and identity provider. File storage, SMTP and egress requirements were not stated on the pages read. Startups that need SAML or audit logs must pay for Business or Enterprise.

findings.name: Open-source Caddy server: free, no paywalled features
findings.detail: Caddy server (binary and source) is licensed under Apache-2.0 and has no paid edition, no license keys and no feature tiers. Official wording: caddyserver.com says 'Caddy is free software and relies on sponsorships to survive' and 'It's all free. No enterprise-level paywalls.' The /sponsor page says 'Caddy has no paywalled features', and its FAQ says sponsorship leaves 'Your license to the software remains the same regardless of sponsorship status.' The repo LICENSE file (read 2026-10-22, https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/LICENSE) is the plain Apache License Version 2.0 with no EULA, no commercial-use restriction and no sponsor-header requirement. Included in the free build per the README and home page: automatic HTTPS (ZeroSSL and Let's Encrypt for public names; a managed local CA for internal names and IPs), reverse proxy with load balancing and health checks, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 on by default, Caddyfile plus JSON config API, and On-Demand TLS. Price: $0. No instance, domain, bandwidth or seat caps are stated; the sponsor page says sponsorship does not restrict 'functionality or instances'.
findings.eligibility: None. Open to everyone, including students, startups, individuals, nonprofits and commercial companies, in any region. No .edu email, startup age or funding cap, credit card or region limit is stated on the official site or in the repo.
findings.claim: Download the binary for your OS from GitHub Releases (https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/releases) or from the official download page (https://caddyserver.com/download, which lets you pick plugins). Alternatively build from source with Go 1.26 or newer. No payment, sponsor login or account step is stated for the download. Put the executable on PATH and run it with a Caddyfile. On Linux, binding ports 80 and 443 needs root or setcap cap_net_bind_service (per README).
findings.expiry: None. The Apache-2.0 grant has no term or renewal date.
findings.gotchas: Self-hosted only: no managed or hosted Caddy service appears on the official pages, so you pay for your own server, bandwidth and DNS, and you patch and monitor it yourself. The sponsor page itself says open source grants 'freedom but not assurances of help'. Third-party modules (for example a DNS provider needed for wildcard certificates) are compiled into the binary, so each plugin means a custom build that must be rebuilt for every Caddy upgrade. 'Caddy' is a registered trademark of ZeroSSL GmbH (download page footer), so forks must use another name. Automatic certificates come from Let's Encrypt and ZeroSSL, third-party CAs with their own terms and rate limits (not checked here). No usage metering or trial limits are stated.

findings.name: Free community support forum (volunteer help)
findings.detail: caddyserver.com/support says: 'Participate as volunteers in our forum to exchange free help in our open source community.' The forum is at caddy.community. The site also links free self-help: the troubleshooting and FAQ pages in the docs, and a community wiki (caddy.community/c/wiki/13). This is the only free support channel on the official support page. Email support, and chat or phone/video support at higher tiers, go to paid sponsors ('through most sponsorship tiers').
findings.eligibility: Anyone. No eligibility, student, startup or region rules are published.
findings.claim: Search the docs (caddyserver.com/docs/troubleshooting and /docs/faq), the community wiki and the forum first. If there is no answer, post a new topic at caddy.community with your Caddy version, Caddyfile and logs.
findings.expiry: None stated.
findings.gotchas: Volunteer-run: no response-time commitment and no SLA. A Jan 2023 Caddy forum post by Matt Holt calls community help 'basically charity'. His Oct 15, 2025 post says he no longer personally sees every issue, comment and PR, and a maintainer team now shares triage. Guaranteed response windows exist only in paid tiers (per third-party copies of the official tier list: Enterprise 2 business days, Enterprise+ 1 business day).

sunset_notes:
No free student, education, academic, nonprofit, startup, trial or credit offer exists for Caddy as of 2026-10-22. The two findings above are the always-free open-source core and the volunteer forum; neither is targeted at students or startups. Checked today: caddyserver.com (home), /sponsor (with FAQ), /support, /download, the repo LICENSE, and the requested /pricing, /education and /startups pages. /pricing, /education and /startups all return HTTP 404. Pricing content now lives at /sponsor, but third-party pricing pages still cite /pricing.

Paid startup offers (not free): Startup at $99/mo includes an onboarding call, occasional email support and no professional-services discount. Startup Pro at $249/mo adds a 10% professional-services discount, triage priority and optional publicity, plus the onboarding call. Official copy calls them 'perfect for bootstrapped startups' and 'bootstrapped, early-stage startups'. No age, funding or revenue cap is published. Startup-tier sponsorships already existed by Feb 2025 (Matt Holt forum post, 2025-02-05).

Full official sponsorship ladder (read 2026-10-22): Indie $25/mo; Indie Pro $50/mo; Startup $99/mo; Startup Pro $249/mo; Business $999/mo (20% professional-services discount with a 6-month commitment); Business+ $2,999/mo (35% with a 6-month commitment); Enterprise $5,900/mo (limited stock); Enterprise+ $11,900/mo (limited availability). Billing is monthly. Subscriptions are managed through GitHub Sponsors, which requires a GitHub login. The FAQ says higher tiers can also pay by invoice, ACH, wire or check (which tiers is not stated). The FAQ does not state whether a credit card is required. Sponsorships are fulfilled by Dyanim, LLC (run by Matt Holt) and do not change the software license.

Retired licensing (sunset): the 2017 commercial EULA made official binaries free for personal, academic and non-profit use, required paid per-instance commercial licenses for business use, and added a Caddy-Sponsors response header. The Oct 2019 proposal (caddyserver/caddy issue 2786) proposed dropping commercial binary licensing, startup packages, build-server subscriptions and private plugin hosting, and keeping Apache-2.0 for all binaries. A Sept 2020 forum post confirmed licensing unchanged. Today no EULA appears on the download page or in the repo LICENSE. The exact date the EULA lapsed was not verified. No academic or nonprofit free license exists now.

2025-2026 changes: (a) Oct 15, 2025: Matt Holt said he would no longer personally see every comment, issue and PR, and a maintainer team was granted tag and release rights. PR 7341 (merged Nov 14, 2025) requires 2 maintainer approvals and signed tags for each release. This affects support expectations, not pricing. (b) Jan 29, 2026: Railway became a Caddy sponsor. Railway's promotions on the Caddy site are Railway's own offers, not Caddy's. (c) Feb 2026: ZeroSSL, the executive sponsor that owns the Caddy trademark, was acquired by HID Global (ASSA ABLOY), per Matt Holt's Feb 5, 2026 forum post. (d) Price snapshots disagree: an older search-index copy of the GitHub Sponsors page showed Business at $2,999 and Business+ at $5,900. The official site and today's GitHub Sponsors page show Business $999, Business+ $2,999, Enterprise $5,900 and Enterprise+ $11,900. The change date is unverified; the official site governs. (e) Aug 11, 2025: a forum announcement says Caddy took part in the GitHub Secure Open Source Program 2025. That is a project-level program, not a student or startup offer; details were not fetched.

Not offers, or wrong: the hosted demo at caddydemo subdomains is 'intentionally restricted' and is not a trial. Sponsor logos on the home page (Railway, Tailscale, Stripe and others) are third-party promotions. Some third-party pages are wrong: Doolpa says sponsorships start at $5/mo (official lowest tier is $25/mo), and RottenWiFi lists 'Open source: No' (the repo is Apache-2.0). Pages also disagree on 'Free plan' (Yes or No) because the free software is not sold as a plan. A Japanese-language mirror of the sponsor page (caddy.dokyumento.jp) was not used as an official source.

Dependencies: Caddy's automatic certificates for public names come from Let's Encrypt and ZeroSSL (per README). Their free-tier terms and rate limits were not checked here.

findings.name: Free and Open-source (self-hosted Community Edition) tier
findings.detail: $0/mo, self-hosted. Free-column limits as listed on windmill.dev/pricing (read 2026-10-22; two separate extractions agreed): executions unlimited; 3 workspaces; max 50 users; SSO max 10 users; object storage 10 GiB quota; max 4 groups; max 100 emails/day for email triggers; job run details retained <=30 days; Git sync up to 2 users; 100 free app guests per 30 days (guests take no seat). Not included: SAML/SCIM, audit logs, Kafka/NATS/SQS/GCP/Azure triggers. Support is Discord community only.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone. No .edu, student status, startup age, or funding-cap condition is stated. Runs on the user's own infrastructure.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim: no sign-up, card, or license key is described for the free column (LICENSE_KEY is for Enterprise Edition only). Download the Community Edition (Docker images or binaries from the windmill-labs/windmill GitHub repo) and follow the self-hosting docs.
findings.expiry: None stated; listed as a standing $0/mo plan with no end date.
findings.gotchas: (1) README (github.com/windmill-labs/windmill, read via raw README): 'The Community Edition is free to use internally.' Commercial redistribution or managed services need a commercial agreement (sales@windmill.dev); the README says a commercial license is required if you sell commercially or embed Windmill in a distributable product or binary. A startup hosting Windmill for customers or shipping it inside its product is outside the free tier. (2) Limits bind as you grow: 3 workspaces, 50 users, SSO for 10 users. Upgrade path is Enterprise from $120/mo plus $20/mo per builder and $10/mo per non-builder. (3) Community support only. (4) License is AGPLv3 with Apache-2.0 for some files; prebuilt Community Edition images/binaries include proprietary code under separate terms (GitHub README summary; check the LICENSE files before relying on it). AGPL network-use terms may apply if modified. (5) Pricing model was revised in Nov 2024 (see sunset_notes).

findings.name: Enterprise one-month trial ('Try it for a month')
findings.detail: The pricing page links 'Try it for a month' to https://portal.windmill.dev/trial for the Enterprise tier. Duration: one month (no day count shown). No trial credits are described. Trial scope is Enterprise: unlimited workspaces and users, uncapped SSO, SAML and SCIM, audit logs, S3 cache, 24/7 support with 3h response time. Post-trial Enterprise pricing as listed: from $120/mo; $20/mo per builder; $10/mo per non-builder; standard workers $50/worker/mo; worked example $170/mo (1 builder, 2 standard workers, 8 subworkers).
findings.eligibility: Not stated on the pricing page. No student or startup condition found. Portal sign-up requirements could not be read.
findings.claim: Click 'Try it for a month' on windmill.dev/pricing, which opens portal.windmill.dev/trial. The portal is client-rendered and the signup steps could not be read.
findings.expiry: One month; start date and end-of-trial behavior not stated.
findings.gotchas: This is a trial of paid Enterprise, not a free tier; the $0 Community Edition is separate. Card requirement, auto-renewal, and post-trial billing are unverified, so do not assume the trial is card-free. Only the existence of the trial link and its one-month length are confirmed.

findings.name: Windmill Cloud free-tier workspaces (existence only; limits unverified)
findings.detail: A free tier exists on Windmill Cloud. The July 2026 changelog entry 'Workspace forks on Windmill Cloud' (release v1.746.0) says paid workspaces on 'Team or Enterprise' plans can be forked, with forks capped at 5 per paid developer seat of the root workspace, and that 'Free-tier workspaces cannot fork'. No Cloud free-tier limits, trial credits, or prices were readable. The Cloud/Self-hosted/White Label tabs on the pricing page are client-rendered, and app.windmill.dev returned a 'Loading...' placeholder.
findings.eligibility: Unknown; not stated in any readable source.
findings.claim: Unknown; sign-up at app.windmill.dev could not be read. Check the Cloud tab on windmill.dev/pricing or the sign-up page directly.
findings.expiry: Unknown.
findings.gotchas: Free-tier Cloud workspaces cannot be forked (since July 2026). A 'Team' plan is named in the changelog, but no price was found. Treat the Cloud free tier's limits as unknown until checked in-app.

sunset_notes: Changes found: (a) 'New pricing' changelog entry, dated November 2024 (not 2025-2026): compute-unit billing (1 CU = 2 worker-GB-month), worker memory options 1GB/2GB/>2GB, half-price operator seats. (b) 'Workspace forks on Windmill Cloud', dated July 2026 (v1.746.0): free-tier Cloud workspaces cannot fork, a 2026 restriction on the free cloud tier. No sunset of the self-hosted free tier appears in any readable 2025-2026 source, and prior free-tier limits could not be compared. No startup program, education/student license, or student credits were found: windmill.dev/startups, /startups/, /education/, /students and /nonprofit all return HTTP 404, and the sitemap (both halves, about 140 KB) lists no startup, education, student, trial, or nonprofit pages apart from the pricing and changelog pages. The pricing page shows 'Nonprofit' and 'Pro' labels with no details (outside the students/startups scope; not verified). Limitations: WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so no third-party or press sources were checked. The Cloud pricing tab, the trial portal, and the Cloud sign-up app are client-rendered and could not be read; the plugin:playwright MCP server failed to connect this session, so they could not be rendered, and a retry of that server is needed to read them. Dates come from official windmill.dev pages and the GitHub README only.

findings.name: Hobby plan (Formbricks Cloud free tier)
findings.detail: Price shown as 'Start free' with no dollar figure. Limits: 1 workspace and 250 responses per month. Included on Hobby: link-based and in-product surveys, all question types, conditional logic, hidden fields, partial responses, recall information, multi-media backgrounds, file uploads, single-use links, and 'Full API access (incl. MCP)'. Hosting: 'Hosted in Frankfurt' (Germany). The page lists no survey cap, seat count, or data retention for Hobby. Overage handling is offered only on Pro and Scale. Hobby is an open-ended free tier, not a time-limited trial.
findings.eligibility: No eligibility rules on formbricks.com/pricing: no student, teacher, .edu, startup, funding-cap, company-age, or region rule. Frankfurt hosting describes data location, not eligibility. A third-party StartupPerks listing says 'No funding needed' and 'Global', but also says 'A company email on your own website domain (not a personal address)'. Formbricks does not state that email rule, so treat it as unverified.
findings.claim: Open https://formbricks.com/pricing/ and click 'Start free' under Hobby (its sign-up link includes plan=free), or 'Get started free' in the header. Sign up. The pricing page closing section says 'No credit card required. Dive right in.' Then use the single workspace; API and MCP access are included.
findings.expiry: No expiry or renewal stated on the official page. StartupPerks (third party, as of Sep 24, 2026) lists '250 responses/month, ongoing'.
findings.gotchas: Hard cap of 250 responses per month. The page does not say what happens at the cap on Hobby: overage opt-in is listed only for Pro and Scale, and the FAQ answer to 'What happens if I hit the monthly response limit?' is missing from the page text returned. Only 1 workspace. These features are listed under Pro, not Hobby: hide Formbricks branding, contact and segment management, attribute-based segmentation, all integrations, custom webhooks, iOS and Android SDKs, AI translations. Hobby seat count is not listed (Pro lists unlimited seats). 'No credit card required' is page-level text, not stated per plan. The free cap was 1,000 responses/month in Formbricks' own Feb 2026 blog posts (see sunset_notes).

findings.name: Self-hosted Formbricks core ('Self-Hosting Free')
findings.detail: Official self-hosting docs list 'Self-Hosting Free' at price 'Free' and say: 'our core product is free however certain advanced features are a part of our Enterprise License offering.' Install routes: One-Click Setup (shell script for Ubuntu), Docker Setup (prebuilt image), Kubernetes Deployment (Helm chart). Free-tier support is community only, via GitHub Discussions. You run setup and upkeep yourself. Minimums on the page: single host 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 20 GB SSD for evaluation, or 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 50 GB SSD for low load; a valid HTTPS certificate is required. Kubernetes starts at 3 nodes of 4+ vCPU and 8 GB each (scales to 6), with PostgreSQL, Redis, and S3-compatible storage run as managed services outside the cluster. License: the docs say 'AGPL' without a version; the GitHub README says 'Formbricks is available Open-Source under AGPLv3 license' and 'You can host Formbricks on your own servers using Docker without a subscription.' Formbricks' Feb 11, 2026 blog comparison table says self-hosting is 'Yes (free forever on Community Edition)'.
findings.eligibility: No eligibility rules: anyone can self-host the AGPL core. Advanced features and AI require the paid Enterprise License ('EE'), priced 'Fixed Per month' with no figure published. Licensing questions go to hola@formbricks.com. No student, education, or startup discount for EE was found on the pages checked.
findings.claim: Follow https://formbricks.com/docs/self-hosting/overview and pick One-Click Setup, Docker Setup, or Kubernetes Deployment. Provision a host that meets the minimums above, with an HTTPS certificate. The page mentions no license key for the core.
findings.expiry: None stated. Formbricks' own pages describe the core as 'free forever' (formbricks.com/community, undated; formbricks.com/typeform-alternative, Feb 11, 2026).
findings.gotchas: Hosting, upgrades, backups, and TLS are on you. Single-host installs go down during reboots and upgrades, and every replica count defaults to 1 (no built-in redundancy). Redis rejects new writes when full rather than discarding queued jobs. The page says '4 GB is a floor, not a comfortable target.' AI features require the Enterprise License and heavy compute (Hub embeddings about 4 vCPU and 8 GiB at runtime; worker pool another 8 vCPU); the page recommends an outside endpoint. Free-tier customization is 'Moderate' versus 'Full' with EE; the page says EE covers 'All Advanced Features' but does not list which are missing from the free tier. No dollar figures for hosting or EE, and no egress or bandwidth pricing. Naming differs: the docs say 'Self-Hosting Free'; Formbricks' blog and third parties say 'Community Edition'.

findings.name: Annual billing promo: 'Get 2 months free'
findings.detail: The official pricing page shows 'Get 2 months free' beside the 'Annually' option. It does not name the plans it covers, show annual prices, or give an end date. If the promo means 2 of 12 months free, annual billing works out to about 16.7% below monthly billing (an inference, not a stated figure). A third-party listing (1launch.eu) says 'Save with 2 months free on annual commitments'.
findings.eligibility: Buyers who choose annual billing on a paid plan; eligible plans are not named. Not limited to students or startups. Not a free plan.
findings.claim: On https://formbricks.com/pricing/ select 'Annually' and check the annual total at checkout.
findings.expiry: Not stated.
findings.gotchas: Applies only to paid billing; the free Hobby plan has no annual price. The promo terms are not on the page, so the 16.7% figure is an inference from the wording.

sunset_notes: Checked 2026-10-22 against formbricks.com pages read directly, plus one successful web search. (1) Free tier appears reduced in 2026: Formbricks' own blog posts dated Feb 3, 2026 (https://formbricks.com/blog/surveysparrow-pricing) and Feb 11, 2026 (https://formbricks.com/typeform-alternative) cite 1,000 responses/month for the free/Cloud plan. The pricing page read on 2026-10-22 lists Hobby at 250 responses/month and 1 workspace. A third-party StartupPerks listing (as of Sep 24, 2026) also shows 250. The GTM Directory (https://thegtmdirectory.com/tools/formbricks, third party) says the pricing page 'changed 2026-10-19'. The exact effective date of the cut was not found. Older context: formbricks/formbricks PR #3824 (Oct 2024, https://github.com/formbricks/formbricks/pull/3824) raised the FREE responses billing constant from 500 to 1,500. (2) Paid prices conflict across sources. Official page (read today, USD): Pro $74/month for 2,000 responses; Scale $325/month for 5,000 responses. Formbricks' Feb 2026 blog quotes $49/month for 5,000 responses (Startup). The GTM Directory says the page shows EUR 59 and EUR 199, and third-party listings (1launch.eu, digitalmarketingcommunity.com) show older free and Startup terms, one at $490/year. Treat the official page as authoritative but re-verify, because currency and plan details vary by source and date. (3) Startup program: none found. https://formbricks.com/startups returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-22. The only startup-related listing is StartupPerks, a third-party aggregator that lists the Hobby plan as a 'perk' ('No funding needed'); it is not a Formbricks program. (4) Education license or student discount: none found. https://formbricks.com/education returned HTTP 404.
