The pricing FAQ asks 'Do you offer discounts for students, teachers, or NGOs?' but the answer is absent from the text returned by WebFetch, so this remains unverified. No .edu requirement is stated for Hobby. (5) Trials and credits: no trial length, trial credits, or trial terms appear for any plan. The FAQ 'Can I try Formbricks for free before committing?' has no answer text. The 'Start free' buttons on Pro and Scale state no terms. (6) Adjacent, not for students or startups: https://formbricks.com/industry/survey-tool-nonprofits says 'Formbricks offers up to 50% discounts to support nonprofits' (a ceiling; actual rate, duration, and eligibility not stated; 'Request discount' button). (7) OSS Friends (https://formbricks.com/oss-friends) is a directory of 38 open-source projects. Its 'Wanna join OSS Friends?' link (https://formbricks.com/join-oss-friends) redirects to a Formbricks page titled 'Backlink Squad'. No free plan, credits, or discount was found for OSS Friends. (8) Contributor program: https://formbricks.com/community (undated) says contributor levels 'Unlock benefits like cash bounties, limited merch and more'. Terms were not verified, and it is not a free-service offer. (9) Free-forever scope: the community FAQ (undated) says in-app surveys 'are not part of this Deal' and that Formbricks will 'keep full control over the pricing in the long run'. Do not assume the free-forever statements cover in-app survey pricing. (10) Search coverage gap: the session-wide WebSearch budget was exhausted after one successful search, so the education-license search and the 2026 pricing-change search did not run. This limit was not worked around. Coverage of 2025-2026 changes rests on the official pages fetched directly and the snippets from that one search.

findings.name: Personal plan: free cloud tier at $0/month
findings.detail: Pricing page lists Personal at '$0/ month' with Billing 'None (free)'. Limits: 1 workspace owner; storage 'Up to 100 MB'; upload limit 'Up to 7 MB'; revision history 7 days; 1 form; 1 chart. Pro is '$12/ member / month' billed annually ($144 per member per year), or $16 per member per month billed monthly. Pro removes the storage cap, sets revision history to 90 days, and makes forms and charts unlimited.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone who signs up. No student, .edu, startup, company-age, funding, or team-size check is stated, and no region restriction is mentioned. This is a free tier, not a student or startup program.
findings.claim: Open https://appflowy.com/pricing/ and click 'Get started' on the Personal card, or 'Start for free' in the header. Both link to https://appflowy.com/app. The pricing page describes no payment step for Personal.
findings.expiry: No end date stated for Personal. Per the pricing FAQ, cancelling Pro moves the workspace 'immediately' to Personal, and 'any usage above the free limits may be restricted'.
findings.gotchas: The 100 MB storage cap and the 1-form and 1-chart caps are reached quickly by a small team. The changelog (v0.14.5, 2026-09-22) mentions file-size and workspace-storage limit messages, which suggests the limits are enforced. The brief's 'unlimited guest editors' is NOT confirmed for Personal: the pricing table shows Personal guest access as 'Not shown', and the FAQ's free guest-editor wording is attached to Pro. No credit card requirement is mentioned for Personal; this was not tested at sign-up.

findings.name: Self-hosted AppFlowy under AGPL-3.0 (free to download and run; $0 cost not stated)
findings.detail: License verified on https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy: the About sidebar reads 'AGPL-3.0 license' and the README reads 'Distributed under the AGPLv3 License'. The homepage has a 'Self-host AppFlowy' button and says AppFlowy can run 'on your infrastructure, in your cloud, or in a fully air-gapped environment'. No page read says self-hosting costs $0. The pricing page's AppFlowy Cloud / Self-Hosted toggle shows no self-hosted prices or limits, and 'Contact sales' is the only enterprise route. The homepage and docs call the product 'open core', and the homepage lists SSO, SCIM and LDAP with no cost wording. Changelog v0.14.10 (2026-10-21) says self-hosted workspaces require AppFlowy Cloud v0.19.10 or later.
findings.eligibility: None stated. The license applies to anyone who obtains the code. No student or startup verification or cap is mentioned.
findings.claim: Get the code or releases from https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy, then follow the self-hosting guide linked as 'Developer Docs' (https://appflowy.com/docs/Step-by-step-Self-Hosting-Guide---From-Zero-to-Production). That guide returned only its title in this run, so its steps were not read.
findings.expiry: No sunset or end date stated for self-hosting. The AGPL-3.0 terms attach to each release a user receives.
findings.gotchas: AGPL-3.0 section 13: if you modify the code and let users interact with it over a network, you must offer those users the source of your modified version. Startups that fork it need to plan for this. 'Open core' suggests some features may be paid or closed; which ones was not verified. Hosting, storage, and any self-hosted LLM or embedding models are your own costs, and AppFlowy does not price them on the pages read. The full LICENSE text was not read; the license name comes from the repo page.

findings.name: AI features labelled 'Limited trial' (meeting notes, transcript, responses)
findings.detail: The pricing page feature rows show 'Limited trial' for 'AI meeting notes', 'AI transcript' and 'AI responses', and 'Local AI' for 'AI search'. The page does not say which plan includes these, how long the trial lasts, the usage quota, or any credit amount. This is the only trial-type item found on official pages.
findings.eligibility: Not stated.
findings.claim: Not stated on the pricing page. Access presumably runs inside the app at https://appflowy.com/app; no steps are given.
findings.expiry: Not stated. 'Limited trial' implies a time or usage cap that the page does not disclose.
findings.gotchas: Not a free tier. Do not build a student or startup workflow on these AI features until the plan and quota are confirmed. 'Local AI' search is not explained; its cost and whether it needs self-hosting are unverified.

findings.name: AppFlowy Partner Program (terms not readable)
findings.detail: The pricing page links 'Partner program' twice, as a support card ('Learn more') and in the footer Resources column, both pointing to https://appflowy.com/docs/appflowy-partner-program. That page returned only its title, 'AppFlowy Partner Program | AppFlowy'. No benefit, discount, credit, eligibility, or application terms could be read, and nothing read ties it to students or startups.
findings.eligibility: Unknown.
findings.claim: Unknown. Open the page in a browser and read its terms before relying on any benefit.
findings.expiry: Unknown.
findings.gotchas: Do not assume a benefit exists. 'Partner' may refer to resellers or integration partners rather than discounts for end users.

sunset_notes: Bottom line: no student, education-license, startup-program, trial-credit, or Pro free-trial offer was found on official pages. The only free options are the Personal cloud tier and the AGPL-3.0 self-hosted code. The partner program is an unverified lead. Education and startup: the pricing page header (Product, Download, Resources, Pricing, Self-host), plan cards, FAQ and footer contain no education, student, startup, nonprofit or discount-program link or text, and the homepage and docs pages read today contain none either. https://appflowy.com/education and https://appflowy.com/startups returned only the page title 'AppFlowy' in this run, so their content and existence are unconfirmed. 2025-2026 changes: the official changelog (https://appflowy.com/what-is-new) shows entries dated 2026-01-09 to 2026-10-21 and no 2025 entries in this capture, so 2025 pricing history could not be checked. The only pricing-related 2026 change found is v0.14.7 (2026-10-06): 'Changed new Pro subscriptions to start checkout with monthly billing.' This matters for the 25% annual saving, which needs the Yearly option selected. The first page of the blog (https://appflowy.com/blog, 2026 posts only) has no pricing or trial posts; pages 2-9 were not checked. No sunset or removal of the Personal plan or the AGPL self-hosted release was found. Search gap: web search was unavailable because the session's search budget was exhausted; this was not worked around, so third-party reporting and 2025 changes are unchecked. Not free offers: the Pro annual discount (25%, $12/member/month billed yearly vs $16 monthly) is a paid discount, and the pricing page 'Learn more' banner announces the v0.14.10 release, not an offer. Unconfirmed brief item: 'unlimited guest editors' on Personal (see finding 1). Pages read with content: https://appflowy.com/pricing/ (several passes), https://appflowy.com/, https://docs.appflowy.io/, https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy, https://appflowy.com/blog, https://appflowy.com/what-is-new. Title-only captures (content not read): https://appflowy.com/education, https://appflowy.com/startups, https://appflowy.com/partners, https://appflowy.com/partner-program, https://appflowy.com/docs/appflowy-partner-program, https://appflowy.com/docs/Step-by-step-Self-Hosting-Guide---From-Zero-to-Production.

findings.name: MIT-licensed BookStack software is free to self-host (no trial, no expiry)
findings.detail: Source is MIT licensed and free. Homepage: 'There is no cost to downloading and installing your own instance of BookStack.' FAQ: 'No, we don't provide custom, or enterprise versions of BookStack.' and 'We do not, and we don't intend to' (official managed hosting). 2025 blog: no paid features, no dual licensing, no open core, no in-app up-sells. Requirements per install docs: PHP 8.2 or newer, MySQL 8.0 or MariaDB 10.6 or newer, Composer 2.2 or newer, Git, and a PHP-capable web server.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. No .edu email, student status, startup age or funding cap, team size or region limit. No card and no sign-up form (per the open-source documentation page).
findings.claim: Get the source from the Codeberg repository linked on bookstackapp.com (GitHub is a mirror), or follow https://www.bookstackapp.com/docs/admin/installation/ and pick a manual release-branch install, a community Docker image (LinuxServer.io or solidnerd), or the Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 or 26.04 script. Supply your own server, MySQL or MariaDB database and SMTP mail details.
findings.expiry: None. The MIT licence has no term or renewal.
findings.gotchas: Your server, backups, SMTP and upgrades are the real cost; the homepage's '£2.50 IONOS VPS' is an example, not a fee. 'BookStack does not currently support shared PHP hosting.' The Ubuntu 26.04 script is for a fresh OS only and could overwrite an existing web setup. You apply security releases yourself; 2026 releases include v26.05.1 to v26.05.5 and v26.09.2 (21 Oct 2026). Not a student or startup programme: the licence is the whole offer.

findings.name: BookStack community support is free with no response guarantee
findings.detail: Free channels: community discussions, Codeberg issues and Reddit, plus free documentation and YouTube guidance. Support page: 'No assurance of response, support or resolution.' Paid plans are separate and carry no discount: Professional £450/year (email or help-desk support, install and update help, priority triage) and Enterprise £4,500/year (includes Professional, up to 10 video-support hours a year), both provided by HTTP Functions Ltd. The support page lists no education, student, startup, nonprofit or trial terms.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. No account, card, .edu email, startup or region condition is stated for community channels.
findings.claim: Search the docs at https://www.bookstackapp.com/docs, then post in the community discussions or on Reddit, or open a bug or request on Codeberg (https://codeberg.org/bookstack/bookstack/issues). Do not email for general help: the contact page lists only security reports and donation or sponsorship questions not answered on the donate page as email topics.
findings.expiry: None; nothing to renew.
findings.gotchas: No response, support or fix is promised. Discord was deprecated in 2026 and a new Zulip-based community site was set up (14 Jul 2026 post), so older guides that point to Discord are stale. The only route with a response commitment is the paid Professional plan, and it is not free. Current support pricing says VAT is 'not included in current pricing although may be chargeable in future'.

findings.name: BookStack public demo instance (free trial of the software, not hosting)
findings.detail: Official 'test drive' at demo.bookstackapp.com, linked from the homepage, using the demo admin login published there. The demo database and image storage reset automatically every 30 minutes. Restricted in the demo: user deletion, user updates and setting updates.
findings.eligibility: Anyone who opens the demo. No sign-up, card, .edu, startup or region condition is stated.
findings.claim: Open the 'Open demo site' link on https://www.bookstackapp.com/ and sign in with the demo admin login shown there.
findings.expiry: Data resets every 30 minutes; no trial length applies.
findings.gotchas: A sandbox only. Anything entered can be wiped within 30 minutes. It is not a hosting trial and does not give you an instance you keep.

findings.name: Third-party Stellar Hosted: 14-day free trial, no card needed to start
findings.detail: Not a BookStack project offer. Vendor page: 'We offer a 14 day free trial and 100% money back guarantee.' FAQ: 'You can sign up and use BookStack for 14 days without entering your payment details.' Standard and Premium show 'Start free trial'. List prices (EUR, monthly, ex VAT): Standard €49, Premium €99, Custom from €199; add-ons €25 to €499. Annual billing: 'Get 2 months for free, 17% discount on a yearly plan!' (17% applies when paid upfront). Hosted in Amsterdam (EU).
findings.eligibility: No conditions listed: no .edu, student, startup, company-size or region rule for the trial. No card is needed to start.
findings.claim: On https://www.stellarhosted.com/bookstack/, click 'Start free trial' on Standard or Premium, sign up without payment details, and use the 14-day instance.
findings.expiry: 14 days. At the end you must pick a plan and enter payment details to keep the instance and data. The page does not say what happens if you do not subscribe.
findings.gotchas: Stellar Hosted is a bronze sponsor on bookstackapp.com, but the homepage says listed services are 'not tested, vetted nor supported by the official BookStack project in any manner', so this is not a BookStack-endorsed offer. The money-back guarantee has no stated conditions or time window. Add-ons and enterprise terms cost extra.

findings.name: Third-party Elestio: $20 free trial credit with 3-day validity
findings.detail: Not a BookStack project offer. Elestio pricing page: 'Our free trial gives you $20 in credits to use with a 3-day validity,' usable for BookStack or any other app in its catalogue. Credits bill hourly against the chosen VM. The first support level is free with each instance. The currency is not named (shown only as '$').
findings.eligibility: Not stated: the page gives no new-account, region, student, startup or card requirement for the trial.
findings.claim: Create an Elestio account and deploy BookStack from its catalogue, drawing on the trial credit. The page does not describe the sign-up steps.
findings.expiry: 3-day validity (start point not stated). The same page also says 'The credits never expire', which conflicts.
findings.gotchas: Contradictory terms on the page. If auto-recharge is disabled and credits run out, the BookStack instance and other resources are stopped; Elestio says it emails before that. Confirm the trial terms with Elestio before relying on them.

findings.name: Third-party fresh.dev: £8 credit for new accounts (BookStack from £5/mo)
findings.detail: Not a BookStack project offer; the page says fresh.dev is not affiliated with the BookStack project. New accounts get £8 of credit and 'nothing is charged up front'. BookStack app from £5/month, billed by the second (App Small: 1 vCPU, 1 GiB memory, 15 GiB storage). HTTPS on a free your-name.apps.fresh.dev address; own domains supported. The page shows BookStack 26.09.1.
findings.eligibility: New accounts (per the credit wording). No student, .edu, startup or region condition is stated. A saved card is needed to launch (see gotchas).
findings.claim: Create a fresh.dev account, open Apps, Launch, choose BookStack, name it and pick a size. Save a card with Stripe when prompted; the £8 credit applies to the new account.
findings.expiry: Not stated for the £8 credit.
findings.gotchas: A card must be saved with Stripe to launch, although nothing is charged up front. Search snapshot says '£5/mo, billed by the second. Excludes VAT' while today's fetch says 'Includes VAT'; check before quoting. No automatic backups yet ('keep your own copy with BookStack's export or backup tools'); deleting an app deletes its data. Outbound port 25 is blocked (use SMTP on port 587). The page shows 26.09.1, one patch behind the 21 Oct 2026 security release v26.09.2.

findings.name: Third-party AWS Marketplace listing (DevSecOps, Inc.): 14-day free trial, then usage billing
findings.detail: Not a BookStack project offer; sold by DevSecOps, Inc. Listing: 'Try this product free for 14 days according to the free trial terms set by the vendor.' After the trial, usage billing applies: $0.01/hour listed for each of seven instance types, plus 'Additional AWS infrastructure costs may apply' (the listing describes EFS and RDS). Listing version: v1.0 (BookStack v24.05.4).
findings.eligibility: Vendor trial terms. The listing states no .edu, student, startup, region or card conditions.
findings.claim: Use 'Try for free' on the AWS Marketplace listing (an AWS account is needed), then deploy the CloudFormation template into your own AWS account ('Deployed on AWS').
findings.expiry: 14 days. The trial converts to a paid subscription when it ends unless cancelled before that. 'We do not currently support refunds, but you can try it for free and cancel at any time.'
findings.gotchas: The vendor EULA (wiki.devsecopsinc.io) says 'Redistribution, modification, or reverse engineering is strictly prohibited' and grants only a licence to the software; this conflicts with BookStack's MIT licence for the same code. The listing's version (v24.05.4) is well behind the 26.x line. The listing does not say whether AWS infrastructure is free during the trial.

sunset_notes:
No BookStack-issued student, education, startup, nonprofit or trial-credit programme exists in the sources checked: homepage (with demo section), support page, project FAQ, donate page, contact page, and the 2024-2026 blog posts. Nothing was sunset in 2025-2026 because none existed in those sources. None of the seven findings has a student, education, startup or nonprofit condition, a .edu requirement, a startup age or funding cap, or a region limit. Findings 4-7 are third-party vendor offers, not BookStack's, and can change without notice.

Changes in 2025-2026: the 2 Jan 2026 review says paid offerings saw 'little outward promotion or change/development'. The 14 Jul 2026 review reports average support revenue up 47%, the move from GitHub to Codeberg, a new Zulip-based community site, and Discord deprecated. Support prices (£450/yr, £4,500/yr) match the 12 Jul 2024 post, so no price change is visible. The support page now says VAT 'is not included in current pricing although may be chargeable in future' (a caveat, not yet a change). 2026 security releases include v26.05.1 to v26.05.5 and v26.09.2 (21 Oct 2026).

Excluded as not verified or not BookStack-specific: Hostinger VPS page (generic 'free domain for 1 year' and limited-time deals); Node.uk managed hosting (from £25/mo, no trial found); other sponsor-linked hosts (Cloudabove, NETWAYS, BookHost, Practicali and others), not checked for offers and not vetted by the project; aggregator pages (costbench.com discounts page, inferse.com, apis.io, startupik.com), whose education, startup and nonprofit sections are generic templates (costbench says 'We don't have BookStack-specific education terms verified yet'), so they were not used as sources.

Gaps: the HTTP Functions Ltd paid-support terms PDF (https://www.httpfunctions.com/docs/bookstack-support-terms.pdf) could not be read. WebFetch returned compressed bytes, and the Read tool needs poppler, which is not installed. Paid-support contract terms, renewal, and any trial or discount in them are therefore unverified. The AWS listing and the 2025-2026 blog posts were read from search excerpts, not full fetches, and the blog index fetch failed.

findings.name: NGINX Open Source - free forever (2-clause BSD)
findings.detail: NGINX Open Source is free software. nginx.org says it was 'distributed under the 2-clause BSD License'. The LICENSE file (copyright 2002-2021 Igor Sysoev; 2011-2026 Nginx, Inc.) imposes no fee, registration, or usage limit. Its only conditions are that source and binary redistributions keep the copyright notice and disclaimer. nginx.org says 'Enterprise distributions, commercial support and training are available from F5, Inc.' (paid).
findings.eligibility: Anyone and any organization in any region. The license has no student, startup, or company-size criteria and no sign-up step.
findings.claim: Download from nginx.org or your OS package repository and deploy. No account, license key, or card is needed.
findings.expiry: None. Perpetual open-source license.
findings.gotchas: Open Source lacks the NGINX Plus feature set. F5 pages list Plus-only features such as advanced traffic control, active health checks, and the NGINX Plus API and dashboard. Commercial support is paid through F5 or partners.

findings.name: NGINX One free trial (includes NGINX Plus) - 30 days
findings.detail: F5's NGINX One free trial page is headed 'Try NGINX One: Free Enterprise Trial' and says 'Get your 30-day free trial started.' F5's trials hub lists NGINX Plus among the 'Trial Includes' products, along with NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX Instance Manager, NGINX Gateway Fabric, and NGINX App Protect. A separate F5 page for NGINX Plus with NGINX App Protect says 'Try them free for 30 days.'
findings.eligibility: Anyone with a MyF5 account, which is free to create. No student, startup, or company-size criteria are stated. The pages read do not mention a business email, region limits, or a credit-card requirement.
findings.claim: 1) Log in or register at MyF5 (account.f5.com/myf5). 2) Under My Products & Plans, select Trials. 3) Find the NGINX One free trial tile and click 'Start your trial'. 4) Download the licenses from MyF5 and use them to license the trial instance.
findings.expiry: 30 days. The page does not say when the clock starts or what happens when it ends.
findings.gotchas: The NGINX One page has no end-of-trial terms (no statement on auto-conversion or expiry), so read the MyF5 terms before starting. NGINX Plus R33 and later require a valid JWT license. Traffic is not processed until the initial usage report reaches F5, unless enforce_initial_report is set to off, which starts a 180-day grace period. Whether trial licenses follow the same rules is not stated. Source for the JWT rules: https://docs.nginx.com/solutions/about-subscription-licenses/getting-started/

findings.name: NGINXaaS for Google Cloud free trial - up to USD 100 credit, 30 days max
findings.detail: F5's June 1, 2026 changelog entry 'NGINXaaS for Google now supports free trials' says the trial is sold through the Google Cloud Marketplace. The billing doc describes it as 'up to USD 100 in credits for a maximum of 30 days, whichever comes first' and says the credit is tied to 'solution provider fees'. The doc does not say whether infrastructure charges are covered.
findings.eligibility: Not stated on the changelog or the billing doc. No first-time, startup, student, or card rules are listed. Sign-up is through the Google Cloud Marketplace listing.
findings.claim: Open the NGINXaaS for Google Cloud listing in Google Cloud Marketplace (the changelog links console.cloud.google.com/marketplace/product/f5-7626-networks-public/nginxaas-google-cloud) and subscribe to the free trial.
findings.expiry: Ends at 30 days or when the USD 100 credit is used up, whichever comes first.
findings.gotchas: At the end of the trial you are charged under the Enterprise plan unless you stop or end the subscription. You can cancel before the trial ends. Per the billing doc's cancelation section, all active deployments move to a suspended state immediately on cancelation. The billing doc says the product has moved to 'F5 Application Delivery Service for Google Cloud', so terms may have changed. Whether Google Cloud credits can pay for NGINXaaS charges is not stated.

findings.name: NGINX Plus Standard on AWS Marketplace - 30-day free trial, then hourly billing
findings.detail: AWS Marketplace listings sold by NGINX, Inc. say 'Try this product free for 30 days according to the free trial terms set by the vendor.' The Amazon Linux 2023 listing (prodview-wp322f6mkwxbo) was read directly. The RHEL 10 listing (prodview-hrntvqzgmpu4i) shows the same 30-day trial in search results only. After the trial, hourly software charges apply. Every visible rate row (10 of 516 entries) is $0.50 per hour, for example c5.large and t3.micro. Standard support is business hours (9am-5pm customer time zone) by email and phone, with a 30-minute SLA for urgent Severity 1 issues.
findings.eligibility: Any AWS account that can subscribe to Marketplace software. The listing states no student or startup criteria and does not describe payment-method rules.
findings.claim: Subscribe to the NGINX Plus listing in AWS Marketplace and launch the AMI on EC2. The trial covers the software charge, and AWS bills EC2 separately. Cancel before the trial ends to avoid conversion.
findings.expiry: 30-day trial. The listing text read does not state the exact start point.
findings.gotchas: The listing says the trial 'gets automatically converted to a paid subscription when the trial ends' unless it is canceled first. There are no refunds for hourly usage after the trial expires. 'Additional AWS infrastructure costs may apply.' The listing says free-tier credits can cover eligible AWS infrastructure for Free Tier customers. Legacy EC2 Micro benefits apply only to accounts created before July 15, 2025. Only 10 of 516 price rows were visible, so the lowest price across all instance types is not confirmed.

findings.name: F5 WAF for NGINX preview in NGINXaaS - free during the preview period
findings.detail: F5 changelog entries say F5 WAF for NGINX is in Preview for NGINXaaS and is 'free to use during the preview period'. The May 15, 2026 entry covers NGINXaaS for Google. The September 1, 2026 entry covers the AWS offering. The preview does not support custom security policies or custom logging profiles.
findings.eligibility: Customers of NGINXaaS on the named cloud. No student or startup criteria.
findings.claim: Not described in the changelog entries read. No enablement steps are given.
findings.expiry: The preview period end date is not stated.
findings.gotchas: Preview only. The price after the preview is not stated. The September 1 entry is named 'F5 ADS for AWS' on the fetched page, while a search excerpt named it 'NGINXaaS for AWS'. The fetched page notes that NGINXaaS is now F5 Application Delivery Service. Confirm the current product name before relying on it.

findings.name: NGINX Fundamentals digital badge (F5 Academy) - listed as Cost Free
findings.detail: The Credly listing for F5's NGINX Fundamentals badge shows Type 'Experience', Level 'Foundational', Time 'Days', and Cost 'Free'. The earning criteria are the 'F5 NGINX Plus Fundamentals Accreditation Track'. The program is described as hands-on lab journeys across the F5 NGINX portfolio.
findings.eligibility: Not stated. No student or startup criteria are listed.
findings.claim: Not stated on the listing. The listing links to an 'Additional Details' PDF, which was not read.
findings.expiry: None shown.
findings.gotchas: This is a learning credential, not a software license. The listing does not say how to enroll, whether an F5 account is needed, or how long lab access lasts.

findings.name: NGINX Kick Start webinar - complimentary 2-hour session
findings.detail: F5's webinar page says 'NGINX and F5 are offering this complimentary 2-hour NGINX introductory session conducted by an official NGINX trainer.' Topics are NGINX as a web server, reverse proxy use, load balancing and cache, and the NGINX Plus API and dashboard.
findings.eligibility: Open to anyone. No criteria are listed.
findings.claim: Register through the F5 webinar page. The registration steps were not shown in the text read.
findings.expiry: No date or end date shown. It may be a past event or a recurring one.
findings.gotchas: The page shows no date, delivery format (live or recorded), or sign-up steps. Confirm it is still running before planning around it. It is not a student or startup offer.

sunset_notes:
1) NGINX Plus for Development free annual license: NOT CONFIRMED. The nginx.com/developer-license URL now returns a 301 redirect to https://www.f5.com/products/nginx, which describes no free developer or development license. The F5 trials hub lists NGINX only as the NGINX One trial. A third-party reseller (WorldTech IT, not an official source) lists paid NGINX Plus non-production and WAF developer SKUs, priced per instance per month or per 5/10/25-user block per month. Drop the claim unless F5 confirms a current offer. Whether F5 removed the dedicated page is not confirmed.
2) Changed or new in 2025-2026: NGINXaaS for Google Cloud free trial added June 1, 2026. NGINXaaS was renamed F5 Application Delivery Service, and the Google billing doc says the product has moved. NGINX Plus has published LTS and Continuous Release tracks since May 13, 2026 (a release-model change, not an offer change). Archived F5 article K40429408 (originally Oct 2020, updated Dec 2024) describes an older form-based 30-day NGINX Plus trial; it is superseded by the MyF5 NGINX One trial. NGINX Plus R33 (late 2024) introduced JWT licensing and usage reporting.
3) Not found, student or education: no NGINX student or academic license was found. The F5 education portal homepage shows paid options only, for example Administering NGINX for Web Services self-directed training at $480 for 8 training units, and NGINX Learning Path bundles valid for 1 year with no automatic renewal and all sales final. The free-tagged course catalog page returned zero courses, so no free course list is verified. F5 Academic Alliance and other student programs were not checked because the WebSearch budget ran out.
4) Not found, startup: no NGINX or F5 startup credits or discounts on nginx.org, the F5 trial pages, or the education portal. Cloud startup programs do not confirm NGINX coverage. AWS Activate (up to $200,000 in credits per its page) says credits are redeemable on third-party models on Amazon Bedrock and says nothing about Marketplace software. The Google for Startups Cloud Program perks page returned truncated content, and no NGINX or F5 entry was visible. Using Activate or Google credits to buy NGINX Marketplace listings is unverified.
5) Not checked: Azure Marketplace and Google Cloud Marketplace NGINX Plus listings other than NGINXaaS; NGINX Ingress Controller and Gateway Fabric licensing; nonprofit or open-source-project discounts.
6) Third-party only: itechguides (checked 20 Sep 2026) says NGINX Plus has no free plan, a 30-day trial, and pricing on request. This is not an official source.
7) Method and limits: nginx.org, the NGINX license, F5 product and trial pages, the NGINXaaS changelog and billing docs, the AWS Marketplace listing, the AWS Activate page, Credly, and the F5 education portal were read directly with WebFetch on 2026-10-22. The WebSearch quota (200 calls per session, shared across agents) ran out after four searches, so search-based checks for student, startup, and academic programs were not possible.

findings.name: Hosted Free plan (5 documents per month)
findings.detail: Hosted Free tier: 5 documents per month, up to 10 recipients per document, and 3 direct templates (docs plan-limits table). The pricing page says 'Free forever', 'Access Forever' and 'No credit card required'. There is no trial and no credit grant. No region limit is listed. Paid comparison (not free): Individual $25/mo or $300 billed yearly (unlimited documents, API for personal use only); Teams $40/mo or $480 billed yearly (5 users included, $8/mo per extra user, API for automation); Platform $250/mo or $3,000 billed yearly (unlimited documents and users, unlimited API).
findings.eligibility: Anyone who signs up. No .edu, student, startup, funding, company-age or region rule appears on the pricing or docs pages, so students and startups get the same terms as everyone else.
findings.claim: 1) Open https://documenso.com/pricing and click Get started under Free (the docs give documen.so/free as the sign-up link). 2) Enter name, email and password, or sign in with Google. 3) Verify the email address. 4) Send documents. No card is requested and nothing is applied for.
findings.expiry: No end date is stated; the pricing page says 'Free forever'. All plans fall under the Fair-Use-Policy linked from the pricing page; the policy text could not be retrieved.
findings.gotchas: The 5-document monthly cap is the binding limit. A startup that sends more must pay; the cheapest hosted step up is Individual at $300 per year. The 10-recipient cap is current; the Sep 2023 free-tier announcement had promised unlimited recipients. The Individual API is 'for personal use' only, so company automation needs Teams or Platform. A June 2024 blog said free accounts may keep using the API for non-signing actions; this was not re-verified for 2026. Free is not a trial: there are no credits, and no paid-plan trial is listed.

findings.name: Self-hosted Community Edition (free AGPL-3.0 code)
findings.detail: Official self-hosted page: the Community Edition is 'Free Forever', with no usage caps, community-only software support, no enterprise functionality, and no infrastructure help. Its stated purpose is 'Testing, Evaluation, Internal POCs'. The code is AGPL-3.0 (github.com/documenso/documenso). The paid Business Edition was announced 2026-01-30 on the official blog; it is a yearly 'Fixed Yearly License' with no published price, labelled 'Serious Production Use', and adds enterprise functionality and support. Enterprise is priced on request.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. Open-source license with no startup, student, funding or region rule. No edition-level discount is listed for startups, students or nonprofits.
findings.claim: 1) Get the source from https://github.com/documenso/documenso (AGPL-3.0). 2) Deploy it on your own infrastructure using the Docker setup, with Postgres and SMTP mail that you run yourself. 3) There is no sign-up, payment or approval step.
findings.expiry: None; listed as 'Free Forever'.
findings.gotchas: Sources conflict on production use. The English self-hosted page labels the Community Edition for testing and internal POCs, while the Spanish pricing page (documenso.com/es/pricing) says it can be self-hosted 'para uso privado y comercial' (private and commercial use) with some enterprise limits. Confirm before running the Community Edition in production. Self-hosting means you run Postgres, SMTP, TLS certificates, backups and upgrades, and no edition includes infrastructure support. AGPL-3.0 applies: if you modify the code and users interact with it over a network, you must offer them your modified source. A third-party article estimates $20-50 per month for hosting; this is unverified.

findings.name: Staging demo environment (free sandbox for evaluating paid features)
findings.detail: A demo (staging) environment has the same features as production and is meant for development and testing. You can choose a paid plan there and pay with a test card. It is a sandbox, not a credit or a trial, and its accounts and data are separate from production.
findings.eligibility: Anyone can create an account there; it is intended for developers evaluating the platform. No startup or student rule is stated.
findings.claim: 1) Open the staging environment linked from the Documenso demo-environment docs. 2) Create a new account there; a production account cannot be used. 3) Choose a plan and enter the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 with any future expiry date and CVV 123.
findings.expiry: Not stated in the docs.
findings.gotchas: The test card and staging billing work only on staging; nothing carries over to production and no credits are granted. Use it to evaluate features, not for live signing.

findings.name: StartupPerks listing: 'Free forever' for early-stage startups (third-party)
findings.detail: Third-party aggregator entry (StartupPerks) labelled 'Free forever' for Documenso (open source eSign). The value it describes is the free self-hosted open-source edition. No Documenso-run startup program was found: documenso.com/startup/ and /startups return 404, and the official pricing page lists no startup offer. The listing says it is an independent comparison and is not endorsed by the programs it lists.
findings.eligibility: Per the listing: idea, pre-seed or seed stage; no funding or accelerator required; global; a company email on your own website domain (not a personal address). Not verified against Documenso.
findings.claim: Per the listing: self-host the open-source version from GitHub. Documenso documents no application or approval step for this.
findings.expiry: Listed as 'Ongoing' with no end date. The listing says terms can change.
findings.gotchas: The benefit is the same free self-host as the Community Edition, which has no enterprise features and no infrastructure support, so it adds nothing beyond that offer. The listing was added 2026-08-18 and marked 'as of Oct 7, 2026'. Confirm with Documenso before relying on it.

sunset_notes: No official startup program, education or student license, nonprofit discount, free trial or trial credits was found. The official startup and education pages return HTTP 404 (documenso.com/startup/, /startups, /education and /education/). The pricing page (read today) lists none of these, and the OSS Friends page (documenso.com/oss-friends, read today) is a partner list with no offers. The only free offers are the hosted Free plan and the free AGPL self-hosted Community Edition; the staging sandbox is a test environment. Changes found: (1) The Early Adopters plan (first 100 signups, $30/mo, price guaranteed for life) was sunset on 2024-06-12 per the official blog post 'Sunsetting the Early Adopters Plan'; it cannot be claimed now. (2) Free-tier terms changed: the 2023-09-29 'Singleplayer' post promised a free account with unlimited recipients and '5 free signatures per month'. Current pricing and docs say '5 documents per month' and 'up to 10 recipients per document'. The change dates are not verified. (3) Paid prices changed: the June 2024 blog set Individual at $30/mo and Team at $50/mo (5 users, $10 per extra user). Current pricing is Individual $25/mo or $300/yr and Teams $40/mo or $480/yr (5 users, $8 per extra user). The change date is not verified. (4) The official blog index (read today) shows 2025-09-02 'Organizations: The Foundation of Documenso for Enterprise', 2025-09-18 'Introducing Self-Hosted Signing Infrastructure for Enterprise', 2026-01-30 'Introducing Documenso Business Edition for Self-Hosting' (paid production license with enterprise features and support, no public price), and 2026-06-10 'Splitting Our Email Sending Infrastructure' (free and individual accounts get separate email sending domains; no limit change stated). None of these adds a free offer. (5) Not re-verified for 2026: the 2024 blog's statements that free accounts may keep using the API for non-signing actions and that heavy API use on Individual can prompt an upgrade request; the Fair Use policy text (documenso.com/fair and /fair-use return 404, and the documen.so/fair link resolved to unrelated content); and whether the 2023 loginless single-signer free mode still exists (it is not on the pricing page). Third-party reviews (SignWith, ToolGPA, Doolpa, iTechGuides, Toolradar) match the current Free and paid prices. The WebSearch budget ran out mid-task and the changelog fetch failed, so some 2025-2026 changes may be missing.

provider: Ghost (Ghost(Pro) managed hosting and the open-source self-hosted Ghost software)

findings.name: Self-hosted Ghost open-source software (MIT, no license fee)
findings.detail: Ghost core is MIT-licensed. The LICENSE on the TryGhost/Ghost repository reads 'Copyright (c) 2013-2026 Ghost Foundation' with standard MIT terms, so there is no license fee, no member cap and no revenue share. Ghost's hosting docs (docs.ghost.org/hosting.md) give the supported self-hosting stack as Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, Node.js 22 LTS, MySQL 8.0 or 8.4 and NGINX, with at least 1GB RAM. The install docs (docs.ghost.org/install.md) offer Ubuntu via the Ghost CLI, a local install on macOS, Windows or Linux, and Docker labelled 'preview'. Newsletters need a bulk email provider: the newsletter docs (docs.ghost.org/newsletters.md) say basic SMTP cannot deliver bulk mail and that Mailgun is the only supported provider, set with Mailgun API keys in the newsletter settings.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. No student, startup, nonprofit or region rules found.
findings.claim: Get the code from github.com/TryGhost/Ghost and install with the official docs (Ghost CLI on Ubuntu, or the Docker preview). For newsletters, create a Mailgun account and enter its API keys in Ghost Admin's email newsletter settings.
findings.expiry: None; the MIT license has no term.
findings.gotchas: Free license is not free hosting. Ghost's hosting docs list starting prices of $10/mo for a self-hosted base, plus separately paid CDN/WAF $20, newsletter delivery $15, analytics $10, full backups $5 and image editor $12 (docs figures, not checked against vendor pricing). You also run updates, SSL, backups and security; the docs stress keeping software up to date. Mailgun's pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22) shows a $0 plan with 100 emails/day and no expiry stated, and Basic from $15/mo for 10,000 emails/mo; Ghost's newsletter docs say 'free for up to 600 emails per month', which looks stale. Ghost(Pro) includes email delivery and unlimited email sends. A third-party guide mentions a $200 DigitalOcean credit for a one-click Ghost droplet; not verified, and not a Ghost offer.

findings.name: Ghost(Pro) 14-day free trial (time-limited, not a free tier)
findings.detail: All new Ghost(Pro) accounts start on a 14-day free trial (Ghost help center, 'Manage your Ghost(Pro) subscription'). You are not billed when it expires, but you must select a plan to keep using Ghost(Pro). 'Try for free' appears on Starter, Publisher and Business; Custom shows 'Get in touch' with no trial. There is no forever-free hosted plan. Official pricing page (fetched 2026-10-22): Starter $18/mo, Publisher $29/mo, Business $199/mo, each shown as billed yearly; monthly prices were not captured. Starter includes 1 staff user, 1 newsletter, 1,000 members and 5MB uploads, with no paid subscriptions and no custom themes.
findings.eligibility: All new Ghost(Pro) accounts. Credit card requirement NOT confirmed. The billing article says subscriptions use 'the card placed on file at the time of signup'. A March 2025 Ghost community reply (not Ghost staff) says Ghost requires a card for the trial, and a January 2018 comment on GitHub issue #6026 by a TryGhost maintainer said card details were required but the trial was free. Third-party 2026 reviews say no card is needed. Treat a card as likely required until the signup screen shows otherwise.
findings.claim: Click 'Try for free' or 'Get Started - free' on ghost.org/pricing, which opens account.ghost.org/signup, then choose a plan. Before day 14, select a plan under Ghost Admin > Ghost(Pro) > Billing to keep the site online. Plan and billing-frequency changes take effect immediately, with unused time credited and the new charge prorated.
findings.expiry: 14 days from signup. No charge at expiry, but the site needs an active subscription to stay online (Ghost(Pro) help topic).
findings.gotchas: Member cap: free accounts count toward members, and going over the plan's member limit temporarily disables publishing until you upgrade. Cards: Ghost's payment article says only Visa, Mastercard and American Express are accepted, and prepaid cards are declined. Paid memberships need Publisher or higher; Ghost takes 0% on Publisher and up, but payment processor fees still apply. Third-party reviews say Ghost gives no refunds (not verified on official pages). The help article is dated 2023-04-18 in search metadata; the page itself shows no date.

findings.name: 20% off all Ghost(Pro) plans on annual billing (the only discount Ghost offers)
findings.detail: Ghost help center answer to 'Do you offer student, open source developer, or non-profit discounts?': 'We offer a 20% discount on all Ghost(Pro) plans if you subscribe annually.' The discount article names no student, open-source or nonprofit eligibility or verification, and says that as a non-profit Ghost cannot go 'beyond the annual discount'. This is an annual-billing discount, not a separate program. The footer 'Non-Profit Foundation' badge describes Ghost Foundation's status and is not a discount.
findings.eligibility: Any Ghost(Pro) customer who chooses annual billing. No student, open-source or nonprofit verification described.
findings.claim: Choose yearly billing on ghost.org/pricing or in Ghost Admin > Ghost(Pro) > Billing. Changing billing frequency takes effect immediately, with unused time credited and the new charge prorated.
findings.expiry: None stated; applies while the plan is billed annually.
findings.gotchas: The official page does not capture monthly prices, so the real saving cannot be checked there. Third-party sites quote different prices (for example Starter $15/mo annual against the official $18/mo billed yearly). Failed subscription renewals are retried over 28 days, then the account is suspended and the site goes offline (Ghost troubleshooting article). For any program not listed here, contact support@ghost.org, the support address in the Ghost help center.

findings.name: Student Beans '20% Student Discount' on Ghost (third-party listing, unverified)
findings.detail: Student Beans (US) lists 'Ghost 20% Student Discount' with 'Verification required', 'This offer will be redeemed externally' and 'Full terms apply'. The captured page names no external provider, plan scope, expiry or redemption link. Ghost's own help center describes only the 20% annual discount for all customers and mentions no student verification. It is unclear whether this listing is that annual discount relabeled or a separate arrangement that Ghost's pages do not mention.
findings.eligibility: Per Student Beans' generic FAQ: students over 16 in full-time education, including apprentices. Verification through an external provider; exact terms not shown.
findings.claim: Register and verify student status with Student Beans, then follow its external redemption link (not captured on the page).
findings.expiry: Not stated.
findings.gotchas: Not confirmed by Ghost. Check with Ghost support before paying for an annual plan on the strength of this listing. The page title says Oct 2026; no last-updated date is shown.

findings.name: Free first-year .link domain registration on Ghost(Pro) sites
findings.detail: Pricing page: 'All Ghost(Pro) sites include a one-year free domain registration using the .link TLD. Domains registered through this promotion renew at standard rates after the first year.' Help article: '.link domains are free to register for the first year through a partnership with Entri and .link.' Every Ghost(Pro) site also gets a free ghost.io subdomain. The help article's standard purchase flow runs through GoDaddy.
findings.eligibility: Ghost(Pro) sites on every listed plan (the pricing table marks 'Yes' for Starter, Publisher, Business and Custom). Not stated: new vs existing sites, trial eligibility, one domain per account, or card requirement.
findings.claim: Buy a custom domain through Ghost Admin's domain purchase flow (help article 'How do I buy a domain on Ghost(Pro)?'). The help article does not say how the free year is applied at checkout.
findings.expiry: First year only; standard renewal rates after that.
findings.gotchas: The promotion is .link only, and its terms sit with Entri and .link, which were not reviewed. The renewal price after year one was not captured.

findings.name: Free Contributor seats on Ghost(Pro) (not counted toward plan staff limits)
findings.detail: Pricing page: 'Contributors and Suspended users are always free, they won't count towards your plan limits.' Staff users are people who can log into Ghost Admin and publish (Author, Editor, Administrator and Owner roles). Staff limits: Starter 1, Publisher 3, Business 15, Custom unlimited.
findings.eligibility: Any Ghost(Pro) site. Contributor and Suspended users are free seats.
findings.claim: Assign the Contributor role to the user in Ghost Admin's staff settings (menu path not verified).
findings.expiry: None stated.
findings.gotchas: This is a seat-counting rule, not a discount. The permissions of the Contributor role beyond the pricing note were not verified.

sunset_notes: No free hosted tier, trial credits, startup program, or education license was found for Ghost. The trial is time-based only. ghost.org/education/ and ghost.org/students/ return 404; ghost.org/startups/ shows no startup offer; the official discount article says the annual 20% is the only discount, including for non-profits. Member free trials and complimentary plans are tools publishers give their readers, not offers to Ghost customers. Changes and conflicts: (1) Starter no longer includes paid subscriptions. Third-party sites date this to a July 2025 pricing update; the official page confirms the current limit, and no Ghost changelog was checked. (2) Starter price conflict: the official page on 2026-10-22 shows $18/mo billed yearly, while several 2026 third-party sites show $15/mo annual and $18/mo monthly. This may be a 2026 change and is unresolved. (3) The official page lists Business at 1,000 members in its feature list and 10,000 in its comparison table. (4) Historical sunset: a no-card 14-day trial existed in October 2015 (GitHub issue #6026), and card details were required by January 2018 per the same thread. (5) Ghost's hosting and newsletter docs cite a $15/mo Ghost(Pro) base and a Mailgun free tier of 600 emails/month; both conflict with the current pricing page and Mailgun's pricing page. Research limits: two WebSearch calls succeeded, and a third was refused because the session's search budget was used up. The 2025-2026 change checks therefore rely on WebFetch of official pages plus those search snippets. Unverified: the trial card requirement, the .link promotion terms (Entri and .link), and the Student Beans terms.

findings.name: Open Source edition (self-hosted, AGPL): free forever
findings.detail: Free to download and self-host under the AGPL (the input note's Apache-2.0 is wrong). Unlimited users, unlimited questions and dashboards, 20+ data sources, REST API with API keys, MCP server, query builder, SQL editor, dashboards, guest embeds, and Metabot AI using your own model key. Self-hosted transforms are unlimited (no per-run fee). Support is community forums only. The official pricing page lists Open Source as the only free plan; Metabase Learn says Metabase is free forever.
findings.eligibility: Anyone: students and startups of any size or age, no .edu email, no funding cap, no region limit, no card, no account needed to download.
findings.claim: Run: docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name metabase metabase/metabase, then open http://localhost:3000, create the admin account and connect a database. Without Docker, run the JAR on Java 25. Download page: metabase.com/start/oss (Download and self-host for free).
findings.expiry: None stated; the AGPL license has no time limit.
findings.gotchas: Free to download, not free to run: you pay for the server, application database, backups, upgrades and admin time. Pro/Enterprise only: SAML, JWT and OIDC SSO, row- and column-level permissions, usage analytics, serialization, white-labeling. Email subscriptions need your own SMTP server. Metabot AI needs your own model API key (you pay the provider). Guest embeds show a Powered by Metabase banner. Embedding in an app requires AGPL compliance, the Embedding License (keeps the logo) or a Metabase Commercial Software License.

findings.name: Metabase Cloud 14-day free trial (Starter and Pro); no free Cloud plan
findings.detail: Starter and Pro each start with a 14-day free trial: time-limited, with no credit amount or usage quota. Store copy: trials are free, with no obligation to buy, and can be cancelled any time. The Store offers the trial for self-hosted or Metabase Cloud; the embedding article mentions activating a license token from the self-hosted Pro trial. After the trial: Starter $100/mo (5 users included, +$6/user/mo) or $1,080/yr; Pro $575/mo (10 users included, +$12/user/mo) or $6,210/yr. Enterprise has no trial (from $20,000/yr, sales-led). Cloud regions: US East (N. Virginia), EU (Frankfurt), South America (Sao Paulo), APAC (Singapore, Sydney).
findings.eligibility: Not stated; no student or startup restriction on the Store or pricing pages. Card: the official Learn page (read today) says the 14-day Cloud trial needs an email and a credit card. The Store sign-up step as fetched showed only email and password fields, so the card step may come later (not seen). Card and conversion terms for the self-hosted trial are not verified.
findings.claim: On metabase.com click Try Metabase Cloud free (or go to store.metabase.com/checkout), then Start your 14-day free trial. Choose Starter or Pro, self-hosted or Cloud, enter email and password, pick a region and enter payment details (order per Metabase's migration guide).
findings.expiry: 14 days from start. Post-trial billing is not explicitly stated; Store docs list Cancel a subscription or trial, which implies a card-backed trial converts to paid unless cancelled (inference). To cancel: Store, Instances, Settings, Cancel subscription and delete instance.
findings.gotchas: If not cancelled, expect the $100/mo Starter (or $575/mo Pro) charge after 14 days (inference). Cloud supports only Metabase official databases: SQLite and H2 are excluded, and community drivers and file-based DBs are unsupported. Queries time out after 20 minutes. No access to the application database; email sender cannot be customized. Annual billing saves about 10%, but annual payments are non-refundable (docs). Starter includes 5 users; extra users are prorated daily.

findings.name: Included Cloud allowances on Starter and Pro: AI tokens, transform runs, storage rows
findings.detail: AI service (Metabase-hosted model, Cloud only): first 1M tokens free, then $3.75 per 1M tokens, billed monthly on prior-month usage. Transforms: first 1,000 successful basic runs free on Starter and Pro Cloud, then $0.01 per run. Advanced transforms: 1,000 included runs on Starter and Pro; the page lists $0.02 and $0.01 per run after that (which applies is unclear). Storage (optional Cloud add-on for CSV/spreadsheet uploads and Google Sheets sync): $2 per 1M rows; first 1M stored rows always free. The official pricing page calls these included credits to get you started.
findings.eligibility: Requires a paid Cloud subscription (Starter $100/mo or Pro $575/mo); not a standalone free tier. The AI service and Storage are Cloud-only; self-hosted users bring their own AI key and have no Storage add-on.
findings.claim: No separate sign-up: the allowances come with a Starter or Pro Cloud subscription. On Cloud, choose Metabase's AI service instead of your own API key. Storage is an optional Cloud add-on (enable steps not verified).
findings.expiry: Reset period not stated. The first 1M tokens and first 1,000 runs may be one-time rather than monthly; 'always free' for storage suggests an ongoing allowance. Confirm in the Store before relying on it.
findings.gotchas: Allowances sit inside a paid plan, so the $100/mo minimum applies. Self-hosted transforms are unlimited (pricing page). A third-party tracker says Metabot AI on Cloud Pro/Enterprise was free for a limited time when introduced around Oct 2025; end date unverified. An official June 9, 2026 blog post (as quoted by WebFetch) says Metabase does not charge an add-on for AI, while the pricing page still lists a $3.75/1M-token AI service; check in the Store.

findings.name: Guest embeds: free on every edition (Powered by Metabase banner on Open Source and Starter)
findings.detail: Guest embeds (server-signed JWT, locked parameters, anonymous viewers) are free on Open Source and every paid plan. Viewers need no Metabase account and do not count as users. Open Source and Starter show a Powered by Metabase banner; Pro and Enterprise remove it and add white-labeling, custom colors and fonts. SSO embeds (JWT or SAML), the React SDK and full-app embedding are Pro/Enterprise.
findings.eligibility: Anyone running Open Source, Starter, Pro or Enterprise.
findings.claim: Have your server sign a JWT with locked parameters for each dashboard or question, per the embedding article. No purchase needed on Open Source.
findings.expiry: None stated.
findings.gotchas: Licensing decides compliance: the license page gives three routes for embedding in an app: abide by the AGPL, abide by the Embedding License (which keeps the Powered by Metabase logo), or buy a Metabase Commercial Software License. A legacy Premium Embedding License also exists for logo removal. Removing the logo requires Pro/Enterprise or one of these licenses.

findings.name: Meetrix Metabase image on Google Cloud Marketplace: 5-day trial, up to USD 50 licence credit (third party)
findings.detail: Meetrix, a third-party reseller of the open-source Metabase build, lists Free trial: 5 days, up to USD 50 licence credit for its Google Cloud Marketplace image (e2-medium, 20 GB disk, deploys with Terraform or gcloud CLI). The page does not say what the credit covers, eligibility, expiry, or whether Google Cloud compute is included. Its FAQ separates its software fee from server cost, so the credit probably covers only that fee (inference).
findings.eligibility: Not stated. A Google Cloud billing account and project are needed to deploy (inference).
findings.claim: Subscribe to the Meetrix listing on Google Cloud Marketplace, pick a region and machine size, and deploy (about 5 to 10 minutes). Point a DNS A record at the server, then run the setup wizard.
findings.expiry: 5 days (stated); the USD 50 is a cap, not a guaranteed amount.
findings.gotchas: Not Metabase-operated. Server and disk charges likely bill to your GCP account. No terms beyond the listing. Third-party AWS AMI listings also charge software fees (one listing shows $0.014/hour per instance type), so third-party images are not free by default.

findings.name: AWS Marketplace listing sold by Metabase: Try free for 14 days (terms not stated)
findings.detail: SaaS listing sold by Metabase says Try free for 14 days. Its pricing table shows a Platform Fee of $20,000.00 per 12-month contract plus $210.00 per additional user. Trial price, card requirement, eligibility and post-trial billing are not stated. The listing says to contact Metabase for custom pricing, EULA or a private contract.
findings.eligibility: Not stated; an AWS account is needed to subscribe.
findings.claim: Subscribe through the AWS Marketplace listing; further steps not verified.
findings.expiry: 14 days (stated). The listing states all fees are non-cancellable and non-refundable except as required by law.
findings.gotchas: Enterprise-scale price ($20,000 per 12 months), not a student or startup route. Metabase install docs say the company does not currently distribute Metabase on AWS Marketplace or Azure Marketplace, which conflicts with this listing; treat the listing as unverified. Whether startup cloud credits can pay for it is unverified.

sunset_notes:
CORRECTIONS TO INPUT NOTE: (1) Metabase Open Source is AGPL (pricing reference, license page, launch article), not Apache-2.0. (2) Metabase Cloud has no free plan. Open Source is the only free plan; Cloud has only a 14-day trial (Starter and Pro) plus included allowances on paid plans.

NO OFFER FOUND: Startup program: none. metabase.com/startups returns 404 (fetched today); /startup and /pricing/startups are reported 404 by a third-party check (not fetched by me). The pricing page, homepage and lp/bi-for-startups show no startup discount, credits or application; 'startup-friendly pricing' is marketing copy only. Student/education license: none. metabase.com/education returns 404, and the pricing reference lists no student, education, nonprofit, promo or credit program. The Learn section is free tutorials (content, not a license). The GitHub Student Developer Pack page (fetched; long page summarized) does not list Metabase (medium confidence). The only discount is about 10% for annual billing on Starter and Pro. No sunset of any startup, student or nonprofit program is documented for 2025-2026, because none was found.

2025-2026 CHANGES (third-party tracker PricingSaaS Pulse, captures Jul 4 and Oct 5 2025; not verified against archived Metabase pages): Starter $85 to $100/mo; Pro $500 to $575/mo; per-user Starter $5 to $6 and Pro $10 to $12; Enterprise minimum $15k to $20k/yr; storage flat tiers $35 to $40/mo (500K rows) and $70 to $80/mo (1M rows). Current official prices match the post-change figures. Storage is now $2 per 1M rows with the first 1M always free (official today; switch date unverified). Metabot AI on Cloud Pro/Enterprise was introduced around Oct 2025 as free for a limited time (tracker; end date unverified). Official pages now say the first 1M tokens are free, then $3.75 per 1M. Tracker headlines (not verified): Feb 9 2026 storage add-on at $40 and AI pricing at $100 for businesses; Feb 23 2026 Advanced Transforms add-on at $250/mo for 72K runs; Apr 4 2026 'Launches Data Studio and Storage Add-Ons, Expands Free AI Access' (this post could not be retrieved, so the exact 2026 AI change is unverified).

THIRD-PARTY LISTINGS ARE UNRELIABLE: ITQlick (Feb 3 2026) says Starter is free forever, Pro is $85/mo, and there is no free trial; all contradicted by official pages (Starter $100, Pro $575, 14-day trial). The CostBench free-plan page lists limits not found on official pages; frontdeskreview marks its Open Source row stale.

VERIFY IN THE STORE: trial card requirement (official Learn page says yes; the Store sign-up fetch showed only email and password fields); a 2021 Metabase staff reply said a card is required 'to prevent abuse'; self-hosted Pro trial and license-token details; annual payments are non-refundable (docs).

VERIFICATION LIMITS: the session-wide WebSearch budget (200, shared by all agents) ran out during this run, so the GitHub Student Pack and metabase.com-restricted startup/education searches were replaced by direct page fetches. The pricing reference first fetch failed on output size and succeeded on a narrower retry. Date basis: official pages read 2026-10-22; unverified items are labeled above.

findings.name: Vaultwarden software license: free and open source (AGPL-3.0-only), no paid tier
findings.detail: Vaultwarden is free of charge under AGPL-3.0-only (Cargo.toml license field and LICENSE.txt in dani-garcia/vaultwarden; README badge says AGPL-3.0). This corrects the workflow note that said MIT. The README calls the project unofficial and states it is not associated with Bitwarden, Inc. It describes no paid tier, trial, credits, startup or education program, and no managed or hosted service. Listed features include Attachments, Send, Organizations, Emergency Access, Authenticator, Email, FIDO2, YubiKey and Duo two-factor, and the admin backend, with no paid gating described. Official images are vaultwarden/server on Docker Hub, plus ghcr.io and quay.io.
findings.eligibility: Anyone. No .edu email, student status, startup age or funding limit, region limit, or credit card. Students and startups get the same free terms as everyone else.
findings.claim: Nothing to claim. Pull vaultwarden/server:latest (per README) or build from source, then run it on your own host behind HTTPS. Support is community-only (Matrix, GitHub Discussions, Discourse); the README asks users not to use Bitwarden's support channels.
findings.expiry: None. The license is perpetual and has no renewal.
findings.gotchas: (1) This is not a student or startup program, so there is no eligibility to claim. (2) AGPL network clause: if a startup modifies Vaultwarden and users interact with it over a network, the modified source must be offered to those users. The 1.28.0 release notes (2023-03-26) say unmodified use only needs a pointer to the repository. This is not legal advice. (3) The web vault requires HTTPS per the README, so in practice you need a domain and a TLS certificate. (4) No official hosted service exists; treat third-party 'hosted Vaultwarden' offers as unaffiliated with the project.

findings.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free: compute and storage to host Vaultwarden (third-party host)
findings.detail: Per Oracle's Always Free docs, the monthly allowance is: Ampere A1 compute totaling 2 OCPUs and 12 GB RAM (1,500 OCPU-hours and 9,000 GB-hours); 2 VM.Standard.E2.1.Micro instances (1/8 OCPU and 1 GB each); 200 GB combined boot and block storage plus 5 volume backups, in the home region; and 10 TB outbound transfer per month. This is an Oracle offer, not a Vaultwarden offer, and is a common place to run a self-hosted Vaultwarden.
findings.eligibility: Any new or existing Oracle Cloud account. Not limited to students or startups. Oracle's free-tier overview says most users need a mobile number and a credit card to create an account; the card is not charged unless you upgrade.
findings.claim: Create an Oracle Cloud account and choose a home region (Always Free compute and block volumes must be created there). Create an A1 or E2.1.Micro instance within the free limits, then install Docker and run vaultwarden/server behind an HTTPS reverse proxy.
findings.expiry: Oracle says Always Free resources never expire (free for the life of the account). The idle-instance policy below can still reclaim instances.
findings.gotchas: (1) Idle reclamation: Oracle says idle Always Free compute instances may be reclaimed if, over a 7-day period, 95th-percentile CPU utilization is below 20%, network utilization is below 20%, and (for A1 shapes) memory utilization is below 20%. A lightly used password server could meet these thresholds, and the docs do not describe the reclamation process. (2) 'Out of host capacity' errors can block creating A1 instances. (3) Block volumes created outside the home region incur regular charges. (4) Trial credits and Always Free are separate; see the Oracle trial finding.

findings.name: Oracle Cloud Free Trial: $300 in credits valid up to 30 days
findings.detail: Per Oracle's free-tier overview: $300 in cloud credits, valid for up to 30 days. The page shows only a dollar sign and does not name a currency code. Trial credit pays for paid resources. Always Free resources are separate and are not time-limited. If the trial ends without an upgrade, Always Free resources keep running, paid resources provisioned with trial credits are reclaimed, and any OCI Ampere A1 instances above the Always Free allowance are disabled and deleted after 30 days unless total A1 usage is no more than 2 OCPUs and 12 GB before the trial ends.
findings.eligibility: New Oracle Cloud accounts. Most users need a mobile phone number and a credit card to sign up. The card is not charged unless you upgrade.
findings.claim: Sign up for a new Oracle Cloud account with a mobile number and card. The oracle.com/cloud/free sign-up page returned HTTP 403 to this check, so exact sign-up steps are not verified. Before the 30 days end, either upgrade or keep A1 usage within the Always Free allowance.
findings.expiry: Trial lasts up to 30 days from sign-up. Always Free does not expire.
findings.gotchas: Do not confuse the time-limited trial with the permanent Always Free allowance. A1 capacity provisioned beyond the Always Free limit during the trial is deleted 30 days after the trial ends unless you cut it back in time. Upgrading is a separate, deliberate step.

findings.name: Google Cloud Free Tier: one e2-micro VM, 30 GB disk, 1 GB egress per month
findings.detail: Per Google's free-tier docs, always-free Compute Engine limits are: non-preemptible e2-micro runtime free up to the hours in the current month, combined across us-west1 (Oregon), us-central1 (Iowa) and us-east1 (South Carolina), which effectively covers one VM running all month; 30 GB-months of standard persistent disk; and 1 GB of outbound data per month from North America, excluding destinations in China and Australia. GPUs and TPUs are not covered. Unused limits do not carry over to the next month.
findings.eligibility: Any user with a Cloud Billing account. Not limited to students or startups. Region limit: the e2-micro free runtime applies only in the three US regions listed.
findings.claim: Create a Google Cloud billing account (required for Free Tier access; signing up for the trial creates one). Create an e2-micro in one of the three eligible US regions with standard persistent disk, and keep usage within the free limits.
findings.expiry: Google says the Free Tier has no end date, but it may change or eliminate limits with 30 days' notice.
findings.gotchas: (1) Usage beyond these limits is not covered by the free tier. (2) 1 GB per month of egress is small; any transfer above it is outside the free allowance. (3) The e2-micro free runtime is US-only. (4) A billing account is required for Free Tier access, and trial sign-up requires a valid payment method.

findings.name: Google Cloud new-customer Welcome credit: $300 valid 90 days
findings.detail: Per Google's free-tier docs, new customers get a $300 Welcome credit valid for 90 days from trial sign-up, usable on paid services. Trial sign-up requires a valid payment method; Google places a temporary authorization hold, which is not a charge.
findings.eligibility: New customers who sign up for the free trial. Requires a valid payment method. Not limited to students or startups.
findings.claim: Sign up for the Google Cloud free trial (this creates the billing account), add a valid payment method, then create resources within the 90 days.
findings.expiry: Expires 90 days after trial sign-up.
findings.gotchas: The credit is time-limited, unlike the Free Tier limits in the separate finding, which have no end date. Do not confuse the two. Trial sign-up requires a payment method.

findings.name: AWS Free plan for new accounts: up to $200 in credits, account closes after 6 months
findings.detail: Per AWS's free page, the Free plan provides up to $200 in credits: $100 at sign-up, plus up to $100 more by using key services. Credits and the account last at most 6 months, and access is limited to select services. The account closes automatically 6 months after opening or when credits are used up, whichever comes first. Charges apply only if you move to the Paid plan or enable paid-only services.
findings.eligibility: New AWS accounts that choose the Free plan. The page states no student or startup condition. The page does not say whether a credit card is required.
findings.claim: Create an AWS account and select the Free plan at sign-up; use the key services named on the page to earn the extra $100 (the list was not captured by this check).
findings.expiry: Up to 6 months, or until credits run out, whichever is sooner; then the account closes automatically.
findings.gotchas: A self-hosted Vaultwarden on the Free plan will be shut down at the 6-month or credit limit unless you move to the Paid plan, where usage beyond credits is billed. The page does not describe the legacy 12-month Free Tier (EC2 and EBS limits), so that is not covered here. The page does not give an effective date for this plan structure.

findings.name: AWS Paid plan promotional credits: up to $200 for new customers who may qualify
findings.detail: Per AWS's free page, on the Paid plan (all services, billed for usage), new customers may qualify for up to $200 in credits. Only the Paid plan is eligible for promotional credits. Usage beyond the credits is billed.
findings.eligibility: New customers who may qualify. The qualification criteria are not stated on the page.
findings.claim: Choose the Paid plan at sign-up. The page does not describe how to check eligibility or apply the credit.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page.
findings.gotchas: Qualification is not guaranteed, and the criteria are not stated. Credits run out, and the Paid plan bills for usage after that.

findings.name: AWS Activate startup credits: Founders up to $5,000, Portfolio up to $200,000
findings.detail: Per AWS's credits page: Activate Founders (self-funded) gives up to $5,000, starting at $1,000, and select participants may qualify for more, up to that cap. Activate Portfolio (pre-Series B) gives up to $200,000. AWS Credits for AI Startups is $200,000 or more, invitation-only and available after Portfolio (contact your account manager). Credits are in USD under the AWS Promotional Credit Terms. The page does not state a duration.
findings.eligibility: Founded within the past 10 years; pre-Series B funding stage; AWS account on a paid plan; new to Activate Credits or seeking more than a prior award. Portfolio also requires accelerator or VC backing through an Activate Provider Org ID; Founders does not. Incorporation and region rules are not stated. Not for students.
findings.claim: Create an AWS Builder ID with a work email and complete your profile. Choose Founders or Portfolio, answer questions about your product and funding, connect an AWS account to the Builder ID, and submit. AWS says to expect a response in 5 to 10 business days.
findings.expiry: Not stated on the page. The AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions govern; they were not read.
findings.gotchas: The amounts are caps ('up to'), not guarantees. Portfolio needs an Activate Provider backer. The page does not say whether a credit card is required.

findings.name: Azure for Students: $100 credit for one year, no credit card
findings.detail: Per Azure's students page: $100 in credit, spendable on most Azure services (not Marketplace offers), valid for one year. The subscription renews yearly while you remain a student; the page does not say whether the $100 is granted again at renewal. When the credit runs out, Azure emails you to choose pay-as-you-go. If you do not switch, your subscription and its products are disabled.
findings.eligibility: Students enrolled full-time at a university, signing up with a school email. No credit card needed. One account per person.
findings.claim: Sign up on the Azure for Students page with your school email and verify your student status, then create a VM or App Service within the $100 credit.
findings.expiry: One year, renewing yearly while you are still a student. Renewal credit amount not stated.
findings.gotchas: A $100 credit may not cover a VM running all year, so plan the switch to pay-as-you-go. If you miss the email and do not switch, the subscription is disabled, which can take your vault host offline. The GitHub Student Pack page lists this Azure offer as 'Students 18+', which does not match the Azure page's full-time university requirement; rely on the Azure page.

findings.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack: 1-year domain offers for the HTTPS a Vaultwarden host needs
findings.detail: Per the GitHub Education pack page, read through a summarizer (amounts not independently re-verified): Namecheap offers a 1-year .me domain registration with a free SSL certificate; Name.com offers one free domain with a choice of 25+ extensions; and .TECH offers one domain on the .TECH TLD for 1 year. The pack also lists Azure ($100 credit, see the Azure finding) and other offers, such as MongoDB Atlas ($50 credit) and a Heroku credit, that do not fit Vaultwarden hosting, since Vaultwarden runs on SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL.
findings.eligibility: Students verified through GitHub Education. The page does not describe the student verification method or whether the whole pack requires it; it names verified students only for specific offers (GitHub Copilot, Codedex, DevCycle).
findings.claim: Apply for the GitHub Student Developer Pack through GitHub Education, then claim each partner offer separately. Per-offer claim steps were not captured, except that Name.com needs a unique account address.
findings.expiry: Domain offers are 1-year terms per the page. Renewal pricing after that is not captured.
findings.gotchas: Offers change; verify on the pack page before relying on them. Name.com warns that a request may look like a repeat if the account address is not unique. Check the domain's renewal price before the 1-year term ends.

sunset_notes:
Bottom line: Vaultwarden itself has no trial credits, startup program, education license, paid tier or official hosted service. The software is free for everyone under AGPL-3.0-only, so the only free offers that help students or startups are third-party hosting programs, listed above and labeled as such. No pricing, education or startup page was identified in the repository sources read.

Corrections to the workflow notes: (1) The license is AGPL-3.0-only, not MIT (Cargo.toml license field; LICENSE.txt). The project moved from GPLv3 to AGPLv3 in release 1.28.0 on 2023-03-26, which is not a 2025-2026 change. (2) The start URL https://github.com/vaultwarden/server returned HTTP 404 when fetched today, and the raw README path also returned 404. The repository resolves at https://github.com/dani-garcia/vaultwarden (formerly bitwarden_rs). The Docker image is vaultwarden/server.

Coverage limits: two WebSearch calls succeeded (license; 2026 release changelog). A third query was refused because this session's search budget ran out, so no broader 2025-2026 sweep for Vaultwarden offers was possible. The absence of student, education, startup, trial or hosted offers rests on the README, LICENSE and release pages read today (medium confidence).
